_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't feeling too confident about this game, especially after my experience with the Man of Medan, and how that was such a let down from their previous game, Until Dawn. It had such mixed reviews, and the fact that I had gotten partially spoiled about the ending (which didn't really end up being a big deal in the end), I didn't think I was going to enjoy it and didn't plan on taking it seriously. Then the game pulled me right in from the very start.I'll start with the positive side first. The prologue was really fun and startling. So much went down at once and you feel like you have little control, and without warning it throws you into present day. Then you're left wondering, what does this all have to do with what just happened? The game doesn't waste time setting up the scares and introducing the supernatural, unlike Man of Medan. I was immersed every second of the game, and I scare easily, so between the atmosphere and the jumpscares, it really got to me. The QTEs were fun and certain aspects made combat fun while freaking out at the same time, not as annoying as Man of Medan. Also, the soundtrack is amazing!! The music is so intense and hair-raising, and the opening rendition of O' Death... Flashbacks to Until Dawn came rushing back. Plus the small stuff like accessibility options, dyslexic and or color coded font, ability to disable QTE timers or button mashing. Makes conversation less stressful and also lets you do a casual playthrough if needed.Ok, here's where I'll start with the negatives about the game. The biggest thing first is the amount of replayability. With all the routes, the previous two games they've done had a lot of value in replayability. I don't quite feel the same with this game. I felt no drive to start over and try to get everyone to survive, even though a few characters died in my run. I played the other games multiple times in my first session to either get the prime ending, or just to see what happened. Here I  I'll probably play once more just to see things from the other characters POV that I missed out on.Another big thing is that the characters also make very little smalltalk. Most of the time walking around investigating, there's no casual comments about anything and you can't even talk to the others. I want to be able to talk to everyone between events, get to know how they feel and build relationships with them, even learn a bit more of their history together. I played it with a friend so we could at least talk to each other, but for those who play single player, I think it would make for a silent and unlively game.Then there are smaller things like, sometimes I didn't quite catch when I swapped from one character to the other because it happened mid conversation. I didn't respond as I thought that character would, because I still thought I was the person I started out as. This game is unplayable when using keyboard & mouse, and I still had a bit of trouble using a controller. It was hard to aim during QTE events because you either moved way too far or too slow and you wouldn't make it to the target on time. It was a bit of a nightmare to control the flashlight, as it always moved too much despite the gentlest nudges and I couldn't properly use it to examine the area. The camera angles made it hard to walk, as they really focused on making the camera angles look like you were being watched or priming you for a jumpscare. Sure it works out for the most part, but sometimes there's awkward scene changes that end up with me getting turned around. I never experienced any lag or frame drops running the game on ultra, but there was this visual glitch with lighting and backgrounds not loading in that happened a couple times.All in all, it's a 4/5. I liked it loads more than Man of Medan. The story was way more interesting, the characters more likeable, and dialogue actually felt like it was something a real person would say (most of the time). I recommend that you catch it during a sale, then play it using the online coop with a friend. It makes it so much more enjoyable in my experience. I'm writing this directly after playing the game so I hope I didn't ramble too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the Dark Pictures Anthology series. Having played all three in the series I think they all have their strengths and weaknesses but are generally of the same (high) level of quality. Little Hope was definitely the creepiest and most unnerving of all three games, and it had by far the most jump-scares (some might say too many-- they work on me so the game was a suitably stressful experience). It's a horror game and it is scary. I was also a fan of the the setting (an abandoned town). They had a lot of classic horror themes to work with and they used them well. My major criticism is that, overall, the story didn't deliver quite as well as the other games. It was scary, and the game keeps a mystery regarding the witch-trials and the secret of the town and the subsequent need to escape in front of you, but it feels a little disjointed. There is a mystery but it isn't really something that is treated as a mystery because key parts are revealed at what feels like "check points." The characters aren't bad by any stretch but they feel a little inconsistent as they develop during the narrative. There really isn't a lot of well written tension between the characters but the writing sometimes tries to act like there is. As a consequence, some dialogue choices (the story choices are solid) feel a little unrealistic. It still works fairly well but of all three games I'd say some conversational choices are very obvious and more frequently so than in other games.The ending will be divisive. I see a lot of reasons for saying that it was actually a clever and strong ending, and I can see reasons for saying that it was the least interesting way to resolve the events of the game. I liked it. Overall, I really enjoyed Little Hope. If you are interested in an interactive horror experience (not quite a game really) then Little Hope will be worth your time. If you are interested in the Dark Pictures Anthology and wondering if you should try another title in the series, Little Hope will be worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Game review: Little HopeTitle: Little HopeDeveloper: Supermassive GamesGenre: Interactive Drama, Survival HorrorPlatform: SteamRating: 9/10Spoiler Alert: This review contains major spoilers. Proceed with caution!Overview:"Little Hope," the second installment in The Dark Pictures Anthology, delivers another gripping horror experience that fans of the series will thoroughly enjoy. Following the eerie success of "Man of Medan," "Little Hope" dives into the macabre, weaving a tale that blends psychological horror with supernatural elements.Story and Setting:The game centers on a group of five characters who find themselves stranded in the seemingly abandoned town of Little Hope. As they explore, they uncover the town's dark history, filled with accusations of witchcraft and tragic events. The story unfolds through a series of flashbacks and eerie visions, creating an atmosphere thick with tension and dread.The narrative's strength lies in its ability to keep players guessing. The hallucination theme from "Man of Medan" reappears here, blurring the lines between reality and illusion. The constant shifts between past and present, coupled with the characters' shared visions, make for an engaging and unpredictable storyline.Gameplay:Like its predecessor, "Little Hope" relies heavily on player choice and quick-time events (QTEs). Your decisions impact the story's outcome, determining who lives and who dies. This mechanic adds significant replay value, as players will want to explore different paths and endings.The controls are straightforward, with a focus on exploration, dialogue choices, and timely QTEs. The game's atmosphere is enhanced by its detailed environments and haunting sound design, which together create an immersive experience that keeps players on edge.Characters and Voice Acting:The characters in "Little Hope" are well-developed, each with their own backstory and motivations. The voice acting is top-notch, bringing the characters to life and adding depth to their interactions. The dynamic between the characters is compelling, with their relationships evolving based on player choices.Themes and Analysis:A recurring theme in "Little Hope" is the concept of hallucinations and psychological trauma. The game expertly weaves this theme into its narrative, creating a sense of unease as players struggle to discern what is real. This approach, while familiar from "Man of Medan," is executed with finesse, maintaining its freshness and impact.Conclusion:"Little Hope" is a standout entry in The Dark Pictures Anthology, delivering a thrilling and chilling horror experience. Fans of the series will appreciate the continuation of the hallucination theme, though there's a desire for a fresh narrative direction in future installments. With its compelling story, strong character development, and immersive atmosphere, "Little Hope" is a must-play for horror enthusiasts.Final Thoughts:I'm eagerly anticipating the next game in the anthology and hope it explores a new theme to keep the series exciting and unpredictable. Supermassive Games has proven once again that they are masters of interactive horror, and "Little Hope" is a testament to their storytelling prowess.Rating: 9/10Pros:Engaging and unpredictable storylineStrong character development and voice actingImmersive atmosphere and detailed environmentsHigh replay value due to branching paths and multiple endingsCons:Hallucination theme, while well-executed, might feel repetitive for some playersHave you played "Little Hope"? _childDocuments_.review: Supermassive Games have really outdone themselves with their latest spooky joint. The game takes place in the small town of the title - Little Hope. After a bus crash, a group of college students and their professor are stranded among the trees, fog, and darkness with only their camera phone flashlights to guide them. But as you can imagine, something about this quaint factory town isn't quite right...In classic Supermassive fashion, you will have to make decisions and defeat QTEs (Quick Time Events) in order to progress the story. But not all well intentioned decisions are good, nor are all logical ones. The game places a heavy emphasis on the war between the heart and the head. Do you take the rational route? Or do you go with your gut? There is no "right" way to play.The story is fantastic this time around. If you were disappointed with Man of Medan like I was, chances are you will enjoy this go around much, MUCH better. And I dare say it surpasses Until Dawn. Not as scary, but just as tense. The "visions" that are present in past games are here, and the amount of love and care put into the notes and books littered around the town shined through. I was sad I didn't find all of them in my first playthrough considering how interesting and well written they were! The characters were natural and well acted. There were some hiccups and jarring transitions in a few scenes, but I think those are hard to remedy in a game with so many different and branching story beats. Overall, very impressed with the story and characters.Graphically, it looks just as good as previous games. Maybe even slightly better. It was hard to notice if they were, but Supermassive has the graphics down and the game looks beautiful despite the brooding and dark aesthetic. My biggest gripe was the syncing of audio with characters speaking. They didn't match up amazingly, but not bad enough to look cheap, and not often enough to be jarring and annoying. This game is very much a "AA" game, and it shows, but I think it punches above its weight in places too. Very happy with the game graphically.Sound was passable. In a game like this, you *really* want to be using headphones, and I didn't encounter any sound issues with the game. It also wasn't all that remarkable. Decent sound is better than bad (or no!) sound!Overall, this is probably the second best entry in the Supermassive catalog of this style of game, and arguably better than Until Dawn. With the hole left in the hobby by Telltale, I think that Supermassive is filling the niche spectacularly, and doing a hell of a job with the medium. I congratulate the entire studio on a job well done with Little Hope, and am looking forward to the next entry in the Dark Pictures Anthology next year!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start off with some positives:I actually appreciate the idea of keeping characters alive by making them act more empathetic towards each other. That also makes sense in terms of story if you look at it from a condemning vs forgiving or self healing vs self destructive angle. That was new & fresh to me. Even though having them start off "bad" in order to make them better of course comes with the inherent problem that it's hard to care for them right away. At first I was like "Wth is everyone so antagonistical? What a bunch of a-holes! I don't wanna spend time with these people." But I came to enjoy the mechanics of "bearings" & "traits".I also like the variations in character designs. Having a middle aged woman for example, and that no one is traditionally pretty or beautiful. They look like normal people.The intro scenario reminded me of a Final Destination film, and had me giggling with glee. That was fun!The enemy designs are what I liked the most. Johns personal demon for example is amazing, and interestingly enough it is supposedly the only completely hand animated one, due to the complexity of its jerky movements and broken limbs bending in the wrong directions. Also liked the idea of everyone having their own assigned demon that focuses solely on them, and how the presence of them lingers everywhere, sort of relentlessly, unavoidable, just a matter of time. When you catch glimpses of them in the background, almost out of focus, that's when the game occasionally shines.Overall the game looks fantastic.Now onto the negatives:The acting and voice acting, apart from the Curator, isn't very good. I never once believed any of the characters sincerity, it all came across pretty flat & uneven. Combine this with the exaggerated motion capture acting, and it becomes even worse, with wildly flailing arms and what not. People don't move like that, we don't flap our arms like we're a bird taking flight when we're angry (apart from toddlers perhaps). And the eyes often don't seem to be looking in the right direction. And you occasionally have the usual weird grins on peoples faces, that could be either a smile, or a pain grimache, or the worlds biggest smelliest fart taking place. You can't make it out. Daniel in particular looks really goofy all the time.There are too many jump scares that aren't in any way earned. If you build up to them correctly and you earn them, then they work (look at James Wans horror films for good examples), but almost none of them work here. Maybe one or possibly two. But the fact is, it would be a better horror game without them. It's just not very scary.Premonitions were of no help whatsoever in my opinion. They are simply collectibles without use masquerading as something more.And here I'm going to make a massive dump. It overstays its welcome by hours. The story and script is weak, locations are boring, dialouge consists mainly of "Wth was that?" & "We gotta move on." And exploring doesn't feel natural since you'll accidentally walk into triggers that won't allow you to finish exploring areas, so to explore properly you have to know all triggers beforehand which sort of defeats the purpose of exploring to a degree.Some have complained that the QTEs are far too generous and that saving everyone is too easy. I did my best first run and still lost one to a QTE and another one I believe for not facing their demon on their own, something I didn't realise was a thing until I read up on it after the fact. A nice detail is that, apparently, the worse your character is the faster the QTEs and "Stay Calm!" segments get. And so maybe that's why most players got slower/more time for those sections of the game?I also seem to be in the minority in this, but I didn't really mind the ending that much, it's fine to me.There are some different modes and collectibles to find, I haven't tried the true co op, I only did the pass-the-controller-around for some pickups and the achievement associated with it. I do admit I like the idea of playing something like this with a beer-infused gang on a sofa, that's about how seriously you can take it. It's dumb fun, but unfortunately a far bit onto the boring end of the playable movie spectrum.All in all I can't recommend it. There are much better examples of these types of games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was near unplayable without a controller.There are missing scenes.Weird pointless cuts.Horrible optimisation.The story was somewhat intriguing, though, much like Man Of Medan, struggles to recapture or even be as close to interesting as Until Dawn. I like the change in formula for the last 2 games, making them multiplayer narrative choice driven games, however this concept is quite new for games like this and seems like there was little to no testing whatsoever (on this and the previous title in the series) so completely takes you out of the immersive experience and all of the issues are infuriating.The characters, again, like Man Of Medan are paper-thin nothing characters and (spoilers ahead) once revealed to be... in Anthony's head, mean literally nothing. The facial expressions and line delivery are reminiscent of the expressionless faces of Pokémon Sword & Shield and awful acting is much like a 1st year film student's project: only worse. Really is a shame because the story is fairly interesting, not as interesting as Until Dawn but not as weak and predictable as Man Of Medan.DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THISIt is ridiculous that another game is in the works when this game isn't even finished. I am not sure how this game has mostly positive reviews considering all I've seen and experienced from it is a vast engulfing pit of disappointment. I don't want to blame the developers, I know how hard the industry can be/is, but the ones above them churning out these games with little development and testing time. But also, I do blame the developers a bit because no matter how rushed your game is: SCENES SHOULD NOT BE MISSING FROM A £25 GAME!2/10 (at a stretch)

_childDocuments_.review: So, to start, I always play this with friends in “movie night” mode.I thought this story was better and more interesting than Man of Medan. But, unlike MoM, I didn’t like that other players got to randomly play instances for your character. Two different times I had friends of mine accidentally miss some instance and my character died on their turn. The fact that this was possible defeats the whole idea of having your own character and decisions. This wasn’t a decision THEIR character made, but instead were decisions they had to make for MY character during their turn. These were mostly escape instances, but they still shouldn’t have any control over what my character does. I hope this doesn’t continue in the 3rd and 4th installments.Other than that, story was great and acting was spot on. Great graphics and definitely fun to get together and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently I played with my bf Man of Medan and Little Hope. They're both really cool if you're into decision-making stories that may affect the outcome. I liked this one better, it definitely showed improvement since their first game Man of Medan.I wanted to clarify one thing about the friend pass system. It's a "time limited event" because it eventually expires. That means once you activate the code it is available only for 30 days. In order to play it with another friend using the friend pass, the one who purchases the original game, should have both the original game and the friend pass downloaded. I repeat, BOTH should be downloaded in the owner's library. The code is provided when you open the original game and should pass it to the other person. The other player should redeem the code in Steam which is followed automatically by the download of the friend pass version of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love these games, but this one is just pi$$ing me straight off.These games are meant to be played with a controller, so if you're playing with keyboard and mouse the game is already a thousand times harder.So for starters, when they're teaching you how to play the game the instructions that show up on the side are COMPLETELY wrong. All the QTEs are done with the mouse, but it instructs you that the QTEs are WASD. Just not true.Another thing, and I HAVE experienced this in another one of their games, The Devil in Me, where the prompt for the QTE that comes up is just WRONG! I was told to click RMB, and I did, but when I did the game told me it was wrong! You know why? Because to survive I was actually supposed to click LMB. Makes me think they didn't even play test it with keyboard and mouse, because that's such an unfair thing that takes me out of the immersion COMPLETELY.Also, currently on my FIFTH try of trying to save Taylor in the scene "Reflections" which is borderline IMPOSSIBLE because not only do you not get the prompt of where to click, like people on CONTROLLERS do (I literally had to LOOK UP where to point it because the demon takes up most of the screen), but the sensitivity is SO SLOW during the aiming scenes that I simply can't MAKE IT to the spot in time to SAVE HER. How is that fair? I'm about to do it again with sensitivity set to 100%, but now I have to sit through the ten minutes of talking just to get to it and not even know if it's going to work. Ugh.Also, the "story" of the game is predictable after the first clue from the curator. Usually these games aren't so obvious, but the first clue you get is something along the lines of "don't blame yourself". Okay, so this is all  It's insane to me that everyone is mad about the ending when the game borderline tells you that This is NOT their best work. I LOVE these series and don't own a controller, so I've been playing them on keyboard and mouse and have noticed that there's a huge disadvantage when you're playing it like so. I REALLY hope they play test the games coming out in season 2 with keyboard and mouse, because I should not have to replay the game a thousand times to save one person when it's not even my fault that she's dying.

Medan was kinda fine, but in Little Hope we spent half of the playtime restarting the game/computer/sessions and searching in forums for random fixes that worked half of the time.  Nonstop desyncs, freezes, blackscreens etc. I want to love these games and I even already bought House of Ashes just to support the devs but I'm starting that one up in multiplayer straight away and if this kind of crap wasnt fixed yet, I'm refunding it (and even if it is fixed there, FIX THIS ONE TOO DAMN IT).Devs, you pour so much resources and love into the fun characters, amazing graphics and design and hundreds of story permutations and yet you can't get your main draw of "PLAY WITH FRIENDS" right??? It's literally the FIRST option in the menu instead of playing in singleplayer! I would rather have a shorter, simpler story with less useless arching so that I can have a stable  MP experience that I can enjoy. I can't recommend this game, not at the state it's at at the moment. Even if you want to just play singleplayer, their plain disregard to the issues that fill the discussions and are still present is not ok. I want to see this series grow and feel good about supporting it if developers will realise they need to support us back.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying these a lot and don't mind getting a new one each year, they arn't perfect or for everyone but they are at least a unique experience in horror gaming. I think this might be the strongest narrative so far in the anthology and some solid if not heavy handed use of metaphor. Characters are a step up from Man of Medan for me personally I liked them all for different reasons, the performances are good but some inconsistencies for sure. I enjoy the little mini documentaries they put in these games as incentives helps put how much work that goes into these into perspective. Ran into some FPS issues again seems to be an issue early on with these games but Man of Medan ended up improved in that regard over time, had 1 hard crash as well as janky scene changes and awkward mocap I feel there is room for some polish here. Even tho I like these sort of games they still leave so much to be desired in terms of gameplay they are very poor in that aspect they leave so much on the table, disappointing. Again with the excessive use of cheap jump scares? Jumpers do have there place in Horror and if done well they are actually very scary(The Conjuring) but the devs just don't use them right now 3 games in a row still doing this wrong, it's annoying. Visually it's a stunning game especially the lighting, some real eye candy best looking graveyard haha. The creature design is also extremely impressive and a real highlight, disturbing stuff. I recommend playing both the Original path through the game along with the Curator's Cut, it adds some nice details and alternate dialogue, Overall it's another entertaining entry to an enjoyable series I just hope they arn't getting complacent. Recommend to anyone looking for a narrative driven interactable horror experience. 8.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: This game is another very well done game in the Dark Pictures Anthology series. I loved the characters as well as the wild storyline. I enjoyed the jumpscares as well as the twists that kept happening. The ending was the biggest shock as I didnt even expect it, as I had many theories but I wouldnt even think that THAT was how it actually went, despite the slight clues. I definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys good horror games. Also I just LOVE the librarian guy and Im already looking forward to play the next part.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda getting into the Dark Pictures games quite late on, but I would imagine if i played this game for the first time the ending plot would've actually shocked me like "woah cool twist". The ending also kind of made me feel like "Did my choices really matter?". Overall, would recommend if you're a big fan of Dark Pictures and want to play a game with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope obviously has a Silent Hill vibes, which is great.If you like horror, fog, abandoned towns, dark history, witches and such themes, you will get it here :)For me, Little Hope is the most serious, personal and thought-out game in Anthology (only 3 games for now).It has a story that can make you think and question different life situations and points of view.Now it is more pleasant to play, because you have a warning before QTE, unlike in Man of Medan.Some people say that game crashes and coop is broken. I had no crashes, haven't played coop, so have no problems with this.Definitely worth a buy if you ask me :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: It was very hard to choose whether to recommend this game or not.Since I had a blast playing it all the way trough, I ultimately decided to recommend it, but god dang did the ending leave a sour taste in my mouth.This is the second game in the Dark Pictures Anthology and this was way better than it's predecessor, Man of Medan.-The characters were way more interesting-The story was way more exciting-A lot of the problems Man of Medan had were solved:--The QTE's sometimes came out of nowhere in Man of Medan, in Little Hope, there are warnings before a QTE, which is a very nice quality of life addition--The "Button Mash" QTE looked almost exactly the same as the normal QTE's in Man of Medan, resulting in some deaths because you didn't realise you had to press the button multiple times. In Little Hope, the button mash QTE is very distinct.-The Movie night gamemode was way better implemented. Movie night is a gamemode where everyone gets their owncharacters assigned and you pass the controlled when it's your turn to play your character.In Man of Medan, you were often responsible for the lives of other characters, making you feel like you didn't really have control over your own fate.In Little Hope you're usually in control over your own character during the crucial moments and one feature I especially liked was where the controls switched between characters during 1 scene. For example, when 2 characters have to run away and jump over a bunch of obstacles, then you'd first control the guy in the front and do the QTE's to jump over them and then the camera switches over to the character in the back and now it was their turn to do the QTE's.It was a very fun feature when playing with multiple people.So, after all those improvements. It shocks me that they still managed to screw up the ending.The game would literally been better if the game suddenly just stopped instead of showing that ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Man of Medan, and I didn't like how it would constantly switched from the present to the past. Got very annoying, especially because it came with a jumpscare every time. I like scary atmospheric horror, not loud noises that only make you jump because they're loud. Graphics are very impressive, but that's the best thing about the game. Story is very disappointing, and that's the most important thing about a game like this. The ending also sucked, so I'd say stay clear of this one, maybe get it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for these. I love choice games and am a big fan of the horror genre, and the Dark Pictures anthology delivers both of those things. Little Hope I'd put in the middle of the pack, it wasn't nearly as good as House of Ashes (my favorite so far), but was still quite enjoyable. I'm not sure how I feel about the overall narrative with how the ending played out but I did love the theme of the witch trials. Will Poulter is always amazing in what he does and I thought the rest of the voice cast did an excellent job as well. The one big negative with this series for me, that once again shows up in this game, is that I wish character fates were more directly related to choice rather than a single quick time event. This is the second time now where the same type of point and hit quick time event bugged out for me and got someone killed, even though I'd had a perfect run other than that with both choices and other quick time events. That's my only complaint with the mechanics though of an otherwise very well made game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mild spoilers ahead, be warned.As a huge fan of Until Dawn and Man of Medan, I expected a similar quality in pay off, pacing, and story.  Unfortunately, that's not the case.  The early and mid game are pretty well done, with some horror/spooky spots, good exploration, and atmospheric areas.  Unfortunately none of it pays off, as the flashback scenes end up making very little sense in the grand scheme of the story (unless you consider it all a bit nonsensical, then it's consistent) and the finale is a deus ex machina that invalidates many of your choices.  As I watched the credits roll, I wondered, "What was the point?"I'll look forward to Supermassive's next game, but I won't be buying it on release like I did with Little Hope.EDIT:I replayed this with a buddy yesterday (1/21/22) and realized maybe I didn't give this game enough credit.  I think there's a lot more going on than you see initially and I've only started to peel the onion.  Check it out and don't think about playing it just once!

It is extremely frustrating to have all of your playable characters killed because some other person messed up their quick time events. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play through of Little Hope.  Great story. I really enjoyed how different it was from Man of Medan.  Not that I didn't enjoy it, but I really enjoyed finding a gaming company that doesn't just recycle the game with a new skin and changing the dialogue and call it a different game.  I really am looking forward to their newest release.  *Liked*1.) Graphics on point.2.) Story, top notch.3.) Character interaction w/ decisions that mattered.4.) Music/Sound, kept you at the edge of your seat waiting for what was coming.5.) Replay value. each play through takes about 6 hours.  Every choice you make or don't make changes the outcome of your current play through so, you could have hundreds of hours and never see every possible ending.*Disliked*The one and only thing I didn't like are the controls, I don't use a game pad and that might make a huge difference but mouse and keyboard you feel very awkward trying to navigate through rooms. _childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Played the Co-Op version.Massive fan of the Dark Anthologies, played Until Dawn and Man of Medan (Co-Op) so had an idea on what was in store for us. The jumpscares didn't fail once and you're always sat on the edge of your seat. The story was just as twisty and turny as its sister games and the 'Noooo!' from a friend as you get broken up will never get old. Angela is a babe and must be protected. The only downfall to this game is the known bug, the loading screens of death. Our game would crash on cut scenes when inspecting items, after chapters and when reloading the game. Perseverance is the only fix I can advice. On one of our experiences with this bug we spent half an hour Alt-F4ing and reloading the game, starting the chapters from the beginning and having 'Little Hope' (pun heavily intended) in getting the game to work. We managed it and was so glad we just stuck with it. I have no faith in this bug being fixed with the new game now close on the horizon, but all I can suggest is you just sit tight and keep trying (if you have the patience like we did) because it will not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly a thumbs down even on a sale.  No spoilers.Firstly having to use a number of work around's just to get the thing working leaves a very bad taste in the mouth.  That aside this is a big step down from the previous title anyway.Technically it's marginally better than Medan and runs smoothly maxed out but this is due to using the Silent Hill trick of covering everything in thick fog reducing the resources needed.Unfortunately this reeks of being rushed through and could have done with being delayed for at least another Six Months and has all the feeling of an outsourced project.  The acting is very poor compared to Medan and comes across as people just reading lines with no investment in them.  There is no connection with any of the characters and the interpersonal relationships are distinctly synthetic as opposed to the stellar performances in Medan.  Even the legendary Pip Torrens is curiously bland and unconvincing in this like he's just doing it for a paycheck.A handful of the monster cut-scenes are well done and nicely creepy but that's about it.  The sound is inconsistent and will often have you reaching for the volume control.What kills it though (as is often spoken about so it's not a spoiler) is that nothing you do makes any differences no matter what choice is made either in conversation or action.   Failing a QTE can result in a character being bumped off but even so there is still only One ending.  I'm on my Third run through and making different choices with the same outcomes so it's pointless.The final nail in the coffin regarding value for money is that there isn't a Curator's Cut either so when you're done then you're done.I would only recommend this on a very deep sale for a One and Done experience unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played Man of Medan already with a friend and now I've picked up Little Hope with them, and boy is it good. I would not buy this unless you're interested in experiencing 75% of the story and then being unable to continue.

_childDocuments_.review: Just gonna leave this here because people are disliking this game for its ending without looking at the whole picture of the story at hand.I will start with the bad: it does have a tendency to crash I've heard, and i did experience a crash one time. the controls are a bit wonky when the fixed camera moves scenes, and i constantly had to readjust which key i was using. not being able to skip the intro song and credits also kinda sucks. this one is just a personal gripe, but i found it annoying that there is no toggle sprint button (that i know of) just holding it, so i found myself remapping it to M4.the good: if you seek all the collectibles (like i did) the true story becomes more clear, i will not spoil it here though, searching each new area for collectibles was really fun. the interactions between the game's characters was fairly solid, nothing too amazing, but i felt genuine chemistry, unlike in Man of Medan. certain areas having a 360 camera felt nice, and i'm glad that the next installment if gonna have a 360 cam 100% of the time.overall, i feel this game is a major improvement over Man of Medan, but is still flawed. if you do not like reading and piecing clues together i feel this game is not for you, as i expect you to be disappointed by the ending in this case.

You need to be aiming at the 'right' spot in order to land a hit.  So, even if the head is closer than the body, if you don't click the right part, you fail the QTE.  The aim is also atrocious.  Some instances you can't even drag your cross hair in time no matter how fast you drag the mouse.  The story is all over the place and the ending is literally .  The clues you pickup are mostly useless lore.  The whole witch trial horror and the doppelgangers are explained in the ending and it is so underwhelming.  The dialogue is mostly 'huh? what's going on?' what's happening?' and the character relationship meters do absolutely nothing for the narrative. _childDocuments_.review: If you go in with the right expectations, Little Hope and its kin (games like Man of Medan, and Until Dawn on PS4) offer up very enjoyable and quite thrilling experiences that warrant more than one playthrough each. This particular go around I played the game solo, but having experienced Man of Medan in multiplayer mode, I can't wait to do the same for this one, as it transforms the experience substantially.With games like this where the story essentially  the gameplay, it is impossible to discuss it in any detail without heading into spoilery territory. With that in mind I'll stick to the general characteristics. The atmosphere of Little Hope is sufficiently tense and spooky, and never once while playing did I feel at ease or comfortable. Jumpscares abound, of course, but they never feel cheap. The story presents questions and discussions of innocence, guilt and forgiveness, and the struggle against personal demons is an ever present motif throughout.If you enjoy modern horror, and the style of gameplay that can only be described as the Telltale formula (albeit with more impactful choices) then Little Hope, as well as Supermassive's other games warrant a purchase and a playthrough. Little Hope, like Man of Medan before it, leaves me excited for the next entry in the anthology.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like scary games that focus on story rather than kill-all-the-monsters gameplay I bet you would enjoy Little Hope. I loved it, and if this type of game appeals to you I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.I was a bit disappointed by Man of Medan, the previous game in the Dark Pictures series. If you are in the same boat (ha!) I would say not to worry; I liked Little Hope as much as or better than I liked Until Dawn.If you don't like these kinds of games at all (story-focused, with light gameplay and contextual quick time events), however, then I doubt you would like Little Hope. Although executed very well it doesn't change the core game mechanics of the previous games at all. I don't think I personally wouldn't classify it as a "walking simulator", but you will spend your time walking, looking for clues, choosing dialog options, watching cutscenes, and doing quick time events during said cutscenes. If what I just described sounds kind of boring to you but the subject matter is appealing then there's still a chance that you might like Little Hope; even if you might complain that it's too much like an interactive movie it's still a pretty interesting movie and there's enough to do that it might keep your interest. If, on the other hand, you  that you never like games like I described then you should probably give this one a pass.[Update after reading some other reviews]: I played with an Xbox controller and by myself. I can imagine that it might be more frustrating with a keyboard/mouse, and I can't speak for how the multiplayer works. For what it's worth I didn't encounter any bugs in my playthrough. [/end]I don't want to spoil the story at all (my opinion is that it's best to go in completely blind), but I can at least give some tonal comparisons to help you decide. It felt a little bit like the VVitch movie (which didn't surprise me), and also quite a bit like Silent Hill 2 (which I hadn't expected, but was a welcome surprise). If either of those appeal to you I would recommend Little Hope even more.I was really interested in the story the whole way through and wanted to figure out what was going on. I also liked all the characters (except one ;), even though they all had flaws. I also found the game more scary and tense than I had expected; your reaction may vary depending on what you find scary and I would never describe this as the scariest game I had ever played, but it definitely got  heart beating fast in places. Finally, I thought that the pacing of how the story unfolded might be the best I've ever experienced in a branching "choices matter" storyline (where the combinatorial possibilities can sometimes make stories feel disjointed and patched together); there were a lot of things the story set up that had satisfying payoffs through all of the twists and turns, and there was a gradual crescendo of tension right up until the end.I'm resisting my natural tendency to give more analysis so that I don't risk accidentally spoiling anything, but not only have I found myself still thinking about the game's story and themes after the ending but I even immediately started a new game the day after finishing just to see things again with new understanding.If any of this sounds like something you would enjoy then I would highly recommend playing Little Hope!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game i tried from the anthology and it definetly left me with Little Hope for the other games in the seriesI expected at least a fun schlocky horror experience, but, honestly i should have just watched any 80's slasher or splatter film, because frankly, i would get more enjoyment out of 90 - 120 minute movie than sitting through this 4.5 hour bore. Story revolves around students on a bus trip crashing and ending up in town shrouded in fog called Little Hope. The main character is being played by Will Poulter and he, along with the rest of the cast, does decent job, which is one of few positives. However the characters they portray are unfortunately kind of annoying. Aside the Rod Sterling - esque presenter, everyone was either bland or unlikeable.Another flaw is that, despite the game being short, it still feels weirdly padded. You could cut it down to a 2 hour horror movie/game and not miss a thing. It's very repetetive. It's almost always scooby doo routine (i.e. running from undead ghouls) followed up by short exploration section, where the goal is to find something that triggers a flashback, which shows Town's witch hunting past. That actually made me stay till the end, because it was interesting enough to keep me playing and i wanted to see what the game will do with it. So what i got for being patient? Middle finger to the face with the ending that gives Mass Effect 3 ending run for it's money. It makes the most interesting part of the game pointless. They did foreshadow it, but it still feels like they had 2 writers in studio, the first wanting cursed town witch hunting extravaganza and the other psychological horror about processing grief and couldn't decide, so they just mashed it into one.I didn't talk about the gameplay, because there is not much to talk about. It's an interactive movie with QTE's and shoehorned in exploration sequences so it could be barely called an adventure game. And that would be fine, but these games should compensate the lack of gameplay by focusing on story, which has a few bright spots, but it's not enough to save it from being dull, uninteresting and having an ending that erases anything good that plot had to offer. To sumarize, it would be cheaper and better to just buy a horror movie to watch on a friday night.

_childDocuments_.review: A great horror game haunted by its own ending.Let's start with the positive stuff. The game looks pretty good and has an awesome atmosphere, music, and sound design. The characters and story are also well-written (for the most part, but we'll get to that later). Overall, I really enjoyed the many thrills and chills this game had to offer even though there were some phasing problems now and then. Some dialogue also felt pretty unnatural at times. However, it was still a pretty well-made experience and I enjoyed every monster encounter this game had to offer.This can be largely attributed to the fact that the monster designs were solid and gave even someone like me goosebumps. I honestly wish the monsters were even more relentless in their pursuit since they were easily the highlight of the entire game for me.Now let's talk about the bad stuff. The game suffers from quite a few bugs and glitches. There's a small chance that quick-time prompts won't react to your input which results in failure/death. Also, I had a weird glitch where my prompt didn't appear in two fight scenes so I was forced to watch a minute-long slow-motion scene.That being said, the game also relies on jumpscares way too much. It was scary once but it got quite tedious when something jumped on you with a loud sound every two minutes.And now we finally arrived to the ugly stuff. The third act. Before I get to the ending itself I just want to quickly say that in my opinion, it was incredibly dumb to design the final showdown segment in a way where every character who didn't face their monster alone and won was still instantly killed off. It felt extremely cheap and I felt cheated since I managed to keep everyone alive up until that point.Now to the actual ending. Little Hope is a solid game that's being held back by not only its underwhelming twist ending but also overly relying on cheap jumpscares. It's a shame because if you take both of these things away, you have a truly frightening horror experience.

The first game allowed keyboard + mouse no issue so I don't really understand why they decided to switch to the point and click method only.)Not only that but the game really isn't all that scary. They reuse the same jump scare over and over and over again, to the point where you know it's just leading you into a flashback. Honestly compared to the jump scares from the first game....this seems very sloppy. Not to mention the many plot holes in the story and how characters still die despite passing every single timed check that they have you do.Also there's a glitch (one among many in the game) where if you're in the middle of reading something and a cut scene comes on (whether due to the game itself or the person you're playing with progressing faster than you) what you were reading previously will be stuck on half of your screen until you either come across something else to read or restart the game completely. The game seemed like it was rushed and wasn't thought out nearly as well as the first game. And seeing how these are also the creators of Until Dawn, it's a double letdown as I enjoyed both of those games and was expecting a lot more.The only thing about it that I did like was the surprise ending and who they chose as the narrator (who's in the first game too so not really a big plus.) Otherwise I would not recommend the game. I do not plan on playing the game over to change results as I have in their other games because it's honestly not worth my time. If they would add a variety of jump scares and fix the controls to where I can use my keyboard and mouse, as well as even make the game longer (it took less than 4hrs for my boyfriend and I to complete the game) then maybe I'd be happier with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is an excellent experience, one that has clearly learned a lot of lessons from Man of Medan. Don't get me wrong, I love Man of Medan-- but when I recommend that game to friends it's with a caveat: play it in co-op. The unique and engaging co-op experience carries Man of Medan through a lot of things I wouldn't necessarily put up with in a single player game. That unique and engaging experience is still present (and highly recommended) in Little Hope, but this game doesn't need that crutch to stand on its own. It's a wonderfully written and well-executed horror game start to finish. The performance and graphics are much improved from its predecessor. The sound design in particular is en pointe and really adds to some of the death sequences. All in all, I fully recommend this game.

I left the game with a lot of unanswered questions, and was ultimately wondering what the point was. Early on, we'd started piecing some of the story together, and I was thoroughly enjoying it and feeling excited to see things unfold. The ending , and I seriously don't understand how a huge chunk of the story ties into the end. I think at the end of these games, it's fun to talk about your interpretation of things and to make guesses about what some things could have meant. Guessing at almost the entire game, though, is less fun. All that said, I do wonder how much of my confusion may be due to missing out on those chunks of lore.

_childDocuments_.review: *no spoilers*I was a little worried about this because Men of Medan kept bugging out on me in weird ways like skipping parts of the story, characters appearing when they shouldn't etc but thankfully this game didn't give me any issues and it ran great at 4k60.Graphics...They are average at best but average doesn't mean bad by any means.  Its just a very dark game and while it's detailed you can't see most of it.  One thing I thought was really good was the design of certain.. characters.  Don't get me wrong, every character is well done and facial animation is well above average it's just the art design on some are just awesome.One major issue with the visuals is the HDR implementation... Its not very good nor is it consistent.  Some areas look fantastic and how they should in HDR while others are oddly washed out or have crushed blacks and you can't calibrate it out.The SDR implementation isn't great either because in SDR the game is waaaay too dark and just doesn't look right.  It can be helped with changes to calibration but even with it's flaws HDR is the way to go.Sound...Not much to say other than the voice work is generally really good and so are the music tracks and sound effects.  No issues here and it sounds especially good in genuine surround sound.  I played with an atmos setup but the game is only 5.1 which is fine.Story...Like I said no spoilers especially because the story is the game.  All I'll say is I enjoyed it and figuring things out and how to change stuff is fun.Controls...Awful lol just awful, at least with a controller, I didn't try MKB.  What made it awful was unlike their past games this one doesn't use many fixed camera angles so you control the camera but you also control look separate but at the same time and with the right stick. Its hard to explain but it just feels weird and you can never really get the camera AND the flashlight exactly where you want.  It hurts gameplay a little but it's something you just push through.  Hopefully they go back to fixed camera for the next one.  There are lots of quick time events as well and sometimes the game gives you literally no time to push the button.  Thankfully that's rare.. when I say no time I mean the prompt appears and then it's gone instantly.  Overall..This is definitely worth $30 if you like the genre.  Unfortunately I didn't get a chance to try online coop yet but it does sound interesting.  There's also a mode that says it's about passing around the controller but I didn't try that either.  I played with my wife and she just enjoyed laying on the couch next to me and watching me play.  "Its like watching a movie, keep going" is what she said once when I asked if she wanted me to stop and watch netflix.The game isn't perfect but I definitely like their style.  I played Until Dawn on ps4 and both games in this series.  I don't think they have made their "masterpiece" yet but they have the formula nailed and I think they have it in them, maybe next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, it's okay. If you want to "play" a decent episode of Twilight Zone or Beyond Belief with substantial production quality with a couple QTEs here and there this is your game. Since it's about 4 years old as of now, won't be too much to handle for a modern mid-level system but will still look great nonetheless. If you want the long story however, just keep reading and expect minor .Let me start with the "Lethal" difficulty which I don't think is designed the best. More than half of it is fine; correct button pressing, button mashing and the stealth "rythm" sections all work. They can get plenty challenging, and that's what I expected and wanted out of the difficulty. But the "aiming" parts where you have to drag a reticule to a certain point on the screen are almost always bullsh*t I have to say. On other difficulties, where you need to aim is highlighted by a circle; with Lethal you only get the reticule and when you aim correctly it turns red. So far so good but when the correct spot to aim doesn't make any common sense, you feel you get ripped off. I mean I have a sledgehammer and I'm expected to hit a monster's hand of all things when its head is even closer to me? To me that's just nonsense. The whole thing just makes me feel like Lethal mode was designed just as a mode to be played when you compelete the game on easier difficulties, with prior knowledge of the QTEs you need to execute. I just would like that to be disclosed in some way on the menus. Don't get me wrong either since I'm not salty or anything because I couldn't save a character (I'm actually completely content with the ending I got), I just think this difficulty and this specific QTE could've been designed better with little context clues to ever so slightly help on the dot rather than having nothing and making it completely nonsensical guesswork because almost every time, that's what decides if a character lives or dies.And then comes the overall gameplay of the game, which ends up consisting of walking in a very slow speed, interacting with certain objects and trying to make the character you control pointing their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flashlight or light source to where you actually want them towards. I don't get why anyone would hold their flashlight in pure darkness at the side of their body to only illuminate anywhere but where they are headed towards. Don't know for sure if that was an issue with gamepad controls but it sure was weird. Camera was also odd might I add, it just felt it was way too far back from the character that it made looking around a chore sometimes; just one movement of it and a tree branch obscures your view or even another character standing somewhere. And when you add the non-existent level design on top of it all -which turns most of the game into one long corridor where you walk in a painfully slow speed, trying to wrestle with the controls- I was shocked to see my entire playtime was somewhere around 5 to 6 hours, because I swear just walking from point A to B at any given time alone  like it took hours to me. I would even just take the characters to not have the agility of a fridge at that point and have everything else stay the same, because screw "realism" and give me a character that can at the very least "stroll" dang it!     It's a crying shame too, because I really liked the overall premise and much more than I expected I have to add. The whole "Curator" aspect was pulled off excellently; not too cheesy nor too serious, it just hits that sweet spot, almost to the point that I couldn't even wait to see him again. So props to both mocap, voice acting and writing for that. On the other hand, while not incredibly satisfying, the story is also decent as well. I just think writers play their cards too early with little subtlety to boot and that takes away the mystique of the whole situation away too quickly. If you are even a little observant, you understand where the story is going towards rather early on. But even with all these combined, I don't hate the game, however- I simply couldn't go without mentioning all its issues. Without those, I would play this many more times to see every ending, every secret and detail but as things stand that's not gonna happen anytime soon. It's almost the perfect embodiment of a "" game even though I'm not too fond of that scaling system.Thanks for reading this entire, unnecessarily long rant.

Play Movie Night and look upon the faces of your companions as they transform into expressions of absolute horror. Just don't choke on your popcorn while flinching at the sight of that...THING. My friends and I are quite addicted to this series. The sounds, the music, the eerie fog, the sins, long forgotten, getting unearthed... man, this is what horror should be. _childDocuments_.review: While ultimately this is still a good game, I have to say this review pains me to write. Little Hope introduces a complex, layered story with twists and turns throughout the game play. The design elements of this game may even surpass that of Man of Medan. The demons, especially, are an example of the effort the team made in improving the visual element of the game. The interactions between characters are believable. The voice acting is great. This really is a game that currently sets itself apart from other products in the market.However, it really falls victim to sequel syndrome and falls to surpass Man of Medan in my eyes. The main reason is the inescapable feeling that I am on rails through the whole story. I have replayed this game 4+ times hoping to have that experience of finding a new branch to the story, only to experience the same scenes no matter what. The dialogue gets nicer/angrier, the characters become more/less rational, but the scenes do not change. This in the echoes of Man of Medan's branching options () just does not compare. This is only amplified in the two player experience where Man of Medan really succeeded () and Little Hope barely registers. While it improved on ~atmosphere~ the scares themselves fell short (and I am a chicken). The repetitiveness of the jump scares got old quick. I acknowledge they were important to the story, but  have to happen the same way 6+ times?I wanted to love this game the same way I loved Man of Medan, but while the superficial elements improved (visuals, sound design, etc.) it lost its way in the actual game play. _childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I didn't really plan to write this review. I mean... what is there to say? It's the second game in 's horror anthology (a series of short spooky stories told in "choose your own adventure" way with some  elements) and I already wrote detailed review of  (which was the first one), so, like I said, what else is there to say? Surprisingly, it turned out that, even though the core mechanics here is almost identical to what we've seen in , the actual storytelling, the  of the game is pretty different and it does make it to feel... well... . So... here goes.First of all, unlike , this game allows you to re-play previous scenes at any point. In other words, you don't need to play through the entire thing to be able to return to the main menu and re-start from any place you've already visited. And you  want to do that. For two reasons. First –  play (way) bigger role now and it'll be easy to lose one of your characters pretty often. And second – unlike ,  heavily relies on the exploration. I mean, sure, you needed to do some exploration in  to get the full picture of what's going on, but in this game? The entire ending will depend on what you will discover on the way. This time we've got ourselves a witch story (you know,  kind of stuff) and technically speaking, you'll need to discover who put  in the  (if you know what I mean), otherwise, no one will be happy.And that's... quite an interesting thing. See, what we've got here is a multi-layered story. With tons of details, some of which will become clear only during the ending. Which is way,  more interesting than what we had in , in which things were pretty obvious since very beginning. But at the same exact time... it feels a little bit weird. Especially for those of us who play in either co-op or hotseat. Because yes, multiplayer mode is still the main dish in this game, with single player being only five-hours-long thing that, while being totally fine, can't really compete with what you'll get in a company. You see,  with its unique structure that used to make you question everything, was  funny in multiplayer exactly because of that. It was impossible to say what's real and what's not. People used to panic and therefore make a lot of stupid mistakes. And it was  exactly because of that. If you've ever seen horror movies before, you know exactly what I'm talking about. Remember all of those kids on the screen? Screaming and running like idiots and therefore ending up dying in some very stupid ways? That's exactly what  used to make you to do. Here? It's exactly different story (pun not intended). Together with your friends, you'll try to discover as many clues as possible and make some right decisions, while trying to survive all the  encounters. In other words, it's not about panicking anymore. It's about the exploration and  skills. And somehow... it's hard not to miss what we had in previous game.I'm not trying to say that  feels bad, or something like that. Quite the opposite. I'm a  fan of this kind of stories  I'm very glad that the amazing idea of people playing adventure games online that  brothers ( / ) had back in early s () is still alive and kicking. But at the same exact time, the new formula doesn't feel nearly as exciting as the one from  where it was easy to lose the character just because one of your friends panicked and made some really poor choices. Even in single player the new formula doesn't feel nearly as exciting. Just because... you know. After you learn the truth, the game starts to get boring and not only I didn't feel motivated enough to play through the alternative cut (an alternative mode that puts a different set of characters from your group into the spotlight and shows you about an hour of cutscenes you haven't seen before), I didn't even feel like I wanted to save everybody. Just because... but no, I won't spoil it to you. I already said that the story is more complicated this time, let's just say that there won't be nearly as much sense in saving everybody this time.So... yeah. I totally admire the fact that  didn't try to just copy / past things from their previous game. While using the same exact mechanics, they did their very best to make  to feel different. And it does. For both good and bad. I totally loved the story this time, the setting is very solid, the atmosphere is fantastic (as long as you love woods, fog, abandoned houses and stuff like that) and all in all, the game has quite a lot of things to surprise you during your first run. But at the same time, multiplayer mode (again, let's not forget that multiplayer is a main dish here) doesn't feel nearly as exciting. Just because the entire “don't trust your eyes” thing is gone and it's all about the  now. Also, the endgame development can feel a bit frustrating. Especially during your first try. For example, even if you'll be able to achieve the good ending, some of your characters will still be able to die. Just because of some choices you've made ages ago, without even knowing about the impact they'll have on the ending. It's like “Hey! We won! Yay!” and then BOOM! Some monster appears and one of your guys is dead. With no way for you to interfere. It's kinda... smart and when you'll look back and think about all that during your second run, it'll start making sense to you, but at the first time... no, seriously, it's a mess. Playing through the entire thing and then watching your guys dying? Doesn't feel right.I still do recommend this game, though. Heck, I think I'm turning into ' fan. Totally love the way they tell their stories. From  to  to . Can't really call any of those games perfect, but somehow,  never fail to create that certain feeling that makes you feel like you're actually diving into a movie. And I'm not even a big fan of the interactive movies. It's just... I dunno, with  it's always  to be a part of all that. To explore, to make the mistakes, to try and figure out what's going on... I always end up feeling like everything I see in the game is real. For whatever screwed up reason there is. And the multiplayer mode that  offers? I don't think you'll find anything else like that on the market. You have friends who love horror movies? You're in for a treat. Especially if those friends are living nearby. Because personally? I'm totally in love with the hotseat mode here. Just make sure to order enough pizza and the next five hours of your life will be awesome. I'd say, play  first, though. Because, even though story there isn't as cool as in , multiplayer-wise, it's the best one so far. Dixi.

_childDocuments_.review: This will maybe be the only review I post to steam, but for once I actually do feel like it's important for my voice to be heard. I thoroughly enjoyed 4 hours and 57 minutes of the time I spent playing Little Hope with my friends, using the steam remote play option. Even though the jump scares felt cheap, the narrative threading through several time periods, syncing up the past paranoia of the witch trials with the constant pursuit of the current period protagonists was legitimately gripping. The pairing off of the doppelgangers, with ghosts of the past haunting their present counterparts felt like a cool and unique mechanic, and the idea that your behavior in the present might impact your ability to deal with them was interesting. Imagine by correcting your current behaviors you might be able to fight off the spectres of your ancestors, that's the legitimate feel I got! But that's not what the story of the game gave me. I have never felt so disrespected by an ending to a game in my life. To say that my choices over those five hours meant nothing is an understatement. If they meant nothing I would have neither gained nor lost investment over the whole arc. I ended the game with a net loss in investment, I entered this game which I was actively looking forward to so frustrated with how emotionally bankrupt the ending was. Everyone playing with me was so mad they *gave me money* to compensate me for the loss we all experienced. Look, sometimes movies or shows set up plotlines they don't know they can't finish, and they let them whimper and die in the end. This game sets up plotlines and character arcs knowing full well they mean nothing, and in the end only the decisions of one character truly matter. Just a master class ♥♥♥♥ you of a game.Supermassive I want to love your games, I feel like you're doing a style of gameplay very few people are putting out there nowadays. Seriously, the only company outside of David Cage's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to do this style of movie hybrid gameplay. Please do not disappear up your own ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like he did

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend the game? Yes, BUT! I don't want to give it a positive review, because it has some problems that can sour the experience.First of all, the Friend's Pass. If this was a limited time only, add a message to the front page stating it, or just plainly remove it from the library. My friend and I, spent a lot of time researching how to use it, downloading the game multiple times, to find out that maybe it was just a limited time offer kinda thing?Second, we had to buy a second copy of the game (which in on itself is not a big deal if you know beforehand that the Friend's Pass does not work). Also, every other game in the series has already been discounted on sales, but not this one, why?And this leads me to the third, for a game that has never been discounted on sales, to have so many bugs it is just simply unacceptable. For what I've seen in the forums the bugs have been reported in countless occasions but they are still present in the game. They don't even seem to be that hard to fix, i.e.: a black screen for one player in co-op, that magically fixes itself once the other player hits a cut-scene (by the way, that's how we managed to actually play and finish the game, using this "fix" in at least 3-4 places during the story)Now, on to the actual game... the MVP of course is the curator, like in Man of Medan the narrative and the way that he introduces the story to the players and builds up the mood is excellent! Little hope has a good story to tell, however, in my opinion Man of Medan was a little bit superior.For a ~4-hour game that it still has game-breaking bugs, the price tag seems a bit steep to me, regardless of the nuances, I had a great evening playing through this game and I look forward to playing the next title in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I have reviewed the first story Man of Medan, and Played through a solo play of Little hope.Disclaimer: this is not a sequel. They are stand alone short horror stories, under the umbrella "the dark pictures anthology".  Think tales from the crypt, twilight zone, etc.    This means you don't need to play Man of Medan to understand what is going on in Little Hope.  Man of Medan is about a story of a ghost ship, and Little Hope is about Witch Trials.  With this said, let's move on to the review.It's a story driven, choice based and quick time event game.  Movement in the game has been tweaked from Man of Medan, but still can feel clunky.   At times the camera angles can be disorienting.  This is more noticeable when your characters enter buildings; also during static camera angle scenes.  During outdoor scenes, they improved by being able to rotate camera angles as you walk.  It is good that they improved this.The old dreaded quick time event system.  This was improved as well.  Man of Medan's QTE's were too sudden, felt unresponsive and didn't give enough time.  In Little Hope, they give you a symbol briefly before the QTE is needed.  It gave you time to mentally prepare yourself that you were playing a game and not watching a movie.  Type of QTE's,  Target and aim selection, single push, button mash, rhythm based.   The rhythm based added slight more complexity in Little Hope compared to Man of Medan.  In Man of Medan, you only had to worry about one button, in Little Hope, they upgraded it to two buttons you needed to worry about.  I liked that.The soundscape and scenery were great, both are comparable Man of Medan and Little Hope, you can't go wrong.  Very good.I am very pleased they are sticking with "Oh Death" as their opening and credit songs.  It makes the individual stories feel connected through that song.  The credit songs are "oh death" but are different renditions compared to the intro song.    I like it and hope they continue with this format. So that will bring us to the actual story or theme and I will try to not spoil it (just get the game).  Little Hope's theme has to do with The Witch Trials.  This story blew Man of Medan out of the water if we compare.  Little Hope got the idea across of confusion, guilt, what is to believed or not and paranoia very well.  Comparing to the historical events of those times, I could only imagine what those people went through.  This story follows a group of students and a teacher through the Town of Little Hope. After a detour, the bus crashes.  These group of characters must make sense of what happened as they look for help.  Meanwhile, the ghost town seems to just keep them there.  They certainly gave a nod to silent hill in that sense. What did Little Hope learn from Man of Medan?....Not to be very obvious about the clues.  Man of Medan's "twist" fell too early and was riddled with early spoilers.  The horror fell short of the mid point of the story.   In Little Hope, it was not spoiled for me with my first play through.  Looking back there might have been hints, but they were not as obvious as what Man of Medan did.  I think they got it right in this story.I grew more attached to these characters compared to Man of Medan.  Something felt right with the acting.  The scenes made sense and I was genuinely invested in the characters and not just "hope I get a good ending" invested.  The tone of voice made sense for the scenes characters were in.  Just, all I can say is, it is a much needed improvement from Man of Medan. Do note, there were scenes which did not give explanation of what off stage characters experienced.  However, I believe if this game has an alternate story line, you will get to play those scenes on a second run through.  You may also be able to see them if you make different choices compared to myself.The horror aspect of this game, they nailed.  Just enough jump scares, tense scenes and calm scenes which felt balanced.  Man of Medan was riddled with jump scare after jump scare which soon wore thin.  Little Hope's Antagonistic enemies felt relentless.  I did end up saying "OH COME ON, give me a break" at one or two points.  So I would say, that would be a good thing, as you felt pursued by these things that just never gave up.My ending was a complete disaster...for all characters involved.  In little hope I didn't feel cheated out of the ending I got.  My mistakes were and felt like my mistakes.  I genuinely got upset at these characters deaths. It was a mixture of, wow how did I mess that up, to oh man, not that character!!!..Man of Medan had one pivotal moment which sealed your characters fate and gave you a not so great ending. Man of Medan's QTE situation without warning, unresponsive button pushing, I felt cheated.   Little Hope does not feel this way.I played the full game through 4.5 hours in one sitting.  It was worth it.  You may be a bit under or over with time play depending on how quickly you read or what events you get.  If Co-op play is anything like Man of Medan, it is worth playing with a friend.  Also, Movie Night mode was a blast in Man of Medan, so I don't expect anything less with Little Hope.  5 players take on a horror movie?  Now you will see who would really survive a horror film or not.Yes, I recommend this, yes it has replay value, yes it might not be perfect, but I assure you it is worth it.  If money is tight, just wait for a sale.  As for the bugs, I didn't experience anything like what other users are experiencing.  However, read up on the discussion boards and ensure your computer can play it with the specs it asks.Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is the second story in the Dark Pictures horror anthology. Three college students and two teachers have been trapped in a small abandoned town, and the player must guide them to safety. As is usual for this type of narrative focused game, the primary gameplay mechanics involve making dialogue choices and performing QTEs during action scenes.After the first hour of establishing the story, I felt like the group was in constant danger, being attacked frequently by strange monsters, whose visual design is very creative. Any of the main characters can die if you make bad choices or mess up the QTEs, and while I wouldn’t say the game is scary, this certainly makes the action scenes feel intense. I kept everybody alive on my first attempt in Man of Medan, but I didn’t have the same success in Little Hope.The story was mostly well written and has an interesting sense of mystery, incorporating different time periods and themes of witchcraft, but the ending was kind of annoying. It makes sense, but it made me feel like ultimately nothing I did had any relevance. Its a shame, because until that final scene I really enjoyed playing Little Hope. It took me 4.7 hours to finish the story, which is almost an hour longer than Man of Medan, but still quite short.Voice acting is very good, although I have to mention one moment of unintentional comedy, when one of the group insists that another character spoke in a strange unrecognisable accent, as more evidence that weird stuff is happening in the town. Where I live, we call that accent “Yorkshire”. I guess they’ve never seen a Sean Bean film.Controls worked fine with my Xbox 360 controller, and I didn’t have any problems with bugs or framerate. However I’m disappointed that the developers insist on continuing their version of Telltale’s “x will remember this”, where pretty much every choice made or item collected flashes up a message in the top corner informing the player of “traits updated” or “bearing updated”. Its hard to be scared when you’re constantly being reminded that you’re playing a game.Little Hope is worth playing if you like horror stories, but I definitely advise waiting for a sale, because its short and the replay value is questionable.
