_childDocuments_.review: The graphics created to scare are well done and the story is interesting but the problem is in the execution. I've never had an issue with wasd controls but because all of the scenes are dark the only indication of where to navigate is when "inspect" or "examine" pops up so the wasd in this game made it more difficult to navigate. I enjoy allowing the features of a scene to capture my attention then navigating to that spot. The scenes are featureless so the only reason for me to inspect or examine a spot is because those command words pop up in that area. Most of my time was spent navigating a scene to make sure I didn't miss a vital element in moving the story to it's conclusion. SPOILER ALERT Two of my characters died not because of my choices but because I didn't understand what key or button to use and how to use them. An icon would appear such as which mouse button to use but other icons such as a fist telling me to fight weren't clear in which keys to use to do so. It isn't because I'm a newbie in gaming. Even though action games like Halo or Call of Duty aren't my favs I've been a gamer since 2005 so I do know my way around a keyboard and mouse. SPOILER ALERT again. Your characters find themselves unexpectedly observing the past. Those conversations they witness give you hints of who the real bad guy is and what choices to make. You do get to see the bad events of the past but most questions the events create in your mind go unanswered. The Death character in the library is very frustrating. He doesn't add anything of substance to the story and the few hints he gives you doesn't save any characters. He's just a cool graphic that quotes Shakespeare. The ending was just awful. At one point I thought alright! I got the bad guy! Yes! Justice is served! Then after the characters patted each other on the back and exited the house without any explanation another one of my characters gets killed. Huh? What just happened? To make the confusion even worse the only living resident of the town, a character who's past is never really explained only hinted about tells you there is nothing left and don't come here again. You are then enlightened to what actually transpired. I realize the Dev wanted to create a game where different choices have different endings so that the gamer could have many hours of play but the gamer needs to understand exactly which choices brought upon which set of consequences. What a Dev doesn't want is a gamer to be sitting in front of the monitor, eyebrows furrowed, mouth slightly opened saying out loud wtf? WTF? WTF!!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: *Friend Pass / Online controversy aside (I understand the hate)The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope's story is fantastic!I found the story to be more engaging than Man of Medan's, The atmosphere and visuals compliment each other very well, especially if you're either on an ultrawide or playing on the couch with a 4K HDR tv. (*More on that later)The graphics, lighting and fog effects are some of the best you'll see in the current age of gaming, especially in cinematic genre.The characters are great, despite not learning much about their background  they made a good attempt at character development, as you're choices will affect how the relationships between characters are.It's always exciting to see the likeness of actors in video games, and having Will Poulter as Andrew was perfect the character.I found myself on the brink of ****ing myself multiple times due to the jump scares. (despite how predictable half of them were)Gameplay was great but fixed certain camera angles were not it, thankfully not like the OG Resident Evil's cameras.I am not one for Quick Time Events, so being an interactive, cinematic title I didn't feel bad about playing on the easier difficulty with the QTE warnings.Not sure if it's just me, however walking feels no different when you hold shift or LB. (Game claims that you'll walk quicker holding Shift or LB on controller)Fortunately, I did not experience any bugs or crashes like some reviewers have mentioned.I really enjoyed this entry to the Dark Pictures Anthology and despite the mixed reviews at the time of this review (Most seem to be due to the Friend Pass / Online controversy) I do recommend it to anyone who is looking for an engaging interactive cinematic game, however be careful if you're wanting to experience with friends. I have not tried the online part yet so I can't comment.*I originally started this one first out of the trilogy, and started playing at my desk before deciding to finish the story and play the others titles on the TV with a controller, and honestly that made me regret not doing that to start with.The Dark Pictures Anthology games are definitely in my opinion best experienced with a controller with a large HDR 4K tv.

_childDocuments_.review: While I thought the way the game did a fairly good job at creating an eerie setting and the story line had some interesting stuff going on when it linked itself to the past, overall it wasn't great. A lot of the time when I see people criticise the dark pictures anthology they immediately get responses saying 'well you can't expect it to be as good as Until Dawn. the whole point is that they're lower budget games', but a game being lower budget isn't an excuse for it being bad. Plenty of low budget games are good because they are still well executed.It doesn't excuse the poor choice system where decisions that have no real meaning behind them in the moment lead to a character death, or the crappy (in my opinion, ik some people like it) ending, or the weird writing of the characters dynamics with each other where they seem to stir conflict for no reason even if you pick friendly dialogue. One thing I will give it is that while I find the ending to be cliche and to detract from the main struggle of the story in keeping everyone alive, the story does actually consistently support the build to the twist, so the thought into the writing there was good. But damn I hate the ending. Just wasn't it imo. However, the characters feel pretty one-dimensional, although the voice acting is done well. I also enjoyed the curator as a narrator. Parts of the story seemed to get interesting and pulled me in, just for it to lull again. Also, why does a 5-6 hour game take up 42GB of space? RE2R takes up a little over half of that and is a bigger game and about twice as long.A lot of people like this game, and I see why they do, especially if you're a fan of the ending. However I just found the game to be a bit lackluster, especially when there's so many solidly good horror games out there that are worth playing instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Man of Medan, Little Hope is based to some extent on true events or legends and this time it's about the Salem witch trials of the late 17th century.With a great atmosphere, we are a group of college students and their professor on a school trip when the school bus has an accident.And things seem to escalate relatively quickly.The bus driver has disappeared from the scene of the accident and an impenetrable and mysterious fog makes the search for help one hell of a trip.We are inevitably stuck in Little Hope, where, it seems, time has stood still.Apart from the witch trials that took place here, the city was once a thriving business location. At least until the local textile factory closed and the residents gradually left.What remained was a ghost town that is now haunted by the past.And I can tell you this much:The resolution at the end is quite successful and whoever survives Little Hope's nightmare will be surprised. This is largely due to the fact that the story remains relatively unpredictable and delivers good moments of tension and comes along with a twist at the end., the game is again more like a movie than a classic game. Although you have the opportunity to move freely with the protagonists in the limited areas, Little Hope remains true to its roots and itself in a playful way.As usual, in the dialogues you have the choice between two conversation options that influence the future behavior of the character and, depending on the action, is a decision that can sooner or later affect the course of the story.In the more action-packed passages, some QTEs have to be passed again. In this part there are new small "pre-warnings" so that you don't get caught on the wrong foot like in Man of Medan.Different icons briefly show in advance whether you have to press a button or, for example, face a challenge in the form of aiming at your opponent.These QTEs are sometimes the most important when it comes to keeping all characters alive.Also important again are the secrets that are often found off the obvious path. These secrets give you information about what's really going on in Little Hope. And as usual, when exploring, you "stumble" over postcards or pictures that point to a possible, mostly fatal event in the future.But the same applies here: if you want to see everything, you have to play through the game several times.The game deliberately uses horror clichés in its narrative and offers a thoroughly exciting story. Still, like its predecessor, it's an absolute jumpscare-fest and spooky-wise the game is no picnic.The abandoned village, the mysterious opaque fog, the forests and the cemetery are almost too many horror clichés at once, but for no reason they are not represented in so many games and films.Coupled with the cruel witch trials, you know why you might get goosebumps while playing. But it only gets really disturbing when Mary, the little girl, appears.With every contact you experience memories from the time of the witch trials and in the form of the protagonists.Unfortunately, the whole horror is destroyed by too many jump scares, always the same and unfortunately predictable over time.A bunch of stupid teenagers: check ✓The cat running through the picture: check ✓A scary little girl: check ✓In his stylishly furnished library, he comments and evaluates the actions of the player and obviously enjoys teasing us with a few cryptic clues and tips packed in riddles. However, he does not have a direct influence on the story and what exactly the curator is all about remains a mystery so far.For me, the great thing about The Dark Pictures Anthology is that I can very well do without my unloved phrases like "the other was better". This is of course subjective, but I think that “the game is different” is much more accurate and does justice to each and every one of the games.. But that is due to the actual scenario with the foggy ambience and I personally found the characters more interesting.The plot with the little "time travel", the bizarre creatures and the mysterious doppelgangers remains quite exciting until the end, even if the "shock effects" wear off a bit over time.The tricky animations, respectively the facial expression transitions and the controls can certainly still be improved, but unlike in Man of Medan, the story in Little Hope is not only forward-looking, but a story that overlays several epochs, which actually makes the biggest difference.Little Hope isn't a psychological masterpiece of horror, nor is it a "continuous shocker". It's interactive cinema and anyone who can get involved in this way and can overlook the cinematic staging in terms of game depth, mechanics and length can expect an atmospheric and audiovisually successful and sometimes convincing horror experience.✅ Atmospheric environment and sound✅ oppressive mood✅ cinematic staging✅ Worthwhile co-op through more scenes✅ exciting story✅ Decisions affect the course of the story✅ Detailed locations✅ mysterious curator✅ different endings✅ alternate history✅ increasing level of difficulty✅ good tutorial❌relatively short❌minor technical defects❌unsympathetic pale characters❌Cracky animations❌ Consequences seem arbitrary❌Predictable jump scares❌End with open questions

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is an entertaining and often scary ghost story set in an abandoned small town. The setting is perhaps less ambitious than Man of Medan (or the next chapter set in the Middle-East), but the creepiness of the town and the surrounding darkness are definitely unsettling. There are several endings possible, but each has subtle variations depending on the actions you take from the start of the game until the very end.As with Until Dawn and Man of Medan, this game is a mix of exploration, dialogue choices, and quick time events. I played single player and streamed the game to my friends, but two players can play together cooperatively. It takes about four to five hours to get through the game. This might seem relatively short, but that length fits the story well and makes subsequent playthroughs less daunting as you get more impactful choices quicker. The short form experience of the Dark Picture Anthology games compared to Until Dawn allows for much more experimentation in the storytelling, as not all stories can easily be stretched to more than ten hours without losing their impact. Overall, this is a perfect game for Halloween or to have a spooky evening with friends. And it's arguably cheaper than going to the movie theater (when there's no pandemic)!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played Man of Medan and House of Ashes. These two games were phenomenal. However, Little Hope was a buggy nightmare with bad mechanics, worse characters, and a horribly concluded story. Mechanics - QTEs are separated into two types: dialogue and aiming. Dialogue was fine, but the aiming was done horribly. Ridiculous aimpoints make you feel cheated when you lose a character. Keep in mind I lost characters in other playthroughs of the anthology, but none made me feel like it was a result of poor game mechanics. There is no aiming indicator (not to be confused with crosshair), which made it difficult to even know what to aim for. A QTE should not be a guessing game of where to aim, it should be quick and reactive. In a game where immersion is key, these QTEs broke all immersion and I quickly found myself just trying to beat the game rather than getting lost in it. Story - Without spoiling, my main issue is not the story itself, rather how it's told. When playing in multiplayer, we had random cuts out of scenes at the end of the game. There are many different endings so it's hard to judge the story, but I definitely have zero drive to explore alternative endings (keep in mind we saved all characters).Characters - The characters were boring. None of them had any substance. In fact, I would go onto say you gain more substance of the characters in the prologue than you do with the group across the entire game. There is even a part where one character (which was the least able character of them all) disappears to fight their monster and just appear back and nothing is even said. Characters are nearly killed and they seem to have no real response. There are no special dialogue events either. TLDR: Buggy, poor mechanics with QTE, and boring characters that seem unalive and bland make a plot feel empty and void despite having potential. Real letdown from the Anthology.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember the days when you’d take field trips in school. Loading into the bus with all your fellow miscreants, driving for an hour or two, then touring some historic place where Betty Boop, or Mr. Potatoe Head lived 450 years ago, walking through their boring house or historical sights, and wondering when it would be over. The boredom forcing you to rip out chunks of your hair.. Then after 3 or 4 hours, you scuttle back onto the bus, and drive another hour back home.. Imagine, if you will that trip back home gets detoured, and then your bus crashes…..  not the cool fiery crash you see on youtube videos, but the, that sucks I banged my head and scrapped my knee type of crashes..   Upon exiting the bus you find yourself trapped and unable to escape, being forced to travel towards an uncertain fate surrounded by bags from school that you probably hate..Well if you can imagine that scenario above then you’ll probably know what to expect in Dark Pictures Little Hope, the second entry into the Dark Pictures Anthology (Think they are calling it season 1, and it has four entries thus far, Man of Medan, Little Hope, House of Ashes and Devil Inside me)  If you’ve played any of the games you sort of get the idea how the game words,, for those who haven’t here goes.. The Curator, introduces you to himself, and proceeds to pull out a book, which he claims is unfinished and says you will be the one to write it.The Story – Four students and their teacher are returning from a field trip, their bus is detoured into little hope and eventually winds up crashing after the driver swerves to avoid hitting a little girl.  Lost, confused and with the Bus Driver no where to be found the Five lost adventurers start their quest to find the driver, find help or maybe even find themselves.Gameplay – If you’ve played any of the TellTale style adventure games you’ll get a good idea how these games work.  Third person exploration, with loads of cutscenes, some QTE’s, finding collectibles and making lots of choices, choices which unlike most of the later TellTale games actually matter in the grand scheme of things..Pros Tremendously interesting and engaging storyUniquely replay ableEasy achievementsBite Sized 4 hour adventureCons Poorly Optimized (was getting lag with my 4090)Minor Graphical and sound issuesCan’t skip cut scenes you’ve already seenRecommendation – Little hope set aside the atmospheric approach to horror that Man of Medan took and went with Jump scares, and since we’re in 2023, jump scares are kind of weak sauce..  With that said, Little hope tells a compelling story that blends elements of the past with the present to create a edge of your seat thrill ride up until the end.  The game is worth the price of admission for some of the gore, which was clearly ramped up from Man of Medan..  So I’d recommend picking this game up if you’re into Telltale Style action adventure games, the story is out of this world.. or dimension and you’ll be happy you did..

_childDocuments_.review: I'd rate this as a must-have in the horror genre, provided you have friends to play with.The pacing is improved over Man of Medan, kicking straight into the mystery where MoM felt a bit sluggish early on. Quicktime events seem a bit less make-or-break and the personality changes you inspire in the characters appear to play a much larger role.The story is quite compelling, with a similar vibe at times to The Shining, Silent Hill and Blair Witch, but with a thoroughly satisfying twist in the works that completely changes how you see things. That alone is enough to encourage a second playthrough, but there's also the fact that, depending on who you choose at the start, you'll follow a slightly different path through the narrative, so your second playthrough can take you through the scenes you missed keeping the mystery alive.A reasonably paced playthrough should clock in at 4-5 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope - A Haunting Tale of Mystery and ChoicesLittle Hope is a captivating and atmospheric psychological thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. From the creators of Until Dawn, this interactive horror experience delivers a chilling narrative filled with twists, turns, and moral dilemmas that will leave you questioning every decision you make.Set in the eerie town of Little Hope, the game's visuals are hauntingly beautiful, with a sense of foreboding that permeates every scene. The attention to detail in the environments and character design draws you into the story and enhances the feeling of isolation and dread.The story of Little Hope is a gripping blend of supernatural elements, psychological horror, and mystery. As you guide a group of characters through a series of terrifying events, you'll uncover the dark history of the town and its inhabitants, all while trying to survive the night and escape the malevolent forces at play.One of the standout features of Little Hope is its emphasis on player choice and consequence. Every decision you make, big or small, can have far-reaching effects on the story and the fate of the characters. This creates a sense of tension and urgency that keeps you invested in every moment, wondering what repercussions your choices will have down the line.The characters in Little Hope are well-developed and complex, each with their own fears, secrets, and motivations. The stellar voice acting brings them to life, making you care deeply about their fates and adding emotional weight to the unfolding events.Gameplay-wise, Little Hope offers a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and quick-time events that keep the pace engaging and the tension high. The game's multiple endings and branching paths encourage replayability, as you strive to uncover all the secrets hidden within the town of Little Hope.In conclusion, Little Hope is a must-play for fans of narrative-driven horror games. With its atmospheric setting, compelling story, and impactful choices, it delivers a memorable and immersive experience that will stay with you long after the credits roll. Prepare to be scared, surprised, and thoroughly entertained as you unravel the mysteries of Little Hope.

_childDocuments_.review: Some time into the game, I get into a state of mind where I completely ignore all the screamers, and just laugh as the characters chase little girl in the fog. I started screaming in scottish accent "MARY! BLOODY 'ELL! COME 'EHE, MARY!!!!"The setting is great, you get your Silent Hill foggy town, Blair Withy dolls and witch trials. Some of situations are dumb like when instead of handing the phone with a flashlight they toss it in the air, but overall nice story.The only dissapointment is the ending because it's just not that original.  And all endings are kinda the same. The bad one is the most logical and true imho.

_childDocuments_.review: So I don't wanna be super formal on the title therefore won't beat around the bush. The game is not for everybody so if you pretty much tired of screamers and clichés then it would be better to pass on this game. You will not get new experience here or something that'll blow your mind.However, it is a really good game. The script is well written. You may even end up finding a few interesting twists! _childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. One of the best horror stories I have seen recently, up until the ending. It is a huge step forward from Man of Medan, with a slew of gameplay improvements: -you can now actually see which dialogue choice changes which traits and which relationships;-secrets are linked between themselves, offering a much clearer picture than Man of Medan's disjointed pieces of information; -you can now choose to overwrite previous saves; -you are alerted previous to QTEs as to what will happen; you are alerted before leaving an area so that you don't miss out on exploring-each scene shows whether you made heart or head decisions, actually making this mechanic relevantOverall, the gameplay feels much more pleasant and fluid, which I deeply appreciate. Moreover, the game also features a far deeper mystery, which is kept until very late in the game.I think that the length is also a lot more decent (I got close to 8 hours on my first playthrough, after hunting thoroughly for secrets and replaying a scene several times) while the replayability significantly decreases (from what I could tell so far, fewer branching decisions than Man of Medan, and secrets are far easier to find, meaning you don't feel as motivated to play through the game so many times to discover all the details about the story).Overall, however, it is a phenomenal game in a gripping setting, which definitely deserves your attention. The anthology seems headed in the right way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part this game is great. I think it's better than its predecessor, Man of Medan. It's creepier, the characters are better, and the story is more interesting. The ending though. The ending is the ultimate sin in storytelling. It's a lazy trope that cheats the audience out of a satisfying resolution. It's frustrating because 98% of this game is great, but that last 2% is unfortunate. I would recommend this game, but only if it's on sale. It's a fun way to spend an evening with a friend, even if it leaves you frustrated.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game and it's story are great from a movie standpoint! It had a fun cast of very likable characters like John and Angela--both of those characters were especially memorable to me, and the actors did a phenomenal job. I think there are a lot of great sequences that make you and your friends feel like a badass. There is a bit of a gripe I have with the game's story, but I'll save that for the second half of the review. I played a Movie Night with 4 people using Steam Remote Play, and I think I definitely prefer playing the Dark Pictures Games this way. Occasionally you'll run into a bug or it won't remind you to give the controls to another player which led to me scrambling to pause the game in order to give that player access to my mouse and keyboard. Overall though, the experience was very smooth as long as everyone has a good connection.I played as John and shared Angela to a friend who lost a character before the final act. Had a really great time!--------------But all of that aside, this game was crafted into a very memorable experience, far greater than Man of Medan in my opinion. If you're okay with a story being enjoyable for 97% of the playthrough and can look past that  3%, you'll love this game, warts and all.

_childDocuments_.review: :I am reviewing three aspects of the game specifically,  The story review will have no spoilers and instead will focus on the quality of the story and the implementation thereof, however I will still add a spoiler tag just in case I slip or for anyone who wants to be a purist.  As soon as the title screen came up I could tell this game was going to perform significantly better than its predecessor on PC. I experienced very little hitching, especially noticed the increased performance during the "maintain heartbeat" sequences. Earlier on the game hits the frame rate a bit worse (I only noticed thanks to StreamLabs dropped frames notifications) however it smooths out towards the 2-3 hour mark, maintaining 60 fps more often than not. During QTE events I noticed zero hitching or input lag which was very noticeable in MoM. The new dimension for the "Look" system was mostly smooth, only on rare occasion did it seem to fight the controller but even then it was momentary at worst.  Gameplay felt very smooth for the most part, the new Free Look system has almost completely eradicated the decades old issue of controlling a character with Fixed Camera Angles, though there are a few sections where the free look is limited. That said sometimes moving the Free Look camera itself isn't always intuitive, but far from immersion breaking. The new QTE prompt is a nice addition especially for those who may have a reduced reaction time (or if you are tired), it manages to be brief enough to keep the timing an important aspect while also being displayed prominently enough that you shouldn't be confused about what you are expected to do or when to do it. Initially the prompting felt like it made the QTE easier, however after the first play through I can say this isn't the case, instead the developers slow down the QTE timer for a large portion of the game, ramping up the reaction speed the closer to the end you get. This feels different from MoM however I cannot say with any evidence if this is true or if the performance issues from MoM made it feel that way. Besides these new additions nothing else about the gameplay has changed from what is expected. Note: I compare this game to Man of Medan simply because its the only other game the developer has released on PC that I have played, but it should be noted that while the mechanics are the same the story itself is vastly different even if they share a few common tropes.TLDR: Game Good, performs better than MoM, New stuff good, story good.

_childDocuments_.review: After a great "Until Dawn" and a disastrous "Man of Medan", I thought to give Supermassive another chance...and I didn't regret it! "Little Hope" is way better than the first installment of the Anthology-Series. The characters aren't as plain and way more likable than the previous set. The atmosphere is a mix between Silent Hill, traditional American ghost town and a good old witchcraft plot. Even though some aspects are really predictable, the final twist at the end of the story managed to blow me away. It was unexpected, emotional and melancholic in some way. So, all in all, after hating the Medan-stuff with its many stupid, often unlogical mistakes and flat chars, I definitely recommend "Little Hope" and hope the best for "House of Ashes"!

_childDocuments_.review: ** Spoiler Free **Overall, a pretty good experience! The monster designs were great, I was on the edge of my seat all throughout trying to piece together what was going on, and after having completed it I'm looking forward to my next playthrough to see what can be done differently. Just as a quick note, I played this once in Movie Night mode alongside my girlfriend though I'm sure it would be enjoyable to play solo as well.If you have enjoyed their other games (Until Dawn and Man of Medan) then you will definitely enjoy this one as well. If you didn't like the others than you probably won't find anything here to change your mind though I will say that I felt like all of the characters here were better than in previous entries and none of them felt like full-on stereotypes as you got with some of their previous ones (I say this knowing that Until Dawn was purposely set up to have stereotypical characters).I have seen people giving the ending of this a hard time. I believe the ending is something that would work better in film than in a video game. The overall execution of leading up to it could also have been better which for me it didn't ruin the experience but it also didn't really enhance it either. Still, I see what they were going for and I commend them for trying to do something different.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its fair share of problems but I would still say its a fun time. I played the game on movie night with a couple of friends using the steam remote play. I have also played the previous game Man of Medan with the same people and enjoyed that.Pros-The graphics, lighting, sound design, and overall presentation is such an improvement over the last title.-The setting makes this game terrifying. The thick woods that surround the town make even walking a gut-wrenching task, especially when walking on the road.-Quick time events are improve from the previous gameCons-The ending is not great and hurts the games replayability. -The movie night mode does not have even playtime for each character which caused one of my friends to only play a couple of times throughout the game. -One of the jump scares is almost identical for each of the six or so times it happens-Two of the characters are not easy to become invested in.Without going into spoilers, this game is worth getting on sale if you have a group of friends to play it with. The game is not a perfect horror game so I would not recommend playing it without friends to enjoy with. I also personally prefer the first game Man of Medan so I would start with that if you have not already played it. _childDocuments_.review: Look I enjoyed the game, I'll probably get a few more runs out of it for achievements and collectables, but that may not be for everyone. Whether or not I recommend this game totally depends on you. This is an Interactive Cinematic Experience (ICE) (like Heavy Rain or Detroit: Become Human) so if you don't like a game that's effectively just a Story-Rich / Choices Matter Walking Simulator with Quick Time Events do not get this game. I will rate the two aspects of this game, as an ICE and as a Horror game.As an ICE: As an ICE this game is ok. I think its wiki states it has 7 total endings depending on some of your choices, and compared to games like Detroit: Become Human (which has a literal flow-chart to its story including missions you may never see depending on your choices) this game is incredibly linear as an ICE. Your actions do have consequences and you can have different endings, but generally speaking after playing it once you've seen all the locations and all the interactions (depending on who is alive or not). Strictly as an ICE i have to say buy it on sale, never full price.As a Horror Game: As a Horror Game its good. Due to it being an ICE it's more like engaging with a really good Horror Movie, but the game is well written, I was thoroughly invested in the outcomes (in my first playthrough), and I have to say the atmosphere was very immersive; there was a few "gotcha" moments with jump scares but they were so few, far between, and well placed it was a great use of a generally overused scare tactic. If you are a fan of Horror I say buy it, it's a great horror experience in a genre generally bloated by action games or cheap jumpscares. It also mixes more "traditional" Gothic Horror with sort of "mind-bending" Lovecraftian elements in a way I honestly don't think is done enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise it is a massive improvement over Man of Medan (which I also found fun). The story is engaging and the characters are surprisingly well written so far. I didn't like them at first, but that is precisely why they make for such strong characters. There is always some form of tension brewing in the narrative, often due to these character's differing opinions and attitudes. I simply had to leave this review when I saw so many negative ones here. I haven't finished the story but the graphics and sounds are great, and the scares are much more abundant on this Dark Picture game compared to their last. The prologue alone sucked me in, and I can't tell you how exciting it was to experience the fog first hand in this game when I finally had control over my character. Definitely a creative "visual novel/walking simulator"     I would recommend this game to any fans of horror movies or any fans of Telltale games. After having completed my 1st playthrough I was left with many questions. I have seen countless horror films and I honestly did not see the twist coming even though there were definitely a few warning signs to give it away. Because of this, I'm currently focusing my entire 2nd playthrough around uncovering the truth behind the truth and will update this review for a 2nd time once I have finished with that.      I also wanted to mention that the overall structure of the setting & the storyline itself is handled more interestingly than Man of Medan. One is able to explore a bit more freely and walk at a more reasonable pacing which all helps to lend to the atmosphere set up by the plot. The game is fairly short, but keep in mind that these games are essentially short stories and they're supposed to be able to be played and completed alongside friends on couch-play, so it would have to be decently short. At the end of the day, I'm excited to see what else The Dark Pictures anthology has in store for us in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope is a story driven horror game, where 4 students and a professor suffer a bus accident around Little Hope and can't escape from the fog around them. They need to venture more into to stare into their dark fate.This review is based on Shared Play Online.One is definetly something I need to mention, is the gameplay. If you played Men of Medan or Until Dawn, it will be familiar. You get small areas to check, search for clues and moments, which give you hints about your future and making hard decision, which might save your characters... or kill them. What I liked about it, the game is straight forward playing. It's not too difficult at all. Also, playing with a friend through online is really fun in my opinion, because you can play both type of scenes, which makes the whole gameplay better. The game has Quick Time Events and they are not annoying at all, and got easier, because the game will show you in advance, where the button will appear and you can get prepare. It's not too easy either. You get difficult choices too, which can change the gameplay greatly. In short, gameplay is really sweet, but some people won't like the fact, the game is 6 hours long. Also, the game has some issues at online, like the infinite loading screens, which happens when you stop after loading times or sometimes mid cutscenes. You can try to fix it with loading back a previous checkpoint or if the other player can move, try to trigger a cutscene. With us, this problem occured 2 times, thankfully we were able to continue it. Really good gameplay, short playtime and few annoying or some gamebreaking bugs, but still a really good point so far.About the story itself... I will compare the game to Men of Medan, but this one felt better for me. There are lot of symbolic meanings throughout the game, the constant fight and run scenes makes you think and the lines which the game has can help you out to understand the game. I think the game is logically right with it. Some player won't like the ending, they will feel cheap, but for me, I really liked the meaningful things and the more in depth about certain events. Better than Men of Medan and we got a really good story, too.Songs and sounds are also a really good and workable things in the game. There is nothing wrong about them, really good to listen the songs and the sound effects works really nicely in the game.About the controls... it suffers from the usual Supermassive problems, which is the hard and heavy control of the characters, but atleast the map desing and the controls not make your character get stuck, so I would still say, it's good enough and bit better than usual Supermassive games.Little Hope is definetly a good one to pick up to play, but it's full potential is in the multiplayer. It worth every money you can pay for this game, so definetly pick it up. The game has bugs, but atleast some of them has a workaround and few won't appear too recently.

_childDocuments_.review: For 50 AUD, I can in no way recommend this game. It is a 4 hour walking simulator with a VERY cheap jump scare every 10 - 15 mins that might get you the first time, but as it becomes a plot device for the time jumping back to the 17th century story line, it becomes pretty obnoxious after a while.The entire story is cheapened by the ending which makes every choices you made pretty much pointless. These games should be released at 10-15 each then charged s a full priced game for all four. Not 200.00 for four 4 hour games.... You've been warned!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. Immediately after playing Man of Medan, I binge-played this one in a single session. I loved every minute... right until the ending. The premise hooked me instantly, the story is rife with mystery I was eager to solve before the big reveal, the Silent Hill-esque ambiance is delightfully eerie, and the character dynamics kept me invested throughout. Then the ending abruptly slapped me across the face and said "lol jk, it's not that deep." For a moment, I was sure it had to be a joke, a fake-out, a bad ending through poor choices on my part... something, anything other than what it really is: a cheap cop-out ending that invalidates the entire journey and makes you ask yourself if you just wasted 4-5 hours of your life. It's an ending that undermines the entire experience because the more you examine it in retrospect, the less the story makes sense. It sets high stakes and promises a clever twist it never makes good on. As a writer and avid fan of the Choices Matter game genre, I can't forgive such a lazy, cliche ending to a narrative with so much potential. This could have been a phenomenal game, but instead it damns itself to being the most frustratingly skippable entry of the entire anthology. Like a chocolate-covered brussels sprout, Little Hope creates expectations and offers only the most shocking disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this game a positive review because I want the devs to make more, but this installment was disappointing.The ending is fine. I have no problems with the ending. BUT:THIS GAME IS SO LINEAR. This is Until Dawn levels of linear. Choices barely matter. The game tricks you into thinking traits can determine a character's death, when really it's just one dialogue choice you make that will result in a character surviving until the end or not (assuming you hit most QTEs).Andrew and John -- that is, 2 of the 5 protagonists -- are GUARANTEED to survive until the game is almost over. That's ridiculous. In Man of Medan, anyone can die before Act 3 (while there is a maximum of two deaths, those two deaths can be a variety of combinations). This game is so much more linear. Every chapter is guaranteed to happen, and while there is admittedly variety in who does what in those chapters and in the dialogue you get, the situations stay the same.The Bearings are not like Until Dawn or Man of Medan at all. They just update as things happen on screen, regardless of the choices you make. Guaranteed cutscenes while activate/update Bearings even though you didn't make a choice. Apparently the devs forgot how to their own Bearing system works.I guess the main pro is that it's longer, and the characters and plot are fine -- but it's barely a choice-based game. Until Dawn isn't, either. This and Until Dawn both have barely any variety in terms of situations and plot developments. Man of Medan is much better than Little Hope in this regard -- it doesn't give certain characters plot armor and it has branching gameplay.Supermassive, you did branching choice-based horror right with Man of Medan.. Until Dawn was not good when it came to its "butterfly effect" concept. Little Hope is not good when it comes to its "moral compass" concept, which is the same thing. Man of Medan got it right. Please do better than this in House of Ashes.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with a warning. If it wasn't for the brilliant story I would not recommend this.The simple fact is that I did love this game. The visuals are great, the sound for the most part is too, but if it had directional audio I couldn't tell. The voice acting (or acting in general) was top notch and the whole vibe of the stories was perfect. There did seem to be odd scene changes at times though, as if something else was supposed to happen, but didn't. Perhaps these change depending on your choices and the reaction to them from the game world and it's characters.What nearly killed this for me was the bizarre choice of turning the game into a point and click with incredibly twitchy quick time events that caused many of characters to die off in ways that felt no fault of my own, unlike previous efforts where I just wasn't quick enough. Add to this a laborious camera that fought against you every inch of the way and you have a build up of dread for the mechanics instead of the story, which deserves to hold centre stage. Those game mechanics felt like such a bad choice for this. I don't mind the odd quick time event (after all, they are a staple of The Dark Pictures), but please get rid of the point and click style. They just didn't gel well together.Still, if you liked Supermassive Games' other stuff, you'll no doubt still get enjoyment from it. I look forward to the next one with excitement.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Little Hope' is arguably the best entry in the Dark Pictures Anthology! Ignore the negative opinions on this game. Most who hate on this one don't appreciate nuanced storytelling that has more depth than straightforward titles like 'House of Ashes' or 'Until Dawn'. The plot of Little Hope far exceeds any of the others and is easily the most original (with House of Ashes in 2nd). Some may find its ending controversial, but I greatly applaud the dev team for crafting a story that has more to chew on than just what's presented at face value. Not only does Little Hope have the strongest character models, soundtrack, and visuals of the entire anthology; but the plot, setting, atmosphere and creature designs are outstanding! This game also isn't a buggy mess like 'Man of Medan' or the 'Devil in Me'. Although many would agree 'Until Dawn' can't be topped, the creature designs and visuals here shine brighter than any other Supermassive game.

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I played this and enjoyed it for the most part, but there were some pretty glaring problems:The absolute worst issue we had was, after four and a half hours of play time, near the end of the game, the game just disconnected from the session and booted us to the main menu. It did not crash to desktop; no errors, no nothing. However, this CORRUPTED our save. We were not able to get back into our session to finish the game, which really turned us off. We had to restart from the very beginning (where you can't skip the long music cutscene).The second-largest issue we had was the controls themselves. During dialog events you have to kind of "fight" the compass selector. At times, we had to constantly jiggle the right thumb stick to make sure we selected what we wanted. The game characters themselves get stuck on each other if they get too close. The flashlight control is horrendous. You control the flashlight and camera with the right thumbstick. However, the flashlight will move at a faster rate than the camera, so they are not synced up. This results in a constant fight to actually see what you want to look at. The flashlight will re-orient itself to the center of the camera, but it takes a full 5 seconds of not touching the controls for that to happen.The camera will often times change from a leashed camera to a fixed camera and, due do the 3D controls, our characters will suddenly go from the direction we were initially moving to a completely different direction, which will often result in them moving backwards, where the camera changes back to a leashed camera.Subtitles were broken for me (player 2), but not for my player partner (player 1). I enabled subtitles in the game options, but they only worked during pre-rendered cutscenes. The printed text when reading an inspect-able item would work sporadically for me (they worked about 20% of the time), but my partner got them every single time, so I often couldn't read the small print on the items.The pacing is sometimes FORCED by the NPC characters. In at least two parts of the game we are forced forward instead of being allowed to look around. In two specific instances I was able to spot an inspect-able object, but while my character was bending down to pick it up I was forced out, because my partner (who is not controlled) decided to move to a advancement trigger, which starts a cutscene and pulls me out.The ending of the game is rather lame, in my opinion, since it's very cliche. I was able to figure out what was truly going on just a couple hours into the game. I do like the subtle nuances that are in the game that hint toward what is really happening though. I think they're added in a well-done way.Overall, I don't think I can recommend this game in its current state since the buggy controls really take you out of the immersion. Because it's using the exact same system as the previous game (Man of Medan) they should have been able to iron out the bugs to smooth out gameplay. Honestly, I'd get a refund if I could. Perhaps they'll get it right next time?

_childDocuments_.review: Like in most Dark Pictures Anthology games the only reason your characters will die in Little Hope is because you failed one Quick Time Event (QTE) out of a rapid chain of about 20 of them.Seemingly intelligent choices will never pay off, which also means that making really stupid choices will not matter either. An example from a different game from this publisher: You have a premonition about a character dying in a fire. So naturally, when it comes to picking up a lighter in the game, you decide not to pick it up. However, your NPC partner will instead pick it up for you. What was the point? There is none.It might be unreasonable to expect a developer to make every choice matter in such a game, but I always believed that it was the choices in those games that got people/characters killed, but after playing through this game twice and watching multiple videos about it on youtube, I have concluded that in every single one of these games, your choices do not matter at all. It doesn't matter which dialogue option you pick of if you choose door A or door B or what have you, in the end of the day the game will progress the same way about 95% of the time. And the only way to screw up and get a character killed is by failing a QTE.I just wanted to clarify this for everyone who is looking to buy this game and is thinking that by playing "smart" you can keep your characters alive. This is not true. You keep your characters alive by pressing the right buttons when they appear on screen. Trying to get immersed in the story and predict what is going to happen / what makes sense does not reward you with a more interesting ending or unique events/dialogue scenes in the game.However, I did enjoy the very last cinematic as that was something I did not expect to happen. PS: Filling your game to the brim with jumpscares does not make it "Psychologial Horror" or "Horror" in general. It just makes it annoying. My verdict: Buy it on sale, it is not worth 20€, especially since it will crash occasionally and the multiplayer is still full of issues as well, mainly connectivity issues and desync. And that after 2 years still, and their newest game has the same issues. Lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hill meets The Crucible. It's a straight to the point, CYOA styled, suspenseful, interactive movie game.. but it's a bit rough around the edges. SIMILAR GAMES: Silent Hill, Man of Medan, Until Dawn SIMILAR MOVIES: The Crucible, Blair Witch Project, Sleepy HollowFor those unfamiliar with Supermassive Games (the developer), they make interactive movie games (Until Dawn, Hidden Agenda, Man of Medan) much like David Cage (Detroit: Become Human, Beyond Two Souls, Heavy Rain). Those names right there should give you a fairly good idea about whether or not you'll be enjoying this game. In general, these movie games are heavily story driven and usually have minimalist gameplay. You'll explore some fairly linear environments, take control of a group of characters, learn the backstory to each character, find some collectibles, view some premonitions, make important split second decisions that can potentially kill off your character (CYOA approach), and encounter a bunch of quick time events that can also kill off your character. Everyone can live or everyone can die - that's what makes this genre so interesting. Yes they are a lot of QTEs and jump scares so if you don't like that, this game might not be for you. Additionally, if you want to do a lot of actual PLAYING, this might also not be for you. Little Hope is the second game in Supermassive's new video game horror anthology - The Dark Pictures. You don't need to play Man of Medan at all to enjoy this game. There is no relationship except the Curator who hosts this horror anthology.Without going into too much detail, Little Hope is set in a deserted New England town with an infamous history of witch hunting. Our five protagonists find themselves being forced to journey through this town after their bus crashes and they are stranded in the middle of nowhere. Pretty soon, weird horror stuff starts to happen and they'll quickly find out they share more connections with the town than previously believed. Going into any more detail would just give it away. However I will say this - the story is quite refreshing. It's slightly more supernatural in nature giving you a break from the usual zombies/demons/science experiment gone wrong. The graphics are fairly nice for 2020 - I had no trouble maxing it out - 1440p/ultra/120+fps on my 2070 Super. No major glitches, crashes or bugs that I encountered. The game took me 6 hours to beat on my first playthrough hence the $30 price tag. Furthermore, the game is meant to be replayed at least once or twice as there are multiple endings so you'll get your money's worth. Great overall performance from movie actor Will Poulter and a decent so-so performance from the supporting cast. The game can be played alone or in a group of 5 people (everyone gets a character to babysit but you have to take turns watching your friends play). Each character's segment is about 15-20 minutes long. You can also play online with a friend but I haven't tried that yet and I'm not sure how well it works. I also played on the XBOX ONE controller and everything worked perfectly. Now as for my biggest complaint - the QTE segments. I'm fairly neutral on QTE. I don't love em or hate em. They are fine in small doses - just be clear and concise what and when you want us to press especially if you gotta press it once or tap multiple times. This game doesn't do that. So during a button mash segment, you'll press it once and waste a second realizing you should have been tapping. By then, it's too late and you fail. Additionally, there's a segment where you have to press buttons in a rhythmic manner, like a heartbeat, and the timing has to be near perfect (can't be too early or too late). That was fine too BUT you gotta tell us WHICH segment is coming up. There ARE indications telling you a QTE is coming up but not WHICH QTE and it's hard to differentiate between the three. I thought a QTE quick press was coming up but it was a QTE rhythm thus I failed the entire segment because I pressed the button that I saw pop up. My girlfriend played with me and encountered the exact same problem. We failed the segment. When you do that - your character is at risk of dying.. and that's exactly what happened, a character died. But you eventually get use to it on your second playthrough. It's not too complicated but when it's the only gameplay mechanic, you really expect it to be perfect. Also don't bother jumping back to the main menu hoping to reload an old save and make an alternate decision, the game makes SUPER FREQUENT autosaves as soon as you press the button. Some other things - the game really wasn't all that scary but it really depends on your definition of scary. Suspenseful? Yes definitely. Engaging? For sure. Scary like Outlast, P.T., or Amnesia? Not really. It's primarily here just to put a cheap smile on your face and give you an interesting narration, not raise industry standards on horror or anything like that. Yes there are a bunch of cliche horror tropes like no cell phone coverage, arrogrant characters wanting to split up, and poor decisions resulting in ridiculous hung by own sweater deaths. Yes there are a BUNCH of jump scares - some love it, some hate it. I believe in moderation they definitely went overboad with them towards the end. That being said, I still enjoyed the game and I'm gonna replay it later tonight. It wasn't as good as Until Dawn (my favorite Supermassive game) but I liked it better than Man of Medan. For $10-20 it's definitely worth playing at least once or especially on Halloween.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope offers an intriguing horror experience that combines a gripping storyline with supernatural elements. The game immerses you in a fog-covered town haunted by eerie visions from the 17th-century witch trials, creating a chilling atmosphere filled with suspense. While the story is compelling, especially for fans of the Dark Pictures Anthology, it can feel repetitive, with a predictable cycle of jump scares and exploration.The choices you make in the game impact the fate of the characters, but some players found the consequences of those choices inconsistent or underwhelming. The game’s visuals and ambiance are impressive, particularly when played on a high-quality screen and with a good sound system. However, issues like bugs, awkward character writing, and some control frustrations can detract from the experience. The acting and dialogue choices for some characters, such as Taylor, were mentioned as weak points, with several players feeling disconnected from the characters due to poor writing.Despite its flaws, Little Hope shines in its atmosphere and mystery. If you’re into choose-your-own-adventure games with a horror twist, you’ll likely enjoy it, though you might be left wanting more in terms of depth and smoother execution.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is a huge fan of Supermassive Games' prior titles, including Man of Medan, It really pains me to have to negatively review this. While the graphics were very well done, the premise intriguing, and the horror unique, the story leaves a LOT to be desired. It leaves the entire theme of the Salem Witch Trials to be almost inconsequently thrown away with almost no explanation for why it was ever used in the first place. It frustrates me to have such high hopes be crushed under almost blatant disregard for the story. I hope the next in the anthology will have better writing, or else it'll be just as disappointing if not more so.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope takes the Supermassive Games formula and improves upon 2019 Man of Medan, in a lot of ways. With a more captivating story with fewer plot holes and the masterful building of a tense atmosphere, The Dark Pictures series evolves from cheap horror into a well-executed thriller that uses jump scares but does not over-rely on them like before. The excellent branching narrative increases the gameplay value exponentially, encouraging players to seek different outcomes by making different decisions on new runs. But despite all that, does not reach the AAA overall quality of 2016 Until Dawn. Both dark Pictures titles still look like baby brothers.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope is a much more refined and polished version of Man of Medan, a game which I already enjoyed immensely. Music and graphics were fantastic, and the story kept me entranced for 6 hours (almost) straight. The QTEs in this game are much improved over Man of Medan's by flashing a prompt 1-2 seconds before the actual QTE, so I don't feel so caught out of the blue by them. One minor complaint I still have is the navigation can be quite awkward at times, but it wasn't enough to turn me off of the game itself. The twist at the end may be received well or poorly depending on personal preference, but I felt like it was a good twist - it surprised me but didn't come entirely out of the blue.I'd honestly rate this an 8/10, mostly as there were a few visual bugs and the movement trouble I was having. I'd still honestly recommend this game to anyone looking for a new horror game to play, and I eagerly await the next in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: 🎀He can have the face of a Witch, a religious fanatic, a mad preacher, a child. Even a doll. The Devil is everywhere, and there is no escape from him ().Among the dense fog of the town of Little Hope, forgotten by God and mankind, the Devil snakes, lurks in the sewers, in the dilapidated houses, in the churches, in the minds. The fire does not drive him away, nor does it purify the spirits of those poor souls who, at the stake, died because of him.🎀Once, at the sunset of the 1600s, Little Hope was reportedly a haunt of hags, Satan's concubines, to be hanged, drowned, burned. And so over the years, centuries later, that provincial town has morphed into a place that, while lacking the fame of Salem, attracted a good number of onlookers and, for a while, even thrived on this macabre past. Little Hope Now, all that remains is the haze, and a few memories to forget. Like the fire in which, in 1972, an entire family lost their lives. 🤔Maybe because of a doll ?!🎀Welcome, ladies and gentleman's, to the dark second chapter of The Dark Pictures Anthology.Little Hope reinterprets in its own way a sub genre of cinematic horror, specifically the "witch" one, made up of possessions, satanic rituals and many, many murders.The peculiarity lies in the possibility of living this nightmare in the company of other players. Maybe to try to be less afraid, maybe....🎀Many years after the tragedy that struck the unfortunate family, a bus with four university students on a trip to Little Hope, accompanied by their professor, goes astray due to a sudden accident. Waking up in the middle of nowhere, in a night devoured by fog, the five protagonists, each with specific behavioral characteristics, try to find a way out, while they are hunted by supernatural presences. Among these there is also a little girl, with her doll: once they come into contact with these spirits, the students are transported to 1692, at the height of the Witch hunt.🎀For a limited period of time, before returning to the present, they can interact with the inhabitants of the seventeenth century, all strangely identical to them, in order to discover the mystery behind the executions that took place in Little Hope. Will tearing the veil of doubt around the past be enough to save his life? In a continuous coming and going between the present day and the dark age of obscurantism, the adventure will also lead us through the twists and turns of the protagonists' psychology, whose temperament we will also be able to shape. On the basis of our choices, moreover, we will have the possibility of unlocking character indoles, which will influence not only the relationship with the other characters, but also the progress of the story and which, in the most extreme cases, can even affect the salvation of the group.🎀Little Hope places us in front of crossroads that will significantly change the continuation of the story. The impression, in this case, is that greater importance has been given to the relationships between the protagonists in relation to the first chapter of the collection, orchestrating a plot that gives great importance to the concept of bond that unites the members of a group. Trust, support and understanding are the key elements of a disturbing story.🎀The atmosphere of Little Hope is oppressive, high class horror, with some not too veiled references to Silent Hill: the adventure of SuperMassive Games at times offers visual solutions of undoubted impact, visceral and anxious, full of restlessness constantly hovering between tachycardia and pure fright.🎀We tremble and die together.In Little Hope we will have to control, according to the needs of the story, the various protagonists, alternating fairly long dialogic phases with more interactive moments, linked to exploration and to the sequences in which the QTEs are the masters. When the game allows us some freedom of movement along the environments, we will also have the ability to analyze the game areas, all very small, in search of small collectibles or information that broaden the lore, they provide us with some useful clues to let us understand what the solution to the mystery could be.🎀It is in this almost investigative soul that one of the best ideas of the team hides, which carefully sips the various tests to accompany the most intuitive players towards a full understanding of the story before the end credits arrive. It's just a pity that the freedom of movement is in any case limited by quite claustrophobic areas and by a management of the frame which, in its desire to be very authorial, sometimes does not provide the right perspective to orient the user's gaze. In addition to the clues, in the settings we will also be able to find special postcards called "Omens of Death": the game will thus provide us with visual aids, a quick glimpse into the future aimed at suggesting what actions could lead to the untimely death of the protagonists.🎀Little Hope offers a fairly well balanced advancement between dialogue, action and sheer terror. If we exclude a very simple minigame in which to press some keys with the right rhythm to keep calm in the most tense situations, the QTEs prove to be extremely basic in the concept, and also quite simple to complete.Little Hope's sense of challenge felt more lenient than Man of Medan's, and getting all the characters to safety might prove easier than expected, luckily. Where the game loses complexity, it gains a degree of tension: the choices we will make move on a more ambiguous scale of morality, and there are many gestures, even minimal, that could almost radically change the development of the story.🎀If another person is playing with you, then, the relational dynamics between the characters could completely escape your control, causing unexpected branches. Like the previous chapter, in Little Hope we will be able to face the adventure with two options dedicated to local and online multiplayer together with other users we will also be able to witness completely new sequences, which in the single-player mode are precluded, real additional portions of plot that clarify some points of the story. Such an approach to storytelling is downright intriguing, and opens the door to replayability.🎀Little Hope is a town where not even the light of the moon filters through. The fog is so dense that you can't see it within an inch of your nose, the shadows play tricks here, showing images that perhaps don't exist, or which, perhaps, are all too real. To give substance to the fears of the protagonists, Supermassive Games uses the Unreal Engine 4, whose quality in terms of detail and optimization is undeniable and amazing.The result is a good level of effects and in general a sufficiently detailed setting, while the animations of the characters and their facial expressiveness, especially in the close ups, would have deserved a greater refinement but not disdain at all. On the other hand, there is an improvement in the direction and in the editing that contribute to making the story more fluid and less botched. The sound accompaniment has been able to confirm itself as a terrifying and suggestive travel companion.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to say anything about Little Hope I would say for any fan of the anthology that this may be the weakest entry at the time of reviewing this, in my opinion. Without spoiling there is a lot of threads and plot points that just essentially amount to nothing at all in the end, you're constantly thrown new things that mean nothing at all to try and cobble the illusion of a story, even if that story is not the actual one that's playing out, and it all comes to a climax at the ending which for sure wins the award for worst series ending. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start with a warning. If it wasn't for the brilliant story I would not recommend this.The simple fact is that I did love this game. The visuals are great, the sound for the most part is too, but if it had directional audio I couldn't tell. The voice acting (or acting in general) was top notch and the whole vibe of the stories was perfect. There did seem to be odd scene changes at times though, as if something else was supposed to happen, but didn't. Perhaps these change depending on your choices and the reaction to them from the game world and it's characters.What nearly killed this for me was the bizarre choice of turning the game into a point and click with incredibly twitchy quick time events that caused many of characters to die off in ways that felt no fault of my own, unlike previous efforts where I just wasn't quick enough. Add to this a laborious camera that fought against you every inch of the way and you have a build up of dread for the mechanics instead of the story, which deserves to hold centre stage. Those game mechanics felt like such a bad choice for this. I don't mind the odd quick time event (after all, they are a staple of The Dark Pictures), but please get rid of the point and click style. They just didn't gel well together.Still, if you liked Supermassive Games' other stuff, you'll no doubt still get enjoyment from it. I look forward to the next one with excitement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this, I love Until Dawn and even got some enjoyment from the first Dark Pictures Game.But this has a barely coherent story that lacks any consequences. Game defaults to a were you a good boy/girl check at the last minute to determine if anyone survives. Absolutely riddled with unnecessary jump scares (sometimes you can even tell they are coming because the subtitles end abruptly)Some animations seem to be missing for example: End of a chase-scene cuts to everyone standing around or2 out of 5 are attacked and pulled away about 10 meters, 3rd helps, action scene happens. 1&2 are rescued by 3 reconnect with 4&5 which are just standing at the same spot for no apparent reason neither helping those who were attacked nor running away.clishee but intriguing premise turns to dumb jumpscare ride with bad pacing.

WELCOME TO LITTLE HOPE

DON'T PLAY ALONE

name: Meet Your Maker
detailed_description: Sector 2: Shattered Peak SECTOR 2: SHATTERED PEAK — AVAILABLE NOW Deep in the desolate Arctic wasteland lies the Shattered Peak Sanctuary, home to the latest in lethal advancements in tech and cloning. Battered by suffocating snowstorms and facing endless isolation, fear and paranoia ensnared its residents, turning Custodian and Advisor against each other, and the former research facility into a blood-splattered nightmare. All Meet your Maker players gain instant access to a new environment and themed Deco Pack . A new Custodian and guard are also available, letting you harness the snowbound horrors that tore the Sanctuary apart. Meet Your Maker: Deluxe Edition Ready to Meet Your Maker? The Deluxe Edition includes the base game and the Scorched Necropolis Collection that expands your post-apocalyptic toolbox with a full set of ancient-Egyptian-inspired cosmetics. Combine myth and machine to build and raid in deadly new directions. Create post-apocalyptic pyramids and temples, or gear up with golden weaponry and Custodian Suits to take on other players’ creations. Deluxe Edition contents: Meet Your Maker Base Game  Scorched Necropolis Deco Pack 2 Blocks (each available in 3 shapes)  Limestone  Golden Age   2 Props  Winged Molding  Temple Light  1 Animated Prop  Spinning Enigma  8 Decals  1 Scorched Necropolis Weapon Skin: Sunclaw 2 Scorched Necropolis Custodian Skins: Desert Cyclops and Gilded Warrior *All items in Meet Your Maker can be mixed and matched freely when building an Outpost or creating a Raider loadout. About the Game You are the Custodian of the Chimera, a living experiment created as a last resort to save life on Earth. Enter a battle of skill and wits for the only remaining resource that matters and the key to your Chimera’s evolution: pure genetic material. Mine the darkest corners of your imagination to build and fortify deadly fortresses known as Outposts to extract and guard your Genmat. Infiltrate and survive other players’ Outposts to steal more. Adapt, upgrade, and evolve… or die. The world’s deadliest toolbox is at your fingertips. Combine a huge array of blocks, traps and guards to build a fortress that’s devious, cunning, and utterly without mercy. Enjoy complete control over your creation, modifying traps and recording custom patrol paths for guards, then share your Outpost and watch others try to survive it. Reap rewards from those who die, learn from those who live, and never lose progress by being raided. Put your will to the test raiding other players’ Outposts. Rely on your instinct, intellect, and reflexes in a do-or-die heist to steal the materials you need to fuel your next build. Choose the right loadout for each unique challenge, then get in, grab the Genmat and make it out alive mastering every Outpost that stands in your way. Keep your friends close and your enemies closer. Combine creativity and build with an ally or join forces to raid as a team of two. Use the replay system to watch Raiders challenge your Outposts. Grow your reputation with accolades left by others to reward your ingenuity. Easily find your friends and favorite Builders to play their Outposts at any time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played one other game like this where you fight and build up bases to kill "raiders" and have really enjoyed it! It is very fun to watch others take on your creation and visa versa. I really like some of the mechanics like being able to create your guards paths by going 1st person as them, it can really change up the flow of the build since you can control there paths to such a degree! In one base I used a Guard and had there path include peaking around a corner just enough so the player could see to hopefully distract them from seeing a wall trap. Or having the player hunt a "Retreating" guard just for me to place him in a hiding spot to ambush them. You can upgrade your traps, guards, weapons, defensive equipment. A very fun game for sure that I hope gets lots of updates!

_childDocuments_.review: The core game loop of: Raid bases, get resources, get inspiration.Build outpostraid more, watch replays of attempts on your outpost, get inspired moremodify outpost, watch more and more people die in your outpost.Its just REALLY fun. I really enjoy the core raiding gameplay, and its even more fun in co-op. And I'm equally having a great time just watching replays from other raiders on my outposts.There is definitely a lack of content right now, in that the game could use more trap types, enemies and weapons/upgrades for when you go on raids. But there's still lots of room for creativity and ingenuity in the outpost design and trap placement to both keep raiding fresh and give you plenty of inspiration. I'm looking forward to future updates to change up the gameplay, but still logging in every chance I get to check on my replays and sneak in a cheeky raid.

_childDocuments_.review: I am glad to say that this game's devs have finally come around. On launch, this game had a few glaring issues with design and implementation of certain systems. I am glad to say that they have made the necessary changes for the game to be great. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes the idea of raiding player made bases, and maybe making your own to throw into the pile. Game is very snappy and responsive most of the time, and the movement is absolutely fantastic. Highly reccomendOLD REVIEW:I would absolutely love to recommend this game, as it's fun and super interesting of an idea.The problem lies with the devs and their decision to punish the playerbase for doing well.tl;dr if you make a good base, it inevitably becomes literally useless after a ton of work and resources have been poured into it. Good concept and gameplay, but kneecaps you for doing wellLong version:This game's bases have a level system called Prestige. Bases only stay active for up to 24 hours at a time (based on a randomly generated stat you can't change or upgrade) and every time they run out you have 2 choices. If your base did well, you HAVE TO prestige the base, which levels it up one, and fills it back up with time. If your base didn't do well, you have the "reset" button instead that refills the time without going up a level, but this is ONLY available if your base didn't do well at all. Both resetting and going up in prestige cost an ingame resource, with the cost going higher with level.Upon hitting rank 10 Prestige with any base, once it runs out of time that base becomes "retired", meaning that it CANNOT BE ACTIVATED EVER AGAIN besides social (friend only) raids. So our reward for making an ingenious and deadly base? Killing it with fire.I get that they want fresh bases for people to raid, but there are ways to accomplish that without kneecapping their players like this. There's even have the champion system, where a base that does exceptionally well becomes a champion base, and gives extra rewards to raiders in exchange for bringing a ton of extra raiders in. The caveat is if your base has to "reset" instead of prestige, you lose champion status. They could easily just make it so once you reach 10, you have to reset every time, so you can't become champion. Then all champion bases are fresh and interesting, and no one loses hours and hours of work + resources.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, everything about this game seems great. The problems stem from the developers and their treatment of this game.The absolute worst choice was to make user levels temporary. I think your levels only last in the rotation for 2 weeks, with ways to extend that to maybe a month? Why not just keep them all in rotation, but decrease the odds of older maps? Oh right, because BHVR really like for their players to be forced to grind, see their other games. In this game, the only currency that you won't have a surplus of is Cells (the red one). Cells are needed to unlock new weapons/suits/guards/traps, upgrade anything mentioned in the previous point, and also if you want to activate a temporary buff to see statistics about maps on the worldmap (trap/guard count, top 2 most used traps/guards). Have Cell drop rates been improved much since launch? Not really: you can now get a slight amount from daily challenges + each map 'sector' will usually have 1 "free space" (worth about 1 map). Sadly, the latest weapons/suits/traps/guards (and their upgrades) added cost 2-3x the price of the older ones.Because the maps are in rotation for such a short amount of time, builders are encouraged to make very spammy bases to generate Cells. The most common spam bases you will find are either: a chokepoint leading into a large room filled with tons of ranged traps and guards ("kill boxes"), or a maze with the roof being acid cubes dripping all over the floor. The latter is more personally annoying, as you are forced to low-jump at all times to minimize your time on the floor.After a while you've seen a million of these and my solution was to just abandon them on sight, hoping to find a quality map. And there are some very, very cool maps. Very pretty ones, detailed or themed ones, or ones with a really fun idea/challenge to them. The problem is that most of the great ones are out of rotation by now, so playing them will earn you NOTHING.I should have learned my lesson from Deathgarden, BHVR's game before this that was killed within a year (like this one). It seems that any game that isn't a money printer (DBD) is just pumped and dumped. Take these last few 'season' updates: maybe a few sentences, and 1-4 lazy recolors.The developers gave up on this game after anniversary. There is no reason to buy this game at full price as there will be no new (actual) content.
