_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game and great concept. I am excited to see where this goes. Being able to play on player created levels make for a wide range of difficulty. Obviously there are some downfalls, only two melees, guns, and suits to choose from at the moment, (which I am sure there would be more to come), some texture packs will be cool too. The biggest downfall in my opinion is that I would like to see 4 person squads in the future, not just two. Its not a deal breaker by any means but the "squad" would love to play this game all together.

_childDocuments_.review: You can build or raid; you aren't required to do both.The game has impressive polish and balance, especially for a new release.Don't let the negative reviews scare you away from a good time. Some maps require a lot of patience and practice to complete, but you can do it! It doesn't cost anything to keep trying.(Yes, there are consumables like grenades but they are purely for convenience and are never  required.)You have a grapple and a double jump, it rewards skilled movement and has a very responsive feel.It is satisfying to break traps and kill guards, you can find the game currency from destroying them.You can bring a friend with you for 2 player co-op if you enjoy more relaxing gameplay.Building is very intuitive and there are many quality-of-life features.Every time another player tries your map (even if you are offline), it will save a replay so you can see how they played it.When you go back to your map to edit it, you can pick up currency from the places where players died.The game feels very unique and I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: 2 phases to this game; both are good, but could be great.1. Raiding. You pop into a random person's outpost/fort/deathtrap based on how "dangerous it is," and you have to fight/speedrun/navigate your way through the traps and enemies they placed in order to get the sweet sweet stem cells for the fetus overlord. -The thing here though is the variation between forts is kind of minimal because of the builder limitations. Improving the building system an a few ways will inherently make raiding more varied and fun.2. Building. You pop into a mostly vacant lot with only one goal in mind: Make raiders die. You can do it either through brutal trap quantities, clever placement, or even making a "loot room" that makes people self-delete on purpose so they can farm materials and XP from the self destructing traps. It's a good time.-Building is limited because you need the gatherer to get to the point and thats the requirement. So no parkour maps, no puzzle maps, nothing like that. Just halls and rooms with a handful of traps and enemies. Replacing the gatherer requirement with a "complete it yourself" option would immediately allow for more creativity.If you are like me and like being clever, you are able to watch replays of people surviving/dying in your outposts so you can see what does and doesnt work, making you a better insidious killer; H. H. Holmes style.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one.I'd say yes if you enjoy this type of gameplay and you can get lost creating levels. But I'd probably say no if you expect the game to deliver a lot of content as is.This type of game, just like geometry dash etc. , thrives with it's community and the user created levels.At the moment there's not too much variety in the level design, as users get used to and try out creating their first levels. There's a lot of incentive to kill people to earn points to prestige your level, so most of the levels are actually just challenging and you try to avoid certain death, most of the time referred to as killboxes. I don't mind this personally, but it would be nice to have other rewards or incentives to make your level unique. The other problem is, that you don't have to complete your own level. The only condition is, that there's a clear path for the harvester and some pre determined value of traps / guards.I feel like this is pretty obvious, why this could lead to some problems.On another note this game could also use a kind of story mode with developer created levels to teach some mechanics / provide progress outside of the user created stuff.To conclude, i'd say get it if you enjoy building and raiding bases and you can deal with the amount of content that is provided. Otherwise wait for more updates / the community to create more diverse levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it for a week or so, then realised how utterly shallow it is.You have three shapes/bricks/primitives to build out of; a cube, a slope, and a pyramid. No concave shapes at all. You place traps, which trigger when they see a player. That is it. Place enough traps to make a killbox or place traps aimed at traps, aimed at traps. Make a maze. Yay for a day or two. Oh and nomatter how good, your bases are removed from play after lvl 10, so try keeping enthusiasm while building your 30th base from scratch.The core concept of asynchronously raiding other player's bases is solid, and I look forward to more games inspired by MYM, But I don't think there's enough here to maintain a playerbase. It's neither complex nor rewarding enough.Edit: Uninstalled now. Sorry devs. Make it more.Edit #2: I feel compelled to edit again after the dev response. I want to get back in to it, because the game is beautiful and moody.. But as a builder there's nothing interesting to do beyond trying to distract raiders enough to walk into traps. As those raiders know they're raiders, they are expecting traps. Give us more SYSTEMS to mess with. Motion detector blocks linked to separate trap blocks, moving blocks, conveyor belt blocks, water/swimming/underwater traps and enemies, commander guards that make subordinate guards act as a team, Cube (movie) style laser guillotines running down tracks... There are so many places you could go with this whole asynchronous base raid thing but all a creative player can do is place block traps.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really satisfying watching the replays of people go through your course and get hit by a trap that you knew would create a problem, had me wheezing on how people died. There's different ways of doing your layout with a point system they have with placing down blocks, traps and guards. You're either ballsy and run through everything, one stutter and you're dead. Or you're cautious and check every corner up until someone's course forces you to run through all the traps. Good funAdded: Every outpost can be beaten, you just need the right equipment, either one or both of the cautious or speed tactics and a step by step trap kill order if you've died already. Sometimes, creative problem solving.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a uniquely fun idea of mixing the thrills of a roguelite with the cackle inducing machinations of a dungeon builder. This game is actively co-op and passively PvP, where every outpost you raid is player made and you can do it with a buddy too! The cycle of raiding and gaining enough resources to upgrade and then improve your raider or outpost is fairly straightforward. If you don't like spending a good chunk of time building and planning trap setups you can focus on just raiding and vice versa.The game is definitely not perfect and has some rough edges, latency can very rarely cause some timing issues with traps and getting specific styles of bases to show up on the list isn't really an option. The base prestige system decay is also a bit disappointing because you can work very hard on a base that can become inactive and only playable as a social outpost (no gains just for fun). SO far not seen an alternative to this. Barring little gripes about more block shapes and allowing decals on trapped surfaces, I think it is a solid start.Now, the REAL problem with this game (as I see it) is twofold:1.The game is barely 2 months since release and people are already calling it "dead" and clamouring for more content. A few bits of post launch content were already given, not much but still there. The game is a new IP and a generally new idea for a game so it is still reasonable to not have a TON of content yet. We have a roadmap and it IS coming, just enjoy the game until then!2. People are claiming the game is stale and that the traps and setups are all the same or impossible killboxes trivialising raiders and hyper dexterous speedrunners trivialising builders. The fact of the matter is that most of this is on the players and not on the devs. There is only so much they can do to encourage certain behaviour but at the end of the day people will want to speedrun as their desired playstyle to get the maximum efficiency and for them, fun. For the killboxers its the same, farming raiders until a few get lucky. Is it fun for EVERYONE? No, but speedrunners and killboxers are a large enough group to be significant in how the MYM experience rolls out, and sadly raiders who are methodical or builders who want to create a longer, balanced game experience are not seen as a priority by a large part of the community.All in all, it is up to US as players to make the content we want to see and support each other to make this game truly shine. The "strategize>deploy>fail>adjust>redeploy" cycle can get addictive and playing with a friend adds a whole new layer of fun and often hilarity. I sincerely recommend taking the negativity with a grain of salt and realize that the game is made or broken by the players and your cunning or ingenuity, perceptiveness or creativity will drastically affect your experience. That is a large part of the fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I was not expecting to like this game so much. Movement feels great and map creation is fun and rewarding.- Both modes of play earns resources, which can be used to unlock and upgrade gear for raiding and traps/enemies for maps.- There is no penalty for dying, and it is still rewarding to complete a map even if you die a lot. The only thing you really lose by dying is time, and you can still get small amounts of resources from repeat destruction of traps and enemies.- Maps earn additional resources when players die on it.- There is a REPLAY FUNCTION for both your raids and raids on your maps by other players. Watching other players fall for your traps and learn your layout is pure gold. There are also many smart limitations on both raiders and creators that make the game much more fun and tactical than I was expecting from the trailers.- Raiders have very limited but reusable ranged ammunition. (So you can't machine gun or snipe every enemy and trap. You have to use your brain to prioritize targets and plot how your going to recover your used ammo.)- Base maps have a finite number of points to spend on building blocks/traps/enemies, and a clear path must be made to the objective. (So a creator cannot cover every tile with a trap or make maps impossible to complete, I think).- Maps farm resources for the creator while they are active and open to raids by other players. Once they run out of resources, they automatically deactivate and cannot be raided. Creators can spend resources to recharge and open them back up. This system ensures that only active players' maps are in rotation.Even if the game only slightly interests you, I recommend picking it up especially if it's on sale. It might surprise you like it did for me.

_childDocuments_.review: (Review revised after 9 more hours of play.)Lets get the easy stuff out of the way first. The game is well presented and while the graphics won't win any awards the aesthetic is great. The sound design is on point and it needs to be, as the sound cues are important as you're working your way around a level. The UI is intuitive enough and the game plays just as well on K&M as it does on a controller, including the base building (though given the nature of the game, K&M is probably the preferred option).That's the pleasantries out of the way...Games like these live or die by their community and their creations. Being given away for "free" on PSN has given it a grace period as thousands of people can try the game without a dog in the fight, bring in fresh content and add more meat to the grinder (more on that later). Quite a shrewd move by Behavior. Though even 4 days after release its showing signs of dying within a couple of months.Every base you go into, you go into blind. Not in terms of it's content, that can be overcome by the abilities o f your "advisors", which will give you a rough idea of what you're up against once they're levelled enough. No, the problem is that you have no idea if you're going up against a boring labyrinth or a killbox (of which there are many). The game gives you four feedback options upon completion of a level, of which you can select two; "fun", "brutal", "artistic" and "ingenious". As oversimplified as these options are (God forbid we're able to leave a comment on a level) they're ultimately pointless, as you can't see the feedback a level has received prior to playing it. In an era where people are incapable of taking any form of criticism, there is no facility to leave any kind of negative feedback, so the only option available is to block the player, preventing them from viewing your replays or their maps appearing in your rotation.Even if your life depended on those little dopamine hits from your intricately designed Reddit post, it wouldn't matter. You are the only person who can see that feedback and it doesn't incentivise you to create a level that is challenging or good to look at, because the mechanics of the game are geared towards you killing players for their resources. Killbox it is then.Bases are not permanent. Once they have extracted their resources they are deactivated. To reactivate them requires one of the three resources (mobile game mechanics?) to "prestige" your base. Your base can go through 10 levels of prestige. Once you hit the 10th level, your base is disabled permanently and can only be played "socially" and won't net you any resources or XP (as far as I know). The gameplay loop here is that to maintain a base it has to operate as a meat grinder, as the easiest way to obtain the resources required to keep it running is by killing players. Am I the only one that can see the problem here long term? The plaudits you might receive are meaningless. Thumbs up don't maintain your base, resources do. Why create a fun, challenging aesthetically pleasing base? Head pats don't keep the lights on.The multiple types of resources should be a dead giveaway for what type of game this is. This kind of thing is a staple for F2P games. The three resources are cells, parts and synthite. Three levels of obfuscation. I won't go into detail, but once you realise that there are multiple levelling systems in this game you know what you're up against; its a treadmill. The same kind of mechanics can be found on any cash-grab mobile game.Once you've obtained all of the tangible stuff in the game (unlocked and upgraded all weapons, traps, mobs etc) theres very little on offer. You don't even get any kind of cosmetic alterations to your hub to signify any progress. Your hub will look the same on day one as it will a week from now.The one saving grace of this game is the level editor, but even this is flawed. Buying a location for your base doesn't come cheap and the price varies depending on the size of the plot and the resources on offer. The problem is you can't preview the location before you buy it. How is that a problem? Bedrock. The first location I purchased was terrible and didn't lend itself to making a decent level because of the positions of the genmat (the "goal") and the indestructible bedrock. A level cannot be activated until there is a clear path to the genmat (no jumping allowed!) and as you can't relocate the genmat you have to work your way around a randomised set of bedrock which can't be previewed before you commit your resources. There is no option for a blank slate, so that's another thing impeding your creativity. The tools to create your base are fine, the material you have to work with? Not so much.There are some serious and, more disappointing, intentional design decisions that will prevent this game from having any lasting appeal. The gameplay loop is very cynical and you can see the obvious gaps waiting to be filled with DLC/microtransactions. The basic premise is fantastic; an FPS version of Super Mario Maker, whats not to love? The execution has all of the worst aspects of gaming over the past decade or so. If this was more accessible to touch screen controls you would see it propping up the Google Play store.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game but know what you're getting into. Regarding the developer content itself, it looks good and the traps and their properties feel balanced. A little too balanced (will get into what I mean by that further on). It's grindy but at the same time it's enjoyable watching the replays of people dying to your favorite traps and learning new trap combos and building techniques so for me the grind isn't an issue, there's a lot to enjoy other than progression. It could use optimization regarding the sudden pop of resources when you hit a cache (always get a lag spike with the sudden instancing of the resources). This also happens with bomb ejections from the trap and even at times with the cannonbacks. It runs well enough but not spectacular on Nvidia 1060 on low. This probably isn't even an issue on higher end cards(?) Now onto the real issues.As I said with being "too balanced", it's hard to make clever levels that are fun for the raider while getting a K/D ratio above 2 or 3. It's really either make fun levels or kill boxes which many in this game find to be cancer. It's balanced enough where anyone with enough hours playing a fun level can get through it with 0 to 2 kills if they check all their corners and know the dirty little tricks for hiding and using traps. As you can read in the guides though, the people who want high K/D find no other choice but to make "kill boxes" (levels where their is one central room jam packed with traps instead of spreading them out). If you're running this on a console or a higher end PC that mine, kill boxes can be the ultimate reflex challenge. If you're running lower end, not-so-much. I used to be in the camp of kill boxes being cancer but now, no, I see why. Most traps are too slow and easily avoidable. Never thought I'd criticize a game for being too balanced.But on that note, I have 180+ hours in at the time of this review, Master rank and I am recently seeing a lot less kill boxes. Either I think that the sweatier players left the game or raiders got sick of the kill boxes so they abort and abandon (I've done this from time to time) so people stop making them. Or maybe it's just my matchmaking(?) There's no penalty to abandon other than elo/LD (I think) but if you don't care about that, it's no big deal. I just play to have fun and enjoy the replays.It's gratifying watching people either nod yes (look up/down a bunch) when looking at your level or dying to your favorite traps (especially when they shake their head in frustration) during the replays so this game offers something you don't see in other games (closest I can think of is Mario Maker). It's fun to build, fun to see other people's levels, fun to raid and performs decent for the most part. That's why I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate to give this game a no, but right now this game just isn't in a good spot.Quick TL;DR For those who don't wanna read my whole review: Game is good, but lacks content and has some pretty poorly thought out mechanics in it's current state So then, i'll start by saying the concept of the game is AMAZING! Really love the idea of crafting your own bases for people to raid, it's a very fun concept. The issue that currently exists is the complete lack of content. You have four or five basic primitive shapes to craft your base with, about 7 traps (each with about two mods to slightly change how they work), and 3 minions. Once you have completed 10 or so enemy bases you've seen pretty much everything. This makes replay-ability piss poor in it's current state as everything feels kinda samey and boring. There's also only 4 total weapons to choose from, 2 combat suits, and 4? grenades/utility items to choose from, doesn't really allow for much movement in how you're clearing bases or offer any real difference in gameplay, not enough for me at least.Now onto the systems, currently the core gameplay loop is raid, get materials, build base, rinse and repeat. You earn rep/exp with your different advisors who you then can buff yourself temporarily in various ways either as a raider or to your base directly. This seems kinda pointless since the buffs don't feel that impactful or worth your while, especially when you need those mats to build and run your bases. There's also a chimera that you're upgrading constantly. Like every other raid you go in and press the button to upgrade it, and every so many upgrades you get a couple of mats... cool... I guess? Idk, it feels kinda pointless and the rewards are boring. There is a ranking system in this game, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it a SLOG to rank up. You start at the bottom of bronze or iron or whatever and you need something like 4k Ranked points to go up a rank, at most you get 200 points for a perfect brutal level raid clear. Perfect meaning no deaths, which... good luck.This brings me to my last point, but like many others have said, why the ♥♥♥♥ do you not make people beat their raid before publishing it? The amount of raids where you go in, reach the end, then get insta killed by tens of traps all going off at the same time is infuriating. There is no way to beat some of these maps.IMO, before you purchase the game the following changes need to be made: +Add more content, specifically traps, guards, and building blocks for more interesting bases+Tidy up the gameplay loop and give us more interesting rewards. Cosmetics, upgrades, things we can work towards. +Make it so you HAVE to beat your own level before you are allowed to publish it. Seriously, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this wasn't thought of. +Make the ranked system not as horrible to climb, or if you're going to, give rewards. Currently there's no reason to climb besides shiny symbol on your profile.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me say that I LOVE the concept of this game. Isolated on a dying world, you are a Custodian, the protector of a Chimera, the last genetic hope to save mankind. You need to raid the so called Burial Sites, steal Genetic Material and resources to build your own maze of traps and prevent other players from stealing it.An endless loop of death and rebirth.There is, unfortunately, a downside to all this. A good 50% of player-designed burial sites leads nowhere. It's just a door with a pit full of spikes you can't escape from. This is unfortunately the way some people play here, and unless Behaviour Interactive forces players to add more layers or at least a path to get the GenMat, getting into player bases is technically useless.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game about building your outposts with traps and guards so invaders would be killed, and raiding other players outposts to steal some resources.The game starts very fun.Raiding bases, when they aren't just a crappy kill-room build, is fun for a few hours. Then you get used to every trick and it becomes repetitive.Building outposts and watching players get killed by your carefully setup distractions and traps is hilarious, until you realise the map you have spent two or three hours building will only be online twelve hours, plus twelve hours for every time you "prestige" it (you have to pay resources for it).The killer here is that even if your outpost is online, there is no guarantee anyone will raid it before it goes offline again.Update 1 : there has been a patch allegedly fixing that specific issue. I've tried to play a bit more and to prestige a couple of times : the fix doesn't work.Update 2 : an additional issue is the ever-increasing amount of outposts exploiting some mechanic or building bug that hasn't been fixed yet since the Beta.My original conclusion stands:In its current state, this one is for a sale.

As a casual player I can't invest 2+ hours per day to farm Synthetite, I am sorry.Also, after re-activating your outpost for 10 times you can't activate it anymore, so your hard work becomes unusable after like 10 days of regular activation.Unless they change these mechanics, I can't see this game surviving the next six months.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of BHVR's projects, I felt compelled to try this game, even though TO BE COMPLETELY CLEAR, it is not like BHVR's Magnum Opus, Dead by Daylight. With this said, there are elements of the gameplay that show the hallmarks of BHVR's creation-style, taking after the dystopian landscape that Deathgarden was excellent at portraying.For those completely unaware of "what" Meet your Maker is, a quick rundown. The levels are community made, designed by players with the express goal of catching/killing as many players as possible. So naturally, that creates two main playable parts of the game; building outposts, and raiding outposts. While building, you can buy your own "burial site" with it's own features that determine how much creating one can do, and how much "GenMat" can be harvested while it is active (GenMat is a resource gained passively by having bases active). With your burial sites, you are free to place/modify a variety of traps and guards while adding some personal cosmetic touches to make your outposts a blend of fun and challenging. While raiding, you undertake a mission to steal GenMat from other player's bases. To do this, you will enter armed with weapons, assisted by gadgets and perks and moving around with both a double-jump and a grappling hook at your disposal, turning this raiding experience into a dystopian parkour/temple looting experience. I suppose the big question is, has this very weird game concept worked out? Answer: definitely. MYM has a simple idea conceptually and allows the players to challenge each other within the bounds of some very simple rules that ensure that every raid is possible, even if it proves challenging. Personally I have much preferred the raiding side of the game (the prestiging system with the burial sites is slightly confusing, hence why I am not as big a fan of building).I will note that I have had some weird game crashes and I am not entirely sure why. But beyond that, I have had a great time and look forward to more content (and some small fixes to stop the crashes XD).Would defo recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Meet your Maker is an asynchornous and synchronous multiplayer game wherein players create bases of various levels of complexity and hide "GenMat" deep within their territory. Players are then able to play these levels through random generation in an attempt to steal GenMat for themselves in a gameplay loop of build, steal, upgrade, repeat.While the game's mechanics build on top of themselves, the light guidance about where to go, the telegraphing of enemies and traps, and the general feel of a well-balanced game is very prevalent.Players who are familiar with Behaviour Interactive's other titles (Dead by Daylight, Hooked on You) will feel a little amiss in this new IP which strays from the DBD formula they are known for and doesn't interact akin to the Visual Novel of Hooked on You gameplay. However, players who ARE familiar with The Legend of Zelda's Dungeon maker mode on the switch, or Mario Maker, as well as PC players who play Satisfactory, Cities:Skylines or even First Person Shooters will feel as though this is a familiar departure with a bit of strategy sprinkled throughout. Players who were fond of Phantom Abyss will like the pseudo-random nature of the puzzles and bonus objectives scattered throughout levels made by players.If you're looking for a fun, puzzle-solver with a less-intense Doom atmosphere, You'll find this game fun. However if you come into this game looking to be challenged with intense gameplay, you'll be hard-pressed to find it without self-imposing challenges (I will beat this level in 0 deaths, I will beat this level in 5 minutes, etc.)A unique level sharing code or favorites system which would allow you to go back and challenge for significantly diminished rewards, or "difficulty modes" alongside this system for enhanced replayability would go a significant way to ensuring levels will continue to come for a substantial amount of time.Meet your Maker is a phenomenal attempt at making new IP in a genre-blending puzzle-making, looter-shooter with many avenues to tantilize players. The blank slate base building for puzzles, combined with excellently made tutorial levels and a currently rather easy level of challenge for learning the puzzles make this a great game to pickup, play one puzzle and set down while providing for that "just one more" itch.

Does crash every now and then as well, but the gameplay is fun and unique, player built levels can lead to a variable quality of levels but can also lead to potentially infinite gameplay variety.  Being a low price-point seals the deal for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: A new entry into Behavior's catalog that I'm surprisingly hopeful for. Whether you enjoy running through death gauntlets or building them yourself, there's a few dozens of hours worth of entertainment currently in this package with free content drops coming this Summer. All bases require a straight forward path to be published and even if you manage to find a base that you find too cheesy to your liking, you can easily back out and re-roll your choices with no consequences. The game itself supports content sharing across multiple platforms (not crossplay, sadly) and PS+ users were given the game for free at launch. As long as Behavior sticks to a healthy update schedule and balances out any problematic metas that emerge, this game shouldn't have issue holding a healthy playerbase for the years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all time. The only limit is the creativity of other players and after 300+ hours I keep getting pleasantly surprised. However, some base builders can make lazy kill-boxes that aren't fun to play to grind in-game currency, but those bases are few. Overall, there's something about this game that I keep coming back to and the community around it is very supportive. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing in my opinion but that is not to say that it does not have any downsides.Raid wise its pretty fun if you don't run into a killbox especially with how some people try to include the short "boring" path thats required because of the harvester and then the fun one.Build Wise its also pretty fun until you come across two of my biggest annoyances, the harvesters path makes it impossible to truly go all out in design, if the maker could actually somehow customize this path or the harvester itself could make different paths (where it would randomize between the shortest/longest on entry and exit) it could be more fun, however the harvester also doesn't take into account how the play themselves can move which makes the building aspect really limited. The second is that you can NOT move the gen-mat, this makes it incredibly  hard to implement cool base designs because of this. (I built my first outpost with a high tower with two optional paths and the top would be a cool fight scene once I got more guard types and traps but because of the harvester COMBINED with the inability to move the Genmat I had to scrap it and go underground like everyone else....)Overall I DO recommend this game for people who enjoy a doom like vibe mixed with a love of building. I recommend bringing some friends alongside an understanding that this game has potential its just a matter of seeing how the current roadmap holds out quality wise(hopefully the first or second update can add more than they list AI wise).
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Meh, Decent concept, bad execution.The main problem is that so many elements of this game feel like a f2p micro-transaction game.  So much grinding with 5+ separate currency/xp systems. If you want to build a cool level, you need to grind playing A LOT to get unlocks.The other problem is, most of the levels suck. There are no official levels, only player made, and not very many of them are good. When building a level,  You only get rewarded for killing other players, so most of the "difficult" levels are just cheap/impossible to win. The game would have been a lot better with well designed maps that players could customize, blank canvas is just too much freedom. Worse of all, you don't even have to beat your own level before you publish it, so you can build literally unbeatable levels. The last problem is, what's the point of putting time into building a good map? It took me nearly 8 hours to grind enough to build 3 maps....a whole 4 people played them. Then the maps go "offline" and you have to grind even more to bring them back up again. What's the point of putting time into designing a map if no one is going to play it? Day one DLC too... I wouldn't be surprised if you start seeing weekly paid-DLC or micro-transactions for resources for this game. It seems basically built for that. I won't stick around to see it.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I thought this would be the type of game you could choose be a builder or a raider without been greatly handicap in your options in choosing to participate in playing as one over the other. Unfortunately before you can build your ideal outpost, you'll need to play through others players outposts just to get the necessary materials to research the traps, guards and further modifications for them.Which leads into another problem, the level design for most outposts are all similar. Follow a long narrow corridor filled with 1-2 types of traps as they are the only ones other players have unlocked, grab the objective, have 3-4 traps instantly spawn around you and back track through the tunnel again and avoid all the new traps on your way out. That's basically the game design in a nutshell.If the grind wasn't so tedious and the maps weren't so repetitive or there was more creative map options I would consider recommending this game but in the games current state it's disappointing.Edit: Not sure what has happened with the recent update but the crashing in this game has increased 10 fold since the original date this review was posted.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after playing this game for over 40 hours, I think that's plenty of time enough to write a pretty solid review on it. First off, I will start by saying completely ignore ALL negative reviews about it not requiring you to complete your map to make it playable for others. This is literally not the case as I've tested it on various outposts and not one would actually activate if there was no path that could win. That said, yes, some maps can be EXTREMELY tedious in trying to find a way to win, but there is always a way to do it. The overwhelming majority of players have constructed well thought out bases for fun and a hefty challenge. You will die...often times a lot in some cases lol. I've seen people die to obvious traps, well hidden traps, and even their own friends hehe, which is always fun to watch the panic ensue. I myself have also wound up dying to my own grenades before, so I'm not innocent to stupid deaths either lol it happens when you least expect it to. Don't beat yourself up if you can't beat a map, simply play other ones till the next day. The choices refresh everyday as to what outposts show up for you to raid so if you have troubles beating one, simply play others till it refreshes and changes to another that you might be able to beat. So I highly recommend this game, especially if you have friends or enjoy critical thinking like myself! it's a ton of fun and despite the negative reviews, much of the community is even nice enough to put arrows to the "tombs" without any traps by them (especially true in the harder maps as these players tend to realize their traps are difficult to escape lol). Most people will test their own maps before activating them, so do not sweat that at all. Every outpost I've raided there was always a way to win, and that's even with some extremely difficult ones too with only 1 way out lined with traps lol. If you upgrade your weapon and suit, you'll do just fine. If you fail the first time, simply take what you learned and try again. And often times I've found the shield and grenade to be extremely useful in getting out of really difficult situations, so it's worth using both depending on the situation. Lot of enemies, use the grenade to clear some out. Lot of traps near the genmat? Use the shield after grabbing it and destroy the immediate threats while it's active. It's not too difficult once you learn how to maneuver. And as a last resort, you can always place a respawn point at a safe spot then grab the genmat and leave even if you die so long as your quick to do so.Overall, pros:Fun every changing maps (no 2 are the same)Great to watch the replays of those who raid your outposts (some really fun moments like the one I saw where this guy very narrowly missed getting hit in the left eye by a spike! It was so close I could just see the guy's heart attack moment unfold lol, I was like "I don't think that could EVER be closer than that!" and I saved that replay as it's awesome! And he won after that so great job to him! But there's a lot of fun replays like that too!)Easy to learn the mechanics and controls are quite smoothEverything is one hit to kill unless it's an armored enemy (psst, use grenades on those or a really big sword!)Critical thinking required to excelGreat fun with a friend!Lots of challenges and various updatesGreat concept and great delivery on it tooTons of potential future additionsCONS:There are definitely a few unfair maps that are 1 in 1000 to win. These are more of a waste of time and not fun to enter. Just leave those when you find em, save your sanity! lol but it does feel great if you stick to it and win at one of em too though! Some of the blocks can easily disorient you since they can be rotated in odd waysEnemies can easily be an unfair disadvantage if a lot of them are in one big room against you where they all see you at once.A lot of players put tons of traps pointed at the genmat with no clear way to escape it unless you're very luckyBadly laid out outposts make designing nice looking ones difficult at timesLimited number of blocks to build with/outpost customizing is pretty limited for nowThe really neat blocks are locks behind paid DLC that is half the price of the base game (feels like these shoulda been base game to be honest)Limited number of potential outposts you can raid (if you're having troubles clearing them you can't refresh to new ones manually, making it impossible to progress sometimes if you're getting only bad outposts to raid)Keeping your outposts activated requires a LOT of raiding from yourself (best done wth a buff and even then it can take 10 raids to get enough coin to reactivate your own, which increases as you prestige up your own too)You die to anything with one hit. (This makes certain areas very difficult to survive such as a tight cooridor with 4 armored enemies rushing at you with nowhere for you to get away to....yup that situation sucks when they take up to 4 hits each and you die to one....would definitely be better with at least a free revive back to the spawn with all the traps cleared from previous life (but you'd have to go back and get the genmat again of course). Dying to the simplest of traps is inevitable, and it will happen lolKilling yourself is easier than you think, yes you Spider man imposter! Swinging around like that will eventually make you die to something you shoulda seen coming a mile away!Players aren't required to give a clear way to safety at the genmat location (yup, can be completely lined with traps all pointing at you from any direction you can potentially escape to. You're only way out is sheer luck custodian!)Resources feel lacking at times from players killed at your base, sometimes not giving anything at all.Coins are very difficult to get compared to the other materials (say about 25 or so per raid in most cases when an outpost activation starts at 600 for the smallest one and each upgrade takes anywhere from 250 to 800 and each outpost prestige starts at 650 for the next level or 600 to refill if it doesn't have enough prestige (more or less, this takes so long to replenish that by the time you do, your other outposts have farmed up all the materials while you were doing that so you have to repeat it in an endless grind)But anyway, take it as you will. I quite enjoy the game, will get it for my friend so she can play with me too cause I think she'll like it too! Playing together is definitely more fun than alone, but a lot less challenging if you're looking for the challenge. I'd say give Meet Your Maker a shot if you are looking for a great game with repetition but not endlessly grinding the same map over and over. Every raid will be different, guaranteed! I really hope the devs take this game even further and make it way more expanded on traps, suits, gadgets and just the overall potential that is already there being filled out more. They can do so much with it and I really hope they do! I bought the game thinking "welp I'm going to be terrible at this but hey I'll give it a chance" and wound up being pretty good overall, but still die a few times here and there. If you take your time, you're set for the most part! Hope you found my review helpful!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very cool premise, but there's barely anything here. A mere 10 traps, and a miserable 6 different enemies to place around your levels. There is not very much block variety either. And aside from traps, enemies and blocks, there's basically nothing else. The level design is also very restricted, requiring you to make a path that can be walked along without using any movement abilities, even though your character has practically infinite mobility. If they can make level design a bit less restrictive, and add more things to unlock, then maybe I'd buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: 20 hours in and I absolutely love the concept, tower defense/base building meets Doom/Quake like combat and a lot of player-made content. In only 2 hours and with some basic trap unlocks I made a really cool medieval castle with lot's of soldiers inside. There are a few cons like some level's being purposely impossible to complete due to nothing being implemented to stop players, hopefully they do something similar to Super Mario Maker where you must complete your own level before publishing it, Its a live service game so there is a road map which i'm somewhat optimistic about.  Overall, highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: In short - Great ideas hamstrung by terrible negative reinforcement loop.The primary problem with this game right now is that the only sort of behavior that is rewarded in map design is kills.  In theory that would at least spur sadistic designs and kaizo traps.  In reality it breeds what every metrics driven system does: minimal effort, maximal output to try and get as many kills as possible.  Sure, you could develop an interesting, clever, themed level with multi-layered traps and routes that corral player movement.  But why would you do that when you can just dump the player into a featureless box with no cover and maxing out the build limit with lasers/plasma balls/spike infantry covering the walls?  The game gives the player some limited tools to deal with it, they're not impossible to complete.  It's just a tedious slog to get through them.  They're built to get maximum kills, not to trick people.  People don't even bother with stickers to spice things up most of the time, it's just spammed default blocks and projectile turrets.The problem isn't even that it's hard or that you're dying a lot - if you play this game, that's not really a concern.  The problem is that it breeds extremely boring and bland levels that aren't interesting to play.  I rarely get got by a clever trap anymore, I just fall into a big, open box and sigh as I hear the projectile turrets starting to spin up.  That's why the steam player count cratered after launch and is just limping along with 100-200 players.  People will say "just don't play brutal levels" or whatever, but limiting building freedom isn't going to fix anything.  Really all that needs to change is that map makers should get rewards only based off of accolades given by the player, not kills, and there should be a downvote function.  They could keep the game balance exactly as is, and all the trash kill farming levels would settle to the bottom where they belong instead of flooding your level selection screen.  There's good mechanics here.  It's a salvageable game.  It's just built to reward blenders and meat grinders over clever or thoughtfully themed designs.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cool game, love making stabby homes with my fiance. The games difficulties are managed well too, for example my fiance is getting used to the game so we can play easy/medium matches in co-op but when I play alone I like to feel it so I play on hard. Creating bases is a cool loop too, make a base (with an assortment of different looks and traps) watch people run your base and then update your base to counter. Things I would love to see in the future:More TrapsMore SuitsMore WeaponsMore Guards(There is a good selection but more will keep the game alive longer)Side Note: Also DLC Traps, Weapons and Guards are not locked behind a paywall you can earn them by just playing which I find commendable.

Really needs more to do different types of raids with different objectives would be great. Game encourages killing but punishes death makes map building toxic. _childDocuments_.review: Really hoping for more content because I blazed through it all pretty quickly (playtime is 50/50 actual playtime and me leaving my computer running during WFH).Building is fun but after a dozen bases you see most of what can be done with the tools at hand.Raiding is fun and really responsive, but outside of some novel creations most maps fall into 1 of about 6 categories ranging from trap labyrinth to boring murder room to my least favorite, long boring hallway which becomes full of armored berserkers after picking up the genmat.Lots of potential, but not a lot of staying power currently.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die hard dbd fan I was excited to try this but it ended up disappointing me, and its not even because the premise is bad. What shouldve been this neat little casual game (akin to COD zombies or payday 2) has all of these unnecessary features that push this weird competitive narrative that feels totally forced.Its a fun little game dont get me wrong but it was advertised as this game being developed by a large scale professional team but it plays like an early access indie title developed by a small group of hobbyists, but unlike a group of hobbyists, the game doesnt get the love and care a passion project would normally receive. It feels so lifeless and the several DLC packs pushed only a few months after launch are just the icing on the cake.If BHVR really wants this game to have a constant playerbase like dbd they need to A) drop the stupid competitive stuff B) Lower the price, good riddance DBD has offered me 2,000 hours of gameplay and its entry price is $10 every other month and C) put some effort into forming some kind of community or connection to the playerbase, one look at the steam forums shows that all the developers do for this game is push out fixes and maybe a QOL update, a good place to start would be a summer event or something idk Shame, the game had potential. Thanks for the free trial I guess

_childDocuments_.review: Building is a little limited by the need to have a walkable path from the entrance to the exit, though. I'd love to create some jumping / grapple puzzles if Harvey could do more than walk up ramps.Update: Also, unless you're maintaining and prestiging multiple killboxes, ranking up kinda feels like an exercise in futility. Going from Bronze 1 to Bronze 2 requires 3500 xp, and raiding a single base typically nets you 150 xp at most. With 16 total ranks to work through (that reset at the end of each season), getting to max is looking like a chore. It's not enough to put me off of playing the game (5 month update: ), but like... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ y'all, how many bases are you expecting us to raid in 3 months? I would expect to have at least ranked up once in 24 hours of playtime!

_childDocuments_.review: I have know this game for a while now. But i never was interested in play it. The idea behind the game seemed cool but the game-play didn't look appealing enough. After they had made a demo available I decided to give it a try, because what is there to lose? I have played the demo for about 5 hours buying the game myself. Seeing someone else play this game doesn't convey the joy you get out of when you're playing it yourself. It's amazing to zip around a dungeon with your grappling hook and destroying traps. Or just barely avoid getting killed by a trap. You're constantly alert of your surrounding because you're not sure what the other players have made and what might be coming for you. Yes it has a couple rough edges: (visual) glitches and user interaction. But the majority of the time, they won't be a problem.For the devs: - Why do I need to hold my interact button sometimes but other times not? There is probably some logic behind on which places I do need to hold and which i don't. But currently i'm constantly going: "oh wait, i need to hold the F button for this conformation." At first I didn't even notice that i needed to hold it down to be able to use the button. I only noticed the double arrows above the button after I noticed that i needed to hold the mouse button down for as well.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I changed my review to negative until some issues with base building are addressed: namely the prestige system and bases not getting anywhere near enough runs to level up and having to grind just to keep them open as a result.  If those issues are addressed it would push me into positive again.  Its still a great concept and a decent showing, but it needs some of the launch feedback addressed sooner rather than later.I get fed up and quit playing this game every day.I'm tired of it today, I'll be back tomorrow.Awesome concept that needs some tweaks, the base building is awesome, but the difficulty settings don't accurately take into account how some combos go from annoying to flat out broken or even worse: tedious.  I'd rather bash my head against a difficult base than spend 10-15 minutes in a boring maze or clearing a single large trapfilled killbox room.However, getting people to actually raid your base, then give it accolades, and hope you prestige it (level up) during the window has been my biggest issue.  So many things you need to know aren't taught to you in the tutorial to the point where you absolutely want to watch a beginner's tips.   First is that your bases are only open for a certain amount of time to be raided, and if they don't get kills or accolades you basically aren't getting enough points to level and if you don't level during the time its open, you have to reset progress to re-open it.  Some bases are open for longer but this isn't really spelled out, and the timer starts when you activate the base, so its entirely possible to open a base and not get a single run while its open and you have to spend resources to reopen it.So yeah, I have a lot of complaints and issues with this game but the most important part and the reason why this review is still positive is that the bones of a great game are there, the skeleton is partially fleshed out, and some tweaks will make it something unique in gaming.TLDR: Recommend but watch a tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: How can this game has such high positive score with a active playerbase worldwide with 40 peoples via steam xD this game isnt good, it dosent got fixed or advanced. 6months only cosmetic updates :))) what a joke. Words from smarter guys- Bug patches are being released way too slowly, many bugs that have been actively ruining the players experience have been in the game since its release and it's been more than a month now. Usually developers prioritize fixing exploits and bugfixes, especially soon after release. Not BHVR.- Not enough new content to keep players hooked. A lot of people tried this game in the open or closed beta, and there's basically nothing different about the full version and the beta versions. People who already experienced the game for free don't have anything new to experience in the full paid release.- Lack of proper marketing. They did a streamer event and paid for a game awards ad and such, but that's still clearly not enough.- The roadmap tells us that any new substantial content will be released in two months from now. The trap mods they've been releasing so far aren't interesting enough to get players to return to the game.- An unfun meta has formed and the developers are fine with it, as evident with their recent blog post. Despite what a handful of pros might think, just because killboxes are technically possible doesn't mean they're fun to raid over and over again. Variety is the spice of life and all that. In fact, making fun levels in general is punished by the game itself. The game asks you to make unfun, hard levels.- Almost every player retention/player reward system in this game is done poorly, in fact most systems in the game are.Accolades and prestige are done poorly and lead to people losing their good outposts or having to refill them daily due to circumstances outside of their control.Difficulty calculation is done poorly and is very buggy, you can gain rank for adding a mod then delete the trap and still keep the extra difficulty. Normals can be as hard as brutals, brutals can be as simple as normals.Rank is done especially poorly and not just me but many others here have gone in detail as to why it's actively harming the game.The game feels early access despite not being labelled as such.

_childDocuments_.review: From the building side:    Hours of fun just in creating a base. Having the ability to watch the replays of players running through the level you make is great. You get a decent selection of blocks to work with, different skins and markings so you can create your own masterpiece.From the raiding side:Grappling hook, two "rifles", two swords, and a shield.Pros and cons to all of them, easy enough to find what fits you play style.YOU CAN LEAN!!!!! Speed run, or slow and methodical. Maps can be slow paced, or the 9th circle of hell.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Meet your Maker is a fun, base building pvpve shooter. You'll never fight another player (unless you and your co-op partner get trap madness) instead you raid player built bases for genetic material to improve the abomination of science you keep back at your sanctuary. That isn't the only abomination in this game, from the lack of things to buy and customize, from the level ups of you, your test tube messiah, and your npc level ups only giving you material and slight time increases to buff you'll begin to ask where is the content? Welcome to predatory "asym gaming" where the creators release a beta, put the full game behind several dlc walls (only one is out now but I'm confident in saying there will be many more), don't show any ingenuity or creativity in what goes in the game, and short change the players because to them the players have to make it fun. Concepts like locked doors that require keys, boss enemies, levers, leveling up npcs to unlock new items and gear, more than 5 "weapons" in the game, hell even more than 2 suits. What about teleporters? Having your bases last more than half a day irl? Nope, this dev team is not interested, just drop in some looney toons style traps and a handful of guards straight out of let it die and viola you get this game. I cannot recommend this game for the simple fact that it is not a full game. It is missing so much content and basic concepts that the devs are either highly predatory in how they plan on making it feel complete or they are so uncreative they truly believe this game is complete. Either way the future of the game as it is now does not look promising.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game so far.A common criticism is "Players should be required to beat their own base before uploading it" and I disagree with this. The requirement for base uploading (the little harvester bot has to have a walkable path from beginning to end) is plenty restrictive enough. Some bases are extremely hard to complete, but the game JUST LAUNCHED 1 DAY AGO. Upgrade your character, get used to the game's systems, and GET GOOD.9/10 game- Setting is really immersive, but could get stale (they have confirmed they're adding new locales for some variety, booyah).- Gameplay loop is really fun, although I wish the game was a teensy bit more fleshed out in some areas (weird method of leveling up your vendors, base location selection/preview, glitchy replays, co-op makes raiding too easy).- Aside from 2 times when my screen froze, the performance has been PERFECT.- Co-op is a very welcome addition!!My biggest complaint is that I WANT MORE <3For half the price of most modern games, this is a steal at $30
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't rage easy, id say its a great game. Everything one shots you unless you have a shield. You build your own base how you like with only one exception that the Genmat has to be accessible for the AI. There's no PvP only PvE but the funniest thing is going back and watching people try to raid your base/see them sucessfully raid it, then fix what they got through. 8.5/10 Just wish there was a way to create Co-op/Singleplayer only bases. Because most bases are built towards solo players, and the co-op players have unlimited revives.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: I glad Behaviour finally made a good game (sorry DBD fans). Really though, this game is a ton of fun in both the raiding aspect and the building aspect. Don't get me wrong, it's by no means perfect. I think my biggest complaint is that the game needs more content, though it feels like it's been designed with the intent of adding content in the future, so that works out I guess.On a nit-picky note, I do think that co-op should get a limited number of revives and that players should have to successfully test their base before they activate it (not to discourage big "kill-rooms" but just because it's customary for this kind of game).All in all though, I highly recommend this game. I think it's a ton of high energy chaotic fun while also being surprisingly tactical. It's one of those games that you can get lost in for hours.Also, after watching the many replays of people raiding my bases I think I can safely say that this playerbase is the most paranoid group of people on the planet. I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Building your own level, watching replays of people playing through it and making adjustments to it on the fly can be extremely addicting. Despite some needed limitations that can sometimes feel too constraining there's enough tools to make some really clever traps and level designs to outsmart raiders and (hopefully) make sure everyone has a good time, as you don't lose any resources if someone successfully raids your base. You get resources for every raider kill, but there's no upside to making players ragequit.The raiding part can be a mixed bag, as is expected from community generated content.Although there is a rating system that tries to incentivize making levels that are fun to play, it doesn't quite do enough to stop people from making levels that are simply as tedious and frustrating as possible. Still, there's plenty of fun levels to play out there for now, it remains to be seen how the meta will shift in the future and whether or not interesting maps will eventually disappear in favor of cheesing for resources

It seems this game suffered a lot from lack of publicity and exposure, which we can also confirm just from the several comments over here.If you like running dungeons and put your skills/awareness to test, solo or co-op, this is really a fun game. You can also make other people "suffer" with your dungeons, or just create a maze like i have seen with no traps at all. Its a wild ride of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: this game is like if Mario maker and doom had a fling and decided to keep the kid. yes its buggy but its very good and very new HIGHLY RECOMMENDGIVE THIS GAME TIME this game has only been only a few months, and the devs have already added many bug fixes, more blocks, decals,and props to make your base look good. yes it is currently lacking a tiny bit in content but the beauty of the game is the complexities that players can MAKE with the content we have. and yes some peoples bases are ridiculous but they are 100 percent do able with the right load-out, my base is near impossible to do without dying at least once, UNLESS you bring the shield or the shield consumable, in that case my base can be a cake walk, but that is how the game retains its balance, you cant make a base that trashes on every playstyle because the playstyles themselves trash on specific base styles, not to mention even if you don't get to the core and out alive any exp or drops you gained throughout all of your tries stays with you! my simple answer to all the negative reviews about bases being too difficult is to either get good, or to just play the lower difficulty maps xDNow yes there are bugs and glitches but that is inherent in any game that isnt exceptionally long standing or long developed, once again this has only been out for 4 months and yes some bug fixes come with instability issues and what not but if yall review bomb a game before the devs get time to fix it it will lower the chances that the devs will have the funding to fix these over time...

_childDocuments_.review: Having played for some hours now, I begin to see the issue of "kill boxes" as my champion thing just selected, I think was next to impossible, at least to complete in any reasonable time frame.I wouldn't recommend this game at the moment at no particular fault of the game itself, it does seem fun and you can clearly be very creative, some of the bases are super fun and cool. The issue is that "killbox" type bases, filled with armoured enemies, are near impossible, or very unfun to try and complete, and to try and build up your resources to try other builds or items, is VERY slow. Added with the fact that the "champion" bases can be these kill boxes, really seems to hinder any kind of progression.To anyone wondering what a kill box base refers to, its shoving loads of ranged enemies in a a large room, usually armoured, paired with corrosive cubes and drops to trap your ammo. And a lot of traps to funnel you to the genmat, where your ammo cannot sustain to fight and progress normally, only forced to rush through hoping you won't get hit (everything is a one shot kill).TLDR: A lot of players are taking advantage of poor balancing and progression feels very slow. I would suggest to wait for a sale or at least a first balance patch, to try and reduce the amount and effectiveness of the "kill box" type bases.**EDIT** This review I amend slightly, while I still wouldn't recommend the game in its current state, I would say definitely wait for some updates like before. MY change would be, if you avoid all Brutal bases, and/or have a friend to play with, it is still a fun experience and would greatly recommend it :)

_childDocuments_.review: Before any other point:The top review I see is ''You dont have to beat it yourself''. I understand this frustration if you're only going through Outposts which are one long corridor filled with Enforcers, Lava and boltshot/grapple... but this is simply not the game. There are so many outposts out there that are sick, innovative and leave you either refreshed or surprised! On top of this, THERE IS NO COST TO RETRYING, DYING OR ABANDONING. Either get better at the game -- you get good time per trap to react -- or stop whining with your 1.5hr playtime-ass. The game draws mainly from Dungeon Keeper, Mighty Quest for Epic Loot and Quake. A grimy, post-apoc setting and artstyle bring home the brutality of it and an easy to use base-builder make it a breeze to design outposts after your ideas. At time of writing 30$ with a roadmap planned with free-for-everyone content, an entirely new biome and several other additions. Currently in the game are several weapons to upgrade, traps, guards and boosts to unlock. Additionally it has crossplatform capability -- PSN's Gamepass has the game as well (Steam User Data is thus not representative of total players! The playerbase is much higher than indicated on just here).I give this game a worth-it/the price. Three hours of work on minimum wage will get you this game which has entertained me for many more!

_childDocuments_.review: Ja Meet Your Maker war zum Beginn ein gutes Spiel, das kann man an meiner Spielzeit wohl mehr als sehen. Ich spiele immer noch, wobei es mir kaum noch Spaß macht. Diese Killing Rooms sind die Pest, es hat nichts mit können zu tun sowas zu bauen und dann zu sehen, wie man alles tötet. Meine Geduld ist eigentlich durch Souls Games echt hoch, aber wenn es reiner Zufall ist, ob man das Level schafft oder nicht, brauche ich es nicht immer wieder zu machen. Die meisten würden diese Räume nicht mal schaffen, wenn Sie Ihre eigenen Level spielen müssten. Deswegen bin ich dafür das man bevor man ein Level "Aktiv" schaltet, muss man es alleine schaffen. Ist es nicht möglich, darf man es nicht "Aktiv" schalten. Damit hebelt man unfaire Karten aus.Dazu kommen so viele Abstürze, dass man manchmal echt keine Lust mehr hat. Mitten im Level fliegt man raus und kann die Karte nicht mehr spielen. Solange das so ist, spart euch das Geld und wartet auf einen Sale.Ach und ich packe wirklichen jeden, der ein Killing Room baut auf die Ban Liste. Sobald ich es sehe, verlasse ich die Karte. Bewerte auch nicht und es ist mir egal. Wenn Ihr keine guten Karten bauen wollt, lasst es und spielt was anderes.---------------------------------------------------------------Yes, Meet Your Maker was a good game to begin with, as you can see from my playing time. I still play, but I hardly enjoy it any more. Those killing rooms are the plague, it has nothing to do with skill to build something like that and then see how you kill everything. My patience is actually really high through Souls games, but if it's pure chance whether you clear the level or not, I don't need to keep doing it. Most people wouldn't even make it through these rooms if they had to play their own levels. That's why I'm in favour of making sure that before you switch a level to "active", you have to manage it on your own. If you can't do it, you can't make it "Active". In this way, you cancel out unfair cards.In addition, there are so many crashes that sometimes you really don't want to play anymore. You get kicked out in the middle of the level and can't play the map any more. As long as that's the case, save your money and wait for a sale.Oh and I really put everyone who builds a killing room on the ban list. As soon as I see it, I leave the map. I don't rate and I don't care. If you don't want to build good maps, leave it and play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the game has problems, Meet Your Maker is hopefully a start of a new trend of games. I haven't experienced so much pure fun while watching someone play something until I started watching people repeatedly die in my small levels. Rarely can a game motivate me to build stuff out, since I am more of a 'doer' but the building system and the replays are a super fun addition. I wish there were more social features like 'map of the day', 'clubs' and leaderboards because it feels like this game would SHINE in a social setting, while right now it feels rather lonely. That being said your ninja controls amazingly, the accessories don't break the game but give you different options to deal with different maps and the upgrades are minimal, so you're really 'playing' since minute 1. Downsides are that you ARE incentivized by the game to make the map as hard as possible sadly and I hope that the accolade filters out boring death-box maps AND the fact I don't see too much incentive to actually grind maps for times. I go WAY more in depth in a video review if someone's interested, I since nobody wants to read a 50000 word steam review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dog. A lot of bugs. My game crashed TWICE in a run of a single map. Evolving your Chimera is pointless, as there is no story or visual changes to her. There are like 5 different currencies, and getting a hang of them all takes hours. The tutorial doesn't help with anything.The concept of the game is awesome. The little splash art trailer at the beginning of the game/tutorial tells an interesting post apocalyptic story, but doesn't get elaborated on any further no matter how long you play. The maps you build cannot be saved or reused (They only stay for a limited amount of time) so you have to build a new base very often. Also, they cost currency to upkeep daily.The maps don't have enough variety and are either TOO EASY to cheese or TOO DIFFICULT to beat. (You don't have to play through your own map to complete it. You can just make a room full of deathtraps and enemies, then release it.)There is barely any progress (only a handful of weapons, three armor types, like 7 different traps and 3 mobs you can place.) and NO ENDGAME. You are not playing to get to a certain point. You just play.If the point of the game is to just play, there should NOT be any currencies and upgrades, as there is no plot or endgame that needs pacing. The way the game is at the moment, you'll be playing the game without the loadout you want for 20 hours, until you finally upgrade everything you need, at which point you've probably seen every type of map and the game gets boring.Also, there are like only 100 players online at any given time. That is laughably low, considering that the only content this game offers is player made. No player = No Content.I was hyped when I saw this game was free to play, but it's a massive let down. Don't waste your time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of potential, but ultimately a grindy waste of time.Avoid.In this game, you raid bases built by other players, and build yourself some bases.Doing so level up councellors, which in turn level up a chimera, which in turn gives you some ressources.There's three main ressources. All let you unlock some stuff, but : the red one is only used for unlocks and thus become irrelevant after a while, the blue one is used for consumables but is dropped quite frequently so you'll be swimming in it, and then there's the yellow one, called synth.Unlocking a level slot to build cost synth. Unlocking traps cost synths. Unlocking guards cost synth. UPKEEPING YOUR LEVELS cost synth too, and lots of it. Because there's a prestige system in this game : after a while (max 24 hours), you have to reactivate them by paying some more synth, an amount close to what it took to buy the slot at first, but it gets worse : depending on your outpost performances in killing players and gaining accolades, you may have to prestige it. Doing so allows you to put more stuff in your level, but it'll cost more and more synth each time. It's NOT optional, and eventually, a 24h activation become more expensive than the first time, for the same result.Best part being, after the outpost reaches level 10, it won't be reactivated again. After that it gets relegated to "social" raiding if you so choose, a mode where no one gains anything.You gain pitiful amounts of synth by killing raiders in your outpost, a little by raiding yourself destroying traps, and a bit more by leveling up the chimera. But even when using drop boosts, it's a slog to maintain levels running - and remember, it's also used for unlocking stuff, so you're making no progress on that front in the meantime.On top of that, while some outposts are fun to raid, the current meta is a glitchfest of traps hidden behind opaque cubes, or a good old overwhelming spam of traps in a killbox. Allegedly some people find that "fun". Current steam stats tell me there's not that many of them and they'll be enjoying a stale game pretty soon, as devs aren't showing any sign of changing anything. Maybe they're willing to keep the server on but even that isn't that sure.So yeah, don't buy it. Maybe give it a try if it goes F2P one day, but expect tedious grind.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game has the potential to be good, but right now it's probably not worth your time.  I'm pretty average at games in the FPS genre and I was able to beat player-made maps that were on the highest difficulty while only dying 2-3 times. One of the main reasons for this is that all defenses in the game have some sort of delay, there's nothing that will punish you instantly for stepping somewhere. Knowing this, you can full-speed run through almost every map and not have to worry about dying as long as you know where traps are coming from, which the game tells you with the heads-up display. I can imagine the game is much more challenging on controller/console, but that's because your movement is more restricted. There's also a huge lack of traps, guards, weapons, and mods to unlock. Genuinely, where is all the content? There are just not many ways to make creative and fun maps because map creators have such few tools at their disposal. There will be more content in these areas in future updates I'm sure, but as of right now there's really not much. You can probably unlock everything in less than a week of playing. Overall, fantastic concept, but the execution is evidently rushed and poor. It'll take some time for Meet Your Maker to shape up to the game it's meant to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad saying that I don't recommend this game. Behaviour definitely showed a lot of care when making this game, but just made a bunch of stupid decisions on the way that slowly killed the game.My biggest problem with the game is that the only requirement to complete your base is if there's a straightforward path to your little flag at the end. This kills the opportunity for parkour maps, puzzle maps, things like that, making every map just the worlds worst rust base. Full of killboxes, trap spam, enemy spam. It was definitely one of the major reasons people dropped this game shortly after release. Another absolutely stupid thing is that your base will just stop working after about a day, give or take a few hours. You know that super cool base that you spent hours decorating, handcrafted every little detail on? Its going to go away, don't worry though, you can prestige the base which keeps it public for another day, it just costs in game currency that scales up in price everytime you do it, I don't know why they did this. They could have had the perfect rust mixed with mario maker game, but by trying to keep it competitive, and with decisions like this just to try and increase your engagement, it had the opposite effect, many people just stopped working on bases, or stopped playing the game overall.Despite this the games not all bad. The graphics and atmosphere are top notch, and some of the levels were genuinely fun, but with an average player count of 20 players, and Behaviours tendency to pull the plug on failed projects, I don't see this game lasting much longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for a few hours via PS Plus before grabbing it on Steam.Short version: It's a solid foundation, already enjoyable as it is but also with the potential to become a proper little gem with attention and support.Long version: I really like what this game has going on.  Content is a bit bare-bones at the moment (there's something like half a dozen each of trap and guard types, two each of ranged and melee weapons, and two combat suits); however, the developer's stated their intention to start adding more early and often, so I'm not terribly worried about it.What's encouraging is what they've already gotten right.  Visible, obvious traps are easy for even a half-competent player to avoid or disable, so the game is in figuring out how to place them to catch raiders off guard--hidden spots, layered gauntlets, intentional funneling of movement and the like.  It feels like a proper battle of wits.(Yes, killboxing is occasionally an issue--however, in several hours of playtime I can only think of two outposts I ran across that actually felt unfair to the point that I wasn't sure if it was legitimately possible to complete them.  Thankfully the game gives you an option to pass on any given outpost that pops up on your map, so you're not stuck banging your head against a wall forever.)The onboarding experience is well designed; you'll need to do at least a few runs as a raider before getting the chance to build an outpost of your own, and if you're smart you'll be taking mental notes the whole time of which setups managed to get you so you can give them a shot yourself.  Your outposts will also not only tell you how many kills they got, but where and to what, so you have a record of what's working and what isn't.  Combined with the progressive unlocking of mods that tweak the functioning of your traps and guards, it feels like there's a lot of depth to be had in learning how to design a good, lethal outpost that will only get deeper as content is added.Overall I think it's pretty easy to get $30 worth of enjoyment out of this game even as it stands right now, and if the devs live up to their promises with content drops then I can see myself continuing to play this for a long time to come.
