_childDocuments_.review: To summarise briefly, Moncage is a point-and-click puzzle game the gameplay loop of which seems to be heavily inspired by Gorogoa: rotate a cube to seamlessly combine motifs in two adjacent images into new objects in order to advance the actions or to unlock new scenes. Since Moncage is 3D (rather than 2D as Gorogoa), it also has some flavours of Monument Valley.In terms of visuals, Moncage is absolutely stunning. However, sometimes the puzzles become rather obscure and unintuitive; the in-game highlight and hint system will come in handy. And some designs are questionable:- There is no manual save, no level selection after completion, no save slot, which is particularly annoying due to missable achievements and collectibles, on which the underlying story depends (not that it is a coherent one, anyway);- After getting all the collectibles, you need to play through it once more to unlock the true ending, with virtually no difference in gameplay;- To see either ending again, you need another playthrough;- There is a speedrun achievement. For a point-and-click puzzle game, seriously? Maybe a tribute to Gorogoa?As a result, you probably need three playthroughs to 100% complete the game; completionists should think twice before purchasing this title.All in all, it is an enjoyable journey, which feels more like playing with an exquisite and well-crafted toy than solving puzzles, hence my recommendation. If you are interested in this game, you should also take a look at Gorogoa and Monument Valley that I mentioned above. If you truly are a puzzle lover, I also strongly recommend getting the Brilliant Boxes Bundle: the other three titles from this bundle are all excellent puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a beautifully designed and unique puzzle game. I finished the game in about 3.5 hours and then redid a run for the achievements I missed along the way which took another ~45 minutes. This game is similar to other titles such as Gorogoa (the developers said they were inspired by it) and Superlimiinal, where you play with perspective to solve puzzles and to move forward with the narrative. While I think the storyline is ambiguous, there is enough there to keep you interested even aside from the really great puzzles.I personally found the puzzles to be fair, though some of the solutions are on the harder end. The game has two separate and really solid hint systems. The first is the ability to highlight critical parts to the puzzle and the second is the ability to have three hints given to you, and finally, if you're really really stuck, a video of the solution. I used the hints probably 3-4 times and a video once for a puzzle I was completely lost on. The hints are nice in that they start out explaining a "what" aspect to the puzzle vs. a "how" solution to solve the puzzle (e.g. the first hint might be something along the lines of "A pressure plate is not activated" indicating you need to do something to the pressure plate, but how you actually activate it is left to you). The second and third hint for an area will become more explicit, allowing for players who are stuck to get the help they need, but without having the puzzles be easy (unless you want to watch a video solution to all areas, which is an option, just not a fun one lol). I think that because the develops incorporated the hint systems, the puzzles are challenging enough for those who want to work/think outside the box (cage?) for a solution.All in all, this is a really great pick if you're looking for a moderately challenging puzzle game against a moving, though implied, narrative. If you enjoyed Gorogoa or Superliminal, I suspect you'd enjoy this title too.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a game I just found and had sitting in my library for a long time, but I finally got around to it and I will be blunt. I really enjoyed it. A lot of the puzzles are really solid and I think the game does a good job at showing most of the mechanics. The photos may be something you could miss some of, but they are simple collectibles that help tell the story of the game in a subtle way. I think it is a nice example of telling a story without needing to spell out anything to somebody trying to follow along. In this case you are walking through the events and learning what happened as you also try to solve the puzzles the game has for you to solve. In short, I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: (Обзор на русском тут: )There's the cube where each side is a scene from one person's life. By rotating the camera, we can combine two objects from different sides of the cube – do a  – and then something will happen: an object will move, a mechanism will start working, or even another side will be changed.– The game is confusing. The usual logic doesn't apply here, because the player doesn't know the end goal or often even what will happen after combining objects.– Some items are hidden behind extreme camera angles – and then you're wondering what to do next.– I didn't like the controls. A single click is to apply/zoom in, and a double click is to zoom out. When you're trying to do something quickly, you click a lot, and the result isn't always what you need.= There is a highlighting of active objects. By default, you are brightly highlighted the next object, what looks more like a cheat.= Some of the non-story achievements are hidden — and it's unclear how the player has to get them, except to get accidentally (or look in the guide).After the first hour, I wanted to abandon the game, because I didn't understand what to do without using hints every minute. Then I calmed down – and accepted the rules of the game: now I carefully examine each scene and think about montage.+ Re-using mechanics. The game teaches you some tricks you'll encounter later. For example, that color is important to match objects. Or you will know a way to light a lamp.+ Collectables: there are hidden photos in tricky parts of scenes.+ Small details. If you look more closely at the locations, you can see both clues and additional story details.+ Variety as much as possible in a game like this: you can rotate valves, open/close crates, there are several time-based segments, and even a simple puzzle.+ Motivation to replay. To collect all the pictures, get achievements and find uses for some suspicious scenes.I passed the game three times. The first one took  because I was stupid. In the second one, I collected most achievements and all photos – 50 minutes. The third attempt was a speedrun and  – finished in 25 minutes.During 2nd walkthrough, I started putting the pieces of the story together – to get a pretty sad story. I have no regrets that I gave the second chance to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this as a Christmas gift from my SO.This game is an experience, not only a puzzle game. Music, art, story, puzzles, everything screams care and attention to detail. Some of the puzzles are quite challenging, and you will find yourself banging your head at walls for quite some time if you are the type that does not peak at hints or walkthroughs for a helping hand at any cost. The hints. The hint system is nice, it gives you a timed window to pull your hair for each puzzle, then offers the option to ask for hints. There are 3 for each panel, and a video solution as the fourth hint if you REAAALLY dont get it. I'd say first playthrough may take you anywhere from 2 hours to 5-6 hours, depending on how skillful you are at optical puzzles and perspective vision. Subsequent playthroughs (for achievements, for eg.) can take as little as 20-25 minutes if you are clockwork. 30-35 min if you take your time to smell the roses.All in all, a wonderful experience. Totally worth the time and money. 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little puzzlegame, interesting mechanics, a nice story.Good relaxing musicGood hint system if you are stuck.Too short, first playthrough in about 2.5 hours, altho I remembered the mechanics and some of the puzzles from the demo.graphics are nice too.As I said, it is short, but on the other hand, a game you can finish in an evening (or two)

_childDocuments_.review: mysterious box In front of you containing a story of someone. He lived his life, the good and the bad, and here you are trying to find out its details.The gameplay here is unique. It is a box with each side of it containing a story and a world and also a puzzle and you try to solve these puzzles by rotating this box to try to connect the items between two different worlds. You may even get to the point where you are trying to change something in one world and transfer it to another. the puzzle idea is very beautiful, especially with every progress the story reveals to you and what happens in it. Sometimes you may have difficulty solving puzzles (it only happened to me twice) but with the hint button you will find it as soon as possible.The story here is beautiful and the way it is told is even more gorgeous. The game never talks to you, but the events that take place in these worlds and the images that you may find scattered is the story. This type of storytelling I rarely come across and find it very interesting.The game pleases the viewers, I find it very simple and there are no details that might distract you. _childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: "What am I thinking of?" if you like that kind of riddle, then you'll like Moncage.The game started out really interesting, but after playing it for a while the novelty wore off and I felt less embarrassed for using hints until I realized I stopped caring about the puzzles.Moncage doesn't make YOU feel clever, because you might have a ton of great ideas how to solve the puzzles, but only the developers' intended solution is accepted.What a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe this one didn't grab me. I absolutely love puzzles games. And the overwhelmingly positive reviews on Steam! _childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: I like other puzzle box games like the Room, and Moncage is doing something very cool with the bleeding of elements between frames.  However, I found it to be mostly tedious and had to rely heavily on the focus / highlight mechanic, as the pieces that connect are not visually obvious.  This is made worse by some elements only connecting when the color temperature in a scene caused the connecting elements to match colors, and the use of reflections to find some objects.  The story is very understated, and there's not much reward for solving a puzzle.  This game might be a real hit for some people, but not for me.

The mechanic of the game is simple to understand but can get highly complex, the hallmark of a good puzzle game. On a cube in front of you shows five scenes, and by adjusting your perspective, objects in different scenes can line up to activate machines or trigger events. The game should take you less than 2 hours in full, and there are a few achievements to go hunting for. I've played a game like this one time before, called  And after playing both games with a similar mechanic, I recommend  above this game. They are both priced at $15.00, and tell beautiful stories in their own right. But the story you are given in  is less satisfying, less thematic, and not as tightly constructed as  Often times I wondered, "What are we doing in this random location?" _childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle games, and this one is beautiful, but it still hasn't been doing it for me. The solutions often seem arbitrary and frustrating, and the game trains you early on to look for glowing connections to proceed, and then later on, it starts breaking that convention, leaving me confused. _childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a multi dimensional perception puzzle game with beautiful visuals, a text less story and a great ambient OST.The whole game revolves around a single cube, with each one of it's sides having a different scenery with multiple observation levels in which you can also change the position of certain objects. Our task is finding the right angles & properties for connecting multiple cube side's into a single scene that leads an optical illusion & each individuals side's solution. Difficulty is somewhere between mediocre & hard but you can solve any puzzle at your own pace since there is no time requirements, making it a very relaxing experience. There are also "hidden" photographs you can collect that leads to a different ending.Totally recommended to all puzzle junkies & not only !
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: A unique approach to "perspective" based games - each side of the cube is a different, manipulatable area.Pros:* Some moderately difficult puzzles.* Great music* Interesting take on perspective-based games.Cons:* Short.  Like, maybe 2-3 hrs max on your 1st playthru.  Like, has an achievement for finishing the game in 45 min - which ought to inform how short it is.* Plot is vague and forgettable.Meh:* Collectibles that are only rarely in a-hole'ish locations.* The game doesn't bother explaining that COLOR matters as much as SHAPE, for matching up sides on the cube.TL;DR: If you like puzzle games, it's worth buying - maybe on sale, but get it.  Otherwise, avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a somewhat similar gameplay design like Gorogoa; a pattern matching game where you need to locate said patterns in different, distinct areas next to each other. However, where Gorogoa tells a story (said story is a bit vague, but it's definitely there) here it seems like a series of puzzles with no discernible theme.Look, the pattern matching is all fine in and of itself, and if this is enough for you then definitely get this. For me it's lacking that extra something to make it memorable and I found I just didn't enjoy it as much as I hoped I would (I really liked Gorogoa, even if I still think the base price of that game was disproportionate to its length).
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another 'puzzle' game with hardly any actual puzzles. Most of this game is just 'find the interactable'. You can either play with the highlight function and trivialise that process, or drag it out to the point of tedium without it.The few actual puzzles are pretty good, but anyone buying should expect to go about twenty minutes between them.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking for a neat game to play on Steam, so I decided to check out Steam awards to find out what's the highest rated games around on PC in 2021. Bunch of AAA and highly rated titles, and Moncage was one of the nominees for Most Innovative Gameplay. Haven't heard of this game before unlike the rest, so I check out the Steam Page to learn more, and sees overwhelmingly positive reviews.Decided to give it a try. It was nominated for most innovative gameplay, and have bunch of positive reviews, it gotta be good right? And yes indeed, the game features refreshing gameplay. Its a perspective puzzler title , where you have to solve puzzles that happen across the cube faces. You'll have to align key elements across 2 faces of the cube to get the game going, in addition you'll have to rotate around and explore (via trial and error) to see what you just solved and triggered.In the background you'll be collecting photos which depict a story as you solve the puzzles. It is a soothing game which gets your brain cells kicking, and is very, very good. Now I understand why it is getting so many positive reviews.More players should definitely check out this title. I clocked in at 3 hours gameplay time, so I guess the down side is that the game is kinda short. Still a great weekend game.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting idea and fantastic visually, but the puzzles and pretty weak. You solve the "puzzles" by lining up two different pictures from two sides of the cube. The big problem is that you often don't know what you are trying to achieve apart from lining up said images for the sake of it.This means that instead of having a test of logic to solve a problem, you are must mashing the button which highlights the features and seeing what fits. So the majority of the game is basically a very pretty 'spot the similarity' and then fiddling with the images until it lines up  the way the game wants it to. For some people, the good design will make up for the lacking puzzles and thats perfectly fine,
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Infuriating.I am a fan of puzzle games and was really hyped for this one. Such cool optical illusion / forced perspective mechanic I thought - this will be so much fun!Well, it's all just about as much fun as late-stage Sierra adventure games. There is no logic to the progress, no way of figuring it out organically. I ended up constantly waiting for hints to refresh and then realized "hey, I can just watch a walkthrough on YouTube" and quit playing.It could of course be me, but I am currently having a ton of fun with Talos Principle 2 which presents just the right level of challenge - so I guess maybe puzzle designs in Moncage are not the best.Sure looks like a game that was designed for mobile devices with a paid hint system.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was going to be exactly the sort of thing I usually enjoy, but there was not much point to it. You just spin the box around finding pieces that fit together with no real story or purpose for what you're doing. Eventually you find some pieces that go together and one of the sides of the box changes so that you have a new room full of junk to try to fit together.It would have done well to have some sort of narrative or purpose the puzzles other than just 'can you find the crap that goes together so that you can move forward to the next stage'.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Moncage! I would recommend it if you like puzzle games, with a recommendation multiplier depending on if you like or don't like puzzles that lean more towards observation and visual lateral thinking.Moncage had a very similar vibe to Gorogoa. If you liked Gorogoa then I think you would like Moncage.Mechanically the game consists of figuring out how to match up elements of different scenes visually. This is a 3D game and so you can rotate the perspective view any way that you want, and your task is to find a way to position the viewpoint such that two different things match up. Early in the game this is all that you do, and making a successful match triggers some event that allows you to find the next match. As the game progresses so does the complexity, but the focus is always on "how can I make two different scenes interact?" Not only did I love this as a mechanic, but I thought the game did a good job of utilizing the core idea in many different creative ways. It's a relatively short game (Steam says I played 3 hours), but it felt like exactly the right length to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Half of the time it's unclear what the goal is, then it's completely random why the solution works. Without careful design, it really does feel random. The premise of the game is combining elements on the edges of the cube, yet sometimes a puzzle step is contained within a side completely, so it's more of a camera perspective-only piece. "The moon is a source of light". Made no sense. And with the "cart over the bridge" puzzle, the hint video is the first ever place that explains a thing in the game is even possible! _childDocuments_.review: A small but smart game based on connecting and functioning objects through the various perspectives, all viewed as the edges of a space-time cube. Each plane show and hold a memory of a war veteran and his journey from grief to redemption.A very beautiful story that tries to express itself through different planes of times and each withholding a distinct stages of the man.A beautiful yet melancholic experience, Moncage is worth exploring and finding 'new perspective' in life.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Innovative puzzle game concept that makes full use of 3 dimensional space and 5 subspaces with a short and sweet story. Unfortunately this work is heavily held down by it's clunky controls and clunky-ness of navigation. Puzzles are awkward as they don't snap in place intuitively, lack of jingles/snap feeling from solving a puzzles takes away part of the joy of solving it. Hints are intentionally spaced out with arbitrary timers akin to timers for mobile game ads. In fact, this is available on GooglePlay for a quarter of the price.Overall an interesting concept with a wonderful little story  that dampens itself from poor gameplay and quality of life  designs. Get it only on >75% off or on mobile.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: A unique, involving, intriguing puzzle game where you have to move a 3-d cube around that itself has a world within each side.  The puzzle is finding how some piece of one scene fits into another - sometimes it's obvious (an arm of a desk lamp with the bottom part of a crane) and sometimes it's much harder.  The harder stuff is a satisfying effort, and sometimes you have to change perspective, lighting, or do something dynamic within one scene.  There a lot of times I asked myself how the creators were able to think up this or that thing, the answer is that they're very creative and smart.The game proceeds at your pace, with a zen-like musical backdrop.  It follows a loose story that you put together in your own head, in a non-linear way that is perfectly compatible with the way the puzzles are structured.   It's absolutely worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm getting old and dumb. but shouldn't puzzle games give you clue to investigate. rather than point and click randomly and see what sticks? and a lot of times you know something works, but the game just refuses to let you process, until certain point or certain angle. Which yet again, can only be achieved by random chance. This is the worst puzzle game I've played that has a Overwhelmingly Positive review score.I've previously played another perspective puzzle game, Superliminal. That's what I expected from this, but was very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, super great game. It has the same level of puzzle complexity and environmental story telling as Gorogoa (which is to say, its top-tier-best-a-da-best *chef's kiss). The intimate art + atmosphere mixed with its steady pacing can result in some real impactful moments (SO IF YOU WANT A GAME THAT GIVE THE BIG CHILLS, THIS GAME WILL GIVE THE BIG CHILLS). The puzzles are greatly satisfying to complete, and the game does a really good job of providing hints to guide you along if you are stuck. If you were to play it, HIGHLY RECOMMEND 100% it. It's totally worth the little extra effort as it is a relatively short game (took me 5 hours to complete and 5.8 hrs to 100%). Judging from the credits the dev team is really quite small, and to pull this masterpiece off is really impressive (sheeesh pop off)
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Well I do not like giving thumbs down really but that is how I feel about it. The Game itself it a very big thumbs up. Imaginative, original and intriguing type of game play.But, what is the point?I am quite new to gaming so maybe I do not have the skill set yet to get the most out of this sort of thing. But overall it was a tedious experience. How folk manage to make the visual link ups is beyond me and I virtually always needed the 'clues' and the videos to work out what the heck I was supposed to be doing. Perhaps developers who are so closely into what they are creating forget that us mortals come at these things from a different angle? There is also some narrative here but what? Scenes of warfare nestle along side a fairground - all very confusing. A similar game I have played is Gorogoa but I enjoyed that enormously. Moncage I found impenetrable and ultimately it is just not for me. To me what it 'looks like' has taken precedent over the coherence of the content. Sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Runs really well on the Steam Deck. The puzzles can be a bit too subtle or hard to spot at times, and hints don't always give much useful information to actually point you down the right path. You can also find stuff out of order which makes getting stuck even easier as you wait for the next hint to be available.The biggest issue i have is complete lack of a full custom controller config. The game may be simple, but when its designed for computer it helps massively to have an OOTB controller config that binds the menu, hints, double-clicks, point of interest highlighting, etc. You can do it yourself on Steam Deck, but each game has slight differences to how it accepts inputs. So using Steam input to string together menu interactions doesn't always work the same and can take hours to get working. It improves gameplay a ton though once its setup to your liking, but some form of custom controller mapping from the devs would be preferred.Despite those shortfalls, its still a good creative puzzle game. Worth checking out on sale for sure. But be prepared for odd control scheme OOTB on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Very well-made puzzle game.  I absolutely adore the setup of having to connect different objects across multiple faces of the puzzle to get the solution, though on occasion the solutions are a bit too obtuse (specifically ones that require specific colors to match up, which makes it unclear if you're matching items that aren't supposed to match or if you're just doing it at the wrong time).  Thankfully it has a good hint system built-in, and there's also a lot of collectibles hidden throughout and a ton of cool details in the levels.  Just be aware it's a bit short if you aren't going for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game, I struggled quite a bit until I finished the first playthrough. I usually really enjoy playing the likes of escape room games, The Room series, House of Da Vinci series etc but my brain just didn't want to work for this one for a lot of it ^^" Glad the hints were there. I often wanted to jump ahead and there is no clear indication of order until you get it, so I guess neurodivergents might struggle with it XD Take your time and think everything through or use the well-timed help. Once you understand all, you can then enjoy a re-run to find everything that you missed in the first attempt and it is really worth it!I enjoyed the imagery and themes in the game and the music was very relaxing. To me it also evoked Hemingway a bit, but that might just be me ^^" So if you like puzzle games with a twist and having to rethink perspective, I highly recommend it, just don't try to rush it.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say that this game was a journey. I originally bought this because it was listed as a puzzle game, which is a genre of game i enjoy playing a lot. At the time of this review i have 3 hours played, which is how long it took me to beat it my first time around. This is not an ordinary puzzle game, this is a story. The soundtrack is outstanding the whole way through. The art is wonderful in its own way. This is a very visually appealing game to play. I had a lot of moments I was super stumped as well, which is what makes a great puzzle game great in my opinion. As you follow the story along and collect memories and actively think outside the box, you are constantly reminded that anything goes as long as you can connect it. In the end, I will be replaying this as I've missed several achievements. Hopefully though whoever may see this truly considers picking it up because THIS is one gem of a game for an outstanding price. I don't want to spoil what the deep meaningful story it will take you on is, you have to find that out for yourself :-)

_childDocuments_.review: A short, fun game with a cool concept. I think I got the gist of the story from playing through it, though it feels very left up to interpretation and imagination. If I have any complaints about the game, it would mainly be that missing anything means you need to replay the entire game again. It's relatively short, but with no way to make things move faster, I was getting impatient. If you're good and thorough, you can probably 100% the game in only 2 playthroughs, but I kept missing things due to my own impatience and mistakes, meaning I had to play through it at least 4 if not 5 times. Some kind of checkpoint or level select after you finish the game to make either getting the true ending or specific achievements (mainly the exhaustive method) would have been appreciated, but the game is short enough that I can't hold too much of a grudge. Overall I enjoyed it, but if you're going for 100%, be careful of replay frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a clone of Gorogoa. It's slicker, but the puzzles are more obtuse and the story is even harder to follow than Gorogoa. It also doesn't feel like you are directing your journey as much. It does have a much better hint system though!So, if you loved Gorogoa, then you'll like this. If you haven't played Gorogoa then go play it. It's amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmm,Let's see. On one hand, it's a concept I love, a bit similar to Gorogora where all the game revolves around visual tricks to solve puzzles.The hint system is great to make your understand the few basic principles you can play with.It's incredible that this game is kinda unexplainable. It's quite difficult to predict what the level designer had in mind before you actually see it in one very specific angle and it's quite satisfying once you do.On the other hand, it took me 4 hours to complete the game including all achievements.4 or 5 play through. (less than 25 mins once you get used to it)So, it's rather super short but still satisfying. Maybe a bit expensive though.The story and scenes, despite the weirdness of the puzzles do really tell a story that is pleasant to follow.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is an interesting perspective puzzle game. They did a great job of working the hints into the game through allowing you to highlight important pieces, and even receive small hints through the pause menu. The game is exceptionally beautiful and many of the stunning environments felt like tiny little worlds to look at and explore.In some puzzles I felt that in the eventual solution, there was little "connection" to the objects being linked or to the action being performed. Some puzzles felt very intuitive and satisfying but others were difficult because of sheer obscurity.Overall a great addition to the genre, 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games do not typically attract me, but the visuals and mechanics of Moncage piqued my interest anyway. In my opinion, the game hits a balance that puzzle games often struggle with, being challenging enough to be satisfying to solve without being a constant irritation. The mechanic, rotating the camera around to match objects in adjacent faces of the cube, is creative and elegant, yet simple so one does not need to learn some complicated, unruly system, making it easy to pick up.The game is also somewhat short (likely just a couple hours) and I think being short and sweet in this way helps keep it from becoming tiresome.There is something a narrative, subtly told, that takes you through the life of the protagonist. However, I confess that I was not inclined to pay much attention to it nor was I extremely motivated to find the collectibles that really help tell it. This is not because that story is bad in any way, but simply because I was perfectly satisfied with solving the puzzles for their own sake.A nice, casual, interesting puzzle game worth a couple hours when you can spare them <3
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, took me two and a half hours. There were plenty of parts that I got stuck on and had to use the hint function (which has an annoying timer). There were only a few parts that I thought were counter-intuitive, one part made you do the same thing three times in a row to progress, which completely stumped me because I thought "well I already did that, and it didn't work" so I didn't do it again much less two more times. There were a few parts that were tricky to align, to the point that I thought that I wasn't supposed to align them until I looked at the hint and saw that I actually was supposed to align them.The art and music are great though, and if you are clever enough to not be constantly having to use the hints then I could see how this game could be really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda neat. My issue with this game is that since the puzzles are all based around the cube, the only continuous thread gameplay wise is the cube itself. This resulted in me holding the space bar to know how things are connected, but not piecing together the physics of it all and how they connect. I get that's the point, but it just wasn't fun to see the solution to the puzzle was one click away yet such an obscure element that I'd never have gotten it. Although it's very possible I'm just dumb.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting puzzle game with interesting mechanics using a combination of different schemes in a cube where you progress by interacting and matching scenes to achieve an outcome to move ahead.Good+ A unique take on a puzzle game, similar in some ways to Gorogoa.+ The premise of war and peace is interesting but not really fleshed out fully on the message it wishes to convey, but interesting nonetheless.+ Challenging but satisfying results when you get a solution right after a hard try.+ Lovely art style and design in their graphics.Cons- Frustrating at times at what the solution, they do have a multi tiered hint system which does help somewhat but it would be better if some of it was more intuitive.- The matching lock between puzzle pieces can be frustrating when you know its the solution but it doesn't align well enough or need such a precision that it becomes tedious or too difficult to just get it right in certain positions.- Some of the timing puzzles require too much precision. - Tedious, I really wish to like this but its really frustrating (yes i have used this word multiple times) that I just feel like giving up despite it being interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, as much as I would have loved to be able to recommend this game, I can’t.It was simply missing logic when trying to piece two things together and felt rather like random pattern matching.Don’t get me wrong, some puzzles were alright, where you knew what you were trying to accomplish but most of them just felt random. The story was okay but with 2 hours it definitely was too short for 12€.

_childDocuments_.review: Unique take on solving puzzles from multiple settings into one, worth a buy if you're specifically into puzzles that will take time to solve. Sometimes easy to get stuck by overlooking/misunderstanding something small, but there are hints (but sometimes these aren't much help). Unfortunately no controller support.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is built around a quaint yet enthralling puzzles, involved around making an object look like it crosses scenes. As this mechanic is fully explored, you are taken on a journey through a subtly compelling story. I played this game assuming it would be good, and was repeatedly surprised by how great it was.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful puzzle game that tells a tragic and bittersweet story about war in the background, how it changes us and the world around us, and how even after tragedy, there can still be beauty. A lot of the connections force you to think outside (or in this case, I suppose inside) the box. There was only once or twice where I used hints where I thought "how would I ever thought of that on my own?" But even in those cases, I wouldn't say it was the developer's fault for making a bad puzzle; instead, it was just that the solution was very clever and required more steps and more brain power. Highly recommend. One of the best puzzle games I've ever played, if not THE best one I've ever played. Extremely unique and simple. The diverse hint system allows for varying levels of difficulty depending on how much of a puzzle you want (and if you want an extremely challenging experience, I suggest never hitting the space bar).
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Recommended. When people talk about games as art, Moncage should be an example, Minimalist art style, minimalist story telling, and yet it tells a powerful story with strong imagery. This is a puzzle solving game based on perspective, similar to Monument Valley and Maquette, and while not particularly groundbreaking the execution here is probably the best I've ever experience for this style of game. The puzzles had a good amount of brain strain, I was never stalled for long, and found I got a good sense of momentum and some "a-ha" moments where everything clicked and you could make good progression. The hint system was very well implemented in that it would give you multiple nudges in the right direction before showing you a video if you were truly stuck, letting you control just how much help you need.Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: The hitboxes for where it wants you to line things up have a good chance of just not working, even when doing the very thing the video hints do. The achievements were also super buggy, where I had to beat the game 4 times in under 30min each to get the 'veteran' achievement, which only requires time under 45min. This was due to a couple things including not accepting a completion if all album cards weren't found and the final alignment before the credits playing but never starting the actual credits.Game is also quite short for the price buggy or not, with no replay value as the only way to do new runs of the game is to wipe all progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: DNF - becomes a chore only way to complete is read the clues. This unfortunately means it becomes unenjoyable with no sense of achievement. There's a great game mechanic here - but too many issues in puzzle design to recommend it. The game fails due to it's locking together mechanism being immensely shonky, and also no real cohesion within the puzzles. With the locking mechanism sometimes you can be miles away and it will autocomplete, others you're fiddling for ages just to get it right on that spot.There's also a couple of Goat Puzzle moments where the game throws in new mechanics without any warning. Even after you've looked up the solution and found what you're trying to do is right your left fiddling for 10mins to get it to the exact mm of where it wants.This unfortunately ruins the entire game by removing all fun, as it's no longer logic or guess work but looking up the answer via the hints or the an online walkthough. And as I've mentioned them - the "online walkthrough players" with there "Oh I'm just gonna try this... " no, it's quite obvious you already know the solution.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up only because I refunded this after fifteen minutes so a negative review didn't feel entirely fair. I wish there was a "Neutral" option. I found the game a little too focused on...how should I phrase this...Polish in place of Art (Heart). It had the flavor I might expect if a AAA developer tried to make a "point, click, rotate" puzzle game. And I just didn't feel the puzzle element; it felt much more like I-Spy, with a number of the connections relying a bit too much on blind flailing. Perhaps this would've changed if I played longer, but I think the first fifteen minutes set up exactly what the whole game will be. Also, the last "point and click" puzzle game I played was Gorogoa, and Moncage just didn't live up to it by comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Great visual puzzles.And not only visual.Admirably crafted, Moncage really makes you think inside the box, and is challenging enough that I had to take a couple of breaks to figure out solutions.Some reviewers might confuse you by claiming, in the same sentence, that the game is too short and that they used the hint system.Unsurprisingly, if you solve all puzzles by yourself, i.e., if you play the game, the playing time doubles.The only missing feature is a post-game chapter selector.It would let us hunt for our missed secrets without the need to replay the entire game.It's a minor flaw; I'll hunt anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful puzzle game taking place in different scenes in the sides of a cube where the player has to line up different objects until they look connected between the scenes, causing some change to occur. There are plenty of puzzles that felt pretty easy to solve and plenty that made me scratch my head a bit and spin around the cube multiple times. Thankfully, there is a hint system in the game that seems to only be based on time, so you have a lot of time to try to solve the puzzles without being tempted to get a hint for something you could have solved with a little more thinking. The art style is beautiful and the game tells a story without words that mostly depends on the number of pictures you find throughout the game and put in your album. The story went in places I didn't expect and honestly made me tear up a bit at the end and I felt that I managed to get a good grip on what was going on both without words and without having found every single picture. The soundtrack was at times quietly minimalist and at times building up with the story beats and it could be quite sorrowful and beautiful. A truly enjoyable experience with depth beyond its face.

_childDocuments_.review: A very short but sweet perspective puzzle game! Hints and clues are built into the game, so you never had to look for the solutions online. I manage to finished it in 2-3 hours.There is an underlying story hidden somewhere here about a PTSD war veteran and the cycle of generational trauma, but to be honest... I don't play this game because of its story. But hey, it's there if you want to dive deep into it.Overall, very nice game!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: A short but great puzzler with a surprisingly nuanced story to go with it. The hint system is good and nonintrusive & some of the puzzles can be a little finicky but it's not frustrating. Overall would definitely recommend on sale as it isn't even really a couple hours long unless you go for every collectible and achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a captivating puzzle game where each box reveals a different world. The intricate puzzles are brilliantly designed, and the outstanding soundtrack adds depth to the immersive experience. The way the scenes connect is mesmerizing. Highly recommended for anyone who loves innovative and kinda of challenging gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Though it was frustrating at times, I did have a good time playing this game. It was creative, interesting, colorful, and a lot of love clearly went into it. And considering it looks like it was made almost entirely by 2 people, I'm willing to be more lenient on it. The frustration mostly stemmed from the fact that some of the solutions can feel finicky, in the sense that I had actually solved the puzzle, I just hadn't gotten things in the exact right spot. The hint system was also not my favorite, but that's kind of a minor issue.Aside from all that, this is short, clever puzzle game that I think is worth your time, especially if you were intrigued by the screenshots. Also not too tough to 100%, though I do recommend using a guide, because some of them you only get one shot at per playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely. Brain melting. Fascinating and paired with a surprisingly dark story.Unique and beautiful, and the only marring factors are some puzzle solutions feeling very "moon logic". There are also puzzles that are intensely clever. Too clever for me. I loved them, but felt bad resorting to the hints. Definitely worth the time. Most likely not worth the time to 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: EXTREMELY confusing at times, the hint system is great in that it is on a timer that feels very well-tuned but sometimes the different sides of the cube change with no real indication except that  the story was very whatever at the start but it got pretty heartfelt by the midpoint and none of it felt forced, had a nice little bowtie at the end. Also, it sometimes randomly throws timed sections at you and it makes the puzzles even more confusing. You also never know what your objective actually is so sometimes you're stuck behind the most meaningless thing ever but once you get used to the lack of logic and try to connect things it works out.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of puzzles games I crave to see pop up on Steam.The idea of have a simple box be the puzzle and having it change when you turn the object in genius Having also simple puzzles but complex enough that you have to really think makes it feel like a really solid puzzle, I love when I figure it out because that feeling is so satisfying If their was a sequel I would play it in a heartbeat!!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: If you like quiet contemplative puzzle games, then Moncage is for you. It has an innovative puzzle system of rotating the image to create new scenes by combining existing ones, and this mechanic becomes more elaborate and introduces multiple unexpected extensions as you play. There's a bit of a story here, told in images alone, that you piece together through play.It's not a long game, as I finished it in about 4.5 hours, but I found it quite satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: A short puzzle game about combining different 3-dimensional scenes in order for their contents to interact.Moncage plays very similar to Gorogoa, presenting different viewports on the sides of a cube. You can interact with certain objects in the viewports and move their camera to fixed points within the scenes they display. The cube itself can also be moved around in order to change the viewports’ perspectives. Doing this, you can line up objects from the different scenes in order to combine them, leading to their behaviour changing or even to them moving between the different viewports. At times, these combinations are also dependant on timing and/or order.Puzzles are usually quite simple and the game offers a help system. However, certain sections require the repetition of sequences, which can get quite tedious, especially when replaying the game for collectibles or achievements.Along the way, Moncage also tells a neat, if not too original story through the puzzles’ theming and a number of optional collectible images. While the visuals are nice enough, they look very flat, due to the way objects need to fit together from different perspectives.All in all, while Moncage feels less special to me than similar games, it’s still a decent puzzle game and holds a couple hours of enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah. I Really like puzzle games but this one, even tho it`s a beautiful one, is often confusing, arbitrary and a mess all around. No sense of direction, objective or goal. As others have said, keep spinning the cube until something pops out and you get a relieved "Finally!" instead of a excited "Aha!" (perfect definition!)Not a bad game, see, but once I noticed I started using help waaaay to much for such a simple concept of a game (and it is, and there's not wrong with it), I realized it's not for me; It became more of a chore. _childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: First off this game looks really nice! You use the 5 sides of the box, along with optical illusions to solve puzzle and continue the "story"? Most puzzles flew over my head as many answers did not present themselves as clearly obvious. Thank god that there was a hint feature that would show after a few minutes have passed and even gives you an option to watch a video that shows you the answer outright. If anything I found this game to be quite stressful as I wasn't able to find the correct solution most of the time, especially when the answer involved more than just connecting objects across the sides of the box.Overall I'd probably recommend this game for people who enjoy puzzle games that make them think outside the box (literally). If you are here just for the visuals, the hint feature is there to make the journey more bearable. Still consider a good game despite my lack of ability to solve most puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: It's really a good. Its graphics is clean but rich. It looks more vibrant than the Monument Valleys but more charming than the Room series. It's a very well designed 3D game based on visual illusions. I would say it's the best game I've played so far in this topic, because I just realized that it comprises a complete and coherent story. It's not like other games that let you run away from scenes to scenes with no reasons. Every scene in this "cage" is telling a story and it's very fascinating! Definitely recommend to every one!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: is a captivating and imaginative puzzle game that will transport you to a world of floating islands and mesmerizing music.The visually stunning graphics and unique concept make it a truly immersive experience. For a keen eye, game length is shortish. That said the  is a must-play for anyone looking for a delightful and thought-provoking gaming adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 95% great, 5% meh.The perspective puzzles are mostly really interesting, but a few of the solutions feel really unintuitive. Not many, just a couple. Also the game sometimes tries to rush you to the next stage by providing hints even when you haven't explored all the options yet.The story is mostly understated and nice, though there are a couple heavy-handed parts that kinda clash with the whole subtle "varying perspective" theme. Again though, mostly great. If you think you will enjoy this game, you probably will and I recommend you play it. If you're not a fan of "arty games" you will probably find it pretentious and if you're not a fan of perspective-based puzzles you'll probably get sick of it pretty quickly. Still though, all I'm really saying is this game kind of wears its identity on its sleeve, if you think you like it you probably will and if you think you won't you probably won't.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: The game has nice and effective, low textured visuals with an interesting twist found in overlapping spaces around a cube, as well as relaxing music. Most of the puzzles consist on aligning objects from different areas shown on every visible side of the cube, but it manages to push the concept further at times, having the player manipulate objects in the right order, or aligning more than 2 spaces together at once, for instance.It is not very long (easily doable for the first time, without a guide, in more or less 3 hours), nor too challenging, though you are expected, as in most puzzle games, to work a bit at times for a solution. If lost, pressing space highlights which objects should be aligned together next, and in the worst case scenarios, there are additional hints in the menu (never needed them personally). The story can be a tad vague, especially if you are not trying to find the hidden images, yet it remains powerful and while it might not seem like so at first glance, every single area serves a purpose within the narrative. Just brilliant!9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a puzzle game that is both challenging and visually stunning. The game involves rotating a cube that is made up of different objects, each with a unique theme and story. The aim is to manipulate the cube so that the objects fit together to reveal a hidden image.The graphics are beautifully designed, with each level having its own color scheme and style. The music and sound effects are also well done, creating an immersive experience that draws you into the game.The puzzles themselves are challenging and require careful consideration of each object's orientation and placement. The game does a good job of introducing new mechanics and ideas as you progress, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging.Overall, Moncage is a fantastic game for puzzle lovers who enjoy a visually stunning and immersive experience. It's a game that will keep you entertained for hours and leave you wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, gorgeous puzzle game with solid themes and music throughout.   Some of the visual transitions are simply stunning, and quite a few of the puzzles make you feel smart.Some of them are a bit too precise for my liking for a perspective puzzle game, though, as some times I immediately got the solution, only for the perspective snapping to not kick in and make me think that wasn't the correct answer.   Thankfully, the hint system is nice and even shows video of the solution if you get to those moments, but I would prefer the snapping to be a bit more generous in some of the puzzles (Lighthouse : [  general, a high recommend if you can get it between 7 to 12 bucks, as completing all the achievements took me about three hours, and if you like games like this I would recommend Gorogoa as well, which also is about connecting perspectives, albeit in a much less finicky fashion since it is a 2D game.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Gorogoa before and are in search of a game that can scratch the same itch... Well, you are in luck! Cause Moncage does exactly that! The story in Moncage is nothing to write home about, but is quickly obscured by cleverly designed puzzles (that frankly makes you think outside the box, rather than in it). A must have for a puzzle fanatic!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- Simple shapes and flat colors makes it easy to digest what is in the environments, and allows for some complex puzzles where shapes as well as color have to match.- While playing, it's easy to forget that you are looking though the sides of the cube, because everything is in 3D inside the cube. I also like how all photos you find then appear on the wall outside the cube.- The hint system is excellent ... and nobody had to write a guide or include their stupid YouTube playthrough in the community section because the devs included those things in-game.Neutral.- The more there is on the screen for potential solutions, the more tedious the game gets. It's mostly obvious what to do because the relevant objects' shapes are unique, but for some puzzles, it's just a matter of constantly pressing space to highlight the puzzle items and then trying all possible combinations (of which there are sometimes too many because the environments can change). The best parts are when the edges of the cube get used (with 3 sides of the cube contributing an item).- A story is told through the environments and the photos, but it didn't grab me because I was too focused on the puzzles.- The game can be controlled with only a mouse, and so it can be very relaxing to play e.g. laid back in the chair while watching some videos. But, it would be nice if I could re-bind some actions so I can play the game without the spacebar and without double-clicking to zoom out (which felt weird).Negatives:- There is no way to restart a section or just reset to the start of the game. So, if you think you missed a photo, you have to complete the game and start over.  It resets the game completely as if you have never played the game. This is especially bad, because there are things that can only be gotten on the second (consecutive) playthrough (without pressing the button).- All achievements are hidden and some of them are for very stupid things, like if you solve a puzzle the wrong way.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a puzzle game that unfortunately didn't live up to my expectations. Despite having played many puzzle games, I found this one to be difficult to understand and often confusing. The gameplay felt slow and boring, and I struggled to find enjoyment in it. While the game's visual style is interesting, it wasn't enough to make up for the lackluster gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: A story focused puzzler where you connect different parts of a cube to move the plot forwards. The story is told through the scenes in the cube and the movement encourages you to absorb the story through it which is pretty cool. The scenes mostly connect well but there are a few that seem like they exist just for the puzzles. The puzzles themselves make sense and if you’re a moron like me and missed obvious things, there is a great hint system. Overall, a decent puzzler with a decent story.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a fantastic puzzle game with innovative cube model mechanics that kept me engaged throughout my playtime. The interactive nature of the puzzles added an extra layer of depth and challenge to the gameplay, making for a truly enjoyable experience. I would highly recommend Moncage to fans of puzzle games.Game play: 10Graphics: 8Value: Buy on sale

_childDocuments_.review: I love the cube idea, and the perspective view inside the scene(s) via its faces is really intriguing, The animations are really nice and continue seamlessly across perspectives, i.e. faces of the cube.I like the graphics approach so much that I took too visual an attempt at solving the puzzles. Initially I used the space bar (clue highlighting) too much. Don't make that mistake. Instead try to understand the scene and focus more on the mechanics of the objects in the scene involved, and look for potential interactions/links.I haven't finished the game yet, but even with others indicating it can be played through in a relatively short time period, I'm absolutely happy with what I got for my money. I would recommend that game to anyone who is into that genre.

For example,  I got a contradictory situation, Still a chill puzzle game but I would have taken the game on smartphone for a better experience imo. Also doesn't worth 10 euros on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game back in April. I was having an awful night, one of those where you question every decision that's gotten you to this point, and had soft songs on Spotify shuffle when the title track for this game showed up. For some reason it stood out to me, enough to go back and play it again...and again. Something in the album cover spoke to me as well, and after finding the game itself I went "screw it" and bought it that same night, because hey, I needed a distraction. What I got was a kind of beauty that couldn't have had a better time and place than right there. The simple yet gorgeous visuals coupled with the incredible soundtrack made me feel existential in the best way possible. I was completely immersed, and got through a full run through of the game that same night, and by the time I was done, I had felt more at peace than I thought possible the previous evening, and that effect hung around for another month (not all because of this game, but it was the spark.) It's short, yes, but that short length left me satisfied, which I desperately needed then. On some level this game saved me that night, and I'll always remember it for that.(Also the title track still makes me feel how it did when I first listened to it, props to Berlinist for making this haunting beauty)

_childDocuments_.review: Alright THAT IS THE MOST BEAUTIFUL GAME I HAVE EVER PLAYED.I don't have words to explain how amazing this game is. So awesome how they got a really beautiful story, inside a puzzle game.The story is amazing, the music is awesome, game play is fantastic. I would buy it again and again.There is a surprise once you finish the game. That was a plot twist for me

_childDocuments_.review: Saw it and remembered a demo on Youtube from a while ago so I picked it up.  -I do wish it was longer-But it was exactly what I needed for a little chill time last night and this morning.  Lots of environmental variation that all seems to have had a lot of thought/design put into it, doesn't stick to "this is the underwater section so you need to complete 20 puzzles in this section and learn this mechanic before we move on to the space section" but everything does have a cohesive theme to create a nice sense of unity.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap it's phenomenal. One of those games that completely envelopes you as every element works together.This is a point-and-click style game with a puzzle mechanic reminiscent of Goragoa's sliding blocks, but in 3D. It's gorgeous, perfectly polished, and so so satisfying. The sound design and soundtrack are seamlessly blended with the gameplay, and the flat-shaded art style lends itself so well to the core idea.Oh and there's a story. A simple and down-to-earth but beautifully told story about life and change and taking the good with the bad. This game would've been 10/10 without it so that added level shows how much love was put into every part of this experience.The only weakness is it's hint system (which you can generally ignore although you probably can't avoid using the "focus" mode) and the fact that it's fairly short, shorter even than Goragoa was. It does have collectibles to go back and find if that's your thing.Overall: dopamine / 10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely beautiful game. Its puzzle mechanics are really clever and something I have never seen before, they will leave you bamboozled at times but that's half the fun. Its music takes you on a journey and compliments its story throughout the entire game. Its worth every dollar and I urge you to play it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Decent ~2 hour experience and about 4 hours to get all achievements with guides. The puzzles aren't too difficult and can be brute force enough by rotating the cube and finding whatever matches. There were some puzzles that required slightly further thinking than that which was a nice surprise. If you do get stuck, the hint system is very well done. It gives you three gradual hints and then a video walkthrough right in the game. $14.99 is a bit steep for what it offers, but I enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool puzzle game. It is similar to Gorogoa if you've played that. You have to move the cube to an angle where something on one face matches something another face and changes something or creates something new.. Sometimes you focus in and change something and when you back out the scene has changed. Some of it was pretty hard and I had to use a few hints. It's all logical though. You may spend twenty minutes stumped, but when you get it it makes you feel smart.  It's hard to explain, but it's a cool game with cool art. A little short, but worth it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful perspective-based puzzle game that's backed by some lovely music and has an unexpectedly deep story scattered across its many scenes. The only notable nitpick I can think of is that the game’s hint system was often a little too eager to help. Even so, those hints were much appreciated during Moncage’s more obtuse puzzles. There’s much more to Moncage than a series of visual riddles within comfortable low-poly environments, and these delightfully designed dioramas as well as their collective narrative are certainly worthy of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Took a bit over two hours. My brain hurt itself in confusion while trying to comprehend its own stupidity. Puzzles are interesting and hint system is *very fair*, got slightly stuck on some confusing places (I knew what I had to do but not know how). Not too challenging, not too long, quality way above quantity, can only 100% recommend. Check out Gorogoa for similar game.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric deeper meaning puzzle game with a wonderful concept of connection concerning a cube. The game itself only takes about 45 minutes to an hour to complete, which is fair considering it's a rather short puzzle game. Most of the achievements you can get on your first playthrough, though you wouldn't know since they're all kept secret. After appreciating its message and narrative I aggravatingly had to play through the game about 6-7 times. I kept missing one single thing and then had to repeat the entire game to unlock it, then repeat the game once again to unlock more things only to miss again a single thing and repeat the cycle. I wish there was a chapter select of some sort to ease that process. The only other issue I have with the game is my playtime policy. If I can get about twice the price in time played I'm content. For a 15$ game I got only 4 hours out of the whole thing. It's acceptable considering it's a puzzle game, but I think 15$ is excessive. Mad props to the relatively small production team and I cackled when I saw a special thanks message to Bennet Foddy, but I don't think it's worth 15 dollars. Maybe 8$ or 10$ because it's artistic and more narrative driven.I will still recommend this game but perhaps buy it on a discount and keep your mind open.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique Puzzlegames i've played in a long, long while.The whole game revolves around a single cube you can spin around, each face of the cube acting like a window into a different 3-dimensional space. Your task is to find objects in multiple faces of the cube that, if your viewpoint is angled just right, will connect and be able to interact with each other.While i got stuck on some puzzles for a little while, it was never frustrating, instead it was still very engaging, spinning the cube around and around, angling it this way or that, trying to find items that might connect.Also, the game has a great tip-mechanic, where at any given point you can reveal one of 3 tips for a puzzle that get increasingly more direct in pointing you toward the solution, which is something i wish more puzzle games had.The story is told completely through the different scenes that unfold on each of the cube's faces and little collectible photos - to put it simply, it tells the story of a family and what war will do to people and the land.Moncage is a rather short game, clocking in at roughly 2-3 hours for a playthrough, though completionists will want to do a second one on top, but this is exactly the right kind of length for a game like this. Short and sweet.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, if rather hard.  There appears to be no real story line, although there apparently is a trajectory supported by the pictures that you optionally can pick up.  It's a pretty creative puzzle-like game, with your progress depending on combining elements from different screens in less than obvious ways.  The mechanism is somewhat similar to that used by Gorogoa, only the screens are arranged in three dimensions.  That is, the main action consists of exploring the items in a room or screen, zooming in or out, and finding hidden connections between objects or screens.  Once you've made a connection, there is a video sequence that takes you on to another room for exploration.  While we're on the subject of zooming in and zooming out,  I have to say that as you progress inward through a couple of layers, you may run into slow to nonexistent game response to your mouse.  I've found this to be true of a number of games that require zooming with the mouse.  And it's not just one particular mouse or one particular computer that is the problem.  "Double-click, you say?  Ha, you can just wait a while until I decide to respond--or not!"  Back to the action: as I say, the game does seem rather hard, but there is a hint system which essentially reveals all if you're patient, and sometimes if you review the video till you're exhausted, trying to figure out what they're doing that you're NOT doing.  There were several moves from one location to the lighthouse and back where very small details in the display have to be lined up before they will work, and then ONLY if you have switched, and switched back, and switched back yet again between Day and Night modes.  Sequences like these are far more annoying than fun.  I've paused the game for now over my last episode of frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the ROOMs, you will like this one. Easier but more cute and story rich. However... I'm not a fun of infinity. *Spoiler: at the end of the story , it loops back to the first scene. I thought it may reveal some new story. Unfortunately it's just for collectors. A little waste of another hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple and unique game that uses the visual components creatively. It was quite enjoyable and frustrating at the same time because it may be confusing (and you end up using several hints) but once the image clicks it's really satisfying. The game was really short so perhaps get it on discount, but its a great experience overall. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is a beautifully executed game with the type of puzzles which can frustrate at first, but when resolved can leave you in appreciation of the vision required to be able to craft such clever optical trickery.The odd paradox i find myself in is, it probably took me longer than it should have to complete the experience (even with the default setting of highlighting necessary components) but somehow the game still felt short. Not too short, but maybe the 'that must be hard to keep creating innovative puzzles' kind of short.All in all though, as a puzzle game fan, the vibes of Gorogoa are strong and the hook was there to the end, in fact, i had this game almost as a spare time filler. If i had 10 minutes here or there it was nice to come back and try again at a puzzle, i wish i still had that. I think with a few weeks passing, i may come back and turn off any highlighting/hints and enjoy the experience again.Thanks for the game, developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Moncage is an innovative perspective puzzle game, where you must link objects in different scenes across different sides of a cube to advance the story. The game itself is quite short, a lot of the time is spent looking for the correct objects to match. Thankfully you can highlight key objects in each scene. The art style is fantastic. The game is very similar to Gorogoa in terms of the key gameplay mechanic and the abstract nature of the story. Even the achievements are quite similar (both have a "first attempt / quick reaction time" achievement, as well as a "timed completion" achievement). Overall, a great, niche puzzler, but a tad pricey given its length.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cool game. It is so, so sweet. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for this kind of game, where the rules of reality are reshaped around a simple, yet elegant perceptual mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! The mechanic of solving puzzles with the use of perspective to merge to different places and affect the objects that are in them is really fun. The puzzles are not that hard once you get the hang of it. I loved the subtle storytelling that it's got going with the pictures and scenes, really liked the story. Definitely would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Moncage

_childDocuments_.review: Solve visual puzzles to discover scenes and photos that form a simple narrative. It will appeal to people who enjoy the genre. In my opinion it's actually a little too clever, which helps tell the story in an interesting way, but means that the puzzles are frequently quite obscure. In particular, there are times when you're supposed to be solving a particular "problem" but the scenes contain enough items that it's not really clear most of the time what the "problem" is. It seems that the developer recognized this, because the game has a very strong hint system, which includes highlighting the parts of the scene that are currently part of a puzzle, a set of text hints that become available on a timer and, once you've exhausted all of those, the ability to watch a video of the stage being solved. I would prefer not to have to rely on such an extensive hint system, but the game kind of does need it and at least having it there means you'll be able to finish the game without resorting to searching up solutions online. Overall, I'd say if this game looks like something you'd enjoy based on the promotional video, you'll probably like it, but you probably don't want to pay full price for it, since it's quite short and many of the puzzles are quite obscure.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited over a year and a half after the demo release for a game which I thought was just going to be a bunch of levels with different locations and items. What finally released was something 10X better, beautifully polished, and addictive.Moncage is an image POV manipulation game which takes place on up to 5 facets of a cube. Part of the game is point and click (interact and zoom), and part is alignment of adjacent cube sides (mouse movement). Instead of having levels, it's an ongoing game which unlocks new scenes and a storyline as the game progresses. It is not , but it is . Joining objects isn't 'part of this and part of that look like they form some other random object'. Instead, you most often have 2 or 3 pieces of similar looking  which either join or overlap to form a .There are 2 types of hints you can use: Highlighted objects which are used somewhere, and text clues. I used the highlights quite often, and the text clues twice. For achievement seekers, you will need multiple playthroughs. Not to worry though, as the 2nd (and 3rd) time around will be less than an hour of play.Similar games: Gorogoa, Superliminal, Looksley's Line Up

name: Re:Turn - One Way Trip
detailed_description: Re:Turn – One Way Trip tells the terrifying story of five college friends on a post-graduation vacation. This might be their last trip together before the adulthood swallows them whole. Unfortunately for them, a far more sinister force has found them and hungers for their souls. When Saki awakens in the middle of the night to find that her friends have disappeared from their campsite, she is soon lured to an abandoned train. It stands silent, as if has been waiting for its final passenger to board. Waiting for her. As Saki searches the train for her friends, the barrier between the past and the present starts to dissolve. Otherworldly horrors confront Saki as she begins to learn the train’s deadly secrets. Re:Turn—One Way Trip is a tale of unrequited love—and unrelenting terror! FEATURES : * Intricate horror story * 2 Playable Characters * Side-scrolling 2D with unique pixel art * Optional VHS render mode giving an authentic retro visual experience * Original Art and Assets * Carefully composed music specifically for each situation of the game * Original Sound Track * Minimalist interface so your focus never wavers from the experience * Supernatural elements * Challenging puzzles * Past & Present world immersive storytelling
