_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game - it had a great premise and the first half of the game was really well done. Unfortunately, the issues I found with the story and gameplay really hampered my enjoyment of the game, leaving me feeling extremely disappointed.The story is poorly told and paced, leaving far more questions than answers. Initially, the first half really pulled me in when one of Saki's friends vanished and she finds herself in the past where no one can see her. I thought that the story would evolve more around Saki trying to work and communicate with Eiji to solve puzzles and the mystery of the train, but it never really did. It ends up being more about Saki trying to find her friends and sometimes gets transported into the past for some reason (which is never really explained), which I found to be disappointing. The story doesn't really tie together at the end, leaving too many unanswered questions and an unsatisfying and anticlimactic conclusion. The characters are also fairly....lackluster. You never really get to spend enough time with anyone to build a connection or learn more of who they are, which makes what is supposed to be emotional scenes ring hollow. It does feel like the story is trying to set up a sequel by leaving so many questions unanswered, but the story is plotted and told so poorly and the characters too forgettable to really make a sequel worthwhile. The controls are frustrating as well. I played with a controller and I noticed that navigating felt...weird. It's very hard to explain, but it feels like Saki/Eiji's trajectory hard-stops whenever you enter a new room. For example, if you keep holding the control stick to the right and go through a door, in the next room Saki/Eiji will remain stock still even if you are still pushing the control stick. Instead, to resume moving, you have to release it and push right again to resume movement. This was annoying overall, but EXTREMELY frustrating during the token chase scenes - I died far too many times simply because I could not get Saki to respond right away, instead staring there stupidly looking at the monster that was clearly going to kill her. I also dislike that for the first chunk of the game, you can't run and can only walk....but you get the ability to run halfway through. I honestly don't know why you couldn't just run at the start. It's better than games like "Until Dawn" that don't even give you the option to run, but still - just give the player the ability to run at the start. There was no need to keep the run mechanic from the player for most of the gameThe game also doesn't have puzzles, but rather is a giant, nearly five-hour long fetch quest. The few puzzles the game does have are alright at best, and are repeated over and over with little variety. None of these puzzles are interesting enough to warrant repeating, and some are back to back. You also don't get much instruction or clues as to what you need to do next (your journal is a joke as it only documents certain items you collect, not tasks or anything), so if you're wandering around aimlessly looking for an item and are confused as to what else you need to do, good luck because the game isn't going to repeat itself. Overall, I feel that this game had a lot of great potential, but was poorly executed. It shines in the first half, but then crashes and burns (hard) in the second. I can see the skeleton of a great story and an interesting game mechanics, but it sadly fell short. It the game was longer and allowed the character to develop more, the story to develop more, and included more interesting puzzles, this could have been a great game. Unfortunately, as it is, I can't recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Re:Turn - One Way Trip

_childDocuments_.review: - Its price: with a duration of 4-5 hours the first game is not bad at all. We also have some moments where our choices will ‘mark’ the story in one way or another, but only in appearance, not in result: watching those scenes and wanting to get all the achievements can encourage replayability.- It has a very nice pixel art style.- Its story is very interesting, and especially at the beginning it will hook us.- Its biggest drawback is the lack of variety of scenarios that it has, which we repeat over and over again to get new clues or solve puzzles.- It's too repetitive: when we're halfway through the game we'll be tired of going from one place to another constantly: just because we've been in a room doesn't mean that later on there won't be something useful in it, which makes it tedious.- Its puzzles are too simple, with the exception of the two endings, which are overcomplicated compared to the rest of the game.- The music doesn't really stand out, although it accompanies the game well.- The ending is somewhat open-ended, and leaves a couple of important unknowns unresolved.We find ourselves before a game that mixes in a somewhat clumsy way the genre of interactive adventure with that of puzzles, with a very well handled touch of Japanese horror. It has a very nice pixel art style, mixed with illustrations in the form of ‘cinematics’, which do their job, with a personal and interesting artwork. The adventure has a lateral development in 2D, and its story mixes horror and thriller in a remarkable way. Unfortunately, as we progress through the game and get answers, it will seem to be deflating, and it doesn't bring out the full potential of the main characters, although ironically it does stage the supporting characters very well. Its gameplay is based on going through the scenarios in a more or less guided way (we will not be able to access certain areas unless we have solved the situations where we are), and use the objects or clues that we find in puzzles so logical that most of them are too simple.- 6/10.It's a sincere game, that doesn't aspire to more than what it can give; in a way it's a pity, because taking a little more care of certain details would have made it much more interesting (we end up very tired because of the repetitive mechanics). Still, highly recommended thanks to its low price: if you find it on sale, and you like games of this style, don't let it pass you by.

_childDocuments_.review: is an indie team that put out a demo for Re:Turn back in June for the Summer Game Festival (seriously so helpful and eventful) and I thought it was on the right track~ At least in its atmosphere and train setting- which btw we don't seem to get a lot of in horror; excluding RE0 and a few other sleeper titles from 2019-20. As great as demos go and I get that they're only placeholders that may not be in the final game, but I want to point out the demo was a far cry (we'll return to this later on)!! So, all aboard?    Saki and her college friends are about to graduate soon. They have a wilderness excursion to ponder over the end of their school lives and future relations. That is until a quarrel ensues, suspicion thrown followed by the appearance of a train well out of nowhere. Now, where will this take them? 2D side-scroller that doesn't take much to learn; you move, gather key items and unlock things. Simple right- relax, enjoy the view and partake in the occasional puzzles having both creepy Japanese folklore and childlike charm involving dolls, colored drawings among other things. This is where the in-game notebook comes in handy but also grab a pen-paper or flip out that smartphone because they could test whether you're smarter than a 5th grader. As of a recent change, you can run from the get-go~ The plot is extremely pulled off! It touches on university anxieties and soul-searching *snorts* which ngl really stuck... Definitely for lovers in mind and to appreciate, but it evokes a sense of compassion nonetheless. The hardships of love and what could keep them apart; circumstances sometimes outside the couple's control. What's also invigorating is the duality in the storyline because you may think the past is done and over with but here it's very much still kicking. Of course, the characters also standout! Most notably Saki whose empathy is strong but is only human in that she doubts herself. She along with the train inhabitants (some never named) definitely carried the drama to its conclusion! I have been drawn to more pixel arts recently, this is no different~ They get the job done and looks delightfully pleasing. You'll spend a lot of time in the train so opening up its areas gradually and seeing a different side to it entirely would make up for more than a passing interest. There are also what I call 'breathing moments' which are CGs but shows their conviction and body language. Though fewer in number, I live for these!! The complete piano composition is to die for~~Truthfully, the horror isn't always very obvious (until I've had my way bwahaha). Yeah, I also wanted that "horror" genre to be removed but then I got to thinking. It's never expositioned, but the events that occurred from the beginning were . I know it sounds obvious but that's because it's made out to be "coincidence". What's even more chilling is that connection the with our physical environment. The train is an object of tragic history yet its negative emotions of heartache, misunderstanding stay on affecting others, worst being similar-minded individuals. Some puzzles bear meanings that go beyond the surface level- the reflections segment require more understanding of the actual Japanese folklore masks to truly appreciate them. Similarly for saving progress, why a phone? Makes you wonder~Now to interpret the "one-way trip" metaphor! Firstly, growing up and the responsibilities along with it. The characters expressing their disdain and fret about what's next, but some look forward to it (or are they?). Number two (yuck) is the relation to death.  Last but not least, time being irreversible. Ultimately linear that it moves forward but it can still be warped by emotions and feelings. There's a black hole in game design and objectives. Picture you're in the first few chapters, can only walk jauntily to get a key item here and then magically another appears all the way on the other side. It can be pretty frustrating, because this occurs many, many times! The logic goes "I wasn't looking for this" or "this should reveal new objects" but mhmm... Some oversights with characters can be way off. Kanae reacts to the terrible sights witnessed thus far adding to her personality. But other partners paired up don't really, not as much. Or how Yuuta's claustrophic but then goes with you in cramped restrooms. Minor thing is the first venture of the luxury ride; decorative doors (no description whatsoever) and you're expected to just walk to the end of both carriages. Next thing ya know- they can be interacted with. It's eating away at me because this is the only instance it haPPpPpe-The underwhelming scares owes much to the demo which portray a wholly different experience. Because that one was more intense in pace and atmosphere.. Even bringing a scripted chase much earlier ahead of chapters. I get demos are not accurate representations but that was a low blow. The end product turns out to be stuck in gear one for way longer than it needs to. Deaths also are heavily scripted with QTE sequences... The big bad beastie could have been omitted altogether. Parting thoughts? First, the train setting which is dope af but it also means you'd be confined primarily to its interiors and you'd see much of what it has to offer by chapter 8. But hey, it's 10 bucks sooo~ May I also say while the story started off excellently, I'm hurt by the abrupt ending but that's probably because we've been conditioned to want and expect wholesome ones. It actually makes more sense some things just don't have resolution, at least not in our eyes.In short, Re:Turn was a commendable 2D sidescroller with much emphasis on interesting themed-puzzles and one-track attention to a well-crafted story. Romanticizing the notion of love transcending all barriers and dimensions, perhaps much too literally that overtakes the horror elements at times. Furthermore, I was captivated by the overall pixel art and dynamic CG stills, giving a lasting impression that much like the train- also brought the atmosphere to life. As with all tube rides, the scheduling isn't always as promised and no less true here. Held back further by the need to travel back-forth for its fetching but still . Thus why the game design here is largely at fault, sending the game into...who knows. Beyond some initial unsettling, cliched scares in the beginning the gears do shift into a full on romantic mystery (I know!) for the remainder of the touchingly nostalgic 4 to 5 hour journey. Now THAT'S a fitting price for a train ticket!

_childDocuments_.review: Anime melodrama that is also a never-ending fetch-quest that is also a back-and-forth central.  There are plenty of better things to play in a similar vein, so you might want to look for those first. Some thoughts:-	I gave it a try for the horror that was (as I see now) greatly upsold by the now nonexistent demo. While there are some horror elements here, and it is an underlying basis for the game, what you’ll get is an over-the-top drama with a bunch of cheap theatrics that all but erase anything even remotely spooky with its vapidity.-	If we’re talking soap opera of a story – it also takes a certain talent to write it in such way that it will capture the heart of an audience or, at the very least, touch a player in at least the faintest way, and this aint’t it. We spend way too little time with the characters to relate to them or learn about them in a meaningful way, so when they express some big emotions or make heartfelt proclamations – it rings hollow and has a degree of cringe to it.-	The story itself is a straight train track that allows for no player’s agency and will have you chasing a grocery list of items 95% of the time. Even that list can’t be done out of order as procuring an item usually triggers having access to another one, so if you thought – you can get those at your own pace – you’re out of luck. The other 5% is one easy, recycled puzzle, and one puzzle that had the potential to be decent but was ruined by an enormous amount of back-and-forth.-	Speaking of which – that’s what you’ll be doing most of the time in this game. Going back and going forth. The game takes place on a train in two different time periods, so we have 6-7 train cars available in both – a shiny new version, and a decrepit one. And that is what will happen for the majority of about 5 hours it takes to complete this – you’ll walk to one end of the train to pick up an item, so you can walk to the other end of the train to use it, so you can walk to the other end of the train to get a little scene, so you can walk to the other end of the train for a newly open dialogue option, so you can walk to the other end of the train…. You get the point. You have to constantly double-check every single one of available locations, because new hotspots pop up there without any rhyme or reason (looking at you, toilet), but don’t worry – at least they tend to pop up on the different sides of the train – so your journey feels truly fulfilling.-	As far as fulfillment goes – the game ends in the most anticlimactic, brisk manner, and, apparently, developers say that all the questions will be answered in part two. I, however, think that there’s a difference between needing a sequel to expand on, deep dive into, tie up certain things or give answers to side stories/secondary questions, or maybe start another leg of the journey… and needing it to simply finish the core story. Hastily wrapping it up and promising sequel to answer main questions isn’t how you make a great impression with the first game when you’re planning to make more parts to it.I was debating whether this game is a genuine thumbs down for me or if I’m simply not the right audience for it (not being a fan of anime that often tends to go for angst-ridden plots), but then I ended up thinking that issues underlined above wouldn’t work well in any game, regardless of the style’s penchant for melodramatic narration. After all, there are plenty of deep, meaningful titles that are made in that genre, and I don’t have to like them to see that. Here, however, you get a rushed attempt to combine a horror element together with almost VN-like convoluted storyline, together with time swap plot twists, together with side-scrolling adventure (that probably should have had more/better puzzles) - and not quite succeeding on any level. No doubt, developers’ heart was in the right place, but it should have culminated in focusing on all the parts separately and making them excellent instead of sending it out to the world as is – a promise of a good thing, but a hurriedly wrapped package full of brochures that good thing is yet to come (in the next package!) in reality.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this was a bit difficult to decide how I felt about this game. At it's core, it's a side scrolling pixel puzzle visual novel. It does some of these elements well, but there's some moments where the pacing is killed and the puzzles seem a bit ridiculous as well as some odd design choices. I'll do my best to be concise, here goes!Pros: The art style for both the pixel and the characters is just great. There's light animations and varied expressions to make the characters feel like they have more personality to them. The story starts off a little weak, gets really interesting in the middle, but it does fall flat in the end. More on that (spoiler free)Cons: The beginning of the game was a bit of a slow start. The dialogue was a little cringe, but it was kind of whatever. There's more pacing issues where if you miss a single detail, you could be searching the train for a long time. You can also search the same thing multiple times, but it has different results based on where you're at in the story. Like you can search a cabinet and it's empty, but then you get a clue that something might be there, so if you search it then, you'll find something. Not the end of the world, but just slightly annoying. The puzzles for this game are kind of obnoxious. Most of them are 100% super straight forward, but towards the end there's a couple where I'm still scratching my head where I think they could've been design a bit better as they rely on children's drawings and the details kind of get lost in them. This isn't really a CON, but more of a note, this game isn't really scary. It's creepy, it's dark, but it's not really scary. I don't think there was a jumpscare in it. Just worth noting in case you were looking for something to get the heart pumping!Also this being a 2d side scroller, yes you will run all the way right to run all the way left, which then means you have to run all the way right again. This should be fairly obvious, but it does get to be a bit obnoxious when it's several screens of travel back and forth. I did experience a chase sequence where I died doing something stupid. My bad. But when the game reloaded, it had some dialogue and when the dialogue ended, I was immediately killed because the Saki (the player) didn't move despite holding down a direction. Turns out, you have to press it at just the right time after the dialogue. Not too soon otherwise she doesn't move, but not too late other wise you're too slow to make it to the next screen. That was incredibly annoying to deal with. Finally the story. No spoilers, but that's where this game shined really well for awhile...until eventually it just kinda fell flat. The game just kind of ends. You have a couple of questions, but the game just packs it in and says "that's basically it" I felt a little robbed after the last quarter of the game was a let down and really I just finished it to finish it since I was so close to the end. TLDR; Great art, mostly solid story, confusing puzzles, nonsensical logic, abrupt ending. This game is decent, but it ends on a low note.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty solid and engaging adventure game about a group of friends who run into a mysterious broken down train in the middle of the woods. It's got a horror vibe without actually being all that scary through most of the game. There are a few jump scares and other surprise scares, but generally the game doesn't really ratchet up the tension or make you feel nervous or creeped out. But it's got a generally good atmosphere and story. The art style and music are really solid. The animation is limited by the format but generally fine. It has some of the usual adventure game problems of not being sure what to do because you don't know where to find an item or where to use an item, which sometimes leads to just going from hot spot to hot spot, searching and trying each item in turn. Sometimes it can be rather tedious to progress but mostly it's not all that bad. Overall it's a pretty good game which will only take you 5-10 hours to beat depending on if or how much you get stuck or if you attempt to all the achievements. Despite not being anywhere near as scary as I'd hoped, it was still engaging and interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Curator: Re:turn One way trip is a 2D Side Scrolling puzzle game, releasing October 14th from the developers from Red Ego Games. You play as Saki who is out on a camping trip with her friends, until, (shocker here), in the middle of the night every one disappears. Saki walks through the wood looking for her friends till she falls upon an old train. Thinking her friends may be in the train she goes to investigate. Lone and behold her friends are there and they all return to the camp happy and safe. Well except the doors are locked and there are ghost haunting the train and the train keeps teleporting Saki back to the past. So Saki must investigate why the train is there and haunted while trying to save her friends and survive an unspeakable evil hellbent on avenging unrequited love.  Re:Turn in all honesty labels its self as a horror game but I would really class this as a suspense, puzzle game. There was nothing really scary about it, more of just the tension and atmosphere that’s in the game can keep you on edge. No jump scares nor things that will make you ♥♥♥♥ you pants, it may have more to do with the symbolism in the game to scare people, a lot of Japanese mask and what I would imagine are bad omens, are in the game that would scare an audience who is families with the myths or legends . I do now some of the mask and references they are making, but I don’t have them vividly in my mind like someone who would have grown up with them. But there are some outstanding things in this game that still make it great, One big one is the Story its self. Its well flushed out and well written, even for being localized I due believe. I already gave you the sarcastic synopsis of the game and that’s where I'm going to leave it because the story is the main focus and I’m not going to ruin that for you.  Another is the Art and Sound design, The sound track and ambit noises that are in this game are solid, giving that suspense and tension that you will feel in the game. The art work on the other hand is amazing hand drawn elements place in the game that give great detail and giving some of the spooks along the way, also with the nice vibrant pixel art with a nice smooth fluid animation its candy to the eyes. My biggest thing I loved about this game was the puzzles some of the puzzles had me grabbing a pin and paper so I could remember thing I needed to do, others kind of hidden in plain sight till you have the,   ah ha moment and it all falls in place, and some cryptic puzzles that I don’t think I solved and may have to go back and try again. They took the time for there puzzles and wanted this to be a key feature in the game, and you can tell. And in all honest I can’t think of any negatives for this game its pretty solid, I think if anything to complain about, it’s the fetch quest you have to do. Walking from one side of the train to the other can be annoying at time, but really didn’t detract from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Re:Turn is an interesting game - Its a great concept with compelling pixel art along with a pretty compelling story but let down by some repetitive gameplay and somewhat abrupt ending.Pros - Story is compelling and keeps you engaged through its around 4-5 hour runtime.Pixel art is great helping to create a creepy atmosphere.The characters were believable with realistic reactions to the situation along with well written (If a bit cringy) dialogue with some nice touches such as characters commenting on things that Saki has already encountered in later chapters.The soundtrack is suitably creepy and well composed.Neutral -The puzzles are simple but fun however some of them you can get stuck on if your not paying close attention to the dialogue.Cons - The ending felt a bit abrupt and left a few plotholes and unanswered questions.The gameplay had too much backtracking along with the odd choice of not being able to run until half way through the game which made the backtracking feel a lot more tedious and making the game feel repetitive near the end.No replayability (except for one alternative ending)In conclusion - The game is not half bad and i would recommend playing it as its an enjoyable experience if a bit short and frustrating at times.If the devs are reading this: You did a good job with this and i cant wait to see what you come out with in the future (Hopefully something a bit more creepy and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up in my opinion)

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a super over the top scary horror game, turn back now this is not it, but that's not to say it's a bad experience. Re:Turn One Way Trip is an interesting game. Without giving away too much, it starts off with a fairly generic setup, but then quickly takes a turn into strange territory. The story is nice, and I found myself invested in the characters despite the games somewhat short 5 or so hour playtime, but my main gripe is the ending and the pacing. The ending just sort of happens, it didn't really feel like it was building towards a finale and then boom, roll credits. It was disheartening, but I still enjoyed the main body of the story. The game can definitely drag at times though.The game's presentation is it's greatest strength. It's like a mix between RPG Maker horror and visual novels. The pixel art for the characters and the environment are great. I also appreciate how the game's lighting is dark but not too dark, there are a lot of horror games that just make you not see anything. Re:Turn also uses it's relatively small amount of tools pretty well, the whole game takes place in one location, but I didn't find myself getting annoyed with it, and was enjoying exploring it. The game's sound design is also great, it builds the ambience and atmosphere well, I recommend following the instructions of playing with headphones.Finally there's the gameplay. It's mostly just finding objects, bringing said objects to a place, and solving riddles. They're fine for the most part, although near the end of the game some of them require some head gymnastics to solve. I was disappointed by the lack of danger in the gameplay, I really only got one game over.Re:Turn is by no means perfect, but I found it to be an overall enjoyable experience.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Re:Turn - One Way Trip is a good Horror, Adventure game. Okay what is the story.Saki and her four friends are on a camping trip, a last hurrah before they have to enter the adult world after college.But after a stupid argument everything goes to hell, her friends gone. But as Saki looks for them she discovers an old abandoned train, what Horrors will she find? All aboard for Pure Terror next stop evil.So what is there to like about the game? The pixel art style/graphics is very good; it's pretty detailed and nice to look at from the old broken old train.  Those picture cutscenes like when we first arrived at the train and see it for the first time are very good and nice to look at.The levels in the game were good to see and to explore as you go from car to car of this decrepit old train. The atmosphere in the game was good and spooky as you explore the train and seeing the detail they put into it.The game isn't scary per se but there were times where I jumped or some parts that were definitely uncomfortable.The music and sound effects were very good and it helped with the game's atmosphere. The story's pretty good it had some good, sad, creepy and some Sweet Moments in it. Though there are some plot holes/unanswered questions. But I heard that a sequel is going to be made that's going to fill them up.The characters in the game were interesting and cool; I really liked Saki especially that one moment where she's had enough of the train’s ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  And lastly the puzzles were pretty damn good they were hard but fair, except two puzzles.So what is there to dislike about the game? Well as you know if you go into a new room and you're still holding the walk button your character continues to walk or run. But in here it doesn't if you're still holding the walk button your character won't move you have to let go and then touch it again to let your character walk, that was just really annoying. Now that I have said all that, Re:Turn - One Way Trip is a good Horror, Adventure game. With very good pixel art style/graphics, a pretty good story despite some plot holes and a good spooky atmosphere.If you're looking for a pixel horror game with an interesting story and very good art this could be the game you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a side scrolling 2D Puzzle Adventure Horror Game, you play as a girl called Saki, you are apparently camping with some friends, and when you wake up in the middle of the night, your friends have disappeared, and you have to find out what the hell is going on.The controls are super simple and this is an easy to play game, this is not a platforming game as such, so you won't be jumping to avoid enemies etc, instead you will move around methodically, collecting items and trying to solve puzzles which then allow you to progress through the game.As you play the game, the action is mixed in with beautifully drawn cut scenes.As you move around you will see a magnifying glass icon appear if you are near to something that can be interacted with, that may be a child's drawing, or a knife, or all manner of items that you may need to continue the game. After some wondering around you will find an old abandoned train, and once you go inside, this is where the game really starts, and you will spend most of your time in the train.Since this is a horror game, despite the cute 2D graphics, there are adult elements here, and once in the train you will have to not only solve puzzles but also deal with suddenly finding yourself in a different time line, a time when the train is full of passengers and staff. So as you play you will move between the past and the present, all the while trying to find your missing friends as well as understand how the train came to be abandoned.The puzzles themselves aren't that hard and much of the time to progress you just need to walk back and forth looking for the magnifying glass icon to appear so you can examine an item. Some of the puzzles are a bit tricky, and one time I simply couldn't figure out how to open a lock, and I think I just got lucky in the end, instead of using any true puzzle solving skills.The GoodThe 2D pixel art graphics are perfectly fine, but the true star of the show is the sound track, it really does help build tension, I found playing with headphones on was the best option. The game will also easily run on pretty much any computer, so no worries about having a fancy graphics card.The BadThe game itself is relatively easy, but you will find yourself walking backwards and forwards a lot, not really achieving anything as you try to find the next clue, this can feel a bit tedious at times. There is also only one save point in the game, that is on the train. SummaryA simple game that does deliver some good horror elements. I score this game 7/10Originally published on

_childDocuments_.review: Simple looking old style adventure game with cliched horror plot and just OK pixel art graphics. There are some clever puzzles now and then,  but the gameplay is overall poorly designed. Even thought it is a horror story with some disturbing imagens, the cute-looking character avatars make the game somewhat less scary, and the cheap jump scares don`t quite manage to change that. The playable character is controlled by using the joystick or the keyboard WASD keys, but this style of direct control actually adds nothing to the gameplay.  In fact, the inventory and mechanic puzzles would look better in a point and click mouse driven adventure game. The joystick controls only manage to add tiresome backtracking and the ocasional irritating quick time events. The ending of the story unfortunately feels pretty rushed and lacks real conclusion. This is a regular looking game that could have been better.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty shameless that Green Man Gaming, a company that focuses on selling other`s peoples games as cheap as possible, would publish this overpriced short game. Almost 14$ CND for a game worth 3$ CND at most... you can easily beat it in 3-4 hours, and this is actually just part 1 of the game.It utterly fails as a "horror" game, because a)its sprite based and everything just looks cute b)half the game is set in a brightly lit train.  There is a few "creepy" moments, but definitely nothing that will make you jump on your seat. Its also laughable the devs list "2 Playable Characters" as a feature, because you play as another character for like a single short chapter, and he adds nothing that is not explained through the main character.The game is extremely repetitive, you will be walking left and right of the same few areas of the train for like 95% of the game, I was pretty exhausted by the time credits hit. Also puzzles are either brain-dead (ex interact with the right spot to grab item, then backtrack and use item somewhere else) or completely obscure. I also got stuck like 2 times cause the interact icon blended with the brightly lit sections of the game.The plot is also nonsensical, boring and not compelling at all in my opinion. You are jumping between 2 time periods either helping your boring friends, or some ghosts from the past with boring stories. Also its never explained why the main antagonist is so powerful, I am sure they will expand on this on part 2... but I wont be around for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing this on my Youtube channel, so if anyone is interested in seeing a sample of gameplay before buying, see the link at the end of the review. First, I'll provide my thoughts.This is a decent 2D side-scrolling horror, in which you play as a young woman named Saki. Out in the woods on a camping trip with several friends on a dark night, sinister things happen, the group gets separated, and Saki finds a derelict train lost in the wilderness. Cue the remainder of the game, with Saki struggling to find her friends, having flashbacks to how the train came to be lost, and encountering ghostly presences...Overall, I found Re:Turn - One Way Trip to be an enjoyable horror. I beat it in about 7 hours(ish), so it's not terribly long. However, I'm going to get my criticisms of the game out of the way first, as there are a couple of things that could put people off this title. Firstly, sometimes the gameplay can involve a fair bit of backtracking (especially in later parts of the game). Obviously, being a 2D side-scroller set on a train means there are only two directions you can go - left or right. Much of the game then involves finding clues and items, figuring out where said items need to go, and solving puzzles. So there will be times where you make your way to one end of the train, find a clue or an item, then have to backtrack to the other end of the train testing what you've picked up on anything you can interact with to see if it works. It is worth pointing out that this is not going to be everyone's tastes - particularly in the latter chapters of the game, by which time it can start to become a little tedious.Secondly, there were one or two puzzles (involving doors with chains and locks on them) that I did find very unclear, and as a result I had to look at a walkthrough. Looking back on them, I'm still not entirely sure how I was meant to figure out the solution to these particular puzzles.However, with those criticisms aside, I still felt there was a lot to enjoy in this game. The pixellated, RPG-maker style visuals lend the game some character, and the game does have some decent spooky moments. The flashback chapters, where Saki finds herself seeing back into the lives of the train and its passengers, make for some more relaxing segments after the grim darkness of the train in its derelict, haunted state. And there are plenty of interesting characters with their own little stories, which unfold as Saki attempts to figure out how to escape her supernatural predicament.On the whole, I'd recommend Re:Turn - One Way Trip. Just be aware that the gameplay may not be to your tastes if you aren't a fan of puzzle games that are likely to involve a fair amount of backtracking!

_childDocuments_.review: Re:Turn is a classic horror RPG adventure game that reminds me of horror classics such as The Crooked Man and Misao, but it chooses to ground itself in atmospheric, spooky horror rather than gross-out gore like you'd find in the Corpse Party series. This makes it a great entry for horror game fans, but also for those who are maybe more squeamish. Be sure to explore everything thoroughly and double back to locations if needed when you're completing quests or trying to solve puzzles--I've noticed that sometimes certain events won't be triggered when I expect them to be. While the whole "locked in a haunted area/structure" story may not seem that unique or interesting, Re:Turn manages to keep the concept fresh with its engaging cast of characters and gorgeous, stunning visuals. Although I haven't finished the game as of yet, I'm definitely looking forward to seeing this through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game left me feeling cold.I'll try to keep spoilers light but it's hard to discuss this game without going into some of them.First off, pixel art is tricky to do horror with. The game has a few decent jumpscares but that's pretty much where the horror taps out.The puzzles are hard and in some cases borderline nonsensical. What I mean is that, even once I had looked up the solution in some cases I still didn't understand how one or two puzzles worked.One (the draw puzzle) in particular was awful due to a terrible interface design. You're seeing a drawing of 'dolls' with associated numbers. One of the dolls has a clear "three" written on it which will confuse you terribly until you realize that it's not a three, it's just part of the doll's design. This gave me close to an hour of frustration trying to figure out this puzzle.Moreover a lot of the game involves searching the same areas over and over again since frequently in the game, the plot will say 'you can now find item X at this location even though you already searched the location three times and didn't find anything there.'The story initially seems to have potential but ultimately peters out. The twists in the game are so far foreshadowed that they're really not twists at all. And the central theme of the work feels confusing and inconsistent. While I think the ultimate resolution of the game had some pathos it also borders on completely nonsenical and I can't imagine what the protagonist does either breaking the 'curse' or pacifying the ghosts.Honestly, I'm not sure this game is really worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Re:Turn - One Way Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I think Re:Turn is a pleasant experience. I'll be honest though. It really isn't horrifying apart from eccentric sounds and noises. It really is a story about love, hate, and anger. Throughout the game, you'll be solving puzzles with saki and her friends. There is also nothing to be afraid of because there are few deaths in this game and you can easily restart where you left off, so saving is optional. It does have great visuals, storytelling, and character design and development, and it has a good soundtrack. I think this is a good game for those who want a story about romance, or just want a atmospheric horror game. I finished it 100% and the puzzles are intense and difficult. I think it was a good game, and i'll be buying Re:Turn 2 when it launches January 28th. The bundle also includes a 7-page story on Saki and Sen's relationship and the soundtrack of the game. It's up to you if you would like to purchase that, but in my opinion you should wait for a sale to buy all that stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really my first dive into a horror game that wasn't just a visual novel so perhaps my perspective might be a bit naive. My perspective is a bit rosy at the moment as I've quite enjoyed this game. I feel I should complete the game 100% because I can't help but feel like I'm missing something which is a good sign in my opinion for a short game like this.The plot. A haunted train where Saki and her friends get trapped in and Saki(the player's avatar) must find the means to escape with her friends. As far as a set up goes this is about as much as you'd expect from a horror but true to the genre you dive deeper into the history of the place you're in and slowly uncover the tragedy that befell the passengers of the train. There's nothing groundbreaking about the characters, their motivations are relatable and the drama is there. I wont spoil it for those interested. The pace of the game does serve the plot well as you slowly unravel the mystery.The Puzzles in the game can be a bit frustrating at times and you do have to do a lot of backtracking. As a Massive metroidvania fan, this is something that never bothered me at all. The game world is extremely small in comparison to those games so solving puzzles on this scale allows them to be a bit more complex than What I'm used to but also they're housed in a much smaller space so it about balances itself out. I ended up using my phone to snap photos of the codes for the puzzles as it does require some memorization which is something I personally struggle with. The Puzzles were mostly enjoyable, keeping me engaged to the end, only a couple of spots were I really got stumped. From what I understand from Horror games you pick up Objects that seem to have no purpose at all but are key puzzle pieces. This was a bit strange to me but didn't remove me from the experience.Overall I enjoyed this game. Its Puzzles and world structure was reminiscent of the Zelda and Metroidvania games I've come to love over the years with a creepy atmosphere. And as a first shot into horror I feel this has turned me onto the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Re:Turn - One Way Trip is a 2D side-scrolling puzzle-adventure horror game. Trapped in a ghostly train, Saki must search the past and present to find and save her friends. More importantly, Saki must use her wits if she is to survive against an unspeakable evil hellbent on avenging unrequited love.

name: Scars Above
detailed_description: Scars Above is a challenging sci-fi third-person action adventure shooter combining the rewarding feel of overcoming difficulty with a compelling and intricate story, set in a mysterious alien world to explore. Some things were not meant to be discovered… A colossal and enigmatic alien structure appears in Earth's orbit and stuns the entire world; humanity names it ‘The Metahedron’. The Sentient Contact Assessment and Response team (SCAR) - consisting of scientists and engineers - is sent to investigate. Things don’t go as planned and the Metahedron hauls the team across space onto a mysterious extrasolar planet. Playing the role of Dr Kate Ward - a SCAR member - who wakes up dazed, alone in a strange, hostile environment. Determined to survive, you set out to find your crew and unravel the mystery behind what’s happened. SURVIVE AGAINST ALL ODDS Kate is an astronaut and a scientist – not a soldier - but she's resourceful and determined to do anything to survive. Use a combination of ranged weapons, devices, consumables and melee attacks, you need to manage stamina as you run, dodge, exploit weak points and discover effective tactics to defeat your foes Combine different elemental attacks to beat the odds and break through otherwise impassable obstacles. Craft different items and gadgets to aid you against the countless threats in this exoplanet. EXPLORE A MYSTERIOUS EXOPLANET Immerse yourself in a carefully crafted adventure, inspired by the sci-fi classics. Explore an alien world filled with countless threats, gorgeous landscapes and ruins hinting of an ancient - yet advanced - civilisation that somehow disappeared. Journey through different biomes, such as marshlands, freezing wastelands, underground caverns and alien facilities – all with their own set of challenges, enemies, secrets and environmental hazards. EMBARK ON A RESEARCH JOURNEY Kate is a scientist to her core and you'll use that scientific expertise to extract information from your surroundings by scanning artifacts, materials and creatures in order to learn about their features, properties and weaknesses. As you explore your surroundings, you will conduct analysis and gain knowledge which will allow you to craft new gadgets, weapons and unlock abilities in Xenobiology and Engineering trees. THRILLING BOSS FIGHTS Ghastly enemy designs - with diverse strategies and tactics - will keep encounters fresh, forcing you to find creative ways to defeat them. The Scars Above Experience: Immerse yourself in an exciting sci-fi adventure inspired by the classics of the genre Explore an enigmatic and intricate alien world - with plenty of mysteries to uncover Fight tactically, using a combination of elemental attacks, gadgets and items, exploit the environment and enemy weaknesses Engage exciting and challenging enemies and bosses, from hulking rock-covered monstrosities to nightmarish creatures lurking in the dark Gain knowledge and acquire new skills Scan enemies to learn about their weaknesses and behaviours Use your scientific skills to conduct research and extrapolate information Mature Content Description The developers describe the content like this: Violence, Depictions mutated human bodies, Depictions of dead and mutilated aliens.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that really surprised me in a positive way. On first glance it looks like it might be a small indie game, but it's really a proper game, rivaling the bigger games out there. There is plenty of story and gameplay, and the game system is nicely fleshed out with a lot of upgrades, weapons, gadgets, etc. But what matters most is the story and this game has a great one. A small team of scientists is sucked through something a like a wormhole and you are taken to another planet with a civilization that once was, but is nowhere to be seen, and you have to find out what happened. Really a must game for any fan of sci-fi exploration and action.

The gameplay was simple. I wish however there was a reason to kill the enemies whether it be experience or something other than the very random drop of ammunition. Also I ended with 10 skill points that I couldn't use, it just felt there could've been a broader talent tree. A solid 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a unique game that has many elements of popular games but has its own recipes. We have some dark soul elements that, after you die, you will return to the pillar; however, you do not collect any soul or point to use, and you will lose nothing when you die. Also, killing the enemies does not give you XP. The skill tree is small, and you need information qeub and scanning new enemies to get points for the skill tree update. The graphics are mid-range, the story is not that bad, and the voice acting is okay. Overall, the game is not that bad, and it looks like the developer tried their best to make it a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a third person sci-fi adventure game.  Graphics and sound are fairly average Unreal engine stuff.  The writing/plot is indie level beck filling to try and explain the mechanics of the game and is so full of plot holes.I'm mostly posting a negative review to complain about the janky controls, where it tries to contextually work out what you're trying to do:Example 1) The same key us used to roll or vault over chest high walls.  So you hit the key and if you're not in *exactly* the right spot you end up rolling into the base of the wall, rather than vaulting over it.  Which looks really dumb.Example 2) The same key is used for melee attacks and scope guns.  So trying to scope up on a mob of visible enemies only to whiff with my melee weapon, because an enemy was hidden in the swamp next to me.  Hidden enemy gets a free hit in, mob closes in and swamps me, because the dumb ass game chose the wrong context for my input.I assume this is because it was developed to be controller friendly.   That just means everyone has to put up with this contextual jank.  Don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game may seem small and modest but playing it I find that it is quite rich in content we have an interesting plot, well-written characters, a combat system that is very well done I liked the weapons we have here because there are not many of them but they are well balanced and thanks to that you can play however you want. In general, the game in my opinion has no major problems and is a good title.

_childDocuments_.review: "Scars Above" impresses with its stunning environmental graphics, creating a hauntingly beautiful alien world. The mechanics blend shooting and exploration effectively, offering smooth combat that feels rewarding. However, the character models are stiff, and the lip syncing often falls short, detracting from immersion. The puzzles are generally easy to solve and don’t require much critical thinking, which may disappoint those seeking a deeper challenge. Overall, it’s a visually striking game that balances action and exploration well, despite its technical shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Caution, your mileage may vary as Scars Above scratches a very particular sci-fi itch of mine.As a game; fine. It does what it has set out to do, it wears its influences on its sleeve and the story is well realised although the conclusion is fairly predictable, not that that in itself is a bad thing. As a piece of sci-fi it is great, something that I would fully enjoy as a book, but in this case rendered in game form.This is a good effort by a small team, a quintessential 7/10 game, and I mean that in the fondest way imaginable.

_childDocuments_.review: Only an hour into the game, but having fun with it so far. No unreal engine shader compilation stutter (thank you devs). It does have some Returnal vibes going on, but keep in mind that this does not have a AAA budget (which is fine honestly). It does not at all look cheap, the character models are high quality and the animations look good. The world is perhaps lackluster (at least in the first area) but nothing that has hurt the immersion. It does have a souls-like save system where you activate pillars to save progress and heal, which respawns enemies. But beyond that, I would consider it a 3rd person adventure game with shooting mechanics. You have to scan a lot of enemies and objects which helps you upgrade your gun, you start off with just an electrical attack and build out from there. I’m happy with the purchase and think it’s easily worth the sale price with 15% off. I will update if I run into anything that changes my opinion of this game. Performance is fine, I’m getting between 90-120fps at Ultra with a 3070 + 5800x3d @2954x1231(77% scale of my 3840x1600 Ultrawide).

I have provided my system stats, dx stats, followed their instructions to reboot, update drivers, etc, and provided video of the occurrence after every attempt to follow their direction. I've given up, and have told them as such. For now I'm walking everywhere and avoiding obstacles. I just lost 20m of gameplay because I forgot and ran into a rock. This is silly. Tech support is not interested in collecting info for bug fixes, or even telling me that a patch is being worked on. 48 hours and I have barely gotten past "have you turned it off then on again?". I'll update my review with a positive recommendation as soon at this is fixed. Hell, I'll change it to positive if someone from the devs acknowledges the issue and says they're working on it. I've been looking forward to this game but I'm tired of losing progress because I wanted sprint and not have to watch out every obstacle like I'm playing a game of "Operation".

_childDocuments_.review: O.G. POST = 03-27-2024:I've been playing SCARS Above from one of the recent Humble Bundles. It's a sci-fi & horror-based shooter/action-adventure/Souls-like hybrid of sorts.You're a scientist & engineer named Kate and she's trying to find out why she's on this weird alien planet, as her ship w/ many of hew crew-mates got taken down. Genre-wise, there's a more emphasis on the shooter/action-adventure stuff, as you do lots of shooting & some easy puzzle-solving, not say stat, skill and number-crunching. You will learn skills & craft stuff, as you go along - but don't expect to sink lots of points into that stuff as this ain't a RPG; this still feels and plays like a third-person shooter, more so than anything.For the Souls-like part: you do have these Big Obelisk-like things for Save points there & when you reach them (which are like Bonfires in a Dark Souls game), you heal & replenish everything and cure all diseases & issues (such as Toxicity from poison, Hypothermia from being too cold in freezing environments) - BUT it also respawns everything back (like a Souls-like does) for enemies & encounters, once you reach these Obeilisk-like things.You also have environments that you need to use to your advantage (i.e. you have an electric-gun, so shoot this at water but don't stand in water - you'll do more extra damage on certain enemies). A lot of enemies have weakness points - so you need to use the right weapon to defeat them much easier & exploit that.Game's running at 1080p maxed-out looks great & runs very well at max on my RTX 3060-based laptop, at often 50-60fps.I'm having a blast with it (SCARS Above) so far, some 7 hours in.ADDENDUM - 04-02-2024:After about 20 hours or so (some handful or so of the 26 hours, I was either away or asleep - so it's probably more like 20 hours or so that I played this game), SCARS Above is now finished & in the books as Complete. I know, most players seem to finish it in the 8-15 hour ballpark - but I was certainly taking my time and let's be real: when it comes to hard games, I'm not always great at games that also have Souls-like and/or Rogue-like elements.Overall, the game and its many levels & plot twists was very good. And there was even some awesome boss fights later on, which were tough - but eventually, I found my way through some of them and they certainly weren't easy. Some of them boss fights & mini-bosses felt like puzzles too, as you also had to figure out how to defeat them w/ the environment, situation, and weapons & items you've at you disposal too. The premise & story is always intriguing - but once the story reveals all of its hands & cards later on, after it slowly gets peeling back info like an onion, it certainly hits hard with some really good and bonkers type of awesome twists, turns & revelations.In the grand scheme of things, SCARS Above is an awesome shooter/action-adventure/Souls-like sort of hybrid & is an easy recommendation. Even more so, if you caught it recently in the recent Humble Bundle that it was in and/or can catch it in a sale.Awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting story in the beginning but the gameplay comes down to "shoot shiny spot on monster to progress". The beginning ape-fire-chest guys suck and really drag the whole thing down, and I'm FAIRLY sure the pattern of the game will continue that way if my experience with clunky games like this is anything to go by. Not a great gameplay loop or way to handle combat that CONSTANTLY happens. When I ran into my fifth rock-fire-gorilla in a 5 minute timespan I refunded the game. They are NOT fun to fight against and there are way too many. I also had to fight two near the end at the same time after the first boss and I was just like "jesus christ, man." I can't imagine what other gimmicky enemies are later in the game.Let's just say there's a reason the trailers are only the first hour of the game, I'M SURE.Combat: 2/10, gunplay feels okay but the constant swapping of elements in your gun with having to freeze enemies to even get a shot in is not great. Then you run out of freeze ammo and you're dead in the water. Elements don't swap fast enough because they're assigned to the DPAD, so by the time you swap, the enemies are unfrozen.The enemies you can just shoot and kill feel good to kill though, more of those and less elemental enemies please. Save that for the boss fights.Visuals: 8/10, beautiful alien world you're running around in, gear and equipment look great, the aliens look cool.Music/Sound: 8/10, gives a real feel of running around an alien planet, I'd liken it to Returnal's soundtrack/world-feel IMOGameplay: Movement is kind of clunky, much better with a controller. Shooting is okay, dodging is hit or miss it seems like sometimes. There are some "mini puzzles" but they're mostly solved with finding items and bringing them back to a place or shooting a wall with a certain element.Check out my Let's Play review of the game here (3 episodes):  (2 more episodes coming today)

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting Sci-Fi story and a girl scientist/astronaut protagonist keeps you engaged with the game and the world.It's mostly simple shooting and dodging around the enemies and a lot of exploring, with different elements (fire, electrical, ice) which is cool when making combos (shooting electrical into the water, freezing then melting...) :DThe bad side is the save system (checkpoints) which re-spawns all the enemies, and god forbid there is a cinematic somewhere inbetwean, you can't skip it - so prepare yourself to run through the same fields and bushes and watch the same cinematic over and over again, while you are dying from some boss repeatedly.I mean, games should be challenging, and losing to some boss is expected and it should be a bit frustrating until you win it - but respawning back at checkpoint (a couple of minutes back) and rewatching the same cinematic for the boss makes it really unpleasant experience if repeated. Maybe I am just not hard-core enough :(I would recommend the game nonetheless, exploring the alien worlds is always good fun -  7 / 10 .

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a Soulslite with an excellent sci-fi plot with a hint of body horror.As Kate Ward a scientist who is part of "SCARS" a team designated with making contact with aliens who have appeared above earth, you find yourself and the crew of your vessel lost on a strange planet. To make matters more intriguing as you navigate the hostile environment led by a strange alien hologram who appears to know who you are, every time you die... you are reborn moments later in a strange cycle of life and death.The basic gameplay of Scars Above is focused on exploration and combat, you must navigate the mostly linear alien world battling different enemies with your four different elemental weapons (which later unlock different fire modes) . The combat is simple, featuring a dodge roll, melee attacks and gun play. The basic premise of the combat involves exploiting each enemies set environmental weakness in order to kill it quickly. It's fast paced, and once you get the hang of some of the clunkier weapons very, very compelling. The exploration and story though for me are the games strongest points, you gain experience to unlock abilities not by killing but by finding "knowledge" - small purple tokens hidden through the map. It makes exploration very rewarding and you want to check every nook and cranny of the gorgeous alien world. The plot is also excellent and while it spells itself out early on it's a satisfying story with a great conclusion with a good cast of characters who are all well voice acted and realised.The game also has a horror aspect in that the plot revolves around mutations to DNA which leads to some pretty disturbing moments and body horror as the story progresses. Excellent stuff.Overall Scars Above is a fantastic shooter and while it's no where near as difficult as Dark Souls theres still reasonable challenge to be found in this great little "AA" title. The story and horror aspects only push it to new heights and it runs great and looks great on PC. Highly Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game to be played for the story, which was interesting enough to keep going to a point. But at some point the goal of being souls-like conflicts with the goal of telling a story. I get that it's supposed to be hard, and that's fine. But being set back very far (in terms of distance and having to repeat fights) when you die is a hassle, and at some point I decided it was more fun to delete the game than make another long run to the target.Also, the image for this game on the steam library page does an awful job of selling it: a woman sitting around with her eyes closed has nothing to do with the action in the game, which is performed by a woman running around with her eyes open. Seriously, it gives nothing of the flavor of the game, it just says, here's a female protagonist, in case that's your thing - but she looks kind of bored, so maybe you'll be bored, so maybe you should go play Tomb Raider again instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a AA-tier soft "souls-like" third person shooter with linear level structure and not much customisation options. I found the setting and story to be generic and forgettable, but at least the game looks quite nice graphic-wise and having purchased it for £6 on sale, I can't complain too much about it.As of time of this review the game is a bit pricey for how short it is (you can complete it on 100% in ~5 hours), therefore I suggest waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with the concept of a "popcorn movie" - a movie where you turn off your brain for 2 hours and then forget all about as soon as the credits roll - then you understand what this game is.  It's a Popcorn Game.As a notably mediocre and forgettable game it manages to do everything competently while not offering anything that stands out or makes it unique.    The most interesting part might be the weapon you have which can fire 4 different elemental types (electric, fire, ice and acid) and the way you can combine two of them to create two additional combo effects - ice and electricity play off one another and so do acid and fire.    Most of the enemies have some ill-defined weakness or weak spot but they can be defeated with brute force as well.The various maps and levels of the game are mostly linear with a handful of obvious side paths which invariably lead to extra skill points or weapon upgrades.   The enemies all follow the same general rules.  If you enter an area with water deeper than your ankles, some snake men will jump out of the water to spit at you.  If you find yourself on a path no wider than two widths of your character, some spiders will jump out of the ground to crawl at you.   In between these recycled ambushes are bigger areas where you fight a half dozen varieties of minibosses, most of which become trivial once you find their weakness.The story is fine but is every bit as forgettable as the gameplay.   All in all it's fun way to kill 10 hours, at about the same price as watching 5 popcorn movies.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game overall. One hiccup at the beginning with a major patch that removed my save file, this wasn't anything major as I was able to find the old folder where the save was and cut/paste into the new to retrieve it. Other than that, I didn't run into any other bugs during my playthrough.The game itself I think won't win any awards but don't let that stop you from playing. The combat was fun, learning the monsters attack patterns and also what gun to use in what situation, being able to combo with elements was also great. Gadgets were fun and unique, you will probably rely on certain ones over others like I did. The story was decent, the graphics are very nice and yes while the artwork does resemble Returnal in a lot of ways I assure you the game is very different in playstyles. Overall I enjoyed myself even though it only took me roughly 7 hours to complete the game.I do look forward to see if they improve on this and continue in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Story and game-play were great. Guns were interesting and fun to use and the combos were quite satisfying to pull off.The game was not too hard even on commander difficulty however you need to be very efficient with your shots (and combos) to kill enemies fast before it becomes overwhelming. I'm guessing it is similar in lower difficulties just with more room for error.One small gripe I had with the upgrade system was that there were very few actively useful upgrades, namely the rapid reload and the better scan thingy (and of course the top 2 upgrades). All other upgrades were extremely minor and did not really feel like actual progress was made. Also it needs a system to dump excess upgrade points (can be minor like 1% dmg per point). I finished the game with 8 point after having unlocked everything.The graphics were very good but the facial animations were quite bad, however this can be easily excused by the fact that it is an appropriately priced AA game.All in all I highly recommend this game for the price-point of ~30€

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully relaxing to play. It was exactly what I was looking for on a weekend. I find the graphics appealing for my taste; the U4, which I believe is the one used in this game, looks really good.The weapons and attributes that you unlock during the whole campaign are so satisfying; they're not too complex but not too simple either. The cutscenes looked kind of odd; I believe they were pre-rendered and not in-game, so it felt a little bit funny and made me question why such a decision was made. It didn't stop me from enjoying it, of course; my eyes were hooked!The scenarios in this game are very interesting as well. I've seen many aesthetics similar on some sci-fi book covers that I usually read from the 80s'/90s'. Giving that feeling of a world unknown, exploring areas that look very odd to you, and making you not expect what is yet to come. Many times during the game, I spent a couple of minutes appreciating the effort made on these levels. Now to the story, which I found pretty interesting—the main theme of the game and its conclusion, along with everything else. I could see many other great works that were probably used as a base for inspiration (I might be wrong). Some enemies reminded me of Metro: Last Light, Venom, and Alien. The story itself reminded me of a couple of movies and books, too. So that was really good to see these similarities to other contents; I have already enjoyed them myself. Gameplay is fun and brings me back to some old third-person shooters from the PS3 or some recent ones. I really liked kicking some aliens with the new weapons and always finding a fun or different way of eliminating them. The abilities and the weapon upgrades make it possible for you to vary in your gameplay and combat techniques so the game doesn't get too repetitive for you. I really don't know the difficulty of the game; I played it on normal difficulty and only died once, but the game got pretty tough many times, making me almost die during these events, so it must vary from person to person. Bugs: There were only a few bugs for me; one of them was that I entered the wall for no reason and got stuck while being hit by the enemies. The second and third ones are related to achievements. I don't know if it's meant to be this way, but I got some achievements during the training sessions when you get new gadgets. That's all. It's a good game; if possible, get it on sale and have a good time. That's my quick review, without trying to spoil the game, but you'll only know if you'll truly feel the game when you play it! At least that's how I think.And good job to all the developers who worked on the game; I can clearly see some love integrated into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a game that doesn't reinvent the genre but it does what it does really well. The ambience, the action, the gameplay and the story are pretty good. I really liked the combat mechanics. Each weapon has their use and so are the tools. You can't just pick one gun and blast your way through the game. I liked that this game gives you different guns and tools that you'll have to use and switch regularly to make your way through the story. The game isn't too hard even though some fights are more challenging than others. All in all, it's a pretty solid game that surpasses even some AAA games out there.On the down side, I think the price is a bit high considering the length of the game. It only took me 10 hours to complete the game and get all the achievements.I still recommend it though but you might want to wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I agree with the general consensus on the pricing of Scars Above, all things considered, its still a solid game for what you get honestly, and I enjoyed every second I played of it. A rough 8 to 10 hour short, linear experience with some not half bad voice acting, smooth controls and really good optimisation. I can't say I ran into any glaring issues like bugs and the game didn't crash once.The story is probably what you might expect from a sci-fi game, or even something you'd see in a sci-fi horror movie where there's always some sort of body horror of some description. If you've watched a few then you kinda know what you're in for.As mentioned, although linear, the maps are generally quite interesting though stereotypical when it comes to the whole alien planet vibe, you could pretty much play science fiction bingo with the tropes you run into. Still, its designed nicely for what it is. The meat sections gave me dead space vibes for sure.I liked the elemental damage aspect, especially where you can combo for extra damage. Essentially every weapon has a use for maximum efficiency along side a rather decent selection of abilities that run on battery charges ranging from a shield that negates damage, to the ability to slow down time through a throw-able "chrono-bomb" that slow time in an area, or to temporarily stop time itself and move behind enemies to hit weak spots. I honestly love some of the design choices and wasn't once thinking "my god whats the point in this gun/ability" because everything had a well thought out use instead of just been filler garbage. There are also consumables that can be crafted using fiber found around the world or on defeated enemies that can help keep ammo topped up or recharge battery power to name a few uses.For some reason they decided to sneak in a pseudo "bonfire" mechanic like that of the souls series, and gave it some lore, but I reckon it could have been fine without it honestly. Too many games these days recycle these mechanics where it just isn't necessary .All in all an 8/10, dropping a number due to the price...again, for such a short indie experience shaving off £10 to £15 would make it much more acceptable. Its one of those situations where I want to recommend it, but only when its on sale, unless you got a whole bunch of expendable income and need something to kill time for a day or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game biomes. Good and engaging combat with enemy weak spots and different element types to use, that even act differently in different environments. Level designs are good but nothing over the top. Exploration is fun and well rewarded. Human character models, faces, and voice acting are rough but doable. The good gameplay makes up for it. So far I am liking the story and is keeping me intrigued.An indie action adventure shooter recommend for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short indie adventure game and is mechanically a third person  shooter. It's nothing special, everything you see in the game has been done before. The weapons use an elemental system that correspond with colored weak points on enemies. The levels are semi-linear with branching paths and collectibles strewn about. The premise is unknown aliens visit earth with bad intentions, you're the hero that deals with it.  I felt very meh about this game but it wasn't bad, this is soft thumbs up. bugs were minimal, all the game play systems work, the story exists and follows a clear narrative. If you're interested in adventure games, get this when it's on sale and keep your expectations low. It probably won't disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing this game i read the reviews that said this game was too hard, even on easy mode. After completing the game on normal mode, i cant say these things:Overall the game is really good, especially since this isnt my normal, go to type of game. Story is good, mechanics work well.XP SYSTEM NEEDS REWORK. . The reason for the complaints of this game being too hard is just because the character is under powered. I found levelling early game really slow but after the 2nd boss xp from knowledge cube began to increase and skill points dropped more frequent. Too frequent in fact. I managed to complete all skill with 7 skill points over at the end of the game. this game just gets easier as the game goes onIN GAME FEEDBACK FOR LOW HP NEEDS TO BE IMPROVED. I often found myself dying in boss fights because i didnt realise i was on low HP. many times i took a hit, stood doing damage, took another hit and died. with the amount of mechanics and abilities in Scar Above, the volume of the Low Health warning should be increased and potentially red border on the screen before death, as it is too easy to miss during an intense fight.overall 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above feels like an indie version of Remnant: From the Ashes. Combat feels good, enemy variety is decent and the levels are well designed, although quite linear. The game gives you a lot of interesting weapons, tools and gadgets to approach combat however you want. Combining your weapon elements with your time manipulation gear feels like a good power fantasy. With that said, it ends up making the player a bit too powerful. So if you want a challenge you should go for the harder difficulties. On normal the game is very easy. Each enemy is well designed with a very specific way to approach them well thought out, but the sheer power of all your tools allow you to simply power through all those mechanics.Definitely worth picking up at a discount, but don't expect anything revolutionary. Game is fun for the duration of its short campaign, which should take around 6 to 8h depending on how much you explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid 7/10 game with fun combat and good enough story. Unfortunately it's a short one and too often it limits you with invisible walls. However, it's definitely worth its price and I would love to see a bigger sequel that provides more freedom of exploration to the player. The groundwork is here and it definitely has a 9 or 10 potential. Scars Above definitely deserves more recognition and love especially for dabbling  into horror in a few sections which was really interesting to experience. For such a short game you also encounter a lot of different environments. To sum up, definitely worth it especially if you are a sci-fi/horror fan. Now please make a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed my playthrough of this game from opening cutscene to end credits. The gameplay is very smooth and fluid; The creatures telegraph their moves clearly through wide motions and distinct sounds; The gunplay works within the setting and the story flows quite well. It took me a while to realize it was playing a lot like a souls game with guns however the path to strength is not found through fighting but by exploring the areas. Although I couldn't put the game down without thinking about it for 2 minutes and picking it back up again I wouldn't call it perfect.The first area being the swamp and having to deal with poison from the outset made the beginning moments a slog and it didn't improve until after defeating 'The Alpha' boss (sub-boss?) and getting an upgrade from it. The 'scientific' elements of the game were well integrated to the upgrade system and it was a nice to see all the available upgrades from the start. I only have maybe one or two gripes for the game overall but I would still very much recommend this game to anyone else who, like me, sees this trailer and thinks, "wow this looks awesome!"

_childDocuments_.review: Good AA game, with some caveats. 7.5/10Good: GraphicsGunplay / Combat / GadgetsSound DesignMonster VarietyGreat boss fights with a good deal of challenge and tactics to take them outVoice Acting4 Elements to mix and match in attacks and using the environment to take down enemies and surviveProgression, finding new enemies almost all the way to the end of the game. Was surprising. Performance / FPSNo crashesDecent:Story: While the story was wrapped up, the most interesting plot point was left unresolved. Leveling / Perk System: Nice to have, but nothing special. You unlock better perks and bonuses as you play through the game.Bad: Woke - Every character is ugly as sin. Not "just a normal person" ugly, but intentionally making ugly women with weird faces and the cast of characters are all "strong, diverse and brave". Strange, considering the game devs are Eastern European.Major Bug - About halfway through the game, in certain levels you may encounter a bug that causes your movement inputs to not register. As in, you literally can't move or go anywhere. As you can imagine, this becomes very frustrating and I found no solutions online. TLDR: A good linear A to AA game. Third person shooter with great 4 element (fire / electric / freeze / toxic) battle system. Weapon upgrades, lots of good enemy variety and engaging boss battles. Would be a near perfect little AA adventure if not for a major bug (see above), ugly / woke characters, and a decent story that while being concluded, leaves the most interesting part of the story unresolved.Strong recommend when on sale. Not rushing, exploring and decently taking my time, full playthrough on medium difficulty took around 12 hours of gameplay.
