_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly great game!I love how weapons are used to interact with the world(they're just tools, after all :D ) and not only for fighting. How obtaining new weapons changes exploration and combat strategies through the game, Also, gadgets are actually useful and versatile, and not something you forget you have, like in most games. Enemy variety is also very good and persistent throughout the entire game(in 9 hours of gameplay I've seen more different enemy types, that require different strategies to defeat, than in most 40+ hours action adventures/rpgs). Very well written and acted characters(most of them at least, especially Kate), main character that actually acts like a scientist, simple, but well written story that can sometimes be creepy and terrifying, and sometimes heartwarming and hopeful. Great art direction and environment design, Great sound design and music, that appear to be very well above AA budget of the game. Only few things don't work in this game (and it is kinda baffling how bad they can get sometimes) - cinematics and facial animations (especially lipsync).  It's hard to believe that same team that pulled off rest of this game, goofed so hard on these. I guess they were low priority tasks, left for photo-finish of development. No matter how bad these can get, they don't take away from great experience that this game absolutely is, and I'd rather have engaging game with tight gameplay, great world and characters, then fancy cinematics.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game. A bit mysterious at first, then gets downright creepy until it you get into the lore a bit. Dig the protagonist's back-story. Voice acting is decent. I do really like the atmosphere and game play. The combat is intuitive and you get a multitude of guns. You can melee, but it's not very effective - you can perk into it but it's still kinda useless. The combat on the regular difficulty is challenging but not impossible and you get used to it really quickly, it's mostly about dodging and knowing which weapons/gadgets to use. The ability progression system is pretty neat, and by the end of the game you can get them all too. All in all, a great game for the price (Mind you, I bought it on sale 50% off).
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocre at best.It's game-play is interesting enough but the story, characters, and rigging are atrocious. It is an unfortunate case of politics creating a soulless piece of neo-propaganda that could have easily gotten a better message across without the heavy-handed and completely uninspired approach that it took. As it stands it's somewhat boring and joke-worthy while ultimately committing the worst sin imaginable. Being utterly forgettable and bland.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a decent story with fun game play. You can tell it was made by a smaller team and there are definitely some ideas that didn't get flushed out all the way but you can also tell that there were really good ideas that went into this.It's a straightforward play through that should take 6-8 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I will be honest and say I really enjoy the combat and interactivity with certain pieces of the environment, however I will warn though that it is quite buggy. I have gotten stuck in the floor and had to restart at least 5 times in a single hour which is incredibly frustrating to the point I want to uninstall. The graphics also tend to feel sluggish, and while it may be an issue with something like v-sync, it feels like I am playing at half the fps and refresh rate as it says I am. The narrative imo is also pretty weak so far, but some of it was interesting enough for me to want to trudge through.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mix of Lost Planet and Metroid Prime, in all the good ways. While the environments and sound never reach the peaks that Prime did, they are serviceable enough and never get annoying. Combat's clean and I never felt like the game was cheating me. The story's fine, but the human characters writing and their models looked weird. I do like the detail of the neck and elbows. As odd as that is to say.The only negatives I have are that the crafting system is kinda needless, but it's there more to justify your equipment on an alien world. I just wished the research that you did was tied more to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Ha ha ha ha, this game sucks. What a waste of money. Talk about a generic waste of time. WTF is wrong with the gaming industry, it's all hype. It's like watching something I love wither away to nothing. Terrible story, terrible voice acting, terrible mechanics, just overall terrible. Millennial console cucks are the bane of my gaming existence, mediocrity is their go to, uselessness is their answer.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: You know weird period when you finally try to move on after playing a game you really liked? You're still grieving the loss of your last fantasy world, so you don't want anything too serious, but also nothing that totally sucks.This game is literally built for that period. It's not great, but doesn't do anything horribly wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Became stuck in the environment twice while dodging and once when using the cryo rifle in just the first hour before the first boss/big enemy (the Alpha). Not a great start to a game that already had a slow and boring introduction. Graphical options are very limited (unable to even turn off motion blur). Characters are highly detailed but bland and boring; the main character doesn't even sound interested in (or maybe even bored by) what's going on around her. Refund requested after an hour and a half.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Except for the major performance drop in which a simple restart fixed, there's not much negative to say about the game. However, not too many positive things stand out either. It was fairly easy, even on the hardest difficulty. My low-mid end system could keep it at 60fps on Ultra settings most of the time, which was unexpected for a newer game. Story was...okay, gameplay was...okay.It's just an okay game. Got it as part of the "Humble Heroines bundle".
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: 6h from beginning to end. Good story, good performance. Some animation in cinematics are lacking, specially facial animations but overall good work. Graphics are good, but not ground breaking. Gameplay is good, making use of status effects is nice specially when they can be combined with environmental elements. I find that on easy difficulty the experience is more enjoyable but most consumables are pretty much never used as well as many of the gadgets and going to harder difficulties is in this case a way to ruin the story. It is a bit expensive for what it is yes, but I recommend it. Wait for a sale if you think you might enjoy it. It is a very linear game, just don't expect dark souls type of freedom even with the resurrection mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: If you like dark souls you'll like this. Even though the game 'CLAIMS' to have adjustable difficulty IT DOESN'T!!! Setting it to easy will result in you dieing just a tad slower than the medium or insane difficulty. Why bother putting this in the game? It doesn't make the game easier. I ended up asking for my money back because i couldn't get past the dang first boss so this game is no fun for someone like myself. Don't put different levels of difficulty in the game when they don't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is simple and there is no accumulation of resources. Consumables are made directly from a resource you only hold a little of and are constantly running out of and replenishing. Sizable amount of time is walking down hallways and holding E to interact. Dialogue is very stilted like it was AI written and never reviewed.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this is a nice game, like many other players, I did not manage to get past the first big boss and uninstalled the game after only 3 hours of play. This is very unfortunate, as I like the graphics and settings overall. Due to its insane difficulty in this regard, I cannot recommend this game for the casual players like me right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: clear, simple, relaxing, no stupid secondary mission, graphic is ok, runs well, story is good, weapon and ability are good not like other games where you have 154 abilities and 72 weapon that you will never use because you'll stick with the only 2 that you really need. if you have some free time play this game. like i said, it is relaxing.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 62 yo and really enjoyed the game. Was hard at the start with first few boss but I cruised thru it. My hardest areas were when you can get hypothermia and die while fighting due to freezing. Other than that I enjoyed it. I played on easiest setting an ach's were straight forward w/o guide. Wouldn't mind a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't very difficult, and the story and lore don't bring anything profound to the table. However it is a cute little niche gem if you're looking for an action crafting game like The Last of Us. You can ignore the souls-like tag on the game because, despite it being a dodge roll shooter, it's not a very difficult game by itself. You can expect to kill any of the bosses within one to two tries.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A solid Sci-Fi story, interesting alien environments and decent third person shooter mechanics, utilizing elemental attacks. There are checkpoints, which you can activate and where you respawn if you die without losing your overall progress in puzzles, unlocked paths or the story, and you occassionally unlock shortcuts back to some of the checkpoints you visited. But the world is overall designed in a linear fashion. Some encounters are very difficult, some even require using the environment to beat them - but the game is forgiving enough to not hinder the enjoyment of the well crafted story and characters.Recommended for hardcore Sci-Fi fans, especially Trekkies! Mature Sci-Fi entertainment on an alien planet with alien technology. If you are fan of interesting Sci-Fi scenarios and good design for tools, ships, weapons and alien tech - this game is definately going to grab your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed the game, fantastic story, great variety of alien mobs, 4 elemental weapons and many gadgets to help in multiple playstyles, weapon upgrades on discovery throughout the game. Dying respawns at latest pillar but no loss of items. Pillars are nicely spaced throughout the game so you don't lose a lot of time if you do die. Good length of game too, Three difficulty levels. Well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: 0/10 the game ran fine ONCE.after that ive never been able to make it past the logos without it giving me a black screen- also, not supported on steam decki have no way of playing this past the 1st time i got it runninggot it working using this method+ looks nice- gameplay- everything respawns- you get nothing from killing things so just run past them- boss can stun lock you to death from full health

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. Kind of a breath of fresh air... sure it's lower budget but it's a solid game that you can tell they cared to deliver a solid product. While I can see the Returnal influence it kinda has it's own thing going and the two games really are nothing alike IMO. Can't wait to see how they evolve and hopefully enough success they can invest in better animation etc... but what's here is solid enough. Very fun and that's what matter most.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not hard, it is just frustrating. I have pushed forward until the second Construct boss fight because there were good parts (story and some of the gameplay). But this fight is just not fun. You know what needs to be done, but you have only 1 opportunity in every 10 minutes and you have to survive until that. And even if the boss is in the correct position, there are several mechanics that can prevent you to do what needed. Yeah thanks no, I value my time too much. This boss design is the worst I have seen in my 20+ years of gaming life.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Annoying save system that forces you to replay the same thing over and over again. Offscreen enemies hitting you without any indication of their presence. Your character is sluggish in movement and hit detection seems to have a massive delay. Your hit box is miles wide and you are getting hit by attacs that are nowhere near your character. Story seems to be interesting but the game play drags everything down. I don't know why developers insist on usig this "souls-like" mechanics. It doesn't work. It's boring and annoying to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summarized as "It's not THAT bad"... Was it worth paying around $10 on sale? Kinda, it's six hours worth of gameplay that's not entirely horrible. TBH though, you could spend that time playing a better game for around the same price. Dead Space remastered or countless other games that are in a similar style to this one. The graphics are some five years behind, gameplay can be more of a jump scare and a pain than fun, and the story is from a C-class SiFi, I think the only redeeming factor is that it is cheap, but again, you can spend your time and money in many better ways than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games that actually created some curiosity and eagerness to figure out more about the story in me. While it certainly has some flaws like the stiff animations and sometimes comically bad mouth and face animations, it does not deter from the overall experience. The voice acting is very good, the graphics are nice and the gameplay interesting.Sometimes I felt like there were too many gadgets and guns and not enough game to actually try all of them, but that is somewhat of a good thing as nothing is streched too long or too thin. Another great thing for me was, that this is a mostly linear game, some side branches, but it feels refreshing to experience a story and discover on the side without open world fluff.I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, if you can accept that it has quite some flaws, but otherwise punches above its weight class!
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok and that is all I can really say. The difficulty will swing wildly at times with fights. The graphics are meh, the combat is meh, story is meh I guess, everything is basically only ok. There are some basic features the game is missing that it really should have such as toggle aim and ability to cancel sprinting without just stopping or aiming. I would wait for a sale, I'd say this game should be more in the 20 dollar range, not 40.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars above is a beautiful sci-fi game, very similar to tomb raider. Sadly, it fails in many ways to replicate what makes the latter a great series. Exploration feels rather dull as you find yourself looking around corners for the only collectable in the game: purple cubes that gives you xp to unlock perks and the occasional upgrade for your weapon which are pretty much unlocked toward the end of the game.The combat experience is good, you're required to pay attention to your environment as well as what weapon to use with limited ammos. Ice breaking is absurdly op btw.The game is rather short, I'm someone who enjoy exploring a lot and waste a lot of time looking around every corner for collectibles and whatnot, yet the game lasted roughly 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay with good pacing of receiving new tools and weapons.Game is not that long but it is ok if you buy it on sale.Interesting worldbuilding, simple story which is not necessarily a bad thing.Really like the voice acting, especially the protagonist.Just playing the game will net you 100% acheivment unlock.Cutscenes are quite horrible, some cutscenes look like they are low resolution.Dialogue animations of characters are really bad. You can obtain way more exp than you can spend on skills, i eneded up having 10+ skillpoints with nothing to use them on upon completing the game. Should have been able to spend it on increasing damage or something similar.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the light souls-like aspect to it. I'm not good at souls-like games, but ones you can tweak on easier are definitely something I've come to enjoy. It was an enjoyable game with a good story, and a really good soundtrack that reminded me of Mass Effect 1 (and one particular part that gave me Stranger Things vibes). Overall, it was a good experience with interesting creatures and an easy combat style. I did get it on sale, but I would have been happy with the result if I paid full price. :) I do wish it was a little longer, but it did still hit a sweet spot with the game style and soundtrack, and I do like a good space game. :D

I tried multiple times with multiple strategies, even went back and looked for some power up I had missed, but, nope. I never got it under 50% health before it killed me.Bear in mind, I'm no third-person shooter newbie. I can see why most people haven't done the majority of storyline achievements, which is unfortunate because it is interesting. Not sure I'll pick this back up.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a decent and intriguing sci-fi game. A hidden gem in my opinion and criminally underrated. An interesting story revolving around a crashed space crew on a mysterious alien planet. Hidden paths that lead to upgrades adding an element of exploration. Vast array of different hostile creatures and neat mini bosses in each chapter. Ending could have been a bit better but could lead on to a second title maybe? Mechanics where good although nothing special. However, the game had a good amount of difficulty and challenge to it. Felt very Remnant and Souls like in a way. The gadgets and skills where simple but effective. Also very easy to max out towards the end game. Although, after maxing out, points could have be allocated elsewhere instead of building up aimlessly.I did encounter two bugs during my play-through. One when near outer edges of the map and a water pool towards the end game. These bugs left me stuck and having to restart at the last pillar. However, I had nothing game breaking, progression loss or crashes, despite many people saying in recent reviews. Game played absolutely FINE apart from these minor areas. Nonetheless, the game is great. But it could still do with some optimisation and performance updates to iron out these issues and the clunky textures during main story scenes.I would still recommend Scars Above as for me it was a good experience, great story and something different to the usual sci-fi genre. I enjoyed the game immensely. But ONLY grab Scars Above when it's on sale. Current price is too steep for a game offering nothing to do after completion and with recent reviews it would be hard to say you would even get to experience this hidden gem. Edit: Thanks for the Jester Award, clearly coming from someone that can't get the game to work :steamfacepalm:. All the people saying this game doesn't run or work should update their PC or stop claiming they got a high spec PC. I had two minor bugs and the game ran as smooth as anything, it never dropped below 60 fps. Completed story and no crashes throughout the entire play through. Don't be fooled by these band wagon negative review bombers. They're just salty they got a crap PC build and couldn't experience this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I'm running a PC well above minimum spec for the game, and I'm running into frequent crashes and bugs. I'm glad I chose to play the game on the easiest difficulty because then it's not too bad to replay the game after the last pillar (savepoint) I reached before the game crashes, but it's kind of ruining my immersion in the story when the game locks up every 20 minutes if I look the wrong direction in an environment.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.Gameplay-wise a streamlined version of Returnal, but still very enjoyable to play. If you are (like me) playing with mouse and keyboard - don't play on normal. I don't like soulslike games for their difficulty and time-investment but even this game was too easy for me on normal.Score and story are actually really good and made me push through the game in about 6hrs total playtime.Only thing i would slightly critize is the level design. There aren't any major secrets or other reasons to step aside the main path since most things are already in massive supply. But still, that is a very slight criticism for a game that came out mostly bug-free without ingame purchases and for only 40 (34 currently) euros. If you can afford it buy it know and support these type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: For me this would fall under a neutral review, but since it's more pro than con, it gets a thumbs up from me. What's Great:- It runs very well (240+ FPS with 4090, 12700K, 32 GB DDR5 RAM and NVmE drive)- The environment is beautiful- The voice acting is well done- A good mix of combat, puzzles and exploration- An intriguing stroy- Combat is fluid enough- Decent arsenal for the gameWhat's Not So Great:- Boss fights can be annoying. Not overly tough (minus the first one), but dying can cause grief (see next point)- No Save Anywhere/Weak Autosave if there is one. You activate pillars (save points) throughout the game and return here when you die. That in itself isn't bad, but it does suck when you have to repeat some content over and over again after dyingNeutral (Nitpicky Stuff):- The mouths don't match the animations. This is far more noticeable during live scenes than cutscenes. It's immersion breaking, but not a deal breaker- No jump mechanic. You're pretty much railroaded on paths most of the time.- Very linear. It fits the game, but it would be nice to have more to explore than an offshoot here and there from the main pathOverall the game isn't bad, and I feel the 34 dollars I spent was worth it. With a beautiful environment, enjoyable characters and a decent arsenal of weaponry, it can be a fun game. Solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it - technobabble was too jarringly stupid at times, but otherwise it was a good experience. Also, constant scanning of every crevice for power upgrades (and missable ones at that!) detracted from my immersion in the story because I wanted to be powerful and there was that alluring data cube in the background of a lot of very important and dramatic cutscenes. To dews credit at least there are enough of them that for the final stretch I was maxed out and fad 11 perk points to spare. In my opinion it would be better to give perk points for scanning creatures and progression (knowing your enemy and whatnot) - this way you didn't need to account for little Timmy who could not be assed to find cubes and could not finish the game or at least died like 100 times on every boss. And again - conflict of motivations of player is bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A great mix of sci-fi, puzzle solving, and interesting combat.  I love that you have to use strategy and an array of gadgets and weapons instead of just button mashing.  The story and environment are engaging and immersive and the soundscape is well done.  I'm looking forward to what else this game has in store for me
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a great experience! Many different types of enemies, which some even have reactive strategies. Maybe not great, but a good storyline which I enjoyed very much. Weapon design is very cool, but the crafting mechanic involved with said weapons is heavily underutilized and feels like it was put there to fill a checkbox from some list... Soundtrack was fun, felt right at home with the setting. Overall graphics were good (besides human modesl). I liked the spin on experience and leveling done here, altho it felt rather random. Facial animations were absolutely wooden, dipping into the uncanny valley. Besides a couple of unexplained performance drops, it run smoothly. Bosses were either bigger versions of normal enemies, or really cool entirely new creatures, with at least one having a fight sequence through terrain interaction. Elemental reactions were nice, but no info was given on them, so some people could have missed out. Scars Above is a solid 8/10. Most souls fans most probably wouldn't find this up to their liking, but I wholeheartedly recommend. It reminds me a lot of "Remnant: From the Ashes" in a positive light. If you had fun there, you should have fun here and vice versa.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The Alpha Boss appears too difficult even on Rookie mode with Strong aim assist, so the game is basically over after about 3 hours of play.  Since the save point before the Alpha Boss fight requires 5 to 10 minutes of  repetitive play just to try the fight again and again, the game quickly loses its initial appeal.  The option to bypass a frustratingly difficult boss fight after several failures would have made this review a positive one instead of a negative.  Games can be very enjoyable entertainment, but not if game progression is blocked early in the course of the game and cannot be bypassed.  Some gamers may be less skillful than others or may have less time to master a game due to work or family commitments.  Difficulty levels that scale to the player's abilities or that can be adjusted by the player to maximize enjoyment of the purchased product would be appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said the second Construct boss fight is not fun at all. It's really frustrating because of the delay on the fire weapon. I've been trying for days to get past this, at the point now of giving up and playing something else more enjoyable. Shame really as I was enjoying the game a lot up until this point.

Weapons also poorly design. This game is like childish kids dodging and running around. Enemies are also one dimensional. The game thumbnail is deceptive. _childDocuments_.review: So... This game is quite something... I confess I bought it not knowing what I would get (I got it for 8€ at a sale, mind you) and it turned out to be quite a fun short adventure! The levels are intricate and have different paths for you to explore with different enemies and bosses to fight against. The skill leveling is a solid enough - you have to grab some small cube-like alien structures and you get Knowledge from it - and it has some good and useful perks. The story is cool, maybe sometimes a bit predictable if you pay close attention to some stuff, but overall cool stuff! The gameplay tho has some weird issues. I don't know if it was because I was playing with a Xbox controller but sometimes Kate wasn't moving at all or it seemed like she was glued to a specific path - like she had a specific hitbox around her. The enemies are challenging and can make you sweat! Some more than others! Overall I would give this one a solid 6.5/10, maybe a 7. It's a nice game but make sure you get it on a discount tho, cause for the normal price it's totally not worth it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game. As others stated, the save system is a little bit annoying (once you use the pillar, enemies respawn) and sometimes parts can take longer than necessary because of that. Honestly though, it ain't that bad - yes it is annoying sometimes (one part I did, I believe, 13 times or something, just bc I couldn't figure my technique out xD), but that was on me. Rookie difficulty is still challenging sometimes, so don't underestimate it - but it really shouldn't be a problem, it's also not that bad. _childDocuments_.review: Interesting game. A good story that doesn't try to explain what it doesn't have to. The weapons are different and the soundtrack fits well.It's funny to see all of the comments about the stiff animations, because as soon as you start playing, it makes total sense. Never before have I seen someone trained to survive drop off a two-meter cliff and land with their legs straight. Nothing about this ruins the game, but it was entertaining.I played on Commander (hard) difficulty -- it was tough. I'm not a phenomenally skilled player, so I'd say it's accessible. After the first two creatures, it seems like they introduce the new enemy in a boss-style format. One-on-one in an arena-type location. Then immediately that creature is just a normal enemy that swarms you. True bosses don't keep coming back.Your exploration is almost rail-based with few branching options. There are a few hidden paths, but largely when I thought I was being clever by not going toward the waypoint on my HUD, I was actually doing exactly what I was supposed to be doing.Most of the achievements are hidden, which I dislike because when you beat the game, there is no load. It wipes your game. I was so excited to beat the final boss that I ran through the next doorway and forgot to scan the body. That and one other equipment-based achievement that I didn't get because I never used the gadget. I wish the non-story achievements had been visible to me.I made up some new swear words as I played this game, and there was a fair amount of horror-esque elements. The developers weren't afraid of using the good old jump scare. The save/respawn system lets you breathe a bit easier after finding a pillar, and I liked the 'shortcut' system of moving forward without necessarily putting save points around every corner. I think playing it on the hardest difficulty really made the horror elements pop.TL:DR: Fun game. Buy it on sale, it's short (12 hours, even on the hardest difficulty and pausing while I did other things at times).

_childDocuments_.review: Sci-fi TPS with an interesting story, but lots of flaws in itDifficulty ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ (at the beginning more difficult, later quite moderate)* good graphics* story line was good (with some lacks in the storytelling)* interesting fight system that rewards you a lot using the right weapon for the correct weakspots* 3 difficulties* enough XP cubes to unlock anything without the need to find all of them* traps and ammo does respawn over time as well* the face expressions are weird - you clealy see that they are coded and not motion-captured* only rare placed checkpoints with a bonfire system like in souls games* running passed enemies is sometime more efficient than killing them* linear pseudo-open-world* you gain still ability points if fully skilled, permanently highlighted in the HUD* you need to charge the thermal gun for firing* dialogues / logs get stopped when you trigger another audio unintentionally* combat system flaws:  1. enemies may occasionally shoot through other enemies  2. hitboxes of attacks or enemies causes you to get hit or blocked by thin air  3. (especially at the beginning) getting poisened is a death-sentence (too strong)  4. freezing in some areas is just too fast  5. controller even w/ aim-assist is still not as good as mouse w/ keyboardI am in general not a fan of soulslike games. The bonfire technique, evading mobs and focus on boss fights is just not my understanding of a good gameplay. As this game uses some of those things, or at least tries to be a half-hearted soulslike game, I did not like it.The game got tagged with open-world and Metroidvania as well, but it is in fact neither of it. Your backtravelling is quite limited and thus you have missables (like weapon upgrades). I know those tags are sometimes placed by players, but still it caused me having wrong expectations about this game anyway.The final kicker was the fact that the game just auto-deletes your savestate as soon as you finished the game. A no-go if you ask me. No NG+, no chapter select, no repeating the finale how often you want to, devs just decided to force the player to begin from scratch.Good visuals and story driven game, but paired with a very bad executed gameplay concept. Problem is that you just can't like this game even if you want to, as long as the 'little flaws' just slap you in your face every 5 minutes or so. The game made just too many mistakes to be called good for me, unfortunetally - and it looked so promising at the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun. While I wouldn't say it's going to win any awards, it's solid. Not all games need to be AAA perfection after all! If you come into it with that in mind, you will enjoy it.STORYFORMAT: Semi Cinematic LinearThis story is fully voiced and follows a linear story style. It's not choice based or heavy Cinematics like Last of us. It's story overall seems interesting enough. The voice acting is good, and I am interested in what's going on. In general it's not going to leave you at the end of your chair.COMBATCombat involves light melee, and elemental weapons. I don't believe you get a tone of weapon types, I think you just get one per element, but I could be wrong. I'm not super far into the game. That being said, It's not a looter shooter. Elements play a huge role in the game. It makes combat fun, but for those who are looking for difficult game and can master these mechanics well, it may not be as challenging for you. If you play games more for fun than challenge then it will likely be enough fun to keep going! However while it has souls like elements, don't mistake that for it being hard. It's meant to be challenging if you don't master the elemental mechanics or don't hit the weak points. However using the tools the game gives you will make it easier. In the end, if you prefer a fun combat system that you can feel the benefits of different strategies, than this is for you. If you prefer all strategies to be equally challenging, than this game is NOT for you.GEAR/CRAFTINGSo far this is pretty bare bones. Do not play expecting any robust crafting or gear.RPG ElementsThis game plays similar to how Jedi fallen order plays in this regard. You do not gain levels, you gain "Knowledge" and when you gain enough you can get a skill point. However, unlike that game, you don't seem to loose any knowledge and you pick up purple knowledge cubes to gain it, so while actions themselves might provide this cube, it's not always gained. Therefor, going back and fighting enemies isn't beneficial as many of the smaller ones don't seem to provide any benefit. You also don't seem to be able to restore knowledge you might have lost from dying. However, since the world is so linear, I honestly can't tell if it even takes it away or not between save points. All in all, I wouldn't really call it an RPG in any way. Having skill points isn't really an RPG in my opinion, it's more of a natural progression that is bare minimum if no other progression exists.Overall the game is a fun adventure to have in between all the big hits. I would certainly wait for a sale, but if you like space, science, and want something a bit different than a typical shooter, than this is a great choice. Just keep in mind it is not going to knock your socks off!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  I think the developers have some solid ideas that play out enjoyably enough.  Some feedback:Understanding the enemies and utilizing their elemental weakness allows you to dispatch them very efficiently. The bosses aren't too hard, they do require some puzzle solving to defeat which is enjoyable.  The Alluvial boss is a delight to fight, it's easily the best boss fight in the game.  What makes it enjoyable is it serves as a final test to everything learned in the first biome.  You have to use every tool you've received up to this point, and often in quick succession.  The following bosses feel like... quizzes in comparison which is disappointing.  I think the Neural Parasite was pretty close it just needed a bit more going on with the fight to be great.  The construct is meh.  Audio elements feel a bit flat, should the studio make a sequel this really needs to be improved.  There are a few too many invisible walls for my liking, please try to avoid this going forward.  Character facial animations are Oblivion-tier.  Really need to improve this.  Honestly I really enjoyed this game, if the developers can iterate further upon this game and come out with a more polished sequel, I think they'll have something truly special on their hands.  Just, uh, maybe do some marketing next time.

_childDocuments_.review: To start the video  Above shooter from the Serbian studio Mad Head Games looks like a hybrid of Returnal, Dark Souls and Mass Effect. Is it worth paying attention to such an unusual "cocktail" we tell in the review.When an unidentified space object of clearly alien origin appeared in Earth's orbit, humanity, of course, wanted to get to know it better. For this purpose, the SCAR squad was created, and one of its members was Dr. Kate Ward, the main character of the game. Approaching the object, the spacecraft of the researchers landed in an unknown anomaly. Kate lost consciousness, and woke up already on an unknown planet, surrounded by aggressive monsters and the ruins of an ancient civilization, without the slightest idea how she ended up here. Acquainted with the ghostly figure of a resident of this world, who promised to help her get to the bottom of the truth, the girl went in search of the surviving crew members.The plot, the use of a female protagonist and light interspersed with soullike elements are reminiscent of Returnal, and the visual style also gives a little bit of Mass Effect games. However, this project is not as hardcore as a roguelike shooter from Housemarque, if only because after death we are not returned to the very beginning of the campaign - no, Kate is just reborn near one of the obelisks scattered around the world in abundance. Opponents are resurrected along with her, but the player is not required to run to the monster that killed him to take experience and loot - all this remains with the girl.And in everything Scars Above is so, not special. A generic world with unsurprising biomes (there are countless times we traveled through swamps and alien complexes), the most common combat system, the Dark Souls "bonfire" system seen many times, the mechanics of accelerated weapon reloading peeped from the Gears of War series.However, I don’t want to scold the game for this: it’s well-tailored, all its elements work well, and you don’t get bored throughout the entire passage. If you need a linear action movie for six to eight hours, take a closer look at the project.Reader Rating0 Votes0PlusInteresting, stupid scriptIntense firefightsBeautiful landscapesgood soundtrackMINUSESThe game is completely secondarySometimes there are bugsMy mark 8.5

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game it is clear to me that a lot of dedication went into the game but ultimately, the developers wanted too much. Scars Above is a roughly 7-9 hours singleplayer game. It is pretty linear, has Remnant From The Ashes like fighting and some light puzzle elements. Additionally, it tries to present itself in a cinematic fashion with a lot of cutscenes. And right there the problems start - the animations are really lacking, in every aspect, from the lip syncing to the the combat animations, especially due to the very realistic tone the game tries to set. The gameplay mechanics do work properly but just on a very basic level. Neither the combat nor the puzzles are very interesting or exciting. The levels are designed competently and here and there are some really nice environments, but all in all the world you explore is pretty lifeless.Up to this point, I would say, get it on a sale, but there are some technical problems, especially freezes. The game used to freeze quite often, forcing me to replay stretches of the game several times. At some point I discovered that sprinting into objects/scenery seems to cause this and carefully avoiding that reduced the freezes. But this is not a minor annoyance, but borderlines on breaking the game.In the end, I think the developers should have cut the costs somewhere and focus on fewer features. A good example of how to achieve a game on this scope might be Mortal Shell. No cutscenes, no facial animations, but therefore refined gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: A good and simple game to spend a few hours of your life with!I'd say the game is a souls-like with a sci-fi environment, slighlty reminiscent of Dead Space but more nature oriented. Don't expect the most brain-twisting plot or really deep character development, but not in a bad way. Storytelling is direct and you can get most of the lore if you look around every corner (get the scan upgrade, really important). The maps feel the correct size and the art department did a good job with the colours and ambiance. The models of the enemies look great, the design behind them is cool and you even get some small explanation on why they look like that. Your character will explain a lot of stuff as if she was documenting it, which I found really nice. Didn't find any major bug or problem and it ran pretty well on my computer (8GB RAM, 6GB VRAM).Now for the bad stuff. There isn't much but I'd say some hitboxes are a bit misleading. Thankfully they're not the attack ones but the collision ones, enemies are wider than they appear or at least it feels like it. Fights, despite seeming a duel of wits between you and the mechanics of the game, are more like match color with weapon and shoot the glowy parts. Still, they feel nice and challenging enough to provide a good experience without getting you stuck for 2 days. In general, I'd recommend this game if you're searching for a quick SCI-FI adventure with a simple plot and a not-too-difficult challenge. I give it a 7.5/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, even if very limited. No jump, no possibility to fall, sometimes really bad looking animations. Overall game doesnt look like game from 2023. Invisible walls with huge hitboxes. I was expecting game similar to Tomb Raiders in gameplay or Horizon with linear gameplay. And game is not really like that, but was fun to play after all. Was more like Dark Souls with guns, and few other mechanics that was interesting. Some detective missions, overall was complex enough. Too easy, even on highest difficulty I died like few times in 17 hours. Achievements are too easy also, not challenging at all at this aspect too.Before I buyed this game I read that game crash and have issues, which I thankfully dont had any. Game was running well, with stable fps. And was longer than I expected, at some point I thought I'm gonna finish in like 8 hours. So overall I have my issues and expected a bit more, especially as it is exploration game I expected some climbing or at least some mechanics for moving around, and there is not really. It is my biggest problem here, also falling from height have really bad animation, landing on straight knees, not even try to absorb impact, was really bad looking. Game definitively need more polish in my opinion. Because story and world are really good. I really liked terrain we moved and how it looked, it is really good and creative world. So I give positive review, but game isnt worth full price, but on sale it is interesting enough to check and play. Have to many flaws to be that expensive, but thumb up for effort and idea. With more polish it actually could be great linear game

_childDocuments_.review: Yikes, this one was rough all the way around. The graphics by themselves were not terrible but the character animation... what the hell happened there? I've seen stroke patients with better facial control. The characters don't show expressions so much as have facial tics , It's like they left the animation up to Chat GPT. The combat system is clunky and repetitive, the weapons and their upgrades are very incongruous with the world setting. I found the lack of a map, mini-map, or even a compass to be a very confusing choice with frustrating consequences. Personally I'm not a fan of the "souls-like" save mechanic, I find it to be a very tiresome experience. The lack of a jump feature meant that I had to restart more than once because my character got stuck.  The fact that the description for this games includes:  really makes me want to report them for fraud. I've seen more character development at the bottom of a bottle.  The story is about as coherent as an Ayn Rand novel and yet somehow worse at the same time. I've been more emotionally invested in a game of solitaire. You cannot have the main character rattle off a bunch of large words that sound fancy and go "science!". That's not how that works, it's just a bunch of gibberish that you made up hoping no one would call you on your BS. There was this beautiful opportunity for the exploration and discovery of an alien world and all the creativity that goes along with that. All of that potential squandered and reduced to a few sound clips that honestly sound like they came from a different game.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above isn't going to blow anyone's minds but it's a solid sci-fi action/adventure game with some light Souls/Remnant elements. The story is cool it reminds me of Prometheus which is a favourite of mine, the voice acting is pretty good as well especially the protag and the friendly alien lady but man the facial animations are dated for sure. The visuals in general are really meh but the music and sound effects are awesome so it's a mixed bag. The game definitely has some jank I got stuck a couple of times and had to quit out and the character movement is stiff and awkward. The game it's slow to start but chapter IV and V were the strongest, however the finale chapter is really disappointing, it's mainly just a backtrack thru previous areas leading into a laughable reused enemy as a finale boss encounter. The combat is satisfying each enemy is kinda a mini puzzle figuring out how to kill them efficiently is enjoyable. The gadgets are well designed but clearly one is much more powerful, the "gravity field" once you get this the game becomes pretty easy. Overall for the current sale price it's decent albeit kinda short but I find this type of narrative and gameplay worth while but don't expect anything groundbreaking. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game thinking it would by some mystery RPG something similair to Control or Observation. From start it was but without going into much detail it kinda mellowed out quite quickly. The game it self and mechanics are quite fun different weapons for different monsters and even places/situations kept the game fresh and on my toes. Game isn't that difficult even on the hardest setting, the enemies didn't had really a difficult moveset but still it kept it interesting. Last thing i don't get is the souls-like respawning enemies. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem.Money well spent.It is simply a straight forward story driven adventure sci-fi game, where you are a scientist awaken on an alien planet which is in ruins and you have to find your crew and uncover the mystery behind what happened on the planet. The game is NOT souls like. The only mechanic adapted from souls games is the "bonefire"/pillar save points which if activated, refill your ammo and energy, but respawn enemies. Just pure straight forward gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a game of modest scope and production value but it's fun, feels good and doesn't outstay its welcome. Features:- Souls-like player/monster respawn mechanic, stamina bar used for sprinting, dodging and melee.- "Science shooter" focused on targeting weak points, using the correct weapon and gadgets, taking advantage of the environment.- Unlockable skill tree with free, unlimited respec, some weapon upgrades.- Light puzzles and science themed mini-games.- Fairly linear levels with side areas to explore and shortcuts to unlock.- Pretty fun and interesting boss battles except for the final one which is very recycled.- Somewhat dated visually but still looks nice imo. - A more low tech (by sci-fi standards), down to earth "astronaut" aesthetic and characters. I like it but some might find it bland or vanilla. Scars Above won't blow anyone's mind but its combat mechanics are satisfying, it runs smooth and it's over before it becomes repetative. I guess it's hard to recommend it over Elden Ring or whatever but it deserves better reception than it got imho.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is good, graphic nice and story interesting.The problem is their save system; In that you have only ONE save, there is no autosave, no fallback point, no restart from the beginning of the chapter/map. The game also only save specific game states. And if you somehow had the game gotten saved in a wrong state, then tough luck, you're now locked out of progressing and there's no old saves to revert to.For an example of how to get a broken save state; In the Glacial maps, after you have obtained the two Power Sources and arrived at the two-slots door, put one Source in the door's slot and head back down the ramp to save point. Now exit the game and resume from save. After loading back up, you'll fine yourself with the single Power Source item in inventory, but with the other power source missing from the door and the door remains locked. It is also NOT possible to pick the item up again as the game objects you picked them from can no longer be interacted with!And if any dev actually read this, I will say I still have NOT resolve the issue. I'm going to stop playing unless I got a response+help from custom support. I'd also have asked for refund if it hasn't been more than a few hours already.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a little in, and for the first 2 chapters, the music and atmosphere make it mysterious and thrilling, My heart is pumping sometimes I'm not sure I can take it. It's damn scary and there's no way to really trigger the monsters that jump out in the lake.  The devs have done a Good job so far, but I wasn't sure if I was able to play through the whole game at the time...UPDATE 9/3/23; I've just finished the game. Actually, I did not find the rest of the game Past Chapter 2-3(?) as scary and learned to anticipate when creatures would jump out of the water etc. I even found myself looking forward to these moments (for the mild adrenaline rush when you jump in your chair a little) as my character had the 2 level 4 upgrades (15% more dmg and 15% more dmg resistance) so I was never at risk of dying from these. I actually enjoyed this game quite a bit. It is a decent narrative, with decent weapons, the creatures and bosses weren't overly difficult and obviously the difficulty is something that can be changed. There were some times I missed the save points or had to walk a little bit after respawning, but on the whole, it was just a bit of a nuisance, not a flagrant fail. I generally don't think that only being able to save at Monoliths enhances the experience (although it fits the narrative). Maybe when dying the devs could make it so that you had a choice to load a save game (this feature would have to be added) that saved your resources and health stats OR the choice to respawn at a monolith in which case you would have full ammo, health, and fibre,Also, I found it a bit frustrating that later in the game scanning creatures such as the Fungus-'humanoid' didn't yield any weak points and when I checked the audio and the log it really didn't provide any useful intel - more just a description for the sake of it. It would have been nicer to only have the creature with it's description, strengths, & weaknesses catalogued in your log IF you have scanned the creature purposefully.Thank you to the dev's for making this game and their time and efforts - I really did enjoy it. No gross errors and nothing is going to be perfect. I think it had a 2010 feel to it somehow, where the graphics or character models esp of the advanced alien race, aren't the best, the narrative is simple, straight forward, fun to play, provides challenges along the way, and kept me engaged until the end. (96% achievements 43/45, 2 hidden features not completed.)Well done. I'm Happy with my purchase. It was worth the time and the money. Really hope they continue to improve and develop similar games in the future!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. Solid Sci-Fi narrative experience that experiments with souls-like mechanics, kinda similar in feel to Remnant. Good variety of monsters and biomes. Beautiful art.It's not too long, but keeps a good pace. There is no grind to pace the progression. The combat feels pretty solid and the variety of tools and guns make intuitive sense. It's also really easy to pick up and go. No need for lengthy tutorials, explanations or a half-hour intros for exposition. The default difficulty can be a bit brutal, but the lower settings make things pretty smooth and enjoyable.A lot of people seem to complain about freezes and crashes in recent reviews. Not sure what's up. The game ran solid without any issues, even when alt-tabbing and messing with monitor refresh rates. Windows 11, 7900 xtx here. Consider the refund window if you're having doubts on that front.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to like this game, it's a pretty hard sale.Combat is kinda wonky, there's no real lock on mechanic to incentive use of your melee weapon.  Ammo pretty much never runs out, and if it does, your dead, the character models look terrible, animations are awful, etc.You can tell this is an indie game trying its hardest to be with the big boys.  It works, to a degree, but there's many things within the game as well that show a clear lack of polish, like flickering textures, geometry fusing together, and more.Game has full Dualsense support out of the box, but you have to mod the game to give it the playstation button icons. That being said, I can't recommend this at it's base price.

_childDocuments_.review: Kate is an astronaut and a scientist – not a soldier... I'm glad she lied on the resume, it was the dodge rolls and shoot the glowy thing that saved Humanity.Not the most unique game out there, but it is really good with a simple story, basic exploration, and a space mage combat system where you match elements while switching through a bunch of technology. It is not a completely positive experience either. Player animation and characters are generic, maybe they were generated using UE Metahumans and used as it is. Combat mechanics don't feel responsive enough, a lot of times it felt like I was fumbling around in the UI. For some reason, I hated Kate's ponytail swinging around and into the head like some lantern with bad physics. It was so distracting because I noticed it once and now I can't stop looking and was trying to make it do a 360. Character development for all felt sufficient but not enough to get attached to. The game could have been a lot better because the developers have genuinely put a lot of effort into it and I feel bad because it is also not polished enough to avoid the annoyance. It is just a step or two below from a AAA title because the graphics is really good.I would rate it a 7 out of 10 for the casual players, and recommend not taking the game too seriously like Dark Souls. It is a "Dead Space" like with small nit-picky issues with UI and Combat mechanics, it doesn't come out as responsive which if fixed will make the game more re-playable.

_childDocuments_.review: Games isn't going to win any GOTY awards but is very well done, even if pretty basic.  Sci fi story based 3rd person shooter. Game has a solid story, good character development of the protagonist, pacing,  nice enemy design and fights, especially the bosses, and variety, weapons, gadgets, items, everything pretty well flushed out.  Again, its just basic and not overly complex.  If that kind of thing turns you off you may not enjoy it as much but don't just pass it up with at least looking.  I think this game speaks volumes as far as what we consider acceptable from some of the massive AAA devs out there.  We get countless piles of games on PC that are bug ridden, barely run, poor ports, constantly crash, laggy etc, and have massive multimillion dollar budgets and we are still left unsatisfied.  A game like this comes along, a AA title with AAA aspirations done by a significantly smaller team (Mad Head Games, a smaller susbsidiary of Saber) and I get far more enjoyment out of it.  Game never crashed, ran butter smooth @ 4K Ultra with almost constant 120fps, which is pretty rare for a DX12 UE game.  Is it worth the full sticker price of $39.99?  Debatable.  Had I paid full price I wouldn't have been mad, but buying it from a 3rd party partner for about $26, no brainer.  If 3rd person or sci fi shooters are your thing, give it a go, head in with tempered expectations from a dev standpoint, and I'll bet you walk away happy. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game a few times now, never completing it, but still played several times. I REALLY WANT to LOVE it...but I just can't quite get there. The game is beautiful. It is simple, which I like, sometimes games can be wildly overly complex (and sometimes I like that too, but SCARS Above seems to have found its niche.) The story seems very very interesting, at least for as far as I've reached. The key drawback is the save system and combat. I'm not a real fan of repetition, but the way this game is designed, you repeat, a TON, if you fail to survive a boss (or any other creature). Your resources are very limited, your health is very limted, so you have to approach every single fight with extreme care. You need to be precise, accurate and quick. I don't mind that aspect of the game in general. The problem is, the combat system frequently puts you in situations where you didn't hit EXACTLY the 5 pixel square region you HAD to hit, and therefor your shot had zero effect. Small mobs, big bosses, it doesn't really matter much...if you miss your critical shots, your gonna PAY for it, and if you miss just a few....Well, this is where it really gets frustrating. You restart, way back wherever it was you last had an OPPORTUNITY to save. For the most part, I can get through all the various mobs and little bosses without issue (unless I make a careless mistake with one of the bigger guys). So I'll make it to a final boss in some area, or maybe a group if really fast monsters...make that one fatal mistake... And bam, I'm way back where I started, 20 minutes ago. Every time you respawn, AND every time you choose to save AT a respawn point, ALL the enemies respawn as well. This prevents you from going backwards in the game to a save spot to save, and it can completely screw you if you get to the end of a segment of the game and die for any reason. You then have to repeat not just the mob you died at...you have to repeat that entire segment of the game. Incredibly frustrating.I thin the problem is primarily the save system. You have VERY FEW monoliths where you even can save. The farther into a section of the game you get, the more risk you take on at every turn, every mob, every boss. One mistake costs you more and more and more the farther you get from your last spawn point, and it seems they get less and less frequent as the game progresses. I'm not really a fan of repetition at all in general, but a little bit here or there to master a boss is generally ok for me. But having to repeat entire segments of the game, sometimes over and over and over, just to master a boss, or even just some big baddie? It makes the game extremely difficult to play for very long, when you aren't a big fan of hyper-repetition (there are numerous games that try this, few ever seem to get high ratings from any game rating agency, organization or players in general, as it is rarely done in a way that works. Elden Scroll's bosses may be one of the few cases where it works.) I think the core of the problem is the extremely scarce spawn points, which make progressing difficult, and their scarcity (perhaps increasing scarcity as you move through the game) forces you to repeat THE GAME over, and over, and over. It gets really tedious. If you really love repetition, then SCARS Above is probably just for you. If there was more of an aspect of mastery to the game, vs. just survival and wits, then the repetition might have more of a purpose, and I might be able to swallow it better. As it is, the repetition is rather mindless, excessive, without any real mastery. The bigger monsters and bosses are all rather  line with the overall simple nature of the game. There isn't much depth to them. You just have to be able to survive, use a little bit of wit to nail each one in JUST the right place at JUST the right time, while concurrently avoiding death, to take them down. There isn't much mastery to it, there is just timing and precision. Over and over and over. If the save system was a bit more plentifully populated with save/spawn points, I think that would have mitigated the vast majority of what irks me so much about this game. Its beautiful, the story is interesting, its generally fun in the moment...but the RE-PE-TI-TION. The repetition is insane. I don't want to repeat large swaths of the game over and over and over, just so I can manage my timing and precision a little bit better. There is no real reward for the repetition aspect. None. You just repeat. It puts massive onus on not dying, which itself increases your angst over not dying, which means your gonna die. And repeat. Reducing the amount of repetition would have really helped here. Especially if spawn points were placed more strategically near notably difficult points in the game. Repeating a single fight, eh, ok. Repeating 15 minutes of gameplay over and over BECAUSE of a SINGLE fight, gets extremely old, extremely quickly. So much potential here, so much potential...and I want to just love this game... Its ALMOST there. The save infrequency, the excessive weight put on being hyper accurate and precise in every combat situation, and the constant angst over having to repeat some large swath of the game, takes a lot of the fun out of it. It would be nice to play through the story of the game, without the constant intensity of failing and having to repeat. I think additionally, perhaps a little bit more to winning a fight, perhaps slightly more complexity to the bigger monsters and bosses, would have added something to combat to make it more interesting and fun.There is this fundamental concept in games: The 30 second gameplay loop. SCARS Above doesn't quite get it, I don't think...and the repetition scale, scope and frequency really hurts this games loop. This was one of the same mistakes Anthem made (although, they made others as well)...the 30 second gameplay loop was utterly mindless and insanely boring, with little to no reward for your repetitive efforts. Hopefully Mad Head Games will figure out how to rectify their mistakes here, and the next game will be better.I am going to "recommend" the game, as I am probably more averse to excessive and boring repetition than many others, and there ARE great aspects to this game. I really wish Steam would provide a third option, "On the Fence" or something like that, as that's really where I'm at. I don't really want to overtly recommend the game, but, I don't want to NOT recommend it...the game definitely has its attractive factors!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR. Scars Above is a solid (AA? B?) game with excellent performance, responsive controls, a fun story, and relatively minor flaws. Game Feel. The controls (I played with a Dualsense controller) feel great. Movement and shooting feel very responsive, the guns are punchy and sound strong, and the gadgets are fun & effective. Character upgrades mostly feel good to unlock; I found some to be significantly more useful than others. My main criticism is to do with dodging enemy attacks; the timing simply does not feel right, but is *very* forgiving as long as you dodge early.Combat. Combat is generally fun, but it has some glaring weaknesses. The enemy variety is lackluster, with many variations of the same enemy types, using the same move sets, with simple differences that encourage/require different weapon elemental combinations. It can be frustrating to tease out enemy weak spots (I played on hard difficulty, which fittingly seemed to demand exploiting weak spots). Boss fights are very limited; there's one boss enemy that stands out as good, but I was deeply disappointed by the anticlimactic final fight.Exploration. The world and art design are fantastic -- I think this was my favorite thing about the game. With few exceptions, I was consistently curious what surprises waited around the next corner. Scenic vistas, spooky swamps, gravity-defying landscapes, twisting tunnels... lots of fun. It's not open world, but the pathways loop around and link together with shortcuts.Story & Characters. I found the characters and story to be worthwhile and interesting. The voice acting is great, even though the lip syncing is pretty clunky. Animations are mostly good/okay, but facial expressions can be goofy sometimes. The story ties everything together pretty well, and I was never annoyed or bothered by the narrative.Performance. I have a laptop with an RTX 3060. I had absolutely no problems whatsoever (after the Day 1 Hot Fix that corrected the issue with cutscenes not playing). Extremely stable, high frame rate, fast load times, responsive controls, all at maximum settings. Perfect.Takeaway. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Scars Above. By no means is it perfect; there are minor gripes I have with the limited enemy variety and boss fights, and I wish the facial animations and lip syncing were a bit more polished. Those drawbacks aside, there's plenty here to satisfy someone with reasonable expectations, particularly if (like me) they are someone who enjoys using punchy science-themed guns to cause elemental combos against alien monstrosities, supplemented by physics-bending gadgets and classic i-frame dodging, all to protect your friends and solve the mystery of first contact. I really enjoyed my time with Kate Ward, and hope to see her return in another installment :)

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, a fairly short and simple but generally decent game.Everything is very indie/AA - story, writing, graphics, level design, encounters, bosses, mechanics - and has a bit of an underdeveloped feeling, but it's enough for some casual fun if those things don't bother you. I might recommend waiting for a better sale, though.The game is extremely linear, and each chapter is quite short.  The gameplay is mostly following a linear path to collect the item(s) necessary to unlock a barrier and move to the next area. Combat is entirely scripted encounters, and relies on a simple element-based system (electricity/fire/ice/acid/water/etc).  Enemies and bosses are extremely basic. You unlock abilities along the way, but most don't add very much or change gameplay.  The story aspires to horror, but doesn't really make it.Still, as long as you aren't expecting a big-budget title with high immersion and a great story, this is a fun little game to play for a little bit, and I'm looking forward to their future titles.Also, Mr. Jefferson is adorable and I want one irl.

_childDocuments_.review: Some spoiler-free bulletpoints from my experience with Scars Above:General points:- Decent graphics (except for character expressions) and great ambiance;- Dead Space vibes but with a lot of open environments (like an alien planet). There are a few different biomes including things like swamps, grassy fields, snowy mountains and underground caves;- There's no map, but honestly you don't need one. This game is a mostly linear experience with light backtracking at times and some partially hidden short paths for additional resources and xp. That is to say: The game does reward exploration, though there isn't much to explore;- Voice-acting is decent (main character is good, while other characters are mostly mid);Gameplay-wise:- Smooth and satisfying gameplay;- 3rd-person shooter where you can't shoot from the hip, you need to aim to shoot (otherwise you will perform a melee strike) - the gunplay is simple but solid enough considering it's not the game's focus;- Simple puzzles like hitting color-coded targets with specific elements are abundant;- Some souls-like mechanics in there as well, like a focus on timed dodging for defense, bonfire-like savepoints that reset most mobs while saving and regenerating your health as well as recovery items, opening shortcuts between areas and so on. Though this game is not very difficult in general (even on hard mode). For instance, although the inventory layout carries the aesthetics of a survival horror game like Resident Evil, there's no real need for inventory management in any way, items just have their own place regardless. There's also not really any shortage of resources for most of the game, especially ammo, which is abundant in most areas.- Boss fights are entertaining enough for a first playthrough. As said above, not very challenging difficulty even on hard mode, combat is mostly centered around simple puzzles like color-coded weakspots and having to cycle through your gear to combine elemental effects, straightforward environmental interactions and so on.Conclusion:A well polished Dead Space meets Dark Souls AA game. I had fun and would easily recommend it. Replayability is limited, but definitely an entertaining experience. Probably better to get it during a sale, the game is a bit too short for the pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a great sci-fi action TPS with a good, intriguing story, a sympathetic and competent main character, which is very rare these days, some difficult, but not impossible boss battles, a visually great environment, and plenty of enemy types to clash with. Only the balancing may need a little polishing as at the beginning it's too hard, in the last two chapters it's almost too easy if you max out your character traits. Some compared this game with Returnal. I played the two games parallel with each other and I liked Scars Above much better, regardless of its much more linear. The spacing of the story and the difficulty level is much friendlier in Scars Above. The game itself is about 8-9 hours to complete, but I enjoyed every minute of it (Except for two boss battles, which were a bit hard in the first two chapters.). So I can highly recommend Scars Above. Oh, and its music has a Mass Effect vibe and atmosphere, which was a huge plus to me. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Strong points :- A story that can be enjoyed from start to finish...- Gameplay with well-oiled mechanics- Pleasant, more strategic and less nervous confrontations- A challenge that keeps its promises during the first half of the adventure...- A classic but effective level design- An intriguing universe with a scary atmosphere that gives the game a certain charm- Weak points :- …Despite an unoriginal narration and a simplistic staging lacking in finish- A bestiary that struggles to make an impression- A graphics engine that quickly shows its limits- An AA status preventing the title from exploiting its full potential- … But less during the second- Introductory price may be a bit expensive in view of the quality of the experience offered (between 40 and 50€ depending on the platform)- Small tweaking issues Summary : Carried by a sympathetic story but without great surprise, a well-oiled TPS/action-adventure/Souls-light gameplay and an immersive universe which only asks to be exploited more, Scars Above is a good game victim of the chains visible to many current AA productions. This is really unfortunate because, with more time and resources, there is no doubt that there was a way for this new license to do better while being more ambitious in the depth and quality of the experience it offers.14/20

_childDocuments_.review: Generally A Great Game8/10I really enjoyed this game throughout. The combat and weapons worked well together, the exploration and level design was unique and interesting & the upgrade system was well implemented. The game also gives you a lot of interesting "gadgets" to use that really allows you to customize your game play. Again, a really well implemented option that adds to and works well with the combat. This game comes together well, and I would recommend it without hesitations.There were a few issues that got to me at times though. The second Boss Fight makes you slowly walk (like crawl) up to the area to trigger the fight. It takes a good minute plus to go from the check point to the actual battle. Given the fact you are probably going to die a few times, this becomes very tedious and honestly just sucks. It's pretty dumb that the devs designed it this way. There are also some encounters that lock you into place and essentially get you "stuck". One in particular is later in the game, in a very confined spaced where 4 large monsters attack you at once. It's just poor level design and seems kinda like an amateur move that's comes across as a lazy difficult encounter than one that actually requiers skill. I wish the game was a little longer and had a few more boss fights. as well as some more options for upgrades, like having the fire gun charge faster. I ended up completely upgrading my character and finishing the game with multiple skill points i couldn't use.  That being said, I was surprised how much I enjoyed this game. Glad I bought it, considering some of the reviews out there weren't so positive. They were wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the aesthetic and mood of the Prometheus (Ridley Scott) movies. For some reason, the environments in this game (especially interiors) reminded me of those movies and I loved it. The central plot premise is also very similar to one of the plot elements in the films, which makes me wonder if the creators of this game were specifically inspired and influenced by those movies.But besides that, the combat is engaging and fast-paced enough to not get boring throughout the whole game. The voice acting is pretty good. Environments are beautifully eerie. The music is minimal and ambient, making it a great fit to the existing mood.Main downside is the level up system. It feels immersion-breaking. It seems like a lazy design.  I know people seem to be complaining about the length but it was perfect for me. I have a full-time job and hobbies. Games of this length are perfect since they arent a huge commitment and don't take forever to slog through.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a fan mod for Mass Effect: Andromeda. There are moments when you're sprinting over an alien landscape and that synth-heavy soundtrack comes in where I almost, almost had a feeling - and that feeling was 'hey, I should play Mass Effect 1 again". The character models are all ugly androids, they do those crazy random gestures while talking because HuMaN, the cutscenes are overly pretentious, and the dialogue is clunky and banal. It's 'hard' in a completley unfulfilling sense; even on the lowest difficulty enemies will two-hit you, and they pop out of the ground as if it were a rail shooter. When you die, you will go back to the last checkpoint - and all the enemies will respawn *in exactly the same places*. At least you've got some variety in your weapons; I made it nearly an hour in and so I got both the blue gun AND the red gun. The blue gun is for shooting blue enemies. The red gun is for shooting red enemies. You'll get the hang of it.I played one session and then requested a refund because I can't imagine ever being bored enough to come back to this.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is good for what it is. The idea behind the plot is really good and I liked how different it was. The environments were phenomenal in this game and is one of the games strong suits. The characters are well written mostly. The alien designs are great. However it falls flat when it comes to combat. It is quite clunky. The weapons are cool but have very little difference in terms of fun. There are element mechanics for killing certain enemies, but nothing to amazing. The design of the enemies were really good too. Each of them looked unique but in terms of combat again nothing too exciting. I had an issue that was bugging me for most of the game that I couldn't put a finger on and figured it out near the end on one of the cutscenes. Its the facial animations or any of the human animations. They do not feel right or look right at all. You don't notice it at first, but after awhile it gets kind of irritating. Another complaint I have is that some points in the game the characters would talk for a whole 3 minutes and you couldn't do anything in game besides walk around. And the end boss was the biggest disappointment. The whole game you are led up to the antagonist. He looks really cool but you don't actually fight him. You fight a somewhat copy paste of a standard enemy. The boss midway in the game was really cool and fun and was better than the final boss. Having the end boss be disappointing was kind of a let down. The game in all told the story really well as a scifi like game and had a really fun vision, but falls flat when it comes to the end boss, human animations, and a clunky combat system. If this game was refined a little more it would have been perfect.
