_childDocuments_.review: Update after beating the game:This game is meant to be hard, the regular enemies were harder than the bosses. You want to explore in this game. I had all skills unlocked towards the end of the game. The combos you can pull off our fun and feel great. Anyone complaining about killing mobs to get to a boss after dying did not fully explore the area to open up paths for easy saves to get back to the boss. You have to be careful on stamina, make the wise combo choices for killing enemies. 10hrs to beat a game in my book is perfect on the hardest setting. I got burnt out on Hogwarts around level 30. Jumped over this game and i'm glade I did.Zero issues with FPS, played perfectly with everything maxed at 4k 60fps. I hope they continue the story! I'd purchase another run through of new content using these mechanics. OG:Played the demo twice. Saw huge improvements between demos. Now after playing the full game, i'm happy with my purchase. The feeling you get when you perform a combo on the enemies is awesome. It's raining shoot them with frost gun, then shoot them with lightning gun tons of damage. If they are caught on fire shoot them with a lightning gun for extra damage. You can even shoot the enemy bullets so they don't hit you or yes you can dodge which works perfectly for me. Playing on a 13900k/4090 at a solid 60fps with Ultra settings at 4k. I have not had any issues with dodging and being hit. If I didn't dodge I got hit. If i dodged into another enemies attack i got hit. If I dodged successfully away from enemies nothing hit me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very brave to be a small studio and try to develop a sci-fi epic. Scars above is an interesting 10 hour long game that gets much better in the second half than it is at the beginning. The beginning feels empty of content and you are not really sure whether the game deserves the effort. But, as you progress all the game system's come together to create a very satisfactory experience in the end. Story is fairly safe and common in Sci-fi. Get some Prometheus aliens, sprinkle some Rama into the mix and round it up with some rogue AI. Luckily, it is well rounded up story that, although not revolutionary, does not hurt the experience at all.Visuals lack experienced craftsmanship and the animation work in both cutscenes and dialogues feels like a student project at times. However, as you discover more of the game there are truly some remarkable looking environments and enemy design and animation feels great.Combat felt interesting with trying to match the best element to counter specific enemies. Gadgets were fun to use and, yet once more, it felt like ti was a really mediocre experience at first, but by the end I yearned for more bosses and encounters. Same goes for level design that is reminiscent of Dark Souls design that comes to its full potential in the last fifth of the game. Overall I'd recommend the game especially to people wanting to support new studios. The price might be a little too high, but for a discount the game would justify its price.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game was really fun and enjoyable. I found the story interesting and the gameplay is varied enough that it doesn't tend to feel like it's too much of one thing and not enough of another, though it does tend more towards combat than puzzle-solving. The voice acting is reasonable for a game of this size and budget, and it's better than some I've heard in bigger games.It's not perfect, however. The cinematics seem to be rendered at a low resolution and can be quite jarring, they would have generally been much better if they had taken place in the engine with the game's assets. The early hour or two of the game is disproportionately difficult compared to the later stages which seem to just get easier and easier. The pacing of upgrades and knowledge (how the game rewards XP for ability upgrades) is also a little rushed towards the end and I ended up with 11 or 12 surplus ability points by the end after completing the whole ability tree. If you want a short game with an interesting story, I think you could do much worse than getting Scars Above, and I would like to see this game get a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are into high-level sci-fi story-telling, you'll enjoy Scars Above. Is it perfect when it comes to game mechanics, development, cinematics, and controls, no. But it's on par for what's out there coming from smaller studios that have a lot of young talent with plenty of room for growth.Sure, the controls aren't super smooth, and the speech during cut scenes is out of whack with the characters lips from time to time, or you might get stuck in a location resulting in you needing to revert back to your last save point to continue on, but it's nothing that is game breaking. You'll still enjoy the experience and the story if space odysseys is your thing.Would I recommend it, yes! The story keeps you engaged, the visuals are stunning, and the world-building is on point for an alien planet with creepy creatures. The dialog isn't too shabby either. There wasn't any overt cliche lines that are over used, the information is easy to follow, and they're smart with their science.One thing I could say about Scars Above is that if it was developed by a really big studio this would be a top-tier game. But with the studio that developed it, it certainly stands on its own as a good overall sci-fi game with a few kinks that could be ironed out, so it being on par is good enough for me.The whole team should be proud of their work too! Everyone involved put a lot of care into making this and I wouldn't mind checking out more from them in the future. With eyes wide open, much can be enjoyed in the universe we live in.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth $40 as there's too much jank, complete lack of polish. Your character will at times clip through world geometry, other times will be blocked when you wouldn't expect it. It lets you pick up XP beyond the point where it's of any use and leaves a permanent UI reminder that you have XP to spend from then on (which is easy to reach at least on medium/Specialist difficulty).It's a shame too as the game does look pretty at times (even if it doesn't support HDR which would be perfect for some scenes), it just feels that they didn't bother to clean up animations, add some more variety in the enemies or at least how you approach them, and didn't bother to ease you into the story in a way that would make you care about the characters, particularly at the beginning. The facial and overall animations are also stiff as well, no motion capture here it seems.The main combat loop is fun though, even if it gets repetitive. It's at its best when it's forcing you to pick the right weapon (or ammo) for each encounter, forcing you to prioritize your targets in some (not enough) encounters, and maintaining tension at certain points (there's a particular enemy that likes to ambush you that the games still allows you to avoid damage on if you're quick, and a mechanic where certain enemies can be taken out if you're quick to react when you first spot them). I'd still recommend it at $20 or lower, but at the current price of $40 I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I was really looking forward to the release of this video game.On the other hand, I want to leave my constructive criticism about "Scars Above".I'm a big fan of Souls Like Shooter and this is not, it's not worth it at all. It is not worth at all the 40€ that they ask for in Spain, at most 20€ and really not even that.I understand or I want to understand that it is a small studio and that is why it has so many shortcomings.First of all, both the monsters and the animations are very crude, they barely have different movements.The cinematics are tremendously out of context, they lack a lot of strength to the story.The map is totally linear, only one path with 2 options (sometimes) and once you pass the area you unlock the door to pass the area faster. This way constantly.The gameplay is literally horrible, the "Spanish" translation voices are not funny at all. I hope that in English the voice is not as neutral as here.On the other hand the penalty for death and pillars, even in another type of souls the penalty is not so great as to redo again practically 10 minutes of games.Weapons are very unbalanced, the item system is not well implemented, you can only do a couple of combos, as long as you don't feel like using EVA and kill anything at any time.The machete is not worth anything, it's ridiculous (playing in commander).The two skill branches add nothing, the upgrades are ridiculous.The music does not go in context with the game itself, it lacks a lot of desire.Due to all these problems, the game is not fun at all, with this I do not mean that it is not playable, but if it is making me very difficult to continue and not precisely because the difficulty of the game does not allow me but all the problems and errors that this has.As far as I can see there is no NG+ mode to complete achievements or free world to perform such actions.I don't feel like starting a game like this again, I'm really sorry.It literally looks like they have taken the graphic engine, created 4 maps implemented 3 assets 1 mechanic and run.I was holding on and on until the game crashed.I've had the bug with the sound of the girl shivering from the ice zone.I have had another bug in a puzzle system with the core which the piece that rotates automatically changed from red to blue and did not match the wall.I am very unhappy with this game I really tell you.There are enemies that literally barely change, they ARE SKIN CHANGERS, they have 2 attacks.IT PULLS A CRAFTING TABLE OUT OF NOWHERE THAT DOESN'T EVEN EXIST, IT'S JUST IN YOUR MIND.It is not an enjoyable game, it doesn't say anything, it doesn't transmit anything, it moves forward, moves forward, moves backwards 15 minutes.The cinematics last SECONDS, they have no introduction part, they are ridiculous, the main character has no feelings, it is an asset of "Tomb Raider - Lara Croft" Literally.WE ARE USED TO DEVELOPERS RELEASING UNFINISHED GAMES WITH SEVERE PROBLEMS AND WE, THE PLAYERS, HAVE TO PUT UP WITH THESE PROBLEMS.I have not said anything that is not the reality today, this is how the game is.Remnant from the ashes does not come from a "Big Company" the budget was infimum due to economic problems within the same company.And that if it is an example to follow, to get something like this give much more love.This is my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, at least this game will almost certainly become famous for the goofiest, laziest, boss creature ever to be ill-conceived.  I don't mean the boss is lazy, though it does waddle in circles like a giant clam on stilts.  I mean the developers were lazy in every aspect of its design, animation, conception, reason for existing, etc.   Yes, I'm referring to the (soon to be) infamous 'HamburGroot'; a 15-foot-tall stick-figure Groot with a giant Portabella mushroom burger head... with chicken feet?Clearly the whole 'genetic mutation' theme was provided more out of necessity as an excuse for poor design than it was required as a plot point.  "This thing looks stoooopid, man!"  "Dude! Who cares! It's a mutant!"To be fair, the laziness and incompleteness is at least consistent throughout the creature and player design/animations… In a dimension of selective physics and anatomy, where feet suddenly become disconnected from the ground and magically hover and slide into place after stiffening into '1st position'.  But even among the rest of the goofball ensemble of this game, or every enemy in every other indie game in existence for that matter, HamburGroot 'sticks’ out.The creature looks like it might have the usual leg and arm joints, as a two-year-old could draw them, but apparently even those must have been too much for the animation team, apparently abandoning the bone concept altogether to let it waddle around like a scarecrow in a full body cast... made of seaweed?  In fact, the creature is so pitiful and pathetic, that when it came time to try and give this thing some kind of attack (and to avoid complete humiliation from players and fellow designers alike), the only possible solution was 'blindness'.  And perhaps deafness as well since I don't recall this 15-foot-tall walking wood pile making so much as a peep...Yup, as soon as you see the HamburGroot, you don't.  Somehow, out of nowhere, it instantly blinds the player with a green fog.... spores(?)… which lasts for an inordinate amount of time, leaving the player with no other strategy than to waste ammo into the green void.  As an added attack effect, and to achieve complete disorientation and incapacitation of the player, the fog then seems to somehow attach itself to the player, so that even as the player turns their body to attempt to gain bearings, the fog turns with them... making it impossible to tell if your character is even moving at all.  I think the devs literally just place a semitransparent green plane in front of the players FOV to create the ‘spore fog’ effect… just insanely lazy.  You literally see nothing but green; no breaks or density in the fog, no floors or walls or any surroundings.  Yet it is certainly highly effective at blocking the player from ever seeing the pathetic HamburGroot itself... as they are simultaneously tasked with somehow defeating it.Occasionally, while 'battling' HamburGroot, random green lines appear in the sky or orange circles appear on the ground.   I have no idea what these are?  Presumably these are (elemental?) condiments emitting from the HamburGroot?  I think these shapes cause damage(?) I mean I died while otherwise completely blind, so I assume they did?The saddest part is that the game does start off with some hints of promise as it begins to reveal its overall 'plan' and 'formula'... it's clear the devs thought a lot about what they wanted the game to be.  The elemental weapons and weaknesses provide some interesting ingredients for a much better game than this managed to be... nothing new here, but certainly stuff that could work well if it were only given the proper environment in which to flourish.  However, it becomes clearer early on, that the game is only ever a bland and half-baked version of what it wanted to be.  I was really 'rooting' for this game... I really wanted to like it, but I cannot in good faith recommend it.  Not even a 'maybe on sale?' caveat, as you'll just end up sorely dissatisfied, jonesing for the game it teased you about and pretended to be.  It's a real shame because it does have the occasional 'cool' factor that leaves you wondering 'if only...' that magical thing would happen, but it never does... and it just gets worse, not better, as it’s better instincts are abandoned and disappointment sinks in.One can only hope the devs aren't so badly humiliated by the legacy of HamburGroot that they flee off the grid forever, and instead, pick themselves up, take what's left of the good ingredients here, head back to the kitchen, and cook up a bigger/better (fully baked) dish.HamburGroot:

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice sci-fi story 3rd person shooter game. I’ve played the game on medium difficulty (Specialist), and this was the right setting for me, as I was looking more for a story driven game but also with some difficulty in the shooting. As is stands, the game is easy on regular enemies but is very hard on boss fights, which I find balanced. On a nutshell, you are a scientist on a first contact mission on an object that appear above earth orbit, and from that point on, the story unfolds in a compelling, way, with some twists, sufficiently engaging. The sound track is right on track, but the game graphics seams not well optimized and on a non-gaming PC, it often drops the FPS to a very low setting, and the cutoff scenes are not of the best quality. Still, a nice sci-fi story, not a lot of replay ability value, but still worth to buy on sale, not a typical shooter game, but I would give 8/10 (mainly for the sci-fi setting).

_childDocuments_.review: Scars above is a sci-fi 3rd person shooter set on an alien world where your space ship has crashed and you managed to survive and all of your crew members are missing.You awake on a dreary planet filled with hostile aliens and a spirit that seems to want to guide you somewhere. You eventually learn that you were purposely brought to that planet to be part of a large experiment that is going to change all of life itself.This game looks great graphically, and the alien world goes from rainy and fog, to bright open areas, snowy landscapes, futuristic bunkers, and straight to the depths of hell.Oddly enough the facial textures of the human characters don’t look nearly as good as the aliens or the world itself. It’s not terrible but could have used some tweaking and cleaner textures.The voice acting is really good, Far better than most games and the game world is filled with ambient sounds that blend nice when exploring.You get 4 weapons that are somewhat futuristic that consist of electric, fire, ice, and poison. Most enemies are weak to certain elements and will damage them much faster. You also have powers that can cast barriers, make holograms, slow time, and heal.This game can be rather difficult at times and will throw an army of enemies at you that will kill you in seconds. There were spots I was stuck at that took multiple attempts before I figured out the best method to killing them. This is not a game where you can pick story mode and breeze through it.  I though this game was great. I wish it were longer and took about 14hrs to complete and get 100% achievements. The story was very interesting and kept me playing.I played this on a steam deck and it ran between 45-60 fps. Solid game and extremely underrated 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: After a few hours in, I can already say the game was definitely worth a buy!The story is actually interesting and pulls you right in from the start, and the environment and visuals overall are pretty good and rather stunning. All this makes it really fun to roam around searching for all the clues trying to peace the story together - that is until you stumble upon some gnarly creature trying to kill you in all so many creative ways.Speaking of which - the combat mechanics were a nice surprise, because for a change we get to play as an actual scientist and not some typical brawns-over-brains dude and go Rambo on everything, so instead we need to use our noggin to get through the puzzles and also through the more challenging fights, which was surprisingly refreshing.And yeah, the characters' might have the level of facial expressions of an over-botoxed celebrity, but let's face it (pun intended) we only notice it during a couple of cutscenes, while the devs went all out with the world, the monsters and all the cool gadgets, and most importantly the game is super snappy.All in all, it's a fun little game from an indie studio that is definitely worth a shot, and I honestly can't wait to see how the story continues. So if you are a fan of the genre I would recommend you give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a Dark Souls-style checkpoint system so that's already a massive red flag for anyone who values their time. And while the core gameplay loop is fun, the very first boss fight (or was it second one?) already tells you all you need to know. Not only is it an insane difficulty spike after a fairly relaxing first eara, but it also has area denial that you cannot permanently remove or avoid, and have to switch between mitigating it and actually shooting the enemy every 2 seconds (yeah, they are two different actions).If this is the kind of crap developers put at the beginning of the game, I don't want to know what they do later. If you are looking to waste time on this, for the story, pick it up on sale or something. It's kind of a shame because it otherwise seems like a fun game, at least the combat loop is fun (when there is no area denial) and the story has enough intrigue to keep you going. But for some reason developers decided to shoot themselves in the foot by adding unavoidable area denial to the first boss and using a DS-style checkpoint system to their otherwise pretty fine game.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game, finished it. It was not long, about 10 hours altogether and that is with short breaks and trying to explore everything. Right from the beginning, the game gave me vibes of the classic point and click adventure/quest game "The Dig" from the mid 1990's.I liked the story, it was interesting, but I did not find the game to be scary, or part of the horror genre, but more of a cosmic horror, although, again, I would not classify it as horror - if you think that this is anything like Dead Space, it is not, it is more of a rated E type of a horror game.Combat is very basic, and you do use the same weapon with different configurations throughout the game which does give the illusion of different weapons and combos you can use, so it was alright.I had a problem, although fairly minimal, with the fact that the game is very linear, rather than be an open world where you could run all over and figure things out as you go - the linear part made it rather easy and the exploration, although interesting, could have been funner (is that a word?).The animations were alright, 95% of the time. Jumping off a ledge has no animation so it looks like you are falling, but other than that, it was ok. It did not bug me though, I just thought it was an odd choice to not include it in, or put some work on such a small detail.There are way more collectible skill points than you need, which makes the game and the skill points build sort of redundant at some point and not very meaningful. I maxed my skills out around 60% into the game.Overall, it is not perfect, sometimes a bit buggy - I got stuck in a transition area, trying to move under some roots and had to try and move around until it finally kicked me back out, but it is entertaining if you are into space adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: SCARS Above initially caught my attention because of its aesthetics - the similarities to Masterpieces like RETURNAL and 2001: A Space Odyssey are, indeed, striking. What I found during my 20 hours of playing (three playthroughs in order to review and create content) is an utterly enjoyable experience, crafted with dedication and respect towards the consumer. It's not going to turn any heads with its tech, but the artistic direction and sound design are sublime. It's also extremely well-written and voice-acted, something we rarely see in smaller productions. After Asterigos: Curse of The Stars, SCARS is one of my favorite indies coming out of a new studio. Comes highly recommended. - FiOth

_childDocuments_.review: This is just my personal opinion and doesn't claim to be a complete or balanced review: There's several points that came to my attention even without intentionally looking to write a review for this game. STORY:The story is just too flat / linear. You can basically guess the whole plot by the end of the first quarter. And unfortunately, there are no plot twists to surprise.The characters appear 2-dimensional and have little to no development. From the trailer, I was hoping to get some loreBUGS: As of this review, the cutscenes-bug remained - even though a hotfix-release was published.Cutscenes will freeze after a few frames, and Audio will get scattered and delayed to the point of being incomprehensible.I basically had to view the cutscenes via YouTube everytime I got to one to understand what was happening. For a game that can be played in two day's time / over the weekend, this is quite annoying - especially since the cutscenes encompass pretty much all of the big story moments, or are announcing boss fights. I once also clipped through the floor while trying to pass through a bush to enter the next region, because I was slightly elevated, standing on frozen water. Nothing too annoying, but it shows the limits of the game design quality imo.GAMEPLAY:At first, I found the gameplay to be quite challenging - especially with a gamepad. The tools and gadgets just seem unintuitive at first. I had to switch difficulty after dying multiple times against some very basic mobs. Then, after a while, and after continuing with Keyboard and Mouse, I got the hang of it. But very soon, the fights were getting way too easy. To be honest, I didn't change the difficulty again at this point, as I was more interested in the story anyway. But the gameplay just felt a bit rough or unbalanced. Riddles and puzzles are few and very easy, prompting the question why they were even included at some times. LEVEL DESIGN:The levels seem maze-like at first, but soon turn out to be quite linear. There are a few "hidden" areas here and there, but simply by looking out for them, I got all on the first try. With the scanner update you can get later in the game, there's little left to be discovered. The Biomes offer nice graphics upon first contact, but over time they feel a little monotonous and repetitive.GRAPHICS:This was probably the biggest disappointment. I played the game on highest graphics. In general, the graphics are okay, through I would say definitely not up to current standard.But the meshes of the environmental model are sometimes so rough that you cannot overlook it - again, I wasn't looking for this, it just sprang to eye. The worst were the waterfalls, which could as well have been copied from a 90s video game.OVERALL: Overall, the trailer promised more than what was delivered. I would say it's an okay 12-hour main story game. But even with reduced expectations, I found it to be too disappointing and barely worth the 33,99 € that I payed for it.I am sure the developers did the best they could with what was available. But it just feels like the game was forced to finish or cut short, or simply not given the time to develop its full potential. My personal rating: 4/10Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with "ok" graphics and an enjoyable story.The game is simple and linear, but I enjoy the journey. As the story goes on, you start to discover more and more of what happens with your crew.Gameplay:I have played on the medium-difficult, and I think you should go for the Hard on your first playthrough as the game is easy after you discover how to use the right weapon for the right enemy.You have one weapon that gets an elemental upgrade throughout the game, and the gameplay is based on matching your weapon type to the weak point of the enemy and sometimes combining elements to gain bonus damage because of the combined effect.Graphics:The game's graphic is "OK" and is similar to loads of other games made on Unreal Engine 4. The game lacks refined animations when jumping from a high place or falling. There were some moments that they could give the character animation of sliding down a hill or something like that instead of having your character just walking down a steep hill like there was no problem at all.The weapons and combat animations are excellent and responsive.One of the problems for me is the quality of the cut scenes. The voices are great, but the animation takes you out of the scene with characters without any expression and sometimes with a blank face that loses the entire purpose of the scene and the excellent voice acting.Sound:This is a part of the game that I enjoyed. The sound of the items and gunshots as the recharge sounds are great. The enemies have some generic sounds, but nothing terrible. But what's really good is the soundtrack, with highs and lows eating the right moments, which complements the narrative and the scene's intensity.With 10 to 13 hours of gameplay, this game is worth your time. It's a good game, and I recommend waiting for a sale to get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say first, I enjoyed parts of it, but it, overall, was not worth even the $20 I spent on it. I feel like everyone who purchased this game felt like it was going to be something grander than what they got, which is partly on the marketing and partly on us as players. Still, the basic combat loop and puzzle mechanics were fun to an extent, but honestly, not worth my time, which I feel bad saying because I like the atmosphere and the general design of the game's environments, enemies, and story. There were many needless parts during the first 2 hours, too, where you would have to complete a puzzle by just looking at an item and pressing a button. It felt very annoying, honestly, and I wished that there would've just been a cut scene or something instead. It feels like it is trying to be both Dark Souls and Halo, and just not meeting up to the standards of either. It somehow felt both completely unique and extraordinarily generic at the same time, and I don't know how to put it into words better than that.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo of this back in 2022 and it was decently fun. Sci-fi horror with your basic boss-fights and different enemy types, it was fun but nothing special. I grabbed the release this year once it was on sale for below 10 dollars and decided to blast through it in a week, wanting to feed my sci-fi fix. Unfortunately for the game, its about as barebones as you can get. With a relative runtime of around 7-8 hours, I constantly found myself fighting the same enemies over and over with the same weapons. The story had promise, but ultimately fell flat along with the gameplay with little to no emotional impact or stakes. The only reason I didn't drop the game and just move on was because I was hanging out with friends on discord and we were laughing at the game together and I figured "eh what the heck, its not that long. I might as well finish it." I try not to dump on smaller devs because I know how much work goes into it, but I can't really recommend the game. It wasn't the worst game I've ever played, but there's really nothing that stands out for it and unless its on super sale, You're better off trying some other game. 30 dollars is way too much for this game

_childDocuments_.review: But in all seriousness, don't expect a blockbuster or anything like that. However, at the same time, don't expect anything resembling an indie title either because this is actually one of those rare instances where the devs hit the "sweet spot" with a small-ish passion project which landed their game in between the "AAA" and "indie" market and resulted in an overall more than decent experience.And on that note, the game itself has a rather intriguing story set on a very interesting planet with some good mechanics, adequate graphics and awesome vibes and atmosphere behind it all.Personally, I 100%-ed it in roughly 7 hours while taking my time and not rushing any part of it and I honestly enjoyed the overall experience that it had to offer. Fingers crossed for a sequel. - Ever wondered what would happen if Mass Effect, Tomb Raider, Lost Planet, Dead Space, Returnal and Dark Souls had an orgy while doing cocaine, speed and ecstasy? Well wonder no more - just play the game and get your answer!

_childDocuments_.review: This was an enjoyable game!The story is interesting, combat is good enough (particularly boss fights; looking at you Construct), the puzzles are a nice change of pace from shooting things and the graphics are solid.There were some minor performance issues (fps drops) and I would prefer some kind of a story twist, but these aren't huge issues. Scars Above doesn't try to punch above its "weight class" by pretending to be an epic sci-fi opera with megalomaniac aspirations and I salute it for it.I really hope there's going to be a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a soulslike, and I hate soulslike games. But the story is surprisingly interesting so I can recommend it to soulslike-haters like myself if you get cheats for it. I know it is not the intended way to play it, but when you even struggle on the easiest of difficulty levels despite being usually not too bad in third person games, it is either refund or using cheats. I'm glad I decided for the latter.Harsh difficulty level aside:The game has quite good graphics and as mentioned the story is also very enjoyable. The combat is fun too, when you adjusted it to your taste. Soulslike fans can grab this game without hesitation.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, had a story-feel similar to Outriders but without loot and classes.It is very short for a 40 euro's game (7-8 hours for me) but fun nonetheless.This definitely should have some kind of endgame to it, although that would be kind of weird without loot.The bossfights are quite cool, and as they said they took mechanics from different games, most fights have got a Resident Evil type of mechanic, where you shoot parts of the body to weaken 'em. The elemental-weapons are a welcoming twist.There's a decent amount of dialogue which doesn't interrupt your playing. Cut scenes can be skipped (y) but don't take too long and are interesting for the story.I recommend this game anyway despite the price-to-length ratio.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is decent. It's about what I expected for the price.Gameplay is fun, story is decent and it looks nice enough.Other games Scars Above reminds me of when I play it:It reminds me of Destiny 2(as of this review The Final Shape has not released.) From what we've seen in the trailer for The Final Shape expansion, this game is a reskin of that. Literally there's a giant triangle in the sky in this world to.It reminds me of Metroid Prime. It gives you four different guns that do different elements and have purposes in the game world to explore and fight simultaneously. It provides various gadgets to help in fights and exploration. Some of the guns also get alternate firing modes. I swear she's just a knockoff Samus.It reminds me of Far Point. It feels like a story reskin of Far Point right in the intro, but I liked that game so I don't really care. If you've played it, you'll get what I mean.It reminds me of Returnal. Honestly it's the first biome mostly. Also the way she is resurrected and it is acknowledged in the story. This ones a bit of stretch though since this game does it differently.It reminds me of Dark So-... Wait. No, never mind, no it doesn't. I haven't felt an actual penalty to my deaths yet aside from respawns and lore items. The pillars(bonfires) refill ammo to max even though they say the will fill a "limited amount." Ammo upgrades don't change that.Biggest complaints I have about it: The animations in cut scenes are kinda janky. The characters don't move in a natural way a lot and the mouths don't always match the words. ...but then sometimes they do. It seems to be character specific who can speak with a semi-realistic mouth animation and who just goes :O :I :O :IIt could be better at saving items when you die. I don't mean consumables or anything that would add/remove difficulty of the game; I mean voice logs and stuff like that. I just find it annoying to have to go pick up a voice log again that I already found and isn't providing me with any benefit other than story context/lore. You could just listen to again anyway because there's a log menu when you pause the game, so it just creates unnecessary work on the player. This one might be a bug though.All and all, I don't really have much to say about it that's bad. It could really just use a heavy layer of polish in my opinion. If it were a AAA title I'd ♥♥♥♥ on it, but that's not the case here, I think they did a good job but just need to refine it a little.I would personally would say it's worth the full price tag if you're unsure, but it's definitely something to pick up if you see it on sale.Edit: Oh! And Kate has some dumb lines sometimes along with just overlooked writing flaws. It's all super minor stuff, but just sometimes I facepalm. This super intelligent hand picked scientist to make first contact with alien tech has 0 situational awareness sometimes. Meanwhile, I quit school before I got into Highschool and I know what's happening immediately. Bruh, we're doomed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play itself is not bad. Multiple 'elemental' weapons to leverage against enemies. Each enemy has its own weakness to exploit, so combat isn't to bad. Dodging is a little clunky compared to Dark Souls/Bloodborne though. Some of the big boss fights have unique mechanics. I'd def recommend figuring it out yourself. I will say that the game doesn't hold your hand completely. Make sure you read your scans and listen you character dialog. My one gripe is that the game completely freezes if you run into an invisible wall or hit terrain that you can't walk/run over. Its happened to me a number of times and caused me to lose a bit of progress here and there between "bonfires".

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence about buying this game, but gave in and I was so glad that I did.  This game takes place on a beautifully crafted alien world.  The game play was smooth on ultra graphic settings and the story was very enjoyable.  The Alien world is mostly linear.  You can wander around some, and it gives you the feel of an open world game, but you must eventually venture back to the intended path, which in this game is not a bad thing because you are on a mission to find your ship and fellow crew members.I am not normally much of a puzzle person, in fact I despise puzzles, but the puzzles in this game were enjoyable and not too difficult, some requiring a little more thinking than others.  The developers went into a lot of detail in creating the creatures inhabiting this beautiful alien world, and there are several different species.   Each time you encounter a new species you can scan them, log them and learn about their origin and vulnerabilities.  You acquire several really cool weapons and add-ons as you progress in the game, and some of the fight scenes can be quite difficult.  Just remember to use the right tool (and weapon) for the job.Ignore the negative reviews.  I think that some people just expect too much from games these days.  The developers deserve a lot of credit for all of the work that went into this masterpiece.   I look forward to a sequel or similar titles from them.  Overall a very good game !

Endboss-Fight is over in a pinch...• The choice of weaponry gets repetitive and boring• You play a game of match-patterns with enemies.  Fire on red, lightning on blue, ice and poison accomodate the first two.   There are less combinations than I hoped at the beginning, since the last two are just combo-multipliers.• The dialogues are okay-ish. The audiologs and texts found scattered are not that enticing that I feel the need to learn more of the story.• Tube levels sparsely strung together to form a worldThe problem here is with this puzzle -> arena -> puzzle -> arena loop that kills emersion. Some lore pieces are thrown in, but it just has this taste of: "Rinse and Repeat." or "Tried and True" or "Never change a running system" vibe...ConclusionOverall okay game. I would give a "neutral" if I could, but since there is only "good" or "bad" this one sadly tends to more bad than good. Buy if on sale maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: The story for SCARS Above is absolutely amazing. I loved the gadgets and weapons, particularly after some upgrades. My one complaint is the tuning on a couple of the areas - The Alpha fight was way too hard and I almost quit there after several defeats. I am glad I came back and eventually beat it, since it's not indicative of the rest of the gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: If you quit out the game at the start of Chapter 6, when you load back in it will place you in the Hub area, but with an invisible wall between you and the exit, preventing you from progressing any further. There's a discussion from just over a year ago that a developer responded too, so the team knows this is a problem, but they just don't care enough to fix their game. There's no way load a previous save, and no way to die in the Hub area to try and reload to a revive point. Don't waste your money, go play something made by competent devs. This exact bug has been creating a hard-lock in the game for over a year.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were my friend, I wouldn't recommend this. If you really want it and it is on sale, as in a BIG SALE, because the achievements are easy, sure.You can see what they were going for, but it fell flat and there were many tech issues. Enemies suddenly popping in, enemies spawning above me and I had to wait for them fall down, i went to change the sprint button from "hold" to "toggle" and it reloaded my entire game and set my progress back and then the next day when I opened the game up again the sprint had reverted back to "hold". But this time when I turned it back to "toggle" it didn't reload anything?! The cut scenes are in an entirely different quality and at a couple points, suddenly ended (i can't tell if it was designed to end when it did or a glitch) and a boss fight had begun and the boss was already landing hits giving me little time to react. It felt cheap. A lot of the shots this game gives you is cheap, you are getting hit not because you aren't paying attention or because you are a bad player, it's because it is full of cheap, swarm the player placements.If you are looking at this game, it is because you like soulslike combat. Like many who try to recreate such combat styles, they think added LOTS of enemies is what makes the game. You know how in Dark Souls 2 they went the route of "it's this boss but there is more of it and it is a skin change"? yeah that is nearly the whole of this game. You'd be introduced to a new enemy (and there are not many at ALL), kill it, and then like 10 minutes later it is the same enemy but now there are 2! Or maybe it has lots of smaller enemies, or maybe they've just put it in an environment which damages you. It's the same thing, just slightly remixed. The final boss is just a reskin of a normal enemy. I couldn't believe it was the final boss, I legit thought "oh this must be the enemy before the BIG FINAL BOSS". No, just ANOTHER reskin. I thought I was going to fight the big bad guy, THE guy we've have been after. No, just what is basically a Bullymong from Borderlands. It got to a point where yet the same enemy popped out that I went "oh what a surprise". Like how Callisto Protocol was just the same thing again and again. Guess you can say with this, they just added a random elemental to the enemy. So instead of hitting with electric, you shoot the same part with fire. but that's it. They would place some enemies right next to where you respawn (this game's version of a firelink). You would walk 2 steps and enemies have appeared out the ground, which is awkward when these places obviously give you health and ammo. I opted for using them as little as possible as there was no safety with them, just another chance for a cheap enemy placement. There was a moment in a cut scene where there was a crew member I was talking to, and when the cut scene ended, they were no longer there. Just to say, that person was in a jail. There was no where to go, in fact you had to go and free them from it. Multiple times things existed only in cut scenes. The cutscenes felt completely cut off from what was actually happening. At one point during a scene, the character is looking out at something in the distance, and it looked super close. When back to gameplay, it was gone, which was really awkward because it was my next destination. It went from "okay so it is over the ridge, that is easy to see, it's right there I could throw a rock at it" to it being FAR in the distance and in an entirely different zone?! I thought my graphics were messing up but I had the highest settings on. Most cut scenes ended in ways that felt jarring and like 15 seconds were cut out. They also often transport you with no warning.Story wise, eh. There is really nothing. The lady you play as couldn't be more unbothered that she can not die, and she knows how everything works on this alien planet. It does get to a point where it is hilarious, and the facial animations are very Mass Effect Andromeda.I could go on, as I still have more issues. There is no brightness option so don't play this if daylight is out and you don't have blackout curtains, controllers might work but I had issues and I know all my controllers are fine, if I have to hear the character go "brrrr" one more time.... we get it, you're cold. I really wanted to like this. Heck my friend told me about it and was like "this looks inspired by Returnal and that's one of your fav games", but it is nothing like that, don't be fooled. The story in this game is as deep as the combat.If you have played this and think you suck at it, I promise, you don't. the combat is not well done. This feels like a base demo for a game that is still in development.The worse thing I had.Healing damaged me twice during my gameplay. I had no elemental affects on me. I just needed to heal, and it nearly killed me. I went from a third health to just a tiny bit left.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is an indie video game title that does its best to emulate some of the 1960s’ most memorable alien invasion literature, unashamedly incorporating various themes from extraterrestrial stories to craft its adventure-based storyline. It works, for the most part. Developed by studio Mad Head Games and published by Prime Matter, Scars Above follows the story of scientist Kate Ward of the Sentient Contact Assessment and Response (SCAR) team as they interact with an alien structure known as the “Metahedron.” It’s a very 2001: A Space Odyssey-esque story, but I’d be lying if I said the game didn’t deliver with its extraterrestrial terror.From the get-go, Scars Above flaunts its strengths as a tried-and-true sci-fi narrative, opening with a surprisingly well-developed — though technically unpolished — cinematic onboard the SCAR team’s starship as they prepare to conduct fieldwork to understand the Metahedron’s mysterious appearance and origins. Their attempts to probe into the impenetrable construction goes awry, and the team is transported à la 2001 to a hostile extraterrestrial planet. Kate comes across plinths that echo the monoliths of the Space Odyssey series, meets an imposing alien that looks suspiciously like Dragon Ball’s Frieza, and the game takes off from there.Throughout the game, the player is treated to Kate’s miscellaneous ramblings while she records log entries of the flora and fauna she encounters — both peacefully and violently — as she explores the planet, putting her academic background in xenobiology to the test. Scars Above is outstanding in this sense, and the game’s science and faux-research mechanics are quite developed. Kate scans each enemy she kills, taking note of the downed creatures’ physiological and often societal characteristics on-the-fly; she stops to understand the nature of the planet’s complex ecosystems and even scrutinizes the rocks and minerals scattered around the different regions she explores. Kate’s log entries, covering everything from blue sky fresias’ lack of chloroplasts and arachnid jumpers’ physiologies to ancient ruins’ internal conduction systems, are weirdly substantive.The planet’s visually defeatist wilderness is a touch too Death Stranding, though I appreciate the attention to detail with the admittedly derivative (yet nonetheless immersive) Xenomorph-esque monster fauna and the forgettably exotic flora.With regards to its eeriness, the game was surprisingly scary, but in a good way. Actual jumpscares with the Cronenberg-ey monsters were a particular source of grief for me, and on more than one occasion I jumped back in moments of true terror (with yelps that were much too loud) during inopportune quiet hours in my dorm.Despite all its immersion, Scars Above has more than its fair share of technical blips and design snags. Textures overall just feel off: liquid and landscape textures are awkward and don’t fully mesh with the environment, lighting and shadowing often feel wrong, and there is a frustrating level of uncanny valley with the characters’ seemingly uninterested faces. (It’s not a good look when the most viscerally emotional moments come from when Kate’s back is turned to the player.) Awesome and excessively flamboyant sci-fi visual effects only just barely make up for the rough textures.Still, there was a fair amount of graphical and gameplay control awarded to the player, with the standard set of user-adjustable settings that more and more games seem to do away with. Controller support is sufficient — the player doesn’t suffer any more or less using a controller versus MKB — and the ability to hot-change difficulty in-game was a welcome addition (though any actual change was minimal as death approached from every corner anyways).Mechanically, the game is pretty middling, though not in a bad way. Scars Above features some tame RPG mechanics with its ability tree’s xenobiology and engineering branches (representing Kate’s two Yale PhDs), and the player unlocks four elemental weapons throughout the course of gameplay. This is quite sufficient for getting through the various simple puzzle obstacles presented in the main path, but not quite enough to make it past the sheer difficulty curve of each area’s countless enemies.I loathe to call it a Soulslike just because of its science theme and shooter-based fighting, but it nonetheless has those mechanics (most notably, repeated death at the hands of the same non-boss enemies) to justify its place in the ranks of the faux-Soulsbornes. It’s not a AAA title, so a certain level of jank and iffy design is to be expected — but for an AA-level studio, Scars Above is worth checking out for those action-adventurers looking for that unique Death Stranding/Dark Souls/Mass Effect amalgamation that this game offers.

_childDocuments_.review: I acknowledge that this review is about as much of a weird mix of points/jumbled mess as the game is at times, and I'm sure those things are connected somehow. Scars Above is a competently made AA game without any critical, deal breaking low points. It does, however, never reach any noteworthy highs, either. It's feels like the  bastard child of Resident Evil (minus the , mind you) and that other generic Third Person Shooter you played last year. Even though some people will try to make you believe it, it is nothing like a particular series of games. Yes, it has checkpoints that you have to activate and - when you squint really hard - the healing system could kind of maybe look a little bit like it, but that's it.Should you spend full price (40€ at the time of this review) on the game? If money has any value to you, probably not. If it's between buying food for the week and buying this game, definitely buy food. So, if you want to go all technical on me, no, I cannot recommend this game at it's current price. If Steam ever added a "[YES/NO], BUT" I'd say that it's not a bad game, and if you're into this kind of stuff, and maybe can nab it at 50-90% off, it is likely worth your time. Speaking of time, according to Steam I have spent 6.5 hours on this game. Sure, I skipped all the cinematics and story bits that could be skipped, but I have gotten 43 out of 45 achievements (I checked; the two I'm missing are about using certain gadgets in certain ways that simply weren't necessary in my playthrough) and that includes all of them for exploration. I ended the game with 8 or 9 ability points left over. Let me quickly throw this in here because it kind of annoyed me:You don't get experience points by killing enemies, you have to collect data cubes that are more or less hidden in the world (Mainly, you get experience for scanning one enemy of a new kind that you kill). These will give you varying amounts of "Knowledge %", and once you hit 100%, you get one ability point. The same goes for weapon upgrades. I can't really tell you if you would find them organically if playing through, but I seem to remember at least 2 that were kind of hidden. In a game that doesn't have too much variety, that's not a great thing. That also means if you want all the upgrades, you will have to explore the world a bit. And there's no map. At least not that I could find. Not that the levels are super complicated or sprawling; they're not. But it's still annoying.Picking up from the 8 or 9 ability points I had left over: As I said, I did nearly all of the exploring, so if you rush the game and don't go looking around too much, you might end up with none to two or whatever small numbers left over. But there's another problem: I explored damn near everything and I finished the game in under 6 hours of net play time. And that's still with the unskippable portion of slow walking and "wait here until I finish my monologue" included. Then again, the talent trees are tiny with very basic passive talents, I'm not sure you'd need any of them to complete the game, because other than the 15% weapon damage increase at the top of one of the trees, there's nothing that really changes how you play the game at all. I'm the guy who wants RPG elements in every game, but ugh. I'm not sure this talent tree counts for much.The shooting is not super inspired, it's usually finding a weakpoint and exploiting it. Sometimes you just kill them by shooting out the ice from under them (which is always an instant kill) or dropping a stalactite on them. You have 4 times of damage (lightning, fire, ice, poison) to cycle through, and for 2 out of the 4 you can pick between projectiles and beams. You also have a bunch of gadgets (slow, decoy, shield...) that are occasionally nice to have, I guess? I personally only ever used the gravity trap regularly. Which brings me to my final point:The game seems generally a bit too easy (and I suck at video games). I was thinking "Why couldn't you let me use the additional ability points on SOMETHING?" but then the tuning would've probably been even worse. On the medium difficulty option out of the 3 it was mildly challenging at times, but when I first fought the construct, I actually quit the game about 5 minutes in, because I couldn't figure out that 3 was the right number of legs to drop into the water (I stopped at 2), without ever being at a real risk of dying or running out of anything. Never died to any of the bosses, and only died once because I never really had to keep an eye on my health.So, this all sounds fairly negative and I guess we, especially  old people like me, tend to focus on the not so great things. However, on a scale from 1 to 10, where 5 is  the average, I'd rate it as a solid 6, leaning toward 7. Depending on how you handle it, it can probably be anywhere from 4 to 8 hours of decent Third Person Shooting with some never too complicated or super contrived puzzling with absolutely no replay value. Choose your entry point accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying, don't get discouraged by the negative reviews. Some of them point out the fact that the game is way too difficult especially in the beginning, not mentioning that you can a) change the game's difficulty, and b) the game has a  tag, and by now pretty much everyone knows that soulslike = hard game. The others are complaining that the game is too bland, doesn't have amazing graphics and the story is weak.Out of curiosity I checked out the Developer and browsed through their other games and observed that the other games they made are "hidden object", "puzzle", "point and click" etc having those 2010 graphics we've been accustomed with for that genre of game. Why did I feel the need to say all this? Because what they did with Scars Above is an IMPRESSIVE "upgrade". It's a completely different game and genre than what they are used to making and that alone is spectacular. It's also good to note that the difficulty could be related to the fact that Kate, the character you're playing as,  is an astronaut and a scientist –  - something that is said several times throughout the game. You wouldn't expect a scientist to pull a John Wick, right?  because of this, she's resourceful and determined to do anything to survive.Fighting wise, you have ranged weapons, melee attacks, devices and consumables. You craft different kinds of weapons throughout the game and you can switch through them at any given point. You use a combination of elemental attacks, a lot of gadgets and items with different functionalities that only enrich your game play. You can exploit the environment and enemy weaknesses by scanning them and gaining valuable information. Exploiting the weak points of your foes makes the fighting even easier and helps you to discover effective tactics against them. Kate, once again, is a scientist so with her help you can extract information from your surroundings by scanning artifacts, materials and creatures in order to learn about their features, properties and weaknesses. That, of course, if you actually check out the journal and don't get bored by reading the available information.The game has gorgeous landscapes and good graphics, I often found myself slow walking and taking in the scenery. The story is also interesting enough to keep you playing the game  and questioning what is so special about you, a simple scientist, that you're pretty much humanity's last chance.

_childDocuments_.review: (mini-review.)A predominantly inaccessible, derivative mess that pretentiously thinks that a badly written Star Trek Voyager episode is the height of cerebral science fiction.  The game shows its best features in the trailer, with good facial animations, only to provide perhaps the most God-awful running, mantling and shooting animations I've seen in a third person shooter in the better part of a decade.  Coupled with a story that only dropped one relevant tidbit of plot in almost an hour of game play and a stream of cheap, off-the-shelf bug-worm alien foes and you start to wonder what the developer was even going for, when they assembled this title.  Creature designs look like they were obtained wholesale from an online store and the combat is nothing to write home about.  I was looking for the escape menu before the end of the hour.  At least it runs, I guess.It's Stray  space. Avoid.6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If playing sci-fi, third-person shooters that feature dodge-rolling and exploiting elemental weaknesses in enemies as their central combat mechanics, published by Prime Matter over the past year, pocketed me a quarter every time it happened, I’d have exactly  quarters. It wouldn’t exactly make me rich, but it’s weird that it happened twice!From the minds over at Mad Head Games comes —an ambitious and promising departure by a developer best known for hidden object point & clicks. Sadly, what was no doubt conceived as a bold and fresh vision for the team, and is made up of some great concepts and ideas, takes a tad too long to get going and lets the stale parts take up a sizable chunk of the whole.With  being a budget title, it’s best to temper expectations, even if it manages to avoid some common hazards that AA releases—those that go for a cinematic, “photo-realistic” look, at least—consistently slam into.For starters, none of the environments will give off that air of a cheap movie set, trying to sell you on the illusion with cardboard walls and poorly matte-painted skies. A holdover from the studio’s days spent working on hidden object games, I’m sure, there is a lot of detail put into your surroundings, which can be frequently interacted with and inspected.The spacecraft you start the game on is filled to the brim with little chunks of the characters’ personalities; feel free to rummage through their stuff, turn and flip it around to reminisce about the past. Hold it dear, for you’ll be soon stepping foot on a desolate alien planet, where fog descends onto the soaked swamps, an ominous geometric shape of dubious intent hangs in the distant sky, and glowy-bitted, uninspiredly-designed creatures roam free. It’s an elusive atmosphere to pull off, and here it manages to click.The gameplay, while not without issues, is quite functional. Dodging enemy attacks actually works, maybe even too well, and the guns have ample kick. But, is there some clunkiness to the way the game controls? Are there stiff animations? Is the storyline something you’d find airing on the Syfy channel? Absolutely and unfortunately—the game looks good and plays well enough, but its presentation is a parade of played-out trends.The environments too, no matter how much weight there is to them, become stale; was there a law passed while I wasn’t looking? One mandating that fleshy goop and blocky, granite-like alien architecture must appear in every up-and-coming sci-fi setting? Must be the same one that defines aliens as “ethereal, hairless humanoids, with a vibrant skin tone”.The story isn’t as offensive of a cliché, but sadly unremarkable and without a strong emotional core. The endpoint of the journey is a hopeful, science-positive message. The game has this optimistic, wide-eyed view of our place in the universe and you’ll need that same outlook on the game itself to get the most out of it. If anything, it'll warm your heart a little bit if you don’t roll your eyes at such moments.A breath of fresh air is the likeable protagonist, Kate, thanks to whose background as a scientist, exposition never feels unnatural. Coming across certain lifeforms or technology will let you inspect them up close in a hidden-object-like minigame, allowing Kate to surmise her findings at the end. What you’ll learn isn’t all that interesting, but at least the learning is fun! Kate’s frequent remarks are also welcome—it all makes perfect sense and ends up as an immersive way of presenting the science in this science fiction.I also greatly appreciate the minimalistic UI. It seems so thought out that, since Kate’s capable of explaining a lot herself, I can’t help but wonder what’s up with those holographic tutorials that came barging in ever so often, transporting me to an alternate world of flickering blues, as if the Animus from  reared its ugly head.What  lacks in originality, it tries to make up for with a solid gameplay loop, lurking underneath the fluff. I say “lurking”, as it’ll take roughly half of the game for the training wheels to start coming off, being shed completely only in the final stages. You get four different guns, each corresponding to a different element. These can interact with each other, but also with the environment. Throw in the additional fire modes, the consumables and tools, a skill tree, a “crafting system” and an inventory, and you'll find yourself spoiled for choice when looking for ways to deal with what the game has in store for you.Unfortunately, it’s painfully clear that there’s just not enough room within its scope to warrant it all, as it messes with the pacing and leaves other "mechanics" feeling like placeholders. Don't feel bad for not experimenting, because the blame is on the game. It doesn’t let you play around with any of its options; rather, it just showcases how everything works, sort of like a tech demo.When a new idea is introduced, the next hour or so is a gauntlet of all its potential applications. You unlock a gun that freezes things, so here’s 45 minutes of ponds you have to turn solid to get across. When do I get a say in this interactive experience? Why is there no dynamic between any of these features?You do get a glimpse of what could have been in the final few hours, when the game is out of tricks and starts throwing at you the greatest hits of everything that’s been an obstacle up until that point. For the first time, experimentation won’t feel trivial. You’ll actually have to figure out the best way to go about things as you won’t know what to expect next. It’s a blast to play, albeit a humble one, as the ending is right around the corner.As for the rest? The “crafting” isn’t crafting in the way pretty much everyone out there understands it. Kate will “craft” a new gun or gadget when you come across it as an in-universe explanation of her acquiring it. While she won’t do it unless you hold E to fill up a bar, there’s no actual mechanic behind it.The same goes for the inventory—there’s no management, just a tally of what you’re carrying. Both these and the barely exciting skill tree—which offers meagre stat boosts and "Personal Skills" in the same sense that Doom Guy has the personal skill to shoot a gun—are neat, ludonarrative ways of introducing what your protagonist is capable of, though having actual mechanics in a video game where combat takes so long to come together would have been nice.It’s easy to write positively about a game you enjoyed, and even easier to trash one you didn’t. To write mediocrely on one you're on the fence about is a skill I haven’t mastered yet, as all my writing is mediocre! So, how can I expect you to tell that I didn’t hate my time with  after everything you’ve read?Having that wide-eyed view towards it, I enjoyed picking at its neat bits. However, all the missed opportunities and trite design make the rating more so a guarantee that you won't get burned too badly if you have an undying interest to check it out, rather than a recommendation.Of course, if you want to avoid being complicit in another goop-filled title, you can do that, too. Whichever your decision, you can take this review as an endorsement of it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out great, giving you a lot of fun weapons and mechanics to play with. But.. after about three hours this wears off and you're left with what seems like a rushed and unfinished game. Spoilers: you have to run through every level you've been through in the last chapter of the game and get some stupid keys to activate some pillars or something and I just had no interest in doing this at that point. I'm giving up on this game but I was ready to give up after the 4 hour point. This game is NOT worth $40, absolutely not. _childDocuments_.review: For what its worth, Scars Above turned out to be quite an enjoyable game, with an interesting blend of sci fi, and light souls like aspects. The game is quick and to the point, and while some would say that the game is 'short', id rather phrase it as Scars Above doesn't overstay its welcome, and the game was still fresh and interesting even towards the end.There is a little bit of AA studio jank happening, but I encountered no crashes, and performance was very good.The only real annoying deficiency was UE4's lack of Ultrawide support, but this was easily overcome with UUU + Console commands (set /script/engine.localplayer AspectRatioAxisConstraint AspectRatio_MaintainYFOV) to solve the ultrawide cropping. Hopefully the devs can set this to be the default for the game in a future patch.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game really enjoyable.Its fairly short so it certainly doesn't outstay its welcome, and if you are into that kind of thing, can get 100% achievements in 1 normal play through.Graphically its a mixed bag, with lovely outdoor environments and decent enough monster designs supported by unappealing human characters with distracting up-close facial animations.The exploration isn't too heavy with some minor back tracking, the game gives the impression it was originally going to be a full "Dark Souls with guns" project due to how it has saving and its effect on the world similar to bonfires, and each map has a shortcut opening, but was abandoned mid development for a much more linear affair.Combat is really fun, as well as i-frame dodge rolls and enemy weak points, you have a full elemental system that you have to mix and match depending on the enemy you face and the environment your in. On normal terrain? Freeze them with ice shots and gun them down afterwards. Is it raining? Shoot them with electrical shots and fry them. On ice? Shoot the ice under them with fire and make them fall through for an instant kill. You also get gadgets like shields and time slowing devices to help. _childDocuments_.review: If I had to summarize this game it's a reasonably short horror puzzle shooter. The horror aspect is ok and if you're in the STEM fields the "science" in the game is cringe. Lastly my major complaint was the animations which were barely ok but felt out of place. Gameplay is fun and involves puzzles and combat. Often combat itself is best thought of as a puzzle with optimal and, conversely, inefficient solutions. Environments look great but get a bit repetitive late into the game. The story is passable though a bit preachy - not bad, not great. (No spoilers) The story is very linear and involves elements of cosmic horror and action/adventure. As the game progresses the horror aspect of it peaks mid-game and then the tone transforms into action adventure find the mcguffins quest to win the game. The story is ok although I was annoyed by how poor the presentation of "science" can be in this game. It's not a big deal unless you're in a STEM field. There are two main aspects of the game: puzzles and combat. The two are often intertwined together as appropriate use of weapons and gadgets in this game can make combat a breeze. While the puzzles and the combat are pretty straight forward I enjoyed my experience for the most part. The combat relies on using 4 types of elemental damage to take on enemies with individual strengths and weaknesses and interact with the environment (electric damage boost in water as one example). At the end of the game the combat does become a bit boring and nothing really challenges you anymore because you become quite OP. Even the final boss was relatively easy compared to some of the earlier ones. The save checkpoint system is based on the Dark-Souls campfire formula.For the most part the game is beautiful when it's supposed to be beautiful and disgusting when it's supposed to look disgusting. There aren't that many environments (swamps, snowy mountains, caves, grassy hills, alien structures, and an extra spicy one that I won't spoil here). For the most part each environment is done well but they feel a bit repetative near the end of the game. My major gripes were with animations - facial animations weren't done well. The basic running animation looks out of place - it doesn't seem to match the speed at which your character moves and seems very floaty. I've only ran into one bug while playing the game. I got stuck in the terrain. Reloading at a checkpoint fixed that and I wasn't able to reproduce it

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with the TL;DR: This game is Not Perfect (TM). It's not going to be your favorite, or your game of the year. But it's more than what a lot of reviews give it credit for. In short, it is absolutely worth a playthrough. I genuinely enjoyed the game, and found it well worth the purchase. Give it a shot (it's not that long anyway). I'll start with the stuff that might result in you bouncing off of it, or choosing not to play it:- The game is poorly optimized; it occupied nearly 100% of my GTX 2060 super, meaning I literally couldn't do anything else involving moving pictures at the same time, when even very recent AAA games like Elden Ring didn't have that issue.- Despite being a major resource hog, the game had some pretty lackluster graphics on my machine, even on the highest settings. It's not a matter of underpowered specs; my hardware isn't top of line or anything, but it's very capable, and I never had frame rate issues.- There were some glitches, most of which weren't terribly disruptive. At least once, though, I literally had to reload a save, because the character got stuck. She would perform the normal movement animations for walking, dodging, etc., but wouldn't move from that spot.- The story is at times incredibly stilted and mediocre, the dialogue especially. In some cases, moments or lines that might otherwise land fail at least in part because you've spent so little time with these characters, and see so little of their relationships. The voice actors do a great job trying to convey the weight of apparent off-screen history between all of these people, but you just have so little to go on, making the emotionality and drama hard to justify. - The game can feel a tad repetitive at times, even in spite of how short it is. It's the same enemies in every area, just slight variations related to elemental affinities. And many of the environments can blend together somewhat, at least internally. The cold area is cold and frozen. The swamp area is swampy. The high tech areas are techy. If the paths weren't so linear, it would be pretty easy to get turned around (which actually happened to me a lot in a late-game underground section). - Many of the ideas in the game, from story to gameplay seem a little like reach exceeding grasp. Some elements are legitimately interesting, but don't get enough attention or development to fully capitalize on them (more on this in the "good" section below). - The game is short. I picked this up on a sale as a palette cleanser after a 200+ hour first run through Elden Ring. I finished this one pretty casually over a single weekend, with time to spare. While that can certainly be a plus, especially compared to the many never-ending collect-a-thons some games have evolved into, I found that the game left me wanting more in a way that was just a bit less than satisfying. - Finally, difficulty is a bit weird in the game. There are three difficulty modes, analogous to easy, normal, and hard. I played on "hard" mode, and I struggled significantly in the beginning of the game. Certain sections and enemies were more frustrating that I was expecting or wanted, and it wasn't until I had collected some of the weapons and gear, and learned the intended combat rhythms that things started to smooth out. Then, the difficulty actually declined, with the final boss proving a nominally challenging single-run endeavor. Compared to the second major boss, which took me at least 45 minutes of repeated respawns and retries, it was a stark difference. Now, let's discuss why I'm not actually bothered by any of those issues.| Story, Characters, and Dialogue |I'll start with the story, since that's kind of my home territory. I'm a writer by trade, and I will almost always choose a game with compelling characters, plot, setting, and narrative over one with fun gameplay but virtually no substance. So when I say this game is worth enduring the dialogue, I mean it. Some of the lines are *painfully* cringe-worthy. The team captain has a speech in the beginning that's so clearly maid and butler dialogue, that he actually uses the phrase "as you know." It's grating, and I almost turned the game off before I'd even finished the opening cutscene. What's important to know is that it's not *all* like that. There was a surprising amount of insight in some of the ideas and commentary. Even the ending, where your ghostly companion urges you to keep seeking knowledge, just don't don't do so at the expense of morality like they did.| Gameplay and Combat | There's a shocking amount of nuance to the way combat works. It's not breaking any records, but it was a lot more than expected. When they started handing out elemental weaponry, I expected a rock-paper-scissors system, a la Pokemon. That's not what I got. Any element works on any enemy, but none of them alone puts out enough damage to deal with the things you face. Instead, you have to amplify damage via elemental combos using the environment, alternating weapons, and hitting weak spots. The gadgets also factor heavily, and the second major boss presented as much trouble as it did because I hadn't used the non-weapon assets much. I had to retreat to the save point, and completely respec the build I had thus far. There was no way I would have succeeded by just unloading magazines into the thing. How consumables work was rather inventive. Maybe other games I haven't played work similar, but I had never personally seen it before, and it created a fun little tug of war—sometimes I had everything I needed, and other times I was pressed hard for lack of resources. I benefited by being judicious, but gained nothing by hoarding, so I had to choose carefully. I liked how the game provided diagetic explanations for things like respawns and even mega-manning new abilities. You're a scientist; why wouldn't you study a big monster you killed to see if you could reverse engineer it's weapons? | Design | I'll end with the section I have the least authority in, but had the least to complain about. There was a bit of repetition in some of the environment and creature design. But to be fair, the game is short, and I didn't notice it much. What I did notice is that the game didn't immediately look like others it pulled inspiration from. Each enemy passed the silhouette test easily. And there were multiple times the background environment itself presented some stark images. You know that thing in shows/movies where the characters are going through a cave, and the lightning strikes, and the stalactites look like monstrous teeth? That. They pulled that off, in a video game, several times, to very significant effect. What I'm saying is, the game had a very potent atmosphere, and though it didn't lean too heavily on horror aesthetics, it swung back and forth, and did so effectively. | Bottom Line |The game is not as cool as I had hoped when I first saw trailers for it. But I still enjoyed it. The creators clearly put a lot of passion into it, and I'm glad I got the chance to play it. It was probably a major leap for them; it's very different from the rest of their catalog, it's a new IP, and it came out in 2023, the year that gave us both Gollum and BG3. They deserve due credit for reaching beyond their grasp. It's the only way we learn and grow toward excellence, and even the steps between here and there can be a fun adventure.
