_childDocuments_.review: The game's has a semi-interesting premise, but the story doesn't really go anywhere with it. The characters are extremely bland and uninteresting. But more importantly, the gameplay is not very good. For some reason it has to be "Souls-like/light", with pillars that resurrect you and respawn everything, but it doesn't really benefit the linear level structure. There is actually an interesting narrative aspect to the resurrecting part, but gameplay-wise it's not convincing. Enemy design is annoying. You have 4 weapon-types (unlocked as you progress, from electricity, to fire, cryo and acid), and most enemies have weakpoints for a certain element you have to hit. But these weakpoints are often hard to hit because some have it on their chest but protect it with their arms, others have it on their back, so you have to dodge and then hit them from behind. With most weapons this works well enough, but the stupid fire weapon has to charge for a second before being able to fire, so often you miss the shooting window because the weapon hasn't charged yet. This was the most annoying design of the combat for me, basically all enemies with fire weakness were an absolute pain to fight because of this garbage weapon design.Then there's "environmental" effects. Toxicity (which is a non-issue) and hypothermia, which is one of the most BS designs in the game. Hypothermia depending on the enviroment builds slowly or extremely fast. Once it's full, it quickly drains your HP and kills you. The only way to counter it is to ignite certain plants with your fire weapon and stand next to them while they burn. This works relatively fine out of combat. But there was one particular section where the game throws the highest level of hypothermia at you (which basically kills you in less than 10 seconds if you don't use the heat plants), but you also have to kill 2 tough enemies before being able to proceed to the next area. Trying to dodge these enemies means leaving the safety of the heat plants (which also only last for a few moments and there was only 3 of those plants in that area), meaning you quickly die due to hypothermia while desperately trying to get at these enemies' weakpoints. It was such a terrible and frustrating design choice, I just ended up using a trainer to disable this absolutely garbage mechanic entirely. It's not fun, it's not balanced, and it adds nothing of value. The following boss fight also has the hypothermia mechanic for its entirety (but at that point I just ignored it with the trainer, otherwise I would probably have just completely rage-quit the game at that point).Overall I cannot recommend this game. The story has some interesting parts, but overall is pretty generic "dangers of AI" sci-fi. The characters are completely uninteresting. And the gameplay is mostly mediocre to bad. Also for some reason the game only has 1 save file, you can't manually save and once you finish the game, your save gets deleted. This apparently also led to breaking the game for some people, since there's still a bug at the start of chapter 6 that completely bricks your save (meaning you'd have to completely start over from chapter 1, since there's only 1 save file) if you exit the game at the wrong time. This didn't happen to me because I was warned about it, but it is a major game-breaking bug that the devs have been aware of for over a year and still haven't fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10A young woman's amusing romp through an inhospitable alien world.Bugs:This game definitely has its fair share of bugs. Some worse than others, but none were what I'd consider 'game-breaking'. Sometimes you'll get stuck on a piece of terrain or there'll be invisible walls preventing you from moving toward certain objectives when there definitely wasn't meant to be. In fact, I had to dodge roll the entire path to the final boss because Kate just gave up on walking. However, once the battle started, I could move normally again. Interestingly enough, I never encountered any serious bugs DURING combat situations. They always seemed to occur during the exploration phases of gameplay. Which, I mean, I'd say that's a step-up from a lot of games nowadays.I think the game crashed a total of one time during my 10 hours, and I got sent back to a checkpoint once because I spent just a little more time in the menus than the game was comfortable with. But other than that, no major issues.Gameplay:It's not spectacular, nor is it particularly unique in itself. But it is fun. It's a fun game. No doubt about that. The learning curve isn't too intense either, though your first encounter with new new enemies have a tendency of being kind of annoying, as they seem to have a lot more health the first time around than they do the rest of the time. But once you unlock all of the weapons and you learn how to combo the different elements, it's a fun ride. In the end, it's ALL about the combat for this game. Knowing when to use certain weapons and when to combine elements for maximum effect, it's all part of the experience. The exploration is very limited and there aren't many 'extras' to find along the way - a handful of audio logs, some weapon upgrades, and such, but it's not a whole lot.The abilities are all fairly standard: increase stamina, all consumables heal the player, immunity from stagger effects, etc. Nothing too outlandish there, just your usual Action-Adventure stuff. What's odd about the system is that XP isn't earned through combat, it's primarily earned from progressing through the story, but you also get it from picking up lore elements (like audio logs and text documents) and from knowledge cubes (items you find scattered throughout the world which are just boxes of XP basically). It's sort of an interesting concept because it gives you a reason to step off the beaten path and explore the admittedly limited optional areas, but it definitely doesn't add much to the game itself. Like, I said, I completed it in just over 10 hours, having earned all of the achievements and having picked up every piece of lore and every weapon, upgrade, and knowledge cube. Which actually brings up an interesting point: there are more ability points available in the game than there are abilities to use them on. Like, quite a few more. By the end, I had 10 ability points leftover, but nothing to spend them on. And that's totally fine, I don't really mind it. It's just kind of odd.Another thing worth mentioning is that the unlocks are weirdly arranged. For instance, one of the gadgets is given to you in the final chapter, and it's a really useful tool, but I found myself never really using it because I'd already learned how best to dispatch enemies. It would've been much better if it had been given earlier on, before some of the other tools. That way, I might've actually gotten some use out of it. But realistically, out of the 5 gadgets, I only really used 3 of them. Which just feels like a waste because they were all useful, but they were just given to me in the wrong order I think. I mean, the first gadget you get in the game probably should've been one of the last ones because it's honestly just too powerful and it makes combat easier than I think it was intended to be.Narrative:I'd say this game is full of interesting concepts, but some of them aren't executed very well. The overall story is kind of unique, but the way its presented isn't entirely compelling. I won't spoil anything because I do believe this is a game worth playing once, but I will say that the antagonist is a huge cliche in the sci-fi genre, made only mildly interesting because of their limitations. The ending is kind of cool though. And it does make me hope for a sequel, but I'm just hoping the devs don't try to milk it and turn it into a whole series. One more game would be plenty, and if done well, it has the potential to be a truly unforgettable game. The writers just need to work a little harder on their character writing. The dialog isn't bad, by any means, there's just not that much of it to begin with. And I finished the game feeling like I didn't really know any of the main characters, including the protagonist, Kate. Like, I know why they're on the planet and what their job is. I even know how they all know each other, but you don't get much beyond that. It's one of the instances where the writers think giving each character one personality trait (in the form of a quirk or a quote they use all the time) is enough to give them depth. It's not, and it's a little disappointing when that's all you get, especially when there are so few characters in the game. And who knows, maybe they're saving all of that for the next game. I just wish there was a bit more character development in this one.It felt a lot like the first Tomb Raider reboot where all of Lara's so-called 'character development' was just  bad stuff happening to her and changing her into someone new. We didn't really learn much about her as a person, we just watched her go from a normal girl to a stone-cold badass over the span of a few hours. Which is fine, I'm not saying every protagonist needs to ramble about what they're feeling and tell us exactly what they're thinking at all times. I just want to understand their motivations. I want to know why they're driven to do the things they do. And sorry, but 'to survive' isn't a good enough reason for me. There's got to be something more if you expect me to believe it.Finally:Anyway, yeah, Scars Above is an interesting title with some cool elements that make for a fun game. I would, however, recommend waiting for it to go on sale, if you can. It's a pretty short game, and it is entirely linear, so the full price is a bit steep for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Jak na pierwszą poważną grę tego studia, świetna robota, choć oczywiście ma swoje wady. Bardzo często podczas gry odnosiłem wrażenie że jest tam wszystko, co podobało się designerom w grach, bo i czuć tu mocno residenta, i soulslike, i pewne elementy z gears of war (przeładowanie), w końcu, są tu pewne akcenty gier które robili wcześniej, tzn. HOPA. Niestety HOPA czuć trochę w oprawie graficznej, gra ma momenty gdzie rzeczywiście potrafi zachwycić, jeżeli nie pomysłem, to chociaż rzemiosłem, ale często miałem wrażenie że jest tam trochę za dużo koloru, trochę za dużo detalu, wreszcie, że jest to wszystko zbyt serowe w tym znaczeniu, że powiela ograne schematy wizualne. Tu można przejść płynnie do historii, która, eh, nie powala. Niby tam wszystko jest, ale to jest takie serowe (znowu) i było milion razy, że zachwycić może co najwyżej 12 latka który nic SF w życiu nie czytał ani nie oglądał. Od strony technicznej ciężko się do czegoś przyczepić, jeżeli coś w grze jest, to jest zrobione porządnie, czy to śnieg w którym się brodzi, woda, co tylko sobie wymyślicie.Przydałby się lepszy scenarzysta, bardziej wymagający art director, być może kompozytor, który bardziej siedzi w undergroundzie, zamiast serwować nam coś, co angażuje trochę bardziej niż muzyka w windzie. Nie żeby była zła, ale miałem często wrażenie że te dzwięki są zbyt gładkie i ułożone.Podsumowując, studio ma solidne podstawy żeby ich kolejny projekt był naprawdę czymś, tu zabrakło trochę ogłady i budżetu, co nie zmienia faktu że to jednak porządny średniak.ENG:For the first serious game of this studio, great job, although of course it has its flaws. Very often during the game I got the impression that there is everything there that designers liked in games, because and feel here strongly resident, and soulslike, and some elements from gears of war (reloading), finally, there are some touches of games they did before, ie HOPA. Unfortunately, HOPA feels a little bit in the visuals, the game has moments where it really manages to impress, if not with the idea, then at least with the craftsmanship, but I often had the impression that there is a little too much color, a little too much detail, and finally, that it is all too cheesy in the sense that it duplicates common visual schemes. Here you can move smoothly to the story, which, eh, does not knock you down. Seemingly everything is there, but it's so cheesy (again) and has been a million times that it can delight at most a 12-year-old who has never read or watched anything SF in his life. On the technical side, it's hard to complain about anything, if there's anything in the game, it's done decently, whether it's snow you're wading in, water, whatever you can think of.It could use a better scriptwriter, a more discerning art director, perhaps a composer who sits more in the underground, instead of serving us something that engages a little more than elevator music. Not that it's bad, but I often had the impression that the sounds were too smooth and arranged.In conclusion, the studio has a solid foundation to make their next project really something, here it lacked a bit of flair and budget, which does not change the fact that it is, however, a decent average.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10Review after 100%The game’s strengths are its stunning graphics, atmospheric sound design, and varied gameplay mechanics. You can use different weapons, devices, and elemental reactions to fight and survive against the alien creatures and environments. You can also craft items and upgrade your equipment to improve your chances. The game’s story is intriguing and well-written, with plenty of twists and surprises along the way.The game’s weaknesses are its lack of difficulty, repetitive enemies, and bland melee combat. The game becomes too easy once you unlock most of the weapons and devices, and the enemies pose little threat. The melee combat is also dull and ineffective, and you are better off using ranged attacks. The game could have benefited from more enemy variety and challenge.Overall, Scars Above is a solid and enjoyable sci-fi shooter that offers a lot of fun and exploration. It may not be very original or innovative, but it is well-executed and polished. If you are a fan of sci-fi games, you should give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Dark Souls fan, I was initially drawn to Scars Above due to its familiar gameplay mechanics and challenging difficulty. However, what truly sets this game apart is its unique implementation of guns, which adds a refreshing twist to the traditional sword and shield combat.From the moment I started the game, I was immediately immersed in the dark and haunting world of Scars Above. The eerie atmosphere, coupled with the stunning visuals, creates a sense of foreboding and sets the tone for the unforgiving journey ahead. The level design is beautifully crafted, with intricate details and hidden paths that keep players on their toes.What impressed me the most about Scars Above is its intuitive and seamless integration of guns into the gameplay. The gunplay feels fluid and satisfying, and it adds a layer of strategy to combat that is not present in other Dark Souls games. I found myself constantly switching between my melee weapons and guns to adapt to different situations, creating a dynamic and engaging experience.Furthermore, the boss fights in Scars Above are nothing short of epic. Each boss has its unique design and attacks, and it takes precise timing and strategic planning to defeat them. The intense adrenaline rush I experienced while facing off against these formidable foes reminded me of the boss fights in Immortals: Unchained.One aspect of Scars Above that may divide players is its steep difficulty curve. While this is expected from a Dark Souls game, the addition of guns does make combat slightly easier. However, this is balanced out by the increasing complexity and intensity of enemies and bosses as the game progresses.In conclusion, I highly recommend Scars Above to fans of the Dark Souls series and those who enjoy challenging and rewarding gameplay. The incorporation of guns adds a unique and enjoyable element that sets this game apart from others in the genre. With its immersive world, intense combat, and exhilarating boss fights, Scars Above is a solid addition to the Dark Souls franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally play up to the two hour mark so I can keep or refund a game as needed (Thank you, rather liberal Steam refund policies!), and this is one of the rare times I've blown past that mark without even realizing it. I was already going to keep and 100% the game, but this just forces the issue 😊 If anyone tells you it's a Returnal clone, that only partially captures the feel of the game. If anything, this feels like Returnal if Returnal had more of a soul. In Returnal I felt like a super soldier that happened to have some scientific interest and method background. In Scars Above you play as Dr. Kate Ward and, throughout the entirety of the game, never lose awareness that Dr. Kate is distinctly a scientist first and foremost that just happens to be building her combat acumen out of necessity due to the situation she's in. She never stops being curious and she never crosses the skill gap needed to break her character traits. This is a breath of fresh air in a AAA-loaded genre that makes habit of breaking that immersion before handing you the controls.That said, if you're going into this looking for a AAA killer that'll put Returnal to shame, this isn't it. Returnal is an *excellent* game and Scars Above wasn't made to try to dethrone it. If you're going into this looking for a solid sci-fi Souls-like shooter that's got an excellently woven story peppered with fun combat, sciency mini-games, rewarding exploration, and fairly constant intrigue, you won't be disappointed regardless of whether this is a AA or AAA game.Of note, the game does support 32:9 super ultrawide monitors natively. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty damn fun for what it offers. Is it brutally unfair/challenging like Dark Souls or Sekiro? No.. But not all souls-like games need to be like that! The boss fights are very fun, some fights do require trial and error, while others are pretty straight forward. The atmosphere is a mix of creepy yet tranquil and there is a talent system that works very well with the gameplay! I really enjoy FPS/Third-Person Shooters and Scars Above being a Third-Person Shooter Souls-Like game definitely did a great job at keeping the gameplay fun and refreshing. Overall this is a solid game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a game with an identity crisis. On one hand, it tries to mimic the souls-likes' mechanics and difficulty, on the other, it all gets watered down the further you get. The cutscenes are low-res, the facial expressions are bad and the graphics aren't exactly pretty, but it compensates those downsides with pretty good shooting mechanics and an interesting plot and world's mythology. You have to adapt and change the ammo you use depending on the enemy you face and make every shot count, so finding their vulnerability may be the key to victory.Many people give up on the first boss, but I recommend you to look up the tactics if you struggle because the game gets easier and better beyond that point.I really want to see where the devs would go plot-wise in the sequel and the game gets good discounts frequently, so I recommend you to give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Neat, simple little Remnantlike with a passable story and fun take on combat mechanics. It's also easy, mind. I played on medium and more or less breezed through it. But that's fine. Keep in mind though, once you beat the story, it deletes your save file. There is no NG+ or continuing from previous save or anything, though to be fair, there'd be no point to it. You can max out everything before endgame.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars above is a competent 10-15 dollar game. it is not a good 40 dollar game. It felt like it wanted to be Control, and it was shipped half done as a tech demo.The maps are very linear and there is little to no exploration. EXP is done based story and on little cubes you pick up that are hidden around the map, HOWEVER there are way more then needed to get all the ability perks. I ended the game with 8 excess perks and could not dismiss the onscreen notification that I had unspent perks (its a little number on the left side of thee screen) The gun play isnt too bad, but the sword is near worthless. your dodge being less effective then just running around. The tools you get are interesting but for some reason a "gravity well" is actually a time bubble. you get things semi randomly from crates or from bosses in a metroid prime kinda way. I took 7.5 hours to 100% the game, and I tend to wonder and had some issues with a few areas. One achievement is bugged where scanning all types of enemy's will not triggered if you have ever died during your save. There are effectively three big boss fights, and one of them is memorable, but the game lacks a true last boss. It is "souls like" due to how you come back after death and can use the pillars like bonfires . it is part of the story, but it feels like a number of games crunched together. it seems to lack any soul of its own, and about 60% into the game the dialog goes downhill. You are also meant to be a scientist studying aliens but ask ZERO questions of the one that starts helping you. you just kinda do what they say without question. its like a solid 5/10 buget syfy movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is a bit hit and miss.Some people might enjoy it, but for me it feels like it is missing a little bit in each of its aspects to be good.The story seemed interesting at first, but turns out to be pretty generic and without any twists and turns.The effects would have needed a bit more polish and seem a bit outdated and sadly the atmosphere suffers because of that.The weapons play is okay'ish but feels more like it is just there to facilitate their elemental system.The boss fights have interesting mechanics, but as soon as you figured it out they get easy, but repetitive.The crafting is mostly press 'E' at certain spots and be done.And the 'puzzles' are very simple and also feel kinda generic.I think I would recommend you try it out when it is on sale and if it isn't your cup of tea, just refund it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of the game as well as the story are very interesting. It doesn't have a huge variety of enemies or weapons but it not necessary because the game is quite short and that is it's strong point. The developers managed to put a pretty solid story and gameplay in a decent amount of time, so that it doesn't feels just the right amount of time to finish it, not too long, not too short. Even though that's not exactly the type of game I'd like typically, i really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'll give this game a NEUTRAL review which, given the current average on Steam, translates into a negative one.Some people call this a Souls-like, but it's honestly more of a hybrid between Remnants of the Ashes and Metroid, both in terms of difficulty, and in terms of being RPG-lite and more focussed on mechanical puzzle solving (in combats, too) rather than timing and precision.Which, honestly, is a good point: I strongly loved the Metroid vibes the game gave: From the inquisitivey minded female protagonist, to the sci-fi setting, to the 'explore remnants of an alien race' to the various biomes and the well-executed backtracking (aka, you do visit some locations twice... but from different angles, and without constantly retreading the same paths).Graphics are solid, sound design likewise, and the story is decent, if VERY predictable. It's also a bit immersion-breaking that your protagonist is this scientist lady that can instantly draw conclusions to the most complex alien mechanism and xenobiology by a glance, but then misses the obvious clues to the story occurings and acts all surprised when 'the big reveal' comes around.The puzzles aren't too complicated, but executed nicely. The AR reconstruction / scientific analysis parts are fun and interesting. The combat itself is not too complex in mechanics, but the constant recombination of enemy types and environmental effects creates ever new and interesting puzzles to tackle.That is, until later in the game, where you unlock more and more passives from your skill tree (I ended the game with the FULL skill tree plus plenty of points to spare), and have figured out the most efficient ways to deal with enemies. At that point, difficulty just sharply falls off the cliff: There's five boss fights. The first was a fair introduction, the second a fun challenge, the third very long-winded (because the solution to defeating the boss wasn't as intuitive), the fourth was a joke (and died faster than many of the regular enemies you have to deal with at that point) and the final one? Even worse of a joke with no challenge whatsoever, mostly due to the amount of gadgets and gadget charges you can just leverage to trivialize the fight.There were a few minor bugs, mainly in the dialogue animation department, and one annoying one where leaving a freezing biome would continue to play the constant shivering 'oh I'm freezing' voicelines, even after you had long since left the biome. A reload fixed that though.Overall, Scars Above would make a solid game and a positive recommendation...except for it's brevity. 5.3h for a full playthrough, with absolutely no replayability value. At a 40€ price tag? Look, I'm all for quality over quantity, but compared to masterworks like Hellblade, Scars Above is a solid game, but *not* a great one. And thus I would argue the slim width of content defintely doesn't justify that price tag.So my recommendation is 'this is a good game, but not exactly a must-have, and you would definitely want to wait for a sale to pick it up'. (Got it on a 60% off sale btw, which puts it into a much more reasonable, if still high, price category for it's length.)Overall rating: 6/10Good, but not exceptional, and way too short.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this a lot more than I expected. Of course the limited budget shows - this is not an AAA title. Animations are stiff and lack variation, facial expressions (emotions) of the characters are almost non-existent, which is painfully apparent when combined with the good voice acting (Act V has some awesome creepy music and atmosphere), graphics are mediocre, creature design doesn't have much variation. Gathering "knowledge cubes" to increase stats is a rather lazy mechanic. But in the end the things that matter work: The story is pretty good and well told, shooting is satisfying and combining your different weapons makes for some fun gameplay; there's some change in pace with small puzzles and mini-games. Also the game is short in a good way, it doesn't outstay its welcome. If you like hard sci-fi and story driven third person shooters with some mild puzzle elements then this might be for you as well. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game! Combat is decent, its not challenging but the combination of elemental damages and a dodge mechanic do make the combat enjoyable. The graphics are good. I got this on sale for $6 and I think its a heck of a deal at that price. Not sure if its worth $30 with all the other offerings out there, but if its on sale I would definitely grab it if I were you. Play it on the hardest difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game.  I love a challenging game.  If you do too, this game is for you.  Worth every dollar!I took it nice and slow trying to get every achievement possible. I looked around and took in the nice graphics.  I only wish that there were more games like this.  I love puzzle type exploration and survival games.  Ones that make you think a bit. Great story and nice work on this game devs.  Make another like it.  Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. Honestly. Gameplay is really good, progression is linear, combat feels nice and intuitive and exploration isn't too grindy. Even though it borrows some elements from the souls-like genre it's certainly nowhere near as difficult. To be honest, it is a bit short, i finished it in about 2 days and no New Game+ is kinda tragic. There are no other modes or anything, you play the story and that's it. But for $9 i had a really good time and I might even play it again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I want to be able to recommend this, but the way it is for fights even on the easiest setting makes it impossible to play through. The Aim Assist feature doesn't seem to actually assist you in finding targets to make fights easier. I started on the normal difficulty and without Aim Assist. I wanted to try the 'expected normal experience' but that was becoming very hard to beat certain enemies. Mostly I focus on the story and I like fights, but I do not enjoy punishing fights that make you die, run, fight, repeat, over and over and over again. It becomes relentless and makes the game very much not enjoyable. I switched the difficulty level to Recruit and turned on Aim Assist to see if that made things easier. It did not. At the moment I have chosen  to stop playing this game as I do get migraines easily and they also grow worse with different impacting experiences. And this game definitely is one of those experiences. I may try again, because I do love the idea behind this, but for now it's not something I'm even attempting. I do hope that there will be a game update to make the easier mode with game assist actually more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: My Review of Scars AboveReally enjoyed the story of this game, got to admit was a bit put of by the difficulty at first but after about 1 hour in i got use to controller buttons really enjoyed the action and game play.i Completed the game and love the little hints to SI-FI movies the music is really good to graphics really good if you enjoy SI-FI stories and third person shooters then give this a go you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Please keep in mind that this is an AA game, and for an AA game it delivered everything I'd expected. The best thing I can say about the game is the music definitely, reminded me of that Mass Effect feels. The guns design all looks unique to its own world, and the enemy is varied enough so much so it's not just an endless dodge and shoot mechanics. The facial expressions could improve a bit though during in-game and cinematic, as the story is decent enough to pull you in.Solid 8 out of 10!
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game for less than £7 when I was going to purchase it for much more. I was curious as to why it was so cheap after release. The game itself is a sci fi game that is based around souls type games. It is about 8 hours in length, the length of a call of duty campaign so quite short. I only played an hour and a half so far and like it. It is difficult like souls games but not as difficult. I would say this is not a big budget game but it is still unique enough to spend £7 on. I just faced the first Alpha boss, and it was tough, I thought it was too tough to start with but then I realised the strategy to beat it. The game is not as fluent as it could be but it is simple in nature which I prefer in a game. Definitely worth a purchase especially in this sale they have.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I can tell that the game is good. From my perspective I'm in no place to say it's short since creating it took much much more time that just playing it. Nonetheless comparing it to Mass Effect it is shorter I would say. There's just few characters out there and whole sci-fi setting is a bit locked to life (plants and animals) on one planet. But that's how the story is designed and it is designed good. Having said that I would say it's 8/10 from my perspective. It is a bit too hard to my taste.If you'd ask: It runs on steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Decent sci-fi game with all the typical elements of the genre. Nice to have a woman as the main protagonist. Sadly the planet's swamp area and creatures are ugly and off putting which is a shame since that's our introduction to the game. I changed the game mode to rookie to move on from this place quickly and after that the game became a lot more enjoyable. I went back to normal difficulty halfway through and it was fine. As you unlock gadgets, weapons and skill points the game becomes more fun. Lots of good ideas with the gadgets I thought. Some of the creatures are interesting but others (the "alpha" who acts like a gorilla) felt very unoriginal and out of place. But overall fine, a classic sci-fi experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is, decent at best. Decent Story, Decent Graphics, Decent Combat. The monsters and combat can seem tedious at times, and the boss fights aren't exactly "hard", but moreso frustrating, as in, you're supposed to kill the monster in a certain way, but somewhat unpolished hit-boxes and AI mechanics make that impossible or hard to achieve. I am however invested in the story, and would want a sequel. It'd have to be on sale tho or a cheaper price than this.

_childDocuments_.review: The story feels captivating and interesting, and the combat is kind of fun, I was expecting a game like mass effect or even outriders, but this game act and feel like a soft souls game where you lose all progression if you die or log out, and all the enemies respawn when you use the pillar save, and the enemies are rather brutal.I don't mind the difficulty of the enemies but i really hate the save system.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm sure many people will love this game, it's just not for me. Certain aspects of this game are AAA quality, while other aspects feel like a Wish product. refunded.Graphically this game is a mixed bag. The scenery, effects and game world are visually stunning, while the enemies look straight out of a 20-year old PS2 game and the human faces look like they're made of play-doh, even with all graphic settings maxed out. The voice acting is good albeit the lips don't seem to sync up with the voice all the time, and there are little to no facial expressions.The controls are janky/clunky. They're not terrible but something feels off for a third person shooter. I prefer to play this style of close combat game with an Xbox Series controller, but it feels more like a mouse and keyboard experience. Even the Menu layout screams mouse and keyboard. They're trying to go for a Soul's-like experience but with guns. All the ingredients are there for a stellar AAA game, but a good recipe does not make a good cook (as they say). As for difficulty, if you like a hard game then this is probably your cup o' tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Although firmly on the soft end of the sci-fi scale, there's still plenty of imagination here. To find it, you may need to beat your forehead bloody on the 'Dark Souls: IN SPACE!' design philosophy that apparently infested this game like a neuro-parasite in the second half of it's development... but it is there. The game clearly went through multiple rewrites and reevaluations of scope, and honestly it's kind of a mess, but there's a certain indie charm to the sheer ballsy ambition of it.It is certainly worth playing, if you can look past its many faults. Note that I said it's worth playing, not worth buying. You should put as much money into buying this game as the devs put into the characters' facial animations: that is to say, get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: An underrated third-person shooter/puzzler that weaves an interesting story through a well-crafted world.I came in with no expectations or context and was pleasantly surprised to find a tight game without compromises. I nearly 100%'d the entire game but didn't feel like I needed to in order to enjoy myself. I especially liked the simple 4-weapon system and the chemical interactions/weak points system, which made intuitive sense and made the moment-to-moment gameplay really fun. The game is "short" by some standards but I feel like this is a strength of its design.I hope to see more work from this studio in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. The story is intriguing and keeps you wanting to find out what happened and it does leave you with an interesting sequel bait while nonetheless finishing up the story it sets up in the game. I do look forward to a possible next installment. Now, that said, although I'd recommend the game, I'd also say the game was not what I was expecting based on how it described itself. It did give me vibes of a 'space subnautica' exploration game as you explored the life in a new planet while finding out ways to survive and leave it. So....the game is none of that. It is fairly linear. The crafting is rather automatic. Also, for a game based on a story about testing every possible DNA assembly and every possible combination of it, the diversity of life on the planet was lacking. It was a weird choice to make the final boss a slight variety of an early boss who was itself a variation of a common enemy. And it was also weird that the entire alien species you find in the game consists of identical people. That also being said, the alien backstory is interesting and it makes for a likable character in the game, and the enemies in the game are very interesting in terms of the game play elements they add. So, in summary, it is good, could be much better, hoping they improve for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, a bit linear but the story pulls you in despite being simplistic, yet effective. Atmospheric experience with synth music like Mass Effect and great visuals. You are Kate, a scientist lost in an alien world... Yes, a bit hard at first, but soon you will find yourself being unstoppable. Explore every nock and crany and you are set! I really needed a game like this, impossible to get lost but easy to progress; sometimes you need a "corridor game". Sci fi tropes and quick gameplay, what's not to like? Totally recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: My fist 5 hours and I couldn't stop playing, the enemies are only difficult if you don't know their weakspot/don't take advantage of combos, other than that it's a great time, interesting story so far( reminds me of a Dead Space meets Remnant From the Ashes. It's a difficult game to be sure but only in the sense of it's very unforgiving if you mess up.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my nine hours with Scars Above, been playing alot of triple-A 70$ open world games and this simpler more linear experience was a breath of fresh air.I never got lost and no area overstayed its welcome, i played on highest difficulty and while i died a couple of times it was not too difficult, i was never frustrated with the combat system.My only gripe would be the stiff facial animation during the pre rendered cutscenes but that's a minor issue. I enjoyed it enough that i'm currently looking for similar games, if anyone has any recommendations please let me know.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: What Calisto Protocol could have been. While not on the same level, the game is highly enjoyable albeit a lot more simplistic. You can see the Dead Space inspiration for the story and set but it still spins some little twists of it's own.While I can't recommend it at full price it's a must have for shooter horror enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above was a great game for a few hours worth of playtime. I completed the game in 14 hours, some of that was not actual playtime as I had to step away for a bit. The combat is a little weird to get used to with the element mixing and matching, requiring fights where you need to rapidly swap weapons in order to defeat certain enemies, as any difficulty higher than Rookie cannot be brute forced. Story was a little slow to start, but once I got going I wanted to finish it to see the conclusion.Combat and gameplay is very similar to Remnant, which I enjoy. The game is pretty much on rails but exploring those side paths lead to plenty of weapon upgrades and skill points. Story was satisfying and not overly complicated, which I enjoyed.I got it on sale for 5.99 US, however I would've easily paid more for this game, it was well put together, and had fun mechanics once I got the hang of it. If it's on sale, it's a must grab.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay if you can put up with it not doing anything perfectly.The graphics are okay, the gameplay is fine, the story is nothing special, but also quite okay.Cinematics are not very good and the game gets a little repetitive after a few hours.But it's a fine deal if you are looking for something to spend a few hours on.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: You play as Kate, a Scientist who has undergone training to be a member of SCARS and are joined by her crew mates to investigate a unknown entity that has recently appeared near Earth. As the SCARS members heads towards to strange entity, it would seem a strange force had pull the crew members towards the strange object and crashed landed to a strange planet. It is up to Kate to find the missing members of SCARS and to escape the planet they crashed landed on. What mysteries will Kate find during her search and rescue? Welcome to SCARS Above.Control Kate, as she explores with the dangers of the wild creatures that inhabit the planet, Gun you way with 4 unique guns and many upgrades to find for them during you adventure. Many guns deal different types of effects, and you can combo these effects to deal massive damage to the enemies, Explore and discover cubes that increase your skill points to spec out Kate to help her survive, and use the many gadgets to your advantage to help you on your adventure.As great as the game is, there are many times where i would get stuck on the geometry while explore the planet, which causes to lose a bit of progress i had made since i had to return to a previous pillar (These are practically like Bon Fires.) causing the enemies to re-spawn again to reach the area i was stuck at. Even on the hardest difficulty, the game was very easy to accomplish. A lot of the extra unlocks for weapon were really "all in your face" so it really didn't feel i explored as much as i had hope to unlock these upgrades. Speaking of Upgrade, you will have a lot of left over skill point once you are near the end of the game. I had about 9 Skill points that i was unable to allocate due to the fact i had already unlocked everything. while this isn't a problem cause i don't expect everyone to explore, the main issues is the constant "9" in the middle of my screen informing me i had unused skills points. While not too big of a deal, can get a little annoying to see.I Highly recommend this game... at a discount. While i did have a great time with it, it was still only a four hour experience.. and that ain't  a lot for a $40 game.  Thanks for the great game!-KokoLocoRoco
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: It’s pretty good, and underrated. Decent story, voice acting and combat. The visual design is a highlight, with the presented world being very alien and quite awesome to behold. Sound design and music are also very good. There isn’t much incentive to replay the game, unfortunately, but it’s still worth a play through, especially for fans of Dead Space and Remnant: From the Ashes.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Smooth gameplay so far. Good pacing with the story and easy to follow along. Forces you to be a somewhat proactive player, not be a completely braindead player.-Many puzzles -Boss fights have you use multiple weapons due to elemental weak spot mechanics -Environmental mechanics to adapt to during fights -Always rewarding to explore side areas for exp.-Very little to no backtracking to progress the story-Character leveling & crafting is simpleOverall a good game. Not an overly complicated game with super in-depth customization / build-crafting, just a little bit of everything to be simple & enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals are beautiful. Short, but very interesting story. As a family man, i started appreciating games that are well paced and not too long as i can rarely find time for long gaming sessions, and this game fits that perfectly.Even though im not into souls-like games i enjoyed it. Might be due to the lack of difficulty some of the reviewers are mentioning, but on the other hand a lot of people are disliking the save system most probably because it was too hard for them. For me the difficulty and game mechanics were perfectly balanced. Died quite a few times but not too much to lose interest in the game. Game mechanics are simple, but interesting. While they dont really add too much to the difficulty, they keep the played enaged just enough so it doesnt feel like grind between story chunks.All in all, this game was really out of my comfort zone and not something i usually play, but i really did enjoy it greatly

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where majority of AAA games with huge marketing, budgets, massive dev teams fail to deliver any fun or meaningful experiences, AA and indie developers are our only shining light. Mad Head Games have delivered an amazing experience with Scars Above. A massive thank you for all the people that worked on this game, I loved every second of it and I hope that you guys will be encouraged to stay on the same path and make more games like this one! Disclaimer: I finished the game on another platform and bought it on steam to post this review.I will break my review into sections for those who are interested or are on the fence (people that negatively affected the score of this game just because of motion blur should be ashamed of themselves, that has nothing with gameplay, story or performance and can be fixed with an update).- Gameplay:You have elemental guns and also gadgets that are not only for combat but they also act as puzzle pieces or helps with traversal, just as a small example: you can use the ice gun to freeze the water to avoid hazardous monsters, freeze enemy and bosses or use it to solve a puzzle. Furthermore, the guns react to each other and cause chemical reactions which also extends to the environment where the electric gun will shock enemies in water or covered in water (rain).Any monster is a threat, so you have to keep your eyes open 24/7 and if you die, you will respawn at the last resurrection pillar you activated (bonefire from darksouls). Exploring is very rewarding and you should always do that to acquire unique upgrades to your weapons and gadgets. There is also a leveling system where you pick abilities to add to your combat style.- Story, environments and atmosphere:I will not post any spoilers regarding the story.If you love Sci mysteries, you will love the story, and even if you don't, the cast, events and environments will suck you in. The game is moody, has a soft horror vibe in some sections and has a nice selection of varied levels, some of these levels you will not expect or see coming.- Performance:Runs buttery smooth on my 3070 laptop, max settings 2560x1600 resolution (2K)- Things that can be improved:Facial animations, lip sync and music (in some levels).- Things I wish were there:New game +Nvidia DLSSMotion Blur slider
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

I think areas could have been a little more interesting if they really forced you to rotate through the different weapons more or if the gadgets you can use felt like they had a wider use. _childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately not interesting enough to me that I felt like trudging through the really quite awful, clunky gameplay. I was on board at first because it seemed to be trying to do something with elemental reactions; your main (possibly only) weapon can switch between different damage types and it was setting up the ability to do things like lure enemies into water and then shock them for a damage boost and AoE effect. I wasn't super jazzed about the bland levels and unresponsive controls, but I felt I should at least see what else they were doing with their central mechanic.The first real boss of the game? A tedious slog in a perfectly circular, flat arena with strategic ammo pickups scattered around the edge against a giant monkey with a weakspot on its chest that it revealed about once every five minutes. Nothing clever with the environment, no point using the new freezing grenade option you just unlocked for your weapon, just run around and dodge and hope that the crappy hit detection allows you a hit maybe every now and then. When it did finally go down I just sort of gazed at the screen blankly for a while before deciding I had better things to do than another few hours of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a nice AA game using some elements from the Souls Franchise to create a Dark Sci-Fi experience on an alien planet.All in all Scars Above won't rock your world, but the developers did a good job with it. I don't see half baked ideas floating around screaming "we were outside the scope and budget of our developers", I don't see bs workarounds for the game mechanics to force ideas into the game that simply have no place there. _childDocuments_.review: A very interesting and enjoyable amalgamation of various genres and styles, albeit a bit rough around the edges. It's like a janky old school story-driven survival horror shooter. If that's even a thing. I guess it is now.Kind of felt like I was playing Tormented Souls in the Mass Effect universe after it had been populated by the Precursors from Subnautica. One hell of a ride, needless to say.Combat is overall fun with cool abilities and interesting elemental combos that together make for a very rewarding experience. Bosses are diverse and interesting and often reward some levels of thinking outside of the box. There is a good balance of the old school horror-aspects with limited resources, specific save points, having to run quite far if you die, and so on - but not so much so that it becomes frustrating.Also, I was positively impressed with the story and especially the voice acting. The story probably won't blow anyone away as it's nothing new per se, but it managed to create something that felt sufficiently fresh that's not lacking in intrigue or excitement.  I got about eight hours or so of entertainment which is perhaps a bit on the low end for what we're used to these days but considering the genre and what the game is trying to accomplish, it makes sense to me.Overall, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Dev has fixed sprint crash.  I'm further along in the game.  Really liked the area that's basically an HR Geiger version of a Forerunner installation.I have a soft spot for good low-budget B-grade games, and this one hits that spot.  Especially if you get it on sale, it's worth it, but even at full price, the devs probably deserve your $.  It runs very smoothly (I get 90-120fps on ultra with an RTX4060 at 1440p ultrawide).  This game plays like Remnant by way of Metroid Prime.  It can be kind of difficult at first, but it has adjustable difficulty and once you figure out how to make the best use of all your gear (some of the earliest additions aren't explained well enough, and occasionally the tutorials misled me into using the wrong tool for the job... Let's just say "Vera" is your friend), it's actually moderate to easy.  Graphics are pretty good, but rough around the edges occasionally, showing the budget.  The art direction is really pretty great, and the sound design in general is fantastic... One of the later areas has truly unnerving ambient sounds.All in all a brief (8-11 hours) sci-fi Remnant-style game with light puzzling and exploration elements.  If you don't mind a few rough edges, and appreciate a good game that respects your time, you'll enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a new sci-fi game that kept me entertained and engaged throughout its 15-hour campaign. The story was well-written and kept me on the edge of my seat, always anticipating what was going to happen next. The gameplay was equally enjoyable, with diverse and interesting combat against unique bosses that required different strategies to defeat.However, there were some areas where the game fell short. The lack of detail and FX in the world, especially in the lighting and shadows, was disappointing and made it difficult to fully immerse myself in the game's futuristic setting. Additionally, the leveling up of abilities through the collection of "knowledge cubes" could use some balancing, as some abilities made the game much easier and the enemies didn't get progressively more difficult as the player progressed through the game.The story was a highlight, but the lack of cutscenes to fully flesh out the characters and the world was disappointing. The few cutscenes that were included were short and crudely animated, which detracted from the overall experience.Despite these flaws, "Scars Above" was a fun and engaging game that I would recommend to sci-fi fans and those who enjoy challenging boss battles. It's worth noting that I completed the game on normal difficulty and was able to achieve 91% completion in my 15-hour playthrough.

Voice acting was also really well done, made me care about the characters. Exploration was good enough for me. The only negative thing I can say about this game is that some parts of Chapter 2 and 3 made the fps severely low and that made me frustrated.Overall I give this game a 9/10. Mad Head Games, you guys have done a phenomenal job in developing this game and I can't wait to see what new games you come up with in future. <3

It breaks its own combat rules pretty often, and there's no explanation except dying without feedback, which is not fun.The animations nearly never align with the voice acting and are a staggered, stilted mess.The storytelling is sub-par with too much telling instead of showing, and the telling is boring and emotionless.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is an interesting game. You play as Kate Ward who is part of a first contact mission from Earth, who awakens on an alien planet  with no clue as to how she got there. The local wildlife is vicious to say the least and every time they snack on her she awakens near one of the pillars that serve as the game's bonfires.Yeah, it's a third person shooter with soulslite elements set to the tune of sci-fi horror. Unfortunately one can't describe the story without heavy spoilers, but it is a fun game even if it lacks polish in spots. Controls are mostly responsive, bar that using B (x-box controller) to exit the menu's launches your melee attack, and that switching weapons locks you out of your item selection menu for a bit.The environments are kinda varied, but enemy variety is only so-so. Story related that, but still. The worst part on that front may be the Final Boss.... Facial animations aren't great, but serviceable. The voiceacting is better, thankfully. And I do really like the ability to craft weapons, gadgets and upgrades to get ahead in game. One thing I dislike though is hypothermia, a status effect that's triggered by snowfall. The light a bush on fire mechanic is meh, but the devs didn't playtest apparently. Some areas are filled with those bushes (but don't get snowfall) while one area where the buildup is speedy and an armoured enemy lurks has a grand total of three bushes. And no, you can't use the flammable liquid plus your thermal blaster to warm up.The difficulty is also a bit of a concern. Early game you're literally a punching bag desperately dodge-rolling... but after the third weapon it snowballs into being mostly trivial. Except where the game cheeses through a bottleneck or letting drones repair enemies.Scars Above is a fun game. It's not perfect, there's enough to gripe about... but it definitely is a good experience to have.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so massively disappointing. First off, the game starts off way too difficult, even on easy, but by the end of the game you're so overpowered that the final boss could be done with your eyes closed. Second, the story itself is weak at best. The characters have no defining features, no real personality, no development. Everyone is a generic stereotype. Everything is remarkably black and white, and the closest we get to characterization is a half-assed hallucination sequence that has no real impact on the story. There are no twists, no real developments. It doesn't deviate at all from what is laid out in the beginning: Bad guy destroy aliens, bad guy must be stopped. That is quite literally the entire plot. It contains no real substance, and compounded with the often-aggravating gameplay and the uncanny (and crude) animations, the game is just a severely mediocre drop in the bucket. This would all be fine if the game otherwise made up for it, but it simply doesn't. It doesn't play well enough or look pretty enough to justify having virtually no actual material. I spent the entire game being reminded of things I'd rather be playing. This is only really worth it on a very big sale, and only if you really have nothing else to do.

_childDocuments_.review: It's labeled as a soulslike game but while it borrows from that genre it doesn't really fit. _childDocuments_.review: Scars Above does not raise the bar for shooters, but that does not make it a bad experience. It offers a relatively brisk seven-hour adventure that does not get too repetitive. Its shooting is competent, with elemental damage quirks and decent gadgetry. The various alien creatures and their weak spots keep the combat fresh, with a few respectable boss fights. Although the beginning is tedious, with sparsely placed pillars acting like Dark Souls respawn points, it gets much easier (and fun) as it transitions into a more traditional third-person shooter. Scars Above certainly needed more creativity to break away from its generic attributes, but at least the pieces it borrows from other games are stitched together well.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like combat that feels like a quicktime event? Do you like games that are artificially difficult? Then this is the game for you! Really, none of it is difficult, none of it actually feels like combat, it's not balanced, it gives no wiggle room for how the player wants to play, and if you don't jump through the exact hoop the developers want you to jump through, you don't progress. Simple as that!Let's start with combat. One of the earliest enemies you fight is what is essentially an armored gorilla. The reason I've chosen this enemy is because every enemy in the game essentially has the same gimmick.This armored gorilla takes little to no damage, from any weapon, except from your fire based weapon. This weapon has a three second charge time before it fires what is essentially a puff of smoke, unless you hit a specific weak spot, on specific enemies, that are actually vulnerable to said weapon. Even better, once charged, the weapon only allows you to hold this charge for about another second before it releases the shot, regardless of if you want it to or not, making your timing crucial, and inserting even more artificial difficulty into the fight. The gorilla's weak spot is only vulnerable for a split second when the gorilla closes in and rears up to slam it's fists into the ground. Forcing you into a very specific, tedious pattern of close range play to deal with this enemy. Then, once you've shot this weak spot enough, the gorilla roars for a split second, which gives you a tiny window of opportunity to change weapons and fire a different, but again specific, weapon into it's mouth to do more damage. You then rinse and repeat this process until one or more enemies are dead in what feels like one giant quicktime event after another.I know what you're thinking.. Not EVERY fight can be like that, right? Okay, let's talk about Chapter 2. During chapter 2 you're caught in a snow storm, forcing you to fight several gorilla enemies that are covered in snow, making them immune to fire damage. Good news, tho! You're on a frozen lake! You can use your fire weapon to punch a hole in the ice, allowing the gorillas to fall into the water and freeze solid, allowing you to shatter them with a well placed shot from a different, but again specific, weapon. Sounds easy enough, right? Except the ice takes two shots, in the same place, to break, your fire weapon, again, requires you to charge it, and the gorillas are not just moving, but actively avoiding the places you shoot to try and break the ice, once again forcing you into the same close combat play style, the only difference is now you're aiming and the ground.Still sounds too easy? That's because it is. During one particular fight with two of these gorillas the ground is also swarmed with spiders, are the spiders particularly dangerous? No, but they will catch your shots, protecting the ice from damage while trying to play out the quicktime event.Still doesn't sound that bad? Well, do I have a surprise for you! During the quicktime event, in the middle of a snow storm, you also have to deal with hypothermia. That's right, if you fail to warm yourself up, you will flat out die by freezing to death. How do you warm yourself up? There are bushes that are interspersed through out the level that, when shot with your fire weapon, burn and emit heat for a short time, allowing you to warm yourself as long as you stand within the aura they emit, and after they're used, they're gone forever, giving you a limited time, and limited amount of resources, to combat the cold.That's right! Quicktime events where you juggle the invulnerable gorillas, can't shoot the ground and break the ice because the spiders will catch your shots, AND you get to freeze to death in literally one minute! Should you need to warm up during the fight? Good luck trying to stand in that tiny aura while juggling two gorillas and a hoard of spiders!TL;DR? The developers of this game need to resign. They haven't made a game, they've made a giant quicktime event, then, I can only assume after they realized this, inserted needless mechanics into what is already tedious combat to artificially boost difficulty. My only regret? That I really tried to like this game, and didn't refund it before the 2 hour limit.

_childDocuments_.review: The Earth is approached by a giant alien construct, and a select team of specialsts- SCARS are chosen to approach it and make first contact. After initial introduction section (where you get to meet the stereotypical crew members and learn the basics of item manipulation) something goes very wrong and you, Kate Ward, double Ph.D in biology and Mech Engineering- find yourself on a hostile planet, among wrecks of your ships' cargo and haunted by a strange alien apparition. That's where the game really begins, and its a mix of third person shooting, light exploration and puzzle solving. The shooting involves juggling 4 elemental weapon types (electric, fire, ice and acid) to match specific enemy's weakness. certain enemies have elemental weak point that need to be exposed first, and then you can shoot them for massive damage. In this sense, it's similar to the Horizon games. Some people like to say this is a "souls-like", but honestly, I wouldn't say that. There's a stamina bar, that's used for melee attacks and dodge-rolling, enemies respawn when you save at a checkpoint, and your health pickups and ammo refill, but there's no penalty for death, and only rudimentary shortcuts. You can also unlock a skill that gives you some health for  killing enemies with melee, but it's only really useful for a few enemy types, and is rather risky for everyone else. The levels are pretty linear, with some side-paths that yield either extra XP (used to unlock passive Skills), or weapon upgrades. The main path is always marked with blue or red lights, so it's pretty easy to navigate and make sure you don't accidentally lock yourself out of extra stuff. Overall, there's a lot of extra XP (I finished the game unlocking all skills, and then had enough extra XP left over to unlock 7 more skills). Sometimes you need to solve puzzles to progress, but there's nothing particularly complex. Game ran flawlessly on my Ryzen 3700X and 1660ti at 1080p Ultra; no serious bugs to report- occasionally the waypoint would dissappear, but going into the menu and back into the game fixed that. Overall, a really solid linear game with a decent story (VERY strong System Shock 2 influences), varied level design and interesting, albeit basic combat system. Easy title to recommend to anyone who likes action-adventures with some climbing, shooting, exploration and puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, but lukewarm.  It's pretty enough, with a modicum of predictable and cliched story, but the dialogue is terrible, and (with the sole exception of the protagonist) not well voiced either - fortunately, it is skippable, though missing the cutscenes means you'll miss a few contextual clues about what is going on.  Oddly mechanical character movement which I guess is lacklustre motion-capture.  Combat and crafting are on par for this sort of game, though the boss fights are tedious, relying on hitting weak points in order to do any damage, and sometime with weapons that you need to charge by holding down a button, then shoot by releasing it (button-up to shoot can be frustratingly counter-intuitive, making it harder to hit).  Also frustrating to navigate and too easy to end up wandering in circles trying to figure out where it wants you to go; it's quite linear and insists you go where it wants you to, so if you don't spot the path to get there, you can't make progress.  All things considered, it's enjoyable enough to pick up on sale, but hard to recommend at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I rip into this game, let me state this: I definitely don't dislike this game. I'm giving it a thumbs up because it's worth playing on a good discount. It's nothing incredible, but you'll get a solid eight hours of fun out of it. What I have is mainly just a bunch of small gripes that brought the whole experience down to "average" rather than "good."I got this game gifted to me for my birthday after having it on my wish list for a year. After playing through the game on the standard difficulty, what I was left feeling after a bit under 9 hours was that I'd played a tech demo for a larger game. There's a decent game here, hidden under a solid first couple hours but a very bland mid/endgame, a painfully predictable story, systems that don't really interconnect, and "puzzles" that devolve into "shoot thing with matching color." The only time the game surprised me was when the one time a puzzle required me to inspect something in my inventory and manipulate it. I hadn't done that since five minutes into the tutorial, and seven hours later I didn't remember it was a thing you could do until a popup told me to go do it. After a few jump scares here and there, figuring out how to deal with a new enemy, and then it's all just same-same. Resources were so abundant the only time I ran out of ammo was figuring out how to beat bosses. The final "boss" upset me because it really was just a reskin of something you fight repeatedly through the game, just with a bigger health bar. The typical combat "puzzle" is that an enemy has a weak point you need to hit with a matching color of weapon. Color and element are basically interchangeable terms when it comes to combat. Blue spot? Shoot electricity. Orange? Fire. Once you know what color to shoot, there's no puzzle left. Kate, the protagonist, will even talk out loud and tell you the right thing to do to kill things. And you'd better do what you're told, because you can dump every point of ammo you have into an enemy and not kill if if you don't shoot the weak point. And yet... A thing I really do love and hate at the same time is that enemy weak points are guarded. It makes total sense that a creature would hold up an armored arm to prevent you from shooting the glowing bit in its chest. It's completely reasonable that a creature turns to face you rather than let you shoot it in the back. But the enemies are often TOO good at avoiding the damage. The enemy with the armored arm is only really vulnerable when it's swinging up to attack you - and if it's doing that, you need to dodge or you're going to get whacked. The enemy with the weak point on his back can turn 180 degrees in a fraction of a second to swing at you.There's tools to fix that, like the "stasis" field that really is just a "make everything move slower for a few seconds," but the first few times with each critter type you won't have those tools, and really you can just wait for them to make the swing, dodge past them, and shoot them in the back. Or just use the cryo gun, freeze them, and line up a shot. It's just... bland.I think my biggest critique of the game, despite enjoying it overall, was that I had to take several days of a break between chapters 5 and 6 for work reasons - and I came back to the game having forgotten all the controls, and still completed the last  chapter without ever coming close to dying even once. I didn't use a monolith (campfire) the entire last chapter.And for anyone coming in with "just play it on Commander," the story won't change, there's no new items, no achievement for doing it, and the enemies don't get new moves - they just get more health and deal more damage to you. You might scrape a couple more hours out of the game because of the increased health pools though, so if you want more challenge, go right ahead and play on Commander. Now that I've complained a bunch, here's some things I genuinely liked:The unique bosses requiring you to use the environment to kill them.Body horror and sci-fi are always a good combo.The weapon upgrades actually felt like real upgrades - piercing on the lightning gun, more ammo per clip, different firing modes, tighter spread on the acid shotgun - these are good things that made the weapons easier to use.The little virtual arenas that teach you how to use the new gadgets you make were a nice, quick break from the routine, and did an excellent job of showing you what each gadget's purpose was.The Big Bad seemed appropriately threatening as the villain of the story (outside of the ending which I don't want to spoil.)The elemental combo system always felt like a nice bonus when I could pull it off.The game has solid potential, and I WOULD be interested in a sequel if they made one. I just hope they do better than merely average next time!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an AA title for an AA price. You have to go in expecting that. Already seen some reviewers criticising the game for a certain level of Jank. This game is on par with a title like The Chant which released at the end of last year.  I personally love a good low budget game the same way i enjoy a B-Movie and i also think that horror titles in particular are better off when they are a bit gritty and rough around the edges. It adds to the uncomfortable atmosphere.The game gets you into the action after a pretty short intro section. This section does a good job of introducing you to the game world and characters as well as some of the base game mechanics. There are things to pick up and read or listen to that will increase your immersion and understanding of the game world. Once you get into the meat of the game it plays a bit like a metroidvania title with different areas locked away until you have certain powers or tools. You progress through the story but each time you die you reset to a save point a little bit like a souls game where enemies reset. You have skills you can gradually level up and unlock as well.There are weapon upgrades to craft that make things easier. Some are more hidden and some are on the main path. The enemies are all pretty neat so far. The weapons can combo to create more damage or impact weak spots but there is an element of resource management at play as well.The game is also pretty challenging in places - and while you can tone down (or increase) the difficulty on the normal setting i have died a fair number of times - but in a way that feels fair. Some encounters just catch you out the first few times until you start to learn. So its got some really nice gameplay and combat elements woven in.The puzzle design and interaction is also really nicely done. I love the way you interact and move around the puzzle scenes. It feels very tactile. So far the puzzles haven't been too challenging but i have had to stop and think a  bit. Almost got tempted to cheat and look something up online but finally figured it out after looking around the puzzle scene a bit more for an extra clue.I can tell that this is going to be one of the rare games for me that i actually play all the way through,I haven't gotten too far in yet but so far it seems great and i'm excited to really give it some solid play time over the coming weeks.Oh. And it runs flawlessly on max settings for me which for a release in 2023 is worth recognition as well. Nothing seems overtly broken or buggy.So if you are a fan of indie / lower budget games and want to try something different from the main stream cookie cutter game factory machine then this is certainly going to be well worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming game. It reminds me of the feelings I had when I played A Plague Tale Innocence and Hellblade for the first time. Game from a small studio that tries to provide rich gameplay and story. Perhaps, a sort of AA game. I really did like everything about the game.  Core game mechanics are actually quite nice. You have to consider combinations of different elements, such as environment and weapon choice + gadgets to take down enemies. I think that was really well managed in the game. You can make the combat difficult, if you don't consider the options you have been given. I like that approach in this game.I think the game would had benefit for more richer exploration and crafting. The idea behind crafting is actually quite clever. Some good engineering small game to craft items and components would had fit perfectly in the game regarding the background story. Now items are pretty much just there to find. Also game world seems to be rather small scope. You actually run corridors and secrets are just behind different corner. I think the level and world design is probably the biggest down side in the game. Really pity, because if that had been better this would be an excellent game.I think the game pace is actually really good. There are moments when things go slower and there the emphasis is more on story and world building, then pace gets more intense and it's more combat orientated. There's a really good balance of when combat is provided and when small puzzles are offered and when everything leads to conclusion of level and a chapter.Like said, I really enjoyed virtually everything about the game. Well spent 10+ hours. With some more development and fine tuning, this would had been really an excellent game. But it's not bad at all for such a small studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up in a Humble Bundle as the description sounded interesting.  Given only the option to vote yes or no, I have to vote no.  If I could give this a thumbs middle, I would.  It's an OK game overall, but there's a lot of inconsistencies throughout and the game is severely missing any kind of map.Combat mechanics are good.  Different creatures are affected differently to the different weapons that you have, so you have to think on your feet to beat them.Level design is OK.  It's very linear, and it makes it very easy to get all of the collectibles in the game.  That being said, the open-world aspects can be confusing at times as the game has no map whatsoever, so you have to remember which path you've taken to get to your objective.  The story is set in the future, where you have a mobile 3D Printer that can print entire weapons in about 3 seconds flat and a scanner device that can analyze mechanisms hidden in structures, but nothing that can generate a map of the areas you've been to so you can reference paths you have already taken.  It does have a waypoint though, which at least is something.  Climbable ledges aren't consistently marked, so you might find yourself wandering around for a bit until you realize that there's a ledge you can climb up on.  Some of them are marked with a whiteish top to clearly identify it though.The story is OK.  Very straightforward Sci-Fi story, but for whatever reason, you're special because reasons.  Bad guy is using bad methods to do something good, so he needs to be stopped.  The game feeds you audio logs that spell out the reasons for things, and then has you watch a non-cutscene explanation of the very things you found in the audio logs previously towards the end.  Very little character development, if any, The story would have been better served with a twist ending.Graphics are good.  Not great, but good.Controls are OK.  I like to play with a reversed Y-axis camera, and that seemed to throw off the entire mouse in the scanning parts and the gadget wheel.Overall, I would say not to get this game unless you can get it in a really deep discount (like I did with the Humble Bundle) or you just absolutely love these types of games, otherwise, it's not quite worth it.  I do feel that the devs have some promise though.  They have good gameplay, and if they can just tweak the rest of it, they could have a really stellar game, or maybe a sequel.
