_childDocuments_.review: is a game that managed to surprise me and I mean that in a good way. I never considered myself a gamer, I mean I basically played League only for years but I decided to branch out and Scars Above became my first game I finished (on 100% completion too) so here's my humble opinion.The movement in this game doesn't feel as smooth as I would prefer. I think that the main problem with this is character's movement speed, whether it is attacks, dodging or running speed. I imagine the devs of this game realized that despite the large areas in the game and many enemies that will try to stop you on your every step, the game can be completed relatively fast. I mean, I myself managed to finish it in 8 hours which is not much game time, so I imagine they purposefuly set the character speed very low. But I mean, it does feel realistic, so if that's what you prefer. The guns feel very good and I enjoyed using all of them - of course, preferably in combination, because that is something you will use a lot in this game. Yes, you can combine your guns and you will have to switch to a fire gun if enemy has a weak spot to fire. But that is not all, you can also interact with the terrain in this game and use the guns accordingly, so if enemy is on frozen lake, you can shoot the ice and the enemy will fall through. That is a very cool mechanic and I had so much fun combining all the guns and gadgets, made me feel smart.There is also great variety of enemies, ready to be blasted. They all represent a certain challenge and they are all capable of making you hate them, especially if they jumpscare you by jumping out of the the water. The boss fights were fun and challenging. I liked that it's not only about blasting, but also using your brain to find advantage against your enemy. Again, made me feel smart. The one bad thing I have to mention is bugs. Sometimes the character would randomly get stuck in place, not being able to move. That would usually resolve itself after a few seconds, but other times, when I was in a river for example, and I got stuck, I had to use my cryo gun to freeze the space under me to finally move and jump out. I also died a few times to hypothermia while standing in the zone of the fire plant which was active, so I don't know about that. But none of these ruined the experience for me.One other thing that really bothered me is the respawns. When you respawn, the game resets all your ammo so you are ready to go at it again. But what about your fiber? If you fight, use heals, die and then respawn, your fiber doesn't reset so you are not able to use your heals again. That just doesn't make sense to me. Same thing if you switch the guns in your inventory. After respawning, the game resets your gun selection back. Why?I would say the world is a fine mix between Control and Alien universe. Grassy parts breath life into you and the slimy parts feel... well, slimy? Whether it is snowy mountains, smelly swamps or inside of a living organism, I always spent time looking around me and admiring the amazing textures. I had fun exploring the world and I think you will too. You get rewarded for it too so don't be lazy and just do it. Might add you some game time as well so win win? The monsters look very creepy so that's a good thing. The only problem I noticed is that some cutscenes look laggy, foggy and the expression on the character's faces are just bad.The music is okay, kinda catchy but nothing special. Some scores remind me of Mass Effect for some reason. The voice acting is great in this one, the actors really put their hearts into this. The sound effects of monsters and enviroment are also very decent.Big part of this game, of course it is. They work very well with the mysteries around you to keep you intrigued. It's simple, but it's good. The characters are rather bland, especially our main character. I think the problem with this one is, that our main character is only reacting to what the game throws at her. She never mentions what she likes, what she doesn't like, how she feels... She's just on a mission and that can feel empty. I also think the opening sequence could have been a little longer. Maybe the crew could have played some card game together, having fun before the mission starts. We would see them interacting, get the idea of what their relationships are like. Don't tell us Kate is friends with Mike, show us. But yeah, might have been a budget issues. Also, the hallucination sequence in the caves towards the finale was a bit unnecesary. Feels like you see this kind of thing in so many games and I wish the devs went for something a little bit more original.Overall, I had a great time playing the game, but it has it's issues. The game is short, it has some bugs and the characters feel bland, soulless and uninteresting, especially the MC, despite the amazing voice actors. I would give this game a solid

_childDocuments_.review:
Something strange has entered Earth's orbit; an object alien and unknowable, made out of matter that seems not to obey the laws of physics - the Metahedron. As a part of a hastily gathered group of astronauts and scientists sent off to explore it, your fate takes a jarring turn as you awaken in another world - dazed, alone on an alien planet... but determined to stay alive.  Scars Above is a challenging, immersive third-person shooter inspired by modern type action-adventure games. It takes the genre staples, such as the rewarding feeling of overcoming difficulty, and combines it with a compelling and intricate story, meticulous and lavish world design, and a living, breathing ecosystem to explore and endure.

This is a game of mystery and discovery.

name: WE ARE FOOTBALL
detailed_description: As a manager and trainer in WE ARE FOOTBALL, you’ll come face to face with the latest trends in the world of football, experiencing all the emotional highs and lows of your favorite club. For the first time ever, this modern football manager game also offers a women’s football game mode, featuring all the same functionality as well as many unique gameplay elements. To maintain and ensure the highest quality across all game modes, WE ARE FOOTBALL has been developed with experienced football management veterans such as Gerald Köhler, Rolf Langenberg, and Dirk Winter. You’ll get immediate feedback for every decision, big and small. You’ll have to plan out your deadlines effectively in the game, and will only be truly successful in the club by working together with your colleagues. WE ARE FOOTBALL focuses on real management tasks. The goal of the game is to build up the club over the long haul, including growing the team, colleagues, infrastructure, fans, and more. As a result, the football players in the game are individual personalities who spin their own stories. A season can be played through in a few hours: You’re in the middle of the action after just a few minutes. Alone, several seasons can be played through in one afternoon, and two players can even finish a season in an evening. There’s always new challenges to face in WE ARE FOOTBALL. The bigger the club, the bigger the challenge! Features: Beginner-friendly and playable without long introductions or tutorials – easy to learn but hard to master Just as complex as traditional manager games Club selection and career mode via settings quiz Comprehensive manager functionality (finances, sponsors, HR, organization, fan support, followers, IPO, sale of shares to investors, fan shares, and much more) Manager skills can be upgraded Implementation of the latest developments in football Detailed team and player attributes Modern training and realistic training planning Individual skills tree for each player Full psychological profile for each player – the team’s types need to match each other perfectly to have any chance of success Huge youth sector – manage player development even from a young age Comprehensive list of playing styles and basic rules New match engine with a focus on the ball and the players involved in the offenses with additional text commentary All matches in the game world are calculated equally Spectacular half-time speeches Expandable 3D stadium and 3D club grounds, as well as a club museum you can walk through Weekly progress with exciting negotiations and many small and big decisions to be made Comprehensive statistics section – a real treat for fans Critical fan commentary after the match Simulation of the ups and downs of major football teams Simulation of national team tournaments with changes in the market value of team players The game doesn’t include any official football licenses. The game comes with an editor which lets you create your own leagues or clubs: Any country in the world can be edited Men’s and women’s leagues Choice of official or personal database at the beginning of the game Open league systems with editable promotion and demotion rules Expandable names list per language Automatic creation of players and teams Comprehensive editors for crests and shirts Options to integrate your own graphics WE ARE FOOTBALL is future-proof: the game’s start year can be adjusted in the editor.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing football management games all the way back to the original Football Manager, through the Championship Manager era and right back to the current iteration of FM. Throughout this period I have fond memories of games such as Ultimate Soccer Manager, LMA Manager and FIFA Manager, and to me these were always good stable mates to the more tactical approach of the FM series.Recently, I’ve burnt out on the FM series, I’ve hardly played it this year to be honest so I was really excited that we may have an alternative, something a little more casual and less of a time sink. So far this This Is Football is nicely filling that gap for me, and I’m really pleased I took a chance on it. It’s a great change of pace and I think that as a first release of a new franchise the devs have done a good job. Basically, this game focuses more on the building of an entire club, through the building of club facilities, sponsorships, looking after the fans etc. rather than just heavy tactics.So I’ve seen multiple reviews berating parts of game, but in my opinion anyone expecting a new football management game to be ‘perfect’ on day one is not being sensible. There are so many moving parts and simulations that interact that I fully expected that to be the case. Even the current iteration of the FM franchise has to issue multiple balance patches every year.What I think we have here is a very solid foundation of a franchise that sits very nicely as an alternative to Football manger, and competition is important to drive both franchises forward. I truly believe that the devs can build on this create a really strong product.But the most important thing is I’m having fun with this game. I’ve had a terrible couple of weeks due to the loss of my mother, and this game has successfully provided moments of respite. I’m happy with my purchase and hope this review helps you decide if this game is for you. A few things for people to consider who may be thinking about a purchase:•	The UI is confusing at first, but after spending some time with it I think I know where everything is. It certainly gives a fun throwback vibe to some of the other games I mention above. •	I really love how you can literally just drag and drop players anywhere on the tactics pitch and enjoy the more simple way the player rating is shown.•	The teams and players are not real, however it can very easily be patched with one download. Its very simple so it’s not really an issue. •	The match engine is very different to FM, I suggest watching a YouTube video if that matters to you. I wasn’t sure about it at first, but it’s grown on me. The devs have said that they are looking to develop a fully 2D/3D engine. •	Some of the German to English translations are a bit weird – it can make things a bit difficult to understand at first.•	There are a few minor bugs, nothing major or game breaking that I’ve seen. I’ve had no crashes. The worst one is an issue with young players asking for way too much money when signing a contract.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the right idea, but is in dire need of patching. There are some baffeling design choices that are unexpected from such an experienced team, and there are some additional annoyances that are easy to fix.1. Let me start with this: The game is easy. Very easy. Sadly, it is easy for the wrong reasons.Having a more accessable and therefore easier management game is not bad, but maybe the only way to challenge the more complex managers out there. But there is a basic truth to these games: Balance is important. The game gives you tools, and you use these tools, that is what a game like this is all about. If the game overpowers one tool and makes others useless, then the game becomes far too easy once you understand which tool is the only one you need.That tool is the transfer market. It is downright funny how easy it is as a 4th league team to get players that would be in the best 3rd league teams. They are cheap, they are willing, they are far better than the alternative. Said alternative would be to develop players - but forget about that. Training is just there to raise fitness levels, and young players shouldn't be trained, they should just be bought cheap from other teams.2. Player availability is something that is also a big problem, because... there are just too many good players. In this game, all countries are generally at the same strength level. As English team, you will find great first league players everywhere. Russia, Switzerland, Turkey - and not just a few, but many. The whole league is full of them, wherever you look. And some of those players will be on the transfer market, so you can buy them for 40% of their value. Which is by the way the same vaue for every league - players from a lower league in Austria will be priced identical to first league players in Italy, so do not think that you can make a better deal in smaller countries. Every country is just the same, only names are varying, but the numbers won't change. And while you can get a nice team going very fast, you do not feel happy doing that, you do not build a connection to your players, because they are not rare, it is not an accomplishment to get them. They are just numbers, and you will sell them the moment a opposing team offers you 300% of their value (which happens not as rarely as you would think when you keep in mind how many identical players are on the transfer market at the same time).3. Some small things that are annoying: No explainations about some of the features in the game. Why is my manager stressed even though he only works 8 hours per week? Why can't I scout players in a country, why do I have to scout league specific? Why does a game that wants me to play it fast paced and with the bigger picture / long term goes in mind all of the sudden have me answer press questions that I could not even answer if I would analyse the match I just played for half an hour (What do I know if the catcalling of my supporters was justified, I did not see more than some moving pictures and even those I skip half of the time! And no, I have no idea how hard the fouls were, because again: I cannot see them, I just see the amount of cards given and even those I do not keep in mind because interviews are only onced every 10 games!). Interviews feel like surprise exams, and I am out of school since more than 10 years, so no thanks, I want to play games for fun.So - how to fix things? Well, here are some ideas:1. Leagues need to get some simply variable that makes them weaker / stronger and lowers prices / wages for players.2. Players need to develop faster and more, talent needs to have more of an impact. Young players have to be weaker than they are, but need to get stronger fast, otherwise I will just always buy very strong young players.3. Development needs to also happen in lower leagues. It cannot be that a player buys a young, talented team and then watches how all those 17-20 year old players do not get stronger at all for the whole year because they are only winning every game in league 2 (doesn't even change much in league 1 though, cause: Development is soooo damn slow and unfulfilling!).4. Transfers need to get harder. There must be a middle ground between the AI saying "I only sell this player for 400% of the market value" before having a stroke and selling it 2 month later for 40%. That is just weird to watch. And again: It amkes development useless! I will not wait 5 years for my 18 year old youth prospect to reach a level that I can also just gain by buying some random dude from Greece for nearly nothing.I hope this helps the developers. I want this game to succeed, and like I said: It gets the idea right. The market needs a more casual, but fun oriented football management game. But right now, things are too chaotic for me to recommend the game to anybody.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have enjoyed this game, and will probably continue to play it for a while, I wouldn't recommend it in its current state.  There are several issues with it, and I will go into some detail about issues I have found. Keep in mind that I have played about 10 seasons in different leagues and in different nations (with different players, of course).First of all, matches certainly seem to be stacked against the human player (not surprsingly).  Regardless of the skill of your penalty takers, you will miss most of your penalties during matches, where as your opponents will almost never miss. 90th minute goals from opponents (that have never been in the match) abound, stealing wins or even draws away from you. Opponents will score on their first attack about a third of the time, your team will likely score on less than 10% of its first attacks. Red cards (or second yellows) are given for ridiculous things, like "re-entering the pitch without permission", which I'm not sure I've ever seen a card given for in my lifetime. There also seem to be commonly-used formations that do not work at all.Outside of match play, there are other issues. Recently, while playing as a English Championship club, I was able to win the League Cup. In real life, this win comes with a spot in the Europa League the next season, which is a huge plus for a Championship side because of the money that comes along with it. In this game, I somehow did not get entered into the Europa League, nor any continental competition. I realize that this is a German game and centered around German football, and I was playing in the English league, but the German League Cup winners also make the Europa League in the same manner, so this issue doesn't exist because of a difference in the leagues.Also, with the winning of the League Cup came another problem. I was in the midst of playing 5 games in 15 days, and because of the importance of the League Cup final, I pushed my players hard in the match, which went extra time, then to penalties. I did my best to substitute tired players, but the match took a lot out of them. After the match, they never physically recovered for the rest of the season. No matter what I did in practice during the week for the remainder of the season (about 10 matches), my squad of 23 players came into every match absolutely knackered. I tried resting them all week, or using active recouperation all week, but nothing I did made any difference. Two months later, when the season ended, they were still just barely making it through matches, and getting absolutely destroyed on the pitch in every match.A couple other issues I've found are having to pay for changes to club grounds on infrastructure that hasn't even been started yet (pay to "destroy" what doesn't exist, and of course, fail get the money back that you invested to place it in the first place), and not being able to ask for a raise during the length of your contract (I got promoted from League One to the Premier League during my contract, but was not offered a raise, and was expected to see the last two years of my £4810 p/w contract as a Premier League manager).While this game has some great elements and ideas, it definitely needs some work. I do enjoy it to an extent, but there is plenty of frustration as well. It does scratch the itch that I have when it comes to allowing you to run a club from the view of a chairman and manager, so I will probably continue to play it. If you are still thinking about buying it, I would suggest waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Are we Football?Let's face it: Outside of Burgerland (and even they catch up slowly), everybody loves Football. It's a real sport, so we are Football, because pretty much everybody at one time or another played it. But is this Football?I write this review in english because most so far most are german and don't help people who don't speak the language and since we're on Steam: I'm trying to help out but the first segment will sound like ancient hyroglyphs to most non-german people. Anyway, I love football, i watch it, i'm in the stadium, i'm a lifetime member of my club (1860) and i played a ton of football manager games and when i say a ton, i mean a metric ♥♥♥♥-ton of them. All of them: The entire Bundesliga Manager series, the entire Anstoss series, Hattrick (and its "we don't speak about it" sequel), Kurt and its "all grown up" Kicker sequels, english games like the Ultimate Soccer Manager series (truly the Ultimate, if it wasn't for a few dumb bugs and a lack of youth players, it would be the best of all time), the original Kevin Toms Football Manager, the later Sega Football Manager and some experiments like Teamchef and even some of the worst of the worst like Club & Country, Team Manager, Split Screen Manager....shortly: I played them all. Now, Gerald Köhler is alongside Jens Onnen and Werner Krahe (those 2 made the Bundesliga/Eishockey Manager series) one of the absolute legends of german football manager sims, he made Anstoss (up to the 3rd game) and went to the dark side of EA to make the Fussball/FIFA Manager series until it got cancelled with FM14 which was FM13 in disguise (for a full price with just updated rosters, yeah, that's EA!). And now he's back like a franchise character that can't be hold down. A new game from him. You'd think with nearly 30 years of experience (Anstoss was conceived around 1991/92, came out in late 93) he would give us the ultimate, absolutely greatest football manager there is..Well...no, if you have a turntable, put on some cheap crappy vinyl and imitate the screeching halt sound,  because it fits this perfectly.WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ HAPPENED?!You'd think this game would at least be on the level of Anstoss 3, from 2001You'd think it would have a few features from EA's Manager, considering Köhler hired a few people from that staff.But no. What you get is like the beginning of football managers. It's like Bundesliga Manager Professional (1991)But let us start from the begining: You can either choose a team directly or answer question at a breakneck pace to determine what team in the lower league would be a good start. The problem already is: You answer it, it says "3 clubs want you" but you only see 1. In Anstoss 2, 3 and every other game, you'd see all 3 offers, be able to compare them and choose but here, you basically either take offer 1 or decline untll offer 3, which might suck. This is stupid. Now one thing german football managers always sucked at was the important part: The game calculation. Even as far back as the crappy Bundesliga Manager Hattrick, most of the time, it was a random number generator that slightly takes your overall team power in consideration to compare it to the opposite team and ♥♥♥♥♥ out a score. You might win, you might lose, you never knew why you won or lose. Sega's Football Manager and even that old Ultimate Soccer Manager gave better feedback: You know if a player was too slow, wasn't good enough to mark an opponent or why the other striker could dance through your penalty area like it happened at the current Euro between Wales and Turkey. In this game here, you get nothing. Youi don't get to watch games, you don't get scenes of goals or anything ,you get no feedback at all. Instead highlights are shown as the player face with lines were the ball goes - you don't see the other team though, so you don't even know if somebody was out of position or whatever. After the game you get no stats at all either, you get a message in the newspaper that is a bout as far removed from reality as somebody who swallowed some LSD. I lose 1:2 and it says "My Tactic was perfect, the team was set up great, just unlucky", on the other hand, i win 6:0 and apparently my setup sucked, i had no "analyst" on the field and i just got lucky. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥? If i curbstomp a team like that, nobody would call it "luck". The other areas are just as broken, You can only plan a week in advance and everything takes up hours in your calendar. You want to put some money in the bank? Takes 2 hours for no good reason. Also the games wants you to waste 2 hours to do sport on your own for no real reason.You also can't plan training in advance, you have to plan it week by week, nothing else is possible, not even outside the season. The training camp option is horrible as well. You say "Let's go to a camp" and you have to do it, but you get no feedback if it was good or bad, how players got better or whatever. Again: This is from the same guy who made EA's Manager which had futuer week planing, future training plaining and total feedback on how training went, how the camp went and all that. Even the whole stadium and club area section is just sad. In the old Football Manager games from EA you could design every aspect of the Stadium, even to the point of adding fireworks and litter. Here? Nothing, you just add rows of seats/stands/vip places and a roof and the worst thing: it looks ugly, the roof ultimately won't even cover most seats. Same with the club area, you just put down a few areas like a Gym or some "Football Tennis" area, it gets instantly built and that's it. You can't even additional pathways, so everything will just looked half-assed. So the fundamentals are totally broken, unfinished, unsatisfying and there are bugs as well. At least i hope the negotiations are bugged. Because it's ludicrous you can sell players for far more than their worth, while coercing the CPU into selling them your players for far below the market price. Even the sponsores are broken. I played a season, went up to League 2 in Germany, looked for new sponsors, now the board sponsors for the most part offered me 280,000 to 380.000 - except 2 who offered 2 and 4 million for 2 boards each. It's totally unrealistic, it made sure i went out with a profit for the entire season - and the best thing? I still couldn't negotiate more money for transfers and wages, even though i had 25 million in the bank, plus the money from those 2 offers. It's just broken and unrealistic. Also i just never actually have the feel i play a football game. Exchange the field during the "game simulation" and it could be "We are Hockey" or "We are American Handegg". Ea's Manager felt like football, thanks to the FIFA engine for games, Sega's game screams "Football!" and the older german games catched it as well, especially Anstoss had an atmosphere that made it obvious it was a "By Fans, for Fans" affair and had the mascot Pallino. This game on the other hand has the personality of a McDonald's Burger. What else is there to say: Not much to be honest. The music is atrocious, there aren't alot of sound effects, even the "games" sound weak. It was promissed to have the legendary half-time speeches from Anstoss 3 but it doesn't, except the one time you pay for a motivational speaker. I guess for total beginners to the world of football managing, the simplicity and lack of anything might be ok, it's not as overwhelming as Sega's behemoth (or any older manager), but for anybody who played the old games, this isn't worth it. Stick with Anstoss 3, EA's FM13 (both still have active communities creating current data sets) or Sega's Football Manager.Edit; Several Updates got release, which are just patchwork, they try hard to fix some of the issues while breaking other things, by now this game really is a lost cause. Updates add bugs,rarely remove any and the few "features" that get added are so small in scope, they don't even matter.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It has its issues - some bugs to be fixed and features that are missing - but I really enjoyed this direct competitor to Football Manager and found several aspects that I would love for Football Manager to take note of and possibly add their own twist to. This review is really more of a WAF vs. FM22, so I'll structure my biggest points as to which things I preferred from each game.Things I Feel WAF Does Better:- Negotiations in general are more fun and hands on. FM22 is certainly more granular when it comes to all the possible options for contracts and transfer offers, but at the cost of being a bit too opaque for all the but the most hardcore negotiators. Negotiations in WAF feel more like a minigame.- I really enjoy the passage of time in WAF, and how you need to balance your time and thus pick and choose which items you're going to address in a given week.- WAF gives you the ability to add and negotiate with sponsors directly, and I loved having direct control over this aspect.- I love having full control over both the training grounds and the stadium. In FM, your training area is a hidden number between 1 to 20 that controls how well your players train, but in WAF, you have all manner of buildings and fields with specific bonuses. Likewise, choosing when and how to expand your stadium is left up to you in WAF vs. oftentimes infuriating back and forth with your board in FM.- The UI itself feels much more accessible in WAF. While there are plenty of great skins in FM, all of them fail to achieve the kind of openness and intuitiveness that I found in WAF.Things I prefer in FM:- Attributes. For both staff and players, the single most important attribute in WAF is basically a "level" between 0 and 15 that is indicated by the number and color of stars. On the one hand, I love the simplicity and it does generate some excitement when a player or staff gains a star...but on the other, there is next to no indication of what staff/players are good at on any kind of granular level outside of a handful of skills they can unlock.- I feel much more connected to the games themselves on FM. WAF has the ability to see the stadium and plays during games, but I quickly turned it off once I realized it was just going to show me diagrams and not actual gameplay.- This is an area I hope will improve as more people play WAF, but while both games suffer from a lack of licensing, FM has a MUCH larger collection of add-ons to be able to mimic real-life teams, leagues, and tournaments. WAF has a great database editing tool that allows you to import custom databases, so I was able to play with real teams in roughly the correct league structure, but I still felt pretty disconnected calling the English leagues "1st Division", "2nd Division", and so on and without any of the correct cup titles.- Coaching licenses, work permits, cup registration restrictions, finance rules, and I'm sure plenty of others that I'm forgetting about. FM is ridiculously accurate when it comes to its depiction of the leagues, and everything I mentioned above is missing entirely from WAF. This makes WAF a bit easier to approach, but is still a net loss for those of us that appreciate really feeling like we're managing a real club.All in all, I really enjoyed my time with WAF, and would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys the genre, but after a week or two, I found myself back on FM22. I'm hopeful that this marks the beginning of a rivalry with both franchises pushing each other to be better. I definitely have room in my life for more than one football management sim.

Not that good but has potential.The UI is bloated and confusing, the upside is that you can delegate most of the tasks so you can just do that if you feel overwhelmed and get into it in a later date.The UI in itself feels generic and boring, did mention bloated already so you're quite busy looking for thing...you do get used to it at some point, I'm in my third season right now.A lot of quality of life improvements are due, more often than ever I found myself using the arrow keys to navigate the ListViews the UI presents just to be disappointed that you can't use arrow keys, instead I have to move and click my mouse around which is a pain and personally annoying.When setting up a Training Camp or Friendly Matches you don't have access to the Calendar, so you can't doublecheck if you're accidentally creating a friendly right before an important or busy week, only showing the date is not enough, I don't have the Calendar memorized, even if I wanted I wouldn't be able to memorize it since you don't have access to the Calendar at all.More often than ever during contract negotiations you're forced to accept the very low transfer clause players want, you can't outright remove it...only increase or decrase which takes away an action point from the negotiation per change in that one value...Things like saving formations and games doesn't let you overwrite an existing one by double clicking it, in the formation screen in particular selecting an existing formation you saved and clicking on save will NOT overwrite your existing formation, it will instead create a new one, to actually overwrite it you need to input the name on the TextBox and once you try to save it detects that the formation already exists with that name and asks to overwrite it, how annoying is that?The soundtrack lacks soul, I was expecting the kind of banger track and sound effects you'd get from Anstoss 2, instead you're left with listening to something so boring it feels like it was _childDocuments_.review: I'm leaving a positive review because I would like to encourage the development of this game and others like this one.I have been a hardcore Football Manager gamer since it was called Championship Manager, and before that I used to play games like PC Fútbol (PC Calcio, PC Premier...) and Ultimate Soccer manager, so, been playing this genre since around 1995.I haven't bought any new Football Manager games since FM2015 because I don't think the upgrade is worth it. It's essentially the same exact game every year and I'm tired of the super repetitive press conferences and all the flaws the game has always had. Plus, it gets boring once you kinda settle with your tactics and just keep hiring or developing the new best player for each position. FM series doesn't allow you to play the game in the rol of a club manager, so you have nothing to say about marketing, merchandising, finances, stadium, academy and so on, which are truly thrilling parts of football that were widely covered by PC Futbol, Ultimate Soccer Managers and other games back in the 90s.To me, it is simply absurd that for the past 20 years we haven't had one decent game about football club management besides the Total Club Manager series, long dead since EA decided to kill it. So, this is what We Are Football is trying to fix, and that's why I bought the game in the first place.As many other reviewers mention here, the game  has the right idea, but it's still far from being a truly enjoyable game, in my opinion. I won't take too long reviewing it. On the positive side, the game looks nice, is not hard to play, has an enjoyable and immersive music, and has everything that Football Manager is missing: you can build your stadium, negotiate with sponsors, hire or sell players, manage the economy of your club and so on.On the negative side, the interface is just hard to manage. Everything is somewhat organized around your weekly schedule, which you have to determine beforehand. This is trying to give you the feeling of being an actual manager of a club, but I don't think this is a good approach, since club managers don't actually take care of every little thing by themselves. They are presented with different options and they get to decide, so dropping this scheduled organization would be a better approach for me, just like the old PC Futbol or Ultimate Soccer Manager did.Besides, the match engine is very lacking. Most players won't mind having a 2D layout just like Football Manager had for years, as long as they can get a grasp on their tactics. However, in its current state, this part of the game doesn't even meet the basics and is just truly lacking. Also, since the games are quite dull and hard to watch, it feels even worse having to spend several minutes for each match just staring at what is basically nothing, simply waiting for the game to end.Despite all this, however, I think this game could become something much better and is on the right track, so I'm hoping to play it again maybe a year from now and check on its progress. And I recommend anyone interested to give it a spin and keep an eye on it as a potential Football Manager alternative.Don't pay the full price for this game, however. I bought it on sale for around €26 and it still was way too expensive for what the game actually is in its current state, which is what I have refunded it. Either becomes a game as enjoyable as Total Club Manager, in which case it would be worth €35, or is sold for the right price for what it truly is right now, which to me would be around €10.
_childDocuments_.name: WE ARE FOOTBALL

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to start off by saying that I never write reviews for anything, but this game has made me want to. We are Football is a great game if you understand what this game is. I feel like a lot of people want to compare this game to Football Manager and that's the wrong idea. This game does not focus so much on the tactical aspect of every match like Football Manager. WAF focuses more on the overall development of a club (ie. designing the stadium, deciding ticket prices, finding sponsors, etc). We are Football is a much more casual game when compared to FM and that is what I really like about it. I love soccer/football, but after a long day at work, I do not want to come home and play a game where I have to meticulously decide tactics for a team (I am looking at you FM). We are Football still allows me to enjoy my love of football, but not have to be so intense about my every move. If you want an alternative to Football Manager that offers a different experience, then I highly recommend WAF. However, if you absolutely love the tactical aspect of FM, then this may not be the game for you. If you want a new experience with managing a football club, then give this game a try!On a side note: WAF does not have licenses, but this can be easily remedied with the FM-Zocker mod which actually has a total of 86 countries you can manage in around the world.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried my best to like the game but I find the entire experience lacking. For sure WAF tries to be different in a lot of things and I do find the interface refreshing and modern in comparison to FM. However, while it's always nice to look at the 3D views of the museums, stadiums, training ground etc, the core product of this game is severely disappointing. This is first and foremost a football manager simulation game so it is only normal for players to pay attention to the match day experience. I've complained about FM's early 2000s match engine multiple times before but if players hated that, what they're going to get in WAF is way worse. There is no match engine, which is already a step down from the Fifa Manager series that the game was built upon and if you want to rely on the commentary-only option, well all you're going to get are a few simple lines. It's just a very frustrating game because they've spent so much time on all the side stuff (some of which i really appreciate) but when push comes to shove and once you played a match the only feeling i got was why the hell did i spend hours setting the team/club for? _childDocuments_.review: This is the football game I've been waiting for. I've played a lot of FM, but it is a manager/coach game where as this is an owner/manager game. With WAF I can make the decisions about whether to expand the stadium or improve training, if we don't have enough fans to justify expansion then I can choose how to spend resources to boost engagement. I also am really enjoying the skill tree for players, it is more fun and rewarding to craft a player in this way than how training works in FM. For a career taking a club from the lower divisions up to the top, I think WAF have the right game design that gives me the freedom to make investment decisions to support what they want to achieve while making the training of the next generation of players more engaging.This game also feels like a game - it's fun, doesn't feel like a spreadsheet, and has lots of depth. Really looking forward to how WAF continues to evolve.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable game not to be compared to Football Manager. As a game in its own rights it is great, yes its rough around the edges for example the gimmicky things are not needed like sabotage of a match, building things like directors house in facilities and such these things are not needed and make the game almost childish. The game would really benefit from a 3d match engine although saying that the stadium view and facilities need a graphical overhaul, stadiums at the moment just look all out of perspective with the stands and corners all massively oversized but the roof not getting any bigger as the stand grows. this game has been made great with the edition of mods to update team names/badges and updated league positions. having randomly generated players hasn't bothered me in the slightest. i think if there are any newer versions in the pipeline then they should take influence from the FiFA Manager Games of years gone by namely the EA SPORTS FA Premier League Manager 2002 game which was by far the best in this game type. the range of building and stadium types you could build were fantastic and something i would like to see this game develop into.Tactically the game feels good and it feels like the decisions you make influence a game, team talks for me seem to a be pointless task tho. moving players freely around the pitch is great. overall i think they have made a great game that is FUN and not a second job like other manager type games, season can be quick but but also take time with all the facility/stadium/sponsors and such that needs attention. i hope this game keeps going with new releases and more improvements in the right direction going forward. i know i will purchase newer versions if they come along. (would like to see English Lower Leagues added as well :) )

_childDocuments_.review: I can highly recommend We Are Football. It's just fun to turn a small club into a big international top club and to have all the powers in your hands, from the first team to the second team and youth team to the expansion of the stadium and club grounds to disputes with club members and much more.The overall focus here is more on the long-term development of a club, mostly through good management, appropriate transfers, youth work, etc.  It is not necessary to deal intensively with tactics and individual instructions before every game.However, if you like just that and dislike everything else than tactics and training, you are probably better off somewhere else. So you shouldn't compare the game with Football Manager, because it has a different focus. If you like original licences and want to have all the real club crests, player names and pictures, etc., I can only recommend the fan patch from FM-Zocker (just google it), which enhances the game considerably and ensures immersion! In the editor you can also create your own club or completely new players and change all the money and values.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the Anstoss series, this game is for you!It's a well made mix between Anstoss, the EA FM and Sega FM.In this game you'll progress through a season a lot quicker than in the Sega FM and your main focus is the long term development of the club, instead of spending hours per matchday.Some negative reviews state that the match engine is bad, because you can't see the whole pitch but only the active player. While that is factually true, it's not a bad thing at all because it takes some of the complexity out of the game.Same story for the player stats. Instead of having 20-30 stats to analyse, you'll just be presented with some of the strengths and weaknesses of the players.This game keeps it simple, and that's great!Huge thanks to Gerald Köhler and his team for this game, we've been waiting for this for so long!PS: Don't forget to install a fan patch to have a fully "licensed" game (like the one from FM Zocker)!
_childDocuments_.name: WE ARE FOOTBALL

_childDocuments_.review: While this pup draws a lot of its ideas from the older football management games (looking at titles like the old Premier Manager series or FA Premier League Manager/Total Club Manager), somehow manages to be somewhat worse than those.The ideas are there, but the execution feels cheap and unnecessary complicated by the poorly designed UI. It's not a bad game, it's actually a decent football management game, one in which you are actually a manager and not simply a bloody coach (Championship Manager/Football Manager series style). But it still needs a lot of work. As this is the first game from a new studio, i am probably more forgiving, as i hope that a new entry in what i hope is a new football management game series would solve most of the grievances we have with the game. I would love to put a recommended note there, but i can't just do it in good faith. So far now, it's a negative. But i might change it after more updates.

_childDocuments_.review: **UPDATE**So after 13 Updates it seems to be a time for an short update:The positive feedback still stays and if i could I would gibe the game an even bigger thumbs up now:1. The team is working consistently on bugs and new features. They are listening to the community and do their best to include their wishes.2.  All but one of my negative points were addressed and greatly improved.3. The remaining one being the difficulty of the game: It is still, and probably will remain, an easy game. As mentioned before this is not inherently bad; I do enjoy this difficulty a lot, but hardcore lovers of the fm franchise may be disappointed.So without any more words: Buy and enjoy it, so we can get a lot more great updates and see a We are Football 2 in the future!**Original Review:**So, first of all: This games receives a positive feedback because it is a lot of fun. And by a lot I mean a whole lot of fun. For me it is a much appreciated counterpart to the football manager, which is also great but can get a bit tedious. Let's start with the positives:+ I really like the UI. Espacially in comparison to the fm: More colourfull, more icons; just overall more fun to luck at+ The different areas you can interact with+ Personally, I really enjoy the match display. I don't need a 3d match, since it always looks and feels clunky at best+ the fast paced gameplayThe negatives:- The match calculations seem a bit off: Positioning of players doesn't feel right, Participation of a single player in a play at different points looks like he might be using a portal over the field- Player prices: I am able to sell my players at really really good prices and on the other side to purchase players at really really low prices. That makes it way too easy to replace large if not the whole team as you like and improve it- Match results: The game seems to favour you when calculating the matches. It feels to easy: I started as Eintracht Frankfurt and won the championship. Another game I got contracted in the german 3rd league which had the object to avoid relegation. Instead i achieved second place and now I am playing the 2nd league. There again havong the objective to avoid relegation I am currently ranking at 6th place just one point behind 2nd place.- Overall feedback of game elements is missing- Buildings are built instantly- The week has to be interceptable: As I am getting older my memory is getting worse; having multiple player interactions on monday how am I supposed to remember after a full week and a game what I wanted to do or what I told himFeature whishes:- Manager area. Please let me do something with the money I earn- Let me save right before a game

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this as it was on offer. Terrible. Felt absolutely soulless and unexciting. I downloaded the real player mod which took ages to intergrate into the database. Once loaded, I chose Man Utd and started off with a League Cup game against….Hornchurch. WTH!?! League Cup game against a team who play in the 7th tier of English football and aren’t even in the league. Whether this is an error with the database or the game, I don’t know. That aside, the game felt soulless as I already said. There are no attributes and the player cards were very basic. It looked very slick…..for 2010. It reminded me alot of those awful EA management games of the early 2000s. There were also some highly dubious transfers as well, Declan Rice to Wolves for £100m, yeah right. I bought this as an alternative to FM23, which I love, but have played to death, sadly it hasn’t filled that void. I don’t think there is a solid alternative to FM, so I’ll stick with that. The game would probably more suit someone looking to get into the genre for the first time, but sadly think they would soon move on to the giant that is FM. Sorry! 😬Managment games and football games nowadays should come with licenses, however a lot of those have been hoovered up by the likes of SI, Konami and EA Sports. Sadly a community based database leads to errors, even if it is made using data from those said companies.As others have said, I really wanted to like this, as a viable alternative to FM, sadly I was left found wanting and looking for those extra details that other titles have.The biggest let down is the lack of a 3D or even 2D match engine. In WAF all you see is a ball pinging around with small details of commentary. These days a decent management game needs a match engine. FM and even FIFA and Soccer Manager have upped their game in the last decade or so and have included a decent match engine, Whilst the developers of FM have acknowledged the faults of the ME, they have listened to the fans and are making a complete brand new game for FM25. Whilst EAs new incarnation of EAFC as it is now called will be remained to be seen what the career mode will be like.With the progress the aforementioned titles have made, WAF is looking like being left behind by the bigger boys in the genre. A big improvement will be needed if WAF is to challenge for the title, they seem more like relegation candidates right now.I managed to get a full refund after 1.6 hours of play.My rating: 3/10

_childDocuments_.review:
As a manager and trainer in WE ARE FOOTBALL, you'll come face to face with the latest trends in the world of football, experiencing all the emotional highs and lows of your favorite club.

For the first time ever, this modern football manager game also offers a women's football game mode, featuring all the same functionality as well as many unique gameplay elements. To maintain and ensure the highest quality across all game modes, WE ARE FOOTBALL has been developed with experienced football management veterans such as Gerald Kohler, Rolf Langenberg, and Dirk Winter.

WE ARE FOOTBALL focuses on real management tasks. The goal of the game is to build up the club over the long haul, including growing the team, colleagues, infrastructure, fans, and more. As a result, the football players in the game are individual personalities who spin their own stories.

detailed_description: Resident Evil Village Gold Edition Experience survival horror like never before in the eighth major installment in the storied Resident Evil franchise - Resident Evil Village. The Gold Edition includes: - Resident Evil: Village game - Winters' Expansion additional content - Trauma Pack DLC - Access to RE:VERSE online game Note: Resident Evil: Village and the Trauma Pack DLC will become playable upon the release of the Gold Edition on 28/10/2022. The Village of Shadows unlock included in the Trauma Pack allows access to content which is otherwise unlockable through gameplay progress. Details of the service period for RE:VERSE can be found on the official website. The service period may have already concluded, so please check before purchasing. Access to Re:Verse may become available through other means at a later date. Set a few years after the horrifying events in the critically acclaimed Resident Evil 7 biohazard, the all-new storyline begins with Ethan Winters and his wife Mia living peacefully in a new location, free from their past nightmares. Just as they are building their new life together, tragedy befalls them once again. FEATURES • First-Person Action – Players will assume the role of Ethan Winters and experience every up-close battle and terrifying pursuit through a first-person perspective. • Familiar Faces and New Foes – Chris Redfield has typically been a hero in the Resident Evil series, but his appearance in Resident Evil Village seemingly shrouds him in sinister motives. A host of new adversaries inhabiting the enigmatic village will relentlessly hunt Ethan and hinder his every move as he attempts to make sense of the new nightmare he finds himself in. • A Living, Breathing Village – More than just a mysterious backdrop for the horrifying events that unfold in the game, the village is a character in its own right with mysteries for Ethan to uncover and terrors to escape from. _childDocuments_.review: Shady business practises aside the game is exceptionally solid. The graphics are wonderful. The game performs well and I experienced 0 bugs throughout my play-through. The gun-play is tight and responsive  and most of the weapons have their place. The horror falls off near the mid-point once you become a walking armoury but until then it's pretty scary and that's to be expected of an Resident Evil game by now anyway.The sound design is extremely well put together, most of the weapons sound great, the environments are audibly spooky and the voice acting is top notch for the most part. Fish-Boy is a bit hard to understand for my liking but that's really my only major gripe with audio.Overall it's a great game, my only complaint being the game is a little under 8 hours long start to finish on most difficulties. Some might argue for a $100 they would expect at least 10 hours of run-time from it but it was a well crafted and engaging 8 hours and there is some replay-ability to be had from mercenary mode and the harder difficulty. I can 100% recommend this game but it is a direct sequel to RE 7 so you might want to play that first which I also recommend as a good game although not as good as this one I should say.

_childDocuments_.review: Eh.If I could give this a middle option I would because I did enjoy it but this is a step down from RE7. This new first person RE formula works great for it's atmosphere and horror elements and RE8 is no exception. The environments are gorgeous and there are some genuinely scary moments in this game. Unfortunately though RE8 decided to focus on the worst aspect of this new RE style which is the combat. Lackluster enemy variety, awkward gunplay, sluggish movement, and a large amount of boss fights that all play out the exact same way. Run in a circle, wait for weak spot, shoot, and then repeat. These bosses are so cool and look straight out of Bloodborne but they are just so damn boring. The game is also so scripted that I don't think it will be fun on a repeat playthrough. Overall it is good, and you will probably like it more than I did, but I'd be lying if I said I wasn't disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved RE4 then this game is probably your cup of tea, actually, you'll probably love it. The game is objectively very good, except for some minor things like; during my gameplay I often had to back up into a different room to not get swarmed... more than 30 times doing that the enemy aggro just unleashed (they slowly walked back to their spawn), making for some super easy cheesing and huge immersion breaking.With that said... I do not love RE4. I love the more slow, psycological horror with some action in it, but with RE8 we're back to a heavier lean towards action over survival and the game plays much more like RE4-6 than say RE2R. The world is more of an anime-horror than a semi-plausible scenario where most bosses are very over the top, with one guy basically being Magneto with Nicholas Cage's voice. There are several morphing-from-human-form-to-a-giga-Chad-in-an-instant moments. There are tons of super cheesy one-liners along the lines of "I will be even more powerful!" or "I will destroy youuu!". There are tons of disjointed events that breaks the logic and immersion of the universe, such as the Duke which is a merchant that nobody but you seem to notice. Finally the story is just... very weak. There's not much story going on and the big events are shock value for the sake of shock, without actually working it into the ongoing narrative well (imo, laughably bad)....Great game though and the final boss is just amazing in atmosphere and design (but the fight felt more like Silent Hill than Resident Evil).Oh right, and the port is bad: the mouse is super slow even at maxed sensitivity (I had to triple my DPI to make it playable), there's no FOV-slider and menus are clunkier than all hell (to the point that a controller is to be preferred when navigating them). At this point there are no excuses for this.

_childDocuments_.review: (TL;DR at the bottom)I still remember when six year old me sat next to my dad for the first time he fired up the first Resident Evil on our Playstation back in the nineties, and I remember even more vividly how terrified I was the first time I saw the first zombie turn it's head to look at me with that dead, stone-like face and blood stained lips. At that moment it became my favourite game and as time has gone by and, though the overall quality of the subsequent games has been up and down to say the least over the years, Resident Evil still continues to be perhaps my favourite game ever created, from the characters to the stories, the puzzles and the atmosphere, whether it was traversing the dusty, dimly lit halls of the Spencer Mansion or the zombie-ridden streets of Raccoon City, it all came together to create an experience that I still fondly revisit often and will be with me 'til my last day.It is no doubt this influence that leaves me to give this game a positive review, as I feel it is a very well put together game for reasons I'll go into greater depth with, but I'll also be including a rather big caveat at the end, keeping the entire thing as spoiler free as I possibly can. Please also note that this review is the culmination of my experience after completing the game on Standard difficulty.So, with all that in mind, here we go:As mentioned previously, I don't want to risk any spoilers, intentional or otherwise when it comes to the story; suffice it to say that the game is a sequel to Resident Evil VII set in a rural village somewhere in Europe, with the enemies taking on a much more folkloric and gothic flavour, with some stunning art assets and scenery to emphasise it all, from the run down and rotted houses and basements of the village itself to the extravagant and decadent halls and corridors of Castle Dimitrescu.The story itself I thought was really quite interesting, with plenty of files scattered around the village dropping various hints about what happened there to keep me guessing and drawing theories as to what was going on, with a very satisfying information dump towards the end that tied all those threads together very nicely and had me raising my eyebrows in surprise on more than one occasion.I am very happy to report that the guns both look and feel incredible, from the recoil to the aesthetics, meaning the combat feels fluid and very satisfying. The guns look, sound and feel fantastic with brilliant recoil and feedback; possibly some of the best gunplay I've seen in a game that I would be willing to put on a par with Hunt: Showdown, and the enemies all react in a very satisfying way that really emphasises the weight behind every carefully, or desperately aimed shot.During my playthrough I came to see that Capcom has struck a very nice balance between the feel of both Resident Evil 4 and Resident Evil 7; bringing back the attache case style inventory system (big hooray for the Inventory-Tetris OCD gamer like me), the merchant-style economy system of selling treasures for money to buy supplies, weapons and their upgrades along with the overall action of Resident Evil 4, whilst maintaining the first person perspective and atmosphere of Resident Evil 7 and, whilst you are still very much at risk of running out of ammunition if you don't properly aim your shots and get too trigger happy (also much like in 4), the ammunition you find and the materials you need to craft it are plentiful enough that you should rarely find yourself in a situation where you're having to count every single bullet; leaving you much more at liberty than in the previous game to enjoy blowing that wolf man's head into meaty chunks with the hefty shotgun you spent all that sweet, hard earned dosh upgrading; go on, treat yourself!The puzzles, sadly, are kind of a neutral point for me, never really complex or imaginative enough to make them all that memorable but not exactly stuff you could do with your off-hand pinkie whilst fast asleep either.So, all that being said, here is that overhanging caveat I mentioned earlier, and that is the overall length of the game. As much of a life-long fan of Resident Evil I am, and despite the wonderfully put together experience that is Capcom's latest entry into a series I've adored since childhood, I can't help but feel a bit stung that I paid £50 GBP for a game that I completed in around 7 hours and 40 minutes, Resident Evil title or not, and that was at a fairly steady pace, taking the time to explore the places I was in, looking for stray items etc.I have no doubt that more will be added with future DLC, and I look forward to that, but considering the asking price for the amount of game that is currently there, the thumbs up I give in this review should really only apply to the hardcore fans of the series who want to see how the story has progressed since their foray in Louisiana and those, like me, who just really love Resident Evil.TL;DR: A fantastic and well-made entry into the series in it's own right, but too short-lived to really justify the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most detailed graphical fidelity I've ever had the joy of experiencing, my third Resident Evil game, and the first game I played on my new RTX 3060 Ti GPU!  Despite it's name this is no small Village and you can expect hours of gameplay in a large open world with unique settings for each.While I skipped Resident Evil 7 (due to my prior GPU being under recommended specs) I was happy to see that the story is largely separated from Village's prequel and didn't find myself lost thanks to a brief optional synopsis that Village provides on the main menu.  Aside from the aforementioned gorgeous environments I found myself thoroughly enjoying the voice cast, especially the variety and unique personalities of each iconic enemy.  There's also plenty of weapons to use and I found that ammo was fairly limited but balanced on hardcore mode as-is synonymous with the games in this series I've played.  Lastly there's a fair amount of bonus content you can experience after finishing the main game like an arcade score attack, new powerful weapons (with infinite ammo unlocks), purchasable concept art, and a model viewer.I had a lot of fun playing but wished there was a way to increase your Field of View.  I imagine this was an intentional design choice to tighten the combat and suspenseful sections by making the player claustrophobic but this oftentimes made it more difficult to enjoy the scenery and ultimately made combat a bit clunkier than what I'm used to.  I also found the first Lycan fight to be unreasonably challenging.  It happens at the beginning of the game, and you're only given two weapons, starting this game on hardcore meant I needed to deplete all of my ammo just to survive.  In addition the soundtrack was serviceable but largely forgettable due to it's focus on ambiance over catchy melodies.  Finally  but I longed for the Beneviento chapter to be a bit longer in retrospect.  Navigating my way around Village's scariest enemy was one of the best highlights this game had to offer in my experience.  Overall a great time and after enjoying more of the post-game I look forward to playing the DLC when it's ready!

_childDocuments_.review: (Full Video Review Excerpt)Resident Evil Village is not a perfect game by any stretch of the margin, since if you’re in here expecting a return to the roots of the series – you’ll be disappointed, if you’re in here for a great story – you’ll be disappointed, and if you’re in for a game that revolutionizes the series, you will still be disappointed, but… If what you’re looking for is a really enjoyable semi-open world - survival horror experience, with great exploration, solid combat, neat scares, wonderful art design, cool even if really easy boss fights, and just tons of grotesque absurdity filling out your screen – missing out on this title would truly be a mistake… And that’s probably what surprised me the most about all of this, that even after going from singing praises of RE:8 until the later half of the game, and then begrudgingly starting to wish for its story to just finish its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ , I’m coming off quite content with what I got from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. The only major complaint I could have is that it isn't really a  follow-up to RE7, in the sense that it's just such a different tone. It's kind of like the Aliens to RE7's Alien, or the Terminator 2 to Terminator. In RE7, despite all the pseudoscience fantasy stuff, the story was pretty grounded, and the challenges you faced felt insurmountable, like you  just barely scraped by (even though really you didn't have much trouble at all). RE8 has a lot more action and a lot more large threats, but at the same time, Ethan really feels kind of ready to face them, so some of that tension is lost. Oh, and another flaw with the game: despite having more varied enemies than 7, it still really didn't have great diversity of enemies. Most of the enemies were just the same sort of AI with different costumes, that stagger more or less when shot.But overall, it's incredibly fun. The story is compelling enough to keep playing, the setpieces are very refreshingly different with their own unique experiences, and the action is harrowing but - again - not overwhelmingly so. While the emphasis on action  does distract from the horror to me, I'm actually surprised at how effective some of the scares really are. Since the events of the game delve way more into the fantasy side of RE, there was also more freedom to set up scenarios that genuinely toy with you deeper than just a jumpscare. There are tons of secrets to find, and the map is incredibly helpful in finding them without just giving everything away. There was only one puzzle that felt a little obtuse, and unfortunately it comes pretty early on in the game, but everything else is comprehensible enough to piece together without feeling like the game is just holding your hand all the way through. It's got an almost metroidvania feel, where you have the titular village as a hub with 4 main baddie-controlled areas to explore, then as you beat a boss in that area, you unlock something that will grant access to even more of the village. It really makes exploration exciting, and again the map is helpful for finding things you've come across but couldn't access before.Performance-wise, I was blown out of the water by this game. With a 3060ti, I have moderately high expectations for what I can  run well, but at 1440p plenty of games struggle to stay over 100fps at all times. But, with very rare exception, I maintained a stable 144fps throughout the entire game! The graphics settings are decently comprehensive. I thought it was pretty cool, albeit in a mundane way, that the game has minimum and maximum brightness settings. Great for those who like to pump the brightness up a bit - you don't have to completely blind yourself in lighter scenes now.All-in-all, I could keep going, but it was just completely fun. It has a kind of slow ramp up, but then the pedal hits the metal and this game never slows down. Simultaneously, I played for an hour or two and felt like it was 8, because I was so absorbed in the game, but then later finished the game in ~10.5 hours and it felt like it just flew by. I wanted more, and yet it never started feeling like it was overstaying its welcome.I just hope RE can keep up with these last two games. If it goes back to the classic style after these, they'll have lost at least one fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered and got the Trauma Pack which unlocked the hardest difficulty from the jump, and I don't regret a thing. It might be too hard for most people, but I love a challenge and dying over and over again on a boss might sound masochistic, but for me it makes it extra rewarding once I figure out the weak points, attack patterns, etc. and kill it. The game is definitely do-able on a fresh save on the hardest difficulty, but I do think some sequences are a bit unfair objectively.The exploration and puzzle solving is all classic Resident Evil and a lot like VII (fetch this item, etc). Some mechanics from 4 have crept in as well like upgrading weapons and hunting down treasure which was a welcome addition.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to a lack of AAA games this year due to the pandemic, Resident Evil Village is one of the saving grace for 2021. The game is an absolute classic as it succeeds in balancing survival horror, which we saw in the first three Resident Evil games, with fun and engaging gameplay from Resident Evil 4. The story was good and I appreciate how this game resolves most of the plot holes left by Resident Evil 7. One of the nitpicks that I would like to add is the underwhelming and uninspiring villains. Besides Lady Dimitrescu and Heisenberg, the other bosses felt mediocre as they didn't get a long screen time compared to the previous two. It would be interesting if we get more backstories from Mother Miranda and her other families in a form of a DLC. Overall, Resident Evil Village is another great addition for the resurgence of the Resident Evil franchise and I look forward to where Capcom will go from here.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that diverts from its set path. Albeit a horror game in nature, this latest installment takes a less scary approach by making the game into what can accurately be called an action thriller. Jumpscares don't come often, for better or worse, and only a few scenes (or perhaps a single one all together) can be categorized as proper horror. Still, the bonuses that are provided after the main story is finished make you want to play more, adding to the replay value of the game. Overall, a solid Resident Evil game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just gotten the 100% with SSS's across mercenaries mode and am sad to have wrapped this game up. For anyone that is a fan of the franchise, especially RE:4 and RE:7, I highly recommend this at full price. While I am coming in at around 34 hours of gameplay (played it at a friends before buying) and have completed everything within this run time, I still believe this is worth $60. It is not without it's negatives like some unsatisfying head shots, poor gore in comparison to RE:2 Remake, lack of enemy variety, annoying puzzles that piss on quality of life, and ridiculous bullet sponge difficulty increases that aren't really complimented with a solid enemy AI. You just can't find a gaming experience like this in titles other than Resident Evil. It is such a joy to play from the beautiful atmosphere to the gun play being far more refined than 7 had left it. I am personally a big fan of the new mercenaries mode but wish that there were more stages. Every time I beat this game it was in a sitting and that is how I like my Resident Evil experiences. It is a very satisfying game to speed run due to typical RE fashion of stumbling and exploring the village in depth on the first run and remembering the big puzzle this campaign is in order to fly through it. Did I mention it is gorgeous? I will be replaying this game past my 100% just to spend time in the world they built. The village itself has given me the sense of exploration I have been craving since the original Dark Souls. The story was better than I was anticipating it to be as I think it kind of started out weak and got better as the game went on. I dislike some boss battles and get a little fatigued on every enemy doing a mega transformation as it feels like we don't spend enough time with the characters. Some bad casting on the voice acting side is a bit of a bummer and some of the antagonist interactions could have been longer but it makes me very excited for RE:9 whenever that happens. I was skeptical about this game upon playing the demo and didn't think I would care to much for the setting and characters this time around in comparison to the family in RE:7. I am happy to have been proven wrong and given a game play experience I haven't had since the RE:2 Remake or other game titles (God of War, ect.) that demand I sink my time into it.

_childDocuments_.review: ******MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS******Way better that Resident Evil 7. Way more enemy types, wayyyyy more weapons, the ability to upgrade those weapons whether it being with attachments you can find to increase the weapons damage, recoil, etc but you can also upgrade the fire power, reload speed, mag capacity, and rate of fire from the merchant, Similar to the upgrade system in RE 4 and RE 5. Not only do you have all of that you can do but there is also treasure hidden EVERYWHERE. Again similar to RE 4 and 5 in the sense that you find treasure you can sell standalone or treasure you can find to actually put together in order to get more money when you sell it, Its nice that it labels it as a treasure that is actually able to be combined, You can also hunt livestock all around the village that you can use to upgrade things like you overall health, decreasing the amount of damage you can take when you block, or even being able to upgrade your movement speed, and when you're running for your life from Lady Dimitrescu or from a pack lycans that can be very helpful.  Overall the game is a boat load of fun and is absolutely beautiful both in design of its environments and sound. It has much higher replay value compared to the last game do to the insane amount of weapons you can get, the upgrade system, the treasure system, and with the return of the mercenaries mode. The game is kinda like RE7 and RE4 had a baby and it was done absolutely incredibly. It also does a great job further explaining the story of RE7 both with further explanation of the mold and its origins, and how both games tie into the original titles involving Umbrella corp, Raccoon City, etc. Also explaining further how Chris is involved within Ethans life.To sum it all up the game was incredible my first playthrough and I can't wait to start a new game+ run and do it all over again,

_childDocuments_.review: I've heard mixed reviews of this game. I remember hearing one person tell everyone to avoid it because he hated it. Of course, he gave no reason why he hated it nor did I inquire further. Which, if you're going to proclaim stuff like that (Positive or negative) you should give more reason for your claim(s). Anyways, after playing it myself, I have to say I really enjoyed it. Honestly, it felt like Resident Evil: Biohazard with its first person perspective. Like the previous game, you really felt you were there the whole time. Similar to how VR works. So, I appreciated they kept that part. I think it would have been weird if they hadn't. I think this game has more action in it. It sure seemed like it! But, within the context of the story, this makes sense. Ethan was just a husband looking for his lost wife in the RE7. Three years later, in RE8, he went through military training. So, naturally, he is more skilled at defending himself than he was when dealing with the Bakers. Plus, the area he was in this time was way bigger and had more going on with enemies. Overall, I didn't feel like the action was too overwhelming. I thought it was just the right amount. The story kept me interested the entire time, with Ethan searching for his daughter while dealing with Mother Miranda, The Four Lords and all the other enemies in between. Each one kept me on my toes and it never dragged on in one spot or another. Again, I liked this game. I think it's a great sequel that concludes Ethan Winter's story very well. So, if you're looking to play this game, I say give it a try. While I can't promise you, you, personally, will enjoy it, but being someone who has played it, I highly recommend it.
