_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: This game is in first person, but Capcom thought it would be best to NOT add in a FOV slider for their game, because getting motion sickness with a very narrow field of view is "mOrE CIneMaTiC!" However, there is a mod you can download to fix their game, and ultimately helped me enjoy the game significantly more. Now, let us get started -Pros of what I thought made this game awesome:1). The enemies. When I first heard that this game was announced, I thought this was the stupidest thing I ever heard, Lycans and Vampires. However, upon playing this game, this worked amazingly well. The Lycans are creepy, scary, and can appear at a moment’s notice sometimes without you even noticing. They are fast, they get in your face and they are relentless. The other enemies are varied, and they keep things changing, helping the game stay fresh. Especially toward the end of the game, the enemies are awesome to fight including some of the bosses, resulting in fun fights. 2). The locations: The location that Capcom marketed the crap out of, is incredible. The Village really sets the tone right from the get-go. Everything is destroyed, ripped to shreds, houses left abandoned, giving that tense and uneasy feeling of what could be lurking behind that door or around the corner. The locations here are breathtaking at times and is fun to be exploring in. There is one location near the end of the game, that I really did not care for, it was something that I did not care about being in. And we all know the castle, another beautiful location that was very fun to explore and try to complete puzzles. The locations in this game are very memorable and a blast. 3). Gameplay: There is a lot here, so this one I will try to keep condensed down. The game almost feels like Resident Evil 4 but in first person, the gun play is fun and fighting the enemies, which you will be doing a lot, is very enjoyable for 8 plus hours. There is a "decent" amount of weaponry in the game to kill enemies with. The new merchant you will interact with is an awesome character, not as awesome as the merchant from RE4, but there is a hidden gem that he talks about in that regard. The game play in terms of shooting mechanics is self-explanatory and pretty bog standard when it comes to first person shooters. No aim down sights unless you are using the sniper. There are things I will not spoil, but there are items for each location that you will find and be able to use in the game. I thought that was a very nice addition to the game. 4). The exploration: This is where this game truly shines. A big component of Resident Evil has always been exploration, looking for treasures or for key items to continue with the story. This game probably has one of the best exploration components in a Resident Evil game because of the amount of it you can do, and you very well might come across some new sightings too. 5). The characters: The characters in this game are fantastic. The last few Resident Evil games have been doing such an awesome job when it comes to their characters. I already knew the characters of RE2R and RE3R, so I knew what to expect with them and they were on point. And with this game with newer characters, they were awesome, and I really enjoyed when they appeared on screen. There are a couple that I will get into later during my complaints/negatives. But overall, I really liked most of them, that includes the new merchant as well. 6). The Environment and tone they set I love the environment they go for in each of the levels and they all have a distinct stress and fear factor involved, always wondering when the next enemy was going to pop up. There was one location, that took this beyond my expectations and was one of the most tense and horrifying experiences I have played in a video game. Also, adore the gothic and medieval setting. I loved how they took something like that would be in Bloodborne or Dark Souls, and brought it into RE. The best part, it works. My complaints and negatives of the game:1). This is the first complaint or negative aspect that I will combine into one, because I believe they are both just as bad as one another. That is the aspect of first-person camera views in a Resident Evil game. One of my biggest fears with RE7 was that was going to create a terrible new trend in Resident Evil where first person becomes a focal point, and the survival horror elements go out the window. While focusing on more horror like Outlast and Amnesia. Resident Evil can and HAVE done their games in 3rd person and made them scary, a prime example is Resident Evil 2 Remake. They showed that it can be done, and now with RE8, who knows when they will drop this garbage first person perspective from this awesome series. There were times I completely forgot I was playing a Resident Evil game, that is because of the camera angle and who our terrible main protagonist is. Continued...The second part is Ethan Winters. In fact, the whole Winters family is terrible. The thing about this game is that it tried so much to be a Resident Evil 4 spiritual successor, but they have this bland, unfunny, boring personality of a character as a main protagonist instead of someone like Leon. I honesty could not care or less about the Winters story, his backstory, everything. At least with Leon, in RE4 specifically, when he made a funny one liner, he was funny and never took himself too seriously. Capcom, stop putting in main protagonists that represent "the player", I do not want to play as a character that more or less "represents the player" like Outlast or Amnesia does. I have those games, if I wanted something like that, I would go play them or Penumbra. This is Resident Evil, give me a legendary character like Chris, Jill, Leon, or Claire, etc. Not this character that we cannot put a face to, it's stupid, and doesn't work in RE.2). Any bugs/glitches, or bad game design? No bugs or noticeable glitches. There were times where bad game design came into play. There was a section later in the game where I was exiting a corridor and if enemies were to appear, all I would have to do is back pedal and they were not able to follow me farther into the corridor, so they would just run away. In that same instance, the enemies ran away, stopped and were looking away from me. So, I proceeded to shoot them, and they did not even react, they just stood there until they died. And that is not the only instance, it happened multiple times where if you back peddled into a certain room or hallway, the enemies would not follow, they will just go back to walking around forgetting you are even there. I was able to cheese a few enemies, including some powerful ones. C'mon Capcom. If you were not able to do that in 2005 for RE4 and cheesing enemies was not allowed, you could not do it in a game that was released in 2021? Unreal. It honestly just took me out of the moment at times. 3). The opening hour or so, is a drag.4). The audio: There were times that the audio was terrible. The gun sounds sucked and sounds like there is no depth to them. One instance there at the start of the game, where a loud crash was heard, made me chuckle more than it did frighten me. I wear a pair of 7.1 surround sound headphones because audio is very important in video games. But this effect sounds like some cheap effect they pulled off the internet somewhere. Even the crows sounded terrible sometimes. Plus, on some of the characters, it almost sounds like as if you can still hear them in the recording booth, the editing seems like it was hit and miss. 5). The music, or lack thereof: There was only two major sections in the game where I noticed any decent noticeable soundtrack playing. Other than that, its atmospheric sound effects.Overall, with my complaints of how I feel about this game, and if you're a not a Resident Evil fan or have been playing since the 90's, I still think the game is great, a must buy.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all games from RE0 to this one, including the remakes of some of the titles. Cleared the game in 7 hours in hardcore (first playthrough), with skipping a few parts of the village because I was very much intrigued in the story. Currently taking my time now in my 2nd playthrough.Having played previous titles and specifically RE7, the game that preceded RE : Village, this entry is definitely a huge improvement from RE7, and overall a very good entry in the franchise. RE : Village, comapred to RE7, leans more towards gunplay and action, but still a very 'classic', slow, and methodical approach when it comes to movement and gunfights. I can still call RE : Village a survival horror, since that is the genre of the RE series. If RE7 was more horror than action, and RE4 being more action than horror, RE Village brings the great parts of both titles. Action/gunplay feels great, but not the 'best' course of action for every encounter. Avoiding/dodging and enemies and just 'speedrunning' several parts feels very rewarding and cool, but some segments require precise gunplay if you want to go through as unscathed as possible.I don't want to spoil the story because I found it to be one of the best in the series, but several plot elements in the game just wow'd me. Of course, like true RE fashion, some parts are cliche and need a bit of suspension of disbelief, but overall, the writing is great.If you were disappointed in RE5, RE6, RE3R Village more than makes up for the shortcomings of those games. It feels complete, well thought, and greatly executed.Having said that, I have a few problems with this title.-There are performance issues when fighting the Dimitrescu Daughters, specially when their bug swarm shows up and when they bite you.-A little nitpicking, but while Ethan and other characters have splendid voice acting, some segments of the game have...odd direction/choice when it comes to voice lines or lack thereof.-FOV feels a bit too low. I wish Capcom added (or at least add it in the future) an FOV slider. It can be disorienting at certain areas.After playing this title, I'm very much excited for the ending of this trilogy. I hope you are too, after finishing this game!I just want to warn people. There IS a segment of the game I love and hate for a specific reason. If you have Pediophobia, which is a fear of dolls, it may trigger you, so do take that in mind. The pathway leading to that area may also trigger unpleasant thoughts. This area is fairly early in the game, so many people will encounter it early, so I thought this information is needed, specially for those who are considering buying the game, since it may cause you to try to refund it, but because of where it is, you may not be eligible to.I honestly think Capcom should've included that trigger warning in particular.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with the Village, but i won't play it again any time soon. 6.5-7/10 Spoilers included. No matter what part of franchise do you like, there's no accommodation for you and no peak point where it feels satisfying. RE1-3 fans will feel like at home at castle Dimitrescu (the best part of the game), but characters don't have any actual growth in your humble 1-2 hour stay here, and by the end you'll wipe them all out. The overarching puzzle feels like it needs to be at least 1 or 2 layers deeper. But i gotta say, when you crawl out onto the roof of the castle you may trick yourself and think that this is the best game in the series. Mostly this effect cause by astonishingly beautiful graphics, that reeks of quality and love put into them, too bad this whole illusion fades away right after you defeat 2nd of the 4 underbosses of the game. Surprisingly, this is not even the half mark of the game, because events that are unfolds in the House Beneviento(lost in vivo rip off) are short, suggest something deeper for the story, but doesn't even matter in the grand scheme of things. And you could say this bout any of the 4 big sections of the game. My rewrite of the story would rely heavily on the dynamics between Lady Dimitrescu and her revenge for the killing of her daughters or much more psychological focus on mother Miranda posing as a Mia and trying to steer us directly or something like that, because right now this is a story for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ daily cartoon, especially the ending. I'll be kind and won't even mention two other lords, if only in the passing with all boss fights of this game. And, oh boy, i gotta say, i didn't have nostalgia for re7, but that whole game feels more tighter and much more interesting(excluding the boat section) cause of the interesting boss fights that induces fear and claustrophobia, none of that is present in re8 which have 1 interesting concept that was done much much better in MGS 4  13 years ago. Concluding i may say that this game feels disappointingly shallow compared to other entries, even to the absolutely horrible re6, but at least we got cool mercenaries/raid mod, which makes it aaaaall oook!

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village (RE8) is a direct sequel to Resident Evil 7 and a spiritual successor to Resident Evil 4. As it so happens to be, it is also a pretty fantastic game.RE8 picks up a few years after the events of its prequel. One day while chilling at home, some “boulder punching ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” turns up and straight up murders Ethan’s wife. As if that wasn’t all, the muscular ape-creature also kidnaps him and his daughter. Now finding himself in a strange village, Ethan must go on a quest to save his daughter by killing a bunch of monsters.The setting is immediately familiar to anyone who has played RE4 (with its castles and villages and whatnot). Many aspects of the gameplay have also been lifted from that game. You collect and combine treasures, upgrade your guns at a merchant and keep all your stuff in an attaché case (where  they keep that by the way?).The gameplay itself, however, should instead be familiar to anyone who has played RE7. The first-person perspective, the block button, and the way you move through the world is the same. Only this time, it’s much faster. Enemies are more aggressive, often come in large packs, and will weave and dodge your shots constantly. I know I bring up RE4 and RE7 a lot here, but that is honestly the best way to describe this game. It’s like a meticulously crafted love child between the two. It’s like RE4, but scarier. It’s like RE7, but with more enjoyable combat. Anyways, the list goes on—but how does the game stand up on its own?RE8 carries on with the  as told by RE7. The dialogue is campy, but at the same time, most of the characters feels a lot more “real” than they ever have before. There are some contrivances and convolutions in the scenario writing, but at the end of the day, the game just plays too well for it to detract from the experience. The story itself, while no masterpiece by any stretch of the imagination, is surprisingly engaging. There are enough twists and turns to keep you engaged to the end. RE8 also manages something that no other Resident Evil game has done before it (at least in my experience) by achieving a genuinely heartfelt and touching ending that feels like a proper conclusion to Ethan Winter's story. Then again, I don’t think you should play these games for the story, and RE8 is no exception.The  is a rather standard affair for an FPS. What elevates it, is the environments and the well-balanced enemy encounters. While the enemy variety itself is low (still better than RE7), the weapons and locations are many and varied. The puzzle segments are fun enough (at least on a first playthrough) and mixes up the gameplay just the right amount. Bosses are about what you expect from the series but are better than any of the fights in the RE3 remake (and even RE2, I would say). The expanded crafting system, while also pretty standard, adds some spice to the gameplay loop, while also incentivizing backtracking and exploration. You can also hunt animals to cook food, I guess.The game took me roughly  to beat on my leisurely first playthrough on the Village of Shadows (VoS) difficulty. That might seem short to some, but keep in mind that these games are meant to be played multiple times. Even then, this is rather lengthy for a Resident Evil game. I’d have to play through it again to be sure, but I didn’t feel any one particular area to be worse than the other in the usual Resident Evil fashion (where everything falls apart at the end). The game doesn’t feel quite as heavily scripted as RE7 (which made subsequent replays kind meh), but still has some railroad-y sections. The reintroduction of the in-game merchant and upgrade system makes new game+ very enticing. Also, mercenaries are back!My  with the game are relatively minor, and the first one stems solely from my decision to do a VoS playthrough on my first go. RE7’s “Madhouse” difficulty made for a stellar way to experience the game for the first time. The same cannot be said for VoS. Not only do we not get the ink ribbons, but the game is littered with checkpoints and autosaves—as such, dying never feels much like a threat and more like a nuisance. The bosses become actual shores to kill. Not because they are hard (you just have to learn and remember the patterns), but because they are bullet sponges. For real, one of the bosses took me almost 20 minutes(!?) to kill (with weapons upgraded). Sure, that’s with me conserving my valuable ammunition by sticking to my handgun and shotgun for the most part, but even then, that’s ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane.Another flaw with the game regardless of difficulty level is the blatantly instanced nature of most of the encounters. I imagine this is something that becomes more apparent when you play on VoS where you actively try to avoid fighting—but enemies can (and will) de-spawn right before your eyes just by you walking into the next triggered event. The enemies are heavily restricted to which areas they can and can not be in, which makes cheesing the game all too easy in many cases. In most areas of the game, enemies can easily (and repeatedly) be pulled to the threshold of their aggro range where they either stop dead in their tracks or start running back to their spawn point. This completely takes the tension out of many encounters when you realize it—and worse still, it even holds true for some of the game’s mini-bosses. Like, did no one playtest this? Is this intended? A game is going to be a game, I get it, but it kinda shatters the illusion when Ethan can obliterate an entire room of enemies by putting his hands on a door. There’s even some cutscenes in which NPCs literally de-spawn in front of your eyes as soon as the cutscene ends (no, a rickety door ridden with holes is not enough to hide the fact that the hag on the other side just popped out of existence mere moments after going through it). As I said, it wouldn’t be so bad if it wasn’t so blatantly apparent.On a more technical level there's also the lack of a FoV slider, which is important to mention.Buuut, with all that said I think RE8 is a pretty damned good game. The two aforementioned flaws are my only gripes with the game as of this writing. That, and maybe the slight overreliance on scripted events, which still isn’t as bad as it was in RE7. Sure, I’ve hardly analyzed the game to the fullest extent here, but I think the best praise I can give is that the game was a genuine blast to play from start to finish. In fact, this is probably one of the best single player experiences I’ve had in quite a while. It’s an improvement of RE7 in almost every aspect (unless you enjoy the horror aspect exclusively) and is worthy of being talked about in the same breath as RE4. Crazy, I know.(TLDR for real; Decent FPS with intricately designed environment. Genuinely scary at parts. Has a good story with endearing characters and charming bad guys. Improves on parts of 7 and adds to some aspects of 4 to create an entirely fresh and enjoyable experience. Bosses are a shore to kill on your first playthrough (if you’re doing VoS) and enemies are too easy to cheese during many encounters.)

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I have to say I'm very disappointed. It is certainly a spiritual successor to Resident Evil 4, and I'm positive that people desperate to scratch that itch will be very happy.But for me the story and the characters have been an enormous let down and the horror aspects are almost non existent for a Resident Evil game.Compared to the horror masterpiece that was RE:7 this game feels like it was made by a completely different studio.Warning: There will be minor spoilers in beyond this point. (Only two and a half hours in so far)Ethan is just...bad.His voice actor is not doing the character justice, no emotion just flatly reading a script.The character is running around this game world acting as if he didn't survive the absolute nightmare of RE:7 – scared of everything, surprised at the existence of monsters, cowers in fear non stop ect. It may as well be any random person.Also Ethan is an immortal, unstoppable juggernaut that belongs in a Marvel movie due to his superhuman resilience. It's beyond typical video game shenanigans, this guy may as well be Thor.And I'm not referencing the games (limited) fighting, within my first 2 hours, in the cut-scenes he has suffered the following injuries;:Been in a serious car accident that was dangerous enough to destroy the armoured truck thingo he was in and kill all the other passengers. The crash also left him outside in the freezing snow for hours. And Ethan is from Texas, so not exactly conditioned for such temperatures.:2 fingers and a good chunk of his left hand bitten off. Doesn't even bandage this for quite some time.:Punched, stabbed, beaten and pulled through a wooden floor.:Impaled through the chest by a long metal pipe. :Knocked unconscious by having heavy metal objects slammed into his entire body via some characters psychic/magic abilities.:He took a full swing to the chest by a gigantic hammer (hammer taller than him) wielded by a monstrous werewolf troll creature – this monster could throw a car around like a toy, getting hit by this hammer would splatter an elephant.:Tied up and dragged a not insignificant distance through hewn rock passageways, and he was unconscious for most of the journey, banging his head into the rocks the whole way.:Has a sickle slashed deep into each leg by superhuman strong vampire babes and then dragged through the castle. Somehow his legs are still attached.:Has a blade driven through each hand and is then suspended in the air via those blades....Ethan then pulls himself free by slicing his hands in half. (not joking).But nevermind those injuries, he is running around jumping, handling firearms and crafting bullets.It's just absurd. Immersion breaking.Speaking of immersion, it's NOTHING at all like RE7. RE7 was scary, it was tense, it was unapologetically gory, gross and gruesome in equal measure. Nothing of the like so far in village. It has about as much horror elements as Skyrim thus far.Your just the terminator running around, but voiced by a scared, confused nerd.As for the other characters.Well.Lets start with everyone's hotly anticipated favourite, Lady D.I dunno about you but I was expecting an evil, sadistic yet glamorous Romanian vampire queen.What I got was a big lady with an American accent who whines and throws temper tantrums.When you are introduced to her, she is literally having a sook, whining and even stamps her foot like a toddler. It wasn't scary or impressive, it wasn't even sexy, it was pathetic.Everyone has an American accent by the way, maybe we aren't in Europe, but Alaska or Michigan. Sigh.All the other characters so far have been empty, one dimensional tropes just there to die.The Daughters being the exception, the voice actress really put her heart into the role and combined with the excellent animation, the daughters are fantastic. And yes, for those wondering, very sexy, in the way that only blood soaked murder-torture vampire women can be.As for the gameplay? It's RE:4 style, with RE:7 modernisation, but none of the flair of either.In RE4 the 'arena's were interesting and featured all sorts of elevation so you could shoot enemies in the legs and have them fall off the cliff, or hot swap to your knife to stun enemies that got close.None of that fancy stuff here. In Village you … shoot enemies in the head until it explodes. When they get close, hold spacebar until they hit your fists and then you shoot them in the head some more. Takes 5-10 bullets. Woooo. Super exciting. The port quality is mostly decent, navigating the menus is clunky and obviously intended for controller, but no major issues other than changing resolution was a pain. Rather then a drop down menu, you have to change it one selection at a time and go through the (short) process of black screen + clicking yes to accepting the new resolution. Going from the default console resolution to 4k was more annoying than it should be.Graphics are fine. Not good by todays standards, not even close to the RE2 and Nemesis remakes, but on par with RE7 so more than good enough for me.Sound is ok. Under-utilised so far compared to RE7. It's just not spooky.TLDR: 3/10. Boring, aged gameplay, dumb, zero effort characters, pitiful villains, superhuman invincible main character, total lack of horror elements compared to other RE or similar games such as Silent Hill or The Evil Within.The good: the animations are fantastic, particularly the character animations. The Daughters.Wait for a big sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute garbage from start to finish. Disappointment after disappointment. Aside from like 3 decent parts, that make up like 15 minutes worth of 12ish hours it takes to beat, things were at best mediocre but mostly just frustrating, un-intuitive, unrewarding, stupid, insulting or tedious.Caveat: My first play through was on Hardcore (so no NG+ weapons or Infinite Ammo) and maybe on that difficulty the game issues were much more apparent than they would be to someone who just played 1 play though (or didn't finish the game) on Casual or Standard but I imagine even those players would run into a lot of the same issues. I'm not trying to crap on the game or make myself feel better about giving a highly rated game a bad review. I generally rate/recommend games based on the ratio of Good Things / Neutral Things / Bad Things. I can happily recommend games that are mostly Neutral with only a few Good Things. But man, this game just had so many Bad Things in it that it soured the rest of the game.I really wish there had been more bad reviews to save me from wasting time and money on this game. I don't even care about the money, I just want the wasted time back and I wish I had saved myself the frustration and disappointment and never played this.I played the demo and thought, "man, this is pretty bad, I wonder if the whole game is like this...". I tried googling it and looked at the positive steam reviews and high metacritic ratings and thought, "well, maybe the rest of the game is better than the demo." It wasn't. It was worse. This would be my recommendation if you're trying to decide if you want to buy the game or not: Play the Demo. If you think "That was amazing! Great gameplay, great story and dialogue, enemies are fun to fight" - then maybe you'd enjoy the whole game. But if you think "eh, I'm not really enjoying fighting the enemies, the story seems kind of stupid, the puzzles are simplistic/insulting" then the decent graphics and atmosphere and Tall Lady Tits probably aren't going to make up for the rest of the frustrations you run into after you buy the whole thing.Do not believe the positive reviews/ratings. If you've enjoyed games like the Dead Space series, Mass Effect, Stalker, Amensia, Bioshock. Or really any decent-good shooter/horror/puzzle/atmospheric game or story... then I'd say that chances are good you'd just find this game to be frustrating, lame, tedious, confusing, stupid, disappointing, repetitive...--Garbage:Story/DialogueCharacters- Characters often don't act in ways that make sense (Ethan/Chris especially)- Lack of character depth- Lack of characters interacting with each otherGuns and Gun PlayGrapples / BlockingCutscenes- Don't move mouse or install a mod to get rid of the "P to Skip" on cutscenesConsole Port IssuesEnemy Design- So many enemies have invisible walls or leashes that they won't pass while you're fighting them and if you move even farther away they don't just *walk* back to where they came from, they instantly disappear and are teleported away. This wouldn't be really be an issue if the walls were farther away from where you encounter the mobs but so many times when you'll be doing the natural thing (and sometimes the only thing you could do when you're in a narrow corridor and there isn't an almighty table for you to play ring-around-the-rosie) - shooting at enemies in front of you while backing away - you'll see the enemies just stop following, turn around and walk away. wtf?- No damage indicators. There's very little "feedback" to let the play know how much damage an enemy has/is taking. Am I doing damage? Is it almost dead? How much health does it have left?- High HP Pools / "Bullet Sponges" / Enemies take way too many_bullets/long to kill"> It's less challenging and more just boring/repetitive/tedious. It doesn't feel like your guns are doing much.Enemy variation- Like 80% of the enemies you'll fight are "Lycans" - a single type of hairy man (2 different haircuts tho!) which don't really seem anything like "werewolves" and 15% are like shriveled undead zombie things that slowly shamble towards you, with melee weapons you can't use or drill hands (2 have jetpacks!). So most of the game you're fighting just 2 different types of mostly uninteresting enemies.Level Design- Very "on rails", linear- Very little replay valueMechanicsMovementBoss Fights - Very cramped, uninteresting rooms. Mostly just a flat circular surface. - Just strafe left or right in a big circle and click the left mouse button repeatedlyPuzzles- The puzzles are extremely simplistic and easy to the point of being insulting. No one is gonna say they were fun or interesting. And they don't change at all on future play throughs so they add negative replay value.--Fine/Good:GraphicsMercenaries mode- Actually fun, challenging and requires some thought and learning to improveVoice Acting- Script bad, VA fine--Nitpicks:This Village is full of clones?! The floor's been magically fixed?> Early in the Village when you get pulled through the floor by a lycan, like 7 of the dead corpses you see are the same model. There are 11 bodies made using 3 models. I was like, "oh ****, are these a bunch of clones or something!?" No. Someone just did a quick copy&paste x8 and called it good. And when you return to where you got pulled through the floor, you'll see there's no hole there. It's been magically repaired!Werewolves and Vampires? No, just mold people.> These are Hairy Men and Bug Ladies. You might be like, "oh, I know a little bit about werewolves and vampires and have enjoyed them in video games before." No. The only thing in common with the usual Werewolves and Vampires you're used to is that the Lycans are hairy with claws and the Vampires have fangs and drink blood. This felt like another "bait" or cheap gimmick to prey on fans of Ws & Vs.--The issue with combining: Limited Resources, Points of No Return, Hidden Things and Endless EnemiesLimited Resources / Resource Management> When Fighting Enemies, you either need to kill them "efficiently" or avoid them (or find ways to get more ammo, although not always possible - sometimes ammo is finite).Points of No Return (PoNR) - Unable to access previous areas> After you've passed through an area and reached a certain location or trigger, you will no longer be able to return to that area this play-through"Hidden" Collectables/Secrets> You must carefully (slowly, methodically, thoroughly) search every areaEndless Enemies> No matter how many Enemies you kill, more will respawn so your only option is to attempt to navigate (move or kill) past that area faster than the enemies can block your way or deplete your ammo.The issue/conflict: If you enter an area with very little ammo compared to the amount of ammo it would take to kill all the enemies (or if there are endlessly spawning enemies) and you won't be able to return to that area at a later time, how can you search for items and secrets without getting overrun? Maybe on lower difficulties or with infinite ammo it's not a problem, but on harder difficulties without infinite ammo or with less dedication to ammo efficiency/procurement - you'll get overrun and die if you try to search every corner instead of just rushing through an area. And you're left with only garbage options if you're a "collector". Cheat (look up online), suicide-explore (focus on searching, knowing you'll die a few times until you've figured out the area), or rely on another play-through. "I'd like to take my time to explore but I can't just kill everything to make this area safe and I can't come back later."--So many parts of it felt like they just put in as little effort as they thought they could get away with and still turn a profit.Worth A Buy: EFAP: Char limit reached and I don't want to continue in comments or I'd add more.

_childDocuments_.review: so my review is done taking as a baseline re7, which I think it is the natural thing to do as this game is a direct continuation:- The kind of terror terror feeling has changed, I felt it a bit softer but probably because the scheme went supernatural/fantastic, gore is kept, perhaps there is even more gore scenes.- Action has increased a lot in this game, if you want a survival challenge I recommend you to start directly in hard mode as normal for me felt like easy mode, enjoyable but too easy (died like 2-3 times and not precisely because of monsters)- Controls, UI and gameplay felt much better and easier to handle, the game pace was increased a little and that was really welcomed from me- Story, events, village and the different zones were perfectly linked and designed, I loved to move around the different zones of the Village (the Dimitrescu castle was the cherry on the cake for me, too bad you cannot go back once you finish that zone!)In a few words, this game was for me a clear re7 evolution and a nice way to close down a epic character storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of RE as it is, but I really enjoyed how this game was quite different from the others, yet still managed to pull in elements from the older games to morph it together into this one. It was scary and horrific, and somehow managed to be gorgeous at the same time. These are some notes I have for it:1. Grotesquely beautiful game art that sometimes I just had to stop and stare in wonder at2. Confining, tight (well-designed) map layouts that are perfect for building up tension3. Stunning monsters and villain designs with compelling boss fights4. The casual level is just difficult enough for, well, casual gamers (me) to enjoy the story and design without ripping out their hair. Although sometimes it felt a little too easy (just toss some mines down and gg)5. Story was weird, but that is pretty standard for RE. Still manages to be interesting, though!6. Only main "negative" thing is there are some areas where there are massive frame drops even on my high end pc, I think these areas are bugged out (such as armory in castle). But these drops didn't strongly impact my gameplay or enjoyment of the game.10/10 recommend! Just make sure you play RE 7 Biohazard first, or else you probably won't understand a lot of the references made.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed my play through of Resident Evil 8. There were some tense moments the game designers expertly created through out the game which kept me on edge. I particularly enjoyed the  segment which was an exceptionally eerie set up for a really disturbing scene.Having said that, I didn't think the game was perfect and had issue with the following points:1. Vast segments of the game are filled with 1-2 standard enemies which become tedious to deal with very fast. They don't have much difference in terms of attack patterns and are easily dispatched by running and blasting. It isn't till later in the game, and only for the briefest of moments, do we encounter some variety in combatants.2. It didn't really feel like a survival horror game. RE8 gives plenty of inventory space from the start, so space management was never really a thing and we were given so many guns and ammo that it never really felt like much of an issue. Also it was easy enough blasting past enemies. 3. I wish they had included a field of view option. It was available in RE7, not so sure why it was missing here. I got a bit dizzy being unable to change the FOV. Had the same issue in RE7, but increasing it helped.4. Ethan seems different in this game, and not his cool self from RE7. It was strange hearing him utter cheap comebacks after defeating a boss OR being defiant by simply cussing an antagonist. i.e. "Well NOW you are the cursed one" OR "F#@K you B@!#H" I am OK with cussing, but here it feels lazy, almost tacked on.5. Story wise, it starts of well enough but by the end it just all comes crashing together, and is a bit too wacky for my tastes. The end scene teases that we aren't quite done with the winters family, but it left me with questions as to how someone who never  If you got through those points, you might think I didn't like the game. _childDocuments_.review: For any long time RE fan, this feels like a combination of RE7 with strong RE4 vibes.  First play through will likely be somewhere around 15 hours depending on how thorough you are collecting things.  There are a few different main areas of the game each with their own theme and feel--I really liked this aspect, they felt distinct from each other.  Per usual, you'll have access to quite a few weapons and they can all be upgraded via stats or weapon parts that you'll find along the way.  Speaking of weapons, the game has an odd aiming mechanic where you can hip fire a weapon, but ADSing just sort of tightens the spread rather than actually aiming down sights--while this works mostly fine, it didn't feel quite right.  This is definitely something that I wasn't a fan of, but fortunately isn't a deal breaker either.  Melee combat feels par for the course for an RE title, but feels a little under-powered if you're an RE veteran.  Story has some great characters, some cringe/cheesiness which I've come to expect with any RE title, and is paced overall pretty well.  Not my favorite RE story, but it serves its purpose and kept my interest for the entire play through.  The characters on the other hand are excellent, especially their visual design which I thought were mostly fantastic.Overall, I really enjoyed RE8 and I think it did a great job of taking the RE7 formula and combining it with more traditional RE areas and puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best resident evil has ever looked, more immersive and cinematic than its predecessor, its still as tense just not as scary. There is one creepy level where you lose your weapons and it becomes a very standard horror game for like 10 minutes other than that it wasn’t scary at all. So it doesn’t really feel like a survival horror game. On top of that not only did they cut down the horror they also completely removed the sense of inventory management by removing chests and moving crafting materials to another tab, which honestly sucks because its such a huge part of the resident evil spirit. I have only been encumbered once which I could easily solve by moving items around. However it is very actiony, if RE7 was RE2 RE8 would be RE4 though the combat is nowhere detailed like RE4’s but still a major upgrade from RE7. One of the things I disliked the most about RE7 was that there were very few enemy types. That got fixed thankfully and its still not as varied like RE4 but at least you don’t only fight enemies with the same texture like in RE7. All of the boss fights were fun and different from each other even the minor boss fights were varied. Exploring the whole village was so fun and rewarding I also love that instead of finding coins for upgrades like in RE7 you hunt animal meats and bring them to duke for him to cook with and you get upgrades from the meals he cooks, that was interesting. Another thing I disliked about RE7 was its pacing and I think RE8 pacing is absolutely amazing like its too good, probably my favorite part. Insane prologue that will make you say wtf, amazing introduction to the village and the chaos state that its in, crazzyy introduction to the antagonists, chateau dimitrescu (the first big level), open world and exploration section with beneviento and moreau levels (beneviento and Moreau levels are smaller than those of lady dimitrescu and Heisenberg but as a whole with the open world its the second big level), the factory (3rd big level), Chris section and final boss are the end game. Chris’s section and the Ethan twist is sooo well made. Its the most story heavy resident evil game and they made a great job with the pacing if it wasn’t this long I probably could finish it one sitting. Ending was great too, its both satisfying and sort of a cliffhanger teaser for the upcoming installments. Shadows of rose dlc was really fun, emotional and lowkey the most scary RE has ever been featuring a great final boss fight and it makes a great job wrapping up Rose’s story and preparing it for future installments. Resident Evil franchise was already great and I think its going to get even better.My current ranking of the franchise: REMAKE2 = REMAKE4 > RE8 > REMAKE3 > RE7 > RE0 > RE1 > others were so bad I legit skipped them but I might try out rev2 on coop splitscreeN

_childDocuments_.review: Good:-Horror element is totally there, I only had one major scare but I love horror. I could see this spooking a few people.-Action you get to just blast ♥♥♥♥.-Lighting nailed it with the dark caves that swallow light but when the sun breaks the dark sky the village is blanketed in soft light.-Story explained itself well with notes that you did not need to read but if you did they would be hints or plot to other RE games.-Gun play was fun but practically the same as RE7, not a game you ADS. I am a fan of that hot garbage but some people are not so be wary of that.-Movement complements the gun play well no jumping or dodging but you are able to sprint and block.-Graphics good optimized good.-Bonus content is there with a nice reward system that feels like you actually are being rewarded for doing stupid ♥♥♥♥.-Voice acting was not perfect for the geological location of the game but was good none the less.-Replay-ability I got four runs before I had done everything I wanted to.-World is an interesting Transylvanian town that four very different areas surrounding it.-Small ♥♥♥♥: collectibles, inventory management, Duke, gore, save points, challenges, difficulty settings, ammo concerns and Duke.Bad (most of this is just small stuff)-Some parts of the game dragged for a bit as far as a second run or more is considered. Just slow paced but the game benefits from that greatly since it is trying to build suspense for your run.-Enemy types vary by area but some are repeated at random times during the game but this does not happen often.-No grade after beating the game (C,B,A,S,SS,SSS)-Wish there was a bit more character building at the start of the game.___________________________________________________________________________Overall this is one of my favorite Resident Evil games I have played, I got all my worth with this purchase. _childDocuments_.review: Might get roasted, but I honestly am not a huge fan. Where as RE7 nailed the texas chainsaw aesthetic it set out to emulate, this game seems to lack identity, flitting from one theme park of horror to another with very little linking them thematically. Actually reminds me of the sort of nonsense set pieces that 5 and 6 catch flak for, but everyone seems to love it here. Shooting and guard mechanics work well enough, but boss fights are weird, cheese filled one note affairs that ultimately left me bored. Doing a 1st playthrough on hardcore and I havent broken a sweat. The OST seems non existent, which is a shame for an RE game. Will say sound design is top notch, from frigid and frosty wind that takes you straight to fellowship of the ring, to tight and cohesive gun sounds that serve to immerse you in each fight- great use of virtual surround as well.  Idk, something about this as a package just doesn't click for me. Definitely in the minority, but as a superfan who has played almost every game in the series, this is easily the weakest of the "modern" arc. The focus seems to be on ok shooting rather than fight or flight choices like other games, and with the introduction of the shop, almost every treasure or piece of loot you find doesn't feel rewarding because you just sell it for $. So an RE game without tense combat and devoid of motivation to explore leaves it feeling very out of place. Not bad per say, but a bad resident evil for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: When I think about my experience in this game, I think of two other games to compare it to, which might seem weird.The first is Half life 2. HL2 was a game consisting of many setpieces that linked together. The trainstation, the canals, the airboat section, Black Mesa East, Ravenholm, Highway 17, Sandtraps, Nova Prospekt. I remember them vividly, though that's partially because I've played the hell out of Half Life 2.Resident Evil Village also has some fantastic setpieces. The village, of course; the castle, the dollhouse (and the basement underneath), Moreau's section, and the factory. All of them fit together and lead from one to the other perfectly. The progression of areas in the game didn't feel too rushed or forced. I only wish I could go back to completed areas to get things I missed.The other game I think of is Dead Space 2. Funnily enough, Dead Space was heavily inspired by Resident Evil 4, and if you've played both, you can clearly see that.I think you can compare RE 7 and Village to DS 1 and 2. If Resident Evil 7 was Dead Space 1 — a slow paced, scary, haunting experience where power is taken from the player constantly — then Resident Evil Village is Dead Space 2 — a more action packed sequel that strayed away from horror and toward thrills to broaden its audience.The devs for DS 2 said in interviews that EA wanted more sales, and forced them to go in a more action-oriented direction since horror didn't bring in the massive audience they needed. And, wouldn't you know, Capcom ran into similar problems with RE 7, saying that it was too scary for a lot of players. So they made RE Village more empowering, still giving it the scary moments and tension, but overall straying from the horror aspect (barring one area in particular).I don't mind that the game isn't as scary as RE 7. In fact, I think it might have been the right way to go, since a lot of people don't like horror.----------------This is a great game, one of the best AAA games to come out in a damn year. I haven't ran into game-breaking bugs and everything seems polished — something I shouldn't have to compliment a game for.I recommend this game if you're looking for a fun and dramatic shooter with some horror mixed in.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ruined by cut scenes that are out of sync as well as stuttering, slow down and crashes when being attacked by three or more enemies. Been playing Resident Evil games for 25 years and while not all of the games themselves were very good (5 & 6), I've never had technical issues playing them. RE, RE2 Remake & RE7 are my 3 favourite games  - so I've been hyped for this since it was announced. My PC has no junk on it, it meets the requirements, Windows 10 is updated, all drivers are updated, I've made running the game the PC's highest priority, set the game for best performance, I've applied the Nvidia Optimal settings for the game - I've tried every "solution" out there - nothing has helped much, if at all. This has been a terrible, frustrating experience. The game looks like it's great but it doesn't matter much when I can't experience the story or play it because of lag, stuttering, slow down and crashes.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Usually sequels don't live up to its predecessors but Village in my opinion surpassed Biohazard in several different ways. Re:7 was more of the freaky jump scare infested experience out of the two but Village has its moments of freaky. There is several times where  I was extremely unnerved and had to take a second to take in what was happening. In this game it's more of a action horror rather then a horror survival like RE:7. The story is very compelling and keeps you wanting to know more but it isn't without it's flaws. Ethan winters isn't exactly the greatest character out of this franchise and is a pretty bland personality. With that being said it kinda makes you the person experiencing the wild events going on. In RE:7 the enemies felt very lack luster. Not a whole lot of them to shoot other then the baker family but in Village you have several enemies to keep you on your toes.  The lycans are fun to fight and other enemies that show up in different moments of the story are a welcome sight. The main bosses in this are an absolute blast with each giving a very different and intriguing experience. The mechanics in this game seem to have been adjusted in a good way and the gun play which isn't exactly the best seeing as this is a first person experience but does feel loads better then the previous game.The throw backs to Resident Evil 4 was a very nice touch and has very similar vibes for many different reasons. Play time for the story to me felt a tad bit short but that's only because I wanted more of the story. For the average player I would say it's a good play time. I didn't rush through it but I wasn't slowly going over everything that's in front of you. 10 hours felt reasonable. All in all If you are a fan of the franchise I would say this is worth the 60 dollar price tag. If you like RE:7 this may not be exactly what your looking for giving the fact this game went in a different direction but if you want to know more about the stroy grab it. If a score was asked of me I'd give it a solid 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing RE for about 12 years now, and i can say without a doubt that I love this game more than RE4. It brings back a lot of RE4 mechanics, but modernizing it. There are good plot twist and great storytelling with a satisfying ending.Do yourself a favor and play it. <3

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all time. Fixes my only two gripes with RE7 (which was also great). RE7 had no enemy variety while 8 has ample variety and keeps it fresh throughout. 7 also had a boring final movement and lackluster final boss while 8 has one of the best late-game areas (with appropriate terrifying late game enemies) and a Bloodborne-tier final boss.My ONLY problem is the lack of a baked-in FOV slider. Otherwise, it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 8 is a fetish introducer disguised as a survival horror video game in the long running Resident Evil franchise. We once again take the mantle of Ethan Winters, the poor schmuck who got way in over his head (Along with all his other extremities) after chasing down his missing girlfriend led to him having a hoedown in a house full of super powered rednecks. After that small business was rectified Ethan and his wife Mia have moved deep into Europe and has gone into hiding against the various organizations that stalk them due to the horrors they witnessed 3 years ago. All seemed peaceful, and they even had their first daughter, Rose! It looks like everything “might” be settling down for good…But so of course, that would make for a pretty boring video game, so of course ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan.The Boulder Abuser himself, Chris Redfield makes Ethan’s wife, Mia, do the bullet dance, and kidnaps him along with their daughter. After passing out, Ethan awakes to find that the car he was in had crashed and landed him in a remote village with a bunch of unique gothic architecture. Looking for answers for why his greatest ally had shattered his hard-won peace, as well as the whereabouts of his daughter drives Ethan onward, into the evils that take residence here.Resident Evil 8 veers several more notches into action horror, being somewhat of a more subdued Resident Evil 4 (Well, at least until the climax). The game looks amazing at 1440p, and since I was one of the lucky SOBs who managed to only pay over $200 over MSRP, it ran really well, with no slow down besides the boss fight against a certain Nicholas Cage impersonator. Not sure how older cards would run on the game, but I’m sure should be fine as Capcom’s RE engine tends to be very well optimized. I was able to max it out, no issues. The game builds atmosphere for about an hour, giving you little in terms of weapons until then, then after an ambush by the Lycans, you basically spend most of the game blowing the baddies away. The game gives you a rather unremarkable arsenal, which includes pistols, Shotguns, A Grenade Launcher, Sniper Rifle, as well as dynamite and mines to deals with groups of enemies and to set up traps. You also can use the various treasures you find around the village to upgrade your guns, such as their damage, minimizing sway, have them carry more ammunition, etc. I found this aspect of the game to be very dry, ands more could be done to differentiate the different models of the gun like in RE4.The basic gameplay loop is that you are tasked to take down Mother Miranda, a powerful matriarch who is treated in the village with religious fervor. But before you get to her, you must collect the 4 “Keys” (You’ll find out just what the key is, it’….gruesome) from ther 4 Noble heads that serve her. Alcina “Vampire Mommy” Dimitrescu, a scornful mechanic named Heisenberg, and 2 other weirdos. This is one thing that the game may have embellished, with all the focused advertisement on Lady Alcina and Heisenberg. Alcina and Heisenberg both get their own dedicated areas, but the other two Nobles, Salvatore Moreau and Donna Beneviento, are much shorter in comparison. I did find Donna’s area very unique and enjoyable (Apparently it was heavily inspired by Kojima’s P.T experiment, which I never got the chance to play), but very short in comparison to Alcina and Karl’s. In Moreau case, besides a little puzzle to get to him, his boss fight is your entire lot. In addition with the somewhat more fantastical elements being expanded upon, with Ethan “Everyman” Winters going from fighting Radioactive republicans, fighting Vampires, Lycans, and even piloting a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tank, the game seems to have tried to take aspects from 7 and 4 respectively, but ends up failing to really meet either at the middle. The camp and cheese in 4 was part of it’s identity, as well as the slasher movie vibe from 7, and 8 really does fail to get those aspects to come across. 4 is portrayed with a light hearted tone, 7 the complete opposite. You can’t really tell me thqat some of the shjit Ethan fights in this game aren’t completely ridiculous (Which is fine, but it really clashes with the game’s everyman appeal, especially when you find out something about him that I do admit has some nuance, but is the most obvious ♥♥♥♥ in the world).All in all, I did enjoy the game, but I feel that it was undercooked in many ways. Enemy variety was largely lacking (Sure, RE7 had the same problem, but that wasn’t really the point of it.) Game starts off with a tiny bit of a sandbox vibe but becomes largely linear even though with the premise it’d be cool if you could have fought the lords in any order (Though maybe having certain weapons/ items would make the area easier). I did find the Nobles very charismatic and memorable, such as Alcina and her daughters, Moreau’s insecurity, Nicho- I mean Heisenberg’s…. everything, and the less said about Donna the better. It’s still a good game, with some aspects of it I’d call great. But I’d wait a bit for a sale. I wonder if part of the problems might have been caused by COVID, so I can’t 100% fault them if the undercooked ideas in the game didn’t have the means to come into fruition with something like that going on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game did not dissapoint. It definitely lived up to everyone's expectations but didn't exceed them like RE 2 did. The story is the best out of all the games in the franchise, and the atmosphere just screams "Resident Evil 4".I do admit, the game does have a slow start. But it definitely becomes much much better, unlike One Piece where the fans just keep on saying "IT GETS BETTER AT CHAPTER 7432784623874 I SWEAR" (joke).This game plays just like RE7 (First Person) but in comparison to 7, this one has much more action. This game is also quite easy on standard and SOMEWHAT challenging on hardcore mode and the bosses are not that difficult either.However, when playing on Village of Shadows difficulty (you unlock it by either beating the game or buying the deluxe edition) it gets much more challenging.Either way, very enjoyable game that did not let me down. A very good addition to the RE franchise for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: After the excellent resident evil 2 remake, this is a let down. This game tries to modernise the genre of new audiences but end up losing what made the old games special. With a boring protagonist, mediocre plot, bullet sponge enemies and generic uninspiring bosses.  With any game franchise, there is normally a point in which you say to yourself, "This series is getting stale and I probably won't get the next instalment unless I have nothing to play". For me, this is the one.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere and it jumps up the scares from Resident Evil 7 well. The scale is much larger but you can tell when COVID production started on the game. There is a noticeable change in pacing by the third home of the village. Cutscenes start taking you out of the first person perspective which normally did not happen until that point and the intensity drops a bit. The ending simply is horrendous.    The final boss sheds anything scary that Resident Evil had become with Ethan and goes right back to the sci fi action shlock of the fifth and sixth entries.Ending aside this was still a very scary and fun experience I would recommend, the beginning 95% of the game is phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like Resident Evil 4? Did you like Resident Evil 7? Do you want a horror game where you don't have to constantly run and hide, but the option is still open? If you answered yes to any of those questions, this is the game for you.While it is a HUGE departure for the Resident Evil games to feature more monsters than "infection" based entities, the classic European horror of the 19th and 20th century makes for a presentation that any horror fan will love. It's been a long time since a horror game made me feel nervous in the daylight and well lit rooms.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: The story is a little meh in the beginning because of the lack of detail Chris gives you later to find out that he totally could've told you why he did what he did from the start. Other than that the game play is pretty good and the level designs are unique. The DLC was a fantastic addition where you get to play as Ethan's daughter and her play style is refreshing and in 3rd person. The DLC also included the 3rd person mode for the original game as well. The game is optimized to get the most out of your GPU and the graphics menu lets you see the changes based on the graphical options you select but I didn't see a benchmark test option in there. I give the game an 8/10 it lost 2 points with info unnecessarily withheld from your main character and because this game had a few missed opportunities to be scarier. RE7 had lots more scarier moments than this game in my opinion. All in all it's a great buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the internet going crazy over the tall lady the four villains you face throughout the campaign all have pretty poor character design. The Baron however is an incredible character and a few of the survivors you meet early on are believable and interesting.  In terms of the story the series jumped the shark long ago so every installment stretches things even further at this point. If you stop to think about the plot at all things immediately start to fall apart and make little to no sense but if i'm being honest i'm not here for plot or character design. This is a Resident Evil game. The characters are rarely interesting. The stories stopped being good a long time ago and i'm here for the gameplay and atmosphere.  I'll start by addressing atmosphere. The good news is RE8 has a incredible atmosphere. The environments are visually stunning and distinctly Resident Evil.  It doesn't do anything exceptional with environmental story telling, but you can expect to find a few interesting documents and letters to read throughout the campaign that add to the world building of the universe and aren't that bad but nothing like what's found in early installments. Overall i will say the world i wonderful to live in with a brilliant gothic atmosphere and captivating scenery. Now I saved what i consider most important for last which is the gameplay and I am happy to report the moment to moment gameplay is lots of fun. Continuing in the footsteps of RE7 this installment is first person but takes ques from RE4 in the speed and pacing of the gameplay. This game is a massive improvement over the gameplay in RE7.  You move faster, there is more enemy variety, the story and campaign moves at a very nice pace all things that Capcom from the feedback they got with 7 and it really shows. However the addition of enemies dropping ammo and lots of heavy firepower really take it more towards that RE4 Action Horror genre and away from that traditional RE Survival Horror genre that I do much prefer but honestly both are great.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: The game is well done, with an interesting story and an even better twist to it. I do like how they tied this game to the last one, and even little pieces of lore linking to the older Resident Evil games. I enjoyed the feel of the action this game offers, and the controls are clean in my opinion. If you like Resident Evil stories, or Resident Evil 7 of course, this game is definitely worth a try.

The beginning and ending sections are great but the middle part drags HARD. House Beneviento and the Lake feel like they take forever and detract from the game a whole. Especially on repeat playthoughs. Speaking of repeat playthoughs there are too many cutscenes and it really turns me off from playing the game again when I know I have to sit through 30 minutes of barely interactive gameplay just to start the game. And the plot makes ZERO sense when you think about it for more than 5 seconds. I wanted to like this game but honestly I cant.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: A fine entry in the series.It doesn't leave as strong an impression as other recent darlings--namely, RE7 and RE2 '19. The novelty of 7's first-person take has kind of worn off, and there's nothing in here as compactly intricate as RE2's puzzle-box police station. But, it's got everything else an RE fan should expect: lofty production values, slow, deliberate combat, meticulous bullet rationing, and laughably bad writing.The emphasis on exploration feels lighter here, and long segments are pretty on-rails. Almost every time you get a key, you already know where the door is. The body horror moments now come so frequently that they kind of read like gruesome jokes. The maguffin-guarding area lords have decently cool designs, but other than that big vampire lady, you get the sense that you've seen them all before (they are--no spoilers--Chucky, yet another giant fish, and Magneto). And none have anything to do with the narrative, of course. But what did you expect? RE has never tried to hide that it's just a video game.For a triple-A series that has reinvented itself so successfully and frequently, an entry like RE8 is always going to feel a little disappointing. But, some of the zombies have jet boosters and drill arms, and that's pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not believe what I am seeing. It feels like my eyes are playing tricks on me but no, it's legit. I had my FPS counter up the entire time to confirm I wasn't crazy.In short, this game runs like f*cking butter. Holy sh*t it is so, so smooth. Rock solid 144 FPS in my 3 hours of playing (at the time of this review) and it never dipped once. Not even from gameplay to cutscene transitions (which is typically when FPS dips occur), or even when moving from one area of a map to the next (another common offender of FPS stutters). I am nowhere even close to finishing the game but the performance alone gets a thumbs up from me. It's extremely rare I say that in this day and age with all the god awful PC ports constantly being released. I do recall hearing back when this game originally launched that there were performance issues regarding how Denuvo was implemented or something along those lines. So, I came into this game wary and with expectations tempered. Either it was fixed or those FPS drops only affected a small selection of people. Regardless, as it stands this game is unbelievably well optimized. I got this game for sale along with RE7 for roughly 60 bucks and that includes the gold edition of both of them. If you were like me and got any of those 2 games on sale, they are an absolutely steal. Yes I recommend Resident Evil: Village, it is fantastic. May or may not come back to update this review when I finish the game but like I mentioned before, the performance is so good it gets a thumbs up from me regardless.Alright 10 hours later I have finished the main game and everything I wrote before still applies. There were a couple instances where the FPS would dip for a second but those instances were so rare it doesn't matter. It's not like I expect games to run flawlessly 100% of the time without any single hiccups. This game still runs like a dream and is an absolute blast to play. In comparison to RE: Biohazard, this game is a little less scary in favour of more action. Not necessarily a bad thing depending on how you view it, but something to think about. I personally didn't mind and found the wide arsenal of guns and the implementation of a shop system quite a fun departure from what was done in 7. I really liked how each antagonist had their own area and theme surrounding said area. The game has a village in the middle and surrounding it are 4 areas that each of the lords occupy. Beneviento's was my personal favourite, though it was shorter than I expected. For a roughly 10 hour game there is a surprising amount to do and see. It certainly felt much longer than 10 hours and it's one of those games where it's so good you wish there was more. However, it's easy to miss collectibles and with the game's challenges system, it incentivizes repeat playthroughs.  On the topic of playthroughs, I finished my first game on standard difficulty. Definitely consider ramping up the difficulty if you're considering doing more playthroughs because at that point you are familiar with the game's systems and layout. I think I can count on one hand how many times I died in this game on my first playthrough. That is certainly a byproduct of the game giving you lots of resources during combat, but it's also a testament to how well the game gives instructions. There's plenty of chase sequences and puzzles to solve where it's not like my ammo or guns would even matter in those scenarios. But the game does an excellent job of nudging you on the right path to take when you're being pursued, or dropping subtle hints when trying to piece together clues to solve a puzzle. So I had a very smooth and pleasant experience with this game. Certainly part of it was the abundance of resources, but also the game itself just does a really good job of guiding the player without frustrating them. I could have all the ammo and healing in the world but if I kept dying to some chase sequence or stuck in a room for an hour it would be a very different discussion. None of this is to imply that the game is boringly easy or anything like that, it's just a solid experience all around and it strikes that perfect middle ground of challenging but fair.In short, Resident Evil: Village is fantastic and I recommend it to anyone who isn't afraid to try some survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: , the latest instalment in the iconic survival horror franchise from Capcom, continues to push the boundaries of the genre with its innovative first person camera view. Set in a chilling, Gothic European village, the game takes players on a roller-coaster ride of thrills, intrigue, and heart-pounding action while also delivering the franchise one of its most iconic, if not iconic villains, Countess Alcina Dimitrescu. From the moment she appeared in an early trailer for , Lady Dimitrescu captured the attention of the internet: her towering, sultry frame; her sickly-sweet smile; her massive hat; her proper yet authoritative tone. Viewers were instantly obsessed, labelling her "tall vampire lady" and demanding to know everything about her, which prompted Capcom to reveal her exact height — 9'6" including her hat and heels — months before  launched in May of 2021. Lady Dimitrescu, and her murderous three daughters preside over Castle Dimitrescu which towers over the village protagonist Ethan Winters (the lead from ) finds himself in at the start of the game. Countess Alcina Dimitrescu is not the only villain Ethan Winters will need to outsmart in this sequel, but she definitely is the most memorable. From the get go  manages to deliver an intense and memorable experience that should keep fans of the series on the edge of their seats.:One of the standout features of  is its stunning visual presentation. The RE Engine once again proves its prowess, delivering detailed character models, breathtaking environments, and impressive lighting effects. The titular village itself is a masterclass in environmental design, seamlessly blending decrepit architecture with eerie ambience. The transition from the village to more fantastical locales is seamless and adds to the game's sense of mystery and foreboding.: continues the franchise's shift towards a more action-oriented approach, akin to . The gameplay strikes a balance between tense survival horror and intense combat sequences. Ethan Winters, the protagonist, is more agile this time around, allowing for smoother movement and dynamic evasive actions. The inventory management system returns, adding an extra layer of challenge as players must strategise on the fly.The weapon variety is satisfying, with each firearm feeling impactful and unique. However, the game occasionally suffers from pacing issues, with certain segments feeling too action-heavy, diminishing the sense of vulnerability that defines the series. The addition of crafting and merchant mechanics adds depth, but the inclusion of some survival elements may alienate purist fans of the franchise.: boasts an intriguing narrative that combines supernatural horror with 's signature bio-terrorism plotlines. The enigmatic Lady Dimitrescu and her vampiric daughters steal the show with their eerie charm, but some secondary characters lack development. The overarching story sometimes struggles to maintain a cohesive tone, veering between chilling horror and campy action. While the central mystery is compelling, some plot twists may leave players scratching their heads.: excels at creating an unsettling atmosphere, with its haunting sound design, meticulously crafted environments, and relentless tension. The first-person perspective heightens immersion, making encounters with grotesque enemies genuinely terrifying. The game's psychological horror elements, especially in the dollhouse segment, are spine-chilling and showcase the developers' mastery at crafting scares. However, some areas lose their fright factor due to predictable jump scares and reliance on shock value.: runs smoothly on current-gen hardware, maintaining a consistent frame rate even during intense action sequences. However, I did experience severe frame drops when fighting one of Lady Dimitrescu daughters who deploys swarms of insects during the fight with her. This swarm lowered my framerate in to single digits which was jarring.  Load times, for the most part, are minimal, and the game's visuals remain impressive throughout. Some players may also experience minor glitches or texture pop-in (as I did), though these issues are infrequent and don't significantly impact the overall experience.: is a worthy addition to the franchise, offering a visually stunning and atmospheric journey through horror. While the game occasionally strays from its survival horror roots and stumbles in its narrative execution, it still manages to deliver an intense and memorable experience that will leave players eagerly anticipating the next chapter in the  saga. With its exceptional graphics, spine-tingling moments, and a gripping sense of dread,  solidifies itself as a must-play title for both series veterans and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe RE8 is that it's a mix of RE4 and RE7, although fans of RE2 Remake and the classic RE games may be left disappointed. Capcom has crafted a refreshing gameplay experience that draws on what made RE4 and 7 so great, while introducing features never before seen in an RE game, such as a semi-open world to explore and ... cooking? The gameplay is much more fast-paced and action-oriented than say RE2, RE3, and even RE7. Regardless of how you feel about this shift in pace, one area where the game excels is creating an atmospheric world, that makes you feel isolated and watched at the same time. In terms of negatives, I'd say the default keyboard controls are a bit convoluted (especially for the menus),and that this game feels like it could've been its own thing, rather than an RE game. But I understand why Capcom wouldn't want to give their own horror series competition.

The weapons were direct upgrades from previous versions, and if you bought upgrades for the first weapons, it was a waste of money. No "this gun can reload faster, this one fires faster, and this one holds more ammo", it was just "You get a new gun! sell your old one it sucks now." Surprising lack of melee weapons, even though there's 3 versions of the Pistol and Shotgun, there's no other melee weapons (until after you purchase them with "challenge points" or whatever) which I thought they might change after 7. Also, no storage bin. Dunno if that's more in line with 4 (which I haven't played, but hear 8 is relatively closely based on in gameplay) or just a change they wanted to make. Oh and don't worry about storage space at all, buy 2 storage upgrades and never worry about it again.
