_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 8 The Village is a good game. That's it, that's all there is to say really. It's just good, not great, not amazing, but good. It tries to be like its big brother, 4, but it just falls so short. In fact, if I closed my eyes, I could probably imagine playing as Leon hunting down Ashley in a nondescript Spanish countryside. Instead, I open my eyes and see myself as Ethan hunting down his daughter Rose in a nondescript <insert European region here> countryside. Both 4 and 8 have castles, they both have a mysterious magical cult, but there are a few inherent differences between both of them.1. I hate self-insert characters in a series like Resident Evil. Ethan in Resident Evil 7 was just weird to me, I didn't like it then, didn't like it now, but at least the storyline provides adequate reasoning for him to be the main character this time rather than Chris or Leon or Jill or any of the other characters I love.2. Lady Dimitrescu is abhorrently over-hyped. Like, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I LOVE BIG VAMPIRE WAIFU, but, first boss? There's a challenge that requires you to kill her in under 5 minutes? If you paid attention to the ad campaign, she was a fan favorite and everyone wanted to know more about her. They played her as this grand figure that would be involved for a good portion of the game, but then just kinda uses her as a knock-off Mr. X/Tyrant from Resident Evil 2. I want so much more about her, I want to know who she was before she became the giantess. She has to be more interesting than just the first boss.3. Consistent bugs. I've discovered at least 4 consistent bugs in the game, 3 of which can make the game impassable at certain areas, but can be fixed with save/reload mechanics. Mainly, the biggest culprit, is a monster in "Chapter 3" that gets stuck in a hallway and blocks the exit.4. The Settings Menu. RTX Mode resets your graphics settings and the graphics themselves can look like Playstation 2 graphics at times. It's weird, like, the first time you get into the game you of course fiddle with the graphics settings to make sure you're getting the best experience and what-not, but it took me about 5 minutes to set up graphics. I get in game, the graphics look almost PS1 era. Back to the menu, I see RTX mode set to "Off", so, I flip it to "On". All my settings reset, I don't notice this because it's not that apparent. Back to game, now I'm in PS2 era graphics. Go back to menu, fix all the graphics settings after another 5 minutes, back to game, and the graphics are now tolerable. Get to a point in the game where they give me a gun. Up until this point, I had assumed that aim/look sensitivity was contextual, you know, like, because I wasn't in a spot with danger they turned the sensitivity down. Nope, it's slow as hell all the time. Back to the options menu. Find the mouse sensitivity, crank that bad boy to 11, and boom, doing great. Wait, no I'm not, because there is a SEPARATE SETTING FOR AIMING SENSITIVITY! Back to the options menu, set that to 11, and finally, the game is playable.5. Chris Redfield - Why is he a ♥♥♥♥? Why is he a military genius? In Resident Evil 1 he was an ex-military marksman who joined STARS and then joined BSAA and started travelling the world destroying bio-weapons. Since when did he become some badass super soldier? I know, nit-picking, but I never really pegged Chris for the "tall, dark, and brooding super soldier" type, you know?6.  You can always tell when the writers start to run out of ideas. They reuse old concepts, they stay away from anything new or anything too old, and they just beg for dear life that no one asks any questions. Umbrella is hardly mentioned, BSAA is tossed around willy-nilly, viruses are passe, and anything that isn't supremely over-the-top isn't worth mentioning or doing. Just get to the final boss and you'll see what I mean. 1. This is a decently fun game, it has some awesome creep factor (Chapter 3 (the second boss) in particular gave me flashbacks to the Seaside Hotel from Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines. I literally had to pause the game, stand up, and walk away to collect myself. The fights are fun, the gameplay is challenging, and it feels like Resident Evil 4's younger, less cool brother.2. Lady Dimitrescu - Seriously, she's probably my favorite character of the game simply for the amount of character development they put into her. In fact, all of the bosses were just fun. They each had their own quirks, their own personality, and aside from some voice acting issues from Heisenberg's weird gameshow host voice, I love all the bosses. They needed way more character development like Lady D got, but each one is memorable... Except Moreau... Moreau was just... weird. You'll understand when you see him.3. The Meta - There are a lot of references to previous games. The merchant makes a joke about "What are you buying?" from Resident Evil 4, during Heisenberg's fight, he makes a passing mention at Chris' boulder-punching past (I swear, I feel like I hallucinated that moment, but I know it's there!), and the big reveal at the end . The Meta elements in this game are fun, but can break immersion if you're someone who really likes that in a game.4. It is a different kind of Resident Evil. The fact that Ethan is some faceless protagonist and is some weird self-insert for the player, I had a hard time connecting with this game. Resident Evil has always been, "Here's Chris/Jill/Leon/Claire, they are trapped in a nightmare, now help them survive", but RE8 gives the feeling of a diet version of Outlast 2. It's creepy, but not scary. It's less survival-horror, more action-horror. It has story, but it's not story-based. I think that this being different from RE2, RE3, and RE4 is a positive. It gives Capcom some new directions. They don't have to always stick with their roster of characters, they can throw a new character in every so often, and when they do, it can wind up being fun.5. Replayability. While, technically, this game has slightly less replayability than RE4, but theres still some great reasons to play RE8 more than once. It's a chance to unlock guns, infinite ammo, and bonuses like concept art and character models.So, for my final ruling, I'd say if you really want to play it, then go play it right now, but other wise, I'd wait a bit to see if the price drops or if any DLC makes some more fun available. As I said at the beginning, this is a good game, but it's just that, just good.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village continues the storyline of 7, favouring action more than horror (though there still is plenty of horror to be had); the gunplay is very enjoyable and the tense atmosphere in the village lends even more adrenaline to every encounter. Following suit with Resident Evil 4, Ethan Winters evolution from normal guy to action hero emulates Leon Kennedy in more ways than one, while it can vary from epic to incredibly corny at times, the plot is endearing and left me on the edge of my seat. I had encountered some bugs such as audio not syncing up with the cutscenes and graphical errors, but they simply went away after the first portion of the game. YMMV when it comes to software issues but they seemed to be minimal after the first hurdle.Overall the game is a strong 9/10 and definitely worth picking up. It suffers from the typical Resident Evil story progression but it has more than enough nuance to its plot to make up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't a normal RE game, what is it then? I think it pulls a lot of new things in that makes it better and it still holds a lot of things that is RE before RE7. My best guess on what this game is is that they combine RE4 and RE7 together to make this Bloodborne theme game. Without spoilers here is my cons and pros...Pros: Game is beautiful and I am thankful my PC can handle the full graphics, shadows, and every small detail this game has to offer. The landscape itself around you is breathtaking and very stunning.The combat is much like RE7 but with a new function of you being able to push off certain enemies off of you before you take damage. There is also more space/room so you can pick up more items. Certain items are now stored in a different counter instead of filling up your bag. They did balance this by having weapons take up a bit more room (like RE5 for example).The story does make me wonder what has happened, it is a good reason to get me to push myself as to why I am going this far.Interesting bosses.Cons: This isn't a con for me since I kept myself from spoilers, but the first boss was a bit too easy and much of a let down.You can crouch and avoid 80% of all attacks, cheesing your way through the game.The map is a bit confusing, gets tiring trying to figure out how to get there when doors that were open is now closed and old paths get randomly block with a fetch quest.I do recommend this game and I am not a huge fan of RE4 or RE7 but do like how they took this game. I still have a good heart of RE1, 2, and 3 but I think this much of a change is refreshing.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village stands as a testament to the pinnacle of modern gaming, excelling in its visuals and a narrative that keeps players enthralled from start to near-finish. Its storyline, rich in depth and intrigue, captivates players, leading them through a thrilling and eerie journey filled with twists and turns.However, the brilliance of this game takes a slight hit due to its conclusion. The ending, unfortunately, doesn't quite match the incredible build-up, leaving some players feeling a touch dissatisfied after investing deeply in the game's narrative.Nevertheless, Resident Evil Village remains a standout title in the franchise, showcasing the developers' expertise in creating an unforgettable gaming experience. Despite its minor flaw, it manages to deliver an exceptional horror adventure that fans of the series and newcomers alike should not miss

_childDocuments_.review: This is my personal favorite resident evil game. It used to resident evil 4 but once i played this game it was knocked from its throne. This will be my second play through of the game my first was when it came out and i played it on playstation. both versions have their pros and cons with the playstation haptic feedback really adding to the experience but pc running better and looking nicer. For this play through i played on hardcore and have made it all the way to the final fight their were a few moments that really tested my patience mostly due to the lycans... i hate the lycans. Other than that the game is great. The lead Ethan Winters is my favorite MC of the franchise and even knocked the one liner stud that is Leon Kennedy. I feel he is more relatable when compared to the super elite MC of the past (I am looking at boulder punching chris and back flipping style on your ass leon) and without a doubt he is worlds best dad. I cannot recommend this game enough do yourself a favor and treat yourself to this master piece of a game. On a closing note i like how tense the game is and how it makes you feel weak through most of the game. My personal favorite part was the benevientos section. It scare the hell out of me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just now finished my first playthrough on standard difficulty. Great game.I really do prefer the first person view in general so I'm glad they're keeping it from 7, it provides a much more immersive experience.The game takes a step back from the horror intensity of 7 and goes for more action although it does sport some very capable horror sequences where the tension is built up very well.I really liked the different approach to the enemies, it felt quite special compared to other RE games. The way they look and behave really caught me by surprise. They dodged, sprinted at me in packs, climbed from above and below, used ranged attacks and high ground and had all sorts of different attack patterns and various ways to defeat each particular one of them. I also thought the enemy variety was quite good for an 8 hr playthrough.The visual design for bosses was fantastic and they were quite different in terms of gameplay, I especially enjoyed the final one. It is worth mentioning however that some mini bosses get repeated, although only once from what I've personally experienced.I think there are two compelling action sequences that are worth mentioning which contrast eachother very well, one in the beggining that had me on the edge of my seat, trying your best to survive while getting overwhelmed and one at the end where you're a complete badass, mowing down enemies with high tech equipment to make your way towards your objective.The environments were beautiful, loved the medieval romanian architecture and attention to detail, game has a great sense of atmosphere as well.Story was a blast, I didn't expect these developments, I don't wanna spoil anything but it does have some "holy ♥♥♥♥" moments especially if you're familiar with the previous games.The graphics were improved from 7 in many ways but I especially liked the facial animations and model quality in this one.As per usual with RE games, if you hate puzzles you will probably get frustrated with this game, although I thought they were done pretty well all things considered. Besides for some of the more classic RE ones where you have to find different components and keys, it also had a few physics based puzzles and a detective one that involves a mannequin which was pretty decent. Puzzles usually offer a moment of respite where you can take recent events in, away from all the action and horror.The game did freeze once for about 5 seconds right after defeating a boss. It also suffers from weird controls on mouse and keyboard and it doesn't offer to rebind some keys such as middle mouse button for moving the map. As with most other Resident Evil titles, the survival horror aspect makes the gameplay quite meticulous and slow if you're used to other games like Doom for example. You have to conserve resources, go for aiming precision and headshots, time blocks, avoid attacks, sometimes avoid fighting enemies altogether and so on. Keep that in mind if you dislike this type of gameplay.Overall an enjoyable time, I'll play it on the two higher difficulties as well and the other game mode and try to complete challenges too since the gameplay is quite fun.I'd say this is probably my favorite RE title since 4.

_childDocuments_.review: this is an all around amazing game, it was a horror survival game with a small hint of psychological horror in it, i just wish it was a little more scary. the graphics are great and the amount of detail of characters, map design, and physics are beautiful. the replay ability is absolutely there, at the time of this review I am on my 3rd play through and it has not gotten old, looking for Easter eggs and chasing achievement are fun to try. the story in it of itself was very fantastic and told very well, it was the first time in a long time where the ending touched me in the feels. and the return of mercenaries mode is fun but very challenging i can definitely see myself repeatedly trying for that SSS rank aross the board.

_childDocuments_.review: While being good overall, Resident Evil 8 does have a couple of major sections that are primarily puzzle-based that would get cumbersome on additional playthroughs.In addition, the game lacks any sort of cathartic purpose to grind for unlimited ammo weapons. Resident Evil 1 or 2? Yeah, get the unlimited weapons and cut loose. No need to manage each shot. In Resident Evil 8, you feel prepared for each engagement to where you can kill all of the enemies with little ammo management.Mercenaries is enjoyable, but is different this time around. Instead of getting to choose from different characters with different loadouts for each, you go through a series of stages as Ethan and purchase weapons / upgrades between stages. Does it work? Sure, but it feels more like an exercise in optimizing purchases between rounds rather than enjoying specific characters and loadouts.Overall, you will enjoy your first playthrough of Resident Evil 8, but subsequent playthroughs will feel like an absolute slog through the lengthy puzzle sections.

_childDocuments_.review: New player to RE and I must say the game is astoundingly beautiful and  very well thought out.  I love everything about it.  The story has me sucked in, the aesthetics have me drooling...just the amount of detail is so incredible.  I don't want to give any spoilers but there are things that happen in the game that are just unexpected and eerie.  I have never played a game where I literally jumped in my chair.  I'm over the moon with the game and think if you like well paced, well written stories this game would be for you.  I also enjoy the combat, though still a bit early in the game, it feel right i.e. the gun shot sounds, the impact of shots, the way creatures attack all A +The only complaint I would have is that you really need to tinker with the graphical settings to get it where you want it. _childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village takes place 3 years after the events of Resident evil 7, Ethan, his wife Mia and their daughter Rose live a quiet life till some night Chris Redfield breaks into their home and shoots Mia while taking Ethan and Rose with him. Things go sideways and Ethan finds himself in the middle of a forest without his daughter or any other survivors and the only way forward leading to the village. Re Village takes its core gameplay from Re7 adds some Re4 mechanics like treasures and weapon upgrading and gives you and "open worldish"area to explore. The world is split into different thematic areas that you visit through the story while the village itself serves as a central hub you come back to after each one, Areas are pretty diversifed you visit a gigantic castle and industrial and a few other things on your 10-15h journey and meet their eccentric owners on your way to find your daughter.

_childDocuments_.review: I have had great time playing the story mode. This review is spoiler free (I think).Graphics: great. Very good looking. No major complaints except for occasional frame drops. FOV a bit too small and causes motion sickness especially on the small boat.Story: has some clear plot holes but in general no huge issues. Great to see they try to tie the story to the old RE lore.Characters: RE8 improves Ethan as main protagonist a lot compared to RE7. Human villagers are interesting but short lived. Main antagonists are interesting but inconsistent - a couple are more interesting and have much much longer screen time than the others.Combat: It feels great and it is satisfying to shoot and to upgrade the weapons at the merchant. Enemy variety is not amazing but good enough, and some rooms are interesting with environmental hazards and enemy placement. Boss fights are okay. There is one boss fight that just feels like interactive cutscene, but same can be said for RE7 final boss fight. Final boss definitely better than RE7 Eveline or Lucas.Puzzles: designed pretty well. Not brain-dead easy (maybe the piano one is) but most importantly not feel like a chore to go through in repeated playthroughs. I see some reviewers say that some puzzles should have had more backtracking, but personally I think that would just be a forced backtracking and a chore especially in repeated playthroughs.Horror: the start of the game and one part in the game are very unsettling. That one part is really nice and the length IMO is good too. Compared to RE7 I think the two games are "different". All places in RE7 are dirty and disgusting while RE8 has some beautiful and gorgeous locations so RE7 is more demanding. The tension is higher in RE7 but it is constant tension throughout the first half of the game so the scare feeling wears out fast (at least for me). RE7 becomes quite bland for me after Margurite, but RE8 is still quite interesting in latter sections (maybe the part when you don't play as Ethan is a bit chore). The pursuer in RE7 and RE2R are much more aggressive, but RE8 pursuer is literally invincible so it makes sense that they make the pursuer less terrifying.Length: 10 hours to 12 hours if you fully explore the game and read the documents. On metacritic some complains the game being too short (<8 hours) they are probably rushing through everything too hard.Replayability: extra weapons are expensive but only takes a few runs to get enough funds for them. Challenges and achievements are reasonable. Highest difficulty is interesting but I wish they change things a bit more like in RE7 mad house.Mercenary mode: RE8 shotgun is heavily nerfed compared to previous entries and I think this affects the mercenary mode.  I find myself just selling everything and only using the pistol because other weapons don't feel as effective. I have only SS'ed two stages as for now, but can't find the urge to play more. It kinda feels repetitive. I will update this review if my view on this mode changes after I 100% the game.To summarize I definitely recommend RE8.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Play Resident Evil 7 Biohazard before you play this game, as it's probably the most direct of a sequel that any of the games in the Resident Evil franchise has ever been. Village is indeed an incredible on its own, but appreciation of it will be greatly enhanced if you have at least played 7 and maybe 4.It's a little too cutscene heavy at the start, but once you get to the castle the game becomes a great RE title. I thought the areas after that part were good too, but perhaps a bit too linear for my tastes. The last big area of the game and the finale parts are really incredible though, if you are a big RE fan like me you will love this game.This PC port itself however isn't perfect though... microstutters can happen when you kill enemies, and the ray tracing implementation leaves a lot to be desired, but this is undoubtedly the best way to play if you don't have a next gen console.Overall, incredible game. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Resident Evil 8, where Capcom once again try to physically break a divergent path in their story back into line with the rest of the canon, even though everyone has been happy with the ending of certain plot points 3 games ago. Also witness as Capcom try their hardest to explain away the complete apathetic attitude and utter invulnerability of their new main protagonist in a so-called twist which sees the head of everyone who witnesses it turn 142 degrees in a direction though impossible in utter disbelief. Aside from this, behold a game which takes what RE7 does for it’s gameplay, improves on it, give you a bigger area to walk around in, more weapons to slap ♥♥♥♥ around with but still keeps pulling from its past games for every single one of its ideas. Old ideas, done very well.In this game you will be fighting the following:•	Furries•	Bigger furries•	Hammer furries•	Meth addicts•	The gargoyle gremlin from Gremlins 2: The New Batch•	Aggressive gardeners •	The Internet’s new waifus for the week•	Silent Hill’s cast off•	Raggidolls•	Your fish supper from last week•	Meth addicts hired by Facebook•	Wolfenstein’s  Supersoldaten•	A B52 bomber on legs•	Jim Carey’s Dr RobotnikThe majority of the game’s first run will be trying to figure out where the hell you are going, fighting off attacks from one or more of the above and cackling in laughter as you watch Ethan get battered, thrown and mutilated throughout. Not much has changed from RE7, it’s still first person, you still can only have 4 weapons in your hot-swap bar at any one time, you craft ammo and healing items out of stuff you find on the ground. Adding to this is a health dose of RE4 mechanics. Enemies drops stuff, ammo, craftables and money, the inventory system is a straight copy of RE4’s attaché case and there is a merchant dotted around the area that you buy things from, never explains how he’s able to move around as quick as he can (Which is even more impressive given this guy’s size) and allows upgrading of your weaponry.  It all comes together to make a game which is functionally good and works… mostly. Odd glitch here and there, but it works.The story is… typical Resident Evil. As said before, RE8 is trying to break what was done in RE7 into line with the rest of the canon. There was something said way back when in a Zero Punctuation video on a RE game, RE 5 I think. RE had a twisted mess of plot threads and non sensical stuff, then made a game only tangentially related to that mess. It sells gang busters, and the next game follows up on that, but then bogs down the narrative with all the mess from the previous games. That last game was RE4. Then e had RE5, which really should have finished off the whole ‘Umbrella’ arc, and then RE6 which was RE 6 and had Neo Umbrella and bioterrorist dinosaurs and we do not talk about it. Then, we get RE7. Fresh take on the series, tangentially related story wise to the previous games. And now we have RE8, which tries to shoehorn the previous game’s canon in like a demented baby trying to push its own bulbous head into a square hole two inches wise. You can see the strains, and the contrivances are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous. Capcom needs to make this the underline point. They have a world where bioterrorism exists. They have the opportunity to do something fresh with it. They almost made it this time but could not help themselves and had to go back to their crutches. As well as that, the whole deal with Ethan is hinted at throughout the game, but the big reveal actually had me stop playing for five minutes before saying ‘That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid’. One story beat does have me interested in what I am hoping is the DLC and not the next main game, but only time will tellAll in all, this is as close gameplay wise as you’re going to get to RE 4 in the modern age. It’s an enjoyable game to run and re-run, trying to blast past bosses and obstacles with New Game Plus and the god like arsenal you acquire, or start fresh on harder difficulties with self-imposed rules. Aside from one or two characters, however, there is not a lot of charm in the characters that would make this a 100% RE4-like for me. Ethan is still a brick with an affinity to reject fall damage. Chris has not changed since RE5,. The internet’s latest waifu, giant vampire lady, has presence for the short time he’s around but it is short. The other bosses are given even less screen time aside from Heisenberg (Who is given about the same amount of time as Vampire Lady) and the overall antagonist is just… there, really. The Duke, the vendor for the game, is the only one with any sort of charm that you can like and you actually want to know more about him.Overall recommended game if you want something to enjoy for gameplay but don’t care on story

_childDocuments_.review: I started Resident Evil 8: Village on it's release date in 2021. I finished it the nearly 2 years later. Just one day before the RE4 Remake comes out. It took me 2 years and multiple restarts with giant gaps between play sessions. It probably doesn't seem like I love Resident Evil 8...but I do love Resident Evil 8.I can't entirely explain how i got so distracted so many times but every time I sat down to play this game i had an absolute blast and yet I didn't come back for some time. Resident Evil 8 is not particularly scary...at all really. I mean there's that one level that everyone talks about. It's spooky once. I certainly jumped a few times but none of this game really scared me. RE8 is very campy horror. It's fun horror but maybe that's why it's so fun. I love the aesthetic of horror even when it doesn't scare me.Resident Evil 8 is also not particularly challenging. This is one of the easiest RE games i've ever played. Resource management isn't really a thing. Maybe on the higher difficulties and maybe i'll try those some day but i barely died in this game. Barely ever ran out of ammo. Not that you can't instantly craft more with your bottomless crafting inventory. It's not ideal but it's in no way a deal breaker for me. The shooting is fun and the enemies are fun to shoot. I'm not complaining. So what worked for me if the game wasn't scary and the gameplay didn't challenge me? Just being in this world. It's just fun. The 4 antagonists are a lot of fun with huge personalities and their own personal domains. Each sporting a different campy horror theme. 2 of them clearly have more love given than the others. So basically you have 2 well crafted villain domains and the other 2 are shorter set piece driven sections. That's where the Village itself comes in. It's ever expanding as a sort of central hub that you keep returning to. Sporting more treasure and threats every time you return to it. So besides the charm of the setting, themes and villains the other part that really worked for me was the story and Ethan Winter's himself. As a Father the story of village really effected me way more than it would have a few years ago. I know it's become a meme to make fun of Ethan but he's easily my favorite RE protagonist. Sure he's goofy and arguably kind of stupid sometimes but he's an every man. A dad who will do anything to save his daughter. I unironically love his cheesy trash talk that he spits out every time he takes out a big enemy. "Hell yeah brother! Tell em!" His insults are hilariously tone deaf and sometimes unnecessarily nasty and they never ceased to make me laugh or sometimes they just buffed my ego. Give me Ethan Winters over Chris Redfield any day. Village currently still has Overwhelmingly Positive reviews on steam and I remember people being super positive on it when it came out but recently the discourse seems to have soured on it significantly. Not so for me. It certainly doesn't fit with old school RE games in terms of tone or themes but when you reach the 8th mainline game in a series (more if you include all the remakes and spinoffs) you have to reinvent yourself. Without this new direction and the remakes I doubt the series would still be going this strong. I love the og RE titles and we can have both but for my money I'd prefer Resident Evil to keep being this Horror Bio Weapon Anthology series over the endless "evil corporation with zombies vs 80's action movie characters" thing. Keep being weird and keep being fun and that's all i can really ask for.

This game is right up your alley.Now what if I told you this game took what made RE: 4 the commercial success that is was and took what made RE: 7 great, and put them together? It gives off so many good RE: 4 vibes and this feels like the Resident Evil 4 Capcom wanted to make all those years ago, for any of you old enough to remember the early concepts of 4. _childDocuments_.review: In short: it's good though it has a identity problem and about 1/3 too expensiveUnfortunately after the indie horror approach taken for RE7 (which was excellent btw because it went for a more rural a la Texas chainsaw massacre slasher experience ditching the absurdly over the top anime shenanigans that plagued 6) the devs decided to bring back some schlock, albeit in more moderate quantities this time. This leaves RE8 with some experience disconnecting moments as on one side, it's dark, serious and downright horrible (in a good way) and on the other, it's cringey, hilariously bad and unamusing when it tries to be funny. The constant back and forth between those 2 gets tiresome as you can't be in grave danger doing your best to save your family while being chased by horrific creatures one moment, witness a bad soap opera drama banter between "lords" the next, back to "Oh this is serious and horrible!" after that while your character, out of the blue starts spewing "Fk you!" quirky one liners. The gameplay is basically a RE7 (improved) rehash though this time it has some questionable mechanics: even though now Ethan has "military training" he's still moving like he's stuck in water all the time and some enemies are clearly programmed for a quick dodge/roll response that probably ended up on the cutting floor. You can now push immediately after blocking but you can't do a quick attack (let alone a finisher) along with it but hey, you can now quick turn in a flash which makes the whole tanky movement even more jarring. I won't bore you with the story because frankly, at 60 euros, that's what you're playing this game for but expect it to be as the whole experience itself: bipolar, with a rushed exposition/explanation dump towards the end and self-contradictory at times if you look back. Good thing there's a whole Chris Redfield and his team segment toward the end to shake things up because by the time it comes, the whole thing was getting stale. Now a few words about the marketing for this game: if you're expecting Lady Dimitrescu to be some kind of Nemesis, you'll be very disappointed - she's in fact quite tame, boring and has a hilariously bad boss form ripped straight from some 90s B horror. Truth be told, she's kinda the least interesting thing that this game has to offer as there's one segment further down the line that will seriously creep you out especially if you're a parent (no kidding, it's probably the most horrific and well made encounter i've seen in a game for a long time) and while the game constantly ups itself it still can't help fall flat on his face on the final boss, which again, is such a bad B movie clicheic bullet sponge that it makes you think you're playing a completely different game. There's another personal issue i have with this game and it ain't a "cancel culture" one but in fact a "missed opportunity" one: If you decide to go full on rural Romania aesthetic (though it's more like 1900s) and lean heavily on it's linguistics (yes, the Duke's chef menu is in romanian as well as some other terms peppered along the story, like the "Cadou" Mcguffin, which means "gift"), at least do your homework and call werewolves "strigoi" (they stole the moon from the night skies in our folklore) not "lycans", because you'll rarely hear that term in eastern Europe and this ain't Underworld. Still, kudos to the team for not going Vlad the Impaler/Dracula bananas on Lady Di and her offsprings, which are just blink and you miss it mentioned as being vampires. So, all that said, why am I recommending it? Because i had fun with it, cringey story and voice acting aside (looking at you Heisenberg), because it's still a predominately well made game (borders on photo-realism with RT on) and because it had the Chris Redfield segment to save the day. Then again, 60 euros for a stretched out 17h game (hardest difficulty, a lot of wondering around and exploring) is about 20-25 euros too much for what this game has to offer so i'd wait for a more down to earth price. Lastly, Capcom, please get the hint and give us a fully fledged Chris Redfield standalone adventure - it's the 2nd time the guy elevates games with not that interesting protagonists (sure, Ethan is....fine at best but i couldn't care ♥♥♥♥ for the after credits Rose stinger) or downright detestable characters (looking at you Mia).

_childDocuments_.review: INTRO - 11-24-2022, Morning:So, I've been playing Resident Evil: Village (PC/Steam), taking my time & soaking in this game in. I'm some 18.5 hours in so far, on the 8th main entry here in this RE series (Resident Evil). Got some thoughts on it, of course...so, let's get this show on the road.WINTERS...WINTERS IS COMING.In this game, you play as Ethan Winters, the protagonist from the awesome RE7. So, yes - you should play RE7 first if you haven't, as that game's awesome & since this is a direct sequel to that. Without giving a ton away here, this is after those events from RE7 and he has now found his way to a Village, to go find his daughter & hopefully save her. In doing so, he's going this village that has a ton of things going on, without going too far into this & into Spoiler Turf.GAMEPLAY, COMBAT, ENEMIES & MORE.This feels basically like RE7, combat-wise & gameplay-wise. In the OG version of RE: Village here, you're in first-person perspective here, seeing through Ethan's eyes. Like RE7, the combat's awesome in 1st person and flat-out just feels great; it's extremely satisfying. A lot of times here, you'll be exploring areas, defeating enemies, solving puzzles, combing items to make another item, and other things of the typical survival-horror sort - and it's awesome. So far, this game is nothing short of that.Enemies here are not always the typical RE enemies here either, which is great...and they are often not of the zombies sort here. You don't always deal w/ zombies & those type of RE enemies, since...this Village has a lot more on-going than that. Just know, since the game is split up, more or less, into 4 major different areas in this Village, each area often has its own enemy types - such as Vampires, Lycans/Werewolves, Cyborg type of Frankenstein-like creations for monsters, and more. Simply put: I love what this game is doing w/ the enemy type variety here.There's even a section that feels mostly like a small puzzle section almost entirely, as if it was right out of an adventure game like Myst - but oh, is it so a lot more creepy and indeed does have a bit of combat here & there, too.Also, you'll be running into a Merchant named The Duke a lot, from whom you can buy, sell, and upgrade your assortment of items (guns, equipment, etc.) - in which this mechanic of running into him so reminds of the merchant from my favorite RE game (Resident Evil 4). PERFORMANCE.My PC's have no problem w/ this one pretty much. On my desktop loaded with i7 10700KF, 16 GB RAM, 8gb RTX 3070, 1 TB SSD - yeah, easy 1080p60fps here & eating around 7-8 GB VRAM on the regular, with Ray-Tracing On paired with either DLSS or FSR - I'd have to check again but I normally use DLSS, if both options are there. My Gigabyte gaming laptop loaded with R5 5600H, 16 GB RAM, 6gb RTX 3060 (laptop-GPU), 1 TB SSD & W11 runs this no problem at Medium settings w/ RT and either DLSS or FSR On. Flat-out, this game both looks & runs great. Can't say anything bad here about any of that stuff, as the game runs & looks great here.OUTRO...FOR NOW.And, that should conclude what I've got to say for now, on RE: Village. So far, it's been great and has been awesome. This is so far a fantastic sequel to the awesome RE7 - and all of this RE: Village talk & partial-reviewing makes me want to go finish the game up, since I'm probably getting there & I am probably close to the end anyways. More to come, when I finish this - but so far, it's awesome & looks like a certain "Must Play" and a very easy recommendation, provided that sticks the landing & ending.ADDENDUM - 11-24-2022, 4:55pm EST:After 21 hours, I have completed RE: Village. And in the grand scheme of things, it was awesome overall & is definitely "Must Play" and an easy recommendation here. While the main story does wrap up here & the conclusion to this game's story is satisfying, there's obviously going to be more to come b/c there's always something going on w/ the Resident Evil/Biohazard Bio-Weapons. Certainly, I do look forward to at some point buying the Winters Expansion & to the inevitable Resident Evil 9, whenever that's going to be coming.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off with the bad: Resident Evil 8 has some issues with conveyance. Without spoiling anything story-wise, I can tell you that there are at least three different times where the game straight up drops the ball when it comes to letting you know WHAT you need to do. Don't get this confused with a lack of clear objectives (otherwise known as a "WHERE THE ♥♥♥♥ DO I GO?" type of game.) I mean the game puts you in situations where it's not clear what you need to do to progress and you die. Over and over. Like failing a QTE in older games. I don't like that.Otherwise, game is solid as hell. It mixes some tense situations with solid weaponry and an absolutely bonkers story, like most RE games before it. BUT. A lot of enemies do that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing where you shoot them and they don't react. I get that the enemies are supposed to feel powerful and you're supposed to feel underpowered but shooting a lycan in the eyeball should elcit SOME KIND of reaction, even if it's just a head shake or an eye rub. Also, the game actually managed to scare me and that's something no game has done since the first Amnesia. You'll know the scene I'm talking about when you find it. I'm not gonna spoil it here. Oh, and you don't have to worry about Dommy Mommy. She's a cool character and is appropriately threatening, especially after you've ♥♥♥♥♥♥ around in her castle for a while. I honestly wish she was a bigger part of the game, though. Also, if there's ever a Marvel vs Capcom 4, you better believe Alcina Dimetrescu is gonna ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ be in there. _childDocuments_.review: For someone who loves horror and enjoys the Resident Evil games, I have to say that Village is an amazing entry to the franchise. One of these reviews pointed out that each section of the game is very unique and feels awkwardly connected. And after playing Village I totally agree. _childDocuments_.review: A fine enough experience but far too short for what you pay and horrible PC consideration control wise and optimisation. A lot of people prefer KB+M but the menu and navigation was ridiculous without a controller. Frustrating to do something like scroll down in a shop window yet be unable to just use the mouse wheel, you HAVE to use the mapped menu scroll buttons... The inventory itself could have just had tabs to click thru as well for another example.Content wise it felt like a step back from 7 which was what I considered more of a return to the roots (with still a bit too much action) but now it's doubled down on the action at the expense of survival horror elements.Ethan is also illiterate I believe. You can read thru a whole journal about someones motives and he will still be shocked and stupid when the boss comes around for exposition time. You just read a very plain explanation, why are you shouting about stuff you have the answer too?Hand-holding is also extreme, you get about 2 seconds to think about something before a prompt will pop up and spell things out for you like a child, in case those mean puzzles were getting in the way of the shooties I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: So to start off I want to say this game is amazing considering how well biohazard did it was no suprise that this game would be good as well. I recommend playing Biohazard if you haven't, so you can fully grasp the story but if not they give you a recap so you know where you are. I really have no problems with the game but my only concern is for people with lower end graphics cards. In order to enjoy the game at full max settings it is required you own a Rtx 3090 because even going a little over halfway up on the graphics settings will overuse memory while most cards have a limit of 8 gb video memory. Also mentioning that it says in the notes Rtx 2070s or above should be able to run ray tracing but I have a Rtx 2070 super and the option was locked for me in graphics settings?  My only suggestion is to wait for them to drop more optimization patches to make it run even smoother for lower cards. But even for playing on semi reduced graphics the game looks gorgeous and runs fairly well. although be careful fighting Dimitrescu's daughters as they have a bug attack where bugs surround them it will guarantee drop your frames to 10 or below. Once again highly recommend to anyone looking to play a thrilling game with a great story and graphics this is it. Edit-Needed to be on latest windows update in order to use ray tracing for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Resident Evil 4 this game should absolutely tickle you. Apart from the change in perspective and general modernization, this is an extraordinarily similar game.As someone that only relatively recently played (and 100%'d) RE 4, I can say with certainty that I could tangibly feel Capcom yanking my wiener as I played RE 8, the wiener belonging to someone that likes RE 4.So, how's the game on its own merits? S'good. Graphically it's certainly the best in series. My system (which at the time of my first play had a 4690k and now has a Ryzen 5 3600) with its GTX 1070 ran it cranked at 1080p on Linux, where it runs flawlessly with no fuss. Good show all around.The actual basic core mechanics are all as polished as they've ever been. Blocking is still a weird addition, though there is a canon reason why Ethan is so ridiculous in both 7 and 8. It took quite some time to acclimatize myself to the mechanic, and this is having played 7 all the way through twice just before. Once you're aware of it and using it, it's quite nice to have and does give the player the means to stretch their resources a bit further which is good in general.Returning for one of the aforementioned wiener yanks is a merchant. Not  merchant, but a merchant. The Duke, a dapper and rotund gentle(man?) you meet fairly early in your adventure. Beyond buying and selling things, there is now a sort of hunting minigame you engage with fairly organically to collect ingredients for the Duke. Collect enough of the correct sort and you get some meaningful upgrades to your abilities. Capcom has in short basically one-upped the merchant from RE 4 in every way apart, perhaps, from the voice acting. I have my doubts any lines from Duke will be recited ad nauseum.Otherwise, it more or less follows what I'd call the RE 4 formula, collect key items to get to new areas where you collect more key items until eventually the game ends. It's a good formula.Now for spoilers. If the game sounds good based on what you've read so far though, I think it's safe to say it's a certain hit for you and you should pick it up. Despite the fact that I haven't purchased a game for $60 since 2016, I can say now in hindsight and in confidence that I'd gladly pay that for this game.One of the most common complaints, apart from this being more "action-oriented" than many in the fanbase would like, is that the game's general pacing, mystique, intrigue, and perhaps even writing drop off after Castle Dimitrescu. I suppose I agree, but when you're going from what is a near-perfect experience that in a vacuum would likely be a 10, anything will seem lackluster. I don't think the writing is perfect, and I don't agree with every decision, but I do believe that the game as a whole is still well above even the average quality of the series as a whole at this point, personal preference for style aside.The section that follows  Castle Dimitrescu is that of Donna Beneviento, the P.T. inspired true horror section. True horror referring to the fact that Capcom was obviously trying their damndest to spook you, not in that the other games or other styles of games aren't horrifying. It's the "you can't fight back" style of horror, largely popularized by  and perpetuated by countless others. It begins with you walking through a reasonably and comparatively pleasant segment, until it takes away your arms (or rather your entire inventory) and sends you off to do some puzzle solving. The long and short of it is that the section is a bit of a slog for those playing the game over and over like myself, but is more of an exercise in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ your pants for the average single-play player.Between those two sections is village exploration with the normal gameplay loop. You return multiple times with new key items for both progression mandatory and optional searching about. These sections are largely similar otherwise and will not be mentioned in their own paragraph again.Now you're off to fight Salvatore Moreau. After some scooting around a swampy area that contains a heavily transformed Moreau, you drain a reservoir to fight him head-on. The area is largely fairly simple, but contains a few fun set pieces and the boss fight can be challenging the first time.Next, and second to last for Ethan, you fight Karl Heisenberg. He's been fairly present throughout the game, scooting to the sideline until he thinks he might have use for Ethan. This is a rather lengthy section of the game, going through Heisenberg's factory. Eventually you come to meet Chris Redfield for the second time, the first being near the beginning of the game. Why spoil the fun explaining why here? At any rate, your fight with Heisenberg is largely on a vehicle that Chris lends you. This ends in Ethan's not-death to Miranda via the violent removal of his heart.Let's play as Chris! Lovingly referred to by Karl as "that boulder-punching ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥," you can be certain he's a series staple. Why not Jill, Capcom? Chris has his own weapons in a totally separate inventory. He carries a full auto rifle, a fairly strong pistol, and a knife that is  better than Ethan's. Knife-only achievement good. He also has a laser pointer for designating places to bomb, but you can't use that so liberally.You stomp through the now quickly burning village, smiting enemies as you pass, and eventually laser designate a giant mold structure to death. This leads you underground where you fight a big lycan (there are werewolves of a sort in this game, which I failed to mention among other things because this game is so absolutely packed) and plant a bomb on the megamycete, a mold (heart?) just causing an entire game series worth of problems. Last for Chris' section, you find that Mia is still alive, just chilling underground in Miranda's lab just past the megamycete.Mia explains to Chris that Ethan is a special boy, and we return to playing Ethan post his "death." Duke carts you off to where you can finally kill Miranda and reclaim your daughter Rosemary. This was the primary motivation for Ethan. His daughter born of his mold infection and presumably sex with Mia evidently can't die, so Miranda wanted Rose for reasons I don't have the space to expand upon. This led to Rose being chopped up and put into four flasks which you collect in the previous sections. After killing Miranda, she somehow left Ethan dying as well. As Chris tries to get Ethan out Ethan steals the detonator for the explosive, goes back in, and dies in the explosion. Mia and Rose escape, and a cutscene plays where it's clear that Rose is being utilized for her Wesker-esque abilities by some organization or another some 20 years later.The point of that whole section where I basically just explain the plot is to show how convoluted the whole thing is, and how ridiculous it is. Just how much of it is actually more understandable if you have even a general knowledge of the plot of Resident Evil up to this point. Miranda and  were working together before the events of the first game. He's the man that owned the mansion from the first game, was a founder of Umbrella, named and given a logo from something that was here, in this game's titular village, before both Miranda and Oswell even got there.This is exactly what I've personally come to expect from Resident Evil, and I love it. It's got all the hallmarks of the first game, with the polish of millions of dollars. It's as ridiculous a Japanese view of American society and personality as ever, as well as being as ridiculously Japanese in its story telling, and balancing the two in a way only Capcom knows how. It's difficult to express how much I actually like this game. This is coming from someone who didn't even start playing the games until maybe 2018.Buy this game. Even if you've never played another Resident Evil game in your life.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers basically asked the question:What if, Dark Souls 3 + Half Life 2 + Rise of Tomb Raiser, where put together, but they were Resident Evil though!And what came out, was an awesome game.I'm not joking that it was heavily inspired by all three of these, cos the map visuals look foreboding and beautiful, much like Dark Souls 3, together with creepy villages and grand castles, all the way up to how certain bosses look, with massive weapons that telegraph their attacks, how you have block mechanics.It has the atmosphere of Half Life 2, wandering alone in the wilderness and abandoned structures and just marveling at the quiet and tranquility of nature, And Tomb Raiders crazy jumping around, running away from things chasing you in the snow and creepy places.The story is also absolutely amazing, all the characters feel real and three dimension, you get easily immersed in the story and feel like you're really there and its happening to you directly. The ending segment is one of the more satisfying I've seen in a long time.I genuinely did not expect the game to have so many different elements to it and all of them significantly enrich the experience.10/10 would buy again

_childDocuments_.review: To start with, this game is the best game I've played in years.As a follow up on RE7, I really enjoyed the story and it's environment .Before I started playing RE8, I expected a bit too much of the game so my review will have a more negative point of view.As I played almost every RE game on different platforms, I do have a lot of "skills" in these games, at least, that was what I thought.Since the very beginning of the game, I started complaining about how overpowered these lycans were, but maybe I just had a bad day, because later in the game, it felt like they were too weak.At the same time, the game was disappointing in a way that it wasn't that scary as RE7, what I actually liked since all the previous games were so non-horror as well.The environment gave me that scary feeling in some parts, where they (CapCom) did nothing special.Overall it did surprise me how they gave Resident Evil a new look and way how to play, examples enough such as the duke, animals to kill for some extra health or stamina and the various amount of boss fights.Another thing where I think CapCom could've done way better, was the amount of puzzles combined with some "chase scenario's". I like it when don't understand the puzzle and someone is chasing me, get's me hyped lol.The story was really, really entertaining or maybe it's just me since I did like the story from RE7 that much as well.Spoiler!!!!Ethan x Mia x Rose, was a story that was way better in my opinion than any other Resident Evil story, because after 6 main story games, they milked their franchise out.What I would've liked was a part where we could actually see Ethan's face before he died to the c4 explosion, if he even is dead ;).Instead of giving criticism to CapCom, I could talk about positive arguments as well, since Village was actually the game where we did receive a lot of ammo ( I played the game at the standard difficulty ), we had huge parts to discover, a way to buy ammo and/or guns throughout the game and we had some mind ♥♥♥♥♥ in the game, such as the thought that Mia died, Ethan died but he stood up once again, a teasing story at the end of the game for the new upcoming Resident Evil.Overall, I give this game an 8/10, 10/10 for it's story, 5/10 for it's "horror" and a well deserved 8/10 for the combat in game.I hope that CapCom uses all the reviews on this game, for making an even better new game in the future.I hope this review is useful for you if you're about to buy this game or thinking about.Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I think this was a pretty good game, with a few issues keeping it from being great. Overall it was incredibly atmospheric and interesting story wise, and I think it's a better game than RE7 for sure. The first half of the game really shines, with my favorites being Castle Dimitrescu and the House of Beneviento. I feel like this section of the game was more horror based, whereas the latter half felt more action orientated. In the end it strikes a better balance than RE7 did, which is why it's a better game in my opinion.My biggest gripes are probably some of the scripted scenarios that can be immersion breaking. In the intro there was a scripted cut scene which was meant to occur outside, however I was inside at the time causing my camera to warp through some of the textures which was pretty jarring. There was a few more examples of these, however it was only mildly irritating. My second biggest issue is some of the voice acting and sounds, which can be flat out bad at some points. The most notable ones for myself was some glass shattering in the intro, which sounded like a desktop recording, and a few lines in the closing cinematic, which had some very audible distortion over it.Some other issues were definitely the mouse sensitivity, which I had to crank up on my mouses DPI for it to be comfortable, and the locked FOV. I had to download a mod in order to unlock and customize it, however it's pretty ridiculous a game doesn't include this in 2021; the low FOV actually made me slightly motion sick in the demo. I also had a few frame drops in some of the boss fights, however it was smooth otherwise.Negatives aside, this game does a great job at drawing you in and keeping you interested. All of the characters were very  unique, and I felt like all of the lords had something to add without feeling out of place. The Duke was a great addition, and I really enjoyed the shop aspect and upgrading which weapons you preferred. It was also nice to see a wider variety of monsters and enemies, which was a great change up from only the molded in RE7.Overall, I think Resident Evil Village is a pretty good game. It has a few glaring issues, however the story and atmosphere that it creates was well worth the purchase. I wouldn't call it incredibly scary, and would advise you to look elsewhere if you are only interested in the horror elements. However, if you are looking for a blend of both horror and action I think this game really scratches that itch and recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, but  too expensive for what it is. It's the first Resident Evil that I've played in a long time, and having heard to much about it, I wanted to try it out.To start with the good, the  graphics, and location design are really good. As someone who's travelled in rural Romania I can tell you that they got a lot of the artstyle, and feel of the village / castle exactly right. I was impressed. I found myself admiring the view on more than one occasion. And that's pretty much the only thing I really can't find fault with.The weapons you use are lame, and frustrating. They shoot rather slowly, and the second you look down the sights, and try to adjust your aim, weird stuff happens (he tries to look away from the sights, then immediately zooms back in). Many of them are also unsatisfying to shoot because they barely do anything. All the pistols, shotguns, etc sound the same, shoot slowly, reload slowly, don't do enough damage ...  All the best guns can only be unlocked on newgame+, which is kind of BS.The story is also really weak. Just how isolated was this village that someone could disappear hundreds of people, start their own cult / religion, and have it all go completely unnoticed at the height of Romania's commie regime? Difficult to explain, really.But let's say you really don't care about any of that. Fair enough. The characters are still weak, and difficult to give a sh!t about. All the most interesting ones are only on screen for short periods of time, and we only get to find out a little bit about their background from written logs that are scattered about. I mean, come on, the scenes with Lady Dimitrescu that you get in the trailer is literally the most interesting piece of the "Story" that you get to experience. It's BS, and could have been so much more interesting.Ethan keeps getting hurt in preposterous ways, but he doesn't seem to "notice" that he's special until a very annoying dream sequence tells him he is. Last but not least, I ran through the story on normal difficulty in a little over 8 hours. The reason it says 14 is because i played Mercenaries game mode for a bit, and forgot the game on. Literally nothing worth going back and playing newgame+ for. Boring, and forgettable. Couldn't possibly justify spending more than maybe $40 for it, and even then I'd tell you to buy it on sale if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare AAA game that is not a pretty disappointment.  It's a tour de force!Some people are saying this is an unfortunate mixture of RE4 and 7; I've played both and I think it's true on the surface but this game has its own thing going.  It's definitely worth the purchase; it is a lot of fun and it's almost like several smaller games tied together by a hub.  The locations have very different play styles and atmosphere.  I suppose you could beat it in 10 hours but I've enjoyed just walking around and taking in the sights.The visual presentation is also amazing, though, there is a bug where the FPS dips (which is usually a buttery smooth 60 + FPS with everything turned up to 11 on an RTX3080; I have a 60 Hz monitor so I am not sure what the internal FPS is) into the teens and does not recover until the game is reloaded.  It's not scene-dependent and it does not seem to be the GPU overheating since the FPS recovers immediately upon returning to the main menu and then the same scene plays just out fine.  Turning some of the settings down (specifically, going from ultrawide 1440p to 21:9 1440p and leaving all quality settings intact) does make this more bearable since the fps goes down to a technically playable 30 FPS but it needs to be fixed because it is SUPER annoying!  The autosaves are sparse and it basically comes down either suffering till the next save point or losing progress.  I hope this is patched soon; no complaints otherwise.  I hear this is a memory leak specific to NVIDIA RTX cards.

_childDocuments_.review: *Possible spoilers but might save you 60 bucks*Look, look look look. If you're here for Resident Evil, knowing full well what this series is, what 7 was, how the games usually play out, you're probably going to be satisfied. I'm only 3.2 hours in & leaving a review now to let you know one very important thing. If you're here SOLELY because of Lady D & her daughters, well, I think 95% of you who are interested for that reason alone need to wait for a sale. A deep one. 3.2 hours. That's from an experienced RE player yes that likes to speed run. But yeah, I think this was marketing feeding people with what they were already into so if you were hyped for that reason alone, you might want to wait. If you're cool with that & it simply makes you happy to know there's more to go? Go ahead & dive in.After finishing the game once: I'm in love. Will every RE fan also love it? No, absolutely not. This absolutely feels like Capcom trying to take some of RE4 & blend it with some RE7. I honestly think it works. If you liked the gameplay of 7, no reason to suspect you would be disappointed here. Yet to try out The Mercenaries but happy it's back. Plenty of replayability both in difficulty levels & things to unlock for further runs such as yes, infinite ammo weapons. Same purchase model as the 2 & 3 remake. Complete in game challenges, use that currency.I do disagree with some reviews that this game doesn't stick the landing. Though that one of course is more personal taste. Hard for me to talk about the story at the moment in a non spoiler way. 7 I felt meh on that third act. Not so much here. So final word is this: If you enjoy most of this series, 7 included, I think you'll be happy with your purchase if you did so now. If you're on the fence, probably wait for a sale & you'll be happier. I'm a fanboy of this series, so I'm relatively easy to please. Trying to think of people that are harder to please, especially other fans, I feel you have to enjoy the combat of 7, not be turned off by first person, not be turned off by monster choices, & be okay with marketing possibly leading you to believe that certain characters the internet loves, are so not the central plot of the game. If that is one of your big selling points, absolutely wait on a discount. Even if you go through RE at a slower pace, sure, you could spend plenty more time than I did with Lady D & her daughters. But in the grand scheme of things, while happy, even I wanted more in that department. So once more, if your gut says yes, go for it. If you're on the fence, wait. I recommended it regardless, only trying to help those that could regret it at the current price point & possibly hate the game at this price point vs enjoying it later for a different price.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been 10 years or so since I played a video game last and all I can say is.. Breathtaking. The cut scenes were better than a modern day Hollywood blockbuster. I can even go as far as to say that some made me feel things I hadn't felt in years, especially at the end. _childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free in the first halfThis entry to the series feels like the production value was put into it to make it a triple A title which is the only reason I didn't return it.  It's a fine generic fps where you play an action hero in a horrorish setting. Transitioning from re7 to 8 has the character grow and feels extremely analogous to resident evil 4 where the story and horror took a back seat to the action gameplay. This entry also feels a little like resident evil 6 where all the different gameplay styles that encompass the series is in it but in the end it feels unfocused and you end the segment that encompasses the style the game seemed marketed towards very early on when the game just when it starts to open its stride.  That style being the mysterious semi open world setting where you explore and eek out clues and mysteries.  SpoilersThe character dissonance you feel with Ethan is jarring as he's now admittedly very competent but his dialog and reaction to things feel extremely under emphasized?  For example, body horror of re7 is played up in this one and is mostly a gimmick, Ethan is well aware you can just glue appendages back on when the need arises.  They eventually  fill you in on the far back end but the reveal losses is impact because you cant relate to Ethan who reacts very densely.  The first two hours of my nine hour playthrough on normal felt like a slog, more walking simulator than game until it really opens up with the first set piece.  Other people have written about this at length,  at this point I was getting ready to return the game when it finally started to feel like resident evil and by the end of my 6 hours i wasn't incredibly impressed but believed if the game continued in a similar manner I would be happy enough.  Then the first set piece ends and with it the semi classical resident evil style.  The second set piece I actually did enjoy despite it being an extremely linear version of the escape room style mechanics introduced in re7. At this point the story was more campy than re4 and while I was trying to be invested there's not enough supplemental information here to really hook you or feel for this villain whom later you find could have been very interesting.  After this point is the mid and turning point.  Ethan becomes more heroic and your arsenal is padded out and you go on the offensive capitalizing on your momentum.  Its action shooter from here on out with a cool looking section in a factory but ultimately kinda forgettable as there's no more puzzles, just hallways and newer and bigger enemies.  Harder difficulty might make this more engaging but that's not really the core experience I'm looking for in these games.  Then the game ends and the loose ends are given to the player via refreshing Exposition! You just get told everything as if there were major clues to be picking up.  If you're a fan of the series you probably already knew how this would link up to other games. You just get the info so late into the game it's hard to care when I think it was supposed to be this cool reveal.  Alternatively maybe they just tossed it in there last second just as filler. So late into the game If it wasn't in there at all then random speculation might have been better.  All in all the game does play well, the settings are beautiful. The action plays well,  if you enjoyed re4 I don't see why you wouldn't like this game but after re7 i was really hoping to get that orginal resident evil feel again so this game gets my negative review. AlsoThe narrative and characters seem to act in a way that insults the viewers intelligence. End rant

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is a wonderful game.Split into four main sections, each covers different themes, so there is something for everyone to enjoy while playing. The villains are all very well written, and their battles all feel very different from each other, creating unique challenges for each fight. The story is also well intertwined with previous installations and you can tell a lot of time has gone into everything, from the beautiful environments to the lore scattered throughout the various areas. Coming straight from finishing RE: Biohazard, it takes a little while to get used to the new systems such as the inventory, but once you do it is a major improvement on the old one. The currency system is also a great way to allow the player to get new upgrades without it feeling like the game just hands it to them when they need it.The game is also not very demanding, I use a laptop and was able to run the game perfectly with no crashes or frame drops and the game still looked absolutely stunning. There is also content in game that you can unlock after completion, allowing you to replay the game with a completely different experience. As I bought the game with all DLCs, I will mention that the bonus content is somewhat lacking, such as the odd choice of safe room music you can enable, but I would not recommend using them anyway, as it breaks some of the game's atmosphere with out of place objects such as tape recorders rather than typewriters for save points, this is of course personal preference.The positives of this game definitely outweigh the negatives though, and I cannot recommend it enough.10/10, would definitely play this again.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Very poor graphics/textures/models during several points of the game. RE7 had the same problem, but 4 years later I kinda expect a little better. I also had a major graphics issue popup that ruined most of the visuals during the final fight. 2. Repetitious as hell and bloated. RE games are known for having fairly tight loops, but this one gets old fast due to the world being divided up into several small self contained "stages" that you can't revisit and thus have no connection to each other. Lots of segments based around dodging a big dumb unkillable monster till you scoop up all the items needed to open up the boss. Happens back to back to back way too often. Puzzles aren't as fun or dynamic as 7's. Boss fights are flashy, but dumb easy save for one that's kinda cool, but still easy. Most of the areas are needlessly large and wear out their welcome quickly.3. The story, moment to moment action and overall plot are just too stupid to tolerate. No spoilers, but the overall script for the game is non-stop stupidity from start to finish. Not fun, cheesy B movie stupid either. Just...stupid. The last 2 hours of the game are brain-melting dumb. I should've just watched a live stream or a Let's Play. $60 down the drain.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure weather I was supposed to be scared or horny during the first act, so I just decided to be both. I believe this was the intended experience. The game could have benefited from a slower pace. The first half of the story felt a bit too fast. I was left disappointed by how quickly the most advertised and hyped character was just swept aside. This ended up making some characters come off as shallow and uninteresting. The second half of the game, however, is paced extremely well. I just wish I could have spent 10-20% more time in the vampire game I was expecting. Overall, on par with RE7 and good sequel.After Act One, I stopped being horny and was just straight up scared. I beat Alien Isolation on max difficulty and assumed this would be a cakewalk in comparison. I was partially right, I wasn't TERRIFIED but I cowered in hidy-holes and procrastinated walking down a hallway for an hour because I no longer had my emotional support shotgun. RE7 WAS terrifying, this was a step down in that regard. The atmosphere and visual storytelling is top tier. This is one of the two W's eight takes over 7. I felt like a lone rat scurrying form place to place, always at risk of getting pinned by one of the cat's many claws. The world is beautiful and unsettling. I prefer it over the bayou.Combat, what this game lacks in fear, it more than make up in panic. Overwhelming forces constantly kept me on edge. I never knew where an enemy was going to pop up and on higher difficulties a single hit will put you on the brink of death. The bonus content, additional orders, is nonstop action combat, and unlocking the special knife is a challenging but worthwhile quest. Additional orders alone is worth getting the gold edition for. The Rose DLC isn't bad either, not great but not bad.Overall, get this game on sale so the gold edition is worth it. Otherwise, just replay RE7 and RE4. It's not the best game in the series but it's far from the worst.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game I can safely say that this resident evil is the best in the series aside from 4 and 7. I've literally spent countless minutes just staring at the impeccable attention to detail this game has to offer, it doesn't have that triple A slapped together feeling. The environments actually feel handmade like someone's soul actually went into it.The horror is REALLY good, much better than 7's sort of cheesy over the top campy horror. The regenerator moment for this game is in the second house and believe me, that thing is absolutely horrifying, coupled with the suspense when running for the elevator. And lastly, the story is absolutely a home run for series veterans. If you're really into the lore, this game is definitely for you, there's a lot to read about, and a lot of puzzles to piece together with some loose ends left here and there. I found myself surprised throughout the entire game, always asking questions and the game subverted my expectations entirely. The ending is REALLY good.Whatever DLC may come will certainly be worth looking forward to.
