_childDocuments_.review: While Steam says I played the game for 19 hours, it actually took me 8 hours and 30 minutes to beat the game, and I did almost everything: I found almost all treasures (except for one which I couldn't get because I progressed to far into the story to trigger a certain thing), I found almost all guns (except for the ones you can buy) and I have been pretty much over the entire map. So, the game is only around 2 and a half hours longer than last year's very disappointingly short game Resident Evil 3 Remake. But does that make it bad? And is that why I am bit disappointed? No. I always enjoy my time with these games. No matter how weak an entry might be. I never finish a Resident Evil game with the thought that I wasted my time. This game is no different. And truth be told, it is better than 7 and 3R but not by much. The gameplay loop is exactly like it was in 7. Resident Evil 8 is a first person shooter with inventory management and "limited" (more on that later) ressources, it has puzzles (more on that later too) and levels that a structured like Metrovania levels, you know where you (although recent games have unfortunately had less of that compared to the first couple games) backtrack through the levels in order to progress to new areas from the main hub level. The shooting is solid enough, it can be a little stiff as to be expected with a survival horror game. If the combat was too good then we would have a Dead Space (read my reviews for those games to see what I mean) situation where you don't feel any tension in the fights due to being too much of a beast yourself to be afraid of the actual beasts. You get a arsenal of weapons as you play through the game that you either buy from the merchant or find. You can upgrade these weapons by either paying said merchant or add attachments on them that you either buy from the merchant or find. What do you use to buy stuff? Well just standard cash that you get from either finding it or selling treasures/items to the merchant. Well, so far so good right? While I do enjoy this loop I do have some complaints. Resident Evil 8 throws a lot of enemies at you, but at the same time it also gives you a LOT of ressources so they aren't really ever THAT limited. I don't really like that. It makes it feel more like a regular shooter than a survival horror game. The stiff aiming and all that wasn't really a issue tho, no matter the amount of enemies the game threw at me so at least that's a plus. Overall, I enjoyed the combat in 7 and I also enjoy it here despite the issues I got with it since it is exactly the same.The puzzles were a big weakness of 7. Resident Evil generally moved away from them after 4 but 7 kinda brought them back-ish. They weren't particularly challenging and overall they were very same-y. However, while the puzzles in this game aren't hard, they are a nice break from the action and they do have some variety to them.The same can be said about the enemy variety and design. This was another thing that sucked hard in 7. Besides the Baker family, the enemies were really bad, just different shapes of black goo basically. While this game doesn't have the same insane variety of the games of old, it is at least a step up from the previous game and it never really got too repetitive.The bosses, however, have not improved. There are more of them than in 7 but they straight up suck for the most part. I attribute this mainly to the arenas where you fight them. Since movement is very limitedand since they more often then not are either too big or too small. The fights themselves are also often tedious ranging from bad to alright. I didn't really care for their designs either and it didn't help that they have so little screen time that they hardly made an impact on that front. You can read notes about them or from them that you find through out the levels but that hardly adds much besides some back story and maybe also a little bit of their motivation. Even the big vampire lady (who was totally overhyped btw, since she barely appear in the game). I did appreciate that we got a scene where they were all together, like in Metal Gear Solid 3, I really like when games do that. It makes me feel like I am taking down a actual team instead of just a string of villains that appear one by one. As far as the levels are concerned. I feel like the first 2 levels were solid that being the village which is also the hub level and the castle, the middle portion was alright and the ending levels were tedious. That is EXACTLY what I felt about 7 as well. Although, it doesn't become THAT bad but you can feel a dip in quality after you leave the castle level (which is ironically also the one they showed the most in the promotional material). The house level afterwards is also pretty solid but kinda short.The story isn't good. But that is hardly a surprise. It's Resident Evil after all, it's been the case since the first game. These games tell their stories through their levels and their atmosphere. The actual written story that plays are usually pretty campy and the characters are paper thin. I like that because it usually contrasts the actual game quite well. That is why it feels especially odd that this game takes itself so seriously. This is bad, yes, but not in the way as the previous entries. The graphics and facial animations look pretty good in 2021, the voice acting isn't terrible but it isn't exactly good either especially from Ethan Winters, the protagonist, who is not convincing more than half of the time, the music and sound is solid and the dialogue is generic, but hardly bad. There was a charm to the previous games that I feel like the newer games really lack. Oh, and every frickin villager speaks perfect english even though they appear to be in East Europe. Contrast that with 4 where they either spoke spanish (since it took place in Spain) or english with accents. That kinda broke the immersion for me a couple times too. So to conclude. I had a fun enough time with the game. Despite all the issues I got with it. If you enjoyed 7 then you are likely gonna like this one too. The gameplay loop is solid enough, it looks and sounds great, the puzzles are a nice addition and getting loot and better gear while traversing the Metrovania styled levels is always fun. I think i will give it a low...Score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5 hours in this game. Before I go into this review (of a game I have not yet completed), I would like to present a recap of my introduction to the series. I've been a big fan of the Resident Evil lore since I was 6 years old (1997) and my big brother showed me how to blast the head of a zombie with a shotgun in the spencer mansion. Didn't understand much at the time, but I knew that the whole thing was kinda creepy with the music, and that the character (Jill) was alone in this big ass house with all of those doors and all the wierd moaning guys walking around with their arms stretched out and reaching towards her. I never got to see my brother complete the game because we didn't have a memory card for our PS1 at the time. Fast forward to 1999, and my brother is playing RE2. And yes, I got to see him complete that masterpiece. I understood most of it and I remember how hard he worked on all those bosses. It was just good times. Again, fast forward to 2006, I've got a PS2, and I've heard many a cool things about RE4. So I bought it for my 15th birthday and started playing that. And I seriously loved it. It took me 1 more year to realize. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I never saw completion of that 1st one! So I got myself a crappy laptop, BUT! I had the opportunities to play RE1, 2 and 3 on that ♥♥♥♥! I got to play the RE1 remake on the gamecube as well! and I got to play RE Zero and Code Veronica. Loved em all! And then... the 5th came... I liked how capcom decided to stick to the 3rd person view. And all in all, the 5th game was a good couch co-op experience! But I felt htat they were going in more of a action, and less horror style in the series. I don't know what they were thinking about the 6th game in the series... I completed it, but I just cringed all the way... and I guess there's alot a RE fans out there who sat with that exact same feeling.And now, let's get into this. Resident Evil 7... I saw the trailer when it was about to come out. And it looked good. But after the disapointment i felt after the 6th game. I didn't know what to believe. So I thought "man... now they're going for 1st person view? how many changes can be enough?". And you know what? I am so glad I had low expectations for RE7. Because I got to play the demo. It had everything in it. Everything that I now today realize is what capcom really wanted the first Resident Evil to be. Dark cramped hallways where you really do not know what to expect, now in 1st person. So yeah. I bought it and I loved it. Played through it a couple of times. But in the long run, I wasn't to fascinated about the molded. They were scary at first... but they could be so damn boring as well. Now, running around this mysterious village that goes so well into reminding me of how good RE4 was they really made it. THIS!! Resident Evil Village is like Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil 4 had a baby. Where there is alot more action and so many monsters to fight, I am satisfied. I really can't wait to play more of this. Village has also taken this type of Farcry approach. Looting means so much more in this game. Hunting as well. Because I have not yet completed this game, I feel like there is not much more for me to say. But! 6.5hrs in it, and I have already lost track of all the jumpscares I've been through! Capcom really ain't losing their touch!So far I recommend this game to any action/horror fan out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Well i didn´t like RE7 so i knew i will most likely not like this, but it´s worse than i thought.Characters are pretty badly written and utterly uninteresting apart from Karl Heisenberg that one was kinda cool.Ethan especially is such a bad character and the emotionless voice actor doesn´t help.Mommy Alcina is a pointless character pretty much, nice castle but bland enemies there...considering all the hype including her "daughters" she had like 20 minutes screen time and a boring boss fight. And each sister had like 5 minutes, fights included.The ugly blob Salvatore Moreau has an interesting transformation, kinda meh area, and not even new enemies, but his screen time is even worse like 10 minutes?, the boss fight again boring.The doll Donna Beneviento her whole part of the game was like 20 minutes to get to her, 5 minutes of screen time and not even a fight (you kill her but...its just find her + press F 3x), what acrually looks like an interesting character is less than a random side quest monster. Her mansion could have been interesting, but it´s empty, nothing in it including enemies.Karl Heisenberg...discount magneto, but the best of the bunch by far. Short but very nice area with biomechanical theme, actually had some sort of personality and the most screen time, and a somewhat interesting backstory and drive to be who he is. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did i enjoy the bossfight - nothing new or groundbreaking but damn.Village is actually the area you spend most time in due to exploration and it being a hub to other areas. Kinda like the place. I like snow, it´s quite nicely done and has some interesting side stuff to do.Music...cant really say anything, either it´s not there or it´s too silent.The overall atmosphere is decent i guess, it didn´t really make me feel anything at all.The story: It´s bad....just bad, it is kinda explained at the end but there´s still a load of why? how? when? who?Lords all had like 4 opportunities to end Ethan but chose not to for ????? reason.Chris is finally explained but it still doesnt make sense how he became what he is?, why?, and where did half of his boulder punching body mass went? His character is pretty much defeated dude with anger issues. They really ruined him.Gameplay: While i am not a fan of the first person like i wasn´t in RE7 it kinda works.Gunplay is 100% average, nothing good nothing bad, except for the part that like in RE7 Capcom still has no idea what iron sights are for and instead you use your telescopic eyes.The RE4 treasure aspect of the game is it´s main redeeming quality on standard dif it took me 6.5h to finish the game with 95% treasures (missed a few by the end i just couldn´t be bothered anymore) without that i´d be done with the game in like 3-4h. All those reviews saying story is 8-10h i seriously have no idea what takes people so long??? I explored as much as i could and barely reached half of that. I did skip a few cutscenes because they took forever without anything happening or were just pure cringe (and i stopped caring near the end) but that may be like another 20 minutes at max.The game itself is quite fun at first then you get to castle and slows but somewhat maintains it´s momentum. After that its like they just gave up and remains pretty bland till Heisenbergs part. It feels like each Lord and his/her area was done by a completely different studio and then they just created the village in the middle and stapled the pieces together.Oh and apart from Chris and one name mentioned in a note at the very end of the game it has absolutely nothing to do with Resident Evil...nothing.On a less serious note the Duke (merchant):Just like in RE4 i dont like the shop inclusion it takes away from the immersion. Who is he? What is he? How the hell is he moving between locked locations ahead of player completely ignored by the monsters and lords and establishing shops in their domains? Where is he geting all of the money and why the ♥♥♥♥ is he trading in a godforsaken random place in romania ruled by fanatics filled with monsters and the only customer being some radnom american that just arrived.If you thought that Ethan getting limb chopped off and then suddenly having it back is weird and out of place (RE7) well its back but thank god its explained in the ending but it actually creates more wtf questions and undermines the story even more.Also why are all characters using perfect american english? Including the "medieval" looking villagers? There´s not a single word in romanianOh and the mercenaries....Yea nah that....that ♥♥♥♥ is a joke.It´s not a terrible game but for the current price it´s just a waste of time with barely any content and absolutely no reason to replay. _childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is the 8th main installment of this series, and it brings some awesome things to the table.  I was very close to giving it a 10/10 for the first few hours I played, but some glaring issues came about that kept bugging me and hindered my enjoyment of the game.-Resident Evil 4 inspired inventory and gameplay that is great to see return.-Beautifully crafted, varied environments.-An interesting story that kept me engaged which continues the events of Resident Evil 7 directly.-Exciting combat counters with punchy weapons.-Some intense boss fights.-Guarding is required more often in this game compared to RE7 which keeps you on your toes.-New characters that are mostly interesting and likeable.-Tall Vampire Lady!!  Jokes aside, Lady Dimitrescu and her daughters were awesome.  .-Some earned scares, and moments where I really felt afraid.-Kind of silly, but you can't assign the Mr. Raccoon/Mr. Everywhere charms on more than 1 weapon, the first pistol and first shotgun.  That just seemed strange to me.-Base enemies don’t feel that varied.  They all behave pretty much the same way, but have a different model to fit the area they’re in.-Some parts leaned too much towards the action side of things, and felt more on-the-rails than I would have liked.  I get nervous when that happens in this series, because I don’t want it to go back in the direction of Resident Evil 6.-The game frequently told me I could press LB to push an enemy away, but I couldn't get it to work at all.  I tried several times but I just never got the timing of it.  As of 5-10-2021, I still don't have the achievement for doing it once lol.  -Story issue: . -The story moves  quickly towards the end of the game despite moving pretty slowly for most of it.  It suddenly goes from 0-100 and throws so many revelations at you I found it kind of hard to keep up.-The voice lines for Chris and Heisenberg lacked good direction at some points.  The actors did great work with what they were given.  But, there were some lines where if I was the director I would've called for re-recordings.  The most notable one for me was when Chris is talking to , and he sounds like he has a Boston accent.  I felt like that delivery just didn't work for Chris's character.  There were also times with Heisenberg where his sentence inflections really stood out to me as odd, but this may have been intentional.  -The RE4-style inventory is really cool, but it doesn’t work as well as it did in RE4.  In RE4, if you were moving an item and pressed the button to place it down over another item, for most item pairs it would swap them so you place down your currently held item and pick up the other one.  This was useful if you wanted to place a gun in a spot but there was a grenade somewhere in that space – it would put down the gun and pick up the grenade so you could put it somewhere else.  In Village, this  happens with ammo over other ammo, after pressing the button multiple times.  This got frustrating fast, as my muscle memory from RE4 kept kicking in (I beat it 3 times before Village came out).  It makes organizing the inventory slower.-The game is really linear.  There is rarely a moment where you have to stop, look at your item inventory, and think about what you have to do to progress.  The way forward is always pretty clear.  It makes the Resident Evil 4 influence obvious, and I felt like it didn’t work as well for this game.  It’s still a really well done game world and its areas flow from one to the next.  But, the no-loadscreen open world design gives the impression that it will be more like a bigger version of the RPD from RE2 Remake or the Baker House of RE7, where you’re having to run back and forth through areas you’ve opened to solve new puzzles as you acquire more key items.  I suppose this could be true about the Village in the middle, but .-Mia. In RE7, she was a badass double agent who put up a cute wife façade for Ethan while fulfilling her own Ada Wong-style agenda with her other secretive work.  In this game, .  I wasn’t a huge fan of that.-Sometimes after getting grabbed by an enemy, another one would grab me immediately after I got let go, before I could get a chance to guard or heal.  Uncommon, but really lame when it happened.  Broke immersion.-We still do not get to see .  That really annoyed me because it felt like we were going to see it, and then we don’t.  - and  were criminally underused.  I felt like you could’ve cut out  entirely to focus more on expanding .  On that note, I found the castle to be really short despite marketing making it seem like it would be one of the game’s main recurring areas, which was disappointing since it and Lady Dimitrescu are two of the best things about this game.  I really didn’t like that .  Lame.Despite my criticisms, I did enjoy my time overall with Resident Evil Village.  It is a welcome entry to the series and a polished experience.  It's an impressive feat to keep the series feeling fresh and fun despite being over 20 years old. It's not a bad game, it's a good game in its own right. It's just not a great Resident Evil game.7/10

TLDR; Overall, it's NOT a Cyberpunk, but its still a rushed release that could've been better. Definitely not worth 80 dollars.1.) NO MATTER WHAT YOU DO, You may have constant stutters and sometimes crashes in many of the game areas. This is shown in cutscenes (Village visits, Castle fights, Places where the Vampire sisters spawn, etc.), sections of the game and will even CRASH your Mercenaries game in the Mad Village Sections and the like. No FOV slider, so some may experience really uncomfortable motion sickness issues. Mods are available to circumvent this for now.5.) THE POST GAME CONTENT THEY PROMISED YOU ABOUT THE MERCENARIES? _childDocuments_.review: Story picks up directly from RE7, you should play that before starting this game. RE8 looks amazing but has a few PC performance issues. Gameplay is also like RE7 with RE8 having memorable characters and a good amount of content for casual or speed runs. Simps have latched onto this game for their weird fetish and for some reason, Chris is not a werewolf.Set a few years after the events of Resident Evil 7, Village has Ethan & Mia Winters moved to Europe for a fresh start and to give birth to as well as raise their newborn daughter Rose. This peaceful family is promptly shattered when Mia Winters is shot in cold blood by none other than Chris Redfield. Ethan & Rose are scooped up but are separated shortly after and Ethan is charged with finding his daughter as he approaches this snowy village in the shadow of a foreboding castle.Village is a 1st person survival-horror experience as a natural continuation of RE7 but does tend to feel a bit more responsive as Ethan has been studying in firearms training after the events in Louisiana. There is a lot more weapon  variety that's improved from RE7 that becomes more apparent later on in the game. Ammo can be in short supply depending on what difficulty you start with but RE8 as includes a crafting system you can use in a pinch if you have the required materials to proceed. RE8 is also much more puzzle heavy compared to previous entries in the series and was a welcome surprise as a form of downtime while still being engaged in the game.Map variety has really stepped up as you'll have 4 main areas to tackle as you progress guarded by 4 lords. They as well as each area is very unique visually, enemy types, & even game-play at times. Enemies react differently depending on where you attack them but also approach you to attack dynamically by rolling or sidestepping as they close the distance. While this all takes place in a village, Resident Evil has never felt bigger with large maps rife with detail. Exploring houses in the village gives you an impression that they felt very lived in and the generations of people that have come and gone there.Speaking more on visuals, the character & enemy models look fantastic. The mega-scan tech that Capcom is using looks amazing with even minor things that can be made out like eyelashes or pores and the more supernatural elements like claws & fur in fine detail.The actors that did motion capture & voice acting did a great job here especially with some characters having starkly different heights or other different physiques to convey in the game. Music is great when used and never felt overused as you progress.RE8 could last around 8-12 hours depending on how much of the side content you complete. When you eventually beat the game is where the extra content comes in.You'll be rewarded with Completion Points based on what challenges you beat, similar to RE2R & RE3R. These challenges include and expand on the achievement list and the Completion Points that you get are used in the Extra Content Shop. A fan favorite mode that you can unlock is The Mercenaries, try to build up your high-score against the clock that you tackle in a handful of maps with the opportunity to gain weapon upgrades & power-ups along the way. Other unlocks from the Extra Content Shop include some exclusive weapons, infinite ammo for each weapon (that doesn't affect achievements\challenges), character models & concept art.I'm going to include some tips that are just generally good to know before you start.I really don't have anything negative to say about Village, its a fantastic game and my personal favorite so far in the series. However there is some less than ideal results in PC performance.For some reason, the retail release performs worse than the game-play demo that was released a week ago. Ray-tracing in particular really tanks performance, I was getting a frame-rate in the single digits at times on a 3070 when enabled and yet when I enabled it the demo, the frame-rate was very smooth. Performance with Ray-tracing turned off also performs slightly worse as well compared to the demo, lowering texture memory usage helped the most but it's a baffling situation. Unfortunately, I highly doubt we'll get DLSS as a workaround since Capcom went with AMD's Fidelity technology instead.UPDATE: Turns out Capcom had their own layer of DRM separate from Denuvo, this home-grown DRM was the source of all the strange performance issues the game has had unlike the demo. Capcom has since patched the game to either remove or perhaps turn off their DRM and performance has improved quite a bit. Denuvo is still here but doesn't have any perceivable impact, Denuvo likely will stick around for a while with RE8 DLC in development. Capcom has once again hit it out of the park with their recent releases with Village has been their best yet and a huge leap forward compared to RE7. Outside of some needed performance optimizations that'll hopefully be patched in, this is absolutely worth your time to experience and will probably be my game of the year for 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really a Maybe rather than a no, but this game is a disappointment for me, and I came into this expecting maybe the BEST RE yet.  Instead all I can say is RUH ROH.In before clowns leave jester emotes and so on, all because they can't handle someone didn't like their precious take on action RE and can't accept that liking this take on RE is entirely subjective. I didn't hate the game by the way, just found it OK. StoryI am not going to say much here, you already know the story if you have watched any footage, Ethan Winters is back and so is Chris, this time it’s personal (at least that is what they want you to think). The story progresses and while it does have some great highs, it also has some REALLY BAD LOWS. With the use of the umbrella logo and such in the trailers and demos, I expected some real deep dive into how umbrella came into existence, do not get me wrong you do find out the link, but it is incredibly underwhelming to say the least.  I was expecting the story to really go places, and to be honest the ideas in my head make significantly more sense than what Capcom ultimately came up with. There was potential here for so many opportunities for future games set in the past and future, all of it is squandered for what frankly feels pointless and I can honestly say based on the ending I am out when it comes to RE9. RE7 felt like RE was getting back on track and onto something old yet new, but RE has lost its way more than ever with RE8. The final act, as per RE tradition really falls apart, but it wouldn’t be RE without that. It’s just if anything, it falls apart more than normal.GraphicsYes, this is a cross gen game, but thanks to RE engine’s great IQ and clean renderer the game is stunning, even sexual to look at times.  The ray tracing is incredibly minimal, but it does add to scenes, especially inside and elevates the game, even if not by as much as one may hope. The overall visual package is a significant step up and the loading stuttering inherent with RE engine is still present but reduced significantly. Overall, I think RE8 artistically is a fantastic game, and while it is ultimately a cross gen game, thanks to all the techniques built upon from RE7 it is still good looking.GameplayThis is where the game really falters. In ways it feels better than RE7 for sure, it feels refined, movement feels better, sound is overall improved, animations are solid. However, the guns, which you will be using a lot as this is what I would call an Acton RE, lack feedback, visually and sound. Knockback on enemies from the enemies feel lacking, the guns don’t feel like they have any weight to them, it’s serviceable and good enough, but it sticks out, this is something that should have been a priority for improvement it however is not.On the action front, this is one of the things that makes the game feel very odd, it has its moments, but it feels like a slow action RE, there are a lot of lulls, and even when things do get going it feels more like RE2 encounter wise for the most part.I think this may ultimately be the tone in these moments, others may feel different but for me there seems to be a miss match of tone and what you are doing. It is a mish mash of action and horror, but it does not feel like it quite gels most of the time.This leads me onto the biggest problem of the game. The game is very varied and some of it works, some of it does not, the problem is it never stays with any of these long enough to build on them as soon as it feels it is getting started it is already over. Even lady Dimitrescu does not stay around for long, which really surprised me, if anything she is relegated to an inferior MR X mechanically, and story wise it feels like there should have been much more from her and others.  The game feels like a compilation of the last 7 REs (yes even 6, there is a tank). It is an RE mash up good and bad, but without focusing on anything for long enough. This ultimately makes it worse than 7, and with its pacing issues, I am not actually sure where I would place it in a list of REs best to worst.  SoundOverall, the use of sounds environmentally and everything excluding the guns (which are good but not great), is high quality and used to great, even phenominal effect with their surround sound solution on, however I am in an odd situation here as someone who has listened to the game on PS5 and PC. The mixing and overall quality on PS5 seems higher than that of the PC version. I have had to turn my amp up way higher to hear the environment on PC and the sound quality sounds more compressed and overall worse.Full review below.

_childDocuments_.review: "Be careful, that glass jar is your !" Resident Evil 7 was my first RE game, and it scared the bejeezus outta me.  This one kinda continues that feeling. Plus a bit less "you can't kill that guy, but you can buy some time and waste your precious ammo".The fairytale animation that bookends the game is fantastic.Sometimes the humor comes from how goofy it all is, like your hand getting chopped off and magic fluid will heal it right up!Some negatives: the whole guard up/push thing I feel is clunky, and if you don't press it early enough you go through a long biting animation for every enemy.  I think you should at least be able to push them off you at any point, maybe with a dmg penalty.  As is, I just throw my hands up for awhile as I enter an unskippable small cutscene of getting bit.Some dumb storytelling- Chris Redfield won't even tell Ethan why he did something to his wife until the end cuz he ain't got time for two minutes of dialogue!  You kill a hundred monsters and multiple bosses and he's like "Just stay outta this, kid!  You're useless!"NG+ is a bit disappointing after playing RE2, there's literally no changes, you just keep your gear. _childDocuments_.review: Although it may not be considered one of the best games in the franchise, it certainly exhibits a remarkable level of boldness and originality. The feeling of wanting to explore each area further is a testament to the game's quality design, which skillfully balances content and progression.It is important to note that the introduction of new protagonists and the renewal of the franchise are necessary to maintain players' interest and relevance over time. Therefore, the change of direction that the game seems to indicate, with the post-credits scene suggesting a new phase for the franchise, is welcome.In summary, although the game may not be flawless, its boldness, originality, and quality design make it a fascinating and engaging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil has faced a myriad of backlash after the slightly disappointing Nemesis (which I have not personally played) but CAPCOM secures another hit and continues the success of 7 with various improvements (both under-the-hood & in design/story telling). It is important to note that this is a successor and continuation of 7 and is designed to feel that way so if you enjoy the more "traditional" over-the-shoulder format of RE, you might be a bit disappointed.You can tell CAPCOM experimented a bit with mechanics in this iteration and not all of them succeeded but boy did they have an impact when executed flawlessly and the game has a lot of those moments for me, personally. At first, I was a bit apprehensive and confused by the story but questions & ambiguity in the beginning hours fuelled my drive to keep exploring. I just had to venture deeper to understand what was exactly happening and the revelations (whilst somewhat cliche at times) did satisfy me. The story's ebb & flow was smooth, the pacing somewhat fast but the end the delivery: impactful.The puzzles are not hard (it's not like your traditional horror in that regard) but they are somewhat interesting and help break up the action to take a break and lose yourself in the scenery. Have we spoken about environments? They are gorgeous. The world isn't large enough to be considered open or even semi-open but the way the levels are intertwined with smart blocking & locks help to pique that curiosity as you progress only to go "ooh, that's where this leads". Enemy design has been meticulous and the attention to detail impressed me immensely. There's a good chunk of variety in here so you won't feel like you are fighting the exact same enemy over and over but it's just large enough that you WILL think "not this guy again". As for standouts: I think we all know and can appreciate the "lovely ladies of the castle" as one prime example.As an avid horror fan, the biggest aspect I appreciated is when the game decided "okay, you've had some fun blasting your way here, now buckle up and put your diapers on". It leaves you helpless, it tortures your senses and creates the sheer terror of a truly psychological thriller during segments of the game. I would've loved more but when they cropped up, I was both terrified & filled with adrenaline. What sets RE:8 apart from a lot of other horror games is its balance of action & horror which are designed to complement each other to provide a varied & engaging experience. There are specific sections where you will simply not be able to shoot your way through, no matter what weapons you have or how good you are. If that is a negative, so be it but for me this was nothing but a positive. It's rare to find a game that employs a risky approach of trying to meld the two genres in such a unified manner. After you are done with the story, Mercenaries mode is a lot of fun with a heap of replayability & CAPCOM has gone the extra mile to make a second run more enjoyable beyond the usual "here's a crazy weapon for the next time, enjoy".Let's talk difficulty. I finished on "Hardcore" which is the "Hard" version of RE and it was challenging but not overwhelming. There's a steeper mode beyond that if you truly wish but I actually enjoyed not having the burden of having to min/max everything and potentially spoiling things just to understand what I would be up against. I died a good amount of times for me to reconsider elements of strategy and adapt my approach beyond running into everything and gunning things down. The bosses themselves are probably on the easy side but again, the story was what I was there for primarily so take heed.The lack of a FOV slider is a big no-no for a lot of people and I cannot defend CAPCOM here. I do agree it's unacceptable at this point in time that the game requires a mod for this but hopefully with time, this will get patched in but whilst this was inconvenient, it did not detract me from enjoying the game in its full glory.There's not a lot of good "horror" games lately and whilst this may not fit the full bill of what a horror game should be, it created a VERY fun run of emotions for me and for that, I say "well done". I might be easily pleased for some standards but I would consider this a huge and welcome success in my eyes. I thoroughly enjoyed every minute and only wish there was a bit more.As for that and in closing, m8, I r8 this 8/8. Recommended purchase from me if you enjoy a healthy mix of horror & action in a first person perspective. Think of this like a love-child between Resident Evil 4 & Resident Evil 7.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. It combines RE7 style gameplay with more combat and a snowy village and castle environment. I got it for 29 Euros which is a fair price. I think 59 Euros is too much though. Here are the pros and cons:Pro:- excellent sometimes even stunning graphics and good sound- original and creative environments (village, castle)- interesting and unqiue characters- good fighting mechanics- there is a fun mercenary mode- RE4 style inventory and merchant- entertaining boss fights- interesting puzzles- refreshing Chris game-play towards the end similar to RE7- unlockable bonus features like weapons and contentNeutral: - the game tries to be scary visually but the fact that killing enemies gives you valuable items makes you the hunter rather than the hunted. Meeting enemies feels more like "how do I kill them effectively" and not "how do I survive this". The hero does suffer pain but feels invinvible nonetheless which also takes away some of the scariness. - red explosive barrels (I personally dont like them in survival horror games because they cause a game-ish atmosphere)- Standard difficulty might be too easy for you if you are good at shooting. Try hard mode right away.Con:- The game introduces new characters just to kill them off within seconds or minutes which is a bad story telling style. You dont care about them enough at this point which makes it feel like an unnecessary and cheap effect. - Towards the end of the game the style changes very much to a typical game-ish feel. It adds unrealistically huge levels that dont fit the style of the previous chapters. Like that one bad guy who lives in a village has a factory that is so huge that a million people should be working there. - The game breaks with the style so much at one point you think it is Battle Field. It was fun to play but imagine sitting in a flying tank with machine gun and tank cannon shooting on a gigantic Transformer-like monster. Yeah, that happens. - Many scenes where characters interact - mostly in the later parts of the game - seem so awkward, especially with Chris. - The ending is way over the top in scale. It comes out of nowhere and wasnt necessary.Overall I give this game an 8 score. If it was just for the first half of the game I would have rated it higher but because it breaks with the style so much I had to substract some points. I'd say first half is 9.5 and second half is 6.5.

_childDocuments_.review: “It’s RE4+RE7.” This is true, but it also has inspirations from almost every RE game. The game feels like it’s a celebration for RE’s 25th anniversary.I’ve enjoyed my time playing it and I think it’s A MUST BUY for every RE fan or a survival horror fan.- Easily and by a huge margin, RE8 is the best looking RE game ever. It's INCREDIBLY detailed, well designed and STUNNING to look at.- Very atmospheric, and its got a lot of variety in that aspect as well.- Sound design is also the best in the series. The intro is horrifying!- From the first few hours, you'll quickly notice how big and diverse the game is.- Levels are intricately crafted, with more ways to explore them. Really liked how the village was structured with more ways to explore and search its houses.- The game INSANELY nails the interior design of its levels; I find myself stopping every 5 mins or so just to absorb the beauty of it all.- The game's setting really makes you feel like you're playing in a horror themed amusement park.- There is clear emphasis on exploration and side content.- The game allows you to take control of your own pacing at certain sections. It’s not really a linear game. It has more freedom and exploration than previous RE games as I mentioned before, which I liked very much!- The game does a really good job of changing its intensity from time to time. Presenting different types of horror along the way, mixing them up with action / adventure elements & sequences while still being within its survival horror medium. It’s well balanced, diverse and refreshing.- RE8 has some of the highest highs in the franchise. When it hits, it hits real good. :D- NO LOADING TIMES. That's a technical marvel considering the quality of its graphics, level design and performance. RE Engine strikes again!- Puzzles are fun and rewarding.- Backtracking here is the most fun and rewarding in all of the RE games.- Music is top tier.- The merchant is cool.- The story is intriguing and thrilling.- The characters are some of the best in the series. Really interesting, very well acted and fun to watch. Not including Ethan though lol, however he's honestly better this time.* Advice: if you're playing with a controller (consoles or on PC), turn off the movement camera acceleration and aiming camera acceleration settings. They somewhat introduce input delay and make the camera movement feel slow. Terrible settings!

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is not only the best Resident Evil I ever played since the very first release on the first Playstation. it is one of the best games ever made and the new standard for the Action-Horror genre. From the first moment Village draws you into its intense atmosphere and world building. "Good graphics" doesn't cut it here anymore, it's more like interactive art in fluid motion from start to finish. Especially Lady Dimitrescu herself and her castle and daughters are iconic and unforgettable character and location designs up there with Bioshock's Rapture and Big Daddy. Village covers a wide range of European history from the mentioned exterior medieval and interior Victorian Age castle, the title giving village itself, but also deep woods and mines, dungeons, rivers and lakes, finally a steam-punk factory crossing into Terminator territory. And the Capcom team just nails every single one. You can also really tell the team respected its characters, Eastern European, Slavic and Orthodox source material which, mixed with some Japanese Oni anologies, feels very fresh. Only From Software also does it this good.For years I was somewhat skeptical of the Resi games. I found them okay, but forgettable and sometimes very cringe when it came to writing - the "b-movie flair" was never my thing. The Remakes were too action focused for me and they actually lost all horror and dread for me, in Resi 7 the terror was there, but it could play tedious and slow at times: although this fit for where Ethan was at the time, it often wasn't a great fun experience for me. I was also never a fan of achievement hunting for replayability. But Village is different! Revolutionary for the series even. And it has converted me from a skeptic to an admirer.I was very impressed how the team managed to orchestrate a design symphony that almost perfectly mixes all of its elements to a fresh, captivating and smooth experience that is more than the sum of its parts: from exploration and treasure seeking, riddles and survival-combat, to Nemesis like unbeatable enemies, some stealth and passages of naked terror. As varied as the locations and atmospheric experiences are, so is the gameplay. Ethan through his tour de force developes from the normie fighting for his life as in Resi 7 to a commando soldier and monster slayer hero at the end. Every location feels great and you always do something new and interesting.I also can't understand why some people think Village has less horror than Resi 7. Not only has it equal peaks in shock and awe, Village varies its themes greatly: classic survival-horror, Blairwitch Project like helpless isolation, Silent Hill and existential dread, body horror in all varieties from Dead Space and Alien, over Cronenberg to cyberpunk and Terminator. Somewhat negative were only two things:  felt too drawn out to artificially make the game longer and it is not quite up there with the other locations (too many identical looking tunnel and box levels), and I wasn't too fond of the one shooting passage with , but it's still thematically interesting and certainly didn't ruin the game for me. And although the writing isn't exactly The Brothers Karamasow, it didn't ruin the atmosphere for me, but supported it this time. Finally we can only be thankful that Japanese games do not try to force a political agenda on you like so much that is coming out of the USA and wider West since several years. Resident Evil's cosmos of terror and dread is certainly still perferable to Clown World.At the end I could tell myself: these are the experiences for which the pioneer technologies and humble beginnings in the 90s and around the turn of the millenium were made, when everything comes together now and starts to bloom. Making gaming to the most interesting entertainment medium on the planet. Who needs Hollywood anyway? 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:- Graphics are incredible (plus HDR)- Sound design is great, constantly has you on edge- Level design: different areas felt connected naturally, and within each area the map was fun to explore- Atmosphere: dark, moody, tense. However after a certain point it loses the moodiness as you become more powerful (that's a game choice, it's more of an action game)- Enemy models - freaky, gross, awesomeDisliked:- Voice acting: hit or miss. Some characters better than others. One in particular is downright cringey (you'll know when you hear it). This has never been RE's strong suit. less is definitely more when it comes to dialogue- Pacing: game file said I took 13 hours to complete, but it felt like 20+ hours. There were two or three points where I would have been satisfied with it ending there. This could be a problem with the expanded scope of the story- Tech issues: I switch between a 32" 4K monitor and my 65" LG CX. It seemed every time I started the game on a new screen, I had to redo all the settings. The resolution would default to 720p (why???) and it was a pain to change back to 4K and toggle HDR back and forth to get the settings right.- Inventory management: I only had one or two moments in the game where I had to manage my inventory. This aspect adds to the previous games and I definitely miss it. It's a game design choice, probably to make things more approachable, but when I think "what games have inventory management", the first thing I think is RE games.If you've ever enjoyed an RE game past RE4 (my personal favorite, really an incredible game), then you will enjoy this as well! It was a great ride!

With how RE4 makes upgrading a weapon to max worth it is by having an exclusive upgrade for all guns, the Striker shotgun for example gets a 100 round magazine as its final upgrade, making it able  to spit lead and not have to reload till everything is dead. RE8 Has Exclusive upgrades as an unlock-able through the dlc Mercenaries, and when you have them turned on rather than making it something you earn by fully upgrading a weapon to then buy the exclusive upgrade, the exclusive upgrades are just on the weapons with no consideration for balancing, and a lot of them are just more power, which is boring. i got excited when i saw that the lemi had healing as its ability, and tought it would be cool to actually have use from it, because it is a garbage weapon base game. when i picked up the 1911 i realized that this was not the case, the lemi was still not worth keeping because the 1911 just gets more damage after a reload for its ability, which when i have the choice between healing for dumping 10 rounds into a monster, or reloading and then blowing its head off in 1 shot, i take the one that kills good.Overall this game is great, fun bosses, great music, decent story, giant crying fetus, and on top of all of that the dlc is a solid 2 hour playthrough.If you can get this game for 30 bucks, do it, as its a fair 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say that RE8 is perhaps (one of) the best in the series. The RE2 Remake is the only really comparable one. RE3 Remake was good, but butchered and short, RE4 Remake was great as well, and RE7 was good, but extremely short. (we can skip the remaining ones, because they're either not all that great or very hard to play (RE1 Remake, although that was kinda enjoyable as well, if not for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ doors!) today).The 1st person camera does wonders here and the graphics are superb, while the game just ... works and runs without glitches, bugs or graphical issues at a solid frame rate.Gameplay wise it's probably the most varied entry in the series as well, with 4 very different areas (and bosses), as well as a sort of "hub" you'll be returning to multiple times, but every time it's changed and you have more possibilities (hopefully).Shooting is fine and the guns finally sound more like guns, instead of pea shooters like in RE7.Puzzles aren't too difficult, but there's lots to explore and upgrade. All in all just solid. Just too bad, that there are once again no iron sights, but oh well.And, again, unlike RE7 this game actually has some varied enemies!Then there's the story ... and imho I think it's pretty good. A father is on a quest to save his daughter and has to fight evil forces! It fits the fairy tale intro (literally an animated children's horror story Mia reads to Rose) perfectly.On this quest he meets a mysterious ally and an old acquaintance and, of course, all is not as it seems.My only real gripe with the story is that it involves Mia. And I hate Mia with a passion. I let her die in RE7, but of course that's not the canon ending. I just can't fathom why Ethan would risk so much for an ego-centric bio-terrorist of all people. Or why the new Umbrella (not to be confused with Neo-Umbrella, I guess -.-) or the BSAA don't put her behind bars. Maybe I missed something, but as far as I'm aware she's the sole reason the whole debacle with Eveline and the Mutamycete even began, although it feels like they retconned a lot with the latter anyway ... or purposefully mislead people/didn't explain stuff.Anyway, the Muta is back, baby... Ethan on the other hand is just a soft noodle and a blank slate, but I can forgive him for that. I can't forgive Mia though. That character should have died in RE7. Rose could have been already born by that time, held in an Umbrella lab, for instance. Or they could have "created" her with their genetic material later on. Fits the character better anyway imho, but we'll get to HER in the DLC review (Spoiler: It's not going to be positive).If you want like 13 hours of fun horror gameplay (seriously, that 2nd level!) in a gorgeous game with solid mechanics, go get it. Beware though: Without having played RE7 you're missing big parts of the experience, even though there is a "Baker Files" recap video.

_childDocuments_.review: The best way of describing Resident Evil Village is that it's all the best aspects of Resident Evil 4 combined with the best of Resident Evil 7.That is a big deal to me because Resident Evil 4 is not only my favorite game in the Resident Evil series, but also one of my favorite games, period. Or it was until I played Resident Evil Village. While Ethan Winters is no Leon S. Kennedy, Village is truly the spiritual successor to RE4 and an absolutely perfect blend of horror and action.I will admit RE7 was a bit (or a lot) too terrifying for me, but a return to the survival horror roots of Resident Evil with a switch to a first person perspective made it a great game. Village tones down the horror enough to still have terrifying moments without feeling like you're constantly about to have a heart attack, and ups the action with a lot more guns and a merchant, The Duke, to buy and upgrade those weapons a la RE4. If RE4 was your jam but RE7 was a bit much, give Village a try.Lastly, I rarely, if ever, finish or replay a game in my library. At the time of this review, I have beaten Village five times so far and have started my sixth playthrough. Yup.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident evil village is an action-horror game. In this game you'll follow Ethan Winters, the protagonist of Resident Evil 7, this time on a quest to get back his daughter and discover why she was kidnapped in the first place.You will explore the titular village and different dungeons, all while shooting or running your way out of monsters.The producer of the game called it a "theme park of horror", where it would feel as if you were going to different attractions and experiencing various types of horrors.This is a very on point description, as each of the areas have different gimmicks that for the most part are over fairly quickly and don't overstay their welcome.I called this an action-horror game because it feels like a midpoint between action and survival-horror. This is an fps where bullets are not exactly abundant and you have limited inventory space, so deciding what to carry is a decision to make every time you pick a new object, especially weapons.The game starts very horror like, but as you advance through the areas and amass a greater arsenal it naturally becomes harder to scare the player, so the game focuses more on its action elements, until a certain sequence close to the endgame where the game stops being horror anymore, and turns into an action shooter.There is a light crafting and upgrading mechanic where you find materials in the game world that you can use to upgrade your weapons, increasing parameters like firepower and bullet capacity.While this is a nice mechanic on its own, you'll also unlock more weapons while advancing in the game or solving puzzles, and the new weapons supersede the old ones in all practical regards, meaning that if you are able to, you should always use the latest weapons available, even when you had upgraded one of your weapons before.I'm sure in high levels of play in mercenaries mode, you have to pick the correct tier of weapon and upgrades, but if having to consider a small extra mode to redeem the lack of choice is a lost cause.Add to this that each type of weapon is either unique or has very few different models, so the weapons diversity ends up feeling very lacking.The game has puzzles, as all resident evil games do, but the ones in here are very simple and straight forward. Only one comes to mind that wasn't immediately obvious how to solve it, but all the others had the solutions right beside them or were simple enough to not warrant putting much thought into it. While I would have prefer puzzles that were a little better, they don't take too long to solve and are there to break the pace of the game in between fights more than anything. In this sense the theme park analogy still works because the game isn't as focused in giving you a good challenge as it’s focused in giving you a good time. Really I feel the last point is core to the whole game and the biggest reason I would recommend it. The game wants you to have fun with it and enjoy it, albeit sacrificing depth in various parts. I have mostly talked about the flaws I find with the game but I still had a blast playing it on two difficulties and some mercenaries.If you don't feel any of the cons I have described are deal breakers for you, I would say Resident Evil Village is worth your time.Although, if you think you'll just play it once (I'd guess the majority of people fall here) then I'd recommend waiting for a sale.One last thing: if you decide to buy the game, I'd recommend using a mod to increase the Field of View, as I felt the default is too tiny for a monitor. Increasing it to 90 made it much more comfortable to play.

_childDocuments_.review: As an individual of discerning taste and considerable means, I have had the pleasure of experiencing many a fine entertainment. However, few have captivated my refined sensibilities as thoroughly as Resident Evil Village. In my considered opinion, this installment represents the most complete Resident Evil experience to date, deftly blending horror and action in a manner that is both compelling and sophisticated.There is an undeniable sense of nostalgia that harkens back to the beloved Resident Evil 4, yet simultaneously, Resident Evil Village forges its own unique identity, distinct from its predecessors. This delicate balance is a testament to the developers' artistry, crafting an experience that feels both familiar and refreshingly novel.One might argue that this is indeed one of the finest Resident Evil games to grace our screens. It eschews monotony while maintaining the core essence that fans have come to adore. Such a balance ensures that each moment is as exhilarating as the last, providing a nonpareil gaming experience that is anything but repetitive.In summation, Resident Evil Village stands as a paragon of its genre, an epitome of horror-action excellence that deserves the highest accolades. It is, without a doubt, a crowning jewel in the illustrious Resident Evil series.

_childDocuments_.review: (NO SPOILERS!)I cannot begin to describe how absolutely relieved I am that this game exceeded all my expectations. As someone who enjoyed RE7, but did NOT classified it as a main title Resident Evil game, I am blown away with what they took from 7 and turned into a full fledged, truly Resident Evil feeling game. This game is not only Beautiful in Graphics, Story Telling, and emotion itself, but its a clear step forward in the RE series that deserves every ounce of praise it gets.- It feels like a mix of all the best aspects from RE4, 5, 6, and 7 combined into one fantastic game. Gone are the bland molded enemies and replaced with actual enemies that give you not only a challenge but a feel of "What are they going to do next?"- The guard feature has been improved upon by simply giving it a knock back feature after successfully guarding.- Ethan had more lines/character development in the first 30 minutes than he did in the entire RE7 campaign. - Ties to the past RE games also come into play here (No Spoilers on what). Thank GOD we are not rebooted!- Bosses FEEL like Resident Evil bosses! This is a big one! While I love the Bakers for what they were, the only true RE boss in that game was Jack's final forum!-Gun play and mechanics from RE4 and 5 are used to upgrade weapons and manage inventory that makes the game WAY more exciting! - NoneLinear Gameplay, (For the most part) DONE RIGHT! - SOMETHING FOR EVERYONE! From hardcore fetus horror to action packed Call of Duty esc gunplay, this game literally is a perfect blend of everything for everyone. - I couldn't even find a single bug, (gameplay wise) in my whole play through. Capcom really let those bugs have it! A really good release launch!- The RE Engine has never looked more stunning! Honestly, RE7 was made as an indoor game, and you could tell outside was NOT the focus with how ugly it looked. But this new RE Engine is just straight up beautiful! And its not that big of a GPU hog either!For hardcore Resident Evil fans, and people just looking for a good story/horror game in general. You MUST pick this game up! Worth its price, worth your time! Thank you Capcom for not screwing this up!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: -My Short History with Resident Evil-Heard a lot about it but never played any until 5, and it was great fun if only because it was something that was co-op. As I grew older I've grown to love every bit of the franchise, no matter how varied. 5 remains special to me but like most people I consider 4 to be the best, or at least the most fun. I've played every mainline entry that's on PC at this stage, including Revelations. I've been drawn to similar games too like Evil Within. Resident Evil made me love survival horror.-Reviewing The Game (Spoiler free)-It's definitely less scary, while i am a veteran and i appreciate the similarities to RE4, the fact that every single enemy drops loot without fail in all difficulties removes a big question of when exactly they die. Of course there have always been other tells, audio or visual but having something so concrete removes much of the fear from the enemies themselves. Along with neatly placed documents that tell you how to kill whatever's in the next room. The franchise has always had hints like this but i don't feel like it's ever been so detailed and conveniently located. This also removes a lot of the spooks. There's some new additions to the formula with a shove ability after you block certain attacks. If you are looking for a survival horror game and not an fps with a horror dressing, play on hardcore right from the start. Obviously doing so won't entirely erase the fact that this game is more action and exploration focused. With that said, the range of environments, like most RE games will surprise you. Sometimes you will wish you could spend more time in some versus others, and a strong complaint for me in this game is just wanting more. Many of the threats you encounter are kind of isolated. There's several notable hostile NPC's but it's extremely little the amount of internal interaction they have. When you are in X persons area, they and their particular cronies are the only threat you will face. In RE7, it felt like the family was really toying with you as a collective. There was times when it focused on one more than another but it felt more unpredictable on a first time through and even replaying it, it feels more interesting being able to see them all more often. Basically in 8, the characters are just as interesting but really not built upon as much as the Baker family was. It feels too cookie cutter. I don't think a narrative/puzzle driven game like Resident Evil could handle a "pick your own adventure" approach to which threat you went toward, but if they were determined to quarter them off in their places as they did, maybe it would've been worth trying? But besides the quality of spooks, it's a great game. The story is great, and it's a decent sequel from a franchise that doesn't really do them. It's still funny, it's still surprising and shocking. But it's game-play at least, isn't as spooky. It feels like the combat really has become too formulaic in this entry. Even in RE4 you were dealing with tank controls if combat became too predictable. In this, to it's detriment, it's too fluid and easy. About the only thing limiting you is the fov, but even then enemies don't seem too dangerous when you can't see them. In the end it's a fantastic entry, a great starting point for newcomers and a great continuation of the franchise and Ethan's story. While being at times both a subtle and heavy handed homage to earlier titles in a truly endearing way. Sometimes it's cool, sometimes it's meta, sometimes it's respectful and at times downright hilarious. Even without comparing it to the rest of the franchise, it's like a love letter to classic horror aesthetics (not so much thematically though, this is still Resident Evil). The references to RE4 and 5 in this make for some interesting discoveries both in the games lore and stories about the real life development of the games. The potential for dlc and a sequel is strong. Also the mercenary mode this time around features almost rogue-like combat elements. Makes replaying it more fun despite the fact it's still kind of just a time trial in a preset location from the story.-Summary-I love this franchise, I love this entry. If you liked 7, you will enjoy this without a doubt, but bear in mind it's differences. I have no idea where Resident Evil goes next, but you will see me there.

_childDocuments_.review: It is an excellent game in my opinion. It is less frightening than re7 and feels much different as it seems to be more action based than horror like re7. Ammo is much more abundant and you can actually purchase and sell stuff helping you rid of what you dont use and buy what you do. RE7 had a much better feel in terms of horror. Less stuff making you scrounge and try to use whatever you had while in this game you can pretty much use the same weapon and not really worry about ammunition after 3-4 hours of gameplay. After all that its still probably my favorite of the 2. Collectibles give the game replay value and new game plus allows you to permanently unlock weapons with unlimited ammo letting you play through the game easily without worrying about anything and lets you get collectibles and unlock achievements without having to grind nearly as hard. Still creepy with a couple very frightening parts but overall a less frightening game than re7, but still a very enjoyable experience. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible, but not without its flaws! Village, the follow up to RE7 is a fantastic blend of horror, action and the usual Resident Evil over the top crazy plot. But somehow, they managed to ground it even more. You play as Ethan from RE7 again, and without spoiling anything, they develop the dangling story threads of RE7 in a much, MUCH stronger fashion than any other mainline RE game. Graphically, stunning. Music? Fantastic, and the atmosphere is terrific. There is one level in particular that reminded me of Kojima's cancelled Silent Hills. Really really good stuff. The gameplay is the ONLY part i am going to nitpick on. One of the levels is a bit of a drag to get through, with increasingly annoying enemies and too much busy work. For the MOST part though, i loved it. And Ethan feels much more satisfying to control this time.Overall, i rarely buy games at full price these days. And when i do i usually regret it. RE8 is an exception. It took me 11 hours for the first run and i cant wait to jump back in again.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like the original RE4... but in first person... it's so good.Some people say RE4 had too much action and it left the horror behind and I only agree with them a little bit, RE4 was plenty scary for me but it was full of satisfying action as well.That's Village for me all over again, the game scared me a ton, had me going through hectic sections and other wild stuff. Sometimes scary sometimes not, but always an incredibly fun game that has a LOT in common with RE4, in the best ways.Inventory is fun to play with, awesome characters are in the world and it's really fun interacting with the shop.This game is a huge W.The DLC felt very by the numbers and it's EXTREMELY short, so I'd say to hard pass on the DLC in general. If you're a huge fan of the character Rose then the DLC will be enticing for you but otherwise I strongly suggest waiting for a big sale... even at 50% off I would consider the price of the DLC "decent"tl;dr game has as much horror/action as RE4, feels a lot like RE4 except first person view. It's so freaking fun yoooo like for real, it's a huge W ... DLC isn't worth full price due mostly to length and slightly to quality.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm using a 1070 which is not that old and is listed in their recommended settings.  The only way I can play at all is by turning the entire game to bare minimum settings.  Even then the gameplay is enjoyable most of the time, but there can still be a problem with "micro-stutters" that happen a lot.  I have to reboot the game or my pc to flush it out.  The game has been out for almost a month now and no patch for this.  The problem here is they put so much good stuff in the story (ignoring plot holes), the detail, the enemies, the level design, etc that I just wanted more and more.  The 4 Lords could have had much longer segments that explored more of their history and background.  What is there is quite nice, but right now it's only around 3 hours per lord (if that) and that's if you try to stretch it by being thorough. The enemies are well detailed and most have their own ways of behaving.  In addition many have multiple kill animations for poor Ethan that really look "intense". I'm going to give the Story and the Characters a bit of a pass on the "making sense" or "using good judgement" since most characters in horror games / movies don't.  Capcom did a better job at making Ethan seem more intelligent than RE7 IMO.  Traveling cross country (UNARMED AND WITHOUT BACKUP!) to a a creepy abandoned estate where people have been known to go missing; sounds like a great plan. Hey, like I said before, characters in the Horror Genre don't roll very high Intel stats.  At least here there is a bit of an excuse as to why he shows up at the Village. Hopefully we get some DLC that expands on what's going on and at least does a half-arsed attempt at answering questions and plot holes.  Be nice to see the entire cast of this little Quaint Village again somehow.  Ethan's time in it was far too short.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 8 is a more action-oriented game after its direct predecessor firmly returned the series back to its survival horror roots, but fortunately it doesn't overindulge in action schlock: this is still a very spooky, very tense Resident Evil that maintains an excellent balance between frantic combat encounters and quieter moments of exploration, set in often visually stunning environments that are excellently designed and featuring some of the best and most charismatic antagonists I have seen in any media in a while. Absolutely recommended!It's also worth mentioning that the Winters' Expansion DLC not only adds a few hours of fantastic story content and enhances the Mercenaries mode with extra characters and maps, it also allows you to play the main campaign in third-person perspective instead of the default first-person; a welcome option that should make an already highly replayable game have even better replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with a lot of weird design choices, or lack of design choices? I'm not sure, but the game is basically trying to be resident evil 4 (one of my favorite games ever), and nails things like cheesy ass stupid story that made me laugh, a good world to explore and back track through. Combat in this game is so-so, the game is an action game for sure, but for a first person shooter it doesn't really feel that good to play compared to other modern and even indie titles. I also find the in game economy to forgiving, maybe I should have just played on hardcore instead of standard since i'm a long time RE veteran but there wasn't any moment in the game where I was low on ammo and thinking, "oh ♥♥♥♥ I need to hit this next shot or I am dead." I think the crafting system just makes ammo and resource management a joke taking the survival aspect of this survival horror game pretty under developed. All in all very good I would recommend, but be aware that it isn't the best RE game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried about the length of this game but it was very well-seized in my opinion. The game says I spent like 8hrs44m but that is just pure gameplay, I actually spent around 12.5 hours in my first run, including inventory, cutscenes, stuff like that. I didn't do CLOSE to everything the game had to offer, and still haven't touched the stuff you get after finishing it the first time.I had a fantastic time with this game. It has so much variety in areas and atmosphere, from P.T. levels of psych horror, to gothic monsters, and more that I won't get into. The story takes steps I did not expect as well as some that I did, but was intriguing and gripping throughout.I heard a lot of talk about the game being a lot more action-heavy than 7, and I'd agree with that, but, speaking as someone who loved 7 and didn't like the idea of heavier action, I really enjoyed a lot of the action heavy sequences, and found the contrast between these sections and the more horror-focused sections to be really cool and it kept things fresh and engaging. One boss in particular (the second big boss, for those who have played) felt slightly under-utilized in my opinion and their power/ability could have been used quite a bit more, but that's a very subjective thing.The ray traced lighting in this game was extremely pretty, and definitely added to the atmosphere.I have my problems with the game, most memorable of which being Ethan's somewhat weak VO, especially in moments of anger. It just seems really off and broke the tension a couple times.I also had some bugs that were so interruptive that I had to restart my game and get rid of them to keep playing. Generally though, my complaints aren't major enough to truly damage my experience with the game. I had a great time, and can't wait for Resi 9.

_childDocuments_.review: "herp derp big mommy milkers, me give thumbs up"I've been a Resident Evil fan ever since the first game in 1996. I know what the franchise used to be and what it is now - and what it is now is... confusing.Resident Evil Village is a very beautiful game with some cool mechanics (like the new inventory system), and some very memorable characters, but aside from that it's basically a game that doesn't know what path to take. CAPCOM wasted a very good opportunity to focus on the Dimitrescu castle, by spreading a good base story into many "bosses" that you have to defeat, each feeling like it's own little universe and a total different game. - You start on a village with zombies. OK;- You go to a castle with a giant vampire lady. Meh, OK;- This lady and her "mother" have experimented with a mold that turned 3 girls into flies, and these flies have a collective conscience that is basically that of a human. What?;- The castle part was OK, but it was super short. You just killed this giant lady and will go onto a total different boss now, one that controls dolls;- Super short as always, after you've killed the "doll lady" you'll basically go fight Megneto;- After that, you'll fight the "final boss", Mother Miranda.Playing this game will feel like playing Resident Evil, Silent Hill, Cyberpunk 2077, and Far Cry. And don't kid yourself, after finishing the game you won't feel as if the story makes any sense - apart from Ethan and his family, which is actually a nice continuation from Re7.It's like 3 OK stories that don't connect put together with Re7.Enemies are super slow and stupid, even the bosses. You'll yawn many times while fighting Lady D, the Doll Lady, Heisenberg, and even Mother Miranda. Not once will you feel actually in danger while fighting the bosses and most enemies - only in the beginning is where you actually feel like an outsider and that everyone's out to get you.The daughters' are cute, but non-threatening. Boring.

Stupid-ass dialogue, incredible atmosphere, fantastic art direction and creature/character design, satisfying gunplay, and some legitimately scary moments. Seriously, ♥♥♥♥ that baby. I knew it was in the game, I had seen my friend play that section, I had seen Dunkey play that section, I knew it was coming. _childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil has finally made its way into eastern lands of Europe, more specifically one unnamed village in Transylvanian Mountains of Romania. You're left off with Ethan from the previous installment now settled with Mia in his relatively modest home somewhere classified location, taking care of their very so normal baby girl. All of the enthusiasm you're experiencing in the beginning will slowly dissipate as you're thrown at the heart of swarm, unknown beasts and monsters alike roaming your surroundings like rats amidst harvest. The dreadful, sinister and abandoned looking village will entice your gaze on every single yard corner, remnants of bodies from farm animals and wasted grains paint slowly and intensively the vicious encounters you'll partake. The visual fidelity through protagonist's eyes is an experience to behold, life-like artwork and animations worthy of unique appraisal. You're provided with a powerful arsenal to choose from which allows you to annihilate every single grotesque creature paving the path to your precious daughter. Raw true survival horror experience occurs and indulges my expectations, I can attest it stands firm from previous titles in the series. There are several areas to explore each with its own theme and ridiculous but thrilling traps that will coax flight or fight responses, leaving oneself more often than not forced to improvise and adapt to each situation. The whole system of first person shooter is vastly improved from Ethan's previous adventure as mentioned earlier with lots more weapons to behead ghouls, everything feels more responsive especially when you're blocking enormous werewolf claws with your bare hands; obviously enhanced by the fact you're superhuman with fast regenerative abilities fully recovering your endurance after every encounter. OST & sound design as always is at the peak creating and augmenting the already intensified terror you're forced to withstand. The major character actors being into their roles one hundred percent strengthens the attachments and bonds you'll feel towards their personas, there's a tragedy lying in wait getting you to only empathize through their harrowing stories. Location & characters lore is well written to emulate further involvement, boosting the immersion as if you're there yourself strolling with your own feet and smelling the cold appalling environment. A worthy journey with authentic design of local tradition and culture (approved by a romanian native™) there's lots of fun things to explore, decently difficult puzzles and high variety of monsters to go decimate in most gory manners.- graphics & artwork - fluid first person combat mechanics- good replay value & mercenary mode- OST & sound design- voice actors fitting their roles perfectly- attention to detail when it comes to romanian culture- vos difficulty poorly designed- pointless character deaths as per your typical RE experience
