_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I played this game for roughly 3 hours before refunding it. Some of this stuff may be somewhat changed later in the game but it was not worth playing more to find out, and I wish I had known the majority of this information before I made the purchase.This negative review is mostly for the sense of humor this game has. I could forgive it if it wasn't constant, but it is, and my eyes have rolled back into my head so far that I am having trouble finding them. If you like quippy, meta, self aware, quirky, and memey writing, this game might blow your mind. If you, like me, grit your teeth when a character references the fact that they are in a video game, look elsewhere. The game gives you a companion that has the humor of a social media manager and he never shuts the ♥♥♥♥ up. The point seems to be that the companion talks to characters so you don't have to, as you are a silent protagonist, but instead he just makes jokes constantly about how we are in an RPG and how its so messed up that we are making creatures battle.This is particularly sad to me because I was shocked to find that I liked the world they had set up, something I wasn't expecting to be that great. The world at hand is interesting, but you can't take anything seriously because you will never forget that you are in a video game. The gameplay itself is passable for a Pokemon "clone," it does little to deviate and the lack of double typing dilutes the more interesting features like stamina (which replaces PP from the aforementioned Pokemon). Complaining about a Pokemon inspired game playing like Pokemon may be a bit silly, but I was hoping for something that tried to build on a tired and simple formula. And speaking of formulas, I would really like to see the type match-ups in game and while battling: if having a type chart on my other monitor does the same thing but just takes extra effort, then there is no reason to not have that built in. You could even have match-up discoveries unlock as you see them unfurl in battles. That is all about the battling, however, and the exploration and open-ended nature of the game is somewhat interesting, but not exactly mind blowing. A general positive.I want to give kudos to the visual designers as there are many Nexomon designs I found myself enjoying a lot, and the visual presentation of the game overall is rather good, particularly the UI and the overworld. This just was not enough to keep me on board. All in all, a fine Pokemon type game that doesn't do much I consider special. If you can stomach the jokes and you really just love the "mash flamethrower" type gameplay from the Pokemon franchise, you might enjoy this game more than I.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who tends to enjoy Pokemon-type games more than actual Pokemon games, I really love Nexomon Extinction, even more than I love its predecessor.  If you liked the first one, you'll like this one, it's essentially more of the same thing and that's exactly what I wanted out of this game.  It's easily my favorite game in the monster capture/battle genre.  There are so many reasons to love this game.The characters and dialogue are nowhere near perfect and the story isn't groundbreaking, but the game doesn't pretend to be perfect or 100% original.  It knows exactly what it is, a lighthearted game about imprisoning wildlife, making them fight their own kind, and improving their skills by performing the same attacks over and over until they're strong enough not to get crushed by bosses.  It's just a fun time.If you like turn-based RPGs or creature collector games at all, please play this game, it's worth full price and you'll enjoy it.  And go buy the first one too, it's a very similar game and it's just as fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Nexomon Extinction is the second game in the Nexomon series and it fixed some issues that I have found with the first game. - You can name your nexomon.- Every nexomon has a codex entry.- Healing is much better balanced with nexomon no longer healing after level up and max healing items healing 300 HP, but most nexomon have less than that for overall health. You do have other ways of recovering health like the crystal rocks that appear on maps that you can smash to instantly recover your nexomon, but at the cost of losing access to that crystal for a while.The world is much more open in this game. You can wander around a fair bit. Although some places are blocked off until you get to a certain point in the story, you are able to go visit various locations and catch the native nexomon from the start, which is quite a boon to get a diverse party right from the getgo.Enemies do level along side with your party's average level, so you are rarely if every going to be totally overlevelled for a specific fight, so fair warning. The new catching mechanic is somewhat contentious for me. I can certainly appreciate the fact that the developers went out of their way to include Playstation and Steam Deck controls for the catching inputs (I use a PS4 controller on PC) as most games default to Xbox controls. I'm not sure I like the actual catching minigame where you need to rapidly hit a bunch of inputs first though. The thing i do like is the fact that you can feed the nexomon to increase their catch rate as well as the game actively displaying various catch rate percentages depending on the state of the nexomon, the nexotrap you are using, the food it ate, as well as any status ailments that would also affect the catch rate.The combat system is a bit more refined. Some combat system thoughts here:- I like the fact that some enemy tamers will switch out their nexomon when at a disadvantage initially, something that other games in the genre rarely do, although I understand why this isn't done a lot as it would be pretty annoying really fast. Here it is done just the right amount to mostly avoid that feeling.- Unlike Nexomon 1 you can't switch your moves out of combat anymore, you need to go to a healing station and speak with the move tutor person. I'm not sure why this was changed as the Quality of Life that Nexomon 1 had where you can freely swap your moves out was great.- Your nexomon will only learn moves of their own type and maybe a normal type attacking move, so a single nexomon isn't going to be able to have move type coverage. A shame really, because I find that pretty fun to play around with in Pokemon.- I personally found most setup moves like giving yourself extra speed to be somewhat useless. Defensive setup moves do work pretty well, but I didn't find a nexomon that was particularly bulky enough to take full advantage of it.The story is a direct continuation from Nexomon 1, but many, many years into the future. I enjoyed it, but found the mid to end game a bit rushed especially with characters offering to teleport you back to X location as if the developers/writers just wanted to hurry up and get to the next scene ASAP. Characters will still very often break the fourth wall and speak to the player directly or reference that they are in a video game in a joking manner, which I found somewhat charming here, but I absolutely hated in other games, so your mileage may vary. It doesn't take itself too seriously. There is a Marvel styled joke towards the end that I facepalmed when I saw the setup for it, but you may find it funny or groan at it.This is a great game and a worthy sequel. There is also a custom mode that unlocks after you finish the game that allows you to setup a subsequent playthrough with various changes like doing a nuzlocke run, randomizing starters and other nexomon, disabling shops, or even just making the game harder by raising opposing nexomon levels. It is a terrific follow up to Nexomon 1. Absolutely recommended to give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game that has worked out many of its flaws. I'd give it a solid 6.5/10. The gameplay is a lot of fun, and the story is decent. The constant fourth wall breaks really brought the story down from what would have been an 8/10. I know many games have issues with silent protagonists, but this was one of the worst examples I've seen. However, if you're looking for a creature collector, then this game is for you. They patched in healing stones to fix the biggest issue that the negative reviewer was complaining about, and they have toned down the autoscaling. Originally, the wild Nexomon would scale to equal the level of your strongest Nexomon, however, the scaling is now gated behind different checkpoints in game. Those two adjustments address the issues that were (correctly) called out in the negative review that is on the front page. I recommend this game at $20. If you can get it on sale, even better. _childDocuments_.review: I've really wanted to like this game, but I can't. Perhaps my expectations are too high after seeing some of the designs for the Nexomon and the world's visuals, it had me hoping this would be a charming little game with a story that was at least coherent...... it was not.Here's a list of the pros and cons if you don't want to read about my experience with the first hour of the game, that rant contains spoilers but it goes into more depth about my problems with this game.Pros:- Great looking visuals- More open-ended exploring- Wide variety of Nexomon- You get to choose between starters of every type, this is probably the best positive- Lots of choices in starting character avatarsCons:- The dialogue- Despite being made in Unity, it looks and feels like an RPG Maker game, with a lot of common tropes in RPG Maker games being used here (Glowing spots for items and very out-of-place chests everywhere.)- Non-configurable controls, or at least I couldn't find any in-game- The dialogue- Very easy to lose track of what you're doing- Animations look weird- Weaknesses are confusing- The dialogue- Almost all of your 'friends' hate you- Pulls a Sonic Boom and spoils later scenes at the beginning- Inconsistent theming- The dialogue- Your best friend is a cat person. Are they a Nexomon? Are they half human? Who is the mother and who is the father? Is he a tamer? Why doesn't he have a Nexomon? Did he just forget to catch one? Is he aware of his reality? Why does he know what an RPG is? Does he cough furballs? I have no answers.Now the next section of this contains spoilers, but understand that the game spoils you on this within the first five minutes of you starting the game by pulling a Sonic Boom, so... legal spoilers??? You start off great with you're character plummeting to their death because an airship they were riding died (Which made choosing my character's avatar difficult, the screen wouldn't stop shaking violently), and then it has a hard cut to some people you aren't supposed to know or care about yet fighting a dragon who is apparently you, and you're the cause of the world ending via a sort of "Third Impact"... What an opening! I've never felt this confused within the first minute of a game! :DSo when the game actually starts at the beginning, I thought "Okay, the intro was bad, but maybe the meat of the game will make this a little better, it can't get worse." And hoo-boy, it not only got worse, it got annoyingly bad. I like to think I have a high tolerance for cheezy dialogue considering I can watch movies like Food Fight and The Room in one sitting and survive, but this game tests my limits by constantly switching between being serious, and pulling the "calling out your own tropes" every other second something happens on the screen. Going into a forest? "HAHA, this is like those RPG games!! Everyhting will go wrong! XD" Doing the capture tutorial? "HAHA, you and I both want to skip this tutorial! We could've just had a skip tutorial option, but we love this joke! XD" Breathing? "WOW, you're such a failure, how are you so STUPID?! Go die in a hole you absolute failure!" Oh yeah, did I mention that the game hates your character despite the fact that you didn't even do anything?! Because it seems like almost everyone wants to take shots at you at every dialogue choice!So yeah, definitely not my favorite game. This whole review may seem like a joke, but so does Nexomon: Extinction, it's made like a parody on games and yet none of it is funny. It might get better later on, but I had more fun in the hour it took me to write this review than in the first hour of the game, so take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: Nexomon:Extinction is a monster catching game. You as the tamer build a roster of nexomon which you then use to fight other nexomon in a turn based fashion. As you progress through the game you will find new nexomon to add to your roster or improve your existing nexomon by leveling up. You as a tamer can improve as well by finding items, which improve things like amount of exp from battles And for the price it does a great job at it. The nexomon (300+ in total) themselves look really good, they are vibrant and each of them tend to have a unique look. There are many type of nexomon: animals, humanoid, edgy ones, cute ones, ... . So all in all there is something for everyone. The only downside is that mechanically they tend to be little variation; they have a single typing and their stats and movepool seem to be pretty similar as well. Most of my nexomon played the same. This also made the roster look less like a cohesive team but rather a bunch of individual nexomon.The battle system itself is pretty good. the most interesting thing is speed and stamina. Speed helps determine whether a move will go first or not, so move with less power tend to have a higher speed. Stamina is the resource moves consume, if your nexomon has no stamina you either have to use an item or simply wait to recover stamina. Stamina does not recover after a battle. Powerfull moves use more stamina. This means that early game moves are in general fast and consume less stamina making them relevant even at the end of the game. Difficultywise the game tries to strike a balance. it tries not be so easy that you can spam your way to victory but at the same time does not require big team considerations. I just picked nexomon I liked and progressed smoothly.  It's not completely perfect some moves are clearly undertuned and some overtuned.For the rest of the game, the world is big with lots of things too explore and quest too fulfill. Each area has a unique feel and looks just stunning. You are free to move to most areas you want throughout the game. The nexomon and trainers in the areas themselves are based on your story progression so you are free to explore those areas at any time. The story is great. It had an interesting plot and was filled with a lot of interesting characters. It is a bit literred with 4th wall jokes but it wasn't over the top and it isn't overdone. So all in all I enjoyed Nexomon:Extinction a lot and would recomoned it.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster catching RPGs are a personal fave since these are usually lighthearted games that are easy to get into, and are usually a lot of fun. Nexomon Extinction caught my eye a few weeks ago, and I have definitely enjoyed this game quite a bit! Things you may like about the game are:- It's a very colorful 2d game with nice artwork and some great monster designs here and there.- It has a really good soundtrack. Seriously, some of these tracks are really good!- It takes inspiration from the earlier pokemon games so it's a more simplistic take when it comes to types and movesets, which is not really a bad thing since you'll get used to it quickly and no nexomon feels useless thanks to this.- Lots of customization options and some great QoL options that pokemon fans keep asking for pokemon games but we never get. Things such as multiple save slots (Thank goodness!), and being able to rematch trainers in the wild who keep improving their teams (Seriously, why this isn't a thing in the pokemon games?) among many others.- Features an epic story that, despite taking itself quite seriously at times, doesn't have any troubles with poking lots fun at itself and the genre quite often! (Coco and Atlas got quite a few laughs out of me, that's for sure!)- The game encourages you to consider type coverage when building your teams and training (grinding obviously!). Otherwise the game can and will get somewhat difficult if you don't!Things fans of these games may not like are:- At the moment, the game features no multiplayer content.- The game could use some extra things to do besides battling or fetching stuff to NPCs to add some variety. (Salem's little challenge early in the game was a fun little distraction, why isn't there any more of that for example?)After beating the main story, I can say with confidence I really liked this game a lot. If the more recent Pokemon games have let you down, this is a really nice alternative to consider!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. This is what I wish Pokemon currently was, and what I feel Pokemon used to be (at least, how Pokemon used to make me feel). I don't like typing out 5000 word reviews, so I'll try to keep this succint:Combat - Very fun. I think the stamina system is a 100% upgrade to the PP system (I am inevitably going to compare this to the most prolific series of the genre, sorry). There are some interesting abilities that allow for tactical choices in the combat, and not being able to sweep the entire enemy team with one of my Nexomon (assuming they are within ~10 levels of me) makes the play feel more engaging. I wish there were some more unique animations for abilities, but that's a very minor gripe. Typing is also a bit imbalanced, with some types feeling slightly stronger than others and normal type being pretty objectively the worst.Catching - This is just straight up better in every way than catching Pokemon in the core games. The ability to feed the wild Nexomon different food to increase your catch chance is neat, and the fact I can acquire a LOT of the 100% chance Nexotraps is great as a collector. I also personally enjoy the little typing minigame you do during the catch sequence, but I could see that being a downside for some people.Story - Honestly, very well put together. During my first 20 - 30 minutes of the game I felt the writing was going to be pretty weak, as it was primarily meta jokes and other sorts of humorous quips (I do enjoy the jokes, to be clear, I just assumed because of the early writing the actual story wouldn't be particularly interesting), but I was wrong. The story has plenty of awesome twists, the characters are all likable or interesting, there are some truly cool moments later on. Kudos to the writers!Travel - I like the Metroid inspired upgrades you get throughout the game (minor spoiler, sorry). It's fun to go back to places you've been before and explore new parts of them that were inaccessible before. I also like that you can tell exactly what patches of grass will trigger an encounter, so if you're just trying to get somewhere you can avoid all of the wild Nexomon. I was much less frustrated playing this game than I have been historically playing Pokemon.Items - One of my favorite parts about the game. I like that there are passive items that increase different stats or give much needed QOL features for this genre. One example is there is a stackable item that increases how much XP your Nexomon gain from battle; another is a stackable item that increases your chance of finding a shiny (called Cosmic Nexomon in this game). Story battles have also been difficult enough that I find myself using potions, revives, and elixirs frequently, causing money to have value even towards the end of the game.This review ended up being pretty wordy anyway, sorry about that!Overall personal score: 9.8/10 losing a small amount of score only for some balancing issues with typing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what Pokemon in 2020 should be. With an actual good story. -------------------Pros: --Ever feel like it was weird that no one in Pokemon was acknowledging your badassery? This one strokes your hero boner harder than any game. You will constantly be praised for saving things, advancing your rank, and a host of other things as you progress through the game, a lot of times by NPC's you have already talked to who have updated dialogue every time you advance. --Lots of awesome Nexomon to choose from with designs that honestly are better than Pokemon in a lot of cases. I find myself wanting to swap mons out way more in this since I run into so many cool ones. --Gearing up Nexomon is fun--TONS of boss fights--The catching system is much more involved. --Collecting in general. There are so many ways to advance your ability to catch, buy, get money, and other things. --Scaling wilderness areas removes the need to level up super low level nexomon if you want to switch. You can just go back later and catch a higher level one. --Scaling trainers makes for a fun challenge later. Refighting any trainer after a short cooldown,--Challenge in general. It's so much better than Pokemon on that front. Instead of fighting 30 people in a row with 1 pidgey each, you fight 2 with 5 fully evolved beasts each. 100% improvement. Items are actually useful, and you will be restocking constantly to keep your mons healthy. They are also really cheap, so can use them freely and wild encounters drop gold. --Grinding is stupidly easy with EXP items. 2-4 kills a level. --The story is actually neat. Much more involved and epic than any of the recent Pokemon games. --Freedom. You can go pretty much anywhere early on, with tons of side areas to explore. More unlocks as you get abilities. --HM's don't need an HM slave. They are just part of your character. --Tons of side stuff throughout the game. Feels like Zelda almost with how often you get distracted with another side quest or path. --It's cheap--Coco. Coco is hilarious and best companion. -------------------Neutral: --No EXP share. Some like it. You don't really need it though with scaling mons.--No PVP. Honestly I never enjoyed rock-paper-scizzors pokemon PVP, but lots do. --Only one ATK stat, no special ATK. I don't really miss it, but the complexity is nice in Pokemon--No EV/IV/Natures. Every Loki is the same as every other Loki. Personally I've always hated the grind that was EV/IV/Natures, so I'm good with it. I know a lot of people love them though. -------------------Cons: --No online trading--Nexomon only have a single type (though some of them get a lot of abilities from another type, so your normal might get tons of rock abilities) --Not a ton of side game things like Safari Zone or game corner in Pokemon--Less systems in general than Pokemon. Nexomon can wear 4 pieces of gear, but the gear is basic stat stuff. No evolution stones. No special evolution. Just level based. --No TM system --No genders and breeding, but without IV/EV its kinda pointless anyway. -------------------All in all, it's a great game. Character designs are top notch. The art is beautiful. I really hope it does well so we can get more. Expanding on this formula will only do it well. If you are tired of easier and easier Pokemon every generation, this is the answer. You can't beat it for 20 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I have played the full campaign. I guess steam hasn't updated with the cloud yet because I have over 27 in-game hrs. LolI am only talking about the main campaign. Not the expansion or the post game:I've been making my way through the majority of so-called "Pokemon clones". I hate using this term because it often muddles genuine efforts like this game as a cheap knockoff when it's really not. Something sharing similar elements to another genre doesn't inherently make it cheap. The execution is what makes the game good.Compared to Nexomon 1, Nexomon: Extinction is a great two steps forward but it's flaws also make it take one step back. Positives:-The game is definitely a step up in terms of quality. The overall feel of the game is less "cheap" compared to the first. I know this might not be fair as Nexomon 1 (N1) was made for mobile users, but the devs really worked hard to make Extinction feel like it wasn't. The environments are more expansive and memorable, the characters have more personality with a nice amount of development, NPCs are abundant and well worth talking to, Nexomon have more variety with their designs than the first game, capture mechanics have been expanded upon greatly, and the music is a genuine improvement from the blander soundtrack of the first game.-The battle system is more refined with Nexomon no longer dying in just a hit or less after spamming your strongest move. Buffs/Debuffs got a nerf. No longer do you have the confusion spam that was present in the first game (thank goodness) meaning you can't just rely on cheese strats. Nexomon have less variety with their movepoolss in this game, but more than make up for it with a better variety of Nexomon to use. As most Nexomon can evolve in this game, you're no longer feeling like that Common Nexomon you caught feels pointless to raise. It's not a strong as a rare, but that's the point anyways. You can still use it and that's what matters.-The story. I won't spoil much but the story as a sequel is a great continuation to N1's light-hearted tone while also shifting to darker storyline. It really is a wild ride from start to finish and I do think it's best to go in blind to get the full experience of all the neat twists and turns.-Dungeons are much more expansive with a decent amount of puzzles to boot. I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of dungeons to explore, even if some were dead ends.  N1's dungeons left a lot more to be desired because of how linear they were (which was found in the post game). Here, I'm glad the devs took the feedback from that to make the world feel more explorative. You can explore the begining of the game to your hearts content and visit most places within the world without an issue rather early on. Levels scale so there's no fear of missing out on something or being in an area you don't want to be in yet. The game will give you plenty of hints if you're going in the right direction.-Cores add a nice layer of depth to Nexomon by giving passive buffs. You can have only 4 cores at a time, but the benefits are crucial to surviving in battles. I found myself picking up shards because I wanted to either make them into Cores to buff my Nexomon or trade them off during side-quests. The only downsides is that Cores are limited in what you can use them for. You have Attack, Defense, Stamina, HP, Immunity to status ailments, EXP, Money, and EXP share. That's it. I wish that there was more of a variety of options (like for speed) because by late game, you aren't going to need the EXP share or Money cores when you're drowning in collectibles aka. Shards to sell/trade for money.-The music. I'll be frank, N1's soundtrack was rather bland. So while this soundtrack is certainly not winning any awards any time soon, it is a major step up from N1. There's a better variety of music that doesn't just focus on "happy track, intense track". There are a variety of background tracks and battle tracks that set the mood just right.Negatives:-Ui is a step up from N1, but lacks the streamlining found from those menus. I understand N1 was a mobile game first and foremost, but the streamlining with the game worked well. Everything was clear and easy to access. Not so much in this game. While the general UI no longer looks cheap, how it functions is a different story. You can't move your Nexomon in your party freely. You have to "Set as Main" unless you're messing with the PC. I haven't encountered any other monster-taming game that's done something like this (for modern games) and it's such a bizarre decision because N1 allows you to freely move your party. I've tried messing with the controls on my Steam Deck to see if I missed something, but I couldn't find anything. (I'll edit this review if it's fixed and I'm just missing something. Lol). However, my complaints with the UI and visual consistency don't just end with that example. There are other tiny things that really start to pile up. Specific buttons are now tied to your actions in battle, but they never feel "right" to use. I know describing controls is hard to explain, but compared to N1's tight controls, it never felt comfortable using buttons compared to a simple touch ironically. In cutscenes, your character will be shown as the default MC despite changing your skin tone/appearance. I understand this working in N1 as you couldn't change your character but here it comes off as a little jarring for story-related scenes. Now, I'm definitely not saying for the devs to redraw every design they made for your MC customizations in the cutscenes, but when other cutscene CGs don't feature your character and still work, I have to wonder why those few CGs are so visually inconsistent.-The difficulty spikes. Other reviews have mentioned this but while N1 was grinder than this game, you could catch up in levels easily due to the EXP all for every party member. You even get the ability to double the EXP you earned in that game. The issue is that Nexomon Extinction's level curve is fixed. Meaning, whatever level you're at, other Nexomon will be around the same level. This works very well in the early/mid game when exploring but not so much in the later game in which simple random encounters will send you to the Healing Center real quick. Obviously, this is not as impossible as people make it out to be, but I absolutely agree with the overall criticisms of it originally being poorly implemented for the later half of the game. Thankfully, by that point you'll have more than enough resources to manage, but when you get to that first difficulty spike it is ROUGH. The inclusion of difficulty modes was added to alleviate this, but this is a fundamental problem with how the game is designed in itself. This is why I hope for the next game, that the devs take what they learned and make things more balanced from the start.-Catching Nexomon is a double-edged sword. Nexomon have more depth in how you capture them. But with a horrible catch, a mini game. Every time you want to capture ANYTHING in this game you have to play a boring catching mini game. Press the right buttons and capture the mon. It should be simple, but I found to be rather clunky in execution. Not only does it make capturing mons more tedious, it feels intrusive to other mechanics. Even if it does increase your chance of capture, it doesn't really add to the immersion of getting a Nexomon. I think the food mechanic already did a good job, but having the mini game just felt pointless. I wish there was an option to just skip it.-You need to capture 70 Nexomon AND RELEASE THEM in an obscure sidequest to get the Portable PC and Teleporter. Why wasn't this just a key item late game? It's so tedious to get.Overall while I do recommend this Nexomon Extinction as it IS a better game than N1 in every way, there are stipulations that come with that recommendation. I want to recommend it more as I did enjoy it but it's flaws are apparent.

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a monster tamer RPG. Nexomon: Extinction is an excellent game and a fantastic follow-up to the original Nexomon. The massive step forward in pretty much all aspects from gameplay to story is very impressive.Let's get this out of the way now: It's very obvious that yes, Nexomon: Extinction is not the first game to ever attempt this genre. Just like Nexomon 1, the inspiration taken from Pokemon and similar games is obvious, and for some people that carries with it a certain expectation of similarity. It's best to let those expectations go because despite appearances, this game is very much its own thing.For one, Nexomon: Extinction has an excellent sense of self-aware humor. It knows when to crack a joke, and when to take itself seriously. I was so entertained by the characters and world that I felt a bit empty when the credits rolled. To me, that's the sign of a really well made world in a video game.The gameplay is a little bit less refined than I'd like, but I can appreciate it for what it is. Battles are very straight forward and your go-to strategy will probably always be to use a buff if you have one, then spam your strongest attack until you run out of stamina. Rinse and repeat. In the next game, I'd like to see a more involved battle system with more nuance and harder decisions.As a whole, this game is very impressive and definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: The short summary is that this is a masterpiece of epic proportions. The long, well...Story. The start of the game is probably the weakest part of the entire plot. You live in an Orphanage, you head out, you encounter a woman with anger issues. A few minutes later, you got attacked by a Dragon, time suddenly stopped, you're forced to pick a Starter to fight for your life (and lose duh) before a Ghost saved you by opening a hole to a cave beneath a statue. I never understood why the Dragon just stood there and waited for your cat to drag you inside after going through the trouble to kick your ass, btw. I wouldn't go as far as to say that it's a bad impression, but it was a meh one for sure. The early meta jokes certainly didn't help to improve said impression either.  If some people quit the game, it must be within the first hour or so. Anyone who survives that basically gets hooked in until the end.That being said, the plot improved drastically once you're about an hour into the game, and it never stopped getting better until the very last moment. I won't spoil the overall plot, but suffice to say it can probably be sold as a movie trilogy and actually not flop. The writing is very strong, and the attention to detail is very appreciated, especially the part where opinions of you change as you clear a main story quest or ascend a Tamer rank. If I remember correctly, a generic guard can have up to 7 lines based commenting on your progress and achievements, and considering that there are hundreds of NPCs in the game, it's incredibly impressive.Gameplay. Gotta have to keep this short because there are so many things to talk about. Nexomon differs greatly from other Pokemon or Pokemon-like games in that you don't level up your Nexomon to play, or at least the method won't hold the more you progress the story. More specifically, you focus all the experience on one super powerful Nexomon that can 1 versus infinite like a super boss and then just keep changing the other 5 so they don't fall behind in levels due to dynamic difficulty. This is because the amount of experience you get for defeating a Nexomon that outlevels you by 10 is still piss poor, and it's faster to just capture a Nexomon in the wild anyway. I personally don't have problems with this, it's a refreshing change to the grind formula and one that I actually like.And no, I'm not telling you what Nexomon I'm using to 1 versus everything, dev. You ain't nerfing my main, and that's that.Money. You're always going to be short on money. Even if you can farm Elemental Shards to save money on Nexotraps, the need for consumables is still going to drain your money like a sink. Even if you grit your teeth and fight 10 trainers in a row, and THEN capture Nexomon in the wild to catch up in levels, you're still going to run out of cash very soon, so that's a problem. I'm pretty sure people hate dynamic difficulty because of this.Nexomon battles. Frankly, it doesn't have the complexity of a Pokemon game. Stats are extremely basic. In fact I think that most Nexomon share the same stats, only separated by their rarity. There are only like 10 real skills per Nexomon(?) and they loop again and again as you level up, although this is a good thing because this means you don't have to go to a relearner constantly. Also, they don't matter that much. There's a joke in the game that goes something like: "You only use one move over and over anyway!" and that's true for the the other 5 Nexomon you're constantly recapturing. In the end the goal is to kick the enemy's ass so a move that gets the job done is a move.Flow. Probably the best thing about the game besides the story. It's hard to describe, but I can feel the amount of hours the devs and the game testers put into the game to make the gameplay loop as fluid as possible. Things feel natural and intuitive, and once you shed your old Pokemon shackles and embrace the Nexomon formula you find it very, very pleasing. You take less overall damage if you just suck it up and feed the wild Nexomon, so just do it, idiot.Puzzles, or almost the lack thereof. There aren't many puzzles, and I appreciate that to hell and back because I HATE puzzles in a game like this. There were some Pokemon fangames that I adored but could never muster the strength to play again because their puzzles are as nightmarish as they are genius.Warpstones, or your equivalent of a world map. The exclusion of a mini map of sorts is definitely a risk the dev took, but it also made me memorize practically every location except the caves, so overall I believe it was the right move. I still want an Escape Rope/Smoke Bomb equivalent though, especially since everyone in the god dang world seem to have the ability to teleport to somewhere except you.Characters. This both a plus and a minus. If we just look at interaction with minor characters, then it's the most well done in an RPG game I've ever seen. You get a clear perception of how the people of each city function etc, and as mentioned both most of them have plenty of dialogue. The bad? Everyone's a minor character besides Coco and the miner girl, shockingly. You feel disconnected to pretty much everyone else, including your "rivals" because they just don't have much scenes. This also diminishes the feeling you get when a certain scene happen very near the end game. Even the Tyrants left a bigger impression than the rivals, and that's saying something. Flaws. The standout is obviously no "new game+", or more accurately no teleporting you back to the world after credits roll. Does it make story sense? Not really, but this is one part I feel like the game should just say ♥♥♥♥ it and let us enjoy whatever content we haven't cleared yet. The rest are very minor. Some I already mentioned above like almost simple battles and characters etc. There are hardly any bugs, although the one I remember was Renovate not clearing status conditions despite advertising so, and the middle trader in Lateria saying "Yes I can finally sell you my wares at a reasonable price!" and then the dialogue just ends there. For now I can't think of anything else but nitpicks so I guess I'll leave it here.All in all, absolutely don't regret my hours spent on this game. Easily the best single player Pokemon-like game I've ever played ever, so much so that I'm DEFINITELY not playing the first Nexomon because I'm almost certainly it would disappoint me and pollute my good feelings for Nexomon: Extinction. Also the rating for that game was pretty meh. But really, this game is great. Absolutely worth the money, time and energy I spent on.P.S. Oh, I remember one flaw now. You took away our attack on Parum, you should've at least let us drop Amelia in a pit of spikes or something, like come on.

_childDocuments_.review: When compared to the likes of Pokemon, Nexomon has a better, more interesting main story, hard(er) 'mon battles, and a massive variety of 'mons, side-quests and other content that really keep one going. However; the bug when using healing items is annoying and something I wish would be fixed; the typing's are varied but not that new or unique enough to warrant the amount and are thus repetitive; some parts are a slog to get through since an ass load of story is piled on at certain parts without much room for a break in between, and is something I wish was mitigated with more trainer battles; certain battles are an endurance run and therefore very boring / not fun, and are made worse by not having better healing points or flat-out not healing you after key battles that lead into another two or three key battles; and finally, there are typos sprinkled throughout the game but don't detract from the game to much that they are a major problem. Overall, I really loved my time with Nexomon, and plan to play the end-game content since I have enjoyed this game very much, but there are bugs that can be annoying and kind of game-breaking to deal with, endurance battles with very minimal or no healing checkpoints, and run-of-the-mill 'mon typing's drop this games score to a 7/10, but is definitely a massive improvement over the original title, Nexomon. Highly recommended to pick this up while on-sale or at full-price for a great creature collector / Pokemon-like with tens of hours of entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: While there are some minor inconvenience to the game, i think the good FAR outweight the bad. Everyone claims it as a Pokemon clone, which is fairness it somewhat is, but it does enough to seperate itself from it.Pros:- Monsters are actually really good looking. Everyone has a charm of their own and it makes you wish you had a lot more room in your party.- The game doesn't really force you on one single path. The open-ness of the paths are really refreshing. Pokemon (especially the later games) always have you on a single track and you never feel like you get the mons you like until the game tells you you can. Here you can kinda go anywhere.- The story is really endearing. The writing has some quirky jokes that sometimes break the fourth wall. I enjoy it.- Quests are fun. They don't feel like chores and you can kind of get to them whenever. - The catching mechanic is a series of QTE which is really fun (but can get tedious after repeated misses)- While you can't customize your character, there's a lot of variety to choose your avatar so it still feels rich and unique.- I love that the game offers you a starter of whichever elements you want and that you can actually find them in the wild with enough searching.Cons:- The typing chart is pretty convoluted. It's hard to know what works against what and what's resisted by what. There's no answer flat out after a few hours in so you kind of have to figure it out past the obvious Water -> Fire deal.- The battle menu is a bit clunky. Running away always send you a prompt, or catching something requires some extra steps then just pressing A but overall those are rather minor inconvenience.- There's a severe lack of healing which adds to the challenge, which is nice but always get you to backtrack.- The game doesn't use a system of PP but rather Stamina, which is almost always empty. It can be annoying if it's your last monster and it's too tired to battle.All in all, I absolutely recommend the game if you enjoy the monster capture genre. It's well worth it's full price and I would recommend it to all my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I went in just wanting "sort of pokemon but on PC". I neither expected nor wanted more. I was blindsided by an absolutely fantastic writing and story. A mostly hilarious and friendly tone telling a tragic story in a way that just works. It's a tragicomedy that constantly breaks the fourth wall, amidst a pokemon-like experience. If you're a pokemon fan looking for something different, especially if, gen after gen you keep hoping for an actual good story and characters, this is it. If you're a pokemon fan, get it on those grounds alone.If you're not a pokemon fan, let's talk about the bad.The battle system is simplistic pokemon. The leveling moves are often nonsensical, you unlock worse moves as you progress, and pokemon only ever learn their own type and normal moves. (Or normal moves + another type if normal.) These make the experience feel both easier to read and less interesting to play. It's okay, nothing heinous by any means, but a missed opportunity. If they make a sequel, that's the part they should improve.That said, even with those cons, the battle system has some things that are absolutely great. Trainers switch on you constantly, keeping you on your toes instead of just standing there getting bashed super effectively. They do it just enough to be challenging but not enough to be annoying. The core system, while pretty shallow, is an interesting take. The game's big upside are bosses. They are actual bosses and feel difficult. Grandmaster tamers will absolutely dumpster you if you go there underleveled or carelessly, tyrants (legendaries) will eat your face off if you let them, overall a very pleasurably challenging experience that i wish pokemon games would copy.The world also scales with you at specific story triggers, keeping every trainer fight interesting and wild encounter relevant to your party. Overall, it is truly a great experience. It has flaws, of course, but it is a very enthusiastic recommendation from me.Play this !

_childDocuments_.review: So I've spent a few hours in the game so far, and while it presents a lot of interesting dynamics to the genre, I don't think I can quite recommend it yet.  First is the battle system- I think it's interesting, but limited. I really like the idea of having a single stamina pool rather than each move having it's own uses like in other games, but for at least the early game (as I'm only about 4 hours in so far), pretty much every single battle against an equally leveled opponent depletes nearly all of my stamina, which if I'm trying to train up that one monster to be more in line with the rest of my team, results in my running back and forth to a healer pretty much every battle, which is a big minus on my part. That, when accounting that it splits XP if multiple monsters participate and there is no EXP Share as far as I can tell, means that leveling up your nexomon is an incredible grind    The type system is pretty simple, with there only being 9 types total with each having 2 weaknesses and usually 2 or 3 resistances, but each monster only has a single type and that makes me wonder why there are so many Nexomon? There are really only 3 stats to worry about aside from HP and Stamina (Attack, defense, and speed), so none of the nexomon of the same type really feel all that different aside from their appearance. Like, once you find a rare nexomon of a certain type, there seems to be very little reason to ever use one of the common ones. Second, thus far the game has done an awful job of informing me of the game mechanics. There are these types, but after looking high and low for some in-game teacher (ala Trainer Schools in pokemon for example), there appears to be no one willing to explain the basic information you would need to know. What do the status effects do? Damned if I know, I can't find any explanation in-game. I get if you don't want to bog us down with a forced tutorial, but at least have like, an in-game manual or some NPCs that will explain mechanics for those of us that would rather do that than go to google. My 3rd complaint is really just personal preference, as I've seen in other reviews that other people love this so I'm in the minority but- I really hate the game's humor. The game presents the world as being in a bad way; the Nexomon Tamers are the only bastion against these Tyrant monsters, and humanity is on the brink of extinction, and the story has been touted as a main selling point... but then every other NPC breaks the 4th wall, if you walk into people's houses without being a high ranking tamer, they complain about protagonists breaking into people's homes, NPCs say there aren't that many towns because of lazy developers, that people are loitering around because it's expensive to draw them walking, etc. Just immediately takes me out of the world when every other interaction is a tongue-in-cheek joke on either the genre or games as a whole. Also, I really, really, very much so, HATE the companion we are forced to walk around, who also breaks the 4th wall constantly and doesn't seem to have a high opinion of your character. I would leave them behind in an instant if I were given the option.The art is good, I like the music and the stage design, the monster designs are cool and cute, but the things I listed above have annoyed me and lessened my enjoyment

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't revolutionary but it is good.  It does a number of things better than Pokemon.  A quick list of some things I like1: Fast battle animations2: Nice art work and scenery (I like the background and environment art better than the monsters)3: I like that Nexomon are static with their stats and not the random BS that Pokemon does4: You can farm money any time, even by wild encounters.  5: Game plays smooth and I haven't ran into any bugs yet6: The game has a good sense of humor and quite a number of funny bits here and there.7: This is a real game, none of that gacha garbage.  Just buy the game and enjoy.A quick list of things that I don't care for1: Too many new Nexomon early on.  As someone completely new to the series it seems like every area I enter has a good handful of new Nexomon and I don't know one from the other.  It's kind of overwhelming2: The Nexomons don't have any special abilities, only up to four attacks and it doesn't look like there are that many different types of attacks.3: Nearly all of the Nexomon I find seem to have very close to or exactly the same stats (Between completely different Nexomon).  This could change a lot as they level up more, but right now there is hardly any difference between one or another.Overall, if you like critter collecting/battling games like this then I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been wanting to fill a void in monster taming gameplay that pokemon has left, and this game absolutely surpassed my expectations! It makes me wonder how the genre hasn't expanded more than it already has. I'd love to see more like this in the future!Pros:✦Beautiful art direction and animation✦Stellar creature design✦Great writing and a truly captivating plot that kept me enthralled throughout my whole playthrough✦All the player avatar options and the ability to change it anytime mid-gameCons:✦Inability to use status moves on bosses meant they were kind of redundant when normal enemies could be killed in 2-3 hits✦Status moves in question didn't feel like their percentages mattered, anything that had a 30% hit rate and under might as well have been at 0%✦Odd that nexomon would learn weaker damaging moves at high levels✦The final boss was more a test in how many health potions you were able to use than actual skill✦It was frustrating that after a full party wipe that all the items I used in the fight would be gone and my nexomon wouldn't be healed afterwardsWould have been cool if:✦The avatar the player chose could have showed up in the CGs/cutscenes rather than always showing the default character avatar✦We could choose the exact nexomon that follows us (maybe those that we've caught) instead of having to find a select few throughout the game

Something like a dynamic difficulty where you can just play the main game and finish with as low level as possible can! But unfortunately, they didn't do that, and did what every other type of this game does, GRIND until you actually get so bored that you don't finish the game rofl.The game has really good humor. As for the rematch and npc battles, It was pretty rewarding so that part is all good. And for wild encounters, just don't venture too much because story wise you'll be brought back to cities by npc, but if you venture into wild areas too deep you'll have to walk  yourself back.Nexomon designs cool as always! And the story is so immersive that it's basically a rpg. If you're into monster capturing games, dont miss this game. Totally worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid 9/10.Nexomon is quite possibly my favourite game in the monster-catching genre. Some may argue that the combat system is too simplistic, but as someone who plays games to wind down and relax, I find myself quite thankful for it. However the fact that the level of the tamers and monsters scale to your party level can get quite annoying as it means you will constantly have to backtrack and heal up. The graphics and art style are absolutely stunning! I am not much of a fan of the pixel art style, so this is a huge plus for me. The Nexomon themselves are well-designed and really nice to look at. The story is alright, and the character development is... eh.Coco, the cat companion is annoying but in an endearing sort of way, and I absolutely love him. This may be controversial, but I also do like how the game breaks the fourth wall pretty frequently. The sense of humour in this game may not be for everyone, but it definitely made me laugh a lot.All in all, I would definitely recommend this title to anyone looking for a fun game in the monster-catching genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Nexomon: Extinction

_childDocuments_.review: This review is for those who are put off by the artwork.Even after 40+ hours, the cover art makes me want to load up a different game. The good news is once you start playing it's borderline addictive.Highlights- Interesting lore & story. My favorite games are usually JRPGS, and the writers did a good job with this. There are some genuine laugh-out-loud moments and a fun climax.- Combat is a decent challenge. There's an emphasis on type advantage and buffs/debuffs. Nexomon don't learn moves outside their type, so you're supposed do a little planning with your party to cover any weaknesses. The A.I will switch out to gain the advantage (quite a few times).- Quests & Exploration. There's a quest system that offers good rewards. You're even able to acquire multiple copies of the golden Nexotrap (which gives 100% catch rate). Exploration is fun; there are hidden areas, vaults to unlock, equipment/abilities that allow further exploration.- Continued game support. After launch the devs have listened to feedback and rebalanced bosses, added exp boost, and even added a custom mode! You can play the game with built in "Nuzlocke" rules, start a new game plus, remove the Nexomon level cap, randomize trainer battles, randomize wild Nexomon, randomize move sets, etc. This adds so much replay value.Room for Improvement- Nexomon customization. Currently the only thing we have is Synergy cores, which are gems that gives various buffs, and relearning old moves. There are no "min-maxing" options and Nexomon stats are very similar across the board. This allows you to play with whatever 'mons you think look the best, for better or for worse.- Filling out the Dex. For a single player game, this is way more time consuming than it should be. Everything in the world scales with your party (up to a point), which means stage 1 'mons are nearly impossible to find in the late game. There's no trading, breeding, or in-game ways to track where wild Nexomon are located. Don't get me started on the encounter rates for some of the Legendaries. As a completionist, this game is a bit of a nightmare.- Combat depth. Outside of type match-ups and your usual buffs/debuffs there's not a lot going on. If you want Radical Red levels of strategy, you'll have to stick to that game for now. There's a lot of potential with the synergy cores. But that's up for future iterations to improve on.SummaryBuy it! For 20 bucks it's one of the best creature collectors out there (in a genre the surprisingly sparse). The Nexomon designs are very hit or miss, but you'll find enough that look great. This games deserves more attention!
_childDocuments_.name: Nexomon: Extinction

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It's a bit different from the first Nexomon game so when I started playing it, I was a little confused but you get used to the changes really quickly. I wasn't sure how I was going to like it at first, because they initially made the game A LOT harder than the what you're used to. I went through so many traps trying to catch Nexomon, I swear it was like every 5th one I tried catching let me catch it, all the others broke out. Leveling up was also really rough and it seemed like you had to stay behind in a zone and level up more to be able to fight the Nexomon that were found in the next zone, even if you had quests ready for that next zone. Luckily, the devs realized how rough this game was and fixed the issues and it's a lot more fun. I definitely recommend. Pros:- Super adorable and fun Nexomon to catch!- The art is great and all of the zones are fun to play in.- The prices for stuff you need, like traps and potions etc., are fairly priced. - There are either towns or medics close enough where you don't have to stray too far with knocked out Nexomons and no one to fight with, but far enough where you still need to be strategic about your potion usage and 'mon catching.Cons: - None of the Nexomon from the first game are in this one which is a bummer because there were some from the first game I really loved and wanted on my team. - Some of the conversations can be a bit silly, since some of the characters just say ridiculous things at times. For example, I was called a "scrub" early on. It's 2020, people. XD- If you want to swap the Nexomon in your party with the ones back at the computer, you have to be at a computer. Sadly, we don't get the option to do it from within our inventory, like you might with Pokemon in Sword/Shield. That would be a cool thing to add. Overall, I love this game and definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: TRUE VISUAL MASTERPIECE.Let me tell you why. You think think this is just another "mobile" port? Wrong. What's bad about typical mobile visual (HD + 2D) is they use 2D assets with skeletal animation that squeezes and stretches the assets, resulting in weird artistic output (bad). Some PC games do it too and the result is as expected: artistically weak. This game also use skeletal animation (if that is the right term) but it does it in a way that doesn't squeeze and stretch 2D assets like common mobile games, resulting in the output being closer to true realtime 3D rendering (on the characters, npc, monsters). Except you don't need fancy anti alias to make the edges looks smooth like in realtime 3D rendering coz the 2D assets already be smoothened like crazy. Basically like the characters in Harvest Moon: Back to Nature. Visually looks like sprite animation but based on actual 3D model. There is consistency that you would expect from 3D model. This game is just like that but with 2020 technology. Ain't that fancy.I am very glad to buy this game. HD 2D art in games should be either like this or classic sprite animation. Squeezing + stretching 2D assets in the fashion of many mobile games is weird man, nobody should ever do that.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: This game is fantastic, i would highly recommend, funny and engaging story, and excellent game play that has challenging aspects. _childDocuments_.review: edit: i think i reviewed this game too early. the story is 10/10, genuinely. and levelling becomes much less of a problem with the cores you acquire/craft yourself. overall i really enjoyed this game and i highly recommendif you're looking for a pokemon clone, this honestly isn't a bad one. the creature designs are good, the story is interesting with some humour sprinkled in. the battle system is extremely simplistic which i feel isn't necessarily good or bad, but it does make the game more accessible and less frustrating. however, i do feel like there are needlessly frustrating elements to the game. one of them being how slow it is to level up your nexomon. within the 14 hours i've played so far, my nexomon are only really averaging around level 26 or 27 or so. another frustrating thing is that, when your party faints, you teleport to the last place you healed... with half of your nexomon's health remaining. why not just have the nexomon restored to full health? it's extra steps that don't make the game more challenging, but more time consuming over the course of a playthrough and mildly infuriating.overall, i think it's an enjoyable pokemon clone with an appealing art style, pretty decent designs and a fun story. i also think it's nice to have the choice of what to do next, as you can select quests depending on what you feel like doing, something that i feel pokemon doesn't really have. the main cons are only really things that are mildly frustrating and don't totally ruin your experience, as long as you don't mind some grinding and travelling back and forth between places.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the better Pokemon clones out there, and I definitely 100% recommend it.I'll skip the pros and just write the cons, since there's already a ton of people already covering that stuff.Cons:1. All the Nexomons feel really samey with their stats, there's not really any that have stats WILDLY different than anyone else, like there's none that have way more health than another, or any built like a glass cannon (except maybe dragons). I get that the devs probably intended that as a way to allow players to just pick what they think looks cool, but it makes it more boring in my opinion.2. No traits on any Nexomons. Same as con #1, all of them are just stats+moves+type, no traits to help make them feel different from each other. Also I was really expecting the thief mice to have something like Pickup.3. RNG-heavier than Pokemon, annoyingly. Too many moves come with statuses that have awfully low status rates, and even the non-damaging status moves usually have a 70% chance to work. Heck, I've got almost six hours into the game and I've literally never seen the grass starter's poison move actually poison anything.4. The not-Pokedex isn't great. There's no faster way to scroll through it, there's no location function, none of the sorting tabs are labeled, and I wish there was a way to sort by stats.5. Yuck, level scaling. I don't know if it's tied to the story progression or if they're really scaling automatically, though.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and charming monster collecting game with an enjoyable story. Journeying across the continent and the many habitats we are provided numerous opportunities to fight and discover these unique Nexomon. This game is unafraid to break the fourth wall, and while this may be disconnecting, does offer moments of levity, self-awareness, and express the love the developers have for their product.A massive positive for this game was its inclusion of the Custom Save, allowing us to take on many fun challenges like Nuzlocke or Randomizer with full game support.Though I will list what I found negative please understand that I have greatly enjoyed this game and don't feel any of the issues listed should deter others from playing it. The game is great regardless of my percieved issues, I intend to keep playing and enjoying myself, and I'm looking forward to what VEWO may create in the future.-Straightforward: While there are plenty of side missions/stories to entertain ourselves the game is very direct with its story. It may have benefitted from more time/opportunities to interact with and learn of the world and the people we ally with.-Endgame: This is an arguable issue as the Custom Save system serves as an infinite option for replay-ability. However, the game, outside of collecting the Boss Nexomon, lacks significant challenges or activities after you beat the main story. A tourney system, new area, or Post-Game story could've aided this.-Level Scaling: This is an issue I'm conflicted on. While I love that we can train anywhere and see more Nexomon as the enemies progress in difficulty to the story, it makes it significantly harder to search for specific Nexomon when we're now faced with all the evolutions of an area. Perhaps having determined locations (and an indicator of them in the Nexopedia) for wild Nexomon would've solved the search issue. And instead of only adding evolutions, that can reach the 3rd/Final form, introducing new enemies locked at lower levels would've made it more rewarding to return to these areas.-NPC's: In relation to my first point on story, we just don't get enough time to get to know the people around us. Ross gets humorous moments, but he and Nora don't get enough time to develop as Friends/Rivals for the MC, this is a shame as I'd have loved to work with/fight against them more often to learn more about them. Coco is a dear and constant companion, but it may have been nicer to have a chance to stop and talk to him, or see him fighting with his own Nexomon. Finally we don't get to see many other Tamers, save sparse moments with the Gold ranked, and it would've been great to work alongside or see/hear how others were faring in shared/different missions.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I recommend this game for anyone who likes playing Pokemon games for just the main story world stuff, or people who aren't really into the complex battle related stuff of Pokemon.The story is surprisingly interesting. There are good twists, the main steps in the plot made sense and the world was suitably interesting to work with without feeling too much of a drag at any point. My only problem with the story writing would be that it feels like there are too many 4th break references, but thats honestly just a personal taste.Gameplay is a lot simpler than Pokemon. Theres the standard set of Health/Stamina/Attack/Defence/Speed and the range of Elements that the Nexomon are categorised in, each with weaknesses and strengths in regards to attacking/being attacked. But thats basically it. There doesnt appear to be hidden stat values like EV/IV and you can't really modify a Nexomon's stats apart from using the in-game swapping buff core system. This isn't really a good/bad thing, just something to keep in mind.There have been some feedback about having a EXP Share in the game and at time of playing they had added it in. While it takes some effort to get, if you get enough it actually works more efficiently/effectively than it does in the Pokemon games.One big thing of note is the world of Nexomon itself. It scales up depending on how many fights you have done (i think?) as well as your progress in the main story. Its also free roaming when you get to an early point in the game, albeit with some blocked off areas that need story progress. This means that its nearly impossible to get an absurdly powerful Nexomon to just sweep through story progression with, but even I managed to get a decent team that was at least 10 levels ahead of what the NPC's had at times. The free roaming was an interesting choice, but it does hurt the story a bit when you get to places you've already wandered around in and your expected to look surprised.Overall while this game might struggle to have a non-Pokemon comparison it honestly does itself justice. I played this having never played the first Nexomon, so maybe one day I'll give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn in by the art style, but in all honesty this game is basically a cheap ripoff of pokemon and neopets. I can't get past the first area because the leveling up system is so difficult. Capturing new creatures is a waste of time if they aren't the same level as you because is take literally forever to level up. I was annoyed with the idea of having an SP bar and level 10 moves cost 15 SP when you start out with only 100, making leveling up extremely tedious, i would have one or two battles, backtrack to the medic tent to heal which was three-four maps away depending where i was grinding, and rinse and repeat.I played an hour of this game and only got one creature up three levels. I personally won't be playing this and from now on be cautious in trying any Pokemon game ripoff.

_childDocuments_.review: Come on. I loved the first one so much. This one is so much better than the original in every single way... Except, well... I'll let anyone reading this know that you should watch out for 2 things (these things alone ruined the game completely for me) :1: Everything in the world levels up as you do. Trainers, wild battles, bosses ESPECIALLY, everything. Oh but it's not based on your levels, no. It's based on how many fights you've won. Captured a level 10 and want to level him up later in the game? Too bad, everything around you is now level 33 and that level 10 is literally useless, even if you go back to the first area in the game; everything's level 33.2: DO NOT level only one nexomon up. DO NOT focus on one character and let him carry you. Why? Well, that tactic works for about half the game (way too well, I might add) BUT then the game suddenly throws you into an area where you have to fight 3 trainer battles in a row with no healing between them and no item usage. It doesn't matter if your nexomon is 23 levels higher than the opponents (that's how it was for me), they WILL destroy you because you can't heal him. It's like going against an army of 5,000,000 ants. They each don't do hardly any damage to you, but the sheer longevity of the fight to kill each one drains your nexomon to where they WILL eventually faint (I tried 3 times with various core combinations (cores are items that change your nexomon's stats, and can be interchanged on the fly) but I just CANNOT proceed past that battle sequence. "Well why don't you level up the rest of your party?" Read the previous point. Because I captured the rest of my party so early in the story, I now can't level them up at all. Also, the game doesn't have EXP share as an item otherwise I WOULD USE IT. The first game had it, but this one? Nope. I heard they plan on adding it eventually, so until they do this will remain a negative review simply because the developers don't allow for my playstyle until I reach a certain point in the game in which they then PUNISH you for playing that way and get you softlocked 20 hours into a playthrough.No, I am NOT making another save file and starting over. This is just bad game design. I will swap this review if they can simply do two things:1: Add exp share. Some of us don't want to spend hours levelling up our entire party (Seriously, I spent 20 hours levelling up a single nexomon and I'm not even halfway through the game. I don't know how you people can level up an entire party. ESPECIALLY with...)2: REMOVE THE RUBBERBANDING ENCOUNTERS. I don't know what else to call it, but the thing where the world levels up as you do. Developers, let me give you a hint: There is a reason no other RPG has done this before; it's because IT DOES NOT WORK. If you're not going to remove it COMPLETELY, then add an option to DISABLE IT. I have nothing against it being in the game, just do not make it MANDATORY. To me; the more options a game has, the better, even if I don't use them all because I understand some people might like it that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Nexomon: Extinction

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:The main draw of these types of games is the monsters. The Nexomon are generally well designed (honestly, the only ones I don't really care for are the legendaries which tend to look like giant monsters with lots of spikes).The story is engaging, the graphics are charming. Way better than any modern Pokemon game, imo. The game mechanics are really fun. I was surprised that I actually enjoyed the pickaxe mechanic, I thought it was going to get old really quick, but the payoffs are good and there's something really satisfying about popping some gemstones (maybe it's the sound fx?). I also enjoyed the scaling of all the monsters which means that over-levelling one huge monster does not solve the game.Negatives:I think the combat could be deeper. There's very little reason to use attacks that do not deal damage. Most status effects do very little. There is no real reason to play a monster over another of the same type and level other than the difference in stats. Meaning that all monsters will play the same role on a team. I know that not all games can go super deep on these type of stuff and it seems that the devs decided to spend their time making the casual play and the story more interesting which is fine.I do like that the weakness and resistance does not immediately mean win or loss and that it's very unlikely you're going to be one-shotted by some enemy monster.
_childDocuments_.name: Nexomon: Extinction

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, for what it's worth.TLDR; Get this game if you played the first one or are really into Pokemon-like games. Otherwise, don't.I played the first game on another platform, so I kind of had to get this one too. Extinction does build upon the original game quite a bit, in terms of lore, but you won't really ever feel lost if you didn't play the original. Most of the story building from the previous game is basically trivial. Although, it did feel kind of cool to understand every aspect about the past of the story, so you should play the original if you're into that. Otherwise, you can play this one without doing so.As for the gameplay, it's honestly okay. I thoroughly enjoyed myself for the entire game, but there were a few things that bothered me. Firstly, the game constantly makes the monsters you encounter be at or slightly higher than your current highest leveled Nexomon's level. This was really annoying sometimes because it felt like there was no good reason to level up other than to beat your opponents, which brings me to my next point. The type-system in this game is somewhat frivolous. The only thing that really matters is your level, as well as the general strength of your Nexomon's moveset. This actually made it kind of tedious to beat this certain part of the game, keep in mind I'm using the word 'tedious' and not 'difficult', because, in terms of difficulty, this game has none. You are essentially constantly guided into where you need to go and what you need to do. Whenever that wasn't the case, it would instead just be tedious and frustrating instead of fun.Also, don't be fooled by rarities in this game. Those all mean nothing. What I mean by that is that the legendary ones are literally stronger than the commons by a hair. And if I'm wrong about this....well, it doesn't matter, because it certainly feels that way.I know I just trashed all over this game for the most part, but I enjoyed it. The character designs are great, for the most part and the story is also pretty good. For $20, it's worth it. Although, I'd only recommend it if you've played the first game, or are really itching for a Pokemonesque experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Great art- Self aware dialogue that gave me a few chuckles- Challenging, a bit too much at times, but it  feels right- Unique movesetsCons- Animations are fast but feel too fast at times which made it hard for me to grasp what was happening until I got used to it. I feel like a better battle log system would help with this especially because many moves have second abilities to them other than just damage. There is sort of a battle log system in the bottom left but it goes by way too fast to even read what is happening. I'll put this in here too but determining type advantages was pure trial and error which was a bit annoying if you're too used to Pokemon and I feel like a more advanced log system would help new players figure things out quicker.- Nexomon in the world scale rather than being a set range for the entire game (just an opinion and I recommend new players experience it first hand before judging off this review)- Stamina < Power PointsMy first hour was great. I was really into the art style, the music was catchy and relaxing, and the world/story felt new and interesting. I wanted to keep playing to discover more Nexomons and progress the story, so I did. Six hours later I'm finding myself kind of frustrated yet not at the same time. I think all of my years playing Pokemon have spoiled this "monster/pet battling" genre for me so this game felt like a chore to keep playing but I was also enjoying myself. It really is a huge leap in difficult from the hand holding recent Pokemon games give you. My biggest complaint is the leveling system. I progressed to the 2nd major fight using the same 2-3 Nexomons while switching them around to keep them at similar levels. This is similar to how I would approach Pokemon. Once I got to into the fight, I immediately felt useless and I barely won after spamming potions and ethers. Even lesser battles up to this point felt super difficult and, at times, unwinnable but I prevailed to the major fight. It felt like I was severely underleveled even though my levels matched (+1/-1) those of the opposition.I backtracked a bit to derail from the main story and catch some new Nexomon with different types to get some diversity in my team and see some new faces. However, was met with the tedious challenge of grinding any Nexomon that I caught to a similar level so it could compete. This game has world scaling levels. All wild Nexomon scale up as you progress. Grinding any new Nexomon you catch to a similar level of your main party absolutely sucked. I was barely winning 1v1s with my new Nexomon against wild Nexomons with type disadvantage at similar levels. I would fight 1 wild Nexomon, have to either backtrack and heal at a camp or use the potions I was saving for important battles, and repeat the process. Switch training doesn't really work in this game either as I rarely OHKO wild Nexomons and the experience gain from splitting is so very small. I enjoy this game's uniqueness especially after wishing Pokemon would evolve it's core for once but I personally feel that world scaling is the wrong approach.
