_childDocuments_.review: This is a really really good game. Frankly it's fantastic with a few downpoints.+Extremely good monster designs! There's a few duds but overall some amazing designs with many to love+Stamina instead of PP as a system is a good balancer+Really really good STORY. who plays pokemon for the story? But I found I got really engaged in the plot. there were jokes I laughed at! Characters I enjoyed! I got really into the lore and mysteries. It's a sequel, I later learned, so there's characters from the first game... but because it takes place hundreds of years later, it doesn't feel too past-plot reliant. In fact, most old characters are ghosts now, adding to the atmosphere of it being post-apocalyptic+yes, that's right, this game has ATMOSPHERE. it takes place in a current-post apocalypse world and it feels quite spooky how you are exploring around bomb craters, old cars, ancient ruins of modern cities, and even a downed trainline. The plot and such matches this. It feels like the good happy days were in the past, and you're in this broken, struggling world. with cute monsters.+A challenge!! the game levels with you, so fights never get to the point of you being able to just slay easily. The last few fights are actually hard, and especially the final boss! I hated that prick so much!+Open world ish. You can very early on freely explore the world. The plot limits some areas, and you'll likely revisting places you've been before when you follow it, but it's nice how you can explore almost everywhere right away and catch a huge variety for your team.Downsides of note-There's no tutorial really. This is a plus in some ways, but also is frustrating when it comes to status effects and type advantages. You learn types eventually, but it's a lot to pick up without a guide. Status effects have no explanation anywhere, which is tricky. A lot of them overlap in strange ways (like puzzled VS confused)-If you want to 100%, as I did, it takes a while. I beat the game after 32 leisurely hours, but to 100% it took me 53. Most of that was grinding the nexomon database. The trick is that the encounter rate for mega rares is very very low, and for legendaries it's about 2%. it can take hours to find one. you will grind a lot. getting to level 99 is not hard when you consider the grinding you'll do to catch them all.-There's a place where the majority of rare nexomon are, and it's just a small island. This feels fun when you first explore it, as it's full of cool nexomon... but then when you go grinding you realize it's TOO MANY. Most zones have like 5 or 6 nexomon types, one patch on the island will have 12. Additionally, encounter rates in many places aren't based on screens, but on specific patches of grass- and in large patches, it'll be sides of parts of grass. This means if you're hunting in the right area, you still may not have any luck because you're on the wrong part of the grass.-When you try to fight every trainer (twice) there's no way to keep track of this, and it also means a lot of grinding.-basically, don't try to 100% unless you're ready to grind

_childDocuments_.review: Warmly recommend this game.It successfully scratches the Pokemon itch, easily one of the best games of it's genre currently on steam both by price tag and content it offers.Story is interesting enough to hook you in with twists, turns and a little bit of 4th wall breaking.The grind i felt was self imposed, mostly due to previous experiences in other games. I found myself levels way above the opposition but after doing side activities the difficulty level picked up the pace and i found myself right back into the leveling curve. This game offers quality of life mechanics that are very much appreciated. (Tutorials for different mechanics feel a bit late compared to when you actually have access to them)Compared to other games, the rarity of 'mons do not influence their combat effectiveness, the stats are mostly the same with 1 maybe 2 points difference in rarity, this is barely noticeable given the weaknesses we're all too familiar with. My personal suggestion is to find the 'mons that please you aesthetically and roll with them. Do not be afraid to change your party, you might find yourself pleasantly surprised by some common,uncommon or rare ones that absolutely mop the floor with any opponent boss, legendary, you name it. (this game has some hidden gems, real diamonds in the dirt when it comes to its 'mons)All starters can be acquired in game some as early as the very start of the game after choosing your first.The map does feel a bit cramped, most areas you find yourself backtracking a lot, it felt as the game was about to end after basic exploration. Concerns aside, activities pop up after progression, areas that previously were inaccessible require certain elements to be unlocked as well as new 'mons that become available in previously explored patches of grass/caves.As a finishing note, both games, this and the previous one have different mons, some of them have made it into this game, as a flavor but most if not all are newly designed, that makes the work and dedication given very much appreciated as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches that sweet sweet pokemon itch from my childhood. The beginning tone is a little off to me - it seems like it's a little embarrassed to come across as cheesy, whilst also ramping up the stakes super early, and in trying to avoid the cheesy stuff so much and escalating the stakes so quickly it kind of rubbed me the wrong way at first. Now that I've settled into it more and gotten further into the game, though, not only have I gotten a better grasp on the world and the tone of the game, but I feel like the writing is just 'clicking' so much better. I like the mechanics of the battles, and I have gasped so many times at some of the creature designs - so CUTE! I really, really appreciate the journal section, it is so helpful to keep track of main quests as well as the extra quests. I kind of wish it was a little easier to see at a glance in the storage base what type a 'mon is, and to a lesser extent that the database had a bit more detail. The worlds are beautiful (if a bit challenging to navigate owing to my innately atrocious sense of direction) and the world-building is amazingly robust and satisfying to unravel the more hours you sink into the game. The NPCs who do trades are a great inclusion, and I'm really digging the Shards, Cores, and Whistles and how they affect battles and captures. Speaking of captures: it's well executed and satisfying, imo.It might scratch that pokemon itch, but it is very much its own game, and deserves its regard and respect as such. Nexomon: Extinction stands very well on its own merits alone, and I'm really, really enjoying it!

_childDocuments_.review: Nexomon: Extinction. It is a monster capturing RPG developed by VEWO Interactive and published by PQube. The Nexomon series started on mobile first and has been loved by many fans. Later, the PC Edition ported from the mobile version was released on Steam. It has received very positive user reviews as well. Finally, a new season, Nexomon: Extinction, has come to us. Why was this game loved by so many players? Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)The Nexomon series seems to be inspired by Pokémon. In particular, Nexomon shows a similar impression to the 4th and 5th generations(NDS ver) of Pokémon. We can experience several monster capturing RPGs besides Pokémon. Temtem, Monster Crown, Nexomon, and so on. Temtem focuses on online gameplay. Monster Crown adds online PvP content to retro gameplay similar to the 3rd generation Pokemon series. The Nexomon series has story-driven gameplay. Especially, Nexomon: Extinction captures the charm of the genre's roots and boasts about more than 20 hours of playtime. There are lots of animated scenes as well as back sprites in battle. There are also almost 381 Nexomons you can collect or meet. In addition, it features the gorgeous the open world. The game has neat gameplay overall, but it's a bit repetitive. Nevertheless, the story-rich adventure is quite interesting.Nexomon: Extinction. This is a pretty interesting anime adventure RPG that features taming and capturing monsters. The 2~2.5D anime graphics are vibrant, the story is rich, and the gameplay is neat overall. This game gives you a modern flair while raising nostalgia for classic monster RPG adventure games. Also as we play it, we get to know how much affection and effort this dev team put into their game. Of course, it has some lacking parts mentioned above, but it delivers the fun and possibilities to players that a dev team of only  two brothers can show. If you are interested in a monster taming adventure with the nice anime graphic style, Nexomon: Extinction is the game for you. It's one of the best classic monster catching games. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: More than just a clone, this game shows why passion and creativity will always result in better games. More like the original Pokemon games than Pokemon has been probably since Emerald.After clearing the main game, you unlock a Custom Mode that lets you set your own Nuzlocke rules, alongside other challenges or ways to mix up the gameplay. This was added for free by the developers and I challenge Pokemon fans to recount the last time Nintendo/Game Freak did something like that for one of their games despite their fanbases playing with that ruleset and asking for challenges+story for years.Nexomon: Extinction has a good story. It incorporates elements from gameplay and is self-aware about some of its more ridiculous elements, but the overall plot is engaging and better than any Pokemon plotline that's ever been done. It's not revolutionary or anything but hey, I'm here for the gameplay.And speaking of gameplay, Extinction has so many quality of life changes (convenient move respeccing, better move balance for mons, equipment cores) that Pokemon feels hard to go back to after playing this. Looking forward to in-engine randomized Nuzlocke runs for a while to come. A personal thank you to the developers for caring about gameplay and what players actually want instead of only doing what works best for your bottom line.

_childDocuments_.review: An inferior Pokemon clone. I completed the game and even as an achievement completionist, I'm disappointed to say I have absolutely no interest of going the extra mile for this game. The humor of the game is kinda good though (in my opinion), which is to say, Coco can be quite funny at times, but the rest of the characters are as generic as they come.Combat is more repetitive than regular Pokemon and the skills are incredibly unbalanced, with many being completely inferior versions of standard attacks and thus unusable, while others are so OP they break the game completely. The game is supposed to be harder than Pokemon and yet I've beaten the entire game with a simple Nexomon (Feliblanqo). Also, all Nexomon of any given element are basically the same, since their stats are dumbed down to the point where they don't even matter, just your level and skills, giving you no incentive to find or train new Nexomon except as a mindless grind for achievements.Since Gamefreak has become extremely lazy, a lot of people have been looking for a decent new franchise for the genre, and I can say for sure that while this game can be fun at times, it sure isn't what people are looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: I have reviewed the original Nexomon game already, so for this review there will be a lot of comparison between Nexomon 1 and Nexomon Extinction.So let’s get into the review:Price & is it worth it?Nexomon Extinction is priced at £16.99, and despite being over double the price of the original Nexomon game, you are still getting your money’s worth and more with the £16.99 price tag. In comparison to the original Nexomon game, Nexomon Extinction has a LOT more content: a better in-depth story, more innovative Nexomon designs, side quests, lots of end-game content, the list can go on. You are paying for what you get, and with Nexomon Extinction, you get countless hours of fun monster taming content.Storyline & QuestsThe storyline is extremely enjoyable in Nexomon Extinction. Character backgrounds, character development, a diverse range of beautiful environments, Nexomon universe lore, this game has a lot to offer in terms of the story. Whilst Nexomon 1’s was quite basic and shallow, Nexomon Extinction’s storyline thrives and really keeps you intrigued. Especially with the multiple plot twists that happen throughout, everything links together in a clever way.Nexomon Extinction DesignsIn my opinion, the Nexomon’s designs in Extinction is a big step above the Nexomon’s designs in the original game. The design in Nexomon 1 had gotten quite repetitive and felt basic. It felt like quantity was prioritised over quality. However, Nexomon Extinction stepped up their game, and to me, each design felt more thought-out and interesting.Nexomon Extinction TypesIn additional to the original 7 types in Nexomon 1: Normal / Wind / Fire / Water / Electric / Plant / Mineral - Nexomon Extinction has added 2 additional types: Psychic and Ghost. I felt like this is a nice addition as it brings more diversity to the game and allows for more strategic gameplay. I also am a big fan ofthe ghost type Nexomon in particular, as they give a very cool, sleek and creepy appearance.Nexomon Extinction StartersWith the original Nexomon game featuring a starter for each type, Nexomon Extinction has followed in its footsteps and gives the option for 9 different starters, an additional 2 for the newly introduced types: Ghost and Psychic. Starters are catchable in the wild, and so I played through the game with 6/9 of the starters to really a get a feel for their use and capabilities. Overall, I can confidently say that VEWO Interactive did an amazing job with the starter evolutions lines. Each starter felt different, and most specialised in various altering playstyles. Each evolution also felt very refreshing in design and appearance.Nexomon Extinction’s Experience / Level Up / Stamina mechanicsNexomon Extinction’s mechanics has improved MASSIVELY compared to the original Nexomon game. Nexomon’s 1 experience was far too easy and quick to grind, making the levelling up incredibly fast, and the stamina system obsolete. Nexomon Extinction has improved on this by making the experience required per level-up higher, and scrapping the original system of regaining full health and stamina after each level up. Overall, Nexomon Extinction feels like more of a challenge and a finished product compared to Nexomon 1.Nexomon Boss BattlesIn my opinion, the boss battles in Nexomon Extinction has improved a lot in comparison to Nexomon 1. The boss battles felt more challenging, more diverse and a lot more enjoyable overall.End-game ContentNexomon Extinction’s end-game content is one of its strongest offerings. Unlike Nexomon 1, Nexomon Extinction offers a plethora of different content such as side quests to unlock important items, vaults to find high valued loot, findable companions that follow your in-game character around, additional post-game completion quests to unlock all of the Legendary Nexomon and a completely FREE DLC: Nexomon Abyssmal. Overall, there is a lot of content still available past post-game completion.Likes- Good character development and greater links to the overall plot of the story- Able to choose character design- A better introduction to the story than Nexomon 1- 9 starters to choose from, 2 more than Nexomon 1, including new Psychic and Ghost types- Great starter choices & evolution lines- Game soundtracks are very fitting and well suited- UI is a lot more neat, sleek and better in layout compared to Nexomon 1- Moves now display full statistics of power/accuracy/stamina/speed and crit chance- Moves are more diverse- Nexomon’s stats are better displayed in battle (HP/Stamina) on display compared to Nexomon 1- Love that the game gives a link and starts with an immediate reference to Nexomon 1 when you are in the tombs (shows a picture of the crew from Nexomon 1 and says how they were bravest warriors of their generation) sets the scene and time frame of how far in the future the current storyline is- More Nexotraps diversity in Nexomon Extinction compared to Nexomon 1- Improved animations, such as hand throwing animation of Nexotraps- New ‘Capture Change’ breakdown screen where it shows your chances of capturing the wild Nexomon with each subsection and factor- New feeding feature for Nexomon to allow for easier captures- Lots of different Nexomon traps available for each type to improve capture rate- Countdown timer when capturing a Nexomon- Gives Nexomon’s stat information when capturing them as well as description of them- Finally given the option to nickname Nexomon- Nexomon Extinction has critical hits- Better organised storage box system - able to create different groups- No more instant attacked after defeating enemy Nexomon mechanic- There are now held items “cores” and key items- There is now a journal system to show main quest and side quest task progression- A much more in-depth story with plot twists and shock factors- Semi open world exploration available- Nicer environments (dragon island) (underwater city) etc- Better Nexomon designs, more detailed- Unique pathing elements (using Tyrant’s eggs to get rid of fire, jump over gaps, freeze water etc)- More exp required to level up each level - makes it more fun and challenging than Nexomon 1- Fixed overpowered status moves- Status conditions have been fixed and are no longer overpowered- Status conditions no longer automatically heal after each battles - makes the game more challenging- Move accuracy and status accuracy are longer mixed up and can be read separatelyDislikes- No difficulty option to toggle or make the experience more challenging (because of the above reasons)- No EXP granted after each Nexomon defeated in trainer battles - you have to defeat the whole team to get experience- No IV/EV system - lacks diversity- No HM/TM Moves- Rarity System is a bit unstable - you sometimes would find Mega Rares within a few seconds of each other and then Uncommons wouldn’t show for about 10 - 15 minutes of searching- Pre-shaken grass to show where Nexomon are - makes it so you don’t have to go through wild encounters and can just skip every wild battle during the whole gameUnique things to note- No more automatic EXP Share mechanic- Only partial HP & Stamina recover upon levelling up- First turn is based on Speed Stat- There is a rarity system - each Nexomon falls under: Common/Uncommon/Rare/Mega Rare/Special/Legendary rarity brackets- You can get multiple Golden Nexotraps (master ball equivalent to Pokémon)- Legendaries are catchable in the wild

_childDocuments_.review: I had only a single issue with this game (The dev forgot to add an exit from the game, lol) But even that has since been resolved.Right from the get go, Nexomon sets out to let you know, this is NOT pokemon.  He even starts in almost the same way and then throws all the garbage out the window and says "No, ladies and gentlemen, this sh*t is for real, these are vicious little sh*ts and people are dying and not everyone is happy with the situation."A few points to ad that might tip the scales for you as well...*  You get to CHOOSE who you are and what you look like (out of like 20 some odd selections)*  You get to choose from ANY element in the game for your starter* Some adventure/zelda-esque additions to the exploration of the game.  (it was quite the welcome breeze to this kind of game, honestly.)================================================================And that's where the positive ends.================================================================Honestly, I feel like the game is trying to hard to keep a tight hold on the player.  The devs seem very bent on trying to make sure you can't grind or get anywhere.  The biggest problem for me is that ALL the creatures in the game level WITH YOU.  This means that, in most cases, you'r efforts to get ahead a little bit are actually making you weaker in comparison.Then the element system.  It feels.... lack luster.  I feel like everything is inherently the same.I've player a little ways into the story now and the plot holes just keep piling up.  The story hasn't compelled me to keep playing and neither has the battle mechanics.  The game is simultaneously too easy and frustrating at the same time.  Full healing nodes are EVERYWHERE, making any damage you take rather meaningless.  On the other hand, since all creatures will be at about the same level you are, EVERY battle will be a pitched duel to the death leaving you walking back to the full healing node again.I think the dev was trying to make the game feel open ended.  To me though, it instead feels like it lacks any real direction while also lacking any reason to explore.  If you've played a few battles, you've played them all, so no excitement there either.If I could give this a neutral review, I would. _childDocuments_.review: This game plays a lot like the pokemon franchise, but it's a lot harder. The battles can be unforgiving early-on due to the monsters not having decent attacks (type advantage is critical!). You can pretty much adventure from the get-go. Although it is best to progress at least past the first main quests to do so. This will unlock a few options for you which will aid you in the rest of your story. Whichever way you decide to adventure, keep in mind that you will have to follow the storyline eventually... Either to progress further or because the game becomes too easy. Be warned about the active level-scaling. The monsters scale upwards to about your level. Which keeps the game challenging, but a bit harder than most. The level-scaling depends on where you're at in the main story, so if you rush the game it will become real difficult real fast. The level scales up by 5 levels or so, each time. So early-on this might seem a bit drastic if you rush through. Keep in mind that there is (by my account) no exp-share item in this game, a monster needs to participate in a battle in order to gain experience. There is an alternative to this in the form of some exp-sharing cores (a core is an equipable item for your monsters). But if i'm not mistaken, this is something which is recently added to the game. At the very least, I just found out after about a full lvl 50 team and progressing pretty far in the main story.   All in all, I like this game and its challenges. It's a bit more difficult than most games of the genre, but its very much achievable if you keep certain things in mind. What keeps me playing the game is the way the story is written, it's not a typical 'pokemon clone' where you adventure to become the very best or to catch them all. No, this game has a few funny, intruiging and unexpected plot twists.EDIT: There have been some aditions to the game since writing my initial review. These include the resting option in combat, the synergy cores, tamers not automatically want a rematch after you already beat them once, these healing stones that spawn in certain areas. Having played for 6 whole hours with these aditions, I can already say this makes the game so much easier. Too easy even for me! It took some of the challenges out of the game... challenges I, myself, really enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: There is this stigma that because something is inspired by something that came before it, that automatically makes it bad. That is completely untrue in the case of Nexomon: Extinction. You can't avoid drawing comparisons to Pokemon, no matter how hard you try. People just do it all the time, but in my humble opinion, Nexomon ups Pokemon in many ways. Story, Gameplay, and level design all come together beautifully in Nexomon to make a game that feels like a return to more classic Monster-catching games but also finds a way to outdo them. You will find new ways to traverse the environment as you progress through the story, allowing you to travel back to previous areas to explore new nooks and crannys.The game is also completely open from the moment you complete the small intro. You can go to almost any region that isn't 100% plot important. All wild battles scale with your level, so it is hard to be over or under leveled for anything. If you want a good challenge and story that remind you of the golden era of Monster Taming games, then give the game a shot. It has enough bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: Having never played the first Nexomon game, I went into this game with no previous impressions or allegiance. The steam reviews show that over 90% of the people who have played the game enjoyed it, so when my friend offered me a free key from Humble Bundle I figured I would give it a shot. Nexomon, as a creature collector, boasts having over 400 unique monsters to tame. This, however, I believe to be an incredibly devious deception. Having played the game through to the end and spent a multitude of hours completing the database (pokedex), the majority of monsters are functionally identical. There are attacks that are indistinct from one another that simply exist in each of the different Nexomon types. Meaning that by the time your monster has learned all of its moves, it will be unlikely to be any different from another one. Alongside the move-pools being shallow and uninteresting, individual Nexomon do not have unique abilities or traits that set them apart from each other - even the base stats that they possess are indistinct; the ranges from one to the other hardly make one more compelling from the last. The only exception to this rule is the 'rarity' of the Nexomon, with common monsters often having strictly worse stats (making them pointless to carry for long).The one thing that Nexomon does that is unique is the Core system; each monster can have up to four 'cores' equipped at any given time. This would be interesting if it offered anything beyond base stat modifications. The cores increase stats like attack damage, monster health and defense. These are so incredibly boring. The only cores that I found compelling were the Bonus Experience and Experience Share, which are almost entirely mandatory because the rate at which the player receives experience is abysmal; the player receives the same amount of experience from any monster, no matter the evolution stage or difficulty. Gaining experience is an incredibly painful aspect of this game, as it takes a great deal of effort to level up (without the full set of fully upgraded cores). Another major complaint that I have, in my pursuit to complete the database (pokedex) I realized that there is no way to know where specific monsters spawn... the database does not show where they exist; it does not even record where in the world you've seen them.Nexomon Extinction is very clearly a mobile game at heart; the graphics make it look like it was an early Flash player game, there is no mouse support (and keyboard keys cannot be rebound), and certain item systems in game (bonus experience, bonus gold, shop discount items, etc.) feel like they come right out of a microtransaction shop - these are not compelling items for a player to find.The story of the game drags on, but never takes itself seriously enough for the player to become invested. The player's main companion, a talking cat, acts as the protagonists voice. Throughout the game there are countless failed attempts at humour which are mostly at the expense of the player's sense of immersion; the NPCs are constantly referencing the fact that you're playing a video game and breaking the fourth wall. It is a tired and overused trope throughout the entirety of the story.  Having no previous experience with Nexomon, I had no idea what to expect with the monsters themselves. I figured I would go in blind and play with 'the rule of cool'; choosing monsters that I thought looked interesting. Despite there being over 400 monsters, so few of the designs feel original. Outside of similar designs like Mimi and Mimorus (psychic-typed humanoid mime monsters, comparable to the likes of Mr. Mime), there are some designs that are actually just established pokemon; shameless copies. When I encountered Enercer (identical to Vikavolt) and Blublub (besides its horrendous name, it is identical to Solosis) I had to look twice, I could not believe how shameless these were. Nexomon: Extinction is a $26 (CAD) game, yet there is hardly anything here to justify its price. This game released on Steam in 2020 and is unlikely to be getting any meaningful updates to correct the many glaring issues with the game. Upon looking further into it, the studio is already working to release the next installment of the franchise, which all but confirms that this game is dead in the water. I cannot recommend this game. There are few, if any, redeeming features. The price is too high for what it is, especially considering that the game is free on mobile. Stay far away from this title.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of Pokemon, I was a bit skeptical of whether or not this game would live up to that series' legacy... and I haven't been disappointed. In fact, Nexomon: Extinction has so far exceeded my expectations - it is not a mere clone but a fresh take on the genre with its own identity and ideas to explore. To me, it is simultaneously new and nostalgic, reminiscent of the first time I played Pokemon as a child but incorporating elements from RPGs and darker stories that I've enjoyed as an adult. Pros: + Environments are unique and colorful, art design in general is great+ Worldbuilding in general is just very well done, each city/town has a lot of depth and NPCs have a lot to say+ Most Nexomon designs are very appealing and creative, there are a lot of mons (and you can actually catch 'em all)+ Dialogue is fun and self-aware+ CHALLENGING. The latest patch has decreased the amount of grinding required but the difficulty is still very much alive+ Story is engaging. Going into why might be a bit spoiler-y, but it keeps hitting all the right notes for me+ The music is just outstanding. I particularly love the capital city theme+ The devs have been great so far at fixing bugs and addressing community concerns Cons:- You have to grind in this game or the bosses will utterly demolish you. The game offers some solutions to help make the grind smoother with the most recent patch though- In my experience, mons of the same type tend to play similarly because stats don't differ too drastically between them and there isn't a great variety of moves. This really lessens the personal touch of each mon, but means that even Common mons are viable- There are tons of cat-like Nexomon but I haven't found a single horse-like Nexomon?? What's up with that??? Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone whose felt let down by recent Pokemon games (particularly if you enjoyed the Genius Sonority games) or anyone who wants more RPG elements and sarcasm in their monster catching games. Newcomers to the monster catching genre might want to prepare themselves for a more challenging experience, but I think it would still be rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Your enjoyment of this game will depend on how easily you unlearn the bad habits picked up in . No roadblocks! They're gone! At least mostly. Hit the ground running in any direction to build up a full team in the early game. Wild encounters and battles scale with story progress (with small wiggle room of an extra few levels to keep up with a slightly over-levelled party). No more endless steamroll, no more pointless loading screens to birds eternally at level 2! If you railroad the story, enemy levels will overtake you. But don't just sit there and train in the same spot like some traumatic recreation of Victory Road. Nexomon are similar levels everywhere - go explore! Find some vaults, go to locations the story doesn't take you, level as you go. A single over-levelled starter isn't going to cut it. Defense grows slower than attack, so lower levelled nexomon can still take chunks out of you. Enemy tamers have diverse parties too, and they'll switch between them constantly. It's rare to leave a battle without a few scratches and maybe a lost limb. Battles aren't usually hard, but are always punishing. Get used to buying items. There are also rocks that will heal your party, but the game doesn't tell you about them. They're a secret. There's a story! It's quite good, in an anime way, with a mostly funny sidekick and decent writing aimed at teenage+ gamers.  is a fresh bite of Pokemon Gen 2/3 nostalgia. The monsters are generally quite good, and all are usable this time, with stripped down mechanics (no IV/EV, hidden powers, abilities, minigames, safari), single-types (of which there are 9) and equal exp progression. The world is nice, though becomes a little soft on my screen, and quite dark in the details: with parts Pokemon, Twitch chat and Attack on Titan. It is, all in all, very well put together and I've enjoyed playing it immensely. I wonder, with how long it took me to really get my head around the strengths/weaknesses of each type and how to win battles consistently, how accessible Pokemon is to newcomers these days. Kids must go through the thing in a constant state of mild confusion without quite knowing why things work/don't now that there are so many combinations of moves/ stats/ abilities. Although that's much the same as I experienced AoE2 etc. back in the day and I played that as much as I could without getting caught transgressing my 30minutes/day.Small gripes: often a lack of weight/vastness/awe/wonder in key moments. This is not a game that wants to take itself too seriously, and I'm glad it doesn't, but it's stuck at "cute" until it finds deeper chords to strike.

_childDocuments_.review: I went from playing the first Nexomon game to this one within a week. I really enjoyed the first game and put about 22 hours into it. While this game does have some improvements, there are also a lot of things I didn't like. I actually initially stopped playing and refunded this game because of the atrocious QoL changes it had from the first game. Luckily, I learned that custom mode existed, though I had to rely on a kind soul from the Steam community to provide a save file since they lock it behind game completion. The game feels much more playable by even simply doubling the XP rates to more closely match the first game.Pros:- The graphics are improved from the first game.- The music is very well done.- The combat interface is better.- The story and overall feel of the game are still great like the first Nexomon game.Cons:- This game removed many of the nice QoL features that the first game had.-- No more auto-run - not even a toggle. You have to hold the button. -- XP rates were nerfed into the ground so you have to kill like 4x more Nexmon to gain a level.-- You no longer restore HP and Stamina on leveling up.-- Exp share (early game) is now in multiple individual items which you have to manually add and remove to each Nexomon which feels very clunky.- Custom Mode is locked to completing the main game.- A lot of the gold-star and blue-star quests in-game are just pointless. I don't do most of the blue ones and only some of the gold ones. -- For the trade quests, why can they not just take from my box? Why do I have to have them in my inventory?I am enjoying the game with custom mode from the get-go, but man was it a rough transition from the first game. I feel they focused way too hard to customization and really missed the mark in many areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Like pokemon, but unhinged.I prefer this game's story over pokemon and all of the others in the genre, by a long shot. The writing is especially funny if you're familiar with these type of catch-em-all games. I really appreciate that character motivations make sense and no one is evil just because. I was expecting the usual shallow story to push your character forward but was pleasantly surprised.That said, the combat in this game is pretty simple. There's no IV/EV, nature or passives. Equipments are kind of bare bones. This isn't an issue for me, I was never big on min/maxing my pokemons so this suits me just fine. There's also no variation in stats from nexomon to nexomon, so there's no breeding and there's not really a point to ever catch more than one of each type. The designs and evolutions for the nexomons are pretty cool, I like most of them. There was a few derpy looking ones, but most of them are very well made.Finally, the custom mode is worth mentioning, it allows actual nuzlocke runs, new game+, etc, and has a lot of customisation. It adds a lot of longevity to the game imo.Looking forward to the sequels!TL:DR cool little game, definitely worth the money if you're looking for a casual experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bought this game so I could dive into it and make fun of it for being a lame Pokemon rip off. But what started as a couple of hours one night, sending screenshots to my friends making fun of the game.... Eventually turned into wanting to get a little deeper, find more secrets, learn more about the story, grind to level and evolve my mon, etc.What really kept me engaged was the story and the characters. The story actually has heft to it and the characters have a semblance of substance. Pokemon games, for me, have gotten too samey... too flat, they take themselves too seriously, characters and the world feel like cardboard cutouts and nothing really matters. And where Pokemon lacks in those departments, Nexomon: Extinction has in spades. The game actually gives you a REASON to play it out, story-wise. Is it God of War level story? No, but for this genre of game, it more than surpassed my expectations. The characters you meet along the way... guess what? They actually have a purpose and reason to show up multiple times. Characters actually have real motivations for what they are doing. As other reviews have mentioned, the writing is VERY "meta" and joke heavy... and early on it turned me off, but the deeper I got, the more I came to appreciate it. There were multiple 4th wall breaking moments that made me chuckle out loud. And to be honest, the story itself, at it's core... is pretty dark and serious. When they say Extinction, they mean... Extinction. That light-hearted, jokey dialogue really brings a tonal balance to the overall game which, again, I really came to appreciate and enjoy.The map, the art style, the monster designs... All really top notch. It's all just really good, it's hard to even expand on these areas. Just very very SOLID in every way.  Kind of a small thing, but something in these types of games that really annoys me is when evolutions don't "make sense". Like you will have a starter / base monster and it evolves into something completely unrecognizable or just flat out stupid. That isn't an issue with Nexomon: Extinction. And as silly as the dialogue is sometimes, it seems like they took their monster creations very seriously -- which is GOOD. You aren't running around catching literal trash bags or ice cream cones. THANK YOU DEVS. Content wise, I felt I more than got my money's worth. Plenty of side quests... I enjoyed the adequate but not over-the-top resource grinding / collection aspect of the game. The mechanic for creating cores and using cores was really well done. I much prefer that to Pokemon held items. Loved the vault and key hunting. Wish there were even more quests / side activities like this in the game. Perhaps maybe the best mechanic / feature in this game is the ability to re-fight trainers... trainers get stronger, their Mon get stronger, and they have cool new dialogue options as you get stronger and keep beating them which is great. Truly one of the better features in this game and I hope the devs keep building on this and making it even better. It truly makes "grinding" levels and evolutions enjoyable. I forgot what they are called, but in many areas of the game, they provide these "healing rocks" , which fully heal your party and respawn after X amount of time passes. The game itself actually makes fun of the fact that devs were kind of bullied into adding these because players thought the game was too hard... But to be honest, I liked them. It makes grinding / leveling just that much nicer. Spending half the game walking to towns to heal my Mon isn't fun to me. So I don't care if it makes the game "too easy" I see it as a really nice quality of life improvement on the genre.For some quasi negatives.... Nexomon and their evolutionary lines are locked to certain locations, as you level up and progress through the game those wild Nexomon also level up and you begin seeing their evolved forms in the wild more often. This is a cool feature, however, if you miss some of the base forms early on... It's really kind of a pain to go back and try completing the equivalent of your Pokedex because the base forms just aren't as common to find / catch. Maybe it's in the game and I missed it, but we could really use a breeding / day care center. It doesn't even need to be complex. Put two of the same Mon in the daycare, you get a base form back... And added bonus of slowly leveling those mons in the daycare. Simple fix to an otherwise cool system.Also the battle system just feels a tad one dimensional. It isn't BAD, but I feel like there is an aspect missing here. Moves between mons are VERY VERY similar if not identical (depending on type) and the move pool just feels really limited. We might just need a bigger variety of moves, we might need more types, perhaps dual typing... I'm not 100% sure the fix here. But it does feel like the system is missing just one more layer of depth / complexity. The only other thing I would look at improving kinda goes with the battling. But I felt like often times.... moves, stamina, Mon and move type.... just didn't really mean anything. And what I mean by that is, as long as your mons stay at or above the level of the enemy mons... You're gonna be fine. If you do some grinding, you can have one lead mon really carry you. Doesn't matter the type, their weaknesses, nothing. As long as the level is higher, you're mostly gonna be fine. Now, I understand it's that way in most games like this but it feels even more relevant here. If this complaint is true of all monster catching games, it's relevant x10 for Nexomon. Again... I don't know how to fix this exactly, but the formula just needs tweaking and balancing. All those factors of a Mon need to matter more and be weighted beyond... Higher level = More Power = Win.All in all.... Really great game. If  you like the monster catching adventure genre, pick this up. As I mentioned at the start of this review, I bought this game for the memes. But I ended up staying for a funny, meaningful, and truly enjoyable experience. I really look forward to whatever comes next in this franchise. You've all won me over. Thank You.

_childDocuments_.review: Nexomon: Extinction may at first seem like yet another  Pokemon spin-off. BUT, after playing it for quite some time, it is so much more than that!I still have so much left to complete - and I'm so eager to continue the story - but I really wanted to review this game because it really deserves more recognition.You start in a world that at first feels like an old-school Pokemon game. It even has that challenge that newer Pokemon games lack! But, as the plot picks up - and it does so very quickly - you soon realize that  I won't leave any spoilers, but the adventure and characters are really fun! You can see for yourself that the art style is great, but there's so much more to appreciate in the game as well!There are 381 different Nexomon to tame (catch). There are unique types, moves, and evolutions to each Nexomon, much like in Pokemon. The designs of the Nexomon are actually, for the most part, very interesting. Some great cool and cute ones to match different trainer's preferences!For those shiny hunters out there, you're in luck!!  I still haven't found one, but my sister's first wild encounter was a cosmic!! (Still so jealous btw, if you're reading this!)I know I keep comparing it to Pokemon, but I can't help it. I'm a huge Pokemon fan, it's what I know!! But, I enjoy this game so much on its own. I've grown up playing Pokemon, learning all the things that go on in that universe. But as I jump into the Nexomon universe for the first time, it feels fun, fresh, and exciting!! It is definitely worth playing and trying out! It has a growing fan-base for a reason!I've already sunk 12 hours into the story and just going around the grass looking for new Nexomon! Also, there's a ton of side quests to gain some extra coin or cool items! I plan to attempt to 100% the game, or at very least catch all the Nexomon! I currently only have around 60 lol!Walkthrough series:  Do yourself a favour, and get this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this one, it does a couple of things right and also a couple of things not so right.The good:-you can actually rematch trainers-and related to that, the levels scale to your team so you'll never end in underleveled fights.-Money is actually pretty easy to earn since you can actually get money from wild encounters.-You can actually tell at what level they evolve in the database.the bad:-Even though there is a large selection of Nexomon, every one of them is single--type and there are only 9 types so there isn't too much variation.-Adding to that, the nexomon can only learn moves of their own type and normal moves-Some of the type match-up is kinda weird, like rock being weak to wind and a bunch of others, i advice looking up a type-chart(for Extinction because it's slightly different from the first game)- This one might be a personal preference thing but when you use a potion during battle, it's always on the first Nexomon in your team by default, not on the one that you're currently fighting with and it can be a bit disorientingAll in all, as far as pokeclones go, this one was more enjoyable than Temtem

_childDocuments_.review: The good: This game has a charming atmosphere, solid worldbuilding, and takes the pokemon formula into uncharted territory. For the most part, the world is very grim dark, with humanity on the brink of extinction. This is offset by the goofy characters, which are pretty solid overall.The Bad: If you're looking for even a modicum of strategic depth, this ain't it chief. This game is 100% dependent on your creature's levels, and that's all that matters. Even the typing advantages and disadvantages don't amount to much. All in all, you just use you're strongest attack over and over until the enemy dies.Overall: I'd give this a 7/10. If you've ever played Siralim or Monster Sanctuary, this game's not comparable in depth. The extraneous factors are better, however. If I didn't like the genre, I wouldn't reccommend this, but if you like monster catching games, go ham.

_childDocuments_.review: Great for casual play. Story is super cute, mechanics are refreshing and I see a lot of potential for complexity in the future. I enjoy the shard and mining aspect of this game, it gives purpose and more meaning to exploration. I also like the idea of basically moving stat points on whatever 'mon you want to. I also enjoy the feeding mechanic, I think they can expand on that in the future as well. The story is funny and entertaining with lots of anime-esque characters, but I think that brings a charm. Cons: The battles itself don't have a lot of depth but that's okay. This is the second game released in the series and it does not need to be that polished. The moves are very repetitive and offer little to no variety. The status are poorly explained, if at all. Due to the lack of abilities and held items, every mon seems like a reskinned version of each other. Lastly, some of the 'mons are a little over done and the design is kinda ugly.That being said, I see huge potential in the future. This game is still being improved and worked upon. I love how much effort and care they put into this game. If you like pokemon (casually), I highly suggest this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a monster tamer game, but tired of Pokemon, this game is one of the best alternatives I have seen. The game play is simple which, I think, is perfect for its genre. The designs are great, some can be too similar to other games like pokemon, but that's only 2 or 3 monsters. What makes this game shine is it's story and humor. The story for a monster tamer is great, and the game isn't afraid to make fun of itself nor the genre it's apart of for the sake of comedy.Now, it is a budget game, so somethings maybe off and there isn't really an after game; however, I find these vary easy to look over all its charm.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent game with a good story, interesting creature designs, and a massive roster of different creatures. They even added in a bunch of really cool extra features that can be unlocked after beating the game once that hopefully will become a staple in the series (and that more games should have, honestly), such as a built in randomizer and nuzlocke mode.Unfortunately... they got rid of the biggest draw for the series (for me) which was the the fact that creatures swapping in could attack the same turn. This made the game much more challenging than other monster taming style games, which generally are designed so that 6 year old children wearing a blindfold can beat them without issue.  Creatures also never get any kind of elemental based moves other than their own type and status effects are all over the place, and always low% chances to even apply the status (including moves that only apply a status effect).  As a result, battles just feel like a rock-paper-scissors match.  Switch to a Nexomon with a type advantage, click the move with the biggest number, rinse/repeat until the battle is over.  No strategy or thinking required.This game also lacks the most mandatory thing for a monster taming game to be good: multiplayer. There is no trading, which isn't a really big deal, but it also means there is no PvP battle system for the game. As a result there's no real meaning to playing after you finish the story a single time. "Catch all the legendary Nexomon!"... why? And do what with them? "Train your members in the box up to make a new team!"... and do what with it? The game is already over, there are no fights left to beat, just chores to check off the game's list that I skipped because they're all just boring fetch quests where the rewards don't match the resources I have to give up to complete them. Without multiplayer, a monster taming game has no life.TLDR:Good game with fun writing and a large creature roster, but unfortunate mechanic changes from the first game and a continued total lack of multiplayer make this only worth buying on sale and not worth the $20 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Great pokemon clone. Quality of life features GREATLY improved from the first nexomon title.Pros:- Addition of shards. I like that they can be used for cores, nexotraps, or some extra coin so the player has agency in what to use them for.- Improved encounter rates for rare nexomon.- Addition of tamer (trainer) rematches. Tamer rematches are infinite(!) and on a cooldown.- Wild nexomon and tamer rematches scale with you. NPC dialogue also changes with the story this time and it’s cool to see them react to your different feats.- LOTS of cameos from the first title. I like seeing my old friends (and enemies).- Addition of stackable key items. Provides a good incentive to actually explore the land and dungeons.- Fast travel is available MUCH earlier in the game than in the first title. Thank god.- Addition of specialty nexotraps. I like that they can be crafted with shards or bought outright, so you have two options for acquiring them based on what currently works better for you.- Nexomon designs are great. There are some middle evolutions that just look like a midpoint between the first and third that have no unique features, but this doesn’t really bother me.- Stamina battle system is the same as the first title and still works great.- Character portraits look cleaner and generally more appealing.Mixed:- Core system. It’s neat, but it’s also a pain to have to switch the EXP share ones into the party every single time you change your party. Maybe some sort of loadout system would've been helpful here?- Addition of ghost and psychic types. Ghost is ok but psychic is basically useless. It does, however, open the door for some very cool nexomon designs.Cons:- A few encounter rates, EVEN WITH LURING, are abysmal. If you want to catch every single nexomon you will have to sink extra tens of hours into this.- Still too many 4th wall breaks. It’s funny the first time, not the 20th. A lot of the “game budget too small” jokes don’t land because the game looks and works perfectly fine. Your companion this game is more annoying than Atlas in the first title.- Can't get rid of cores. It's annoying to scroll through all of your obsolete cores. You should be able to sell them and/or destroy them to recoup half(?) of the shards back.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is really great. I can't remember a single story line from any pokemon game, but Nexomon is very memorable, and with many unpredictable twists. Other reviews mentioned the music and it's true that it's really good - becomes light and playful when the story is having fun, becomes dark and foreboding when the story is serious, and becomes powerful and exhilarating when in a big battle. It made me actually notice the music in a game! The humor is appreciated, and the vast number of Mons is great. Will probably play through again to try some of the others. Creature design is really cool, and the overall art style of the environments is bright and vibrant. The one area that could be improved is the battle system, which isn't bad, just very simple and lacking depth. This is well made up for by the rest of the game. This game made me a Nexomon fan. Can't wait to see what they do with Nexomon 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Nexomon: Extinction is one of those games that perfectly fill the void after how Pokemon fell from grace and has become stagnant. A story-driven experience that rewards exploration, a soundtrack full of excellent songs, unique (albeit hit-and-miss) monster designs and thriving community interaction and the addition of new features.It's far from perfect, with a slow battle system, rarities that don't feel like it and mildly frustrating resource grind, but the experience is complete and offers an excellent experience much like the glory days of Nintendo's behemoth franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it on a whim.Now?I like it more than I like Pokemon games.Designs are cool, the jokes are (in my opinion) pretty damn good, and I had a blast playing through the story. ~~~There is a point when you're meeting a certain enemy that you can actually just agree with their demand. Surprised, they congratulate you on your wisdom, essentially give you a Master Ball (1 use 100% catch rate) as a reward and then you just immediately turn around and beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of them.~~~My time in the game is a bit skewed, its really closer to 45 hours since I went at the game a very specific way the first time I played and just wore myself out. (I essentially was trying to do an all-Phantom type team, which was a pain in the ass later on when typing is a huge battle factor.)If I had to be realistic, you could probably finish it MUCH sooner than I did, but I really enjoyed the world and had a good bit of fun doing quests and searching for Vaults. I also ended up fighting the last battle with a team of Level 72 Nexomon, and it was a fair fight if I'm being pragmatic, so if you're worried about it being too easy or something, don't even sweat it; the game will challenge you enough.I won't lie though, I definitely abused a game mechanic to cheese some of the tougher fights, but I feel like that's part of what makes this game beautiful; the fact that you can slap 4 Level 3 Health Cores on a Foreer, first turn use Natural Healing (Ingrain) and then use Green Sphere (delayed Recover) every other turn as a strategy is absolutely amazing.~~~For those of you unaware of a majority of the game's mechanics, that's the setup for a health tank who has a massive health pool and heals 10% of it every turn, with an additional 30% every other turn if you're diligent with the move Green Sphere. It's probably my favorite stall mechanic because on the turns where you aren't setting up Green Sphere, you can attempt to Poison or Bind (Wrap) the enemy and they can't do anything about it other than hope that RNJesus is on their side.~~~That aside, it really is a fantastic game. Again, I bought this expecting to be disappointed. I most certainly was NOT disappointed. It truly is your loss if you end up ignoring this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not exaggerating - starting the campaign hard-locked my system. First, it dropped me in an unskippable cutscene. Then, it set my resolution to 4 times the size of my monitor's viewing area so i couldn't see any way to escape into the menu. I eventually did, however, by mashing every key on my keyboard, at which point i found out that "Confirm" and "Back" were bound to... K and L. Then, I tried to Alt+Tab out of the game, only to find that the game continually re-grabbed focus from the other programs, so I couldn't escape that way either.Then, somehow, it did the same thing with Ctrl+Alt+Del - meaning my system was now hard-locked with no way of escaping from Nexomon. Then, I literally had to restart my computer, which I haven't had to do in over 4 months.Overall, this is a great game, probably. As for me, refund.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is good, but not without its flaws. I'd recommend buying it if you want a Pokemon clone to pass the time.Gameplay in general is nice, although some aspects felt really lacking, like the core system, which is pretty slow to setup and made almost necessary in the late-game for beating the Abyssal Update, or the lack of a more complex movepool.About the nexomons themselves, the overall design is great; obviously, there are some nexomons which I didn't like, but that's subjective and will inevitably happen to all games in this genre. The only thing that would be nice for a future game is combining nexomon's types, which would certainly add a layer of complexity for the game.For me, the worse about this game is it's history and the interactions between characters. Without spoiling anything, it feels like it was written by a 12 year old addicted to the most generic animes imaginable. Once again, my opinion in this topic is very subjective, as it might have been a case of just not being part of the demographic this history was made for.If you are a completionist, this is not a bad game to get all the achievements. It took me 56 hours to get them all, and you don't have to go out of your way to do it (the hardest one by far is getting all nexomons). And even after you get everything, there is still the cosmic hunting, which is an equivalent to shiny hunting in Pokemon.I hope this review can be of use for anyone wanting to buy the game. It's my first serious one as of yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite game of the year so far. To any looking to pick this up, I'm just going to be short and sweet. I've been trying lots of different "pokemon-like" games aka Monster Tamer games. Some good, some bad, some in the middle. This game is at the Top for me. The monster taming is crisp. Definitely feels as if the devs WANT you to catch them all. Instead of some monster tamer games that really limit you at the start, That doesn't mean you will have everything at once. No. Plenty of depth. Speaking of the monsters, they are varied and colorful. I like them, even if some of their names are ...odd. Also it's kind of metroid-vania, in the sense that you acquire terrain-moving abilities that allow you to go back to old areas and find new stuff. After much complaining, they recently added their version of a shared experience option in the form of cores you equip to your monsters. You can spread them out, stack them up, and level how YOU want. Story is also a lot of fun. Very comical but not the BAD kind, with cringe and taking away from the moment. It just makes you chuckle. This game deserves more attention than it's gotten, and I definitely say buy it if you like the genre or are looking to get into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like people who have never played Pokemon trying to copy Pokemon. - All the nexomons have almost identical base stats on their final evolution- The move diversity is really bad. Many of the moves are completely useless except the damaging ones. - Expect to have only 4 moves per mon for the majority of your playthrough and even then you'll only ever use 2 -  Even mega or ultra rare nexomon will have pretty much the same potential as a common first route nexomon. - There are no abilities that would differentiate nexomons from each other- Nexomon can only be one type so even that small variation is gone- Many of the designs are actually pretty good but some are also pretty basic. There are about 5 evolutionary lines that are just cat + element, two are fire type. - There are 301 Nexomon but because of all of the above I struggle to see why you'd want to bother catching all of themIt's almost feels like a parody of how non-Pokemon fans see Pokemon, you just click the supereffective move and win. The core gameplay is extremely basic compared to the other Mon games I've played like Coromon and Temtem. The dialog heightens the feeling of parody as a lot of it is self-referential and fourth wall breaking making fun of the tropes of the genre or directly referencing the player. It's kind of hard to get immersed in a story that treats itself like a joke.

_childDocuments_.review: I've probably been waiting for more than a decade for Pokemon games to get good again, and it's good to know some people weren't as patient as I was and decided to do something about it.This isn't just "Pokemon, but good"; it's got a delightful, and perfectly distinct identity while keeping many of the mechanics some of us grew up with, and adding a couple new ones along the way. The story is both interesting and hilarious at times, the characters are endearing, the Nexomon are pretty cool and the environments are nice enough to make up for the pandemic-related lack of travel we've been experiencing.Two minor nitpicks :1) It would be nice to have an ingame mechanic giving us indication as to where to find a specific Nexomon (just the general area would be awesome)2) Allow scrolling in the database, or some kind of way to go rapidly down the list when the Nexomon we're trying to look up is neither at the start or at the endBut aside from that, awesome work :)

_childDocuments_.review: To begin, I would certainly recommend this game for anyone looking for a decent monster tamer. It has good fundamentals and overall is rather enjoyable up until the end where it becomes a tedious slog.The Good-The narrator / cat person is really funny and is worth buying the game for his dialog alone-The game is relatively challenging compared to Pokemon-You can't just overpower this game by spamming one monster and one move you will need a diverse and well balanced party. Not being effective is a big deal.The Bad-The story isn't very fleshed our nor is the climate change angle factored in as well as it could be. We never see nexomon migrations fleeing changing climate or anything of that manner.-The characters outside the cat are incredibly boring and we barely interact with them. The two friends of the MC are two dimensional when compared to the rivals of the pokemon game.-The art in cutscenes is bad-The game levels with you so all zones are at your level at all times. This makes it difficult to level up to an appropriate place to beat one of the Tyrants (nexomon's equivalent of pokemon gyms). The gameplay loop ends up being, do missions until you have enough money to buy items so you can face tank your way through the PVE events.-The leveling curve is so annoying that it becomes more efficient to just go and catch fresh leveled nexomon at a certain point to fill the type hole that has developed in your team.-Never felt the need to use any of the behind the scenes crafting systems you can just buy potions and ignore most challenges until the final few boss fights. _childDocuments_.review: Difficulty scaling in this game is completely illogical. There is 'dynamic difficulty' scaling in this game that basically renders all nexomon you catch early completely useless. Once you catch a nexomon, they immediately begin to get out-scaled just by virtue of your main party leveling up. This means there is no point to catching any nexomon early in the game and there is almost no point in leveling your own party--you just have to catch new nexomon as you go along. I suspect this is to incentivize changing up your team often, but in practicality you just never get to keep your nexomon except for your starter. Everything else will get outleveled after an hour, so you just need to catch new nexomon to replace the ones in your party that haven't kept up.

_childDocuments_.review: I only played about 2 hours of it, but I didn't have any fun during those two hours.  People complain it is a tedious grindfest, and I tend to agree.    The biggest issue is the dynamic leveling system.  It is a risk that the devs took, and I appreciate them trying to bring something new.  I understand that it is suppose to be a challenge; however, having to heal after even a few fights with wild monsters so early in the game is incredibly annoying.  Back and forth running for heals after every fight or two is discouraging and feels like a waste of time.  I don't feel as if I am making progress.  Just leveling one or two nexomon takes forever.The devs are active and answer questions about the dynamic leveling, which I admire.  They state that there is a 1-3 level cap regarding opposing nexomon.  The devs continue saying that the game gets a bit easier the more you grind/progress the story; however, at least in the first 2 hours, I felt that my hard work of running back and forth for so many hours felt useless.  I was not rewarded for fighting wild monsters, and after two hours, that is discouraging enough for me to put down the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential, but it's just too imbalanced to be fun in the long term. TL;DR: Elements are useless, all fights go down to potion-spamming, the scaling sucks.1. THE ELEMENTS OF YOUR NEXOMON DOES NOT MATTER IN FIGHTS.So your enemy has a fire-mon and you have a water-mon? The enemy still slaps your butt with just a few hits. It's not worth it to switch your nexomon in-fight, because your nexomon will instantly lose 40-50% health with "ineffective" hits. So you just fight with any nexomon until it's dead and then switch to the next one. You can't play strategically. Also status effects like "freeze" won't happen too often. I had a nexomon with "sleep" (like Jigglypuff), it didn't do anything at all. Not a single time. Not even once. That's a huge downer.2. YOU HEAVILY RELY ON POTIONS.You can't go out and start a fight without having at least 5-10 potions and 5 revival potions with you. Potions are a core aspect of this game. The dmg in every single fight is just so ridiculous. Even when you fight some nobody in the middle of nowhere, you'll have to take a few potions. All your nexomon are down to 10% health after every fight. You will end up spending all your money for basic potions. So your "prize money" is just a compensation for the potions that you needed to win the fight. The normal routine is: Fight some stranger, use all your potions, win a small amount of money, go back to the town to buy new potions and heal your nexomon, go back to the wilderness and fight the next stranger. Repeat.. This leads to the third point.3. ENEMY LEVELS ARE SCALING WITH YOU -> YOU WON'T EXPLORE.Because the fights are so unbalanced and draining, you end up avoiding every single trainer-fight that you can. You carefully walk around the trainers to not trigger them and you only fight if you really really have to. The main goal of the game is to rush the story. All the enemies are scaling anyway, so why would you grind your nexomon and explore the world? It's just an annoying waste of time and ingame-money.CONCLUSION:What are the core elements of a monster collector game? Exploring, collecting and fighting strategically. But these are exactly the things that you want to avoid in this game. The game is punishing you for even trying and drains the fun out of you. Which in conclusion, makes it a bad game for this genre.I understand that the game designers wanted to try something different, but rushing a (not bad but mostly childish) story is just not what I expected it to be. I wanted to collect Nexomon and have entertaining fights against trainers. But that's not what the game wants you to do. You just spam potions like in Diablo.The Nexomon series has potential, but it needs lots of balancing in future releases.

_childDocuments_.review: A TLDR I recommend grabbing this if its on sale or if youre desperate for a new monster collector. Engaging text and quests often quite funny.The world and story is great but perhaps at a cost to the gameplay.Everything you do will be scaled. Your highest lvl is 50? Wild mons are gonna be nearly 50. This is for wild, all trainers, and maybe bosses? So lots of healing is needed to traverse the world. It semi-deals with it in the form of healing gems found around the map that heal your team. Type advantage only seems to hinder you. What I mean by this is switching into a mon thats "weak" to yours feels completely worthless. You switch in and take an "uneffective" move that does over half your hp. Then go on to do one hit (sometimes even two!) then heal from bag/move and rinse and repeat till the battles over. Status effects are worthless to you and incredibly OP on all enemies.The UI doesnt explain anything, it may say that your move will put them to sleep but fails to say for how long. This goes for almost all ailments. Most of the time your status moves will only effect them for a turn. This does depend any maybe Im horribly unlucky but the only thing Ive gotten consistently more than one turn of is sleep or para. Meanwhile, when an enemy hits you with a status its 5 TURNS. 5 WHOLE TURNS ARE YOU KIDDING ME. Demotivated for 5 turns? Gotta swap or just use your bag for 5 turns. Sleeping? If you dont have an anti sleep have fun waiting and watching your mon die. Frozen? Eat a bag of REDACTED. You 100% need to rely on bag items to the point where it feels less like my team vs theirs and more-so my spam heals and anti-status items vs their team.Its so bad that Im 90% sure you cant even hit bosses with most status', when spamming a 30% freeze move (over 10 times) I didnt get a single ONE TURN freeze. These mixed with the fact that most mons only learn their type and a normal move makes the combat feel like a clunky and really unbalanced game of rock paper scissors. This paired with the emphasis of NEEDING items to succeed really lowers it on my list of monster collectors. All in all it is a fun couple hours but needing to constantly grind makes it feel like this singleplayer game doesnt respect your time at all.Endgame consists of gathering all Tyrants/Greater Dragons/ and Omnicron Children. There are "shinys" in the form of Cosmics aswell.

_childDocuments_.review: Around 60h  2/10   1  No   I have made a guide to list which Nexomon I found where. You can find it  3 on Astats    No  No  You can see the achievement for catching all the Nexomon as grindy but it is also a very normal achievement in this type of game  No  No  No  No difficulty option  No  If you’re thinking about getting this awesome game, let me start with a piece of personal advice to start with the first Nexomon game in this series. You can find my review for that one . Nexomon: Extinction is a direct sequel to the first game and the story continues here, taking place 10 years later.  The main reason I highly suggest starting with the first one is that the story is the best part of both Nexomon games. There are a lot of puns and 4th wall-breaking jokes but that doesn’t get in the way of an in-depth story.  This is a monster collecting game in the style of Pokémon. A lot of people will compare it to Pokémon and it does have a lot of similarities, but in my opinion, this game isn’t a clone as it adds a few twists in comparison to Pokémon.  As I've already pointed out, Nexomon has an amazing story, which I just haven’t seen in the Pokémon games that I have played over the years. This game has a mechanism that it increases the catch chance by a lot if you first feed the Nexomon you are attempting to catch and after you have thrown the trap, you'll have an optional minigame in which you have to push a few buttons in order in 5 seconds. Each button you have correctly hit increases the chances of catching the Nexomon.  Another difference is that the Nexomons that roam in the wild get higher in level. That means that when you first encounter them, they are around level 5 but if you go back to earlier maps later on in the story, those Nexomons are just a few levels lower than your highest Nexomon.   I would highly suggest to first play the game for its story and catch what you can but don’t go out of your way to find them all yet. Most Nexomon have 3 tiers and at certain points of the story, the Nexomon from that tier can be found on all the maps in the wild (the earlier tiers of Nexomon will stay available on those maps too).  You’ll get a few tools that will increase the chance to catch them and you'll get the option to buy the best food which every Nexomon likes instead of having to have the right food type for the full effect.   The developer is still actively worked on the game. It did release with some small bugs and the rating to find mega rare Nexomon was very low but the developer has listened to the players and improved the game a lot in the past few weeks since its release. For example; there are now ways to share experience between non-fighting Nexomons; this was highly requested. There have also been new items added to the game to restore a bit of health or stamina after each fight.   Most of the achievements are for beating the game and catching all the Nexomons. There are a few others for selling ores and have gathered X amount of money during the game but those are not missable and not that hard to achieve.  I've really enjoyed this game a lot and so, I highly suggest getting it, if you like monster collecting games.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this because I wanted a new monster catching game, figured I'd just play it little bits here and there. Then I played it for 30 hours over the first three days.Pros: - Really nice art all over the game- A very compelling story that keeps pulling you in and hitting you with plot twists (and a ton of fourth wall breaks)- Plenty of mons to catch as the dex has 427 of them (Little too many legendaries and mega rares for my taste but still great nonetheless)- Everything only has one typing and it shows in the battle as well, making it a lot easier to learn all these new mons- Open world that scales every single area according to your process. You can go almost anywhere you want in the world and every encounter will be around your own level, allowing for a wide variety of mons to catch whenever you want- A custom mode once you beat the game that lets you basically adjust every single aspect of the game. Including nuzlocke and randomizer settingsCons:- There isn't much postgame to speak of sadly, it's just your standard "Go catch every legendary and complete the dex" part of the game. And with a 20ish hour long campaign it leaves a bit more to be desired. Though despite that, the campaign is still a lot of fun and more than worth the price tag of this game- It's a console port and they didn't seem to care much about keyboard and mouse. There is no keybind changing and the mouse doesn't do anything. Still very playable with the keybinds you're given, but it's a little annoying for sure.Overall a solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is really good; I honestly enjoyed it more than most of the more recent Pokemon games.It has a lot of character, the story is interesting, but never takes itself seriously (for better or worse).Simple and difficult, but not too difficult.I kept a full team roughly equal leveled. I think having only one over-leveled mon could make the game more difficult because of the stamina system (You are expected, towards the end, to beat 3/4 characters in a row without healing). There is an EXP share system (at least now there is).The enemies level up with you to an extent: you can grind past them, or deal with the difficulty.The grind really isn't that bad, especially with the number of monsters you can catch.In addition, enemies leveling with you is actually nice in the end game. It help you max out your mons, plus, everything you catch is leveled with your team if you want to use a new mon.You should not lose your starter after beating the game, it should be in the "box system".Looking forward to the next update, and I really hope that a sequel gets made (and that Derek somehow finds his way into it)!
