_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Overall, this is a great game.30 hours in, it's time for the review:This is a roguelike deckbuilder. If you played slay the spire, this is exactly the same kind of game, but with lots of cool new ideas.The visuals are not what I would expect for a game in this genre. Roguelike deckbuilders usually have simple or cartoonish graphics, but Tainted Grail decided to go for a darker setting. Yet, this game is beautiful to watch.Each of the three factions feels incredibly unique, and the subclasses are also very distinct. I feel like this game will take hundreds of hours to master.I've encountered a visual bugs and one gameplay one. Nothing major that I couldn't resolve by restarting the game.Difficulty-wise, the game relies on ascencion leves, i.e., every time you beat the game in a difficulty level, you unlock the next one. The game suddenly got really punishing at difficulty 5, though it might get a lot easier when I unlock more NPCs, which I intend to do at difficulty 4 for a couple runs before venturing into difficulty 5 again.

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand, very nice looking game with fun classes and interesting combos!   Very much a solid copy+paste rogue-lite card builder following so many before it!On the other hand, the developers decided that because this is a "rogue-lite" game, you must grinding for endless hours replaying the game over and over and over in order to unlock more fun...Ultimately, if they reduced the grind in many areas of the game I think it would be worth recommending.  As it stands, I estimate I'd need to invest 30+ hours of grinding out the same few levels over and over and over in order to unlock any meaningful progression on the account.  For example, you unlock most of the buildings or "features" pretty quickly.  And each of them effectively require a different currency to upgrade what they offer.  The issue comes where the buildings you care about most and offer the more enjoyable changes to your runs, will maybe result in ~3 currency drops in a run... and you need 15-30-50+ for one upgrade.   If a run takes you say ~15-30  minutes?  You can do the math but likely see that you have to grind A LOT to unlock stuff.Compare this to other rogue-lite games I've played where if you beat bosses, you straight up get new items to use (this game isn't like that from my experience).  Those other games do have currency, but it's ONE currency that you choose to use wherever you want.  This game has MULTIPLE currency types, one for each building, and you don't get equal drops of that currency every run.  Some of the currency you have to actively and specifically grind for (often at the expense of others).

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 8 hours of actually playing the game as I leave the game running in the background when I'm not playing.So this is more of a take on what it's like getting started.The tutorial/first fight is one you can't win. You beat on this boss character which is supposed to teach you some of the combat play. You ultimately lose and start the game.When you start the game you begin as a basic warrior. Why the devs force you to play what is one of the weakest characters in the game is a mystery. The devs supposedly want you to learn by losing - AKA getting your butt kicked. I think a little butt kicking is fine, but a new player has enough to learn without playing a character that is weak because it can't heal itself.New players that want to learn the game and not get their butts continuosly handed to them should put the game in Story mode from the first menu, which will give you more of a chance to get through the first level.Now I just have to take my own advice and try another run.Good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best games I have played in years. Not an expression. Been a lot of games over the last few that I thought, "That looks good!" - and it was meh. OR "that has potential, I will give it a try" - refunded. This game came out of nowhere. Wasn't even on my radar really, and it's been great so far. Combat: Satisfying. You use cards, but feels way more strategic than most of these card battlers. Also, you have so many classes that you can play however you want. Which spices things up quite a bit. _childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! As a long time rpg fan, I only recently discovered I like the "roguelike deckbuilder" formula a lot, and it was the excellent Slay the Spire that got me the message.Tainted Grail is by no means inferior, on the contrary I find it far more charming, deeper and richer.I never played the early access (I prefer playing games only post release) so I started directly from 1.0. The game has a diablo-esque atmosphere peppered with Witcher-y and Lovecraftian elements, with some Gothic roughness thrown in.The game boasts a ton of classes (9!) divided into 3 archetypes (warriors, rangers and summoning-focused mages), with each sub-class covering a specific variety of playstyle.I'm not going to spoil much about the lore, the classes etc. because part of the charm of the game is the joy of discoverying bits and pieces by yourself in a cyclic journey of challenging unearthly horrors (my only advice: if you unlock a class but it seems clunky and hard after trying it out, go watch 1 or 2 video guides about it, you'll be surprised...).The game flow is divided among these things:- the chosen class gives you a certain preferred playstyle and potential to grow;- the (upgradable) hub is used to rest and recuperate and to strategize about how to spend your limited resources according to your situation;- the nonlinear dungeons alternate between combat encounters and events/exploration, where you'll spill blood and make obscure decisions about all the many NPC you'll encounter;- the combat relies on a bit of luck (which cards are selected from your deck and what card upgrades you'll be rewarded with) and a lot of strategy, there are MANY ways to tackle situations by combining enemy patterns (all attacks are telegraphed to allow strategy), cards of various types, passives, consumable items, permanent upgrades, helpers, runes, crafting, barriers, armor, summons, etc.- there is no "stress" in building your deck because A) you can continously get new cards and everything can work all right (but you can also limit your deck and discard cards if you want) and B) you will accumulate a ton of passive abilities that will shape the way you play your cards, and as far as I know there is no upper limit, as many as you can get.Really, if you like a dark atmosphere and are remotely intersted in deck building rpgs (there are so few of them yet!), THIS gem you just cannot miss!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Very very good game! Deckbuilder and Turn based strategy lovers should play this game.A dark fantasy game with lots of different stories, characters and choices. Highly addictive, joyful an suprising. There are total 9 specialized heroes in 3 main classes which gives you 9 different experience and strategy. Moreover, a complex strategy is created with Passive Abilities, Cards, Runestones, Items, Enemies, Upgrades, Trades, Randomness, Wyrdness and damage ranges. Every moment you should make a choice considering also future events. Furthermore, game has not only high replayability but also necessity to play again to unlock tons of new items, abilities and cards. When you die and you start another campaign with all your previous upgrades and story continue where you left. In addition, game increase the level of difficulty according to your accomplisments to give you a balanced experience. You can also manually change the difficulty.The philosophical and psychological content of the stories and structure of the new world is very good. Dark humor and jokes are fun. Sounds and musics are very good. Suprisingly first class game. One of the best game in this genre is Slay the Spire (2017). I think the developers enhanced it and made us a very solid game. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game shows a lot of promise and as a Finished product this game could really push the single player deck building Genre,as of posting here are Pros and Cons with the game.Positives:. The Game Has a Town building Aspect to it which is its rogue lite element. Unlocking New armour, Weapons, trinkets and skills will help you overcome the odds and carries on through to your next playthrough.. The branching paths in the areas of the game so far is littered with events, characters for your Town and enemies Both Weak and strong. its pretty unique for a single player deck builder, giving quite a lot a room for strategy between building your deck, tackling groups of enemies in a particular order and interacting with events.. There is a Torch mechanic in this game, Fighting enemies in the wyrdness as they call it, means you will take more damage but you get more rewards or fight in the light to make the fight easier.. Multiple events and characters have been fleshed out with some good voice acting and the dialogue is well written.. The Deck building element (For the warrior) was great, an assortment of different blocks, Debuffs, attacks and talents with room for variety of different types of decks.. The enemy difficulty seems very balanced with room to make the game even harder hopefully in a possible ascension mode not yet available as of this review.. Replayability at the moment there is just the Warrior with 3 different sub classes to choose from with a promise of more Characters available down the later.Negatives:. The thing that hurts this game the most is the Music, especially the battle music at the moment it is the same track for all regular enemies and it sounds very dull and monotone.. The enemy models could be better, they're not terrible but certainly not great.. At the moment most of your skills when cast look the same, no special effects or different animations for some of the better moves you have acquired.. Enemies could have more varied debuffs and buffs for the most part they either give their allies a barrier or try to flood your deck with useless cards.. Consumables such as potions and damage battle buffs seem to acquired too easily in the current build and i wish they were more scarce.. Content:  Obviously with this being early access, between the campaign and endless mode There quite a bit of stuff missing. I would say currently there is at least 15 to 25 hours of content.with the right improvements this game could be something really special. I have never seen so many different elements thrown into a single player deck builder, between the gold, character gear, consumables, area exploration, town improvement and interactive events there so much strategy to this game.Hopefully with enough love and attention to detail this game could be one the greats in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me for a surprise. The narrative and the voice acting gives life to the world and brings an overall great deck building and roguelite experience.Initially, I didn't like the flow and progress of the game; however, game's mechanics grew after the first three or four runs. 9 classes to pick from that unlock over progress, each with their own card base. Difficulty choices increase as you clear each run. You eventually unlock an additional boss near the end, which is a comparison of damage in leaderboard score. Lots of replay value  for the small purchase price. I've played 30 hours at time of review and still have not completed the game's main story -- involving the saving of all villagers from the corruption (wydrness described in game).If you like deck building card games with some strategy, this game offers that and then some. Good pickup for single player enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this is in early access its looking very polished and stable. Runs smoothly on my 5 year old machine and I have experienced no technical issues with the game. There are two versions of the game to choose from at startup but I have only been playing the "rogue like" Conquest version of the game because I have found it so addictive. It involves overhead third person  exploration of the Wyrdness where you are balancing your survival resources to judge how far you travel to try to recruit useful people to improve your village or meet other situations and make choices that effect how the game plays out.  Enemy battles are played out with a card based, deck building mechanic - this seems a bit simplistic at first but once you start coming up against tougher opponents you realise that it has lot of tactical depth to it. Its also very atmospheric with quality voice acting and beautiful artwork setting just the right tone for immersion, Its early access, so there is plenty more to come and I am really looking forward to how its develops through to the finish.

(get on sale if price below 15 or less) Save file disappeared. (being a roguelite you carry over some things) Removing all progress i had after completing last boss on a run. Lost all buildings and upgrades i had.Not complete game. Still a lot of missing content.After figuring out strategies of each group fight because slightly too easy. after complete first (act) i could simply run to each boss and beat them without any issues or items. Overall this looks like it will be a great game eventually and i would hate to see it stop being produced due to releasing too early and asking for too much. If the price doesnt bother you, buy it and you will probably enjoy it once you figure it out (give it a few deaths). Probably dont bother with the campaign at first. If not wait a bit for a sale or more content.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just "beat" the game and was shown a "Thanks for playing please leave a review" message so thought I would.I wish there was a maybe option. This game has some upsides and downsides. The Good: The game play is what you would expect of a rogue-like deck builder. If you enjoy that you will like this. There are a lot of classes and they all feel different from one another. This is great since it will make replay value high. After playing some more I learned that there are 3 Classes (Archer, Warrior, Summoner) then within those 3 classes there are 3 Variations. (ex. Archer has Sentinel which is a flurry of arrows and Zealot which is one huge charged shot every few turns)The art, the 2D art specifically, is gorgeous. Love the art style and how it is very dream like but grotesque. Reminds me of Nils Haam who has made plenty of Magic the Gathering card art. The combat visuals while I touch on graphics in the bad section, it gives a sense of power. The various mechanics seem to work well and intertwine cohesively at least with the 3 characters I have played so far. The audio in this game is spectacular. Whoever worked on the brutal gushing sounds, give them a bonus. The audio makes the game feel so impactful. The music is hit or miss with some tracks but over all I can get behind the tribalism vibe they are going for. The voice acting is appreciated and some of the voice lines don't have that emotional weight behind it but damn if they didn't try. Not perfect voice acting but far from bad either.The Bad: Because I am only 7.2 hours into the game as of this review there is a lot of unknown here so take it with a grain of salt. There are permanent upgrades which affect all characters each run. If you are into that, cool. The reason why I listed this as Bad is because over time it will trivialize the game to the point of boredom. My guess is there is a Max value of upgrades and "Ascension Modes" (see Slay the Spire) which will make those permanent upgrades required so the player doesn't die on the first battle, If this IS the case, then this is a positive.This is a personal opinion but the 3D art is a lot worse than the 2D. I feel like the direction of this game could have been in the 2D art style during combat. See Darkest Dungeon which does this extremely well.The Open World portion of the game seems like a gimmick and I don't think it was done well. First off the terrain has some odd hills and what not that make moving around seem janky especially when there is an enemy or person that is on the 60 degree angle mountain. Second I feel this could have been done with a top down 2D view and made a point and click and still be just as immersive. There are a few bugs but those are just audio related nothing game-breaking.In Conclusion: The game is a lot of fun but I feel the direction in art both enhances and sours portions of the experience. If this was a full 2D game using the same art style they have for the splash art I personally would enjoy it more but that does not mean I do not enjoy the game. I look forward to playing more and definitely will. I would give this game an honest 83/100. There is room for improvement but those improvements are minor critiques that do not distract from the core of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dare I say this is one of the best world building card games I've played. The lore, drawing, voice acting, music, story - all are superb. Hats off to the writer and art teams. However, the game needs a lot of tuning: class balance, progression rewards, all of these seem out of whack and 'early-accessy'.If the above issues would be sorted, this would be a game I would recommend to anyone. As it stands, I would recommend this game to players who are looking something new to play after games like Slay the Spire or Monster Train.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Feels extremely janky overall which never allows you to get into a flow state, you are constantly fighting the camera, its strange torchlight system or looking at the weird map layout. As many other reviews have stated this game should really have been 2D like most deckbuilders, because combat is great but outside combat is HORRIBLE.Deckbuilders have this ability to make time fly, but this never gets there because you are constantly fighting the game, the aesthetic is also terribly bland, its basically Grim Dark shorthand mixed with Unity asset-tier 3d models that just feels like it has zero originality. The Quest system also adds nothing because each run is random, there is no continuity or stakes because you might not see a character for awhile, meaning its just a bunch of fetch quests.The story starts of strong but then basically becomes background noise to wandering around in the dark and dying to samey encounters. The balance also doesn't feel well calibrated, your character goes from a weak pushover to a juggernaut as soon as your build comes together without any stages in-between, this feels really janky and more like you are exploiting the combat system instead of developing your character and winning through strategy or tactics.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Slay the Spire, with the aesthetics of Path of Exile, Diablo 1 & 2's sound design, Dark Souls Lore, but more difficult and still enjoyable. You unlock the classes after playing the newest unlocked class, I really enjoy the Summoner. The early game is NOT about patience, you NEED to die to progress, once you find a playstyle you like don't worry, there are more aspects than most other games have! The Quest cards are interesting (a digital only sort of system). I prefer Slay the Spire for the streamlined combat and how intuitive it is, but I REALLY enjoy this game in other ways, it has a unique level of complexity that allows each class so far to FEEL honestly distinct.

_childDocuments_.review: After 23 of ingame playtime on this game, I will list the pros and cons.Pros: Amazing story with a bunch of voice acting added in!Multiple different stories with different options.A repeat gameplay that changes with each time you die or kill the final boss. Great class system that has a bunch of uniqueness and game style. Difficulty determines rewards and xp bonus. The more runs the more likely you will receive loot drops from upgrades and difficulty. I love the darkness/gothic theme through out the whole story line. Gameplay is smooth and unforgiving.Cons:\Some build are just absolutely silly, doing about 10k+ a turn. The grind of repeating events will eventually ware on you and make you question why it's stuck in a constant loop. Defeating the final boss doesn't really feel like a challenge at the very end and was a let down for me. Some of the content may put people off with how dark it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with a cool gruesome style. It's a little limited in areas but not hugely so. There's 9 classes each playing uniquely and having distinct strengths and weaknesses but each have a "correct" way to play so once you've played a class you've experienced all that class has to offer. There's a fairly limited, but still creative array of mobs to fight in each region as well but it isn't really noticeable as each interacts with each class differently, Pathfinder getting bullied by multi-hit enemies or Barbarian suffering at the hands of single, heavy-hitters. The bosses kind of suffer from the way mobs are done with many mobs posing as much challenge as the bosses. The biggest thing for medium term longevity for me is the quests and characters. There are tons of encounters and quests that can't all be encountered and completed in one or even have a dozen runs. These characters have interesting quirks and personalities and the solutions to their problems are often as suitable insane as they and the world are.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely masterful! I had immediately presumed this game would be listed as "overwhelmingly positive" in reviews and alas have become perplexed that negative reviews actually exist. What a pity. Among a sea of mediocre RNG/Rogue-lite/strategy/card/dice games, this one surpasses almost every one  I've played (and check my game stats, I have sunk my life into these type of games.) A huge roster of characters to pick from which play significantly different from each other -- and more importantly, are actually fun to use. Gorgeous art for the NPCs you encounter and story boards. The music is ominous and rocking. Runs are extremely challenging but never overwhelming nor unfair. Rewards after death feel hopeful and worth the effort. There are several unique opportunities to enhance your character when you play and the game doesn't attempt to screw you over for taking calculated risks.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Quite fun and sometimes unforgiving rogue lite card battler.  8/10+ Nice graphics and soundtrack (3d card battler is always welcome)+ Addictive and has usual "One more run" formula+ 3 factions and each has 3 classes that play bit differently+ Grim and dark, creature design is interesting as well+ Gameplay in general is done right, there are some bugs with certain abilities etc., nothing that cannot be resolved in a patch or two. Some bugs were already resolved in last patch.+ I haven't completed the full story, but I'm very close. It's is nothing spectacular but it is interesting and fits with rogue lite mechanics quite nicely- Game has some optimization problems, I can run many games (indie or AAA) that look better and run better, this one is overusing GPU a lot and FPS can be all over the place. Devs have acknowledged this and are working on it- The Wyrdness filter/fog ruins the game if you ask me. Each biome looks more of less the same because if you don't have lit candles, whole screen will get foggy/blurry. Personally and don't find it easy on the eye.- Meta progression is slow in some aspects and in later runs doesn't really motivate you to play that much (ofc this is highly subjective)- Some classes are unbalanced, some are way too OP. Having OP class would be fine it it weren't so easy pick certain passives and cards for that same class.I have 43h clocked in per Steam, although I feel I played more. I'm starting to get bored now even though I haven't unlocked everything fully. I feel like I've seen everything the game can offer, but I get easily "bored" when it comes to roguelite games like this.Definitely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally backed the board game (which is amazing) and received this game with it. I really wasn't expecting much from the digital game. I've been popping in on it here and there the last year and honestly didn't think it was very fun initially. Boy, have they come a long way. They have really poured so much effort into making this a great one. When I came back in to see the work they've done, I was shocked. With my love for the board game aside, this digital stand alone game is absolutely amazing on it's own. It captures the same dark, twisted fantasy world. It is (as expected) very well-written and the voice acting is superb. The graphics are not the best, but honestly I was so entranced with the beautiful artwork and story that I don't find myself noticing it all that much. If you love Slay the Spire, but want a little more story in your game this is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid entry into the grossly overpopulated deckbuilder genre, this game manages to capture a lot of the elements of Slay the Spire, looks infinitely better graphically, and fills out a lot more design space. None of this should come as a surprise as Awakened Realms is a traditional board game company with multiple high pedigree products. The runs do tend to take a bit longer than a Slay the Spire run, and the roguelite elements make the difficulty a little harder to suss out, you do gain power in between runs, but with the amount of classes, several of which have multiple passives to choose from at the start, you'll definitely be able to find a LOT of depth here.

_childDocuments_.review: Music hits different when you're looking at a useless hand. You get a sense that you are going to perish or become an unstoppable aberration slayer from the first couple of encounters. It's story progression is very similar to Hades in that death is the only way to progress. Keep dying, keep growing stronger. Game is a slow burn at first but ramps to be one of the most immersive card games out there with a stunning ominous atmosphere, gripping characters arcs, and stellar voice acting. Easily one of my favorite roguelike card title.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for awhile. The game seems unfinished. Almost 2 years after release and you can still talk to guarded NPCs without first fighting the enemy by staying just outside the aggro radius. Needless to say, getting benefits from NPCs without risking anything destroys the balance of the game and should be avoided unless you want easy wins. And speaking of balance, the devs aimed too high with the number of classes. Sure, there are lots of characters to play, and some of them are really interesting, but some cards are absurd, while others are laughably bad. If you make a mistake and pick a bad card, you're pretty much stuck with it because card removals are very rare. There might be an argument that some cards could be good if there was more enemy diversity. Seems like every fight goes pretty much the same, and there aren't really any enemies that punish turtle builds so you can just stack defense which leads to very boring gameplay if you want to win. Will I play more in the future? Maybe, but there are better roguelikes more deserving of my time right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Filled with magnificent artwork and story telling, but unfortunately hampered by an atrocious graphics engine, poor balancing, and thematic inbreeding.Balance is all over the place depending on class and enemies you encounter. Some enemies will be significantly tougher for some classes to what feels like a plain unfair extent. The same goes for bosses. This does not seem to be an explicit design decision rather than an implicit one by having a few too many classes.The graphics engine feels outdated, choppy, and unnecessary. This can largely be ignored, but those cool 3d-models for enemies sort of fall apart when the animations look cheap, and the different classes look too samey. In this case, simpler would definitely have been better.The thematic overlap between classes is too apparent. While the three summoners have a different behavior at their core, and different playstyles, it feels cheap when you essentially get the red/green/blue flavor of the same class. Time could have been spent adding depth instead of breadth. This would probably also make balancing easier.However, in spite of all my complaints, you'll probably enjoy this game if you can look past the issues described! If you think you can't I'd suggest spending your time/money on Slay the Spire/Monster Train/Banners of Ruin/Griftlands instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this because I  have worn Slay the Spire out!Only played for a hour or so - but this game is better in every way to my previous addiction. > The more detailed gritty graphics.> The lore and background story (a unique take on  the Arthurian legends)  is worth the price of admission alone. > The game mechanics are far deeper, far more interesting. In short, it trumps what is a classic of the genre in every way. So much so that any comparison in redundant. The game is in early access, but already is a complete experience and well worth the asking price. Also,the devs are surprisingly open (being more self critical than they need to be!), and obviously passionate about this project. If they left the game as it is, I would consider my money well spent - yet there is tones more coming on their road map. So - move over all other deck builders - This is the new king of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: While it implicitly states the game has multiple classes the archetypes are so disingenuously the same both in combat and ability that it caused me to instantly quit. Summoners with the exact same summons only reskinned, attack animations recycled, and the sheer draw this damn game has on my cpu despite looking like someone took Path of Exile and zoomed all the way in on low settings is hillarious.Despite having "300 abilities!" I saw them loop but of a different color in each class I unlocked. Oh here is a "New ability" just like the old one only BLUE!!! Like 5% minion damage every card played working for both the Summoner and Blood Mage which is EXACTLY THE SAME F*CKING CLASS ONLY THE BLOOD MAGE SACRIFICES ITS HP AND IS FAR WORSE! AND NO YOU CANNOT "Upgrade" YOUR CLASS. ITS BY LEVELING BY KILLING THINGS. NO POINTS INTO STATS...NOTHING...RPG MY A-S-S.In some sick way I can say this could fall under false advertising but I don't know since they could stretch "300 unique passives" to be whatever the hell they mean by unique as in "You only get this ability on this class because its the blue one! The green one on the other class does the same but you can't get them both!"If you play the game you will stick to summoner because it's broken and the first class is so terrible it can't even make it to the second level 80% of the time out of sheer crap mediocre damage cards with essentially 0 defense because 1 block means NOTHING when you fight 3 enemies half the time. And sure you can even walk around the enemies to talk to the NPC's in the game but THAT SHOULDN'T BE A THING!!And the unlocks like the vendor giving better trinkets? I doubt I could unlock them all in under 400 hours and thats not like 1 unlock per hour...Thats ONE 1/100 MATERIALS NEEDED TO UPGRADE ONE NODULE THAT CAN MAAAAAYBE DROP WITH RNG ONCE PER RUN IF YOU DON'T GET KILLED BY CARDS SCREWING YOU OVER!Oh and a 68-80 HP pool in a game where the second level enemies hit for 27-377 which I saw hit a golem of mine is utterly ridiculous.This screams cashgrab and it sure did mine *unless steam gives me my refund which it probably wont*. Don't let it take yours.Edit: I did not get my refund.. It took me 6 hours to unlock the class that was just a reskinned Summoner and already had a reskinned first class.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Adapted from the extremely popular Legacy boardgame, Tainted Grail Conquest started off a little uneven but Early Access has done it wonders. It's addictive gameplay loop ensures your "one more game" scratch is well and truly itched. Initially they tried to write a single-player legacy style campaign along-side the conquest mode but I am glad that they ditched that to focus on this.It is a combination of Roguelite, Deck-building and RPG which sits somewhere between Slay the Spire and Trials of Fire. Graphically, they have done a good job of ensuring the Wyrdness feels oppressive and the enemies uniquely terrifying. My only bug-bear is that progression is glacially slow. Non-Class unlocks take so long to obtain and have very little impact as a whole. The wide variety of classes however does help mix up the content with 9 different options to choose, each with a unique way of playing. Overall, this game is excellent and deserves your attention if you are even remotely a fan of Slay the Spire, Monster Train or Trials of Fire.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly fun and addictive experience. I have so far completed one full run with sentinel and tried a few unsuccessful runs with other classes. My impression is that without several permanent upgrades some classes are vastly inferior to others, but the good thing is - the game is fun enough to encourage trying out different classes and builds. For a couple of euros this is absolutely worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: The game definitely has some balance issues but my god the story, characters, and music are incredible. Worth the pick up at full price. The gameplay is stellar. My biggest complaints are the optimization problems that I'm having as well as the balance as I mentioned before. The game just feels too easy. I beat the final boss on my second run with an unupgraded Sentinel. I also have a beefy computer and my game can't be run on Ultra settings. Definitely needs addressing. Other than that this game is spectacular. Please buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere and great dialogue which is largely voice acted, and is done fantastically. 3 archetypes of decks with 3 subclasses within them allowing for 9 different characters to play as. A handful of characters to rescue and gain permanent residence in your village. With another dozen or so that are just met throughout the run while outside of the village, each with their own story and quests. Lots of different enemies with varying abilities. The 3 deck archetypes play vastly different from each other, the subclasses not so much but enough to keep it fresh if you have never played the subclass before. So yeah can't really recommend this game enough considering the price its at and the amount of hours you can get out of it. Even if you just played through as each class once. I wont say the game is perfect and some things and details seem obscure but i almost prefer that to a tutorial heavy game that feels the need to explain everything to me while holding my hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm a total novice in this genre and don't really have any similar games to compare it to, but I've played TCG games like Hearthstone and MTG Arena. What attracted me to the game was honestly the screenshots and the way other reviews described the atmosphere - and honestly they were spot on. The game has a very mature atmosphere (and by that I mean it features existential horror, dark myths and general creepiness - not porn) and some sick music that repeats often but never feels repetitive. For art style think of a mix between Diablo 1/2 and Warhammer Chaos with some Dark Ages mythos thrown in (witches and wendigos et al) and for the music there is a very strong resemblance to the Witcher 3 in tone and choice of instruments - and that's a good thing. Story seems like it should be good although I'm a little early on to really say, thinks are fairly vague at this point but all the characters you meet are definitely.... interesting, and the game gives you plenty of sidequests and permanent resources to progress so you probably never have a run that felt like a total waste of time.As for the deckbuilding part, I have no other games to compare it to, but I like it. Some classes definitely feel more powerful than others but it will also depend on your personal tastes. Some classes like the Wyrdhunter (the starting class) are sort of "OTK" heroes where you will spend several turns just sustaining yourself until you fill up your ultimate meter and draw the perfect hand to go in for the kill with massive damage, other classes are summoners where you progressively increase your board presence whilst keeping yourself shielded until you overwhelm your enemies, and other classes use bows (I have one unlocked but I have yet to play it). There's still a bunch of classes and NPCs and cards I haven't discovered yet, but as someone who got the game on a whim for the story and setting, that's what will probably keep me coming back. So far I have zero regrets about my purchase and there is a good amount of polish here for the price (all lines are voiced and pretty well too for the most part, artwork and visual style are top notch). Good job devs. If you are a fan of the genre and the setting appeals to you, I imagine you can't go wrong with this one, and even if - like me - you have no previous interest in the genre, you might still love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most underrated rogue-lights I've ever played. Awesome soundtrack, great gameplay, a surprising amount of quality lore and good replayabilty with a lot of unlocks. Each class plays very differently across 3 archetypes. This game deserves more attention, don't miss it if you enjoy games like Slay the Spire or Monster Train.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been on my wish list for a while and I finally gave in and bought it. I was not prepared for how much I was going to fall in love with this game. For being early access, it shows soo much promise for much more to come. All the current characters available have different play styles that let you tailor different builds for them, making every play through different from your last. There is some limited character customization but it looks like they'll be adding more to it in the future; but overall it is still nice. They reward you with more cosmetics to tailor your character's appearance to your liking. Overall, a solid 9/10 right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie at first I didn't think I would like this game. If you asked me earlier if I thought this game was good, I would mention that it is visually polished and the sound aesthetic matched the atmosphere.  It is a presentation in the deck-building genre that hasn't been seen.  Then I started unlocking cards and characters, and I saw the subtle brilliance in the progression and storytelling. Rather than being a silent protagonist, your actions lead you to unique experiences and individuals if you are brave enough to explore the wyrdness. The settling of this amorphous, formless wilderness where enemies and allies are littered throughout equally is a stroke of inspiration, in videogame development.  I wish the setting was far less grimdark at times and more of a beautiful surreal horror like the movie Legend, or the Cell. But that is a stylistic critic and not a real drawback from the offering. This is a superb addition to the deck-building genre. A surprising game that surpassed what I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the worst optimization I've seen in a game.  It's a real shame, because there is a good game in here.  This is a fun take on the Slay the Spire formula, with some good new ideas of its own.  Unfortunately it's a stuttering mess that sends cpu and gpu temps through the roof.  At launch the devs seemed like they were working on some fixes, but over the last couple months nothing has been patched except some extra language support.  When it came out I had a gtx970, and the game would run (poorly) on low/medium, but even then it was heating my system up far beyond acceptable.  Now I've upgraded to a 3070ti, and while the game does look better, it still has out of control temps and constant stuttering/frame drops.  Do not buy this unless a solid optimization patch is released.  This genre is very saturated these days;  there are plenty of other deck builder games that don't run like garbage or turn your pc into an oven.

_childDocuments_.review: The stylish graphics gave me classic Diablo vibes. The gameplay is easy to grasp and interesting and the soundtrack sets a nicely foreboding atmosphere for this deck building roguelite. There are various classes to play and the many unlockable cards and skills and different game modes that bring in variation for many hours worth of gameplay.My only gripe is that some of the card descriptions are misleading. For example, while a specific class uses a "gain barrier" card for creating an additional shield of hp that remains until it's broken, another character gains this barrier ONLY for the duration of ONE round. Also, there are cards that have a flip side, but for what I can tell, there's no way of reading what says on the flip side before the card comes in play again.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not followed the development very closely, but a few updates ago, this game had a fun combat system that used different types of runes to combo them together, it was very novel and fresh.The game I played today is jut an imitation of Slay the Spire. It does it competently, but still feels tired and threaded. It's sad to see a game with a fun and original combat system turn itself into an unimaginative copy of another game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Starts slow, but once it gets going there's a ton of fun content built on top of a solid deck builder. One warning - the controller implementation is pretty bad, be ready for some serious frustration if you're not using mouse+key.For the first couple of hours I felt frustrated and found unlocks to come trickling in too slowly, but after unlocking a handful of new cards and abilities I began unlocking more per run. Runs have been taking me about an hour each, which is a nice length imo, and you can save and exit any time (thank you!)Deckbuilding is competent but a bit hit or miss in my limited experience. There's a ton of classes to unlock, the 2 I've tried have been nicely themed even if playstyles are a bit similar (mitigating incoming damage is key because healing is limited). Base decks are pretty boring and it takes a bit to pick up enough cards/passives for things to be interesting. Story and atmosphere are fun, there's a ton of events and NPCs to encounter, I really like the concept of the world so far. There's a lot of upgrades to unlock but I've only earned enough currency for a couple.Playing via controller (XBOX) has been super frustrating. Card selection is done via thumbstick instead of dpad, and there's no dead zone so it's way too easy to accidentally move up/down when you only want to move left/right. DPAD can spend consumables even if they're not shown on screen, cancel/confirm buttons are not consistent, etc etc. I've definitely had some rage inducing moments caused purely by the controller implementation.If you like deckbuilders this is 100% worth a look, especially if you like the atmosphere. Prepare yourself for some frustrations if you use a controller. Overall I'm really enjoying this game and I'm looking forward to playing it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game was my surprise game for 2021. I played this game, and the first run through I wasn't too sure. However, the more I delved into this game, the more I enjoyed it. The achievements push you to try different builds, and were mainly challenging. They also push you to find out more about the story line. I have recommended this game multiple times to friends. 10/10 wish I could go back and restart the experience again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: My first deckbuilder game and i absolutely love it. In many ways it reminds me of Dark Souls. It has nightmarish atmosphere, death being a part of the story, challenging boss battles and feeling of great accomplishment after winning, NPCs with wicked backgrounds and quests, phenomenal art style. And the music... it has to be one of the best OST in games. It pumps so much adrenaline during combat, think Witcher 3 mixed with Hellblade, simply amazing. Highly recommended even if you think you're not into this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Great roguelike deck builder that pulls you in a grim, Arthurian/Norse atmosphere with a fantastic soundtrack. Your village grows across each run which adds a nice rpg element. It's in early access, so expect a few glitches here and there. But it's clear the developers are working on it continuously - every time I login I see another fix/polish. Recommended.P.S.: It also has a short campaign (still in development). Play that first to get acquainted with certain mechanics (e.g. "wyrdness").
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Darkest Dungeon's clone. Not as good, but not horrible.The game is complex (at least complex enough), fun, atmospheric. I actually liked it slightly more than Darkest Dungeon just because I find the gameplay much more fun.Cons - the writing is a bit simplistic, the story and the writing style resembles Thea a lot, which is extremely annoying. Writing feels like "what if Thea, but in Arthurean setting." One thing about the atmospheric part, Darkest Dungeon genuinely felt like a horror game, good writing and good intro, interesting dialogues play a very important part. This game, unfortunately, lacks all of it. There are encounters with interesting dialogues, sure, but overall they aren't particular important, they barely influence the gameplay and they feel like an afterthought. Bottom line, if I were to introduce someone to the genre, I would have recommended Darkest Dungeon over Tainted Grail. It is hard not to appreciate the efforts put into this game though, and at the very least the technical implementation is not bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I mean all I really have to say is wow. This game is an excellent combination of Deck-building, rogue-lite, and RPG...which is something I never expected to say.The mechanics are different enough from others (ie. Slay the Spire, Monster Train) to really let Tainted Grail stand out on its own and be a unique, individual game. The aesthetics are gorgeous! A lot of time went into the art for each card and each enemy.The story is very entertaining and it actually makes me want to talk to each character multiple times, and the voice acting is very well done!If you like StS or games of similar style, this is a must-have.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: got to the boss of the third act in my first run.. seems a bit too easy, maybe. but it is super fun! pretty sure this also has difficulty settings, so having a fun - not super difficult - base difficulty is probably a good idea. encounters are fun, even though some, especially with a lot of enemies, turn out to be a bit chaotic. you play a card or two - bam, everybody explodes.highly recommended for the price though! while somewhat similar to slay the spire, this has some very distinct unique features that make it a lot of fun in different ways.edit: after some more hours.. it seems the game might be not very well balanced. as stated above, my first playthrough was really fun and simple. but since then i stumbled upon some pretty major roadblocks in different places. the different classes are also not well balanced either. e.g. the summoner class(es) are rather weak, but also make it seem like there would be cards in the game later that completely break their difficulty.

And sound design! And Presentation!Mechanically the game is solid but the writing takes this 10 levels beyond that!If you enjoy worldbuilding and quality cRPGs, this game is a must-have!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Decent rougelike gameplay.- Runs are mostly less that 2 hours so losing each run isn't so bad.- You can mix and match the cards from the different classes to create quite lethal combos. My favorite was using Blood Mage (with its minion auto-level ability) with cards that increase attack and auto-delevel, making a loop that can increase the minion's attack to 1K+.Cons:- The candle burning mechanic is annoying and I'm still not sure what burning the candles even does, it's never properly explained. Because of this mechanic, you are incentivized to rush from mob to mob before the candle burns out without fully taking in the world and game atmosphere etc. - Lacks replayability, probably because its so easy once you figure out the mechanics. Compared to the classics in this genre like "Ring of Pain", "Slay the Spire" or even "Monster Train", I don't feel any drive to do more runs to unlock more stuff etc. - There seems to be a story here but all I was able to grasp were mostly undertones regarding King Arthur mythology. Kinda wish there was a more coherent plot to set this game apart from other roguelites.Overall, 5/10. Not a bad game but not one I would recommend either. The aforementioned games: "Ring of Pain", "Slay the Spire" or "Monster Train" just do it much better and I would rather spend my time playing those games instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is amazing and straightforward, though it has a lot of variety it doesn't try to make it overly complex or difficult, yet it still manages to give you a challenging way of discovering how to build your deck. You might think that you will get overwhelmed by all the RPG elements and currency but that doesn't happen. Difficult-wise the game is also pretty fair, it provides a challenge for every type of player from beginners that only want to enjoy the game as a casual player and know more about the lore to higher levels of difficult for those who want to test their limits. Graphics and design are great together with the soundtrack. Fair price and provide a lot of replayability.If you enjoy card games, give this one a try and you will be surprised!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enoughThat I can overlook overflow of bugs.As the game asks you to leave review after killing first "last" boss, I can say that the game is a buggy mess, but this mess is ambitious and fun.I am not a fan of drab aesthetik - everything "sucks", black and mad. In the end you are told that we played the "bad guys" side the whole time, but it is not an exuse to have 75% of the game be "Broody black with pinch of spilled guts".The game asks you to keep playing more cycles, but I feel exausted after 2 runs.1st run ended after starting second zone, because of bug in perk interaction.You see there is a perk, that gives you +300% damage on the 1st hit of the next turn, if this turn you played 2 cards or less (on starting class). I built my character around that, and even killed 1st boss in the 1st run.After killing the boss I got to choose 1 free perk, and I choose one, that activated on the same condition, but granted +100% damage on the whole of the next turn, thinking that it will have nice synergy.Litlle did I know, that currently this perc interaction is broken, because while this perc have same counter, they count cards each on they own.So - 1 card played - 1st perc counts it and 2nd perc counts it. If I want my bonus, I can't play more than 1 card a turn, and I did not have "I win" card, so my build and run ran down the drain in 2-3 normal encounters.Second run was wih summoner, and with a bit of thinking, a lot of reading, and a lot of patience, I cleared all 3 areas and 4 bosses (and recruted bunch of NPC).In the time of 1,3 runs (7 hours by steam count), game crashed on me 3 times, while I played with minimalest grafic options possible (exept resolution - I played on 1280x720 and you can go lower).Disscussion indicate that corupting save (even auto one) is a problem you can face, some loot can dissapear, and you can softlock game if you will moove slighly not the way devs intended (as example if you tried to use more than only mouse for interactions with a game, or even tried to drag and drop reward loot, intead of clicking "take all button")Music is cool, nothing bad to say here.There are 9 classes (card packs + passives packs), and even by playing only 2, I can say that they were distinct enough, and with some variety of possible builds inside a "class".Voice acting is good, but due to desing choises of devs, it dosent make me want to explore more of this "grimderp" universe. I am not runnig to see more stuff, because I already know that I will find nothing more than more "grimderpness". There is just no humor here, and this direction is just not for me (Yes I know that comparing it with Hades is not fair, but come on, I feel like this is movie DC universe, with nothing emotionally pleasing in sight).Mechanics are fine, fun and complex, when they work as intended (see bugs).All in all could be a lot better, but ambition, that I see under the rough surface makes me want to suppot game, so I can see at least intended game as is "presented", and not as it "is".If they will make DLC, instead of fixing the damn game, or will focus all of their attention on the other game that they are making, instead of fixing this one, this will be the last game, I buy from this team.With your ambition and vision, you bought youself some wiggle space from me, lets see what will you do with this trust.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, interesting characters, extremely addicting and very fair, compared to other rougelite deckbuilders. I would actually recommend this to people, who didn't like Slay the Spire or similiar games.The only downside I found, is that the classes are quite unbalanced - some are very difficult, others are almost auto-play. Future patches and feedback from the community will fix this however.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game so far, really enjoying it. The atmosphere and gameplay have been excellent. The sky is the limit for future potential in this game. If you enjoy deck building and dark fantasy, this is a must buy. I'm also very impressed with the work done so far by Awaken Realms Digital as a company and team. Other Early Access game developers need to take note, the amount of communication and progress I've witnessed since purchase on this future master piece of a game is truly impressive. _childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations by a long shot. Definitely up there with my favourite deck builders right now. Pros:  - Good voice acting and writing, paired with a story that fits a rogue-lite game. Worldbuilding is pretty solid for a deckbuilding game. The first time round I definitely enjoyed listening to the stories but future encounters are kept short for re-runs. - Lots of freedom of choice. You are very frequently given the option between 2 or 3 things which makes tailoring your build easier. Rerolls are also fairly cheap. - A large variety of enemies that have many different behaviors that allow for interesting interactions. They don't just feel like stat-bloated versions of weaker enemies. - A large number of unlockables as you progress. - Cards scale well (from cheaper weak hitting cards to more expensive heavy ones). Damage is based off of a % of your base damage (in contrast to say Slay the Spire where a 0 cost attack will scale with strength the same as a 3 cost attack). - Well explained tool-tips on cards and hovering enemies. - Decent quality models and artwork. - No major bugs so far - Cheap, considering the amount of content and replay-ability - Interesting mechanics (leveling up, passives, runes etc.) that combine fairly fluidly without being overly complicated.Cons: - Definitely some issues with optimization. Game runs relatively smoothly most of the time but has frequent frame drops when transitioning or loading battles. - Animations feel a little clunky and repetitive. A lot of cards use the same animation. - UI is passable, but definitely lacking. - The overworld feels rather bland and scarce. It's not particularly fun to explore, just walking from one battle to the next.I would definitely recommend it at it's current price. Quite frankly, I'm surprised it isn't more expensive.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 2Changed it to a negative review as they senselessly increased the difficulty in weird ways. All classes are now available.... NOT-you get one to start the melee class that uses multiple hits to build ultimate (forgot the name)-All other classes are unlocked in a random order by end of run xp gains-The berserker no longer heals when killing  things with his ult, making him 10k times less survivable-You can no longer return to town (at least in the tutorial level I haven't passed it yet) to heal or buy more goodies, the teleport feature for wyrdstones no longer exists-The boss of the tutorial zone summons minions every 10 hits, their damage is multiplied by the number of minions out. Since the only class you got is based on multi hit cards, which target random enemies, you will easily get 2 or 3 minions out even accidentaly the first 2 rounds of combat if you built your guy how he should be built. -After failing multiple times to down the boss ( 3 or 4 runs of simply just dying with 0 excitement as I can't play a class I'm actually into) I unlocked my first class... the druid... yaaaaay another class I don't want to play, at least he's not hit based? Idk I've never played him. the ENTIRE tutorial level feels like a scripted wipe you have to relive until you unlock another class by... dying. Womp freaking WompThis is sad because they added a lot of new cards and  stuff which feel good. Too bad I'm forced to play in ways I don't find enjoyable. =====================================================================UPDATEThey have tweaked or even overhauled many aspects of the game and it's working better than ever. Decks feel better and they did away with gear and replaced with a runestone system that works much better. ======================================================================A Wyrd take on Aurthurian legend that isn't a bad experience for 20 bux if you like slow moving deck builder roguelikes. Playing the Roguelike mode atm. I've downed the first of 3 bosses.  Classes need balancing I found the guardian to be rather hard mode compared to warrior. Haven't played mage yet and Druid is still heavy testing phase. The game aesthetic is pretty but I'm not sure why they bothered making it look like you have free control of your character as there is no "open world" to explore at all it is very path based and may as well be set up similar to Darkest Dungeon but top down you know? So far the card games are neat and have fun combos and such I'd like to see more ability to edit your deck. Gear is like non existent. When you spawn in initially you get one regular shop guy that has one armor and a sword for sale and until you complete a quest and gain 4000 Wyrdstone (20 hours in and I have like 400) you won't get to expand that at all. You'd think once you find your blacksmith you'd get more. Well you do, one more weapon and one more armor option (for the blacksmith they are randomized per run, the item vendor always sells the same armor/sword) So, assuming they are an upgrade you have all the black smith has to offer until you get thousands MORE wyrdstone. You can get this from downing bosses or fighting enemies without being protected by the wyrdcandles. You get like 5 -15 a fight if that. The only way to heal is Healing potions or any random event that may offer a bit of healing (often risky). Which is rough to start but about halfway through the first "leg" of the map you are downing things efficiently enough to keep enough potions stocked to keep going.  Then once you got things seemingly in hand you open up the second leg (this is after I have killed and looted everything I possibly could on the first leg) and you're back to getting your ass beat. harrrrd. Enemys go from (literally) *trivial* and *easy* to *talesworthy*... there was no "medium" anywhere lol. It feels like a pretty game with some Heroes of MnM in its heart. Minus the gear, units, skill trees, world, etc. That said I did play it for like 20 hours straight for some reason. I'll likely play it again its just hard to justify  that kind of time played and so little actually shown for it. No fancy gear or anything. I got a legendary card that was bad ass but you lose that when you die so woooop woop. Usually a good roguelike will have you "building" something up between runs and so far I haven't been able to expand anything beyond simply getting my Blacksmith (1 new wpn and armor and offers no other reason to be there) and my seamstress (sells nothing just wants you to upgrade her ♥♥♥♥ for... you guessed it... thouuuusands of Wyrdstone). I feel like I'm not even experiencing the game reallly.

_childDocuments_.review: not a fan of card gamesnot a fan of rogue-games, no matter if they are "light" or notbut i do love Tainted Grailimagine Diablo, Soulsborne and Path of Exile had a love childboth the visual design and the plot ooze athmosphere and moodit also helps that the voice-work is spot on and the soundtrack is a mix of The Witcher and more mainstream nordic-sounds. it just bangs.the only downside are the somewhat lacking sound-effect, they lack some "oomph", but that's just nitpicking.when it comes to gameplay the game is a card-game, but also a Diablo-rpg-clone. your village stands for the permanent progression (there's more permanent progression) and ties together story, gaining power and actual gameplay goals in a "just one more try"-manner that many other rogue-lights fail. tbh. this is the first rogue-light progression-system i can live with.you pick your character amongst a wide array of chars, which are quite well done and would even be great in a hack'n slay or action-rpgpassive effects, active "ultimate abilities" and actual card-decks create unique classes that actual grow during each run like they would in a normal rpgwhile playing you not just unlock more upgrades and support-items/abilities for your village but also totaly new cards for subsequent runs. so yeah, while each run starts you kinda fresh both the story and the actual gameplay support real progression, both in a lore sense and in actual "power-gain".battles vary between the more standart trash-mob combat and quite interesting boss-battlesthe wyrd mechanic is also interesting, kinda like light worked in Darkest Dungeon; while you do not get benefits for running with maximus "wyrdness", it ads unique cards that often offer ups and down for playing or not playing, which ads another strategic layer; also certain enemies gain or lose special skills depending on the level of wyrd.all in all i realy didn't think this game would be for me, but after a friend's recommendation i gave it a chance and boy am i glad for it. i cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun deck building auto battler card game. This game is a rare 3D game with beautiful graphics, but also means a beefier setup. There is a large variety of classes and cards, letting you have fun with a style you like. Everything you do will grant you experience / currency in some form, so just enjoy the game and farm if you want a specific currency. There is an overworld with a town in the centre (including shops) and a few areas surrounding it; after defeating the boss in each area you can exit and progress to the next area - but you can't go back! So make sure to clear everything out before you take the portal out. There is a miasma surrounding you that can decrease your stats and acts as a fog of war, blocking your vision and making it hard to move and see anything. This adds to the immersion, but I found it really annoying so I turned off the vision blocking darkness, which made the game a lot more playable. The miasma can be warded off with candles, which at the start is scarce and your "light" level starts off low. You will encounter events as well as static mobs on the map, making it easy to plan a route to navigate. Like normal maze puzzles, I worked backwards from the boss and plotted a path to my starting point. It's important to note that the candle only depletes when you make a step, meaning you don't need to light one until just before a battle. Shrines have an AoE aura that can pause your candle depletion, and also has an option to extend the aura. This is pointless however, as you can gain the much more important gold, or enhanced stats; I usually save shrines for a stat boost before fighting the boss.---{ Rating }---10 / 10---{ PC Requirements }---☐ Potato☐ Decent☑ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computer---{ Audience }---☐ Beginner☐ Casual Gamer☑ Normal Gamer☐ Expert---{ Graphics }---☑ You forget what reality is☐ Beautiful☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad---{ Audio }---☐ Eargasm☑ Great☐ Good☐ Okay☐ Bad---{ Gameplay }---☑ Great☑ Fun☑ Challenging☐ Generic☐ Frustrating---{ Difficulty }---☐ Just press 'W'☐ Easy☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Difficult☐ Dark Souls---{ Grind }---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if you care about leaderboards☑ Isn't necessary to progress☑ Normal☐ Too much grind---{ Story }---☐ No Story☐ Bad / Generic☑ Some lore☐ Good☐ Fantastic---{ Game Time }---☐ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☐ Short (4 - 8 hours)☐ Few hours (10 - 20 hours) [if you focus on the main story]☑ Many hours (20 - 40)☐ Long (40 - 60 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Very Long (61 - 100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)---{ Replayability }---☐ It's a one-time experience☐ Only for achievements☐ If you wait a few months / years☐ Definitely☑ Infinitely replayable---{ Bugs }---☑ Never heard of☐ Minor bugs☐ Can get annoying☐ Lots of bugs☐ Bugs destroy the game---{ Price }---☑ Full price☐ Wait for Sale☐ If u have some spare money left☐ You could also just burn your money

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a pretty cool Dark Souls-esque aesthetic to it, which I love. It's all voice-acted as well, even with a narrator, and the voice acting in the game is quite good. It looks and sounds beautiful. The music, the sound effects. And being all 3D with a party (summonable minions anyways), it has an old-school RPG feel and doesn't feel totally like a deckbuilder. It's more like Baten Kaitos or FF8 than Slay the Spire. I do recommend this game, and I got a good 42 hours out of it before I felt "okay, that's enough".The game has, in my opinion, one REALLY big flaw. That is, it has three character types, and those types each have 3 basically clones with slight differences. Melee, summoner, and archer. But, in my opinion, most of the characters just... simply suck. For example, the default Summoner's minions don't die, and you can level them up to 20 or more pretty easily, Golem absorbs almost all the damage, so you just level him up to get more health and you're basically invincible, whereas Blood Mage's minions auto-die after four turns, and Necromancer's special kills all of his minions for a transformation that only lasts one turn and has too many cards that focus on sacrificing minions (and I think his minions auto-die, too? I don't know they die easily though). The archers kind of suck because they focus on the flipping mechanic (using a card transform it into another card) with the exception of the third one, who doesn't discard the flips upon use, but they all have terrible defense because they focus on Barrier which expires after a turn and is just a shield with hit points. The melees get Block and an ability to make it lasts two turns, plus they fully absorb 1 hit per block, but at least one of them has a kind of garbage special.Anyways, despite all the unlocks and meta-progression stuff and trying to unlock the true ending, it gets a bit boring after 30 - 40 hours, because quite honestly most of the characters just aren't that fun to play. Only two, three, four tops are fun or well-made.I do overall recommend it, it's got an old school RPG feel to it and it's extremely well-polished.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Deck Building that lets you become quite OP on some classes. I am Currently Difficulty 9 and rising.Voice acting was pretty decent, eventually there was just too much dialogue and i just wanted to get my run over with so i'd skip a few and listen to a few.You can practically play the entire game one handed using the mouse since it uses point and click as well as WASD. I prefer WASD because you can step close enough to some NPC's and trigger their dialogue/event before bothering to encounter the enemy. Decent amount of classes to unlock and cards and even some cosmetics.The 3 Factions are basically Bow classes, Melee Classes and Summoner Classes, 3 of each.Bow has 2 of the funnest classes, Apostate and Sentinel. Zealot as well, but i have barely played this class.Apostate is borderline broken imo. It is very easy to build damage and practically 1-2 shot most enemies, sometimes even bosses if you got the right setup. If you like big numbers but long set up time, this is the class.Sentinel is more balanced, you basically shotgun blast the enemies with a bunch of arrow cards and its ultimate skill. Quite satisfying to play.Melee has Pathfinder, which is basically a tank that build damage each turn he's not hit. Wyrdhunter who uses multi-hit cards to build up his passive and ultimate for big damage. Berzerker that needs to be low HP to do good damage.Summoners are Blood, this ones my fav of 3 summoners. Blood loses HP to summon and promote his minions. His minions attack each turn and overcharge (activate a stronger attack basically) on every 4th promotion and die, they also promote automatically each turn. Have to manage HP as a resource.Druid type of Summoner can promote his minions and make them stronger, but if they get hit, they deal their level as damage to the PC. and i haven't played Necromancer.The game gives out tons of upgrades as you do a run. You'll be choosing new cards, and passives often, getting items for use in combat and even a Flute that you can obtain from a Pied Piper who can change what it does, you keep this flute between runs and can use it once per combat. A Dog/wolf companion if you followed the quest right.The Village stuff gets upgraded as you play and you can complete runs on higher difficulties with enemies having more stats and annoyances for extra gold, which is used to upgrade combat items. Eventually you'll have some decent upgrades and a lot of runs can become easier, you'll have more options and gold to spend on returns to the village. Definitely the best part of this game is coming up with broken builds. The worst part of this game is the optimization. It's pretty bad, this game has no reason to run the way it does.

_childDocuments_.review: Tainted Grail: Conquest is a deck building roguelike with light RPG elements set in the dark fantasy setting of Avalon. TG:A has 9 classes that are unlocked gradually as your complete runs. These classes can be broken down into 3 play styles of melee, archer, and summoner. The 3 classes under each of these 3 play styles share a lot of cards between them but differ in execution. Some of these cards are not unlocked until after completing runs with that class encouraging repeated runs. Some classes are more interesting than others. I personally found the 3 melee classes the most fun to play whereas the archer classes did not distinct enough from one another.In addition to class specific cards, there are cards granted by NPCs and vendors, sometimes requiring the completion of a task or quest beforehand. These quests and NPCs are where the RPG mechanics come into play as you are given a handful of dialogue options when solving various dilemmas in Avalon. Unfortunately, these choices never felt very meaningful as there was often a clear right choice with the wrong choices being downright punishing to your character. These NPCs were well voice acted (in most cases) and the dialogue was written well enough to make repeated runs feel distinct enough for a good while.What did NOT contribute to distinct repeated runs was the exploration and environmental design. This is by far the weakest element of TG:A. Once you've gotten enough experience/cards/stat increases to complete a full run you will see that a full run consists of 3 wings each with its own boss fight and then a final boss fight. These wings have branching paths, but there isn't an choice involved as you can clear an entire wing (and often should to ensure your level is high enough to face the later fights). The game uses a system where you have a limited number of candles that ward away the wyrdness (penalties in battle) that in theory encourages path planning but it doesn't take long until upgrades make the mechanic meaningless. Additionally, these environments are just downright drab and ugly to look at. I understand they are going to dark fantasy setting, but the majority of the wings are just desolate, muddy-brown, vistas. They serve merely as a means to present the combat encounters and NPCs to the player. The monster and character design is well done, however, with some particularly unsettling looking creatures whose design often encapsulates their unique abilities well.Music is also fantastic and fits the atmosphere perfectly. There was one particular boss theme, Reida, with Nordic chanting and a throbbing bass line that gave me goosebumps. It was the kind of track that sticks with me long after I've played the game which is the highest praise I can give to a song in a game.I'd recommend TG:A if you are looking for a great deck-builder roguelike. The RPG mechanics the game advertises aren't anything special enough to write home about and story elements become gradually fewer and farther between leaving you with just the core gameplay loop. While the "exploration" itself is not good, the combat is addictive, varied, and fun enough to give you a large amount of replayability, which should be the ultimate goal of any game of this genre.

But I love the deck building, exploring, RPG parts of the game. I found that the Wyrdhunter was so difficult that after 4 or 5 runs I just got frustrated with it and gave up. By then I'd unlocked some other classes though. I got 3/4 through the game with the summoner, which felt balanced. Then completed my first run with the sentinel, which was OP but my favourite. Then completed 1st try with Necromancer too which was fun later in the run once I got the hang of it. Then I went back to Wyrdhunter with all my extra knowledge and skills and got flattened before the second boss. 🤷‍♂️I think what I liked most though is that I couldn't find any guides or info online, so I had to actually play the game and figure it all out for myself, make all my own choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So let me begin this with a disclaimer.I break every game I touch. Eventually.This one broke super fast. My runs end because I let them.So.. the game is beautifully made, in the sense that the ambient horror and gore of the blastest environment conveys a real sense of "well this places is ****ed." from the very begining.The music that accompanies it could only be described as a deep and primal mix of chants and percussives of both metalic and organic nature.Choices have consequences, as they should, and those may or may not be to your detriment.Healing is.. something you have to aquire and regulate carefully until you are able to aquire a modicum of minor healing through passives or actives.Several of the mechanics given to you can absolutely turn the tide of a battle, one way or the other. I accidentally saved the first boss from me and was murdered as punishment.The voice acting is entertaining in it's own regard and the lore, along with it, together create a superb compliment to the visual panorama of gore and despair.Defer back to my disclaimer.This game is, in my experience, one that is punishing only if you fail to turn yourself into a raid boss through deck building, passive selection, and intelligent slotting of runes.10/10 - would recommend. sterling example of the deck-building rogue-lite genre.
