_childDocuments_.review: Do you not have this yet? That is a mistake, quick, fix it, add to basket and check out.Why? Okay, I will attempt . . . Do you enjoy deck-building card battling roguelikes? If so, this is a standout top tier example in many respects. Variety, theme, haunting thematic visuals and audio (terrific audio!) and longevity. It can be compared to Slay the Spire, Roguebook, Griftlands and other similar games. It has some absolutely stand-out features that make it special though. These being . . . *Role Play & Village Building*A huge hook of this game is that the meta-progression from run to run is first establishing your own village and then satisfying the unique desires of the people that settle in your village. The people that settle all become vendors of some special range of bonuses and items, requiring their own special currency earned in-game in various ways. In a fantastic twist that I have not seen in any other similar game, the quest-lines for your villagers, and other non-village NPCs, carry over between runs. Some quest lines have six or more stages, and you may advance them from run to run. This does not take up any 'busy work' as  you do not need to track, and the journal provides a very effective recap.*Darkly thematic visuals and audio*I was initially irritated by the need to walk around a 3D world. It felt unnecessary and I preferred simple node-to-node movement seen in similar games. However . . . the visuals are just gosh dang gorgeous and especially when you operate *without* a Wrydcandle, meaning everything is being distorted by the in-game effect of "wyrdness". It really does upgrade the immersion factor, and the audio is a beautiful match. You absolutely have to listen to the cultist chanting and tell me it is not spooky creepy awesome!*Enormous variety and replay value*There are about a dozen character types to play and these each have a huge range of cards, and a huge range of passive abilities, and huge range of runestones that can add extra effects, and a huge number of consumables . . . .and this adds up to provide amazing variety, with lots of very viable and different styles. There is a flipside, which is that moving from one character  type to another presents an initially steep learning curve. How the heck does this one work? This really adds to the interest over time though, as it feels like playing a very different game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed I didn't buy the game before it officially split into two products, but it takes two minutes of research to figure out why that was necessary.  Turns out I'm the bozo since I should have owned this long ago on account of it being a really solid roguelite deckbuilder.  I was initially scared away by the early access related lack of polish and problems that I'd seen around the forums, but realize that my lack of faith would eventually be replaced by a lack of getting the second game for free lol.  So it goes.  A grim-as-♥♥♥♥ tale of King Arthur card battler was not something I knew I needed in my life but this game seems to be fully my speed.  The VA work is top shelf so far and the goofy 3rd person controls will hopefully be sorted out a bit before release.  Not a dealbreaker, just not very effortless in current form.  Lots of comments about how this is a good game for people that like Slay the Spire but that's just a bit broad.  If those comparisons are invoked because both games have...ya know cards in them, then sure that's accurate.  But Slay is a bit more symbiotic with its approach to the cards and at no point is STS trying to be an RPG which allows itself such freedoms.  But 'being an RPG' is what Tainted Grail is actually nailing pretty well.  So it really is like comparing two very different things.  I'd say this is a better fit for people who are into Bard's Tale 4 or Operencia: The Stolen Sun, more than a card game only like Slay (or any of those).  But it would make perfect sense if someone that liked STS liked this too, though.  Can't wait to see the finished product here soon.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best rougelites I have played. There are number of neat permanent upgrades you can get that transfer over runs giving you satisfactory feeling of progression without overdoing it. Everything in this game is voice acted which helps to build atmosphere and immerse you more into the game. You will encounter number of unique and interesting characters many with their own questlines to pursue. Visually the game is very pleasing.The combat is similar to Slay the Spire - you have a recycling deck of cards and you encounter manifold different enemies each with their intents. The game offers you lots of varied factors to keep you entertained for a long time. To start off you have 3 main schools. Different schools have their own deck of cards, abilities and each school has 3 classes - each with their own unique passives, ultimate abilities and even some cards. Depending on what class you are playing with you get very different playstyle and fresh game experience. On top of that you get many random upgrades to diversify your runs such as combinable runestones, consumerables, neutral/quest cards, passive abilites etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Three of my top fave genre's are: Grim dark, Rogue-like, and Deck-building. Tainted Grail Digital combines all three of these with wonderful twist of their own. Not only is this a re-imagination of the lore that came with the board game of it. The developers added their own unique vision to it.For any fan of at least two of those genres this game offers something fun. The Conquest (Roguelike) is the one most developed for now and has already given me many hours of fun game time. The Campaign has been completely remade from scratch compared to the alpha demo and you can see major improvement in development in less than 6 months. In those 6 months they not only remade the Campaign, they also added Conquest.While this game is currently in Early Access, as a backer of the board game (which I enjoyed massively) I personally see a good and unique game coming out of this in the long term.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I came to this expecting another Slay the Spire clone. While it certainly has its roots there, this is a solid evolution of the emerging genre. You have the roguelite elements, the card selection, the character powers... but you also have deep (and difficult to obtain) permanent progression elements. If I had a con, it would be that they're too expensive for what you get... but at the same time, it's also a pro, because it's definitely not handed to you. Those progression elements (passives, especially) really make me feel like I'm developing something unique every run, rather than just putting together the optimal card set and hoping for the best.However, there are two elements of Tainted Grail that truly stand out as being all it's own:Music. Wowza. The music is dark, grim, a bit futuristic, and really meet the theme of the chaotic elements of the Wyrd so well. It's not like anything else I can think of, and it's perfect here.Top billing goes to story, though. As an older guy, I'm a little fatigued of story after a lifetime of playing RPGs. Somehow, the story here though is just brief enough in chunks, and... weird enough... to keep my full attention. All the NPCs have their stories and quests, and there's an interweaving that I'm still catching on to ~30 hours in. And I'm captivated. Every time I run into an NPC in the game area or the town when they have something new to say, I'm hungry for it. I still have quite a ways to go there, but I'm truly enjoying the story in a way I haven't in a video game in a very long time. It's brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It's a really fun spin on the roguelite deckbuilder genre, the playable classes and enemy types are really interesting, writing and voiceacting is good and the gameplay is engaging.It's also a very easy game compared to mainstream successes like Slay the Spire, which combined with the story elements and progression system can be good for easing in players who are newer to the genre.However, I can't recommend the game in its current state. It is absolutely RIDDLED with bugs that make the core gameplay unsatisfying and confusing. Several cards don't actually have the effects described, cards and ability effects simply stop working in particular encounters.I really hope the developers fix these problems soon. This could be a really fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've read a few long form reviews to see if I'm missing some late game weaknesses, but they all seem to confirm what I've thought since the first few rounds I played:This game is fantastic.I would go into so much detail why, but I'd rather just give the short version - the developers hit all of the right notes with this one.  I've seen some say that some classes aren't balanced, but of the ones I've played, understanding the mechanics, making sure there's synergy with your passives and deck, and finding the strategy that fits your play style is key to successful runs.  And if you're not successful on a run, go through another time, unlock some more stuff, meet more NPCs, and keep refining your approach.It may not be the game for everyone, but if you watch the trailers and think, "This looks pretty good. I wonder if it's actually good and worth buying..." The answer is an emphatic "Yes" from me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very close one for me, I think if I had played this before games like Spire I would have given it a much kinder look. It runs kind clunky with animations, and there isn't much to look at, everything is sort of grey and brown. Some of the character feel much too similar, and you unlock cards so slowly. The same is true of Spire, but a run of Spire takes 40-60 minutes if you're just moving along normally.Runs in this game take forever, and there are, in my opinion, too many options for upgrading that just don't do much interesting. You run around these areas, you clear all the monsters, then you fight the boss. There really isn't much reason it had to be structured the way it is, the same thing could have been achieved with different sets of branching paths with choices and rewards and it would have trimmed down a ton of the meandering. You only get cards on level ups, not after every encounter (barring certain rewards that give them after fights) so your deck doesn't really feel like it's progressing very fast, and that means you don't really get excited for the next fight, because your deck isn't that much better than the last one. All in all, I would recommend this game when it goes on sale, try a few characters, and then see if you want to keep it. The devs have obviously put in a lot of work, I just found playing it a chore more than a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game. It's NOT Dark Souls. That being said, do not expect some mass open world. There are 9 play able toons. But really there are like 3, the other six are just re-skined and a lil tweek here and there. I tend to think it mostly done for the player and their likes. I prefer the Neco over the summoner. I just like messing around with the undead. Either way they really are one in the same. It can be challenging but still fun. I like the npc's and the side quest. The voice acting is great! Sounds to me like the actors really tried to play the part. The music is on point to me and the graphics are not to shady at all! Again, this is not some huge dungeon crawler. It's a deck builder card game with some RPG spice. I Like to play this when I am on the road or staying in a hotel for a night or too. (I'm a truck driver). I recommend this game to people that like card deck types of games. I was not a fan of them until I played this. As well, for $20 bucks, not a bad deal. I have 7 hours into it now, so for me, it has half paid for it's self with the entertainment it has provided me!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Tainted Grail doesn't bring much new to the table that other games have brought before it. What it does, however, is blend turn based RPG elements and Rogue Lite gameplay quite well. If you enjoy a challenge and repeating yourself until you get it right, you'll love conquest. Your decisions have consequences as you build up your personal village. While it's difficult, the game feels rewarding and does in fact reward good decision making. If you rob a shrine, yeah, you're gonna get cursed. I haven't played much for the normal campaign so I have no insight on that, but I would recommend this game if you're looking for a dark, difficult Rogue lite RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having "cards" in it, game definitely have it nicely balanced. If you expect huge amount of RNG because of cards, I must disappoint you in here. Gameplay requires player to think about his next moves and to use his cards wisely. Gameplay may be harsh to new players, but its fair to very high degree. Encounters at first seems overwhelming, but later on they became easy (but not too easy). Expect high standards in terms of graphics. Performance-wise game works constantly at 60 fps for medium-end specs. So far, only one class is available at the moment, which isn't great (hope it will change in the future). Since it's still EA, expect some bugs, even those game-breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the best deckbuilder roguelike I've played. The game is very generous with its learning and difficulty curve, I feel, compared to other games in the genre. A common practice with these games is when you beat a run, the *prestige* run afterwards is usually very difficult to the point where it doesn't feel rewarding to challenge yourself. But this game introduces that in a gradual manner that made each finished run that much more exciting to play just to see how much I've improved with my tactics. The classes that you can play are all so functionally different from one another that it feels fresh no matter who you go with. Personal favorites would be Apostate, Necromancer, and Pathfinder. I liked the story a-lot; the character art and voice acting used was phenomenal and everyone did an amazing job. The setting and atmosphere presented are unique and the environments are downright gorgeous. The music, while something I'm not used to listening to, was different at first but it fits the moody atmosphere and grew on me the more I played. I would 100% recommend this to anyone who is a fan of the genre or looking to get into it.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me say this game is fun and I am looking forward to a full release of this game, but it still needs a lot of balance work.  I like the idea of an adventure card game like this in the vein of a Slay the Spire meets Diablo type game.  This is a really fun and unique concept.  After playing all the available classes, I feel all of them need some work.  I have some general suggestions about the game, and some specific ones that I really think will improve this game.GENERAL SUGGESTIONS:(1) In battle, the camera angle starts at a weird position.  It should be rotated more to the back of the player about 20 degrees for the following reasons:     - When more than 4 enemies are present the fifth enemy on the right can't be seen, and causes surprise attacks     - When using the Druid and you have multiple summon creatures, the info for your creatures will overlap each other and makes it hard to read.(2) When encountering enemies on the map, there should be a confirmation screen that pops up to accept or decline the battle.  Several times I accidentally go too close to a creature that I wasn't ready to fight when I was just moving around the map.  Some type of ambush type of mechanic is okay, but no one likes to accidentally start a fight from a missclick.(3) The fast travel system is kind of hard to use.  When using the portals, clicking an arrow to go from portal to portal is kind of annoying.  It should bring up a map of the entire area and you can click on the portal you want to go to.WARRIOR SUGGESTIONSWarrior classes are all underpowered.  The following should help a bit.(1) The energy charging for the Ultimate ability charges waaaay too slow.  With the Guardian and the Berserker, the battle was usually over by the time I got 3 energy to use it at the lowest level.  Energy should be retained at the end of every combat so it can build up.  I had a run with that ability, and it made the run much much much more fun.  This should be a default characteristic of the warrior.  Kind of like he always stays mad like The Hulk.(2) Attack cards are too weak and don't scale very well into the 2nd and 3rd Tier battles even with stronger weapons.(3) Warrior has a severe problem with multiple enemies because its attacks are too weak and they can't absorb a whole lot of damage.  Their attacks should do more damage and/or hit more enemies(4) Their cards cost too much for what they do.  I think maybe increasing the warrior's base energy to 4 would really help these classes in general.(5) Warrior should have more 0 cost cards (particularly with attack damage) and maybe a 0 cost attack that is always in-hand every turn like the Druid's 0 cost card that activates a summoned creature.  that would go a long way to helping the warrior seem more fierce.(6) The Berserker's Ultimate should charge when blocking attacks.  Since it doesn't, the fight is usually over by you being dead and charge is maxed out or being at 3 and the battle is overDRUID SUGGESTIONS:(1) The Druid, particularly the summoner is too strong.  It's fun to dominate the game, but it is currently too powerful.   This class is kind of a glass cannon, so toning down the damage output may make the class too weak.  I think toning down the damage of the Abomination's attacks might be good.  That thing just facerolls most battles with multiple enemies.  (2) With the Golem summoned creature, I found it to be underwhelming.  It doesn't 0 damage and is exclusively a damage sponge. it should have a little bit of offence capability.  With it only being a damage sponge, it kind of makes it somewhat useless because it is more beneficial to take down the enemies quickly instead of chipping away at their health while the golem takes the hits.  In fact, I kind of skip over any Golem related upgrades because damage output is more effective than damage absorption.(3) If the Golem is going to be 100% defensive, maybe give it some damage return or poison or something like that so it outputs some damage when it is attacked.

_childDocuments_.review: Changed to recommend, although in its current state I'd still wait for a sale. It very EA, with a lot of work that still needs to be done. I'm getting 50FPS on a 3060ti, which is constantly running at 98%. -Gameplay is very luck dependent. -Very unbalanced. Some playstyles are overpowered. _childDocuments_.review: There's no need for it to be free roam in the "dungeons", it just feels janky. Card games are usually laid back, where you only use your computer mouse. Why the hell do i have to use my damn keyboard as well? The characters are just copies of what you've already seen in other games but worse. The story & world feels forced in a weird way, like a story that has been done hundreds of times before. Is the setting supposed to be taken seriously or as a joke? Is the world real or not? The decks go from feeling under powered to over powered, it's rarely in-between. The torch system they've implemented (kind of like Darkest Dungeon but worse) is just straight up annoying. I played through multiple bosses but whenever i won (which was every time, strangely enough) I didn't feel like as if it was due to my own efforts. It just felt like straight up luck. It feels like it's their first published game. It's unpolished, they don't expand on parts they could to make the game better & other parts of the game just feels unfinished. I was really excited for this game so it's sad that i disliked it this much.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope that more content continues to be added to this game, DLCs, other game, or something. This game is amazing! I think if I had one "issue" it's that while there are 9 classes, it's really 3 base classes with 2 other subclasses. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of bang for the buck.  Great looking game with cool music.  The game does get repetitive and grindy pretty quickly. _childDocuments_.review:
Avalon is dying. King Arthur is long gone, and Knights of the Round Table are in disarray. Guardian Menhirs, the only thing that makes it possible for humans to survive in this remote land, are going dark. Your village chose its best and brightest and sent them on an epic quest to reach Kamelot, find the Grail, and save the land.

You were not among them.

They've never returned, and now it's your turn to lead a band of unlikely heroes, the only ones this land can still provide. These ordinary people set off far too late, under-equipped for the task ahead, and with little hope of success.

Tainted Grail is a dark fantasy open-world RPG with fresh turn-based exploration and combat. It is based around deep, immersive story from one of the best and most innovative board games (biggest Kickstarter project of 2018!), but introduces a whole new experience crafted directly for PC.

name: Gleamlight
detailed_description: Welcome to Gleamlight – a 2D action game that will take you through an adventure traversing a beautiful, transient world. Immerse yourself amid the beautiful stained glass artistry as you navigate without the reliance of any standard game UI, while tracing the world’s mysterious unspoken story. What will you, as Gleam, sense and feel through your travels across this beautiful, yet fearsome world of glass? ◆A World Made of Glass The world beautifully unfurls before you with lush trees, boulders of all sizes, and various paraphernalia, all in the form and shape of glass. Prepare to explore this fantastical world where light warms the glass and darkness stains it with bitter cold. ◆A Game Without UI The game has been designed to immerse players into the world and story without being obstructed by any standard game UI, allowing players to organically enjoy the action and tension of defeating enemies and traversing the world. ◆An Unspoken Story The story behind what happened in this world, and what is to come is up to you as the player. Discover and piece together the story through your adventure, and save this beautiful, transient world of glass.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no real reason to spend money on Gleamlight when even the most mediocre platformers on steam offer better content for a fraction of the price. It's clunky, poorly designed and generally a slog to play through.It's Very sad to see a game i was looking forward to fall flat on its face like this.There's not much to like and much to complain about, so i'll separate this into categories.The game looks fine in screenshots, but in motion you realize the animations are very rough.The environments look pretty good, but they tend to hide stuff they really shouldn't (enemies, switches, spikes...).Unresponsive and clunky. Inputs will sometimes not register and some things are completely unintuitive (you can't drop through a platform unless you stand completely still). Your attacks are frustratingly slow as well.The game overall is easy, since every attack you land regenerates some of your health instantly. It's hard to die unless you get combo'd by a bunch of enemies, which will happen in some areas.The music is forgettable and somewhat repetitive but it fits the game's atmosphere well enough.The sound effects, however, are weak. Enemies make little to no sound, despite being bulky machines.You can get your first ending withing the first hour of playing. You can then replay the game in the opposite order (going from the end to the beginning) to get a second ending. Once that's over, you can .It feels kind of insulting for a nearly 20$ game to recycle its entire world  and make you go through it in reverse only one hour in. That's something NES games would do, and that trend died with good reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly lackluster. 6/10.It's impossible to not compare this to Hollow Knight as it's obvious where this game's inspiration came from. My major gripe with the game is the combat. As it is, you leech HP from enemies with every attack. This was an incredibly bad move by the developers. It is quite literally impossible to die as long as you spam your attack. I cheesed through the first boss without moving at all and the 2nd was more of a goose chase than a challenge. Gleamlight also lacks any sense of purpose for the player. You start in a cave and move left to right, killing enemies and jumping around along the way. There's no explanation about the lore through either notes or NPCs. The premise for the story is that you get punched/mugged by a crystal guy and you now have to chase them. No context at all. Even after killing the first two bosses I found myself asking who are these people and why am I killing them? Graphics and soundtrack are fine on their own. Enemy appearances quickly get repetitive but the backgrounds still look nice, and while you'd never intentionally listen to the OST, it fills the game with white noise well enough.Overall, Gleamlight just feels uninspired. Despite the initial criticism of it being a Hollow Knight clone I wanted to give it a chance and now I've ended up thoroughly disappointed. If you just want something to tie you over until Silksong releases, I still wouldn't recommend playing this even if you plan on refunding it.

_childDocuments_.review: So.  "Gleamlight."  A wildly misunderstood game.  If you want a TL;DR review, this game is too expensive, but the game itself is a perfectly good little linear action platformer with a subtly dark plot (for lack of a better term), some fun story twists, decent bosses, and a short but satisfying run time.  It's worth a play . . . if you can get it on sale.Now, if you want a little more depth, please continue on.So, there appears to be a lot of negativity born of misinformation about this game, so let's clear a few things up right off the bat:1) This game is NOT "Hollow Knight," nor is it ATTEMPTING TO BE, no matter what a vast majority of so-called "games journalists" (or enraged fanboys who didn't play it) claim.  Anyone who thinks that either didn't actually play this, or didn't actually play HK.2) This game DOES certainly share some of HK's artistic style (simplistic character designs, black outlines, fast arcing sword slashes, caves with crystals and spikes and shadows, etc.), but these visual elements were not created by that game, they predate both games by DECADES.  And especially with the outlines, those are inherent to the stained glass aesthetic of "Gleamlight," which honestly gives the game a more unique flavor than most detractors are willing to give it credit for.3) This game is NOT a "metroidvania" (and seriously, that word is atrocious and always has been, can we, as a gamer community, PLEASE finally come up with something less stupid??), and again, it is not attempting to be one.  It's a straight action platformer with minimal power-ups, no power-locked gateways, no branching exploration, and no map, a straight linear path that (mild spoiler) you have to repeat three times to truly finish the game.  Yes, there is "backtracking" as a result, but only because you're repeating that linear path more than once.4) This game is short.  INTENTIONALLY SO, I firmly believe.  Because it is a linear path spanning only four "levels," and the game requires you to repeat them to finish the story, and there is limited environmental differentiation or enemy variety, the designers clearly set out to make a game that didn't overstay its welcome.  It is not overly difficult, attacking enemies heals you, it is not easy to get lost, dying spawns a checkpoint IN THE SAME ROOM, it is not particularly deep as far as story is concerned, and thus it is very brief (I finished it and got the true ending in about 3.5 hours).  This is a GOOD THING, mind you.  If it had been long, it would have been a SLOG.  Keeping it short kept is mostly enjoyable the whole way through.5) This game is a year old.  That is to say, it has received multiple bug fixes and minor QOL improvements since its release.  Yeah, a lot of the negativity is from people going in expecting something this game wasn't ever supposed to be, and that's on them.  However, I've noted that a couple reviews have noted bugs and mistakes when the game first released, and to that, all I can say is "well, it plays completely solid now, I had no problems!"  I figure people should know this by now, given that it's a standard videogame industry practice nowadays, but *shrug*.  I found no technical issues.6) This game . . . is DEFINITELY overpriced.  $20 for a less-than-4-hour game is kinda ridiculous, not gonna lie.  Me, I got a Steam Key from an independent online retailer for only $5, and THAT was TOTALLY worth it.  So . . . your mileage may vary, in terms of cost/return analysis.IF you go into this game WITHOUT the silly preconceived notion that it's a "Hollow Knight" clone (which I will stress, IT IS IN NO WAY TRYING TO BE), what you will get is a tight, short, fun little platform hack-and-slash with powerups that make combat progressively easier and faster, some fun (if not super complex) bosses, a few interesting "twists" (the game fakes you out with a "game over" credits sequence . . . TWICE.  Make sure you look up how to get to the REAL final boss) along the way,  It's got a dark, foreboding atmosphere and environments that help to subtly tell the minimal story, and the whole thing just works.  Not a major time investment, not a lot of replay value, but if you stop treating it like something it's NOT, you will find that it's actually really good at being what it's SUPPOSED to be.You want Nintendo hard?  Get "Dark Souls."  You want metroidvania?  Play "Bloodstained."  You want dozens of hours of gameplay?  Join an MMO.  You want a cheaper game? . . . Find a coupon. *LOL*  But if you want a fun, low-stakes, semi-gothic fantasy dungeon crawl with a pretty art style, solid controls, and plenty of action? "Gleamlight" is by no means a bad game, and I enjoyed my afternoon with it!- J

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be the outlier on this review page. I do recommend this game HOWEVER, I recommend it if you go into it without expecting HK 2.0 or a sequel or anything at the same level and polish as it. So far I played roughly 2 hours and got to the end of the first major boss. I will highlight my thoughts.It has a beautiful soundtrack and art style. The setting is nice and feels dark and mysterious. However its UI and menu is clunky as hell. It tells you and explains NOTHING. Which is both a pro and con. Some mystery is fine, but not knowing what the new attack you learned is can get annoying. The aiming of swings is off and you don't hit at angles you'd expect to. and be prepared to die a lot, but there is no penalty. Every floor has an entrance and exit, it has spots you respawn at if you die. you will die because you cant see your health. Some things will kill you by touching you and the next time will hit you 100 times and you wont die. Each floor is the puzzle, you find a button to hit or thing to kill to move on and open the end door. It is fun, however you have to treat it like its a puzzle/platform with some "I want to be the guy" challenges (aka that floor will fall and crush you, but you don't know it until it does). I do find it fun in its own way and I hope it gets some love and polish because I see the potential in it to be good with some tweaks and updates. Its like Dr Thunder to Hollow Knights Dr Pepper; its not as good side by side, but if you are thirsty it still is nice to quench your thirst and doesn't have any less merit as a drink because it took some inspiration from another. So in conclusion, if you go in with a certain mindset its fun but just janky at times. Hopefully the Devs will fix some of that and make it hit the potential I am sure it can hit with the right love and careUPDATE 8-22-20: Today I went to play after not for a few days and my save file was gone as well as my in game achievements. :/

_childDocuments_.review: Had this game on my wishlist, appeared to be a cool 'Hollow Knight-like' platformer so I was looking forward to it.Played through the game, but the credits rolled after the 3rd boss, I was confused and almost refunded. It's hard to recommend this game for it's story, since it's veryyyy passively told with no dialogue.In my opinion, this will be a good game to speedrun. If you're looking for some boss fights and platforming, this game will do nicely. This game offers a fun experience trying to get all the achievements, but afterward it's even better to speedrun since there's no dialogue to skip through, just platforming, boss fights, and multiple endings to run for.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not sure why this game is rated so poorly. I will agree that it is not a metroidvania and should have that tag removed. But for an action platformer, it's quite enjoyable. The game itself is pretty short even for going for both endings. The art is absolutely a dream to look at. Music is pretty good as well. The game does make the assumption that you'll play it a second time and maybe that's off putting for some. But I could tell at the end of my first full playthrough, I'd be playing again to unlock the rest of the game. I've played other games like this, so it's something I'm familiar with.The downsides for me are the following:- Dreadful controls at times- 0 recovery window after getting attacked- The price for such a short game- The world and its lore could need expanding to make the story actually a storyDespite these downsides, it's still an enjoyable game if you get it on sale like I did. It's not like HK and it's not worth 20$ for it's length. But the game does offer an experience that is worth putting a few hours in if you need something to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I had heard of it through Hollow Knight. I made the mistake of not reading reviews before purchasing and spent my $20 on it. At first, it seemed like a cute little magical game. The controls were my first complaint. I'm a PC user and it was weird figuring out how to move let alone attack. I had to change all of my controls to be able to do anything. When I left the first area and encountered my first enemy, It seemed to be decent enough. The enemies are unique at first but that leads me into my second complaint, none of the enemies are very engaging or different from each other and don't really tell much about the area or the story. They are all dark, red, disformed crystal creatures. Next, the fights. One thing I have to give the game is that the health system is very unique and interesting, with quite literally TAKING health from your enemies, and it being transferred to them when you get hit. However, this doesn't save the fights as they are slow and not very engaging, they're all around boring. I also noticed that the game isn't very good at telling you what to do, as I got stuck in an area for a bit because I couldn't figure out how to get out of it. This is my first review on a game on this account, at least for a long time from my knowledge. So I will close with saying that this game seems like it has potential, but all around it isn't good right now. If you want a better game, I suggest Hollow Knight of course since it is $5 less and has HOURS worth of game play while from what I've heard from others, this game has a couple hours worth of game play at best.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10This is arguably great ideas executed poorly. The art is beautiful. The main character is charming enough. _childDocuments_.review: Hollow Knight might be Gleamlight's greatest curse. Developer DICO created a beautiful stained-glass graphic style for their platformer. Only that, on the very first look it's reminiscent of Hollow Knight, which can create specific expectations.		The truth is that Gleamlight plays nothing like Hollow Knight. It's much more simplified, shorter, without any metroidvania elements. It's an action platformer with a very basic gameplay formula.	The problems arise with various in-game mechanics being directly at-odds with eachother. The so called „unspoken story” might feel like narrative is non-existent. Gleamlight tries to convey it's plot through presentation. Unfortunately the inconsistent gameplay focusing on backtracking and re-runs of the game makes it really hard to get engaged. The poorly designed combat system is the final nail in the coffin. It devoids Gleamlight of any challenge and depth.	I see glimpses of passion and artistry within DICO's team of developers. I'm going to pay attention to their future projects. Regrettably, as for Gleamlight...   	I do not recommend this game.If you are interested in a really thorough review then check out my video about Gleamlight:

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought the game to have my own opinion about it. It costs about 17€ but I've spent 3,30€ on discount and I somehow still feel robbed. I'm not gonna make comparisons with Hollow Knight since it wouldn't be fair, but I have to say this title is as hollow as fried air. From the top of my head (gonna edit with other points while going for the other ending):Avoiding focusing on the plain issues with the main menu (new commands that get overwritten by the default ones as one replays the game; some options that lack sfx; simply uncomfy to navigate in; video settings that just sets the window size), there is no content whatsoever: uninteresting rooms (you cannot be serious to goodness to make the player walk a linear map TO MAKE THEM GO BACK JUST TO HAVE A BUNCH OF MORE ENEMIES THERE. This is NOT level design, let alone a metroidvania!), broken enemies, no story (let's be real: nothing transpires in the playthrough: there is no pathos in the bosses you defeat, they have no personality, many just have the same sprite), unclear and broken mechanics (istg it just praises tanking, it asks no wits from the players. also, losing life for just moving and double jumping is such a bs when you're just going for the other room, im serious), no replayability, ... there is nothing one would enjoy playing it, let alone to justify the prize (the first playthrough can take at most 2 hours. AT MOST, for 17€).Forgot to say it but: another thing, however minor, is how, for instance, when one defeats a boss, you are stuck in place for up to 3/4 seconds with no animation that hints you're stuck (so ig that's a bug).There are other things that, however minor, show the game was not tested and, hence, nobody cared to get the best game for a better experience like:1. how tf can room transitions last so little? And the up-down transitions are so short one can just go back to the previous room because the player has to move to the ledge.2. Also, when the game is in background, somehow it still registers the inputs (I play with the keyboard and even when editing this review I hear the game sfx doing things while I'm just tiping here).3. Also there are no i-frames after getting hit.4. The dark swords' attack (basically hk's greatslash) lags the game so much when hitting an enemy.5. When falling down, the camera cannot keep up with the player's fall acceleration. This means that the majority of times a player can fall onto an enemy or an environmental hazard and keep going down and down, getting more and more damage.6. enemies can clip in the environmental walls and floors. it's especially frequent in the last bossfight (bad ending) and some enemies such as "the airplane" ones and the "jump to pierce" ones (who played the game knows which i mean)7. very very minor but: the enemies that crawl around the platforms just straightly shift when they get to a surface of a different angle. there is no smooth animation for it. while its very very minor, its still an eyesore8. the "melt n spikes" enemies can melt and slide in midair9. checkpoints literally in screen trasitions? like, come on!10. about transitions: some, everytime single time, they play a noise, like a "locking/closing door" sfx11. ambience music changes between area transition very  clearly12. the credit music doesnt even last for the whole credit scene, The only ups may be the artstyle (that is still not justified lore-wise, has nothing interesting gameplay-wise and at times makes the navigation really confusing, since one can't tell what's in background and in foreground and what can be broken due to no consistency in the room level design) and the bossfight song (which is seriously the only think I enjoyed, even if it doesn't fit with action scenes at all).I've yet to do the good ending but I did the bad ending and  This just tells me that Gleamlight tries to be alternative for the sake of being alternative, without the effort of being it.When I have the will to check the true ending, I'm gonna update the review.But one thing I have to say regardless is: developers please, , get your game tested before release and after major and even minor changes, please please please.P.S.: ah yea and credits are unskippable, why? also i cannot believe so many people were involved in the localization like dude, what was there to localize? the achievements and the main menu? so much written content /s

_childDocuments_.review: It looks like a metroidvania, it plays like a metroidvania, it WANTS to be a metroidvania… but it is not a metroidvania.It is a strange game. From the fact that you gain new abilities from defeating bosses to the dungeon-style levels where you have to find the glorified red button (over and over again) to open doors, it seems to me that the devs had a metroidvania in mind but didn’t understand the key elements that make these games fun; exploration, progression and new abilities. The combat is the cardinal sin; surely one of the blandest, most boring button-smashing games you can find, your character doesn’t do anything but monotonously swing his sword; there’s no combos, no jump and smash attack, no shield to defend yourself, no ranged attack and not even a health bar!Truly, it feels unfinished. The art is good, the name is catchy and some of the movement abilities you gain later on (by the point everyone NOT achievement-hunting has already stopped playing the damn game) are kind of fun, but its repetitive nature and uninspired combat don’t do it justice.I guess I’ll go for the achievements and forget about ever playing the game. Too bad.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I recommend this gameI'm not sure why this game has mostly negative reviews. I think it's a pretty good game, and I would definitely recommend it to other players.I found Gleamlight because of a YouTube video that was saying NOT to call many games (Gleamlight included) Hollow Knight ripoffs, and I decided to take a look at Gleamlight because the art style caught my eye.The art style is beautiful, and I love the stained glass theme that the developers used. I like when the enemies die, they shatter into pieces.Also the use of color to indicate health is a great touch, and I love the fact that it was added so a UI wouldn't be needed. Without a UI in the way, you as the player are able to better immerse yourself into the story and the combatThe combat is great most of the time. The life steal mechanic makes bosses a nice challenge, and adds a nice way to remove item drops. I do find some enemies particularly annoying to fight, but that is most likely just a lack of skill on my part.Also, I can tell this game is meant to be played through more than once. If you play through the game one and only one time, you will miss out on a fair amount of what Gleamlight has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Sad to add to the not recommending list, but it really isn't fun to play. It's beautiful, albeit lacking in variety in both enemy and area design. It's not even a Metroidvania as you'd anticipate seeing it, it's very linear and they reuse the majority of it for the various endings. There's only a few areas added to these subsequent playthroughs and sometimes that's nothing, one of the required things to do is run through the game backwards for another ending/boss. It had some neat ideas to deliver the endings, but it just needed more effort. You even unlock a gravity power that shifts the gravity for you but it breaks if you get hit. Instead of that they should've designed it like Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. That level design was stellar when you get to the inverted castle. Nothing in this game requires any effort. Even the jumping is mostly bog standard fluff. There are maybe 2-3 jumps that require any level of "skill" (thought). And that amounts to dropping off a platform, falling below a wall, dashing and then double jumping for required progression. That's the most complex section of platforming in the *entire* game. And on subsequent playthroughs you don't need to do it lol.The subsequent playthroughs also involve reused bosses which are tedious (mostly the flying one). As well as adding really beefy crystals that you have to break to progress each room on the first playthrough they break in 1 hit and it's simple. In the last playthrough (two save deletes later) it takes 3 or 4 hits and it's incredibly annoying. You can use the charged attack as well but it's annoying since it can't be stored properly and loses the charge if you don't use it right away which makes timing so annoying that I barely wanted to use it other than on bosses. You regain HP as you attack and so do enemies so the flying boss is a big tedious battle most of the time as you both chip away at each other while recovering. Just back and forth constantly. Annoying boss. The main questline bosses are all kind of lame tbh.It's very disappointing how shallow of an experience this really is because it could have been a gem. It's just not worth the time and I played through twice on PS4 and PC now. (I bought it on PS thinking it was Unbound for some reason) The time playing after this review will be for the remaining two trading cards and I can't wait to delete this and hopefully forget it.

_childDocuments_.review:
This is a story of light - of Gleam, in a world of glass stained in darkness.

Welcome to Gleamlight – a 2D action game that will take you through an adventure traversing a beautiful, transient world.

Immerse yourself amid the beautiful stained glass artistry as you navigate without the reliance of any standard game UI, while tracing the world’s mysterious unspoken story.
What will you, as Gleam, sense and feel through your travels across this beautiful, yet fearsome world of glass?

◆A World Made of Glass
The world beautifully unfurls before you with lush trees, boulders of all sizes, and various paraphernalia, all in the form and shape of glass. Prepare to explore this fantastical world where light warms the glass and darkness stains it with bitter cold.

◆A Game Without UI
The game has been designed to immerse players into the world and story without being obstructed by any standard game UI, allowing players to organically enjoy the action and tension of defeating enemies and traversing the world.

◆An Unspoken Story
The story behind what happened in this world, and what is to come is up to you as the player. Discover and piece together the story through your adventure, and save this beautiful, transient world of glass.
_childDocuments_.name: Gleamlight

name: A Space for the Unbound
detailed_description: High school is ending and the world is ending with it A Space for the Unbound is a slice-of-life adventure game with beautiful pixel art set in the late 90s rural Indonesia that tells a story about overcoming anxiety, depression, and the relationship between a boy and a girl with supernatural powers. Follow two high school sweethearts, Atma and Raya, on a journey of self-discovery at the end of their high school years. When a mysteriously supernatural power is suddenly unleashed threatening their existence, they must explore and investigate their town to uncover hidden secrets, face the end of the world, and perhaps learn more about each other. Set in a small town inspired by 90s era rural Indonesia, A Space for the Unbound presents an endearing story-driven experience with a vibrant environment waiting to be explored. about_the_game: High school is ending and the world is ending with it A Space for the Unbound is a slice-of-life adventure game with beautiful pixel art set in the late 90s rural Indonesia that tells a story about overcoming anxiety, depression, and the relationship between a boy and a girl with supernatural powers. Follow two high school sweethearts, Atma and Raya, on a journey of self-discovery at the end of their high school years. When a mysteriously supernatural power is suddenly unleashed threatening their existence, they must explore and investigate their town to uncover hidden secrets, face the end of the world, and perhaps learn more about each other. Set in a small town inspired by 90s era rural Indonesia, A Space for the Unbound presents an endearing story-driven experience with a vibrant environment waiting to be explored. Key Features Throwback to the 90s! Let us take you to Indonesia in the late 90s. Explore rural Indonesia and enjoy its relaxing atmosphere with a hint of supernatural events. Chat and interact with other townfolks and listen to their personal stories. Dive into people's minds Inception-style. Listen to beautiful music composed by Masdito 'Ittou' Bachtiar
short_description: A magical adventure about two high school sweethearts set at the end of their school days - and the end of the world. Explore a crumbling town and help friends face their inner demons, which could be the key to stopping reality itself disintegrating. And don’t forget to pet the cats.

_childDocuments_.review: Toge Productions and Mojiken are shaping up to be two of my favourite development teams. Their games seem to always present the most delightful and pretty visuals paired with a fantastic ost and writing that keeps you interested and dying to know what happens next, while delivering a satisfying and emotional ending.The characters that you meet in A Space for the Unbound are written so well and while playing I felt a real connection to them and their stories, which made the emotional impact of all, but especially the later, chapters so much more powerful.The gameplay itself isn't particularly difficult, but I don't think it needs to be as the story, visuals and music are the main driving force of this game in my opinion; that is not to say, at all, that the gameplay is bad or not enjoyable, quite the opposite in fact. I think the simplicity of a lot of the mechanics compliment the heavy and emotional nature of the game well, allowing you to truly think about the story you're being presented with.

Can't comment much without spoiling the story, all I could is that it's about friendship, escapism, depression, growing-up and other things you should experience for yourself.Only downside of the game is the gameplay itself. It's basically  with a few mini games along the way. Could be tiresome so play at a slow pace to enjoy the game, it's a story-driven adventure game after all.You may need to bring a pen and paper while playing this game, some of the puzzles can get a bit involved at times.like math or memorizing a path.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review games often, but I found myself smitten with this game by hour 4.I feel the need to write this now; If you have any interest in mystery slice of life games, play this game. I went into it expecting a fun little experience with charming characters. What I got? A deep dive into the human psyche as Atma's world falls apart around him. A lot of the TWs were things I've dealt with personally, so I was intrigued by how they'd pop up. Every single one hit me hard, and it's a miracle I didn't start crying. I teared up several times near the end, but that's as far as I got.Many of the plot points are very well hinted through out, too a point where I had inklings of what the truth might be the whole way, but the atmosphere and side characters distracted me enough that I was slow to pinpoint every single twist.After both Coffee Talk games and A Space for the Unbound, Toge Productions is quickly becoming a favorite indie developer of mine. Looking forward to whatever comes next from them.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to make things clear from the start, this is a good game but I do not see myself recommending it due to the experience I had with it (and it involves personal tastes).Positive things I can say for sure about the game : - The artstyle is gorgeous : the pixel art is impressive, full of details and very colorful. The game is full of beautiful scenes (cutscenes or in gamepay) - The music is nice : varied and which match with the scenes > even if the ones used at the beginning become a bit repetitive after some time- Some nice game mechanics However, it felt like a pain finishing the game due to its own pace. A Space for the Unbound has the same issue you can find within some narrative games : a lot of fillers.- The story, even if things get cleared up at the end, feels confusing for 3/4 of the game- You have a lot of long dialogues from which you get low to no information from- Some phases feel dragged off with a lot of unnecessary walking / talking / finding things- - Some gameplay phases also feel dragged off due to the repetition of the same thing over and over again - Some cutscenes / sequences are very slow and force you to watch each detail unraveling instead of getting to the conclusion I wanted to finish the game to have a complete view of it since this was very promising. I was a bit disappointed considering the high hopes I had for this game and due to the very nice feedback it had. It still is a good work from the dev team and for sure is a good sign of interesting games to come :)

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Video review: What at first glance starts out as a touching title that smells like the 90’s, evolves into a story with dark contours mixed with supernatural powers, which addresses the lives of two teenagers with a strong connection, in a city located in Indonesia.A Space for the Unbound produced by Mojiken studios, suddenly appeared on my Twitter timeline and I immediately wanted to understand what it was about. Set on a screen full of pixels, surrounded by a touching soundtrack and small notes in cutscene with anime contours, it tells the story of a boy, named Atma, who like most teenagers, although without major concerns about the subject, is trying to figure out what he wants to do with his future after finishing high school. Raya, his girlfriend, on the other hand, is quite methodical and decides to make a bucket list of activities to do with him. On that list are activities like going to the movies, having a party and inviting all of their friends, among others, which serve as a backdrop for the timeline of the denouement full of mishaps of this adventure.Suddenly Atma finds himself wrapped in a mist that mixes dream with reality and discovers that he has a mysterious supernatural power. With the help of a red book he manages to delve into the minds of people disturbed by traumas in order to help them overcome that less positive moment. This “Spacedive” ability will be one of the most defining mechanics throughout this title. Raya also has powers, albeit quite different. Raya can change reality, transport herself to other places or, for example, levitate objects and even people.All of this sounds very interesting, until it gets to the point where the powers used by Raya begin to affect not only her, but the entire city. The inhabitants begin to behave strangely, certain locations seem to have some kind of glitch alternating between parallel realities and even a rift begins to open in the sky of this peculiar location. Is this real life or just a dream? Atma will be the crucial point in answering all these questions, while trying to keep everything around from collapsing.While the story becomes interesting as time goes by, its gameplay begins to gain somewhat repetitive contours between activities. In the end, the gameplay involves a lot of exploration, going through elements of a visual novel and small moments where it is necessary to click on the right keys at the right times. The main “problem” here is the fact that there are quite a few moments of exploration separated between running from one side of the city to the other where the main objective is the search for the necessary elements to overcome the presented problems. While on paper this is an interesting idea, it is rather tedious to go from screen to screen as an errand boy. There are positive moments during this rush, characters to meet, cats to pet and name, bottle caps to collect, among others, but the feeling of boredom is still very present, especially in Chapter 3 which is by far the slowest in its development.It never becomes a difficult game, there is no learning path or anything like that. Except for small sections that can become somewhat frustrating largely because of the collision area that the character presents in moments of finger dexterity, such as when there are objects falling from the sky. The controls are super responsive, even when it takes a double click to get Atma to start its fastest march.Being a linear story, it is unlikely that you will skim this adventure a second time. It is still possible to miss some secondary objectives. As previously mentioned there is a list of activities with some secondary activities. That said, and for hardcore players, there are also secrets and achievements that are harder to unlock.A Space for the Unbound presents a very interesting teen drama story that somehow manages to warm even the coldest of hearts. The attention to detail of Culture Pop, the construction of an interesting city with engaging characters make this title a winning bet for the kick-off in this year’s Indie games calendar.

_childDocuments_.review: **NOTE:** This review was written after I completed the entire game.A very beautiful game. It sounds cliché, but I can't think of another word to describe it.The story in this game is truly touching. The soundtrack used, the illustrated pixel art, the character development, the unpredictable plot, the prologue and epilogue in the story, every aspect of this game is perfect.If there are any flaws in this game, I would say that the side quests are too long and repetitive. They are so lengthy that the main story feels shorter in some chapters. However, these side quests also depict the problems faced by each character, making them not too boring. In fact, some are quite interesting.Last, the message in this game is very relevant to everyday life. This is what made me feel so immersed.And to all the other Raya-s out there, stay strong! You got this! :)10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The good:+ Great story with satisfying finale.+ Endearing main cast/characters.+ Great world building meets with 90s Indonesia culture.+ Pleasant pixel artstyle. The cutscenes visual is amazing, even though i notice few awkward animation.+ Nice soundtrack.+ Puzzle is mostly well balanced. Not too difficult and doesn't make you feel bored/annoyed either.The bad: - The ugly:* Some pacing problem. There are so many sidetrack a.k.a. "To complete sub-task C you also must complete sub-sub-task X, Y and Z" during chapter 2-4.* Sometimes you might have to going around in circles to solve certain task or accidentally skipped something.Despite few flaws, A Space for the Unbound is definitely best game developed by Mojiken Studio and best story-driven/adventure game among all games created by Indonesian developer. If you like side-scrolling/adventure game (such as GRIS, Unreal Life or Oneshot) or game made by Mojiken Studio/Toge production (such as Coffee Talk or When The Past Was Around), you should give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game code given by Toge Productions and as of this review I am 5 hours in the game and reached the start of Chapter 3! I will try to go into as much details as I can about the game overall and being as vague and spoiler free as I can below.Let’s get into details shall we.GAMEPLAY 5/5 :The game goes as a typical Side scroller exploration game, with some minigames and puzzle solving in between. I would say the game is quite accessible for anyone. Also, the game has Controller support and so far it works really fine, and I always play games like this using a controller because it just feels right. STORY AT MY CURRENT PROGRESS 4/5:I think the storytelling in the game starts slightly slow and maybe confusing and even at this point I am still left with much more questions than answers, and at the current point that I am right now the story is getting good and it piques my interest to keep playing I might edit the review once I get to finish the game soon. VISUAL/GRAPHICS 5/5:I would say the visuals is very stunning what you see in the trailer is literally what you are going to get, I’ve always been a fan of retro styled games. What I think is unique they captured the feeling that you are really in a rural Indonesia. Living in Indonesia myself I feel the visual they did is really represented well, and I got quite immersed in a lot of the stuff they are trying to put into the game. As I see it, a lot of love and care was put into the visuals.TRANSLATION 3.5/5:Now you might be wondering why the translation is 3.5 despite giving most of the other category bigger scores before you get your pitchforks here is what I think. Bear in mind I played the game in English, and my gripe is some of the words they are using, and sentences feels weird in a way that it didn’t feel natural to me. Knowing that Mojiken is a studio based in Indonesia maybe the script is in Indonesian and then translated to English and I felt some of the translation feels a bit Raw and can be refined just a little bit to fit the English language better. TBF at least the message they are trying to convey at least get across to me, and it’s still bearable to play but its just that lingering feeling that it might can be refined better to feel a bit natural.WRITING 5/5: I would say the writing is good and despite the translation issue I think they did such an amazing job of the dialogue and got me really immersed in the characters and story. Even side characters in the world are also interesting in a way so that I got to feel like I am living inside of the story and not just a spectator. Immersion is the keyword here and they got it!OVERALL 4.5/5:The game is a love letter to Indonesia, and a good one at that. There was a lot of love and care throughout this project, and it shows. I think Anyone looking for a game with really interesting story and a interesting cast of characters. This will be the game for you!If you read all that thank you so much! Hope this review actually help you out if you are on the fence in getting the game

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★5/5 "Fun puzzles, mini game, and a real tearjerker story"(+) A Space for the Unbound is a game with beautiful yet heartbreaking story. The game showed us a lot of emotion that all people have. The game thought us about fear, regret, loneliness, envy, jealousy, sadness, and emptiness, but despite all that, the game also thought us about love, bravery, overcoming, moving on, and most importantly, acceptance. The game itself is like roller coaster of emotions and twists.I totally recommend this if you really like story rich game! I literally cried while playing the last two chapters. And i gotta say, this game will become memorable. Especially for Indonesian.(+) I also like how it really captures "pixelated" Indonesia's town in that time (90s) and what culture does people have during that time for example collecting bottle caps, playing arcade games or trading for YOMAN collectibles.(+) Characters in this game is also well written, all of them are loveable and a fantastic addition in the game especially in story.(+) Mini games is really enjoyable(-) However there is still minor cons that i would like to point out. For instance, i really wished that there is chapter select or free roam to collect missing collectibles. I'm aware that in every chapter the game gave us a chance to do so but, looking for collectibles using wikis or walkthrough video is kind of ruining the experience for me especially for the first run. This comes from completionist player like me so, it is just some minor cons that kind of annoy me as a completionist. Because, if you miss 1 collectibles then you have to start over to get extra cutscene.(-) Don't get me wrong, the puzzle in this game is really fun and suits the theme based on a person we solve the puzzle to. However, it's a really fun and games until you meet chapter 4 puzzles. It's a damned algebra and to be honest i force myself to cheat by looking answer online because i can't stand math. Pretty sure the devs wants the puzzle to suits the people we are dealing with (in this case, it's a math teacher so i understand) but, chapter 4 puzzle really spikes the puzzle difficulty if we compared to other puzzles in the game which i considered really easy.

_childDocuments_.review: A very unconventional and overall solid narrative game. It plays with some dark subject matter rather lightly - there were a few moments I thought the game was going to go into a more disturbing direction, but it always seemed to come back up quickly  for air, never dwelling on critical or shocking narrative points for very long before pushing the protagonist into the next chapter. It doesn't exactly hide its twists, so you'll likely put together the central mystery before it's revealed. It seems as though instead of focusing on being a specific type of game or genre plot (mystery, dark, or comedy) the authors were more interested in exploring the depth of its central characters feelings.Due to this, the ending may not hit for everyone if these characters don't click for you (they didn't quite for me), but I can imagine there will be a significant segment of people who think this game pushes all the right buttons. Given the overall high quality and thought-provoking nature of the story, I think it's worth the price to find out for yourself if you'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good art, good music, great story.The mix of light adventure game puzzles and a bit of timed inputs keeps you engaged while the mystery keeps getting bigger. Sometimes you need to beat up school bullies, sometimes you play ace attorney, sometimes you sneak through someones mind - the variety is great. Supported by fleshed out characters, lots of cats to pet - the gameplay loops here fit together tightly. Exploring the city in every chapter let's you see changes and gives a feeling of knowing the place. The worst thing about the game is maybe the action sequence at the end - the controls and character animations aren't made for an action game.The english translation is well written and the story really brought a tear to my eye in the end... I appreciate most that it's not super obvious what the angle is from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional. Having previously played and enjoyed games published by Toge Productions such as Coffee Talk, When The Past Was Around and to a lesser extent She and The Light Bearer, I knew beforehand this game was going to go for the feels factor so my expectations were quite high and thus wanted to wait for full release and not dive into the prologue demo. Oh did it deliver!The gorgeous pixel art was a standout of the game and instantly drew my attention, the love and care that went into creating the scenes throughout is truly sublime. The music was fantastic which I expected since I loved the music in When The Past Was Around and Masdito Bachtiar knocked it out of the park once again, rarely do games make me search them up on Spotify/YouTube to listen outside of the game. Especially with the Arcade mini-game song, now that is a JAM. Made it 1000% more bearable going for that high-score achievement haha!The story was a highlight, it was enjoyable and definitely tries to tug at your heartstrings but it did suffer pacing from the puzzles the game threw at you, albeit easy they did make you do a fair bit of them and there was some sidetracking having to be done which can be a slog, other than that it was good. The characters, although I didn't connect with them as much as I did with the characters in Coffee Talk, were not bad either, there were some dialogue moments between them that were a bit iffy at times but I am going to chalk that up to them translating from Indonesian to English and honestly at the end of the day it doesn't detract from the narrative as a whole being great.The game has a few points of no return which they explicitly warn you of, so if you miss a few collectables then you may miss out on some achievements and have to re-do sections of the game (or restart entirely if you didn't save a bunch) as is what happened to me, but my achievement hunting nature isn't going to dampen the monumental praise I have for this game! Mojiken and Toge Productions have created a gem, hopefully they've made the Indonesian Game Dev scene proud as they have in my opinion created an Indie Game of the Year contender for 2023!Also this game has cats. A LOT of cats. So it has my vote already :)

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up can be really difficult. Children have very little control over their situation, and many are at the mercy of abusive family or socioeconomic factors outside of their control. I was horribly depressed all throughout elementary school and there really wasn't much I could do except pick up all the pieces and rebuild everything once I was free from domestic violence. Much later my siblings and I struggled to help my mom through a bout of depression and we weren't very successful, but it was very clear my mother's problems stemmed from things early in her life.A Space for the Unbound does a really good job capturing both these angles of depression: a person afflicted with a crippling range of emotions and a confused, caring loved one who just wants to help. It's a tempestuous Bildungsroman, where happy slices of life collide with horrible events building up to a beautiful close, both narratively and pixel art graphically. The final boss battle is probably my favorite in (non-action) adventure game history, and I cried so much that I need time to process things before I finish the epilogue chapter.This can probably be finished in 8 hours, but you'll be playing for around 12 if you're trying to complete all achievements. I actually missed petting four of the animals, so I cheated and edited the save file. Work smarter not harder ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: A Space for the Unbound is an adventure game set in rural 1990’s Indonesia. It features a poignant narrative that focuses on mental health, whilst weaving in slice-of-life style gameplay. Despite beginning development in 2015, the developers’ hard work has clearly paid off. With a unique setting, quality story, art and puzzles, this is a memorable title that is sure to tug on players heartstrings.Set in rural 1990’s Indonesia, players follow Atma and Raya. The pair are near their graduation of High School and must start preparing for their futures. The story begins as a cozy adventure, exploring their small town of Loka City. Suddenly, a supernatural force seems to ruin it all, inserting itself into the lovers’ lives and breaking up the tranquil atmosphere.  The two must further explore the deep rooted cause of this phantasmal occurrence and uncover not only its secrets, but also their own. Despite this wholesome beginning, and without spoilers, the narrative deeply explores the harshness of anxiety and depression, slowly delving into the human psyche, whilst simultaneously being a journey of self-discovery and maintaining its slice-of-life atmosphere.A Space for the Unbound’s narrative is a tangled one, but it surprisingly manages to uncoil its many branches. With many aspects to piece together and many timelines, rifts and characters to remember, it would be easy to fall victim to its convolution. However, the narrative is conveyed clearly, often repeating titbits of important information over time to allow players to gain a solid grasp on the many happenings. None of this felt like over-exaggeration, hand-holding or patronising, but rather, it all blended effortlessly, creating a fantastic foundation to tell its poignant story. Overall, the narrative was not at all what I expected, and the game completely changes into what felt like a different game than in the early chapters. The characters are expertly written and over time, I felt empathetic towards them. Their hardship, their past experiences, it all felt vivid and realistic. Given the games’ length, they all experience great development and growth, allowing players to better understand them. This game has an abundance of reading. Similar to a visual novel, but it does feature large chunks of gameplay through puzzles, mini-games and exploration. Atma also has the skill to be able to “spacedive,” meaning he can see the inner thoughts and stresses about characters he meets. These are usually interwoven with puzzles and further complicated by entering different timelines or “rifts.” You can also pet all of the animals in the game. Really, its also for an achievement! Pet every stray cat you come across, even dogs and ducks. What more could you want! There are a total of five chapters, but the difficulty of the puzzles ramps up after chapter 4. I was not necessarily a fan of this, and did need to resort to a guide for some things (that cursed mathematics equation!)Despite the large amount of dialogue, the gameplay is also engaging, and manages to create an enjoyable flow from start to finish through its many mini-games. The most common are quick-time events involving the precise and timed copying of select keys, or pressing a button when the moving cursor in a bar is green. This is how fighting transpires in the game, or the Future Fighter arcade game. At first, I enjoyed this arcade section, but for an achievement/optional side extra in the game, you must reach 1500 and 1700 points. Only gaining 100 points per battle, and with no extra lives, it is a slog to reach 1700 and the window of opportunity is very slim. Admittedly, I tried many times to achieve this, but that high score has still evaded me (one day… one day).Other common mini-games include stealth sections. These are extremely simple and just involve staying still when an exclamation mark pops up. Bounce a ball with precision timing 70 times, answer quizzes or choose to do the extras and fulfil Raya’s bucket list. The mini-games inclusion helps solidify the cozy nature of the game, and accentuates its wholesome atmosphere (but only in early chapters).For the most part, puzzles are decent. Most are inventory-based, involving searching through different timelines to retrieve items for a spacedive of a character in another timeline, etc. Collect evidence to convey in court, match up the cake to the description…. And complete a confusing mathematical equation. OK, the latter was not so great. Yes, maths is not my strong suit. But I have never come across such a solely mathematical puzzle in a game before. You must search the areas to find multiple hints to the equation such as N=1 (none of these examples are the actual formula) to solve multiple disjointed equations such as 14=2x+n or 4-7n=-1. There are MULTIPLE of these and fair to say, I had no idea what I am doing. There was no find x, or explanation. Just these varying formulas scattered everywhere that apparently led to a code. I appreciate the difference and complexity, but without a guide, I would have been stuck for an eternity.Despite there being only five chapters, these chapters are very lengthy with enormous amounts of content to uncover. Some extra content and achievements are locked to specific chapters. I was not aware of this and always thought I could come back to parts of the town to complete them. Unfortunately, you cannot, and there is no chapter select (but there are manual save slots). Furthermore, I had apparently missed two of the cats to pet and it would be nice to see these added in on the map in a Newgame+ or underneath the chapter they were missed in.The hand-drawn soft pixel art is stunning, and reminiscent of anime styles. It perfectly fits in with the 90s setting the game covers and there are many beautiful, pastel backdrops to screenshot in vibrant Loka City. The characters are not voiced, but the backing audio is playful and retro-inspired. It fits well with the themes of the game, and the finale song is sure to create an emotive response.  Approx 10.5 hours Yes Not really.. there are achievements but going back for these without a chapter select (and if you did not manually save each chapter) can be a pain, as it is a linear story and there is no auto text skip.A Space for the Unbound is a unique game. Its chirpy pixel artstyle, cozy mini-games and many cats to pet give the impression it is a flippant game, but this is not an accurate description. It is heavily symbolic and covers a journey of self-discovery and overcoming mental illnesses. A wonderful and eye-opening experience with an abundance of content to explore, well worth its full price tag of $AU30.

_childDocuments_.review: This isint really a game it's more like a side scrolling-ish hyper story driven game with very light fighting mechanics. And honestly I am all about it. There was this meme going around in the early 2010s it was like "young people act like spongebob but end up growing up to be squidward" the whole premise behind Raya's character reminded me of that.Honestly looking back on it, its a very depressing story despite it appearing very upbeat and high note for the majority of its run time. Even if it ends on a high note you cant help but question human nature for the lack of benevolence, community, empathy that was required to end up with the story we have here. Hell, id argue that maybe we should return to the rural village life, it seems so nice to live somewhere where everyone knows you and it didn't make me help but wonder if someone who went though Raya turmoil lived in a western society they'd probably be  either beyond broken or dead.Maybe Dr. Theodore Kaczynski was right
