_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it ... it's crap.It's one of those games that insists on choking itself while deep throating it's source material, and paradoxically screwing up the theme in the process.The voice acting is atrocious. It's milking the whole "Would'ya like to know more" bs in the most bland and uninteresting way, possible and the core gameplay loop is beyond effed.Their idea of difficulty is essentially doubling your damage output on easy, or subsequently taking half away for the difficult option ... and relies much too heavily on unit micro-management. Pausing the action would have been a good idea in order to set up some tactics.I get the whole "more meat for the grinder" stuff, but the whole point of the books was that even though humanity is essentially stuck as a fascist parody of itself, picking fights with aliens on the far side of the galaxy for no good reason other than to enact some sort of effed up manifest destiny crap while also getting rid of some undesirables, and when it all turns into the massive cluster♥♥♥♥ of "oh man... those guys are actually waay more fascistic, prepared and have a lot more expendable individuals than we have " thing is held together by the struggles certain people face in that universe. This game misses the point entirely... which is weird since the gameplay is geared towards that hero-based branch of RTS games.... so that whole leveling up after you kill some ♥♥♥♥ mechanic is complete garbage because it's temporarily mission locked stuff in the beginning, and so for absolutely no reason other to make sure you lose some units before that idiot of a CO of yours figures out it'd be a good idea to requisition you the proper counter-measures for the scenario you are in. ... which you probably won't have in the next mission.oh... that CO is the guy who's voice actor is so out of it, muting the game and reading the subtitles makes the experience 10 times more enjoyable. He also decides to force you disobey some " stay there and die for zi greater good " bs orders that make no sense and is subsequently removed from the picture (temporarily i bet because i started writing this review after having to save scum the following mission since it's a crappy escort mission in which you can't lose any unit... by which i mean... it's ok if you lose a unit... but can't lose a squad. ... which brings me to the lack of care that went into designing their scenarios.)Oh... and it glitches like nuts.So yeah... a glitchy game that sucks off the memes associated with the source material, slow paced, inconsistent, weirdly thought out, with no real point to it other than " let's basically play some missions which look like that one movie ".... oh ... and it's so brilliantly designed that when you do get stuck having to save scum a stupidly designed escort mission, both the bugs and marines behave in unpredictable RNG ways. For example, that escort mission I mentioned has this situation in which it pits you against two tiger bugs which are blatantly impervious to pretty much anything short of a grenade to the face, and the only guy in the squad that can lob them randomly decides to forget he's got an unlimited supply while the two snipers get their feet bitten off by bugs while this insipid bastard figures out how to tell his prick from his elbow. If you're a fan of RTS games in general, this isn't for you.If you're a fan of ST ... and you can stomach this crap .. you're probably not a real fan.. you just like shower scenes.And if you're a fan of that movie... ... you're better off seeing that movie again instead of playing this.I mean... like why the ♥♥♥♥ would you go through the trouble of pissing away half the money you can make on a game on royalties to the holder of whatever IP you wan to use... go out of your way in blowing the fan-base with trailers and dev talks and whatnot, telling them the reason you've decided to use the property is to bring the universe alive... and not profiting of of the fact that you know for a fact that your slow paced piece of crap  which'd go well past it's "2 hour game time till you can return it" before revealing itself to be a boring piece of junk which will inevitably disappoint and further ruin the IP.Why... for money of course ... well ... ya got mine... enjoy it... but for the price I paid for this piece of crap, I'll squeeze every last drop while taking a dump on your game.This game is nothing more than a lazy cash grab at best, and if you strip away all the Starship Trooper stickers off of it, it's a bad RTS with half the functionality cut away, bad voice acting, and stupidly designed missions.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 11 hours of game play and blowing through the Campaign, I can definitely say this is a must buy with a huge asterix on it...The Story is fun, cheesy and captures the movies propaganda feel to move the story along between missions. The Voice acting leaves a little to be desired, but its not the worst I've heard in a game before. Before this came out, I watched a few videos of gameplay footage so I knew I wasn't going to be getting 'Starcraft' and more Dawn of War 2. I would've liked if this game had more of a base building aspect to it but that maybe that's something they can do if they make another game. Visually, the game looks great and there's a good variety in maps and missions, considering this takes place on a desert bug planet there isn't a whole lot you can do to make each map super appealing but a lot of the mountain maps, city maps and even the underground complex type maps are fine.There's a ton to see from all the starship troopers movies in this - so if you really liked the CGI movies you'll enjoy seeing the Powered Suit Cap Troopers in the late game, the Marauders from Starship Troopers 3 pop up, and even the pulse rifle troopers from the second movie appear. There's a TON of different bug types as well to fight - you might recognize some of them from the old first person shooter game like the Tiger Bug.Now for the downside of this - there is only the campaign and two scenarios to play.That's it, once you beat them, you've essentially beat the game and there isn't too much in the way of replay value unless you want to play at a higher difficulty. This game is in serious need of a free play mode or something where you can play on all the of the maps against waves of bugs or something, I'm talking like a game type where you defend that fort on Planet P against the massive horde of bugs or something.On top of that it feels like the AI is pretty cheap in some places. A lot of missions have you clearing out bug lairs and things like that which will spawn waves of bugs to take out your troopers, but a lot of the time they'll drop a special type bug like the scorpion bug that will incinerate anything as soon as it pops up out of the ground. I played on Medium for most of the game and there were some very unforgiving missions where RNG played a huge factor.all that being said if you like RTS games and are a fan of starship troopers, this is the game we've been waiting for, if they add the free play feature or something I would say this is the essential Starship Troopers game until we get a proper first person shooter that's not an ARMA 3 mod.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed EVERY mission in this game on brutal. I can say that "I am doing my part.", and I recommend without a doubt that anyone who has not gotten this game should get it as well. And always remember "Service Guarantees Citizenship."Anyway serious talk, I love this game, it's an interesting take on the rts genre and does it beautifully. The game mechanics are smooth and not hard to wrap your head around. Every unit bug, or human fulfills a different role and are useful/annoying no matter what mission you are doing. The story is great and spans 19 whole missions so you will spend a good bit getting through it. If I had to complain about anything, it would have to be the lack of content after the campaign. The two extra missions are cool and all, but I still wish there was more and am hoping they add more in the coming months. I also wish the game had a unique multiplayer where players play bugs, or humans in an nearly endless war of attrition. I think it would be a great take on an rts multiplayer. Having player controlled bugs attempt to dislodge human defenders, or Humans attempting to clear out Bug Hives on a massive battlefield would be amazing. Aside from those two I think the ability to make custom mission through and editor would be nice as well although It can come much later than other things. I'd also like to see the ability to gain more supplies and war support through other means other than objectives. Like calling in supplies to fill and empty depot with war support and vice versa.Anyway that's how I feel about this game and what I hope to see in the future. And as always "A good bug, is a dead bug."The 2024 Update:Since my attention has been brought back to this review, here's an update. I will be going over the base game and the DLCs in this update.Base Game:I still recommend the base game, it was and still is a fun experience you can sink many hours into. The addition of extra scenario missions, and the mission editor help fix the content issue that game had originally since you can always find a new mission to play via the community. Couple all this with the modding scene, and I can say that Starship Troopers Terran Command is a great game.Raising Hell:I won't sugar coat it. Raising hell is not the greatest dlc ever. Honestly it is a rather large disappoint from my perspective. The new campaign doesn't hold my attention that well, combined with how short the campaign is. I think they could have done a lot better with the story especially if they had shifted the attention off the Mobile Infantry onto the Mercs. I think the Campaigns ending was bland and uninteresting. It would have been more interesting if we had several more missions focused on the Merc's point of view. That alone however, isn't why I rate the campaign so poorly. Outside of the campaign the units are abysmal. Although they have rather unique designs for the units, they always end up falling short except for the Frag Mercs. The frag mercs are the only salvageable unit in my opinion. Their unique design and concept make them a fun unit to micro within your force, and the unit itself is fairly powerful. Aside from that the Rifleman Mercs are a decent concept, but generally perform poorly compared to normal Rifleman squads. The Merc officer is essentially just a tactical officer. The Engineering Bi-ped is another salvageable unit that does its job well. Finally the shredder merc is in my opinion the worst by far.  The fact that a mission revolves around their use is a massive blow to the campaign as the Shredder does not do well in my opinion. It does awful anti-air damage, which is supposed to be its primary role. Although it's deploy-able mode is unique, you have to use it all the time for shredders to actually work. Outside of their deployed state, they feel like they fire bean bags at the high hp flyers you're supposed to use them against. All in all, they suffer from a lack of damage, and the investment you put into them isn't worth it since a normal rifle squad could do the same thing at a lower cost. Aside from those, the Power-suit Officer and Incinerators are nice to have and are decent at their roles., The Personally I rate the Raising hell DLC a 4/10. Urban Onslaught:Urban onslaught is a major step up from Raising hell. Although the story isn't amazing. It at minimum held my attention while I was playing the campaign. The units hold up greatly as well. The Police squad is an interesting take on a rifleman squad and serve the role of a front-line rather well. The only issue the Police squad has is the fact it's phased out by the Riot Squad. The Riot Shields squad is a very powerful unit. It works similarly to the Frag Mercs while being a larger squad, and a very tanky squad at that. Due to their ability they can tank any source of damage in the game while coming out of said damage with only scratches. This makes them the best front-line in the game, and I found myself relying on them for most the campaign. Technicians are a new Engineer unit with a variety of interesting and useful emplacements. The squad itself however performs rather poorly as they trade the flame thrower for a taser. I do not recommend using them for combat unless you're forced to do so. The Cyclone, or the Hover Tank is a fun vehicle to have. It is fast, and deals decent damage. Personally I would not spam them as they work better as a simple IFV that gives your squads an extra bit of firepower. The Peacekeeper biped helps serve as an alternative to the Radio Operator, capable of placing landing zones while also being a decent support unit with its grenade launcher. The Pegasus, or the Gunship is rather underwhelming in my opinion. I had trouble finding it useful as aerial bugs easily countered it. If you aren't facing any form of bug air support, then it is an easily abuse-able unit that can shred basic bugs and deal hefty damage to larger bugs. Lastly the Rainmaker is an incredible unit. It serves as the first real artillery unit you have outside of turrets. It is useful both deployed and undeployed. Although I personally found the text for its elite drone ability broken, the unit still performed very well. The Rainmaker is in my opinion the second most powerful unit this dlc adds behind the Riot Shield Squad. Lastly the J.A.C is rather underwhelming, it severs as an alternative to Rocket Troopers, but it feels like the Rocket Trooper was nerfed so that this unit could be an alternative. J.A.Cs can't fire over other units leading to issues when attempting to design fire lines in tight areas that include them. J.A.Cs do have a jumppack which can be used to scale terrain for better vantage points, but I found this ability nearly useless. There was simply no place where the ability was actually useful since I simply couldn't scale certain terrain, or there was no terrain to scale. On the final mission the jump ability isn't even use-able. The J.A.C is simply disappointing in my opinion and I would have preferred Rocket Troopers 9 times out of 10 if they had the range. In terms of level design I liked the Urban Onslaught levels although the Bridge one did end up as an awful slog that took over  an hour to beat on brutal. The final mission suffers as well and personally I think it would of been better if they treated the final hive similar to how they did the super hive from the starport scenario. I rate the Urban Onslaught dlc an 8/10. It is a fun experience, the new units are fun to play with, and the story, although not amazing, wasn't so bad I hated playing through it.

_childDocuments_.review: If this were 60$ and AAA, I would be more disappointed. As it stands this is a decent game, from a small studio swinging for the fences at a discounted price. HOWEVER, it is severely hurt by it's lack of locations, and feeling of no real progression. Every mission feels like a fresh start where your choices in units is limited. (Not that it matters, you will pretty much just bring basic riflemen and a bunch of rocket troopers for most of the game.) The base building doesn't matter, and when the ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan, you will just spam attack-move and micro your rockets and grenades. Oh yeah, and scorpion/bombardier spam late game is ass.It's decent. And it's Starship Troopers. It was a good ride, but I will probably never touch this game again. Your price value will vary. _childDocuments_.review: Dizzy: Rico, I'm dying...Johnny Rico: No Diz, you'll be fine.Dizzy: But it's OK, because I got to have you.Overall this is a good game, but it does have some issues.The great stuff is that the sound and graphics are great and it really sounds like you are fighting a army of bugs. The story is written well and I like the subtle tones in the writing such as calling prisoners "Patriotic Volunteers" when you send them down a mine full of arachnids.The bad stuff is primarily with the difficulty and the mapping of unit movements. The difficulty is based on damage which is not bad, the higher the difficulty the lower the damage you do. The problem is that certain types of bug can only be effectively hurt with a certain type of Mobile Infantry, so you can have moments in missions where you can not  kill a bug quick enough before the other types kill you all. As for the movement issue of units, most Mobile Infantry units can not shot through each other and fire while moving, but when moving they take the quickest path to the destination you send them. So you can have a firing line of ten units in a sewer level and when telling them to move down to the corner the first unit closest takes the corner first and starts shooting a bug and the other nine Infantry units take the same exact path and now none of them will shoot or move and they all will be eaten, even in "Attack Move".So overall it is a good game, not the best, but it's okay, because I got to have you.I also recommend you use Wemod on the higher difficulties just for the resources to span units and then try to kill all the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through on the hardest difficulty and had a really good time. Quite a few missions felt like a real tug of war and I had to fight for every inch of progress. You can no doubt finish the game alot quicker on lower difficulties but I felt like Brutal is the only way to get a true sense of being overwhelmed because you do less damage which allows the bugs to close the gap before they are killed.Theres no base building so its just controlling units. You do have to select platforms to upgrade to buildings in order to unlock units throughout the mission but thats about it. The story is more akin to the movies instead of the book. Its entertaining and cheesy and I loved it. I've noticed there are references to the movies. The overall theme follows the movies as well.There are a good variety of units on both sides. Theres a select few units that are alot better then others and theres a a couple units that are direct counters to certain bug units. Theres a good variety of bugs to kill although there seems to be a problem with their spawning priority. The majority of the time I spent fighting 3 types of bugs and the AI would rarely or never spawn tankers or some of the lesser units. The last Starship Troopers game was in 2005 and the fact it took this long for someone else to mess with the IP is disappointing because there is alot of potential. Its a good, fun, simple game that lets you kill all them bugs. I hope it does well enough to warrant content updates or expansions because I would definitely purchase it. I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Obligatory TL;Dr:  Great game, its not done, hope they add features later.So I conquered it.  I had a lot of trouble stopping playing because it is addictive and fun.  I look forward to the game being completed.Here is my in depth review:There are two universes of Starship Troopers.  There is the book version, where powered armour is the standard.  Troopers die  in training when they fall off mountains learning how to use it.  Training is hard so the Mobile Infantry consists of a few, elite soldiers.  The armour is thick and allows for large jumps with massive firepower.  It is also where the term "Mobile" in "Mobile Infantry" comes from because troopers move, "on the bounce" and scale mountains with ease.  There is only one game that used this universe and that was "Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendancy."  The movie universe is the useless plastic armour that cant stop bullets or claws.  Helmets don't fit right and often go over the soldiers eyes and give them the iconic look of covered eyes and the chin strap pushing their lip up.  Waves after waves of infantry march against the bugs.  This game follows the movie universe but with mechs.  In this game, to beat the bugs you have to weaken bug holes then attack then main bug nest in the middle.  However, the single player campaign only gives you set units in a map to accomplish this.  What winds up happening is back and forth to your base to fix units, back out, do some damage, back to base to heal, then rinse and repeat.  On one mission when I unlocked power armour, the built up quarters meant lightning bugs would hurt me so bad I couldn't finish off the nest before i had to go heal.  While I was healing, the bug nests would respawn.  Basically I had to go back and forth to the nests until I weakened it enough to eventually take it.  On other missions, they would wipe out my troopers, who moved very slowly, and I would have to rebuild the army.Rebuilding the army:To rebuild, you have to have drop ships available.  Drop ships have a timer of 1-2 minutes before they become available to bring one unit.  This means you can make 1 unit every 1-2 minutes every time you get wiped.  It is slow.  The tempo goes make army - go get wiped but cause enough damage to the bug hole to make progress in killing it so your next wave of infantry can take it down.  No sense running - your troopers are painfully slow until you get to the powered armour troopers who are quite zippy.Unit balance:There are a lot of rock paper scissors elements.  Laser troopers kill almost everything, but short range so they get killed by spitters.  Rocket troopers kill spitters and armoured guys.  Lighting bugs kill everything, including frying your mech, so you have to have rocket troopers available.  You'll need radio operators to respawn your squads because they get wiped out so quickly.  You will require a cross section of soldiers, not just a fleet of battlecruisers like in SC2.AI:This game is designed for micromanagement.  You must move every squad individually.  If you attempt to attack move a group across the map, they will die.  They'll trip over each other, get into fire paths, not shoot, and be eaten in seconds.  If you expect anything other than that, you will get frustrated.  Move every squad in leap frog formats,  Be prepared for multi-prong attacks on bug holes.  I really enjoyed this feature, despite the scolding it gets from other reviews.  It is a unique feature to the game and adds a lot of neat mechanics.Graphics:Yup, awesome.  Great job there.  Felt good, explosions were fun, i enjoyed them. 10/10.Music:I didn't turn it off the entire 14 hours I was playing.  It fit well with the gameplay.  I often turn off music that is distracting or drowns out the voices/warnings/commands/whatever of RTS games.  I did not do that here. 10/10.Overall:As i stated at the start, I look forward to it being completed.  There are bugs (programming bugs, not just bad people eater bugs).  There are no achievements.  There are no unlocks like in There are billions, SC2 Co-op, and Warhammer RTS series.  You get unlocks based on the mission you are on and that is it.  Upgrading unit health, damage, speed, reducing dropship respawn time, and reducing time to escalate battle tiers would all be wonderful upgrades.  If Age of Darkness can add these after release, I'm sure it can be done. There is a single player campaign with no freeplay, skirmish, or multiplayer.   As of June 20, 2022 the only thing you can do once you conquer it is replay the single player campaign.  If you turn up the difficulty you will not get any achievement or e-pat on the back.  That's not to say it's not fun, but it does lack a feature that an immense amount of other titles have.Are these features going to be added in the future?  I don't know.  There is no publication about it from anyone.  I hope so.  Slitherine is not a small indie company and this game could make a bazillion dollars.  Obligatory TL;Dr:  Great game, its not done, hope they add features later.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of sci-fi RTS games will not be dissapointed. Starship Troopers: Terran Command offers hours of glorious bug-splatting, featuring all the units and creatures seen in the Starship Troopers movie trilogy and the somewhat-mediocre Starship Troopers FPS game.Gameplay-wise, Terran Command resembles Company of Heroes with elements of tower defense. Controls are fairly straightforward, micromanagement is tolerable, and missions are reasonably challenging. Although pathfinding could on occasion use some improvement, units sometimes getting stuck, it is a minor inconvenience easily rectified.So far the game doesn't seem to have any multiplayer options, though a co-op mode or a Humans vs. Bugs mode would no doubt greatly increase the game's replay value.The graphics are somewhat mediocre by current standards, roughly on the level of Dawn of War 2, though then again, it is not necessarily a flaw for this type of game. Sometimes it's best to keep things simple.All in all, though there is room for improvement, Terran Command is a solid article for sci-fi RTS fans. I rate it as 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Fifteen missions in at time of writing, and so far ST:TC is proving to be a fun, occasionally tough, but satisfying RTS.There's no base-building to speak of, which is a downer; instead the focus is on capturing pre-built command posts to act as reinforcement stations. Resource caches and secondary objectives give you access to Supplies to recruit units, and War Support, which is used to build turrets and base upgrades to unlock additional unit types.This is a very "caster heavy" game, with everyone having at least one ability they can use on a cooldown. These can range from throwing grenades or firing incendiary rockets to launching distracting flares or buffing allies. Each unit has different strengths and weaknesses on top of this, meaning that success relies on getting the right mix of troopers to clear out the hostiles.Tonally, this is fairly true to the movie - though a lot more cynical. It's less Starship Troopers as it was, and more what idiots like Verhoeven wanted Starship Troopers to be. There are not-so-subtle hints that this is a nation run by Stalinesque individuals and that the Federation higher-ups don't care about people's lives beyond their immediate value to the Commissariat. It is honestly rather tiresome to be facing an unstoppable horde of mindless killing machines while being told you're working for the bad guys - well excuse me for not wanting the human race to be devoured!But questionable narrative choices aside, it's otherwise a gung-ho dive into glorious Man-vs-Bug conflict. You get a lot of cool toys to play with, a huge variety of bugs to make those toys feel inadequate, a lot of bug holes to nuke, and a whole host of last stands to gloriously perform. Service guarantees Citizenship!

_childDocuments_.review: While I agree there could/should be something like a skirmish mode, the game has a real Ground Control feel to it and so far I'm loving it. You don't generate resources to spend, you have a fixed amount that you can sometimes supplement and use that to determine which units you call in.  It's best if you keep them alive so they gain veterancy and another ability.It's not a macro base-builder where you harvest resources, turn them into units, and just right click and forget about them, micro is the name of the game.I hope it has good post launch support because I want more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a lot, despite that it's not very long and doesn't allow for multiplayer campaigns.  It's a neat tactical RTS game that is more focused on combat and less on resource gathering/management, like what you'd see in games like StarCraft or Command and Conquer.  Being that the campaigns in this game are exclusively about squad and platoon level infantry combat, and being a former infantryman, I really appreciated what this game had to offer.  Factors such as elevation and terrain, types of enemy you're facing on a campaign and the proper management and use of units you have available (you have to be smart about how you deploy your forces) very much come into play in this game.  Maximizing each squad's arcs of fire and setting up proper kill zones are key.I also liked how the game, sometimes in a very 'tongue in cheek' way, played proper tribute to the satirical themes present in the Starship Troopers films.Overall a good game.  I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a "good" game? A strictly good game? Starship Troopers is that type of game.It's a good RTS, it's got a good selection of units, each with their own good abilities and veterancies, and good fun levels but it excels at nothing it does. As far as RTS games go, it doesn't really bring anything new to its genre outside of its setting.The campaign suffers from a lack of great characters to get attached to, largely because of the voice-acting which is just not that great. Even the propaganda reports, a very cool concept failed to get me hooked as the Announcer was just...generic. It's good but not memorable. There's a very good selection of levels and scenarios to playthrough which is a big plus however none of them escape the feeling of being glorified skirmish missions due to a lack of central progression.Yes, you unlock new units as you play but those units don't get stronger, there's no upgrades and there comes a point where you just get objectively better units that invalidate more than half of the roster by virtue of being stronger and cheaper.Each unit has a basic ability, a way to select which enemy to prioritize, better stats as they level up and another special ability at level three, which only really matters for the early game units. Which, it's important to note can be dismissed to obtain better ones which is an appreciated feature.Most units do have some genuinely great abilities but the gameplay it's compelling enough for them to properly spice things up. Except two of the late-game marine units which are fun by virtue of being utterly broken overpowered. The Third Level upgrades on the other hand are rather useless since there is almost always an objectively superior one which invalidates the ability to choose between three.The enemy selection is great, with lots of enemy types but fighting them largely resume to...sitting your units in a good position. Some may enjoy notion of not having to micro but you'll still have to worry about moving your units back from the mid-game and onwards artillery strikes. Later game you will unlock some more fun unit types that can you can... watch as they mow down through the enemies swarms with barely any resistance. The RTS element was simply not that engaging to me.The "Micro" Missions especially suffer from this basic "hold this position" type of strategic gameplay which the game fails to make compelling. Which is not to say that the macro, aka big, missions don't have their own problems. They can largely be resumed to get a base and destroy the hives just like you did the other 10 missions beforehand. The few times the formula is changed do work pretty well though.The base-system which is your main way of getting troops is neat but on a lot of maps it can be skipped as it's simply more effective not to worry about having to defend another base (or any base) as long as you have units.I don't remember much about the music but I do remember some bad sound design, especially in terms of atmosphere. The game fails to build a proper atmosphere and especially in its later half, also fails to build tension and suspense since you're already used to just, careful positioning or simply a-moving if you use the again, objectively broken units. Performance was good, there's no crashes, graphics are good and so are the combat effects, which is a plus. The game would have benefited from the super-zoom games like Company of Heroes have to see the combat up-close.I think a way to speed-up the game could improve it quite a lot.If you have an RTS itch, this game might scratch it, in the same way a bland meal might get rid of your hunger. I think it can be improved, I'm willing to change my opinion based on the expansions but the vanilla game is worse than vanilla, it's  just bland. Some leniency should be granted since it's their first game and there are some genuinely great concepts but the execution fails for most.I can't recommend the game, unless you're particularly interested in the setting it provides or want to support a smaller studio. There's better games on the RTS market, and almost all of them are older titles.I also cannot say the game should be avoided, after all, it's just...good.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game by any means, but one that won't be installed on your computer for very long. The campaign is quite long and has a nice variety of missions, but there is no 'skirmish' mode like on similar games, you NEED to play a story mission, though you can replay any that you have previously won. Units will occasionally mess up their pathing the most annoying issue with the game is that most infantry units can't see through other infantry. While units are stationary that isn't a problem as you can set them up where you like and take advantage of raised positions, but when you order units to do an attack move 50% of the time they will merge into this giant blob of soldiers and they get destroyed because no one can see through the other units. The bug varieties are also really lacking, they could have been SUPER creative and made nightmare fuel bugs to kill, but the drones, warriors, 'tiger' warriors and royal guard are all the same model repainted and their size changed, and those are 50% of the bug unit types and 90% of what you will be fighting.What the game DOES do right is capture the vibe of the original movie. That might not seem like a huge positive, but that is why you are looking at this game, right? It doesn't break any new ground, but it does make you feel like you are in the world of Starship Troopers. Your soldiers aren't 40K Space Marines, they are fragile little humans that go down in one or two hits, they need massed fire or rockets to take down anything but the most basic bugs, the story is bleak, as soon as you think that your boys and girls are catching a break, something else happens or some troops need to hold the line with no hopes of survival so that you can extract a Fleet Officer. And the news channel/propaganda in between missions is PERFECT. The exact same nationalist, story spinning style as the movie.TLDR; Wait for this bad boy to go on sale if you enjoy the movies.

_childDocuments_.review: A Starship troopers strategy game that does precisely what you would expect. It even surprised me a little. While the game may not tactically be complicated, it's focus is more on you as a player making sure you have your force consistently set up for a wave of bugs.I selected the difficulty below maximum and it feels just about right. The idea is to keep a consistent firing line so that your units can absorb a wave of bugs at any moment, because if you leave a gap, about 6 bugs can take out one unit in less than 10 seconds, once one goes down it can snow ball and within a minute your whole force could be at risk of being wiped out so retreating before it's too late is something you'll have to judge very quickly.The unfortunate part about the campaign are the 'tunnel/cave' missions. They feel very uninteresting compared to the other missions. As the campaign progresses the mission get more consistent and fun but those early tunnel missions grind the gameplay to a hault when compared to the levels where you'll have to face hundreds of bugs at once.The price seems just about right too but I would recommend getting the DLC on sale as that does feel like it should be included in the game. Never the less, the game does what you want and the developers did a great job keeping the gameplay in focus. It's not a lazy cash grab nor filled with any glitches, it does just what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is just bad. for 30$ of value..you get 5$ of game.The bad:Scripted Missions--Unlike in other games where you can complete objectives in different ways, ST:TC only allows you to go to A do this, then go to B and do that. And thats it. No creativity involved whatsoever.No epic war scale--You are not fighting a vast war across multiple planets. Just one. and you only do it in 30ish missons half of which are basically tutorial missions so you dont really get to play with the full arsenal until half way through the game.Boring-- Troops are expendable. You can level them through experience but its completely and utterly pointless and troops are endless. you dont get a "fixed" amount to deal with forcing you to invest in your troops and their "elite" upgrades are boring and useless. Go to A do that, go to B do that. there is nothing to really get you invested in the mission its just the same scripted crap over and over.No Skirmish Mode-- For a Single player only game there is no skirmish....WTF. you play the 30 missions and you are done. ZERO replayability.AI is garbage---the ai is just stupid. you have to micro manage every little thing and there is no pause function to let you queue up orders...The Good:Follows ST Canon...thats it...thats literally the only positive aspect of this game anyone has ever said. it follows the books.The conclusion: someone gave the Deverlopers 10$ and said make a game...and thats what they did. they made a hot piece of crap on a 10$ budget and selling the game for a whopping 30$. _childDocuments_.review: After watching the original (again) as well as 2 and 3 (skip 2, it's pretty bad, 3 is a bit better since CVD returns as Rico), it was time to try out ST Terran Command...Would you like to know more?As a strategy/military game it does the job. _childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, it's a decent game with a promising road map ahead of it.  It's fun, it's engaging.  It has a decent story.  But there are problems.Personally, I'm a Starship Troopers fan.  A BIG fan.  When I was a kid, I watched the movie so many times it used to put me to sleep.  I've read the book, watched and own all 5 movies, AND (this is the important part) played the game Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendency.  A great Starship Troopers RTS game.  Any new RTS Starship Troopers game will be compared to any old RTS ST game.  And the old game is better than the new one for several reasons.* Terran Command has WILDLY swinging difficulty.  It can go from so easy you don't think about it, to enragingly difficult mission to mission.* The unit special abilities are not optional, they are REQUIRED for success.  Even on the easiest difficulties, you are required to micro manage every single unit's every single ability and their cooldown timers.  These special abilities are so necessary that they need their own individual hotkeys.  In addition to this, some upgrade abilities are so good that it's only ever worth it to take one over the other.* There are contradictory gameplay mechanics that need to be fixed.  The game sets up a great LOS system.  (Most) Every unit needs a clear field of fire to shoot at the enemy.  Most units can't shoot through / over other units.  BUT most every unit has a very limited range they can shoot.  Hence the contradicting gameplay mechanic.  If I have to micromanage a battle line, then it doesn't make sense for soldier that can fire a bullet reasonably accurately over a thousand yards to only be limited to start shooting at 50.* Marauder implementation is very lacking / uninspiring.  They are NOT good enough to be worth the extra effort to get them.  There are bugs that EASILY destroy them, but the marauders aren't even that good compared to other bugs out there.  It's not even a rock-paper-scissor system.  Mobility wins battles, and the one Marauder is NOT better than the 1 squad of troopers, plus rocket launcher, plus 4x HMG emplacement replacement cost.Now, these problems don't make the game bad.  But fixing them will change the game from Good / Good Enough, to Great.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game announced, I had really mixed feelings and wasn't sure if I like the concept of an RTS where you just constantly mow down hordes of bugs. My initial skepticism only grew stronger as I watched gameplay trailers and previews, which seemed to reinforce my belief that the game would turn out to be dull and uninteresting.And then I decided to actually try it out and suddenly realised that the game is pretty fun and engaging despite how it might appear. I've got to say that I am a fan of the franchise, so that might make me biased, but I appreciate the game's references to the movie and all these corny propaganda-style cutscenes and dialogues. The diverse array of weapons and units at my disposal further added to the enjoyment, and discovering the inclusion of different Arachnids from different movies and cartoons was an unexpected treat.Having successfully completed the main campaign, I can confidently assert that I find this game pretty good. Despite my initial uncertainties, this game managed to surpass my expectations with its entertaining gameplay, charming tie-ins to the movie, and an array of captivating features. Its straightforward mechanics, coupled with suitable graphics, culminated in an overall positive gaming experience. For the future, I hope that the developers might consider incorporating an Arachnid campaign to further augment the game's appeal. In the meantime, I still recommend it to both fellow fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Two amazing factors about this game:-The atmosphere, dialogue, music, story and art just oozes Starship Troopers.  It's enough to make anyone feel like they are doing their part.-The supply caps and enemy waves are fantastically designed to keep you in the RTS action without feeling like you need to reload the game just because you made a single technical error.  It creates a superb tug-of-war type system where you fight inch by inch to complete the story.It really isn't a game-changing-revolutionary-RTS, but it doesn't need to be.  As long as you like Starship Troopers and strategy, you're in for a treat.  Great game.   Enlist today and see for yourself!

Another glitch is sometimes when you click on a unit and then scroll away the unit deselects... annoying? yes, game breaking? no.Edit: Its been months and the audio glitch still occurs every time I try to play this, I can get through about 1 mission before audio gets staticy and cuts out :/Regardless the story is fun so far, it is limited units and while you are not collecting supplies to make armies, I can appreciate a game where you have a limited supply to make things more... special ops? graphics are good, fights are great evolution of the enemy seems like a good pace most of the time. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this title. It reminds me a lot of an old Starship Troopers RTS released in 2000 I enjoyed as a kid. Definite recommend, especially at it's current price point.Would you like to know more? The campaign took me around 25 hours on normal difficulty which I think given the game's price point is a fair length. The game itself does a great job of capturing the feeling and aesthetic of the films and overall the presentation is great.The game does suffer from a few issues. Firstly the game really could do with a pause ability as the amount of micro you need to be able to do is pretty wild on later missions. Especially when multiple places on the map demand your attention at the same time. I also found that the camera didn't zoom out as much as I'd like making it harder to get a wider view of the map. Lastly the game's tutorial is almost nonexistent so the player is pretty self taught. My pro-tip is to learn where the 'prioritise enemy type' button is and become close friends with it.All-in-all though I really liked this game. The campaign story was interesting and really fit the universe well and I enjoyed the between mission cut scenes.  The missions themselves were mostly fun and varied. Voice acting was pretty good and so was the writing. I'm definitely hoping we get a new campaign or two in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't deal with that dreadful high pitched alarm that is constantly going off and I have no idea why. There doesn't seem to be any way to turn it off. Maybe I could go in and hack the game to delete the sound file if I didn't have 1000 other games I could be playing instead. _childDocuments_.review: Buy if you are a TRUE Starship Troopers Fan and if you get in a sale for 25 bucks or less. Would like to see an expansion with more missions or an editor for designing my own missions.Graphics are OK, a bit outdated but still nice looking in High-Res.There are no cutscenes, but thats ok, the game catches the ambience of ST very good with the artstyle in the menus and in game, as also with the introduction speakers at the beginning of every mission. The musik and the soundeffects are ok, nothing special, but fitting for ST.Mission design is diversified: capturing and holding special points on a map. reconquer fallen bases and rebuild them to clear all bug-holes on the map, withstand a lot of waves of bugs in certain surroundings,sometimes you have limited troops and fight in caves or structures below the surface to clear special points.Felt a bit like the old C+C days where you clear facilities with limited troops.BUT there are also some difficulties with this game which i won't conceal: Managing the troops can be a pain in the a**, because there is no real formation system (the troops alling always by a straigt line at the mousecursor if you press, hold MB1 and draw in any direction - Ohterwise they are moving absolutely chaotic and give themselves no clear line to fire). The usage of the extra functions of the troopers (granades or any special attack which they gain by experience) are very difficult in a fight because of the chaos on the battlefield...There is no real base-building, just some conquering of certain buildings which open possibitities for new troop-types (with flamethrowers, rockets, snipers, better MGs and even three types of Mechs) and collect certain packages on the battlefield to gain more resources for more troops.Its limited, but also fitting for the ST-feeling.All in all a nice time filler for real Starship Troopes fans

_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid RTS/Tower-Defense, which works well for the Starship Troopers (movie ver) setting.   First few missions were easy, it wasn't until they started introducing other bug types that you had to be careful about the composition of your army.  The campaign is serviceable, though I would've wished for more biome diversity instead of the rocky desert.  Some missions can actually be very challenging which was fun.  Though a few were just straight up unbalanced and frustrating.  If you've checked the discussion, its mainly the scorpions being the issue.  Obvious counter to them would be rocket soldiers, but a person with not much RTS experience will find themselves having a frustrating time trying to deal with them.  Gameplay is very simple as RTS games goes.  You have a limited unit cap, so don't expect any death-balls.  Actually having your forces in a death-ball can actually get them wiped out.  As such, like I said, plan your unit composition carefully.  Mix em up and put them in good firing positions.  You're basically letting the enemy come to you.  A solid 7/10 for me.  I look forward for any future updates this game is gonna have.  This game has potential.  A good game for its price.  Rating might change depending on future updates.Things I hope the devs will add in the future:-rotatable camera.  -more unit types.-unit skins.  Would love to see the soldiers from Roughneck make an appearance.  Best thing to do for now is swap unit character models in the files.-future campaigns set on other planets. -unseen/original bug types.  Most of the bugs shown in this game are from the movies.  Would love to see the developers own original designs.

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a very competent squad-based RTS. If you like that sort of thing, and especially if you're a fan of the book or the film, then you'll get your money's worth. I'm just past the halfway mark and the plot so far is good, Excuse the inevitable pun, but I haven't found any bugs, and the missions are very well-designed - there's plenty of variety and they mostly don't to the whole 'build up a big army to take on the big bad at the end' schtick. However, for a modern RTS the range of units is relatively limited, with each having particular specialisms that you will have to use at various points, and they need constant micro-managing. There's no base-building beyond a limited amount of structures that unlock new units, there is (as yet) no skirmish mode, but then the only factions are yours and the bugs, and you don't get the cinematic cut sequences you'd expect from a bigger budget title. Nevertheless, it's great fun. Maybe not a game you'll play for hours at a time, but one you'll want to see through to the end, and the devs clearly have a lot of potential so it's worth investing some cash to support them. As a fan of these sort of games I'd say it's well worth buying - I doubt you'll be blown away but you certainly won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: There's five things plentiful on the battlefield:1. Bugs2. Bullets3. Jank4. The desire to Know More5. The desire to Know More about why I can't rotate my cameraTerran Command plays like a water-downed version of the original Warhammer 40k: Dawn of War in the most loving way possible, where the focus of the game is on utilising terrain and careful unit placement to defeat mass hordes of bugs.Despite some scattered pathfinding issues, this game is shockingly easy to pick-up-and-play.  Gameplay is unfortunately plagued with incomplete or nonexistent animations, frequent graphical glitches/bugs and overall lack of polish. The lack of polish can be forgiven, especially for an indie team, but Terran Command is also borderline unfinished with a complete lack of a skirmish mode, survival mode, or any other sort of classic RTS mode to add replayability and no multiplayer whatsoever.But despite its jank and so-far missing content, the game  like the movie when you play it and makes you feel like a MI commander. Even the  encourage you to be risky and bold... your troops are literally FREE! They just cost supplies that you  when they die! Sure you could use rockets like a nerd, or you can send wave after wave of your own Mobile Infantry at that hive until they run out of bugs!The bugs have the numbers, and so do YOU!

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers is a pretty unique RTS, made by a small studio so people should temper their expectations, the theme of the game with cutscenes mirror the first Starship Trooper film with the satire news broadcasts. The way the characters talk and act is typical of that universe and it feels genuine and funny at times. The game uses a "line of fire" mechanic, so most units will not shoot through each other so the player will have to be side by side or to be at an elevated position, even though this seems terrible at first, it makes sense and helps the game a lot and makes it feels satisfying in every small to big battle!Talking about the theme, one mission entails rescuing a prisoner whos crimes were for "unionising". The reason for rescuing this guy is so that the federation can broadcast his execution of Fed Net on all channels which made me laugh at how ridiculous it was (but in a good way). There was another mission that greatly disappointed me, I am not sure if more content was cut from the campaign but it was either that or an easter egg for the fans. In Starship Troopers 2, the bug the film focused on was the control bug. This bug was used by the bugs to be inside of a person and use them to try and infiltrate the Federation and destroy their leadership and learn secrets/war assets.  Now at the start of the mission the Psi Ops officer kills one of his marines and tells the player that he does not trust anyone and wants biological tests to prove they're fully human. So initially I thought the campaign would shift to destroying this plan by the bugs and having interesting missions were you may not be able to trust your marines or others in the federation. But no, sadly after the mission and cutscene nothing was said about it and it was swept under the rug. I am hoping if they do campaign DLC that they focus on this as even though the second film was awful, the premise of the bug is very interesting and different.The AI is mostly competent although occasionally it will bug out and your soldiers will stop shooting completely or the bugs may stand still, hopefully this is patched quickly as it can take you out of the game especially at harder difficulties. Speaking of difficulties, I played the campaign on 3 stars (normal) and it seemed balanced until a couple of missions near the end that were frustrating at times so on the hardest difficulty it may be a bit imbalanced unless you're an RTS veteran.The campaign overall is good length, around 20 missions overall. Some missions are short, some are long. The missions remind me a little bit of Starcraft II where the shorter missions give you specific units to work with throughout the mission without any new units (unless the mission gives them to you throughout) the campaign does a good job overall at introducing units as at the start very limited units are available to player. This is good and keeps the campaign fresh and interesting. After completing the campaign, I looked for more content and currently there isn't much. There are challenges to complete that are mission length scenarios but sadly there are only 2 at launch.Prepare for a lot of dog fighting, very satisfying when you prepare a kill zone to crush the bugs. Sometimes you will lose troops and that is OK. The death animations are great but sadly the player will not focus on them much due to the chaos on the screen.There are 12 different types of enemies encountered in the game, they all have a various series of ways of interacting with the player. Some are purely more bullet spongey than others, some like the famous tanker bugs have their own mechanics in the game where the player has to micromanage.Overall there are around 11 different types of units too (with some variations in the later missions) most units, like the bugs have their own mechanics. An example of this is the engineer. This unit creates their own turrets (3 variants) that use war support. Overall it keeps it fresh with the different amount of units available. Fans of the film, it is a MUST buy, it does the franchise justice and uses units from other films, games and role playing game lore. It does have its problems but overall with certain bug fixes and additions it will definitely be worth the £23.79 price tag. Again the game was made by a small team so people should not expect AAA cutscenes, gameplay etc. The devs have said they are adding game modes/challenges in the future. 7/10 overall and if you're a fan of the films then its a 9/10 due to the theme being great. [/b]

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, it is probably the best new RTS i've played in a few years, up there with Iron Harvest for quality and maybe better due to the low pricepoint. It's a single player only game, with a pretty long campaign that lasts for about 12 hours with some replayability if you enjoy horde defence modes. In addition to the campaign it also has two challenge missions, i only mention those as they aren't mentioned in most reviews and I assume most people missed them as they are in the scenario selector and there's not a lot of reason to go there. Both of them are good. As for the game, it's 100 percent starship troopers, it takes from the three live action movies and the two animated movies giving it a good variety of units. The missions are varied but mostly follow the David Gemmell plot model of defend area X or move to area X with little deviation. there is a limited amount of tactics but 90 percent is form a firing line and let the bugs come to you. It's very satisfying.  The bug hunt missions in the caves are probably my favourite as you have to be careful ow you move up your firing line and always cover each unit, its the most tactical the game gets. the game does desperately need some extra bits though, skirmish mode, map editor, and horde mode (which would just be skirmish mode again really) but for a 25 euro game its really hard to complain about such a high quality product. Strong recommend. Or in other words, SERVICE GUARANTEES CITIZENSHIP !!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a difficult one, If I'm honest I'm a little disappointed .in current form I wouldn't recommend. This game is crying out for a dynamic/reactive style conquest mode - they talked a lot about decisions having consequences in their interviews and there isn't any.Main positives-Core mechanics of the game are funbig fan starship troopers When using a small force to hold back hordes the game is at it's best. That grinding push and a special ability mirco at just the right time is satisfying.Good number of units and different rolesAreas for improvementThis game is crying out for a dynamic style conquest world, made of lots of individual maps where the battle is fought out front lines style. A war of attrition. Limited reinforcements, control of areas can be gained or lost depending on the whether you win or lose. make decisions matter. make victories or holding out matter. Give squads more value / unique features that can be earned over several map fights if kept alive. more features that spread across maps like commander xp that you can spend on a skill tree - give the player choices on what to units or abilities to buffallow for targeting preferences to be set on units to avoid the boring mirco where units are focusing down the wrong unitsoption for 3/4 or half speed to make up for the large amount of mirco neededlinear campaign - Too many escort style missions. It's as if they are trying to avoid the game being a horde style game rather than embracing it. Prime example is putting a stealth mission in the game. _childDocuments_.review: I've had lots of fun with this game. The atmosphere is spot on for Starship Troopers. The scenarios make sense and in a classic fashion the federation views your troops and expendable tools. The game can also put a serious amount of bugs on screen. When you are getting overrun you can see it. It can be a lot of fun to plan how you are going to hold the line then beat the bugs back in order to destroy their hives. I like all of the different types of units. What really adds to the longevity of the game is community content where you can play missions/scenarios other people have made. By biggest gripes with the game are:The most challenging bugs to face are the scorpion bugs but they're also extremely annoying to fight against. They are not fun to fight, they are just frustrating. They are the arachnid's equivalent to tanks, complete with a cannon. There are no physics in the games besides the hopper (flying) bugs. All the bugs and your troops collapse from a death animation which after a while gets stale. The unit dialogue gets a little repetitive too "Yes sir." "Move it!" "Get your gear and roll out!" for every little movement and you have to click a lot because moving your troops across large areas is treacherous. So you can't just click once and be done or they'll be slaughtered. The dialogue is fine the first 100 times you hear it but then you start to wish they spoke less often or only when the movement was substantial. In the end though these are relatively minor grievances to an otherwise fun game. If you are a fan of Starship Troopers you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: In short very fun game took me 12,3 hours to complete the campaign on 4 start/hard difficulty.Not played the 2 challenges yet.Will replay on brutal/5 star.I assume 10 hours on normal and 15-20 hours on brutal difficulty for the first time players.I give it 8.0 as it lacks many quality of life such as shift queing commands and some polish and content.With quality of life+some more content patched in it is a 9.0.Pros:Nice art style,fun to play nice story,good animations and upgrades,both bug and enemy models are well done.Very micro heavy,with light RPG and light base "building".Many soldiers skills,certain weapons are good or bad againts certain enemies.No macro cavern missions are very well done.Cons:1 tutorial mission,19 campaign mission and 2 challenges as of yet for 25 euro.No RNG maps or skirmish.Only presets for gfx options,no advanced graphical tweaking like AA,AF can be changed individually.Most other RTS games have more content.-Lack of quality of life most RTS game has.-Small for me but no STEAM achives or trading cards.-Scorpions are very overused elite bugs in missions they appear,and take good dmg ONLY from rockets.-Non armor piercing deals almost no dmg to armored targets like scorpions.Of course it makes sense but the dmg % is very low,lower than piercing to fortified in Warcraft 3.Rockets mans in masses are forced due to massed scorpions in many late game missions on higher difficulties.-Difficulty only affects dmg dealt,nothing else-slight skill or weapon balance issues.-The fort mission has insane jump in difficulty over the previous one.Overall if you are truly a fan Starship Troopers go buy it,otherwise I would wait for a few patches and buy it on a light sale.If content gets added,I will update this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Fun missions-Difficulty balance feels just right (I played at 4 stars)-A lot of heart-The pre-mission cut-scenes are in the style of the propaganda reels from the movie-Cool/nice looking pre-mission/main menu art-The micro heavy design/anti blobing mechanics match the setting-Game is reasonably good looking (especially given the smaller size of the developer)-I never felt like I wasn't having funCons:-Not a ton of replayability at the moment. The year one map editor freeLC and DLC should solve this, but at the moment it is just the 15-20 hr campaign and a few challenge missions.-Location variety was all right but not the best (I suppose there is only so much you can do with a desert planet).-If you are really into macro heavy RTS games this game doesn't really have that-Settings and menus are a little limited/rough around the edgesConclusion:A fun little RTS romp, with well designed/balanced missions, and a whole lot of heart. You can tell the devs really get Starship Troopers, as a lot of care was made into making this game look and feel the part. Additionally the promised free/paid content down the track also looks like it aught to be a good time. The $30 price is a little high for the amount of content in the base game as of Sep 2022; however this game still manages to deliver enough fun to justify its price.

_childDocuments_.review: Warm it all up! Everything you've got! Come on, you apes! You wanna live forever?The 1997 film was absolutely iconic but does the game live up to these cult expectations? The re ignition of this game no doubtfully created huge nostalgia for those of us who had the privilege to watch this in the late 90s.Now 25 years later, a creative and collective mindset has brought the big screen to RTS gaming, which I tip my hat off to. If someone asked me if a Starship Troopers game would ever be released now in this age I would have laughed.Albeit a game it is but simply a version specifically based on the Terrans as the title suggests. There is a number of single player missions some hard and some easy. I mean there is no real in depth RTS strategy like Starcraft or Age of Empires, absolutely no comparison. You do not do much building, nor gather resources but concentrate on specifically the mobile infantry, tactical resources that are given to you and management of your forces are vital against the arachnids.You have a different array of units but these develop further into your missions as time progresses. You definitely must be strategic in your movements, utilising unit special abilities to outsmart the bugs at times or face being defeated. Using ground advantage and offensive machinery is also beneficial in this game. Some units can build turrets etc. Exploration will greatly help you, as numbers are a big thing in this universe.The arachnids are as you expect them to be and of course the different types of bugs are present in the game.This game also couldn't be complete without its satirical fednet cutscenes. How else would I be able to keep up to date with the war in Klendathu without the militaristic propaganda machine! would you like to know more?However this game is not without its bugs (no pun intended), I did find myself very frustrated at times. For example the strength of the arachnid forces and your army when clearing bug holes (volitile and slow) and at times the infantry wouldnt fire on arachnids when commanded to. I did find some of the missions was the same and repetitive, specifically fighting on one planet instead of other scenarios and some of the storyline dialog was I guess 'acceptable' including the limited infantry punchlines. Dont expect Michael Iron side or Casper Van Dien to suddenly appear and start spitting fire.I did also feel the arachnids were predictable in their movements and that the AI wasn't fully utilised to act as the hive would. Negatives aside, I do think the game has much improvement to go and a big future to build upon. Coming from legendary games in this arena is a big ask and big shoes to fill. This game is definitely not on this level, but then again it has not been created as such. It is however still fun, it still brings alot of memories and is good for an introduction into the RTS genre.The devs are definitely improving and fixing and updating as they go. Keeping a close eye and even releasing a road map to show the future. I do believe this game will be much better and polished gem as time permits.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is "almost there"  The music is ALMOST good, the sound design is ALMOST enjoyable.  The AI pathing is ALMOST functional.  The map designs are ALMOST good.  The game play ALMOST feels good.  But unfortunately the game falls flat on just about everything.   The guns sound wimpy and the voice acting isn't very good.  The maps are kind of boring and your units constantly get stuck on corners.  There are no original designs in the game, with literally everything coming from the 3 original movies, traitors of mars, and the old strangelite FPS game.  But apparently none of that came with a license for the music, leaving the soundtrack feeling hollow.The resources aren't.  Yes, you can choose what units to deploy, but instead of spending resources, you just have a unit cap, which can be increased a few times every mission.  And should your unit die?  No worries, you can just build a new one instantly (And I do mean instantly).  The bugs feel sluggish which really takes away the tension as you can just run away as long as they aren't too close.  And IF the unit dies, the ONLY thing you lose is the unit's veteran status, so there isn't much of a downside at all.  But the REALLY disappointing part is that the game ONLY has a single player campaign, and ONE single player scenario.  There's no Co-op.  There's no multiplayer at all.  There isn't even a skirmish mode.  You get 20 missions (19 campaign and 1 scenario mission) and THAT'S IT.  There's almost no replayability to this game unless you want to grind the same scripted mission over and over again.Overall, I'd give it a 2 out of 5.  There's the potential for a good game here, but it'll probably take some serious DLC and modding to get to it.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm going to be brutally honest here and say this game has its faults. Yes, the game is actually really good; if you're into the Starship Trooper series, however, if you're not, you're likely going to avoid this one until more is added. Anyways, the game's campaign took me 9 hours to beat but that was on easy (Cause Scorpions are lethal), so give or take another one maybe three hours on the higher difficulties if you're doing the side objectives. Scenario wise, there ain't much... just replaying many of the same missions you beat in the campaign save for two "Challenge" operations at the bottom. Still, would I recommend this game? Yes. Despite it's flaws, it's still an overall, fun game. Is it worth the price? Well... debatable. Graphics? Not bad, but bodies don't stay and disappear into the ground which kinda sucks. Gameplay wise, pretty fun as it has you think a little more tactically and utilize each unit effectively in order to come out on top. Now, a few issues I do have is how unbalanced the game does feel at times on the higher difficulties - I know, that sounds weird to hear from someone who beat the game first on easy, but some enemy units are just literal tanks when they shouldn't be and one hit units that are supposed to be YOUR tanks, so it makes all units feel as squish as your starter units despite being "elite" which sucks. Another issue is the lack of any ST violence... I mean, there are some cool death animations, but nothing like a guy being cut in two or limbs being cut off... just dudes falling and or dragging themselves away until they die. Blood is fine and stuff, but yeah, overall, wish the bodies would stay as well so you could have a bit more immersion on that front.Also! Should note, that one thing that bothered me is how the player is the MC, but we don't actually get acknowledged at all for our efforts in the game, and despite all the victories we win for the Federation, we're not promoted, honoured, or given anything beyond the rank of Lieutenant... which you start as and stay as. You also get to name your Division, your squads, etc, but none of it matters as your Division's name is never uttered or shown in the gameplay, and your named squads don't carry over to aid in future operations. So, the naming feature, while cool, is pointless, and you don't feel like you're the main commander but just some individual doing all the hard stuff while the CO gets the praise and story focus XD. But yeah, all that said, still recommend this game to any who love ST's and enjoy killing seemingly endless hordes of bugs!

_childDocuments_.review: So, have you ever watched a series or played a game where you said, "Oh, I'd love to fight in this space-war!"? If so, this is the game for you if you're a fan of RTS.  I would say you don't even have to be a fan of Starship Troopers to appreciate the game.  The levels are varied in the units given to you over time, the challenges you face, and the maps you fight on.  At first glance, it may not seem like a lot of variation in any of those, but honestly the game itself does very well to differentiate each mission.  Overall, it's a solid, well-built game that I would recommend! This game is a bit of an old-fashioned RTS.  The gameplay itself is a bit slower than you might see in Starcraft 2, or other contemporary RTS games.  It relies a lot on thinking through a situation, bringing the right tools to the right fight, and watching how it plays out rather than a storm of micro to gain victory.  Throughout the campaign, you command troops and complete objectives, and with the comic-book style cutscenes and dialogue, it feels like you're playing through a real war campaign which is rather refreshing even if the only memorable moments will be particularly well-executed gun lines.  Now, for criticism the difficulty curve is a bit.. off? The first 7ish missions, a good 1/3rd of the content available, is a complete walkthrough.  Then, the harder bug types and more interesting missions kick in and the game feels adequately challenging (for reference, I beat the campaign at about 15 hours on second-highest difficulty).  Additionally, I think an opportunity to fight on a planet other than a rocky desert was a clear missed chance to see some other fronts of the war.  Finally, once completed, the campaign and a couple of scenarios is all there really is.  I don't consider this to be a bad thing, as I think too many games try to keep you playing it indefinitely, but I know many will want more. Now, onto what I'd like to see in a sequel or DLC.  Firstly, I wish they had kept the idea of a dynamic campaign where you choose from following commands orders or trying to save civilians and comrades.  I think some choices which could lead to certain units or persistent upgrades, could add an extra layer! I think such an idea should be done if they do decide to pursue a sequel.  Second, I think the game is just shy of my favorite game of the year due to a lack of replayability.  While I did have fun in the campaign, and I'm walking away thoroughly entertained, I wish there was an endless survival mode or a way to create your own scenarios/missions to share with others.  Lastly, I think there's a lot of opportunity to build upon what is here.  I'd love to see future campaigns set in other environments, such as jungles or arctic regions.  I'd love to see some more ability to upgrade your army, and I think a Starcraft 2 style meta-progression would have been really cool to see.  Overall though, awesome game and a great purchase in my book!
