_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write steam reviews, however having played over 14 hours of the game, I feel like I want to take the opportunity to - partly to document my experience in the hopes that the developers will try to fix some aspects of the game, which would make it genuinely very fun and enjoyable, as well as partly to help inform anyone still sitting on the fence for the game.The Starship Troopers setting is actually done pretty well overall - everything feels quite organic, whether it's the different types of troopers you can command, the buildings and maps, the campaign's narrative and characters - not to mention the bugs themselves! This is nice, because sometimes when working on a game adaptation, studios will try to fit the setting around the game, introducing a load of "stuff" that ends up feeling out of place, but you never really get that here. The first thing to say about the core game mechanics here is that they're not sophisticated - in fact, they feel extremely casual. That in itself is no bad thing; not everyone is looking for a "Wargame" strategy experience - and even if they are, they're likely to also be open to a more casual experience, which doesn't require large amounts of micro-management and won't heavily punish you for small mistakes.The problem is that, inexplicably, Terran Command does do those things.  The separated "fire and manoeuvre" mechanic that the game puts forward is by all means an interesting and meaningful concept - the issue is that the actual implementation of it really is not, or not consistently enough. To name just a few problems with it: ...a rule which they will obey, ironically, with the same kind of lack of autonomy that you might expect from a bug possessed by a hive mind. Want to send your troops anywhere except the immediate vicinity? Better check which route(s) they take then - because they might not be the same as others! This happened to me in a mission where I selected a collection of 6 different units at the same time, who were all approximately in the same place - only to find that two of them had gone the *wrong* way around a set of impassable terrain, taking them straight through a bug hive, because the game calculated that was the fastest route for them. Hilariously, when doing so, those units will actually just mindlessly run past or even into the bugs, not stopping to engage them at distance (remember, they're not allowed to run and shoot). You might argue that is what the "attack" move is for - except you don't expect to have to use attack move when you order your troops to go back to their base. Small oversight's like this one - calculating the routes for the grouped units individually, rather than collectively - combined with the rigid "fire and manoevure" mechanic lead to endless problems and massive frustration, which ultimately just takes any semblance of fun out of the game.First of all, you have no choice on how units will position themselves with respect to one another - this is decided by the game, based on the units composition that is selected. Normally, it will do this by positioning the troops that are capable of indirect fire behind the ones that are not - i.e grenade launchers located behind the guys with regular rifles, parallel to the line of fire. Ok, pretty sensible. How about perpendicular to the line of fire? Good luck trying to work it out, as I have no clue how the game handles this. Many times, I've had units that were on the right flank, run over to the left and vice versa, when changing the angle of the firing line, resulting in the centre getting blocked and no-one firing - goodbye units. Oh and about controlling the forward facing direction of your units - the game automatically adjusts this depending on where your mouse is relative to where the troops are now. Want to move a firing line backwards? Congratulations, your troops now have their backs to the enemy, by default, unless you can yank your mouse around to get them to face the right direction! The real cherry on the top is the way the campaign constantly features set pieces where your units will turn a corner in a canyon, or crest the top of the hill, only to have a previously unseen (due to LoS) group of bugs attack them from the side, leaving you unable to either back up effectively or reorient the line - and when I say constantly, I really do mean constantly. The campaign is 20 scenarios, which probably equates to roughly 20 hours - that's not an hour per mission mind you - many of them can be completed in half an hour, or less in fact - however, others can take between an hour to even two hours, simply because you have to go through, triggering all the ambush attacks where your units get slaughtered, only to reload the last checkpoint and cheese it on the next go, because you know it's coming. So the "strategy" is basically cheat to defeat. Honestly, the worst part about this is that it would be so easy to fix - the Total War games have spent literally decades refining exactly this kind of system, to the point that the perfect answer is already there - but we get this terrible system instead.Units will only ever engage an enemy if it is within their line of sight, in range and not obstructed by an obstacle. Therefore, if they're attacked by anything with a ranger greater than their own, they will literally just stand there and take the punishment, until they're wiped out. If a unit next them is attacked by an enemy unit out of range, they will also just stand there, doing nothing. If you order a group of units, some of whom have direct view of an enemy, others whose view is obstructed, the latter will just stand there doing nothing, making no attempt to move to a position where they are able to fire.Units have no ability whatsoever to determine any kind of priority when it comes to choosing which enemy units to attack. Therefore, a Mech will quite happily blast away at Warrior/Tiger bug units which are doing little to no damage to it, completely ignoring the Scorpion bug unit that is able to kill it in 3-4 shots. Rocket troops, that are able to counter the Scorpion bug, will quite happily blast away at the Warrior/Tiger bugs that are too fast for them to hit, whilst the Mech next to them turns into a ball of slag. Basically, any engagement that involves Scorpion bugs means micromanaging your rocket troopers - and if there's more than 4 Scorpion bugs at a time - which happens on a number of occassions - good luck, because you're going to f****** need it.To be honest, I think I'll stop there, because I honestly don't have the patience to write out all the other problems with the gameplay mechanics. Hopefully, some of the other reviews will capture these.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom Line Up Front (Overall 8 /10)- A simple, yet fun game worthy of investment. Probably the best game representation of the Starship Troopers universe yet- Plays more of a Real Time Tactics than a Real Time Strategy game- Excellent artistic style and game environment really shines- Easy at first then the missions get challenging past Mission 5- Very basic base building mechanics- Lacking features of most modern RTT / RTS games such as a 360 degree camera, skirmish mode and multiplayerDevelopers, if this game had multiplayer, skirmish, 360 degree camera and the ability to play bugs this game would be a masterpiece. Gameplay Loop (6/10)- Only giving this score based on the fact that there are 2 DLCs at the moment and there is a lack of skirmish and multiplayer- Few mission varieties but it suits the game universe- Campaign is nice and lengthy especially with the DLCs- Achievements are not difficult to obtain but definitely a good challenge in some missions. Might need a few replays to succeedGameplay Mechanics (7/10)- Very few controls to learn the game- Some units will not conduct their special ability on first click (most prominent one is engineers using the demo ability)- Needs some unit micromanagement (sight lines and unit special abilities) to be efficient in a mission but it is not tediousPresentation (8/10)- Excellent artistic style and eye candy- Some of the unit explanations can benefit with a rotatable unit model when you view their stats- Captures the vibe of the Federation very well- Little to no glitches, gameplay or graphical bugsSound (6/10)- Some gunfire sounds could be a bit more punchy- Some arachnid sounds could also use a bit more volume to convey presence - Voice acting is bearable and relevantHow this can be a 10/10 game / Developer wishlist- Introduce the arachnids as a playable faction- Introduce Multiplayer- Introduce Skirmish- Introduce a 360 degree cameraSpecsIntel I5 13500KRTX4070Ti80 GB DDR4 RAMSSDSamsung 4K TV 60 FPSGame is on the highest graphical settings with VSYNC ON - consistent 60 FPS no issues

_childDocuments_.review: As I start the game, I am washed over with anticipation, I have been ready to join the mobile infantry since I saw the movie as a child, to see the galaxy, do my duty, and kill as many bugs as possible.  	The opening of the game starts off with promise, telling me I have Fednet news so that I can learn more, I eagerly click to start the game as I wish I could watch Fednet clips showing me the story of the game and giving context to where I will be, the galaxy is a huge place and there are millions of troopers, we can't all fight in Rico"s Roughnecks. 	I start my 1st mission, Big K - The worst and most disastrous mission the Skymarshal has ever led. I remember the movies, the hundreds of soldiers, and drop-ships that are lost as they descend to the planet's surface. In the game, however, I am met with a soulless and monotone voice that repeats the reporters' words from the movies. "It's an ugly planet, a bug planet." The voice sounds like a radio personality, reading a radio ad to the midnight shoppers at a grocery store. 	My 1st command comes available to me, an infantry rifle squad, nine troopers who easily dispatch the few warriors who approach my landing site. The combat starts off easy, the troopers automatically shoot and destroy the warriors easily, not much strategic or tactical planning is necessary so far. My ally troopers do the same, static positions set around the drop site, not moving a muscle even as a blue bug bomb explodes on a trooper unit, some die, but not many. I don't know if I am on Big K, or if we went to a local park. The announcer's voice speaks to me as if he has no idea what emotion is as if we are not supposed to be watching thousands of our fellow troopers die in front of us. He leads me to my next objective, helping guide me through the mediocre tutorial, as the bugs try to "force" their way into my troops at a brisk speed walking pace. I don't know if they are rushing to defend their home, or trying to hurry to catch the ice cream man before he drives off. The mission ends. I am greeted by a sliding screen of pictures as I hesitantly prepare for a new campaign. The music fills my room, it sounds like the generic music from most 1950s old military movies, once in a while I can hear music from the movie that I remember, but the other times I feel like getting some green army men and setting them up to create a diorama of an action scene, so far I think that would have more action than what I have felt so far. When I click on New Campaign, I am greeted with Kwalanshiand and my difficulty that I set to Brutal, I need much more excitement and toughness that What the prologue gave me. I choose my division: the 3rd Marine Division, the same one that I served in. The same narrator's voice greets me, this person I will now call Scab. I get a cut-scene about big K and why we need to be on the planet that we are heading to. Another voice comes up, nothing memorable, and the same soulless direction is given. The mission starts, a small OP greets me, buildings that look like they come out of a toy box wrap around a road that leads through the end of the southwest map, and continue north through a small town and to the same what looks like the same type of metal fort that Rasczak dies in. Some Allied NPCs marines surround my two squads of riflemen, the objective is to join up with the advanced team. 	What advanced team?	Where are we on the planet?	Why are the roads blocked off?	Why is there an OP out here? 	Why are we out here?	Who is my commander? My Rico in charge of these troopers? We move Northwest, killing some Chariot bugs, I click on the glowing Icon and I am taken to the worst info screen I have ever seen. Most Star craft fan made maps have better graphics and information, and why does the music sound like it is being played through the free airplane headphones? Who is this guy who keeps speaking? The next battle is numbing, my troopers saw tougher battles trying to get through the chow hall. The mission progresses to the point of a narrator asking what type of half-assed operation is this? I ask the same one. We arrive at a settlement that is roughly 30 yards north of where I started, within eyes view of the troopers who were still standing there. The no named voice who I will call Plastic gets "mad", saying either the civilians refused to leave or they weren't cleared out, maybe we should ask the guys who are standing right around the corner. Continuing east, twelve feet we find a company needing help, we "rush" over by right-clicking once and completing the battle. These bugs are not a match for me, as I write this and play at the same time. I gain control over a few extra teams, the new unit of Engineers can throw an Incendiary Grenade, a Demolition charge, and carry a Blazing Spear (Flame Thrower), but I still don't see my MEDIC!  (Zim Voice). I have to capture a Radio Station so I can talk to the fleet, and I can reinforce my casualties ( I have none from my own brilliant strategic mind). As I capture the radio tower, OH NO A MAJOR BUG OFFENSIVE INBOUND! I "quickly" arrange my guys west of the Radio tower by some buildings, a concrete barrier, and a burning car and within seconds, the great battle is over - No trooper dies. Go North the voice tells me, but I am an explorer and the vast, mostly unpassable map gives me the ability to recon one area before I continue with my main Mission, I find nothing. I get to the base, secure it, have a few seconds of combat, and, it's over.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If the description on the store page is something that you think you would enjoy, you will enjoy this.You pretty much know what you are getting with this.  What you expect is more or less what is delivered.  It is nothing ground breaking, but solid.  It would have been amazing back in the late 90's.  That is not a knock on the game because it is striving for that genre.  It is just to give you an idea.  I'll address a few negative comments that didn't make much sense or apply in my opinion:1)  The storyline makes sense - I think the only way the story would be hard to follow is if you were not following it.  It is not an epic story, but the narrative fits into the theme from the movies quite well.2)  The game is based off the movies and not the books - It does not claim to base off books.  It is clearly from the movies.  So to get the game knowing it is not based off the books just to write a negative review that it is not based off the books is non-sense.  If they did a poor job basing it off the movies, that would make sense.  But they did not do a poor job.  3)  Yes there are mechs - I think this is another book and movie debate.  I never saw mechs in any movies, but know they are in books.  Either way you do get mech action in the game.  They are valuable and used sparingly.4)  Variety - The mobile infantry kills bugs.  That is the theme.  For a limited scope, I would say the missions could have a bit more variety but doesn't do a bad job at this.5)  Choke point conflicts are small portion of game - chokepoint combat can get boring and repetetive, if that is the only form of combat.  Lucky for us, it is not the only form of combat in this game.6)  Not the typical amount of bugs (programming variety) you would expect with today's games on release date, but there are some.7)  I have not seen any commitment to post launch content.  Could be wrong on this, but I know some people would like more than the narrative campaign.  Once again, the game does not mislead you that it is more than the campaign.  I do wish they would come out and clearly state what the plans are (if any besides patching).8)  The right amount of hand holding - in the beginning missions there is hand holding, but not much after that.  Most people playing this game are going to be very familiar with RTS style and strategy, but I agree with the decision that the initial missions should accomodate new players as well.9)  It is probably priced right - Once again, if i knew more about post launch plans I could answer more clearly.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m old enough to remember when the original Starship Troopers movie came out and it was cringe, with at times bad acting, but at the same time strange in a sense that it was borderline between satire and glorification of national-socialism. I personally took that a satire with grotesque and exaggerated fight against space travelling bugs (I mean, hard to take such a plot seriously really), but you are not here to read about the movie aren’t you?The game, well, just like the movie, I liked it, it is true to that satire and exaggeration of all nazi stereotypes (for younger readers nazi is short for national-socialism) of ‘do or die’ and never think about the orders for mobile infantry is not there to think it is there to kill bugs. Of most importance though, behind all these there is a solid old school RTS with a classic rock/paper/scissors formula mixed in with a good roster of units with an insecticide tendencies. The game itself is not hard, however if you fail to properly compose your troops you will be mercilessly annihilated by the arachnids. And I have to say, slaying bugs and setting up defences and counter-offensives was fun, it was the type of the game I wanted where I am engaged, but not overly concentrated add some cool unit specs (you can choose between two different skills upon unit promotion) and there you go, the formula for creation dopamine is achieved. score 7/10 – good adaptation of a movie into an RTS with a military command codex that would make Stalin and Hitler proudFor more grumpy reviews follow me as a curator at

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. I don't often write reviews but this one deserves one. You can tell a lot of love went into this game. It has a few bugs (haha get it??) and issues here and there, however nothing a few future patches won't sort out!- Immersive campaign, nice variety of mission types, great characters and story- The bugs are so fun to fight, one second you have it all under control, the next they have broken through and you are panicking! You sometimes face a very difficult bug issue, and have to really think hard and work out the right strategy/ unit comp to defeat them.- There are tonnes of different units and situations, allowing for a lot of variety in the human and the bug gameplayMain campaign can take a good 15-20 hours and that's before visiting the bonus content and scenarios! All in all it's a lot of FUN which is what games are about at the end of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: Never turn down something goodbecause...IT'S AMAZING!!!! I'm the happiest I've ever been doing my part! Would you like to know more?Ok Amazing is too big a word but it's legit and pretty good, though if you're looking for Starcraft and CoH2 levels of strats and variety then this ain't it chief. With that said the lack of variety is held up by the maps and abilities each unit has as well as the scenarios you are given.To give you an idea of how various the units are you haveRiflemen with 12 dudes and 10 health eachRiflemen with 6 dudes but grenade launcher and 10 health eachRiflemen with 14 dudes but energy and 30m instead of 60m and 10 health eachRiflemen with 2 dudes EXCEPT they have radios/the same rifle but with an ACOG/Rocket Launchers that act as mortars/Flamethrowers and 10 health eachLook you get it Everyone is doing their part and you will more or less end up having freak accidents involving a grenade or rocket because you skipped knife trainingBug wise it's a bit more varied minus the Warrior sub-types like the Tiger and Drone, they get actual 'Vehicles' like the Tanker and Plasma bug and his bigger Plasma brother who'll wipe out you whole army cause you decided to bind everyone to the same button, then you have special cases such as the Chariot who is useless, Spitters and Hoppers who deserve to die like the filthy Xenos scum they are and the list goes on with the last 2 LEGIT existing to counter all your important guys who aren't withing range of the 12 dude firing squad.Map wise they actually play a lot with verticality, LOS and more importantly not flagging the other squad. What do I mean not flagging other squads? Squads can't shoot through each other UNLESS they are one of the select few who can, they're on another level or they have an arcing projectile such as grenades or rockets and I didn't tell you but most of you units are infantry and I kid you not about the health thing you could throw a pebble at them and one unit could die from it.  *ahem* MEEEDDICC!!Speaking of units from the universe's best Mobile Infantry force they all have an ability in addition to a 2nd ability they work up to from a choice of 2 usually consisting of straight damage with little to no utility or an ability with a LOT of utility and possibly no damage giving every unit a subclass instead of guy with gun. For instance the Rifle squad has a rifle and grenade but then can have a 10 second shotgun mode that tears through bugs or a 6 second demolition charge that does A Lotta damage however the trade off for abilities is that using one causes both abilities to recharge.Campaign wise it feels like a Starship Trooper movie and is even told in a similar manner some of the lines don't even feel like they were done seriously. Map wise it follows the attack these locations with some bases between but also defend your bases from another wave of bugs, depending on the map it can be one giant wave with specials or local bug hives are beginning their attack meaning if you haven't destroyed the hives yet you don't need to worry about defence OR it'll be a story map where the game tests you on small unit tactics instead of the bigger base defence missions.All in all 9/10I'm doing my part!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Now finished the first out of three campaign after 20 hours of game play. This RTS game is a masterpiece.  There's a story, there's bizarre humor alá: the movie. There is even political commentary baked into the story and the game play. My favorite part is the side mission of wasting your troops to link up with a camera crew, in order to unlock a powerful but almost garbage unit painted in parade colours, only to bring with you to the main objective. The Federation wants it to have screen time on Federation broadcast. And the federation will get it, at any cost necessary.-------------------------------------------------Great hidden RTS gem. True to the movie lore. Accurate unit designs. High difficulty level and interesting mechanics. Base building mechanic is module building a call-in point. Gameplay is a combination of Command & Conquer / Starcraft and Ground Control.Fun missions with a lot of variety in objectives and functions. One mission has you clearing out a mine with limited ammount of units. Another has you repairing a factory while clearing out bugs. The other has you strategically falling back from hordes of Arachnids to a huge base and defending it until you are evacuated. There's a story, there are cutscenes, there is dialogue and the game is actually difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this. This is pretty low budget and production values aren't very high, it's well worth the asking price. This is a fun strategy game that "gets" the movie and plays like you would expect after watching it. In summary, a lot of mobile infantry troopers are gonna die and the federation won't give one damn about it.The gameplay is pretty good: you get a nice variety of troopers and many ways to kill the hordes of bugs that are out to get you. Squads level up and give you a choice of skills you can activate to stem the tide, but it's not so micromanagey that you get overwhelmed. You can't just make one blob of troopers and attack move, this game will want you to think about positioning, range and unit abilities. Pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the campaign fully on highest difficulty, it's not easy. The no build tunnel missions are especially hard on this setting. The challenge and gameplay is there and it's quite fun. Gameplay, I'd give it a B+. There are times where I'm fighting against trying to target arachnids that I should be able to target, but because they are in some attack animation, or because targeting is maybe animation dependent, I miss. The units walk too slow at times to have fun with positional movement - which is what this game is trying to convince us it is about. The power troopers at near the end of the game, walk just the right speed to change positions often and effectively. Doing a 7 squad, 4-5 hive takeover is fun as you're pulling units back and forth. Medics would make it even more fun I think, as right now if you're out of health, the best you can do is run back all the way to base and reload. Or maybe I should have gotten the fleet liason to do that, I did not try that. The liason can set drop points near your troops to reinforce I think.Campaign mission design is good. Good variety, good phases, all mostly pretty fun. Mission design I'd give an A. The story really took away from it though.I wish they made the story a bit more than what it was. I would give the story a C+. There's no clear goal and not enough character build up. Things just happen. It borrows emotional beats from the movie too much, though the last mission's emotional resonance was good-but because the movie's was good too.

_childDocuments_.review: Terran Command is a mix between Company of Heroes (Less base building, but you still need to hold battle objectives) and Infested planet ( Indie inverted tower defense type of game, where a map gets harder the more spawners you take down).The narrating style is what you would expect from Federal Network, which makes the game fit that universe perfectly.I haven't unlock the big guns yet, but I'm having a really good time playing it. The downtime between missions is really small. You can end and start a new map in campaign in less than a minute.All the keys are customizable. I'm setting up wasd for camera movement, but that screws the grid hotkeys (as in Starcraft2, and any other modern RTS after that) for abilities. We'll see how I manage to end with a suitable key deployment.

_childDocuments_.review: At 21 hours I just finished the campaign and I really enjoyed it! I think the demo gave an accurate example of the game you'll be playing and it is what got me excited about the game. It looks like there are 3 more "scenarios" that I can play that I'm looking forward too.I enjoy RTS games, I really like StarCraft I and II, but I'm not good enough to play them in multiplayer, so I only care about the single player experience.The novel mechanic of having a line of sight in order for your units to be able to shoot their targets is nice and forces you to care more about the position of your troops where I would otherwise default to my usual strategy of building a giant army and steamrolling them in a direction and not care who is where.The small downsides are: - sometimes your units can get stuck when trying to walk around something- Could be a me thing, but when sometimes I'll try to click on a unit ability and it won't trigger so I have to click it again, which is annoying mid fight- In order to heal your units you have to first use the ability that allows you to select a location of where to heal, and then pan the map to one of those locations and choose it. I wish there was something like in Iron Harvest where you can just push a "retreat" button and they will auto choose the closest one so I don't have to move my focus away from the fight.Other than that I just flat out enjoyed my time playing the game, and these issues might be resolved in future updates. I'm looking forward to any major releases or changes they have in store (if any).

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved my time with this game! It's a fantastic RTS with some simple but effective mechanics and a lot of polish - the primary dynamics are line of sight and rock-paper-scissors unit counters. There is no building/resource management, but there is something intangible about this game that just makes it a lot of fun to play and a strong recommendation. It honours the source material aesthetically and tonally with perfection also, you can tell there was care put into this product. Review over - I've done my part!

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers : Terran Command is a restrictively fun game. Lot of the campaign is a mix of what you would have played in other RTS games like Escort Missions, Survive missions et cetra. not much new there. I loved the movie, the first one, not the garbage that came after it. Expected some of the heroes of the movie to make some sort of cameo, maybe it was out of their budget. The game feels great in terms of their use of content(like bug variation and troop variations) and the scale of the fight, like getting swarmed by bugs when your troops are in bunker is satisfyingly fun when you win it.Unfortunately so far (I am in mission 6, 9.3 hours in) the game restricts you in building a massive force against the bugs, I think this is done for the sake of optimization. Some of the mechanics in the game is its downfall, crossfire is one of these. The game forces you to micromanage crossfire between troops to prevent friendly fire(which is a bloody headache especially when moving the troops across the battlefield) that can be solved with troop formation (like found in AoE) and a bit better AI.Troop AI gets the job done but rather clumsily. Troops will get burnt, spit and will right up walk through enemy bugs, if not ordered otherwise. You will need to handhold them as so far i have not seen a waypoint system. Map palette is the same through out the campaign dirt, desert or cavern system.The game has 19 missions including the tutorial, I am currently in my 6th mission as of writing this review.I believe a lot of the game's issue can be easily fixed and hoping it does. I hope the devs give a horde mode for this game as its perfect for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the movies of the same name, this game will be good fun for anyone who loves the setting.The game is a real time strategy game which focuses more on the tactical use of your resources rather than base building. _childDocuments_.review: Solid 7/10.Great graphics, max bugs (and minimal programming bugs). Satisfying in places where you're just mowing down everything around you.  Captures the spirit and feel of the propaganda machine of the FedNet.Spoilers follow:Cons: Too many stages where you have a set handful of units and have to micro your way around indoors.  Nonexistent story and character development.  Bare minimum of references to canon.  Simplistic gameplay, when you get stuck it's usually because you're expected to use unit abilities in a strict order.  No shower scenes, singing Sky Martials or new canon.To get 10: I'd love to see some kind of story-driven between-campaign stuff. If only they had the budget or rights to use live-action footage like the old AAA titles of the past, or slice up and include scenes from even the terrible ST2/3.  Even a Visual Novel style approach to introduce characters and interactions between/during gameplay would be welcome.  Get some characters to care about in there even if it's a carbon copy of the original (3 school friends drafted, follow their campaigns etc).  As it is, I couldn't remember the name of any of the thumbnails that have been barking orders at me for 15 hours so far. Gameplay: Get some named elite units in there at least, I'm  not asking for Johnny Rico, or a chance at having Carmen pilot a random drop ship, but  but killing off a developed character would be totally a ST thing to do, and caring about a few grunts amongst thousands of cannon fodder would be nice.  Oh and more content, map editor etc...Solid game, a must for fans and the best ST game yet.  Potential for sheer greatness with more content and polish.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm doing my part! By leaving a proper review!TL;DR: Game good. Devs currently active and planning more content. PVE only, stop asking for MP. Buy and support. Would you like to know more? Then keep reading.As of this writing - you get a full campaign of over a dozen missions which includes units from all 3 movies and the two Japanese CGI movies. The OVA and Roughneck Chronicles are NOT included. There are currently two Extra Scenarios which allow access to the full roster. Be aware - this is NOT Early Access. This is the core game, around which more content will be added. I participated in the demo and Beta. This is a small studio and they have released a good product within their timeframe and means. Devs have stated they intend to include more content in future. Gameplay - Are there Bugs? Of course, there are Bugs. This is Starship Troopers! Know your enemy! Jokes aside, the game runs well. Terran units work well and generally aren't idiots if enemies are nearby. That being said - hotkeys will save your life. If you're the RTS gamer who doesn't hotkey, some of the missions will be nigh impossible for you. I get definite Starcraft and Command & Conquer vibes in terms of the combat mechanics. Not much in terms of base building, which keeps the focus on combat.Maps are large enough that you may have to fight on multiple fronts rather than just blob and push forwards. Also, units have a line of sight mechanic. So, Squad 2 will not be able to shoot through Squad 1 if they are lined up behind each other and bugs are to the front. This is a good challenge since it requires thought in unit movement and placement. Leave a squad isolated, they will be swarmed and killedThere are multiple enemy types and there is some rock-paper-scissors mechanics. But all units can kill all enemies - some just take longer. Rifle Squads are take a long time to hurt Plasma Bugs, for example. Or Snipers can outrange Spitters.The gameplay bugs are trivial and barely noticeable. Post-release, I've only seen one instance of Arachnid pathfinding getting confused and one instance of clipping. The lost Arachnid did eventually get out of the confused path and start heading towards one of my bases. The clipping issue was solved by killing the offending Arachnid. So, again, Music & Voice Acting: Passable. Could be better but that's trivial compared to the gameplay being nearly flawless. They know how to put corny lines in. My current favorite is "If we ain't dying, we ain't trying!" No, there aren't any cast members from the original 1997 movie reprising their roles. No, there aren't any hero units currently. Maybe in the future. General Rico is only mentioned in passing.Visuals: Good for what it is. Arachnids are Arachnids, troopers die in gruesome ways. It is easy to tell apart all of the Terran units and generally easy enough for the Arachnids. I sometimes confuse Tigers with regular Warriors, but that's only when the two are mixed in large swarms.If new content comes, I will add more to this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game.Its stupid how much I enjoy playing this game. I like the movie, I prefer the book, but this game is just unbelievably fun. The developers did an excellent job, for the most part. Pro's: - Stupid fun to play- Great variety of unit types and abilities for each - Missions are varied enough to keep you engaged - The promotion/reinforcement system actually makes the player   care about their basic infantry units...they're not just cannon fodder- Actual strategy required as enemy abilities scale with the player- Impossible to "kite" the AI, for the most part. Con's: - There is only one campaign...this game could have several without feeling repetitive, ala Age of Empires. - No online/multiplayer options - Some minor AI pathfinding issues/ glitches- No cutscenes and very little narration...not much of a storyDEVELOPER Recommendations:- Expansion campaigns should include planet hopping/multiple locales - Be able to place units in two control groups simultaneously- Do more with bases...one suggestion would be an armory where you can include   an equipment level up system...so the units level up and gain abilities, but also be able to spend supply/war   support on upgraded equipment. Barrel Rifling = +3 tiles range, Lighter Armor Aloy +2 speed, Heavy Armor   Aloy + 2 armor (or more HP) etc. - Removable Structures from Deployment Pads...so only holding one position can swap unit types, but never   have all units available at once unless you have all radio towers secured - Also, the tanker bug needs to be buffed with more armor/damage and the scorpion bug needs to be nerfed, turrets should get at least two hits from one, otherwise engineers become totally irrelevant in late game. - Add a Horde Defense Mode, just a fully walled base with increasing supply/war support after every couple waves as they become harder waves. - AI needs to better prioritize enemy targets, snipers should automatically target spitters, not drones while spitters are doing damage to the place. - Add an Internal Hive mission/mode...no reinforcements, just 2 squads of power troopers. two squads of riflemen and two teams of engineers (power troopers that can be repaired with engineers) with 2 war support  and only regular machine gun turrets available (all the units that can enter a hive currently...the challenge is to get to the center of the hive for a brainbug...if you run out of troops before that, you fail)

_childDocuments_.review: It's great. Has simplistic gameplay reminiscent of 90's RTS without the base building, feels a bit more like a tower defense game mixed with World in Conflict. Graphics looks good and performance is smooth without any hiccups so far. Also works great on a Steam Deck, but your mileage may vary in terms of controlling a mouse cursor with one of those touch pads. Got it on sale for $24 but I'd say it's worth full asking price, although I don't know how long the campaign is yet.Edit - I just finished the campaign, there were (I believe) 19 missions in total and it took me around 17-18 hours on normal difficulty (there are 2 easier mode and 2 harder modes also) and there is a map editor for creating your own missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed the campaign. I feel as if i have some grounds to make judgement call. TLDR: It's a fun game and I dont see myself regretting the three or so trips to mcdonalds that the 30 bucks i spent would've gone to.The games not without hang ups. the line of sight system is a bit finicky and only works well when with small groups like in the early parts of the game. But as later missions require a good build up of forces you're going to be having unites interupting their lanes of fire. Each unite has a role and dont end up being redundant. though some are less useful in a general sense and some are must haves. The Bug's have a nice veriety though strangely the most dangerous unite in the game is the one sense wonder Scorpion bug with the more famous tanker being less of a hassle to deal with with minor micro. Music leans on the generic side  but hits the beats you want it to if you like games like Running with Rifles and Hell divers.Story wise, it's fine. Could've used squadie banter like what you got with the starship trooper FPS game where every one was inexplicably from the Bronx but it was funny. Though brass tacks is that this game is rather on the thin side. 20 story missions and 2 challenge senarios though one is just a basic totorial set in the Klendathu drop. the first 10 or so are a breeze with a big spike around mission 13 when scorpion bugs are more common and fail conditions are more stringent. the game's fair in that you're not screwed out of recourses. Unites are refunded when they die. its not ideal since you lose a vetran unite but you can spit a fresh one of the same type soon as it goes down.If i was being objective i'd rate this as a solid 7-7.5 as of right now. I'd personally would enjoy a more dynamic campaign where you could managed a persistant group of troops over the story. but I get the feeling the Dev's had to trim back their ambitions when they delayed the game. Hoping it get's expanded apon down the line but as of right now its a solid game that'd take you a good 10-16 hours to complete maybe less if you're skilled in games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game a lot of time. But it came with many defects. It has to go back to the shop before it is decently playable. My issues with the game are: (1) Reinforce: What a mess. You have to mark a place in the ground, then hit the stupid button and then after several tries, you get the reinforcements. This should be a simple halo around a special character/base. The current method is exhausting and prolongs the game unnecessarily. The whole routine is boooooring. By the way, The officer should be the one with this perk to avoid wasting time. The radio guy is absolutely useless (very difficult to use). And the HQ pistol officer is another distraction that wastes very limited resources. (2) Special perks: There is no way to use them. it is already too complicated to move the units around. This should be a passive item that gets activated. Clicking them is boring. (3) Units priority fire: This is waaay too crude. Rockets waste their time with non heavies and let the Scorpions move around. It doesn't matter if you have a perfect formation of units, the rockets won't do their job. They have to be micro-managed. (4) Formations: Too messy and have to be micro-managed all the time. There are many games to copy this from. There should be several formation types like Circle (support units in the center); and Chevron (arrow or spear). And more units to have several platoons attacking. (5) Snipers: They are useless. I had several costly setbacks because I used this idiotic unit. (6) Game pace: Too slow and forces the player to waste an unreasonable amount of time. (7) Turrets: There should be more, since the available amount of units is small. So there should be a way to leave defenses in your bases. But no, the game forces you to move and the insects take your base while you are in the map since you have a few units. This is an opportunity wasted for complex battles with multiple platoons all over the map. (8) Robots: I got exited when I saw them, but then got extremely disappointed by their horrible performance. It takes forever to get them, they are too slow and get toasted y Scorpions in milliseconds. Better to replace them for key control areas in the map like artillery bases, that if the player opts to control, they rain fire on the entire map, but have to be defended.

_childDocuments_.review: Would you like to know more?To start off, it's a solid RTS in the Starship Troopers world, it captures that feel of being in the federation by having it somewhat showcase the game in the "FedNet" - A tv show/channel - then during gameplay you feel like a you're commanding your units around like in any other RTS like C&C etc.There's times where I'm stopping to rethink or combat a incoming bug horde attack, keep a certain VIP unit alive, or just plan my move to counter a bug type that I've been alerted to.On that, there's a soft lack of UI tips and tutorial, in game it's just "move unit here", "attack this", "move here" that's the tutorial. On one hand, this was rather bland and basic, and I had to just work out how to set up a firing line myself (left click and drag in the direction you want troops to face)  along with what the red/orange/green crosshair above your units mean. (it's whether they have line of fire on a bug, red is no line of fire, orange is half of them can shoot, green everyone shoots, no-one quits) - The other hand this made me go "Oh, neat, that's how I do that"  - This could be a issue to some people of course.Next good point, they've captured horde amounts well. - You'll watch masses of bugs rush to your defensive outpost, your troops on the walls and blasting away. Then after the horde, you get an objective to send troops to collect something or clear out a bug nest a distance outside the base and there'll be a time limit before the next horde comes.  - Which personally I found a really cool way to do this.The "issues" so far is there's no camera rotation, which at times I wish I could do, but it's not a requirement.Next, base building isn't really a thing, yes you'll find "outposts" that you'll need to capture by having troops stand by them for a while, then you can pick upgrades based on what "resources" you have, and that'll allow you to request different troops. But the problem is; it didn't explain the "resources" at all.One mission, I saw I had 10 "supplies" for troops (each troop costs a different amount of supplies), I had three bases captured and was pushing to a big bug nest, where I started loosing units. I wasn't aware of a Tanker bug removing my other bases (FYI you don't permanently lose them), then I saw I had a no supplies and only three units alive.I had no idea how to proceed, I couldn't reclaim my bases because I was heavily outnumbered and there was a Tanker. It wasn't till I restarted the mission that I saw the "supplies" scattered around the map, I had presumed they was for "war support" - (Base building resource) which I didn't need, but nope, supplies for troops.Game didn't explain that either.But all in all, it's a solid RTS, that I believe on higher difficulties would require more tactical thinking and gameplay (I'm on normal and have only lost one and restarted twice because of errors on my part)Whether it'll be a repeat game I'll play is questionable, the single player is fun so far, and there's challenges as well. It depends whether the Dev's expand on the game to provide more and better replay ability

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely enjoyable homage to the 1997 Starship Troopers movie (No not the book, and that's okay; some people can simultaneously enjoy two different types of media, and if you're on of the weird haters of either who thinks everyone should have the same views as you, well you're a mouth-breathing gremlin). In ST:TA basically role-playing the Federation from the movie, and if you do, this is a great experience. Walls of unsupported infantry blasting away tracer fire at endless Arachnids that twitch and spasm as they are riddled with bullets. Having a squad of Mobile Infantry swamped by bugs on a hill, blasting away with their underslung shotguns, and calling in a TAC strike in on them because, well, they're doing their part and they will be remembered as Heroes of the Federation. GloriousIt's a old-style RTT, I say RTT rather than RTS as this is a squad management game, with the beginning missions having maybe three or four, and the later ones a dozen at most. You get MI riflemen, snipers, engineers, powered armour troopers and, everyone's favourite, M11 Babar "Marauder" battle mechs, among others There's limited elements of base building, but engineers can build turrets to satisfyingly hold choke points (a brief moment of silence to remember the two MI of the tower gun at Whiskey Outpost...). Units are brought in via dropship at node points that are captured, and infantry are reinforced for free in the same manner - in the true tone of Starship Troopers, units wil die, so meh, call in more! The Battle of Big K supposedly saw 300,000 dead, so you're doing okay if you lose a few units. The graphics are decent enough, the MI models are pretty decent. There are a few janky animations (the soldiers go from a "ready" position to firing in a weird snappy animation). The bugs, on the other hand, look great. The tanker bug in particular creates the appropriate sense of "oh ♥♥♥♥". The terrain is relatively simple, being a desert planet but there are a lot of good assets, burnt out vehicles, busted forts - it's very well models on the movie. The lighting, however, is very good, with scuttling shadows in the dark looking great. The cut scenes have a really nice aesthetic, played as propaganda videos for the Terran Federation. The game can be challenging. You will of course see the "I beat this easily on Brutal" threads in the forum, and good for them, but for the average playing it's challenging, and some missions are trickier than others.  Level designs are nice, with multiple paths and ways of achieving objectives on most of them. There are a few "tunnel missions", (think the power plants in Command and Conquer Red Alert). If you hate those, tough luck, but I actually found them quite enjoyable - they definitely bring the chittering hordes in the dark vibe to the game. There's a few balance issues with things like scorpion bugs (urgh), but I'm sure that will be ironed out eventually.Voice acting is good - I enjoyed the main characters and the classic ST story. Likewise, sound is decent and meaty with the retort of weapons (there's a lot of that) and the screeching of bugs. The game isn't too long - the campaign and scenarios took about 10-12 hours. I played through the campaign twice and enjoyed it both times. I really hope that there's additional content in the future with additional scenarios. Overall the game is an excellent addition to a genre that really saw it's heyday almost twenty years ago (oh man, I feel old), and a really loyal depiction of the Paul Verhoeven movie. So remember; the only good bug is a dead bug, and everyone fights, no-one quits!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit-Original game is fun, DLC has been made idiotically difficult. Avoid the DLC. When it's more chance and luck than planning and strategy, you know you have gone ahead and killed the Goose that laid the golden egg. Why would you do that?Original review-A word of advice before I talk about what I think about the game.This game is not a classical RTS. Base building is not focused for example on unlocking research tiers and using that to unlock more powerful units. You don't have resources that you can use to purchase units in the classical RTS sense- in game resources constitute of tiers of battle and unit logistics which sub for old school RTS concepts like currency and raw materials, but are earned very differently. Now moving since that's out of the way, first the good bits. This game is a lot of fun. To the point of being addictively so. There is good balance in how the story unfolds without overwhelming first timers to the franchise. It isn't too deep, but hits all the right spots. If you have seen the movie or Read Heinlein's book, you will instantly recognise the source material.Each mission brings in something new and it's satisfying to continuously unlock new units which allows you to really experiment with your squad load-out and approach victory in different ways. Squelching them bugs when you are at a numerical disadvantage but hold a tactical advantage feels just about right for a committed citizen of the federation.While the unit leveling mechanism is rather limited, it doesn't detract from the gameplay. If anything, the game encourages you to use special abilities wisely and cleverly turn the tide of the battle in your favor. Bugs flanking you? Get your elite rocket troopers to block one side with a firestorm missile launch and funnel the bugs into killzone where them critters run into the muzzle of your troops impressive armament. Now for cons, which IMO don't detract from the quality of the gameplay but are annoying nonetheless.There are minor bugs related to squad animations where your units get stuck in motion and look like they're suffering a seizure. Sometimes units appear through the terrain if you pan the camera too fast.There is a huge amount of micromanagement required from you and while this fun sometimes, it would be nice if we could set some default actions for the units like holding their ground or have a balance between aggression and defense. All too often tactical units which need to be in the back line end, end up in the front and get slaughtered because they aren't supposed to be there, but in the heat of the battle you've selected all your units enmasse to move them to a specific point or to attack a specific location. You can number code units or groups of units but in the heat of the battle, selecting each group through a number on the keypad is rather tedious for a largely point and click game. Also some of the instructions aren't really clear (for example clearing bug hives) and require some trial and error before you perfect it. I get that the game doesn't want to babysit you, but when there is a tutorial (of sorts), these little things that are important within the game context can be helpful especially at higher difficulty levels.Lastly, not a game bug, but this game is too short, needed more content for such an excellent game. I Will look forward to either a DLC or a sequel where we take the fight to bug homeworld and crush them once and for all!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 15 hrs in, I have decided to change the review score. I like to play a game the challenging mode, for instance, if there is easy, medium, hard and brutal mode, I usually play hard (or brutal). In this case here, I played the challenging/hard mode.The game started pretty easy, and it is expected that it gets harder down the road. However, the devs must have never tried this game the hard mode (not even brutal) to realize, that at one point some missions become IMPOSSIBLE to beat, except if you use exploits or follow exact YouTube guides and even there, you realize after a certain amount of time in the game, you actually run out of innovative solutions, you have to follow one particular gamestyle for instance, only found on youtube.Sure, I can lower the difficulty to medium, but no thanks. I have counted approx. 200 bugs rushing at the same time stretched through the map with elite type of bugs, and you are left stretched all over the map just with a few squads, it literally is impossible to hold the line, unless some bugs block each other (exploit) and stop moving through the map (common bug), but that's not a way a game is meant to be played.Also, the game becomes very very predictive. The more objectives you accomplish, the more challenges are being introduced "more difficult bug times, bugs spawning more, etc, etc", it just gets old too quickly about 15 hrs in.If you want to really enjoy this type of game, I suggest playing easy mode because the animations are cool, as well as the immersion is top notch and the maps are well designed in details.I will try this game again if the devs start to patch some things and actually play test the game.I recommend you grab this game only if it is less than 30 bucks, it is at the end repetitive and wears out about 15 hrs in.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: You can really tell a lot of heart was put into this game with how true it stays to the first movie / book and overall lore of starship troopers.Are you ready to do your part? - Great gameplay, very smooth and no issues  - Big guns, lots of bugs- Good story and cut scenes- lots of missions, and repeatability (many ways to run a mission)- Harder difficulty makes bugs scary, just like the movies - Great graphics and sound (also an outstanding soundtrack) - A good RTS to recommend to any strategy fan- Active devs, means probably more to come - Worth the money and priced well- Wishing for another campaign And Remember, the only good bug is a dead one
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: It's a yes, but with reservations.The game is enjoyable enough; glitch--free, well made, it doesn't have an overly difficult learning curve, it looks good, the voice acting is solid, there is a good variety of community content, and it's a decent representation of Star Ship Troopers...mostly.What it is lacking is passion and punch. It just feels repetitive and somewhat lackluster.  There aren't any tense moments, there is no attachment to units (but in the meat-grinder world of SST, that is fully acceptable, it's just that a loss is only a tactical moment, not a regret of losing a cherished squad or character), or any real doubt as to the outcome.There isn't anything wrong with it, but there isn't anything overly right with it either. I don't look forward to playing it, but I also don't look at it as time lost when I do. I will say that after six or so hours, I'm losing interest in it and will probably shelve it for a bit.I don't regret buying it, I'm just happy that it was on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: There's little to say about this one. The RTS mechanics are shallow as a puddle. You can call down units and have units cast abilities on long cooldowns. No resource gathering, no base building (aside from a token building slot system that acts more like an upgrade than a base), essentially no strategic element, this is a lot closer to DoW2 than Starcraft.That's not inherently a bad thing--I'm not really a fan of CoH/DoW2-like RTS games compared to traditional ones, but some people like them a lot more. But I think even with that preference, this doesn't quite cut it. Your units move  slow through vast maps. At least 60% of your playtime will be watching your little apes jogging around in the empty desert and tunnels. Unit abilities can make a difference but there's no thought in using them, you largely just spam them when they get off cooldown.The flavor is right, at least. The mission briefings are done as Federation news broadcasts that invariably sugarcoat the awful situation on the ground, papering over your doomed soldiers with banal slogans and empty patriotism. The few voiced characters also sell the heartless machinery of war you're a cog in, though the voice acting is strange. Very strange. I'm not entirely convinced the characters weren't voiced by a text-to-speech program.Ultimately what kills it for me is the pacing. Every mission is slow, painfully slow, as moving takes ages and combat is mostly a case of standing around hitting the "shoot more" hotkey occasionally. I think I got about halfway through the game's missions before getting tired of it all.Only buy if you're desperate for a starship troopers fix and it's on sale for $5 or less.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: The AI is stupid for the enemy as well as for our soldiers. The controls are very poorly implemented and units often don't do what they are ordered to do. The maps are poorly designed and remind me of an old command and conquer game. There is no story worthy of the name. The voice acting is terrible. Avoid or buy when it's $1.99
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good RTS, if you like the genre for playing campaigns buy this one.After playing through the campaign and scenarios I have to say its a realy good RTS.An RTS that purely focus on single player and does that that very well, something that has been missing for decades in the genre.The units fit well and each has its place for tactical reasons, the endgame units are extremly powerful and fell good as a reward for getting to the end.The mission design is one of the best in the last decades, it has everything from "base building" and non base building offensive and defensive missions, to indoor and survival mission over escort and multi staged missions. I normally hate indoor, escort and survival mission but they are done too well to complain about them. The indoor missions have refill points so you don't have to play perfectly the whole time, the escorts are eighter imbeded in other mission styles or only a short part of multi staged missions and the survival part also is mostly part multi stage missions or has very reasonable short timers, no "survive 30min" bs where you clear the map in 10min and than have to wait because the mission says so.For the setting, I watched the first movie a long time ago but wasn't a fan but even if you don't like the setting and humor the game is really fun to play. When you are a fan of the films than you will definetly enjoy the storytelling and humor and there are scenes that you will recognise from the movies (I assume that there are also scenes in from the movies I haven't watched).

_childDocuments_.review: FEDERAL NETWORK RELEASEOur boys and girls in the Mobile Infantry protect the galaxy from the Arachnid menace, and now they are available on YOUR terminals and personal devices!Starship Troopers: Terran Command is an RTS set in the Heinlein-inspired world of the Starship Trooper films. Set on the fictional Kwalasha, players will command their own regiments of the M.I. as they fight to push the Bugs off this valuable industrial world and secure it for Terra.Focusing on combat, you will command ground elements of the M.I. inspired by all three films, from light infantry to Marauders and the modern exo-armour of 'Invasion' and 'Traitor of Mars'. Against you is arrayed the full force of the Bug race: Warriors, Spitters, Tiger Warriors and even Plasma Bugs. All that need to be put down by your heroic troopers!While rocky to start with, the beginnings of the Year One roadmap have seen valuable improvements in the user interface's comprehensibility, balancing of how effective certain units are against others and - especially a problem early on! - unit path-finding. While some viewers might bemoan the lack of achievements or multiplayer capability, the Year One roadmap issued by the Federal Council assures viewers that future updates are pending that will expand replayability and content.So join up, citizens! Do YOUR part! There's a war going on!SERVICE GUARANTEES CITIZENSHIPWOULD YOU LIKE TO KNOW MORE?

_childDocuments_.review: Just a tight, fun, thematically appropriate strategy game.That your troops have to be stationary to fire is-- okay. It's different, at least. That they can't shoot past each other is great, especially with the inclusion of verticality to allow troops to shoot over each other. I wish more games respected field of fire.If you are familiar with strategy games: play it on Brutal or above (if they ever come out with something harder than Brutal. Otherwise, if you're new to strategy games or just want a lazy experience play this game is actually kind of perfect for that, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed it. Bit slow at the start, but really picks up at the end. Nothing like watching your entire army get eaten by bugs from a tactical error you make - it's strangely satisfying and feels fair. Fortunately you can redeploy troops quickly and try to recover back your line, which can lead to these badass moments where your line is falling and so you quickly need to rush new troops in to reinforce! _childDocuments_.review: A great RTS in a fabulous series. The combat is great with each difficulty not only making more bugs spawn, but do things like lower the damage of your units making strategy a key part of every fight. The use of high ground and true sight lines make positioning and proper unit types key throughout the campaign. I've played this game's campaign through 4 times and still go back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current form I cannot recommend this game. Yes, it is early access and yes, it does have the look and feel of the movies. The maps and animations look nice. What completely ruins the fun is troop management and especially movement. It is impossible to change the formation of the squad, which leads to them standing in each others way in the most stupid way possible. In combination with the very narrow ways (for such a clumsy force) of which the various maps have a lot - which is strange, as most of them are on desert planets, your men get killed.For the first six or so maps you just give the attack order and let your men do the rest, which is quite boring. Sometimes triggered events occur, which leads to enemy units appearing behind your lines and start destroying you scarce resources and building, leaving you stranded, as you cannot train new troops. But movement and room to maneuver is not the only problem, as the controls are very clumsy, slow and often not work properly. Also, you are supposed to place units like snipers on elevated places. Most of the time that is not possible. Or, it is only possible after passing enother chokepoint where you just kill all the bugs. Since all the bugs are dead when you arrive at the elevated position, there is no need to place the snipers here any longer. Stuff like this happens all the time. Currently 5/10 - not recommendable
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Feels good overall, if one is a fan of the movie-verse for Starship Troopers, they'll get exactly the right feel and vibe from this. Managing troop types and numbers is a good juggling act, and the strengths and weaknesses are straight forward enough to easily grip what you need and where.There is one big issue however and that is with the pathfinding, there is a "Troops won't shoot through eachother" mechanic to encourage the player not to just blob their troops and move smarter, but there are pathfinding issues that make that impossible in some places. Even while moving across open areas troops will tend to bunch up on their own and be unable to shoot because the units too close leading to substantial loses from one or two enemies that the troops couldn't shoot at.I recommend the game, but know that this is an issue that I hope is addressed.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow what a bore. The first three missions are a snooze on the second hardest difficulty, there's no story to be had, units are basic, abilities are clunky and ugly, and the arachnids are non threatening. This is a game that is supposed to encapsulate human futility through overwhelming odds (the humans lose a LOT but keep trying anyway, making a singular victory a huge deal). I never lost a unit nor did I ever feel overwhelmed, but the game would just decide that it was retreat time all the sudden. This game does not understand what it means to be a Starship Troopers game. Play Starcraft. Or heck, go find the original Starship Troopers tactical RTS. That was an excellent, albeit clunky, game.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game by any means. Unfortunately for me though, it takes a great game to really hold my attention nowadays. I was hoping for a Command & Conquer and StarCraft hybrid of sorts, with a Starship Troopers theme. This game is simply too linear and too restricting to keep me interested. It's a series of capture-the-flag type of missions over and over again where you can only grow your military presence and strength in primarily predefined ways. It's not the open concept, gather, build, expand, and conquer type of RTS game that I was yearning to play. I've only played the game a little over 3 hours and I already feel like I can see exactly how the remainder of the game would play out.I absolutely loved the movies (especially the first one), but the game just isn't interesting enough to keep me coming back for more. I will say some of the fort defense missions are pretty darn fun, but they are too few and far in between. I picked this game up on sale so I can't complain. I'll say it's good enough to justify the $22 I spent on it, even though I won't finish it.I'd only recommend it to perhaps younger gamers who are big fans of the Starship Troopers movies. If you're young then you probably haven't played as many games as I have, and so your expectations and standards might not be as high as mine have become over the years. If I had to score the game, I'd give it a 6/10. If it weren't so restrictive with regard to where and when you can build and expand, I would have increased the score to a 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. The mechanics are well balanced and every unit and every bug type has its place in the game. I really like well thought out gameplay mechanics which can be found in the whole game.The graphics are perfectly fine and the sound creates a cool atmosphere at many times.I normally don't like these "go with your units through this huge building" - missions but in this game they are awesome because of the mechanics and the focus on micro management.There is no real story in the game, so don't buy it for that. That is no real problem for me but some people might see this as a critic point. I played 18 hours to finish the campagne and the scenarios.Some levels of the game a really much harder than others but you always can restart and adjust the difficulty settings like you want.The only real critic point I've got is that some mechanics are not directly understandable even though they are shown in game. For example do units block their line of side. If two marine groups stand behind each other one of them won't fire. This is a really cool mechanic but not obvious at the beginning. Further more I found only one bug ( :D ) in the game where the tooltips disappeared. After a restart of the game they worked again.Oh and... "I also did my part!"

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is Okay it is not fun, It took me four hours to get over the nostalgia of Starship troopers and realise that this game is far below the standard you'd expect.•There is significant issues with unit pathfinidng. You can't just select a group of units and ask them to go somewhere as they get caught on corners and each other. They end up getting stacked up on each other which results in your units being sluaghtered as line of sight effects them.•Because of the pathfinidng you have to micro manage every unit. Given that you need to keep range from the enemies i find that half the time this command works and the other time my unit will forget it's self and charge at the enemy and practically suicide into it.•Nostalgia was the only think that kept me interested in this game but the actual gameplay it's self ruined it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Early impressions are surprisingly positive. On the previews it looked like a dull and primitive corridor army crawler (which is the strategy game equivalent of a walking sim), but the actual gameplay is much more interesting, with hordes of Arachnids flowing from multiple directions while you need to push for objectives, capture bases for reinforcements (yes, there is some simple economy here) and keep your soldiers alive against an unending tide of bugs.Some aspects of the game seem "cheap" (barely servicable graphics, lack of audiovisual impact, mediocre unit animations) but the love for the movie makes up for it: The tone is spot on, gameplay replicates the lore well, and I think there are even some book-inspired mechas later on. I am a bit torn on the music as it sounds cheap but does its' best at replicating the original movie's soundtrack and I find it hard no to commend it for that.I'll edit the review later once I do my part.

_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: About 20 hours to complete the main story and a little longer to complete the two challenge missions. Overall I liked the game. The first half of the missions I was playing on the 4 star hard mode. But after the half way point the missions get much more difficult. I had to go down to the 3 and 2 star difficulties to complete the missions. It is a unique RTS game with the bug enemy and the Starship Troopers world which is awesome. The game does get a little repetitive, especially on the harder missions that take time to take out all of the bug hives. A lot of the levels have the same objectives. Take out a bunch of bug hives while securing more bases. Some levels are unique though, such as capturing a fugitive and dealing with a prison riot. My favorite level would be the final level. The big down sides are the fact that you cannot play as the Bugs and there is no multiplier or procedurally generate maps vs AI modes for more replayability. If the Bugs had playable missions and multiplayer then this game would get a couple more points. But I do believe for what is included the $29.99 asking price is fair. Positives: Starship Troopers World. Unique RTS against Bugs. Some Unique Missions. Various Units. Good Campaign Length. Cons: Many Repetitive Missions, especially the ones that are longer. Only Humans Campaign, No Playable Bug Missions. No Multiplayer. No procedurally generate maps to play. Very Little Replayability. 6/10 - Slightly Above Average

_childDocuments_.review: Couple reasons why this game is worth it overall. First of all, more Starship Troopers is never a bad thing - it's classic satire anyone can enjoy ironically or unironically. Rarer than you might think, and the game embodies it; not just in tone but in gameplay too. The RTS gameplay perspective itself lends another layer into the Federation's MO and ordering around a bunch of apes are satisfying. They move fast, pathfind in clear reasonable ways, and the line of sight physics are welcome.There's also the simple fact that we don't have too many campaign-driven rts games outside of Starcraft (which has messy consistency so it barely counts) and Relic games - namely Homeworld. This game doesn't have deep great writing, but it does have personality and a clear narrative, which is something.Some problems though. Mostly in balancing. The developers have a very limiting view on what "difficulty" means. Hardest mode just means bullets showered, the core bug AI is predictable as is any mission structure that relies to heavily on scripted "gotcha!" moments. Simply put, don't play this if you're an RTS buff... but do play this if you want a solid starter entry.Beyond that, it's reasonably priced and it's fun - what any person wants really from a game.
