_childDocuments_.review: For a measly 30 dollars, this game delivers a good Starship Troopers experience. The campaign is fun, for the most part. It's a solid RTS experience, it captures the source material well, and takes some particularly interesting mechanics such as requiring firing lines for your riflemen because you can't shoot through allied units.Now, for the negatives:-Clunky Movement: The game is not *difficult* but it is tedious at times. Some units will stop and attack when in range of an enemy during an attack move, other times they will stop, fire, move up, stop, fire, move up, and rinse and repeat until they're jumping into bug maws. This wouldn't be a particularly bad thing if melee damage was not so utterly devastating to your units. Your units are slower than enemies, which means if you need to run away, you're going to leave one unit behind to die off, because you CANNOT escape the enemy. Other units, such as rocket teams and marauders, are constantly getting stuck on corners and have to be manually controlled to get unstuck.-Babysitting: I don't mind a bit of micromanagement, but when the game is designed around micromanagement while also having really clunky unit controls, you're essentially doubling up on the player tedium. This gets especially nightmarish whenever you have to defend multiple areas or attack one area while defending another. I understand it's needed to some extent because of the barebones base/resource building, but I think it's worth mentioning it's a bit too far in the wrong direction.-Trimmed Down Strategy Elements: When it comes to base building and resources, this game is skeletal when it comes to RTS. Base building is limited to capture points with set slots for what units you can recruit, and resources are tied to map objectives and the occasional capture point. This does put the focus on the bug shooting, but it does leave something to be desired. The only real building you do is placing turrets from your combat engineers. I would have liked to be able to construct more, as well as have more intricacy with resource allocation. If you combined the base building and resource gathering of They Are Billions with this game, it would be phenominal. One of the last maps has a system where killing enemies increases your available resources, and I think that should have been a baseline feature. I like having some gameplay/counter play with resources, like having a more vulnerable position that generates more resources for me, risk/reward. There are very few maps that actually utilize this. On the more difficult maps, I just let the enemies take my points that I wasn't interested in defending because it cost me nothing, and that's a negative consequence of the simplified resource system. Losses are essentially nothing, because your resources just determine the maximum number of units you can bring, and you can always replace them with a minor cooldown to transport ships. In some cases, your defenses can be so solid that you essentially stalemate the enemy with no real victor.-Infinite Respawns: The nature of the game essentially gives massive bonuses to the defender, both bug and human.  Humans have defensive turrets, can recapture any lost point, can respawn any unit that dies, and can hold a defense while "healing" a unit on the point. Bugs, on the other hand, can be an absolute nightmare. A hive with 3+ tunnels attached to it is essentially invulnerable short of extreme overpowering on the player's part. You'll often find that when you're trying to clear out a hive, the defenders respawn so frequently that you're fighting more by the time you finish a wave. If this map spawns the scorpion unit, then you are in for a nightmare of a slog. My personal feeling is that replenishing bug caves should be halted, or at least slowed if there is a military presence nearby it. There comes a point where you're moving the needle by centimeters until you're finally able to get that goldilocks moment of having a 0 strength hive to clear out before the next wave spawns. If you're wondering why I didn't just clear it once my army strength was higher, it's because my game was bugged and if you ever sent in an army in there and there was even 1 enemy group left, your entire army will die in there regardless of being stronger. I lost a 4.0 army to a 1.0 hive because the hive just didn't take damage.-Units: Experienced units should be an investment, and a detriment if lost. Veterancy unlocks a choice between one of two abilities to equip the unit with. Usually there is a correct choice and a wrong choice. I also disagree with a shared cooldown on every ability. I think there should be more tiers of veterancy, all of which improve a soldier's output as well. The only units that really mattered to me if they were veterans or not were rocket troopers, and snipers. Everything else was disposable. I think there could be a bit more unity variety as well. I'm not sure why Marauders have 3 individual units whereas power troopers are able to change their weaponry upon veterancy. I think it would make more sense for marauders to start with the grenade bombardment ability, and then upon veterancy select between flamethrowers, gatlings or howitzers. Again, I really want to stress that veterans should be a significant investment and reward. A minor nitpick as well: Rocket troopers should really have an aoe. I know they're already basically the must have unit, but I absolutely hate how often they miss single targets because their big warhead has zero splash damage.-Balance: Good lord what masochist created the Scorpion unit? The units for the most part are reasonably balanced, but this thing is a blight upon civilization. It would be fine as a strong high priority unit, but the problem is that they often spawn *en masse.* I've gotten into the habit of having a sacrifice unit for Scorpions. So I just sent the dead men to their graves while my rockets do their best to focus fire one by one. There's some rebalancing to be done across the board, but these guys are a glaring thorn in the side.-Campaign Design: The campaign is generally fun, and I enjoyed them keeping the starship troopers motif well. I did, however, have a few problems with some of the design for the campaign. There are some questionable design decisions for the campaign.  Having an ambush that you need to hold fire until the right time, but then putting the tutorial for hold fire in the mission AFTER that. There were also several times where secondary objectives just had no value. Like literally no value, or even a detriment. Said ambush was one such secondary objective. It's a difficult fight that you can choose to do. And as a reward for doing it you get nothing. I think the missions need a second look over to make sure the objectives are handled appropriately. Generally speaking, main objectives should just be for victory, whereas secondary objectives should be more difficult things to do with actual risk, but also yield rewards for doing them. I'll also note that the no-build missions are probably the lowest point of the game. I do not care for these kind of missions, especially because the lack of a way to replenish lost troops means you could very well be unable to finish the mission, but not know it until much later on. I'm sad to see that an actually helpful AI partner was saved for the very last mission.  I would have liked to see more missions involving AI players. I also think it's rather bizarre that bunkers and special heavy turrets that cannot be built also cannot be repaired by combat engineers.All in all, it's a good game. Worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially great game but held back by extremely odd design choices, one is that the MI units only fire while stationary , the second thing is when engaged while moving, units do not typically stop until they reach the assigned location. The third common issue is unit selection, most units have a logo, and in most RTS games, when you click and drag, it would only select the units logo, but with this game, if you happen to drag and have one trooper from another squad in that selection, it would also select that other squad as well. So with the way the game is designed, it is clearly pushing a more leap frogging squad game play when advancing, but with these 3 things, it can be very clumsy. Especially since usually you experience these 3 issues the same time, like when you are bounding squads, which this is a bigger issue with more squads as you select another squad to move up, but it also often selects a trooper from another squad (which is usually the squad set up to give coverfire), so you have more troops moving than intended, and when the bugs are attacking that group, you will experience the first and second point since both squads are now moving, and would probably be attacked by bugs, but since they are going to a location, they will not stop attack the bugs, and they cannot attack the bugs while moving either, they just start taking casualties.

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a very faithful continuation of the Verhoeven's classic. As a game however it fares far, far worse, alas. The jank, the bugs (hehe) & the lack of the very standard quality of life features will have ruined this game for anyone but the most hardcore RTS fan. Here's the silly me thinking I could get back into the genre by picking it up. Unfortunately I am not a hardcore RTS fan. Never been. Never will. All the way back in the 90s I played some of the legendary OG Warcraft 2 & Starcraft, some trash like Krush Kill & Destroy (Yes, it was the time of the capital "K"), & even the criminally underrated, ahead of its time diamond in the rough: Total Annihilation. I finished neither. But I did finish X-COM: UFO Defense which guess what, was a strategy game, but not an RTS. It too was ahead of its time by two decades. Such was the style at the time in the 90s, kids.I am convinced that RTS as a genre, whilst not being dead like the immersive sim, is still a very niche genre overall. There's a single culprit to blame for it. You know how there's always a meta to basically every game out there, right? Well, for RTS as a whole it's the actions per minute metric. It all comes down to that simple number. Now, I reject that notion, just like I reject being forced to perfectly memorize boss patterns in From Soft games (it's okay, I adapt to beat them in my own ways). It's just not for me. Sadly, such is the case here. You have to micromanage your idiot troops like toddlers. Running through fire to get an entire squad killed? No problem, boss. We have it. Flocking like morons into a single square meter just to die from an AoE attack? Sir, yes, sir!If that weren't enough, of course the game bugs out all the time. The pathfinding is broken, especially for an army of more than 3 squads. They will either get stuck, or more often take separate paths to your designated destination. They will freeze in the aforementioned square meter surrounded by aliens to be slaughtered mercilessly. I'm not even talking about being able to shoot trough walls, that comes with the job. All of this is but a tiny sample of the ever present jank.For some reason special abilities can only be used by a single squad... I'm sorry, but why? There's no formations that were a standard feature twenty freakin' years ago in games like Perimeter. If there's one thing this game needs more than air is battle formations. The troopers just loosely follow a staggered column. By loosely I mean very loosely. But there isn't consistency even here. The pulse rifle troopers are all glued together in a rigid square, making them the single most useless unit in the game. Yes, sometimes pulse rifles is all you get, so you have to make due. Dear god.The game tells you, the player in the first mission is that it's about positioning troops. You break formation, you die. Only it makes it impossible to keep your troops positioned. It's like herding cats. There's no hold position button. So they'll just run off to do something stupid and hence get themselves killed. At a midway point in the main campaign the game throws AoE attacks your way. Guess what? No disperse button either. How am I supposed to hold my positions like that without micro managing every single squad? That takes a very special kind of person, mind you. Most of those people are in South Korea playing Starcraft on esports. I'm neither Korean, nor an RTS esporter. I want my strategy games be about strategy, not about clicking and pressing buttons real fast. Is this so much to ask, game?The campaign goes off the rails in the second half. The DLCs fare better, but even then it's a coin flip as to whether it's gonna be good or crap. This of course sours the whole experience. I really want to like this game, I really do, but I have an upper limit of frustration & baby sitting my soldiers in real time is an instant disqualifier. If you enjoy ApM gameplay, then by all means, be my guest. I in the meanwhile am going to go hit my head against the wall a couple dozen times.Now, I said in the beginning that the story is good. Yes, it is very good. The only reason why I dragged my feet to finish this holy mess of a game at all. Now, why did I say it was the continuation of Verhoeven's classic & not Heinlein's? Because the former understands the source material better than the latter despite not being its original author. Kinda in the same vein as Mary Shelley & her Frankenstein. That is if you read her radical feminist preamble that completely misses the point. Death of the author & all that. The author's interpretation is just one of many.I've read a rather amusing review here on Steam about how the game "disrespects the source material". I'm not sure if the author was serious or not, but let's assume they were for a moment. Because it betrays them quite a fair bit without them even realizing it.People who regurgitate the all too familiar phrase "service guarantees citizenship" uncritically and hence unironically are missing the obvious external implications for it being a blatant con. The war is waged in perpetuity by design. The "arachnids" are the perfect enemy for a fascist state. An overwhelming external (?) threat that replenishes its ranks faster than they're eradicated. A colossus that shrugs off every federal attempt at hurting it as no more than a mosquito bite. Yet the "superior technology and tactics" shall surely prevail over the uncivilized hordes.We've heard all of this before more than once. Only now we don't even need to unperson each other anymore. They're just bugs that ought to be squashed. Who cares how this war started, who started it. There's no question about it: a good bug is a dead bug. All the intellect and obvious high levels of consciousness? Let's ignore that like we always do.But fret not, there's also traitors among us. Union leaders, mercenaries, people at the end of their rope financially, bug infested (?) humans. Everybody is out to get you, brave citizen to be, who's afraid of their own shadow at every hour of every day.The idea that this world is a utopia because there's gender equality is about as silly as the idea that "communism is when the government does stuff". It's only a utopia if one agrees to the premises. In other words it is a fascist's wet dream. Verhoeven understood that. Heinlein in his novel has created a fascist utopia. Whether on accident or by design. Having read his "magnum opus" Stranger in a Strange Land, or how I like to call it: The Wacky Adventures of Space Jesus on Earth, I tend to think it's probably the latter.Now, you may say that the aliens bad. Aliens might indeed be bad. But that's not the point. I don't need them to be good for my argument to work. There's no shortage of straightforward alien bad media in which they come home to destroy us. You won't hear a single objection about those from me. The point is that the aliens in this universe are the perfect enemy for a regime in a constant need of external & often internal threats. It's their Iraq & their Afghanistan to be waged war in perpetuity in. It's a pretense for something greater. And let me tell you, that greater is not for your benefit or mine. Fascism thrives on fear like a demon that subsists on suffering. Do not let fear control you.Wow, I'm being extremely political lately. First Lost Judgement, now this. How could I not though? Both these properties are highly political. To not speak on their implications is a crime in & of itself. Emotionally I felt dirty by the end of the Gehenna (DLC) campaign. What one of the protagonists does by the end & how it contrasts with the heroic music playing at the end of the mission. It almost made me want to vomit. This is good. I like media that challenged me, that tears me out of my comfort zone & beats the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. This is the best kind of media. This game in my opinion should have been an animated series. The story is that good.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Star craft 2 single player campaigns. I also really like AoE2 and AoE4, Grey goo, the various Homeworld games, Supreme commander/FA, C&C/RA, Ashes of the singularity. This starship troopers game is well worth playing. The tactics are much about positioning. Also about order of objectives. If you mix Ashes (replenishing troops + timing/concentration of force) with Company of heroes (positioning), but with more humor, I guess you get this game. The tutorial is a bit long perhaps, with maybe 5-7 missions being very attack-move-ish. But at around number 7 or so I had to pick up the pace a bit. So far, I haven't yet really had to rethink any of the obvious tactics, so I guess its been a bit shallow so far, but I have not played at the highest difficulty so far, and am only at perhaps map number 10 or so (8 hours in). Apparently there are around 20ish maps. So there is enough challenge in the game for me to have fun at least. 2.5 out of 5 for the depth of the game mechanics so far, but I hope that will increase to a 4 before I'm done.The atmosphere/voices and mission stories are great (in a stupid way, keeping true to the spirit of the source material). 5 out of 5 for the atmosphere.Many of the reviews I found of this game, both on Steam and on Youtube (e.g. IGN) were unnecessarily critical. We don't get a lot of games in this genre anymore. And if you like this genre, specifically sci-fi RTS, you can't really afford to miss this game. Get it. Play it. Enjoy it for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest RTS that came out in a while.Every campaign goes through a satisfying military campaign exploring the glories and perils of battle, while revelling in the satire of the setting and explicitly showing that the federation is not good and none of this is desirable. Each campaign also explores the relationship between a new cast of interesting characters and how they influence each other in extreme circumstances, which provides personal engagement and really makes you care about what is going on not only gameplaywise but also emotionally. It has been a long time since I was genuinely surprised by characters in a rts campaign…It is refreshing to just get a finished, polished game for your money from the premiere, it is even more satisfying to get solid dlcs providing straight up new content in good quality and quantity (instead of some shi tty micro transaction shop like some rts do). It is also very nice to see creators providing extra missions outside of the dlc campaigns with the updates, that’s a nice touch that shows this is a work of someone who cares, not calculated investment of some pencil pushers.The gameplay is solid and innovates the rts formula in an interesting way, providing an extremely satisfying gameplay loop of positional warfare against the endless bugs. There is a bunch of unique units to play around with, and both the formula and level design allow for variety of tactics and combos. Experimenting and coming up with new (mostly dumb) things is very fun, and very much supported.I don’t think it is endlessly interesting like StarCraft2 endless depth and possibility, but for playing a solid dozen mission campaign from time to time it is very fun, simple as. The game has no coop and pvp but I see them as unnecessary to this game, I would not play it much I think, I don’t see how you could bend the formula enough to fit them.The art style is solid, and pleasant. While the models are on the simpler side, animations are lacking and the effect are not crazy, it is all very readable and flows nicely in combat. Also, the bugs look good and that the most important part for me.The sound effects are distinct and solid, that’s all. But the music and voice acting are STELLAR, some incredible work there! (Eli Harris, I’ve cried tears of joy because of you…)Also, my favourite detail:So in the first campaign we are on a desert planet (cos movie, you know how it is), and through the first few missions it looks like it’s going to be boring: endless rocky desert with some houses and walls here or there. But the designers drag you from desert to mines, to bug tunnels, to night missions, changing environments and colour schemes between missions or even during missions so it never becomes boring. Masterful use of limited assets and location types to change up the visual language of the game while reusing most of the stuff they made, that is genuinely impressive. Really! To the point when towards the end of the campaign you’re in the desert canyon again and your glad to be back in the comfort of known environment again… but you were fighting a war on a desert planet all the time! How cool is that!Also, also:Do you want to play as the bugs? Check out “The Defence of Fort Rico” in the stream workshop or ingame “Community Content” menu. The provided editor is superb, and if your hungry for content even after finishing the game you can find fully fledged CAMPAINS in there!That’s what I like to see, so that’s what I’m buying. I'M DOING MY PART! IN SUPPORTING THE RTS MARKET!!! And sincere thank you! to the whole team working on this project. It truly was a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers 19 main missions divided into three types: attack, defence and missions where you have only a small group of soldiers at your disposal, we can call them stealth. Attack missions require clearing bugs on a map or capturing bases. Defence requires you to withstand big waves of insects. Sometimes attack missions change to defence and vice versa. When you play stealth you must complete certain objectives, but you can’t call new units at your base or you have limited support. All missions are well-designed along with the environment. Before starting, you can choose difficulty but it only changes the damage multiplier of your units. After the fulfilment of all primary objectives, there are also some secondary ones, you will get short comic cutscenes that move the story further. It is a good addition otherwise the story is told by three main characters during a mission. I would like to see some stats at the end of the mission too, not only the winning message and short cutscene because you have no idea how many units you lost or how many Arachnids did you kill.All of the mission types have one thing in common – clearing bugs’ hives. While your soldiers are defending the captured point, another group of units must clear the entrance by depleting Arachnids. Some hives are connected by tunnels that you should deplete as well. You can see the strength of your infantry (green text) and bugs (red text) when you hover the mouse over the hole. If red is more than green, it’s a suicide mission for soldiers. Once the tunnels are clear, you can focus on the main hive, but keep in mind that Arachnids can always respawn, so don’t forget to check the red bar above the tunnels. I think the devs make this system well and you must prepare a good tactic on each hive if you want to successfully clear it.In most RTS games you call units from the side menu and they come to the battlefield or you recruit them in buildings. In this game, you have small bases where you call units from the command centre and they will land on the ground at certain points in your base. You have two resource types: Supplies and War Support. Both can be raised by completing objectives or capturing some equipment around the map. For basic soldiers, you just need Supplies that work like population limit in other RTS games, but for stronger units, turrets or new buildings you need War Support as well. The selection of units is good, from regular soldiers armed with rifles to skilled snipers, officers and even heavy mechs, there's a unit for every situation. However, I have to admit that the MK II Troopers with their assault rifles and grenade launchers seem a little overpowered to me. A few groups of them can easily wipe out a horde. It would be nice to rebalance it, so players will try to combine more unit types and the unique skills that can gain from clearing Arachnids. Additionally, while the pathfinding system generally works well, there are some situations when units get stuck on obstacles or in narrow places. Some improvements would be good. Pathfinding is important here because there is some micromanaging of units that is nice. They can’t shoot from behind through other soldiers. You must check their lines of fire because If you have a larger group of infantry, but in the wrong formation, they will end fast, especially if some strong Arachnids appear like Tigers, Royale Guards or Tankers.The game has an Editor where you can create your own scenario. The UI is a little bit outdated, but you can make the same missions like you played in the main campaign. Of course, there is Steam Workshop support, so you can download many nice creations made by the community. I tried The Infernal Crossroads, and it was crazy, there were so many Arachnids everywhere. Also, there is a remake of missions from the old Starship Troopers Terran Ascendancy.

_childDocuments_.review: It is so nice and refreshing to find a game that simply works and does what it promised without compromise. No microtransactions, no nonsense always online servers causing single player lag, just... no nonsense.Starship Troopers: Terran Command provides you 19 campaign missions and 3 scenarios at the time of this writing. The missions are fully voice-acted, there are cutscenes before each mission to further the story and the game nails the feel of the Verhoeven movie universe with every sentence uttered, every mission briefing provided. They even managed to make the flashlight guns from the second movie into some semblance of a fun weapon and they remembered Starship Troopers: Marauder exists.I encountered no issues, no bugs, no crashes with the game in my time playing.The only two points of critique I could offer is that the missions could be a tad bit longer because I do enjoy just seeing waves of bugs crashing against a defensive position and being turned into chunks by superior firepower.And I would have liked a little more information on the HUD regarding the status of the bugs, and attached to that more hit feedback on tougher enemies such as Tigers to show whether your Riflemen are doing damage. The biggest enemies have health bars to indicate it but again, just a few signs of damage or deflection on the bug carapaces would have been nice.If you are a fan of the movie setting, I don't know why you wouldn't already own this game.If you want to play an interesting RTS campaign with reasonable amounts of content, pick this up maybe during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: For a 30 dollar game its pretty good, but there's nothing other than the main storyline campaign. once you beat the main campaign in ~12 hours, that's it. Well, plus one small mission.there's no multiplayer, no scenarios, no skirmishes. So all in all it's an enjoyable game, and it really brought life back into a franchise I wish never died, but it is lacking. There's rarely a loss condition in any of these levels. Enemies wont retake their old bases, your units spawn instantly so long as you have an available drop ship, and most units can create landing zones so even if a unit dies, you can spawn and then drop them back to your front lines rather quickly.For a 30 dollar game, it's not bad. I've definitely bought games that were equally priced and delivered far less content. *cough Democracy 4 cough* So yeah the voice acting is horrible, and yes it's a little simple, and I would have loved to play this game with friends. But I'm happy to fan boy at just the aspect of someone bringing back a franchise that no one ever dared to continue even though it was a cult classic. Maybe this could be the start of something more?

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write these very often but i have to recommend this game!  Terran Command is exactly the sort of game I wanted. The campaign will teach you what you need to know about mechanics as you go; definitely nail these down because you will need them for the community content.  This community is amazing and have gone through hours and hours of map and mission design in a way that make sense; there are whole campaigns made by other players, including recreated scenes from the movies.  This will keep the game fresh as it ages.  Glory to the Federation!

And much more importantly your units just kind of control like crap. this is mostly due to the heavy emphasis on the "Line fighting" way that every unit has to have clear lines of fire, and quite simply when ypu have five or more basic troops the finding does not know what to hell to do and it turns into an extremely micro managing game where units are getting stuck on other units. Very annoying.Mission wise there's some decent ones but a lot of gimmick missions that just kinda felt a little boring, and for some reason the last mission is just way to easy, like weirdly so. I don't understand why so many modern RTSs are more tactical than strategic, if you understand what I mean.  You can't build bases, and even if you can, you can't have very many units. _childDocuments_.review: It has been a while since I've been engrossed in a good story driven strategy game (they don't come along very often which is a shame) which has made me sit down and play for an entire day straight. _childDocuments_.review: Terran Command is a pretty fun Solo-Focused RTS. It's simple in its mechanics and plays kind of like an improbable mix between Dawn of War 2 (You control just a few squads/Vehicles, each with abilities and veterancy) and napoleonic warfare (strong, strong emphasis on line battle, as your units cannot fire through each other, safe from a few exemples)The Starship Trooper aesthetic is spot-on, with each mission having a FedNet propaganda presentation often contradicting what you discover once loading, and every unit basically acting like Helldivers with no sense of self-preservation and unwavering morale.It may become a bit repetitive after a bit, as you are limited to 1 faction (Mobile Infantry) and 1 biome (Desert, with some Urban environment in a couple of missions), at least in the main game. It's kind of the same for the missions, usually revolving around cleaning up Hives and Nest in-between waves of bugs. However, the addition of an Editor is pretty interesting, as I tested a mission where you played as the Arachnids in kind of a reverse Tower Defense fashion.So, yeah, I recommend, pretty solid game :D

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes real time strategy games! The story is interesting and I love the narrative, as the dev said its like a pacific front for this human bug war. I think the game is also great for beginners and the enemy types provide a fun and if you want difficult challenge. This game can be hard if you choose the right difficulty with there being 5. The in game wiki is very helpful and does not come across as too over complicated. The music is great, I can hear in one of the tracks a part of the original Klendathu drop theme which makes you enjoy the fight that much more. It is satisfying to build up an army and exterminate bug forces and also successfully defend bases from the bugs. It is most fun when you realise where if you make too many wrong moves with your troops or use the wrong troops on certain enemies. You will find yourself overrun and dead. So it is good to know you have won because you made the right strategic moves. Making this a true RTS experience. I also love the auto formations the troops line up in when you give them an order to move to a position. Where you will have snipers and officers line up behind riflemen as they should. However Its annoying to have to watch out for engineers moving to far in front when telling them to attack while moving and also the officers like the fleet liaison doing that to on a regular attack order. It would be cool if players could make maps. Then we would have a lot more missions added to the already decently sized game, the devs could basically have people making content for free. With different scenarios like base defence and bug hole destruction. Overall great game that lives up to the Starship troopers fictional universe.

You can move as normal and you have this super cool, yet really basic attack move, where the unit move towards their designation but stop to shoot whenever a bug is within range. _childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr Version: I don't think this a fun game because the tactics are oversimplified, I'm not hooked by the story, and the promise of new troop types and new enemies isn't enough to motivate me to complete such a linear game.Essay Version:I was expecting a modernization of Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendancy, but my impression had me shaking my head in disappointment and boredom within two hours. It's kind of like Terran Ascendancy with an increased polygon count and post-processing effects such that it is visually acceptable in the second decade of the 21st century. Oh, and better gore. However, as far as gameplay goes, it lacks what I consider basic elements of a single-player RTS.Now, I know I've only played a few hours but unless there's a huge engaging plot twist somewhere down the fragmented storyline, I pretty much get the whole idea of the game: I'm in tactical command of the ground forces of a highly-militarized society which finds the continued existence of the giant bugs unacceptable, but the Federation is unable to defeat them directly on their homeworld, so my theater of operations is restricted to one planet conveniently free of canon conflicts with the film. Perks of the game include getting to watch my troops kill bugs, getting to watch bugs kill my troops, and getting to use new troop types for the aforementioned purposes as they are added by the story, which is progressed by completing whatever objectives are given in each mission, displayed in the top-left corner of the screen, and are often something along the lines of "Don't lose your command center," which translates into "defend the only position where you are allowed to build and deploy new troops while simultaneously completing the other objectives," which might be something like "Clear bug tunnels (x/6)," with 'x' being however many targets (locations clearly marked on the minimap) you have neutralized. The promise of new unit types, enemies, and new variations of the same desert/underground scenery are the rewards for progressing the campaign. I've already completed at least ten of the fairly brief missions so I assume there are a lot of them. Thing is, I don't really care to see the rest if all I'm going to get is new unit types. Troops go from recruit to Elite over the course of single missions but they don't even carry over to the next, so I'm not sure why the developers bothered to let you name each squad or building, and the last time I saw the custom name of my division was when I was naming it.Anyway, so, the story. There isn't much of one outside of the actual missions, which are story-driven, as emphatically promised by the developers, but unsophisticated and uninteresting. Various recurring characters constitute the human aspect of the classic Starship Troopers flavor. For example, you are effectively characterized and voiced through what seems to be your second-in-command, who exists as a voiceover character most notable for his passive frustration with the Federation's flawed strategic priorities while simultaneously promoting his absolute acceptance of everyone's expendability. The 2D cinematics (in the same style as the illustrations you see on the Store page) barely tie the missions together, although they often provide some flavorful exposition and dark humor. However, I find it entirely inadequate.Strategy and gameplay are lacking in a very similar way. The missions are extremely linear. No replayability beyond replaying the mission using a different combination of units or physical routes to your objectives, and even those options are few. There are no automatic formation options on a squad level, but with multiple squads/units selected, the automatic formation has each squad/unit stand side-by-side in a simple line, which is the only formation you need anyway because it maximizes crossfire support while making your flanks (which are weaker because the squads have more width than depth, so even though each member of the squad can fire in any direction, getting attacked from the side means your flank isn't as strong as your front and rear) more difficult for the enemy to exploit simply because it takes longer to reach them because they are farther away. The more troops you have firing on your primarily melee opposition, the longer it takes for them to reach evisceration range because there are more bullets hitting them, and the faster it kills them. For other formations, or in small canyons, tunnels, and corridors that the algorithms think are too narrow for squads to stand side-by-side, squad units must be positioned individually. Aggressive/defensive stances are equated by a few commands: "Move," which moves your units to a position, at which point they will immediately open fire on any enemies which are in range unless you have the "hold fire" option activated, which I guess is most useful for sneaking by enemies spotted at the edge of your field of view and still outside of aggro range, and the "attack move" command, which causes your units to halt and open fire on any enemies in range en route to their destination. The "attack move" command is really nothing more than a quality-of-life option that automates the process of halting, firing, and ordering them to move again. The only other tactical mechanics are utilizing elevation to expand field of view and be able to shoot past friendly squads between them and the enemy, as well as using impassable terrain to slow down or bottleneck non-flying enemies. I know I made my explanation overly drawn-out and complicated, but my point is that the tactical game, which *is* the entire game, is unrealistically simple and logical. The rest is all unit-type-specific special abilities. So just move, engage the enemy with normal and/or special abilities, and watch the not-especially-spectacular action until one side is victorious. If you win, you advance a little towards the objective until you're stopped by more bugs. If you lose, you deploy some new troops and pick up where your old troops left off when you got them massacred.If you really love the Starship Troopers flavor, you'll get that for sure, and it will probably motivate you to finish the game. But if you're like me and are primarily motivated by the opportunity to dominate the numerically superior enemy on their own turf by masterfully coordinating a perfectly equipped crack squad that even includes some veterans you've managed to keep alive since the first mission, like in Terrran Ascendancy, you won't be much better off than if you were playing the RTS minigame in Space Rangers 2. I know I've barely played the game, but after more than ten boring missions with no reward besides a handful of new enemies to counter with the new types of now-relevant troops graciously and conveniently unlocked by the admirals and generals seemingly tasked solely with restricting my tactical options to limited unit types and generally ensuring even simple objectives are more of a hassle than they need to be, I'd rather just read the spoilers about whatever else Starship Troopers: Terran Command may have waiting for me than experience any more of it myself on the off-chance the game actually does get good, eventually.Maybe if they added a non-linear strategic campaign that includes building and preparing invasion forces and occupational conquest, and/or expanding the tactical game by implementing persistent stats and equipment, this game would suit me. But as it is, this game is inadequate in almost every area. I do hate to leave a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: An asymmetric single player RTS.RTSes are rare these days and this game certainly filled the void after my second run through Iron Harvest. This is not a AAA game, but it is very well executed within the constraints of its budget. It looks and sounds good. It also excellently uses the license of Starship Troopers (movie(s), not the book), drawing heavily from its over-the-top militarism and ever present propaganda. Even cutscenes between missions are done as motion comics styled as heavily biased news reel and visually inspired by propaganda posters.  The game is single player only and only playable as Terran Federation. This makes sense, as it is heavily asymmetric, reminding me of They Are Billions. The gameplay is based around proper positioning and use of special abilites. Working with line of sight is crucial. The game has a decent path finding (most of the time, trying to use abilities beyond their range is unreliable) and rudimentary ability to keep and angle formation during movement. There are some features that would significantly improve gameplay and may still be implemented later: an active pause and command queue.  I had a great time with this game. I had done my part. Will you do yours?

_childDocuments_.review: Its a real-time strategy game that is, overall, more forgiving than what would be the average for the genre. That, however, does not mean that the game will always be easy. Towards the end of the campaign missions you may find that some aspects of the game you had found to be forgiving earlier had, in fact, been situational to the earlier missions. Certainly a fun game, and I am a fan of the universe and setting. To a degree, micro managing units can be significantly beneficial, however, it is considerably less intensive, and not necessarily a requirement outside of the hardest difficulty.The game is not polished and needs some bug work, but it is not so significant as to break game immersion, more so just enough to cause frustration depending on the timing. Sometimes trying to use a units ability will be met with no result (pressing q to use the q ability simply does nothing, or clicking on the ability simply does nothing and the unit will continue their regular actions). This can happen by either not loading the ability when requested (press q for air drop and no air drop overlay appears), or by not summoning the ability (press q and the overlay appears, but when placed no landing zone is used, and the ability is still available as if it had not been placed in the first place.)  Given that keeping your units at full strength is crucial for their performance, glitches preventing this from happening, even momentarily, can be seriously detrimental to your progress.Sometimes when a unit is given an order, the unit will act very strangely. For example, flamethrower units told to attack move will sometimes ignore enemy units close to them in order to run at a unit further away. Sometimes attack move will result in an unexpected path of movement. Commonly the order of your units in your firing line will randomly change without cause when moved or attack moved, requiring you to re-organize the units to your desired formation multiple times when making moderate movements. For some units attack move will cause them to move closer to the enemy than their maximum range, especially in the case of fleet units. Fleet units have a very short range, so when attack moving with a group they naturally move to the front lines when they're more of a support unit, which is fine, but they may be the only unit that will continue to move towards the enemy already within range until they are literally touching them.Although I do not think this is a bug, it is worth mentioning that attack move when used in small spaces with large numbers, generally results in none of your units attacking as they move due to breaks in line of sight from overlapping units. Occasionally this may result in a small group of enemies completely wiping a large force that should have easily dispersed them. Might not be a bug, but it feels sloppy.Luckily, the auto-save function allows glitches such as described above, frustrating though they may be, to only cause minor problems. The consistency of the glitches, however, is still very common.Overall, if you're a fan of RTS games, or of the starship troopers universe, it is still worth a buy in its current state. I would hope the game is updated to address some of these issues in the future, but it was a great way to burn about a 24 hours worth of game time on the campaign alone.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely good game and a very good RTS take on a classic movie universe. There are mechanics in the game that are revolutionary for an RTS (for example you can't shoot through your units, you actually have to make an effective firing line). There is a unit for just about every scenario, and I found myself using different goups of units in different scenarios and environments. Additionally, this is a very fine looking game, and comes with very few bugs (no pun intended; there are actually a lot of "Bugs" :P). Before we get confused I'll list a few of the more notable issues I've noticed: - Some minor pathfinding issues in which units would get stuck on nothing. More often then not repeating the move order fixes the issue.  - Sometimes hives constantly spawn bugs even when they're not threatened, which ultimately results in me confronting literally hundreds of bugs when I finally decide to clear out a hive. I am not sure if this is a mechanic to dissuade people who take their time (like me) but it can make some missions extremely difficult if those hives are not dealt with quickly. - There were a few issues with troopers moving into hives that were already cleared, and I didn't explicitly order them into those tunnels. - Not really a bug, but sometimes units can shoot through hills.  - Sometimes unit icons get really big, or sometimes they stay hanging over an area that the unit is not at. Other times, the icons move on their own but then pop back into the right spot. - Some issues with select/de-selecting units, but nothing bad.Besides that, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of the series and looking for a good RTS to sink some 15-20 hours into. I'm excited to see if anything else is done with this game, it's really good!

_childDocuments_.review: “If we can use an H-bomb--and as you said it's no checker game; it's real, it's war and nobody is fooling around--isn't it sort of ridiculous to go crawling around in the weeds, throwing knives and maybe getting yourself killed . . . and even losing the war . . . when you've got a real weapon you can use to win? What's the point in a whole lot of men risking their lives with obsolete weapons when one professor type can do so much more just by pushing a button?'Zim didn't answer at once, which wasn't like him at all. Then he said softly, 'Are you happy in the Infantry, Hendrick? You can resign, you know.'Hendrick muttered something; Zim said, 'Speak up!'I'm not itching to resign, sir. I'm going to sweat out my term.'I see. Well, the question you asked is one that a sergeant isn't really qualified to answer . . . and one that you shouldn't ask me. You're supposed to know the answer before you join up. Or you should. Did your school have a course in History and Moral Philosophy?'What? Sure--yes, sir.'Then you've heard the answer. But I'll give you my own--unofficial--views on it. If you wanted to teach a baby a lesson, would you cut its head off?'Why . . . no, sir!'Of course not. You'd paddle it. There can be circumstances when it's just as foolish to hit an enemy with an H-Bomb as it would be to spank a baby with an ax. War is not violence and killing, pure and simple; war is controlled violence, for a purpose. The purpose of war is to support your government's decisions by force. The purpose is never to kill the enemy just to be killing him . . . but to make him do what you want him to do. Not killing . . . but controlled and purposeful violence. But it's not your business or mine to decide the purpose of the control. It's never a soldier's business to decide when or where or how--or why--he fights; that belongs to the statesmen and the generals. The statesmen decide why and how much; the generals take it from there and tell us where and when and how. We supply the violence; other people--"older and wiser heads," as they say--supply the control. Which is as it should be. That's the best answer I can give you. If it doesn't satisfy you, I'll get you a chit to go talk to the regimental commander. If he can't convince you--then go home and be a civilian! Because in that case you will certainly never make a soldier.”― Robert A. Heinlein, Starship Troopers

_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Overall not a terrible game, just lacks quality of life aspects that it desperately needs. Like for example, many missions involve splitting your attention between defending a point while also launching counter attacks, but as the game advances your units tend to get chewed up if you're not actively running micro on them.Also the target prioritization is a little basic, if you're not specifying that you want units like snipers and rocket troops to counter the key targets they're meant to take out they will instead aim at the closest chaff swarm enemies unless, again, you micro every individual unit.Also for such a micro intesive game the controls sometimes feel a little odd. Multiple times activated abilities just didn't feel like activating, forcing me to send the order more than once.It also sometimes feels like there should have been a game-speed option. I'd have more fun and less stress if when things got hectic I could slow it down just a little bit.Also scorpions OP etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from a couple of missions where you barely had the right units to finish it (I ended up just spamming one semi-effective unit rather than think about proper unit composition), this is a very good if somewhat short (finished in 20 hours, but 20 missions!) tactical squad game with minimal resourcing / base building.I wish they had had access to the movie's soundtrack as that would have been amazing ... and the voice acting, particularly for the 'Would you Like to know More' guy was a bit flat, but otherwise, a wide range of missions, voiced throughout, a wide range of interesting units (even if some eclipse and should really just replace the previous ones), so I'd give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: If steam had a normal rating system i'd give this game a 3 out of 5. The game is super fun especially if you like starship troopers, however the way your units behave drove me bananas during a lot of missions.The units in this game are a weird mixture of all the things that annoyed me playing 90's RTS games when i was a kid, combined with a lot of "modern" concepts like line of fire and lot of special abilities.The only two commands you have with your units are move and attack move (they do just that).while in attack move they do engage the enemy, however they won't co ordinate their position to allow other units in the same group a clear line of fire (which is a big concept in this game, your units wont engage unless they have a clear line of fire). instead you get a huge mess of units in which only 1-2 have a chance to attack. clicking on the enemy directly will cause only the units who have line of fire to attack, they wont attempt to spread out automaticly, you have to micro manage it. also while in attack move they somtimes won't engage and instead move right in front of the enemy before attacking/standing there and getting butchered.The game is also super fast paced and lacks a pause button so getting a good position on the attack is near impossible.The game works well when you have a single small army. large army on the attack becomes a moshpit fairly quickly and the bugs will annihilate all your support units because they somehow reached the front line. Managing 2 small teams on the attack was nearly impossible for me and iv'e been playing RTS since the 90's so i think i have a little bit of skill.other that those frustrating moments, the game is really fun and i enjoyed it.Buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Good: Starship Troopers game. Very well polished. Bad: The mission where you have to escape with just your dudes and every radio outpost doesn't work/heal your units and the dumbass sniper sneaking mission. Just let me build my massive army of Mobile Infantry peons wanting citizenship, make them earn it and I'll destroy bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review I have not yet complete the game, although I am most of the way through. I find it quite enjoyable. It rewards tactical use of all your resources and units and does a good job of capturing the feel of the universe from the movie. There are some very minor issues I've had with pathing from time to time and very minor issues with targeting. This is something that happens in most RTS to some degree or another. Overall I would say its a good game for a good price.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: It seems the game was silently moved away from, the devs teased some sort of lava planet and put up a roadmap but it's just dead in the water at this point.The should've probably went for the more traditional approach of building bases and gathering rss. Since this is one of those NuStrategy games like They are Billions, it would've been perfect to add some sort of Co-op like how you can share units and coordinate with your friends in Men of War AS2, instead they focused on... ehm... "not very smart" additions like scoreboards and "challenges". Clearly the game lacks focus and """creativity"'''. Soooo... no don't buy it, it's trash. Since the game is limited in how you acquire units, the maps feel very linear and the way you battle out bugs just falls apart when the field is more open.

_childDocuments_.review: Will you enjoy this game?- You like the Starship Troopers movies and find them fun to watch despite their arguable quality- You don't take Starship Toopers seriously and embrace it's sillyness- You realize this is no AAA priced game- You want to have a good time without expecting the next groundbreaking game of the decadeIt's just plain fun, somehow. Shooting bugs and seeing them die or burn is just fun. There is not much else to say. It's a squad based RTS with light base building and one goal: shoot the bugs. The music score is the same Starship Trooper score you recognize and love. The voice acting is pretty good. The voice lines are cheesy and 100% fitting. The graphics are alright to good, depending on how much you care about it. Sounds and models are what you want from Starship Troopers. Would you like to know more? Then spend 24,99€ and install FedNed on your device, today!Play on Hard or Brutal. Maybe I should finally read the novel. Go get 'em, soldiers."If we ain't dying, we ain't trying."

_childDocuments_.review: Very simplistic RTS game. Its about the same level of complicated as Halo Wars. However, its still pretty fun and has a sizable campaign, taking me around 17 hours to complete on Normal. The only main issue I have are some of the missions have some insane difficulty spikes and feel very unfair. Other than that, its actually a surprisingly simple fun rts game.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: It captured the essence of the movie, but the gameplay mechanics were boring/repetitive. Looks like most of the effort went into the story and theme, but hardly any effort went into the RTS (real-time strategy) basic aspects. Reminded me of playing those old random RTS games and comparing them to Starcraft or Total War games.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers is a pretty solid RTS game. Can see it as a good introductory game for people who want to give RTS games a try without worrying too much about some of the key concepts of RTS games like resources and base building. Unit pathing can use some work and the attack move is spotty. If there was one thing I wish they could implement is a separate campaign in which you get to control, customize and upgrade your own MI division units, making your own mark in history within the Starship Troopers lore. Otherwise, good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the devs missed out on an enormous opportunity by making a game that just outright lacks ingenuity and is just a grab at nostalgia from the SST movies. The entire game just feels like a mod that one guy made in his spare time, not something that has been in the works by a dev team for any notable amount of time. Other than being tied to the SST franchise, there isn't anything this game brings into the RTS genre that hasn't been done already. If you want to spend $40 for some SST cut scenes this is your game. - Bare-bones RTS with repetitive missions, no skirmish/multiplayer modes, and pretty lackluster combat. - Bug movement speed is a brisk walk compared to the movies.- No Tech tree or base building.- Only able to replay the bland Campaign missions.- The cut scenes seemingly took priority over gameplay.- Be prepared to restart multiple missions as the objective log will not progress at key points. - Even though this is a pretty gruesome universe there is little to no blood textures and your soldiers will borderline T-pose    and fall over once killed. - Difficulty has no affect on bug spawn rates and numbers. It only affects your troops damage output by reducing it. - Tankers/Plasma bug target finding is countered by just running in a circle.- Numerous ability and interface bugs during combat.- Units are unable to shoot on the move, and raise/lower their weapons between each shot causing them to bob up and   down like some kind of whack-a-mole game.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, tower-defence-esque RTS. The fun:- Watching bugs die by the dozen.- Setting up defensive perimeters against swarms of bugs.- Having that feeling of just barely holding out against the bugs.- Music has some suitably 'epic', but cheesy, tracks.- Loved the propaganda videos at the start of every level.- Campaign is fun, if somewhat brief.The weird:- Not much replayability (no multiplayer, only two 'challenges', no 'skirmish' mode, no 'last stand' type mode, etc.).- Sound design is average (some weapons don't sound great, units don't feel like they have 'weight').- Campaign story is pretty much just the plot of the first Starship Troopers movie - it's good fun, but nothing spectacular or memorable.The bad:- Unit balancing feels a bit off - some abilities / units don't have impact / some abilities are just flat out better than others.- Scorpions are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - they turn some scenarios from fun engagements to just annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (for context - Scorpions are tough, armoured, ranged, single-entity bug units with a sort of splash attack. It's fine to deal with them in small numbers, but some scenarios spawn these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things by the dozen).Overall - good fun, recommend when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played Company of Heroes or World in Conflict then ST:TC will feel similar. Being a Tactical RTS there is no base building per se, though you can 'call in' supply depot and other structures that provide more advanced units. This is fairly micro heavy game if you want to ensure victory. Its also not as fast paced as starcraft nor is it as smooth flowing as CnC. That said the slower and purposeful movement of units and enemies allows for greater degree of control when micro managing. The latest DLC adds a lot more contentI think the game is fairly polished. Havent run into any bugs so far and the animations are mostly good. One thing I dislike is that there are no unit selection tabs. So you cant see the vital stats of whatever unit you are controlling. This makes it feel a bit low on details. It would be nice to see current units stats beside just a tiny display on the corner showing their veterancy. It would also be nice to be able to allow units to autocast their special weapons like grenades. There is bafflingly no graphics setting either other than a single drop down for quality.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to complain about a few of the units/missions.. I'll start with the good, the graphics are good, the game runs great on older equipment. The missions are mostly fun.Now... to complain a little.The mechs suck!, like really suck. I'd rather use rifleman than use them. Same for the power armor troopers. Normally when you are introduced to a new unit, and then get forced to use them for a mission... you get to see how cool or overpowered they are, but no... not in this game. The mechs have a ranged weapon, and a flame weapon for melee. The ranged weapon..simply put is terrible. I can't tell if they set the accuracy of the weapon to 2% or the damage of it to 2%, but the ranged weapon is useless... which the computer use as the default attack mode. You can't disable ranged attacks on it, so you are forced to micro them into melee lest they die at range to units even engineers can run up to and handle on their own. I can't tell if the weapon is bugged or not, because the power armor units seem to suffer with the same terrible weapon. I say it may be bugged, because it often looks like they are somehow hitting obstacles that aren't there(at least I hope they are bugged, because otherwise the units are just useless). And now to ♥♥♥♥ on the power armor units... they seem to only be able to kill the most basic teir 1 bugs, and you have to use them and only them when they are introduced.. are you fighting only teir 1 units? oh nonononono. They can take a beating though... which is pretty much all they can do, and ffs don't go after the hives out of order on their mission. I know you can normally kill hives in any order you want... but go for the wrong one first and you unlock more powerful units to all the hives... and now you can't take out any of them, of course this wouldn't be an issue if you had any better units are your disposal... but no stuck with the poopy unit.Overall still a fun game despite me wanting to cry about having to play a couple of missions with crappy units.Edit; had to come back and edit this... the power armor units only suck until they become elite... and then become a good unit.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and It's worth the price. It has a long campaign as I'm halfway through at 10 hours at seasoned difficulty. It expands the lore of the movie and acts like the second movie that wasn't made. Its got a mix of MOWAS2 and simplicity so its not overly complicated. The soldiers are tightly packed running around like in the movie lol. This game came out a few months ago and its done amazingly well compared to most companies on getting things done. A new update is coming soon apparently that will give editor and workshop, which I think will make this game have a concurrent community that will stay for years later. I hope they make a multiplayer either campaign or on custom maps. Its a classic fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game and it is a good game! not many bugs but also not game crippling ones mainly to do with path finding.Always been a fan of ST, sadly this game doesn't offer more then one play through to be honest, I completed the game I can play scenarios but there needs to be more content more worlds and would love to see a bit more of a base building asset etc.All in all a good game but doesn't offer replayability but it is still work a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: The game really punishes you for trying to split push, you need to have all your eggs in one basket making a death ball go around the map. there you go i just spoiled your whole game play later on in the game. the only strategy is playing leap frog with your squads.It looks good, adds to the world building, though idk what is truly cannon in this franchise, but unit control leave so much to be desired.Also the insanely... I don't feel like that got the point across, let me try again. *ahem*INSANELY poor pathing. Told a squad to move up and around this rock, what would be like idk 5m adjustment to a north east movement, turned into a 35m hike around a Boulder (It's not just a Boulder *sniff* its a Rock!) to get to the commanded spot, I found this happened a lot on multiple maps with multiple objects (Boulders, Vehicles, Random things with round edges). i would even hold down the mouse button to make sure the squad wasn't landing on the object. Yet they would go on a hike, away from the bugs like Cowards.Also many times squads wouldn't fire till the bug was slaughtering one of the members, Idk if i spawned some kinda pacifist squad or poor coding. I thought it was like maybe a LOS issue but the Wars come in packs of 4, and they would shoot the stragglers in the pack but only after the fastest bug attacked them first... So that lead to some... Annoying game play.Honestly there needs to be like a Meh button, if its on sale get it, it'll be fun I can't imagine these issues are as punishing in lower difficulty as it is on high, but on high difficultly these mechanics were brutal and only lead to grinding game play instead of strategic play.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun-ish. Its a fun game for sure, but don't expect any sort of "story". You barely get a "premise" in the campaign missions but still, the gameplay is entertaining enough to make the game worth it (with a discount in my case 20%). If you liked the movies and want to kill some bugs, go for it, just don't expect a ton of content.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: The game successfully captures the feeling of the first movie, all the well done parody shines and the combat feels right.That being said the serious lack of replayability does hurt. there's no skirmish, only a couple of non-campaign missions and you never get to play as the bugs. A definite pickup on sale if you aren't bothered with the 15-40 hours of total gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review:
Starship Troopers - Terran Command is a thrilling real-time strategy game set in the Starship Troopers movies universe. Take command of the Mobile Infantry and do your part in the war against the Arachnid threat. Build, develop and control your armies to strike an effective balance between tactical superiority and strength in numbers. Ensure that human civilization, not insect, dominates the galaxy now and always!

Planetary Campaigns
Fight for control over an entire planet in the campaign mode, where the storyline and missions develop according to your choices and achievements on the battlefield. Remain obedient to the demands of Terran Command no matter how costly or ruthless to benefit from exclusive unit types and special abilities, or follow your own path to glory to become an irrefutable Hero of the Federation. Develop and customize your forces through a detailed technology tree and upgradeable leader characters that can be assigned to your units.

Tactics & Numbers
While the Arachnids can rely on virtually limitless numbers, the Mobile Infantry must develop effective tactics to overcome this imbalance. Deploy your units at strategic locations to cover vital choke points and gain superior firepower through tactical use of elevation levels. Be wary, however, that battle mechanics such as True Line of Sight and True Line of Fire also allow Bugs to lay ambushes around every corner, as they are well known for their use of surprise attacks and deception.

Units & Abilities
An expansive range of unique units, weapons, and special abilities are at the disposal of MI commanders. Infantry squads armed with Morita Assault Rifles and MX-90 Fragmentation Grenades form the mainstay of your forces. Rocket Troopers deliver deadly payloads with pin-point accuracy while Engineers are vital to shore up defensive positions with MG turrets, barricades, and minefields. As a campaign progresses, technological breakthroughs unlock the true potential of the Federation's arsenal with Power Armor infantry squads, TAC Fighter airstrikes, Marauder mobile suits, and many more developments optimized for spraying Bug ichor across the battlefield.

Key features
- Dynamically generated campaigns for virtually limitless replayability.
- Dozens of unique unit types, each with their own special abilities.
- Terrain elevation, True Line of Sight & True Line of Fire provide deep tactical gameplay.
- An extensive technology tree to develop and customize your forces.
- Persistent leaders can be attached to units and upgraded throughout the campaign.
- Heroics, explosions, gore, and Bugs. Lots of Bugs.

name: Paleo Pines
detailed_description: Welcome to Paleo Pines, a charming island known for its friendly dinosaurs, quirky townsfolk, and mysterious past. Here evolution took a different path, creating a world in which humans and dinosaurs live together in harmony! Set out with your dino companion, Lucky, to uncover the island’s secrets and discover new dinos. Your arrival on the island is met with welcome curiosity by the local townsfolk who can help you on your quest (and just might give you more work to do!). Together with Lucky, build a thriving ranch, assist local villagers, befriend adorable dinosaurs, and unearth the island’s lost history to build your cozy dino sanctuary. Set off on a lively adventure with your dino pal, Lucky, who you’ve known since she was just an egg. Is she the last of her kind? The other parasaurolophus are missing, and it's up to you and Lucky to uncover their whereabouts. Explore Paleo Pines, a charming island filled with friendly townsfolk and hidden corners. Build a new home, make friends, and unravel the island's lost history. Get ready for a journey filled with delightful discoveries alongside your trusty steed Lucky! Set up your home base on the island as you go about your parasaurolophus quest. Paleo Pines is a place where you can express your individuality and creativity; no two ranches are the same! Build square pens, or not (although the locals might have something to say about that!). Use decor to build a romantic garden, give your ranch a witchy vibe, or go full-on-farmer with rows and rows of tilled soil. Furthermore, customize your character as you like with a variety of features, curate a colorful collection of clothing—with different items to be found in each area—and change your style using the wardrobe! The island of Paleo Pines is a dino lover’s dream! A collection of cheeky dinosaurs roam the wild areas waiting to become your friends, as well as ranch helpers. Coax them near by mimicking their calls with your flute, then seal the deal with a tasty treat and trustworthy nose boop! Gain their trust by creating cozy pens and learning what keeps them happy. Dinos move around and some are harder to find than others, or may appear only under special conditions, so new discoveries await you as you explore the island. As your ranch grows, you’ll soon have a dino haven for all your new friends. Check out the Dino Journal to learn all about the creatures that roam the island. Farm to your heart’s content, growing crops all year round with (and for) your dino besties! Start out planting and watering by hand, but earn your new friends’ trust and they’ll help you deliver a roarsome harvest that you can trade with the townsfolk. As your ranch grows, you’ll learn that each dino has a special farming skill to help you with your tasks. With a bit of love, care, and attention to detail, such as matching soil and season, you can grow the highest quality produce in all of Paleo Pines. Soon you and your dino ranch hands will be the talk of the market! There's plenty to explore out in the wilds of Paleo Pines, from the flowery fields of Veridian Valley to the high canyons of Ariacotta. Make the most of each day by venturing throughout the lush landscapes across the island, each with their own charm, collectable items, and dinos to discover. Take a leisurely stroll through green meadows, foraging for wild crops as you go, or hop on your trusty dino mount on a hunt for hidden corners. Pause to watch wild dinosaurs playfully interact with each other, right before your very eyes. You'll never run out of things to find or dinosaurs to befriend! A quirky (but friendly!) array of townsfolk on the island can’t wait to meet you and help you on your quest. Granny might have a stubborn side, but get to know her and she’s an ol’ softie. Building friendships within the community is just as important as building friendships with your dinosaurs. As you ride dinos, farm, and explore, you will come across new characters, each with their own story, items or knowledge to share, and gossip to exchange. Help them out day or night by completing quests, opening up new areas, and visiting the stores and community hubs. And who knows—they may even gift you something to spruce up your ranch!

With a bit of love, care, and attention to detail, such as matching soil and season, you can grow the highest quality produce in all of Paleo Pines. Soon you and your dino ranch hands will be the talk of the market! There's plenty to explore out in the wilds of Paleo Pines, from the flowery fields of Veridian Valley to the high canyons of Ariacotta. Make the most of each day by venturing throughout the lush landscapes across the island, each with their own charm, collectable items, and dinos to discover. Take a leisurely stroll through green meadows, foraging for wild crops as you go, or hop on your trusty dino mount on a hunt for hidden corners. Pause to watch wild dinosaurs playfully interact with each other, right before your very eyes. You'll never run out of things to find or dinosaurs to befriend! A quirky (but friendly!) array of townsfolk on the island can’t wait to meet you and help you on your quest. Granny might have a stubborn side, but get to know her and she’s an ol’ softie. Building friendships within the community is just as important as building friendships with your dinosaurs. As you ride dinos, farm, and explore, you will come across new characters, each with their own story, items or knowledge to share, and gossip to exchange. Help them out day or night by completing quests, opening up new areas, and visiting the stores and community hubs. And who knows—they may even gift you something to spruce up your ranch!
short_description: Welcome to Paleo Pines, a charming island known for its friendly dinosaurs, quirky townsfolk, and mysterious past. Befriend dinos and enlist their help to fix up your ranch and farm crops to create your cozy dino sanctuary! Then set out with your companion, Lucky, to uncover the island’s secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit of a mixed bag in it's current state, but overall I do recommend this game. The overall aesthetic is cute as heck, down to the lil scale texture on the dinosaurs. I love the research notebook aspect of the game, its a nice touch and really adds to everything. However the game has a good handful of limitations and quality of life changes that would improve it greatly. Firstly my biggest gripe is the damn jump button. Either add a jump or don't, don't give us whatever that stopping midrun and going "yippee!" bs is.  Like, it honestly drives me up a wall to be running, and then force of habit use my spacebar only to stop midrun and do a stupid lil yippee. It completely ruins any flow you may be in and adds nothing to the game. I get that the lack of jump is to avoid platforming over obstacles, but like, you could just make the spacebar do nothing. I would love the option to turn off jump entirely. Customisation options are also very restrictive, There isn't really any long hair options and it would be nice to have more color choices. Additionally I would really like to be able to change the clothing color on the character create screen instead of each clothing style only having one color choice. right now it feels like you can pick from a few very cookiecutter options as most of the clothing pieces don't work with eachother well and only work with one/two other pieces each. It would be nice to be able to feel like your character is more personalized.Overall the game is a cute and cozy romp through a colorful little world of dinosaurs, and I highly recommend it to anyone whose willing to overlook a handful of issues and focus on the core gameplay loop. This, a warm blanket and a cup of tea would make for a nice fall evening.
