Maybe we could have storage access points across the map?I enjoy the farming, but I feel it's a little slow and there's some jank in movement. More seeds and things to plant too!More locations and more dinos! I hope more are on the way, I don't want this game to die, it just needs a little more and I'm really rooting for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game was disappointing.I waited for the release for a long time because the concept was so wonderful and interesting! Who wouldn't want to play a cute game with dinosaurs?Unfortunately, apart from the cute dinosaurs with decent animations, there's nothing else in the game that could engage you, and some aspects are just downright annoying.- The world is empty. There are small areas on the map where a few dinosaurs spawn, usually in groups of 1 to 5, and they roam around in that zone, occasionally making noises. That's it. You won't find any fish in the water, insects buzzing around plants, or any small creatures hiding behind rocks in the canyons. There's nothing to immerse you in this world or make you feel like it's alive.-NPCs. Non-player characters in the game are supposed to have personalities and their own stories, but it's not evident. They stand in one place on the map all day and then teleport home in the evening. Sometimes, they're just stuck at home all day, preventing you from accessing a shop. Their quest assignments are random, and you might have to spam the board with tasks for several days to make any progress in a character's storyline, which can be confusing and irritating.- Shop system. The shops operate on a barter system, meaning you can't sell products above a certain limit per day. This is a strange choice for a farming game because if you're growing high-value crops, you can't sell even a single harvest at once. Furthermore, if your harvest sits in a chest for too long, it degrades in quality. For instance, I had 68 three-star carrots, but after a season change, they became two-star carrots.- Cooking and crafting. You can't create even the most basic things in the game, such as fences or food for your dinosaurs. While there is a cooking function, it forces you to go to the center of the map and use a significant amount of resources that you could have sold to feed your dinosaurs or improve your farm. Additionally, the food doesn't provide any essential bonuses and is essentially useless.- Unclear dinosaur taming systems. After bringing a new dinosaur to the ranch, you must make it your companion before you can use its abilities. To do this, you need to make it happy. I brought a Kentrosaurus to the farm to clear bushes, and I ensured its happiness for about five in-game days, but it didn't became a helper. So, I decided to leave it and tame a Therizinosaurus. After a few days with the Therizinosaurus, I received a message in the morning that the Kentrosaurus was now a helper! How did this happen? I hadn't interacted with it during this time, and there weren't enough dinosaurs in its enclosure due to a rearrangement, so it couldn't have full happiness. How should this system work?- Bugs. The game has many issues, such as when you dismount from a dinosaur on the ranch, it runs to the other end, making it hard to catch. Small dinosaurs get stuck in farming tiles and can't plant seeds. Sometimes, when riding, your dinosaur can get stuck and atrat to move very slowly. The camera gets stuck in textures during 'Friend Song' mode, or the "yoohoo" option doesn't appear when hovering over a wild dinosaur. One particularly memorable moment for me (possibly containing spoilers, though it's a fairly obvious plot point)  As a result, I received a new quest for the main storyline that I had already finished. Of course, I couldn't track it because it didn't appear in the journal as the storyline was completed. From the text, I understood that I needed to approach an NPC and then feed her mango, but how do I know if I need to do anything else now?- A vast number of collectible items that are not categorized by regions. If you want to complete an achievement, you'll have to suffer. The game doesn't show you how many collectible items are left in each region, only the total statistics, so you might have missed one item at the beginning, or in the forest, or in the canyon. Or maybe it's in NPC's quest. You'll never know.- The more dinosaurs you have, the more problems you have. Again, you can't craft food for them, so you'll have to spend more money and time to clean up their waste, or they'll become unhappy. This leads you to think that it's better to keep the necessary minimum of dinosaurs on the ranch, or else you'll end up spending too much time and resources on them. This is despite the fact that the ability to tame dinosaurs is the game's main feature.Overall, it was just not a very good gaming experience. As much as I might not want to, I cannot recommend this game for now. I hope it will change in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this game a negative review was a tough choice for me. I've been following the devs on social media for well over a year, they seemed to have put a lot of love into the concept but sadly the game falls short. It just doesn't seem finished and still has a very strong early access feel to it. The price just isn't justified for what you get. The art style is cute, and the dinosaurs are adorable but that's about where it ends.The npcs are bland and few in number, with the same old handful of requests. Hat, notebook, lucky trinket.. It doesn't take you long at all to find the same few spots they spawn at. Given that the npcs seem to have such little luck taming and understanding dinos, you would think there would be requests that involve you using dinos they don't have to help with things, e.g clearing branches/rocks or loaning them a helper for a day or seasonal requests. A lot of the other in game tasks feel very repetitive too. First area, repair a windmill. Second area, repair a windmill, third area.. you guessed it, repair yet another windmill! The areas also feel empty, aside from the dinos there isn't much around to see or do. Even the "townships" are tiny. There is a number of game mechanics that seem to be either not fully polished or lacking. Below are just a few that stand out to me.-**I have been corrected by a fellow player that feeding a dino it's favourite poppin replenish it's stamina, thank you** As far as I can tell, there is no way to regain stamina or your dinos stamina aside from sleeping until the next day. (I had thought that eating food or giving dinos food would regenerate stamina but it does not seem so unless it's a bug.) - Trees. Probably my biggest pet peeve! Even after trawling through the forums, I have not found anyone or found any way to remove trees on the farm. You would think with the size of some of the dinos that at least one could knock a tree down. Some of the trees are annoyingly placed so you just have to build around them.- Your house, it just sits there. This is the first farming game I have seen where you can't go inside your house. You can't even cook in your own home, you have to go to a pot by a lake half way across the map to cook. You can paint your house, but most of the colour options look awful. There seems to be quite a few decorations like a sofa, bookshelves, end tables etc that look like they were intended originally for inside decor which makes me wonder if the devs had considered it, but dropped the idea. - No crafting. At all. You can't even craft a simple fence, but you can apparently rebuild the town windmills no problem.- Not much to do. Even though this is a farming game, outside of farming and shovelling dino crud, there is little to do. No fishing, no romanceable characters (which isn't a biggie) no breeding dinos. You get one event each season.-Item placement. A lot of the items place weirdly and don't line up. I tried creating a cosy nook using the trellis only to find you cannot line them up to make a corner without an obnoxiously large gap. The stone fences also do this annoying thing if you try place them coming off of the wooden fences where they add one extra bit of wood where you would like the stone to go. It does not look good.- Limited range of decorations. Originally I didn't mind Marlo's slim pickings when it came to decor, thinking it would expand over time. However, I am well into year two now and the range has hardly budged.-Fruit trees, I am in summer year two and have only received an apple and a mango tree, but I have not yet found them for sale anywhere. - Dreamstones, while I understand the need to control numbers on your farm (though honestly I think space requirements plus the amount of work you have to do feeding, petting and cleaning after dinos would be a good enough combination to control numbers) dreamstones are very limited in number, they don't respawn, and you can't buy them meaning you are quite restricted in the amount of dinos you can keep.So far the only bugs I have encountered are dinos hitting "invisible" walls on my farm even though nothing is there so I have to go around. It is annoying but not game breaking. I hope that the devs will take all the feedback into account and make changes to the game so that I can happily return and change this to a positive review, but for the time being, I can only recommend this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels very unfinished, like early EA unfinished. The controls are not great, there's a lot of stuttering and screen tearing, also a few crashes. Unless there are patches to fill out the empty world, fix the buggy, slidey controls and optimize the world, I probably won't repurchase. Lots of cool stuff but cute dinos don't make up for shallow mechanics and tedious controls. Such a cool concept, I wish I could recommend it. I'll keep an eye out for patches, though

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a brutal, realistic depiction of what it would be like living with real dinosaurs, where the player or his pets could be killed at any... Oh, wait. That's "Ark," I'm thinking of....THIS game is a rather UNREALISTIC depiction of life with dinosaurs, where the player gets to cuddle with T-Rexes and carnivores happily share the farm with herbivores without so much as a fight breaking out. Oh, yeah... the large dinos let you ride them and use them to smash rocks, clear brush, chop (aka "smash") wood, and run races. The little ones plant, water, and harvest your crops. About the biggest conflict you'll run into is when your dinos get too crowded and you have to split them off into different pens to avoid making them unhappy. I gather they can leave, if you don't keep them happy, but as long as you feed them every day and give them a nice warm bed free of poop, they're fine.Definitely NOT a survival game. And not very hard. You can't romance any characters, and friendship is more or less a given, if you do the character quests. You spend some time patching up arguments, which is sweet. It's adorable "children's" fare, not that I don't enjoy it as an adult. It took me about 100 hours to complete the main quest (finding other Parasaurolophuses to be companions for your first dino), and I'm still working on some side quests, such as rebuilding the town library. My biggest complaint is that, like all farming sims, I end up with so many animals to take care of every morning, I don't have much time for anything else. It starts to wear on me. But otherwise, this is a delightful game.

_childDocuments_.review: This one truly sets a new standard for Farming Sims. Not because it has ground-breaking new farming systems or relationship systems, but because they've managed to seamlessly integrate these adorable dinos as your "Happy Helpers". It's such a clever idea and after as many hours as I have in the game, I can't do anything but recommend it. Full Video First Impressions Review: Pros:- Tons of Dino (38) & Crop Variety (44)- Dinosaur Coat Rarity makes for fun "Ultra-Rare" hunting- Crop Ratings- 3 big open zones with varying biomes to explore- Friendship system with your neighbors- Dinos are GREAT helpers on the farm, worth taming and having- Tons of exploration and hidden secrets- Long main story quest that takes you all over the zones- Daily quests to keep you occupied and build friendship / provide income and awesome items- Town events with some great rewards- Big plot of land to clean up and beautify- Tons of decorative options for yourself and farm- Easy to navigate UI- Map that shows your location at all times- Your guide shows you information about your ranch, dinos, friends, discoveries, quests, and more- Items stack only once, except for different qualities- Storage is huge and has multiple access points- Adorable Dinos + Sounds- Fantastic visuals of the world despite simple character modelsCons:- No tool wheel, so your items will take up space in your bag- Inventory gets full very easy- No Fast Travel so it can get monotonous walking everywhere at times- No Free Save, can only be done from menuNeutral:- No Dating System (we don't want it, this game is too good to worry about it)Much more to come in our Final Review a month from now, so drop a sub to the YouTube if you want to keep up with it ^.^

_childDocuments_.review: this game is lovely and there are many good things to say about it! however you can read other reviews with more details for that, I'm mainly here to communicate a few frustrations I have in hopes the developers see it.1: the cooking is not well explained in game. maybe this is just a me problem but I cannot understand what it's asking me half the time and the foods all appear to do nothing. I will run across my ranch feeding my dinos (and chasing Lucky) and my bar will be empty before I'm even half done. honestly, WHY does the player character need a stamina bar in a game like this? or at least why does running lower it? _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the demo, so of course I went and picked up the full version and have been playing the heck out of it.  I got so absorbed with just the dinosaur raising (and smashing my way through objects on the map) that I only recently unlocked the Forest (and my progress on the main quest has sort of stalled).  Pros:-Cute dinosaurs with good animations and even cuter noises-Decent amount of clothing options and hair/eye/skin colors during character creation-Different rarities in color of the dinos, and they have far better odds than shiny hunting-Staying out past your bedtime doesn't have any negative consequences-Very cozy and relaxing-The dinosaurs have favorite foods, and it's fun to give them different snacks to figure that out-Plenty of things to collect off the ground, and some items only appear in certain weather-There's farming, and crops are not seasonal so you don't have to worry about that-You can order decor to place around your farm-As you befriend the NPCs, they start to give you discounts in their shops-Colorful and "chibi" cartoon visuals-Easy to get extra saddles, seeds, and earn shells with the Bulletin Board in the Plaza-Dinosaurs are essentially your "farm tools", and perform tasks such as moving rubble, breaking rocks, watering crops, ect-There's controller support, and it doesn't feel clunky-If you fail to tame a dinosaur (it runs away or falls asleep), you can try again-Mari can help you get back a dinosaur you released-You can find small amounts of herbivore food out on the map (you won't even need to buy any when you only have one or two dinosaurs due to that)-You can adjust, via the Settings, how fast the in-game day goes with three settings; so if you like to take your time, it's a great option-You can purchase clothing (and the ones you can select increases with more purchases)-The devs (and mods) are active in both Discord and the Steam forums, and at least the mods frequently interact with the players (and they seem to be nice people)--Cons:-The music, while pleasant, feels like it has so little variation in the notes that the songs feel shorter than they are; I feel like I'm listening to the same few notes over and over again on repeat-There are very limited hairstyles for boys-The clothing to purchase/order is on the expensive side during the first year-Some dinosaurs (rock breakers and stompers) move very slowly, so if you don't mount up a decently fast dino after telling them to follow you then it takes forever to get somewhere-Your player movement speed is rather slow, which can get annoying when moving around your ranch-Dinosaurs can level up and get more stamina, but your player cannot-There's no minimap, and it's super easy to get lost (even in Viridian Valley) -Inventory space is limited, and it takes a while to expand it-There's no overlay telling you the time; though there are popups when it changes from Morning to Afternoon (ect), the only way to see generally the time is to check your journal-Many dinosaurs, though different species, can perform the same tasks (watering, breaking boulders, ect)-The cooking mechanic is a bit clunky-Unless it's in your recipe book, there's no indication in the flavor text of a cooked food item of what buff it gives you; this forces you to either try it and find out (thus wasting the food if it's not a buff you want) or look it up online-Cooking often takes a lot of one crop (usually from 10-20; Classic Stew is a big offender in this), which makes me wonder if we're making a single portion or trying to feed the entire village; last time I made soup, even for four people, it didn't take 10+ carrots.-There is a level of RNG with harvesting the crops, which means it is not set in stone when a day loads (I had to reset once after getting softlocked due to a T-pose glitch, and actually wound up harvesting less of a crop than the first time...plus I didn't get bonus seeds with the second harvest like the first one)-Fruit trees take WAY too long to grow on your farm, and I'm in Year 2 with all areas unlocked and still cannot purchase fruit tree seeds anywhere -Some quests are extremely vague.  While it's a nice pace from hand-holding games, it also means that you often get little to no direction (such as restoring the archway to the desert area.  The quest just says "order Planks/Rope" and doesn't tell you how many you actually need)-Some NPC quests require an absurd amount of a crop (some want 20), and others request items later on which you have to order (thus, it'll cost you shells to complete the quest and you don't get any back)--Bugs/Misc:-Taming dinos can be a bit finicky in that sometimes you'll repeat the Friend Call exactly and the dino will just stand there and wait for you to get it right (even though you already did)-There's a current bug where sometimes, when you go to mount Lucky, you instead wind up T-posing through her (forcing you to restart the game as there's no way to get unstuck or do anything)--Overall, it's a really fun game (and very easy to lose track of time with), but you might want to wait for a sale.  Upon release, the game was discounted (to around $26 USD), and even that is questionable.  I'd put this game more around a $20 pricetag, especially with all of the current bugs (some of them game breaking which can softlock you).

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games along the lines of Stardew, Animal Crossing and Ark, this is the three rolled into one without as many screams. I'd recommend this game to pretty much anyone, it's cute, it's cozy and it has THE cutest dinosaurs! I see complaints about the game performance. I'm running a 3070ti and DID have issues in the demo, but the full game runs fine.People who are saying about limited dinos, YES there is a final limit of 45 BUT you can alto tame unlimited dinos and swop them out via Mari, who can always track your befriended dinos you send to the wild. People saying there needs to be a hotbar, there is some kind of that, press 1-5 to hit the first 5 spaces then you can scroll through the rest using hotbar.Complaints about the missing discount? _childDocuments_.review: -Super cute dinosaurs that you BEFRIEND not TAME. This system uses Poppins and certain textures or flavors like: Spicy, Crunchy, Juicy, Fragrant, Etc to befriend these scaley friends. The dinosaurs all make their own super cute sounds, even when they're tired and out of stamina. You can pet all of them, and they DO interact with items in your pen! FE: You put down a flower garden, they will sniff! They will wander and roam around the farm from time to time but like most other farming and cozy games, there is immense amount of detail that you can put into the pens, you can have different fencing, natural decor, unnatural decor. The pen size depends on the amount and size of your dinosaurs. Dinosaurs are able to stay at your farm using dreamstones & keeping them happy. There is a large assortment for dinos to choose from and - It is a very cozy game! I will say that the soundtrack can be repetitive but its soothing. It does keep me calm after working 15 hours shifts at work and helps me relax enough to feel tired. - Farming is different than what I've seen in other games. There are certain games that dont quite scratch that TRUE farming itch for me, but this one does everything. From tilling the land, fertilizing the soil, planting seeds, and then having to plan your next crop on the soil type, is fun for me. You can always change a soils type with fertilizer but im weird. Your dinosaurs have certain skills that can help you till, water, and even harvest the crops. If you are interested in Automated farming, this is another thing in this game, though you probably wont get it for about 1-2 seasons after you start!  Those little ones are not only cute, but also extremely helpful. - THE JOURNAL, let me elaborate. This thing shows you crops you've discovered, dinosaurs you've discovered, artifacts & Relics, your friends and their schedules (ie where they are in bold). It is extremely helpful, includes a calendar you can plan your produce on as well! This is going to be your best friend when it comes to finding information on something. This game is pretty simple in my opinion but can feel overwhelming when you have a bit going on. My advice? ADVENTURE!!!! Adventure, forage, collect, everything you see! Doin this in your first few days will help you substantially later down the line. -Next up, quests. The quests are fairly simple, go gather materials, give your friends some produce, discover a dinosaur or gather more information on it, The first few quests are pretty imperative to learning how the game works. I would avoid getting too many quests from the task board in the town, or sticking to what you know you have! Mari need some wood? Aight i got some for ya. OUuuuuuuuu Marlo needs tomato? I haven't gotten to that so ill hold off momentarily. For some this is common, for others, heres a piece of pie. The tasks on board, will say who it is from, and doing enough for one person can land you some discounts as well. It is a good way for players to make shells, IE: you have 5 wood in your inventory, you can sell it for ehhh, 15-50 shells? Look at the task board. OHHH Owynn needs 5 wood for produce,  shells, etc? Yea sure man. You can sell the produce (or hoard it like me), you can feed it to a dino for some extra brownie points. You also get brownie points for helping someone on the TB. -Clearing your farm; such a daunting task but doing some a day at a time will get you materials that you will desperately want later in the game, (looking at young me, selling all my wood for some shells cuz i was greedy), and most importantly, you wont be flipping out trying to clear space for a dino youve just brought home. Which brings me to my next part, PREPARE YOUR PENS BEFORE GETTING A NEW DINO!! my gosh it is so much easier setting one up for something and then being able to just 3 3 it into a home space for the time being. Clearing your farm also offers items you dont have to buy, theres decorations, troughs, chairs, ponds, etc you can find just by clearing your farm out!

_childDocuments_.review: I had watched the development of this game since the first piece of concept art surfaced on my tumblr a long long time ago. i patiently waited for it to come out, stalking discords, wikipedias and social media pages for 4-5 years straight! it felt SURREAL when it finally came out and i was able to play the demo and then finally indulge in the full version the day it was released. i'm not even joking when i say paleo pines is my #1 favorite game ever made. the artstyle and gentle colors are so pleasing. i'm a huge fan of moonglow, sky blue, portals, pearl and sunray colorations! my only qualm about this game is that the dinosaurs sound like a bunch of apes. not dinosaurs. but that's only a qualm to me because i'm really into huge visceral roars as a stim noise! and this game doesn't have a scary bone in it's body so the monkey noises do fit better into the vibe of this cutie little game than huge thunderous rumbles do! _childDocuments_.review: I've only played Paleo Pines for a short time, only unlocked the second area, met half of the NPCs and befriended 5 of the 49 dinosaurs. (I might rewrite this after I finish it)Paleo Pines is a promising farming sim with a diverse dinosaur roster. The graphics are cute and colorful, but the game still needs some improvement to be more interesting, like:- Lack of NPC interaction. - Quests often feel like chores because they only ask players to take, collect, or find something.As you know, you can ride dinosaurs in this game, and each dinosaur has its own abilities. Dinosaurs are the focus of the game, and they even have favorite foods. You need to give them cupcakes (a sign of friendship) that are appropriate from their favorite foods. However, it is a bit annoying that you cannot collect resources while riding a dinosaur, you have to dismount, collect the resources, and then mount again.Overall, Paleo Pines is a good game for dinosaur lovers. _childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game for so long on social media, I feel like almost the start of their development when they started advertising. And they did not disappoint. The dinos are adorable, the cozy aspect is very nice and is just a relaxing game altogether. The style is cute and cartoon-y, the sounds for the storms are so relaxing. And the music has a nice charm to it. And I know alot of people don't like that the dinos don't sound like "actual dinos". But the squeaks and beeps and grumbles are adorable. I love wandering into my archaeopteryx pen and they all beep at me with little love hearts over their heads.If you're looking for a new cozy farming game, with a little more to it than just farming and collecting resources, this is the game for you. However, I will add some things to my review that I would have liked to know before playing. It doesn't make this game bad or anything, it's just something to know if you have particular tastes or expectations.- Decorating your ranch/pens is very basic. You cannot mesh decors hard against other decors or structures. So there are gaps between fences and bushes, or garden plots and decors. I've still made some pretty pens and areas, but if you're looking for any in-depth decorating, the game doesn't revolve around that.- There is a limit on how many dinos you can have on your ranch. And it is very annoying since there are so MANY PATTERNS AND COLOURS for different dinos. So, if you're looking for a "collect them all" game, this isn't it. You will have to prioritise what dinos you want to collect, or need on your farm. You have no idea the disappointment I felt when I found that out. The Troodons alone have sooo many pretty colors and patterns. I want them all!- After a while, the limitation on the dino collecting gets more annoying when you reach a spot in the game where that's all there is. Either while waiting for things to grow or be delivered so you can finish quests. Overrall, I adore this game. The devs did an amazing job making a game that ticks alot of the boxes I've been looking for in a cozy game. My only complaint is the limit on how many dinos I can have. Please, please, please let me have more. I don't care that there's limited space on my ranch. I'll make it work!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on a total cozy sim game bender, and the fact that Paleo Pines added dinos and special ways they can help you around your farm is amazing! I played the demo and loved it and bought the game seconds after it released. It's definitely super cute and amazing to get lost in for hours. Lots to do, collect, discover, etc. Just some small issues that I have had that I hope get fixed or addressed at some point:1. Bag space - it's basically nonexistent and currently not expandable. If you've got enough snacks and goodies to tame dinos in there plus your tools, you have maybe 3 slots left for collecting gatherables and no way to sell or stash on the go. If you chuck stuff from your inventory on the ground it doesn't despawn. but that's still not really the best solution. I'd really love to see either a toolbelt to remove the tools from your bag or some way to expand the bag space.2. There needs to be a place to sell your stuff on your farm. Every other farming sim has that, so you don't have to run into town and pray the NPC is there still/at all.3. Dino feed needs to be craftable/farmable. Currently, you're stuck having to buy all the food for your dinos. While I get it for the carnivores (it's a cute game that even kids could play, going out to slaughter stuff to feed your carnivores might offset that a bit, but then maybe add fishing..?) But especially the herbivore food...??!?! We're growing crops here, and you're telling me we can't turn it into plant eater food...??4. On the fly tooltips would be so helpful. I have a couple of the little dinos that are discoverers/tenders etc. but have no idea how to use them. Give us a quick run through of new skills we discover perhaps?5. Crafting tables! Most of the other cozy sims I'm playing atm have crafting tables to craft decorations (currently outsourced to an NPC, ok that's fine, I can live with that) or seeds! Especially being able to make new seeds from the harvested crops is an absolute must in my eyes, because buying new seeds is VERY pricey. And honestly it makes just as much sense to be able to extract seeds from old plants as it does to be able to feed them to my dinos.Just kind of my quality of life dreams that I hope will get added at some point, just so the game feels smoother and more like a farming and less like a shopping sim :D

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED AFTER 100% JOURNAL AND MAIN QUESTDisclaimer: this is my first steam game, I downloaded steam specifically for this game, I am by no means an expert, and early access has only been out a few daysI love this game so much. The graphics are cute, the villagers are cute, and the dinosaurs are absolutely adorable. I have only had a few small bugs only one of which required quitting to the menu and reloading. Main Complaint: There is an overall lack of guidance and the character quests are often vague. I had over 100 hours in-game before being able to find all the journal pieces, few of which are in particularly hidden places. The tiny icon that only shows up within a short distance and in certain angles is not enough direction. And when I spend four hours searching for the last of 20 pieces, it's pretty frustrating to not know the general area of the last piece. Maybe allowing Agami or Mari - or even a board post - to provide direction when there is only one or two pieces left would be infinitely helpful. - In the same vein, the white dots for locations or repair quests were definitely not obvious. In on of the historical locations, I had to be in the bush looking at a precise angle to even have the prompt appear. Visibility is a major concern.- Dinosaurs on the farm are *sometimes* leashed to their pens and run away as soon as you dismount. This was not an issue in the demo, so I was surprised by this at first. Unsure of whether this is a bug or feature, but it is confusing either way.- It would be much more convenient to use the flute on befriended/helper dinosaurs while mounted. - The movement while riding larger dinosaurs, especially bipedal ones, is pretty nauseating. Smaller helpers are tolerable, but the issue increases with size.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like slow-paced cozy games with a collection aspect (and dinosaurs/archosaurs/dimetrodon of course!), then this game is for you! Otherwise it might be best to watch from a distance.Like many say, its simultaneously simple enough to mindlessly wind down and play but has enough complexity to make you have to plan and set things up for awhile in an attempt to create the perfect farming set up, especially with the crop rotation mechanics that I don't really see in most games that incentives buying more than one seed type to get the most out of your farm.Dino friendship mechanics are also fun! Reciting tunes back to dinos and trying to experiment with what they enjoy to befriend them and being able to use them to automate parts of farming or ust collecting them is fun but… that's about where my praise ends.The main story quests and character-specific quests were a treat,. If very simple, but otherwise are rather lackluster and rarely give you more than a saddle or a couple hundred shells, occasionally you’ll get seeds, but unless I'm unlucky, its a very small selection, and occasionally you’ll get decor for both the farm and pens.While limited, the ordering (not crafting!) system is nice, though so far clothing is a bit limited in style and color, which is more of a personal gripe. Cooking is another mechanic that's nice… if you have the ingredients. It became easier now that you can have a cooking pot at the house, but otherwise was a huge chore for things that mostly didn’t matter and are now fun buffs to save up to make a profit.My only big gripe is that after playing through the game, theres not much to do aside from finish off side quests and continue to farm and collect dinos, which are unfortunately capped at 45 with no renewable way to grab dreamstones, which is more than enough for every dino but can be a bit restricting unless you start a new farm just for collecting those rare critters, which can be fun but many might not enjoy replaying the game since the replayability, personally, is not super high outside of wanting to collect more dinos.That being said, updates roll out frequently, whether they major or not! I hope to see more be added in the future outside of new dino colors, though the occasional QoL and bug fixes are always welcome post release!(I also hope to see a devkit for modders in the future, but that might also be wishful thinking)TLDR; very fun simple yet relaxing game to play, especially if you really love dinosaurs and more relaxed and unique farming/ranching mechanics compared to other games like Stardew Valley, but outside of the main story and some side quests/projects can feel very empty or unrewarding, though with it receiving active updates I optimistically hope there will be larger content updates in the future :)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since I saw a preview a couple months ago and for the most part I'm not disappointed. I'm recommending in the hopes that with the support the devs might address a couple of the aspects that I think need more polish.Positives:-Good, cute graphics. It's not the next Horizon Zero Dawn but it doesn't have to be. It reminds me a lot of Slime Rancher graphically.-Good variety of cute dinosaurs-Unique/cute mechanic of the dinosaurs helping you on the farm-Dinosaurs feel different and unique not just reskins of each other-Lots of different color variations to collect-Very low key, low stress fun and exploration. It's like Slime Rancher meets ARK Survival EvolvedWhat The Devs Can Improve:-Building. It's kind of painful to build the pens. I wish I could move the camera more freely instead of having to physically move my character. Pens could also do with a sign or something on the outside that you could check for things like size/biome type/food type etc. I know you can check this in the journal but it's tedious to do so at times.-Dinosaurs path/collide strangely with the decor/sleeping spots and can get stuck/have a seizure(visually) on some of the stuff you put in the pens-Lack of pen decor/sleeping spot/trough variety. This game definitely suffers mid/late game from a lack of anything to work toward outside of the dinos. None of the decor really feels all the special or exciting or anything to work toward really. You get the same bonuses regardless and none of it really has a big "wow" factor.-Can't customize your house because you can't go inside it at all. They still give you indoor decor despite this? Which just feels weird. I don't want to build a kitchenette and library in my dino pens. I want to put it inside my home.-Quests are repetitive and boring. The rewards kinda suck too. They usually just end up filling up my inventory with seeds I don't really need. They are definitely not at all generous with the currency either, usually 30-60 is all I get for the few quests that DO give money.-Value of money feels really weird and skewed. Saddles are only 250 (in addition to getting them as quest rewards all the time I think I have like 10+ of them rn) but a wheat seed is 1000?-NPCs feel pretty flat and boring. I don't know or care who half of them are. I remember them based on their dinosaurs.-Kind of small exploration areas and they have loading screens. I don't really care about the secrets/artifacts/etc either. They're just sparklies to pick up.It feels like the devs released Paleo Pines with dlc/expansions in mind. Which honestly I wouldn't really hate. The game has a lot of potential for events with special dinosaur skins for different times of the year or new areas with new dinosaurs and secrets. I think the game not having much of a story is fine but they should really lean into the collecting aspect. That's part of what makes a game like Slime Rancher work so well. I want more stuff to work for and collect besides just dinosaurs. Better pen decor (with bonuses maybe?), furniture and a better place to put it, ranch upgrades/buildings, outfits etc.It's a good game and most won't regret buying it in my opinion but it could be a GREAT game with a little love and polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: If you like dinosaurs and farming sims, buy this game when it's on discount, you will probably enjoy it a lot. I do not recommend it at full price and my reasoning is below.The concept of the game is strong and really fun. Befriend different dinosaurs, look for rare colors, keep them happy, and manage your farm while progressing on the main storyline. And, for the most part, the game IS fun and entertaining, and quite addictive. And props for the LGBT inclusion, which was one of the points that brought me to play the game in the first place! But...I understand this was made by a small indie team, but the game lacks a lot of polish. Several features are way too confusing with little to no explanation provided, being introduced at weird, non-intuitive points of the progression. The animations are pretty simplistic, and for most dinosaurs there is no difference in the walking/running animations aside from speeding them up. The shaders look pretty bad despite making my steam deck(with great support btw) fans go wild. The ending, despite being  pretty good gameplay-wise, feels lackluster and anticlimatic. I also hated having to  - this is something for a completionist to do, not a basic story challenge. The quest system gets very old, very fast, with almost nothing being specific to the NPCs who are requesting things - you always get the same generic response when completing them. I feel like the devs should focus on touching up the aspects the community has been complaining about, instead of releasing new colors and species every now and then. Mod support would be fantastic as well - it could offer a good compromise and allow the community to shape up the game how they want it to be. For example, for me personally I didn't like that I was pushed to have Lucky be my "favorite", for obvious storyline purposes. I would like to be able to befriend a dinosaur myself and have that be my "main" one. A mod for this could be quite fun!All in all, for the full price of 30 euros, I didn't feel like it was worth my money. But I DID spend a good few hours on it, and I enjoyed them. I hope this game keeps being worked on as it is a refreshing take on the genre that obviously took a lot of passion to make, and has a strong community behind it.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed this game for few years before release, I loved the art style and concept. Who doesn't want to work with some dino pals and explore a cool prehistoric world. However, as it stands, I cannot recommend this game for purchase at it's current price point.The game feels unpolished, several features don't feel thought out or cohesive, and I'm surprised they want to call this the 1.0 release. Paleo Pines' biggest draw is the dinosaurs. The narrative is that they're your friends and they help you out on your farm for room and board, basically. It gives me a lot of pokemon vibes. However, the dinosaurs don't control well and have a very small pool of skills and abilities that separate them out and make them wanted on your farm. I find myself frequently frustrated when my Styracosaurus cannot plow the tile right in front of them. My Gallimimus waters in a seemingly cone based pattern, but randomly misses 1-6 tiles of plants. My Wuerhosaurus has no obvious indicator for how many crops it will harvest before I click. The small dinosaurs are probably the most egregious of these flaws. As far as I've seen they all possess two abilities "Tender" and "Discoverer". Discoverer lets them alert you when a resource you can pickup is nearby, they do not dig up anything or produce anything, they simply let you know when the very visible resources (they either sparkle or are very distinct from the environment) are close to you. Tender seems to be the ability to tend small sections of your farm without input, however, 20hrs into this game I have yet to encounter a way to enable this ability. This makes a whole category of dinos freeload on your farm while you crash into fences with your unwieldy John Deer dinos. The world feels... unfinished. The characters and environment have a very cute style. I particularly enjoyed the Dapplewood area, it had a very cool and mystical feeling that made finding dinos and resources feel magical. The other areas feel dead and lifeless in comparison. There are dinos almost everywhere, but they don't do much but run into each other and make little noises. The obtuse geometry and invisible walls make exploration tedious, and the need to move very slow dinos to remove obstacles creates a sort of tension where you wonder how much or your limited in-game day will be spent shuffling your dino to the remote Valley's edge or running into invisible walls. The characters are all flat and pretty lifeless. They mainly serve as shopkeepers and quest givers. There is a friendship mechanic, and when you reach a certain threshold you can do a little quest for them to gain a perk (like sleeping in their house or a discount at their store). However, all the characters feel so expressionless. They fill certain stereotypes and rarely deviate from those roles while offering little in the way of meaningful or emotional dialogue. The granny is tough and doesn't want the whippersnappers holding her back! The carpenter is manly, but has a secret soft artistic side. The vendor is sarcastic and only cares about money. The weird character is weird, but is just misunderstood and misses their homeland. Very run of the mill stuff.Overall, the game feels like it should've been released with about 10 dollars shaved off the price and an early access label. I find myself wondering if the game might've been a little more polished or thought through if they hadn't pushed so hard for a multi-platform release. Those resources could've been spent on testing, character writing, and mechanics development instead of porting the game to consoles. However, I can understand wanting to reach a broader audience with your game and looking to escape the steam pigeon-hole. Overall, I'd give the game a "Good Try". So many of these farming games want to be distinct from Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, and Story of Seasons. So much that they end up reinventing the wheel and leaving all the great innovations in the genre behind. Paleo Pines has fallen into that trap. I hope the game gets a face-lift with a lot QOL and major content patches, the game has charm and some fun moments, but it's not enough at the moment to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Stardew Valley meets Jurassic Park, what's not to love? I've been following this game since day one of its announcement. I'm probably one of the first people to hear of it period, and I was definitely the most hyped for it. In a time where modern games are released as unpolished and buggy, borderline unplayable messes, Paleo Pines is a breath of fresh air. It did have its bugs, as does any game, but I never encountered any that inflicted on gameplay on any system. As a massive fan of farming sims and, of course, dinosaurs, this game is a dream come true. Ever since I discovered the wonderous joy of farming games, I've been asking, "What if this, but with dinosaurs?", and lo-and-behold, here it is. _childDocuments_.review: Solid, relaxing, charming dino-ranching sim with adorable dinosaur models which will steal your heart. The gameplay is smooth and easy to follow. The human characters are personable (despite some, including the player model, having toddler bodies), but the dinosaurs are the real stars of the show. The variety of species, colors and patterns is amazing, and they are all a delight to interact with. It's a shame there isn't room to keep more at the ranch, but it's not a massive game with a huge dev team so understandably there are limits. Similarly, it might have been fun to make the house interior an accessible space with its own decorations, but this is a minor complaint; the bulk of the game was always going to be spent outdoors.I have a few minor quibbles with the UI in terms of changing between tools and skills, but my inner ten-year-old is ecstatic at riding a T-rex through a desert with joyous abandon and I can't argue with that. Absolutely recommend if you like cosy sims and/or were a dinosaur-obsessed child like me. Childhood dreams: achieved.

_childDocuments_.review: So I am no professional reviewer at all, and I don’t expect anyone to read my review to any extent, but it helps me sleep at night writing down how much I enjoy a game and how I think it could be improved. I am first going to ramble about all the amazing things about this game.I don’t know how much of it is coded and how much I make up in my head, but do all of my dinos have personality types? Some sleep all day, some don’t start work until the afternoon, I have some who splash in the ponds, I have others who will run into me iif i pet a dino other than them. Some are foodies and like everything I give them, some are picky and only like one food. And it varies within the species as well. I love it. I love seeing my dinosaurs “escaping” to go check out the orchard, or running up to the gate the second I walk by.Whoever came up with “let's put the crops on the tiny dinos heads” is an actual genius. It is so adorable. Everything about tiny dino helpers is amazing. Walking slowly to throw out water, digging the hole for the seed like ??? Magnificent. 10/10. The glitch where they accidentally kept the crop on their head has left and now I have a chili/pumpkin that flies around instead. I miss the potato hat.There’s a lot of main quest related things I enjoy, which I won't go TOO deep into detail, but I did like having to explore to unlock more quests. It was frustrating to be a slashing dino/stomping dino away from SOMETHING cool but in the long run I can appreciate it. I wish the map had markers that appeared so I knew where I had found stuff, so I could perchance go “Oh I already found a tablet piece over here, I should be looking somewhere else.”.Regarding the things I think could be improved, I recognize this is an indie game company with limited resources but I am an autistic individual with a hyperfixation and I like when Systems And Probabilities Make Sense.Too Much Money, Not Enough Options:So I’m late-stage in the game, I can only imagine a few more quests remain after the one I’m on, and I have 70k+ shells. And nothing to spend it on. I don’t necessarily want more things to buy, but for the money system to be… overhauled. I feel the seed -> food -> cooked meal -> shell railway is a bit uneven, and I’ve absolutely abused it. However, I do think merchants should have their amount of money they can spend increase over time because I’ve had stacks of 0 star corn and turnips rotting in my inventory because Corlan can’t afford them. If the artisan merchants (Orani, Marlo, Freya) offered some of their custom order items in their shops, but at an increased price, then that would make me happier. For anyone who hasn’t started the game yet: making recipes makes money! Pippin buys food, Corlan buys crops. To lead into the next part, don’t sell your resources!!!Weirdly Balanced Quests & ResourcesThe quests are very interesting and I do like the character growth we see in the NPCs throughout it. My disgruntlement comes from having to accumulate 500 fiber to make 50 rope, or 200 forest wood for 50 planks. In the beginning of the game, when you’re clearing your farm, resource gathering is easier. But mid-late game when I’ve spent a lot of resources to build furniture or pens, it’s a little frustrating traveling to the forest and only getting 30-50 wood and having to dedicate half a day to doing so. I’m sitting on top of 70k shells I can’t spend, but I have to travel to the forest and HOPE I don't get 5 wood each from the 3 logs that spawn. If Marlo could sell wood, even at a HORRIBLY EXPENSIVE price, I would be happy. Farm DecoratingI am struggling so much with the decorating system. The large squares each item is locked to makes it difficult to place things naturally. I love the heather bushes! Because when you rotate them, they favor a side of the square. I would be ecstatic if every object did this. I struggle with furniture too, since you can’t place objects on top of each other but they’re also so spaced out it doesn't read correctly. Random Things-I know why some dinos are loners, but surely they need a friend :( The Allosaurus and Postosuchus sometimes have friends in the wild!-If Gallimimus are pack dinos, then why does the achievement want 5 in a pen for a dance party? Wouldn’t they be sad? :( - I should be able to sell back custom orders I did not like. I did not know “desert wall” was not a clay fence for my pens >:(-On that note, desert biomes need a themed fence/chest that fits the pens better than just a wood/rope fence.-Dyes already exist in the game. I think it would be super cool if we could dye clothes.-If dinosaurs who migrate to different biomes could have multiple pen biomes and be happy, then there could be some really funky pen combinations.-Why is Avery like that? He spawns once every 200 years and then for Shenanagin he hides his tiny dinosaurs in places my character can’t interact with. Absurd.-I feel like Triceratops don’t have a lot of color variation, like they’re just one big blob of color. If the pattern on their crowns and feet were just increased slightly in size it would suite them better.-On the topic of color, Gallimimus come in 2. Green and Green. I’ve only seen ONE differently colored Gallimimus EVER. And I've played this game for 100+ hours.-If a dev is reading this pleasepleasepleasepleasepleaseplease change Psittacosaurus to herd I need all of them, my little pistachios.-Veloci Sponge wants to be a Strawberry Delight. Pasta Compsognese and Pasta Carnotaura want to be Plain Pasta. Is this a bug or am I intended to suffer?-I know WHY there’s a limit on dreamstones in the game. But I don’t like it. I want more dinos. AT LEAST give me 50 dreamstones so I can be satisfied with a multiple of 10.anyways thank you, love you, this is an amazing game i shall continue playing for another 200 hours

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It's fun whimsical, relaxing, and still challenging but in a very low-stress way. The design of everything is very thoughtful and intentional, and I adore the satisfying process of filling out my journal with dino species, plants, and artifacts. There are a few small irks I have with gameplay that could easily be smoothed out: some characters have schedules which dictate when they are in the main villa or when they are at their homes/exploring. Sometimes this limits if you can turn in a quest to them or purchase items. So far its been difficult to learn all the schedules, and sometimes whether a character is in the villa feels random (thinking specifically Granny Agami). Maybe some chapter in the journal can help you write down these schedules once you get to know the character? Other than that, I've experienced a bug or two, some vagueness in quests leading to difficulty completing them, and some confusion over items relating to farming. Other than that, there is so much to explore and secrets to uncover. I feel like I'm just barely scratching the surface! If you like games similar to Slime Rancher, then you'll love this game. I can see a bright future ahead of it and hopefully DLC down the road!

_childDocuments_.review: While this game does need a few things to improve quality of life, I absolutely adore this game and look forward to it's development. I highly recommend playing it and giving it the attention it deserves. Pros: 1. Dinosaurs, LOTS of dinosaurs. The dinos you collect can also have skills to help with farming and exploring the world. There are currently a whooping 38 species of dinosaurs. Ranging the tiny and adorable Microraptor to the massive Tyrannosaurusrex (A staple of any dinosaur game).2. Interesting taming mechanics. I really enjoy taking the time to tame dinos using their likes and playing a song on the flute to get their attention.  3. Cute and unique style. It's very easy on the eyes and the visuals create a calm atmosphere that can melt you in for hours. 4. You can pet the dog. (dino)5. You can find a unique ray of dino colors that range from common to very rare and the addition of albino and melanistic always excites me in a game.Cons: 1. Not enough character customization. When I play a game like this I like to feel as though myself is in the game. However there isn't enough to really feel that way in this game. Plus with everyone excluding the old lady character and anyone with a beard they all look like children. Though I understand this is a style choice, just not one that I enjoy. 2. Character interactions are very "Meh". Nothing really grips me as immersive. 3. I feel like it's missing a few things. Like fishing, house decoration, paths for your farm, out buildings, etc. I think it would be interesting if there was a better solution for the lack of dream crystals as currently you cant really have all the dinos you want without the limited amount of crystals. While none of these really ruin the game for me I hope to see modding become available to the game to be able to add just a bit more substance.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying: I've been following Paleo Pines since it's concept art days, and I have eagerly been awaiting for this game (that felt custom made for my exact preferences) to finally release. This game has far exceeded my expectations! I absolutely love it, and I am so glad that this game was launched after the ups and downs of development.  It is because I love this game so much that I am going to be a bit harsh because this game still has a long journey up ahead but not only is this game beautiful it also has beautiful potential. But be aware when you buy this game that there's a sense of overall incompleteness. Some minor spoilers to quests but nothing too specific. - The dinos are clearly the heart and soul of the game! The designs are amazing, they move great, and the sound design for their calls are endearing. I love that some colors are rare, it makes it fun to see what I want out of preference, or out of rarity.- The music is so cosy and comforting! - Lucky is my sweet child, and the purpose of the game is clear: Lucky wants to find other dinos like her, but no one has seen a parasaurolophus in generations!- The design of the game is beautiful! The lighting as the day progresses is perfect. - The farming mechanics are a lot of fun! I really enjoy learning how to grow the best produce.- Everything dino related is a 10/10 in my book.- There are some glitches, but the ones I've encountered have been limited and small which I'm happy to see in a still new game like this. Okay let's get a bit critical here. There are three major pressure points that I feel would be greatly improved with some quality of life changes, and tweaks.You get the usual cutscenes and wiser character walking you through the basic mechanics but only the bare basics. A lot of core mechanics of the game are not explained (not even in the manual). The importance of biomes? How to change biomes? The difference between small dinosaurs and large dinosaurs?  What's a tender? What are the purpose of these plant decorations? On your own! Are you on a quest and you don't know if Marlo lost his chisel in the valley or the forest? Can't check! And repeating dialogue does not help.  Besides asking if you've done the quest, they other no other reactions/hints/guidance to the quests they've given you. I don't expect everything to be handed to me, but I think some structure will help the to feel like I have a paddle instead of a hand to keep the boat afloat.  The dinosaurs are the best part of the game, obviously, but it does not help that the NPC are a bit lacking when it comes to characterizations. The dialogue runs on repeat and I don't feel like I'm connecting with the characters. Marlo declared out of the blue that we're pals and I get a 5% discount at his store. I'm not complaining, but I'm unsure why I have a better relationship with him than the rest of the town. One of the elements I enjoy from games like Stardew Valley, is the different relationships you can build with the NPCs, and every relationship is a result of your own actions (give them gifts? Dig through their trash?). I feel I have working relationship with the NPCs in Paleo Pines because the only way I interact with them is through their stores, or when I'm dropping off yet another hat.  There were some parts that I thought two characters where going to have a conflict and I would need to mediate but no, the NPCs rarely interact with each other and even moments I thought were going to be key turned out to be inconsequential.   The main way to get money in the game is through quests, the little ones on the bulletin board (another mechanic that is not explained). I don't care that those quests are the same three on rotation, the rub is that the larger quests are often feel incomplete. One quest involves tracking a dinosaur that at this point most players have already encountered, but what does it mean to track one? The foot steps are too small and there are five different paths to get to the dinosaur herd so it's very easy to miss the specific sequence you need to do in order to progress. It's a lot of work to either grow the item you need, or wander around the valley for what feels like little progression.  Overall this game is amazing and the 18 hours I've put into it already felt like nothing. I believe that by the time the game is a year old there will already be some major quality of life changes, and hopefully elements that make the game feel a bit more alive. I'm hitting that wall of frustration where I have to wait for specific seasons, or specific moments to happen before I can feel like I'm progressing. I plan to come back after a while and see if there have been some helpful changes since I first played.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could say yes to this game. But at this point in time, I have to give is a solid thumbs down. I've been waiting for this game to release for years. And since the official release, it has been extremely buggy. Personally, I have never seen a game so broken on release outside of ARK DLCs so it's really been a downer. Invisible walls, npcs not having actual schedules, a lot of quest are left open and you have to figure it out and a lot of the times, it's really not obvious (or it's something silly like waiting for an NPC to be at the location /at night/), and the biggest kicker has been the failed cooking. A core mechanic of the game being absolutely bugged and unable to make anything but Classic Stew. While I wish I could ignore it, it now interferes with getting poppins from Pippin because of a quest and her stall being shut down until that quest is finalized. That quest requires cooking. Admins on discord say it'll be patched and they have a fix, but instead of putting a patch out, players are left waiting for the day this patch shows up. No ETA. So now, the game gets put into the corner and really bummed. Again, been waiting for this game for years. I wish I could enjoy it more..

_childDocuments_.review: Between the crashing frame rates and abysmal side quests, I can't in good conscience recommend this game.  I'm shocked that this game has as many positive reviews as it does.Some specific examples of my disappointment:1.) When riding faster dinos - and especially dinos with a speed boost - frame rates practically bottom out.  Not to mention, art assets struggle to load in when going at a moderate pace - I can't tell you how often I'd have to stop completely and let the environment catch up with me, killing any utility of a speed-boost dino.  While my gaming rig is certainly not a power-house, it handles games like Baldur's Gate 3, Dead Space, and Planet Zoo with no issue.  It's a crime that a low-poly, highly stylized game with a handful of assets is struggling so badly.2.) The side quests are a mess.  Boring, tedious time-fillers.  The final straw was a Town Billboard quest that asked me to collect a hat from one resident and return it to another.  I accepted the quest from the billboard and realized the quest was given by one of the vendors - right behind me.  Cool.  Talk to the vendor and formally accept the quest.  Turns out, the resident who borrowed the hat was...another vendor.  The one 10 paces across the street to the left.  Talk to that vendor.  Collect hat.  Walk 10 paces back to the right to the first vendor.  Return hat.  Collect reward.  Grand quest complete.  Seriously, is this even a game?  3.) There ultimately isn't much to strive for.  I ended a few game days about mid-day because there wasn't anything else to do.  For farm sims, I'm usually stretching my days, trying to cram as many tasks as possible into each day to make the most of the little time I have, especially for the first in-game year or two.  I was actively skipping time in this game due to one reason or another.  It felt empty.  Look elsewhere for a farming sim.  Disappointed because this one has dinosaurs, but maybe there's a better dino-collecting farm game out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is potentially the first farm sim to keep my engagement and interest for any prolonged period of time. It's cute, charming and overall just takes you by the hand and gets you hooked on what it has to offer. It has so much potential to be better than it already is, but what it DOES offer at the beginning is more than enough to keep you engaged for hours on end.That being said, this game is not nearly as complex or deep as other farming sims - not yet, anyways. It has very few NPCs, limited crops, simple cooking and decoration and only 3 areas to explore. It's most complex mechanics are intertwined with the dinosaurs themselves, which are the star of the show here. I did, at times, find myself wishing for more in-depth systems and more to do. That being said, as development continues and as support flows in, I'm sure this game will bolster its roster of items and dinosaurs and really blossom!! I'm so excited for future updates and what they may add!

_childDocuments_.review: Over all the game is fun and unique. I adore the sounds the dinosaurs make and the over all design of the game as a whole. This will be a game I definitely frequent and hopefully there will be more updates coming to the game with new dinosaurs and areas to explore.My only thoughts:1. The overall lack of in-game tutorial is a bit frustrating. Things the player should know are not explained but rather left for you to try and figure out as you try to juggle keeping your dino buddies happy. One example being what decorations go in the pen to make it the correct biome and even how to uprgade your dreamstones to the correct biome as well.  2. The click and hold mechanic for getting on and off your dino is a bit tedious and time consuming when a simple click would work just fine.3. A personal opinion, the dinosaur I dismount runs off way too fast when I'm trying to grab something from my home based inventory and I have to chase it down. I don't want to have to use the flute every single time I dismount while at my farm to keep my dinosaur there, I wish the dinosaur stayed a little longer.4. It would be nice if there was more info on each dinosaur you find in the journal. What body marking types there are and all the available colors. In order to see what the color is and if it is rare, ect, you have to get it bored so it falls asleep and then approach it with your journal, and even then your dino or another wild dino can startle it awake and you have to repeat the process. 5. It would also be nice if there was an option to build our own request boards to then place on the farm. Having to go all the way to Ariacotta Canyon just to see what requests on the board, then return to your farm to get the items and then go all the way back eats up a lot of time in game that prevents you from maximizing full use of the in-game days.

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines was a game I was really looking forward to after discovering its existence a few months ago. However, I was left more  disappointed than anything. I'm not saying the game isn't worth getting, it just did not meet the expectations I had set in my mind for what I thought this game was about. This is entirely my fault as i did not do enough research. I love dinosaurs and farming sims so i thought best of both worlds it has to be a great game. I would have loved to see more crafting capabilities. I thought we would have a more open world feel where we can gather more resources at the very least I think we should be able to make our own wood planks and rope and not have to wait a few in game days for a delivery. I don't like that we cannot enter our own home so decorating the outside is pointless to me since i barely even look at it its just a glorified storage bin. Its definitely too expensive for what we actually get in game. I appreciate the look of the game and the dinos are all adorable but I have no emotional attachments to the NPC's and barely any attachment to the story line.  i find myself clicking through the conversations just to get it over with. I will continue to play the game because it is cute and i did spend money on it. its not terrible but definitely not what I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Dino farming game.  This is such a fun game to play, lots of areas to explore and secrets to unlock.  While I think the game is fine the way it is, I really hope they update it or an expansion pack to this game.  The game is fun and wonderful, but it has the possibility to be amazing.  Adding a crafting table and a  cooking pot to the farm would be a plus.  Maybe add more story lines.  One thing I really wish this had was a beach,  Sea Dinos, maybe go diving to see the sea dinos, maybe flying dinos.  I love that you can change clothing in this game, I have clothes for farming, for lumberjacking, dessert, forest, exploring, and heading into town.  I love this.  Hats would be cool to have.   Anyways these are my jumbled thoughts after playing over 50 hours of it.  The game is wonderful the way it is, and I would recommend this game for people that like to explore and like dinos.

_childDocuments_.review: edited 10/21/24i hate to change this review to a negative one, but my perspective has shifted. i started playing in december of 2023, but the game came out just a few months before i was ableto purchase the game. i loved it at first, yes, thats why i have logged close to 150hrs. however... after playing for that long ive come to realize this game isnt as good as i initially thought.point 1: its pretty barebones.theres just overall not much going on. each point is gonna get into some finer details, but theres just... not much. you farm, you take care of dinos, go to the plaza for more dino food, check dino spawns, repeat. earlier in you get to do more exploration and taming, but as it goes along it just becomes the same thing every. single. day.point 2: the characters are not only generic but empty.at first you probably dont notice, as youre so entranced with how cute the game is. becauseit really is cute! i can say that much. the dinosaur models are adorable and fun to watch. but the npcs? not only are they a bit uncanny, but i find myself not interacting with them unless i have to. i get that the devs wanted to make this game appropriate for all ages, but EVERYTHING the npcs say seems like theyre talking to a toddler. i havent noticed anyone point that out, but i always feel like the npcs explain things to me as though im 5. the npcs are also, as mentioned, super generic. not only in personality but looks. nothing too exciting about their designs and their personalities are probably "easy to understand" for, you guessed it, a 5 year old. for so few npcs youd think theyd be more interesting...point 3: its almost purely fetch quests.i literally cannot think, off the top of my head, of a single quest that is not a fetch quest.i finished the main story and almost finished each npcs individual stories, and yet i cannot tell you a single non-fetch quest. you are constantly running around getting items for people and its tedious and boring.point 4: the gameplay loop becomes boring.as mentioned in point 1, earlier in you get to have a bit more of a varied day-to-day gameplay loop, but as you progress further it becomes the same routine every day. you check your crops, feed your dinos, go out and check dino spawns, MAYBE get to tame a new dino, probably have to go to the plaza to get more dino food and/or sell crops, go back home, and sleep. repeat. it becomes especially frustrating when youre trying to get a certain colour of dino to spawn and it just. will. not. spawn. once a day starts, you cant log out and come back, as spawns are set for the day. a blessing, sometimes, if your game crashes, but a curse for being stuck in the loop until you get the dino you want. the rng is fun for the first little bit, but just gets annoying to deal with.point 5: theres little to no replayability.this ties in with the previous points. youre not gonna want to replay when the gameplay becomes a repetative loop. or when the stories are boring and all fetch quests. this point is short but necessary.point 6: caring for the dinos only gets harder and more tedious.WHY can we not make herbivore food??? i understand not making carnivore food, running joke of "where does the meat come from, corlan?" haha, funny... but the herbivore food?? its just plants. it looks like lettuce, which is a crop you can grow. and yet lettuce is considered a treat? this just makes it harder and more annoying to care for the dinos! because we will CONSTANTLY have to go to the plaza to get food for dinos we could EASILY be MAKING food for!! and if youre NOT constantly growing crops 24/7 and selling them, you probably dont have the money to be constantly buying more food! at least, if you have more than 10 dinos. i understand its a farming sim, but you have to make sure your crops are 3 star and sell for the highest amount (like the watermelons) or else you simply wont make enough money, ever, to keep your dinos happy.point 7: a lot of mechanics are useless, confusing, frustrating, or nonexistent.what is the point of cooking? simply for gift giving and minor buffs? ive never used cooking except if a quest needed me to cook. theres so many recipes, for what? both cooked meals and raw food just degrade as well, which is SO. FRUSTRATING. worst game mechanic ive ever seen. i get its realisitic, but what???on another note, dino taming is harder than it needs to be. some of the friendship songs are unnecessarily long and remembering which flavour each dino likes so you dont waste an expensive poppin is annoying. i know ive used that word a lot but uuugh. why cant there be a simple UI that shows the information you know about the dinosaur while youre taming it? that would make it so much easier.and one final one so this point doesnt get TOO long. why are there no upgrades? for anything? other than when you fix your house in the beginning. and even that the npcs do it for you, if i recall. but you cant upgrade your house, let alone go inside. cant upgrade the farm in terms of size. no tool upgrades either. cant increase your stamina, which you never have enough of if youre trying to be nice to your dinos and not tire all of them out. no upgrades at all to make your life easier. if i remember theres not even fast travel. granted, the map probably isnt big enough to warrant it anyway, but it would probably be useful.point 8: putting gameplay behind a paywall because your studio is in financial distress.this was the final straw for me. having DLC is not usually an issue in my eyes, but when youre putting entire gameplay mechanics and in game festivals behind a paywall i have an issue. the festivals already in the game are mostly boring and not worth participating in past the first year, and now they want us to pay for more because their studio is failing? i understand needing help and turning to your fanbase, but asking for them to buy your DLC, merch, etc just so you can fund making a paleo pines 2 instead of saving the game you already have seems scummy to me. maybe i misinterpreted, but from the community post the studio made, it seems theyre giving up on improving paleo pines past patches and focusing on makingpaleo pines 2 instead.overall, i cannot recommend this game anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis during my high school, which is so shocking and inspiring that ultimately leaded me into a path of research with Cretaceous paleo-environments and -ecosystems. A life-changing game. Now I am lucky to receive Paleo Pines during my PhD since it gave me the same feeling again that I had ten years ago. Among all dinosaur games that I played, this one provided me with the best balance between gameplay, art and science (although scientific accuracy is not required for a cute-styled game like this, still, the variety of species is more than expected, and the design effectively captured the key characteristics of most species while being exceptionally cute at the same time). 	  For The Isle and Saurian, it is a pure pleasure to appreciate the reconstruction of the dinosaurs, however, it is inevitable to feel bored as a dinosaur some times. For games like Carnivores and Dino-D-Day, it is fun enough to fight the dinosaurs, although I personally would prefer to watch them roam free. Speaking of live and happy dinosaurs, Jurassic World Evolution does allows you to build a zoo and take care of them. Still, frankly speaking, it is more like a dinosaur breeding farm since there is literally no landscape design. With all the pros and cons of these games, Paleo Pines is just a perfect utopia to appreciate your dinosaur companions. I really like the idea of being equal friends with the dinosaurs, you can befriend so many of them and build a true, beautiful home for them (not just a farm) . This game also avoided the predation relationship between different dinosaurs, a smart move. Some part that I really like:1.	The designs of Corythosaurus, Dilophosaurus, Protoceratops, Parasaurolophus, Psittacosaurus, Styracosaurus and Utahraptor are just extraordinary from my perspective. 2.	Tyrannosaurus, despite cannot sprint, jump several meters high in the air , this is so hilarious. 3.	Many dinosaurs have special interaction animations, the dance of Gallimimus is super lovely. There are a potential improvements that I think could makes the game even better:1.	The absence of Sauropods is a huge shame. I understand that it is hard to fit their sizes into the farm, but your Stegosaurus’ torso is already larger than many Sauropods species in real life. Perhaps considering adding a small one?2.	This may already be mentioned many times so I’m not going to talk about in details. The cooking part seems really last-minute work. That’s why I didn’t get full achievements and probably don’t have the motivation to fulfill them in future either. 3.	The description of some quests should be more specific, I didn’t know what to do when I received them. For example, the quest of finding Marlo at midnight. Without the online tutorial it is literally searching in darkness. Also some thoughts about the dinosaur designs:1.	Troodon, Velociraptor and Deinonychus, some times these three species are hard to identify. Perhaps could consider making Deinonychus bigger (which they should be). Troodon may also have some unique characteristics, such as proportionality smaller head, larger eyes and longer legs to make them look more different to the Dromaeosaurs?2.	Some Kentrosaurus discomfort me. In subconscious, spikes are signs of danger and threat, plus the high-contrast stripes on the spikes really make them look like tiger mosquitos or some poisonous insect from a distance.3.	Allosaurus and Carnotaurus could be slimmer to fit better with their characteristic?4.	Coelophysis may be too big——they are as long as Lucky!Anyway, the flaws do not cover up the beauty of this game. In my mind, it has the same status to Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis, and it is really worthy to hold a title of one of best dinosaur game so far. Keep up the fantastic work!
