_childDocuments_.review: So let me get this out of the way first: The game is enjoyable for a time and it's VERY kid friendly. I'd say 8-10 and up are going to get a lot of enjoyment from it. So if you're just seeking a game to plop a kid in front of and they'll just veg out on it, this is a good option. I believe it's a little pricey even for that but it will certainly do in that framework. I will preface that though I have positive things to say first that overall this game has failed in my eyes. Pros:- Colorful, pretty medium sized open world. = Great colors and patterns on the dinos. - Some of the characters are really nice and fun to get to know.= The concept of the game is actually pretty great, for me, I see a lot of inspiration from Stardew Valley, Ark, and almost Pokemon. - Has a nice lean into biology and ecology that isn't present near enough in a lot of monster/dino/animal games. Sadly, that's about where it all falls down. Even though I mention that you have those inspirations this game falls down on every side of that potential. Here's why:Cons:- NO crafting. There is cooking, sort of... You have to buy EVERYTHING. You have absolutely no skill beyond playing a flute so poorly that dinosaurs think you're speaking their language. You can, technically, cook. Only by using some randomly placed cooking pot with a bad minigame and it eats MASSIVE amounts of food for very little gain. Ultimately, you're at the mercy of the game's economy. = BAD Economy... You can spam quests all day long but SURPRISE! They almost never offer money for those quests and rarely enough to actually keep you happy in terms of buying the things you'd like to beautify and and maximize the gains of, your ranch/farm/home. In fact most of the items they offer don't really scale up with your experience. Pretty much you're going to end up going through a ton of normal monetary gaining paths that you're used to and ultimately discover that you just have to work the farming system for money if you want to succeed and there'a  lot of crops that are just trash. Don't worry though, none of those crops can actually be turned into food, remember the no crafting thing? Yep, go find (good luck...) or buy food for your growing circus. - Speaking of feeding your dinos, don't worry, they messed that up too. The dinos eat an extraordinary amount of food as they get larger but you don't actually get better stats or stamina for all that, you're just going to sit on, not ride, that'll take days on end, a larger food loss for a more spacially inept creature. = BAD RNG. I don't know how else to put this. The game has all the potential in the world for giving you ways to gather resources through the normally expected means, mining, logging, excavating, cultivation, harvesting, foraging, ranching your dinosaurs, growing on your farm... You get foraging, 99.9999% is down to terrible RNG and a little grinding on the very few resource points that are only available once per day and if you want something more than basic materials you'll again be subjected to TERRIBLE RNG... AGAIN...- MASSIVE time sink. If you want to make sure to maximize the time you've got you're going to see a collapse of your energy, effort, and time. See above for the "Definitely a game for kids" preface I have above. Even if you do your absolute, speed runner best in this game, it'll find ways to punish you with time. = Lack of purpose. So there's at least 30 dinos I've seen so far but there's like 8 useful attributes or uses. I have 6 dinos on my ranch and honestly when I only had 5 I had all I really needed. There's no unique attributes to a species, there's no stat options, there's no real value to leveling certain dinos or rare dinos for special upgrades or benefits. It's all just the same washed out and bland gameplay under the very pretty graphics. = Small Map. So the map is actually a fairly decent size until you begin to get deep enough into the game that the only real reward or value to daily life is exploring and seeking RNG blessings throughout the landscape... Once you get there though you begin to realize that the map doesn't provide enough to keep those things supported. - Shallow world building and mechanics.  We get a few moments of shine when Granny talks about her family and when Pippin talks about his heritage. The journaling makes you think there's going to be a strong learning aspect of the game. You're wrong. First, the journal needlessly takes up a space in your inventory when it could just always be part of your key items, like all of the actual tools should be honestly. What you learn from wild dinos can only be learned once you put them to sleep, meaning you mindlessly waste time looking for the rare colors and patterns, because that's the only difference, and have to find out if the GAME thinks they deserve to be a rare or not, like holofoil cards in booster packs if the cards kept demanding you give a nickel to a quarter every day just to keep the card. You don't learn their diets by finding a dino eating in the wild and learning, you don't examine their leavings to learn what kind of fertilizer (which is needlessly complicated for a game with such shallow mechanics on nearly all other fronts, honestly) they might be good at producing, you don't learn about bushes, rocks, or other species they enjoy being around. If you put a dino to sleep you get to write down the thinnest of basics and that's it. Same with all of the various plants. You actually get a lot more from the plants, honestly, their season and preferred soil/fertilizer. See how that was barely 2 points? That makes it vastly more useful than the zero points you get from journaling about a dino. Even then, you'd think that the world started letting you get to know people better but that's also a no. You get to learn some history and address some minor personality development, but at the end of the day not even that is really given room to shine. None of the characters really talk about their lives, families, passions, etc... in any real depth. Even if they did you'd just be wading through endless text. Yes I am spoiled but we don't even get simply voice lines. It's all just words on a screen. Text wall after text wall with no real value added.At the end of the day, had I known what I was getting myself into this game would have been fairly priced at $10. It's enjoyable in the short term but it has a LONG way to go before it's actually going to live up to any of the potential it has. Based on the fact that they are already locking holiday content behind paywalls, we're never going to see that happen. So while I want to believe in the future of the game and see it rise up and stand out, I don't believe that's going to happen here. This feels like it's as finished and polished as these devs are going to make it and so I can't honestly say it's worth the cost. My advice is wait for a wale to massively reduce the price of this game and then take it for a spin. TL;DRPretty graphics are disguising that the game is only really worth playing for about 10 hours of slow and chill gaming with no challenge. I'd price the content at $10 - $12 and don't see a developing future ahead. Wait for a sale. This review has been massively edited due to steam review character limits...

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this came since the first concept art came out years ago, and I'm so happy it's here. It's a really soothing and sweet game, and I especially enjoy how interactive your little dino buddies feel. They don't just sit in their pens motionless - they wander, they follow you around, they nudge you for pets, they sing to you - the devs have really nailed it. The designs all feel charming and I love the attention to details like the feathered raptor arms and fluffy tails!I can see some people saying the world feels small or empty, and I kind of understand that, but the game is also a pretty fresh little thing from an indie studio so I don't think it's fair to expect open world RPG-level maps and crowds of immersive NPCs, especially not a week out of launch.Personally, there's a few things I would be really excited about in future updates, on top of things like map expansions:- More decorations and customisation options for the ranch, interior decorating for the house, and more pen decor and outdoor farming accessories.- Refined crafting systems - an at-home cooking station would be especially lovely, as the distance to travel has made cooking a very low priority for me.- Dinosaur toys or accessories - think saddlecloths, hats, and bowties; think also beach balls and chew ropes to play fetch and tug of war for bonding.- Perhaps some day even fishing or bug collecting (here are a lot of cool prehistoric bugs and fish as well as dinos!)On the whole, though, this is a super cute sweet cozy game that I wholeheartedly recommend to any dinosaur fans, or for people who want to play a farming sim that doesn't require four spreadsheets, six wiki tabs, and a blood pressure cuff.

_childDocuments_.review: The game, inherently, is a good one, and I am technically recommending it. HOWEVER, it does not feel like a full release game, not in its current state, and not at its full price - While it advertises as a farming sim, it really isnt; its a dino collection, and thats kinda it. Frming is only done to sell the veg and buy more fence posts and dino food, because crafting is not a thing AT ALL in game. The dinos used for farming have very janky controls, including watering erratically in all directions bar the one you want, feeling like youre trying to manuvour a quad bike with a flat tyre when tilling with a dino, and tender dinos whos skills are literally never explained unless you finish quests for some random npc that shows up only in one month, and in addition, these tender dinos have a wild skill (discoverer) which is basically useless.- A lot of handholding in certain parts and then literally none in others, so there is a fair amount of looking things up while playing, because theres no in game explanation. It can also be very very grind-y.- I was originally disappointed when I heard that there was no romance in the game, however its a blessing in disguise. Every single npc is so bland, so one dimensional and sosososo limited in chat options that the thought of attempting to romance one of these uncanny valley puppets is off-putting to say the least. Also, having played the demo, i thought those random npcs powerwalking through the market plaza would be....actual named characters once i played the full game?? Nope, theyre literally just random powerwalkers that get in your way. So theres literally  named npcs (not including random traders in the desert), that have limited dialogue and, honestly, are all pretty annoying. It feels like A LOT of effort was put into the dinos and barely any into the characters and you can tell. - The notice board quest thing is handy (especially for saddles-Ive yet to buy a single one) but sososososo repetitive. Theres only so many times I want to search for a lost notebook or bring someone a hat from someone else whos literally across the plaza. - As far as I can tell, there is no estimated time scale between bringing a dino home and it becoming a helper, which is so frustrating, especially when youre waiting for a skill. I had a Kentro for the guts of a full month before it became usable, and in that time, 2 styracos and a baryoynx all came home and became helpers before it. It was happy, in its correct biome, with penmates and food and got daily interaction so Ive literally no idea why it took so long compared to everything else, but it literally put me off that particular dino for no reason.- The art for the dinos and the map is gorgeous, for the humans its super disjointed from the world. I do was there was a tracker of all the colour morphs logged in the wild, maybe making use of all the random telescopes dotted all over that do literally nothing? - Limiting the number of dinos with finite dreamstones is a pain. Limits should only be due to space and ability to feed and care for as many dinos as you can, not an arbitrary number of dreamstones you can find.Despite all of my gripes, I do legit enjoy this game, and will finish it to completion. In its current state, I dont recommend paying full price (I got it on offer, wait til sales), and i absolutely recommend playing the demo before doing anything else (if you do buy it then after the demo, your save file will be moved over).

_childDocuments_.review: "You'll be back."These are the last words I heard before everything went black. I woke up to the stench of dino dung assaulting my nose, a common morning experience for a rancher. Except for the fact I wasn't coddled in the sheets of my loft, no. I was on a hard wooden surface, and when my eyes shot open in alarm, I saw him."Shame you weren't here an hour ago. You missed out on some stuff."Is this what all this madness was about? Did I offend Corlan by not visiting his stall at the time he wanted? That was ridiculous! Nonetheless, I was here now, and I had to face the consequences."Corlan, please let me go! I'm sorry!"I was sincere and afraid, but Corlan shook his head and refused my tearful apology. What was he holding in his hand? My heart sank. It was a butcher's knife, and the last response I heard before my demise was a gruff, "Hmph."And that's how Carnivore Food is made!

_childDocuments_.review: feels like one of the cheap cash grabber horse/ranch games I played as a child, it feels just as empty, lifeless and shallow unfortunately. I really like the concept and I guess it catches me because of nostalgia but it's not really "fun". the quests are all just fetch quests, literally it’s all just “bring me x” or “give x to y and report back to me” there are no other quests. I played shovel ware horse games from the early 2000s that were more creative than that with some competitions or such strewn in or structures you had to craft to progress but well, material is pointless because you can't actually craft, you have to buy everything, you only collect materials like wood and stone to sell them or for quests.the dinos are cute but it's just too much of the same, you have like 5 different ankylosaurids, stegosaurids, ceratopsids, small raptors and big theropods. like you only have very little variety in dinos imo bc it's just the same type of dino over and over again only with minor design differences and it’s always the same type with the same skills, you can’t mix up your team, it’s always the same combo of types. I was especially disappointed by the forest bc it’s just filled with 10 different varieties of tiny useless raptors and by the time I was able to unlock the part were "cooler" ones like deinocheirus and trex are (tho trex just looks like an upscale version of allosaurus/megalosaurus…), I didn't need them anymore. taming multiple dinosaurs seems very unrewarding in general, bc you can’t farm food and they're useless by the time you unlock them. for example you need the stomper skill and the only dino available with that until end game is anky. By the time you unlock other dinos (who just look like recolored ankys anyway…) with the skill, your anky is so highly leveled it’s pointless to get a different one with how expensive and time consuming the upkeep is. like why do I need so much room on the ranch when it’s impossible to actually keep so many dinos and the only stuff I can farm is useless crops? So I very rarely tame any useless dinos just because they're cute, which seems counterintuitive in a farming x creature collector game? When I played ark I grabbed every creature I liked and they were easy to take care of bc you could actually farm their food, here I only have one per skill bc even the cute ones aren’t really worth the upkeep or training them from 0 again, esp not the carnivores.the amount of crops also seems excessive, because they're ultimately pointless, like the materials, all you can do with them is sell them. It just feels tedious to have to plant 20 different “juicy” plants so you can find the single one your dino actually likes best. for the amount of forage and crops + quality levels the inventory is just too small .the characters are boring as well, they don't have routines, families/relationships and background stories like you’re accustomed to by now from similar games. the dialogue in general is very poorly written, again like from these cheap children's games from the early 2000s. Befriending them is not rewarding; you don’t unlock new dialogue or anything, which would make the terribly designed quests more forgivable, if the characters actually said smth fun or interesting.the worst thing has to be that you need to collect pointless collectibles to finish the main story. Yes, all the random shards you find lying about and won’t find all without a guide are main story relevant. in other games like assassins creed at least it’s not mandatory to get the dumb feathers, it’s just optional busy work for 100%ers, but here in a “cozy” game it’s required? What a poor game design choice.the grind for forest wood is also insane, not "cozy" at all.so all in all it’s not really a fun experience gameplay wise, it feels very early access with how shallow it is, a lot of design choices seem not thought through. They have nice ideas for example the taming and dino care mechanics and that the dinos help you on the farm, but it's all just poorly executed, feels unfinished and seems more like a demo.I have to say I don’t really get the other negative reviewers complaining about the lack of “tutorials” as there are no complex mechanics anyway? the game is very simple, like said it lacks depth.I would stay clear unless you’re addicted to cheap early 2000s “horse” games bc of nostalgia, but then buy it on sale.edit: I do believe it's a project worth supporting as said I like the concept and many ideas in theory a cue, chill farming x creature collector should be my fav. the devs are still actively working on it adding updates regularly. I just think it's misleading to sell it as a fully polished title in the current state

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a colorful and lighthearted game about goofy chirpers and cooing chonkers enjoying their days of being not extinct. That pretty much sums it up. If you came here expecting a Stardew Valley with dinos, then you are going to be disappointed. It is not an heir to the Harvest Moon series, and it doesn’t try to be. Nor does it try to follow the footsteps of games about scaly murdering machines or park managers which try to picture dinosaurs as scientifically accurate as possible.Simply put, it is a game about having some cozy funtime with toon pets inspired by dinosaurs. If this still interests you, then keep reading, I try to write down what I think about this.The environment is quite beautiful in my opinion. Though it looks more like a large garden or park, it still has much charm and lovely details. I personally love the animations of the cuddly dino characters, they grant them much personality and each species feels unique. The sounds they make might be not even close to what the real animals produced, but then again, I highly doubt that raptors used to be pink and purple, so these noises are as good as any, and they fit nicely within the overall style.The Farming aspect of the game is rather small to be honest. There is a dozen or so of crops, and these can be cared for quickly in the morning, so you can spend the rest of the day exploring. All types of crop have favorite seasons and soil qualities, but they will produce even if you don’t meet any of these wants, which I think is nice. Beside selling them to earn cash, you also need to grow specific plants for quests or as treats for your dinos. Overall, you can put in more effort planing your fields and adding the right fertilizer, and are rewarded with extra yields, but you can also just throw some seeds in the dirt and water them to get a basic harvest.Caring for your dinos is equally simple. Feed them, keep their pens clean, pet them, and you are fine. Dinos might help you on the farm, some can water, some plow the soil, others might even harvest for you. The main part of having specific dinos is, that you will need them to clear boulders or fallen logs, not only to make more room on your farm, but also in order to reach new areas in the world.Taming wild dinos needs you to befriend them. First you play the species’ friend call, then you need to find out its favorite treat flavor by trial and error. This is a nice approach in my opinion, and encourages you to try around a little, and grow and gather different things.There are three distinct areas with different biomes, where you will find different collectibles and dino species. The world has many secrets for you to find, so leave the path and have a look, you might find something pretty, and an area might offer something else when the seasons change, so keep exploring.The timescale is fair for all these activities. While other games of this type barely leave you enough time to tend to your fields, Paleo Pines allows you to enjoy the world and look at all those silly dinos.All summed up, the game creates a relaxed and playful environment which offers you an opportunity to just slow down a little and do some simple tasks, accompanied by lovable dorky dinos. I do have the feeling that the developers focused on what they wanted the game to be about, the dinos, and did not stray too far from their idea.That said, there are some parts of the game I think to be lacking.Humans are basically decorative in this world. You can’t enter any house (not even your own!), and the handful characters you meet might be fleshed out and given a unique feel each, but in the end of the day, they are givers of simple quests and buy and sell stuff. Nothing more. There is a sort of “story” which has you taming the right dino to clear the path to a new area, and little stuff at the side to keep you entertained, but the social part of the game is almost non-existent. I already said that Paleo Pines does not try to follow up titles like Stardew Valley, but even then, having this little amount of interpersonal activity seems odd for a game about happiness and having a good time.The building aspect of the game could really use some polish. You need to put down specific objects in order to make the dinos feel comfortable in their pen, but the game uses a tile-bound system for placing objects. Which means you will end up with a single object per tile, be it a large bush, or a tiny heather shrub. All neatly placed at the center of the tile. There are a couple of decorations for your human, like bookshelves and benches, but it feels odd to build a livingroom on the farm soil, and since you can’t enter your own home, this will be all you can do. Honestly, it’s not that important, and you can happily live without it, but then again, why implement bookshelves in the first place?Last, I personally think that there are far too few customization options for the player character. Yes, the game is about dinos, I know, but then again it is advertised to allow the player to freely express themselves. Which I hardly can when none of the ten or so hairstyles speaks to me. Luckily, this can easily be helped by adding more things to choose from.As I said, I have the feeling that dinos were always the main focus of this game, which is fine. Though in some cases, I do get the feeling that there should be more. Human characters are equipped with a personality and story, yet I can’t really socialize with them beside talking and the occasional quest.This might be highly personal, but I am absolutely creeped out by the basic human model. To me, the characters, especially the player, look like animated baby dolls, which I am really not enjoying since I have Pediophobia (I’m afraid of human-like models, especially if they are moving). Usually I cope with this putting a headgear on that covers the entire face of the player character, and skipping cut scenes, but since there are no such headcovers in this game, I’m having a hard time. I do understand that in a world full of happy pastel dinos and colorful flowers the playermodel needs to be cute and simplified, but I don’t want to be a toddler.I like it. I followed the developers for a couple of years, from the first sketches to the finished game. I personally feel that they stayed true to their original intention, and did not experiment with stuff that was too far away from what they wanted. This is fine, even though some people complain about the game lacking something, we need to remember that just because a game has farming in it, it doesn’t need to be the same as Harvest Moon. Same for the art style. Yes it’s cheerful and toony, but even an adult can enjoy this kind of thing now and then. Just because the dinos are not the primal monsters other games present you, the game is not automatically meant to be for children. And if it is okay for other games to picture a dog like a bean with legs, then what is wrong about having a dinosaur looking like pink playdough?If you are looking for something to put a little bit of cute into your day, Paleo pines might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little game, that I enjoy when I need to relax. Fairly simple in mechanics and story, but sweet and wholesome all the way. The Artstyle for characters and dinosaurs are super adorable, and hunting for rare skins is quite fun. Theres quite a few bugs here and there, and aswell as some blandess in regards to the Biomes and other things to do after the main story line, which makes the price a little bit heavy, but its easily visible people poured love into this projectand I really hope to see more from this company, so im not too upset about giving my money. Id happily fund a possible future DLC, because im 100% this can be a lovely and fun game in every matter.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a 3D Stardew Valley, but with cool dinosaurs!Paleo Pines has been an awesome de-stresser, as I've put 26 hours in on one weekend. There hasn't been any time rushing aspects, you just farm, do quests for folks, collect dinosaur friends, and try to find Lucky's family! It's really one of those no thoughts, head empty games & I love it.Pros: * dinosaurs, obviously (they come in all sorts of colors!)* the color scheme of the entire game is aesthetic* pretty areas to explore* lots of farming that can be done* daily quests, so lots to do outside of the usual farming/exploring/etcCons:* there are bugs, as expected (some wild dinos disappear into the ether, pathing problems, etc)* could have used to larger backpack feature, or backpack that was able to have slots bought for it (you run out of inventory space very quickly - you do get an upgrade later but it's one single row extra so far)* lackluster tutorial on how to do... anything? (it's very find it out yourself or not at all)* limited character customization & clothing options once in-gameBut regardless, I'm actively bullying my friends into playing Paleo Pines with me & at least 5 have done so. It's worth the purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Paleo Pines the morning it came out (yesterday as of writing this) and after playing for 6.5 hours this is what I have to say so far:The game is very adorable and fun! I absolutely love the dinosaur designs and the simple game play. There are a couple things I wish could be implemented in the future or taken into consideration.Inventory space - 16 slots isn't a lot to work with when going around gathering things or having enough of many different types of food to tame the dinos. I'd like to be able to upgrade our inventory space or even have our dinos be able to hold things for us. Crafting - I'd love to be able to craft some simple items like fences and gates and troughs in a section in the player's inventory. It would be a nice element that allows us to save some time from running back and fourth to the plazaQuest Navigation - There have been many occurrences where quests are a bit hard to follow or I missed a part of dialogue so I am stuck trying to find where to go. If there was a function to locate/ guide players to the quest area or simply allow us to look back to see what the previous quest dialogue was would be helpful for those like me who get lost and stuck oftenDino Abilities - Have a section in our journal to explain what different dino abilities do with a tutorial? (maybe just put this in the "help" tutorial section?)Character Customization - Add longer hair styles/ more customization later on (not as important but I was a bit surprised to not see long hair styles available) More Tools - Gathering stone and wood currently is a bit difficult especially when your dino runs out of stamina. Adding a pickaxe and an axe for players to use at the start would be beneficial to getting resources easierDino Biomes - I didn't know/ understand the dino paddock biomes were important. Nor did I realize that they existed until one of my dinos said they preferred a specific biome. Adding a small tutorial or part in the journal with recommended or required  biome decorations would be helpful as the current biome explanation in the "help" section is a bit vague.Dino Taming - a feature that should be added that would be extremely helpful is to allow players that already discovered the dinos preferred food flavor be able to see that flavor when trying to befriend them or be able to open the journal to check in the case they forget (as I have many times and had to re-do my befriending process because I couldn't remember the dinos preferred food typeDino Skins - add a section in the journal on the dino page for us to see what skins we've discovered and what rarity they are. Helps us keep track of the different types and is a fun way to collect them allDino Herds on Map - allow discovered dino herd/ dino locations be shown on the map for easy navigationDetailed Map? - this one is a bit personal but I'd like the map to be a bit more detailed with locations labeled like the plaza or NPCs houses and different location namesThese are my suggestions so far and I've barely scratched the surface of the game. I am enjoying the game so much and I applaud the small team that is behind this cute game. I'm excited to see where the future of this game goes and definitely recommend the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute and colorful. I don't like the design of the humans even a little bit, but the dinosaurs are pretty cute, which is why I purchased it in the first place.I got bored with it very fast. The quests are all fetch quests. The world is pretty, but ultimately feels very empty, and the "story" is basically nonexistent. None of the NPCs have interesting stories or personalities.If you buy this game, expect your news feed to be absolutely spammed with ads for their dinosaur plushies and no actual updates to the game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The dinos are ADORABLE. It's a game about adorable brightly-colored dinos. Also there's farming I guess. And other human characters to make friends with. But really, it's all about befriending the brightly-colored paleontologically-accurate dinos. Okay, the bigger ones are somewhat pygmified, but given the actual size of e.g. T. rex or Triceratops, yeah, that needed to be shrunk down.Also there's a Kentrosaurus skin that looks like chocolate and I keep wanting to lick it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game may be 'small' in terms of content, but if you like collecting different colours and patterned creatures, eg shinies, you won't run out any time soon. I have taken the game slow, only taking dinos whose colours I am in love with, slowly bettering my farm and decorations. I am now at 85 hours and counting. _childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A must for dino and farm sim lover! Adorable dinos, wholesome townsfolk, beautiful scenery, stress-free farm, intriguing story and quest, and did I say adorable dinos? The game is easy to follow yet still engaging and won't make you bored as there're tons of things to do and discover. And now I want dinos on my own.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute farm sim where you have your dino friends help out, the foliage in the valley is sometimes a bit too bright, as well as some of the dino textures being noticeably unpolished, otherwise I really love the design of the areas and dinos themselves. Once I cleared out the area behind the house though it seems like the character is too slow to keep up with all the things you want to reasonably get done in a single day. Watering, harvesting, replanting, farm upkeep by clearing out bushes rocks and logs as well as clutter, exploring the valley for the herbivore food so I don't have to pay for it even if it is reasonably cheap, and I have to pay for it anyways because the dinos I need to use to clear the logs, stones, and bushes eat a bunch and need extra friends to be happy. As well as checking every single dinosaur spawn to check for ultra rare skins or just a skin you really want, and I'm ignoring getting main quests done or side quests from the board. Overall though I have been thoroughly enjoying this game and exploring the map has been very fun, I would love it if the dinos would help on their own, maybe if they've been doing it for a bit and get the gist? Since they seem intelligent enough to recognize a pattern and copy it, maybe in a mod if it already isn't in the game and I just haven't gotten far enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: (Checks my playtime) Is 400 hours enough to convince you that you might enjoy this game?No? Well, I guess I'll say a few things about it then. This game scratches a collecting itch in my brain. And an organizing itch. It's fun to rearrange the ranch to get it juuuust right. There's also a diverse selection of critters to tame, with each of them having different skills that can help you in the wild AND on the ranch. You can completely automate farming with the smaller dinos!The story is cute and the npcs are fun. It's exciting to come across an ultra rare dino.Only thing I wish it had was the ability to expand the ranch so you don't have to release dinos... 46 is not enough for me 🥺
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Pro'sCute charactersDifferent clothing to buyDinosaurs are your farming toolsCon'sStamina restrictions are harshLots of loading screensVery slow pacedAnnoying questsPaleo Pines feels more like a chore to play than fun and that is due in part to the significant restrictions at the start of the game which makes everything feel slow and sluggish due to a strict stamina system in place which honestly, is far too restrictive and unfortunately this is the grindy core aspect of the game to farm and harvest to create recipes to tame other dinosaurs which steadily make things easier but the problem is the pacing of the game, if you want a more slower paced, more laid back farming game with a twist then this might be your cup of tea, even then I cannot recommend even on a big sale. Character creation is rudimentary but it serves its purpose with some cute outfits and more available to buy,  moving around the map also is restrictive with many loading screens, for example to go to the town and back that is basically 4 loading screens. Farming has its own issues because the main focus is on taming dinosaurs to do the work, and they do it significantly better than you can making your farming skills and abilities pointless and becomes defunct soon enough.    The angle of dinosaurs is an interesting take on the genre, I just think the approach is wrong here but this is my opinion and if you love the game, then more power to you. More could be said, but honestly? I'd read the negative reviews first before making a decision to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: After a couple of months of waiting I finally got to play Paleo Pines, and I will say I really enjoyed it. This game is a short farming sim with cute dinos to go along with it instead of farming equipment that you have to upgrade. every land I felt was done really well, I did not feel that it lacked foliage like certain titles, and the dinos I felt were all adorable and matched their current scientific standard. The only things that really bothered me was the music, there was a solid 2-3 tracks and changing location did not change that. I felt more music throughout for the different lands would have made them each feel more distinct and remediable as well as more enjoyable. The story was also hard to follow, I felt my goal was less on the story and more on the dinos. I loved the dinos and will now be trying to make more of a ranch on my farm, then an actual farm. I would recommend this game still and I hope future updates are already being planned as I want this game to do really well and not go away.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy games. This game let us take our time to explore the world. No one will force us to continue the quests, we can manage our time freely. They make carnivore dinos so friendly, a very huge body which somehow look cute^^. The hardest thing for me in this game is taking care of the dinos, cleaning different ranches and buy food for them. Also, managing the numbers of dinos in one ranches quite cost the time and my skills.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very charming and cute. Very worth the money. I had to stop myself from playing because it's 4 am. I love the system of taming dinos and having ultra rare skins. I got an Ultra Rare Psittacosaurus and I love them so much! That said there are for sure some quality of life fixes I would love the Devs to add:- When designing the farm making it so the camera follows the object not the player. This way I don't have to keep leaving the menu to move my character 2 inches and re-enter the menu.- A section in the journal to show what colors you've sited as well as their rarity and possibly a likelihood percentile of how often they show up.- A sprint button especially for sprint type dinos- A clock to track the time of day so we can track how long we have to do tasks- A noise or symbol to indicate when to stop cooking. Color changes don't help ppl who are color blind.  Like I said it's a very cute game and I could play it for hours on end (and have) but there's some minor fixes that I think would improve it! Can't wait to see what else the devs do with it ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game! It checks so many of my boxes of what I want in games and it makes me so happy. If you or a friend of yours love games similar to Stardew and Ark id think about getting this game. I had 22 hours in the demo and that was only 15 days, now I have an unlimited number of days to go about with my little guys!If your looking for a slow pace, with fairly simple mechanics, a cute art style and a generally chill playstyle then this is a game for you (Dont forget the dinos! <3 ) I love how much detail went into getting the dinos as accurate as the team could while still keeping with the cute style, and following this games development on the Discord has been a blast. DO NOTE - the game is rather repetitive at some points, mainly the running back and forth with fetch quests. While I myself enjoy them as I find the constant tasks nice and I like having a schedule (Pet dinos, feed them, sing them their songs, collect my crops, till the soil, water the crops, and go do whatever else im doing) if you dont like these kinds of repetitive tasks then it might be harder to get into the game.My only gripes are with customization and the inventory, I wish (and hope) to be able to edit the saddles our dinos wear and possibly add accessories to them for some more individuality for em. I also wish that the house itself was accessible, allowing us to decorate our homes and make the house truly "ours" in a sense. Now, with the inventory, we honestly just need more in some way. Maybe a specific level for your dino will allow it to have an inventory of its own, with every 5 or so levels adding another slot. I feel thats the easiest way to portion out how many things you have to carry for the questsSo far id rate the game an 8/10. I like it and it makes me happy, cant wait to see whats to come in possible updates :D <3Edit: I just realized I can increase my own inventory size. Its much better than before. Apparently I just hadnt heard anyone talking about it or seen any screenshots about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very adorable and relaxing game, but could use a few Quality of Life touches the other farming games have (shipping box and crafting being a must). Wish there was a winter season, just because it feels odd not to have one. I have more concern/ complaints but I could just be nit picking at this point,The dinos are the cutest thing ever, my favourite being the ankylosaurus (sorry Lucky). He's not the fastest but I don't care, he's just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ adorable. The dilophosaurus is my second favourite for when i need to run into town before the store closes or just zoom around my farm (again, sorry Lucky).In short; cute farming game with a unique idea, just wish there was more. I hope the devs continue to work and improve it in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Such an adorable game, a childhood dream come true! The coziest of cozy games, dino lovers' paradise. I could barely put it down after 8 hours, it is so relaxing and wholesome. I bought it for my Switch Lite but I decided to buy it also for my laptop and it was a good decision because the game doesn't show on such a small screen. I wonder where is the apatosaurus, diplodocus, brontosaurus and friends? Hope they will be added at some point a DLC would be fine (maybe in the future?).
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game so far! Primarily for the cute dinosaurs, as I don't find the quests or townsfolk extremely compelling (at least not yet at the moment). I tend to backseat any tasks they have for me in favor of my own dinosaur collection.The only thing I really have to complain about is how dreamstones function. To my knowledge, there's a limited amount of dreamstones in the game found around the map. This is a HUGE problem for me because I want to have a bunch of dinosaurs! I wish you were able to purchase them more readily, or for their upgraded forms to also allow you to keep more than one dinosaur with one dreamstone.Other than that, I'm happy with the result and it's been long worth the wait!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The whole point of the game is the dinos. Like, everything else is pathetically shallow, and that's fine, because the dinos are adorable and you can tell a ton of effort and love was put into them. The whole point is to befriend and care for dinos and see them on your ranch.The problem is there's an arbitrary limit on the number of dinos you can have, and it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tiny. Each dino requires a dreamstone of appropriate size, which can be found basically scattered around the world hidden in certain spots. Dreamstones are limited, point blank. So there's a hard cap on the number of dinos you can have. And, there's not that many to start with. In the first area, I only found three large dreamstones I could access before I bumped into walls or rocks blocking my path. The problem with that is that the game has already FORCED me to recruit TWO large dinosaurs, as part of its questline. So, if you aren't literally SCOURING the world looking for dreamstones, you're just straight out of luck. No more dinos for you. Oh? You went out and recruited a dino before the game demanded you recruit a rockbreaker, and you don't  have any more dreamstones? Better get rid of your other friend! I spent an entire in-game day following a map guide someone made, trying to see if I had any more dreamstones to find in the area I had unlocked.I'm not even upset about the idea of having limits that gradually widen. I'm upset that in a game about collecting dinos, I am already told "No more". It's a game SOLELY about the dinos, like, c'mon! Nobody is playing this for the twitchy farm mechanic controls, or the low-quality world textures, or the uncanny human models. They want the dinos! Let people have dinos! There are already other needs a dino has that will cause it to flee if unfulfilled, so why the stringent finite cap on the dreamstones?!Someone in another review mentioned that there's only 24 Dreamstones on the map. I think that can't possibly be right, but the guide I found only has 22 locations on its map. Can you imagine? A game about collecting dinos and you're stuck only being able to have 24 at max, and an arbitrary amount of those can only be large or small dinos? If I wanted to give my small dinos a pack of their peers because I like the colorations and think they're cute, the game is literally telling me I am wrong. I am wrong for wanting to have multiple dinos of the same type, because my space for dinos is a precious, limited resource, and one the game's quests keep demanding that I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ waste.How incredibly frustrating.Oh, also, the whole "we meant for a launch discount but oops it wasn't at launch oops it's supposed to be 15% but we can't fix it oh well" is also unpleasant but I understand that was more out of the dev's hands. It just sounds incredibly irresponsible.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very cute, and fun enough for a little while. The dinosaur controls feel clunky and the lack of explanation on some of the finer points tends to lead to frustration. The poppin system and how to get new poppins feels like a waste of time.tl;dr cute, but progression is unclear and not well explained.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A casual, simple, adorable little farming sim with dinosaurs. I like dinosaurs. Highly recommend to anybody who just wants a feel-good game without a lot of brainpower or focus needed to really enjoy it and have a great time. Did I mention the dinosaurs are the most adorable things I've ever seen? No? The dinosaurs are the most adorable things I've ever seen. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: So cute & so sweet.  I get to collect dinos and learn their names!  Some quests could be explained better, and somethings don't land perfectly, but overall I can't stop talking about how much I love this game.If you're looking for your next low stress, cozy, game without a time lock...go with Paleo Pines!One thing I don't enjoy is the lack of quest notifications.  You know about the main quest, but there are other character quests that come up and you will only find out about them if you happen to be in the area with that character and see the exclamation point above their head.  It doesn't trigger anywhere you find them and the journal doesn't tell you to talk to them at a certain time, you can only find out when you're where the quest starts at the right time. (For example, Mari has a herd quest that only triggers when she's at her home, probably after you complete something else.)Honestly, the devs fell flat on a lot of "how-to" parts of the game.  Trick or Treat DLC? After Agami tells you about it, good luck figuring out what the next steps are or what the rules are, she's never going to tell you again, you have to check the wiki.Don't get me wrong, I still love the game, but I would be livid if I had started this earlier and didn't have google solutions from previous players to answer my questions.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: im going to go against the grain and NOT recommend this game.immediately from launching the game did not feel anything close to being worth $30. and the gameplay only confirmed my thoughts. i was so excited for a fun rpg dino game and this was a MAJOR letdown. maybe i’d rebuy for a cheaper price, but not anything more than $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I think Paleo Pines delivers everything it promises to really well. I've seen a few complaints and comparisons that I don't think are really fair overall, like "this other game has it so this game should too" etc. Anyway my only complaints would be that I feel it should have been more clear how to upgrade your inventory, and it would have been nice if the inventory was bigger or had a separate space for dino taming stuff so it didn't take up so much space. Would also have been nice to have an easier way to track down certain dinosaurs and fruit/plants on the map. Definetly don't think that's worth a lower rating/downvote though personally <3 The dinosaur designs are really well done, the colors and design of the game overall is beautiful, and it's also very forgiving. Nothing about it feels stressful in the slightest. Dinosaur is unhappy for multiple days in a row and leaves? Well, there's an npc that can bring them back for you. Run out of energy to water that last plant? You can still do it, but your character is visibly exhausted and falls down. Low on dinosaur food? Merchants are open all night. It's just very relieving how stress free it is <3
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the cutest game ever. It has everything I need in life. Cute dinosaurs!I've never had any real issues with the game, except that one time after an update, which was fixed almost immediately.It's a little bit sad, that I don't have my most favourite dinosaur "Spinosaurus" but all the other ones are very cute.This game is perfect to chill, there is no stress for feeding the critters or constantly pet them so they don't run away or feel sick. Love the game and good job devs. If there would be any DLC, I will give instant more money. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: If you love dinosaurs, love games like Stardew Valley, and love simple and cute graphics, Paleo Pines is perfect for you! It can both be slow and fast-paced, you get to "befriend" the wild dinos as a way to tame them, and you can literally have as many as you can fit on your ranch. Plus... Dinosaurs. Pet dinosaurs. Must I say more?!There are some slight issues, but all of them I've noticed are mostly just cosmetic issues with the dinosaur AI and some slight lag, so nothing too bad, all things considered!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The dinosaurs are absolutely adorable and make the cutest and silliest noises, you have to progress to get things unlocked so it takes time to do and I enjoy that aspect so I don't finish the game in two days! It has a story you follow along with and you can do a wide array of side quests as well. Take as much time as you want to do things, or there is an option to slow down or speed up the progress. I love the game and I hope they add more content later on
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah this game has only been out for a week and I already have almost 30 hours. This game is amazing. Silly little dinosaurs are so cute. A few small glitches but graphics are great, runs smoothly, optimized really well, and has engaging game play. Haven't finished the full story quest but having fun exploring all the areas and collecting dinosaurs. Even found one that looks like an old toy of mine!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS A MERCH MILL AND NOTHING MOREOf the last 12 posts that Devs have made, 9 of them are advertising plushies, mostly Lucky's.  Of the others, 2 are talking about puzzles, 1 is begging for reviews.  Meanwhile various Quality of Life fixes that need to be made are getting ignored, including the issue that stops me from playing more; the audio sounds incredibly tinny.  Until these issues get fixed, I'm going to say pass on the game.  It's cute and fun to play, but the audio sounds like it's coming out of an early 2000s cheap speaker set, even when they're playing to my high-end headphones.EDIT: Since posting my review, Devs have asked for content creators to help show off an upcoming project, made multiple announcements to 2 DLCs, announced a giveaway, more merch announcements, multiple sales, and now begging for help getting a publisher and announcing a Discord AMA.  Over 30 merch announcements in 4 months, and now they're asking for people to find *them* a publisher/investor, buy their DLCs, buy the game, buy merch, buy more merch, and spread the word.  You pay $30 for a game you can play ONCE and then you get inundated with merch announcements.  Go buy Stardew Valley and load in dino mods.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game that's obviously had a lot of love and care put into it! I've had a lot of fun for the most part, and have found the gameplay loop of taking care of my dinos > collecting new dinos > using those dinos to get resources so I can find more dinos > etc pretty enjoyable so far. I have only one major issue - the game is obviously going for a relaxed experience, and it's 75% of the way there. Where it falls short is in the information it gives you. The mission summaries in the journal are extremely lacking, often giving just the basic task with no information or context on how to complete it. If you need materials for a task, it MAY tell you how much you need, but on some notable occasions it hasn't given me any indication at all, meaning I have to constantly backtrack across the (not small) map to double check. There are a lot of 'find X object' quests, where neither the quest-giver, nor the journal, nor the map will give you more than a hint about where exactly you're meant to be looking for it. It makes the game feel like more of a slog than it has to, since my options are reduced to wandering endlessly around the map until I figure out what I'm meant to be doing, or looking up a guide online, which kind of ruins the experience. The player's inventory is also pretty small, which means if you *dont* have the right items, you have to backtack *again* to go get them. There's also very little visual indication of what certain dinos' are capable of, area-wise (unless I'm missing something.) When using dinos to water plants, plow, harvest, etc - you kind of just have to click and hope. With how slow some of the dinos are when performing these tasks (especially waterers) it can be gruelling to realise you made your farm plot just SLIGHTLY too big to be tended to in one go. Besides these QoL issues, which I think could be fixed in the future, the game has been a blast and I'm going to continue playing it. I just wish it were a little more forgiving when giving you context/info on the world around you, without having to constantly feel a little bit lost. Also I would LOVE for a way to tell what rarity a dino is without having to put them to sleep and sneak up on them with my notebook. Some kind of spyglass or something to get an idea from a distance? But that's a minor issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. And I hope as I get further into it I will begin to enjoy it more and can update this review accordingly, but at an hour in the only thing I can really say about this game positively is that its very cute and scratches that dinosaur game itch we all have.10 hour mark update: Obviously the longer you play the more sense things start to make, and that has turned the biggest issues into the fact I've been stuck going to search the discord for some things that I still feel should just be explained in game, and the fact that as I go on it's just becoming more and more apparent to me how limited you are in how many dinos you can keep. I'm still leaving the hour thoughts as they are, because my opinion on first starting the game hasn't changed. It's somewhat of a nightmare for new players. But I do wish you could give a neutral rating. I'm going to leave it at don't recommend though as it's not a game that I plan to tell my friends is worth looking intoAs far as the gameplay goes, it's been more annoying than anything so far. Some, if not most of the tutorials seem lacking. For example, you're taught how to create a pen, but not how to place a dino into it. Your first dino is auto assigned to a pen, but I cannot figure out for the life of me how to assign my second dino to a new pen, or how to reassign my first to her pen that i moved a little. (Update: It's through the flute, but this still was never explained and was just something I figures out after looking around menus and whatnot for several minutes) It also doesnt tell you the requirements for a pen, as from what I can tell each dinosaur needs x amount of space in its pen, ex 25 sq feet or something along those lines, (along with a dream stone, which has upgrades that aren't explained and a feeding trough), but idk how much space each square is and there's simply no info on how much space your first dino needs at all.You're able to feed your dinos your crops and whatnot as a snack, but I can't see any purpose to doing so. I thought it would recover their stamina, but it doesn't seem to do anything. Maybe I'm just missing something there, though. (Supposedly it increases their happiness. I got it to work once, but I still don't know why you'd do it and half the time it still seems to do nothing)The placement camera is a huge pain. It places itself directly in front of where you're standing when you're opening and it doesn't appear that you can move it unless you close the thing, walk backwards, and open it again.Picking things up and other actions require you to be standing and facing in a pretty specific position to do.The inventory system is a mess, namely when it comes to the use of tools.And my biggest pet peeve, the amount of useless and annoying wandering. There's a map, but no minimap, which is okay, but still annoying given the fact that just about everywhere looks more or less the same. You have to get off your dinosaur to actually pick up or record anything in your journal (same goes for talking to people you run into). You could explore to find some dinosaurs, but if you're not prepared to befriend them there's no point since you can't mark them on the map or anything unless you're able to simply remember it. And then theres the invisible walls and lack of ability to jump. The lack of ability to jump is annoying, but it doesn't bother me as much as the walls, partially because if you could jump it wouldn't metter cause you'd just have more walls to run into. Some walls are fine, but there's plenty that make no sense and just force you to walk the long way around a small slope you should just be able to run down or something. It just makes the already exploration go from lackluster to painful, especially when you put into account the fact you only have so much stamina in a dayI'll admit, this is all fairly nitpicky, but it's all stuff that's been genuinely annoying me. If you're good with playing a pretty clunky game where it's your job to figure out most things, then go ahead. Personally, I wouldn't recommend it unless it gets some good QoL updates

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an autistic adult who loves figuring things out on my own, with a particularly special interest in dinosaurs and cozy games. This game was made for me. I have very few complaints of my own. In fact, the only reason I'm writing a review is because I am so overwhelmed by joy for this game.Pros:Befriending Dinos (and Dinosaur adjacent critters)- Of course, getting to make new dinosaur friends and care for them is incredible. You can have multiple dinsoaurs following you around the valley at once, in addition to the one you are using as a steed. The mini game for befriending them is simple enough but poses a challenge. There is room for improvement, but I think it's done incredibly well. My review, to the best of my ability, will not include main story spoilers. Farming- Farming in this game is significantly different than other farming sims, because the only real way to be an effective farmer is to also be a good dinosaur trainer. Especially early on, having more than a few crops to manage in a day is just frustrating. So why isn't this a con for me? Because it pushed me to set firm goals to find and befriend dinosaurs that would make caring for my farm easier. It also made me learn how to do that. Tutorials- I like figuring things out in a game by myself, and this is a great game for that. It truly gives you such little information on how to do some things. But again, I am the kind of person who disables tutorials because I just want to figure it out by myself. Misc. Dino opinions- For an initial release, I think that the number of dinosaurs was really thought through. There is plenty of room for the developers to go from here, while not being underwhelming for me.  I also actually really like the inclusion of some non-dinosaurs. I think that it makes the game feel more like a love letter to my special interest. Socialization- I love the quest system, and have genuinely zero complaints. Most quests you get are small tasks from the town board that allow you to run errands for people. It pushes exploration and friendship, which is a part of this game that I think you are going to want to participate in. Friendships allow you to stay the night at someone's house, and once it gets into the evening, any building you can stop and sleep in is a welcome sight. Cons:Befriending dinos- I wish that there was an accessibility option for making the number associated to each colored note on your flute appear in notes from the dinosaur you are trying to befriend. Early in the game, following the notes is pretty easy. But once you have to play several varying notes, it's a lot of visual noise to process. There were a couple I had to look up online because I just could not process them because of my disability. I don't think everyone needs or wants that, but I would love to see that as an option. Tutorials- Okay, it also has to be a con for me. I have a tool I have no clue how to use right now. I'm assuming I will unlock more information about it later or something, but there is nothing in the game currently to tell me that. So I don't know if I just messed up and skipped a tutorial, but there also isn't one for the tool I got. Genuinely, I think that might be it. At the very least that Is all I can think of right now. You have to engage in this game to know how to play it. I respect that. I love this little cozy game, and I can't wait to put another 30 hours into it. I am willing to bet that I will likely put much more time than that into it though.

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines combines a charming artstyle and graphics with adorable dinos that you'll instantly fall in-love with!I've never played a farming sim quite like this! You can tame and befriend dinos in the wild, and then bring them back to your ranch, where they can help with ranch chores. It's a super cute, unique concept that immediately caught my attention!Not only are the dinos cute, but they make the cutest sounds and have such unique colour patterns, that are very pleasing to the eye. The game is not intended to be a dino collecting game, but I've been trying my hardest to collect as many cuties as I can, even if it means putting some of them in dino storage for a while, and rotating dinos around.The story is intriguing and long enough, that at about 60 hours in this save, I'm yet to finish the main story line. I also enjoy interacting with the different NPCs and learning about them. Marlo and Corlan are my faves!There are three unique biomes to explore, each with their own dinos, NPCs, and more! At this point in time, I have unlocked only two biomes and the second one is definitely my favourite! There are so many hidden nooks and crannies in each map, that I'm still discovering new areas even now!  I'm very close to unlocking the third biome, and will update this review with my thoughts once I've explored it. This is definitely the kind of game that could benefit from DLCs that add more biomes and dinos in the future!The game graphics and music are very pleasing to both the eyes and ears. I find myself enjoying all the ambient sounds of water flowing in the river, the dinos splashing in a pool, lovely rain and even the insects and crickets at night. I also don't know how they managed to make rainbows, an already cute sight, EVEN CUTER with lovely pastels!This game gives me all the serotonin and lifts my mood immensely! It's my current comfort game for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, Paleo Pines plays more or less like every other cozy farming simulator to come out in the last five years. You’re yet another kid sent to another farm to spend another summer toiling away in the hot sun. You’ll till the land, water your crops, trade with townsfolk, and spruce the place up like you did in Stardew Valley, Everdream Valley, My Time at [fill in the blank], etc.  But videogames aren’t made of paper, and Paleo Pines isn’t made like your average farming sim, because each of those fun if familiar farming mechanics are reimagined here through the ridiculous and wonderful filter of dinosaurs... because why not? Why manually plow your fields one cube at a time when a Styracosaurus can lower its horns and knock out a row in seconds? And why refill your rusty ol’ watering can every few minutes when a Gallimimus can regurgitate dozens of gallons of H2O on command? It’s a fun twist to an always satisfying (if done-to-death) set of gameplay mechanics, and Paleo Pines ends up standing out from the crowded cozy crowd as a result. But, while befriending new dinosaurs through a musical note-matching mini-game and unlocking new biomes with your hard-headed friends adds some spice to these pines, a few underwhelming design decisions add a bit of suck. For starters, Paleo Pines is less open world and more a collection of instanced boxes that are stitched together with loading screens, fussy pathing, and no jump? Ugh. As a consequence, I always felt restricted when exploring in Paleo Pines. Thankfully, some of your mounted minions can absolutely haul, and the more you use them the quicker they’ll level up and the more stamina they’ll get, meaning after a few hours you’ll be able to figuratively fly from one end of the map to the other and back at will. Which is a good thing, because Paleo Pines mandates this kind of backtracking through disappointingly grindy, fetch-questy objectives. Bring me five potatoes, take her ten carrots, find my missing notebook, take him this present—it's uninspired stuff that only seems to exist to clog up your comically tiny inventory and add artificial length to a game with no real plot. And, while the handful of folks you’ll meet along the way are all pleasant enough, they’re merchants and vendors first, characters second. But who needs ‘em? You’re not here for cavemen, you’re here for dinosaurs, and Paleo Pines delivers dozens of them, from skittish Psittacosauri to chonky Stegasauri. After befriending each through song and snack, you’ll lead them home and construct a pen, though the game's static building mechanic roots you to the spot and makes this process a bit of a chore. From there, it’s all about maintenance, cause fail to feed or clean up after your dino friends and they might skip camp and return to the wilds.  As for style, Paleo Pines is a pretty if dated-looking little game that mostly makes up for its low-res textures with bright, fun colors and adorable 3D models. Nice and simple (if repetitive) music and cute, funny low-budget dino sound design adds silly charm to a game already bursting with it... but nothing here really wows, and I can’t help but think that Paleo Pines would run fine on my PS3. In the end, Paleo Pines adds up to an addicting if clunky little spin on the crowded cozy farming genre. At $30 for 10 to 15 hours of relaxed playtime, I think it presents decent value, so I’ll give it an aggregate MEGA score of 2.82/5 (full scoring breakdown available in video form) and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review.  Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the dinosaurs, stayed for the dinosaurs. _childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a great concept, but the game doesn't feel as immersive and in-depth as I expected from an almost full priced game to be.Mentionable areas for growth:- You can't enter homes - not even your own home - meaning you can't decorate or get to see the personality of the characters.- There is no option to romance!! Meaning no getting married or making a family in this game. I mean, the fun part is getting to really know your partner right? And I think for this genre of game being able to at least romance is the standard, and is so for a reason.- The movement when watering crops feels clunky, namely it's difficult to water 1 specific square tile of crop at a time and gets frustrating fast.- The map isn't helpful, I'd like to know where exactly I can find somebody without the icons overlapping.- The building in the game is also not as intuitive as I'd like it to be, it took a while to figure out, I think the POV they chose is good but the controls don't really flow with the design- I'm surprised they didn't take tried and true qualities of past successful farming games and implement them into this game, or at least deliver a decent amount of new features that haven't been in a farming game to make up for the lack of features.This game feels like it should be for early release price, but for now I think the gameplay does not justify the cost. It's an amazing idea and I hope some of these suggestions get to be actualized in future updates; for now keep up the hard work, devs, you've got a great game in the works.

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a pretty fun game overall. Its mainly a farming game which is a bit overused yet really well done and the main focus of the game, at least for me is taming and collecting different dinosaurs using foods and poffins, which are used to tame the dinosaurs. You need to get different dinosaurs to get into areas to get more dinosaurs and more things to care for your dinosaurs, these dinosaurs also have skills and abilities to help you farm, complete tasks and you are able to ride them. After the tutorial (which doesn't explain everything to you) the game gets quite repetitive and feels like to progress, its more helpful going on the wiki or on a fellow player's guide to know what to do to progress, especially because that's pretty much the only way you are able to decide what dinosaurs you want, at least for me. I would recommend the game to others and its quite addicting (especially with dino nose boops!) for its chibi design and cutesy concept with little dinos to interact with.I'd also like to mention that the majority of items feel overpriced with the majority of your foods going into taming new dinosaurs and selling them doesn't gain much, I wish that currency was easier to get and things more clearly explained. Also, in early game if you decide to collect as many dinosaurs as you can with your extremely expensive poffins, the majority of dinosaurs are unavailable to you because they require different poffin flavors, wasting your precious poffins which costed around three times your salary. Dreamstones are an entirely new issue with it being hard to get them and if you manage to get your dinos with poffins they will need one, and they usually leave no matter what else you do in my experience eventually, I searched on the wiki for their locations and still struggled to find any in the beginning. Plus, you need to get enough trust with your dino so they can actually be useful, such as being ride-able, scouting for items and such which takes forever and if you mistreat them then you have to try again, the only exclusion to this being your gifted Parasaurolophus, Lucky. I came into this game looking for a dinosaur ranch game to have fun with but its quite difficult being engaged with the game after awhile and prices are extremely high, for example, a single gate costs 100 shells at the start and without the whiteboard feature being explained, that's pretty much all you have.Has a few issues but I generally like the game and recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game over the course of the past week since it's initial release, and suffice to say I'm hooked. I've grown up playing a variety of chill park and farming simulators, and I'm a dinosaur lover. I played some of the original Harvest Moon games (which eventually became Story of Seasons,) Zoo Tycoon, Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis and several others. You'll find Jurassic World Evolution and its sequel in my library.The artstyle is wonderful. I can't say that the human NPCs stand out to me, but they aren't as important as the dinosaurs, which are the game's selling point. The designs of these ancient beasts are cute and colorful, and balance being scientifically accurate with an appealing cartoony style. The mechanics are simple and fun and easy to grasp.However, having put over twenty hours into the game now as of this review, I can definitely say that the game could have used more time to cook in order to feel 'full.' The dinosaurs themselves, I felt, were absolutely nailed. However, as a farming simulator and cozy game, the game itself feels empty and like it has so much untapped potential.You can't customize your house beyond an exterior paint job. You can't even go into it at all. There's little variety in the customization of pens and farmland. There's plenty of space for you to work with in case you want to have a huge menagerie of dinos—but in my case personally, I felt very little incentive to go out and tame dinosaurs once I had the abilities I needed to clear specific obstacles. After you have what you need, taming specific dinosaurs more or less is unnecessary except for certain quests (if you care for the simplistic story,) or to simply fill out dinosaur entries or find a rare skin to have as a trophy of sorts.The NPCs themselves are flat as cardboard and scarcely memorable, and there's little indication of a friendship system. Apparently you get prices lowered if you befriend shopkeepers and specific items from others, but beyond that, there's nothing that really motivates you to go out of your way to say hi to a specific NPC every ingame day.I think my biggest issue is that you reach a point where you've basically done everything way too early in the game. I'd unlocked every area, cleared just about every obstacle, and cleaned out my farm in its entirety by the third season of the first year. I would have liked to see more areas outside of the valley, Dapplewood and Ariacotta.I should also mention that unlike in most farming simulators, the main way you're going to make money throughout the game is crops. Yes, its a farming game, but foraging hardly nets you anything unless you're looking for truffles, which you can only dig up at the end of the year. You cannot fish. You cannot craft. There are areas and pieces of furniture that feel as though they were meant for something that was cut from the game, such as the tables and telescopes set out overlooking the wild dinosaur packs and herds.This game has me hooked and wanting  though not in a very good way. It definitely needed more filling out, with more content, more dinosaurs and prehistoric animals, more places to explore, more features, etc. I'm hopeful that the devs will eventually be able to add whatever was cut from the game and more in the future.For now though, I recommend it, especially if you're a dino lover who enjoys simple, cozy farming simulators. I would wait until a sale though or until/if more content and DLC gets added, because the current experience doesn't feel like its tapping into its true potential.- Lucky is actually insanely useful throughout the game and not just a replaceable starter- The dinos are well designed, quirky and colorful. I love looking for different skins- The dinosaurs are your 'tools' and have unique abilities that save you time and stamina both on the farm and in the wild.- The days feel long enough that you're not rushing to do everything you want to do, but short enough that you aren't bored by the end of them.- The NPCs are horribly bland- Progression is quick. Unless you have set challenges for yourself, you'll have done most of everything by the end of the first year.- There's little incentive to do much else once you've unlocked the areas.
