_childDocuments_.review: So, after a few hours im really pleased.Let me tell you why:Monster trucks are a very American thing, and from Ive noticed, a very "first motor sport" vibe to it. For anyone who may not have any regular exposure to Monster Trucks, its important to remember that these machines arent racing cars. They arent rally cars, not Nascars, not Dragsters, etc. They are heavily glorified stunt vehicles. Vehicles meant to do high speed, at short distance. Trucks equivalent to hyper active puppies. This game requires you to think about the unique movement and durable nature of monster trucks, but at a level they could never hope to achieve.The real life "Monster Jam" events require you to obey and confer to the rules of MT, giving an "extreme alt sports" feel to the game. In the same vein as Tony Hawks Pro Skater, Taco Apocalypse, or Rocket League. Its a unique way to think about the movement of a vehicle, because really only MT's have this kind of movement. IF you have played Redout, you would be at home, if not, and you dont know what im referring to, its the four wheel steering in MT's. Youll be using both sticks on a controller to perform otherwise "normal" turns and maneuvers so it may take some getting used to. Because, as i stated earlier, these machines were never really meant to perform at this level.And yet, the game allows you to do this extreme level of movement and speed. its filled with real labeled trucks, a very very mixed soundtrack and makes you rethink how you as a player would move and control a vehicle in a "racing" game. On top of that, it offers a New Game+ mode so you could grind the crap out of this with a friend, or maybe younger family member.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, but it can be easily improved by removing the powers/passives (including boost) and freestyle event beacons. Let the trucks represent the absurdity that makes Monster Jam awesome, not some magical fantasy elements! Remove the aforementioned aspects and replace the maps with realistic ones, and you got yourself a near-perfect Monster Jam game. Don't over complicate it! Keep it realistic. Also, the different trucks should offer significantly different driving experiences. It would be neat if the different trucks were tuned to match their real-life versions (eg Avenger being very loose). It doesn't have to be perfect. Even arbitrary differences between the trucks would make the game significantly more replayable and less mindless. Another idea to really ramp up this game's quality is to copy Wreckfest's systems of upgrades and tuning. The upgrades would also satisfy progression in place of the current leveling mechanic. I get that Monster Jam doesn't prioritize games and are just looking to release some quick fun, but I truly think simple decisions like those I've explained can turn this game into an actual good game that hits a broader audience, not just something for those attracted to the Monster Jam logo. From PSP to console to mobile to PC, I've searched for a satisfying monster truck game. Its unfortunate that after all this game satisfied, it disregarded one of the only things that made the other monster truck games fun -- realism.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: For monster truck fans, this second Monster Jam Steel Titans is something that will make your hands tickle.With no fewer than 38 unique monster trucks, some of which are also based on real monster trucks, with which you can refine your best stunts.The monster trucks also each have a special ability that you can use to your advantage during a race.In addition to the wide range of tricks that you can do in the game, there are other activities such as racing or even exploration,In addition to the competitive jams, you will also be able to go out in a kind of open worlds,here you can indulge yourself without limits and you will also have to watch out for hidden objects, each area in the open worlds has 5 of these objects hidden and when you find strings of 5 you will be rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: +Great physics and graphics, if you are familiar with the behavior of the CRD Monster Truck in BeamNG you will find little flaw in this, but it is Forza-esque "simcade" in that you have lots of assists on tap, making it easy to learn and hard to master.+Responsive controls, advanced options for separate rear steering and manual transmission+Decent wheel support, good FFB+Fun variety of racing and stunt modes+Great trick scoring and combo system+Huge hub world and colorful graphics make it feel a bit like a '90s 3d platformer but you are a monster truck.-Cannot reassign controls easily-Missing effects like watersplashes -Odd sticky collisions with other trucks-Not all objects are breakable -AI is very fast by itself but not smart enough to race other trucks very well making some events more challenging than they need to be-Truck special abilities make the AI's inability to overtake worse-Early game events are a boring slog (drag racing in a circle?), AI is quite strong, your truck starts out slow, and the races are short, but it picks up later-Checkpoint races have overzealous cut protection and often just ruin your race resetting you before you even have a chance to return to the trackTo configure the controls on a steering wheel, the only way I've found possible is finding UserWheelInput.ini in "AppData\Local\MJST2\Saved\Config\Windows" and manually changing the numbers minus one to reflect the button labels reported in the Windows Joystick control panel (0 = 1, 1 = 2, etc.).Also, as a bonus, if you make a shortcut to MJST2-Win64-Shipping.exe and add the "-vr" command line option you can play with your SteamVR-compatible HMD. The menus and HUD are broken in this clearly unfinished mode but the meat of the game is still fully playable and lots of fun. Hope to see this as an official feature soon.Overall a great budget racing game with surprisingly detailed physics. It does nothing really new or exciting aside from being one of the few games to have even vaguely realistic monster truck racing, and suffers a bit for it's lack of polish and direction. It's hard to tell whether it's for kids or the old veterans of the MSN Gaming Zone, but it is definitely all fun, and the inclusion of real life arenas along with the fantasy hub world means you can play pretty much however you like.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly low effort game. -No water effects. Trucks look pretty good, environments are pretty bad.-The AI is HORRIBLE.-Stunts aren't physics based, just kind of happen when you meet the right conditions.Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I didnt really like the game to be honest. I got bored of it very quickly. The gameplay was fun for half an hour but I didnt think there was much too it, you do a list of events that are presented to you in chapters, whilst the rest of the game is just exploring a small map in freeride. I cant say I found the game to be all that interesting, the trucks are cool and all but I just didnt enjoy it much. The controls are a bit weird and not exactly ideal. I was using my xbox one afterglow controller and I had to use the D-pad down arrow to look backwards, which makes it almost impossible to do when your in the middle of a race. One of the first things I wanted to do was change this right away and the game wouldnt even let me because there didnt seem to be an option?Something else I could not stand about the game was the addition of powerups. The one I always had was called "Boost" as you can imagine a bit like nitrous, the truck would go super fast. The problem for me it would go so fast to the point where it would send me off track, so generally I preferred not to use it, which then gave the other AI trucks a slight advantage. I noticed one of them had quite a useful powerup that gave them some kind of shield that would just shove everything else out the way. Whenever this happened it would be rather frustrating because most of the time you would not land on wheels and end up having to restart the race again. I just felt like the powerups sort of ruined the game a little bit and I would have preferred it without them.Overall a disappointing game and a waste of money. I cant say I would recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is an improvement over the first Steel Titans, its just still not up to par with what a Monster Jam game should be.Firstly, the huge offender is the physics. They are WAY better than the first game, but still are under developed. The problem is the monster trucks don't feel heavy. They constantly bounce around like they have helium in their tires. This isn't necessarily a problem for stadium events, where the good aspects of the physics truly shine. However, when you are navigating/racing through the open worlds, the uneven ground and bumps send your truck tumbling CONSTANTLY. Also, why does hitting breakable props slow you down so much? It feels like the damn props are heavier than the monster trucks! Utterly baffling...Secondly, this game is for kids. You can easily tell by the collectibles and open worlds. They really played into the fantasy aspect for these monster trucks, which I guess is cool. However, as an adult, I much prefer the more realistic environments of the previous game. If you aren't into the fantasy aspect like me, then you might as well avoid this title.Thirdly, the game doesn't look that great. The reason why is this was also developed for the Nintendo Switch. Because of this, we end up getting a more stripped down, basic looking game on consoles and PC. This is an Unreal Engine 4 game and it just looks so bare and boring!I'm very disappointed in how far Rainbow Studios has fallen, and they continue the legacy of half ass Monster Jam games we have been getting since the early 2010s. If this studio makes another Monster Jam game, I expect much better than this...
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: The inconsistent difficulty completes kills the fun!!!I don't even care about the constant visual glitches, or stupid hard to reach collectibles.Playing on EASY mode to just enjoy the main game, and it's anything but!Arena races, Arena championships - can lap others no problem. Wreck, or spin out in a 3 lap arena race? Still no problem to win!Then you do the outdoor world races, and it's like it's locked at Hard mode?!? If you spin out even one time during a 5 minute race, you mine as well restart, because you're LAST.  Over shoot a checkpoint just slightly, and have to back up, hit it and keep going? Oh well. LAST PLACE. Screw This.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I love this game. It's not perfect by any means, but it  whole bunch of dumb fun, and it makes me feel like a kid again when I play it. (Which makes sense, given it's a low-budget game that's mostly targeted toward kids.) If you consider yourself more "grown up" and you want a more realistic monster truck simulation, then check out , released just last year by Teyon and Nacon. It doesn't have the Monster Jam license and it doesn't contain the map exploration stuff that this one has; however, the driving mechanics and physics feel more accurate and nuanced, and the stadium events feel more real. I highly recommend it.That said, I appreciate racing games of all kinds, and sometimes you just want to mess around in something more "casual" like Monster Jam Steel Titans. There's definitely a time and place for everything.Here's the stuff that I like about Steel Titans 2:Stuff that I don't like so much:Overall, this is a super fun little game. I haven't felt like playing much else this week. All I want to do is kick back, relax, and mess around in some giant trucks.While not good enough to recommend to everyone, if you're at least into Monster Jam, OR you're a big manchild who just likes messing around in giant vehicles, then I do give this one a hearty recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was a fan of the first game and this is basically a larger helping of similar content. The first game had the one main overworld map; this game has numerous themed areas that open up as you finish events. Aside from having "more" I'm not seeing too many other changes. They say the physics were improved, and I think they mainly calmed the trucks down in situations like "power outs" and donuts and other things that in the first game could send your truck flipping like crazy. I was worried it might feel a lot different compared to the first game, but it doesn't. There are lots of extras this time, things to find, special areas of the map where you need to bring a certain truck to interact with something, basically a minor puzzle element. I'm playing events on Hard and there is a good challenge with the occasional frustration. The negative reviews crack me up as for the second time people just want this game to be something it's not trying to be. It isn't meant to be a hardcore sim and to me it even seems slightly aimed at a younger audience with some of the special abilities of the vehicles and the cartoony theme maps. If you watched the trailers for the game and rushed to buy it thinking it was going to be some simulator, you are silly. It's funny to me picturing older adults getting this game and getting angry that it's not their perfect truck simulator (besides, that other monster truck game that came out got bad reviews as well, despite being much more realistic). I think both Steel Titans games do a good job of being VIDEOGAMES, if you remember what games used to be like. It was not a full priced game and performs as I would expect. The graphics aren't amazing me, they are just as good as they need to be. I have had some stutters and some buggy gameplay with the vehicles interacting with certain parts of the map, but nothing upsetting.I would love a more fully featured photo mode, as all you get is zoom in, zoom out, position camera.I am enjoying it. It definitely could have done more to improve, so if you want something leaps ahead of the first game, they didn't manage that. Lucky for me I was already really happy with the style of game they put out, and I was happy to hear these same devs were getting to make a sequel. As of 4 hours played it basically seems like much larger map areas to cover, more trucks than before, and any other changes to the game must be pretty slight. I could even go so far as to say I expected/hoped for more. But I am happy enough to have more Steel Titans to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun - when things work. What are the things that don't work? Controller configuration and co-op freeride.One thing I get really mixed feelings about is hearing "Daddy, let's play Steel Titans 2!" Fun will be had, though only after a solid 10+ minutes of the typical setup frustration. If you play co-op with usb controllers, there will be a lot of quirky magic and luck involved in starting a game session that actually is ready for play. Which controller is player 1? Will the second controller be detected? Or will the mouse and keyboard setup be detected instead? Why does this even mater? Because there is no device configuration option! If you have your controllers plugged in and they aren't detected, you'll have to try your luck again and restart the game. And a simple restart is no guarantee that everything will work as expected. Why in the world would devs make a game without the option to switch controller configurations mid-game!?How about the freeride mode? It's essential to play this mode if you want to unlock content in the game. It's also better to do this in co-op mode so that you can cover more ground in the game faster. Unlocks are achieved by picking up two types of collectibles: Vehicle unlocks and track unlocks. The track unlock collectibles can be picked up by anyone. But for whatever silly reason, only the vehicle unlock collectibles can be picked up by player 1. WHY!?If you have a lot of patience and/or have a kid that knows computers well enough to work around these problems, this game is probably worth your time and money. Otherwise, avoid and save your energy for other battles, like putting your kids to bed when they're cranky!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: The following are my Impressions:Listen, I'm not here to tell you MJST2 is a bad game. In fact, it's pretty fun as far as open world Monster Truck games go.THAT said, it's just not for me.I was expecting more modes, more violence against your opponents, and more variety besides racing. There is nothing like a demolition (derby) mode. This is a  game 1st and foremost. sure, there are rolls/flips you can do, and some occasional challenges meant for stunting, but by and large you are racing...only in monster trucks. Just not interesting enough for me. And at this point in my life, I don't have time for games like this which require a lot of grinding just to unlock the cool stuff.If you have a son (age 4 - 8? or around that range), then this game would probably be great to play with him, but otherwise I would not recommend this to casual racing fans. only if you REALLY REALLY are into Monster trucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the haters leaving negative reviews are just a bunch of casuals whose expectations are far too high.Is this game a 10/10? No. More like a 7.5/10, but definitely enough for a passing grade. Physics are night and day better, the graphics are awesome, the upgrades to me feel more impactful. I enjoy this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: The trucks have a very arcade behavior, you can throw yourself over bumps, high jumps, front/back flips, you often back on your wheels and getting back to 4 wheels is very easy when you still have contact with the ground.This may bother players who are looking for something more realistic, but for those who want monster jam fiesta and arcade, this game will give you all the adrenalin and fun you're looking for.7 single-player modes, a multiplayer mode and lobby games that showcase monster jam's most legendary trucks.It's very beautiful, the universe created by the devs is also linked to the most legendary monster jam trucks, and Grave Digger is the superstar.The trucks are very well replicated and the devs offer us several skins for the trucks, real skins or collector skins to be unlocked in the game.The single-player mode offers 4 championships with freestyle, racing, 2-wheel and destruction, giving you at least 20 hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a spiritual successor to Monster Truck Madness 2? No, is it kinda like Monster Truck Madness 2? Kinda/sorta yes. While I haven't played or thought about racing monster trucks since 1998, when I saw this I thought I'd give it a try since it kinda, sorta, looks like MTM2. What it lacks: most importantly is Kind of the Hill, the best game mode in MTM2, is not in this game. If it gets added in a Monster Jam 3, it's an immediate 5 stars and day-one download from me. As of this review, Oct 2023, the online is basically dead already. Also, the singleplayer 'story progression' is pretty hard, even on easy; and the optional missions to increase your team truck stats are just insanely difficult. It goes beyond the 'git gud' mentality to just a complete unbalance of difficulty. On easy, one bump in the road will flip your truck 20 times over, and you'll go from first to last just like that, with no blue shell to give you a fighting chance to get back to 1st. It's not impossible to beat, but if you get frustrated easily from simple mistakes, you might want to pass on this one.How it's like MTM2: the circuit racing is very similar and had MTM2 vibes to it. Unfortunately, MJ2 has a lot of arena levels for 2-wheel tricks and freestyle, that just become repetitive and boring after a short amount of time.What is superior: The open-world freeplay aspect of the game was actually really great. If you like open world and finding collectibles, you'll love this part. Also, the physics of this game are a little difficult to get used to, but they are decades ahead of what MTM2 was (see what I did there?) so at least it's got that going for it. By the end, I was driving and twisting my front and back tires like a boss. Add a 'King of the Hill' mode like MTM2 in a third rendition or even as DLC and I'm all in.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent arena/stadium monster truck game, really terrible open world/circuit racer. The thing that irks me the most is how bad the physics model is. For a 20 ton truck it sure feels weightless and stoppable. Destroyable-looking objects can crash you and send you to a full stop or flying. The littlest things can tip you over, as if you had the world's stiffest suspension; the moment one side of the truck goes up, you're guaranteed to fall over unless you kill all momentum and come to a full stop. For freestyle/two wheel skills, this can be fine but it happens so frequently during circuit races that it just becomes a burden. The open world is very uninspired and lifeless even with their unique themes. Some are outright annoying to drive through because the terrain doesn't lend itself to the physics model or because you just can't see anything. As stated earlier, so many of the objects in these ares just outright kill your momentum. I understand slowing down a bit when breaking down a tree but having certain trees not break at all is a recipe for frustration.I can't tell if this game is trying to be a sim-like, with how "realistic" its movement and physics are supposed to act, or an arcade game, with such little control you have over your truck.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this 75% off and I'm still requesting a refund.I've played every monster truck game I could get my hands on since Monstertruck Madness from Microsoft.This is an abject disappointment.You're dropped in a tiny "open world" with no effects, the coolest thing they've got going it it appears to make ruts in the dirt, but thats as far as this goes.  You can find hidden items to unlock more I guess?  It's just not fun.  You go too far out of bounds and boom, you're sent flying -- oh look, an achievement for being really high up in the air?I finally found the championship and it was running around a circle in the best time, it did the entire tree of results -- I got 33 seconds, the other person got 31 seconds, and the rest were around that fast, it finished up the tree and I got 7th?  It's barely a game.  It technically works but who looked at this and said "oooh fun!"Buy it at 75% off for your very young kids or cousins.  Don't expect to be entertained because it's not even a competition, it's a video game exhibition.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely no bias. I hadn't watched or been to a Monster Jam show since I was a child, this game came up in my recommended and it was cheap so I bought it in the dark. I know nothing of wheel-support I play this game on a keyboard and it responds very nice with simple controls. The physics can be iffy but you eventually learn how to get used to them. Unlocking trucks honestly isn't that hard, you need to both do completion of career-mode, progress on a truck on each racing team and collect all the collectables on each level which adds more play time to keep you busy. Each truck you can level up their stats by progressing though both the game-modes and just single events so if you don't feel like going into career you can just launch a quick race or freestyle and if you win said event you will level up your truck.Playing this game is very fun and even got me back into Monster Jam again. I don't have much bad things to say other then in the arcadey portion of career mode when you do races on tracks each monster truck has special abilities. Some of them have the ability to use force-fields during a race which makes overtaking them next to impossible as the force-field will shove you and possibly flip your truck, said ability may also shove you off a cliff causing the entire race to be lost. Doing head-2-head tournament races can also be frustrating as the AI is inconsistent. Sometimes it gets stuck and you win a head-2-head with no issue and other times the AI is on a set path and fully determined at going 100mph around hair-pin turns without flipping over leaving you to lose if your truck has low stats. OH AND the physics are much better than the first game but sometimes they can be dreadful, for example during a race you can go through a tree and destroy it but if you hit the smallest pebble or go on a slight incline on the earth your truck will flip upside-down leaving you to lose the raise. Overall this is a very good game that got me addicted and I recommend if you want an arcadey monster truck game with simulation-like aspects. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: Huge disappointment. After the first one, with it's horrible physics, and after the release of Monster Truck Championships, I truly thought there was no way they could release another bad game and hope to sell any. Well, I was wrong, the physics of this game are nearly identical to the first one. If you want a true monster truck experience, go play MTC, it is far superior to this game in literally every way, except this game has licensed trucks. Short of that, MTC is vastly better.

_childDocuments_.review: (51% recommend, 49% stay away!)It's still atrocious, a single stone or minor turn sends your car in zigzag flying. Now imagine multiple racing tracks in narrow twisted corridors, hill shortcuts which... spin you round-round...Goodbye nerve cells, hello event restart.1) controls, with turning on J & L, your nitro boost is on ALT. My fingers aren't that long!2) hide map or HUD info, seriously, they take 1/4 of a screen!3) no customisation at all... I know it's not NFS game, but even "upgrades" are meaningless. Why is it so blurry in a photomode? In freeride trees and mountains lost their sharpness? No water effect? Ehhh =/1) The World is 4 medium size semi-open areas to drive in and explore. Have to complete career chapters to access new maps.2) I like how devs changed the collectibles hunt, those no longer visible in map.Plus there's extra hidden triangles for specific monster trucks, unlocking one is like a figuring mini-game. Brilliant!3) OST still good, doesn't make you turn it off. Several instrumentals distinctive for each area. A bit funny to listen to one epic orchestral while nitro-ing up a mountain. \m/

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this short and straight to the point. If you like any of Rainbow's previous games (MX vs. ATV series, Motocross Madness 1 and 2), or if you liked any previous Monster Jam games, you'll enjoy this. I remember playing a Monster Jam game on the DS back in the day, and this is very much like that game, only better. If you're simply a fan of the subject matter, you may as well buy this game because it's niche in the aspect of only appealing to people who enjoy monster trucks, Monster Jam, or racing games with a focus on stunts (such as the ones I mentioned previously), but if you fall into that category, you'll certainly like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2 has improved alot from the first game!  Improved physics, better system to unlock trucks and upgrades for those trucks and much more.I love doing the outdoor races and not being catapulted 300 feet away from the track after clipping a tree. The boost system is an interesting addition although so far i haven't really used it outside of world exploration.The world exploration is pretty cool too. Each truck outside of the Starter Trucks have world secrets that you can find and get additional xp for that truck for finding those secrets. The Truck selection is alot better too. Instead of like 4 different body colors of the same truck there are actually more unique trucks which i love. Especially when some of the new trucks are ones i haven't heard of before.Overall the game is a very good improvement from Steel Titans 1.8.5 crushed cars out of 10 broken tire rods
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: This review is more in the context of a comparison with the first Monster Jam Steel Titans game, which I and my four year-old loved (and still play regularly).   I wanted to like it, but... While the graphics are better and the HUD and layouts are more polished, this game is mostly a step backwards, especially for fans of the Freeride mode.  The vehicle physics are better, but otherwise the trucks themselves are about the same (though there seems to be fewer of them... maybe it's just that the categorization of them is so disjointed in this game).  What really suffers in comparison to the first is the level design of the "World" mode.  Steel Titans I seemed large and open.  Most mountain ranges and other obstacles were surmountable, and the height of most world locations were variable.  MJU and the airfield were almost perfect in the variations of height, obstacles, and features.Steel Titans II, on the other hand, has worlds that seem much smaller (even if they aren't), and are overly busy with terrain features that constrict play.  The Haunted Forest world is especially guilty of this... it's not even fun to drive around.  Other worlds are either regular (with a flat outskirts rising to a tall center), or have little usable variability.  The wasteland world is one of the few exceptions to this pattern (as well as the dog park section of the beginning world).  It's almost like the developers decided to "ramp up" the visual quality and density of the new worlds, without understanding what made the previous game fun to drive around in.If you are getting the game for the arena challenges, then you might enjoy this new iteration of Steel Titans.  But if you enjoyed the open world driving of the first one (single player or in co-op), Steel Titans Two is a step backwards in fun and in drivability.  My four year-old consistently wants to play the first Steel Titans game instead of this one, despite the fact that we've done everything there is to do in the first one... which is the best encapsulation of my opinion of MJ:STII.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: Did anyone beta test this steaming pile of crap?  This has to be hands down one of the worst monster truck games I've ever played period.  Sure the graphics look good but the gameplay handling of the vehicles is something God awful!  It literally takes an act of God to keep the truck on all four wheels during a waypoint race.  If that were bad enough, the AI is constantly wrecking you or grinding into to your wheels slowing you down.I wish I had taken the advice of other reviewers and not wasted my money on this garbage! _childDocuments_.review: After playing the first game on sale for $5 a couple days before I bought this new sequel, I wouldn't suggest anyone buy this. The game seems like a much inferior version in every single way. The original physics were more of an exaggeration to real life, but in Steel Titans 2 they are 100% broken. The power up system really messes with the racing aspect of the game and the tonal shift into a much more cartoon based look again makes the game feel at odds with itself. Sometimes you'll be racing in a realistic stadium, others you'll be driving up to a 10 story high fire hydrant or dog house to unlock new parts of the really off putting hub world. To say this game is a disappointment is an understatement, as I could see the potential. The hub world allows for more exploration and secrets to be found, the levels could have very interesting environmental changes that brought to mind Speed Devils or California Speed... But sadly the quality of the level design is baffling and making the game straddle this line of fun racer and kart shooter is only further destroyed by the horrible physics engine that seems completely broken. Cars bumping into you can either send you across the road or magnetize to you never letting go. Random clips into geometry making restarting events necessary and the slightest bump can send you flying off course even at low speeds. The opponent difficulty curve is oddly set as even on easy some of the final events can be difficult as the levels are designed for single racers at incredibly slow speeds. Everything about this game is just inferior to the original game and really does a disservice to the Monster Truck racing genre that is poorly represented in gaming now. I wasn't expecting a whole lot from a licensed game where development must have been hit a bit to the global pandemic, but even with the bar set particularly low... This game doesn't even meet it halfway. With updates to the physics engine, I can imagine this game getting marginally better, but not enough to ever get me to play it again. 4 hours to complete the main campaign was enough. Too bad I wasted $20 on it, I'm glad I played the original first because this game would have really soured me on trying a much better game afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this for the sole fact that you can drive monster trucks. However, this game is so noticeably bad right from the get go. For one, the physics are actually HORRIBLE. You'll be mid air, put the throttle on and turn both sticks, and you will literally go floating to the side just defying gravity, it looks dumb, it messes you up, and it's just not how it works. Also, running into obstacles you are able to break just feels like crap. It takes away a bunch of your speed super abruptly and makes the same stupid sound effect every time. Secondly, the music. Oh my god the music. It is SO...BAD. There are some songs that sound OK at best, but everything else is just a pain to listen to. This is definitely one to turn the music off and have your own soundtrack in the back if you want music. For me, I was comparing this game to the very first original Monster Jam on the Wii. Maybe it's just the nostalgia talking, but I vividly remember that game being actually legit top tier. The physics were a little worse in the sense that it all looked almost sped up, but running into breakable obstacles was so satisfying and the worlds were so wonderfully designed. The open worlds in this game just feel really bad, no where to really open up and have a lot of fun. The "open world" just feels like a main menu to me, except I have to drive all the way across it just to do an event. It's a really dumb system. The best word I can use to describe this game is just LAZY. It feels so rushed and the design of doing events and unlocking things is so flawed. I've never had a game leave such a bad impression on me in the first half hour of playing. I'll still hopefully play here and there because no one can deny that any semblance of driving of monster trucks is loads of fun. Only buy if Monster Jam was a huge part of childhood. Do not pay full price, wait for a considerable sale.Edit 1:  I have now realized that what i thought was a physics glitch is a cause of a specific type of class of truck. Nonetheless, this is a really annoying mechanic and driving anywhere close to them in a race just knocks you away. It's stupid. I've been enjoying the game some more just going catatonic and unlocking anything. It's all generally easy but not too easy which I making it somewhat enjoyable. Still, so annoying to traverse the map to do events. Every time you do an event way deep in the map, once you finish it teleports you all the way back to the first starting point and you have to drive all the way back to get to the area you were just in. Just a horrible mechanic. TL;DR- Most lazily made game I've ever played. Only buy on sale if you have monster jam nostalgia cravings.

_childDocuments_.review: After going to our first Monster Jam event, it only made sense to pick this up for my son, and he really enjoys it. Honestly, I've been having a pretty good time playing it as well. Many elements make this a solid game, but it does have it's drawbacks that keep it in the "Good" category, instead of "Great". I'll start with the positives:-Realistic (enough) physics. Trucks handle & behave nearly how you'd expect, just driving them around is fun because this part of the game was developed well.-Truck graphics are pretty good-Lots of different events, trucks & environments to keep you entertained.CONS:-While the physics-based controls are a positive, they will also cause you lots of problems. Even as an adult, I keep the difficulty on easy because of the unpredictable nature of the truck handling. Once super slight turn or move will have you flipped over, bouncing way out of bounds, etc. Or, in a race, another truck can bump you causing you to fly 100 feet in the air. Getting yourself up takes about as long (if not longer) than resetting, which will put you in dead last almost every time. The physics make this game very difficult at times.-It's overly kid friendly. The fantasy worlds setting is a bit over the top IMO, they could have easily catered to both children and adults by keeping it realistic, I mean they already fleshed out a great handling system, they kind of ruined any real appeal for a wider audience with obvious catering to children. Overall, buy it on sale if you have a child that loves monster trucks. You might actually get some fun out of it, too. But if you're like me, and actually enjoy a lot of what the game has to offer, the over bearing child friendly approach keeps it from being a great game, IMO. Also, while it runs fairly good, it does leave a bit to be desired in the optimization department. Would have liked to see it run better considering the low quality textures on everything but the trucks. Not a deal breaker, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster truck games often somehow surprise me with unironically being good and this is definitely one of them. You can't expect this game to be a straight up BeamNG level of simulation, but it does a great job with making the control accessible and responsive enough while keeping the feeling of driving a towering truck with overwhelming torque. The sense of "playing with momentum" is pretty damn great in this one and you can recreate a lot of tricks and saves that you see on the actual Monster Jam event in an intuitive way. Actually it really does impress me even more that this game is not a hardcore sim - because while just driving the truck around itself feels pretty much like a walk in a park the throttle control and weight shifting does share the same muscle memory you got from other sims.Fictional open world tracks are carefully crafted with some nice layouts and terrain types. Although the waypoint events are often disorienting and on the later game they kinda just start becoming evil on level design, but there are some genuinely fun and memorable moments you can get outside of IRL based events still.If you want some grab and go monster truck fun with surprisingly engaging and dare to say even deep controls, highly recommended on discount. Especially if you're not a fan of modding and clunky UIs in sim alternatives of monster truck driving.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{ Graphics }---☐ You forget what reality is☐ Beautiful☑ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad☐ Don‘t look too long at it☐ MS-DOSRuns on Unreal engine.  Trucks look great if not slightly odd proportions when it comes to the Digger trucks. Arenas and stadiums also look pretty good with nice touches of detail like when the lights go down and the crowd brings out their phones for light.  Nothing exceptional but nothing awful.  Outdoor areas are good, too.  Main issue is the lighting and shadows; things can sometimes look a bit flat due to not enough shadows.  A cool aspect of the game is that your trucks leave 3D tire ruts that affects your suspension.---{ Gameplay }---☐ Very good☑ Good☐ It's just gameplay☐ Mehh☐ Watch paint dry instead☐ Just don'tEasily the best Monster Truck game so far.  There's a lot to like and there's quite a bit of content to go through.  There's a lot of trucks to unlock as well as courses.  There's a couple of campaigns to choose from.  There's the main campaign in which you partake in all of the events the game has to offer through Chapters.  Generally you'll do a stadium/arena, an off road circuit, and a freestyle type event per chapter.  And if you just don't really want to do the main campaign (which can get pretty silly at the end), you can do the Arena and Stadium campaigns that feel very much like a traditional MJ experience.The meat and bones of the game is the trucks themselves and they handle great.  Very fun to drive.  They act like how Monsters generally do; very aggressive acceleration, not much of a top speed, slightly clunky, rebounds from jumps, crazy cyclones, ability to do stoppies, wheelies, bicycles, backflips... you see it in Monster Jam shows, you can do it.  The trucks just feel really good; the all wheel drive, 4 wheel steering drifts feel exceptionally good, the way the trucks rebound from jumps makes you think about how fast and hard you take the jumps, the in air control is really nice, you need to take into account of the trucks center gravity being ... not great ... so the trucks will roll over if you take corners too aggressively.  The way the truck's suspension compresses so much when you either are on the gas or on the brakes is also satisfying.  I like that each truck is broken up into Teams which have unique passive abilities.  You got Wildcard trucks that have more Boost shots as well as each Boost shot is more powerful, Ruff Crowd (the dog trucks) which benefit from slipstreams, Defenders which have a repulsion field (this Team is BROKEN AF), Demolition Crew in which they lose less speed crushing through things, Undead in which they cause opponents directly behind them to slow down (also very annoying) and Crazy Creatures in which they speed up when getting air.  Pretty cool concept, kind of goofy, but who cares?And last but not least, each truck has a unique stat that they max out on.  So you have Engine for acceleration, Transmission for top speed, Suspension that absorbs jumps, Tires that increase grip and Chassis that keeps the truck stable and has increased resistance to rolling.  Each truck, when upgraded fully, has an "11" out of "10" in 2 aspects and it's fun to take specific trucks to events with those specific needs in mind.  Really cool.  I find enjoyment in largely everything the game gives.  The arenas and stadiums are generally the events I like the most.  Mainly racing.  The off road circuits are fun, too.  Monster Truck Madness 2 vibes.  The Waypoints are easily the weakest element, though.  Part of it comes from the feeling that an artist made the levels first and foremost then a gameplay designer came in ... quite a bit later.  The other annoying aspect is the specific Teams that the trucks are broken into.  The Defenders are dreadful.  Getting close to any Defender truck will violently push you away.  And they're equally as broken when you're using them, completely obliterating any challenge.  ---{ Audio }---☐ Eargasm☐ Very good☑ Good☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ I'm now deafThe game has an awesome soundtrack.  The more I listen to the songs the more I'm just like "damn, these are some really good tracks!"  A lot of the songs are very heavy metal in mind, with one song in particular sounding like a KillSwitch Engage track.  Some of the fan favorite trucks have their own unique song that plays before each event, which -again- is a nice little attention to detail.  In terms of the trucks, they sound good.  Just not great.  There's an odd thing about the truck engines in which when you hit about 8K RPM the trucks go through an engine revving loop.  It sounds pretty good ... it's just odd though as, as stated before, the engine sound is a loop.  Couple of other things I like is that you can hear the blower of the truck if you listen hard enough.  Not as loud as it probably should be, but a nice little detail.   And that's about it, great soundtrack and the trucks sound good too.  I kind of wish you could hear your suspension working a bit more as well as that goofy reverse alarm that Monsters have.---{ Audience }---☑ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults☐ GrandmaGenerally aimed at kids but you can tell that Rainbow had adults in mind as you can play a pretty conservative, strictly traditional Monster Jam experience with the Arena and Stadium campaigns that forgo some of the more silly open world experiences.  ---{ PC Requirements }---☐ Check if you can run paint☐ Potato☑ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computerRuns pretty damn nice for a $30 low budget game.  ---{ Difficulty }---☐ Just press 'W'☑ Easy☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Significant brain usage☐ Difficult☐ Dark SoulsThe worst thing about this game; it's just too damn easy, even on the highest difficulty.  The AI just doesn't work well.  It doesn't respect how bouncy the trucks are; it often takes jumps WAY too fast, sending them careening off course.  The AI often takes turns way too aggressively, causing them to roll over.  More often than not, the AI is just utterly incompetent.  Which is a shame because the physics in this game are so good, this would be a really fun and competitive experience if the AI was worth a damn.---{ Grind }---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if u care about leaderboards/ranks☐ Isn't necessary to progress☑ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ You'll need a second life for grindingThere's a lot of trucks to unlock as well as courses.  There's some fun little novel things to do in the Open World area where you complete challenges and puzzles.  The puzzles are charming and interesting.  Fairly simple concept that you drive a specific truck to a specific spot in the map, always accompanied by a sound cue to tell you "hey, this is a puzzle". _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the bottom of the review.Monster Jam Steel Titans 2 is actually a pretty good game, despite some of my gripes with it. There are a lot of things I would personally change, but most of them aren't things that would make the game objectively better.Here are some pros:- The Monster Truck selection is really good, I believe that there are about 38 trucks in the game in total, and some of them even have different colour variations, like Dragon, who has three different colour variations. Monster Mutt has literally 6 variations, not including the DLC trucks.- The graphics are good enough. It's not gonna win any "Most Beautiful Game" awards, but it looks good enough.- The driving engine is good, it's pretty much the same as the Monster Jam Steel Titans 1 driving engine. It does have some wonkiness and some jank in it, but you can work your way around it pretty easily.- The control system is actually pretty cool. Your truck drives like a real monster truck, all four wheels turn when you steer. This game has that, however the default control scheme allows you to turn the rear wheels and the front wheels separately, so you can even crab-walk with your monster truck, or steer with only the front wheels, or the back wheels, and it's actually super easy to get used to.- The music in this game is alright. I wouldn't say it's anything special really. I'm not a massive fan of it, it's mostly rock-y stuff, but me personally, I wouldn't really crank up the music to hear it or anything.- The open world is pretty cool, there are 5 areas in total that you can drive around and just mess around in, and they are all of decent size. They aren't huge, but they are big enough.- The truck sounds are really good, the engines sound really aggressive and angry, although I would say they are probably a little more tame than the real trucks. They still sound cool though.- While there isn't a super huge amount of content, I'd say there's enough for you to get your money's worth. There's enough content there to make it worth it for $30 in my opinion.- The game not only has online play, but SPLIT-SCREEN too, which is a rarity these days. We need to preserve split-screen as long as we can.- The game has a tire system that's actually pretty cool. Your tires will make actual tracks in loose surfaces like mud and loose sand, and they will stay there. A detail that not every game bothers to include.Here are some cons:- The ability system I dislike. I'm pretty sure it wasn't a thing in Steel Titans 1, but I wish they hadn't decided to include it in this game. Each truck category has it's own ability, and I would say the worst one is the Defender trucks. Their ability is that if you get too close to them, a forcefield will push you away. Doesn't sound too bad, until you realize this is a passive ability, not an activated one. Trying to race against a Defender truck is probably one of the most infuriating things you'll experience in this game cause often times the races have the trucks quite close to each other, so I hope you like constantly being pushed against a wall and flipped over. You can work past it, but it's just way too frustrating to be acceptable. Thankfully, abilities and nitrous are disabled in official Monster Jam events, so you are only going to encounter abilities in - at most - 25% of the events you do.- It's very obvious that this is a kids game that was modified a bit to allow adults to play it and still have fun. Which is fine, but it feels sort of simple when you compare it to other racing games. It's still something you'll enjoy if you like racing games and monster trucks.- The upgrade system is worse than the previous entry. You don't get any money for winning events, you get experience points which level up your truck, and what gets upgraded when you level up you aren't allowed to pick, the game just automatically does it for you, so if you want to be able to choose how you upgrade your truck,  too bad, not happening. It doesn't really negatively impact the game because it's not like you have to carefully pick what you upgrade or anything, but it's still a little weird. Why down-grade the upgrade system like that? It feels backwards.- There is no way to make custom trucks. There wasn't a feature like that in Steel Titans 1, but I wish they would've done something like that, because making my own monster truck would be a massive feature that I think would make this game so much cooler. Especially if you could upload those trucks to the internet and download and use other people's trucks.- Even though the current truck selection is really good, I wish there were more. I used to play Monster Truck Madness 2 when I was a kid, and while a lot of those weren't Monster Jam trucks, I would love to see them in the game. Bigfoot, Boogey Van, Bret "The Hitman" Hart, Firestone Wilderness, Hollywood Hogan, Monster Patrol, Samson, Snake Bite, Stinger and The Outsiders trucks would all be welcome additions, in my opinion. Although, I'm not sure how likely that is. - The photo mode is very primitive compared to most modern games. You can only rotate your camera around the car, that's it. There are no filters, no camera modes, you can't disconnect the camera from the truck and fly it around the arena, nothing. So I hope all you want to do is take regular pictures of your truck, cause that's all you can do.- The graphics settings are also extremely primitive. You can only select presets. Low, medium, high and epic. You can also toggle V-Sync on and off, change from fullscreen to windowed, and change the resolution. That's it, there's no options to change each individual part of the graphics yourself, I have listed everything you are allowed to do in the graphics settings. Kind of disappointing in a modern game.- I hope you like the keybinds/button binds the way the devs decided it, because you can't change them. You can change shifting and rear wheel steering, but only to the few options the devs programmed in. There's no full-on custom keybinds or anything.- There are no monster truck intros or entrance songs, so if you have a favourite monster truck, you may be upset to learn that you don't get to drive out to your truck's theme song or anything, which I find weird because this game IS licensed by Monster Jam, so they'd surely have the rights to do something like that in this game.- You don't get any rewards for finding a truck's world secret. Nothing at all. The only reward you get for it is the "pride" you feel for finding it. Whoopie. At least when you get the collectibles you sometimes get rewards like a new truck, but not the world secrets.- The camera doesn't automatically look backwards when you reverse, so... enjoy that.- There's no tuning system. I know, I said it's a kids game, but the ability to tweak my suspension stiffness, tire pressure, suspension travel, stuff like that would be a really good addition in my opinion.TL;DR: If you like monster trucks and you don't mind the abilities, in all honesty it's worth a try. I really enjoy it, and I'll be playing it quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting it to be overly childish and came out pleasantly surprised. The physics are decent, albeit not completely realistic (for example, you can easily frontflip just by holding down the brake midair). For the admittedly few games I've played that have monster trucks, this one is certainly still the best physics-wise. If you're looking for a simulator, this game isn't it, yet also isn't overly arcadey to the point of feeling childish. Instead, it strikes a good middle ground comparable to Forza Horizon. The roster on the other hand is exceptional, you've obviously got your fan-favorites like Grave Digger or El Toro Loco, but you've also got lesser-known favorites that haven't been active in Monster Jam in awhile, including Backwards Bob and Crushstation. Not particularly a huge fan of the open overworld and the special abilities the monster trucks have and the game would have been better without them, but the arena and stadium maps are great and true to the real thing. Overall I'd say the game is decent, it's certainly not a simulator but still feels real enough to allow for a bit of a skill curve.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2 is an improvement on the original Steel Titans in every way possible. While I don't think it's quite as good as the older Monster Jam games and still has some big problems, if you absolutely need a Monster Jam game, you will find enjoyment in it. The roster of trucks is very very good, it has all the main trucks and includes some more obscure trucks as well as some fake trucks based off toys. Unfortunately unlocking them all is more painful than it needs to be. To unlock most of them you have to play the incredibly grindy championship mode which is just event after event. The free style, 2 wheel skills challenge, and head to head stadium racing are the only onces tolerable to me. The destruction event gets boring after the first 2 times you do it, and the outdoor racing events are actually some of the worst racing experiences I've encountered in any video game ever. The tracks are terribly laid out and confusing and the ground is incredibly bumpy and due to the physics in this game make it impossible to stay on all 4 tires. These 2 factors combined make these near impossible to win, even on the easiest difficulty. Some of these events even have trucks racing towards each other meaning you're crashing head on into the other racers. It's bonkers how this was approved. The big new selling point to this game is the giant open world full of collectibles and secrets. There's different hubs and each hub has different trucks you can unlock through secrets and getting collectibles. These areas are waaaay too big and empty though to be any fun to explore and the ones that aren't just big and empty are so overcrowded and everything looks the same in them causing you to get lost. I wish the effort put into these areas was put into fixing the racing sections and adding in some more tracks or trucks instead because I had absolutely 0 desire to deal with the open hub and just played through the campaigns instead. The campaigns are way to grindy as well and I quickly lost interest. I did have fun with the freestyles though and spent most of my playtime in the quick play just doing tricks and having fun with the awesome photo mode. The biggest problem for me with Steel Titans was the physics, and while the physics for this game aren't perfect, they're much better than the first one and made even regular freestyle not feel like a chore. The graphics in the game are great. Every truck looks absolutely fantastic and the way the body panels come off is much more realistic and added a lot to the experience. If you're a big Monster Jam fan like myself there's enough here to jsutify getting it on sale, otherside I'd probably skip. For more reviews visit my

Playing on medium some are super easy while others you'll struggle to barely get by. Some are longer than others which is quite frustrating, which means in a series of 3 challenges one can last 15 minutes while others are over by 5 minutes.-Trucks go uncontrollable: Driving on flat terrain is fine, even bumps in the road is fine. But if you drive off a ramp and land on even slightly uneven terrain you run a big risk of having your truck fly and bounce out of control, which is unfortunate considering all the uneven terrain you have to drive on in this game. You can forget about trying to wrestle control back, just put the controller down until the truck stops moving, trying to recover while it's spinning will just make it worse.Final score: 3.5 / 5

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, I wrote my review on Monster Jam Steel Titans just a few months ago, and here I am already writing one for its sequel. Seeing how soon this came after its predecessor, I'd be lying if I said I didn't feel unsure about this. Would it be better than the first? Or would it be more worth it just to get the first game (which costs less than this now, mind you) and stick with that? Well, let's see.+The largest and greatest roster of trucks ever made for a Monster Jam game!+Multiple worlds to explore+A fun new "Story Mode"+The collectibles aren't just stuff to find for an achievement now -- get them all in a certain world for a nice reward+Derby Racing, a new competition to ST2, is fun+Online Mode is fun....if you can find someone to play with++The way you unlock trucks here is very interesting. Unlike the first game, where you had to collect a certain amount of points to get a new truck, there are multiple methods in which you can unlock trucks here. I will not mention them to avoid spoilers, but It really boosts the game's replayability.-The AI is frustratingly difficult to deal with in Circuit Racing and Waypoint-Most of the tracks are exactly the same as they were in the first game, except repainted to match with the 2019/2020 track colors IRL-As of the time this review was posted, the DLC is once again just additional paint schemes for certain trucks, with no new trucks/tracks/modes added when you buy it. If you're fine with that then by all means go ahead and buy it, but as for me, I'll avoid it for the time being-Abilities are either useless or too OP, depending on the truck's team ability--They ruined Waypoint. It was fun in the first game, but the frustrating AI combined with the terrible Abilities made it a chore to play here--Control-wise, this feels too much like the first game. There are literally no changes to the physics. Some may see this as a good thing but it wouldn't hurt to make a few minor changes like most game sequels doMonster Jam Steel Titans 2 is a prime example of a game that can be described as a double-edged sword. It fixes up a number of problems I had with its predecessor, but created a whole slew of other problems in the process. That isn't to say it's not enjoyable, though. Most of the competitions and new additions are pretty fun. So how does it compare? Well, due to the severity of some of the cons, I'd say it's about on par with the first game. If you liked the first, chances are you'll like this too. And I once again have to say that if you're looking for complete realism, get Beamng.drive instead and download the CRD mod from . The game itself is cheaper, and the mod is more realistic than the physics here. Otherwise, have fun experiencing the same destructive action the first game had plus a little bit more.Rating - 7/10

name: Pentiment
detailed_description: Pentiment Release Schedule Pentiment releases next week at the same time for everyone, so to help you prepare, here is a release map showing you what time you can expect to play! 🙌 Find your time zone and get ready! Release Times Monday, November 14th 11PM PST Tuesday, November 15th 1AM CST 2AM EST 4AM BRT 7AM GMT 8AM CET 9AM EET 10AM EAT 12:30PM IST 3PM HKT 4PM JST 6PM AEDT 8PM NZDT About the Game From Obsidian, this game is a historical narrative-driven game focusing on character development, heavily stylized art, and choice-driven storytelling in early 16th century Bavaria. Players will play as Andreas Maler, a clever illustrator caught up in a series of murders in Tassing and Kiersau Abbey over the course of twenty five years. Players will be responsible for conducting their own investigation to decide the fate of the community, but each decision will have lasting consequences and inexorably draws Andreas closer to the center of an underlying conspiracy. Illustrated world Experience 16th century Europe as the master artists of the time saw them. Art inspired by great illuminated manuscripts and the earliest printed books becomes a living, breathing world in Pentiment. Uncover mysteries Choose different academic and social backgrounds and meet a colorful cast of characters as you discover the stories and secrets that lie within the small Bavarian town of Tassing and nearby Keirsau Abbey. Impact a changing world In an era of great religious and political change, each decision you make can have a profound impact on the community’s future. Find your own way through this turbulent time and see the consequences of your choices play out over generations.
