_childDocuments_.review: A thrilling and cozy point-and-click game, right up my alley. Not only did I finish it within one day, I also had to force myself from not Googling details because I was so invested in the story and making the right choices. Even though there's a nice wrap up in the end, I can't help but want to play it a 2nd time. Both due to the character trait customization but also the potential dialogues and choices I didn't make in the first run.I only have a couple of cons (spoiler free) If you're not a fan of reading, this might not be the game for you. I thought the story would be much shorter and contain voice acting, but I did not really mind that it was missing. The second con would be that the story sometimes does not take the conversations you've already had into consideration. There were mulriple times in the story where I had already received information, but characters proceeded to act shocked after talking and referencing to things they had already talked about.(Example, there's a part where a couple of people are plotting something, I talk to them about it and they tell me what they're up to. I talk to them again and the other one gets annoyed at the other "never keeping their mouth shut" when they were the one who just told me 5 min ago.) This doesn't happen too often, but noticed it enough to be worth a remark. Other than that, I hope you enjoy it as much as I did :)
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is one of the best games I've played in years. The characters are great. Writing keeps drawing you in. None of that is ruined by what I write after this. I will vaguely mention characters and events, so if you want to go in totally blind just read this TLDR: In some spots the writers didn't adjust the story in accordance with your actions, which feels very odd considering how many things do change based on one small choice.Long explanation. In chapter one as the trailer spoils, the main incident the story revolves around is a murder. If in chapter one you discover enough evidence pointing to the murderer and tell your information to the investigator, it often results in the person being executed.  In my play through I didn't understand how little time I actually had to investigate and chose the wrong things to look into.  I suddenly had to make a choice, let things end for the suspect they have or implicate someone else.  I chose someone who, in my opinion, was the most "merciful" choice.  I greatly avoided mentioning absolutely anything about another suspect who had a motive because they had been through enough.In the second chapter multiple people I implicated, but didn't have enough information to prove them the murderer, had very strong reactions to you telling on them.  The only one who acted normal, was the one I avoided implicating in the murder.In the third chapter, the person I avoided implicating mentions being traumatized by being accused of the crime.  I was so confused, it felt like I fell into an alternate story line.  There's more moments like this but this was the most jarring since I specifically protected the person and it was never mentioned until far later in the story.Theoretically you could explain some discrepancies by the fact that other people must have presented evidence, but it still seemed odd.  Occasionally it feels like they were trying to avoid making extra scenes to show the small changes or that the whole point is that you don't matter as much in the scheme of things as you think.It was still a fantastic game and I hope to see more point and clicks with such good historic backgrounds and choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, with all achievements as this forces you to uncover new parts of the story. I highly recommend taking your time when playing Pentiment, it took me 1 year to go back to it after completing it for the first time.Should you buy Pentiment?1. YES if:- you love narrative games- you love historical games- you are not afraid to read (a lot)- you enjoyed games like Disco Elysium2. NO if:- you do not know how to read (there is no voice over at the moment)- you do not like to read while playing- you only play games with realistic graphics- you are looking for a linear game (e.g. you cannot get all achievements in one single run)My opinion: this game is a gem and the Obsidian team gifted us with a marvellous game. The historical background, visuals and soundtracks are perfectly rendered. Thank you guys for crafting this piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment takes palace in 1500's Bavaria in 3 Acts spanning 30 years.It is Art imitating Life imitating Art, visually gorgeous and narratively beautiful.The story unfolds over time through dialog the protagonist has with people that inhabit the small fictional town of Tassing.It all begins with a murder, which you task yourself to disprove, that your friend and mentor committed. Along the way you chose your backstory and interest and meet fully realized characters with rich personalities and unique motivations. Tassing is full of interesting people who will live, die and change over the story's arc and numerous playthroughs. Many of these people you will have a hand in influencing and for some you may even hold their life in your hands. All your choices will matter at least a little, some small choice will have big consequences and some that seem big will turn out not to mean much at all, dialog options will present themselves based on your chosen background and conversations previously made - so pay close attention to the person you want to be and the impression you want to leave.Comparisons with Disco Elysium are inevitable and apt but start at "beautiful art style" and end at "story rich experience beyond main plot". Pentiment is rarely sad or self-flagellating and never crowded with exposition. Where Harry avoid his responsibilities in favor of self-indulgent wallowing in his depression, Andreas avoids confronting his responsibilities and self-doubt by indulging in a murder mystery. Events in Pentiment unfold naturally, conversations are organic and lunchtime is always relative. Chose Pentiment if you're interested in experiencing a rich branching story that you are encouraged to re-experience with vastly divergent outcomes.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A well-written narrative game with a wonderful grasp of its historical setting and art style. Excellent story, memorable characters, and meaningful choices, all wrapped in a perfect thematic bow. Nothing but praise for the meat of the game.Pentiment is held back by its gameplay. An entire game about walking around talking to people is all well and good, but Pentiment encourages searching the entire map whenever the in-game time changes, which is mind-numbingly tedious. While this is optional, I kept finding really interesting and/or useful stuff when I searched, so I felt obligated to keep doing it. The map is quite small, so it's not *that* much of a hassle, but it took up too much of my playtime not to mention it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Another Obsidian title with a fantastic narrative and great dialogue. It's a really charming game with a compelling story and mystery, likable characters and interesting conversations. At first I thought it might be lacking due to the lack of voice acting but it grew on me, and I really enjoyed it. If you don't mind reading (a lot) then you'll love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many things I enjoy about Pentiment, I hardly even know where to start. The graphic design is absolutely stunning  - I have a deep background in art, including illumination, calligraphy, and stained glass, and there are parts of this game that feel like I've stepped into a Book of Hours. It's probably the most "intelligent" game I've ever played, and I'm grateful that Obsidian took a chance on a quiet murder mystery rather than action-packed shooter.It almost reminds me of the old text-based dungeon crawlers that we used to play on our clunky old 8-bit "home computers" back in the 70s and 80s.   Oops, I think I might have just outed myself as an old fart;
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is without a doubt a work of art. Both in the gameplay, the characters, the story and of course the art direction. The use of medieval artwork and calligraphy works so well for the story. The plot goes really deep and your choices will change the way the story goes. Sadly I think this is one of those games you can only play once (at least for me), since it is a murder mystery you are getting clues all along the way. And to play it again is going to be hard knowing how the game ends. But it was amazing and I wish more people discover this piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen a game quite like this. The art style is breathtaking at every turn and I applaud all who worked to give it the authentic and vibrant feel that it has. The score was also excellent, atmospheric and perfect for the tone of the game. The story was engaging, kept me guessing with great surprises along the way. So many great details that made the world really come to life. While some may not be as engaged with the game play, this game is exactly what I enjoy in the so called "walking simulator" genre, I was thoroughly invested.This game was an excellent vehicle for learning history and appreciating it in a new way. I hope to see more like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is choose-your-own-adventure/detective game set inside of a medieval tapestry. The uniqueness of that idea alone warrants a purchase, but the idea is also well executed, the game looks great and has some replayability because of the many decisions and character backgrounds there are to choose from. Suffers from slight pacing issues towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I do sometimes wonder how this game exists, especially from a studio like Obsidian, and especially after they were acquired by Microsoft. It's so niche (like ridiculously niche), such a simple, yet elegant and tasteful artstyle and direction. No voice acting, just reading. I would recommend this little gem even if you have no knowledge of the Holy Roman Empire (I barely do), as the game gives you little tidbits of information to help you along! It's a super fun, interactive history lesson, with super fun, often hilarious dialogue, interesting characters, and rather unique setting. I definitely do have some gripes about some of the "choices" and impacts, as well as the final few hours of the game, but overall, I would suggest giving this one a spin, especially if you're a fan of something dialogue based, historical, and simple point and click action :)
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment took me a while to get into. But once I got into it, I was enthralled. Beautiful art, engaging historical setting. Really well researched which inspired my nerdy history major brain. Where the story and themes eventually culminate was very touching in a way which resonated with me during a difficult time of my life. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I have to write this review. I'll give some background, you can just skip it all if you're not interested. The game is great if you like adventures and reading.My wife gave birth to our baby girl at the end of 2022. What was supposed to be a period of joy turned into sadness as the baby was rushed into NICU with life threatning symptoms. The baby had surgery done couple of days later, and the operation passed great.Last few weeks were mostly spent in NICU with her, singing to her, carrying her (when possible) and feeding her.Today she got released. She made full recovery, and the only thing she has from this period is a scar and a couple of check ups.Why am I writing this? Well, I bought Pentiment when wifey went into the hospital a couple of days before giving birth. As all of this happened, I used few spare moments in my day to play Pentiment. And I have to say, it was a perfect distraction from all the sadness I felt in real life. The tone of the game was just what I needed.This game helped me get through a really tough time, and it'll always have a special place in my heart.I can't recommend it enough. Go play it.P.S. My playtime is not realistic. Considering everything happening, I was AFK probably 10-15 hrs. But it's still a long game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: More a play or visual novel than a game but one of the most thought provoking and beautifully presented games out there. Covers themes on theology and philosophy along with presenting a fictional social history as opposed to the accounts of the Great and Good. The immersiveness can be mildly let down by typos or missed words in the script/dialogue, but considering its Obsidian I guess we should be thankful that was all (I noticed they increase in frequency as the game progresses). A recommend solely on story and art, there's little gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a difficult review for me to write because I don't think a game has ever resonated with me as much as this one did.This is a beautifully slow-paced, text-heavy RPG, with rich dialogue trees and choices spread out amongst a cast of extraordinarily well-written characters. I often find myself struggling to care to for characters in games. Not here; in Pentiment, I found a whole town of people that mattered to me.The love behind this game is obviously felt right from the time you press the New Game option. Every scene is a history lover's dream, and the care the creators took to represent what life was like in this era of history and in this part of the world is beautifully clear to see.The art style is equally as incredible. With smart and creative usage of its setting, Pentiment intricately weaves the late-medieval-into-Renaissance era art styles and early printing works into the story and characters itself, and looks absolutely gorgeous while doing so.Clever plot twists, a well-paced and refreshingly creative story and an engaging examination of both the good and the bad that religion brings with it top off the already supreme amount on offer here. It has been a long time since a piece of art has moved me like this one did, and I am sad to leave the town of Tassing behind. I think the only thing that surpasses the developers' love for what they have made is my love for their game. I am grateful that I was able to play this game. It's an experience I won't ever forget.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very niche game. Most people won't like it because it is a lot of reading and there is no combat. But if you like narrative RPGs like Disco Elysium, then you'll like this one. The choices are very difficult to make and the mysteries are fascinating. The world-building is incredible and there is a huge amount of things to learn about history, art, philosophy, etc. I highly recommend this game, but don't expect a normal game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: What a ride it was. Amazing game from beginning to the end. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Reminded me of Disco Elysium with a little less depth. Be prepared for a lot of reading though. Can't wait to play it again and make different decisions.Some bugs while playing: characters that keep waiting at the side of the screen because I play on an ultrawide screen. At the ending, my character was saying dialogue clearly meant for other characters on the screen, a bit confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Rich setting, fantastic art style, meaningful decisions during the game. Made with knowledge and passion for its subject. Finally a game for people who were able to pay attention in school. Gems like this are so rare.(Attention deficit action junkies, this game is probably not for you. Fair warning: This is a game where you need a measure of patience and will learn something about history.)
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is a special type of game that really stood out to me. Josh Sawyer, creative director of Fallout: New Vegas, one my favourite games of all time, brings to life another masterpiece  that I can easily call art, which is also the main theme of the game: art and its lasting impact on people and on history. The story is written wonderfully, the soundtrack by Alkemie is amazing and the artstyle is one of a kind.As many have said, after playing it you'll grow as a person. Extremely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I often play games in a way to see everything I can and achieve all the game allows you. You would think then, a game all about being unsure, without enough time and being forced to make choices with things left half done would be my anathema. A game where you always feel like you should have picked the other path. Instead I love Pentiment. It is a story beautifully told and created by a team with incredible passion that shows in every aspect. At the risk of sounding hammy, it's a game about living with your choices and also just living. And it rules.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game that acts like a visual novel but with some gaming dynamics that help digesting big bricks of text and keep the gameplay pleasant and not too repetitive. Stunning visually and they really nailed the characters, all of them becoming part of the town you'll browse through during the whole game.My only "negative point" is that looking at the trailer I thought the game would have way more occult and supernatural elements, and even if it did have some, it really wasn't the focus. Still a very solid and original game for sure !
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Obsidian Entertainment has got to be one of the studios I least expected to make a basically interactive Umberto Eco novel. They definitely have a great love of fiction and narrative, although it has previously extended to mostly fantasy and sci-fi settings in a roleplaying context, but I feel there is an undeniable dedication and reverence to history in this game. I'm not big on historical accuracy, but it feels like an elegant and well researched introduction to an important era of european history.The narrative design feels incredibly cohesive and flows rather naturally, albeit stressfully sometimes, as you have to trust your gut when you prioritise what threads to follow in the limited time you have. Players looking to explore all the plot has to offer will likely have to make peace with playing the game multiple times to uncover all its underlying images poking through the layers that conceal them.Although not one of my favourite games, it's a good game nonetheless, but I'm infinitely more interested in Obsidian as a studio when they pursue titles of this complexity with such lovingly crafted care, so I hope they keep that trajectory going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game's admittedly not for everyone. The lack of combat and initially intimidating old-timey religious vernacular will leave some people bored, at least in the first hour or two before the story really starts to pick up pace.But as someone who struggles with a very short attention span, take my word; your emotional investment will be HEAVILY rewarded with fantastic dialogue, characters, world building, abundant role playing elements and choices that ACTUALLY MATTER and can totally change the path your story takes.I'm not a religious man, and not particularly interested in medieval history, but the way these 2 topics were utilised by Pentiment genuinely made me care about other characters personal beliefs and local history.Don't be put off by these aspects just because they seem pretentious and artsy-fartsy at face value.TL;DR if you like Persona/New Vegas' dialogue systems and social systems, you'll probably be way into this if you can give it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best game I've played since Kingdom Come: Deliverance. Play this game if you:- are a history nerd (Holy Roman Empire in the 16th century, Reformation-era specific)- are an art history nerd (the transition from illuminated manuscripts to print woodcuts)- love mystery stories (Name of the Rose fans welcome)- love stories about small communities with secrets, with lots of connections and long term consequences (Pillars of the Earth, Twin Peaks, The Wire)- are interested in how our past effects our present and ripples into our future- like narrative driven games with little action and no fail states (you can accuse the "wrong" person and the game keeps going, with consequences, no L.A. Noire style rail-roading here!)The game's title is so incredibly apt for its themes. I finished this game and I was bawling at the end. Everyone's game will be different. For real. I loved this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game, you can clearly see it was made by people that love history and it's meaning to society. I really appreciated it's messages. As other users have mentioned it does reminds a bit of Disco Elysium but it still has it distinctive character and feel, so if you liked Elysium, Pentiment will feel like familiar but nevertheless fresh experience.But I'll also have to mention it does start quite slow. Pacing in general is slow and there were times where I had to yawn as I was traversing around the scenes with little relevant dialogue. But those moments are usually not long and game will reward you for your patience with some exciting new discovery or dilemma. I also encountered a little dialogue bug with some characters not properly acknowledging my previous decisions, but it was not game-breaking as the quest still progressed properly. And there are some small visual bugs here and there.But overall if you don't mind a bit slower pace (it's kinda needed since there are tons of characters to follow), I can definitely recommend it. Obsidian at it's finest (Also Alpha protocol 2 pls)
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment was.. something of it's own kind. I personally absolutely LOVED this game. It is so pretty and as a German you notice so many hidden things, it was great! The only thing I find a bit annoying is that I highly recommend the game, It had a lasting impact and a lot of design choices were picked in a very smart way here!10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games I've ever played. Take night in the woods and medieval Bavaria, mix them together and sprinkle in a whole lot of lovely character writing and you get this game.My choices felt like they had genuine consequence. The decisions I made throughout shaped the story quite dramatically. I'm very tempted to go back and play again to see how differently the story would unravel. I also felt like I learn a lot about a period of history I had almost 0 knowledge of. It feels like you're participating in peasant life in ways I'd never thought about before and through this I got a proper gauge of the sort of life and politics of the time. It really pays off. I loved every minute of it from start to end and I wish there were more narrative driven RPGs like this. Definitely recommend to anyone and everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A game that will truly take you back in time to the height of Medieval/Renaissance Germany. The artwork is unique, the dialogue feels realistic, and, most importantly, the story is a masterclass in good writing. Despite not being an action-packed game, the mysteries of Pentiment will have you on the edge of your seat, and compel you forward into taking that next hesitant yet hopeful step towards your conclusion. The time crunch also keeps things really fast-paced, leaving you with a sense of urgency befitting the tense situations you find yourself in. All in all, a great game, that I would highly recommend to any fans of story-driven adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: You can pet all the dogs and cats you encounter. 10/10.Seriously though, the game does have its issues, namely the fact that, to my tastes, the first act felt somewhat rushed. Also, though your actions do affect the destinies of others, your destiny seems somewhat set in stone. But I'm not entirely sure, I have only played it once.The one thing the game absolutely  however, is the historical setting. Its very clear the developers did their research.Also, every single kid in the game is a precious cinammon bun.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I have developed an interest in medieval art and history but I was not prepared for the beautiful story that moved me to tears. This game does a fabulous job of showcasing the virtues and sins of humanity and it was truly a pleasure to play. If you are interested in art, history, or the study of human nature this game may just be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Must-play for anyone who loves (1) history AND (2) manuscripts AND (3) point-and-click ADV; DON'T buy if you're only into crime-solving. There are way better choices. I guess Joshua Sawyer just delivers. Props to the art team; I do wonder if the game is moddable though. I would be more than happy to change certain in-game fonts into Bastarda and Schwabacher/Fraktur variants.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I guess the studio doesn't have a game designer. The game has a lot of locations with content, but they don't give the player any motivation or sign to explore them. When I was on part 4 or 5, I just realized I missed content with some characters, so many. Even though i'm curious and i always try to explore everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: As a foreigner living in Bavaria, I'll definitely recommend this game to anyone who interested in the history of the region and the history of the Reformation. The experience of witnessing the changing times from the perspective of three generations of ordinary people in Tasching (I think it was Garching) is far more impressive than the mental journey of a small number of upper-class rulers or fictional heroes. The angles of interpretation and observation are different, and the conclusions drawn by the viewer and the gamer can be completely different.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and heart-touching story and a mystery whose solution and reveal at the end every bit live up to the long build up. It's common to hear that your choices mater in a game, but in this game, much more than many other RPGs, I felt like a really saw the impact of the actions I had taken across the game played out through the passage of years. At the epilogue I really felt like I had participated and impacted this world.I first encountered the medieval monastery mystery sub-genre with the video game adaptation of Ken Follet's Pillars of the Earth; I went on to read all the books, and Name of the Rose and this game, which has heavy helping of inspiration from those provided just as wonderful of an experience in the area.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10. Incredibly well written, a masterclass in character development, and one of the first games in a while where I actually felt like my choices did have an impact on the world of the game (I'm not too fussed about games just giving you the illusion of choice, but I know some people appreciate when they do matter).I would put it on a very similar category to games like Kentucky Route Zero or Disco Elysium. It has its own very clear identity, but it's on that same level of excepcional gaming experience that only releases every few years.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment might be the next modern classic, after Disco Elysium. It's hard to not wholeheartedly recommend this game, even though it is definitely not for everyone. Pentiment is slow. Pentiment is quiet. Pentiment is visually simple. Pentiment is part of the evolution of text-based gaming and interactive fiction. Here are some thoughts I had while playing (most art is best experienced as blindly as possible, so proceed with caution):- Interesting lack of music, making the few moments where music does occur quite effective, even though it is often simple Gregorian chant or historically accurate folk music.- I praise the lack of an Exp. system, or just a lack of useless collectibles, ‘numbers going up’, the constantly being rewarded for everything you do, the ‘game-y’ stuff. It’s more ethical and respectful. The story, the people in it, and your decision-making is what matters here, and we know that. The player doesn’t need to constantly be given a small dopamine-kick to keep him/her engaged, it invites us, forces us to seek deeper ways of engaging with the game. Very brave of Obsidian. - The red line indicating that a short footnote-like explanation is available is a clever mechanic, informing the player, helping us better understand the history and culture without having us read long in-game books that could break the pace.- The time advancing when pursuing leads is brilliant. Everything you do becomes so much more weighty and important. Thinking carefully through all your options gets rewarded, you don’t have the usual luxury of doing whatever you want, when you want. This makes the meticulous completionist mindset impossible, which greatly helps push the player into a way more fitting mindset of weighing your options carefully and engaging with the world and its people more deeply. You’re not just going through a list of people to talk to, you never know when certain options will become unavailable.I have some minor gripes with the minigames and the 'This will be remembered' when certain dialogue options are chosen (why does this need to be explicit?), but both never really spoiled the experience for me, and I doubt it will for other people.Pentiment is the result of an artist being given the time and resources to fulfill a passion project he has been itching to realize since the 90's. It has an integrity I rarely find in other games, a strong artistic backbone that is impossible to remain unnoticed while playing, and one of the first pieces of heavily researched historical fiction in the history of video games. It might do it at a slower pace than it's predecessors, but Pentiment propels interactive writing forward, just like Disco Elysium and Planescape Torment did, and should absolutely not be overlooked. Play it in chunks of an hour or so, over a long period of time, and with a relaxed but engaged mind. Give it some time to warm up.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Your choices do not matter at all. This is not an RPG. The main draw of the story is the murder mystery, but the mystery is impossible to officially solve in-game in the sense that no matter how you choose to conduct the investigation, whether you succeed or fail any dialogue checks, whoever you accuse is innocent. This is because the game doesn't let you accuse, suspect, or even investigate the real killer. Even more baffling, there is concrete evidence for other people being the killer, and its never explained why that evidence was there if they weren't the killer. Its a really cheap bait and switch because I guess they thought it would be a good "twist" or whatever if it looked like it was 99% obvious one person was the killer but they ended up not being one anyway. One thing I did appreciate is that its possible to figure out who the killer is before the reveal, even if there is no concrete evidence behind it and its more of a process of elimination (also a couple of really obvious hints in act 3). Still, there are a ton of holes an unexplained issues with the killer being who they are. I just don't see the point in a murder mystery game that's this linear and railroaded. Obsidian are known for having so many branching paths in their games so I don't think it would have been impossible to do. Of course, the story as-is is constructed in such a way that it doesn't work at all if the player is ever allowed to suspect and accuse the real killer. But still...without interactivity actually mattering, it just boils down to a VN with lots of tedious puzzles and slice of life that serve no purpose. They should have written the story in such a way as to accommodate choices better, rather than write a linear story and then try to shoehorn choices into it so they can take advantage of their reputation for making excellent RPGs.  Which is a shame, because if you look at it as a pure VN, the story is actually quite good. The dialogue is well written, the characters are complex, etc. This is definitely the level of writing we've come to expect from Obsidian. Which is why I would rather have had the game just commit to openly being a full VN. If you're a big history nerd, like VNs, and aren't put off by the lack of choices mattering, you might want to check this out. For everyone else, I would say not.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A story-based point and click with a wonderful art style, engaging mystery, and interesting themes of narratives of history and purpose in one's life. If you like visual novels or story-heavy games in general and don't mind a lack of gameplay, then I strongly recommend. Its also appealing to those who know or want to know more about the Protestant Reformation, the Holy Roman Empire, and the Renaissance more generally.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This visual novel is great and the only product to come close to achieving the same level of polish, artistic expression and just genuine love that Disco Elysium had that rocked the market when it released. From its inspired art direction, the writing that weaves between intrigue, drama and sentimentality expertly and its solid pacing I cannot do anything but awe.It is not a product that will please everyone, but everyone can see that its great for what it is
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing story. At first the art is strange combined with the differences in text styles depending on who is speaking. The format is so much different than other games I've played (even Otomes). After the first twenty minutes in, however, I was already deeply attached to many of the characters, and invested in the story. As it turns out, there are three different arcs, (which I do not want to spoil here) which was pleasantly surprising. I especially enjoyed following the village as it changed and expanded over the years and eras that defined the scenes of gameplay. The art became detailed and invaluable to me; I really want to give a shout-out to the artists who put so much work into this. There is an overarching mystery among mini-mysteries that need solving, and what was most fun,  It was such a fantastic experience, the only reason I tacked off a half-star is because I wish it was longer. I wish it continued building onto this world and these characters through the span of several generations. Will there be an expansion to this game? I hope so...but probably not. That being said, I will keep my eye open for more games of similar repertoire.Oh, and you know what else was really cool? All the history in this! I learned so much! It's always a major plus when I get to learn actual historical facts while also having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: For me this is the game of the year. Amazing Story, awesome Soundtrack and a refreshing new graphic style. Also the story wasn't stretched until infinity which I hate on modern games so I could finish after around 25 h (played mainly with the steamdeck offline so unfortunately the time is not correctly counted by steam). Also I loved the educating aspect about late medieval life. Even as German I heard the first time about the Via Imperii which runs close to my hometown and I plan now to ride it by bike. The only think i would ask for a second part (hopefully) is even more historical details you can learn about (via optional texted you can open or even with videos with historians you can watch on the side) . I think the aspect of learning while playing is insufficiently used and Pentiment is for me a perfect example that this can work out. Thanks developer for such a great game !
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very enriching and thought provoking! Especially if you allow yourself to have patience with it and suspend any frustration with a couple semi-janky game mechanics and if you really immerse yourself into the culture and time period as best as you can. A couple things could've been smoother but I found myself overlooking any technical flaws as I sunk deeper into the world through the eyes of Andreas Maler (and eventually Magdalene). I am no history buff but with my constant Googling during my play through I learned so much historical context about not only 16th century Bavaria but also surrounding Europe and how the aristocrats, relgious insitutions, and peasantry all were handling the transitions in culture and innovation of the Renaissance.  The atmosphere, the monastic and folk songs sprinkled throughout, the illustrated scenery as you walk through, around, and beneath Tassing, watching and interacting with the lives of the villagers and seeing the changes throughout the decades, and being able to tailor your decisions in a plethora of morally gray scenarios are just some of the reasons that I enjoyed my 20 hours of playing this game. Pentiment is clearly a labor of love, of dedicated research and story building, a relic programmed into a point&click game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: As the credits to Pentiment rolled, I leaned back in my chair and contemplated how exactly I would write a review for it. The game left me awestruck, and throughout my life where I have finished hundreds, maybe even thousands of games—that happens rarely. I didn't really expect anything different from the likes of Josh Sawyer and Obsidian though, they have consistently proven that they are top tier storytellers, but even more so than their other fantastic games, Pentiment stands as grand achievement not only in video games, but literature as a whole. And when I say literature, I mean it. Only Planescape and Disco Elysium match the levels of seer words in this game. There is a LOT of reading, so be warned. If you are the type of person to skip through dialogue as fast possible in order to get to the action, this will most likely not be the game for you. It's slow paced, deliberate, and is filled to the brim with 16th century history that will make you actually LEARN STUFF. However, if you are like me and you enjoy curling up with a novel and a cup of tea every night before bed, or if you are willing to try something new and escape from most modern garbage AAA releases, Pentiment will leave you satisfied with it's excellent mystery, it's fully fleshed out characters—I love Andreas dearly—and it's choice based dialogue that actually has an effect on the world, story, and ending. I urge anyone to at least try the game out, not only because it is easily worth it's asking price, but so other developers will take notes from what has been done here. The renaissance of single player narrative lead RPGS is upon us, and I couldn't be happier about it.Edit: Also you should read The Name of the Rose.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A deep, moving, and truly human narrative. A complex tale of clashing ideologies, masterfully written and realized.The game can be overbearing with front loading a TON of information in its opening hours, and suffers from slight pacing issues later in the game, but despite that, Pentiment sticks the landing- solidifying itself as one of the best in its class.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventures I played in a long time! BUT: You should enjoy reading a lot, so if you don't enjoy that, it might not be for you. Setting, music and overall atmosphere is incredible and the interesting approach to your character background offers some replay value (although I fear that the story is still rather linear, not sure atm) . At first, I had doubts if I would like this game as I struggled with adventures that are too slow for me. For me it was the art style that made me want to play it and I'm so glad that I did. Pentiment always brought something incentive to keep looking for clues or talk to the characters when I feared it could get boring. So well made and definitely a game I will return to. I wish there were more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: CATHOLIC PRAYER SIMULATOR....Yes, all the good things that people are saying about it are true but there's a few things to keep in mind.  It's very tedious.  I think it's great that they provide tidbits of information about history, but I have zero interest in Medieval history so it doesn't do anything for me.  Petting a cat and learning a little about a species of plant was more interesting in this game but that's not the focus.  Using the map in this game is a chore.  It's not completely accurate in pinpointing your location and doesn't load quickly enough for me.  The text also isn't instant.  It gets printed out in text bubbles.  I turned up the speed as fast as it goes and it's still not as fast I can read.  I'd like to instantly click through people saying a prayer before eating.  It has nothing to do with the story and I really don't care.  You really have to be in the right frame of mind and of a particular taste to enjoy this "game".  I think it barely qualifies as a game.  There's some mini games which are an absolute waste of time and pointless and qualify even less as a game.  This "game" is reading A LOT, running back and forth, doing mundane tasks, etc.  It really bogs down the core of the story which is rather interesting and it's a shame.  You should be able to rip through this game and be left with a memorable experience, not falling asleep at your keyboard.  That's why I'm warning you that regardless of how fast you read, the game will force you to kill time in a way that isn't fun by doing things like running back to your room to sleep.  It's filler.  I mean, the game is twenty bucks.  I wasn't expecting a whole hell of a lot but getting annoyed was not one of them.  The "choices" you make in it are basically dialogue options.  I'm okay with that.  I recommend reading reviews or watching video reviews before purchasing.  I really want to get through this game and finish the story but it's annoying the hell out of me.  For some, I'm sure it's right up their alley and I respect that.  It's certainly unique in some regards.  For me, I won't be playing this sort of "game" again anytime soon ;-)  Late edit:  this game has its moment but FAR too many moments with no moments and some that are incredibly depressing.  I don't play games to endure excruciating boredom to get to the end.  Like, having to recite Catholic prayers after confession.  Why tf would I want to do that in a video game?  Who thought that would be enjoyable?  Why would I want to read a conversation printed out in Latin and have to wait for the game to translate it to English?  E  Great way to ruin what could be an interesting and smooth game.  This is the most self-indulgent boring s*** I've ever played in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, but it's not for everyone (that's ok!), but I have some issues with it.Issue 1: No manual savingI know the point of the game is that it's smaller and by design, it is supposed to be replayed, but it sucks not having manual saving. I've accidentally picked wrong dialog choices and sometimes have no way to reset to that point. It is impossible to know how reacting to certain events might impact future interactions. I get that this is the point, but when I try to be polite to or reassure someone, and it ends up making me fail a persuasion attempt, I can't help but get upset. Issue 2: PacingAct 1 has the best pacing of the game, honestly. You pick your character build, have a clear goal, and a murder happens. There's several suspects and many pieces of evidence. It's early enough in the game where you can reset and explore a 2nd option or a different path. However, Act 2 takes a while to get going, but the investigation part feels very limited. Act 3 seemed like it dragged on too long. I loved seeing how the town builds and changes, but Act 3 had me hoping it was going to end soon, honestly.The game is too long to be a "pick up and play" kind of game. It took me numerous hours to finish the game. While I'd love to replay with a different path, pick a different suspect, and do different choices, it's going to be several hours of a commitment that I am not sure I want to make very often. If the game was a bit shorter in certain parts, or we had manual saving, I would feel more eager to explore every path/choice. Issue 3:Weird logic statesThis game was designed for game pass, and to be cheaper on platforms. It's only 20 bucks. I know they didn't have as much time, but I did find some bugs in the game that impacted immersion.As an example:I had a law background for my character and after helping a widow, she had me examine a letter about her home. She was told she would lose the house because she is a woman and cannot inherit from her dead husband. She will be homeless by act 2 if we do not intervene. If you have the law background, you can point flaws and tell her how to save her house. When you interact with a legal authority later, you can tell him about this and he will intervene on her behalf to make it right. When you start Act 2, she will be happier and still in her home. Despire this, I had some characters mention how she lost her home. One NPC expressed concern about a daughter not marrying and suffering the same fate as the widow I just helped.Another point this happened was that I missed the autopsy of a murder suspect, but I could tell an NPC an aspect of it that I wouldn't be able to know. I was able to tell him that the assumed murder weapon wasn't the real murder weapon and I could say that I was at the autopsy when I wasn't. The game allows you to lie in the game, but it's always prefaced with the [lie] tag. This is rare, but it happens. Logic and branching paths is always hard to handle and it can spiral out of control. I do this for a living and it can be a nightmare making sure all paths make sense. Issue 4: Lack of changes on outcomeYou can make a lot of changes in individual people's lives, but a lot of things don't seem to have a choice. Regardless of what you do, certain events happen. The ending is ultimately the same, key events happen regardless of what you do. It was a fun journey, and whole characters might be missing from the game if you do different things, but you can't do much to the core narrative. I wish the game allowed you to shape certan events in favor of the other party and cause a ripple effect.Still a wonderful game. I'd say 8.5/10 or so.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with a fun and engaging story. Unlike some people, I didn't find it very replayable though. At first I did, but upon my second playthrough I realized that my expectations were a big bigger than the game's scope. I figured my choices would make huge differences and it would be almost a totally different game based on a few key choices (eg. in Witcher 2 siding with Iorvath or Roach in Act 1 kind of differences). Nope. The game sort of ends up in the same place at the end of each individual act no matter what you choose. That said, it's definitely a good game, and definitely worth a buy (I bought it on a good sale and don't feel bad about that), but don't expect as much replay value as I did. You'll get different outcomes based on your choices (dialog and such) but you *won't* get a different world to play in as I believed.

_childDocuments_.review: God bless this game... and I say that entirely as a non-Christian.This entire game so far has been nothing but a delight and a joy, and brings back memories of a happier childhood as well as giving love and care to my habits of a passion for history. It was gifted to me, so I suppose in a sense I got this for free, but it's so much beyond the price that it's hard to put into words.The clear care taken to be historically accurate with the attitudes of the Church at the time, in that era, and being able to see it through a modern lens in such a richly detailed style is a wonder. The tiny little animation details. The dialogue corrections with each character. The color palette and line work...I apologize, words truly fail me. Play this game, please. Despite the heavy subject matter. Even if you're not religious. ... Especially if you're not religious, come to think on it. It won't convert you by any means (nor should it), but the sheer passion on display with this game absolutely shines through from visuals to the music. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: If you like history, you need to play this game. That's really it. If you are like me, and usually more drawn to historic strategy games, give this game a try. It might upend your perspective and your idea on what history actually is and how it's written. Pentiment is an insanely "historically accurate" game (loaded term, I know) but playing this you actually learn a lot about the early reformation era in Bavaria (and Europe), the codex is neatly woven into the game to give you new things to appreciate. You also learn about peasant and religious customs during the game. Initially I wasn't too hot on the idea that there is no voice acting, but the way the game uses font and literacy to convey information makes up for it. The dialogues are also fairly short and straight forward compared to Disco Elysium for example.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Josh Sawyer turned his history degree into a very good murder mystery game. The worldbuilding is great, the characters are memorable, and it's all done in a beautiful medieval art style. Character building is great and the various things you can do within the time limit makes it an interesting feat trying to follow as many leads as you can. Plus the "true" culprit of each case being left ambiguous makes it an even more interesting case of player choice. The different traits and backgrounds for Andreas make each version of him you create feel special, even if the game doesn't branch off hugely from the predetermined narrative. These elements all come together to make a very immersive world, where lore and events feel more like a piece of actual history and culture than just a part of a game.My main drawbacks, after getting all of the achievements, have a lot to do with the limits of player interactivity. The people that are executed, which should be the most impactful choices in the game, often result in minor relationship changes. I thought that the first person I accused () had caused , only to find out that happens regardless of your choice. Plus the final act of the game  makes the game's player reputation feel much less important in the late-game. Thankfully , but the meantime feels much weaker than the writing in the rest of the game.Other issues that weren't too important but are to note are the page turns for each area, making it very annoying when you're lost, and the map navigation for more intricate spaces, like the Cloister, more confusing. There is also no option for manual saving, which makes sense as a way to discourage save-scumming, but it makes it very annoying when you need to do something else but you have to wait until the end of a long dialogue before it auto-saves. Josh Sawyer's stance is understandable, but when there are so many achievements that require you to pick one of many options, you might as well give people the chance to save to avoid tedium.Pentiment is an overall great game. If you like mystery games and strong narratives, or you just want to see some beautiful art, this game is very easy to recommend. Plus, with the game being $20 not on sale, it's a steal to get a game this well-made for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment feels to me like an important game because it stands out in its immersive storytelling that plays out during a long stretch of time. I'm not the biggest point-and-click player as I tend to lose interest (despite my wanting to get more into the genre). Pentiment was engaging and the story took twists and turns that surprised me. _childDocuments_.review: My game of the year, and likely a top 2-3 game of all time for me. While excelling on its own merits as a whodunit, "choices matter" goose chase, Pentiment made me fall in love with a people and a town and a time (so much so that I've been drawn to reading about 16th century Europe in my own time). The art style is excellent, the writing superb, and the attention to historic details is delightful. A must purchase for fans of story heavy adventures or mysteries.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Cool adventure game that makes full use of its setting in 16th century Bavaria.  The characters are memorable, and the plot is intriguing.  Art and sounds are phenomenal, and there are little touches that elevate the game.  For example, the font used when a character is talking is based on their work, education level, etc.  Priests and nuns have a Gothic font, the well educated use a cursive-style font, the peasants have a simpler script, and book printers have a block print.    The major negative to the game is that all the decisions you make don't have a huge impact on the plot of the game.  Each Act ends in pretty much the same way, with some actions seemingly railroaded for the sake of the plot, not how you developed the character.  That being said, all the choices you made can impact many minor things throughout the story, and the ending does a good job of highlighting those results.It's a game more about the journey than the destination, but it's a great journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: A beautifully illuminated adventure set in the life and times of a fictional version of Albrecht Durer.Review: One of the most surprising games to come out of 2022 for me, Pentiment has you playing a young German artist (no doubt in my mind based on Albrecht Durer) who finds that he must solve a mystery in a small German town to save a friends life. Without going into spoilers... err, apart from that previous spoiler, I enjoyed this game a great deal, the artwork is astounding and well-made with details that brought many a smile to this old man. My gripes were primarily to do with plot and pacing - it felt to me that it rushed the story in the beginning (the mystery part), then slowed down towards the middle, then sped up right at the very end. The plot itself didn't have any major flaws, although it did lead me to believe that the choices in the story didn't matter much as it railroads plot at a few crucial points. There is a buzz about how Pentiment is a medieval version of Disco Elysium, however that doesn't wash for me given the freedom DE gives you to solve the mystery (I mean you can finish that game without even looking at the body FFS!).Conclusion: To conclude - this is an excellent game that I will definitely play again (once the obligatory amount of time has past for me to forget who-did-it) and I would 8/10 recommend it if you're a fan of medieval art-work, adventure games, and mysteries. Don't expect an RPG with mechanics like Disco Elysium though, that game is still in a league of its own.Edit: I forgot to add - a similar type of game (perhaps a un-linked sequel) set in medieval Japan with the artwork done in ukiyo-e would be amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is, like its inspirations,  a true work of art.An expansive Story with diverse, interesting Characters that change a lot over time combined with an amazingly detailed Art Direction and Sound Design. Pentiment manages to immerse you in the historic period it plays in while incorperating many Aspects of said History and the Myths around it.If you like the Artstyle, dont mind reading ( a lot ), Enjoy a Story that your choices truly affect,Then Pentiment is a game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is a game developed by Obsidian Entertainment and published by Xbox Game StudiosThe game offers some nice graphics and a superb aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessPentiment overall, however, is an incredibly fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a superbly amazing adventure game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is two parts murder mystery and one part figuring out the overall why. Where it's never revealed if you were right or wrong in fingering a suspect. Which means there is no wrong option only right ones, though some are more right than others. You are given a small amount of time to investigate more options than you can possibly check in a single playthrough. Leading to the illusion there is more to the game. In fact you'll find about 85% of all the info every single playthrough so followup playthroughs don't really change or reveal anything you didn't alright sorta know. You can go down different paths and still end up with roughly the same info. The final act is just going over information you've been picking up throughout the game just encase you missed it. Meaning a lot of it feels like filler. I don't want to go into any more info to avoid spoilers. I feel like the game's main draw is it's appearance. It's got a unique art style as well as an interesting font choice. Where the text is written out in a style related to each persons education, even with typos that are corrected. For a while it looks great... after a while you'll realise it takes ages for each line to be written and it goes from charming to just being pretentious. When going for a second playthrough it makes the game feel so tedious as pretty much everything said is just repeated from the first playthrough. After my first playthrough I was on the fence if I'd recommend it or not, more leaning to yes but the 3rd act really hindered the game, then I decided to see if any choices actually made a difference in this choices matter game... they didn't. That's what put me off recommending this to anyone. (I left the game running if you're wondering about playtime.)
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, the art and historical detail is masterful. The only game I've played that comes close to capturing this level of accuracy in a game is Kingdom Come: Deliverance, but because this covers a different period and perspective of Medieval Europe, there's so much to learn.I won't spoil the story, but the game has some issues, to the point where I disagree with its overwhelmingly positive reception. The purpose and impact of your decisions is not well choreographed. There are plenty of situations where my decisions resulted in the exact opposite outcome from the one I wanted. I wasted plenty of time (maybe an hour in total) trying to cover every potential option I had since the game did not always clearly communicate when all of my options had been expended.There are 3 acts, and the first 2 are very well done. The third is disruptive but never delivers on any advantages that the disruption promises. By that, I mean that the story established in the first and second acts would have been significantly more effective if it was allowed to conclude in the way it seemed it was going to. Instead, the third act introduces a variety of plot lines and story decisions that neuter an otherwise beautiful story. I don't regret finishing the game, but it promised something different and better than it delivered, which keeps it from sticking out in my mind as a game I would ever mention when listing my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game ages ago with the intent of playing it immediately. Life got crazy and I forgot about it. I had the flu recently and that allowed me to get the chance to actually sit down and play this amazing game.I did not read any reviews before touching the game, keep in mind.It is a time based game, and I wish I spent more time at the beginning exploring, because honestly I thought this game was going to be over in 5 hours TOPS.The replayability of this game is amazing, with almost every choice leading you down a different path. I'm not sure if the end result would ultimately be different, but the stories and the lives of the characters surely have to be effected.This game made me cry and I really was not expecting to fall in love with the characters. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing. I don't normally write reviews for games, but oh my god was this game good. It's definitely for a certain niche, but if you fall within it you'll love this game. Pentiment isn't so much a game as it is a narrative experience; you experience a particularly intriguing artist's life split between 3 parts over several decades. There isn't much "gameplay" here, even if there is a good deal of player agency. You almost must have a good understanding of the Early Modern Period along with the Late Middle Ages if you're to enjoy and appreciate this game to it's fullest, though I'm confident you could still enjoy it without such. The art is amazing, the OST is amazing (although a bit underutilized imo), and there's just so much more that I can't say without spoiling the story. Please, buy Pentiment
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Cadfael, or The Name of the Rose, but as a Choose Your Own Adventure.Be prepared for soul-wrenching decisions at every turn!  And yes, every single thing matters!  I have to say it's also quite a lot of reading, including some pretty front-loaded exposition!  Are you familiar with the politics of 16th century rural Bavaria?  Well, you're about to be.  All this stressed me out initially, and it's not even really my genre, and I was honestly a bit overwhelmed at first.But the depth of this world pulled me back in, over and over.  Beautiful, honest, and audacious.  This game is a masterwork.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle with where to begin when writing this review. Rarely, if ever, has a piece of media touched me as deeply as Pentiment has. I finished my first play-through mere moments ago, and I'm completely in awe of the masterwork of both visual and narrative storytelling displayed by the creators of this game. Successfully portraying the game in the style of illuminated manuscripts must have been difficult beyond measure, but the time, effort, and dedication spent doing so absolutely paid off. I was completely immersed in the art, finding myself speechless at the amount of love and attention that was given to every moment of the game. A particular detail that never failed to make me smile was the text; specifically, how the black letters were written in order, with the colored ink filled in afterwards. The choice of having stylized fonts represent the station of the speaker was inspired. I'm also incredibly impressed by the fluidity of the character's movements; both in larger actions, as well as things like a face turning away from the viewer.On a personal note, I'm extremely grateful for the depiction of "smaller" figures, historically given less attention than the aristocracy. In particular, the portrayal of queer relationships were incredibly meaningful to me. So often, homosexuality is treated like a recent phenomenon, but we've always been here, we've just had to hide - however, that didn't stop them from having fulfilling lives and relationships. The same goes for neurodivergent people - Brother Volkbert is an excellent example of how autistic individuals would thrive in the order and quiet of monastic life. The inclusion of the Sommerfields, Vácslav, and Brother Sebhat also added much needed dimension to flesh out the world of the game and address the prejudices of the time, while still respecting them as individuals.This game intersects at so many of my special interests: illuminated manuscripts, 15th and 16th century monasteries, Reformation Europe, and the daily lives of those present. Honestly, it matches up so perfectly that I had accepted that it could never live up to my standards. I've never been more happy to be wrong. As I watched the credits, I found myself truly absorbing every name that passed by, thanking every individual who clearly held so much love and dedication for a time period so often overlooked. Every last person involved in this game's creation has my gratitude and admiration. Thank you for everything.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend Pentiment.While the game's artstyle and setting are something refreshing, the writing and "choices matter" gameplay are not. Going into this game practically blind (having only read a few Steam reviews), I expected to get a deep, story-rich game where you could truly immerse yourself in a setting not often portrayed in games.Unfortunately, all I received was railroading, unexplained mechanics, misplaced minigames and the bitter feeling of my time being utterly wasted. After playing the first two acts, I felt disatisfied with the way my "choices" were being handled. There is always a sense of being rushed along due to time limits. Things that absolutely should have been dialogue options in key moments were completely lacking, most likely because an arbitrary checkpoint was not reached in a satisfactory manner. There is a system in place for persuasion, which the game only informs you of once one actually occurs. Up until that point, there is no indication that whatever is being "remembered" by characters will be used in a persuasion check.In hindsight, most of my time played was spent running around the town to see if any new dialogue popped up after having a conversation or receiving a semi-confession from someone. For a large majority of the time, absolutely nothing changed. There is no real way to shape your character, to make your choices have impact, or to feel like you've actually done something good for a change. After completing about a quarter of act 2, I just stopped talking to people that should've had something useful to say, because it became clear that I was being railroaded into a narrowing path that the writers carefully set out. After act 2 ended, I just didn't see any reason to continue playing the game at all. I tried to care about act 3, but I really just couldn't.As other reviewers have said; take away the artstyle and setting, and you just have a mediocre Telltale-like story.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: While there's an overarching story that's being told and you mostly get smaller decisions to make for the events, Pentiment is a very good Adventure/Roleplaying Game with great writing and historical research done to verify it, in the optical style of the late medieval christian art. Its beautiful, sounds good and the story and characters are well written. I liked this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: It's been some time since I was last so utterly engrossed and DEEPLY touched by a game. Obsidian did an astounding job in re-creating the life and struggles of people in the 16th century, telling a mystery of human psychology, and above all — visualizing the weight of time. You will find the graphics and the "performance" of text in this game so vivid that they blend perfectly with the story and reward a patient mind with one of the most well-orchestrated experiences unique to video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overall positive but it's a mixed bag.The graphical style is excellent.  It looks like a medieval book scribed by monks (which is also what the story is about).  The art direction is superb.  There's lot of nice stylistic touches like how the class of each person you talk to is depicted in the font type in their text boxes.The story is good enough.  You follow a 16th century painter working as a book copier in an abbey who ends up investigating murders that happen around him.  The game is separated into different sections where the game will timeskip ahead years and you see how the setting has changed based on the results of your investigations.  The payoff at the end of the game is satisfactory.  The writing and characters are all quite strong.The problem is the gameplay.  As investigative games go this one is quite weak, on account of the devs going whole hog into the "choices matter" approach.  Regrettably the game is filled with opaque dialogue choices that effect things you can't see, and limited investigation time where you cannot possibly collect all the clues.  The key in these types of games is that no matter what you choose that you feel like you are progressing towards the truth, but in this game the choices instead feel like you're only missing things and losing information permanently.  For example, you might have a choice of half a dozen different people to have lunch with, and if you choose the right people and the right choices during the meal you will get a clue.  But choose the wrong people and the wrong choices and you get nothing but flavor text.  Worse, you will suddenly get "skill check" gates thrown up that you have only one chance of passing and it's all based on innocuous dialogue choices you may have made earlier (and often YEARS EARLIER).  Oh, you can't get this clue because this person didn't change jobs seven years ago because you didn't encourage them to disobey their parents when they were five years old.  Enjoy!  No, I don't enjoy that type of thing at all.Another ugly aspect of this system is there doesn't appear to be a "true" culprit in many of the cases.  You can collect compelling circumstantial evidence on numerous people and then you just have to accuse someone.  The game sort of twists around whatever you chose as reality but it feels massively unsatisfying.  In these type of investigative games the whole payoff is pooling your evidence together, throwing it in the suspect's face, and getting them to crack.  That doesn't happen here.  Your accusation targets often act like victims denying it even as they are executed!  Reminds me of Paradise Killer which had a similar thing going on and it didn't feel good there either.Now the final end of the story doesn't have this problem thankfully, but that's also because you don't get any meaningful choices effecting the plot at the end of the game.  The story railroads into an actual satisfying conclusion, but then your choices really didn't matter all that much now did they?  What a waste.Still, the game is well worth playing overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is an incredible game that delivers a singularly human experience as it delves into how we shape history through culture, oral tradition, and what is finally written down. The sound design is minimalistic but exactly what it needs to be, and the art is as luscious and well thought-out as one would expect a game touting the influence of renaissance-era illuminated manuscripts would have. It offers a thoroughly well-researched window into life during the early 16th century, from duties to dress to social life and even to the food! Tassing might not be real, but having visited Bavaria throughout my life, it feels incredibly real to me. If you have the opportunity to go to Bavaria, Fussen and the surrounding area are likely to give you a feel for what you see in game. Overall, the writing is great, and you really get the feeling that you're part of an older culture. My only complaint is how they chose to tie things together in the end (I would have liked a little more player involvement there) but that's hardly the end of the world. If you're a fan of history, illuminated manuscripts, period whodunnits, oral traditions, unreliable narratives, roleplaying games, and point and click adventures, then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece of a visual novel where your choices do matter - to a point (the arc of history remains intact).  The deep historical research and literary touch to the storyline elevates this game to a level that few other games attain.  I was most impressed by how the renaissance social landscape with its rigid class structures, which is so foreign to our twenty first century minds, was conveyed in the finely-tuned dialogue.  I have just finished the game and look forward to playing it again in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful narrative journey that hooks you with its murder mystery, charms you with its minutiae of 16th century Bavarian life, and breaks your heart with the hefty consequences of your own actions. Few games evoke such a full spectrum of emotions: wistful regret, rustic contentment, agonizing helplessness, communal joy, weary hope. This is not one of those reload-and-find-the-best-path sort of mysteries; you're not going to solve everyone's problems, and certainly aren't going to make everyone happy. Pentiment has you sit with your decisions and witness their effects, both immediate and generational (and for better or worse). Along the way is an unexpected abundance of perspective to be gained. The game's themes of language and translation, religious and mythological syncretism (a word I had to look up just now), and good old-fashioned class struggle are effortlessly relevant today (and, honestly, in any era of recorded history). Pentiment is a one-of-a-kind experience that will leave you feeling enriched and-- if you're paying attention --heavy-laden.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who isn't a fan of text-heavy games, I found the game daunting at the start and was overwhelmed by the amount of information I needed to absorb. However, there's something so compelling about the world of Pentiment that kept pulling me back into the game, and around 5 hours in I found myself right at home in Tassing.Gorgeous art, compelling characters and a gripping story line. Seriously, amazing job to the developers for pouring so much love and passion into the game and for delivering such an important message. Special shoutout to Andreas, Pierro, Claus, Magdalene and my boi Mausfanger, they live on in a tiny part of my heart!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment will not appeal to everyone but it definitely worked for me. It’s an excellent game that was clearly created by a highly talented and passionate team. The writing was great throughout the game and the ending was a worthy conclusion to a nuanced story that constantly had me hooked. The sound design and unique art direction were also fantastic, keeping me immersed in the world of 1500s Bavaria throughout my playthrough. The game's light RPG elements give Pentiment a level of replayability and I expect to try a second playthrough in the future where I make different choices to see how that affects the game. I found Pentiment to be a great game that was well worth the price and while this game won’t be for everyone if you find the premise intriguing I’d definitely recommend giving it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Great and interesting game with a lot of choice outcomes. A murder mystery at its core but more than that it is a very intriguing historical story about change, religion and sense of self. The setting of 1500s Germany was perfect and felt very unique. Disco Elysium is my favorite game of all time and this, while not in the same league of masterpiece, has some comparisons in gameplay and story. There were a couple moments in this that really did resonate for me. Overall def worth trying for anybody who likes this specific niche of walking simulator murder mystery in a struggling small city going through a lot of change.

It is not for reveryone, this has to be said.If you want to learn something while you play good story, this is game for you. If you expect action and fast paced gameplay, do not no buy this game.
