_childDocuments_.review: A bit of a spoiler, but you solve two mysteries (one per each of the first two acts) in this game and there are no "correct"/canon solutions; whatever you choose is right (maybe, we never really know for sure). I hate this aspect of the game. It annoys the hell out of me. When I solve a mystery, I like it to be actually solved, with a correct answer/solution. So don't play this game if you want to be right at solving the mystery or "win" in that way--you literally cannot do that, at least not in the traditional sense.Otherwise, cool art, cool concept, decent game play (even if it was 95% running back and forth talking to people and dialogue was boring or slow sometimes). Excellent use of religious syncretism as a theme and plot device (which is also a bit of a spoiler, but for anyone who is familiar with Roman mythology, you'll *immediately* know something is up if you look at St. Satia's shrine at the beginning of Act I, because you'll be like "gurl, whatchu doin' here, when did you change your name??"). Anyways, lots of cool layers about history, religion, myth, and the cultural stories we tell ourselves about our past.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wondrous game that isn't for everyone. Just to explain what this game is about it's closest to a choose your own adventure with elements of education (You learn a lot about 16th century Europe during protestant reformation & the catholic church trying to stay dominant during that time), murder mystery, philosophical discussions especially about its main theme of how history is remembered which if you're familiar with games like Planescape Torment you'll love your ideas being challenged if you don't mind the game being text heavy & a strong case of a walking simulator that can be engrossing. I know the game is commonly described as the medieval Disco Elysium but I think it more appropriate to what I said above since the only RPG mechanic there is a speech success mechanic depending on choices you make. The artstyle is closest to a holy combination of Monty Python & old medieval art books. I will never forget  which I beg of you to play blind. Having a parent pass away recently  that filled a hole in my heart.I was also pondering thoughts on how to write this review since so many ideas were presented like how we educate the future, possible consequence(s) of erasing harmful parts of history , How grief is handled which I personally appreciated, the beautiful parts of humanity showcasing how destructive & innocent we are in 3 acts, Having a new appreciation on religion especially learning how each of them worked (I loved learning the  & also a rarity to showcase Jewish history) & the love of art despite the chaos surrounding us every day.I don't know how else to say that I'm glad this game was made and I'm grateful for Obsidian for making this despite it not being the norm in today's market especially with how it deals with faith. There might be some prudes that'll be up in arms about how religion is displayed honestly with the amount of swearing it has which is strange to be outraged at considering the other historical subject matter which you're not spared from the details. The only part of the game I was a bit confused about which might require another playthrough was the Overall I strongly recommend this game whether you buy it full price or on sale. If you also want some more reading material Sawyer shared his  for creating this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Charming art, plus an interesting and complex story. It has good replayability due to the various possible decisions at important (albeit, at sometimes seemingly unimportant) points in the storyline.Be prepared to read a lot as there are no spoken dialogs, but it's absolutely worth it. The game really has some Name of the Rose vibes. If you like investigations and connecting the dots based on spoken or seen evidence than you'll like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up loving this game.Ok, so I wanted to start a new game + to beeline the story to get some achiv I missed. I later on found myself talking and exhausting all dialogue options all over again and discovering new information and intrigue. The story is just THAT well told. Also the world-building is so great, that by the end of it, I felt a little empty because I really started to feel a sense of belonging to the community. I don't know if it's a 10 but It might as well be for you. For me sure is pretty damn close. Edit: I actually came back to leave a review because I remembered how much i loved/miss this game but I already wrote one. If only I could recommend this game more than once. Look, as a game, it's garbage. The core game-play loop is reading cause there is no voice acting sadly. That's not why anyone buys games, especially in 2022 when technology allows a far more alluring storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is so obviously a game where the creators had a strong and unique vision. You live through several snapshots in time, all connected by tragedy. As a young artist working in a dying field, you are struggling to finish a work good enough to become a Master in art when along comes a nobleman to the Bavarian abbey you are working in. You have to work to the clear the name of someone very close to you. But can you really say who did it?This game is gorgeous. Every character is illustrated in a different style of Illumination, depending on their age and origin. Marginalia are present around the game screen when you take out your map or journal, or consult the (very thorough) glossary. It is also very well written. There are many people on the dev team that have gone above and beyond due diligence. This is very historically accurate to Bavaria in the times surrounding the Great Reformation. Pagan beliefs merge and intertwine with Catholicism, black magic is whispered about in towns and abbeys, and superstition and paranoia run rampant.You will inevitably have regrets or question yourself in this game. Your actions shape this little town, influencing people's lives for decades as you progress through the story. There isn't really an optimal ending. Time keeps moving. People die and it's senseless. The narrative isn't neat and clean. Which is why I feel this game has so much to tell.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing story driven game.While the very beginning of the game is a bit slow and the third act is not as strong as the 2 before it it's still a very well made game over all.Over the course of the game you'll truly care for the townsfolk that you get to meet.They're so well written that they seem like real people in a weird way.In any case if you like story driven games and you don't mind reading a whole lot I can recommend this game wholeheartedly.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I am a medieval nerd.  Specifically, I'm a nerd about the time period this game is set in (1495-1550).    This is wonderful.  The art is thoughtful and beautiful, the story is compelling, the mystery resolves in a satisfactory, if not 100 % surprising manner, the characters are heartbreaking and real.  I will probably replay it for getting all the trophies.  My only complaint is that the bibliography in the credits scrolled by too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Now that is a solid Role-Playing Game.While nothing here blew me away or anything, every single aspect of it is done in done adequately. There really aren't any glaring flaws. The game is pretty simple in terms of gameplay, you basically just go from place to place talking to people, which is perfectly fine given that the writing is great and the art direction is cute while remaining true to the Renaissance aesthetic. Too many RPGs feel overburdened with pointless additions, from Disco Elysium's long travel times and progress locking behind skill checks, to Persona's boring combat, to... basically everything about those '90s role playing ""games"" that old people delude themselves into thinking are masterpieces.Pentiment does away with the needless trappings of its peers to focus on what really matters: the story and characters. Despite its large cast, each character feels unique and the protagonists' relationships to them feel real. The game also deals with interesting themes of rebellion and tradition, that I don't really want to spoil.A strong recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A real gem for everyone that love and/or study history. The time period selected for this game is quite interesting because it's unusual and that's make it very interesting. Although the events recalled within the game are fictitious, the perks of Pentiment are the accuracy of the historical context.The art of the game recalled very much the artworks of XVI century and that is amazing ! It helps very much to the whole atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought this game, I assumed it was just a really good indie game made by some really passionate people who were inspired by Disco Elysium. Then, the Obsidian Entertainment logo appeared, and I knew I was in for something magical. Pentiment is an indie game with a triple-A budget, if that makes sense. It's filled to the brim with the personality, passion, and creativity that's characteristic of indie titles, but with no expenses spared or creative punches pulled. Obsidian is now a veteran game developer studio. With Pentiment, they had an artistic vision they wanted to bring across, and they brought it across with surgical precision. The writing, artwork, and story in this game are all superb. Story:Pentiment is a medieval murder mystery. You'll be running around talking to people and collecting clues in a very authentic depiction of 16th century Bavaria. If the last two sentences intrigues even the slightest bit, then go ahead and pick this game up. I won't say much more about the story because some narrative experiences are best experienced blind. I'll just say that it's a very compelling and well-written story from start to finish. Characters:Characters talk, act, and feel very human. They also move in a very human way; a lot of attention to detail has been put into the sprite animations for each character: their facial expressions will shift to match what they're saying, and their movements make them feel like actual people who have to physically move their body through space, if that makes sense. Although everyone looks like a paper cutout from a storybook, never was my suspension of disbelief broken in thinking of these characters as actual, living human beings. They, talk, think, act and react very naturally to your actions and the events of the game, and I can definitely believe that this was how people from the 16th century were. None of this was generated using a facial expression algorithm like in a 3D open world game, by the way. Everything in Pentiment is painstakingly hand-drawn, and you need to see it for yourself. Role-playing:While CDPR, Ubisoft, and Bethesda have always struggled with what the term "role-playing game" actually means, Obsidian faces no such issue. Pentiment is a true role-playing game, where you can create your own character who is only good at certain things but not everything, and whose choices actually affect the outcome of the narrative. You really get invested in everything your character does and what happens in the story because they are all directly caused by your actions as the player. Things you say to someone earlier or in passing will often come back up later in persuasion checks, which pushes you to really "roleplay" and choose what you want your character to say to someone, like, you know, in real life. The game is intentionally built with multiple playthroughs in mind, and on each run with a different character, you'll definitely learn more and more to piece together the whole picture.Cons:There is no real complaint I can think of about the game except for maybe a somewhat slow start and slow ending. Oh, and the music is also quite sparse, but I think this is a deliberate artistic choice. The game is filled with sounds that immerse you into the scene like birds chirping, your footsteps underneath, the wind blowing, peasants working the farm, etc. Obsidian opted for maximum immersion over background music, and I really appreciate that. Oh hey, my complaints about the game somehow turned into praise. That's just how great this game is. I 100% recommend you get this game if you're in the market for a mystery role-playing experience like Disco Elysium.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed (enjoying) this game a great deal. I'm not sure if this will appeal to younger gamers, but for those with a few more years on the clock -  a good deal of thought has been put into this tale.  In short it's a bit like being the lead character in a cross between "The name of the rose" and "It's a wonderful life".Not sure if all the characters' stories marry with the choices you make, but that's a reflection on how well the game is put together. You lose sight of it being a game of many characters, rather than just your own story. Can't wait to complete Act 2 and 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best I've ever played when it comes to story and visuals. The humanity of it has touched my heart so many times, and I cried a lot in just one playthrough. The art is beautiful. I learned a lot about 16th century Europe. The game mechanics are simple yet varied just enough to keep you engaged without distracting from the story. You can pet the cats and dogs. Incredible game all-around, I wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot, it pains me, but no, I can't. I cannot reccoment a game that follows on the Telltale formula where it fools you onto thinking choices matter when in fact no matter what you do things play out the same way. I suspected it after the first act and then confirmed it on the second. No matter what you do, nothing changes, the story is linear, and the feeling that anything you do or say has consequence is false.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: God Bless gamers, have you thought about marriage? Do you remember it was so hard for women in medieval times? wanna read some encyclopedia entries or be told off by npcs? Or perhaps you want to enjoy seeing the town and abbey burning after you lose hope of finding anything interesting its inhabitants or their lives?In one sentence after a time, promise of digital 'Il nome della rosa' fades and you don't feel engaged, you feel annoyed by GUI unresponsiveness, slow paced and unneventful story and overall dullness. If you stick with it, and try to play to the end, you may end up doing an exasperated rant in steam comment section as I'm doing right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, thoughtful, visually-striking and well-researched game with a cast of characters I was excited to learn more about as the story progressed. It is also one of precious few games of its type to deal with its subject matter, doing so with incredible detail. Though it is a historical game, one needn't know anything going in -- all manner of allusions, ideas and era-specific terms are explained to the player through helpful tooltips. All in all, a worthwhile experience and one of the better games I've played in 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Remember learning about Martin Luther and his Twelve Theses in history class? Vaguely? Well Pentiment is set in the 16th century during the time of Martin Luther. That time period is a lot more interesting than history class makes it out to be.In Pentiment, you play as Andreas, an artist working at the local scriptorium. You make images for religious texts. After you finish your current project, you plan to go to Nuremburg to marry a woman you've never met. Unfortunately, things fall soon fall a part after someone is murdered. Your friend is the prime suspect, and you're forced to find the true culprit otherwise he'll be executed. However, as you investigate you soon realize that things are much much more complicated than they seem. Everyone is hiding secrets. No one can be trusted.It's clear the game's creators did their research (there is a bibliography at the end after all), and there are lots of historical and religious references to Lutheranism, the Holy Roman Empire, and Christian and Roman figures. All of this was overwhelming at first. The game does underline the name of places, characters, and important religious figures in red in the dialogue bubble. Clicking on that sends you to a glossary that shows the person's face or explains the place or religious figure. That helped a lot and ended up being quite educational. Something else I like is that choices do matter. When I first saw the notification that the person would remember that I rolled my eyes a bit. There's been plenty of games where you're led to believe your choices matter, but in the end they don't or they are only superficial. Well, I ended up being surprised when a character refused to tell me something. All the actions the game labels important affect your success in persuading other characters to help you or reveal information. The game tells you what choices helped or hindered you in persuading the characters. I appreciated that, as I could see how my choices added up, and it helped alter future decision making. The story and ending were unexpected but I enjoyed them both. The art style is also very fitting.While the game isn't a walking simulator, most of the gameplay consists of talking to characters, interrupted by the occasional mini-game or puzzle. If you're the type of person to skip past cutscenes or dialogue, this is not the game for you. If you like choose-your-own-adventure, story rich games with complex characters, give Pentiment a try. You'll see how interesting history can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite enjoyable but has a lot of eyerolling injections of stuff that the devs no doubt think modern people care about like one-way whining about gender roles and the treatment of certain groups by society or whatever.I wanted to be more immersed in an authentic story but alas they have to find their 5 minutes to preach every now and then.Traversing the map gets tiresome after a while and you're not really rewarded that much for exploring at different times of day so it just feels like you waste your time when you naturally do.Despite these criticisms it's enjoyable enough for a single playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Where do we even begin with this game? I feel like it's been talked about exhaustively already.It's brilliant. The plot is compelling; the role-playing mechanics are simple, but effective, and guarantee a unique gameplay experience; the world-building is detailed, thoroughly researched, and immersive; the characters are awesome, and you will get attached to their lives before you even know it; the music is gorgeous; the graphics are entrancing...Pentiment is probably one of the best games I've ever played. Period.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I bought because I heard it was kind of like Disco Elysium, and it is. The setting is very different, but it has some similar themes, and (most importantly for me) it's a role-playing game that's actually *just* a role-playing game. There's no fighting, shooting at things, or jumping on platforms, and so even if you're someone like me with slow thumbs and average-at-best reflexes, you will still be able to finish it.There is a lot of reading, so if you're the kind of person who skips through dialog then this definitely isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10This game is something special.I played it entirely on the steam deck and it feels like the perfect game to play on it. Great battery life with this game too, Elden Ring won’t get you 2 hours but this one can get you almost 6.The art style is what drew me in, plus the price and the amount of gameplay. But there’s so much more here. Well written characters in a small town that you’ll get to know very well, a great soundtrack and an awesome story. If you’re looking for something different from high action, combat focused games, this could be it. It’s like playing through a medieval style graphic novel.The story takes many twists and turns. You need to be ok with playing detective and solving murders in this game. The thing I really loved about Pentiment was that it gives you a few clues to go off of, but doesn’t give you enough time to gather all evidence before you have to present your findings that will mean life or death for the accused. You have to use your time wisely, but if you follow a dead end and time is up, you’ll have to make a decision on the fly based on your feelings, there is no going back.I also felt connected with the protagonist, Andreas Maler. As I got to know him, I sympathized with him through his fears, regrets and struggles. He’s a very relatable character, and one that I will add to my list of memorable protagonists.I would really enjoy replaying this one and making different choices. I feel like this game really shines as something unique and different out of all the gaming options we have today.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I usually bounce off of games where the primary interaction is reading text, but I was completely engrossed by Pentiment. It's hyper focused on a very specific time and place in history that you just don't see in games. Honestly, it's a miracle this game was made at all, let alone by a relatively big RPG studio like Obsidian. Easily one of the best games of the year, can't recommend it highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: There are games that I (very much) enjoy and then there are games that I love. This is one of the latter.Pentiment is like a beautiful puzzlebox with many little doors to open and pieces to uncover. Pieces of life, of different interesting characters, of history and myth, of believes and ideologies. All exquisitly written, and packed up with beautiful illustrations and tunes that reflect the care of the developers thowards their game. It was lovely to see how even the UI was fondly taken care of in the shape of a book full of handwriten notes and handrawn maps... and to listen to the few medieval songs that appeared here and there through the game and that made me connect emotionally even more so with Pentiment's world.I appreciate this game not as much because of the wide variety of choices and consequences, as about the significance of them. Pentiment talks about trauma, about how history repeats itself, about hope and faith, love and despair. It goes deep and it touches you.It's a beautiful gem.If anything of what I said resonates within you, just click, lay back and enjoy the trip.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is a unique game. Aesthetically, visually, and narratively it provides a experience seldom seen before. I reckon it's a murder-mystery, yes: but also a tale about faith and fire and loss. A dilemma as old as human cognition. Now a lot of people like to compare this to Disco Elysium but I reckon the comparison is flawed: character building isn't as relevant, nor are the central themes particularly close save, perhaps, . It is, however, a murder-mystery so feel free to compare it to the Nonary Games, or to Contradiction or to The Case of The Golden Idol in that one specific aspect if you will.All in all Pentiment is a work of art and a game that took a plunge into a territory not usually delved into; it made a gamble and succeeded, and delivers upon us an experience, masked as a murder mystery, with loveable characters and magical moments of sensation.Its only flaws are mayhaps the lack of a quick teleport to places and the sometimes heavy exposition on very specific parts,  things that do not lessen the beauty of this experience in a significant way. 9/10 recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful aesthetics, compelling story, interesting characters. Virtually no gameplay, this is essentially a digitally illustrated novel. Fantastic dialogue system where you have to think about what you say and to whom you say it, often leaving you in conflict between what you feel is right and what you think is most purposeful.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A true labor of love in our gloom, capitalistic times of soulless corporate clones instead of gaming masterpieces! Outstanding visuals, animations, style, and sound. A great way to study history similar to Kingdom Come Deliverance in that regard if not in genre. And also at a very low price! Buy it, rate it, share it, discuss it. If we won't support games and developers like theese - we'll drown in cancer games like Fortnite.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: The game has similarities with Ken Follett's The Pillars of the Earth, which I enjoyed very much and made me read the first book of the series as well. The setting is different from that game, the action happening in 15th century Bavaria during the Holy Roman Empire.It's a well documented game with a glossary in which you can read about all the specific terms and Christian/pagan traditions that are mentioned throughout the game. I think it's a good introduction to a small part of European history. The game play is simple, you have to talk to a lot of characters and based on the conversation you make choices that influence the story.My only negative comment about it would be the bug while  Also, the ending Overall I recommend the game if you like a detective-like point & click game set in 15th century Europe.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent story game, very interesting with compelling plot points and a great narrative. The artwork is beautiful, and they do a great job of obfuscating the ultimate truth throughout the story without just making the plot twists utterly ridiculous and out of nowhere. If you pay VERY close attention, you can yourself get a pretty good theory about what's going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is easily one of the best games I have ever played. I was already hooked from the start with the peculiar art style and its premise of mixing various fields of study together, but I did not expect to be so invested in it. Despite what a few people have said, I disagree with the idea that the start is pretty boring and slow. Yes, it was a bit confusing at first, but I still felt compelled to play the game and find out what the heck was going on.The game made up for the absence of spoken dialogues with the perfect ambience created by well-timed music and crisp, refreshing sounds of nature and everyday activities like the sound of walking on paved floors, flowing water, and paper being written on. As a person who speaks multiple languages and loves learning about other cultures, this game made me feel so at ease and in my zone thanks to its storytelling of medieval times through the intertwine of different fields of study: history, medicine, law, botany, philosophy, foreign languages, etc. Also, as an Italian, the hand gestures done by the Italian characters made me giggle a bit.Following the steps of Andreas was so heartwarming, as I shaped his character and personality around what I am like as best as I could, which in turn made me grow attached to him; the ending I achieved in my first run made me shed a few tears as it felt like a circle coming to a full end and honestly I couldn't have asked for more.I truly, wholeheartedly recommend this game as it made me feel things most modern games do not achieve to do (BG3 aside ofc). If you're a person like me who loves this kind of game and are on the fence of buying it, do it, it will be a rewarding adventure <3
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is a genuinely amazing game, and easily one of the best I've played in a number of years. I've finished it twice - once on Xbox and once on PC. Besides the gorgeous art and music, I found the story incredibly engrossing. This game teaches you quite a bit of history, and can be quite thought provoking. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a book, I wanted to lie in bed and play it, but my computer doesn't work that way. I played it the last 3 days straight. I am excited to play it again and make a whole bunch of different choices and scenarios. This is a very good game, I love the art style and illustration. The history and story telling is immaculate. Definitely recommend if you like storytelling, mystery solving, clues and history.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought I would ugly cry over such a religiously dense game, but here I am. It is a masterpiece and treasure of the point-and-click genre, not even to mention the astronomically brilliant research, meaningful story-changing choices, and truly complex, humanist writing. The art style is just....so, so, so well done, so cool, and really helps put you in that historian mindset as you genuinely learn about the rich history of this game. Personally, I'm an atheist, fairly uncultured in nearly all religions, so I went into this game hesitating if I'd truly enjoy it-- but it is a wonderfully emotional story at its core. It certainly did not give me any faith in god, but I came to love and protect the characters and this town all the same. I absolutely recommend it, 100 percent!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Good story and interesting setting. Having the right expectations is essential to enjoy Pentiment though, because it is not a traditional RPG, it is a visual novel. It is also not a typical murder plot, this element is not the center of the story. The only thing I didn't like is that a couple of plot twists are too tropey and cliché and felt more like stuff from soap operas.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Marvelous niche game that took a while to get into but I was invested in the story after not too long. In the first hour I was actually unsure and considered a refund, but I'm glad I stuck with it. Love the art style and games that try to do something different. Perfect for when you want to relax with a quiet night on the couch.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: great game, dont have much to complain about.If i am allowed to bicker a bit tho (SPOILER ALERT!!!!)-In act 2 the church burns down and control is wrestled from the player by way of Andreas deciding to run in and save some books. The game does choice and consequence well, but this situation always bothered me (even if andreas turns out to be alive).-Once again regarding consequence, the story is suprisingly linear. certain events such as the burning of the abbey will happen regardless of your choice. This is not a bad thing, but it feels like missed potential to not take this framework further. To have more varying outcomes related to different choices and the limitations of time. The type of game that pentiment is can achieve it i think.That would be all i suppose.also RIP caspar.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I was sold on giving this a shot because of a review that mentioned Disco Elysium. This is a very different game, but it lived up to that high bar. One of the most refreshing things I've played in a long time. I learned many things. I made choices that were hard to live with, but I didn't have a choice. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic experience more than a game.  At the core, it is a achingly beautiful story of humanity and community against a detective/exploration of late medieval rural Europe.  If the last sentence grabs your interest, this game is certainly for you; if not, I would give this a miss.  This is a gem that is text-driven and exploratory with very limited interaction and truly focused on a niche concept that will either excite and deliver on the premise alone, or drive you to look further rather quickly.With that said; I thoroughly recommend this title for most gamers to simply experience.  It is slow, methodical and in the end, quite linear - but there is more character and depth in this work of art than in any other game I've enjoyed over the past decade.  The animation of the expressions, the medieval art that permeates the journey and especially the scrawl and sound of text throughout lends an air of authenticity to the world and for me, becomes the focus.  The mystery that threads the plot together is rarely the central focus of the protagonist; rather the emotional engagement with each character takes your focus.  Where the game strays to reference historical events and personalities of the era, there is a lovely function where you lean out from the action similar to looking at a world map in RPG style games-only here we are treated to more artistic representations of key characters and concepts to keep up with the meandrous plot.For those on the fence; it is worth your time - plot driven, heavily texted and resplendent with characters you generally come to enjoy and worry about; even to the point of multiple play-throughs to see precisely what relationships can change or flourish to affect the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game for the story, the rpg aspects of background choices, the decisions you're constantly making in plenty of dialogue and key moments, and seeing the setting develop -- characters be born, grow, marry, die, be replaced by their children, all in the span of the same story.The weak points: Not really super replayable, personally. And the soundtrack is lackluster, forgettable. A good game to get if you're into visual novels with a lot of mystery (Zero Escape, Ace Attorney, Somnium) or heavy-story games with choices (Disco Elysium, Tellyale).
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pure narrative and dialogue driven adventure from Obsidian that amazes with it's attention to detail in the setting. Look through a window to the life of a small Bavarian town in the sixteenth century and guide it's history through your actions. Have no misconceptions: This game is 99 % pure dialogue but it's amazingly written and while the first hour or so is a bit slow once the story gets going it will keep you in it's grip to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I am glad to have experienced in my lifetime. It certainly will shape my thinking when it comes to my understanding and perspectives on us humans as a society, and how life, for better or worse, goes on indeterminately. Word of advice: you should not single-mindedly play Pentiment as a serious detective game, but rather take in the whole experience of medieval strife, conflicting ideologies and ways of life, the well preserved artistic style, and so much more as much as possible. It is that rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Ahhh PentimentDuring the launch of this game I could not put it down I played it from front to back. However my inability to put the game down could be likened more to someone who is unable to avert their eyes from a car crash rather than being enthralled due to the quality of the game.Credit where it's due Pentiment's commitment to portraying the history and culture of the HRE and the middle ages is impressive and makes pentiment very unique.The first act of the game is incredibly strong and the concept of having to be a defacto judge to a group of likely innocent people who have different moral characteristics is compelling and very well written. However as the game goes on longer the more the game falls apart. As soon as act 2 begins it becomes painfully obvious that none of your choices or character building has mattered whatsoever. The vignettes of the villagers by act 2 also start to lose their charm as the tension of act 2 is fully undercut by a giant time skip. The act comes to a close with what probably should have been the climax of the game and in a disapoting turn control is ripped away from you character to preform an action that only makes sense for one of the many chosen backgrounds for your character. With act 2 ending on a disappointing note act 3 follows the pace of the previous two acts and resets the tension with the formula becoming predictable. Act 3 from the outset is clearly rushed the vignettes are less detailed and instead of organically ramping the tension up like the previous two acts the climax comes racing towards you with such an obnoxiously stupid mid act twist it retroactively worsens the game. The worst part about act 3 is the ending and the very overt message of the game being presented as a twist in the  motivation of the killer.Instead of surprising the audience with the message of the game manifesting literally in the characters all the ending manages to do is state the obvious while all the characters act shocked in the most overdramatic phony conclusion in a narrative game I think I've ever seen.This story revelation was so underwhelming it took any and all remaining wind out of my sails and fully turned me against the game.Despite being owned by Microsoft for years now obsidian is still obsidian for better or for worse. Pentiment is definitely worse off  in that respect being one of the worst games of the obsidian catalog. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is the best video game since Disco Elysium and one of the best video games I've ever played. I love it with all my heart and soul. It made me happy, it made me sad and melancholic, it made me feel cozy, warm, grouned, sentimental, calm plus the secret ninth feeling I'll keep to myself. It's an absolute must play for every Middle Ages afficionado and all fans of story-heavy gameplays.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: As a phd student specializing in medieval european literature & manuscript studies, I never thought I'd  find a game I'd be so enthusiastic about! Outstanding, really, and I guess, seeing all the positive reviews, it must be enjoyable for non-specialists, too. The art style is something I never thought I'd see in an RPG game, and the cherry on top is the soundtrack at the end, written and performed by Lingua Ignota. I should also mention that I'm a big fan of The Name of the Rose by Umberto Eco, so, naturally, I loved how this game is inspired by the novel without following/copying the narrative too closely. In short, I'm no experienced gamer but I've found MY game.  I'll definitely replay it several times to explore the different dialogue options etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: BEST ON DECK: 6 - 7 hours battery, 60 FPS, No Setting Changes NeededPentiment is a unique text-heavy, choose-your-own-adventure that sets you into 16th century Europe. As Andreas Maler, you are caught up in a series of murders that span over 25 years. You are responsible for conducting your own investigation and decide the fate of the communities you encounter, but beware, every decision you make brings you closer and closer to the center of a devious underlying conspiracy.As a quick aside, I want to say I love this game's aesthetics. It is gorgeous and fits the game perfectly. This was definitely a major draw I had to buy the game, but the story is quite fantastic too. Takes a little bit to get into if you aren't a fan of the Medieval speech patterns and wording, but if you can get into it, there's a fantastic game here.As a text-centric, it doesn't take much to run, which is true on the Steam Deck as well! Running with no forced compatibility, you can easily hit 60 FPS with no issues at all! Without any changes, you will be getting around 6 - 7 hours of battery and temps below 60c. This game fits perfectly on the Steam Deck and easily fits into our Best on Deck category.Part of the aesthetic for the game has you "reading" Andreas's story from a 3D book. Since the book is rendered in 3D, the game tends to draw more battery during these scenes. In the opening, this spiked to 12W, but when using the glossary when playing the game, I never saw it go over 10W. I would comfortably say leaving TDP off is still okay though as the actual gameplay rarely goes over 7W drain.The game has a wealth of accessibility options along with it. This includes easier to read fonts, how fast dialog will appear, and the essential text size! For the Deck, the larger size is perfect and while the regular size is readable, the larger is just so much easier on the eyes. With the accessibility features it offers, Pentiment will be a game anyone can enjoy.At Pentiment's main menu, you are prompted to log into Xbox. Since this is an Obsidian game, a developer owned by Microsoft, there is Xbox integration. Unfortunately, trying to log in locked my controls after a couple seconds and I had to restart to bring them back. I attempted to launch with Proton GE and Experimental, but nothing fixed this. Not being able to log in didn't impact gameplay at all though, so I don't see this as a huge let down.Pentiment is a very narrative-driven game where the choices you make matter and can greatly influence the outcome of the game. On top of that, the artstyle is such a wonderful addition to the game that I can't rave about it enough. On the Steam Deck, it runs flawlessly and feels like it was made just for this device. Pentiment is a game well-deserving to be part of our Best on Deck category!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, more so than being a murder mystery, i'd say its a history mystery! saying more would be spoiling it, but the small touches, attention to detail, and visual style kept me hooked. Alot of blood sweat and tears obviously went into this game, the playtime is about 12-14 hours about, but i liked running around so my hours were higher. due to character 'perks' (more so just choosing your characters history) and the decisions you make, this game has replayability though i seed some time to think after the ending of Act III, the final act, before i try another. your first playthrough could look much different than say your second or your third. Theres alot of reading, but the way that the letters flow like theyre being writ or print, combined with the impressive emotion of 2d characters makes a fair bit easier to stomach, helps if you like history! Actually reallly helps if you like history, as the history part, living in and learning about is a large chunk of this game's meat, with a murder mystery that keeps you eagerly speed-reading dialogue to find out whodunnit. History in this game was also really cool and it wrapped so many things together and considered many different points of view, leaving no voice unheard.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I've rarely played a game with so much attention to detail. While the game is very short, it is of very high quality in terms of story, ambient, artstyle in my opinion. I really appreciate the detail to historic accuracy and I was well invested in following along the story. If you're on the fence of getting this, I think you should as this feels like a rather unique game, the way it is presented.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: What a treat of a game, brilliantly written, endearing graphic style.Takes a while to get going, but once it gets going it sucks you in and you can't put it down till you finish it.Takes around 20 hours to complete.The only thing i wish you could do is turn down or off the scratching sound when it writes the text.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're still reading, I'll try to explain what I love about this title.First off, it isn't easy to try to explain this, simply because it is so uniquely its own thing. This isn't an isometric RPG in the vein of Pillars of Eternity, or even Fallout: New Vegas's first/third person perspective on post-apocalypse americana, but there  meaningful, tactile role-playing decisions to make here, both in terms of who your instantiation of the protagonist becomes, and how he conducts himself through the game.This isn't exactly a classic adventure game, though it certainly borrows elements and mechanics from that genre.If I had to sum it up, it'd be a period-authentic role-playing adventure murder mystery, rendered as if it was an illuminated manuscript.I keep hearing this described as niche, but honestly I do  understand that. Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous is niche, it has a pile of DMV-grade fiddly mechanics around character builds. Command: Modern Operations is a niche game, it's the best simulation you can get of modern naval warfare shy of getting a security clearance. Europa Universalis is a niche game, running that game feels like getting a double major in history and economics with a minor in political science, each achievement feels like a doctoral thesis in the making.This game? This game is approachable enough that I struggle to think of anyone I would  recommend this to. You find the fun immediately, and the fun will stay with you until the end.It is  beautiful. Every single element was crafted with beauty, meticulous care, and dedication to the craft.It's oozing with gravitas and verisimilitude. The characters feel vibrant and real, the place becomes as familiar as a lifelong home, and the story keeps you guessing until very nearly the end. It's embarrassingly well written,  well-researched.It's jam-packed with impactful, meaningful choices, reactivity to virtually all of those choices, and a deadly-serious story that will percolate in the back of your mind both in between sessions and, I'm certain, long after the credits roll.Get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on a whim because I wanted to play something different than the usual action-driven games I'm usually into. After 36 hours of play time which includes starting, stopping, and trying different decisions (as well as completing all the achievements) I had a pleasant time. Pentiment is a quaint little text-heavy, point & click, that is reminiscent of old Sierra games like Kings Quest, etc... But without the odd, sometimes unsolvable puzzles. For the most part, Pentiment holds your hand as you explore the fictional village of Tassing located in Bavaria in the mid-16th century. Icons direct you to interact with people, things, animals, books, or items to progress the story (or just explore). The story itself centers around a murder at the local abbey and you will turn Tassing upside down looking for clues in an attempt to solve this medieval "who done it" mystery. More things happen of course but I feel even a little hint of things would be spoiler territory so I'll avoid saying anything else other than it is cryptic and interesting.The big selling point are the decisions you make and how the rest of the game plays out. Decisions made in Act 1 can carry over into Act 2 and 3. You can play as a pious by-the-rules Catholic or a rebellious scientific-oriented ruffian based on various backgrounds and areas of expertise you choose. Now this is by no means a robust selection you have to choose from but still whatever you choose will influence conversations down the road. Art style is beautiful and pays homage to medieval woodcuttings, murals, and paintings of that time. Also the the history injected into the story is insightful and gives you a glimpse into how peasants, nobility, and the Church interacted with each other. It points out that no matter at what level of society you were, everyone was fallible. This is a good game if you enjoy reading and immersion into a story with quite a few twists and turns that will always leave you guessing. I think by the end of my foray I was ready to jump back into something a little more adrenaline-inducing though as my eyes got tired of reading text and I found myself rushing through dialogue. But for what Pentinent is, it's fine. Not the ultimate in point & click 2D role-playing but certainly not the worst either. The game mechanics are simple and the learning curve is elementary. The story is great and if you're looking for some downtime and a little peace and quiet, then this game might be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: One of the strongest and most unique gaming experience I ever had. Although it surely is not for everyone. Almost all of the interactions are through text. There is no dubbing, all of the speech is presented with written text. The story is very immersive and there are hard choices to be made. There are quite a few characters, but I felt like I knew every last one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece, though not for everyone, Pentiment is clearly a work of love. It should be fascinating and enjoyable to those with an interest in history, design, storytelling and narrative games. There is, of course, a central mystery that spans throughout the decades in the small Bavarian village, yet I find it less of a "Who's done it?" mystery and more of a reflection on struggle, loss, failure, community, meaning and hope. Strife, relationships and change are as much of a part of the story as the detective work. I think that Pentiment will be of less interest to completionists or perfectionists - unlike much of gaming, this is not a power fantasy. Hard an uncertain choices will have to be made and the best outcomes might still result in someone meeting ruin and perfect outcomes do not exist. After all, you play as but a cog in a history, at a time of uncertainty, religious, technological and social upheaval. Nothing wrong with wishing a power fantasy in the uncertain times we find ourselves in, but Pentiment is unlikely to be a game for it.The designers also made a good choice with the puzzles - rather than be a challenging mechanic, they are mostly a narrative device of their own, a way to communicate something about the setting, historical ideas and practices. These puzzles are not difficult enough to obstruct gameplay, though with this positive it is unlikely that there's as much satisfaction in "solving" them.Where the game excels is in making an interesting, immersive and authentic world. The artwork in particular is wonderful. Not just the illustrations and characters, but the way it says more about the world. People speak in different fonts, revealing more of their background. The words splatter if they are upset or unwell. Food scenes and interiors tell you if someone is well-off or struggling. Characters even look faded and washed-out, the older they get. Along with a meticulous map and journal, all of this serves to bridge the gap between a game and a novel.Much good can also be said about the research that has gone into the game, portraying an isolated yet international region and its traditions. The world feels as interconnected as it was, defying simple explanations of history and people of its time. From pagan traditions, to Saint Mauritius, to the herbal wonders of dill, there is much in Pentiment that I find in my own city, of former Hanseatic league, a thousand miles from Bavaria. As our world is built on foundations of the old, so the appeal of this story is not just that of a small village, but most of Europe and beyond. It's rare that games tackle stories that take place over decades and it's great to see more of them being made. After all, there is still so much to explore about interactive fiction and all the extra dimensions that can be added by choice and visual design included in these games. One of the best games of the last few years and a small wonder that this work of love could be made by one of the better studios out there. Well done, Obsidian.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I played the last couple of years. If you seek for action and peng peng.. this is the wrong game for you. But if you enjoy storytelling, artstyle and are able to dive into a different time of the world, then this is for you. I  loved every minute of it. There should be way more gems like this on the market. Less AAA-♥♥♥♥.. more variety. Dare to play something different.. dare to play this game.

Too long for me because you are just visiting the same places over and over, with almost no change.You end up talking with all NPCs all the time, just to know if they want to talk more. I really enjoyed Act I, less Act II and by Act III story was already too predictable. _childDocuments_.review: Very unique game, no other like it. This is a very beautiful looking game, with wonderful medieval art style and animations. The story is a mystery that you uncover in 3 acts, and the game has many interesting characters. The RPG elements make the game replayable, but I wish the acts themselves could be changed more significantly from the choices we made. A must play 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: The story is amazing, worth playing through twice. It has very satisfying mystery and investigation aspects that kept me hooked even when the lore got somewhat overwhelming. The characters are well thought out and easy to grow attached to, and you really feel the weight of your decisions as the story plays out. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A very moving game. Absolutely beautiful artwork. The writing is very good as well, though it does feel like it drags on a bit through the middle of the game. Well worth playing to the end though. It is very much an interactive story rather than a game but there are a lot of choices that you can make to affect the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game provokes your thoughts on the lives of people under the pressure of authority that had way more power than they do today. You'll witness that it's very rare that people have any choices in their lives and their lives are easily ruined at the whim of powerful people without consequence. There is no hope that justice is served any fairly.Christianity is woven into everything in their daily lives in the period where science is only for academics. God knows how climate will change and how it'll affect on farmers. A new-born child dies but it is how God tests your faith. Both townsfolk and clerics claim the god is with themselves and accuse each other of not being faithful. Although they are religious, and also because of it, they are susceptible to manipulation. Their lack of literacy makes it even more dreadful.Their life is simple and primitive and there is no such things as human rights or freedom of choice, yet their struggles are oddly relevant today.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: What a ride. A work of art as much as a game, literally and metaphorically and thematically. Right now, upon finishing the story, I judge it far more striking than anything in a similar vein - Eco's The Name of the Rose, Tepper's The Fresco, Flynn's Eifelheim, etc. The visuals are gorgeous, and the town and abbey are full of interesting, complex characters. Most of the interactivity is illusory, but it doesn't matter one whit. It's a game I'll remember for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth it if you love story and murder mystery games. Great art, music and characters and the game has a surprising amount of length to it as well. Very much worth the money.If you are someone who are a bit impatient and don't really enjoy the thought of getting immersed into a story or history, you might want to skip.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I can't stop thinking about this game! 100/10 game, I'm begging everyone I know to play it! It starts out as an interesting murder mystery, but then as the game goes in it somehow gets better! I cried several times but all in good ways, and me and my friends talk EXTENSIVELY about it because there's always another layer (haha) to discuss!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A complete disappointment. I was really looking forward to this game, even bought extra copies for friends. Your choices ultimately don't matter, and the story isn't very interesting or insightful. The visual design is excellent, but it's not enough to justify a poorly written game with limited, poorly integrated gameplay elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Once in a while a game comes along that feels like it was made for me. An intriguing mystery wrapped in a rich, detailed period in history. Fantastic art direction and writing. The choices you make really have weight, and the game doesn't let you go back on them. This game is about the passage of time and living with your decisions. And those decisions can have impact for years to come. I highly recommend giving this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. Pentiment really can make you second guess choices you make throughout the game. All the characters are really interesting and developed enough that you can understand motivations for what they are doing. I treated this game as a role-playing game that I became engrossed into.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A story of an artist in a small village in the Bavarian alps, at the border between the Medieval and the Renaissance eras, that turns into a Brother Cadfael style murder mystery, but with constant musings about art, love, faith, history, power, grief as you talk to the peasants, burghers, and monks and sisters of the monastery in your attempt to solve the murder(s). Takes a lot of inspiration from Name of the Rose, or Disco Elysium if we are talking about gaming, but is its own thing. If this sounds appealing to you, you should get this rare gem of a game.Word of warning - at times it is a very slow, almost sedate game. No action, no serotonin drip feed of XP or loot rewards here. There were honestly one or two moments where I had to force myself to continue, but I am so happy I did. Like a good book, the rewards are worth the effort. As well as learning and caring about the characters, you will learn a lot about history, both secular and religious. This is is not a linear "walking simulator" (though I have nothing against those types of games), the choices you make as you explore and talk can have huge consequences over time in this branching narrative. The ending honestly almost moved me to tears, and this is one of those games I will remember the rest of my life.The art and sound design deserves a lot of praise too. The "quill scraping on paper" sound as speech bubbles appear just keeps sending shivers of pleasure down my spine.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting and engrossing game, perfect for history nerds and fans of mysteries.I would love a series of these games set in different time periods and cultures (think Shang China, Incan Empire etc), stylized in a similar way from the art of the era they're placed in (or the closest surviving material culture we have etc). Not likely, I know.The art and style of the game I love, and the often excellent storytelling techniques, which I would have loved to see used in larger volume and variety, pull you in and are memorable. The soundtrack is fairly minimal except where appropriate to plot or circumstances, and if I remember there is often subtle ambiance or none at all, which is a great contrast.The story kept me engaged until the end. While some of the plot becomes predictable, the how is kept mysterious enough, and the history and myth surrounding the setting keeps you going too. There's plenty of character development choices with varying degrees of importance, but most seemed a matter of style preference. Plot important dialogues are made known to you after you make the first choice, which is nice, though there are things not as directly sign-posted, which is also nice.However, once you realize the patterns of the game it gets somewhat repetitive, especially if you're a completionist. There is value in replaying the game beyond achievements; you can choose to have different characters stay more central to the narrative than they might otherwise be, and you can spend more time with other characters you didn't get to on the first playthrough. There's also plenty of terminology and culture to refresh yourself on. Great experience, worth the money and time. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Step into a living illustrated world inspired by illuminated manuscripts and printed woodcuts in a time when Europe is at a crossroads of great religious and political change. Walk in the footsteps of Andreas Maler, a master artist who finds himself in the middle of murders, scandals, and intrigue in the Bavarian Alps. Choose your backgrounds, impact a changing world, and see the consequences of your decisions in this narrative adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: What I immediately loved is that the game offers plenty of secrets right away. I'm a sucker for these, despite being crap at sniffing them out. Alwa's Legacy is colorful, lively, easy to pick up, the controls are intuitive, and the hitboxes are generous. The plot is primitive, almost non-existent, but I can't say that I care about this aspect when it comes to platformers like this one. All in all, it deserves the title of "baby's first metroidvania", and not in some derogatory sense.I also love me a bit of sequence-breaking. Still not sure if most of them were intentional or exploits. Which is a good thing! It takes ingenuity to turn a bug into a feature. I immediately started jumping off my own green blocks after casting them in the air. The secret is to cast them while you're moving up... I think. It's finicky. Then I skipped the first boss's last phase by hitting him whenever possible, pretty sure one can one-phase him with a bit of practice. I adore these shenanigans! And while the sequences break, the game doesn't. At least not on my watch.The setting is a bit on the bland side, but it's also very traditional, familiar even. I like the way everything looks, it's a pretty game. To me, the problem lies in the map design. There are slightly too many empty screens with nothing interesting on them, too many boring dead ends. Traversing the world isn't particularly exciting due to how basic the movement is. It gets a much better flow after you get an air dash, but it happens ~5 hours in, which is slightly too late. I get it that they wanted to make the world feel bigger, but I disagree with the price they paid.Maybe metroidvanias are not my thing? Then again, I adore The Messenger. Although, it's easy to explain: its world was fun to breeze through and had more character to it. Besides, there you could also kill enemies on the go, slash and run at the same time. Alwa's combat is a slog in comparison. But maybe it isn't a fair comparison? Killing stuff doesn't play as big of a role here. At their worst, enemies can be a minor nuisance. On the bright side, the checkpoints are plentiful and you may spend a special "tear" thingie to add a warp function to any of them and teleport at your leisure. It solves many problems, but not all of them.I don't appreciate the obscurity around which Alwa's exploration seems to be designed. I immediately turned on the map markers, but they only work for plot items that are required for progress, nothing else. For some reason, breakable walls, secret nooks, water, and all kinds of optional treasures don't get shown on your map. So, I get a new ability that makes the world my oyster... but I'll be a monkey's uncle if I remember where everything is by that moment! Who do you think I am, game? Crazy... memory... man?.. See!? I can't even make a simple pop-culture reference - I completely forgot each and every character that had incredible memory as their distinctive feature.Due to my memory being trash as a result of numerous concussions and all kinds of intoxications in the past, exploration would've been utter hell for me if not for the 100% Map by Demajen (find it in the guides on Steam). I didn't use it on a whim, it was a necessity. I feel like with all that vagueness, the devs tried to achieve the very first Zelda's sense of wonder, the joy of discovery, or something.Commendable, but desperately outdated. What was an amusing revelation for a lone player once is only a few clicks away these days. Leave the past alone, don't cripple your game's design. Personally, I don't want for modern CRPGs to borrow too much from early Ultima games, no way! See what you can do with all the modern features, learn from The Messenger.The progression system is simple and elegant - you collect orbs and invest them into your three spells. You also get special abilities and a couple of staff upgrades as you go. I don't think it needs further explanation. I have some questions though! Some of the spell upgrades don't make much sense. For example, "drop through a bubble to change your color"? What? "Combine a block and a bubble to create a green bubble"? Eh?You want to know why? To drop through a green bubble and talk to an NPC for a crappy reward. So, you dedicated two upgrades to making a Zelda reference, I see. Lastly, crouching is used so sparingly that it may have been cut out from the game completely. If you don't have a good use for a feature - don't have it.Unlike the overworld, the dungeons are the highlight of the game. This is where my soul found its rest in between the "torturous" exploration. Very reminiscent of Zelda, they aren't too big and offer a great deal of gimmicky puzzle-solving fun. The dungeons have it all! Water puzzles, gravity puzzles, button puzzles, fat puzzles, smelly puzzles, bloody puzzles, come on in puzzle lovers... wait, wrong medium.Naturally, a few puzzles involve busywork, but most of them reward quickness and wit, as they should. And all the bosses at the end of each dungeon are incredibly easy but satisfying. The aforementioned sequence-breaking could also be of use here, but I haven't found a way to do the dungeons out of order, sadly. Yet what matters the most, beating the dungeons and the bosses felt real good, I was enjoying myself.I wanted to praise the game for its mild difficulty curve... but then, near the end, it introduced a ludicrous amount of instadeath spikes, as if trying to compensate for their absence before that moment. I don't consider it the best way to ramp up the difficulty, frankly speaking. The number of instadeath I re-lived during the final hours was quite staggering.I think I know what they went for: the last dungeon should've been the place where everything comes together, where you perfect all the things you've learned along the way, etc. But it ended up feeling like a separate game to me. They definitely messed up the curve I was about to compliment... and you know what? I still will. The spike isn't that detrimental to the experience, the game stays very forgiving. It wasn't a bad 'separate game' is what I'm saying.The more I thought of the game while not playing it, the more disappointed I got. But wondrously enough, when I actually launched it, most of my beefs somehow seized to matter. If this review seems overly critical to you, it's because I made notes when something took me out of the game, but I completely forgot writing them when I was selflessly enjoying myself, which, in fact, constituted the bulk of my time spent in Alwa. Considering the discounts they give, it's a bang for your buck.Yes, all the negative stuff I mentioned above exists. And the good stuff is too basic to write about. But despite some weak spots and occasional inconveniences, it's an extremely warm, comfortable game, a chill time-waster. Connoisseurs of the genre wouldn't even flinch while reading about the flaws I mentioned. They were there from the days of yore, people are used to that stuff. After a year or so, I probably wouldn't remember the game at all, but if someone reminds me of it, I wouldn't spit and make faces, I'd recall the good times.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: Hey guys, first ever review here.I was able to finish the game 100% in normal mode yet.All started with the first game (Alwas Awekening) i played and started to speedrun.It came out they are doing a sequel. _childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? As long as you enjoy jumping and exploring, yes. Defeat an evil sorcerer in a world full of enemies, a few bosses, some secrets and with many platforms. One of the better Metroidvanias, you find a rather big world to explore and it is up to you which direction you take. Genre-typical, all rooms are reset when you re-enter them. One of the first things you receive is a map that helps you navigate the levels. Your magic abilities are quite limited at first, but you soon learn new spells, like summoning stone blocks or bubbles that allow you to reach higher platforms.The game continues the story of Alwa's Awakening. You awake at a portal, not knowing where you are or how to get home in a land where evil creatures roam around freely. Just the town seems to be still free of enemies. Your nemesis from the first game tries to kill you, but just manages to make you loose your weapon which falls into the first dungeon. Reclaim your magic staff and begin to explore the land to finally show him who is the stronger sorcerer! You will soon meet a few inhabitants that might help you, like a smithy or a crazy wizard.I got stuck rather early on in the game when I had to push a switch under a floor panel in a tiny alcove. You can duck, but not crawl. You can summon a stone block, but not push it (far). I really despaired, until I was told that I just had to allow an enemy to push my stone block which then would trigger the floor plate switch. At that time I also discovered that you can cast a stone block high in the air and jump against it. Not sure if this is a legit way to reach higher platforms, but it made exploring a bit easier.Saving can be done at bowls spread thoughout the country, and if you use one of the rare tears you can also upgrade the dish to a teleportation point to traverse the country faster. When you die after loosing your 3 health points, you respawn at the last save point and your death count rises by one. Don't ask me how high mine already is.Gamepad support is fine, the chiptune soundtrack fits perfectly and the gameplay is cool, as long as you like the retro design.Great Metroidvania in 16-bit look. Lots of things to explore, lots of jumps to be made, lots of creeps to kill (again and again).

_childDocuments_.review: I thought Alwa's Awakening was just okay.  It was a decent enough game with some good ideas that was hindered by some clunky execution.  It was the type of game where I came away thinking it was close to being quite good but didn't make its way there.  I was looking forward to seeing the devs take a second crack at it and I have to say Alwa's Legacy feels much more polished and is legit good.In a lot of ways, Legacy is more of the same but better.  You get access to your primary skills much earlier, which means you have a lot freedom in how you want to progress.  There's clear sequence break opportunities that rely on the player understanding how to best make use of the player's primary actions and allows you tackle areas and collect upgrades in a free-form manner.  I had a lot of fun filling out a huge chunk of the map before completing my first dungeon. Warping is also much better integrated here than in Awakening, where it felt there the warp points were placed in a manner that made them feel not as useful as they should.  In Legacy, there's a mechanic that allows you make save points warpable by using a finite item.  There's a decent bit of the finite item spread throughout the game but they're scattered around enough to require some light resource management of the player's behalf, making you give a bit of thought on when to make a permanent warp point.Dungeons are a bit of a mixed bag.  They're fine, but are a bit gimmicky on the whole.  It is cool that the dungeons were designed in such a way that you can play through them with very disparate traversal abilities depending on when you do them. Bosses are okay, nothing great nor irritating.  Overall game difficulty is probably a bit on the easy side.  Outside of the beginning of the game, there's not much talking and I'm thankful for that.  I've read enough witty video-game writing to last me a while and it was nice that once the intro bits (which featured more talking than I cared for) wrapped up, you're basically playing the game uninterrupted with the occasional short npc dialogue.  Previous story knowledge is not particularly necessary.In short, did you like Alwa's Awakening?  If so, buy this.  Did you think AA was okay but could be better?  Alwa's Legacy is basically that.  Do you like metroidvania's that have a real sense of freedom to them instead of having the metrodvania elements feeling tacked on?  Alwa's Legacy gives you legit exploration.  It's good and I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually the game is great.But the level design, puzzles and mechanics are so simple and easy this should be advertised as a game for children. Maybe it gets slightly more challenging near the end, but 3 hours in and its literally ZERO challenge. Enemies pose zero threat and have zero mechanics. The 2 bosses I fought were maybe 1 step above regular enemies which isn't saying much. The platforming, puzzles, and exploration are so simplistic I honestly don't even know what to say about them, there is just nothing there. Its just room after room of basically nothing.Any of the reviews that say anything positive about the combat in this game I would be highly suspicious of, because there is no "combat" in this game. Everything dies in 1 hit, or you run up to it and attack 3 times stunlocking with every hit and it dies. It makes no sense. This was what I did with every enemy in the 3 hours I played. The only time you can take damage from an enemy is once you get bored enough and you start trying to run past everything and you take damage by running into them.There is a fair amount of backtracking, which is to be expected in metroidvanias. But the world and level design is so bland, its not interesting the first time through these areas, let alone the 2nd or 3rd. The game has a needlessly annoying warp mechanic where rather than just finding the warp zone and being able to use it, you also need to find specific items before you can even activate the warp zone. In 3 hours I found about 20+ warp zones and was only able to activate 4 of them.Props to the people that did the art and to whoever made the trailer for making the game look interesting, but sadly its not.Especially at this price point you can get several metroidvanias that are significantly better than this. Though price isn't really much of a factor in this case because even if it was free the game is just too boring to recommend.Here is my current list of metroidvanias you should try before you consider this game.AggelosBlasphemousBone AppetitDad QuestDandara: Trials of Fear EditionEnvironmental Station AlphaGato RobotoGuacamelee! 2Guacamelee! Super Turbo ChampioHollow KnightThe MessengerMomodora: Reverie Under the MooOri and the Blind Forest: Definitive EditionOri and the Will of the WispsOutlandSupralandTeslagradTiny Dangerous DungeonsUnworthyXeodrifter

_childDocuments_.review: Hit boxes on many enemy attacks are larger than their sprite or their projectile's sprite.You can be hit while transitioning to another zone.You can beat a boss and the boss will continue to attack even though it's dead and you can die while the crystal is falling to the ground. You have to refight the boss if you die when that happens.Teleporting around requires a resource to turn a save point into a teleporter. This is just a huge time waster. Just allow for teleporting to them all from the get go.Essential abilities are locked behind a resource that you have to choose abilities with. You have to reset your choices and pick a different one if you need to progress with a different ability. It's just a bad mechanic. The dash ability you get later is activated by jumping in the air. This sometimes activates when you are just trying to jump. This should have been on a different button...Areas of the world are not unique enough to make it easy to know where something is when you eventually get the ability you need to progress, so you end up going to ever map spot that has a possible new location every time you get a new ability.There's more bad designs, but I don't care to list them all. The game just wastes as much of your time as possible and is filled with so many bugs.
