_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Super Alwa’s Legacy.Hundreds of deaths after the first game, I had to prep mentally before starting this one.If Awakening was NES Zelda as a Metroidvania, then Legacy is SNES and N64 Zelda as a Metroidvania.Not really sure I believe a little girl that looks like a mochi ball is able to kill all of these armored monsters but… This is probably the most relaxing metroidvania I've played in a while.I am always pissed off this game is as under appreciated as it is. Though obviously influenced by Zelda, it creates it’s own unique and coherent world. It is it’s own classic. And everything is so fun and cute and beautiful.I loved Awakening, but Legacy is better in every detail. Game balance, graphics, content, etc. Now sure the story doesn't make sense and fits in a napkin. It's a mechanics first game through and through, yet the exploration in this game is the most satisfying and rewarding I have ever experienced. I find the music in this game to be beautifully retro, understated, and nuanced at just the right places. In short: it is addictive in the same way the soundtracks to the original NES game were.It does have its fair challenge as any good metroidvania does, but the smooth ambiance, solid music, beautiful art style, amazing level design, and fun puzzles make this a very satisfying game overall.It's definitely an evolution of the first game; it's still fairly puzzle-focused, and almost every screen features some kind of puzzle you need to solve in order to acquire an item or traverse across the room.  Compared to the first, though, it's got a wider variety of upgrades and more interesting boss fights -- although it's worth noting that it's actually possible (but difficult) to beat the game without killing any enemies.My favorite part was the different magic powers with their respective upgrade trees. The simple yet effective combination of the 3 powers (green block, bubble, and lightning bolt) makes for a really fun time and interesting puzzles. I specially enjoyed how every area/dungeon felt truly different and how each ability is used in different stages of the play through.An absolute must have for every fan of the genre if you ask me.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a great metroidvania / puzzle platformer game by Elden Pixels. I've backed it on Kickstarter, because I've really enjoyed their first Alwa game, with it's unique gameplay. The pixel art style and the soundtrack are beautiful, but my favourite improvement was upgradeable skill tree. There's a nice, big map to explore, so getting all the secrets was fun. I wish there was more to the story than just fight four bosses to get to the Vicar and defeat him, bacause that was the same premise as the first game had. I was hoping that this time new villains would be introduced and Zoe would have more bosses to fight. But other than that the game is polished and deserves a place in your library if you like this type of games. I'm looking forward to Elden Pixels next project.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I was pretty fond of Alwa's Awakening, I had high hopes for Alwa's Legacy. However, Legacy wasn't as much fun as its predecessor:- Graphics are 16 bit now. The spritework is better (no more Ms. Eyepatch) and the parallax sceneries are nice to look at. However, the mid-layer background "rooms" are boring. Every room looks like every other room and nothing stands out, not even the boss rooms. The soundtrack is still stuck in 8 bit land and doesn't have as many catchy tunes as the Awakening one.- Sadly, the level design in Legacy isn't as challenging or as sophisticated as in Awakening. There are almost no instant death parcours anymore (which isn't necessarily bad), but Legacy doesn't have anything else to offer. The mindless, themed puzzles and the increased number of enemies just aren't an adequate replacement - in particular with Zoe's increased agility. Even the boss fights felt less sophisticated in Legacy. Going by my death counter, I'd say Legacy is about half as difficult as Awakening.- The entire game seems a little directionless. There are side-quests and there is one switch-locked treasure chest per dungeon, but the rewards from both of these are laughable. The story remains open-ended again, alluding to, but not solving, some background mysteries from both Alwa parts. At least you can pet a pig!

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa legacy is a sequel that improve everything that the first game was , larger map to explore , better visuals , great soundtrack and a story that is told in a more interesting way.like alwa awakening , Legacy offer an easy mode called assist mode which has an option to re-appear in the previous room when you die instead of going back to the last checkpoint which is a nice touch if you're not super good at platforming.the large map offer a lot's of exploration to do , a rather large ammount of backtracking and while sometime it's can get a bit easy to get lost on what to do next the game is not too much complex nor feel obscure at any points.Alwa legacy offer a good balance between platforming and combat and the various bosses are a good challenge , the fights here feel more dynamic then the one from awakening. you still have the same block , bobble and thunder then the first game but also new abilities like a spell that allow you to walk on spikes without taking damages.after a short while in the game you meet a wizard that can change your skill tree , allowing you to make your green block to floats on water , your buble float longers and deal damages when popping. the more you gather blue orbs the more you can have different skills active to enhance your spells. in the first half of the game you will be going back and foward the wizard _childDocuments_.review: This is the second part of the Alwa series which is a "hardcore" Metroidvania series. This game starts where the first game ended. You play as Zoe and you lost your memories what happened before. You only know that you want to go home. But for that, you have to beat Vicar and you're not ready to take him on yet. I haven't played much of this game but what I saw looked great! I really like the look of this entry more than the first game. The difficulty is in my opinion very high. It didn't have the difficult tag on steam yet, but I've added it because it shocked me how hard it is. everything went fine until I met the first boss. After dying 50 times, while in between having watched YouTubers beat him, I knew this wasn't the game for me. If I get already stuck there than there is no way I can beat this game at all. I still give this game a positive review because what I saw was really good, just too difficult for me. 100% this game will even be more difficult. You have to play the game twice. In your first playthrough, you want to find and unlock everything that you can. Including changing every save point into a warp point. This isn't the hardest part, because after that you have the achievement left for playing on pacifist mode. You have to do this in a new save file and you aren't allowed to kill monsters. For a game that is already very challenging, this sounds insane to me, but I'm sure that the hardcore fans will be able to complete this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off before I get into the details because I do have some criticisms - I really enjoyed this game and would heartily recommend it. Oh, one more thing - if you like me didn't like the first game due to its slow-as-molasses movement and insta-kill back to checkpoint on hitting water that's fixed now. Movement is much better and you can even breathe underwater this time. Spikes will still insta-kill you back to checkpoint though.Ok, the details this is a Zelda-like metroidvania. As a metroidvania it isn't particularly great. It hits the notes right enough to get that sense of exploration and the environmental storytelling is great. But there are some problems with the design. First off the backtracking isn't really handled all that well. This isn't like a proper metroidvania with areas you'll often come back to and you might find something new, instead there are a few (not many) traversal areas and then you have some Dungeons that function like Zelda-dungeons. If any of you have seen Mark Brown's (Game Maker's Toolkit) series "boss keys" the dungeons are a pretty good mix of "find the key" and "puzzle box" dungeons. I quite liked the way they were made out. The bosses are of varying quality, some are super easy, some are annoying, while a few are really quite good. The puzzles & platforming are also a mixed bag between super-easy to somewhat challenging. Being dungeons you have rarely a reason to return. It's not like there is anything majorly missed or progression there's just a few items (mainly used to upgrade abilities) that you simply couldn't get your first time through. It's not any new challenge it's just have the ability and get it back. It would have been better to have them between a challenge so you could get them the first time through. Especially since the map leaves NO option for marking an area so you just have to remember where it was, for ability-gated progresssion for access to new areas/dungeons they are often memorable enough even if you can't remember the exact position, but these are just some upgrade currency lying around wherever. But the dungeons are by and large really good. As for the overworld, also a mixed bag. There's some pretty good exploration and platforming over all the major areas. The ability-gated progression is a bit trick, I was stuck twice I think where I just couldn't see where I could go to make progress because everywhere was locked behind abilities I didn't have, but I was eventually able to make progress both times. Don't expect anything like the great exploration-focused metroidvanias, it does its job well enough and it just about hits the right notes for exploration in-between dungeons. The abilities are pretty fun, the basic 3 of a green block, blue water bubble, and yellow lighting are pretty good and there's even some other ones added in. All in all I really liked the game, but I would recommend getting it mostly for the Zelda-like aspects, the metroidvania aspects in my opinion are not good enough to stand on its own, but as a complete product I really liked the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The great: A fun, story-rich metroidvania with good characters and story, charming graphics, good music, challenging but fair puzzles (including non-linear progression and multiple ways to solve many problems, based on both your phase in the game and your build). Lots of hours to sink in. The NG+ is a bonus. While the price is a bit high for a indie metroidvania, I think the large amount of content justifies it.The meh: Combat. The bosses are rather weak, and the regular enemies are just a boring hassle to get through that don't add much to the game, especially since the game has no mob loot or experience system (although they're a bigger challenge in NG+).The bad: Completing 100% (including getting the best items) involves about 3-4 places in the entire game which require extremely precise (dare I say, annoying) quicktime events and/or racing. This isn't nearly enough to scratch the itch for those looking for a quicktime event game, but more than enough to be thoroughly frustrating for those who DON'T want quicktime (the other 99% of the game doesn't involve quicktime and are just exploration/puzzle/combat.) Enough to say, solving these 3-4 puzzles to get to 100% requires a lot more quicktime effort than even boss fights, and that's more frustrating than fun.Overall: 8/10. Good pickup for anyone enjoying fantasy metroidvania and is willing to overlook a few rough edges.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically an expanded version of Alwa's Awakening, which isn't a bad thing.  I quite enjoyed that little title and this has 16 bit-era graphics vs. AA's 8 bit-era graphics, as well as more NPCs and a smattering of small quests.  It also has an upgrade system to the magic.  I guess it remains to be seen if it has a difficulty spike near the end as there was in AA.  A very charming metroidvania that won't knock your socks off but is well-crafted and fun to play in general.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic metroidvania with gorgeous visuals (especially the backgrounds!), great music and fun gameplay. Even when spending hours just searching for collectibles to get that 100% completion I found myself loving simply wondering around thanks to a combination of the gameplay feeling good and the music, long after I would have been bored of most games. My only possible complaint is that the boss fights felt a bit easy and/or short; I think most of them could be improved with 1.5x or 2x health and a few more attacks/phases. But that's just one small thing; overall I highly recommend this game.

The puzzles require little or no thought. The exploration is boring as there are tons of just dead/empty pathways. _childDocuments_.review: Elden Pixels are back with the second installment of the Alwa universe. For those who played the precursor, the game basics are familiar since this is like an upgraded and expanded version of the original concept, kinda like what A Link to The Past did to the first game in the Zelda series. However, instead of focusing on trying to look like a retro game on a specific console, they have taken more of a high bit approach to the game, taking use of the capacity of a modern gamepad etc.Remember the blue orbs from Alwa's Awakening? This time around, they play a more central role in the game as the are used for the upgrading of different magics, giving you the power as a player to mod your character and it takes the game physics to a much higher level. Along with your three basic magics, you also get four different abilities which makes different impacts on the environment.The game looks good, sounds good and it's got a lot of replay value with a lot of collectibles that can be found and even a hidden dungeon! Of all the indie games I've played the last few years, this definitely make it to the top 5 along with games like Timespinner and Axiom Verge!
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game but does not cross into being great. The best part for me was really that the Metroidvania-style adventuring was at its core really fun and the new abilities opened up really fun gameplay. The visual look is really attractive and I enjoyed the music which created a really fun mood to spend time in the world and try to figure out what to do next.My biggest issues were the story in the linearity of the game. The story is really forgettable and even after finish the game I'm struggling to describe it in any way. For me, the attraction for this game was all about the gameplay. The biggest issue in terms of the gameplay is that it feels that even though you gain new abilities that open up new paths and new gameplay, it feels as if there is only one correct order to complete the game. Too many times I hit frustrating situations where I could see a path to progress or things to do and kept hitting my head on how to solve the puzzle of getting there. And almost always the answer was that you're not supposed to be here yet, you need to complete another section of the game to gain different abilities. It would have been awesome if there was some leeway in the order you complete the different dungeons and places and perhaps more than one solution using different abilities in creative ways to progress. Now it feels like the game discourages you to explore and use the abilities in different ways and instead I feel I should blindly follow the correct order to the end without deviation. This is a shame because the gameplay is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid metroidvania, filled with puzzles and some really unique and refreshing abilities. Combat is solid, but in this game, exploration is king. Alwa's Legacy has some memorable characters, some really clever puzzles, and a great sense of progression. I really enjoyed juggling the ability improvements, which you can respec at any time as you build up your resources to acquire everything. I also really liked their fast travel system, which allows you to set any save station to be a warp station as you progress.This is a sequel, but in my opinion, this is easily the better game. The only story-based reason to play Alwa's Awakening first is to learn the villain and his motives, which this game does a poor job explaining, but otherwise that's the only real thing that carries over between games. The only thing that the first game did better was the soundtrack.Overall, I recommend this title. I enjoyed my time exploring Alwa enough to run around and 100% each region of the map. If you're looking for a solid metroidvania (the 'puzzle-based exploration-focused platformer with light combat' type of metroidvania), you can't do wrong with Alwa's Legacy.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for metroidvanias, and this is no exception. It's a nice, simple, retro style game that other fans of the genre are sure to enjoy. My only gripe is with the map. I found myself getting frustrated when finding orbs/tears in locations that were completely inaccessible and then having to run around the whole area to find where they were again once I had the required ability to access the area. You get the map very early on, and the map maker NPC is just kinda there for the rest of the game. Personally, I'd have liked to see a currency system or maybe some quests you could complete for him in exchange for map upgrades to show more details, or some markers that you could use to mark temporarily inaccessible locations to return to later. Certainly not a deal breaker, but it would have been nice.All that being said, Alwa's Legacy is still a great little game with a lot of thought and love put into it, and I look forward to future similar games from Elden Pixels!

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is an amazing game!! Just a ton of fun. I was looking forward to this one for a while, and I'm SO glad that it didn't disappoint. Here are a summation of my thoughts:------------------- PROS -------------------- The graphics are amazing! The graphics in the previous game (Alwa's Awakening) were good, but this game has definitely taken then to the next level. The backgrounds especially are just gorgeous. Sometimes, I would just stop to look at them for a while. Good stuff!- The animations are also excellent! I love the cute, chunky look of everything. The main character, NPCs and enemies all look nice and sharp. Very cool stuff. :)- The music is also really good! Looking forward to getting a soundtrack when I can. ^_^- The gameplay (much like 'Alwa's Awakening') is moderate and deliberate (which I like). While there are platforming challenges, twitch-fast reactions and super-fast movement is hardly ever the challenge (like in say, Super Meat Boy). Rather, the game provides a set of tools/abilities and the challenge is figuring out how to use these tools to overcome various obstacles. - There is such a wonderful sense of pacing and flow to the whole thing. When I bought it, I played it for like eight hours on day one. I just kept going! It's just really fun to play and discover new areas and see what's around the corner.- The level design is excellent. It's engaging without being too easy -- interesting as well as distinctive (so when you had to return to a spot later it was easy to remember landmarks).- Many cool interactions that are used exactly once. Like, they introduce something, use it for variety's sake -- and then never use it again. Some may not like that, but I thought it was cool. It helped the game feel full of ideas. ------------------- CONS -------------------- While the pacing overall is really good, I did get stuck close to the entrance to 'Eydie's Keep' because I had to perform a mechanic that was not introduced. The only reason I kept playing is that I really like the game -- but it was very annoying not knowing what to do for like five hours. I think that they should add in a tutorial prompt just for that one room once you turn on the statue. It would make that part of the game smoother. (I think they plan to patch in something like that. As of this writing, they haven't).- Also, Sylvan Temple (one of the temples that you go in) was just not very fun to me. I get the overall idea (raise the water and then lower it again to reach new places in the temple -- but I was happy when it was over.) Also, I got stuck in there for like an hour and I thought I was soft-locked (because I couldn't make it to other save-points without drowning first) -- but it turns out that it was fine. I just had to think of how the rooms were connected -- both above and below. (I'm so glad I had my upgraded bubble!)- Some of the items/upgrades that you get I thought were very silly/useless. This was especially clear when I completed an optional dungeon (that was quite difficult!) and my reward was <spoiler deleted>. I was like, "That's it?! After all that work?" So, the level design was universally excellent -- but the rewards (especially for the items) could have been better/cooler. Maybe that's a nitpick, but that's how I felt.--------------------- NOTES ---------------------- The 'instant respawn' from death didn't work for me. I wasn't sure what it was supposed to do, really. I turned it on, went into a boss fight, died, and then ended up back at the last save point. I was like, "If it's going to kick me back to the save point, what's the point of turning this on?" So, I turned it back off. I completed the game with it off.- The 'Hold B to skip' didn't work for me in the credits. I held it down during the list of kickstarters and nothing happened. The credits weren't too long and it wasn't annoying or anything. Just letting you know. -------------------------------- FINAL THOUGHTS --------------------------------Alwa's Legacy is a GREAT game! (Hurray! I found all the secrets for a 100% completion ending!! ^_^) I'm so glad to be in a time where games like this are still being made. I love platformers and I love pixel art -- so this game feels like it was made just for me. Thank you, devs!! I hope this game does amazing for you and I look forward to whatever you work on in the future. Much love and thanks again for making this game! :)FINAL SCORE: 9.5 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a lovely designed and well crafted Metroidvania. It is set in a beautiful classical fantasy world and offers a very enjoyable adventure. Gameplay involves, in roughly equal measures, platforming, combat, exploration, and puzzles.The game is very clear about the fact that it desires to be a retro style Metroidvania. Every ingredient of the result is well prepared. The graphics are beautiful and colorful. The artwork leans to the cute side, but never becomes too goofy. The chiptune soundtrack is atmospheric and rife with catchy melodies. In fact, I sometimes visited certain areas just to listen to the soundtrack (I'm looking at you, Kloki's Bridge!). Gameplay is tight and adequately challenging, but never frustrating. Also, there is a Quick Respawn option for beginners. The world is varied and invites exploration. The game is neither too long nor too short. Taking my time, completing the story took roughly 15 hours. If you know what to do, you can finish it in a couple of hours.As far as shortcomings are concerned, the story will not surprise anyone who has ever played a video game. Also, the game sometimes requires you to explore the world autonomously. It does not always tell you where to go. But of course, this is a basic feature of the genre.On the whole, I thoroughly enjoyed this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely did not love Alwa’s Awakening, but I’d heard Alwa’s Legacy was a massive improvement in just about every way.And it absolutely is. Everything about Alwa’s Legacy is bigger, better and prettier and it holds its own very well in the metroidvania market despite doing nothing terribly new. Obviously it looks much nicer, with solid pixel art and animation throughout the game, and the difficulty also feels a lot better tuned than Alwa’s Awakening, without that game’s erratic spikes.Alwa’s Legacy actually plays more like a side scrolling Zelda than a Metroid game, with a large overworld and discrete, puzzle filled dungeons. These dungeons usually have an overarching theme and gimmick, usually linked to an item you find just before or in a dungeon. None of these are things you won’t have seen before, but they are generally well designed and implemented. Despite a new metroidvania being released literally every week, zeldalikes are still weirdly uncommon which gives Alwa’s Legacy a nice, less saturated niche to sink into.There’s also been a big improvement in both the number and quality of items in the game. The collectable orbs are back, but now serve a much more satisfying purpose – they can be used to power up your main three spells, often completely changing the way they allow you to interact with the world. For example, the bubble spell creates a bubble that you can briefly ride on. Fully powered it up it never pops, allowing you to ride high in the sky, but it also allows you to fall through the bubble changing your colour to blue – allowing you to push blue switches. You can combine the bubble with green blocks, which will change the bubble’s colour.  I won’t spoil any others, but there are loads of interesting interactions that really encourage you to seek out these orbs. There’s a bunch of entirely optional items as well which encourage you to go off the beaten path.Alwa’s Legacy is fun, familiar gaming comfort food – there’s no surprises in store here, but sometimes that’s not so bad.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun open world platformer. Fights are not too difficult, and the game does not require an insane amount of agility to progress. Lots of secrets to discover. There is a fair amount of backtracking to do as new powers and tools are unlocked, but the game comes with a very elegant warp system that really helps with said backtracking. I found the main story obscure,  and the interactions with NPC are minimal, but overall I would suggest this game to anyone wanting to play a 20 hour long open world platefomer that is not too hard to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: Its much better than the previous game, albeit not really perfect. The controls are still quite stiff, i think that the 3 hit point healthbar which can be slightly expanded upon is WAY too small, the NPC are probably some of the worst in videogames consisting of mostly just developer and/or backer that say little if anything important at all, and the story ends in a pretty awful way (Come on, "Go through the veil or portal into your world" but it immediately fades to black and shows credits? Not even a bit of a plot twist?)The music is fine, not fantastic, but its really not that bad, some tracks are memorable, the gameworld is a copycat of the previous game but in a much higher pixel count and color rendering, getting the game to 100% can be a bit of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and some paths to proceed with the game will require you to have one of the two main movement abilities unlocked with the blue orbs in game, either going really high straight up or going through water. The issue is that these abilities and the points you spend on them can be reset at any point so up until you can afford to have both of these abilities always on its always a battle of finding a spot where you need X or Y, going to the place where you spend points, spending the points for X, going to the spot, continuing, then you need ability Y too. This EXACT scenario i think has only happened once if at all, but the game will have a LOT of backtracking to the wizard that lets you spend your orbs into skills for the game.Its really not that good of a metroidvania, i really hope the devs can make a much better game later, but its still a major step up compared to how bad i thought the previous game felt.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: The world of Alwa's Legacy is a joy to explore as you unlock your main abilities and new ways to combine them. Devising a way to traverse a previously impossible path feels like your own discovery, which is part of what makes the metroidvania genre so exciting. However, the introduction to new elements of the game can be a little clunky; picking up a new ability, but then not having to use it immediately after seems like a wasted opportunity to teach the player the mechanics of the game. Instead, you get to run around the world with a Cool New Thing™, not really knowing what it does or how best to use it. This of course only adds to the sense of discovering the world on your own, but it risks being confusing and somewhat frustrating. Luckily, the game's art, soundtrack, and humorous characters make for a mostly relaxing environment. Being unfamiliar with the previous instalment in the series, I can't really compare the two, but I also didn't feel like I was left out as a new player. The game is a little confusing at first, but it picks up after a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of Alwa's Awakening and this sequel doesn't disappoint!  The music, as in the prequel, is great!  Truly some of the best 16-bit style tunes you'll ever have the pleasure of listening to.  Being a metroidvania, I found it very satisfying exploring the map looking for hidden items and passageways.  They have added some much welcomed features compared to the prequel.  The warp system makes it very easy to teleport to different areas of the map quickly, while the upgrade system is also very useful and fun to play around with and figure out what you need in order to progress throughout the map.  As for the level of challenge, platforming is challenging enough to make you learn from your mistakes, but not too difficult once you've run through an area more than twice.  The same can be said for the boss battles.  Even the final boss only took me two tries to succeed, which is where my first suggestion would come:  Add a difficult mode for those wanting more of a challenge.  But that would really only be my one recommendation, this game is great and well worth your time if you enjoy 16-bit style music and gameplay, and are a metroidvania genre fan!Gameplay: 8/10Story: 7/10Difficulty: 7/10Music: 9/10Charm: 9/10 : )
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much unlike most metroidvanias in terms of traversal alongside it's more puzzle platformer style gameplay with combat taking a backseat until the second to last boss which was harder than the final boss. The only classic upgrade you get is a dash and besides that you get around by using spells. The first two spells, the block and bubble, are much more useful than than the third one, lightning, due to the first two having a lot to do with platforming while the most lightning can do is hit buttons and interact with the block while block can be stuck to walls, used as a projectile, used as a raft, can save you from drowning, can interact with the bubble, and can be used as a projectile and the bubble is basically a rising platform that serves as your second jump and outfit color changer. The puzzles themselves aren't difficult but some puzzles especially ones to do with getting to places are pretty free form which makes it satisfying, epsecially when it comes to going to places in ways that aren't intended. I like that areas bleed into eachother and that it feels like you can go anywhere though I'm pretty sure there's a set order to do the dungeons. In addition to that saves are plentiful and there aren't many long stretches without saves besides later dungeons and the sewer alongside the ability to use tears to turn savepoints into warp points which makes getting stuff late game much less of a choir (though 2 of the dungeons don't have warps for the sake of the dungeon specific gimmick). the bosses besides the second to last one aren't much to write home about but they're not egregiously boring either so they're fine I guess. All in all this game is pretty good, the mechanics are unlike most of the metroid genre, it looks good, it plays good, and it's a nice 8-13 hour romp (depending on if you want to go for extra stuff). Another thing I should note is that I didn't upgrade my health until after I beat the final boss so yeah if you want to be challenged, this isn't the game for you

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy recommendation if you’re looking for a “light” metroidvania. Nevertheless, I do have some issues with it, which I will update this review with later after I finish it.Edit: I am more mixed now. This game isn’t worth the asking price. Maybe get it on sale and set your expectations low, but only after you’ve played every other good metroidvania. What are the issues? Too many to really list. The only good thing is the exploration. I wish they went all-in on the exploration aspect. Instead they tried to put in so-called “combat” and it just falls flat. Every single enemy is just a waste of time. The bosses are boring to the point of annoyance. There’s one instance where I thought they were going to copy the Sisters of Battle boss fight from Hollow Knight and to be honest I would have welcomed it just to have a fun fight, but nope, they half-ass even that.But yes. I do want to reiterate, if you focus solely on the exploration aspect of the game, it’s pretty fun. It’s the only thing stopping me from changing this to a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. Don't let the "metroidvania" tags totally fool you though, as I feel like that's a bit of an incorrect label here. There are certainly upgrades along the way but the key focus is on using your three main abilities in a variety of ways from traversal to solving puzzles. You get can place a block, spout a bubble and shoot a blast of lightning. Upgrades further allow you to combine these in various ways. Later on abilities to walk on spikes, dash and zip through certain walls fleshes out the movement tech.If I had to put labels on it this game reminds me more of MSX classics like Maze of Galious, or MSX-likes La Mulana and its sequel, minus the crushing difficulty. There are certainly some challenging points in this game but not nearly to that degree. I felt the balance was overall very good although the final boss fight was surprisingly easy and thus a bit of a letdown. Given the final area really puts your ability use through its paces I was hoping for more of a gauntlet there. All the other bosses were fun though, and although there's not a ton of them they are all quite creative and varied.Soundtrack is stellar. NES-style with VRC6 expansion courtesy of RushJet1. I've been a fan of theirs for many years now and it does not disappoint. It's available on their Bandcamp for a name-your-price fee so be sure to throw them some love if you like the OST as much as I do.Overall I can easily recommend this if you enjoy platforming, exploring, light puzzle solving and that sort of thing. I also think the core gameplay tech here would make for a superb speedrunning game if only I had the patience to do the routing for that sort of thing, so I hope someone out there picks up on that because I'd surely love to see it.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly fine Metroidvania. The way it uses magic is cool. Upgrading the magic is good because it lets you respec as much as you want. You can upgrade the block power so you can just wack it and it flies and hurts enemies and that is really satisfying.The game is also really easy, but I can't tell if its because i was cheesing the bosses with upgraded powers (which i like) or they are just easy.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this game a thumbs down as I really enjoyed the game. Music is great, graphics are great, level designs are decent to great and the boss fights aren't super challenging which is what I preferred.However I feel like the game does not really respect player's time. The map does not really mark the location of items, the lack of guidance during the play through wastes players time. I believe I have spent half of the time on wondering "how to get to that place", "where to go right now?" or "where did I see that item again?". If only this game offers players to leave remarks on the map or provides more hint / bait to guide players to the correct direction, this game would be much much friendlier to the players.If the dev decides to do these in the future, I will wholeheartedly give this game a thumbs up.P.S.: This game worked really well on Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Started chapter 2, I loved this, but really not for the right reasons., and this was my main source of fun so far (see  section at the end :Put simply, abilities can be used in some ways to reach places higher than seemingly intended, allowing to skip small parts of the adventure. Even though it's not much, it's still very satisfying to outsmart the level design.The pixel art carries it, but dungeons (at least in the first chapter) really lack of challenge. Fighting mechanics are barebones, so most of the rooms are about simple puzzles that must be solved using abilities. And since these pretty much only allow to jump higher or throw a projectile, it's always really simple and rather boring.Overall, the whole game feels like devs are forcing me to clear their childish puzzles the way they intended :- A lot of "filler" dungeon rooms : Jump 3 enemies, or climb 2 ladders, or jump above void a few times, etc.- Unlockables-based progression. I don't think there'd be any skill difference between me right now and me when first opening the game, due to how easy it goes. The real only thing that I gained over time was new powers to reach new areas.- There're fish statues that "disable" the bubble ability nearby, like the game just wants to force me into the main path- Despite the childish puzzles, I had much trouble finding out where to go in the very beginning. You first have to go get your wand back in the catacombs nearby, but once you get them, there's in fact no way in there and you must go back at the entrance to climb up. Thing is, the catacombs apply a blindness effect, so I never knew whether there was no path or I just missed it.- Abilities obviously seem to lack playtesting and allow simple exploits- The bubble-disable fish statues really feels like devs went "bruh we planned it that way, wait uh lets pretend you can't use that just for these places"- The music sounds good, but also very random. Feels more like a Youtube VGM playlist than actual music made specifically to fit the gameA) You get the ability to summon a falling block in front of you, to either crush enemies or reach places that are just a bit too high.Though, summoning a cube shortly (up to ~1/2 sec) after starting a jump makes it spawn low enough to allow jumping on it mid-air while moving forwards, effectively turning into a double-(block)jump.B) To reach even higher, start placing a block on the ground, jump from it, then summon another block mid-air.C) Later, you get the bubble spell, summoning a platform with a short lifespan that slowly goes up.Similarly to cubes, you can still get on it if you summon it shortly after jumping, although the window is tighter (1/3-1/4 second)You can't summon a cube while the bubble is active, which means if you jump out of it right before it pops, you can then follow with a double-(block)jump.When you put all these together, you get the ultra jump :1. Place a block down and jump from it2. Summon a bubble shortly after the jump so you can hop on it3. Right before the bubble pops, jump from it4. As soon as the bubble disappear, summon a block mid-air, which you can then jump from

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played a couple of hours of Alwa's Legacy and I can already tell it's a really good follow up to Alwa's Awakening; they have something pretty special that is not just a rehash of Awakening but expands on it in some very clever ways.However, I've run into some fairly serious bugs with the controller, rebinding keymapping, and to a lesser degree dark areas being such a pain that they've stunted my progress. I had workarounds for all of these, but they were such a pain to deal with that I ended up buying The Mummy Demastered instead and playing that to completion hoping that in the meantime a patch would be released or a solution would come up or both, but I've finished TMD and come back to find these issues still exist. They don't really matter to me anymore and I'll update my review once they're sorted out, but I feel it's worth noting them here since they were such a hindrance to begin with and really overshadowed what appeared to be a game that had a prequel that I really loved. The devs I've talked to on discord are super friendly and clearly love their game so I don't expect any of these issues to stick.Edit: I've finished the game now and it was extremely enjoyable. It's a bigger game than Awakening was with a lot more interesting upgrades and pretty good pacing. I did get lost quite a bit, but I'm pretty sure that was more my mistake than the game's. The earlier issues I talked about have largely been fixed; my Logitech F310 controller needed the switch on the back set to D and steam's controller settings had to recognise the controller - this is odd because other games recognise it. The devs have commented on all of the issues in steam discussions and discord.

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a massive improvement over the original Alwa's Awakening in nearly every way! The pace is much more snappy, moving around the world is much less tedious and there's far more items to look for.Overall the game is a bit easier with some of the new additions, including HP upgrades, but it's well worth it for a much smoother experience and better moment to moment pacing. Exploring feels natural and worth the effort this time, instead of a slow chore - especially because the Orbs are used to upgrade your magic this time, with some new traversal options given out as you do. The new abilities are also neat too, although having to wait a while stuck in place to charge is creeping into that Alwakening sluggishness just a little bit.One of my favorite additions includes a fairly unique fast travel system that lets you choose what save points to turn into warps by spending Tears (don't worry, there's enough to make all of them!) This makes a lot of the dungeons easier to get around and backtracking so much less of a chore than Alwakening's was, since you're in full control of what warps to unlock rather than being limited to one per area.The game got a massive overhaul making it basically like a 5th gen era platformer or "SNES-plus," with great high-color sprites and gorgeous backgrounds, with a little bit of lighting and shading thrown in the mix. The music is still 8-bit chiptune which adds a TINY bit of disconnect, but according to a developer on Reddit, this was because they couldn't find a SNES-style composer at the time who was interested or available - kinda surprising, but understandable and not the end of the world.Even the previous game's fetish for fake walls and spikes was addressed - the former still exists, but there's a lot less of them and less of them required for progression, if there even was any - I don't remember there being any. They're still not always signposted the best, but they're much less of an issue and there's an item later on that'll help you know when they're used.The only real issue I ended up having with the game was that the fourth dungeon is definitely the weakest one. Outside of an optional mini-dungeon, it's the only one that has instant-kill spikes and they can require some rather precise positioning and jumps to clear sometimes. Also, I'm just going to warn you right now because the game doesn't telegraph this AT ALL, and the devs have admitted this was poor design: the minibosses of that dungeon are vulnerable when they're midair using the dungeon's gimmick. You'll know when you get there.Also, the story is basically an excuse plot to have a game, again. They added more dialogue and a nice helping of little interactions, but the plot's as deep as a puddle. There's an unlockable pacifist mode as a bonus, but it doesn't look like there's any additional ending for playing it.I can definitely recommend this to most people, instead of just NES buffs like the last game! Alwa's Legacy is a smooth play almost the whole time, with only tiny bumps here and there. I was able to handle just about everything a casual player's expected to without a guide this time, and didn't ever feel like my patience was running low. You can feel good buying it full price, and even better on a good sale (like right now at time of writing, -82%, hot damn!)

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a solid but unspectacular Metroidvania.There's plenty to dislike. I don't know that I've played a MV or platformer with less inspired combat. The story is forgettable and boss battles aren't all that engaging.Thankfully, the game does everything else well enough to keep you hooked for the ~8 hours needed to roll credits. I appreciate the plethora of quality of life offerings such as difficulty options like "respawn on same screen" and the ability to spend collectables to customize your fast travel locations. There's also a skill tree that you can respec on a whim. These upgrades play off one another, leading to some fun puzzles and creative ability-gating.I wouldn't point to Alwa's Legacy as a demonstration of what makes a the Metroidvania genre great, but if you're a big fan of MV titles this is worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a great little metroidvania game by an indie developer. It's not as complex as some of the giants of the genre, but it has a very good map, a limited but enjoyable set of weapons / tools which interact with each other in interesting ways, and it also has a strong and well-positioned retro aesthetic in its audiovisuals. It tends to be a bit opaque, sometimes it takes time figuring out what to do next and how the new skills work (or where they are useful), but that's not a huge problem, and if it wasn't for the one bigger issue, I would say the game is a near-perfect little gem.The big issue is there, however - it's the controls. They are not very bad, but they are not very precise either, and while it's lightly or mildly annoying in combat (which is not very hard in this game), it can get really frustrating in some of the skill platforming sections - especially when the instakill purple spikes come into the picture. So many developers have managed to create precise and super-responsive controls, I can't understand why many games still suffer from this...Having said that, Alwa's Legacy is still a very good experience - highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not usually enjoy the precision platforming that many metroidvania games involve, however, with this game death does not mean everything is undone. Combined with the setting to essentially respawn on the same screen as you died, this for me, made it worth it. This game still requires precision and patience especially if like me, you are not skilled, I died over 500 times just to get to the final boss, however despite this, every death felt less like a failure, and more like part of my journey to figuring out the game, and I did not feel as though I had to repeat too much content that it made it not worth it. I enjoyed the way that skills/magic progressed, with the basic skill staying the same, but changing as it was upgraded to allow you to use it in new ways. The game also allows you to reset your upgrades, and then invest in others, so if you feel you need a different upgrade to proceed, but do not have the orbs for it, you can downgrade other skills to contribute to this upgrade. The map was interesting, and was broad, but had enough warp points so that you were not constantly backtracking everywhere excessively,  and new challenges were constantly provided, without you feeling as though you were abandoning all the knowledge you had gained from before. The puzzles were intuitive, and often required creative thinking on how to solve them. I did have to look up how to solve several of them, but they still felt enjoyable. The game also has replayability value for those who like that, but the game is worth it if you just want to play to explore and enjoy it once

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptional follow-up to an already excellent game, Alwa's Legacy manages to take everything the first game did well and go well beyond. There's multiple ways to use each of the three abilities plus new powers to traverse the world. Secrets are satisfying and the OST is an absolute banger.Two complaints: I wish I could mark the map to know where I need to revisit and the special magic shouldn't need to be recharged so slowly. Minor issues, really.If you like metroidvanias and challenging puzzle platforming, check this out!

_childDocuments_.review: Major improvement from Alwa's Awakening, but still kind of meh in several ways. Visuals are pretty awesome, but I felt I was mislead in terms of progression because of the stupid statues that vacuum bubbles being too similar looking to the flame statues. I only noticed the smoke from the flame ones in the end game, and assumed that I couldn't go a certain direction in early game because I thought the bubble vacuum statues were there and blocked progression. Idk why they have to look virtually identical, it makes no sense. Bosses are mostly better in this, but the first, second last, and final boss are meh in how they play out. Why is Vicar the same as the protectors in his phase 1 except easier, and why are the protectors rinse and repeat 4 back to back fights that are identical except palette swapped? The upgrade system is weird to me because two pathways are required for progression it seems, so this becomes partially a collectathon towards metroidvania upgrades lol. I had a suspicion this might be the case after seeing the free reset of orb allocation, and the fact that the map flashes in the location of the wizard shop like any other major objective marker. Besides the visuals, the tear teleporter system is a major improvement from Alwa's Awakening teleporter system, because as a player, you can decide on the best way to get around, and tear's are not too challenging to get, but still should be used wisely. The chiptune soundtrack was solid but I didn't really like it all that much. I can't believe there was a "bad" choice you could make in a playthrough, but I respect it lol. _childDocuments_.review: A nice retro-feeling metroidvania. The abilities lend themselves well to the puzzle elements, but do leave the platforming a bit tedious at the start. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a little conflicted about this game.  On the one hand, it's not a bad game, but on the other hand, I felt like the controls left a bit to be desired and the bosses often felt like it was up to luck whether I would win or not.  The bosses, in most cases, aren't really all that difficult, they have set patterns they follow that you just have to learn, but sometimes those patterns will change in a manner that will prevent you from using your trusted ability to dodge them, which leads to incredibly frustrating deaths.This game is a sequel to Alwa's Awakening, so I suggest trying that game out.  If you like it, than you'll likely enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Iterates on the original game successfully, providing a more robust experience overall that should please most players. You get more abilities, the game world is bigger, the obstacles more complex, and the graphics have been updated from an 8-bit style to a very colorful 16 bit look. If you enjoyed the first game you will almost certainly enjoy this one.Although the Alwa games take a retro look, they don't really play like games of the era - not that that's a bad thing, it's just different. They're slow, patient platform games where the main challenge is navigating obstacles using a small set of abilities. Most enemies have simple movement patterns and your combat abilities are pretty basic - oftentimes it's better to just avoid enemies rather than fighting them. In a way they're like a precision platformer dressed up like a metroidvania. The exploration aspect is fun and there's a good amount of secret stuff to find, just don't expect to become super powerful by endgame. The pace is relaxed, but many of the jumps the game has you make are very challenging, and I definitely died a lot. Luckily the checkpoints are fairly generous, and backtracking wasn't too big of an issue for most of the game.Only two real complaints come to mind. Some of the boss fights are a little too simplistic, with basic attack patterns that are easy to figure out and no real variation or surprises. This was a weak point of the original, and it's a little better here, but still not particularly a highlight. The story also underwhelms - while it continues directly from the first game it doesn't really feel connected in a meaningful way. Your character has no memory of the first game and it doesn't really address why everything got sent back to square one but the game world is slightly different now. You could just as easily ignore the first game and the plot would be functionally the same, which is a pretty basic platformer story with no real twists or surprises.These are minor issues though, overall this is a solid platformer that is a decent challenge and doesn't take too long to beat, assuming you're not looking to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Alwa's awakening so much I bought this game right after beating it and I liked this one even better.
