Shantae is the only other game that I liked enough to play the whole series, at least in recent history. I hope they make a third game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game and Metroidvania.+ controls are pretty good and thight+ map and dungeons are vast and diverse+ systems are original and useful+ very enjoyable, chill game.CONS:- one of the most generic, poorly written story out there.- tied to the bad story: there is no overall theme, so you'll have a very good, chill time and remember little of it a few days later- because the game is so chill and immediately enjoyable, you are unlikely to feel the emotional ups-and-downs that create a distinct memoryVerdict:+ get Hollow Knight (master piece), and if you're still scratching for the chill version of a Metroidvania, this fits the bill.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, nice action, interesting riddles. The music could be a bit more modern, but I forgo that for a pretty round retro-esc game.What I can't forgive is the eternal backtracking, combined with a map that is almost void of landmarks. When you need to find that one broken house, or that rose petle peddler, you are pretty lost, because there are five green areas , spread far across the map, and no indication of where you need to look.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is even better than the first! Alwa's Legacy takes all the aspects that made Alwa's Awakening enjoyable and expands upon it. The first noticeable difference is the movement speed. While Zoe felt sluggish in the first game, here her movement is quick and natural. I also love the new abilities in this game. I've found several Metroidvania sequels just take all of the abilities from the first game and slowly give them to you again in the second game. While you do get the abilities from the first game, you get them all very quickly. Then the things you unlock for the rest of the game are new.However, my favorite thing about this game is the fast travel system. There are save points all over the map, but you choose which ones are warp points by spending a limited resource. My biggest complaint with the first one was that the warp points were oddly laid out and weren't that useful. This warp system is brilliant and let's you put the warps in the spots you find most helpful. I would love to see more Metroidvanias adopt this system.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Even better than the first one. Alwa's Legacy is a fun metroidvania with great art and fantastic music done by chiptune composer RushJet1 who I suspect was heavily influenced by Capcom/Mega Man style music. It's a bit on the easy side which was positive for me but if you really really need an intense challenge this might not be the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and somewhat easy metroidvania that does things a bit different with the progression system to stand out. Presentation and first impression could be better: 16 bit visuals and 8 bit music (or style that mimicks these without the limitations) is a bit dissonant combo at first, the pixel art backgrounds are sometimes very pretty but largely generic too in themes.The very beginning of the game forces you into a midgame pitch-black dungeon to get back your weapon without the light item you will get later on. Feels unnecessary even if it's just a brief 5 screen detour (if you know what you are doing). The last dungeon feels rushed, including a letdown midboss and generally lacks the "endgame gauntlet of everything you learnt so far" feel.The general map layout is great, the dungeons and the puzzles have excellent flow. Bosses are varied both by  design and mechanics but follow the classic metriodvania route of being rather easy and more of a progression marker than blocker.Collectibles include health upgrade pieces, warp point creators (every save point can be turned into a warp point and for 100% you need to do so) and ability orbs to upgrade your core spells to solve puzzles and general traversal. Some spell modifiers are useful only 1-2 times to solve specific puzzles but you can respec for free ANY time at the town NPC making the system very flexible.You get 2 of 3 core spells before the first dungeon boss and the 3rd can be obtained very very early too (no spoilers). You also get a mixture of activatable powers (that recharge at every screen transition automatically or manually by holding the cast button) and a few items granting you direct or indirect methods of traversing certain parts. It all sounds a bit cumbersome considering all the different categories but for genre veterans it will come naturally.There are no major sequence breaking present in the game but the world opens up fast and sections requiring a certain item might have an alternate solution if you spend spell points in the right way.Some optional sections and bosses exist but neither the rewards nor the challenges are that jawdropping, 100% completion is less taxing than the average in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic MV with lots of great exploration.  Did I need to use a guide to get the last few percent?  Sure.  But the game has a lot of secrets and they're all *findable*, which is something.  The main progression of the game is not entirely obvious, either, which means you have to actually explore, find stuff, and return later when you can properly access it with new abilities.  The magic upgrade system is great too; you spend the blue orbs to level up your magic (same three spells as in Alwa's Awakening), but you can go back to the wizard at any time to respec for free, meaning that if you need one particular upgrade, you can go back to the wizard, take orbs off your current upgrades, and apply them to the one you want.  All in all, this is a very solid MV, full of MV-ness.Negative: the final few bosses are kind of anticlimactic, especially when you're fully upgraded.  The earlier bosses do put up a challenge, but a lot less than in the first game.  I accidentally got the achievement for beating a boss with no damage on the first boss (after dying to it a bunch of times, it should be said).  The real challenge is in the platforming puzzles, which are awesome and plentiful.  So if you don't like hard bosses anyway, this isn't even a real negative.Again, this is a great game and you should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't play these types of retro games because i prefer handdrawn/painted art (Ori, Gris) or modern pixel art (Blasphemous, HLD) but the art on the backgrounds, especially in foresty areas convinced me. I don't regret picking this up, because while the art drew me in at first, the metroidvania map - which i caught glimpse of the full map early - was exactly what i love. A proper BIG metroidvania with different biomes, many interconnected routes, secrets that you can't reach just yet and lots of backtracking. It's not for everyone but i absolutely love it, and the level design in this one is spot on, paired with buttery smooth & responsive controls. In fact exploration and movement was pretty much my main source of enjoyment in this game, because the rest of it is VERY retro. From combat & bossfights, to visuals and even the soundtrack, all of it is super old school and will be a treat if you're into that kinda stuff. The story was pretty mediocre and forgettable though, but I didn't mind it, nor did it detract from the great level design. I'd even say that if you're like me and not that into retro games, but a big fan of MV's, that you should pick this one up. Played the whole thing in pretty much a day and while i didn't completly 100% the map, i walked away from the experience feeling satisfied. Not one i'd replay but nevertheless one i'm glad that i played. Recomended full price for fans of retro games or on sale for MV fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best best retro-style games that truly feels like it could have been on the SNES. Graphics are super colorful and creative, the music sounds like it's from the best era of Mega Man on the NES, and the game offers a lot of innovative fun, with each of the large dungeons presenting their own interesting mechanical quirks. The game is not terribly difficult (the final boss is actually surprisingly easy).My only complaint about the music is that it's much more like NES than SNES in terms of the audio quality. Still, it's an amazing soundtrack.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game, but I was never able to play it.  They seem to have compatibility issues with controllers, including the Logitech gamepad that I use.  I've requested a refund.  Hopefully one day they will fix these issues.  If you plan on purchasing this game, make sure you don't have a Logitech gamepad.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Such great game loaded with puzzles and fun movement and abilities. These abilities even make traversing through the world a puzzle. Combat is okay and dodging attacks is pretty challenging. About 2.5-3 hours into gameplay and Alwa's Legacy reminds me of games like the "Monster Boy" and "Shantae" Series (which are great series in my book). Progression is a little disappointing since the majority of abilities/upgrades are typically found and not locked behind mini bosses or puzzles. These minor shortcomings, however, do not take away from how much fun the game is. If you're a fan of 2D action platformers, this seems to be a great game to at to your library.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixel art, locations differ from each other in terms of graphics and level designes. Soundtracks are original to every locations. Skills system is simple but needs player to explore and gather orbs to develop.Game isnt very hard for example spikes only instakill you in Eydie's Keep, in other locations only hit you one time and at the beggining of the game you can take 3 hits before you die. Enemies and bosses also deal one damage most of the time.Finished the game a year ago but now i decided to do all achievements and NG+ where you cant kill any enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: "Alwa's Lecay" is a logical sequel to the first installment, featuring better graphics, better worldbuilding and redefined puzzle and adventuring mechanics: The world is bigger and feels more alive, the dungeons, the overall progress-system and the movement are more complex. It is still a slow paced Metroidvania, but on a bigger scale and it still feels somewhat generic in the overall tone, but it is nevertheless a polished and well crafted experience for genre-veterans and newcomers alike!
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration is key in this complex, packed full of goodies sequel to an already difficult retro platformer I hate myself for playing. The next logical step from Alwa's Awakening, this overstuffed outing is packed with puzzles of varying style, a weapons upgrade system unlike the last one, and surprising mini boss fights. Even lots of new NPC that actually help! While the music is fun, it's not as toe-tappin' good as the first installment. When you start to see the map fill up the more it looks like SotN. I even saw some nods to other Metroidvania games like Blasphemous and Hollow Knight. With more vast and complex world to navigate through, this one is actually taking me less time. Get it now or on sale. It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: A good puzzle/platforming Metroidvania with NES-level difficulty and guidance. At varying points I was reminded of Zelda II, Milon's Secret Castle, Fire 'n Ice, Mega Man and more. Three related comments:1. I never played the previous game, Alwa's Awakening, so I can't compare the two. I will say that I felt left out of the story on this one...like I was missing something. Maybe both games are vague? The devs have said that some of the story is left to the player's interpretation.2. The game is challenging in many spots due to your low max HP (starting at 3 hits) and some environmental hazards. However, save spots are never more than a few rooms away and death doesn't reset your progress - only your current location. As a casual gamer, I got through it just fine. I blindly one-shotted most bosses, and each fight only takes a minute or so since they also have low HP.3. Like gaming before the internet was available and when manuals were in Engrish, you have to figure out a lot of the game by yourself. This leads to both hours of experimentation, and rewarding eureka moments. I got to about 95% on my own before cheating on a few spots. Also note that the game contains a few large-scale optional puzzles that require an exhaustive amount of time to figure out on your own. In fact, two of the puzzles haven't even been solved by players yet. If you want to avoid wasting time, you can ignore  (no known purpose) and just look up the solution to  (would take hours to brute force, and the end result is unsolved by players so far).+Colorful and cute artwork (I admit to some internal "squee!"ing)+Death (frequent) only moves you back to a (frequent) save point+Responsive controls+Increasingly available fast travel+Multiple save slots, including the ability to copy files+Multiple difficulties+ mode unlockable+Roughly 8-20 hours of play, depending on how thorough you are and at what point you say 'screw it' and look up a guide~Few player iFrames and enemy iFrames are unpredictable~Generally challenging platforming, relatively easy bosses~Game expects you to figure out mechanics by experimentation~No wikis etc, making research hard (not the game's fault)~Story is vague and open to interpretation per devs~Two minor graphical bugs I found~Even with guides it can be hard to get 100% completion in some areas~Map is helpful, but doesn't mark item locations and doesn't explain what contributes to the completion %'s (hint: it counts converting saves to warps).~Two mysterious objects in the game that literally no one has fully figured out yet and the devs refuse to comment on-Hurtbox for spikes is a bit overzealous-Can't cycle backwards through menus-A few areas of troll-like frustration-Optional boss reward is garbage-One of the special abilities is garbage-Different methods of selecting magic and special abilities-One item that I can't see you ever finding without a guide-Needing to frequently farm enemies for health or take an intentional death was a pace-killer-Rose tombstones shouldn't have been visible in first playthrough. Wasted so much time trying to figure those out, especially with all the references to them.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing and solid little metroidvania. It's not an intense roller coaster of action and emotion, and it doesn't demand 40 hours of your time just to do a basic run. It clocks in at about 10 hours to get 93% completion if you take do it with the same effort you put into a leisurely stroll.It definitely scratches the metroidvania itch without asking you to commit the next two weeks of your life to it, which is nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good metroidvania.  I appreciate that the boss fights are not dark soul nightmare battles and FAIR.  Platforming wise this is less difficult than shovel knight but still requires skill.Player movement is great.  The only minor movement complaint is that you can't move while attacking or casting a spell, which is old school but feels alright once you get used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy continues where Awakening left off, so if you have enjoyed Awakening, you should enjoy Legacy.Following the bigger, better, more principle, it adds additional systems while retaining the overall Metroidvania appeal. Graphics look great and I really enjoy having a separate button for powers.What holds the game back are the worse fights (killing a monster with the standard attack is tedious, albeit not hard) and was feels like a far more vague guidance - e.g. why would I want to repair a house? How should I know that I need to find metal for the smith to create a present which turns out to be a bell that I need somewhere else? This way the gameplay often devolved int o running around the map for places I have not been to.Finally the overall gameplay felt less well paced than the original. Where the original build up to a climax, Legacy just kept on going and at some point the game was over - despite having FAR more story.All in all I had a lot of fun, but if you plan on only playing on of the Alwa games, play the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad metroidvania. Too many collectibles for basic things such as health, ability upgrades, fast travel, forcing you to waste more time collecting stuff. No directions or signposting, tons of backtracking and random rooms you can miss in 1 corner to find 1 thing you need for a totally different room on a totally different end of the map forcing looking up walkthroughs. Combat pretty basic, although there are a nice amount of upgrades.  7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little Metroidvania. Feels a bit like it's hampering you unnecessary with the upgrade curve, as the upgrades don't really give much of a power progression and more like "removing annoyances". However, gameplay, artwork and humor are enough to keep you entertained for a solid 9h if you want to 100% it.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: 1. This is a metroidvania/action-explorer game done in 16bit era style and catchy music.2. You will only have 3 hearts. That means you can only take 3 hits. It can be increased to a maximum of 6 hearts.3. Bosses battles can be on the easier side depending on your spell build.4. Unlike the previous Alwa game, there is no significant platforming difficulty spike in the last dungeon.5. Overall this is like the previous game but much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game in the Metroidvania style of platformer.  I haven't played any other Alwa games yet, so I can't compare them, but I've really enjoyed my time with Alwa's Legacy.  The moves you get as you progress through the game are very interesting and a nice change from the usual fare (you summon a block or a bubble to reach higher places instead of the typical double / triple jump , for example).  My biggest frustration has come from figuring out where to go, but the map is huge and there are a ton of hidden items that you need to go back for, so that makes wandering around lost actually worthwhile.  I would say that difficulty is mostly in the average range with a few frustratingly hard moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly endearing and nostalgic. I can't put my finger on just what it is that reminds me of playing the original NES Zelda. This is a side scroller, so it shouldn't, but its definitely there. Maybe its that each dungeon/castle has its own color scheme and new obstacles. As an old school gamer, I don't find a lot of new games I really love. Alwa will be in a small group of new, but old styled games like Axiom Verge and The Messenger that I find awesome. This game is addicting, fun as heck, has smooth responsive play control, and is hard to put down. You will find new challenges with each part of the game and a few puzzles that will leave you stumped for a bit. As you progress, there are multiple ways to reach across gaps and up to new heights. You can get pretty creative with your movement. There were a couple things I thought you'd get the ability to do, that didn't materialize like being able to create more than one block simultaneously. Still don't know what green bubbles actually do? The ability to add warp points is a good way to deal with the necessary backtracking for getting every item. You'll have to revisit a lot of places to gain new access. There's still a couple places I haven't figured out yet but I just finished the game. The final boss was a bit easy, but getting there was the hard part and its fairly irritating when you have a final boss that's discouragingly difficult to beat anyway. I wish there had been more places to use the exploding blocks to open up different areas in the game. Sometimes there were just too many spikes! Never found much use for the orbs that float around you. More to do with the blacksmith and repairman would've been good. Would be cool if there is a sequel or added stages to see a beach area, some lush forest, a wintry or more rocky mountain area, maybe a few more varied side quests and swords/weapons. Killer game this go around and much appreciation to the developers! Will play again for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This is somewhat of a hidden gem. It has beautiful art, especially the background. Nice 8 bit feel sound, and good platforming. The gameplay is pretty good and straightforward, nothing special compared to other games in its genre (metroidvania). Still it has been worked out pretty well, and kept being engaging. The only real downside of the game is that it prides itself on being non-linear. I guess this is indeed a positive thing for many, but it did cause me to feel 'lost' a lot. I had no idea what I was supposed to do at times. After a while this became less of an issue, but it almost caused me to give up on the game. Graphics: 9/10 Sound 8.5/10Gameplay: 8/10Atmosphere: 9/10Story: 6/10Overall: 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: - okay metroidvania with kinda stiff control scheme- I liked pixel art graphics, very bright and colorful. Reminds me of old Dizzy games- it plays a little like Zelda with "dungeon" sections- AL really opens up after the first section of the game, to the point that it is very easy to get lost - spent a major part of my playthrough trying to find a way- there are some uneven spikes in difficulty along the way, while final boss is almost laughably easy in comparison- it has an interesting unlockable Pacifist mode, where you can bypass boss encountersRecommended, but I'm glad I got it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Awakening was better IMO. They made the game way too easy, which took away the difficulty and fun that came with it. Being able to clip the walls in Alwa's Awakening and finding exploits was fun. Alwa's Legacy was more refined but to straight forward for me and not enough "freedom" in which dungeons to explore first. Plus no speed running achievement :/
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. This game is such a latecomer to a bygone era. It would have been a Grade A blockbuster if it were released in the 90's!Graphically, it's antiquated...but that adds to the charm!This game is a blast. Be ready to explore the same maps looking for things previously missed of unreachable; it's a true Metroidvania game, but if you enjoy Metroidvania's I cannot recommend this enough.This game had me hooked, I binged and beat it over a weekend.Give it a try, you'll know within 2 hours if it's for you or not. If it is, you won't be disappointed!I hope they're working on the third one. Really looking forward to it!
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: The continuation to Alwa's Awakening has some definite improvement in art and game design.I do have a couple of complaints:It's a bit *too* similar to the first game. The first one had very similar mechanics so it was a bit underwhelming.And then the bosses, what the hell? Why are they so easy? Probably the easiest bosses in any game I've played. It's a shame because the magic and ability combinations could really have made for interesting boss designs. It's fine to have a longer boss fight with different phases...But still, it's a nice Metroidvania game, some cool puzzles, and fun exploration (could have been a bit more straightforward given the giant map).Pick it up on a sale if you're into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I love Metroidvainia 2D platformers and I'm always looking for a new one to play.  This game definitely scratched that itch.  It's really fun with tight controls and a really satisfying upgrade progression.  I especially liked how you can make the checkpoint system forgiving or more difficult.  I chose the forgiving route.  The warp point system is also very unique and fun.  Great Game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania with heart. The art is lively and well-animated, the music is great, and while the story and characters are not especially deep, they are solid. The gameplay feels pretty tight, and while some parts are a little bit harder than I'd prefer, the game has a few "assist mode" settings which help with the most frustrating aspects of it.I did have some issues with controller input at first; the game doesn't work well if you have multiple controllers connected (including, in my case, a "gamer pad"/half-keyboard). Unplugging all but one controller fixes that.  As a nitpick, I'd like for the the UI and the gameplay buttons to be remappable independently since I use a Nintendo-layout (8bitdo) controller, but I couldn't use A for "confirm" in the menus but B for jump. None of that prevented me from enjoying the game a lot, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Warning, this game can feel unfair. I really like hard games and this one is pretty hard but not too much, sadly, sometimes, it really is unfair. Also exploration is a bit tedious sometimes since you do not really know where to look. Anyways, passed that, it's really fun, puzzles are cool and not too hard, art is fine and music ok. Not for everyone but really satisfying if you put enough effort and accept some game design weird choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: I spent the weekend playing this metroidvania game.It is really good! Top notch pixel art, a great chiptune soundtrack and the best feeling of character movement in a 2d pixel-based metroidvania since Momodora: RUtM (although Timespinner was really good as well).The gameplay focuses more on puzzle solving and platforming than combat. The bosses heavily tie into the puzzle solving mechanics as well in a way that is reminiscent of Zelda bosses.The world map is large, but not overwhelming. At no point did I feel that the game was wasting my time. The puzzle challenges are escalated nicely, but there is not much grinding with the same type of puzzle. Also, all items related to character upgrades are uniquely placed in the world, so there is no combat grinding needed whatsoever.The weak point of the game is the story and to a lesser extent the setting. The developer seems to presume that you have played the previous game (which I have not), which gets somewhat confusing in the beginning of the game. Thankfully, the story content is kept to a minimum, and you don't really have to invest in the story to be able to enjoy the game. The setting is not explained very well, but the pixel art for the different areas look great, and exploring the world can be enjoyed without knowing the details.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun metroidvania with solid controls, excellent graphics, music, and far more forgiving on the platforming than the previous installment (so far, I'm only part-way complete).  Playing the prequel, while recommended for its own merits and some tie-ins, is not required.  Well worth it at the asking price!
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This game improves on almost everything from the previous game, Awakening. The puzzles and dungeons are more fun. There's a lot less hidden walls you have to find. Fun and challenging boss fights. Awesome music.If you enjoyed Awakening you'll definitely have fun with this one as well.My only complaint really is that I wish there was a way to put markers on the map in order to help you remember places you wanted to visit later. Once I beat the game I realized I would pretty much have to walk through every screen until I found what I was looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Really proud to have backed this one on kickstarter.  I found everything about it satisfying.  The puzzles felt just right in terms of challenge, and they struck a nice balance between rewarding you for completing them and designing the game so that you don't need to find all of the orbs (that upgrade your magic).  Combat and platforming worked well for a game like this.  Art is gorgeous, especially the backgrounds.  I feel like that's especially important for a metroidvania that encourages you to revisit areas multiple times.  Music is retro and very catchy.  It took me 10 hours to complete, doing a reasonable job of looking for secrets but also not being a perfectionist.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game, light puzzly metroidvania.Finished the main story mode in like 7 hours or so, probably will push on and get atleast some of the 'end game' achievements. Probably really good game for speed running, since I already figured out so many things to finish the game faster. Soundtrack is also awesome.Only thing I didn't like, warning spoilers:
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: It was a lot of fun. Not a very long game and it could have been shorter if I remembered where I had to go. Music was really nice and the controls were very tight. Almost too tight. Missed ladders a couple times because I decided to stop moving towards it and watched Zoe just drop. My two biggest complaints are probably not having a way to specifically see what your goal is and the UP + Attack button combination using your magic. I read that the devs put it in because that's how Alwa's Awakening played or something but there really needs to be a way to turn it off. Way too many times I took damage trying to smack something in the air because it casted my magic instead.8.5/10 game. If you're looking for a nice, short game to kill a few hours this is definitely worth playing if you like puzzle platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This ticks every box for what I want out of a metroidvania.There are hundreds of screens, but no filler - each screen is individually and lovingly crafted, and most of them have something fun or challenging to do in them. There are lots of upgrades and pickups, but only one I didn't end up having much use for (the shield ability FYI), and each one, even upgrades on existing abilities and items, has its own unique mechanics and use in the game world.The emphasis is on exploration, and the combat really adds a bit of excitement and challenge to it without getting in the way; no tedious and superfluous RPG mechanics here! The bosses are all a little on the easy side, even the final boss, but as I said - that is not the point of the game.The graphics (particularly the parallax backgrounds) are absolutely luscious (although I would have liked a little bit more animation in the NPCs, but that's nitpicking) and the music is amazing.So if you love an exploration and gradual, non-linear unfolding experience in metroidvanias, and don't want to bother with a lot of RPG stats and overly complex combat, then there are few games better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing followup to their first game! The 16-bit style provides for a richer experience compared to the first game. Gorgeous graphics, a very nice soundtrack, tight and addictive platformer gameplay. Characters move fluently and at a reasonable pace. It's not an extremely fast-paced game, but it's also not slow either. And you can pet a cute little piggy <3The main downsides is that the music isn't quite as good as for the first game (which in my opinion had some of the best videogame music of all time) and that the support for joypads was kinda buggy (which has been addressed in the first patch).Highly recommended for anyone who likes Metroidvania-style games from the 16-bit era.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beyond lovely.Artwork and level design are just an outstanding piece of work.Together with the excellent music this is everything I could ever want from a retro metroidvania.Also worth mentioning is the polished Linux build.Thanks for supporting that platform!I applied for the beta test and I can only say these guys totally love what they are doing and deserve your support. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautiful adventure in the land of Alwa. If you thought the first game Alwa's Awakening was good, Alwa's Legacy is even better. The graphics are very well done and the puzzles are good. There are a lot more items to find and things to do. Good game mechanics and controls you saw in Alwa's awakening. The storytelling is excellent. 1 hr into the game, I found it hard to put the controller down. This is a must play for metroidvania and puzzle platformer fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not easy.  You will die, no matter how good you are at this game death will come for you.Currently it has a few bugs, but the game just came out and the very small team are working on hammering them out. _childDocuments_.review: Great game. I'd put it in the Metroidvania Light category personally, but that's not a bad thing. It won't take you 30+ hours to beat, but it's worth the 10 hour or so ride, and I think the price point reflects that.The mechanics are unique (at least, in my experience). Instead of just getting that freeze shot or a rocket launcher or double jump this is about getting the ability to summon a bubble you can ride, a block you push into enemies, and a lightning bolt you can fire off during a battle. There are switches. There are puzzles. For the most part, you won't struggle with the puzzles. They're clever enough to make you think for a moment, but never frustrating. The boss battles are reasonably easy, IMO, but not to the point that you feel unaccomplished when you win.The art style and audio are fantastic, and if your expectations are high, keep them there. One dungeon in particular, had me nodding my head to the melody and beat. Good times.Controls are tight and responsive, but I will admit that using one button by default to cycle through three different abilities constantly in-use gets a bit annoying. I get why they did that because the right bumper does something else entirely, but I really wish they had found a more clever way to incorporate the second radial menu and let the right and left bumpers rotate between main skills. I didn't dig into the menu or config but maybe there's a way to change this. Either way, not my favorite decision.The only other "complaint" I have, and I use that term loosely, is the writing. It wasn't bad in the traditional sense. Whomever wrote the actual dialogue clearly knew how to write, but it was just kinda, I don't know, one-dimensional? I really didn't care about the characters or the story. There was very limited world-building. I still don't know what the hell my character was or why she did what she did. I suppose that information is awarded to the lore deep divers and completionists, but I'm of the opinion that I shouldn't have to find every little piece of lore and items to understand my character's backstory and purpose at least on a superficial level.Regardless, I hope there's a third. This was well planned, well executed, and I encountered no bugs during my plathrough. Also, the devs are very responsive and friendly in the forums.If you're looking for a metroid light and a good time at a totally justifiable price, pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing sequel to Alwas Awakening. "Metroidvania" with gorgeous graphics, sweet music and wonderful animations, aiming for that SNES-feel i so much love. Im in love. Couple of bugs at release (especially with dash and ladders) (probably patched soon). Alot to explore and collect. Well designed bosses (although quite easy most of them) 5/5. Im gonna 100% this for sure over the weeks ahead.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a fantastic follow-up to Alwa's Awakening, and an amazing game in it's own right.It cleverly builds upon the foundation of Alwa's Awakening by quickly unlocking the same magic you had in that game - and then giving you the freedom to improve upon those magics however you choose. Want to go all in on boosting your fiery magic? Go for it! Want to improve the green block and explore previous dead-ends? Have at it! It works really well.The game introduces it's formula in a linear fashion, but after this sequence you're totally free to go about the game however you want. You're provided with hints, and with an excellent map system you never feel truly lost.In addition to being you'd expect from a sequel - it stands on it's own as a standalone game, so elegantly designed it's almost ridiculous. You don't need to have played Alwa's Awakening to appreciate this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Pixels return with this outstanding sequel to an already amazing game.  The amount of love and craftmanship that this game exhibits deeply conveys how personal this project is to this very small team.  It's one of the best examples in the Metroidvania genre and fans will get a lot out of this.  If you like backtracking over already visited areas in order to explore further due to an ability upgrade, then buy it today; this game has a truckload of that. The graphics are gorgeous - the sprites, the backgrounds and all other small attention to details (birds, flies and other ambient creaturs). The excellent music just adds another layer of depth to complement these aesthetics. Everything about it harks back to the wonderful era of SNES/16-bit gaming where you just lost yourself in these vast worlds that were invented.As with the first game in the series (Alwa's Awakening), the game drives you to be a completionist in collecting everything and obtaining 100% in each of the zones. It will drive you to sleepless nights and madness (in a good sense).Stop playing those soulless AAA titles - give this one your time and money. It deserves a high profile on Steam and your love.
_childDocuments_.name: Alwa's Legacy

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely feels like a good buy so far, it brings a lot of what I enjoyed with Alwa's Awakening and adds a solid layer of polish (and smoother, faster, and more satisfying movement). Other than a couple extremely tight bits of platforming (though that's what you expect from Alwa if you've ever beaten the original lol), I've yet to find any issues with the game in the first 2 chapters, and I'm loving the new movement tech they added - it makes it feel much more well rounded. If you're wondering if you should buy this - basically think "Would I enjoy a game that's somewhere between Symphony of the Night/Bloodstained and Shovel Knight?" - if the answer is yes, this is what you want :) If you're looking for something between "Symphony of the Night/Bloodstained and Mega Man" - then you'd want to go for the first game (Alwa's Awakening).Both really solid metroidvania entries, though this one is significantly easier (and faster) to navigate.[after completion edit]Overall, completed the first run in "beaten, 90% secrets found, 11 hours, 55 deaths" (closer to 8 hours of actual playing, I let it idle quite a bit) - a satisfying Metroidvania, a lot more polished than it's predecessor (albeit a little easier). I can definitely recommend this for someone looking for a few hours of good metroidvania action.

_childDocuments_.review: Alwa's Legacy is a 16-bit style sequel to the 8-bit style puzzle-platformer, Alwa's Awakening.  It's slower-paced than a lot of recent indie platformers, but this is by design.  It manages to have a retro feel to it, but is still easy for just about anyone to pick up and play.I've really enjoyed my time with the game so far, and I can tell the developers put a lot of love into this project.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Just needs more polish. Legends is without a doubt an improvement from All Out; but nowhere near as fluid as Reflex. The physics are pretty bare-bones and bike handling feels rigid and imprecise, but gets better with upgrades and tuning. The game is fun despite having some glaring issues that need fixing. Hopefully they get fixed with updates!PROS+ excellent track designs+ impressive elevation and environments+ realistic track roughness+ good terrain deformation+ excellent rider models and scaling+ working scrubs and whips+ more bike weight+ adjustable camera viewCONS- poor sound design- bike sound is out of sync with rpm- sound effects break immersion- tires look like they float on the dirt- limited rider animations- unrealistic collisions- can't change controller bindings- too many micro transactions

_childDocuments_.review: I want to make an early review, unbiased and based on my 8 hrs of game play. First thing I'll say is yes, it has it's faults just like many other releases. All will be fixed in the weeks to come imo quite effortlessly. Generally speaking the game is still fun to play.They've taken the steps to incorporate more freeride ability which to me was always one of the main reasons to play and KEEP playing the game, ie: MX vs ATV Unleashed, ATV Off Road Fury 2, the racing was there but the roaming was always more appealing.In regards to physics, they are not 'All Out' style at all, which to me is good because I didn't personally enjoy it, but to be fair they should make more effort to choose multiple variants of riding styles, including the one that came with this release.In terms of the racing, so far I've managed to get 1st in all MX events I've done, some harder than others but it's playable unlike what I've seen from most people. It does have issues and again I feel as though these things are inevitably going to be handled.My advice to anyone would be to find out for yourself, and give it a chance to iron out the kinks, instead of reading the vast majority of these reviews, especially the people that have invested less than 1 hour of time into the game.Update: 2023 Nov. 22nd - A slow, but consistent effort by the people at Rainbow Studios has really brought this game to arguably one of the best of any mx vs atv game in the series. Without a doubt my favorite and as far as I see it it's only going to get better. A much smaller team, and a re imagined brand new from scratch build should really push this series into new territory for the next game. Look at Legends as a solid, fun to play game laying the framework for the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin on the game. It has so much potential, but it is completely half-baked. I bought the complete pack, and really regretting that. There are so many things that are just missing that previous titles had. But before we complain about that, here is what the game does well:- Incredible Environments (especially the AMA Nationals)But that is about it. I have only done MX as that is what I care for the most in these games, and the bike controls are hard to learn. Not only that, you cannot even map the controls different. You're forced to do the tutorial, and the overall "story" of the game feels like an NBA 2K rip-off (and it's much worse in story telling). Then within the story mode, it doesn't even tell you what bike class you are racing.Speaking of bikes, there are no custom graphics for the DLC bikes. There are simply cosmetics (handle bars, suspension, sprocket, etc.), but you can't really change the color if you want brand name. Those cosmetics also don't do anything, you have to buy tuning packages separate. Rider customization is abysmal. There are maybe 20 gear sets, and you can't even change the color scheme like previous games. I think back to MXvATV Alive when we had Butt Patches, Neck Braces, Rider Perks, and incredibly amounts of customization, and it's all just missing. Finally, I really enjoy time trials, but I have found out there are no leaderboards yet in the game. I am consistently in the top of the leaderboards in previous games and racing you all through lap times is fun for me. Well, I can't even do that. I'm not going to refund the game because I do see the potential, but at this time I cannot recommend it. I hope they have a lot planned for the game, but I honestly just see microtransactions from hell incoming.

IN TOTAL THERE ARE 33 ADD-ON VEHICLES AND ONLY 24 IN GAME VEHICLES!DEVELOPMENT  6/10BUGS FOUND      2GAME PLAY        7/10GRAPHICS          7/10 PHYSICS             6/10MUSIC                5/10ONLINE Race/Freeride              No existentCUSTOMIZATION             5/10VEHICLE SELECTION        6/10Mx Career Completion Time:  22hrsUtv Career Completion Time: In ProgressATV Career Completion Time: In ProgressDEVELOPMENT is solid I have not ran into any bugs yet! So that is awesome. I know when the game first came out the map textures would disappear. The moment of the bike was laggish/sluggish the list at the time period goes on. With that said the game is Night and Day from launch it is a lot more cleaner and less bugs. This is not like the first couple of years like Super cross Encore where it was low key unplayable until the developers released a bunch of patches. BUG ONE: I found a bug containing the AI. There are squids, there riding is all over the place and they are slow on the hardest level with no modifications done to the vehicle. Not too terrible but lack the neck and neck competition the other titles had. BUG TWO: This happened multiple times before I considered adding this to the list of bugs. When in freeride and driving up a steep hill or mountain, if you tap the clutch to get more power the bike jumps in the are about 10 feet. once you land you start rolling backwards slowly. you do not fall off the bike but what in the world is this bug/glitch.GRAPHICS are clean and high definition but I was expecting a little more detail. For some reason it reminds me of farming simulator 2022.PHYSICS are similar to Mx Vs. ATV All out. Especially, when landing from stunts it can be tricky. you must put the time into the game to understand how to ride with the default bike. This is NOT a simulator racing game. If you want a Simulator game get MxGP 2020 or newer. IMPORTANT!!!! The physics will change for the better over time because they are constantly releasing more patches for different aspects of riding. For example. the corning was a little buggy at first and then they released a patch recently to fix it. If there are issues with physics don't give up hope.MUSIC is way better than expected. There is a wide variety like EDM, Rock,metal, Screamo (No pop/hip-pop). If any of you know who Scarlxrd is you will know is music cant even be put into a category and his music is in the game. MULTIPLAYER there are very little lobbies. I rarely can find any. Lacks many brands and lacks styles like most modern gear have (retro Oneal colors or any thing of the such).VEHICLES there are a wide selection. You have dirt bikes ranging from 125cc - 450cc, ATV'S only have 450cc, UTV's 1000cc only. In my opinion, there are too many add-on vehicles and not enough classes. Pitbikes 100% need to be added in. _childDocuments_.review: This game needs a little work. Let me explain.I've loved most of the Rainbow Studios games since I started playing ATV Offroad Fury, through the MX series intro with Unleashed. This game stands out as a different style on how they wanted the player to feel. It comes across as though they wanted to create a more "realistic" feel with the vehicles in this game, and honestly, I love it.The 3 vehicles you get to play in the game (as of right now), are the Motorcycles, which range from 150cc 2 strokes, 250cc 2 and 4 strokes, and 450cc 4 strokes. The second vehicle you can select is a 450cc ATV, and the last one is the UTV (kinda a sporty side-by-side like a Polaris RZR if you know what that is).The game itself feels like Forza Horizons had a butt-baby with an MX game. It definitely feels a bit more sluggish, and less responsive on turns than most of the franchise in the past. But once you start to work around the little nuances of dual stick steering, or how bad you'll get thrown off in ruts or digs, or even corners, the game is one of the best. Speaking of dual stick steering, it seems a few people playing do not understand so let me clarify a little (this is in reference to MX only, it doesn't matter as deep on the other 2 vehicles). The left stick is for your main turn, basically left or right on the handlebars. Up and down on the left stick is seatbounce, to gain a little more height on your jumps, at the sacrifice of distance. The right stick is lean, to tilt your character left or right, and help you dig deeper in the tighter corners, or lean back for a wheelie over some whoops. Like any MX game that I know of, gas and brake in the air is to lean forward or back to do a flip, so make sure you aren't holding down those unless you need to rotate. The last thing that's really necessary, is the clutch. A slight tap of the clutch when 80% through a tight corner, or at the tail end, will give you a little bit more traction and really help assist you to get that bit of speed you might need in something tighter like supercross.Once you break down the game into individual vehicles, you get a little more complex on controls, but nothing that's too hard to learn. MX has one of the most responsive feels, but as the engine size gets bigger, you definitely feel that weight in corners. ATV feels very fun, it's the most straight forward of the 3, and probably the easiest. And the UTV is arguably the most fun, but also the hardest to learn and get comfy with, it's a freakin boat. It should also be noted that the 3rd person view feels really slow and slightly clunky, but I'm sure there's some people who enjoy that more. But I play exclusively in 1st person, as it feels MUCH better, and almost fits the "realism" part of the game I enjoy so dearly. It should also be noted that you should almost immediately be upgrading your vehicle, as it gets harder to hit jumps and actually land them properly, without adequate power.All of this good aside though, there's a few very blatant problems. Luckily they aren't game breaking, just annoying.Firstly, in 1st person, going over any jumps or bumps, your character tends to throw their head up and to the left, probably coded in to help you see where you are landing and what's ahead of you, but for the slightly bigger whoops, or if you case a lot of jumps, it gets kinda disorienting to get thrashed that much without control of your camera or any settings to dampen the effect.Second and definitely the one you will notice most, the audio needs an entire rework. Getting your MX going above 2nd gear, you'll hear the bike re-start its throttle sound, so it almost simulates revving your bike really snappy and fast, it doesn't sound natural at all. And it only gets worse, the faster you go.The 250cc 2 stroke, the 3rd bike you get. God I want to love 2 strokes so badly, but this specific bike ruined the entire experience, until I shut all the sound off on my system. The exhaust sound will leave your ears bleeding compared to other vehicles, and sounds terrible. The only way I can describe it is gargling spoiled milk. Putting frozen beans in a blender. Putting spaghetti in an upside down lawnmower. You get the point, it's terrible. I think it wouldn't sound so terrible if it wasn't clearly the loudest vehicle in the game, by a longshot. You hop on a 250cc 4 stroke and it's really tame. You can even hop on the 150cc 2 stroke and it sounds fantastic. But that god forsaken 250cc 2 stroke is like microwaving bologna in olive oil for 40 minutes, at deafening levels.Speaking of things being really loud, the freakin music, of all things. It's really quite good when you are free riding and exploring, as the sound is almost attached to your player or just background like it should be. But for some reason, it's like the Dev team wanted to make dynamic stadium speakers, like you would have at a real MX event. You go into the Campaign mode or really any race for that matter, and you get music blasting at levels that will make you flinch with every percussion or beat. You could throw your headset across your house and you'd hear the music fine, unless it's an endurance style race, where the map is huge. In that case, the music is usually either glued to the start and finish, or to the crowds. But good luck with that tinnitus on the smaller maps. I'm sure your friend's jet engine fan blowing into their mic, is more quiet than this music.Oh and there's a third thing that I cannot stand. The maps "Vallis Wind Farm" which has an A, B, C, and D variant. Normally, the map is fine. On MX you might struggle a bit as you need to understand how the rhythm of landing jumps works, which I got stuck on because I didn't know you could upgrade the bike to help land more jumps, or to get more power coming off of a botched landing. But once you get into UTV's you'll for SURE hate the map. They decided it would be a bright idea to stuff 8 freakin vehicles, each being about 2x the size of a golf cart, on a single lane map, where even ATV's struggle to not hit each other. It's immediate congestion right off the start, and god forbid you get the holeshot through the start. You have to wrestle this machine, as it fights you to stay straight on the landings, and as you go over countless jumps of all sizes, hoping and praying that you won't just barely budge the stick to the side a little too far and have every other driver pass you while you respawn. It seems like changing difficulty does nothing to help you as, to assist my pain, I set steering to 1 stick, difficulty to very easy, and made the rider physics not pro. But it feels identical to any difficulty, or any setting. I even race it in 3rd person to help see what the heck is happening, but even then it's a tense struggle. BUT on top of all of this, there's literally 7 other guys with their foot through the floor, bricking the gas like they left the oven on at home. It's a nightmare to try to land straight or to control your vehicle and try to get a 1st place win. BUT IT DOESN'T STOP THERE...You have to complete map variants A-D MORE THAN ONCE. The game is measured by seasons, so when you get to the next year, you have to run it again. Off the top of my head, you have to race the set of 4 (A-D), 4 times through the career, PER VEHICLE. Granted, the ATV and MX are much easier to grasp, but still, it gives me the heebie jeebies even thinking about trying to 100% get first place.Fourth, and minor at that. The snow maps, there's specific sections of it like the starting/ finish line, or the huge left 180 corner, where I get horrible lag. I have a 1080ti playing on 1440p monitors, and other than this one specific map, I get zero other stutters or hitches in the gameplay.TLDR. The game looks beautiful, it plays great (once you get the controls down), and it's definitely something I would recommend, as long as you have a controller and are alright with first person racing. But it has its issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin.One of the biggest things I dislike most about this game is how boring it is literally. The career events are so painful and tedious to play, the customisation of your bike and rider etc. The menu could use some improvements and so could the UI, the camera angles are not very good and slightly odd. I mean the game presents itself as a sort of free roam, where you can go around on your bike and have some fun, the problem is the map layout is a little dull and it strongly feels like there is just something missing like maybe a touch of atmosphere, the music is horrible and around the map are interactable characters or NPCs, that act as brick walls when you go near them and talking to them is so uninteresting, I don't know the game world just feels empty and a bit lifeless to me. Another thing I don't like is how difficult the game is. I always seem to find myself falling off my bike its not exactly what I would call fun, there is not like any sort of rewind or instant reset, the actual reset the game gives you forces you to press and hold a button, for like maybe 5 secs and then by the time you do reset, all the AI opponents just slight shot past you and the game will just respawn you like exactly where you were, so say for instance your climbing up a hill or something your not going to gain any speed and then it becomes annoying and quite frustrating.Considering the cost of this game with all the DLC. I would not recommend spending too much money on this, especially at full price its really not worth it in my opinion. There are so many better Bike games out there like Monster Energy Supercross or MXGP etc those games are awesome and lots of fun but this one is not it kinda sucks. _childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Legends might seem like a fun game at first glance, but upon examining the game further in more detail you might come to the realisation that it needed a lot more time in the oven. The premise is there, but the execution is very poorSteam Curator Page:+ Cleverly laid out stages+ Good amount of stages+ Split screen+ Multiplayer- All sale category vehicles behave the same- Upgrades make little to no sense- AI is rubber banding hell- Audio design is mostly broken- Graphically not impressive at all- Hub world feels like a waste of time- No official ultrawide support (DO NOT change out from full screen)- Stretches image on UW monitors instead of black bars- Cannot replay tutorialMX vs ATV Legends feels like a rushed product. Starting off with the good. The design of all the stages is done in a great manner. When the game is taken at its core, the racing CAN be a lot of fun and it does not feel repetitive thanks to the healthy amount of stages there are to play on. Some tend to partially repeat when used between the different vehicle types but each vehicle will bring its own challenge to stir things up.Continuing on to the negatives, my main gripes with the game are the driving mechanics/ handling and the AI rubber banding. Even on the easiest difficulty, the AI will tend to ignore the laws of physics and blatantly rubber band and slingshot past the player. I am well prepared to face the harsh, but fair, reality that I suck at this game. However, the only time I notices that the difficulty was affecting the AI's behaviour was only during the MX portion of the game. UTV and ATV races ignored the difficulty and  there was at least one or two AI units that were driving incredibly fast. This is less blatant in the easiest difficulty, but it is still present. The driving mechanics are also not perfect. The handling is incredibly funky and very arcade style. Getting the jumps right takes a lot of practice and unfortunately, according to my experience, it is impossible to repeat the tutorial. A very close third is the horrific experience I had with the audio design. Sound effects seem to be properly rendered, but the balance of the audio is way off in most cases. Usually the music is too quiet and will start blasting at either random intervals or specific parts in certain stages. Having my bike at full throttle and full revs on the tach on the bottom right results on my bike's engine making flocculating engine noises with it revving up and down. That is not very accurate and contributes in the poor audio design of the game.The menus feel clunky, the upgrade menu of the vehicles is not explained very well. For example, Cutch boost VS clutch speed upgrades in the UTV as shown in the video. What is the difference? I can at a glance see what the end result will be on the bars next to the vehicle, but that still does not provide any values, or any form of feedback explaining what each upgrade offers and takes away. In the case of the UTV, I added so many upgrades to it that the bars were literally off and past the charts. Car still handled like butter wheels on ice though. Fans of the series might disagree with me on this and I would love to hear why, if you do. Please, give me some feedback in the comments of the video explaining to me if, and why, I am wrong with my outcome. Did I miss something? And did I miss it because the game did not do a good job at explaining it to me? Am I missing the point because I am so far past it? Or are my complaints valid? I am well aware that his might blacklist me from ever receiving keys by THQ, a publisher that I hold near and dear to my heart because they helped bring the Darksiders series (1 and 2, 3 was subpar) to the world. They have helped bring Wreckfest to the world. Spellforce, Remnant FTA, SW Jedi knight, ELEX,  Pillars of Eternity... The list goes on when it comes to great games they have published. This is not one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainly a good *looking* game, but I'm having problems actually enjoying it: the biggest problem is the inconsistency of the tracks, the lack of balance, and the fact that the AI bikes "cheat".The core problem is that motocross racing is not just about "going fast." It's about managing your energy and tackling obstacles on  a course to maintain your speed.So let's start with the tracks: I ran the first race and pretty easily beat the AI bikes on the medium difficulty. On the second race, I found myself having to run sections over and over again, because the track had whoops and jumps that were simply impossible to sail through, due to the poor handling of the player bike's preload/seat bounce system. On a real motocross bike, you can compress the front forks or the rear shock by appropriately leaning and managing the throttle going into a jump Do it right, and you can sail further or rise higher on a jump.BvA tries to implement this, and it seems to work to a limited extent, but this is where "the AI cheats" comes into play.You start the game with a smaller bike (a 250 2-stroke, if I recall), yet the tracks are sized for the larger, faster bikes. So you can't actually make the doubles or fly through the whoops like you could on the bigger bikes.Except that the AI bikes don't seem to care about that. They will sail over a double and make a perfect landing, even though they are traveling the same speed as me. I can run the same section, preloading, seat bouncing, or doing both - yet get the same basic result. Looking at the path the bikes are taking, it seems like the AI bikes are basically taking a pre-recorded run - then just playing it back at a slower speed. So they make every double. They go through the whoops with no problem. They nail every turn and basically can't be pushed off their course in a collision... yet the player bike can attempt the exact same path and speed, yet constantly crash or fail to make jumps.For this reason alone, I'm saying "don't buy" on this game. And that's disappointing, because I enjoy off-road racing games and riding ATVs IRL. But the races in this game are just not enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam noticed that I keep playing this and asked if I wanted to update my review. So this is an update - the original is below.The game is still meh, but since I paid for it I want to try and get my money's worth out of it. As you play through the career the difficulty increases because they stunt you from getting as many holeshots. CPU racers are able to immediately jump off the line and accelerate to speeds you aren't able to reach, and the difficulty increases because then you are stuck in the pack and any tap to your vehicle and you're folding up like a lawn chair. You fall off when you are in the pack and you will lose 7-10 positions every time, and that's where the challenge is. The atrocious physics are still present and accounted for. You still get those bounces after landing jumps some times that send you off to Mars, and regardless of how you are positioned, you will always land, turn as flaccid as Leonardo DiCaprio does around women his own age and proceed to slowly drop off the bike. It's unavoidable. Oh and the camera is terrible too. The desert levels with the cave that drops will make you wonder how a camera this bad made it past QA and into a finished product that customers pay for. At this point I'm 20+ hours in and I still wouldn't really recommend it. I don't expect to be great at everything I do but this game just keeps being frustrating for reasons I don't have any direct control over. There aren't very many MX or off-road racing games out there like this unfortunately, but if this is really the best that is out there than I would say save your money. It's like they could have either gone for an arcade feel or realistic but somehow managed to miss both of them completely. ---ORIGINAL REVIEW---So if you like MX or ATV racing games, there's really not a lot out there, so far that reason it's hard not to recommend this game. But man this is such a frustrating game, and it is so inconsistent! Sometimes you take a jump and land it perfect and it still kicks you off the vehicle, or even worse, sometimes it sends you way up into the air for a second 'jump' which you then get kicked off the vehicle for. Sometimes colliding with another rider doesn't do anytihng to you. Sometimes a vehicle grazes you and you turn into a wet noodle, sliding slowly off the vehicle and losing at least six or seven positions before it graciously allows you to reset. Sometimes you can do half the race off track and its fine, some times you go off track and it immediately resets you where you are. When you reset, you start from a dead stop, which is just brutal when there's no real consistent explanation for it. You will always lose at least 3 or 4 positions from having it reset you, and you will be lucky to gain even one of those positions back so you might as well restart the event, in fact if there's one consistent thing about this game it's that you will restart every single race at least a dozen times before you even finish a single lap. You get a bad start off the line? Restart. Someone knocks you off your vehicle before the holeshot? Restart. The lousy game physics knock you your vehicle when you land on a jump? Restart. Go off-track in the wrong space? Restart. Lather, rinse repeat. When the game clicks, everything runs well and it's really enjoyable. But sadly it's more restarts and frustration than it is racing.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan since the Xbox 360 Reflex, this is a nice improvement. A lot of the negative reviews about traction, AI, and overall gameplay are likely to stumble through a minecraft world set-up. You can tune your bike according to your play-style, adjust AI difficulty in settings, and have an improved experience over previous titles. It's a fun Arcade-style MX/ATV/UTV game. there is no additional launcher, the graphics are a huge improvement from previous titles, and the compound is pretty sick.My only cons...There was some serious rubber-banding when loading in. Almost like severe server lag, but on single-player. I'm sure it was assets loading in, but i do periodically experience it on lengthier trails.  Another would be the bails on hard landings. Sometimes a hard cut on a berm can force you to bail. Mostly it's when you land just after the end of a long triple. Most times your suspension would hold it, but dude and his ankles just fold. All-in-all, it's a good game.  It has some quirks, but isn't enough to ruin the fun of it. I'd say it's a 10/10 on sale.

Most other MvA games had much more to offer and with the MESX games you really have a lot to choose from. 3. The rider motions in the game and the whip/scrub physic could use some work. Once you get good at it you really can throw it around, but it is still vague compared to past games.But now onto the good!1. This game has some of the best elevation and track design of any game, period. No matter how much you want to hate on the game you cannot tell me the tracks are amazing and really well scaled to the speed/style of the game.2. Makes you work hard for the part of the career you want to be at. So many have asked for a game that makes you work hard to go from the start of racing to pro and then when you finally have it so many complain that it takes too much work to grind and make it to pro. I get it, the stock bikes suck, but it is so worth it once you level up and build your bike and progress.3. Graphics imo are some of the best we have seen. They are really stepping up the game. So overall I would give this game a solid 7/10. Main reason being that this is a step in the right direction and I really think that once they update the game more and work out the bugs it will be back to how we enjoyed these arcade MX games like we did as kids. Order up that Pizza Hut, get out some SURGE, and call your friends over. Just have fun and enjoy the game.

Racing with those flat out feels like playing one of those cheap Wii games with how bad they control. Every bike/atv/utv feels like it has no power to it. Bogging going up hills, cant make it up certain areas, cant make jumps, cant start off up a hill etc... and whoever designed the sound of the motors needs fired cause its terrible. Your rider also wrecks over everything and anything. A little short on the jump? Wreck. Overshoot a little? Wreck. Hit a rock? Wreck. Lean back when hitting a ramp like you would to do a back flip? Wreck. And it takes FOREVER to get backup. _childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of feeling disappointed in yourself all the time? I know I was. That's why I bought this game and boy let me tell you, its been amazing being incredibly disappointed in something else for awhile. And for the low price of $39.99, you too can feel disappointed in something else!For the real review..Overall: I understand this isn't a Simulator, not everything is going to be "Realistic". However; this game is pretty terrible considering the amount of advertising and how they are literally sponsoring a portion of the AMA National Motocross series. I would expect a much more polished game. CONS:-Upgrade system is a joke. Parts are for show only, no reason to buy them for performance. I'd wouldn't mind the "Tuning" options if it was a combination of tuning and parts to increase performance. But its just tuning.  -Preload/seat bounce doesnt feel consistent in any manner. Sometimes you'll clear a jump, sometimes you wont despite taking the same line, at the same speed, doing the same maneuver. -A 125 with some "tuning" is faster than a stock 450, yet still can barely clear the 700ft  jumps unless you're a master at their poorly designed controls and physics. -You cant really rev it out in the air to prepare to land and get power to the ground, it feels like each landing you just bog out for 1 second before there's power again. -Audio makes no sense, noises hardly correlate to whats going on. Putting around a 2 stroke and it sounds like im blowing out the top end.-Dumping the clutch for quick speed works randomly, sometimes you get a boost, other times you just bog out.-Crash on the MX course thats nothing but 350ft doubles with 60ft take-offs? Might as well restart the race because you aint ever going to get enough momentum to hit the next world record sized jumps.-I know all of these games are the same, but for the love of god can I just play all the stock bikes and all the stock modes without "earning" them for 5 hours in silly races and tutorials? Maybe I just want a have 450 so I can go mess around, maybe an "Arcade" mode versus nothing but Career. -Last one, bikes look really stupid. This isnt a performance thing, I just hate how they look. I'm on this spaceship looking bike that can barely clear jumps at full throttle. I imagine the OEMs (honda, yamaha etc.) are probably contractually tied up with the ME Supercross / MXGP Games, and they probably have to avoid making something look similar but come on... Pros:-Trail mode on MX is actually really fun, I like mode quite a bit because its like wide open desert/dirt roads, then they mix in what is as close to single track type technical turning/gullleys/canyons as you can probably get in this type of game. -I dont mind the UTV mode, in first person with custom camera it can be fun to feel like youre drifting the corners. Just turn the sound off because your UTV will sound like a dying whale the entire time. -Supercross isnt terrible, its actually more fun than the Motocross modes. Still needs a lot of work though.-The ability to explore the large ranch is pretty fun.-Hydroplaning is fun once you have a good bike. I dont recommend this game as it is now unless they drop it to $3.99 during a steam sale or fix all of the glaring issues that are outlined in these reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: If you look at the playtime on the negative reviews, most of them are a half hour or less, don't believe anything they have to say.The game gets significantly better once you get better bikes with upgrades, unfortunately this is usually just passed the 2 hour return window depending how much time you spent free riding the crappy 125 around the compound.I do recommend this game however I feel like it released in an incomplete state. I would have been happier with my purchase if it was labeled as early access to be honest. Pretty severe lack of polish all round. People's complaints about the physics are more or less cancelled out once you're on a bigger, upgraded bike. Yes, it's still a bit too slidey, but, if you tune your suspension all the way soft and your tires for the most grip, most of that issue goes away. Also learning good throttle and brake management is key. You don't want to slam on the brakes into corners and go full throttle out of them. You're better off feathering or easing on each. I got much faster when I learned this and the game immediately became way more fun.I do think they specifically need to adjust the traction on berms/ruts. I am fine with sliding the back out into a berm, but once that back tire hits the inside of the berm, it should hook up and go, not slide right over the berm. Ruts also give the opposite of the desired effect. For some reason, they slow you right down like you're stuck in the mud when really you should feel the bike get down into them and dig in for traction. So far, you seem to get punished for getting your bike perfectly into the ruts instead of rewarded and this should be changed. Audio is also mostly horrible across the board and it almost sounds like all the sounds were just placeholders and they didn't have time to complete the audio before release. 2 strokes are literally missing a sound file or something for max revs so the bikes go completely silent when at max revs which is really weird. Bike sounds need a rework all around and the whole game needs the audio mastered because the volumes are all over the place.I do have high hopes that the devs will continue to support this game, listen to the community and make the most requested changes. MX vs ATV All Out is SUBSTANTIALLY better than it was on release and that's because the devs listened and implemented requested changes. Still not my favorite, I prefer Legends physics to All Out's, but still far better than release. I feel like the same will go for this game, the devs will improve it over time without a doubt.Overall, the game is VERY fun once you get used to it. High fun factor, high skill ceiling. Momentum and flow are everything. Story mode is cool and a nice change of pace from just doing random events for no real reason.Tracks and environments are exceptional.Sound track would be good if it was properly mastered.Overall, I think a lot of the game's criticisms are warranted but are also highly exaggerated. If you're a fan of motocross and arcade racers, you will find something you like here if you just give it the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Why is physics the end-all for these games? If you want real-tier physics, go play MX Bikes or Sim.MX vs. ATV Legends is rough around the edges (I agree with complaints about audio and customization) but it's still FUN. The tracks and environments are huge, detailed and full of character. The racing is hilarious (watching the AI whiskey throttle off track and go flying/ragdoll into space is too good) and with the right camera setup feels fast. The new custom first person camera is one of the best I've seen in any arcade MX game.I didn't know that the upgrades were in the "Tuning" section of the garage, so if you're struggling with races definitely prioritize upgrading your bike. Before upgrading, I thought I was playing the game wrong (casing every jump, missing corners, etc.) but after upgrading everything on track seems doable now.Seriously, go set up a high FOV first person camera, upgrade your bike, and go explore one of the insane new free roam maps. Rainbow isn't pumping out the same bs every iteration like Milestone, they are actually trying new things and it's worthy of supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall really enjoying this game, but it still has its issues.The game starts off quite frustrating on the 125cc, however once you begin upgrading the bikes and move up to the 250f it becomes really fun. This only takes about an hour of game play. Career mode has been fun so far with a progression system that isn't too difficult. Only done a few online races but these have all been really fun with good battles, and the squad system works well. The recent patch fixed a lot of the issues, and the game plays a lot better now. The gameplay itself feels a bit more difficult than previous games, but once you figure it out it is a lot of fun. Terrain deformation works differently, some tracks are only light and some get very very rough. The ruts from other players are railable without too much trouble which is awesome. Really looking forward to the release of the AMA national tracks. Biggest complaint now would be that the AI are just too slow, most races it is very easy to win by a min+ once you have a fully upgraded bike. Some higher difficulty levels would be a nice addition
