_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the hours I've played, but I definitely wouldn't "recommend" it. The physics and tracks are great and I loved the graphics, but it doesn't really go past that. As far as the potential of an online game goes, I'm spewing. It would be a ton of fun, but it seems like the devs thought about the online aspect of the game for a total of 4 seconds. There's no cross-play (I didn't think not having cross-play was even a thing in 2022 lol) and on top of that it's apparently region locked. I've literally never played a single online game because it's genuinely not possible to get one. It's supposed to have been a live service game but there's not even a point to servicing it. Offline wise, you're not actually racing because the AI is so bad even on the hardest difficulty - I generally win most races by 45 - 60+ seconds. I've been playing first person (which is extremely well done by the way) for more of a challenge, but still win most by 30+ seconds. If you just need a chill MX game to play for an hour or two here and there when you're not playing whatever primary game you would normally play it's a bit of fun, but considering Reflex is like 1/10th the price there's probably not a whole lot of point in choosing this, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Legends is a massive step in the right direction. Do not listen to all of the All Out fanboys, that game was horrible and one of the worst mx games made with extreme arcady gameplay. MX vs ATV Legends is a great game after playing for some time, still not as good as MX vs ATV Reflex or Alive sadly. The bikes are somewhere in between of these two games when comparing the heaviness of the bikes, it is very easy throw a huge whip but thank god it is not at all like All Out. Sadly they kept the sliding and at times it feels like you are riding on ice, please patch this (why is this something most of the new mx games have?). With upgrades it does get much better and it is very much possible to not slide in every corner, you just needs to learn how to do it. MX vs ATV Legends got the absolute best mx tracks of every mx game i have ever played. They are very well thought out and have a good flow to them. Sadly there is a massive lack of customization which i hope will be fixed with some addiotion of gear and bike parts.PROS:+ Great Gameplay+ Good Graphics+ Very good deformation of tracks with ruts+ The best tracks of any mx game in my opinion + Massive amount of tracks to be played, and different modes (Something other mx games nowadays do not have)CONS:- Bike sound, i have been told that this should get better with patches- Bike upgrading does not make sense, tuning makes the bike faster while parts are only cosmetic- When throwing the bike back from a whip it handles bad and does not look good- Sliding is way to much at times- Next to none customization and there is no graphics kits for the bikes?!- OEM bikes should NOT be dlc, do better- AI is too slow- Next to none customizationOverall as i have said, the game is good and worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up doing MX in real life, and enjoying MX games as a child, such as Excitebike 64, Pure, MX vs ATV, etc., This game looked like a promising breath away from the super paywalled games like the Monster Energy game(s) and MXGP. However, it was not. Initially, I was hopeful and excited. Unfortunately, while this game felt like it might be okay at its core elements, there are too many details that make it unbearable and frustrating.1. The audio/music experience is annoying. I felt like I couldn't get the music loud enough without the engine sounds overpowering it during racing, even with the music at 100% and the engine volume at 10%. Then, randomly during racing, the music will get so loud it's unbearable. Furthermore, the inability to choose what songs actually play is a feature I feel like should have been a no-brainer. I can think of MX games from the PS2 era that had that feature and it was great. I don't like some of the music in this game and I have zero control over it. Kinda sucks.2. When I started some events, I forcefully got put on the starting bike, even though I had a tuned-up and selected Kawasaki. Why would I purchase a separate bike and upgrade it just to get stuck with the starting one? I tried to figure out why I kept getting put on the starting bike even when I clearly had the Kawasaki selected when I started the event, but could not seem to find any logical indicators as to why. I thought maybe some events were locked to a certain CC, but I couldn't find the CC listed anywhere, so it didn't seem like that. It's frustrating when you are being passed by AI riders in straights because their top speed is faster than yours and you can't do anything about it, especially when you have another bike that is better but the game won't let you use it. Maybe there is some logical reason behind it, but even if there is, it should be stated somewhere.3. I was feeling experimental and switched the transmission setting from automatic to manual, just to see what it was like and maybe what the game demanded in terms of gear shifting. I couldn't really find any significant difference between the two. The rider still shifted up and down gears automatically in both modes. I didn't seem to have any extra controls (I tried to check the controls/keybindings menu to see if there were any controls listed, and then realized this menu doesn't exist). I didn't see any kind of tutorial or mention of the manual transmission mode either. So, to my knowledge, there was no difference between automatic and manual, other than I could hear the engine revving on the upshifts a little more, but I didn't have to really do anything. Pressing the clutch didn't seem to have any effect other than throttling myself, so there was no point.4. Lastly, the riding mechanics are pretty smooth feeling compared to some older games, but it also feels impossible to really hit anything correctly. I started out with the dual-stick handling and got decent at it, but it's hard to not get sideways hitting jumps and I end up losing all my speed in a lot of turns because I end up over-leaning and it spins the rider around. I couldn't preload, seatbounce, or scrub consistently either. Could I probably get better at them over more playtime? probably, but I feel like it's a mish-mash of too many inconsistent suspension mechanics and it's ridiculously hard to have the speed and power at any given moment to actually jump and land anything properly. Sorta like others have said, the bike is too heavy considering how much speed you can realistically achieve to be able to jump and keep your speed most of the time. I switched to the single-stick handling mode to see if it was any better, and it felt about the same, I was just doing less.I could have probably tolerated the riding experience and just tried to upgrade my bike far enough to out-stat the other riders, but the music and bike issues were the nail in the coffin for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played damn near every MX game, and my honest opinion is that this game feels like it wasn't finished yet. The tracks are fun and the game plays decent enough. However, you could thumbs up this review if you agree. The bikes feel like bouncy balls. there are times when you land perfectly and the game feels good, but more times than not, I feel like I land my bike and it bounces up in the air like a golf ball on the pavement. On top of that, turning is pure chaos, you take the inside berm and can fly over the top of it and there is no penalty, you will still carry enough speed to stay ahead of your opponents. I appreciate the arcade-like gameplay as opposed to the Monster energy game I've been playing recently, but come on. a little realism on the tracks is still wanted in an arcade-style racing game. If you are looking for a good ♥♥♥♥ around game to play with the boys, I think you'll enjoy it enough because of the large tracks with giant jumps to hit. But if you are buying this in hopes of a solid dirtbike racing experience, you won't get that with this game. If simulation style racing is what you are after, I recommend Monster Energy Supercross or MXGP ( but even they arent perfect). Overall, I think the game needs work and I'm not sure if we will ever get updates to correct that. I paid $35 for the game ( 4th of July sale  ) so I will be keeping it, but if you are reading this and the price is $59.99 I would reconsider your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: When the career mode AI racers have no smarts and the multiplayer is a me first marathon (with exploitable quirks), this game is still leading to some disappointment. Although the mx vs atv game selection has been around for a number of years, this latest title feels a tad far from crafted perfection & is appears to be more worried about the style,  the wow factor and the high speed. Of course your tuning is more simple, and the game has a touch of arcade (and seems to be targetted for the younger bikers out there) but when you hope on one of the few vehicle types like a dirtbike, atv, or a UTV it has a way of capturing you and forcing you to do better. Make yourself a better racer & properly utilize it's rider & bike functions. The bikes them self feel a bit better then they were and overall the game has some slight improvements versus previous hours and updates. I can say things are looking up, seasons roll by new content is added here and there & options they change to suit the game better come around. But career AI and online Multiplayer polish are a bit far fetched even still. In the end this game brings me back regardless of what feels like or plays like. It cost me a few measly dollars  but I can still have fun on a Kawasaki even if it is digital.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through a bit more, it's a lot more fun. Once you get past the jank it's an okay game. I would like to see the developers continue to work on this to make it the best MX vs ATV game yet, although it doesn't have a lot of features that I loved from older games.If you're looking to buy this game, wait for a sale and make sure to get track pack and a couple vehicle DLCs if you want the full game... Higher-ups fault not the devs.Bugs that should be fixed:- Reversing/Moving backwards in first person on bikes causes your body to clip through the camera.- Fix/Improve the bike sounds, they are horrendous at times, and the awful clipping bug.Suggestions for improvements:- Vehicle flooding timer bar like in Untamed- Map for the compound like in All Out- The display for the UTV's is very low quality in the Garage menu, I'd recommend moving the camera back or upping the quality of the model displayed if there is a higher quality option.- In the audio settings there should be a track-list of the music played so you can remove songs you don't like and just listen to the ones you like. Untamed had this as an option and it seems pretty simple (from a outside looking in player, I don't know how the music system is set up) and a very nice improvement for people like me.- The helmets do not have straps to keep them on, please model it and add to the helmets <3- Improve the compound, it feels empty and soulless unfortunately. Make some of the roads that lead out loop back in, the amount of times I've just tried to chill and ride around and accidentally rode out of the playable area following these roads is quite annoying. Turn some of the main roads to a more gravely texture to differentiate it from the dirt mix. Add creeks and little bridges over them to add a greater feeling of bliss in nature :)- Make it more clear that tuning is where you upgrade the engine parts etc, I was super confused for a while trying to find where to upgrade. I and many others think of tuning as only like gear ratios and things like brake bias.- Revamp the tutorial to include the garage and alter the checkpoint system to just be apart of the starting tutorial because I found it boring and clunky. Thank you!Suggestions for Additions:- Track Editor. I'd love it to be in the normal game, but it can be a DLC but don't make it more than $5.99 if you guys have any control over it, I don't know the structure of Rainbow Studios.- Split-screen mini-games like Untamed had, those were super fun and don't seem to hard to code in :) Might be something fun for you devs to work on and be creative with!This is a suggestion for the career mode that might be a lot of work, but it could be an improvement.Personally i hated constantly riding to the NPCs that don't even move their mouths when they talk. It's fine to have that sometimes but almost after every race.I'd rather have a GUI in between the races where you are in a trailer and you can select over to a laptop to read and hear audio messages from the NPCs. Then when you are done your series you can talk to the NPCs in the compound. So then we would have less loading screens and less annoying driving to the NPCs then opening back up the GUI, there would still be some. I see what you the developers were going for, but it needs to either be overhauled or fixed into a GUI like I have suggested :)(I will edit when any are fixed or added and put a check mark next to it)I hope with the next game we can get more vehicle types again like some of the older games, Untamed and UnleashedRemember, I only made this review because I love MX vs ATV and I want to see it improve and succeed. Love all you devs!

_childDocuments_.review: First off it has to be said that this game looks and plays like a BETA, however if you play these games for the same reason I do you'll still have fun just casually playing and enjoying what is there. There is a lack of customization and the physics are a little weird sometimes, but it's still enjoyable. As much as I could go on and compare this to the glory that is Unleashed like some other people it's not really a fare comparison. Unleashed is from a different generation where the games were more arcadey and DLC and game updates weren't a thing yet. I feel like this game will get improvements over the next few months and things will be fleshed out. To sum it up if you still play this series for nostalgia from growing up with the originals and just want some casual fun, then you'll have a good time with this and the $40 rather than $60 price tag was a good choice on the devs part since it's not a full on super long triple A title that'll take far too long to beat. At the end of the day we play this series not to be competitive, but to have fun, so why should we take the game so seriously that just a few small graphical or cosmetic things deter us from a game? If you do decide on getting this game then I look forward to tearing up some dirt with you if we ever cross paths, and my the best rider take the gold.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, ignore the reviews with a few hours or less.. they haven’t played long enough to get the hang of the game and give it a fair review…Secondly, I almost gave up in the beginning and refunded the game as I was cracking the sheets early on, trying to get the hang of it..I am so glad that I kept with it!!! This game is awesome, the tracks feel like dirt bike tracks and ride like it too! Plenty of difference tracks so you don’t feel like you are doing the same thing over and over.Keep in mind the first bike with no upgrades is crap.. you will crash, you will flat land, you will under jump… BUT, once you earn some money you can upgrade the bike, get better and have a nice flow.Change the settings!!If you want a better feel for the bike and want to be in control, go to gameplay settings and change:Airborne Throttle: User Input (use the throttle to control the bike in the air/ don’t hold throttle flat all the time in the air)Pro Physics: Enabled (gives you full control of the bike)Once you stop treating the game like a simple accelerator/ brake race car game and treat it like a dirt bike, it will get much easier.I never use first person view in race games, but this is a must for this game, it feels like an actual dirt bike and is completely different than third person view.In first person you can really see where you are going and spot you lines and use the track. (the game really feels like it was developed for first person view)In third person I slide out everywhere and under jump, in first person it flows nicely and feels much better.All the buttons/ controls have a purpose and you need to use them all!!Mainly use Preload (right stick down) to get over jumps and use both Preload and seat bounce over the massive jumps until you get the hang of it.Keep in mind there are two brakes, front and rear.Front helps balance the front of the bike in the air and rear helps bring it down and cutting into corners.Rear brake into hard corners and clutch tap out of corners!Use your clutch, its there for a reason.. Clutch tap out of tight corners, clutch tap up steep hills, clutch tap on a slow landing.Don't forget to lean into corners!Lean back and get that front wheel skipping over the terrain!!Just slowly get the hang of the bikes and then worry about coming first place and making the money to progress.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading the rest of the reviews I've come to the conclusion that all of these people are just trash gamers who want an easy experience.First let me get my only gripe out of the way. The sound, and particularly the mixing with the music, needs a patch. Engine sounds are synthetic but nothing different from beloved titles like Forza Horizon 4. Motoheads are sound ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and there's no getting around it. Luckily given All Out received a sound fixing patch back in the day, I expect the same to occur here.As far as the physics goes, I think this expands excellently on the physics of All Out, and fixes a bunch of issues by slowing things down. The heaviness of the bike feels real, and the sliding allows easy scrubs off jumps.What I gather from the other reviewers is they haven't bothered tuning their bikes at all, because whips can be sped up significantly by tuning your chassis, and sliding can be significantly reduced by tuning tire traction. It's as simple as that!People don't actually play the game before giving a review eh? Coming from a person who's held many top5/top10 times on the All Out leaderboards, I can tell these other reviewers just don't want to take the time to learn how to enjoy the game and be quick. You cannot just huck your sticks left and right and expect to be successful. It takes time to learn how to both control your slide and whip aesthetically. The point of a free whip is that it's not supposed to be easy. I personally wish the hardest difficulty was a little harder as a good tune can easily outpace the best AI. All Out received an AI upgrade midway through it's life cycle and I expect the same to happen for this game.The rest of this games strengths are as follows:- Vast open world scale with excellent detail- Excellent outdoor track design- Simple yet effect progression through story mode missions- Fantastic free whip physics unlike any other moto game I've played- Great sense of speed in every vehicle- Killer soundtrack (Finally a game soundtrack with a little bit of testosterone)- Engaging supercross stages that are scaled very well.- Decent customization with real brands- Actually good voiceovers for story characters- New and fresh gamemodes (Trials engages the same part of my brain that Dirt Rally 2.0 does and I love that)- A preload mechanic that takes skill to master + a not-so-OP clutch boost mechanic- Terrain deformation that won't ruin a track in just 2 laps.- Graphics that hold up to modern day titles (cannot speak for the console editions or your brother's shoddy PC)- Bangin' price (especially on sale)At the end of it all, every mx vs atv gets review bombed because there's a cult that just wants rainbow to remaster mx vs atv reflex. Reflex was a great game and I enjoyed it, for the record. But they're not going to do that. Ever. I'll happily play Reflex modded for the rest of my life.For the rest of you that want a new challenge to conquer, while scaling the massive open world stages, this is the game for you! For the rest who want a casual experience I would recommend Monster Energy Supercross. They make one every year, it's basically a subscription! LOLTake care yall

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: + Graphics are really solid. While not staggeringly photorealistic, the colors pop really well and it's fun to look at. It might be my favorite visual style in the series so far. + Gameplay is fun. It feels like All-Out, mixed with Unleashed. It's very arcade-y, very videogame-y, but fun. + Track design is AMAZING this time. Really feels like the good ol' days of MX games. Lots of crazy jumps. + Lots of tracks and a lot of variety. + The career mode is actually pretty fun, it doesn't feel like such a grind to unlock tracks. + All the game modes, including the new trails mode are fun. + Base game is $35 at launch.CONS: - Customization is sorely lacking, especially with the rider gear. There's only a few brands to choose from, each brand only has 1 or 2 color variants, and you cannot change the appearance any further than that. Easily the most bare-bones customization in the series. - While the physics are fun for the most part, the cornering needs more work; The bike tends to drift to the outside a lot and it can be difficult to pick lines and follow-through. Adjusting the Tuning does help a bit, but I still think it could use a bit more work. - The FPS camera constantly drifts to the right on SX tracks (It's mostly fine elsewhere). I really like the FPS camera (a first for me) and the customizable settings are great, but it feels unusable in SX. - The audio is mixed like a commercial; the music can sometimes be stupid loud even on the lowest setting, while the bike can barely be heard at times.FINAL THOUGHTS:This game is fun, it does not feel like a cashgrab. If it was $60 I'd have a lot more gripes with it, but for what you get, I think it is priced fairly. However, it will not blow you away. It's not Reflex 2, but it is a welcome entry to the series, and I do think this game will have a much longer life than any of the yearly Milestone releases. the base track designs alone made it more fun than All-Out for me. All of the issues I've listed can be patched out or improved upon, and I really hope Rainbow does so. I'm looking forward to seeing how it is improved upon.

Whips for example are not really whipping in the sense that Gyroscopic forces act but rather just tilting and spinning the bike all over the place and not really adhering to reality.Hard to explain this but I can turn the bike in the air and it will just stay where I leave it if I let go of the right stick where as in the real world the gyroscopic forces would cause the bike to slightly want to return to forward/upright facing direction, thus creating the whip sensation. MX vs ATV reflex really captured the sensation well where you could flick the bike off the lip of a jump and the momentum would almost carry the whip through and then only light throttle would help guide the bike back to moving direction. - This was a 2009 game and the gyro forces were translated well. _childDocuments_.review: Sure glad I didn't listen to all of the terrible reviews!  Get past a few issues that will be patched ASAP and a few janky animations and this game is incredibly fun (and rather relaxing in free-roam).  Let's get the bad out of the way immediately: the audio - turn off music right away (it'll get patched), manual shifting - leave it to automatic for now (it'll get patched).  Other than that, turn on pro physics and dual-stick steering and you're good to go.  First-person view seems to be a must (for me at least), playing in 3rd-person made the handling feel completely wonky.  I had some weird flickering ground shadows that I simply needed to update my graphics drivers for and that was fixed.  Some people are saying there isn't a free-roam, there sure is:  Exhibition > Quick Play > Freeride.  Many reviews seem to mention the physics or the handling: you can re-run all the career races for as much cash as you need and then simply begin TUNING your bike.  Add as much grip or slip as you'd like.  The progression in the game comes from the idea that your first ride is pretty weak and you get to improve it (and others) as you earn money by racing in the career mode.Tutorial was a breeze and took maybe 15 min max.  This is an absolutely solid racer that still may need some fine tuning (starting animations with the elbows is hilarious) but for it's current price of $35 it's a steal if you're into the idea of free-roaming and racing some simply amazing tracks.  There are two huge free-roam areas currently in-game, (you can free-roam the race tracks as well).   I'm hoping they expand on the racing tracks but also on the free-roam areas - apparently we are going to get 22 new tracks this year.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of the MX vs ATV series ever since I was 5 years old playing Unleashed on the PS2. Fast forward a few years, Reflex and Alive came out on the PS3 and I played those titles to death, Alive especially. The graphics were fantastic at the time and the physics were perfect. Since then, I have never found another motocross game that could compete with Alive (especially when combined with the Stewart Compound DLC).I bought MX vs ATV All Out last year, played it for an hour and immediately lost interest because the physics were just too different compared to what I was used to with Alive. Not to mention, I just don't play games much on my PC so I find it hard to get into anything as is. Recently, however, I bought a Steam Deck and thought I'd give All Out a try again. I still wasn't a big fan of the physics in All Out but gradually got used to it and really started enjoying what felt like the first solid MX vs ATV title in many years.Legends came on sale a couple weeks ago so I thought I'd scoop it up for 50% off and see how the latest and greatest MX vs ATV was. And I have to admit, I am very impressed. So much to the point that I *almost* like it more than Alive. Yes, the physics are a bit weird, strangely in the opposite direction as All Out. All Out felt way too twitchy and I couldn't hit scrubs and whips anywhere near like what I could in Alive on the PS3. But in time I got used to the twitchy physics for the most part. I then came over to Legends and wow, do the physics ever feel unnecessarily heavy in Legends, especially compared to All Out. It's probably more of a 'realistic' feel but it's still just too heavy, Alive's physics are still a little better for sure. Important to note though, the overall feel and handling of the bikes and physics in Legends noticeably improves after maxing out the tuning on each bike.Now, this game is packed with a ton of great tracks and locations. And the design for the most part of these maps is really excellent in my opinion. The graphics are also stunning for an MX vs ATV title and the game plays reasonably well (40 - 60FPS) at Medium to Epic settings on the Steam Deck which is a nice surprise. Customisation is by far the best we have seen in an MX vs ATV title. Yes, you do have to buy OEM bikes (if you want them) but price-wise it isn't terrible for all the bikes you get with each bundle. And my favourite part of all is definitely the first person view. It's just fantastic. I'm not sure why, but the overall physics of the game feel better in this POV. Legends is the first motocross game I have played where I find myself preferring to use first-person for most of the game play. It's fantastic.One of my gripes with this game is the soundtrack. Of course, no one expected it to be a banger playlist as in Unleashed. But man some of the songs in this soundtrack really suck, like just non-stop screamo metal. And you can't skip them either, like you could at least in All Out. This is a pretty easy fix, you can just disable the soundtrack and play music (like the Unleashed playlist if you're old school) on Spotify in the background or something. But sometimes it's just nice to know the soundtrack in-game is bearable, this one isn't half the time.I like the career progression but I think having to talk to the 'characters' after every single race is a bit annoying. I shouldn't have to go locate the mechanic on the map and listen to him say 2 sentences about how he's sad that "we don't hang out anymore" before I can go to the next Supercross race. I get the intention here but it just seems like a lot of unneeded filler to make it seem like there is more of a story to this game than there is.All in all, I think this game is really quite solid and better than some of the reviews make it out to be. If you're a big fan of motocross and the MX vs ATV series, give this a try. Especially on sale, it's really a no-brainer. You'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Legends (Legends) is an arcade style offroad motorcycle/4-wheel ATV driving game with a large amount of outdoor terrain to tear through, jump over, or crash into. On an Nvidia 3080 the graphics are beautiful and the game maintains a high FPS. The physics are there, but on medium difficulty at least, the physics are very forgiving. Alas, all is not well though. Legends is published by THQ, a premier game publisher, and it appears that Legends was released in an incomplete state.Upon starting, Legends present the player with the option to play the game with or without Steam support and also to play in VR. VR flat out doesn't work, not with Vive or Vive Pro, anyway. Some video output in VR is achievable, however, the controllers don't do anything, and several different SteamVR error messages pop up. Frequently the HMD would show one frozen graphic screen in the left eye and another in the right eye. Another major problem with Legends is the total inability to remap any of the keyboard or controller controls. Playing non-VR as a left-handed player and being forced to use WASD is galling. The game uses WASD for the acceleration and turning and keys like IJKL for leaning/pivoting. Also, QE are used in jumps, and probably some other keys, though there is no guide in the game for all of the various controls. It is incomprehensible to understand why Legends doesn't support control remapping. There are several graphics quality options and the usual sound and music options. For game play settings, there are several options relating to control operations, and even some custom camera positioning.Legends game play starts out by presenting the player with several tutorials. In fact, when the game is started, the player is dropped on a motorcycle with no introduction and is apparently supposed to know to drive somewhere. Getting used to the controls takes some time and expect to crash frequently in the beginning. As this is a sandbox game half the fun is performing insane jumps and stunts, and in this area, Legends delivers. Ride the trails and make jumps or go overland and ride right over a rocky cliff. Legends also has a split screen mode, like as might be found at an arcade. In this mode, it is assumed that one player will have a controller and the other would be using the keyboard. Though it might be possible that two separate controllers would be used. Legends has bike upgrades and there are various 'missions' to undertake. There is a garage and various deadpan NPCs scattered across the map. Legends looks like a lot of fun, but there are a lot of headaches to playing it. Hopefully the developers will add in controller/keyboard controls remapping and fix the VR issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the reviews I have read and watched, I found this game to actually be quite good. The physics feel great, the tracks are the best in the series, the free-ride areas are massive and fun to explore, the first-person camera is PERFECT (I cannot go back to third person after trying it), and the tuning system is much less of a mess than it was in the past. Additionally, the career is quite substantial and enjoyable to play through.The only really, really glaring flaw this game has is its absolutely abysmal AI racers. I am not amazing at MX games, just somewhat decent, but on the hardest difficulty, "G.O.A.T", I finished every race in the career (yes, even the 450 races) on a 125 bike just to handicap myself and still placed 1st on my first try on almost every race (there were only 2-3 exceptions throughout the entire MX career). On your home track, the AI literally all ride up to the same point and just stop moving completely by the second lap, almost every time. They don't even try to get unstuck - they just sit there, parked.Overall, it's a fun game in its current state. I've played every game in the series apart from Supercross/Encore, and I believe this to be the second best (with the first being Reflex by a large margin). I did not play the game before v1.19, so I was not around to experience the shoddy launch physics and crashes, but as of now the game is quite worthwhile (especially on a $20 sale).

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are good but I do not like the game play. There is not many settings that allow you to tweak the game play to your liking. The tutorials at the beginning can be quite annoying, they force you to go through all of them, simple or not. It is also unfortunate that when you first start out, you are stuck with one and only one option for a vehicle, and it is the 125cc dirt bike. I would like to have the chance to at least free roam and try the ATV or UTV and be able to choose a career based on which I prefer. The handling characteristics take some getting used to, but the overall physics seem okay. As others have mentioned, there are WAY TOO MANY ADD ONS and not enough included in the game. It reminds me of an EA game and their micro transactions.The trails in free roam at the farm are not trails, they are generally flat and wide paths. The sounds need a lot of work. If you don't believe me, look up a video and hear for yourself. I did not try the multiplayer so I can not speak on that.The AI also needs a lot of work. Sometimes they will stay ahead of you the entire time, or at least the person in first, no matter the difficulty or how hard you try. Then, towards the end of the last lap, their engine must blow because it's like someone locked up their brakes and you go flying by. It seems as this is an attempt to make it a challenge until the very end but it is very noticeable and immersion breaking, nothing about their behavior is realistic and actually worse than many arcade racing games I have played.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to start. This game feels like it should still be in beta, maybe even alpha. The fact that this came out in the condition it did is really bad. There is no dynamic anything. The physics feel clunky and awkward. Whatever you're riding feels heavy in the air and light on the ground. Like Christ, you drop from the air like a tungsten rod, and then drift across the surface like an empty beer can on ice. The sounds are bugged to all hell. You get to hear that iconic 2 stroke whine maybe like 10% of the time. On top of that, the rider customization is pretty boring. The same can be said about the bike customization. Maybe 1-3 real brands are offered. Other than that you are offered the great value edition parts that are branded as THQ, Rainbow, and Phoenix. And then there is the gold edition part in each category if you are feeling particularly Gucci. The manual transmission option doesn't work from what I can tell. I've tried every button and nothing changes what gear i am in. There is no way to change or even look at your controls. And how the hell are you going to allow people to buy the vehicle packs, and then not let them use those vehicles in the career mode. I haven't gotten to a point yet that allowed me to change to something else. If I'm wrong than whatever. i bought other bikes to race with other bikes. Not whatever this cluster truck of a game starts me on. I'm keeping this game around in hopes that it turns into something we all expected. Oh and one of the UTV's floats around rather than having actual contact with the ground. super solid guys.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS--Really Awesome tracks-the bike and rider customization is pretty nice, love that you can pick the color of tire tread, would like a bit more to the customization like creating my own livery on helmets suits bikes etc -cool little story in career mode, its nice to have some character interaction in games to add a little bit of depth -i love how it feels using both joysticks to get more air off of jumps, i play mxgp 2021 and i love it but its nice to have an arcade style dirt bike game with insane air time and tricks-graphics are nice in racesCONS-The ai sucks, they cant navigate the tracks properly, they basically dont exist for most of the races because they're so slow you smoke them and i even play on the hardest difficulty and even if i crash and get reset they still are nowhere in sight-game doesnt support 3440x1440p so the menu looks like an n64 game, that includes the garage and customization screens, bikes are all stretched out and it feels like N64. The game itself in the compound a races the screen fits well and looks good but the menus are an eyesore-like i said its nice to have an arcade style dirtbike game cause i play mxgp and its super realistic feeling so its nice to have a game i can do a 500 yard jump and land, but at the same time its still a bit lacking and i feel like the riders are a bit too stiff and some animations like ai riders revving at the starting gates looks jenky-Having to pay extra money to have official bikes in the game seems a bit lazy and like a rip off to me. like are we really going to start breaking games down this much? its like if madden starts releasing with generic teams and you have to pay $3 per team if you want the real ones, its terrible. Ill gladly pay for dlc if it makes sense and its something you came up with after you release a full game , but these games are now being pulled apart and released as bits and its something ill no longer support. Final thoughts it is a fun game, but the extra charge for brand name bikes is ridiculous and i have zero respect to THQ for that, like come on man people are out here struggling from inflation and you're just digging as deep in our pockets as you can for content that should be included, but on top of that your ai is terrible, how has this not been an urgent fix before release, your ai cant keep up on the hardest difficulty did nobody test the game out? or did they? and you just said aweeee **** it who cares...also no 3440x1440p, its 2022 you put other 21:9 sizes in why not add them all? its laziness...Ive been told they plan on doing more updates, if they fix all these things ill forgive them for charging me extra for honda suzuki yamaha etc and give it a recommend, but in its current state its a no from me

_childDocuments_.review: Decent arcade MX game that we'd all expect from this series. Amazing tracks. It does have some day one flaws but I can look past them for 35 schmeckles. The flaws are the audio. Fades in and out, blares music, bikes sound weak like a lawn mower. The game punishes you for trying to bark corners, without throttle control you blow ruts and slide the rear out and drift. The bike mods seem to do little to nothing to the actual power, traction or handling of the bike. If you get the IRL bike packs they're way bigger than the stock bikes so your rider will glitch through the seat and look like a child riding their dads 450. This series really shines with the modding community of bikes, skins and tracks though. If they can work out the traction some and in air physics to free the bike up some this game will be solid. Right now I'd give it 2/5 stars. It's still better than a milestone game like MXGP or MESX and I'm comfident the modding community will give this game real replayability with friends and solos alike.

_childDocuments_.review: 270hr Review Here!TL;DR: The improvements from the initial release date have been exceptional and consistent from the developers. The team has really listened to the community about making changes to the gameplay while at the same time, adding more content. The tracks have good flow and it's easy to pick up for newbies. Now go ride, Gary.Gameplay physics: 8.5  / 10I tend to like more realism but for an arcade racer, this hits the spot. More improvements are being made here with every patch based on community feedback.Tracks: 9.5 / 10The tracks are incredible and fit well with the bike and rider abilities. Best tracks ever created for the MX vs ATV series imo.The DLC AMA tracks are 10/10Customisation: 5 / 10While they've added a lot from initial release there's still more that need to be added. Dev's in the discord mention that they're looking at a custom graphics mechanic for the bikes and they're constantly sorting deals with companies to bring in more varieties and colour options for bike and rider. Sounds: 5 / 10Still not great at all... ultimately still being worked on with a supposed revamp coming for season 2 later this year.Overall features and options in the menu's: 5.5 / 10There's still a number of standard racing game options they're missing like custom championships, server browsers, career progression, rider stats and levels (think prestige systems) that is missing but a number of these have been considered or are being worked on for later release.
_childDocuments_.name: MX vs ATV Legends

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for MX vs ATV Reflex, this isn't for you. If you're looking for good old fashioned MX vs ATV arcade racing, this is the game for you. The bikes feel kind of heavy like Alive did, but other than that, the ground physics feel very similar to All Out. The tracks are very well designed, and the free roam environments are very well made. Don't listen to all of these negative reviews with .5 hours played. They're playing on a bone stock 125cc bike, no tuning, no upgrades. Of course the bike is going to handle poorly. Play the game, unlock bigger engine bikes, and enjoy the game. MX vs ATV Legends is a very good arcade racer, and feels like a new experience, and if you go into the game with the mindset of expecting something new, you will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unpolished, but something good hides underneath.Pros:- The dual stick mechanic feels great. Sliding into corners, boosting out of the corner with clutch, and use preload + seat bumping to launch off a triple feels really great.- Ground physics generally feels good.- Nationals and Supercross tracks are well designed and are a blast to ride.- Tuning system is OKAY. Wish you could tune during a time trial mode / free mode and not just in the garage. Tuning is not well explained in game (what is handling?)- Game runs well and looks really nice.Cons:- 250 2-stroke sound is headache-inducing bad. I have to turn the engine sounds all the way down. The 4 strokes are tolerable but not great.- A.I. unfortunately sucks. I easily beat the hardest A.I. only after a few hours of gameplay. Not having a challenging A.I. is going to seriously dampen the longevity of this game for everyone, unless the online community thrives.- Trails (the checkpoint) tracks are mind-numbingly boring, especially the desert themed ones. Twice I have caught myself thinking about work problems while slogging through these (again on hardest difficulty, winning by 50+ seconds. I promise I suck at this game, the A.I. is just that bad.)- Tracks and bikes are locked behind completing the career mode. I wouldn't mind that if I could just focus on Supercross and Nationals only. The trails tracks are just a huge buzz-kill and are unfun, and there are way too many of them in succession.- Air physics need some work, but are tolerable at the moment. Scrubbing and whips feels pretty clunky. I do like that you can bring the nose down a bit in air, that is a fun mechanic.- Can't rebind keys :(- Some bugs that I'm sure will be addressed soon, like manual transmission not working (stays in automatic no matter what setting I choose).- A seemingly pointless Parts and Sponsorship system. I have zero incentive to interact with these systems at all. Why not make them interesting by tying them into the gameplay loop somehow?Fans of MX games will probably be able to overlook the problems and will enjoy the National and Supercross tracks. For everyone else, wait for a sale or for the problems to be addressed by the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review:  Steam Curator: MX vs. ATV Legends is the seventh installment in a storied racing franchise that pits off-road bikes against four-wheelers and side-by-sides. Let’s start with the good!  THE GOODWhen it comes to driving mechanics, Legends nails the basics, delivering intuitive and responsive steering, clutch, throttle, and stance controls that render realistic results much more often than not. The result is a consistently thrilling racing experience that’s easy to learn and hard to master. But don’t worry, you’ll have plenty of ways to figure things out, as Legends features a nice blend of game modes, including 16-player multiplayer, local split screen, free ride, and a beefy story-driven career option complete with tournaments and sponsorship challenges. These modes take place on well over one hundred different racetracks ranging from claustrophobic super cross competitions to massive, desert wind farms out west and frigid mountain peaks in the east. Speaking of snow, note that the weather effects in Legends are static—not dynamic, as I’ve seen it so-often advertised. You'll never drive through a sudden rainstorm, for instance, as the environments here are all prerendered. And gorgeous, admittedly! Really, despite each race’s high stakes, it’s easy to get lost in the scenery, as Legends boasts excellent lighting and above-average environmental textures... from a distance. THE BADLook closer and you’ll realize that there’s more style than substance to much of the visuals in Legends. For example, the dirt trail your bike kicks up is mostly cosmetic—there’s inconsistent, largely surface-level terrain deformation that doesn’t seem to have improved much since Reflex 10+ years ago. Rider animations, meanwhile, look stiff (at least, until the hilariously bad rag doll physics kick in) and it took me hours to realize that the disturbing double-jointed elbow-popping at the start of each race was actually the revving of engines. As for music, the selection of songs here is fine, if a little all over the place, but it is HORRIBLY mastered—music cuts in and out, has random volume spikes, and drowns out vehicle sound FX on the lowest level. I couldn’t turn it down enough, so I turned it off. Not that the sound design is much better. Vehicles sound okay, but the same choppy audio problems persist, here, and some of the stock sound effects are downright bad. Sadly, these quirks aren’t unique to the style of Legends, as the longer you play, the more you’ll realize that, despite having the foundation necessary to become an excellent, addictive racer, Legends currently lacks depth and polish across the board.  For example, the game’s economy is just busted. I was able to afford Tier-3 parts for all three vehicle types, thereby maxing out their stats, within a couple of hours—a task that would take weeks in other racers. And, because each unlockable vehicle has the same starting stats, I feel no incentive to save up for them. This all cheapens the overall experience, and mind you, Legends is not a cheap experience! Launching at $40, I can’t help but feel like this game is underbaked and underdelivers on features that fans of the genre have come to expect. THE REST Speaking of expectations, I expected exactly nothing from Legends’ story and received just that. The plot is super generic, you know, win the races and save the farm kinda stuff, and is punctuated by surprisingly low-res cutscenes. There are a handful of thinly-written, one-dimensional characters scattered about who inject some decently-voice-acted enthusiasm into the story, but I would never recommend this game on story alone. I don’t have much to say about the game’s simple U.I., so let’s wrap up with a few words on playability. The load times in Legends are decent, the game boasts excellent camera controls, and besides those animation anomalies I mentioned earlier, I didn’t encounter any noteworthy bugs.  THE ENDSo! In the end, MX vs. ATV Legends delivers on what matters most: racing. For that reason, I can recommend it to fans of the genre. But, for everyone else, I would definitely wait for a significant sale. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read, I have only played about 4 hours. Now that has been stated, let me get into the review. First and foremost, I believe this game is just fun. I play MX vs ATV games for the arcadey fun, for sim racing I will play MX Bikes. In my opinion this game has a great balance between fun and challenge. The physics do take time to get used to, but once you do they feel fairly nice, although slippery. I find that it is very important to tune your bike before judging the game, as without it the bike is fairly slippery, and not great to your preferences. Personally, I believe one of the best parts of the game is the track design. Each track is developed very well and is extremely fun. The nationals are my personal favorite, but in this game they somehow made me enjoy supercross and even the trails mode was super fun. Now that is out of the way let me get into some of the flaws; The first major one being how unironed this game is. The music goes from super quiet to super loud randomly, which is a big problem if you like game soundtracks like I do. Another flaw is how slippery it could be. It isn't too bad but it takes some getting used to. The customization is not very good in my opinion, due to there not being many options or even graphics kits. Personally I do not care about this but it is preference. I feel the biggest flaw is that at the time of this review you cannot create private multiplayer race lobbies with your friend, or choose what track it is. All of these flaws can be fixed, and I am sure they will be fixed, as All Out had a pretty sloppy start too. Now I will say some features I hope that they do release: Tag. Tag was a super fun game mode for me and my friends. The 350 MX Models; These were always my favorite bikes in all out. This is just my personal review so i hope i helped people out. TLDR: At the time of this review I give the game 7.5/10. I have a crap load of fun playing it but it needs to be ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dual stick really should be the default, You will have a much better time playing. In most cases leaning cases sliding, and you only need a little bit.Some context before my review starts, I have played every single MX vs ATV game and almost every dirt bike-related game. You could say it's one of my favorite game niches. I played a lot of all-out but never really liked it. I prefer this game more even with all the cons.For the most part I love the gameplay even with some clunkiness. I will get into more detail but to sum it up, this MX vs ATV takes a bit more skill and practice to really enjoy. I am used to it from simulator games but people who are used to All Out will need some hours to adjust. The days of holding down the throttle all race is over, you have to think more and use brakes + throttle management. Also turning and leaning feels amazing with dual stick steering; a must-have setting for this game.-Best soundtrack out of any MX vs ATV-Quads and MX feel really good at its core-Rewarding and fun Gameplay (see cons about this below)-2 stroke bikes! yay-Tracks are very good (much better than all-out)-Whoops feel very good and challenging-The best freeride from any MX vs ATV (excluding naulstagia lol)-Graphics are good but unoptimized-Straight rhythm is basic but at least its there-Trails mode is great and a big improvement over the waypoint races in other titles-125 sound is great-UTVs have their own tracks-The UI looks good-A basic story but happy to see a story holy cow a lot of cons-Bikes crash for no reason I can't even go through the enduro course without a random crash-Quads glitch over some berms similar to Mx but worse-Random camera glitch or something looks like a stutter but it's not-UTVs are F***ing terrible, I've driven them irl and I don't remember the tires being made of ice, they should have incredibly good traction and power like real life.-AI is god awful, constantly flying off the track like goons-Lackluster customization (it's not that hard to add more colors to models guys c'mon)-Terrible economy (I purchased max upgrade and gear within 1 hour of playing)-Terrible settings. You cant even turn motion blur off. There are no control settings either. Also, the graphics settings are terrible; I have a 3070 and only get 70 frames.-Still, occasionally get that All-out bounce when casing jumps-No Freestyle Events wtf-Charging $ for the worst cosmetic pack DLC I have ever seen (you can't even change the color in-game)-No Map? You made massive maps but I can't see where tf I am (maybe there is a button but I can't find it)-Music sometimes gets super loud along with bike sounds-All Vehicles have the same stats-Reused bad engine sounds from All Out besides 125-UTVs are quiet-Some achievements are broken (it thinks I did a backflip and stunt on a UTV LOL)-No way to save camera settings to presets-Cringy story but who cares-Cutscenes are low res and low frames-Terrain deformation is more realistic on some tracks and worse on others-Mouse comes up sometimes in fullscreen-Cant change name/number font or color-Custom map support-Track creator-Pit bikes, trophy trucks, and buggies-Enduro Races with logs, rocks, and hill climbs-Customization-Reflex 2 lol-New bike sounds (more than just 125)-Intelligent AI

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Rainbow Studios and THC Nordic Team,I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to take a moment to share my thoughts on the current direction of the game, which I believe is promising. I particularly enjoy the new sounds from "Alive," though I feel they could benefit from some minor adjustments, as they currently come across as a bit choppy. Additionally, the physics have shown significant improvement, which is great to see.It would be exciting to incorporate some content from "Alive," as it was one of my favorite games. I also appreciated its preload system, which I found to be very effective. Perhaps an additional setting could enhance the experience even further. I'm eager to introduce my friends to the game; do you think crossplay might be a possibility? This feature would certainly help increase server activity, as I've noticed that the maximum player count on a supercross track has been only three.Furthermore, I wanted to propose the idea of porting "Untamed" and "Alive" to PC. These two titles are among my all-time favorites, and I believe there would be strong demand for them. Many players, including myself, would gladly invest in these games if they were made available.Lastly, regarding the leveling system in "Alive," I found it to be quite manageable. My brother and I completed it within 24 hours, and I believe it provided a satisfying experience.Thank you for your ongoing updates to "Legends." I look forward to seeing what the future holds!

_childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Unleashed is one of my favorite games ever and I have been hoping that magic would come back someday, but it doesn't seem like that will happen here.  The physics strangeness that all others have mentioned in their reviews is a real thing, the most unpleasant aspect I found was that it seems impossible to get back into a rhythm if a single jump lands short. Aside from that, there isn't much to hook the player into with the Career mode from the start:  You race, you go back to free roam and visit a static "team member" who is about 100ft away, then go back to a race.  It's neat that there's a free roam, but I couldn't find a way to open a map to save my life and nothing was in the controller bindings.  If you're going to have a free roam in a racing game, give that free roam a purpose and introduce it to the player immediately!  Give the team members a purpose, give me something to work towards in free roam, or just a map so I can see what's out there.  Without anything to entice me to go wander around, I'm simply going to just go to the next race, and since there's nothing to entice me to keep searching for answers in the game, I'm simply going to just go on to the next game in my library and hope that someday that fun Unleashed was able to provide for hours and hours comes back.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the first game in the MX vs ATV series that I have played, and I have thoroughly enjoyed it. Once I learned how to properly do jumps and tricks, the game makes you feel like a badass. I even went and bought MX vs ATV Reflex based on a lot of people's recommendations. I will say though, that first couple of hours of gameplay felt pretty rough. But, I think its just because my bike wasn't yet upgraded and I was still learning how to play. There are also a few things that the game doesn't tell you. 1st. You can change colors of some items in your garage and in your locker. It will have a paint brush next to the item if you can edit its colors. 2nd. Some "collectibles" can only be accessed way later in the game. 3rd. Most of the game's events can actually be switched. For example instead of doing West coast super cross events, you can switch it to East by pressing Y on your controller. And that's pretty much all from the top of my head.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can look past the glitches, Legends is a good arcade racer. The grind isn't bad, the weather effects are incredible, there's a lot of assist and customization options in the settings, and there's no rubberbanding. What kneecaps this game is the outdated physics/animations & AI. There's little traction and bikes have a tendency to stick to each other like magnets. Bots are skilled in supercross and certain tracks, but are morons in almost every other race style or vanilla stock track. ATVs are as crappy as always in this series, races devolving into bumper car matches. In UTV races, you can even lap the competition they suck so bad. MX vs. ATV Reflex still has better deformation and general ragdolls and physics. In Legends' defense, this isn't an eyesore, possesses slightly better AI, and has way better maps and a far better control system than Reflex's godawful Kb&M set-up and crash QTEs. There's a good amount of content, but the DLC monetization model is EA-levels of slimy. Brand-name bikes are behind a paywall, and they've resold the same tracks and bikes a few times.Edit: The game is constantly being updated, so expect changes every couple months and occasionally to break. Online is dead. So you probably shouldn't buy it if that's all you want.

_childDocuments_.review: Very long review, but I feel like my review might offer a slightly different viewpoint from some of the others.-- Background --I very much enjoyed ATV Offroad Fury 3+4 (had 2, didn't really click with me as much) on ps2 when I was a kid and they were a couple of my favourite games ever. I spent so much of my free time playing these games inside out and it's a gaming experience I don't think I'd be able to replace with anything else. That said, MX vs ATV legends certainly doesn't replace them.Now, I haven't really played these kind of games since then. I got ATV OF4 on my steam deck last summer and had been enjoying it thoroughly, nostalgia and all it still held up great. But a few weeks ago I got looking around at what had really happened since then with these kind of games, and I was led here. I saw plenty of terrible reviews of this game's launch but a few had said it improved greatly, so I watched a few videos and decided (while the game was on sale for a large discount) to pick it up with the track DLC and all the bike/atv etc DLC.-- General thoughts and setup --After beating the MX career in around 31 hours (and most of the achievements along the way) I have some mixed opinions on my experience, but overall, I enjoyed the game! I am basing my experience off of the ATV OF games from ps2 era as well, so I don't really have the same attachment to games like reflex that other people mention often.The first thing I did was change the control scheme to single stick because I was struggling with the double stick (default), separating bike steering from rider leaning just because it's not what I'm used to. After that, the game became a lot more familiar feeling. Other reviews mentioned the AI is way too easy so I also set it to G.O.A.T (hardest difficulty). -- Career --The MX career starts you off on 125 bikes and feels very awkward, the bikes are underpowered for most tracks even after getting all level 3 upgrades and you'll have a hard time flowing over jumps smoothly. Getting to 250 almost completely alleviates this problem, but you'll still have to ride well to make some of the bigger jumps. 450 made me realize that the tracks were designed around it, everything just started flowing naturally and felt right. Overall, the career was fine except for the pointless forced "return to compound" where you have to ride up to an npc in the lobby map and listen to 1 line of dialog (usually amounting to 'great job kid!', or having to take a sponsorship for a few thousand credits). The interrupts were tedious and added nothing at all to the experience, they would have been better to not be there at all. Sorry to the voice actors.-- AI --As far as AI goes, they are complete garbage at the highest difficulty. I haven't played a single other atv/mx type game since like 2007 and I crushed them easily, except for a few maps in the 125 category where it feels genuinely impossible given your weak bike. It feels like the AI cheats in those events and gets far better air time. Except that once you hit 250 and beyond you will have massive 30-60 second leads by the end of the race even with semi sloppy riding (crashing here and there). Compare this to ATV OF4 on expert, you have to drive near flawlessly and dirty to keep the AI from catching you -- it felt like a genuine challenge and was far more enjoyable.Additionally, in some tracks the AI is completely broken. Rawlings invitational comes to mind when you unlock the upper sections with birch logs everywhere. The AI will just stop dead and do nothing at that part. Some supercross tracks are also dangerous, the AI will fly everywhere or not turn for corners, tossing blocks everywhere and missing the track. This isn't incredibly common but you do notice it when you return to certain tracks.-- Vehicles --For vehicles, the base game offers almost no bikes to you (you get a 125, 250 and 450 from Rainbow, THQ and "Gold Edition", these are the only manufacturers). All the vehicles in a class are indentical in stats before tuning and exist purely cosmetically. The DLC bikes are the same, but they are all unlocked immediately when you own the DLC. I would have preferred to buy them with ingame credits during career because the career currency became meaningless from the start when I realized every bike I would ever want to use (branded ones) were already free for me to use and they all ride indentically. Compare this to ATV OF4, different bikes/atvs in a class would have different stat spreads that would favour different kind of tracks, meaning you could still get use out of multiple bikes.-- Customization --For bike customization (both parts/visual customization) there is very little here as well. Compared to ATV OF3+4 where you would buy parts for your vehicles to raise/lower their stats, and tires for different terrain, MXvATV L simply splits bike stats into "tuning" and "parts", where parts are entirely cosmetic (offering around 6-7 parts for each category, half of which are generic THQ/Rainbow etc). Tuning is a 3 level system to the left and right, but in my experience I found that upgrading everything 3 levels to the right made the bike the best in basically every scenario. Compared to ATV OF4, where tuning allowed to adjust max speed at the cost of acceleration, suspension hardness at the cost of stability, etc, where you could configure your bike differently for supercross vs high speed flatter nationals etc. In MXvATV L, you pick what bike you want and buy all the lvl3 upgrades and it's the same with every other bike, and you crush the competition in any race. It is possible to colour parts of your bikes and some clothes on your rider (depending on what ones you buy) but it is very limited here. Don't expect anything like ATV OF where every colour can be customized to anything. Often times the only thing that changes on the bike is an accent colour, and the rider can generally change any colours, but there are very few cosmetics that allow this. Most are color locked. This isn't really a massive drag but I enjoyed customizing all the colours of my bike and rider to match in ATV OF, it's not really possible in this game and will look messy.-- Tracks --I can say I generally enjoyed the tracks the game offers. The DLC tracks are great but aren't included in the campaign -- there is a mechanic where some events along the way can be swapped between two series and you only have to complete one to progress, it would have been nice when owning the DLC to see a DLC series alongside these if you wanted to swap them in, but for now you can only play the tracks in exhibition mode, or online.The terrain deformation can be a bit jarring to race over in some tracks, it's like the ruts are made out of cement and you bounce around everywhere once they're set in place. I'm not sure if this is the usual for the other games that had it too, but ATV OF had none and it was something I had to get used to, but otherwise wasn't too detrimental.Some of the pathing on tracks is broken (random full respawns riding close to obstacles without crashing), sometimes you get told you're "off track" right in the middle of the track, but this wasn't game breaking, just a minor annoyance.-- Other --The physics feel fine to me, some recent reviews hate them but I don't understand the issue. Unlike ATV OF you preload jumps by pulling down on the stick and releasing, instead of pulling down and pushing up. After getting used to this I honestly preferred it because it was easier on the thumbs.Performing tricks is pointless, because during events you get 0 points or rewards for doing them and it doesn't even say the name of the trick on screen or any indication of a combo. Your rider just kinda... does the pose. I can only trigger 4 air stunts (R1+stick+L/R/U/D), I don't know how to do more or if there are more. There are ground stunts too, but sometimes tricks just don't work at all or instantly crash your rider.

_childDocuments_.review: Legends is THE most BUGGY game I have ever purchased. If you join a match online, you will likely not be able to hear your bike (bug), and your camera will also likely be positioned within the playermodels head (bug) where all you can see is the inside of the playermodels head. Lets not mention that the bikes sound like garbage and the engine sound often cuts out randomly after each shift. I have been taken out in practically every inconceivably dumb way on behalf of random glitches and bugs in the game. At one point, my rider hit a barrier block and it launched me straight up out of the arena entirely. Briefly getting tapped in mid air or around a corner by a reckless rider may often take you out which is incredibly annoying. I've talked with many avid players of this game who mention how they constantly get taken out or pushed around by other riders, while those same riders are essentially impenetrable to being hit or pushed. In other words, hit registering in this game is messed up bad. The physics are also quite wonky and are practically unrealistic. Most people land directly in the banks of corners after a giant triple sideways while sliding which just looks completely unrealistic. Sadly, no one even plays this game. I've played for about a month and have only seen the same 20 people play every day with a few new riders who barely last a single round before leaving. I can't really blame new players as they just don't know the countless unintuitive little secret tricks that avid players use to win. Competing in online matches is unfair as there aren't any real regulations on how people should play. For example, everyone has a different camera angles, graphic setting, bike size, bike tune, and bike DLC. Its truly bizarre to me as a player coming from competitive games like CSGO to see a game allow for third person and first person players to play together in the same matches. I have a feeling that they allow it because there aren't even enough players to separate them into individual servers. Aside from all the bugs and terrible online experience, the game on max settings is visually beautiful and somewhat visually realistic.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting in almost 40 hours and finishing just the Motocross career with doing maybe half of the ATV and UTV careers, I think I'm ready to give my verdict on this game. This game has a great foundation that you can have plenty of fun in and it has hours of gameplay. It's the things that it tries to do on top of that foundation that don't really take away from the experience but don't really add much depth to them either. The actual *racing* is fun. The physics are just right and give you a great risk vs reward. Balancing your speed on a knife's edge of going as fast as you can without going too fast that you can't take a corner or wipe out on a particular rhythm section. This was enough for me. The game is fun. If you want to know more about the different aspects of the game, read on.This game has been something I sit down and play when I have some spare time just to listen to music and throw down some laps. It's the actual riding where the game shines. Rainbow Studios knows how to make the game feel good to play between the physics and track design.There's plenty of content here with a number of different tracks and races during the main career. Going from small engine bikes to the bigger/faster bikes was a nice progression and the track design is fantastic. How you race a track can change based on how much power you have on your bike. There are certain jumps you can't make on a 125CC bike that you can on a 450CC bike, as an example. So your speed and how you ride the track change. As mentioned above, the actual physics are great once I got used to them.  The "game feel" is great, now I'll touch on the stuff that isn't quite as good.The AI feels a little bit like set dressing because even on the hardest difficulty, I found them rather easy. Once you get ahead of the pack, you can typically run away with the lead. Because racing itself was fun, this didn't bother me too much. I often just made it a game to see how much of a lead I could have by the end of the race but it is something to note. There are a few bugs still in the game that can be frustrating when they come up. There were a very small number of times AI racers teleported way ahead of me in a track such that it was impossible to catch up and I'd end up getting 3rd or 2nd instead of the 1st place I was clearly running away with. As I mentioned though, that was rare. There were also a few instances where I didn't see myself collide with the top of a jump or a hill or something as I was going over them by my rider would crash regardless. Again, this was fairly rare. The game has a system in place that lets you upgrade your bike, but I was able to purchase the "best" parts fairly early and just kept it the entire time, so I didn't really get anything out of this system. The cosmetics are fine. Nothing too special, there's a decent bit of customization but this game doesn't let you play dress up with all of your favorite gear brands, if you were looking for that. This didn't bother me, as the customization present was more than enough for me. The story here is nothing to write home about, but I wasn't expecting hard hitting story here either. What's there is just to tie races together and give you a visual representation of how you are progressing through the career. Again, it's fine. I actually like that the farm you are on gets upgraded as you go along to add more jumps and tracks and trails.So where does that leave me?In summary: I'm not sure the current mixed rating is justified. This game has a solid foundation and racing itself is fun. They've ironed out most of the bugs (minus a couple here and there). The feeling of speed this game has and the "flow state" that you can enter as you rip around the track is addictive. I prefer this physics system over the slower feeling games of the MXGP/Monster Energy Supercross series. The track design is fun and adds some strategic depth to the game as you try to pick your lines. It's the extra features that they have added onto this one that don't really add much but don't take away from the game much either. I think Rainbow Studios should be proud of this game. They remain one of the best studios in this genre and still provide a fun motorsports game. I'd love to see them iterate on this game, as I think they could take this foundation and build something truly great on top of it.

I suck at Mx sim but it is one of the greatest games of all time and Mx bikes is just pure joy.At launch Mx vs ATV Legends was one of the worst motocross game I have ever played. The bike would slide and bounce all over the place. The bikes felt under powered and the sound made me wish I was deaf. I didnt plan on giving it a 2nd chance because I didnt think it could be saved. I was surprised to hear that Rainbow had a update after just a couple days. Aafter hearing about the changes and how much it improved I had to give it a 2nd chance and I am sure glad I did.Once I upgraded the bikes and played around with the setup I found the bikes to more than enough power. I recommend using first person view as it feels like you are going faster than the 3rd person view. The sliding was greatly reduced and the remaining sliding lends itself to the games physics and skill gap. The bouncyness was greatly reduced. After getting comfortable with the game the bouncing happens very rarely but could still be worked on. The whips are a lot harder to do in this game and that is something that the majority of the community had been asking for in their previous title. I liked the old whips better but they are still fun and a welcome challenge.The bad...-3rd person makes the game feel like you are going slow. Maybe allow the fov to go a little higher?-The sound on the 250 2 stroke is unacceptable.-Online lobbies end too fast after first place finishes, half the lobby gets a dnf and we end up in loading screens more than racing.All in all this is a good game and with a little bit of work it will be a one of the best in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/5 right now, but I do recommend it- let me tell you why. First, the good- physics, especially after the update, are smooth and satisfying. Playing on PC with XBOX Elite controller. Bike weight feels great, especially in the air. Handling manners on the ground feel great, making it easy to thread narrow trails at high speed. The absolute shining gem of the game though is the level design. The outdoor trail and invitational races you'll get to in career mode are hands down the most authentic-feeling dirtbike riding I've ever done in a video game. Exploring the massive amounts of trail in the more open-world levels is great too. First person camera is all I've used. Camera is adjustable, and easy to fine tune. Wide FOV makes the first person mode completely usable, especially in SX. To me (riding dirtbikes since I could walk) this game plays really well, and is extremely entertaining. The bad? Bikes are not very good until they're modded. No pre-race screen to change bikes/settings once you load into the track. Bike sounds are terrible. Sound of the bike is not connected to the throttle at most times. Music replays the same few mostly bad songs in repetition.  Small glitches, etc. The point is, I think the small stuff can be patched and made better, but the core of the game is great. Maybe should've been baked a little bit longer, but hey I'm here for the ugly stuff.
