_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful and philosophical tale about providence and broadening your horizons. This game makes me feel in a way that we are very much limited by our own perspectives, and that all we need to see is that there are so many unexplored possibilities all around us that we haven't even considered. I'm just a few mini chapters into the game, and I plan on continuing, but what I've come to realize from my short play-through is the important meaning of remaining open to possibilities. There will be, for example, a room you're in and unless you've explored it with the paint balls, you have no idea that that room has a chandelier, a stairway, and a balloon in it. If you remain narrow-minded, and focused on getting from point A to point B in a short amount of time, you'll miss the forest for the ink-splattered trees.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game / walking simulator definetely has a few things going for it. The artstyle is great, and the themes and some of the gameplay ideas are pretty interesting. The pacing is way off for me though, it's way too long despite being so short. I didn't enjoy my time with it all that much and I really wanted to like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful little game with a simple, but very unique and interesting game mechanic: Painting the environment as you go -- in different ways.The first five minutes were kind of uninteresting, until I stopped and looked back at the trail of paint I had left behind which created a very beautiful outline of the level. This made me smile, and gave me a feeling of joy that I rarely get from games.The game does not try to overstay its welcome, and I would say the playtime of about 1.5-3 hours is a good length, since I don't think the idea could have been stretched much further. It is not difficult (although there was a puzzle or two that became a little bit frustrating to complete), and if you like short, relaxing games that are different from the rest, this is definitely one to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game, unexpected, creative with great ideas and fantastically implemented. This is more like a bedtime story I would play with my child (estimated 5-9) virtually before bedtime, nothing exciting. walking around and spreading color ... *lol .... calm music, earworm material, everything is fantastically done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful and simple game! As someone who normally enjoys horror games n such, this was a nice break! Its really simple and easy to understand, and the story is wonderful! The graphics are amazing, and the game play is too! This can be a really nice gift for someone to receive. I got it as a gift, and would say my boyfriend did a fantastic job of picking this out for me <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful and very creative experience - I can't get enough, and after playing Edith Finch first, I finally got to know Milton's story! Really enjoyed that the 2 games relate! And even though it's been almost 10 years since its release, I believe the narrative and gameplay choices are still very innovative, even for today's standards.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Way too short and incredibly unsatisfying in the gameplay department. I get that this must be aimed largely at children and is told in the form of a bedtime story but I have to imagine actual children would be far more engaged with mechanics that actually challenged them and made them work for something. As it is, it's such a barebones and unfulfilling experience and I'm not sure I can recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: game so good i nominated it for 'sit back and relax' awardSPOILERS KINDA ima talk about the ending but not directly spoiling whats gonna happen.there is one problem with the game in my opinion, its the ending, the game was so great that they couldn't cope up with the ending, what im trying to say is the game should've stayed unfinished, i see it as a better ending, that game is one of the best, but also it was so great the ending wasn't satisfying, just imagine making a story so great you can't end it right, im just repeating the same thing back and forward, but i see the ending being unfinished is better than the original ending, because it leaves the player imagining what could've happened, having an open ending and fans doing theories is better in my opinion. so it should've ended with an open ending than a normal ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I watched the credits.  The credits screen is as long as a AAA tile such as Assassin's Creed.  You'd think with all of those people involved in making this short game that it wouldn't freeze or crash at all.  If this was an indie game by a small team of 10 people but still had the occasional freeze/crash bug?  Okay, I could accept that.  This game, however, appears to have had hundreds of people involved in its production and the game froze shortly after starting the second chapter.  For a ~3 hour game by such a large team of people, it should be thoroughly polished until it shines like a sexy bald head that's been recently oiled.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from What Remains of Edith Finch that was amazing experience this one became quickly dissappointment.Not my cup of tea at all. Instead emotional story it is motion sickness simulator with random shooting black bubbles in monochromatic world and simple fairytale on background.I am not into such kind of art  - maybe if it would better capture the painting in full color instead just  tedious random shooting I would enjoy it better. The aggresivity of bright light against my eyes did not helped either. Would advise look carefully on what this game has to offer and how it looks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Proof that you don't (always) need to have the newest GFX engines at extreme resolutions to create a game that is amusing & entertaining. No point in playing a game that requires you to Crossfire/SLI two $1k+ cards, if there's no real enjoyment in any aspect.Get over yourself, and let your inner child out to be fully immersed with the story. Entertainment and satisfaction is the point, after all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The unfinished swan is a game that tries to fill the same niche as something like journey, flower or abzu. But where those games shine with wonderful experiences, heartfelt stories or memorable sequences, the unfinished swan falls flat with a core premise that sounds interesting on paper, but in practice is more tedious than fun. Giving the world color as the only mechanic starts to feel bleak faster than you'd think. And even though each level tries to spice things up a bit, the gameplay isn't engaging enough to not just have it be a walking sim. The thing though with walking sims is that they have brilliant stories to tell, experiences that stick with you for a lifetime. The unfinished swan's plot is predictable and nonsensical and the payoff isn't worth sitting through the rather short runtime. The visuals are nice in the later levels but there's a lack of memorable setpieces that leave you in awe. Things like journey's slide level or finding the shark in abzu, there's none of that here. So in the end, the unfinished swan is a rather pale experience that whilst not overstaying its welcome, doesn't offer enough to make it worthwile at full price. The game regularly goes on a very steep sale though, and for that price and time investment its alright but nothing special.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed playing this and will enjoy the second playthrough. The bit of reality warping the game goes through is really fun, especially since its just kind of silly. My only gripe is missing so many of the story pages and missing most of the intro trying to adjust my stream volume. If you're considering this game, definitely take the time to explore the first part of the game a bit. It's beautiful and deserves that exploration anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Really pretty art styleCool premiseCollectables !! I love hunting for collectablesCons:Motion sickness, somehow, don't know how they managed that onePure white graphics put me into actual shock, pitch black graphics had me squinting like I'm 70 years oldWithout spoiling the story too much, I found the ending unsatisfying and (ironically) unfinished. Character that is objectively a not good person is let entirely off the hook for no reason and the main character is just kinda,, given a thumbs up and a dangling thread of an ending to their story. Maybe that's the point, but I personally found it to be lame. Tl;Dr: I kept missing a single balloon on the last level and it would crash every other time I played it a quarter of the way in. On the third crash I looked at my reflection in the black boot up screen and went "well, at least I'm almost done with the game" and then realised that maybe instead of continuing to push on I should just go to bed, so I booted up a guide, was done in a minute, uninstalled the game, and had a pretty mid night of sleep.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I generally enjoy exploration games which are somewhat arty, but this game just didn't do it for me.The story is childish and dull, those reviewers who describe this game as 'captivating literature' need to get a grip, I'm afraid.The (single) gameplay mechanic is strange and sometimes unintuitive. The per-level mechanics (vines, lights, block-building) are a little random and don't build on each other.It starts very intriguingly (the first 10 minutes are cool), but after that the game feels like a collection of arty demos which have been stuck together.The one thing I would say is that this game is oddly pretty. The vines in particular are very nice to look at and play with.This might be something for you if you enjoy arty childlike adventures where the gameplay mechanics don't matter to you... but for me it's a no.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This might have been a decent game, but I only played 20 minutes of it before getting a refund. From looking at walk throughs, you can see that the landscape grows to be more interesting and unique, but at the beginning you are just given black paint and the entire landscape is white. I grew sick of this very quickly because the only gameplay is throwing paint and attempting to navigate. Perhaps it changes, but I get terrible motion sickness, so 20 minutes of throwing paint was enough to make me want to vomit. I think I'd rather return the game and allow others to play it for themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I had a terrible motion sickness playing this game on PC  (only happened to me with like 3 games till now)I played this on PS4 some years ago but didn't experienced that bad feeling at allNow I am not sure if screens' size or more FPS or the distance from the screen can improve or worsen that feeling of motion sickness but sadly I can not go on and replay the game on my fav platformOtherwise the game is pretty and enjoyable
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: very short art game but of course a playstation classic nonetheless.only thing they changed in this pc port are the menus. no cutscene or image texture remasters.if you've always wanted to play it but have never had a ps3/psvita/ps4 or really want to experience this game again (and don't mind the $15 cost) then this is probably the way to go.luckily this game could easily be done in less than two hours so you can refund it right after if you're left unsatisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Art is gorgeous.Creative story-telling.Beautiful music.Cons:Played through in less than 2 hours while taking my time so a very short game. Play mechanics are a bit wonky.I broke a part of the game in the first chapter. Balloons are super difficult to find and collect.Chapter 2 is such a drag I almost fell asleep during it.Overall a 4/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a few Annapurna games, and they are gorgeous and thoughtful. I have really enjoyed my experiences with them, but they are also short. They tell interesting stories, but then it's over.The Unfinished Swan is another like this. I do enjoy it, and I do recommend it, but not at full price. I completed the game in 2-3 hours. Spent some additional time trying to get all the balloons, but it became too tedious to go for 100% completion, and there's no other real reason to keep playing. Keep that in mind for yourself when deciding to buy or not. With that out of the way, the game looks great and is a very neat, novel puzzle experience, and I did have fun with my time in it.I think the first chapter was the most challenging with regard to the puzzles, and the later chapters overall didn't add a lot of new mechanics (some,. but the experience was actually easier). With the exception of the final chapter, there's no urgent drive to solve quickly, so you can just enjoy the experience. After starting the game that way, the final areas, which introduced a "timer" mechanic, were a little jarring.There are a few little easter eggs to find, and some of the balloons are really tricky, even with the end game toy, but still not worth more than 1-2 playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It is just super boring to be honest. The gameplay is pedestrian -- it is more of a walking simulator than the puzzle game I was expecting from the information on the steam page. The game basically consists of you spamming the "throw paintball-thing" button hundreds or even thousands of times. It is just really repetitive. There is a story accompanying the constant walking & throwing, but I don't much care for it. Seems exceedingly generic about a sad boy who learns to see the world in color -- the game is a visual metaphor for this as the world starts out black & white and gradually increases to a more colorful canvass. TLDR -- I would avoid this one. If you want a puzzle game, there are a myriad of other puzzle games out there with more in depth mechanics or fun factor. If you want a walking simulator, just play What Remains of Edith Finch by the same studio ironically. The Unfinished Swan is just a perverse amalgamation of the two genres that just doesn't work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's not apparent from the Steam release; but this game was made for the console market back in 2012 when artistic games were rarer and held to a low standard accordingly. One of Annapurna's weaker games.The visuals are not compelling (bordering on ugly); the puzzle mechanics are limited in range (and trivial); the story is uninteresting (and  short). I expect to forget this game within days of finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing, confusing, inspiring. Got chills at the end. Tbh I got kinda bored at around 65% of the game which made me abandon it for a year. Feels good to finish it tho.7/10, nothing would've changed in me if I hadn't played it, but still I'm just happy that I was able to finish a game that I was looking for since 2012 when I was a kid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This was a wonderful little narrative puzzle game, perhaps not quite on the level with "What Remains of Edith Finch" but still enjoyable in its own right. If you have money to toss wherever you wish and a few hours to kill, this isn't a bad title to do it with. However, I personally recommend wearing blue light glasses or whatever you have because as pretty-stylized as this game is, it did make my eyes hurt. Like, the entire time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This unfinished swan will have to be an unfinished game for me. Got to chapter 2 and couldn't take it anymore. Extreme motion sickness, dizziness and nausea. Far too bright, 1st person and you don't know where you're going. Had to go lay down for a few hours to recuperate and almost threw up. Can't finish this at all or even watch a video to see how it ends. It's awful. Uninstalled and won't get to finish it but it's OK. Never again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games of all time! I played it back when I had a PS3 for five minutes, and loved it then. Just last week I was looking to see if it had been released for PC yet, and here it is!I love this game, and even though it's not a difficult game the challenges are just set right with the whole allegorical nature of the thing. Wonderful art style. Really a joy to look at and splatter!It's a short game. I 100% everything in 6.5 hours. Still worth every penny for an unforgettable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME IF YOU ARE LEFT-HANDED.  DO. NOT. BUY. THIS. GAME. IF. YOU. ARE. LEFT. HANDED.  Not only does this game inexplicably have no ability to remap keys, which is already unforgivable, but .  I have literally never seen a game that deadass ignores AHK inputs before today.  Like, I am almost impressed.  Someone needed to  to refuse to let us play it with keyboard settings that work for us.  Some right-handed person hates us  that they rooted around in the code somewhere with the express aim of making the game worse.I found a thread about this issue , but of course it was too late for me because I naively assumed that a game that came out in the twenty-first century would have keyboard remapping.  I am so disappointed.  Annapurna should be better than this.  Be better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Gave me nasty motion sickness, as did the developers' other game Edith Finch. I think it's due to low default (and non-adjustable) field of view. I'm able to play 99% of first person games, including FPSs, flight simulators, etc, with zero issues.I plead to indie developers - It's 2024, for the love of god give us adjustable FOV settings!!! I think there are more folks with this issue than developers realize. It's a drag feeling like you're about to puke after 30 minutes of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I feel...nothing. While the main gimmick is neat, the game itself just fills me with absolute apathy. I don't hate it, but I also don't want to keep playing it. I'm just disappointed by the overall feeling of pointless tedium. It's like I'm back at a student art show featuring work by the friend of my girlfriend, trying my hardest to "get" what they've put on display. I can see that there is something there, I can see they worked hard on it, but there is no emotional resonance for me whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A properly artistic game with an immersive world and beautiful soundtrack. That being said it was also disappointing to see so many opportunities wasted. I felt like so much more could have been done with the color mechanics and the levels. The game felt a little short, almost as if it ended right when it was getting on a roll. Some of the achievements are fairly frustrating as well, such as having to go through a level completely blind. All that it requires is a lot of time investment to "map out" a path during a proper playthrough and them mimic it going in blind. It's nothing but a time waster. Regardless, I this is a pleasant litle game and its potential ties to "What remains of Edith Finch" makes it a good storytelling experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game. The splash mechanic is a cool idea but some of the levels are very hard to look at giving me a headache and the puzzles themselves are just sort of ok at best and don't make up for the issues of the experience as a whole. I would have refunded half way through if I didn't have to refund Edith Finch as well
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game lacks depth in the stories and the tasks can be a little boring and repetitive. The only thrilling part was when the monument falls. Besides that i love the Edith finch references (wish there were more) and the soundtracks.The entire time I wanted to know what happened to Milton. Monroe was a good addition to the game but we didn't uncover how did Milton disappear.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Was gifted this game after having it on my wishlist for a couple months, and within the first 20 minutes of playing it bugged out twice on me. Some parts of the map are unfinished, and standing in those spots or misinterpreting directions drops you into the floor & plays a godawful noise; much like an old school TV on a no-signal channel. The story line and general premise of the game seem very interesting, but unfortunately putting my ears through the unnecessary torture isn't worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Cute concept, but I was so incredibly bored. Made it about half way through and then got tired of having to search my way with a "paint gun" through a relatively simple 3-D environment. It's a walking sim in the end, but you can shoot balls of water or paint to help yourself find your way in an entirely white world (for the most part).
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan is a pleasant game that takes a decent weekend to beat. It is made by the company that made What Remains of Edith Finch. The game is very unique using a paint brush in order to paint your level. It makes each person’s playthrough unique. Each person will paint the level in as much detail as they want. Each level was unique, playing off a certain gimmick. The first had a completely white canvas that you filled in, the second was more defined with more platforming and the 3rd level had a more dark color palette. The music and graphics were both pleasant. The story was simple, but told a good story about leaving a legacy. Overall the game was fun and pleasant, but nothing about it completely blew me away 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny this game plays with visual themes of light and dark because it sits squarely in the shadow of What Remains of Edith Finch. That's a tough game to follow up and It's difficult to not form expectations for this game if you've played Edith Finch. This is a perfectly good experience in isolation. I didn't mind it. It certainly felt like the right length and it kept the gameplay mostly fresh throughout. my one major criticism is forcing the player to look at things. Not good. Bad game dev! Bad!!! I really hate that!!! it makes my eyes feel weird and I don't like it!!! I will see your game!!! All I'm doing is seeing your game!!! If the gameplay is looking around and shooting paint, don't take over 50% of it because you really want me to see what this chapter is called!!!!! it's only annoying!!!! I'll see it!!!!! I promise!!!!I completed this game in one sitting and I actually did feel like I had my time wasted so I'm not going to recommend it. It felt like it didn't really have anything meaningful to say and I certainly don't remember anything past the king's terrible English accent and the first level with the paint throwing. I'm glad I got it on sale or I'd refund it but honestly it felt more like a waste of time than a waste of money. I'm not gonna refund because I do want to support this dev but this is not a good game imo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: So everyone seems to have failed to mention something rather important about this "game".It is a children's book. Not it is inspired by a children's book. Not it has childlike whimsy. It is an Ages-3-and-Down children's book, but first-person.And while that does mean I'm about 30 years too late to fit into the target audience, I doubt I would have liked it even as a kid. It is two hours of "fun" stretched out to four via slow pacing, glitches, and softlocks that force you to replay entire levels (of which there are four, with no checkpoints unless you unlock them).And yeah, I've only played a half hour, but the entire game is only about four hours. It also allows you to skip to any chapter if you find enough hidden balloons so I can assure you that the end of the game is no better than the beginning.Just buy a funducation game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Terribly bad game design that would make you so much motion sickness.There is a white screen, the only way you can see the world is throwing a black water ball that splatter the world, but if you too much throw the ball you could hardly see the world  because the screen was just changed black from white, so you need to control how much ball you need to throw. You have no idea how long your ball is going, like sometimes your ball hit a wall immediately after you throwing or it goes down into a hole after a second, those unexpected result made me so much uncomfortable and feel sick.I quit after 5 minutes playing because of motion sickness so maybe in the later game the situation will be changed, but I gave up with no regret. As I've requested the refund already, you could understand if your brain would be ok with the game then request the refund if not. The dev should've focus on making a story telling walking simulator instead of this, and I would rather play What Remains of Edith Finch again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't prefer the young/reading to a child-feeling storytelling style, and the puzzles were not what I was looking for in a puzzle game. The moral of the story is extremely heavy handed, which makes me wonder if I played a young kids' game accidentally and am unfairly reviewing.This is a reasonably pretty storybook walking simulator that I was able to finish, and if that's what you want it'll probably go well. From Annapurna I found Journey, gorogoa, gone home to be more compelling, and sayonara wild hearts and outer wilds knocked it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Pure rubbish.  After a short intro, the screen is pure white, except for a small circle.  Using the trigger causes a splotch of black paint to appear.  That's it.  No tutorial, no help, you can make some paint splotches, and that's it.  What a complete waste of time.I asked for a refund, but was refused, since I bought this along with Edith Finch, and apparently even though I had only played this one for a few minutes, the fact that I had played the other one for longer meant that I couldn't get a refund for this one.Absolute garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed opinions, but for the sake of posting I'm giving a thumbs down. Note: This review is preliminary as I have yet to finish the story.I don't consider myself motion sick, but games with liminal space triggers something in me that makes me want to throw up. Unfortunately The Unfinished Swan is one. The very first chapter is by far the worst, splatting colors in a monotonous pure white environment while your head is on a swan's neck by pivoting everywhere is NOT helping. As for the story and exploration, I didn't expect this game to pass the impossibly high bar that is What Remains of Edith Finch, but even with a lowered expectation the story it failed. Cutscenes are few and far in between, revealing barely any story before forcing you on another trek in a monotonous world. However, exploration and level design is very unique and something I have not seen elsewhere, which I like. When I play more of this game I will update this review as I see fit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Not for me.At first I thought the object was to fill all the white with black and then when I had accomplished that, something dramatic would happen. I obviously missed the whole point...Then thought I might do a bit each day and slowly create a picture but alas, no save.Maybe best left to those amongst us who have artistic aspirations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: An artsy game with very little art or game present.  Gameplay primarily involves walking slowly and spamming mouse clicks to throw paint around to either 1) see where you're even going or 2) force puzzle solutions to do what you want.  There's intentionally very little artstyle present in the game because most of the game is designed around being eye-searing white, and that combined with the lack of FoV settings gave me actual nausea.  Not worth $15, especially for a game that's under 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan became the unfinished game. After 15 minutes of the mind-numbing activity of hurling a paintball I just couldn't stomach any more. I literally got nauseous from motion sickness playing this game. Beyond that it was incredibly boring. Slowly throw 10 paintballs take two steps and and throw another 10 paintballs ad nauseam. I did read it gets better after the first chapter but when I found out there was a labyrinth coming up I completely lost all interest. Maybe people with more patience and an iron stomach can handle it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: You are Monroe Finch, its probably not spoiling it but you play as a young boy, exploring a kingdom created by a young prince, with a paintball gun. Simple yet innovative puzzles abound in this game which tells a story of love, laziness, fear and loss. It kept reminding me of this 70's children's toon  .You walk about in a scene where you have to throw black balls of paint in order to uncover the obstacles and trigger machines, and as the balls change colour and effect, also trigger machines and plants that move. It's a bit parkour at times, but actually not hard at all.Eventually the world goes black, and the black balls of paint, really have no effect. You (or rather the young Monroe) must fight for your life to escape many terrors as you traverse an immense maze of a city. Oh, and did I mention, all the while you are following an incompletely-drawn swan who helps you, just a little. Sometimes there are imperceptible wind chimes that guide me, almost as in a dream, but this is no dream for Monroe.Immensely satisfying game, puzzle learning curve development is perfect, difficulty and scale are too. If you enjoyed Before Your Eyes, you will love this title. To find similar titles check out one of my lists here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game as it's not something you see all the time.  It's different because it's a paint perspective. It's a hidden world for you to explore and all you have to do it throw a little color to gain perspective. It's a bit glitchy here and there, but nothing a restart won't fix. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this expecting the same quality of quirky and immersive story telling that I got from What Remains of Edith Finch. What I got instead was a clicking simulator. The gameplay is not married well to the story. The unique mechanics are either used once in passing and then forgotten, or stretched to its utmost to the point of exhaustion.Buy this game if you enjoy watching plants grow, because that is what I spent half of the game time doing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals and audio are great. Gameplay is unironically walking simulator. If the walking speed was doubled or you were given a run button it would maybe be a very slight recommendation. But the walking speed is so damn slow I literally didn't even want to explore. I would see a collectible just across the room in plain sight and literally think "nope too far away, not worth it"Also, the story isn't particularly compelling and the "puzzles" are trivial.Felt like I had enough after about 15 minutes, only played another 30 minutes to see if it would change in any significant way, and it didn't. Full playthrough based on other reviews seems to only be about 2-3 hours so I think I seen more than enough to know I'm not missing anything, and neither are you. Watch the trailer, see the cool visuals, and then go buy a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a toddler's conception of an artsy walking simulator and a genuine disappointment considering the genius of What Remains of Edith Finch.  Edith finch was a mature, nuanced tale about legends, loss, and tragedy disguised as legend, and this game is a two hour children's book with buggy ladders, boring puzzles, and gruelingly slow movement speed.  Buy pathologic instead.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this as a big fan of What Remains of Edith Finch (from the same developers). The Unfinished Swan is a beautiful and well-crafted experience. Everything works well and you can really tell a lot of thought went into every detail. THAT SAID, it is a bit too "artsy-fartsy" for my taste: the story is (deliberately) simple and it didn't really grip me. This could be excused if the gameplay was extremely interesting, which it isn't. It does feel somewhat satisfying to use paint to reveal your path, but that's about it. The game tries to throw some variety to this main mechanic, but most of it ends up feeling dull after a while - or even downright annoying (I'm looking at you, vine sections).I can see this game appealing to more sensitive souls than my own, but if you're looking for something as engaging and fresh as What Remains of Edith Finch, you won't find it here. I recommend other walking simulators such as SOMA and Tacoma.

_childDocuments_.review: rings at the tune of a simple tale for children, but one that can deliver a message.Splash color to reveal the path… or so you think.You have the simple ability to throw a paintball to interact with your environments but the game stays fresh by switching up the experience without changing the main mechanic you have.You’ll see yourself using splashes of paint to solve puzzles, those range from using them to reveal a path, to push stuff, to attract climbable vines, and so on.The premise of tis fairytale-esque thing is: Monroe’s mom has a quirk of never finishing her paintings, and one day the subject of her most famous piece, the titular Unfinished Swan, goes missing so Monroe in search of it enters a kingdom of wonder and whimsy to reveal the secret behind this bizarre disappearance.Gameplay is often halted to deliver story instead of having a flow between the two, and the story is often just text on a wall…In the beginning and end cutscenes there’s a very weird stutters that ruins them as it feels someone is just shaking a blurry picture in front of your face.Short, cute, has a good message, and it’s a classic, price-to-length/content ratio could use some work but as it stands I gladly recommend it, especially on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this sitting in my Steam library for a while, waiting for the whim to strike me to play it, and I'm glad it finally did.The Unfinished Swan is a lovely game. The art is striking, and does quite a lot with a very limited palette -- especially important given how much of the game is about revealing the landscape with your ink. The narration is beautiful, too, and really sets the mood of the game.Occasionally the climbing mechanics felt a bit wonky, but honestly that was such a small part of the game that even in the climbing-heavy sections, it didn't really affect my enjoyment, and it certainly wasn't game breaking.The one thing I will say is that it seems to suffer a bit from small game pacing. The opening is quite lush and the first two chapters feel detailed. But the third chapter starts to feel a bit rushed; there's some really interesting mechanics introduced but the game doesn't sit with them at all, or do much with them. The final chapter is almost a walking simulator with some minor interaction so you still feel like you're playing the game. Now, I get why this is, but it frustrates me so much when indie games do this. I would have preferred that the game either not introduce new mechanics after the second chapter, or be just a bit longer and have some attention to the new dynamics. One of my pet peeves with small indie games is when the openings are quite detailed, but the more mechanically complex later stages feel thin and underdone. Nevertheless, this game is charming and I'd recommend it to anyone who wants a few hours of engaging environments and very lovely art.

_childDocuments_.review: Completionist info at the bottom. Mild spoilers in this review. Rating 8/10The Unfinished Swan is a charming game which tells a very cute story. If that kind of thing appeals to you, you will have a good time with this game. However, if you are looking for really anything else, this game is likely not going to be your thing.The Unfinished Swan is a self-described “interactive children’s book” and this is about as perfect of a description as you could ask for. The player plays as Monroe, a young child whose mother has recently passed away. Monroe is given one of his late mother’s unfinished paintings, his favorite, the unfinished swan. One day, Monroe wakes up and finds the swan has escaped its painting and, upon chasing it, the player finds himself in a mysterious painted world through which Monroe/the player chases the swan who always remains one step ahead.The design of the game is really its strongest selling point, even, in my opinion, above the narrative. It is, as was already implied, reminiscent of a children’s storybook, but with the added delight of three dimensions, which is a unique and pleasant experience. The different vistas of the game are very striking as the game transitions from painted forest to enormous castle to dark forest. Each area is unique and memorable, albeit quite short. Mechanically, the core gameplay is standard and, arguably, boring. Actual movement in The Unfinished Swan doesn’t extend much past simply pressing WASD and the occasional left-click. But to criticize the game for this would be narrow-minded. This game is, fundamentally, an interactive story, and little effort went in to any sort of dynamic movement system. Instead, The Unfinished Swan does have a few tricks, gimmicks if you will, that it introduces from level to level. These include growing vines, moving light sources, and buildable blocks, all of which play a part in different levels to various degrees. These additions keep the game from getting too stale while adding a little bit of a challenge to the player, elevating the game from being a walking-simulator to an actual puzzle game.Finally, the story of the game is well-done. While The Unfinished Swan has more gameplay than many similar games, and therefore doesn’t have to rely on its story quite as much as other games in its genre, much of the final impact of the game comes down to how well the story is executed. The story, and its conclusion, determine the taste which is left in the player mouth once the game is finished and forgotten. And I think the flavor that remains after this game is sweet. I said before that The Unfished Swan is a very cute game, but perhaps charming is a better word. Its story is a very human one, surprisingly deep for the limited time the story has and, by the end, the player who is playing this game for its atmosphere will be left satisfied by it.And really, that is all there is to say about the game. It is a charming experience which has excellent visuals, some interesting mechanics/puzzles, and a satisfying story. It is a short game and shouldn’t take much more than a lazy afternoon to complete. But be warned, the story and world might stay in your mind a good while longer than that.Completionist Information: (Difficulty – 4/10)(Fun – 6/10)(Time: 2-3 hours)The Unfinished Swan is a quick game and has a level select which allows collection of all of the game’s collectibles, which are balloons, easily and quickly. Doing this, however, will essentially require two playthroughs of the game as the player is likely to miss balloons in every level unless you are being very careful, which I don’t really recommend. When playing through just for collectables, you can go very quickly if you know what you are doing and the chapter select is quite robust/extensive.The hardest achievement is one in which you must basically play the first level of the game completely blind for the most part. This is more tedious than challenging, but if you follow a video guide closely, it isn’t too bad, just annoying.Overall, not an overly fun game to complete (it’s not really made for challenge anyways), but also not that bad either. Fine all around.

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Short little narrative experience with a minimalist but compelling artstyle. Despite the fact it's all about throwing balls of paint everywhere, it mixes things up, but isn't particularly challenging. Allegorical story that you might (or might not) like, depending how much you relate to it.Bought it on sale and I'm happy with it. I don't think it quite holds up for a full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely adorable!It has a very unique style, and a very special visual design. The voice acting is great too. I am not sure what to say about the gameplay. It is not exactly boring, but neither is it exciting. It is a very simple puzzle-solver, where the puzzle-solving is not meant to, nor does it, distract from the main focus that is the art design (and the special way of interacting with it). But I am very happy that it is not longer than it is, as it would have gotten boring quite quickly. The game is good though at presenting new tweaks to the gameplay rather frequently. The story is very heartwarming, especially if you end up playing the extra levels as well. An unexpected profoundly deep game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: when i first started I thought it was a worse version of what remains of edith finch, but by the end, I think i loved this game even more. I had such an amazing time going through the game and unraveling the story.  The presentation as well as the puzzles are insanely unique.ps I got the minimalist achievement before I played any bit of the game and it was actually really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A patchwork of okay mechanics over an okay story. A bit overpriced for a game I was glad was over.It seems like half the game design went into replayability, which makes no sense for a short story game. Collecting all the hidden balloons allows you to purchase special upgrades? Why would I keep playing after collecting all the balloons anyway? (Why even keep playing after I beat the story regardless of balloons?)This game really doesn't have much exploration at all. The levels are pretty narrow paths. And for most of the game, you don't have paint; you have rapidly disappearing water. Who would want to go through these levels a third time just to get them briefly damp while using the special upgrades locked behind getting all the balloons? I was hoping for better from Annapurna.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels unfinished. I don't mind games being on the shoter side, but this game is full of ideas that lack growth and development. It's only four levels long, and its mechanics peak at the second level in terms of creativity. If you find it on sale, it's a well-made experience with some cute storytelling, but don't go into this expecting a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to rate this using the 5-star system, I'd have to give it a solid 4. A unique idea and a cute world, there is definitely a lot to love about the Unfinished Swan. But to anyone who is hoping to find a game reminiscent of What Remains of Edith Finch, you might be a bit disappointed. Don't get me wrong, the mechanics here are unique and creative, but they can get pretty annoying from time to time - I experienced a few glitches. But if you're just looking for a feel-good story, this is a great one to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: An artistic game with different game mechanics and gameplay. The music is relaxing and beautiful. The game overall is very good and I liked it. Of course, there are some negative aspects as well. Looking at the screen for a long time can hurt the eyes because the game is predominantly white. If you want to do Achievements, take a deep breath and remember to be patient because you will have to play the game over and over and your eyes will be screaming for help. In addition, this game is a reference of the game "What Remains of Edith Finch". It also has a much broader story and setting that is great and artistic. The fact that these two games have a common point made me extremely happy and I liked it very much. If your eyes won't bother you, I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's a walking simulator with just a bit more- the canvas mechanic is neat and the game is short enough with enough permutations on the mechanic that it doesn't overstay its welcome. I didn't really get drawn into the story that much, and there's not really much special in the graphics/ost department (except the awesome space-bending labyrinth made possible with some scenery duplicating sleight of hand). If I had to place it in the walking simulator pantheon it would be below Journey but above The Vanishing of Ethan Carter. And way above Dear Esther.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm home from work sick with the (non-spicy) flu and wanted a game that felt dreamy, low stakes, and something.. methodical, maybe? Like an Unpacking feel - I wanted to slowly unfold the world around me. It met the prescription. The story feels a bit hollow but coming in entirely blind (just picked it because it was on sale) I was very charmed by it over all with the highlights being first when dropped in and not knowing which way was up, then being hunted' tone shift, and making your own pillars to jump on as the game came to a close. Wish the latter especially had continued on less linearly - too simple but kind of soothing, like the Unpacking feel I was aiming for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished SwanPositives:+ Nice artistic look+ Good idea+ Some nice levels+ Good sound and music+ Nice voiceover and voiceacting+ The puzzle partsNegatives:- So-so story- Some parts are challenging to navigate thru (you see almost nothing)- They could have done so much more with the idea- Some parts are repetitive and not so much funTo be honest this game was a tad disappointing.Maybe my expectations were too high, but I felt like this game was a missed opportunity.Dont get me wrong, the game was good, but it could have been great.I still recommend it though, because it had its moments.Total Score: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I know, this is one of those games where the main focus is the narrative and it's mostly a cake walk with little to no challenge. There is some credit where credit is due, however; not only is the story kind of cute as you basically take the perspective of a little kid going through some storybook to uncover the lore about the world he was brought into while throwing ink/water around to uncover the paths as he goes through the story of the world. I could be wrong about the plot; I haven't touched the game in a little bit.The art style is actually pretty neat and it varies based on what chapter you're in, and there are some unique elements that you don't usually see in other games, but unfortunately there isn't much to say about this game, if you're into story-driven games with a little bit of uniqueness in them, I say give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Really good for the imagination. The creativity and potential at your own will keeps me engaged. The story is cute and meaningful too. Game can be finished in a single sitting but there's always a little more to see or something you may have missed. The collectables add to replayability.Recommend for a cozy experience
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: So, I initially heard of this game as a prequel for What Remains of Edith Finch and expected a kind of addition to its story but in the end I got something completely different... but also extremely interesting. To begin with, the game's graphics, music and aesthetics are just majestic - I think you could have already guessed it by the screenshots. All those things create a sort of fairly tale experience and it is pretty close to what the game's plot wants to be. Speaking about it, I wouldn't say it is something outstanding or unique but despite it's initial simplicity in the end it gives you something to ponder on. The gameplay is far from complex but it doesn't need to be: the game gives you simple puzzles that do not really make you think but rather guide you through the wonderful world of The Unfinished Swan. The game also adds new mechanics and gameplay changes in each new chapter which prevents the walkthrough from becoming boring. You can finish the whole game in 2-3 hours (maybe in 4-5 if you go for all achievements) - it is not much but just enough for this kind of a game.In conclusion, if you liked What Remains of Edith Finch and want to try another more abstract game from the same developer or just like unusual art-house projects I recommend buying it. However, if you are looking for something with a deep gameplay and complicated puzzles you better skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm genuinely shocked at how this game was able to take a perfectly white area and with only a few splats of paint by the player provide enough information to navigate and explore an area. The sound effects were perfect as well and were essentially required to pull it off. The story was great, the way the game eventually elaborated on the character's abilities was also a lot of fun, and the combination of the two was nearly flawless!The only concern is that this game is not particularly accessable by nature. I find that especially sad because I think this deserves having as many people as possible playing.The Unfinished Swan is yet another fantastic example of how games are an artistic medium that deserves respect and admiration!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it. _childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: An artsy game with the tone of an innocent bedtime story. _childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: In a bizarre, sanitzed combination of Paint It Black by the Rolling Stones and Mad World for the Wii, Giant Sparrow deliveres The Unfinished Swan, the first entry in the Edith Finch Extended Universe.All jokes aside, Giant Sparrows first game may not be as great as Edith Finch, but it's artstyle and children-book told story are very lovely regardless. The Studio really shines at Storytelling and Enviroments and there are not too many indie titles that do so in my opinion.Unfortunately i wouldn't call these guys masters when it comes to gameplay. Very basic puzzle elements can be found in this title along with some collectibles that unlock tools that feel more like Development leftovers. The gameplay isn't bad, it is more than serviceable, but i think ditching elements that are found here later for What Remains of Edith Finch was  the right idea.Still, if you like WROEF and ever wonder what happened to Milton in that game i can happily recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast! (Literally, as a main aspect is to launch balls of paint that splatter on impact). I can say I definitely didn't have that same experience, so don't let that deter you completely!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Following a quick storybook intro, it starts off with a blank cursor over an intensely empty white screen. There is some reactive sound to player commands but absolutely nothing to see. The game very nearly feels broken, until you discover the right trigger and start throwing black paint balls that reveal the scenery and single path forward, and essentially define the rest of the journey.Gameplay evolves from base mechanics to keep fresh and avoid repetition. Water balls tint the environment in light blue but dry out rapidly. Velocity of throws pushes light objects and enables simple environmental puzzles. Activate switches to enable traversal, grow vines to climb and reach new places, push and activate lights to repel darkness. Create volumes in later chapters.Find and collect optional balloons. Not all of them colored, some hidden but most in plain sight. These can be traded for toys but have little value except for the detailed concept art that can be unlocked.More interestingly, discover additional narrative entries in the world by shooting bright golden letters peppered throughout the levels. It reads like a live storybook about love, loss, creative discovery and chasing desires, and leaving some form of legacy after a whole life's worth of unfinished accomplishments. Cute story, creative, simple, well achieved.The game does present a beautiful art direction, but it is nonetheless harshly monochromatic and heavy on contrast and brightness. It feels a little too much at both ends of the spectrum, from blinding light to total darkness. While not actual motion sickness, the game did make me feel faintly unwell during longer sessions. Best played in short amounts and in a properly lit room.Overall, I found The Unfinished Swan very imaginative except for the typical collectible chase. I would have preferred discovering more animated story beats to know more about the King and the Boy and their intriguing respective paths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game has such a neat premise and the paint splatter is a good mechanic. I don't want to give it a negative review, but I think it's worth mentioning that I could only make it about 10 minutes into the first level before I got so nauseous that I had to stop - nothing to do with the content but I guess due to the frequent turning in 3D space? I've only encountered one other game where this happens to me so I wouldn't call myself prone to motion sickness, but based on a quick google search it's not an uncommon occurrence with The Unfinished Swan :( Just a heads up
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game!It has a lot of unique mechanics that you've probably never seen before. But it feels like they only touched each mechanic a little bit and then moved on to the next, without realising the potential behind it, so the three chapters feel a bit disconnected. The storyline ties it all together, with great storytelling. I enjoyed finding the little story-bits and hearing more of the fairy tale. And the way they implemented the credits is marvellous.As someone who loves achievements, I aimed for getting all in this game. After you play through the game once, you unlock a helpful device for getting all the secrets. I could find all balloons without external help. Only one of the 10 achievements is a bit harder and requires a guide and some training. It took me maybe one and a half hours.This game is not for someone who wants an intricate puzzle-game. But if you're looking for a game with interesting and creative mechanics and storytelling, I'll definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Other than the story, I really liked this game. The story is good and all, but idk if it was just me, it felt like it was the skeleton and some of the organs of the actually story. Kinda like sometimes there was the perfect amount of story with the perfect amount of detail and other times both were lacking. The game itself ran smoothly and can't recall a time I had issues with long load times, glitching, lagging, or the such. Loved the majority of the chapters and their mechanics but unfortunately the game is rather a short one. Would have loved to have experienced more of everything is white and you have to paint things black to find your way through. Overall a great short game that I thoroughly enjoyed and ran smoothly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: this is... a weird one. kinda hit deep as someone who just got into animation and has no clue what hes doing. pick it up and play it... i think. also very unique game design with paint splats showing more of the world to you. also, dont over think things, just go with the flow as the path really is that straight forward
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny how reviews for games vary from gamer to gamer; each person has their own unique identity and abilities and the way a given game is structured will resonate with some and not with others. I played the Unfinished Swan in just short of four hours, all in one sitting. The first 15 minutes or so feels kind of tentative and a bit slow but the story and the environments really start to kick in after that. This game is short but frankly I was amazed by it's content. The Unfinished Swan is really an exploration & adventure game with a steady dose of excellent puzzles along the way. It's a process of discovery that's very memorable from start to finish. Games like this, that are as good as this, seem to be pretty rare unfortunately. I'm thinking here of a game like "Sable," for instance, although Sable is much longer than this and has more to offer overall. If you're someone like me, with respect to new releases, where you're like "Oh, great, look: it's this week's new top down shooter 'action-adventure' game, with an emphasis on combat featuring Souls-like difficulty...how original!!"--if you tend to have similar thoughts, and yearn for more mind blowing magical mystery tour experiences like Sable or What Remains of Edith Finch, etc., then you really should give the Unfinished Swan a try. And now is the perfect time, considering the Summer Sale!:-) A real treat, and the story, though simple, has something to--I hate to use the word "teach," but for want of a better word I'll use it--has something to teach everyone who plays it. 10 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Stunned, Neat little story to go with although pretty simple gameplay, but the way the environment changes to engage your feelings and thoughts and a few puzzles dotted through can make you have certain eureka moments. A good hour and a half to two hour of gameplay without going for all secrets, Well worth it if you can pick it up on sale, otherwise it depends on the player.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on PS3 when it first came out and instantly fell in love with it. It's completely enchanting and magical. Visually it is lovely and gameplay is unique and relaxing. Since I switched to PC shortly after I lost the ability to play it since I could only access it while I paid on console. I have been waiting for this to come out on Steam and funny enough didn't even notice when it did, someone close to me mentioned it and it made me so happy. Playing again brought back all the joy that I experience the first time. I cannot recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful, soothing, and pleasant.  I was continually impressed with each new permutation of the mechanics, and none outstayed its welcome.  In this era of "games as service," I deeply respect the courage and artistic integrity it takes to make something gorgeous, simple, and exactly as long as it needs to be, and not give in to the endless bleating from both consumers and corporations to add more for the sake of adding more.  This is a very beautiful game, one that does things that are only possible in an interactive medium, and we should always praise and encourage people exploring territory that only games can discover, executing ideas that only games can represent, and giving us totally unique interactive experiences like this one to counterbalance the vast number of games that care nothing and do nothing for games as an artistic medium.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: (To provide context for my review, my system specs are Windows 10/RTX 2080/i9 10980HK)- Very interesting art style throughout, though some areas (the city and palace in particular) are more inspiring than others- The music is fine; it didn't add or subtract from the experience- It's a simple, bittersweet tale about family and overcoming loss- Despite the dark parts of the story, the game's mood never feels depressing or mournful. I feel like the themes could have been explored a little more- The game controls fine, but that's because all you can do is walk, climb, jump, and shoot- The central mechanic of firing paint or water to progress is neat. The twists they put on the simple mechanic are creative, but I feel like the idea could have been explored further- I don't think I'll be replaying this one. The balloon collecting wasn't fun enough to warrant another playthrough- The game ran flawlessly the whole way through- After finishing, I was left wanting a bit more. Is the "unfinished" thing a gag? Whatever the case, the experience wasn't as fulfilling as I had hoped it would be- . Get it on sale if you like the art style. It's a short (2.5-3 hour) game that looks pretty and has a few cool tricks but will leave you wanting more from your experience
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Minimalist art-style, cool lighting,I really liked it.-Good voice acting (what little there was)-Chapter select option (if you missed some collectibles) The collectibles unlock some extras that can add a bit of fun.-Abstract but sweet story. -The game-play was fairly simply but enjoyable if you want something chill, each main chapter introduces a new mechanic but since there is only 4 chapters there is not much variation.-Music was pleasant -I encountered no bugs.Cons-Very Short for the main story (you can get a bit extra out of it if you try for all collectibles and unlocks)-Performance was mostly good but there were certain spots where there was significant dips which were not expected for a game that looks this basic. Specs vega 64, ryzen 3600, 16GB DDR4, Nvme SSD, Windows 11.I guess its a bit of let down if you compare it to their first game; the masterpiece that is "What remains of Edith Finch" but its enjoyable enough all the same. Maybe pick it up in sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Super awesome artistic game :) (around 3 hours). This game vaguely connects to the story of What remains of Edith Finch. It very loosely connects to Milton's Painted world and his disappearance, but it also follows a completely new story. and the story is kinda simple but really cute and magical. the ending made me tear up :)This game is just so unique and beautiful to me.The music is adventurous, mystical and magical :)The game mechanics, level design and gameplay are really interesting, unique and captivating.Also beautiful voice acting and story books ^^beautiful little tale :)I recommend this !
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Nice concept and storyline. The game however is extremely short, and I completed all 4 (yes there's only 4) chapters in 4 hours (a lot of this time my game was on pause whilst I was doing other stuff). I enjoyed the puzzle aspects of this game (working out how to get to the next area etc), but the stark white on black actually hurts your eyes and brain. _childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, before I recommend this game, here's what it is not:It is not a shooter.  It is not an RPG.  It is not a massive, thousand hour adventure.  It does not contain adult themes/language.Now, to why I love this game and highly recommend it.  It is based on a really cool mechanic of using a "magic paintbrush" that can throw blobs of paint around a conpletely white world.  At first it is disorienting, but quickly becomes very fun as you literally paint your own surroundings.  Later levels move away from the absolute white aesthetic, by adding more shading and eventually colors.  But there are several fun unlockables to pick up as you progress and it definitely merits a second or perhaps third playthrough.The story is of a young boy whose mother has died and he begins exploring one of her unfinished works, only to find a realm created and run by a painter king.  I won't spoil the story, but it is definitely interesting and open to several interpretations.This could also be a good game to play with a child that approaches the theme of death in the family in  a relatively safe and mild way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's short and cute. I liked hurling paint everywhere.The game seems to be a little buggy sometimes; it loved to crash if I skipped a cutscene while redoing chapters for achievements. Overall, not a bad experience or more trouble than it was worth.If you're prone to motion sickness from the 1st person POV, you can get into the files and back the FOV up. 70% was much better for me than the default 50.54%.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Some people will call this game a "walking simulator," which is a term I have chosen to completely and totally disregard.  The meaning of the term has been lost since it was introduced a decade ago.  It used to refer to a type of adventure game that was focused on interactive and immersive story telling, often with few to no game mechanics.  These days, people throw it around and it's used as a synonym for "boring."If we were to abide by the original meaning, I would classify The Unfinished Swan as a walking simulator.  But it's not a pure walking sim; the game has several mechanics through the course of the story.  I don't want to spoil them, but I do want to give massive respect for the incredible feat of programming that is the growing vines mechanic.The story being told in this  (the term I prefer to walking simulator) feels like a fairytale.  I think they did a great job of making TUS fit that theme.TUS also boasts what I believe is the most ridiculous achievement I have ever done in a video game.  I decided to get the most I could from TUS and achieve a Perfect Game.  To do that, I would need to get the "Minimalist" achievement.  The blank white icon for the achievement says it all: it requires navigating the first level level, which appears as a pure white screen, without using more than three ink balls.  Sound is the only indication of where you are.  A truly demented mind came up with this achievement.  It took me 45 minutes and carefully following a video guide before I reached the end.  Whew!I'm grateful that this game was ported from PlayStation to PC, though I'm very disappointed that since it runs on Gamebryo engine, I was unable to experience it in virtual reality with vorpX.  I was able to enjoy it on my monitor at 4K, and though the original game is old, it looks nice and crisp on PC.  Really great that we have it here, now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: HOLY SMOKES! Santa Monica Studios NAILS it again. The Unfinished Swan is a story about a boy following just that. However, the art and play style is simple yet novel. Just like many other Santa Monica Studios famous titles, you will feel a curious welcoming to the world as you learn how to interact with it. There will be mood-setting music that is simply Spectacular and it will carry you up and down and far away. You will feel curious one moment, optimistic the next, determined, in awe, and afraid. In the end, you will walk out the door wondering what you just experienced. Personally, I feel a bit of a joyful sadness since my Journey is at an end with this title.I HIGHLY recommend The Unfinished Swan. Oh, and you'll find reference to at least one other famous Santa Monica Studios titles in this game.I get that other people weren't sure what to expect with this, but it is really really good. I hope that you enjoy it too!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished swan is a first person puzzle game that uses paint to uncover the world in an otherwise more or less empty world.It's an interesting concept, but made my finger hurt for clicking all the time. Needs a turbo button or something.The gameplay doesn't really expand all that much beyond the first couple of minutes, and the story was way too childish for my taste. It felt like being in a Roald Dahl story, all the way to the end. The narrator is too much "British librarian telling a kids' story".It's still a unique game with great concept and should be tried for fans of the puzzle genre. Not exactly a walking sim that some people want to point out.Recommended, but I think it felt more like a childrens' game. Get only on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't very fair or correct to call this a puzzle game, this is more of a walking simulator with minor problem solving. The look of the game is stunning and beautiful, which is what you should play the game for. Story is background and not important, but very nice and complements the visuals. You will have no issue completing everything in less than 4 hours.If you see this on sale grab it. It is well worth the few bucks for couple of hours of stunning gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: cute!!!!!!!!!!!! some easy parallels between this and what they would go on to do with edith finch, both have this emphasis on Variety and Discovery. here it mostly serves a single metaphor, summed up in the protagonist "feeling unfinished himself" upon the death of his mother, and while nothing in it quite transcends "this is v sweet" for me, theres plenty of "woa" moments definitely worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: i loved this game. it wasn't exactly what i expected. but wasn't really sure what i was expecting. was kinda confused at first when i was in a pure white void. i'm going to want to replay the chapters a bunch more times so i can find all the story pages and balloons. but for my first time through it was really enjoyable. it was fun using paint to reveal the world in the first chapter.i really do enjoy this sort of interactive art. and this had the feel of an interactive art story book.and if nothing else.... the other two games i got during this fall sale left me more frustrated.... so this game has been a wonderful breath of fresh air. and i'm 100% taking this story as Milton Finch's full story. when i found myself in the white void i was thinking "so this is what Milton saw when he went through the magic door"all in all this game is beautiful and mostly stress free. it was stress free for me even when i was kinda unsure what to do and had to start trying stuff. and what i've got of the story so far is really nice. i kinda love these stories about families that aren't focused on the hetero-romance of the parents.my only complaint about games from this just randomly throw balls in the darkness and hope i eventually get the balloon.... but it would be less frustrating than resetting to the checkpoint and making no progress what so ever in figuring out where that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ balloon is. i just know it's right there but i can't keep the ball from rolling down the hill at that spot so i can't see anything. and i can't just try shooting in the darkness _childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan is very cutesy and fun walking-sim with some puzzle elements. I enjoyed the world-building, uniqueness, and aesthetic of this game. It presents such a interesting and compelling concept from the beginning and really does a good job at telling a simple story visually as well as aurally.I also felt kinda frustrated by some elements. The cutscenes were at a much lower framerate than the gameplay, which was strange. The story after in chapters 2-3 is fairly unimportant to the overall message and story and felt tacked on. The sheer amount of mouse clicking required in chapter 2 to grow the vines really tired out my hand (I have tendinitis, so this probably isn't an everyone thing).Overall, I would recommend it for children, fans of walking-sims, story-seekers, and people looking for unique experiences. I would - n o t -  recommend this to people who want a very deeply layered story with more complex puzzles.

And I'm sure I could get more out of it by going back to replay for the remaining balloons and all and finish up achievements but... the walking speed is soooo slow it feels like that'd take forever and it'd basically just be replaying large chunks of the game which... it's not that compelling, either. There's nothing really wrong with it and the experience itself was enjoyable enough while it lasted but maaaan I cannot imagine paying $15 and getting just this short, unimpactful 2-hour experience in return. _childDocuments_.review: Journey through a wonderful tale as Monroe, a young boy recently orphaned and left only one of his mother’s many unfinished paintings: an unfinished swan.  Waking up one night and discovering that the swan is no longer in its painting; you begin an epic journey through the blank canvas into another world.  Using your only tool in your travels you will paint, grow, and move items to bypass all manner of obstacles as you travel through strange and wondrous realms to reach the end of the story and the start of your own.The Unfinished Swan is a first-person puzzle/platforming game set in a lovely artistic world.  The game has the feeling of a well-loved children’s book and as such you progress through chapters of the story with additional pages to the tale found throughout the game.  Each chapter lets you use your only tool, a paintbrush, to progress through the world, overcoming various obstacles and progressing the storyline further.  Some minor platforming is required, but nothing too difficult.  Quirky scenes, a fun narrated story, and a beautifully simplistic world make The Unfinished Swan a fun diversion and a joy to play.While fun; the game’s mechanics seem to have no cohesion throughout the game.  For example, in the first chapter they are used to reveal the game world to you, while in the second chapter the mechanics are used to develop a way to move forward over various obstacles, and in the third chapter they are utilized mainly for security measures.  Additionally, in the third chapter, another mechanic was introduced that completely different from the rest of the game that didn’t seem to fit the rest of the game at all.  Sadly, the mechanics didn’t feel related—just something to do.The achievements are relatively easy to attain except for one which requires a bit more effort.  Achievements run from completing chapters of the story to collecting items along the way.  You may replay the game from chapters and subchapters which makes the collecting much easier than having to play over again.  Overall, getting all ten achievements was fun.While I did enjoy The Unfinished Swan I found it a bit too short and it had a feeling of being itself unfinished.  I enjoyed the world, the music, the story, and the gameplay, but wanted much more.  However, even with that said, I still recommend this game for those who like puzzles, fun stories, or for those who are looking for a short game that’s easy to learn and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Before Reading: Don't buy this if its not on sale, not worth 15 Dollars. This is worth 5 or 10 at most. Details at end of review.This game is a pretty fun half of a game. The design and art-style are both a little above average and the game mechanics and ideas being presented are detailed enough to make the story interesting and/or involved. The introduction can make the game feel like a tech demo with how simple it is, but surprised me with how creative the next evolutions of the mechanics were. I meant the word "half" in the sense that it feels like there isn't enough to warrant a 15 dollar price tag. The time to beat each level is good, there just aren't a ton of levels. This game does enough good things that it is enjoyable to play, but enough half-hearted things that its a good tool in getting the player to think about even cooler mechanics that could have been implemented, aka aspiring game developers.Overall, I would just say to try this game out if its on sale, but don't get it at full price. Because of almost no replayability, aside from achievements, the game needs about twice the amount of content than current to warrant a 15 dollar price tag.
