_childDocuments_.review: Looks like an arcade game but once you play it...OMG! Physics are top notch. Control is spot on. UI, vehicle and steering wheel settings are impeccable. Loads of extra features & upgrades to unlock. Racing, Drag Racing and Destruction events keep you on your toes. Don't be fooled, this game is not as easy as it looks but feels very, very rewarding. Most of all its maxed out non-stop fun! I was mind blown!I still have to check out multiplayer though. Servers were empty before game's launch. Overall the best monster truck sim out there to date. Nuff said.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: Is it fun yes? Does it feel like you are driving a monster truck? Not really. Driving is very stiff, once you end up on the rear wheels it's a 90% chance of being stuck in that position and not being able to do anything. Score counting is also not very accurate. There are a lot of things that doesn't give you the feel of a monster truck. So that's why it's a thumbs down. Game is at least an enjoyment for time savers.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is fun. I mean, you're driving a monster truck. How can it not be fun? The trucks feel appropriately weighty and bouncy, and you actually have full control over both axles for steering (monster trucks have 4-wheel steering) so you can turn the rear wheels independently of the front wheels, which both helps you maneuver the truck in tight spaces, but also allows you to pull off some pretty cool stunts. And the trucks sound appropriately meaty as well. Graphically I have to say it's nothing terribly special, but it's not bad.Where it falls apart is the mission structure. Basically, you first have to pay a fee to start any event (except the very first one). This fee can get big--later events in the first league can get close to $10,000. And when the first prize is maybe only $75,000, that 10 grand HURTS. So it puts a lot of pressure on you to win.And win you must, or you won't unlock more stages. That's right. A podium finish isn't good enough. Nor does it matter your standing in the league. You could be first place overall but if you didn't win out in the last event you're stuck replaying it (and paying that entry fee each time). So what ends up happening is you just mindlessly restart events over and over if it looks like you might come in any worse than first place so you don't have to fork over all your cash. And God help you if you have damage turned on, because monster trucks aren't cheap to fix, and you WILL break your truck. You are able to reset your truck (on lower difficulty levels) if you flip it or get it stuck, but even on lower difficulties you have a limited number of these, and to be honest, if you need to use one of these resets, just restart the event instead. They serve virtually no purpose.It's too bad. The actual driving is fun, the events are fun, but the way they have progression set up just sucks all the fun out of it. I suppose it's fine if you just want to screw around doing quick events and multiplayer, but the career mode is pretty crap, and it kinda killed it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, The idea is golden but the execution is flawed. For a game with surprising depth in the event types, customization, setups, sounds, and graphics there is just one elephant sitting in the room. The trucks are just awful to control. It's a game that sells its self as "A true Monster Truck simulation" but the truth is it's MUCH more arcade then sim. My first complaint about the trucks is that the starter truck is a four-speed. Almost all MT's are two speed automatics. I couldn't be bothered to see if any of the upgraded trans may change the gear count so take this point with a grain of salt. Second, the trucks feel heavy until you hit a jump then it's like they switch to half gravity while in the air. tapping the gas or brakes in the air should change the pitch of the truck due to wheel torque, however this does not feel modeled at all. You can't roll over on your side. the trucks have invisible training wheels on the doors so you can fully stop on the side walls of the tires the way a real truck could not. When you do roll 99% of the time you will end up turtled on your back because the collision of anything other than wheels to the ground is wonky at best. If you just want a smashy smashy truck go vroom game. This is gonna be your jam. If you want authentic monster trucks and the challenge of controlling 14,000lbs of steel and rubber, sorry to say but this aint it chief.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear I was sent a key for the developers for this gameMy first look and gameplay can be seen hereI was pleasantly surprised when playing Monster Truck Championship. To be clear I know very little about the sport other than the odd video I have seen on youtube or sporting programs. Monster Trucks are not really mainstream in the UK.With that said the game was fun to pick up and play. There isn’t too much to learn to play, but I get the feeling to master it could take a fair amount of discipline and practice. There are a number of game modes at the time of writing this review I had only played career and quick plan. The career mode is split in to individual events with various leagues based on your progression. I had fun with the variety of events. Race, drag race, destruction, freestyle.   With upgrades to vehicles (cosmetic and performance) that unlock as you progress. Additionally you can unlock team members (mechanics & managers) along with sponsors for upcoming events. I think there is a reasonable amount to keep casual gamers entertained and would say this is a must buy if your thing is monster trucks. Although I would hesitate to recommend it whole heartedly a at the current price point.

_childDocuments_.review: It crashes every now and then, one of the crashes even deleted my career progress. Other than that, it's a nice Wreckfest/Flatout with the Monster Truck theme. It's obviously not a sim but it's got very logical physics. As a sim racer I find it rather easy even on the highest difficulty, especially once you upgrade your truck and get good staff in your team. The career can be completed in less than 10h but for the price I got it, it is more than enough. I have not tried the multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: YES! You can go and read my review of Monster Jam Steel Titans, and I had some really good things to say about that game, especially since I felt it showed a lot of progression of the series, it was getting better. Well, one glaring hole in MJST ,as I mentioned in that review, is the physics, it is nearly impossible to do any of the real world stunts, like a backflip into a reverse moonwalk, without your truck bouncing 20' into the air. The physics were really bad, and in a monster truck game, in which stunts are the biggest part if what draws the fans, it was a letdown. Well, I just literally pulled off a perfect backflip into a reverse moonwalk in this game. This game still isn't perfect, but it just launched, some of the dirt track races feel like you're driving on ice. Perhaps this can be fixed in a future update, or perhaps it is simply that I still have the starter truck, with no upgrades, and that better traction comes with better upgrades. Any fan of Monster Trucks, and especially Monster Truck video games owes it to yourself to get this game. I came in early into my playing the game, because I know many of you are like me, and typically want to read reviews before laying down the $. I saw the trailers, and am a fan of the genre so I decided, with knowledge that I can refund if necessary, to get the game, and be one of those folks who always help me make up my mind in the early days of a game launch. I will update this review as I progress, but for right now I highly recommend it. The abilities, that work beautifully so far, during freestyle alone would have been an instant buy for me, but this game is the total package, and the best monster truck game to date, imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: the driving around is fun and that is about it. me and a friend tried to play multiplayer and we would load up and i get booted back to the main menu saying connections lost...the driving is about the only plus side as i dont have to use the controls for the back wheels at all if i dont want to(which is a godsend because that setup is just horrible and i get confused on which side controls which set of wheels at times when i was doing the races)the physics just suck and overall its just not a fun game
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this on sale for about $7. Reviews made me think I wouldnt like it. Color me shocked when I found out this game is a hidden gem.This game is setup like older NASCAR games, or DIRT 4, etc where you build your vehicles, team, sponsors etc. Except its done with monster trucks. Theres a ton of variety in how to play, its not completely linear so you dont feel railroaded (think GT4). Lots of options for how to build your trucks. Bodies, paint, engines, and details like painting chassis components, flags, etc. You can hire different eginers and mechanics that give you X or Y bonus, etc. I like that thers not a huge focus on the "goofy" monster truck bodies, instead giving you lots of options. You can make a serious build or a wacky looking one, as long as youve unlocked the parts. I dont understand the physics complaints. There is a bit of twitchiness, but its easily managed, and mstly goes away with the first set of upgraded tires. There are a TON of settings to adjust controls as well. Crashing/impacts also feels good. The trucks crumble and fall apart, obstacles like railers and barriers disintegrate. Cars crush realistically. Your truck also has a detailed mechanical damage model, which is of course subject to your build and engineers. Lots of small details enchance the experience. Dust whiping around tires, filling the air, fireworks going off, etc.Overall id give this an 8/10. Solid content, A lot of fun
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: I have just completed the game and have a viewpoint.For the asking price of US. $40, I might have expected a little more so I hope the Devs add something to the pot here in the way of some bug fixes, physics tweaks and maybe add another arena or two (A sandbox editor would be awesome!) but all in all, the game is fun. Took about 20hrs. Monster truck madness comes to mind. I play with keyboard controls. It takes a short time to get used to steering with both front and rear wheels and once you get the knack, it makes performing stunts easier and cuts loads off your racing times.No bugs to speak of running WIndows 10 and a 2MB Nvidia Geforce GTX670 but have experienced a little on screen clipping and stuttering going under bridges but all in all, visuals are fine. Nothing special but good enough while not looking too cartoon'ish. It is a bit irritating to pull off a wicked combo move only to be told, "Aww, and he landed on his roof" when, I actually ended in a nose or sky wheelie or something else incredibly cool and there are times the truck won't perform as expected but I think some of that may have to do with me mashing the keys relentlessly at times.There is an invisible roof in one of the arenas on the first ramp but once I learned that, I used it to my advantage and pulled off some killer barrel rolls.As far a physics. If you've ever driven a monster truck in real life, it's a bit off from real world. If your monster truck experience is from video games, it is just fine. Centrifugal force from high spinning wheels do effect your rotation while in the air but maybe not as realistic as it could be. A little more bounce from those huge tires would probably make the realism factor go up a bit more as well.  There is a "Tune" section for engine and transmission for both your race and stunt set ups separately that does make all the difference in the world as you progress and if you don't use it, you will fail or, you'll have to get incredibly good at driving a really poorly performing truck. Upgrades seem to be heavily balanced in cosmetics but the Performance ones, while doled out sparingly,  do make a difference enough that will have you adjusting your driving habits to keep up. Add 500HP and 100Nm of torque and wheelies quickly become back flips. I will agree with one reviewer that "drifting" is something it says you can do but, not really. I did do it once by accident according to text flashing across my screen but have no idea how I pulled it off. It usually turns into a barrel roll. Maybe a bit more time tuning and on the practice track is in order before I call that one a non existent feature? I enjoyed the game and will get a few more hours out of beating my times and tricking out my truck. I think it's worth the buy if you like these types of games. I'm waiting for a few more arenas and if they add the sandbox editor, I'm all in.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this simulation and this is supposed to be a monster truck simulation, but the physics need a lot of work. The truck doesn't bounce accurately when landing big jumps. It's not satisfying. I think the main reason is that tire deformation physics is not implemented. The tire traction physics is also off. It doesn't feel like the tires are digging into the ground. The suspension doesn't squat realistically when accelerating. Is first gear really that short in monster trucks? Maybe I need to launch with second instead of first gear.The sounds when landing doesn't sound good either. It has great sound for the engine though. The graphics are nice too. Runs well on my computer too after switching to full-screen mode vs windowed full-screen. The game would stutter in the default windowed full-screen mode.The engine seems to die out too quickly when doing donuts in second gear. The tires should slip to allow fourth gear donuts after breaking the initial traction of the tires. When braking in a straight line, the tires stop too quickly on dirt. It should lock-up without ABS and slide a bit.I'm an off-road rally race car driver, not a monster truck driver, but has the opinion of monster truck drivers been taken into consideration? Maybe in the future I will re-buy since it has the potential if they keep releasing big changes in future patches.  If the developers improve the physics, I will happily try again after seeing updated gameplay videos showcasing the physics improvements. I'm available to beta-test physics changes and to give input. I have been wanting a game like this for many years and even considered making one myself since I'm a developer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it where it counts--the truck physics are great, and it's tons of fun to perform stunts.  All of the freestyle tricks are fairly easy to learn, and a joy to pull off.  Everything you see on actual Monster Jam can be done here.The gameplay loop is short and simple: win races, do stunts, get money, upgrade truck, repeat.  That's it.  But that's okay.  I wasn't expecting some robust, open world to lose myself in for hundreds or thousands of hours, and neither should you.  This isn't GTA or something.  But it doesn't need to be.  Don't expect too much from it.  It's more of toy to goof around with.  I use it as something to goof around with while I'm waiting for my friends to arrive to play whatever serious game we're working on.  It's perfect for that purpose.  I bought this purely to do freestyle stunts, and for that it totally delivers and then some.It's satisfyingly challenging without being overly frustrating.  Not grindy.  The easy difficulty allows you to blow past competition, which I like because I wasn't looking for extreme challenge with this.  I just wanted to do backflips.  ;)Tons of truck customization options.  The cosmetic options are so much fun.  I made Grave Digger.  They very obviously let players make Grave Digger as closely as possible without copyright infringement.  :DI have only one criticism--they should have let you save several truck appearance loadouts.  You can make so many gorgeous, awesome looking trucks, but if you want to change your appearance, you have to just change everything manually.  I want to customize a truck, then save it to a loadout slot, and have, say, six loadouts that I can toggle between with one click so I can switch between multiple trucks.  I don't care if it costs in-game money.  That's fine.  I really wish they had included that.  It would have been so easy to do, and would have made it perfect.Anyway, still great, and I recommend it.  The game is narrow in scope, but highly polished.  All the reviews I watched placed this above the licensed Steel Titans franchise.  The best part is no DRM, no accounts, no 3rd party software, no in-game store, no monetization, no BS, no f****** BattlEye garbage.  Just your game, and that's it. which is just the breath of fresh air I needed after the anti-cheat travesty that ruined GTA online for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the best Monster Trucks game on steam and probably on the Internet, has:+ A handful of customizations that includes the: Body, Rims, Exhaust and Top/Front/Rear Attachment.----------+ Not forgetting Liveries and stickers.+ Has a Career mode that's basically you racing in leagues and competing against other AI drivers.+ Has a Quick Play mode where u can basically play any event with custom options and custom tracks against AI.+ Other game modes include: Destruction, Freestyle and Time trail. (Total of 5 game modes)+ You can play this either as an Arcade Game (Not recommended) Or as a Sim Game (Recommended). Choice is up to you+ You can also change your Tuning for certain Freestyle Events and Racing to suit your gamestyle.+ Easy is a bit of a joke, but Hard Difficulty is challenging and will you keep on your toes!+ Graphics look stunning and very well done, even the detail when your Truck gets all muddy and and your + Sounds are amazing, especially the Monster Truck Engine audio it's so F**** good! (Music however is poor)+ Has Wheel Support which you can also customize to your liking.+ Works fine with a keyboard and is not overly complicated. (How I played)+ It's well optimized and I had no bugs or crashes or any issues, I played on an Intel i7 6700, 16gb ram and GTX 1060 6gb and never noticed any killer frame drops.Now on to the Negatives:- Online is dead, literally dead. I tried playing some online on Day 2 and I could never find any matches. Trying to find an online race as we speak so I can rate the online but I'm unable to find any. Tried hosting but no one ever joined.---------.- You're also limited to the game modes you play on online, basically you can either play a race or a drag. You can have different stages and set as many laps as you want but then again online is dead.- After you finish the career mode you literally have nothing to do.- For some reason Time Trail is not part of the events you do in the Career Gamemode which is a shame. - You can set up a team to help you give you boosts but they're just that. No real depth of managing wages or interaction, just a passive boost.----------.- Sponsors also have no visual effect except from giving you a bonus but it might just be me nit picking really.- Game time is a bit small as I finished it after 7-8 hours and I'm not really feeling like going back doing the career mode again.- Menu Music (In my opinion) is awful and I wished we got some Heavy Rock type music to up the Atmosphere. (Personally I just muted music)Honestly with all the stuff I mentioned it's still a decent game for Monster Trucks enthusiasts and it's worth a buy for €40. HOWEVER as a gamer who has no idea about Monster Trucks (Me being a bit of both) it's not really worth the €40 BUT! It's still worth it if you can get it on sale, maybe €20-30.Replay ability I'm also not really sure... I mean you can always jump back in do some Quick Races but I'm not sure about how many times I'd do that.OVERALL SCORE: 7.8Graphics: 9/10,... Gameplay: 8/10,... Career Mode: 5/10,... Music: 2/10,... Sound: 9/10,... Online: ??/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and is probably the best monster truck game on the market.The monster truck market i, in my opinion, an untapped game market with a lot of potential. Although this game is GOOD. I don't know if its worth the $40 price tag, I was able to get a key online for around 20 dollars, and I find that to be a much more reasonable price for the product. With that being said...This game is fun. Who doesn't like destroying stuff? Its a blast, and the curve of actually learning how to drive the truck is VERY fun. _childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a weird review for me to write. Growing up, I had a Monster Jam game on the PS2, the car combat one ‘Maximum Destruction’, but I’ve always been more of a passerby to monster truck games than other racers, generally speaking. That being said, Monster Truck Championship is actually… pretty good?Sure, there seems to be no officially licensed Monster Jam content, but I’d argue it’s for the better here; being able to basically put together a junker truck with stock parts and upgrade it as the career progresses is far more satisfying. The career event list is very linear with no calendar system, but the driver hiring and sponsor signing adds some fun twists to the events themselves; stuff like an engineer adding torque to the engine at the cost of some race winnings, or a sponsor demanding a wheelie into somersault trick combo for bonus cash and some extra cosmetic parts. The freestyle physics can feel frustrating at times, especially on the hardest difficulty with no resets allowed. That being said, the destruction events are just plain fun, and the drag races add just enough variety to keep things fresh over the game’s run time, even when I felt that the AI was blatantly cheating.In other words, this is a really great XBLA style monster truck game. You’ll probably end up seeing all there is to offer in 10 hours or less and then move on, but it’s mostly fun while it lasts. Considering some of this developer’s previous games, I’d say that’s a massive success, although I would really like to see a sequel that was more fleshed out.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀When you first fire up your engines, Monster Truck Championship from Teyon Studios seems like more fun than a new set of mud flaps. It’s a definite improvement over previous monster trucking games, though it can’t really compete against, arguably, the best of the genre in Monster Truck Madness,MTC includes over 50 customizable elements, 25 arenas, and three different leagues to compete in. Races tend to include more off-road obstacles, such as water, barrels, and grimy mud, while circuit tracks offer more flat-out racing with customizable laps. The single-player tracks range from the mundane Kilgore Raceway to the chaotic Grand Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. Regardless of the location, each course is reasonably long and heavy on variety. In short, even the weariest off-roader will find quite a bit of long-term challenges in this game.In addition to the newer modes like Destruction and Freestyle, the online features arena style racing in which up to 8 players can compete in thumb blistering action. Measured in minutes instead of laps, the emphasis here is not necessarily to beat the track but to beat your opponents to become king of the mud hill. It’s rowdy, dirty, and fun. In fact, you’ll be repeating many of the courses just to see how much damage you can do.Graphics in MTC are very polished and look great whether you’re viewing the action from the outside or the inside of your truck. The game runs extremely smooth, with tight, responsive controls, and a high frame rate even with every graphical option maxed out on a 4K monitor. Variable customization like tweaking your truck’s color, gear ratio, suspension, and everything else in between spices up the replay value and adds more immersion to the races.Controls are precise but feel very different especially if you are unfamiliar with the behaviors of monster trucks. While the keyboard is supported, playing the game with a dual pad controller, or better yet, an actual wheel and pedal setup is the best way to go to maximize your enjoyment.While Monster Truck Championship offers a lot of trucking variety, it doesn’t quite live up to the expectation set by Microsoft’s Monster Truck Madness. Still, there are a lot of things to like about this version if you’re willing to give it a chance. It won’t quite get you to hog heaven, but it’s the best rough-and-tumble truck racing game thus far.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: MTC has a great career mode, decent graphics and lots of control options. It has some good track design and fun arena layouts. The collision physics in truck vs truck situations are pretty good with lots of flips and tire locking and the AI doesn't really cheat. On the hardest difficulty they provide a reasonable challenge but crash just as much. It plays a lot like Wreckfest but with monster trucks.However the physics are terrible. The vehicles in this game do not behave like a monster truck at all. The center of gravity is far too high, making simple stunts like power wheelies and stoppies nearly impossible and bicycles and wheelies are clearly assisted by physics pushes. The trucks tend to turtle in rollovers because the tires are seemingly massless. This also affects the stability of the trucks doing things like jumps or drifting, and they roll over in very unnatural-looking ways with their big wheels behaving like they are filled with helium. They get stuck on their backs and hover in the air on their comically enormous and poorly placed bounding boxes.The bounding box of the trucks when they contact the ground is different from the one used when two trucks collide. It is a cube that does not ascribe their actual shape so cyclone spins are a very jerky canned effect, and there is no gyroscopic effect from the wheels making the trucks extremely unstable in the air and prone to tumbling if you do not go off jumps perfectly straight. The modelling of 4WD is wrong and every truck regardless of its performance level has an open center differential, meaning that when the front end is up in the air as in a wheelie, the rear wheels do not spin, again making simple stunts that real monster trucks can do impossible. This also makes going around corners very skittish, as the truck has a tendency to spin when it lifts wheels in corners. Anyone who has problems spinning out in this game should not question their ability, the trucks just plain drive wrong. To me it feels like the default UE4 vehicle with silly huge tires and not a simulation of any monster truck.I received this product through Humble Bundle and did not pay full price, but I still feel cheated, as the advertising claim of a "monster truck simulator" is wholly untrue and the developers should be ashamed. You could replace every truck in this game with a Polaris RZR and not have to change a thing. Monster Jam Steel Titans 2 is a physically far superior game that has a more accurate depiction of monster truck physics, and even the mobile game Monster Truck Destruction has superior suspension modelling. I can respect the level of gameplay detail the developers put into the game, as its caRPG elements, upgrades and tuning are perhaps the one place it shines over the other monster truck games available today, but it completely misses the mark with the one thing it overtly claims to do, while games that promise and deliver far less do it better.I look forward to a sequel made by people who have actually seen a monster truck go around a turn and off a jump before deciding to make a game about them.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a competent game and sometimes it feels exciting 'cuz you're driving a monster truck. The physics also go for the "simcade" spectrum, in that it tries to be properly physics-driven, but with some simplifications to make it feel more arcadey.But it just doesn't nail it. The trucks feel like they're skating on ice, and feel like they're modeled with a oversimplified center of gravity. The game also likes to flip a switch and declare that you've lost traction, giving you zero ability to catch yourself out of the that loss of control once it starts.So short review here for that reason. I don't care about any other aspect of the game because it doesn't feel like I'm racing an actual vehicle - I'm just nudging big slabs of meat across ice on the moon.Sad, because it looks like the devs actually put effort into this game. RIP.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Truck Championship is, as the developer says, really a simulation, and not just an arcade-style monster truck racer.  There's a lot of work that's gone into reproducing the mechanics and physics of monster trucks, it's more involved than you might think.  But that does not mean an ounce of the fun of monster trucks has been neglected here.   This is a game that's the kind of thing Jeremy Clarkson talks about when reviewing cars on Top Gear (before he punched that guy).  All the mechanics are there where you expect them to be, but it's still fun.  It's not like they made a regular racing game but the cars have big wheels.  When you're driving, it really feels like you're controlling a behemoth monster truck, with all the challenges and complexities real monster truck drivers have to deal with. You have a range of races and challenges to keep you busy, there's a full tutorial, customisable monster trucks, loads of tracks/arenas.   This all backs up the very fundamental look and feel of the game... and that's great.  It's highly polished, and it looks good because while this is console ported, it's a well done console port, and significant work went into control customisability and graphics performance and tweaks.  You have full 4K, antialiasing, everything you'd expect from a PC native game.This is fully AAA priced, however, but that does match the quality of the game.  It is appearing in game bundles now, however, so my recommendation if you like this kind of over the top fun and racing/vehicle driving sims, grab it when it's in a bundle or on a sale at a price that suits you.  It's worth it.

The physics of the monster trucks is really injoyable: it's not got that dummed-down, everyone-is-special-and-great, console-derp driving physics. _childDocuments_.review: Well... It could have been great. All the ideas are there, including a "simulation" approach, a decent career mode and decent presentation. But the physics and ai are both ABYSMAL. The trucks feel like they have NO weight sometimes and sometimes (landing a jump) they feel like a dropping solid concrete slab. _childDocuments_.review: I really like this. I thought that monster truck drivers must be very talented to usually land upright from their jumps, and now I'm certain of it. If I were given the keys to a monster truck I'd be upside-down on the first bump.The sim vibes work well. The steering of front and rear is independent meaning you can crab drive, and just like real life there's no air control whatsoever. I get the impression that with many hours, you could become very good at driving these trucks, but the learning curve is real.The big flaw is scoring in freestyle events. It just seems to not know when destruction ends and another trick begins, and the gap between tricks needed to count as a combo is too short. This wouldn't be so bad except that the only way to do well in these events is to get up to a x15 multiplier, so if your combo breaks you need to restart.Got it on deep discount, and for that I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Truck Championship

_childDocuments_.review: As Nacon's first foray into a monster truck game, I say they pretty much killed it. The physics are like no other monster truck/Monster Jam game, as you have to try and control the truck as much as you can when you hit a jump, similar to the physics after hitting a jump in Hot Wheels Unleashed. In addition, BOTH sticks on the controller are used to help turn the truck, although you don't always need to use the right stick to control the rear tires in the corners. Another thing is that you have to let off the throttle for jumps and other things instead of full throttling it, which makes this game more fun. You have to be careful over the jumps or else you may screw yourself out of a good finishing position. Honestly, if Nacon can secure the Monster Jam rights and can use the same physics as used in this game, this could make for a really good Monster Jam title. It would be FAR better than the adequate Monster Jam Steel Titans titles. A solid 9/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: From Las Vegas to Orlando, go head-to-head against experienced drivers in drag races and freestyle competitions. But, before you can pull off donuts, wheelies, and bicycles, you must first tune your truck to perfection. These machines are spectacular and impressive, yet highly technical to drive. The game faithfully reproduces all the unique demands of mastering these powerful trucks, including independent front and rear-wheel management, mass transfer anticipation in bends, and predicting bounces after jumps.

name: King of Seas
detailed_description: King of Seas is an ARPG adventure game set in a nautical pirate world. Become the most legendary pirate of all time as you embark on an epic adventure across the boundless and ominous sea. Discover lost islands and treasures, fight rival pirates and menacing monsters all in your bid to become king of the sea. MAIN FEATURES Shape your own adventure : Dive into a magnificent, nautical world. Complete quests to shape your journey and meet unique characters along the way. But be warned, the world around you will react and change depending on the actions you take. Naval routes will change and with each conquered settlement the difficulty adapts to make for a more challenging adventure. Weather the storms : Changes in the weather can knock you off your sea legs. From thick fog to dangerous storms, sail at your own risk and watch out for the direction of the wind. You could be blown right into an enemy’s path if you don’t strategize well enough. Customize your ship : Choose from five different types of highly customisable ships: The Sloop, Brig, Flute, Frigate and Galleon. With over 900 items available to collect and deck out your ship with you can create a battle-ready vessel that’s the envy of rival pirates. Trade with other settlements : Each settlement produces their own unique products. Buy them at the lowest price possible and sell them to other settlements where they are in high demand. Line your pockets with gold and spend on improvements to your ship and on brand new skills. Prepare for battle : You’re not alone out on the open ocean. Throughout your adventure you’ll face off in naval battles with monsters and rival pirates. Keep your wits about you and use strategy to win. Battle mechanics aren’t limited to blasting cannons, on your adventure you’ll acquire up to 20 different combat skills from flamethrowers to voodoo rituals. Each battle you win will raise the bounty on your head and you’ll be challenged by even more fearsome foes. Explore the nautical world : There is so much to explore in the epic world of King of Seas. Discover secret maps hidden in the depths and excavate precious treasures. Go fishing and uncover as many as 30 varieties of fish living below the ocean surface. Complete special side missions and reap rewards that can help you on your adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is a recommend for me.  I have a few disagreements from some of the other reviews so personal experience may be an issue. Pros:- Great pirate theme combat similar to older pirate games like Sid and High Seas Trader- Ship upgrades that provide combat variety- Talent upgrades to give you the RPG feel of upgrading your character- Comic value if you get the humorCons:- Combat can get repetitive- Simple story with a time classic theme- Stat/Talent values can be a bit misleading.  Some talents claim to adjust short/long range cannons but it does not really tell you what that means.  I guess range 8 is short and 10 is long?  Also some values like crit hit chance and reload don't define the value (maybe %, maybe seconds, or maybe some other value)Comment on many issues people are reporting:- Many people are complaining about the scroll wheel.  I am using an X-box style controller on PC and all you do is push the L-stick toward the selection.  It's just like a clock wheel.  I think most people want to have it move in increments and that is just a personal choice so some may not like it but I don't have an issue.-All ships are not locked behind a quest wall.  This is a mistake by people not playing the game.  You get an early quest to unlock the Flute ship and after that all ships are unlocked.  I was able to already get a Frigate after about 4h of play. - The complaints about grinding is an odd one.  Yes you have to buy map parts, yes you kill ships and get gold and loot.  But honestly what do you expect.  Path of exile is a grind let's hate it, All mmo's have a grind let's hate them too.  I had to do tons of quests in Witcher, let's hate that.  Hades ya I ran the dungeon over and over.  All games grind the question is do you like the type of game.  I love sailing the seas and killing stuff so I like it.  Sure there could be more "things" to do but if they are "things" you don't like you will just hate those.  Lot's of people, myself included stream the game.  Watch anyone play it, try the demo and see if it's your jam.  Saying it sucks because you have to grind or only played 1.5h and said I don't have everything could be said about every game ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do not know where to start. This game IS fun. Its a light-hearted RPG with that naval theme and combat. It is very pretty (I personally love these artsy style games). Its some casual fun, unless you are going for the hardcore difficulties.But this is where I could not go further with the positives. Despite wanting a naval theme/combat style game, this does not really do it for me (yet). The AI in terms of strategies, besides chasing you down and then circling you, is non-existent. The scaling of enemies to your level does not really matter, but when it is coupled with the fact that the RPG system for the ship building is a bit lacking, it gets a little ridiculous. No matter what combinations I try to tie together for stat combos when gearing your ships, nothing really comes together and makes you a powerhouse in combat. The only sure fire strategy for combat is to run with the smaller vessels and perform hit-n-runs. The issue with combat right now, with the stats not really meaning much and how the bigger vessels operate, is how it does not allow for pure broadside combat. You are better off not getting hit at all, because no matter what your defense says, or attack says, you never feel like you are in control when you are trying to be an absolute unit at sea. This was a big disappointment to me. I was looking forward to being a terror in a Galleon, but I ended up getting scared when more than a couple ships joined in the fight. The aiming of the broadsides were not really a problem for me, added a tiny bit of skill to it.The exploration is tedious. It is fun to sail around, do not get me wrong, but the cartographer system for unlocking the areas covers too little for the hassle of finding the cartographer themselves. This is just a small issue though. Abilities are really hit and miss. There are really cool abilities, and this is where you get a leg up on the enemy AI, if you use certain abilities. Some are very weak, and others are insanely strong to the point you should not be using anything else. I think in all my time of looting ships I have wrecked, ghost ships, treasures, other loot, and trading; I have only seen two (2) yellows. Definitely a bunch of purples though as I have had enough to deck out (hah) a few ships. I do not find the loot rewarding enough in the long run or vary enough when whats there does not seem to really contribute to the effectiveness of your builds already. Trading is fun but shallow. I like the idea of having a trading ship. But if you wanted to absolutely min-max (which you do not need to do because money just rains down on you) trading by sailing around to buy/sell at the best prices, you would have to guess what port has what. No hints as to what area needs what resources, etc. Lastly, the QoL is lacking pretty hard. There is not much to put in as far as QoL but it is not there regardless. You can see this when you trade. When you trade upwards of 100+ units of an item, sitting there for a minute or so for each one to use the side arrow for it to count up gets annoying and time consuming.With some work I can see this being super solid, especially if they fix the RPG system to allow more solid builds for all ships and maybe beef up the AI a bit. But atm I cannot give this a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Few comments for those on the fence:- Check out positive reviews for why you should buy it.- It is reminiscent of Sid Meier's Pirates and hence has a lot of that game's enjoyability - aka pirate life and booty.However, my negative review stems from the following:- Even in the early stages the game is already a grindfest. I mean.... the grind becomes apparent very quickly. - I spent most of my time early game just picking fights with other ships and generally winning because the combat system seems to focus on the enemy simply being stronger than you and does not factor in any decent combat mechanics or AI (this was on the "Captain" difficulty). Enemy ships don't use any intelligent behavior. --- See other reviews for people commenting on that the combat seem's "arcade-like". Normally I would be fine with this but then the following point is what sealed the deal for me. - Game has a progression lock - you can't purchase better ships until you complete certain goals & you can't enter various zones because it's too dangerous. Final note is that this game is obviously a console port (or seems to be) so I wasn't expecting a AAA experience but I was hoping for at least a few hours of entertainment. Sadly this wasn't the case. Thar may be treasure out there..... but you wont find it here. As always, check out other reviews for pros and cons and make an informed decision.

_childDocuments_.review: A good and solid game. Very similar to Windward but with WAY more polish.Runs perfectly fine on max setting with the following specs:Acer Nitro AN515-5711th Gen Intel Core i7-11800HNVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti16147 MB RAMHaven't found any bugs either.It's beautiful but not mindblowing. If the things you see in the trailers and screenshots catch your interest, then you'll be happy with what you get.The music is ok, but not as good as the trailers. It's your standard pirate and sailor type of themes. Having more of of the trailers music would've been much appreciated.Don't let the beginning of the game fool you into thinking that this is all it has to offer. You start out slow with lots of dialogue and cutscenes to click through and your gameplay options are very limited. Certain features are locked behind story-related events that you have to reach first but once you do... the game really opens up. Every time I felt like the game becomes too repetitive, it throws me a bone by unlocking a new element like being able to conquer enemy ports to turn them into pirate hideouts, for example. There are lots of things to do and lots of things to discover in this game.Don't let the reviews fool you into thinking that this game is repetitive or grindy. It doesn't feel grindy or repetitive at all if you're into games such as Windward or pretty much any hack'n'slash game out there like Diablo. It's the old, golden rule that has proven to be effective for many decades: looting & leveling.Personally, I like to think that if I get one hour of entertaining gameplay for every buck a game costs... then it's worth it. And with a price tag of 24,99€, I've already exceeded that amount of hours and I haven't even finished the game yet.Overall this is a fantastic game with lots of polish. It's not attempting to re-invent the wheel but it's very good at what it's supposed to be. Go get this game if you love pirate stuff, looting, leveling, exploring and ship-to-ship combat. It's absolutely worth it. ♥

_childDocuments_.review: is an open-world seafaring game with procedural generation of the world map, in which you take on the role of an unintentional pirate, following a linear story and numerous side quests. As enticing as that sounds, you will quickly find that the side quests make you run around doing the same tasks, either destroy a single marked ship, bring a quest item, or bring some materials from one place to another--again, and again.1. The different skills you can choose to level up based on your playing preference. You will not have nearly enough points to max out the trees, so you need to choose carefully. (I think you should really be allowed to reset these points so that the player can better experiment. It's not too easy to experiment because of each game lasting such a long time.)2. The equippable gear and skills give nice combinations to maximize power output or your defenses during combat, based on how you want to play. There's enough immediate customization options to allow for dramatic changes to your ship from its baseline stats. The different skills really change the way you approach combat and make it very interesting.3. The combat is pretty fun, it has a certain arcade shooter feel once you get used to the controls and to your ship. I was initially having a ton of trouble controlling the starting ship, but it turned out to be my favorite vessel. It's a small target for enemies and it's fast.4. The artistic design is really neat, I love the way that the ships and settlements look. There are some unique features to different named locations that are nice to look at. There are 3 levels of zoom, but realistically you can only play the game in the most zoomed-out view, otherwise you just do not see enough of the surroundings and of the action.5. The game has 3 starting difficulty options available, with 2 more to be unlocked from playing. I only played in the hardest of the starting difficulties and it felt difficult but fair. I think the two unlockable difficulties are probably going to give people quite a challenge.1. Game balance seems really off. You can save up money and buy the most powerful (supposedly) ship, which turns into a giant and slow target for your enemies. The significant increase in number of cannons do not seem to really do much more in overall damage in my experience, basically making the bigger ships a self-imposed handicap instead of an earned power-up.2. The numerous times (about once every 30-45 minutes) that I had a random physical collision that landed in a "Fatal Error" in the game. It happened when I was in the middle of battle, colliding into other ships. It happened when I was randomly sailing and accidentally run into the Kraken's tentacle, and it just kept happening. Fortunately for autosaves every time you dock, making the loss of progress limited. The one time I really got ticked off was when after dying, I lost my ship and equipped gear, was trying to get back to retrieve them, but such an error made me lose all of it.3. The side quests are literally the same, some repeat without a single wording change. Even though there are so many of them, there's a serious lack in variety. The character designs are basically reuses of the exact same likenesses, with no variation. The cartographer encounter is a single line of dialogue (ever the same, no variation) when you meet him for the first time in that particular section of the map, and every time you visit him after being there before, he gives the exact same second line of speech.4. Keyboard controls work, but are not remappable at this time. No mouse support yet, but should be coming. Unfortunately the recommended controller controls feels finnicky in some inventory-management screens, which you will be dealing with a lot.5. Speaking of inventory management, the set up is less than ideal. You will be handling large quantities of items and you can only use left and right to add and subtract to the number being put into or out of the inventory. So you spend a lot of time watching a number count up from 0. For example, if I move 100 pieces of wood into the inventory from the bank, I choose bank, go to the materials/good section, and select the wood, then I have to hold right and watch the number count up from 0 to 1, then 2, then 3, then 4... until 100. Then I click okay. This is what I call time-wasted. Also in the inventory management is selection of your gear, and it always looks funny when you have some starting gear that seems to offer better overall stats compared to more rare gear, until you learn to actually scrutinize the smaller details involving each piece of equipment. 6. Some things need better explanations, such as the above-mentioned point, and also some stats. I still do not do what diplomacy does, at all, and I am 18 hours into the game!7. The music doesn't loop well, becomes repetitive, and still times out too often. I got very bored of the music after a few hours, because it only changes based on situation and it's always the same tracks for the same situations.8. Fishing isn't even a minigame, you steer your ship into a school of fish and if you are slow enough, you can press a button to catch fish. That's it. I always enjoy fishing minigames, and this was rather disappointing when I finally came around to doing it. Likewise, there's the same simplicity in obtaining treasure deposits on land or exploring sunken ship remains. You control the main character with your choice of ships and gear, sail around and explore the world, unlocking maps sections at the various cartographer stations. Following the main story quest progresses the story, but doing side quests gives you money, resources, and experience, allowing you to level up and choose skill tree upgrades. All of the merchant/neutral and navy/opposition ships level up with you as well, so it's not a game where you can completely out-level your opponents through grinding. Repeat multiple fetch quests and single-ship hunting quests as the side quests indicate, rinse and repeat. Be prepared to reset the game multiple times each play session due to multiple collision "Fatal Error" bugs, so remember to stop by each port that's not unfriendly to keep the autosaves updated.No issues with the default controller controls, everything works well. Keyboard works fine, I only tested it minimally. Mouse controls are reportedly coming but not yet available.As mentioned, it looks great.The music could use much improvementHere's my first hour or so with the game:I do not think it's quite worth the asking price of $24.99 in its current state. has a good concept and some fun aspects of gameplay, it needs a bit of QoL updates to smooth out the game and also the crash bugs need to be fixed. Looking at the reviews and comments from others, I see I am not the only one to face these issues, so it's systemic to the game. Even though I have not yet finished the game, I have seen enough in 18 hours to know all of the different aspects of gameplay that the game offers, and I think it's fair to say that it needs some work before I can make an actual recommendation for my friends and audience.Current score: 5/10 (June 5, 2021)Not recommended in its current state, especially for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Eh ... this game actually started out as a very enjoyable experience for me, but began dragging full-anchor by mid-to-late-game progression, and I just stopped. Can't quite muster the desire to actually finish it at this point.--- To bring up a point addressed in many other reviews: as of this review, keyboard controls can be remapped, and mouse controls are (almost) fully usable except maybe for a couple menu things. I had a lot of special abilities mapped to mouse buttons. ---At the beginning, ship-on-ship combat feels like a involved affair, where you're caring about positioning, trying to fake out your opponent into missing their shots, slowly whittling down their sails and then their hull. A few of the low-tier abilities are very, very situational and can give you a moderate edge, but nothing crazy. In all honesty, these particular fights do start to feel like they go on a bit  long, really, but they're enjoyable to me. I know other reviewers don't like that there's no aim-assist for the volleys, but this ended up being my favorite feature in the combat system, requiring timing, skill, and a good eye in order to land your shots.But then it gets crazy.I don't know why, but later on, the skills go off the deep end in terms of insane magical abilities, to the point where you're shooting a freakin' high-powered laser sniper shot off the bow of your Age of Sail pirate brig ... Or temporarily turning yourself into a ghost ship that . Or letting off a massive AoE fireworks display that melts 5 enemies at once and out-ranges all enemy cannon fire. Or firing off a homing fireball that cannot be evaded (unless you turn yourself into a ghost ship). Et cetera and so forth.Those 10 minute fights? Over in about 20 seconds now. My laser shot (sorry, 'Voodoo Beam'), many times, would instantly vaporize a ship under the right circumstances. After a few WAH HAH HAH I'M SO POWERFUL LOOK AT ME NOW moments it actually ... gets really dull. It's the One Punch Man dilemma - overwhelming power is actually pretty boring.And unfortunately, combat is the bread and butter of this game. There are lots of other aspects in this game but they're very shallow.Trading... this is typical buy-low-sell-high stuff for a moderate profit. There are some quests for 'deliver X units of goods' for rewards. Prices fluctuate in real time based on how much of a commodity the port has on hand. However, picking up loot and cargo from sunken ships to re-sell at port seems to me to be  more profitable than doing any actual trading (trading is what I usually gravitate towards in these sorts of games). You end up reaping 100% profit on the items (since you don't pay for them, naturally) compared to maybe 10-20% profits from trading items. In terms of strict gameplay mechanics, what's the point of trading?Exploring... you pay cartographers to give you a map. You cannot map things by yourself.Fishing... technically in the game but it's a junk mechanic. There are a lot of things in this game where you just sail up to something and press space bar to harvest it. Buried treasure. Derelict ships. And ... fish. Fish are just another thing to press space bar at and then sell at port. (Don't get me wrong, by itself it's not a terrible mechanic, but it ends up being overused in this game). Also, incidentally, you cannot actually even begin fishing until doing optional quests in the mid-game progression, which gives you a fishing rod, which allows your ship to use ... fishing nets? Okay. But by this point it's not the best way to earn gold (that's still plundering imo) so, again, why bother? (It's also infuriating how early-game tutorial blurbs will tell you all about fishing, even when being able to fish is locked behind another few hours of progression.Town management becomes a thing later ... in which you throw gold at your town in order to make it better, so it automatically upgrades itself. That appears to be the extent of your involvement, Governor.The story is pretty forgettable, a routine revenge plot that you've probably already seen 1000 times over by now. I'd use spoiler tags on the previous sentence but that's the games starting point within the first 5 minutes, it's not like it's a big reveal.The difficulty multipliers you can select at the start are a bit weird to me. Like, you get the most loot and such out of doing ... a permadeath mode? Now, I'm not a stranger to permadeath modes, I've used it elsewhere, but ...  It's a progression along a story. So, if you ever die and have to restart ... you have to go through all of the story, again, from the beginning. If permadeath ended up being its own sandbox mode, I'd rate this game much more favorably as a whole, but it ain't.In-game documentation and tooltips are lacking. For example, I still have literally no idea what 'diplomacy' is actually supposed to affect in this game. As far as I know, the game doesn't actually tell you.Outer bounds of the map are locked off in an annoying and lazy way ... if you sail too close to the edge, the game forcefully makes you turn around and sail back. As in, you lose control of your ship while this happens. NPCs are  affected by this and can sail out as far as they want.Something to pick up on sale if you want to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game, as it was recommended based on my play of Windward. Adding story and enhanced combat to that game's exploration and trading sounded fun! Unfortunately after 5+ hours, I stopped hoping the fun would arrived and gave up in frustration.Other's have pointed out that the game is a repetitive grind, but you might be thinking, "I don't mind a grind, I just like sailing around and doing pirate things!"  Well, sorry about that, there are just too many issues with orientation, navigation, and exploration:Orientation: the sameness of the art used for the procedural maps, combined with the constrained view area means that it frequently hard to tell where you are. There are always going to be important things you can't see, just off screen, even zoomed out to the maximum extent. The promotional images and video show many views from the ship perspective looking to the horizon... this is a lie, you cannot do this in game. There is an indicator of the direction to your next quest objective, but it's no substitute for being able to orient yourself. I often had to toggle between the main view and the map, just to know what was going on...Which brings me to, Navigation: there's a core mechanic that the map on fills in when you pay a vendor for it, which reveals a tiny section of the map... one that is completely devoid of labels until you zoom in too closely to see much of the map itself. Add to this that the cost of map sections is prohibitively expensive, and at least in the early game, you have no map. The trading system relies on rumors as to which towns need which goods... but good luck knowing were anything is. The map sections get progressively more expensive to buy as well, so a primary action of a sailing game, navigation is locked behind this irritating mechanic.Finally, Exploration: because sailing to new locations does not fill in the map, exploration is basically useless, because orientation is so difficult, it doesn't do you much good anyway. There's more though: the game feels simultaneously empty and crowded. All of the islands are so close together, that there's no feeling of open seas, and capturing ships always takes place near a settlement and usually with other ships around. There's a constant danger that your sea battle will drift into range of a town you can't see, meaning you can't trade there ever again. At the same time... when you're not near a town, you very quickly run into the message that "these seas are too dangerous, turn back."  There's no sense that this is a world for exploring, and when you do explore, you're not filling in a map anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Kin' o' Seas feels like a one long grind through an empty sea, swabbin' decks, suckin' on lemons and tossin' th' peels from a crow’s nest at passin' seagulls while waitin' fer somethin' excitin' t' happen. Th' grind it has goin' fer it, hidden under th' cute, colorful graphics, fore momentum and th' promise o' a next sunken ship be just th' worst scourge o' th' seven seas.Everyone remembers Sid Meier’s Pirates, right? Yeah, this isn’t it. It may draw some similarities, but this is a much more bare-bones, grindy, arcadey, unexciting, ship-to-ship combat focused sea sandbox. There’s also a disturbing lack of swashbuckling and wooing of maidens. Even though the game lets you choose a character, it’s only for story purposes and accompanying cutscenes. You are your ship here.Story premise is very simple, serviceable, but not really captivating. It does have charming illustrations and character art for its presentation. You pick one of the two available characters, Marylou or Luky, children of the current King of Seas, and get sent on a mission. While you’re chasing ghost ships, your father picks Davy Jones’ locker as his new favorite holiday spot, you’re accused of getting him tickets for it and the Royal Navy tries to send you there with him. Cue pirates dragging your wet, but still kicking bones to their lair, throwing some exposition at you and shooing you on your merry, buccaneering way.You quickly realize the entire sandbox is made to be grindy and chafing in the long run, like grains of sand stuck in your breeches. It’s the name of the game here in everything you do. From story missions gating content to side quests, ship combat, treasure hunting, fishing and port conquering. You’ll be repeating a small number of activities so many times it’s going to start feeling like you’re being keelhauled with your own ship. How hard that’s going to be you can decide for yourself by picking one of the five difficulties the game presents you, differing only whether you lose your ship and inventory or not. Last one, King of Seas, offers permadeath.Side quests can be picked up at any port. There’s a few combat oriented ones, but most fall under fetch quests. Fishing can be started at a certain point in-game and is a somewhat good money maker at later fishing levels. But, it is again, a grind, with some types of fish you need to catch to upgrade your fishing rod seemingly having Korean MMO type drop chances. There are treasure ships roaming about, carrying sunken treasure maps that may drop as loot, but after 18 hours and many sunken ships, I haven’t found a single map from them. All the maps I got came from an end game story quest.Markets and trading also play a role, but each port only has one type of goods in surplus, one in deficit and the market doesn’t really change, making it all overly simplistic. It also feels extremely easy to make money, like there’s pieces of eight instead of droplets raining in those thunderstorms you pass through. Once the game unlocks conquering forts, you can attack and take over any island, making it a pirate port. You can also upgrade them, which is where most of the money will go. But, if you lose the port, it resets everything you’ve purchased and you need to start from scratch. Talk about hornswoggling you out of your hard earned booty. And the fort combat is just another dull task. Ports tend to change allegiances quickly, no matter what level their upgrades are, since they’re apparently made of salted sardines sprinkled with butter and held together by rum and spit.There’s also a vast expanse of sea between you and your objectives and you’ll be sailing way more than doing anything else. You’ll run into random crates, fishing spots, drowning sailors and some hazards, but apart from ships and ports, that’s all there is to it. It all starts looking samey after a while. The idea of adding and filling in pieces of the map by searching for a cartographer feels novel for the first few times, then it also starts being a chore. All of it feels like very little content stretched out over a needlessly large, procedurally generated map with very little thar she blows moments.The map has a weird zoom that controls slowly and wonkily with the controller, not even centering the map on you when you open it. And the game still lacks proper support for mouse and keyboard. But, looking at the port and ship menus, it’s obvious it wasn’t really made with them in mind. Another rather annoying thing is how the game instantly spawns a few military ships whenever you attack a port, while your ships are usually nowhere to be seen. And there’s tons of other little annoying mechanics just rubbing shoulders and cackling with the grind.It doesn’t all feel like you’re marooned on a deserted island with a single coconut tree. Ship combat, as arcadey as it is, is done well and feels very smooth. It’s easy to learn, hard to master. There are 5 ships on offer, from a lowly sloop to the mighty galleon. They all have different stats and once bought can be freely swapped at any port you own. Simple controls with only three sail stages, wind directions and three health bars, for your crew, sails and hull feel right at home here, allowing for some fast paced piracy, plundering and scuttling of ships. There’s no morale in play here, the crew are all old salts and just happy to be pirates, win or lose.Combine that with an excellent and well thought out ship parts upgrade system that even changes your ship visually with every part, an interesting perks system allowing you to become, among other things, a pirate voodoo princess, and a sizeable set of combat skills wrapped into magic and science and you get a very shiver me timbers part of the game. There’s even a great in-game way to reset your perk points and I was pleasantly surprised when I discovered that one.Having no complex designs or mechanics doesn’t necessarily need to be a bad thing. But, most things here feel overly simplified and toned down to a minimum. Like battening down the hatches before a coming storm. Great combat and upgrade systems don’t outweigh the shallow trading, repetitive side quests, tediousness of tasks, and most of all, the grind and gating of content behind it. It looks and feels like a promising pirate sandbox, but it’s not particularly rousing at the moment. Replayability is also an issue. You can’t continue playing after the story, which is a bonkers decision, since the game lends itself to that amazingly. If you start a new difficulty, you start from scratch and that’s a very mind-numbing promise. If you’re looking for a simple pirate life, a ship combat game and don’t mind the intense grind, mutiny on this review and go play it. Otherwise, make it walk the plank. PC specs: It was smooth sailing all the way on an i7-7700K, RTX2070, 32GB of RAM and an SSD.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been gaming for over 30 years, started on the SNES in my early teens, and never stopped. i've seen games change alot, and the gaming industry too. Recently, there's been a trend that kinda burnt me out, and for a lack of better description I'll call it "focus-stealing games". I mean by that all those games that want you top play them, and them only.You know, the ones that reward you with some shennanigans if you complete some daily challenge, and some more for a weekly challenge. The ones with some kind of game pass mechanics. The ones that either lock features behind playing them on a very regular basis, or making sure you need to in order to keep that feature you unlocked.  Elite Dangerous, for exemple, has fleet carriers that cost billions of ingame credits to buy, but also a weekly upkeep, meaning that you need to invest time to keep what you bought. Those games rely alot on the sunken cost fallacy to keep you hooked, and even for someone like me who knows it, it kinda works : either I'm playing along, or I'm disgruntled because something I wanted isn't truly reachable unless I use most of my scarce free time playing one single game.Long-winded introduction, eh ? Sorry about that, but I think providing context as to why gaming nowadays doesn't seem as fun as it should is useful. Enters King of Seas.Let me tell you one thing : this game is  like those games I described above. It doesn't try to hook you up with sunken cost fallacy and rewards from the daily grind, it just gives you a gameplay, a framework within which you use that gameplay, a bit of story, and there you go. It's not the biggest, most revolutionary game ever, and it's not trying to be. If anything, it's kind of a throwback, as it feels and plays alot like "Overboard !", which was released on PS1 something like 2 decades ago.There isn't much else to this game, either you like the gameplay itself and then you'll enjoy it tremendously, or you don't and there will be nothing to keep you hooked. Which is basically what every game should be about, providing good gameplay for those who like the genre, and not trying to pose as anything else.So, what do you  get in this game ? Obviously, ships and pirates. Top down view.  Best played with a gamepad. Decent graphics. A story that is nothing special but entertainingly told, thanks to the peculiar character design. Tons of quests that are repeatable for the most part, ranging from "bring X to Y" to "Some Guy needs Some Stuff, find and fetch" to "Kill X enemies of type Y", and so on. Your run of the mill stereotypical RPG quests. You can also just wander around and pick stuff up, go looking for treasure maps, or just pick a fight or twelve with the navy.You start in a Sloop, a small, nimble ship with limited firepower but exceptionnal manoeuverability. You can have up to 5 different ships, each with their particularities. You've got the typical ship with massive cargo, the Flute, not very good in a fight and not especially manoeuverable, but great for trading, especially once geared for escape. The Brig is a slightly bigger ship than the starter one, and is basically an upgrade on every aspect while keeping the same spirit. The frigate boast better firepower and tankier stats at the cost of manoeuverability. Then you get the Galeon, a hulking beast of firepower and tankiness that couldn't recognize a sharp turn if it were biting its aft.All those ships can be outfitted with sails, hulls, canons, bullets, crew... Each providing stats. The game doesn't do a great job at explaining those stats, but you get it fast enough. Between the different ships and equipments, you can tailor your ship to fit exactly the playstyle you want. There are quite a few negative comments complaining that galeon isn't powerful or tanky enough, but man, I have no idea how they can say that. Give it armor, hull, magic defense, long range canons and the ability to steal life from nearby ships, and you get a ship that simply cannot be destroyed by ordinary enemies. Or use the brig to dart around enemies, dodging broadsides and stinging the enemy with hit and run tactics. Give fighting the finger with the flute, by boosting diplomacy so you're not easily spotted, an ability to GTFO real fast for a short while, and if need be, another ability to haul down the Jolly Roger and basically turn into an "ally" of everyone around for a while. Up to you.I bought this game for barely more than a coffee to go during a sale, the full price might be a bit steep for the content it has to offer, but the game more than makes up for it by being pure, raw, enjoyably fun gameplay. Recommended wholeheartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this but it's just lacking in so many areas.Nothing about the stats are clear and you have to go hunting for definitions. What are the units? Is armor a modifier or additional health? Is the "cooldown" stat in seconds, percentage, or straight minus or plus to what ever the points are? It's so unclear how the "sword" "shield" and "magic" stat are calculated when looking at cannons or other ship parts. A cannon that has the same stats as the one I'm using is somehow a "+2" sword.The menu system is atrocious and the rotary-style category selection is buggy and inaccurate with an Xbox Elite controller. Never mind that this game barely supports a mouse and keyboard.Damage scaling is way off based on your level. I basically got one-shot by one of the three cannonball from a lower tier ship. When he did kill me I lost the ship (difficulty level setting so I'm not miffed with that) but when I quit the game and loaded back in, the chest that was supposed to have my stuff in it was gone.Trading is just a pain as it doesn't give you a clear indication of your profit margins so you have to write down what you bought stuff for. I had to start a google doc to keep track of ports and what they produce and need. Why isn't that info in some "Captain's Log" or something? Not to mention the "high" and "low" prices are so close your profits are so minor it almost forces you to attack ships. And unless you're going to pickup every box you see in the water and grind repair kits or sail back to the farthest part of the map for free repairs, you're not going to make any money pirating.It's just not what I was really hoping it to be. It's a mediocre mobile/console game and not for anyone really looking for a Sid Meier's-esq pirate game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for something to scratch that Sid Meier's itch...keep looking, this ain't it. Combat: Too frustrating to be fun. Even once you get used to the controls all of the ship types handle like garbage and even lower level enemies, if you able to encounter one after you level up since enemies level with you, are able to destroy you faster than you can hope to destroy them. Your only options end up being snaking away from them taking the occasional shot or circling them and whittling their health down shot by shot, which takes forever because even on lower difficulties you are outmatched in every fight. There are no crew fights, if you get even close to an enemy ship your crew count will be decimated but I honestly couldn't tell the difference between a full crew and no crew. Same with the sails, completely destroying my enemy's sails did nothing to slow them down.Gameplay: You basically sale around avoiding enemy ships that chase you far too long if they see you, looking for merchant ships to pillage. Or you can trade, but you have to find the cities first, only exploring doesn't actually reveal the map, you have to buy that from a cartographer who's locations are also not marked on the map so you're sailing around blindly hoping to find one. Also you can't trade much because for some reason in this pirate game you can't actually capture enemy vessels and use them, you have to buy them, from one port on the entire map, and this is also the only port you can switch which ship you're using. Also there are items that give you a plus or minus for stats, but if you go into the details of the items sometimes the actual stats don't match what the overview is. To be clear, I had two different cannons, one was a higher level but the overview told me it would decrease my damage, but when I checked out the details...every stat was better. Also there is fishing but I think better poles are story locked, and there are levels and talent points but they really don't change the game enough to matter at all.Story: The writing is pretty meh, the artwork is cute, but the story is very textbook.Ultimately, this feels like an early beta at best. It had potential but if this is the final product it failed. I never felt like a pirate, let alone a King of Seas, I just felt like I had wasted 9 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I'd like to be writing a positive review of this game, but at this point I just can't.It looks really good, and I purchased it with the expectation that it looked like a bit of a spiritual successor to Windward, which I own and love.It just, isn't. The game is prettier, I'll give it that. The campaign storyline is a little cute. But that's really where the positives ended for me.The ship combat really ends up being about what skills you've been lucky enough to scavenge or find in ports and much less about actually applying cannonball to ship. The combat feels janky due to that, as you're spending most of your time trying to monitor skill cooldowns as well as maintain a position that feels advantageous to your opponent, while occasionally firing cannonballs if you can be bothered. They need to scale the skills back a bit to being a useful support to your ship, rather than the only items that literally matter at all.You'll spend a lot of time sailing around just looking for stuff to pick up until you find a ship to try and tackle, which you might vastly outgear and still lose to if it has a good skill that just can everything you have.This game has a lot of potential. I really hope that in the coming months they rectify a lot of the issues that are bothering a lot of people. I'm requesting a refund at this point due to really not having the spare money for a "same as Windward but worse" game to sit unplayed in my library. However if they fix these issues that it has, I'll hopefully purchase this game again when it's at a point that I can truly enjoy it.I hope the team manage that, because I hate writing negative reviews and returning stuff. I hope it grows into something much more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Sid Meyer comparisons are very apt. If you enjoyed that game I'm sure you'd like this one.Note, I haven't played this game all the way through yet. I'll update this review later to discuss if it gets old and more about the middle/end game, but some of that gets more subjective too, so without playing too much I feel I can comment on the design and what features I find enjoyable and fresh.Breaking the game down though:Controls: Fluid. Controller preferred but works for keyboard too, although an update next month will provide fixes for that.Settings: Simple yet flexibleGraphics: Top notchPerformance: No issuesStory: A narrative is blended with the tutorial and is built into the RPG with your enemies being the military and your allies pirates. Not much control over your character besides basically two gender options, but that's just a style choice. The writing is decent too.Mechanics: Sailing is fun and dynamic. Battle controls feel real. Again, very similar to Sid Meyer's Pirates in this respect. Also a simple trade system, ship upgrades, and inventory. Everything more complex and streamlined.Future development: More updates are planned for the future, so you might want to wait a few months or play now and look forward to new content.Other notes would be the world feels open. There's not the minigames like the exploring on land or dancing or dueling like in Sid Meyer's but despite that this game is much better.4.5/5. Maybe a little too archetypal to the RPG genre and uncreative, but that could just be because I'm old. It's still good and I recommend checking it out if you are at all a fan of RPGs, pirates, or sea travel.

It's graphics and sounds (plus music) is really amazing. It's gameplay is so fluid and it's U.I. is so nice.
