_childDocuments_.review: It's certainly not a terrible game but it's not at all what I was looking for. As a big fan of Side Meier's Pirates!, something I've played to death, I was hoping for something in the same vein that would offer a new and updated experience to the open world pirate genre. Unfortunately the gameplay feels less satisfying to me and the rpg mechanics, while neat in concept, just feel hollow and uninteresting.You choice of ship is limited to five options and each is but a framework for the playstyle. Between the Sloop, Flute, Brig, Frigate, and Galleon the only real differences are in the cargo hold, the number of cannons, and how fast/maneuverable the ship is. Everything else from damage to hit points is determined by your ship parts which work much more like a typical rpg format where you buy or find entire parts of your ship and just swap them out whenever you feel like it. Picked up a new hull while you are out at sea? No problem, you can just slap it on without issue. Another point I want to mention that aggravates me is that there's no tracking for your cannons. As in, your gunners always just shoot in a straight line and don't predict the movement of enemy ships. It makes accuracy a tedious chore and all but impossible to remain consistent.If you want something that's really just a story-based rpg game with a loose, fantasy pirate theme to it then you really might enjoy this game. However, if you really like a bit more realism and a lot more simulation and flexibility to the world you are sailing within then I still think Sid Meier's is the reigning champ despite all these long years.

_childDocuments_.review: A pirate game? Is this the new Sid Meier's Pirates? Or a new Assassin's Creed: Black Sails?Ah, no, sorry to disappoint you.The core gameplay is a little action game. You sail through a (randomly created) fantasy world by turning left/right and raising/lowering your sails. Avoid hitting rocks, islands, explosive barrels or other ships, which is sometimes a bit tricky because you don't see very far and can get rather fast with full sails. The faster you go, the harder it is to turn. The sea is full of stuff swimming around which you collect by sailing near to it. Islands are full of things to get as well, just approach them slowly. Or search one of the many shipwrecks to collect even more stuff.When you encounter other ships (the sea is full of them), you can fire your guns and try to sink them, and plunder what is left swimming on the surface. Combat is not very sophisticated, just circle your enemy and give him a broadside while avoiding his shots. Ports allow you to buy and sell goods, repair your ship (even for free in your hometown), lend money from the bank or hire sailors.You play the king's daughter, who escapes after her father was killed and she was accused of the murder. Pirates rescue you and accept you as one of their own, and so you upgrade/customize your ship with better cannons and useful special abilities while conducting (simple) missions and preparing to revenge your father.Simple, repetitive action game played with a controller, but with nice ship upgrades, trading, fishing and a story to follow.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific concept of a pirate ship game with RPG elements but... not well executed. Game looks decent though. However story is eh and the progress feels very slow. Currently doesn't have mouse and keyboard support but w/e I like using a controller.+Great RPG element of ship customization+Open world+Ship combat gets interesting with abilities-Story is rather uninteresting with an overdone plot and doesn't give you a good idea of how well prepared you are and should be for each coming mission after you unlock ship types.-Quest missions after unlocking ship type are boring and empty. Spend a lot of time to raise 100k, reach a high level... just why? Put some interesting missions here to do that, not just oh yeah do whatever to raise 100k or to reach this level.-Random tentacle attacks can appear right in front of you from time to time. Usually unavoidable as you can't turn in time and so insta loss of ~25% hull, sail, and crew hp. Why is is this a thing?-Having to eyeball the trajectory of your cannonball fire as you navigate is a real pain in the ass and in my opinion one of the biggest downsides. Yes real life pirates had it worse I'm sure. But really a simple line of fire would make a huge difference. You have no idea how annoying it is until you see for yourself.-Equipped ship parts are equipped to that particular ship type and cannot be transferred without a replacement. I really don't think I need separate 'loadouts' for each ship type. Some may find the ability to save and load item sets separate from ship class desirable if that becomes a feature.-Map can only be created piecewise by going to that specific area and finding the cartographer to purchase that segment. A real chore if you want map visibility.-Ship repair with kits is rather costlyNot really a good game but combat does make up for the boring story. However, needs improvement where it matters. I get that balancing is a bit of a process (which I'm sure is an understatement) and so will take some time. I hope improvements will be made. It could change my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: update (05/2023):so after more than a year and (at least) some updates i got it in sale and tested it again.i am speechless, ok there is mouse and keyboard and canon line of sight and other smal qol changes, but besides that the game still feels the same clunky way with keyboard than before. the map scroll is still a disaster, i never seen a game map where you had to scroll hundred times to zoom one cm (do you realy play or test your own game?). there might be monsters now but i don't even got that far, the game is just an strict DO NOT BUY(12/2021):Unfortunately the game lacks on all sides, I played the demo (over 6 months ago) and now tested the final version, and besides that they added mouse support (well, in PC games that should be standard, but who is I to judge developers, except for a PC gamer) nothing has felt changed.Pros:- the art styles looks pretty niceCons:- still no "full" mouse support (it is 100% made for controllers)- It still feels clunky in naval battles- no indicator how far or in which direction the cannonballs are flying- no minimap- you can still not change mission targets outside of the menu- you can still only see one mission target at a time- map zoom is the horror, turn the mouse wheel 100 times and you have zoomed in half, and you don't even zoom to your ship location but in the middle of the map- ingame zoom is too closemaybe after a few months i'll give the game another chance and then change my review, but at the moment i can't recommend it, especially not at full price

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game - it's cartoon pirates, after all. But there's some huge flaws that killed it for me.Firstly, the save system requires you to find a friendly port and dock there. Seems easy enough, except the ports don't show up on your map. It seems like the thing that a captain would note on their charts, but instead you have to sail around until you find one. Which means that if life makes you need to stop playing, you can't until you find one. Add to that that if there are enemy ships there (totally random) you can't dock, leaving you fighting (and maybe accidentally making the port hostile) when all you want to do it save.Secondly, the storyline makes you have to attack three ports. This is the absolute worst. None of your skills can effect them, leaving you sailing back and forth shooting at them, fighting off infinite spawning enemy ships, and hoping the auto-repair that the forts have doesn't kick in and undo everything you've done. And when you've managed that horrible grind once, you look at the other two you have to do and have to ask yourself if it's worth it; I decided no.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a close run thing whether to recommend this game or not. But after completing it in just 12 hours, I don't think I can. The game mechanics are very similar to another game called Windward. Personally, I think Windward did it better. Graphics are nice in this game and very colourful at times. The sound is fine. Story wise it's OK and I was curious as to how it would end. The problem is, that is all this game is. The replayability is pretty much non existent. No new game plus (just higher difficulties in a completely new game). If you wanted to 'complete' the map then the only option is load the save just before the final fight. You can't carry on from the end of the story. There is a serious difficulty spike about 2/3 of the way through the game. Which had me stumped and incredibly frustrated. It put me off playing the game for quite a while. And looking online, I'm certainly not the only person to experience this. The real problem in my opinion is the interface. At this point in time, there is no mouse support. In fairness, the game does tell you a gamepad is best. But after playing so many similar games to this, its very counter-intuitive to not be able to use a mouse. The map is also, I think, a bad decision in implementation. It was only after 10 hours (out of 12) that I realised that by zooming in, you could see port names. However, it makes the map tedious and slow to use. Finding a particular port is a real chore. The mechanic of having to visit a cartographer to reveal more of the map is also a chore. There's apparently 47 of these to find. However, one of the problems with this is those that border sections. Its only by visiting, going through a save/load screen, going into a dialogue selection, that you find out that you already have this section mapped, going through another set of menus, another save/load screen, and then back to play. It's a chore. More, it's annoying. The loot in this game is pretty good and there's plenty of variations, But, as tends to happen, you find yourself a build, and then its only incremental upgrades. The range of ships is small. There's a softlock linked to campaign play (not clear), that will stop you buying half the ships, regardless of your money. But after this is done, it was cheap and easy to upgrade. But in my opinion half the ships are useless, as the top 2/3 are so cheap. The other frustration is that your equipment stays on your old ship. So when you change ship, you have to put new equipment on. You can move the equipment from your old ship to your new one, but it's slow and annoying. I don't understand why there isn't an option to quickly move equipment to your new ship.Although I did enjoy some of my time with the game, there was a lot of times when I didn't and this coupled with the lack of replayability means I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's promising, but it needs some work. I've finished the story on the second difficulty, and it puts you back before the last boss-fight (Always hate it when they do this) Playing a galleon with a certain ability makes the game almost impossible to lose, turning it into a slog because they'll just burn your sails to a crisp and have you ever so slowly try to get to a nearby port to have them patched up again.I don't mind the grinding and I do enjoy the gameplay loop, but other than that, this game just needs a fair bit of work. Couple of things I'd suggest is more ships for one, better tooltips on what damage hits what and clarification on the upgrade system - aka what item is better than your current and why. (bullets often show to be an upgrade when all they do is kill things that much slower, not faster) often times it's a case of things being different rather than better, which the system utterly fails to highlight (like how some shots do hull damage and others sail)I've no idea if there's any new game+ stuff as once I finished with the game, I didn't really have much to go for, other than a high-score. TL:DR I'd say it's currently not worth the asking price. Needs more time in the oven, fix some bugs, add some more things. Shows promise though.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying- I love the game, I want it to expand. However, for the time being it gets a negative review because it plays like a demo. Advertising a game with an update road-map is understandable, but to me I'd rather a full release game with planned content to add, not a somewhat finished game, with the rest of the content planned out. Game is quite slow at first, picks up very quickly, then gets really hard really quick. I got quite far in and the jump from level 35 to level 60 happens in like 2 quests, there feels like a whooooole bunch of content that was skipped, but it wasn't. There is a jump from level 25 ish to 35 which isn't as bad. Side quests really don't give that much variety or exp, its protect this ship on a 2 minute sail with very few if any enemies, go talk to the cartogropher 2 minutes or less away, or something very similar. Then there is attempting to hunt particular ships. On my grind from 25 to 35 I really tried hunting navy ships in the middle for side quests for new equipment, and even near King's Port, basically nothing was spawning. The enemy AI is also very funky, very often when sailing near them they will turn into you when trying to avoid you, stop FAR to late, or just sail into you without even trying to turn. The level 50 boss and his two escorts did this to me a couple times when attempting the fight, effectively stunlocking and killing me.As for bugs, I only really ran into one, the level 50 bossfight boss set me on fire right before the cutscene, and dying, repairing, changing ships, etc, couldn't get rid of the visual and audio. It wasn't damaging my ship, just my patience. Had to close and restart the game.That being said, I like the game. I reallllly hope it gets expanded on a lot further. 5 ship types, where effectively one is the starter ship, one is useless, and the other 3 are basic ship types could be expanded upon to add more ships to the classes, galleons could get ships of the line, frigates could get a bit larger, brigs could get larger or faster, or bonuses for abilities or something, who knows. As for equipables, it would be cool to see randomly generated items kind of like path of exile or diablo, as running into the same few items per slot gets kind of old. I get it with the abilities, and the abilities are great fun don't get me wrong. But the items are just lacking in variety. I really want to see this game fleshed out more. It does not play like a full game. It plays like a demo. A feeling of missing content from the storyline that leads to level gaps that require hours of mindless grinding, lackluster variety in ships and items, odd enemy AI, sparse enemy spawns making hunting during downtime or for sidequests difficult and time consuming, distinct rarity of Commanders to kill for rare loot ( I only encountered 2 on my 11 hour save outside of the quest ones ), and more. Great game, definitely needs more content. I will HAPPILY change this review positive when it feels more fleshed out and a few issues are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a middle thumb, it is not good enough for me to recommend it to anyone else to play but it isn't bad enough for me to steer anyone away from it if they actively asked me.The story is extremely generic, I wonder if any effort went into its telling at all tbh. It is clear this was made by a small team but they could not even be bothered to make enough unique characters, some of the portraits are used for multiple characters just with differing colours. The combat is fine for a start but becomes extremely repetitive very quickly, I am not sure that the number of cannons make any difference at all, I was doing the same damage in my 10 cannon brig than I did with the starter ship. The levelling is very boring, it is just incremental upgrades such as 1% more speed, 1% more range on cannons etc. Nothing interesting, just all very by the book.The levelling is almost pointless, as you level up and get stronger the enemies around you do the same so you never really feel powerful, you just feel the same as everyone else. There is no combination of upgrades that can give you the edge in combat, you are purely relying on the pretty terrible AI and their inability to captain their own ships.The trading system is fine but you can get so much gold so quickly that trading quickly becomes obsolete, you get to the point very early in the game of having so much gold you never have to trade ever again. The exploration is fine but quickly becomes pointless too, as mentioned previously you get so much gold so fast that exploring becomes meaningless. Upgrades are also thrown at you during quests and sinking ships on your travels to and from objectives. There is never a reason to actively go exploring.Progression is locked behind arbitrary progression, for example you start off with a very small basic ship. The carpenter can sell you 4 other ships types, some are aimed at trading, some at combat and some at a mix of both. For a start however you cannot have access to the other 4 types of ships, why not you ask? You just can't. You do a couple of fetch quests that would make any mobile gamer beam with joy and for some reason the carpenter can sell you those additional ship types. Why you ask? No idea, just because. There are lots of little things that are just bad as well such as the rotary menus that do not work properly with a controller, this would be fine if there were alternative control schemes but mouse and keyboard is worse. If you are going to only provide proper support for one control scheme, at least make sure it works properly. All in all a very mediocre to poor game that could have been so much more. If you like near pointless grinding and fetch quest after fetch quest then this is the game for you. If you wanted something with even a modicum of depth, go somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this I was expecting a trading game where you get richer over time and buy bigger and better ships and continue this loop until you finish the story, what I was NOT expecting is everything this game offered, it had Loot, loot rarity, abilities, different ships with unique designs, boss fights, talent tree and an amazing immersive atmosphere. That last point in particular was a very strong point in this, having headphones or surround sound will do this justice, the sound design was top notch, sailing with that ambiance and sudden sea creatures popping up here and there gave real life to this game, some surprise tentacles too......no, not those kinds of tentacles.As clearly shown by how much time I spent in this game I really liked it but it has many faults too, for starters the movement can get tedious and repetitive because its so slow and deliberate, I know what they were going for and it works but the design itself with missions being too far apart, the ship being so slow work against it. There are also a lot of bugs that can happen like quests not registering as completed, selection highlight goes to random places whenever entering a shop, Each time you get a quest a small cutscene appears, sound bugs, visual hbugs, control bugs all are present. With all its flaws the game still managed to remain interesting throughout, hell, if Sea of Theives was half as creative as this game it wouldve been my favorite game.TLDR;Pros:- Fun gameplay- Creative abilities and combat and item pool- Immersion- Good musicCons:- Many bugs here and there- Poor mission design- Slow movementOverall Score 9/10-

_childDocuments_.review: Only get on sale.This game is clearly inspired by Sid Meier's Pirates, but doesn't hit the same highs that game does.My first few minutes were quite promising. I engaged in a lengthy ship fight, learning the controls and applying past experience. It still took me a few minutes to kill just one ship, and this was the tutorial! My first fight against two ships was accidental as I aggro'd a second ship without meaning to, and I sank to those two ships. Unfortunately this fun difficulty quickly faded due to this games loot grind. You will quickly acquire upgrades and abilities that trivializes combat, such as shooting a laser from the front of the ship to turning your cannons into machine guns.I haven't finished the story, and I have no intention to.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not good. It's not bad. It's just okay. That's the best way I can describe my experience. I want to recommend this game but there are simply too many flaws in its design. Some of them are fixable and others are permanent.If you're looking for a story driven pirate RPG then buy the game when it's on sale.There are a few things that ruin the immersion which is listed out.1. The game is more built around RPG elements than realistic naval combat which is kind of a shame. I was always wondering why my 24 gun Frigate was being beat by 6 gun Sloops until I realized that ship equipment stats have much more of an impact.2. Having a crew serves little to no purpose. Had many experiences where my crew were all dead and everything worked perfectly fine.3. There's a Kraken that appears practically out of nowhere and hits you 90% of the time while dealing lots of damage, unless you're lucky and manage to dodge it because you're going over 10 knots. I have yet to see anything in the story mention the Kraken too.4. You cannot take back previously spent skill points. If you accidentally spent a skill point on something you didn't want then you're screwed.5. Cargo is essentially useless for making money once you progress a little bit through because the trade system in the ports is very incoherent and cargo from sunken ships is much less profitable than the ship equipment it gives.6. There is no minimap UI and the game pauses whenever you open the map which makes navigation really annoying. (Especially when you take a mission to hunt down another ship because it's constantly moving)7. Every time the map opens the music stops.8.
_childDocuments_.name: King of Seas

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, sailing and battle very similar to the old Sid Meier "pirates!". Other than full controller support, there's no reason to play this if you have pirates! I'm also not going to harp on things that are commonly addressed in other reviews (i.e. lack of camera rotate). No ship boarding, only sinking. Also, aiming is bad - the old game(s) had a larger margin of error - in this game your aim needs to be perfect. Game would benefit from some lines to help aim cannons and abilities (example, voodoo boom).Stat explanation is hidden. You have both armor and hull health. Trader stats only affect carpenter, not market. Still don't know what diplomacy stat means. Also, the better quality the item, the worse the stats, but you get more perks. So, a base item has no perks. A green item gets 1 perk. A blue item gets 2 perks, but the stats are lower than the green item. Supposedly it's still better? The further you get in the game the more you find that isn't explained. The notifications that "your base is under attack" is too easy to miss. It looks exactly like the message that "your friend are attacking a base". You have about 2 seconds to read a message onscreen, heaven forbid you were doing anything, and there's no log to review if you missed it. Also, trading/banking is not logical. You apparently start the game with infinite bank space that you can retrieve in any city. So, there's no reason for you ever to carry anything in your cargo hold. No real reason to use ships with large holds. Every time you visit a city, dump everything into the bank. Retrieve it wherever you need it. Making money through " buy low, sell high" is extremely easy said you don't actually have to transport anything - just pull whatever is selling high from the bank wherever you are. The game encouragers you too use a joystick, but for me moving the wheel is really difficult. It might be my joystick, but it gets "stuck" on the wrong place and won't move. Again, the main is so small that if you're off by a little, you end in the wrong category. I'm other words, you have about 10 degree to must labs in to hit your mark, but the categories are also sticky, so once you hit a mark you need to rotate 20 degrees to unlock it. After a while this becomes really frustrating. Maybe it's just my particular joystick, idk...The game is "fine". It's hard to find a good pirate game. As I said, no reason to play this if you have pirates! This is very repetitive, and after a while you miss all the other mini games in pirates, like boarding, romance, and taking over towns. This game has 3 factions, you don't get to pick, and 2 of them won't ever turn on you no matter how bad your reputation. Probably the best thing about this game is that it has gotten me back into the Sid Meier's version.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first got the game I struggled with the tutorial a bit and almost regretted my purchase, but once you get past that the real fun begins - I've done two playthroughs now so feel qualified to say that it genuinely is a fun game BUT it's more of a skill based one and so while it could be easier, earning the skills and making sharp turns with sails almost feels MORE rewarding as you start getting the hang of it. Combat is the not easiest at the beginning when you lack a decent sized ship and special powers but late game with better ships, more fun magic (where would we be without haunted ship?) and a better understanding of the mechanics make it worth while. I quite like the unique art style and even sailing around doesn't get too boring since there's new battles, ports to conquer and little whale animations to keep the visuals alive. Bigger ships can be more of an inconvenience for agility despite higher 'health' and damage, but I think part of the fun is finding the ship that works best for your strategy, I like the galleon myself since it's a nice middle ground, but the game encourages you to try all of them with the different abilities for each ship.Do I think it's for everyone? Perhaps not, it's very much a ship battle game with no first person pirate fighting, but honestly now I'm familiar with it I do enjoy that aspect, and strategising how to take over the best ports for profits/defence. I would like some kind of fast travel/warp when getting across from one side of the map to the other but it's a minor inconvenience at most.

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a giant no from me.The graphics are okay, the menus are okay and everything's clear.  Good gamma adjustment options and sufficient graphics options.  5 difficulty settings, which is very nice to see, so you can tune the difficulty enough that you'll probably be happy with one of the 5 settings.  Looking good so far.  Not too keen on the character drawings, and in one scene someone's holding a sword backwards, but whatever.  Gameplay is more important, right?  Well, yeah, if you can play.Gameplay, what I got to see of it, seemed half decent if a bit simple but it was going well until I got to the first tutorial fight.  Keyboard controls seem to work well, even though the game recommends a controller, however after that first fight the wasd keys, and some other keys, refused to respond.  Yep, I was stuck in the ocean and couldn't do anything.  The ESC key didn't even work so I couldn't quit through the menu.  Okay, alt-f4.  Restart.Um... start new game but no load or continue option?  Why?  I played for 15 minutes already.  No save?  Ugh... okay.  Auto saves are all well and good, but they need to kick in after each section.  I don't want to do the first "sail here then sail back" mission over and over again if the game keeps messing up.  It's rudimentary and boring.  The game should save after each section of what amounts to the tutorial section of the game.  It doesn't, so that's a big negative right off the hop.So, I played through again, watching unskippable cutscenes, skipping the dialogue that I could skip.  I got back to where i was in about 10 minutes since I didn't need to re-read the dialogue.  Then a similar issue happened.  The wasd keys stopped working.  ESC seemed to work this time.  I had my opes up.  Maybe it saved this time.  The menu seems to be working so I was able to hit ESC and go back to the main menu.  I was hoping it would have saved and I could just continue but no, all I had was the option to start a new game.Nope.  I'm done.  Refund requested.  I'm not dealing with this garbage.  There should be continual saves throughout the tutorial section, but honestly the game simply should have working controls.  It's too bad, this game didn't look terrible and it felt okay to play.  I think it's probably a decent, if simple, Pirates-like game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the game isnt worth 25 Bucks, there is not enough content yet. The sailing around and combat system is fun for a short while, even though some magic spells (yes, magic in a pirate game) are way overpowered, and some are useless. The trading system is not worth mentioning, since selling dropped equipment is worth much more then any ship could ever hold in cargo. The side quests are not really worth it either, since you could just kill 2-3 ships and get the same amount of exp and way more gold if you sell just one piece of equipment they dropped.For the main questline you have to fulfill arbitrary objectives, like get 100k gold or reach level 35, which is just bad from a gamedesign standpoint. Its like saying: "please grind now, for some hours, have fun !". The Story is not worth mentioning either, since you could explain everything in 3 sentences, without leaving out any details.I stopped playing at level 32, when a navy barge (almost a starting ship) killed my epic and legendary equipped frigate (2nd "highest" ship you can get ) with two salvos and i would have to spend 50k on a new one. Im a fan of hardcore games, ala Dark Souls, and i have no problem with permadeath, as long as it is fair game. But this wasnt. The damage scaling makes  no sense at all and seems convoluted. That was just enough for me.I recommend waiting until the game drops to around 10 bucks. But if you really want to play it, just take care you dont spend more than 2 hour, to get a refund. You will see everything that game has to offer pretty fast and the mechanics dont change. Probably thats why they make you grind as main objectives.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really quite enjoying this so far, it's a lot of fun to play and the devs seem very responsive on their Discord so I'm hopeful that this will get some continued support.I do have a few gripes:Quest Tracking: Picking up a sidequest is all well and good but if you wanted to track it on the map you have to leave the port, open the menu, go to the logbook, move to side quests and then select the quest to track it. It's a pain and automatically tracking the last quest you picked up (or having the option to) would be great.Quest hand-ins: I can understand the need for cutscenes for story quests but for sidequests I would prefer not to be pulled out of the action, as soon as you get in the vicinity of the hand-in the cutscene starts. For side quests I would prefer a small toast pop up with completion and rewards, especially as the sidequests seem to pull from a small pool and as such, you will be doing the same ones over and over.Inventory: The radial menu is functional but rather unpleasant to use, I'm not sure what a nicer solution would be, a category list perhaps. _childDocuments_.review: A loot and fetch game with a singular ship combat mechanic that is intuitive but limited.Loot game: There is loot that spawns anywhere that scales with your level. Don't bother buying anything since there's a high chance of finding something better from digging up treasure as you are travelling. ******** Improvement: I would improve this by lowering the loot probability, while making it exceptionally valuable and the shops should sell expensive yet high base level stat ship components (no magic). Fetch game: Most of the quests and side quests have you travelling at least 5 IRL minutes just to reach the destination. When you get bored of fighting and looting so you just focus on getting the quest done, you point your ship to the destination and wait. Back and forth.******** Improvement: Since you have no choice to travel and looting is just unnecessary "padding," tell the story while travelling without only making it a cutscene when getting the quest and finishing the quest. Maybe give some secondary objectives along the way that can be done closer.Limited ship combat mechanics: Cannons only aim in a straight line, tried an true tactic from start to finish is circling around enemy ships, the only way to win is by destroying the enemy's hull, no boarding mechanic, no ship incapacitation by ruining sails or crew (they can always escape even with a dead crew and ruined sails). ******* Improvement: Cremates aren't dumb, they aim while predicting trajectory, they board if the enemy is stalled and is touching the other ship, they can fire at will if given the order, oh and they can fire independently on either side. Having the player do everything forces you to simplify the mechanics. It might be worth exploring the idea of implementing a 'give crew order' mechanic in the pause menu: Boarding (defend ship, partial boarding, committed boarding), Cannons (Fire at will, on signal, hold fire & steer), griefing (focus on enemy sails, focus on enemy hull, protect & repair own ship)This game can be good. The gameplay inspires me to find ways in making it better. But as is, the experience feels like a $10 game with the mechanics of a free-to-play game. Keep trying, there's untapped potential

_childDocuments_.review: King of Seas has a lot of potential, but it also suffers from a lot of drawbacks as well that really hinder the overall experience. It's one of those games where I really feel Steam should have more than "yes" & "no" options when it asks you "Do you recommend this game". But I'll list my pros and cons below. If you want more details, I'll link my full video review at the bottom.Pros:-Gorgeous overall art style-Decent sense of humor and self-awareness-Decent RPG-esque features, like level-based gear, in-game merchants & traders, etc.-Sound effects are spot-on-Extensive skill tree with lots of useful skills, which can all be upgraded for increased effectiveness.Cons:-Combat feels very stiff and clunky.-Music soundtrack consists of barely 4-5 tracks, which can be very annoying on long voyages.-The story itself feels like an unnecessary & rushed addition.-Menu navigation is downright unforgivably dreadful.In order to alter SFX or other options, you're required to quit the game and return to the main menu.-Camera zooms are extremely limited, with only 3 specific presets.-Players are unable to rotate the camera, which is very odd for an action-RPG.-Gameplay balance is incredibly inconsistent. At level 15, you can sink normal enemy ships that are up to level 25, if you know how to dodge at all,but an early-game level 15 boss required me to be almost level 30 to survive even 3 hits from him.I could go on, but if you're interested in more details, I just released a lengthy game review that goes over many more details:

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun playing the demo so I bought the home version.  Its a fun, single player, open world, casual, action-adventure pirate ship RPG.  You will want to customize your ship piece by piece as you gain gold and find better loot.  Getting gold isn't really an issue, you can loot other ships, do quests or trade.   The quests get old quickly, there isn't much difference in the way they are handed out or the characters involved.  Blow up ships, drop off cargo, and that's pretty much it.  There are some really fun customization options which have a big effect on your game style and keeps the game fresh.  I like testing out all the creative battle tools like throwing a fireball or sending your great white shark out to get them!  Some of these tools are clearly better than others but it's still enjoyable to test them all out and watch the animations.  Ship armour changes the way your ship looks.  You get a skill tree to invest points in which customizes your ship(s) even further.There is plenty of locations to discover across the procedurally generated map. I find myself wondering if I am supposed to be able to just dig up the treasure at the X without having first found the treasure map.  Resources are a plenty.   While most of the game is simple to discern I am left wondering what some of the descriptive icons for my ship stats could possibly be.  There isn't a tool tip to tell me.  Graphics are decent and there are nice touches as the weather changes or the volcano lights up the sky.At this stage of release I would have to say this is not a serious RPG but a fun one.  If you enjoy adventuring around casually as a pirate, modifying your ship to customize how you engage the navel battles in the way that works for you and don't mind skipping out of boring quests I would say to give it a try.  It is a fun, simple arcade style game.  ( I am okay with the keyboard controls for now)  I am enjoying it and see myself playing it for a while.  I prefer single player for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so look: this is a fun game. That said, there are a number of things that could and should be changed to make it better. Firstly, the trade system is kinda superfluous and has very little worth when selling off excess gear will net you as much if not(usually) far more money. Next, the travel can get a bit tedious. When you start at your home base, travel across all of creation only to get gang-banged to death by a random patrol ship and their four buddies, it gets really old really fast. Finally, the power comparison; you get gear of varied degrees from enchanted to legendary, and it never makes you feel any more powerful than the rank and file opponents you'll encounter, which usually ranges from minor annoyance to absolutely infuriating.The game otherwise is fun and pretty, and you can easily get into a groove of running random missions and enjoying the gorgeous sea. It's a fantastic concept with great bones, but it needs community and primarily dev attention to really reach its potential. I'd suggest buying it on sale, but with any luck these issues will be addressed and, if that were the case, I'd be totally fine with paying full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Aspects I like about this game:- keyboard controls and gamepad/controller compatible. No mouse is needed, so it is perfectly working on a laptop during a journey. Thankfully it is not one of those "point and click" games! (use WASD to steer your ship, fire with "left arrow key" or "right arrow key" and zoom with "upper arrow key/lower arrow key")- the combat system is about predicting the enemy's movement, your cannonball's speed and partially the wind direction. The basics are very easy to learn, but hard to master. Spaming the steerboard or portside cannons won't lead to a victory.- thanks to the controls and combat system intelligence is rewarded: the player can sink larger ships than his, but if the player acts headless and short-sighted even his largest frigate will struggle against a small yet fast sloop.- lots of costumization: though I played around 90 minutes I managed to aquire different coloured sails, interesting new hulls etc. - Oh! And there is a story with funny characters!- last but not least: it is not a cheap copy of Sid Meier's Pirates, but a fun little action game with RPG elements!Aspects I don't like that much about this game:- Although I rush through most "early-game dialogues", as I already played the first quests during the Demo, it takes a bit to start your own adventure. After 90 minutes I'm still not done with the first quest(s), but this could be due to my lack of "gamer skills". ;D Maybe I am just impatient.Be aware that it could take you an afternoon to get started properly.- the tutorial and the first quests start with restricted options (buying new ships is blocked, e.g.). I understand that this is necessary to train the player the first time he/she/it plays, but this could be redundant in future playthroughs.-> It might be skippable. I'm not sure about this.- the best part of the game is not simply "unlocked" by playing the main quest/story, but level 35 has to be reached by the player in order to access a series of features. (I don't want to spoil too much, so I won't specify them here) Again, this is okay the first time you play it, but it could be redundant in future playthroughs.Nonetheless I recommend this cute, funny pirate game! As Seahawk would put it:"Aaaaadveeeeeenture!"

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a demo which allows one hour of gameplay before it times out and really gives a good example of what the game is all about. It has some good UI elements and interesting design choices like breaking the health of the ships into categories (hull, sails, crew). Leveling a ship seems intuitive and very RPG-y: get new cannons, compare with current cannons, swap and carry on. The 3D art-style reminds me a bit of Sea of Thieves as well - all good things.However, what it might not convey are some of the mechanics that seem like oversight. I spent an hour in the demo and 30 minutes after having purchased the game and here's a peek into what I've found in that short amount of time:I played this on the games easy difficulty because it strikes me as the kind of game I'd want to just chill out and play without much challenge or fuss. I was sunk in the tutorial. Like, yeah, some of this falls under the "git gud" category but as I continued to play I couldn't seem to sink other ships. Again, some of this is "git gud" but I noticed, for example, that when my ships sails are damaged, I move slower - sure, that makes sense. Not for enemy ships it seems, though. They caught up with fully damaged sails waaaay too easily and quickly to the point where I was sunk - again and again. The sea monsters tentacles cause heaps of damage and storms damage sails and the hull over time as well. A few things like this added up very quickly to a frustrating and sinking feeling that I would not enjoy this game.I hate to say it, but this game, on easy, is too hard for me when I want to casually play a chill game. Maybe I'm a awful gamer and I'll just never git gud, but that's okay with me - for now I'll refund the game while I still can.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed the game on Corsair (The second hardest difficulty) and currently playing the Hardest difficulty, I genuinely don't understand the complaints about the game."The game is too much of a grindfest"I mean yeah, the majority of the game is fighting ships, doing missions and sailing the seas. But I personally never found any issue with that. It's the main focus of the game, I don't expect more than what's advertised in demos or trailers. "The AI isn't that intelligent"I can agree that the ships are quite basic, following you from behind, or circling you if you circle them. however this isn't necessarily a bad thing, You still require environmental awareness and some level of strategy to defeat the higher tier ships."The exploration is tedious"Honestly, I didn't mind exploring the map, yes the speed of the fastest boat wasn't quite fast enough to be not warrant a bit of annoyance, I simply distracted myself with looting crates, fishing, attacking important ships, while heading in the rough direction I need to be, and before I knew it I was where I wanted to be. There are also two abilities to my knowledge that boost your ships speed for a good amount of time, making exploration a lot better."Abilities are generic"Honestly I enjoyed every ability, they're all unique and can be used in many different ways. Explosive barrel for example is perfect for luring the ships behind you, 'Pee on the cannons' is a more aggressive ability that gets you up and close with your cannons. Personally I found it one of the most over-powered abilities, however some that shared the same slot offered up debate on whether what to use, after all majority are situational.I'm not without my own complaints, I still think this an amazing game, it has a road-map so you can have a rough idea what kind of updates with be released, many will be focusing on a lot of other peoples' complaints.My review is less of a review on the game, but a counter-argument against bad reviews, I'm not a huge critic and it doesn't take much to make me love a game, and because of that mindset I can't agree with almost every bad review, the criticism is valid, no issue with that, but not recommending a game because of very, very minor issues people complain about just doesn't seem right.No game is perfect, this game advertised what it had, nothing extra, you got to play the demo before the game released, as I did. Don't expect more than what's shown, and don't be overly critical. You're just ruining the experience for yourself, keep an open mind, enjoy the game for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I have high hopes for this game currently it is not worth the buy. The game encourages you to spend most of your time exploring the map but has many aspects that make it annoying to explore. First, the map doesn't update with you you have to buy it from the cartographer. But you have to find the specific cartographer in a specific area to explore it but someone like me who has a terrible sense of direction will find it increasingly difficult to expand the map as the game progresses. I would appreciate the option of buying the maps from one cartographer or at least easier ways to find the cartographer. Not to mention there are ghost ships and tentacles that spring up from seemingly nowhere. The tentacles show bubbles on the surface when they are submerged but it looks too much like fishes, especially when you have your eyes on something else like the "minimap" trying to find something new. For a pirate game the combat consists of fighting one ship going to the nearest harbor spending half the money on repairing and then running from pirate hunters. Not to mention the second you move from a sloop you can say goodbye to combat prowess. you move much to slowly and fail to have either increased health or enough increased attack. Trading is practically nonexistent because you have to know what sells goods were and that isn't realistic unless your willing to spend an hour or more going to every port and recording what sells goods and then stumbling around till you find the resident cartographer. To summarize: Exploring is needlessly difficult, combat is unrealistic, and trading is incredibly hard to do till you've done a ton of exploration and recording in some document.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the popularity of Sea of Thieves, this isn't a single-player, first-person clone.  Rather, it feels like a love letter to Sid Meier's Pirates!  The game is played from an angled, nearly top-down view, and encourages continued play through ship upgrades, new powers, abilities, and challenges.  It's lacking in much of the minigame content of Pirates!, but the spirit of the older game is there.  Between this and the 2004 enhanced remake of Pirates!, I'd take the remake, but King of Seas is still a good game and stands strong on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: You can enjoy all the fun parts of a pirate's life without the crusty skin and bleeding gums.Watch my 6 minute review here: Here’s 3 reasons why you need to play King of Seas:1-Simple RPG Elements.  While there are many facets to the gameplay and controls, the methods for leveling up your ship and character abilities are so simple, and that’s what I love about King of Seas.  To improve your ship and customize it to your liking, both in terms of combat and cosmetics, you simply need gold to purchase upgrades from the carpenter in each port, of which there are so many to discover.  You can gain gold just by exploring the high seas, looting shipwrecks, but especially by completing side quests, which can be found, again at each port, in the tavern.2-Engaging Battle System.  In the early stages of the game, it may seem rather dull that you can shoot cannons out the left and right sides of your hull, so you might imagine another ship and you just doing a spinarooney while pelting each other with cannonballs.  But the game quickly introduces you to abilities, which can really turn the tide of your battle to your favor.  Some of these abilities are directional, like one which I found early on which allowed me to shoot fire off the bow of my ship and burn the enemy for 5 seconds, or one which shoots a fireball at opponents at more long range too.  These abilities do have a cool down, and when triggered, all abilities will enter their cooldown phase, so you do need to be strategic about which abilities to use and when to use them.3-Soothing Sound Design.  Whenever I see a pirate-themed game, I naturally expect bold, inspiring music like that in Pirates of the Caribbean (you know the song I’m talking about).  But when I opened the main menu for King of Seas, I was pleasantly surprised by a light acoustic guitar track that reminded me a lot of the music I’ve enjoyed in games like Alba: a Wildlife Adventure.  Don’t get me wrong, there are occasions when the theme turns moodier and more daunting, specifically as you sail through enemy territory or in uncharted waters, but overall, the tone and themes of the soundtrack are pleasant and satisfying, like the music you might hear as you sip your ale in the port tavern.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo many times and bought the game while it was on a pre-order discount. I have been enjoying my time with the game so far. The map seems to be a decent size and the world doesn't feel to empty with ships sailing around all the time. There is a story but you can go off and do other stuff as well. The combat isn't to bad and with the many specialist you can find  out at different ports and at different levels, you can be creative with how you deal with certain situations. Like for example, you can lure a ship between islands and toss a powder keg down to hit them or summon a giant cute shark to slow an enemy down while you make an escape. The fishing is an unlock you have to find but it's nothing special with it just being a simple push a button and wait. They probably could of added a small mini game to that but it is what it is. There is suppose to be an economy but I am not much of a trader  yet to understand enough of it to say whether it's a good system or not. There is boarding but it seems to be an ability I think? I've been boarded myself a few times when I got to close to an enemy ship. There is no capture other ships as far as I can tell but that seems fine to me.  There is a lot of loot in this game and each of it's own level and rarity! Currently there is no mouse support but will be changed later, I personally don't see a need for it as there is nothing it would add or help if it was added, but cry babies kept crying about it so the devs will be adding it later. I've also seen talk of people complaining about swapping skills to new ships, this is easily solved by equiping any other item to that part before you swap to a new ship. You wouldn't remove a hull from a ship to add to another without having to add a new one now would you? Just makes sense to meow. Anyway, I've played many pirate and naval games and I like this one but it is certainly not the best, but for the price it's pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I'm going to review this after the latest patch, which is chalk and cheese compared to the game pre-patched, where there were issues galore, the game is essentially Sid Meier's Pirates with just the ship side of things, there is a story that forces you down a path, and the difficulty level and also the game itself spikes and breaks wide open about halfway through. for a while the best thing to do is avoid combat, and work on picking up treasures and wrecks, to boost your ships powers. This has been helped hugely by the patch where all ships are available from the start, and augmentations can now be uninstalled to put on a new ship. selling aug's can be the best way to make easy money as they go for thousands later on. Best advice would be don't rush the story, doing the sandbox is most fun also. pick up missions at Taverns, these can level you up pretty quickly, Battles generally consist of tacking, running, using your powers then sending a broadside off when the opportunity arises, going toe to toe with anything is usually a very fast way to a watery grave.Also sucks when out of nowhere a tentacle will do some serious damage without warning, (think this has been patched to help players with this). overall this is fun and 20 quid. and when you can pull in some other pirates to join in a 3 on 3 battle then this is actually pretty stirring stuff. Probably in the good not great category, and a sandbox mode to get rid of the story would help down the line. recommend this to anyone with a POTC itch they need to scratch.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, but on sale. If you have a controller. Firstly I'll say to play the demo first for yourself and see what you're getting into with it. I really wish more companies would do that. I really appreciate that they not only put out a demo for it but HOW they did it. The hour time limit didn't count toward the time that I spent in the story cutscenes which was actually really refreshing. I hate when you actually DO get a demo, and it's an hour long and has 30-40 minutes of cutscenes and dialogue in it so when you are done you only got about 20-30 minutes of actual gameplay. When I was through with the demo and closed it out I had over an hour and a half and I didn't spend a lot of time in settings, I went straight into the game and came straight out when I was done so that was how long the game let me play. So not sure if that was intended, but if it was, a giant kudos to 3DClouds, Team17 and crew for allowing the potential customers to actually play the product. Now onto the meat of the review. I enjoyed the game, but there are some big issues with it that I found frustrating. There is a HUGE grind wall, there is a Preston Garvey factor in the late game that made me want to beat Capt. D. Morgen to death, however combat can be insanely fun and I found myself giggling madly as I would kite a ship around into a tentacle trap in the environment and then unleash my "welcome to hell" skill to finish them off. The devs have mentioned adding quality of life support so maybe they're going to address some of the grindfest that exists, but man it is tedious at times.  My time logged is basically because I wanted the equipment from the fishing missions (not as fun as it sounds) and so I had to drag myself all over the map dozens of times trying to find the spots to get all the fish for the equipment for my other ships. Pros:*Pretty game*Combat can be insanely fun*Story isn't too bad, you can play as either the son or the daughter so you're not locked to the same character*Sid Meier's Pirates vibes all over the placeCons:*No/Limited Keyboard & Mouse support*With as much customization as you have for the ship, you never can get a super close look at it which is a shame*Can't change the direction of the camera when sailing (or it didn't work for me) makes the dashing skills a pain when moving south. You run into things because you can't seen them. *Fishing section is an absolute grind and feels incomplete. None of the ports actually have any of the fish in demand, they're always selling at a loss, so I never sold any of them until...*The port capturing game is to King of Seas what the settlement guarding mini-game was to Fallout 4 and Capt. D. Morgen quickly becomes the King of Seas Preston Garvey with "XXX invasion ships have been seen off xxx and will attack in 6 minutes!" messages popping up roughly every 10-15 minutes. And you HAVE to go to take care of those because even if the port is fully leveled up and maxed out they can be easily captured back by the merchants. That means the ~200k gold you sunk into fully upgrading that port is now lost because they don't know how to handle cannons. *insert Justin Timberlake blank stare meme* Normally you would say "well then I just won't capture anything else, problem solved!" Well no I'm afraid not my friend because your pirate friends will do capturing (for which you get messages for as well) and then those ports will be raided, and so on, and so on....And you can't turn that off. Any of it. The saving grace to that is that it's very late game so hopefully other players won't encounter it for as long as I did because I was being OCD with ship parts, but my god. TLDR: This game feels like it is a one ship at a time updated version of Sid Meier's Pirates so if you really enjoyed that one I'd snag this one on sale unless you really love the demo. The game needs work, but there is a lot of fun to be had unless you don't have a controller. Then you're left without a paddle.

_childDocuments_.review: My mini-review for 'King of Seas' features in my Indies of the Week video here:'King of Seas' is an action roguelite primarily played from a top-down perspective. You play the as one of two characters, both heirs to the throne. The king, your father is murdered, and you are blamed, so take refuge amongst pirates, as you seek to clear your name.  The majority of the game is spent aboard your ship, a meagre sloop to start with, as you navigate the treacherous seas and complete quests. You are able to dock at ports to buy supplies, upgrade your ship and speak to the locals.  The dynamic world is procedurally generated, so expect surprises with each play, whether it’s a kraken’s tentacle grabbing you from below or a volcano erupting from above. The wind can be your best friend, or worst enemy, and you will need to manage your sails to survive, one button opens them, another closes them.  Combat requires strategy as you attempt to outmanoeuvre enemy ships and claim their bounty. You fire cannons from both flanks, and can equip skills and talents to suit your playstyle.  The game is quite slow to get going, with initial objectives rather rudimentary and the world itself a little empty. However, once you get your sea legs, develop the story, upgrade you ship and discover hidden treasure, sailing the seven seas becomes quite an addictive experience, partly down to the roguelite elements of the game. 'King of Seas' is a highly polished experience. The graphics are gorgeous, particularly when docking on islands and using the camera zoom feature to bring you closer to the action. The music is suitably nautical, and the script full of intrigue and betrayal.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love King of Seas. I truly did - I played the demo over and over again loved it so much I pre-ordered it (something I rarely do for any game). Unfortunately having now played the official release the demo I feel didn't paint a fair picture of just how "grindy" the game actually is. Yes, it's an RPG. Yes, it's expected to have some grinding to it, but there is such a thing as "too much", and considering other reviewers echoing the same I'm clearly not alone. Perhaps if the grinding didn't involveso much getting x amount of x items to x location over and over again I'd enjoy it more, but the rate at which is does it makes this game feel more like a Pirate trading game than a pirate action game. On the plus side when there are battles they feel fantastic, and intense. If you're willing to deal with the grinding aspect of it, it might even be for you. After a couple hours though, I needed to request a refund (something I also rarely do). If you're interested in getting this game I'd recommend watching some let's plays to see if it's something for you before you commit.

detailed_description: Exit the Gungeon is a small, arcade-style, spin-off 'dungeon climber' that immediately follows the adventures of the misfit Gungeoneers attempting to survive a series of increasingly dangerous elevators and countless waves of enemies. The Gungeon has become a paradox and is collapsing! Blessed by the magic of the Sorceress, your gun will change rapidly as you ascend the Gungeon. The better you play, and the higher your combo, the more powerful the form your gun will take. Battle against the last and most bitter of the Gundead at a frantic pace, slowing down just long enough to chat with some familiar faces… and a few new ones. Shifting rooms, enemies, bosses, bizarre weapons and items all combine to ensure that no two attempts to Exit the Gungeon are the same.

The place seems to be abandoned, so who sent the message? Help Jack Ballard find out the truth, exploring the darkest reaches and flooded areas teeming with dangerous predators, solving enigmas and puzzles while you try to survive. Are you afraid of depths? You will be. name: Ageless
detailed_description: Lost, confused and alone. What will Kiara do when she suddenly finds herself with the power to control the age of flora and fauna? An ability that was bestowed onto her by a magical obelisk. Traverse a puzzle-platforming world unlike any other, full of myths and magic. Embark on an emotional journey where you will be faced with tough choices and must confront your inner demons. Follow Kiara as she is thrown into a world of wonder and heart ache. Manipulate the age of animals and plant-life as you find your way through intricate environmental puzzles and defeat the merciless bosses that stand in your way. Become Ageless: Equipped with a mystical bow, master the art of becoming Ageless. Dash off animals and plant-life to navigate through interesting puzzles and intricate platforming challenges. Unique Ageing Mechanic: Play with the laws of nature to control the age of animals and plants in order to progress through exciting levels. Not your Average Fairy-tale: In a tragic story of loss and personal discovery, Kiara must decide if she will use her newfound powers to face her inner demons or run from them. New Worlds to Discover: Explore new areas filled with unique plants and animals as you progress through the game. Each level is hand drawn to pixel perfection to create a beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: As it is, I cannot recommend Ageless to others, which is a shame because it's a very good idea, and it has good execution... in parts. I bought it because I saw someone play and because it reminded me of Celeste (which is admittedly a large shadow cast on this game). In any case, here are my pros and cons:Pros- Adorable art style- The player character controls tightly- The aging mechanic adds a lot of variety to the puzzles- The music ranges from good to great- The story and characters are fairly engagingCons- The game is littered with glitches, which become more and more apparent as you go further in the game, and often time can mess with the gameplay severely. Even the achievements are bugged- While the player character reacts tightly, the rest of the world can be very janky, leading to some puzzle solutions only working some of the time, even when taking the exact same steps. A large problem in a precision platformer, especially one in which the environment plays such a crucial role- The difficulty varies wildly from one puzzle to another from the second biome onward, with some puzzle taking me 10 seconds while others would take me up to 20 minutes right afterwards- A lot of the difficulty is due to things being placed awkwardly and hard to shoot at, requiring tiny jumps or seemingly pixel perfect placement which, rather than give a sense of accomplishment once beaten, is only frustrating, not helped by the combination of a lot of shooting while jumping or falling already- Story feels very rushed, with it going by leaps at a time. An example that stands out to me is when the protagonist discusses the deuteragonist with a NPC, saying that she knew him, but doesn't know who he's turning into; all this despite having only talked to him 4 times- Related to the above, the game is rather short, with only 5 different biomes to explore, and lacks any kind of postgame or bonus levelsShould the developers take steps to fix at least the glitches, janky environment and awkward placement, I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement No. Yes (6 achievements). No. is a puzzle platformer where you can increase and decrease the age of a lifeform. Different lifeforms have different stages of their lifetime in addition to different behavior. There are 5 main areas in total, featuring different lifeforms in each area.- Different lifeforms in each area give a fresh perspective to the game- Optional, harder levels to solve- Time-limited levels can be annoying to finish- Some levels require you to execute actions with precisionsIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The visuals are alright. It uses 2D, sprite graphics with very little detail on the characters. Backgrounds have more details though, and the different theme in each area gives a variation to the mix. Personally, I liked the last area the most because of its mosaic presentation. However, the dialogue font looks out of touch with the rest of the game. I'm not sure if it's because the game fails to load the proper font or not since I'm not seeing the same font that is presented on the store page.The main character has a unique, relatable personality. It features a character that is not confident in herself, and although her negative perspective on things can be annoying sometimes, it works well on the ending. The subtle message will make it easier to reach more people, especially those who have the same personality as the main character. There are still some flaws in the storytelling, but it's not the main meat of the game anyway so you shouldn't worry much about it.The game is a puzzle platformer at its core with a focus on aging and de-aging lifeforms. Each lifeform has a specific usage on each of its life stages, allowing you to reach the previously inaccessible areas. Some lifeforms will also try to kill you, although they can still provide help in some way. The game features 5 main areas with different lifeforms, changing the game mechanics to some extent.Optional, harder levels are available in each area. The game is mostly linear, although some optional paths will be able to be reached as you progress, allowing you to tackle a harder level. You need to familiarize yourself with the existing mechanics to solve them, and it can take a while before you manage to do it since you need to re-learn everything in each area.The time-limited, "boss" levels ruin the game. It makes it hard to concentrate, especially since some areas have a very tight time limit. People who think fast might have no problem with this, but those who don't will be forced to do things by trial and error. Moreover, there is one problematic area that warps you to a place that you couldn't see on the other side, and since checkpoints in these types of levels are quite scarce, you are bound to redo the same area several times if you happened to be stuck.I finished the game in 13.1h. The game is easy at the beginning, although the optional and last few levels can prove to be problematic. Some solutions also might look impossible at first, but these kinds of solutions are usually not the intended ones. Most puzzles are of medium difficulty, with some requiring you to do some actions in precision. Luckily, the levels that need precise actions aren't at the same level as difficult puzzle games, although you might need to redo the level several times to develop muscle memory to solve them.The game doesn't save at the latest checkpoint. This can be problematic when you activated a checkpoint in the optional levels.Despite having a unique concept, I didn't feel anything special after playing . I feel like playing other puzzle platformers, which are mostly caused by the annoying time-limited levels and the different mechanics in each area. While I found the unique mechanic in each area a good addition to the game, I never feel like mastering the control. I always end up making mistakes whenever I wanted to age or de-age a lifeform and had to suffer because of that. The game is still good though, but I won't recommend it for a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I really like Ageless and I hope that in the future it'll find its target audience. Here are some remarks I made while reading other reviews:- If you feel like some levels are impossible: there is always an easier solution for every level and you've probably just overlooked it. I think the creators have really understood how to make a great and unique puzzle game that makes your own efforts feel really good. On the other hand I didn't have any problems with hit boxes or other character movements, so if you do then it's possible that some levels are nearly impossible.- If you're going to say that "this game is only one level repeating" or "bad story". Have you even played Ageless more than 2 hours? Did you even complete the tutorial? I don't say that you should've but don't act like you know everything about the game you haven't even played. There is so many different and interesting mechanisms during the journey and for example  is really rewarding in my opinion.- This last part goes for that one anonymous person who said that Ageless is too girl-gamer oriented: I'm sorry that this didn't resonate with your overflowing masculinity. Let's hope that in the future every game will be purely about WWII and that the only girl characters will have only as much personality as clothes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially Celeste Lite. It lacks a lot of the polish and fine detail of Celeste though, such as just talking about the character’s mental problems in the first minute instead of weaving an intricate story that doesn’t directly rely on that. The core gameplay is that the main character gets the ability to age living things up and down, and then she can become “ageless” thus the name and springboard or air dash off of any living object.  It’s an interesting concept though it feels like it’s a single note game, and there are just different enemies per chapter. There are a lot of difficulty spikes here as well, and oddly enough not in bonus rooms but on the main path.  However there are parts where Ageless feels awesome, but there are also a lot of parts where Ageless needed to get its controls or puzzles to be a little more developed. Pick this up if you loved Celeste, or just want a good platformer, though I would recommend getting Celeste over this.   If you’re not a fan of platformers, you’re probably not going to enjoy this one, even though it has a unique concept.

_childDocuments_.review: In Ageless, you take control of a young woman named Kiara who is currently aimless and looking for a purpose or at least something that will let her get unstuck. A reason to keep moving. So she went to a place called Pandora to search for a Gate that is rumored to grant Gifts. The rumor foretells that if you find Pandora’s Gate, you’ll be granted a Gift that you need, not that you want. Well, it’s been three years since Kiara first started looking. The only thing keeping her from turning back is the fact that she already sunk in three years of her life searching, so she might as well continue or die trying.On the day you join Kiara on her journey, she comes across a huge gap that she tried to jump, either thinking she could make it or was just too distracted by her thoughts, that causes her to fall. When she comes to, she’s greeted by a young man named Vi who ventured into Pandora to look for the Gate. For Vi, he went out to get a Gift in hopes to help his gravely ill little sister that will die any day now. Vi already got his gift of being able to create portals and is heading out, but he assured Kiara that the Gate is close and maybe come visit his town. Well, funnily enough it was really close and she is gifted the ability to age or de-age plants and animals. With this new ability, she sets out to journey through a mysterious world to help Vi, his little sister, and anyone she may come across out.Each area you’ll be traveling through will require you to go through multiple puzzle rooms that you can’t continue before solving them. This will require you to use your newfound skills, platforming skills, and your knowledge of each aspect present if you want to move to the next room. The most important aspect is Kiara’s gift. To age or de-age something, you’ll need to make sure you have the arrow you need drawn and aim it right at them. Depending on the plant/animal and which age stage they’re at, they’ll interact with the world differently. The first animal you’ll come across is this ancient Rhino. A young Rhino is harmless and just wants to eat plants, but aging it up to Prime will transform it into a charging Rhino that can charge through weak walls and kill you if you’re not careful. Early puzzles are pretty easy, but they become harder as you go on as platforming becomes tougher (partly since you’ll need to be precise and fast at times) and figuring out what you need to do with each plant/animal in the room takes longer.Kiara can also become ageless, which will stop time around her for a few seconds. In this mode, if Kiara is touching something that she can age, she can actually launch herself with the energy that is given by de-aging it. This lets her jump distances that she won’t be able to without it. Since what she’s touching launches the opposite direction, you can also launch what you’re touching if needed, though make sure you’re not going to launch yourself into spikes. Don’t worry if you do die, you’ll just respawn at the last checkpoint (which is put at the beginning of each room).If you’re worried about this becoming stale, Ageless does a good job at keeping it fresh. Not only will each area you go to differ based on aesthetics, but what animals and plants show up, how those animals/plants react to the world, and the gimmicks that it has. The next area you go to, Remnant, is a lush forest with gates requiring you to collect three butterflies, dolphins that you can ride during its Prime, and a plant that you can bounce off of or fire thorns depending on the age. One of my favorite areas appears late in the game, but I will say that the gimmick tied with it involves becoming a ghost to bypass walls or enemies.Ageless offers players to play it with a keyboard and mouse or with a controller, with no listed preference that the game might work better with. “But why mention this since most games offer this option” I hear you thinking. Well, while this is going to depend on your preference, there are pros and cons depending on which one you’ll be using that will affect gameplay more than some other puzzle platformers. Considering that the main mechanic is using your bow to age or de-age something, using a mouse will give you more control. Using a controller won’t give you as much control and you can easily throw your arrows off by slightly moving the stick right before releasing, but time does slightly slow down while aiming and you can see the path the arrow will take rather than only the reticle you’re aiming with. Personally, I played the whole game with a controller, with the occasional use of a mouse as some puzzle rooms are more difficult to complete when using a controller.There are collectibles that you can find and try to get. Most areas have Relics hidden around, which are just yellow capital A’s, that you can only see when you’re in ageless mode. Some Relics will be in a main puzzle room, while most will require you to enter a hidden room. To get to these, you have to first figure out how to solve the room puzzle (or find a way to get to Relics placed in required rooms), grab them in ageless mode, and make it to a checkpoint before you die. Each relic you collect will color in one more aspect of a diorama of that area, which you can get to through the overworld map. You can also use the overworld map to check on how many Relics you need left per area and select which part you want to jump to (though you do need to guess where you possibly missed a Relic).All in all, I enjoyed my time with Ageless. It was really creative building a game around aging and de-aging animals and plants and it keeps it up with each area. The story, while not delved into as much here, is engaging and has some surprises throughout. The only frustrations I had was how precise and fast you’ll need to be with some puzzles, as with those puzzle rooms I often knew what I had to do, but I was just slightly off. So if you’re someone that avoids puzzles that require you to be really precise, this might not be for you even if many puzzles don’t require it as much. For those that play with a controller, or thinking about buying this on the Switch, another con comes in as the aiming can get in your way of completing puzzles.If you’re at all interested in Ageless, but not exactly sure if you’ll like it, you can still try out the demo before committing to a purchase. The demo starts right after Kiara receives a Gift and ends once you finish Pandora. I certainly would not have picked this up as quickly without the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: As one of those indie darlings I was really looking forward too, I have to admit I was heartbroken here.  With a cool mechanic and premise on board, I truly expected this to be one of my faves of the year.  Unfortunately, with gameplay and control mechanics that seemed to try and cater to controller and keyboard/mouse platformer players, it ended up missing the mark on both.  The puzzles were extremely easy in some areas, only to be frustratingly specific in the next.  It created this chaos in a balanced challenge that ultimately forced me to give up on entirely on taking different paths. Aging and de-aging plants and animals is an incredibly novel idea, but when forced to make direct shots while mastering the game's platforming, it became a chore.  Although only logging just under a couple of hours into Ageless,  I got a clear idea that this was not a game I could wrap myself around.  Love the simple pixel art and pleasing, if not memorable, soundtrack, but there was too many faults that I just couldn't ignore here.  Great concept with a messy execution.  With a little bit of polish, this may be something I can jump back into.  As is, Ageless definitely feels like too many unrefined ideas.

Naturally, Ageless is a platformer game where you use the ability to change some 'live' objects to get yourself further.
