_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, and I was pleasantly surprised. The controls feel on par with what you'd expect from a precision platformer, and the gameplay was good throughout: with some creative uses of its core mechanics, some unexpectedly dynamic boss battles, and a good enough system that it's sometimes possible to find seemingly unintended solutions to puzzles.My two gripes would probably be the narrative, which feels a bit rushed until about the halfway point (sidenote: I wish there was more of a bridge between chapters, instead of essentially being teleported to the next area), and that some sections can toe the line of overstaying their welcome - though I don't think it ever quite crossed it.Ageless isn't revolutionary, but it's a good time for fans of platformers in general, and of puzzle platformers especially.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a better score, so I had to write this review.Ageless is puzzle platformer which is more puzzle than precise jumping. The main mechanic, aging, is very cool and made me very excited every time I started a new world to see the many life stages of it's inhabitants, but it doesn't stop at that: as the game progress, it becomes even more interesting, with some extremely cool mechanics that created some very clever puzzles. While the difficulty tend to fluctuate (even in the last world some puzzle were extremely simple), it very rarely gets annoying. The platforming also tends to be pretty easy once you figure out the puzzle, with very few rooms were the precision needed feels aggravating.What I liked most about the game, though, is that the puzzles give a lot of freedom. Too many times, puzzle games tend to be very strict in their required solutions, which tends to be very frustrating if you're missing something: this makes the player feel like they have no freedom to experiment and stops them from being creative. Ageless isn't as strict: every puzzle has an intended solution, but, thanks to its mechanics, many times the player can find a different and sometimes even better solution. This can make the player feel very clever, making the game very satisfying.The game is not perfect, as the controls might take a while to get used to them; the story is a bit simplistic and underdeveloped, but it still makes the game better than without it and never gets in the way for too long. There are also some weird things, like the "voice acting" which can feel a bit annoying or the fact that one area has an extra collectable that isn't counted by the game, but they honestly just give more charm to the game. The only issue that annoyed me was the later bosses, which can feel very try and error and make any mistake too costly.In conclusion, Ageless is a very cool game: it has some very interesting mechanics that keep the player engaged and the level design can lead the player to outsmart the game, making the experience very rewarding. Music and graphics are also well done and contribute to make the game very charming and fresh, deserving a try by any puzzle and platformers fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this game needs a review.If you want to play this game for the story rather than gameplay, get Celeste and forget about this one. If it's the opposite, however, get this one on sale or borrow it from a friend (and then play Celeste if you want)I actually liked this game, but honestly the mixed reviews are well deserved.The gameplay is pretty good, even more so if you get the relics in case you're looking for a challenge... the physics, however, can be quite annoying: they feel wonky ( wonky) and it can take a while to get accostumed to them. The mechanics are quite simple, even if they look a bit strange you grasp them in no time.The level design, now  is where it gets interesting, and the only reason I'm actually recommending the game: The level design is , no level feels useless, very dynamic, sometimes action packed and sometimes a stop and think puzzle, no single mechanic is left unteached and none are without a relic challenge, with each passing chapter bringing you a new change in the mechanics, even if the base is the same.So, everything seems good so far, but the game mas  reviews, not good ones... well, the wonkiness in the mechanics can be quite the make or break, but even above that there's something even worse... the story.I'll cut to the chase: The story sucks. A lot. I've seen lots of good stories, average ones and even bad ones. This spans from novels (very few though) to light novels to story rich games. This game doesn't have a bad story per-se, but it's at best average. I'd personally give it a below average, only because the bar  be that low. It's too simplistic, the character development feels terrible and rushed and the ending, while it technically makes sense, it feels like they just threw the entire story out the window and axed whatever build-up they had. Cringe inducing but passable at best, horrible story at worst. It's not even a matter of saying it's "messed up" or something of the like, it's just... bad. It just sucks. And to make matters worse, they tried to tie up loose ends and ended up leaving everything hanging, just without those previous loose ends.tl;dr If you want to enjoy gameplay, it'll be worth the while. Story? Run away and don't look back.EDIT: On the time of writing this review the game had mixed reviews, hence the first sentence.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it with HumbleBundleDont let the childish artstyle and dialogue fool you - this game is very hard/precise.The frequent savepoints make it bearable.On the second boss fight (I am stuck in second phase) there should be more.Some relics (collectibles) are ridiculously hard to get. Sometimes its the players fault for using the abilities wrong, but often its just unforgiving placement of spikes and janky mechanics.I recommend it to masochistsMy left hand hurtsEdit: Your left has to do so much at once -on top of holding/pressing left/right not 0.1 sec too long/short or guess what, you just hit a spike.When you are in timeless mode you sometimes have a different hitbox than in normal mode - this makes you fall off ledges.Some jumps/sequences are so hard you just resort to "cheesing" the encounter by switching the creatures age - which sometimes is also wanted from you which makes it a bit confusing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a solid concept that it sticks to and evolves with new ways to play with its ageing mechanics that some players will be genuinely surprised at how smart the puzzles become. But, I cannot help but feel the game is missing that final polish, that spark that puts it on the same pedestal as Celeste and a few others. There are some irritating issues with the controls, which spoil what would otherwise be a quality puzzle platformer. I can say that fans of the genre will entertain with what Ageless delivers, and anyone who enjoys a challenging game, if sometimes frustrating, will find something to like here.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is a puzzle-platformer where you use special powers in order to change the ages of living creatures to help you along the way. The game is fairly light on tutorials, and expects you to pick things up quickly, which is a boon and a flaw at times.Some more advanced mechanics of the game are left unexplained for you to learn through either trial or error, or a walkthrough, and it adds even more to the frustration of the puzzles with how reliant they are on precise aiming at times.The real amusement in the game comes from the writing, and how enjoyably bad it is. There are quite a lot of lines of dialogue that are just so far out there that I couldn't help but laugh, and I'll be honest, it helped me get through the game.The game has collectables in the form of "Relics", that add colour to some dioramas in Relic Island, but as far as I am aware, they do not affect anything else with regards to the story and, imo, they're not really worth getting if you don't care about 100% completion.All in all, this game is frustrating, but you'll get a few laughs out of it if you don't take it seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Got as part of a bundle.  It's been a while since I've rage quit a game.  There's a difference between challenging and punishing.  At times this feels punishing.  A prime example is the second boss: You need to keep moving constantly, which causes issues because there are also stationary things that can kill you if they hit your finicky hitbox.  As you move through the stage, you need to immediately have an idea of what part of the puzzle you will do next.  While also dodging attacks.  While also not touching the spikes.  While also not drowning after expending a full five seconds of oxygen.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming Aesthetics, Challenging FrustrationsAgeless offers a visually delightful experience with its charming graphics and intriguing mechanics. The game's art style complements its gameplay, drawing players into a world where the mechanics themselves become a key part of the appeal. Additionally, the storyline weaves an entertaining narrative, adding depth to the overall experience.However, despite its visual appeal and engaging story, Ageless encounters significant hurdles in its gameplay. Some levels become excessively frustrating due to either bugs or an overreliance on pixel-perfect precision. This can lead to a sense of unfairness, causing more irritation than challenge.Moreover, the boss battles exacerbate this frustration by requiring players to flawlessly execute pixel-perfect actions from start to finish. This design choice can become incredibly aggravating, as any minor mistake forces a full restart, testing the patience of even the most dedicated players. It feels punishing rather than genuinely challenging, detracting from the enjoyment of the game.Regrettably, these gameplay issues overshadow the game's positive aspects. Despite its endearing visuals and engaging storyline, the frustrating levels and punishing boss mechanics make it difficult to recommend Ageless to others. Unless one has a high tolerance for these specific types of challenges or enjoys masochistic gameplay, the overall experience might not align with most players' expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Celeste inspired puzzle game, where the main protagonist shoots magic arrows to age or de-age creatures to solve puzzles. All around a brilliant concept! However there are some issues...Like many other puzzle games there are great puzzles and then there are some less than great puzzles, ageless is no exception. There were some puzzles I really liked and there were some puzzles that were very sooooo annoying.In general usual puzzle stuff, when it shows you the new mechanic it’s easy, then once you know it, it gets harder. In general the main path through the game is normal difficulty with hard points here and there. Most of the difficulty is due to the millisecond timing and the pixel perfect aiming. The boss's also sucked.A lack of polish is very prevalent, there is a lot of fine tuning that still needs to be done. There are a lot of graphical glitches along with many game breaking bugs.I think most of the negative reviews are because of the price because for most people price = expectations. I think for $18, people expect a little more. If I didn’t receive this game in a bundle I would have never bought it.I enjoyed my time with this game, I really liked the main mechanic. However in the game's current condition I would say wait for another update, then buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually write reviews for two reason: the game is surprisingly good or even exceptional and I have to say something about it, or the game is so bad that I feel the need to caution other people against wasting their time or money.This isn't either of those cases. But currently the game sits at a Mixed rating, and I think it deserves more.Let's get straight to the point: this game isn't perfect, far from it. As others have pointed out, the story isn't great (but by no means bad,) and the generous collisions, rather than the controls, make things frustrating at times. There are some quirks to the controls too, but nothing you won't get used to in 20 minutes tops.The pixel art is pretty, but... it's a bit over the place. It seems like a collection of vaguely cohesive assets that come from slightly different games. Art direction is definitely the weakest part of this game's presentation.The puzzles themselves is where the game really shines. After the tutorial, you will obtain a bow that can shoot two types of arrows: one that ages living things, the other that makes them younger, and each of the multiple stages the creatures have behave differently in relation to both the character and the environment. You can also enter a state called Ageless, where everything but you freezes, and if you touch any living creature, you can boost away from it in any direction by consuming some of the creature's age. You will have to use these powers to manipulate life around you and reach the end of every screen.Each of the several areas has its own unique creatures that behave in strange and interesting ways, and new mechanics are introduced on top of this enemy variety, like teleporting or death/rebirth. And there are A LOT of levels, both mandatory and optional. Some of these rooms stretch the various interactions between your character and the environment to the extreme, pushing the limits of what you thought was the extent of programmed functionality. I was surprised by "oh, so this and this together do that" several times throughout the game. And just wait till the last area, where !Now, yes, bosses are chases for the most part, and I usually hate those in games... But for some reason they worked for me here. I think that's because the bosses themselves feel like chains of puzzle rooms, just longer ones and with less checkpoints; a natural extension of the puzzles you've done up to that point rather than a curve ball.In short, this is a game that I would recommend only to puzzle-platformer lovers, as it's quite long and hard, but some of the ideas and interactions are just brilliant and need to be seen if you're into this sort of stuff. And if you already like the genre, you'll have plenty to chew on with Ageless. If you go in knowing that it's much more puzzle than platformer, and that it could've definitely used some more time in the oven, I think you'll have a good time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the generic title and arthouse-fodder gimmick fool you. This game has great visuals, great music and overall great gameplay. It doesn't overstay its welcome and constantly throws new gimmicks at you. Be warned, though, even some mandatory puzzles as early as midway through the game will have puzzle game newbies stumped. My only quibbles are that some of the controls are finicky, some of the timing is nearly frame-perfect, and some things are unintuitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice puzzling platformer, however there are a few major issues remaining in the game.- Delaying the ability to fire arrows for the purpose of animations is a mistake in my opinion. If puzzles are designed to be solved with quick actions then you should not delay a player's actions for "cool animations".- Boss battles should be tuned for the level of progress the players have made in the game so far. As it stands, only 12% of players have finished the first world and only 6% of players have finished the second world. The 2nd world boss in particular is unforgiving and there is a section that was basically hand crafted to be solved only a single way instead of allowing the player to climb the boss' arms.- Vestige has a section in the game where only 14 relics are tracked, when there are actually 15 relics to be acquired. The fact that players have to go out of their way to figure out which relic wasn't tracked isn't a nice experience.I enjoyed the game, however I cannot recommend it to most players since they would probably not make it past the 2nd boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The ideas that aren't lifted from other puzzle platformers get a few moments of intrigue before they become overused. Otherwise, Ageless is worth very little of your time. The game is shrouded in inconsistency and bursting with weak puzzles that are only challenging in how unreliable it is to execute their solutions. Like stale bread, it’s dry, hard to swallow, and representative of something much better.I constantly considered abandoning it out of boredom and mild irritation only to reluctantly continue playing due to the same sympathy that drove others to post consolation reviews. The ideas change, but polish and ingenuity remain bog-standard throughout. Take a glance at the achievement statistics for some perspective on the game's retention.Ageless doesn't entirely deserve its startlingly low steam rating, but I can't in good conscience recommend something so unabashedly unremarkable. Sadly, receiving it as filler for a Humble Bundle seems like the most appropriate context to find Ageless in.

I wanted to love it and will probably play it through as it seems quite short, but found it way more frustrating than anything else.

I like the visuals, the idea is great and original and there are a lot of different puzzles to solve.The problem is that puzzles quickly become time sensitive and you must be very precise to pass them. Just that would still be alright for me, as it's a challenge I'm ready to accept. But the game lacks proper psychics and especially has a lot of bugs with inputs. _childDocuments_.review: Its a good puzzle game. But there are some parts of the game where you are forced to speed run from a boss. In these instances you will realize how annoying some glitches are such as riding the dolphins. When you approach the creature to ride it, the toggle button appears. However you may press the button 5 to 6 times before the action occurs. This is not a one time occurrence but almost every time you attempt to engage with the creature. _childDocuments_.review: Far too reliant on absolutely pixel perfect platforming and precision timing. Not even the slightest errors are allowed in the beginning and that's before you even get to the intense chase part (which you encounter very prematurely in the demo too). It has beautiful, emotional music and a wonderful aesthetic, atmospheric and pixel art in general but it's way too frustrating to play. There are checkpoints in every area so far but that still doesn't stop it being immensely unforgiving ironically.Also, early on in the first world, you can permanently miss a relic if you choose to smash a wall and go right, instead of using the animal to boost upwards. It's somewhere early in Act 4 and luckily I was able to replay it and get it anyway but the lack of indication of this a risk nor a method to get back was also very frustrating.I really wanted to love this, but I cannot recommend it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: cannot recommend, way too punishing in few places. Difficulty skyrockets out of nowhere. Devs should review those places and either make it easier for everyone or add an opt-in easy more. For the most obvious example, second stage of boss for Remnant is a punishing nightmare with almost non-existent margin for error. You have to nail the whole of it in one big sequence under time pressure, no checkpoints in-between. Some might call it challenging, I definitely call it punishing beyond any reasonable expectation. I passed it (as evident by the achievement), but it took me maybe 60+ attempts to do that, and when I did, it felt more like a pure dumb luck. I would consider myself ok-ish at platformers, I shudder to think what experience would I have if I wouldn't be.It's made even worse by the fact that some of the actions glitch very frequently, like mounting a level 3 fish (dolphin), while some other actions (jumping on plants that kick you up) can be very counter-intuitive - in order to trigger jump you need to move in direction of flower, but if you don't let go of that control immediately at the right moment and your jump is in the opposite direction, it will get messed up.I was always wondering how people can get so frustrated with any sort of game as to throw controllers or break keyboards. Now I think I understand them a little better.Update: finished it, including getting all relics. Still wouldn't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to leave a brief recommendation as a counterpoint to the negative reviews. This game is a really good puzzle platformer with unique ideas and mechanics. I cannot share the common criticisms in the reviews at all. The controls are fully functional, the platforming is tight, the aiming system works fine both with controller and mouse. The difficulty and learning curve is fine. There are a few reviews of people with less than an hour or two in the game complaining about pixel precise alignments etc. These people are, no point in mincing words, just wrong and didn't understand the room they were in and missed a mechanic or alternative way to progress, which is pretty normal and even encouraged to exist in a puzzle platformer. I can confidently say, 5h in and not really getting stuck anywhere, that no room required an absurdly precise solution that the controls didn't support.  I find it a shame that the game went far enough under the radar that a few of those reviews bring the rating of this little gem down so heavily.It shines when the various mechanics combine and open up the solution space dramatically. I'm playing together with a friend and the amount of times we found quite different solutions from each other is surprising. One optional room stands out where after a back and forth of ideas we ended up with six different ways to solve the puzzle, all distinctly different from each other. The game isn't a masterpiece and has some minor issues, none of which have detracted majorly from my positive experience. Sometimes it's a bit unclear how close the ageless dash needs to be to a target. The escapes are a bit trial and error because of the time pressure and checkpoints being more scarce, but aren't a massive difficulty spike and fulfill their function of changing up the gameplay for a bit as well as progressing the narrative. The biggest problem for me is that I missed one relic in an area, know which one it is, visually, in the relic garden, but can't do anything with that information to find it. The best thing I could do is check back every single room which I'm not interested in doing.All in all, this game is way better than its small and mediocre reviewing would indicate. In the indie puzzle platformer genre which I'm quite fond of, I'd rate it 4/5, under the absolute highlights like Celeste which I'm sure was a big inspiration, but it's definitely a good game worth the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Take Celeste and subtract 3 from the score.   9/10?  This is 6/10. I recommend it to people who enjoy this genre and want more after playing the heavy hitters.  Its fun...but its also like playing Street Fighter 2 in the year 2021 when you've gotten used to games like Street Fighter 4 (or presumably 5 but I haven't played that one). The controls feel 'fine' but worse.  Jumps are floaty.  The control scheme works but the flow and polish just isn't there.  The graphical art style is a big miss for me but mileage may vary.  I found puzzles to be very good early on but as they demanded more and more precision I found myself getting more annoyed than having a good time.  I ultimately didn't finish the game but I understand the appeal and would genuinely recommend it to fans of the genre as I said.  I'm NOT a fan of the genre in general...so my enjoyment of Celeste stands out as an exception and not the norm.    I can only assume others will cling on to this game a bit better than I did. Wait for a sale for sure though.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I was very charmed with this puzzle platformer. You play a girl who gains the power to change the age of plants and animals, which also changes their behavior. A young tree can be used to catapult yourself through the air for example, while older trees can lift you up with their roots. This mechanic works very well and is used to create some clever puzzles in a beautiful pixelated game world.Sadly the controls and hit boxes aren't as good as they should be (at least on the Steam Deck). As a result, I often knew how to solve a certain puzzle, but it still took me lots of tries to execute it correctly because my character did something else than I intended.While this is only slightly annoying during the puzzle sections, this becomes a huge problem in the "escape" sequences where you are being chased by fast moving deadly objects. Not only are these sections ridiculously difficult compared to the rest of the game, but they are also very frustrating because of the controls and hit box issues. While I loved the escape sequences in the Ori games, they made me uninstall Ageless out of pure frustration. Such a shame...

_childDocuments_.review: In my quest to 100% the achievements for each game in my library, I quickly stumbled across Ageless. I believe I had received it in a past Humble Bundle or some other bundle because I do not recall purchasing the game standalone. To be frank, the $14.99 price is absurd. The game has no where near enough content nor is polished enough to warrant that price tag. Pick it up if it ever goes under $5 (and only if you like the concept).The game itself is a fun puzzle platformer, however the fun quickly disappears when you run into one of the game's many mechanical bugs; movement is sloppy and choppy, so expect to die often when you shouldn't. Coupled with some rather gruesomely precise puzzles, you will quickly want to pull your hair out. The disparity between "levels" is massive; one second a puzzle will be a simple jump and the next it will be a complicated set of moves with no room for error. Furthermore, end stages for each world have to be completed in a sort of marathon; when you factor in the rough controls, these stages become extremely tedious. Overall, the game has charm and a cool pixel art style. The concept behind the ending is quite cool. Some semblance of a story is there, but it feels like I'm reading a self-help book half the time. Also, do yourself a favor and turn down dialogue, its painfully obnoxious. The characters just moan incessantly.Anyway, I'd only suggest buying this game if you want to smash your keyboard or monitor (or both). If you like puzzle platformers this may be a game you'd like, but heed my and other users' warnings about the quality of controls and mechanics. If they were to fix the aforementioned issues, the game would still be a no for full price, but a for sure grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: === First look === [90 minutes in]At very first the game seems like a cheap clumsy platformer. IT IS WAY MORE THAN THAT.DO NOT LET THE FIRST MINUTES GIVE YOU THE WRONG IMPRESSION. AT FIRST I THOUGHT THE GAME WOULD BE PLAIN AND BORING, BUT I WAS WRONG.Somewhere around 15 minutes to half an hour the game begins to unlock it's potential. The game has really cool unique puzzles. Most games do puzzles wrong. This is not one of those games.The puzzles feel like Portal all over again. You get to experiment with new stuff and come up with creative solutions. I love that feeling.Absolutely recommended thus far.The story seems to be picking up too.I will admit movement sometimes feels a bit clumsy. But when you get past the first part, that doesn't matter so much, and you'll start to get the hang of it anyways.DO PLAY THIS GAMEIf you love Portal // unique creative puzzle games, and you are in speaking terms with platformers, you will have a good time with this one.=== Update === [3 hours in]The game continues to be great in my eyes. That portal-esque feeling of solving puzzles your own way is just wonderful. Priceless to me. The story is... alright. Graphics are rather pretty. Not much to complain about, really. Lacks some polish I guess, but in a way that just makes the game more authentic, and it does NOT bother me in the slightest.=== A rant about Portal === [4 hours in]What made Portal such an amazing experience for me is how intentionally broken game it is. There are literally millions of ways to break the game. Clitches, short-cuts, bunny-hopping, skipping stuff, forcing the mechanics to go crazy, combining them in ways that make no sense, taking items where you should not, building a tower out of bodies, making your own weird challenges ... just doing stuff in ways the devs never meant it to be done. You get to come up with something yourself. There are no correct solutions to the puzzles, which makes them more natural. And even when there are correct solutions, that just means it will be ever so much more satisfying to find one that definitely isn't the correct one.Why is this relevant? I think Ageless achieves the same feeling. I can do whatever I want, I can break the game and it's puzzles in so may ways, and love breaking them every time. Granted, you could argue that here it is probably less intentional than with Portal. The game breaks since it lacks polish, not because it is meant to work that way. While that certainly is true to some extent, the end result is the same. This game makes me really happy, and I love it.=== Update === [7 hours in]The game is a gem. Ageless gem hahahahahaa. No, but seriously. I love this game. I absolutely get why some people might not like Ageless, but I do.The game continues to add new mechanics (to break) in nice ways. Maybe it's just me, but I love breaking puzzles and the whole game in creative ways.The story still is a bit lacking, but tolerable, and at points kind of cute in a way.

_childDocuments_.review: this is like celeste, except the forgot to put in the good parts that good puzzle platformer have.this game feels sloppy, you get stuck on everything, jumps are unnecessarily tight and the mechanics they give you hinder your ability to do awesome stuff or anything your brain wants to do.: Intro story :you are a depressed girl that needs to get away from life, you went into some dangerous trial to get some kind of power, hoping it's gonna fix everything, turns out that feeling like "life is getting ahead of you" means you can now controll the age of things, make stuff grow by making it older, making stuff small by making it younger, and you also become an ultragod that can stop time completely and with some succ from things that are alive get a little boost at the expense of the living thing's stage of life. (i haven't played the story through at all but i can assure you this is all you need to know because they tried to copy celeste): Irritating mechanics :as mentioned before you can change the age of certain interactable objects, you do this by shooting an arrow of life or an arrow of de-life at them, unfortunately this locks you into an animation, this means you cannot jump or move whilest shooting the arrow, making it very hard and unsatisfying to jump, shoot and land on the thing you made grow, this is something that i wanted to do every single time they offered me the challenge, this is annoying.You also get a Goddess form, stopping time (except for your own movement). if you touch something that has life you may use it to get a dash out of it which goes higher then a regular jump, you can dash in 8 directions, after a dash it needs about 2 seconds to recharge before you can go back into this goddess form, this form is also required to collect relics that somehow are the shape of an A, i think it stands for A in Ageless, this is not very original and furthers my di-interest in the game's setting or story.my problem is this : stopping time only hinders the experience of having a smoothe platforming experience, you're just stopping time, giving you time to think but also stopping the action awkwardly, i don't feel rewarded, i feel awkward and the recharge time on the goddess form makes it so that if you make a mistake (for example trying to pick up a relic during a fall and activating too early, forces you to kill the thing you'd be falling down on, killing you or forcing you to get that thing through the maze again so you can fall off of it again.):TLDR:this is a puzzle platformer that is made by people that either didn't have the budget or passion for platformer to make the platformer, celeste was a work of blazing passion, everything works and feels incredible, this feels like a failed copy of celeste with some mechanics shoved in there because they didn't really know what else to do and couldn't just have you jump around for 15 euros.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 6/10:The pixel retro style the game goes for at times is endearing, but overall it feels off. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 4/5Notes: The negative reviews are somewhat understandeable. The animations and visuals are great. The gameplay is solid, but a lot of the mechanics and player control can feel just a bit clunky and awkward both mechanically and in the level design. Overall the game is still decent and definitely at least better than the current 63% steam rating would suggest. Be warned however that the game is not easy by any means. And also be aware that the game is very much a PUZZLE-platformer. The game is much more puzzle oriented than platforming. This is is legit probably the hardest puzzle game I've ever played. Ive fully completed Talos principle (almost 100%) and both portals without ever needing to look up a guide. But I had to look up a guide on probably 7-8 rooms on this game.My main problem with the game is that MANY of the rooms could be "solved" in unintended ways. _childDocuments_.review: Lives may be threads, but you determine which part of that thread each life is on.To see Ageless in action, watch my gameplay video. Your power is to choose what part of the lifespan every living being is in. Is it young? Is it old? Will you steal a part of its life force to empower yourself? Ageless's plot is one of generic introspection (at least to start), but its puzzle mechanics are a breath of fresh air. Each room presents a new challenge. Some are easy. Some are painfully difficult to execute. And plenty are optional for the casual player while demanding the best from completionists. And the music is soothing.I'm not sure if it's the controls, or if timing is tighter than it should be, but Ageless is painfully difficult at times even in its first level.  Each room includes a checkpoint, so you're quickly back to your next attempt, but something in the combination of control and difficulty make Ageless intimidating to get into. Left Trigger rewinds time, Right Trigger accelerates time, and X enters Ageless Mode where you'll either exit via X again or dash via A. On paper it should be fine, but the speed with which these mechanics are introduced, combined with unforgiving timing windows, kicks Ageless to the timeless difficulty of older games right off the bat.There's a good game here for players willing to explore it, and timing is so tight that I would love to see a speedrun someday.

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless looks like . The story is very like. But Ageless fails to nail the one thing that made —and other high-profile platformers—really stand out: the controls. And it’s a shame, really. Some of these puzzles were very well designed. There are a lot of gems here, especially in the more difficult side objectives. The gist of it is the following: levels have animals and plants which you can age up or down, each age group having different properties and effects. And Ageless lets you figure things out. And it works. There are many clever puzzles, interesting solutions, and fun mechanics. The first area, by far the most basic, for example: you can age a plant up or down, raising or lowering a platform. There’s another plant that is eaten by the animal. The animal starts as an egg, ages into a tiny creature which slowly moves towards food, then into a rhino that chases you, breaking walls in the progress, then becomes fat and slow, destroying platforms below it. There are other mechanics that keep interactions fresh. You can stop time, dash out of every creature and plant, de-aging them in the process and propelling them backwards. The Titan area has teleporting, which is also used in clever ways. The Spectre has zones where you can die and come back to life. All of these are used in novel and fun ways. The final area has… timed puzzles, which aren’t very good, especially in levels where you can’t really see everything in the same screen.The bosses were fun and tense. I enjoyed them for the most part, though I’ve noticed a lot of people complaining about them, so your mileage may vary. They seemed to be harder than even the side levels, so if you hadn’t been completing them as you go along, they might be a little frustrating.And that’s it for the good.There’s lots of strange flaws. Wall jumping sounds weird, and I’m sure the devs noticed it. If you do it fast enough, most of the audio just won’t play. The dolphin animal in the second world is incredibly annoying—you seem to have to spam a button to mount it, regardless of whether the prompt is on screen. This makes puzzles in the final section of the game, where all the mechanics come back, a lot more irritating. The final area is probably the worst part of the game, too. A lot of the triumph over finding clever solutions to puzzles is lost, as the insect from the final section can be exploited whenever it is on screen—some puzzles end up with a lot of unused elements because you can pretty much skip them. The timed puzzles where you have to throw the guy around are annoying and not a very entertaining ending to a game with such great puzzles. It left a sour taste in my mouth. But the worst sin of all are the controls and movement. The controls are so floaty and inprecise. Controller aiming is annoying and weirdly sticky. It’s an unforgivable flaw—platformers need to at least adhere to some standard of control and feel. Ageless’ gimmick isn’t that it’s floaty and has weird hitboxes, it’s the interesting, well thought-out, puzzles. Of course, I’m sure it’d be too much work to test every single puzzle if they tweak the movement. Ageless isn’t a twitch reflex fast-paced platformer, as some people seem to think, but there are some tight jumps here and there which could break if movement changes. But it’s the only way this game would get a recommendation from me.This isn’t to say that I don’t think there are people who would enjoy the game. Some of these puzzles are really interesting: Ageless offers a bunch of byte-sized aha! moments. But I don’t think most people, myself included, would have a good time with it. The story could have at least intrigued you to continue to go just to see what happens, but it's really uninteresting.Nevertheless, Ageless feels amateurish. It’s janky and doesn’t feel that good to play. The ending levels felt tacked on. And while the puzzles were good, I don’t think it’s enough to save it. I’m interested in what this studio comes up with next, I think this had potential. Maybe spend some more time in the basics. Then—and only then—go all out on the crazy levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Watching footage of this game I was really hyped to jump in, I thought it might just be misunderstood by the current mixed reviews (68%). This game is not what I hoped it would be at all, and I'm really disappointed by that.PROS:+ The controls and character control decently wellCONS:- Ageless tries so hard to copy Celeste that its hard keep playing because it just feels better to play Celeste in every way.- The UI makes it look like a mobile port at times, and a wall of hieroglyphic gibberish at others. - The levels are either frustratingly easy or frustratingly difficult, absolutely no in between. The lack of "coyote time" (as dubbed by Maddy Thorson, one of the creators of Celeste) is a huge influence on what makes the platforming feel lesser, and it's so disappointing that its missing given that it would be very easy to implement and drastically change the game feel. - The story is a huge letdown so far, it differs from Celeste in that instead of giving the message of all the strength you need being within you (symbolic of Madeline's abilities sourcing from herself), Ageless denies that and says you need outside help from a mythical gate to get superpowers in order to overcome your fears.Overall, just not that great or new at all. The gimmick of aging and de-aging things isn't used that creatively at all so far, its just been the same puzzle copied and pasted for 30 minutes. I don't think I'll keep playing to see if the puzzles get any better simply because the game had its chance to impress meTL;DR: Just go buy Celeste instead, or if you already own it, go replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is one of the best games I've played in a while. It feels like a cross between Celeste & Toki Tori 2. For those who don't know Toki Tori 2 is a metoridvania where you don't have any particular movement abilities of your own, you advance by manipulating the various creatures around you. This game has a high degree of difficulty and optional collectibles like Celeste and a focus on single-room challenges that are pretty hard, though this tends far more towards the puzzle side with very little execution challenge for most puzzles once you worked out the solution. Rather than using your own mobility you advance by manipulating the various creatures in the environments. You have 2 basic abilities: a dash (which can activate in proximity of other creatures) and a bow that will either make a creatures "younger" or "older" which changes how they perform. For instance the creature in the first area has a young stage where it will move to eat a plant if you grow the plant, a prime stage where it will bum-rush you and destroy blocks in front and an old stage where it will crush blocks underneath it. As you advance the different stages has their own unique forms (2 creatures/1 creature & 1 plant for every area). The game has a really good progression of puzzles and challenge that towards the end is quite a challenge, the optional collectible challenges were also mostly good (a few cases of "I didn't know I could do that") I had to look up a few solutions on a guide but not many. I had really good time. I had to take some time for this because later down the line they got very challenging indeed.As for the story: pretty basic,it does the job well enough, but don't play it for the story. Anyone who liked Celeste on a mechanical level will probably find this a very good game. A few negatives: This games take on boss fights are not great. They are usually some variant of timed puzzles with far fewer checkpoints than the regular game. There are only 4 of them (5 if you count the last area, but that one is mostly fine because while it's still timed it has proper checkpointing)

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is one of literally thousands of console ported 2D retro pixel platformers polluting the Steam store.   This particular platformer has you jumping around underground through various die-and-retry obstacle courses and other platformer puzzles. They chose to use obsolete retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.  It's also worth noting the pixel "art" here is really bad.  Like, it's worse than decades old games like Commander Keen, and Apogee at the time weren't using pixel "art", that was literally the best PCs at the time could do.   No excuses for Ageless having such bad visuals. Speaking of excuses, I really hope they have one for charging a ludicrous $15 USD for this console ported bundle worsening garbage.  You can buy all the Commander Keen and Duke Nukem platformers for less than that, they have more content and better graphics, despite being decades older.  It's just impossible to recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Precision Puzzle PlatformerFully compatible with the Steam Deck.I wanted to love this game.  The pixel art is cute, if a little rough.  The pacifist ethos is admirable (the only time you "kill" anything is to reset enemy states).  But in the harder rooms the puzzling tends to require a level of precision that the controls can't quite handle, leading to a disappointing tedium until the controls and targeting do what you're actually trying to do.  Add in some baffling design decisions (why do forest enemies take 2 hits to transform?), and a painfully tedious 4th "boss" (beat 7 rooms without dying while fighting the loose controls and brand new gimmicks that are never seen again), and you're left with a game that's only OK when it could have been great.I don't regret my time with the game, but I think this one is mostly just for pixel platformer purists.

It's got a nice unique concept, but the puzzles swing from brain dead easy to far too obtuse from one room to the next with little progression. A number of the puzzles are far too precise for my preference. Also, hugely hated how while all the puzzles are one room at a time giving a quick try loop, the game has bosses that got multiple rooms which felt horrible to retry again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The ideas this game had were astronomical, the problem is the intent for game mechanics and the story are getting overshadowed by constant lag or bad reactions regardless of keybindings that aren't meant to happen with the difficulty of the puzzles. The concept I very much enjoyed but I can't recommend this game with how it's laid out. I'd check back again to see if OMDS would rework this game because I'd love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid indie puzzle platformer with a simple but decent art style. The core mechanics are unique and lead to some very interesting puzzles that offer a good degree of flexibility in how they are solved. Though the controls can be a little difficult to get used to, the auto-aiming and slowing of time when you aim makes it reliable and consistent once you get the hang of it (i.e., you won't have "cheap" deaths). I would recommend using a controller over a mouse and keyboard honestly.The story, characters, and world-building are also pretty decent, handling the subjects of existentialism and personal disappointment in a believable fashion. It's a feeling most people can relate to and allows for good character development
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely not a game for me, but it is functional, and not as difficult as I saw some claim.The positive I can say definitely is the interesting uses for animals you find, depending on which age you select for them, it's a highlight and sometimes it felt like puzzles could have more than one solution, The music is also nice to the ear, pretty competent composition.The controls are unpleseant, I don't want to think how much worse they'd be on a controller, it's a 2D platformer where aiming is important, but not in a combat sense, your power to change beings' age is an arrow being shot, a thing that also has a short windup, timing of which doesn't really bring much satisfaction in gameplay. Besides that you have a jump and wall slide, pretty standard, but challenges involving those feel finnicky more than anything else, since you're in puzzle rooms, you just kinda squeeze yourself between hazards and onto platforms, and hope for the best. The worst part comes up with your special form, which you activate for a short time, and as soon as you touch another living thing, you are in a static state, completely breaking your flow, and a chart of directions shows up, where you push yourself in one direction, while the being is pushed in opposite (while also reversing its age by one). Now if you also add plant jump pads, being small, and directional in different angles - it all mixes into a really unsatisfying, unwieldy and inconsistent at times, experience. Not to mention you sometimes bug out in environment, or a dolphin ride prompt straight up doesn't work 50% of the time.Well, I sure hope the saving grace is going to be story or visuals, but both are a nope from me. Story is trying to be uplifting, but it's filled with exposition and spelling out feelings, talking to yourself like a schizo. None of it is gripping, and lore intertwining with the see through characters, doesn't save it at all. Visuals are pixelated hard, enough to border on ugly in my opinion. Some slight vfx touches like traces are sprinkled in, and bouncy resizing adding fake life into some of the animations. Nothing that blew me away. Voice acting doesn't exist, it's just grunts and moans, some more annoying than others (unfortunately, in case of the protagonist - more). While I don't think it's a bad or horrible game, for a guy who is not a massive fan of the genre - I could not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly it's a really fun puzzle-platformer. The amateurish character designs and god-awful font choice put me of at first but once ?I got into the grove I realize the amount of heart put into this and how much fun I was having collecting relics and thinking out the solution for every level.I do understand the negative reception however because there are some bugs that ruin the flow of gameplay and ultimately just frustrate.For instance the orcas don't always register my input to ride them and the second to final level arbitrarely allows you to succed depending on how close two entities entities are too each other getting me really pissed off for half an hour.Things like that aside however at it's core their is a really a good game.Easy recommend for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully designed game however my biggest gripe with this game is the sometimes inputs. If I push a button, I want it to do the thing it is meant to do, not shrug and cause me to die. Also why was it decided that part two of the boss fight would cheap out on the checkpoints forcing you to do several minutes of the same thing over and over again because you got screwed on the sometimes inputs or else just an unlucky angle.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Brutally massacre baby rhinos by making them so old that they die in the blink of an eye, making them lose a lifetime of possibility. Run adult Rhinos off of cliffs to their deaths yoshi style.Let Rhinos get old and fat and let them fall through the floor to their deaths. Do all of this while dealing with the internal struggles of depression and learning to overcome low self worth.had fun, will do again some time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, it has some clever mechanisms and if you’re a fan of other precision puzzle platformers (i.e. Celeste) then this game should scratch that itch. That said, there's a lot about it that feels unpolished, so your mileage will vary depending on your willingness to put up with wide swings in puzzle difficulty and the occasional janky interaction.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is a charming puzzle platformer crammed full of original platforming mechanics. I honestly can't understand not recommending this.Ok - It's not perfect in any sense - none of the critical reviews are really wrong in any of the points raised but there's so much to enjoy here. Puzzles - brilliant; Sprites - charming; Music/Sound design - fantastic; Controls - smooth and responsive. It's the first game from a clearly talented and passionate dev team. Look - sure it's not Celeste (what is) but it's much, much better than what the 'Mixed' SteamReviews would suggest. Highly recommend - it's crazy cheap on sale and deserves so much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I joked while watching the trailer "ermagerd, pixel art platformer with wall jumping, just like Celeste", but honestly, it looks like this game is quite clear about its inspiration. Without spoiling much, it definitely feels like that sort of game, but a lot heavier on the puzzle aspect, with what feels like some nods to Ori and the Blind Forest's escape sequences.I'm not sure if something has changed since people wrote reviews about it being buggy 2 years ago, but I only encountered a couple of glitches in my entire playthrough. I like challenging games, and this was definitely one of them. Kept me interested enough to play through the whole thing (100%, achievements, etc) in one sitting.My only complaints are: - While playing with gamepad, your aim snaps to targets, and I don't think there's any way to *not* do that, making it hard to lead my shots- The relics, while an interesting challenge to collect, feel extremely pointless. Would have been cool if you got more than some colour added to some voxel statues.- Might've been nice to give another shoutout to Celeste by showing what part of a stage you are missing a relic in, instead of having to scour the entire level for a single missing thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I don't remember how this game ended up in my Steam Library but I finally got around to playing it and I think it being Mixed on Steam is not giving this game nearly as much credit as it deserves. To preface this review, I will say that the game isn't perfect by any means. Now I can't attest to controller controls because I played on keyboard & mouse but precision and hitboxes can be a little janky at times which is frustrating. The movement and abilities presented in the game should give you a freeflowing satisfying movement system, which it does at its best, but at its worst it will repeatedly cause you to mess up puzzles due to the games own collision issues. With that inconvenience out of the way though, I think my only other issue with the game could be that it gets a bit repetitive at times, but I think that's just a nitpick if anything. To start off with the things I enjoyed about the game, the gameplay systems are incredibly original and refreshing. Each area has a small amount of creatures you can use your ageing ability on but by the time you've mastered all the different ways you can utilize their different stages of life, the game throws the next visually distinct area at you full of new creatures for you to learn how to master. It's a nice gameplay loop and I found myself playing until the end of an area, then waiting until the next day to dive back in and grind through the next. The story has a lot of very fun worldbuilding in it and without spoiling anything, the area called Spectre, has a reallly really fun/cool gameplay/story section that I found to be very appealing. The story can be a bit surface level at times with it's themes of self help and mental illness but I don't think it was ever trying to be anything other than what it was so I don't find it to be an issue.Bottom Line: Ageless isn't perfect, but I think it has enough good going for it that it's definitely worth the play-through (I 100%ed it on my first play-through at just under 12 hours). I am definitely keeping my eye on these developers in the future because I think that this game, despite its flaws, really showcases the talent at One More Dream Studios and what they could be capable of in the future. If you like puzzle platformers and are looking for one with a unique gameplay system then I would definitely check Ageless out.(Between a 6 and a 7)/10 - A fun game with a lot of promise with a few glaring issues. Fun if you're looking for a short, lower budget platformer
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It has the bones of a great game with some good writing and a lot of deep world-building, but suffers from overtly basic mechanics stretched too far. Puzzles are either immediately apparent how to solve, or frustratingly difficult because of the rigidity of the controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Okay...a reluctant thumbs up here because I applaud the effort, even though it has some solid misses.Ageless is almost creepingly similar to celeste: the graphic design style, the overarching story, the difficulty. The main hook here is that you can shoot arrows that increase/decrease the age of living species. And that somehow lets you propel through the air if you aim it at yourself...But video game logic aside: celeste is a masterpiece, so there's plenty of room for a simile. But what all negative reviews correctly point out (and for some reason only a handful of positive ones): it gets frustratingly hard in not a good way. Often, what you need to do is pretty clear (the puzzles are okay and even good), but the game relies so much on pixel perfect execution that it's discouraging rather than challenging. And to be honest: the shooting arrow mechanic would've been great for a strict puzzle game, but it has to share its experience with a development team that wanted some celeste difficulty as well. And I feel that drags it down more than anything else...
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle platformer. The game keeps throwing in new elements to interact with the aging mechanic, and then using them for all theiy're worth. The optional collectabes are very well signaled and offer an extra challenge for those seeking it. I recommend Ageless to all those who want to test their mechanical and mental skills.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Boring and repetitive, despite having good ideas. Could be great with a much better execution.The controls are very annoying and very rarely feels right. Especially if you play on controller. Very hard to make any sort of precise movement with that set of movement.Puzzles are fine but that's really all you do, just very long series of mostly easy or annoyingly tight rooms. The quite bad hitboxes don't help with that.The gameplay progresses way too slowly and mechanics players can figure out in the couple first rooms don't get used until much later, instead reusing the same ones until you get sick of them.I already mentioned it but the difficulty is all over the place, there is no curve, it's a roller coaster.The basic idea of aging and de-aging stuff to progress is pretty unique and I'd say they make good use of the gimmick and it never feels irrelevant. The way the dash works feels quite bad however, despite it being used in smart ways in the level design, it just feels... off and unrelated to the concept of aging / de-aging.The story is also scattered very thin along the whole game, giving you not nearly enough incentive to keep playing it. When playing it, it's pretty obvious to see why only 14.6% of players makes it through world 1, there's nothing to keep you hooked on long enough.The story itself is really unsubtle about its themes, which could've been decent with better writing and way less space between each cutscene.In the end, this game feels a lot like Celeste and yet seems to not take enough inspiration from it which would've made the game much more solid.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty fun little puzzle platformer. I enjoyed it well enough and got it 100% completed. I agree with some of the other reviewers, some parts of the games are a little frustrating sometimes because the setup/controls feel a little clunky, but overall it's a pretty cute little game and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes puzzle platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I think the platforming mechanics are really creative and the story is fine. That being said, as someone who's not the best at platformers, this game has been really difficult and frankly kinda frustrating at times. I want to finish it to get the end of the story (which, good or not, I'm pretty invested in) but I'm really struggling to get through the final levels. I'd love it if the game had some sort of assist mode or even just an option to skip certain levels. It's a great game but I can't recommend it to anyone who knows they're bad at platformers......honestly maybe just get Celeste
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool puzzle platformer. The gameplay mechanics are super unique and interesting, some of the puzzles really had me scratching my head. When I eventually cracked them it was so satisfying. There are a few quirks to the game as it's a tiny build. There is a lack of polish here and there, but honestly I found this game really impressive. Music and art are bloody good too.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot and would recommend it if you like difficult puzzle platformers. While it isn't as polished as the big names in the genre it features some unique mechanics and ideas. Throughout most of the game you only have 3 tools: ageing arrow, deaging arrow and the ability to stop time. The game stays engaging by introducing new environments, animals and plants to interact with frequently. At the end of the game the puzzles get quite tense as you often have to beat rooms under time pressure. It took me ~14 hours to complete this game with 100% achievements.Reasons why you might not like this game:The controls can be quite finicky, aiming the arrows can get frustrating, mounting a dolphin only works after pressing the button multiple times etc.The second boss is quite buggy, it has issues with camera position and it can get locked in the wrong attack patterns.The game has random difficulty spikes for both the puzzle and platformer parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fine, the controls feel a bit clunky, but the puzzle part of this platformer is extremely on point. If the controls had felt smoother this would have easily been a wonderful experience. As is, I still greatly enjoyed the gameplay especially since this game really ties a lot of mechanics together in a beautiful way that few other games do.I would recommend this game, but be prepared to fight the controls more often than the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle game with a good mix of problem solving and side scrolling mechanics to get through different levels and areas. At first I thought the mechanics were going to be too simple and boring but as you progress you get more mechanics that change up the game and how you solve the different puzzles. Each area also has a unique set of mechanics that keeps the game from getting stale. I really like that the size of the puzzles are essentially one screens worth and after you get through a puzzle there is a save point, no pointlessly doing the first part of the puzzle 100 times to be able to attempt/practice the end part 3 or 4 (looking at you super meat boy!). There are also longer sequences at the end of each area that provide a bit more difficulty and use the mechanics for that area in fun fast paced ways. Typically I ignore the stories in most games but this one has a surprisingly deep plot that has a lot of moral ambiguity and highlights the hard choices that we have to make as humans in an imperfect and sometimes brutal world.  Even with how small the game is and the short nature of the story I've actually gotten into it and have some emotional investment that I wasn't expecting at all when I started the game. Overall a solid 4.5 stars from a gamer that's finding it harder and harder to find games that capture my attention and are fun for longer than 30min. I got this game through a humble bundle and am not sure I would ever buy a game like this for more than $10 without knowing how much I'd enjoy it. After playing it I'd probably go up to $20 to support the creators. I also have not experienced any glitches mentioned in the other reviews and I'm about half way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: So. Ageless. Probably the most difficult review for me to write yet.Let's get the obvious out of the way. Ageless is a story based puzzle platformer, whose storey resembles the famous celeste. It tells the story of an young woman, named kiara, who struggles to find her place in the world, and goes to a supernatural journey of self realization and acceptance.The journey, sadly, is a bit of a mixed bag. The visuals are quite decent. The worlds and mechanics are diverse and different from one another. The story and gibberish voice acting are not the best but compelling enough.But I still have several issues with the game, the first being is the controls. They're just not precise enough, and the developers made some weird decisions regarding them. Like the fact that you can't move at all when you're drawing your bow, which was really annoying at specific instances. There are a lot of small annoyances like that in the game.Then there's also the difficulty fluctuations. By and large, the puzzles are well designed. Hell, some of them instilled me with the "OHHHH that's how you do it" feeling, which some of the best puzzle games do. But it's also amazing that some of the puzzles in the endgame are easier than the one at the middle.At the start of the game, I was really enjoying myself. I even collected nearly every extra collectable (I collected more than 60 of them!). But by the end, I skipped them all.Overall, ageless is ok. It has it downsides, but it's still a fun experience.And if by any chance the developers will read this review, I really think you should continue making games. You clearly have a lot of potential. Just because the first try didn't pan out too well, it doesn't mean you shouldn't try again. I'm looking forward to see your next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Interesting puzzle / platformer mechanics that may not seem like much in the beginning, but really gain in depth over the course of the game.✔️ The progressive increase both in puzzle complexity and in execution difficulty is very smooth and enjoyable.✔️ Really cute pixel art graphics.✔️ Nice ambience music.✔️ The story is enjoyable and touching, even though it doesn't have an incredible depth.✔️ The game saves very often, which makes interruptions easy and failure not too frustrating.❌ A few bugs here and there, like the level not resetting correctly on death or music stopping playing. I've only got one game breaking bug once, but since the game saves often it wasn't a big issue.❌ While I found that a joystick offered a more enjoyable experience, targeting with your powers using the joystick proved pretty challenging at some moments. The snap helps, but there are still some tedious moments because of that.❌ The end part of the story felt maybe a bit rushed. Not catastrophically so, but I would have enjoyed a bit more development on the last part.❌ The game doesn't seem to have any accessibility / difficulty settings, and it might have benefited from some.Overall this game is a great puzzle platformer, and I definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys this kind of games. Obviously inspired from Celeste, it pales a bit in comparison but remains a pretty nice game on its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This was very challenging for me. I like challenge in my games, but I'm not the biggest fan of the genre, so committing time to get good enough to enjoy this wasn't really something I wanted to do. That being said, it seems like a fun game. The ageing mechanics are pretty good, the puzzle style environments were well designed in my opinion and I enjoyed the graphics. The only thing I disliked were the noises the characters made during dialogue scenes. It's obnoxious, but if you're into platformers this seems legit. I especially want to thank the developers for taking the time to actually design a useable keyboard and mouse interface. So many of these indie platformers force you to use the strangest keys and combinations. This felt good to play without a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This puzzle game is simply not fun enough to warrant a $5 price, let alone $15. The puzzles contain a lot of tight timing, and that combined with the janky movement is awful. Even ignoring the sub-par puzzles, the story/exploration is extremely lackluster. Also the game crashes a lot for some reason.I had no drive to complete this game, and considering the mixed reviews, I can imagine that many others feel the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are fun, challenging, rewarding, and frustrating at the same time. Almost quit a few times. I had to pause and then come back again and again because it was so stressful at times. Not recommend for hot-headed people of course! The graphic is okay - kind of. I do not personally like the graphic like this but gave it a try anyway, and it was kind of fun. So, it is forgiven and became kinda cute. The mechanic is good. I only hate it when it requires a perfect run for bosses and some puzzles. You really need to die and repeat over and over. and over and over. until you get it ( if not already quit). I am quite new for this genre of games though. But I would recommend you to give it a try. At least it proved me wrong that the games with this kind of graphic are too childish. I am about 60-70% in the story at the time of review. Enjoy the experience so far. Not sure if I could finish it before I can't stand the frustration or not though. Hahaha.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game. I was expecting a Celeste kinda game and instead I found a great puzzle platformer. I must say that that platforming feels quite nice, but the bow controls are clunky and there seems to be some bugs. The story well, it's not the best, but the scenarios and the mechanics included in each compensate making it a great experienc. Died a few times enjoye the puzzles and overall great chill game. 7.5/10 :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Its disappointing to put a thumbs down for that game because I had a great time with the vast majority of puzzles through the game, but coming to the hell elevator where failing a challenge would undo your most recent success trying to force you to succeed through 6 challenges of understanding, timing, and at times accuracy and speed felt like a terrible terrible way to reward the player for coming this far.Once I saw myself regress twice I just alt-f4ed and uninstal. A really awful design decision that leaves a sour taste in my mouth and makes me feel like I shouldn't trust that developer in the future. Really disappointed and sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the normal levels and the collectible hunting, but hated every boss level. The extreme lack of checkpoints in these encounters make them incredibly tedious to go through. I don't know, maybe some people like having to repeat a large number of areas every time they make a mistake (potentially redoing a single screen dozens of times), but I'm not one of them. It's a shame though because I really found the mechanics interesting, and the puzzles are a great treat. There's no feeling quite like finally figuring out how to get a collectible after many attempts. Heck, I also enjoy any specific screen during boss encounters because they're a nice combination of frenetic and logical. I just really wish I don't have to repeat them more times than I really have to.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:- Challenging platforming- Good variety of mechanics without being overwhelming- Some problems have multiple solutions, encouraging creativity- Lots of optional challenges to demonstrate mastery- Interesting story, but story doesn't get in the way of gameplayDisliked:- Some challenges felt convoluted or overly precise- In some areas, failure means a significant setback- Physics occasionally felt inconsistent, making strategizing difficult
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a good story and idea, the main premise being that you can age and unage things. The issue I have with this game is minor - it's puzzles are sometimes too strange and it's sometimes easier to just cheese the puzzle than try to figure out what it seems to want you to do (I will admit I had to go through walk-throughs for some of these, but the walk-throughs I saw also seemed to cheese some of these puzzles). This doesn't happen very often though, and I had a lot of fun playing this. One other issue I had is sometimes the mechanics just break -  but it isn't too much of an issue as it'll fix itself once you shut down and start the game back up. Overall, I find the game interesting, the mechanics are fairly smooth, easy to use and the story is pretty good so I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels a lot like Celeste in a lot of ways, but the gameplay is more geared toward puzzles than platforming.  The game so far is thankfully slower and demands a lot less precision than Celeste.  I would recommend this to anyone who wanted to play Celeste but is turned off by pixel perfect platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think ageless deserves such a low review score (65% positiv reviews atm). Thus, I write a short review.Overall I'd recommend the game. I feel like it deserves a positive review score around 80%. It's not a masterpiece like Celeste or Portal but still good. More details:Ageless-is more a puzzle game than a platformer (platforming challenges are pretty rare I'd say [for example boss levels]).-has extremely good music which I (sadly) rarely recognized while playing the game.-has a fair learn curve for the mechanics. Not everything is fully explained by the game itself but in such situations you just have to rethink a few mechanics you already know.-has good controls. Only the wall jump felt sometimes a little frustrating.-story is good but couldn't create an impact. It feels extremely rushed.-is not a masterpiece but was fun the most time.Small additional cons:-some puzzles felt like I didn't solve them as intended. -minor bugs (2-3 in my playthrough I think which could be solved by leaving the level and continuing the story which puts you at the exact point where you left)-aiming and shooting arrows feel a little frustrating sometimes (with controller)
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game has way too many negative reviews. There is certainly room for some polish, but the mechanics are actually solid and consistent. The first world is mediocre, and the first boss is awful. The game exponentially improves after the first world. Puzzles are interesting. Each world has its own unique gimmick. Aging concept is very well implemented. Definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the reviews I have seen only seem to sum up the first world of the game. I was surprised to see that the game mechanics were used this well all along the game.To me the only let down is that the game expects perfection from us, but doesn't always deliver back to the player. Because if I am asked this much, I also expect the same in return. Unfortunately, the control response, the enemy hit-box and some other minor elements will sometimes prevent you to perform smoothly to feel satisfied. In its whole, the challenge, graphics, story did convinced me, and I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: It could use a few bug fixes, but the main block is the cool-down on the freeze-time ability mixed with the timing of certain... "puzzle"(?) mechanics. It's got the ambition to hit the Celeste sweet-spot, which is a good ambition to have, but it misses the mark. It appears to be the first game from the dev, so hopefully they've learned from this game, and I'd be interested to look at their next trip out, but this one doesn't work for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle platformer where you play a girl with the ability to make things older or younger. It's okay but I found the controls to be a bit too imprecise, and some of the puzzles require specific timing where if you fail, you have to go aaall the way back to the beginning of the puzzle and do it all over again which ended up being too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is a story driven puzzle platformer where you must alter the age of animals and plant life around you to progress. Play as Kiara, a young girl who braves through heartache and loss as she journeys across a mysterious world to discovers its secrets and herself.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator
detailed_description: Join our Discord Upcoming features About the Game Features: Unique visuals inspired by medieval manuscripts and medical books. Hyper satisfying physical interactions with ingredients and equipment. Sandbox style gameplay where you have many different avenues available, and it’s up to you to figure out the best way to complete each task. Sell your potions to the townsfolk while roleplaying as a noble artisan, a greedy weasel, an occult dark master, or whomever else you may wish to be! Work with all sorts of ingredients Leaves, flowers, berries, roots, fruits, minerals, and a plethora of mushrooms are at the ready for your mortar and pestle. Just like espresso, the fineness of the grind matters! Learn the art of potion making Concoct your potion plan. Grind ingredients and carefully mix them in your cauldron. Heat the coals. Boil and stir. Add the base: water, oil, or… something else. Congrats on your first potion! Was it easy to learn? Now try mastering it! Experiment and invent new recipes Carefully plan your route via the Alchemy Map to combine different effects. Be mindful of common sense: you won’t find a market for a poisonous healing potion… right? Or would you? Sell potions Every day customers will come to your store looking for solutions to their problems. You will face consequences depending on what you decide to sell them. Attract guilds, befriend notable figures (or feud with them), gain riches and influence - and one day, you may even decide the fate of the whole town. Buy ingredients or grow your own Every alchemist needs ingredients. You can buy them from traveling merchants: it can be pricey, but successful haggling may save you some coin. Or you can just grow your own! Get creative with customizing Want to give a special appearance to your best potions? Go ahead! Change bottle shape, label type, icon, and colors. You can even give it a custom name and label description. Carefully arrange your unique potions to showcase them on your shop’s shelves and tables… or carelessly throw them around - we’re not gonna tell you what to do, just have fun!
