_childDocuments_.review: By far, in my opinion, this is the best Jackbox Party Pack I have ever purchased, and played, thus far. Through Sub-category, reviewing each segment, as the entirety of the game.1.):The third one in the series, this is a game of wits/clever commentary within about a minute to answer gap, per round. You are given a category, to fill in what you feel would be or not be the best answer for that category, and you generally compete against other people, each person in your party having their own category, besides the one(s) you compete with. 👍This game is really fun, and they even have separate episodes in the options to choose from, for folks who may be getting married, for children and/or a sports team. Overall, this game has a lot of re-play value, and is especially great for friends or family you are close with. Bear in mind too, that you can include an outside audience, if you so chose to do so. :) 2.) :You start as a 'devil' family, over-going daily chores as a family, sometimes having to involve other parts of the family to complete tasks. However, be aware, also, there is one task that is in red, and causes trouble for the rest of the family, and if the person so chooses to pick that task, the other family members have a chance to stop the devious motive. 👍This game is especially fun with family and/or close friends. However, I do feel it could be repetitive, were it to be played too much. 3.):Get ready to show off your creative and/or possibly not creative but hilarious skills of drawing. Each round, you are given a subject of which what your drawing would be deemed the "champion of [random category]" The first part of each round, a person is given this prompt, and then, the second part of the round, the player is given the other player's champion, and has to create a worthy opponent for this champion, pay mind, the second round person involved is not aware of what the first person round's drawing is the champion of, and have to base it off of the drawing. 👍This game is great, especially with the drawing mechanics, and choices between different pen styles, and different colors. The avatars chosen at the beginning of the game are fun. My family has found it to be quite hilarious, even creating "champions" that make a comeback in following games, and we have a lot of fun, creating new champions. However, this game may not be for everyone, especially if they lack the desire to draw. But even, if you feel you do not possess the ability to draw, it can still be a fun game, for everyone. 4.):This game is a true pop culture game where you are given a category [people, places, things, etc] and it may or may not involve time eras that your party have knowledge there of. However, that does not lose it's charm. You have to make your party guess what it is that you are trying to tell them (the subject you had chose at the beginning of the round) and when they guess, you, the person in charge of the subject chosen, may also use what the other players clues to guess the subject to what it is you are trying to reveal. Whoever guesses the subject, also earns points.  Anyone involved in the cluing toward the subject, if the main player chose your guesses in the category round, also get points. 👍No matter of different time eras and possibly not knowing what the subject may be, this game has a lot of fun and cause people to be in cahoots about it. The ultimate goal is to guess the subject. Whether you like to be clever, and/or immature about things, this game is full of fun. 5.):Imagine trying to sell a product, or making a powerpoint about something. This is exactly what the game is. You are trying to convince your audience that your item, is the best. However, it doesn't necessarily have to be this way. You are given a powerpoint, and an assistant (*ahem* another player in your party) to help you with the powerpoint. You create the context, and your assistant gets to choose a powerpoint slide that is given by the game, that they would feel would fit most (or possibly not fit most) to your speech. You can draw on the photo, creating more hysterically lasting memories. Each player gets to make a comment at the end of the powerpoint, and vote on which one they felt was best, at the end. 👍I do not feel this game may be for everyone, however, it can grow quite hilarious, depending on the party you play with. Clever-minded to immaturity, this game is overall fun.

_childDocuments_.review: No disclaimer about the fact that I'm European this time around. This Jackbox Party Pack has a Filter for US-Centric content, to make it accessible to the broader audience around the world. Definitely a welcomed addition. You might still note that all of those games were played with the aforementioned option turned on.- YES, GET IT AT ALL COSTS!!- A classic of the Jackbox Games.- The best of all.- Simple and fun.- Infinitely replayable.Schmitty's back for some more Quiplashing. The concept of Quiplash just never gets old. It's easy to understand in 2 sentences, it's hilarious and moreover, its third round FINALLY was improved with THREE answers to input in a prompt. This leaves space for even more creativity and laugh moments. The "make your own" mode is still there even. I think they've really hit the spot here. My personal note is .- Developed from what was an April Fools' joke.- Cooperation game with a tiny bit of deception.- Interesting concept of interactive tasks on phone.The cooperative game that will really get the interest of Jackbox players. It is fun in its own way (perhaps different from the rest of the series). There is a complexity to it. It marries cooperation and individualism very well. It has many challenges and the theme is just well made. It is however barely playable on a browser or so I'm told, so try to play it on your smartphone. A mic might sometimes be required. It must also be better if played with all players in the same room. Personal note is .- The best drawing game ever made by Jackbox.- Hilarious battle of drawings.- Leaves space for creativity.- AMAZING SOUNDTRACK!Everything is in the lines above. The concept well detailed and easy to understand. Despite being a drawing game, it proved absolutely hilarious and accessible. So many twists. It has an infinite replayability. The universe is absolutely awesome. Nothing else to say, that's in my top 3 of my favourite games from Jackbox. Most of my friends approve as well. Personal note is .- Will definitely please the fans of Patently Stupid.- Can be tricky to understand at first, stressful if first timers are talking first.- Can be quite funny once people grab the concept.- Room for creativity pretty much everywhere.Met with a bit of mixed opinions at first in my own sessions. Despite that, if people understand it and are able to improvise, it can prove to be very funny. The speaker and the assistants' thinking and cooperation is what will make their presentation hilarious. It is best played with a mic. It has to be a lot better if done in front of a big screen with all players in the same room, like Patently Stupid. I have to try that out one day. Personal note is .- Very tricky, even with the US-Centric filter on.- Satisfying when you find the answer.- Requires players making others guess to think a lot to succeedThe less funny game of the pack, but not a bad one. It basically calls for some basic trivia and guesswork. That said, the concept is easy, it's using it that isn't as the host of the guess. Could definitely benefit from some additions in terms of possibilities when creating a sentence. My personal note is .The best Jackbox Party Pack EVER CREATED. To this day, as 2020, I can only recommend that you get this pack above any other. It is the funniest, most accessible and replayable pack Jackbox has ever made. Very good Job, developers, this one will probably be the most played and requested one until - one can wish - The Party Pack 8!

_childDocuments_.review: The most recent entry at the time of writing, and also by far the best pack. 4 out of the 5 games in The Jackbox Party Pack 7 are exceptional party games that knock every other instalment in this series out of the water. Champ'd Up is an endlessly entertaining game about creating characters and putting them head to head to compete in strange and specific tournaments, and is the best game in this pack. Quiplash 3 is the most recent Quiplash, and is probably the most famous Jackbox game, a simple but very effective game about answering prompts and voting for the funniest answers. Talking points is a great improv game where you present a power point presentation while your partner makes it at the same time, using quick thinking very important. The Devils and the Details is a very chaotic coop game where you complete as many warioware-esque microgames as possible to blend in with human society. Blather Around is the weakest entry, essentially just verbal charades, but you can ignore it's difference in quality due to how great the other 4 games are in this pack. I would strongly recommend this pack above each other one in the series, it's easily the best in the series, both for someone brand new to Jackbox, or someone who owns and has played every previous on before. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox Party Packs come in all shapes and sizes, and include a number of different games within them. So I'll break down this review based on types of games in this pack:CO-OPERATIVE PLAY!This pack includes some AWESOME cooperative play games. Devils and the Details is a crazy fun game where you work together to complete random challenges. It involves a lot of yelling so make sure your microphone is working for this one!But the real star of the show is Blather Round, a creative take on the classic Password. You basically try to describe your prompt using awkward language (e.g. you might us "sad liquid event" to get people to guess Titanic). I've played this game with family, friends, and even random strangers online, and it is always a blast. Worth the price of admission 👍🏼FUNNYQuiplash is a lot of fun, a great game to play with friends. Basically you're just trying to give the funniest or most amusing responses to prompts.DRAWINGChamp'd Up is a high energy game where you draw and name characters, and vote for the best ones. I still like Drawful a bit better, but the music and the whole vibe of this game makes it stand out.TRIVIAThis party pack is not the best game option if you just want to play a straight trivia challenge. For trivia heads I'd recommend looking into Party Pack 5 or 6 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Best pack by far.Played through all of the games with a discord server full of friends for 2+ hours. Each game made us laugh and was worth the time playing.Quiplash 3: It's Quiplash. All you need to know. Clay animations replacing the usual in-game patterns was really nice.The Devils and The Details: Probably the most hilarious experience of the night. Everyone screaming at each other to stop throwing the game, the satisfaction of actually winning, etc hits different. Absolutely love it.Champ'dUP: TKO-2. Fun to be had by all when you know people are going to draw bodily things which go up against other bodily drawings. Characters, music, nice to look at UI makes the game work well.Talking Points: [IMPORTANT] Streamers, this is the odd-game out if you are playing alone with an audience on twitch or youtube as talking is basically required. The actual gameplay made it worth it, as once you get going it'll either be really hard or easy to win. _childDocuments_.review: My tier list of these games:Champed upHas awesome art and music. Having your drawing fight for a title is really fun and everyone I've played this game with has enjoyed it a lot. I can see why people would buy this pack for this game. Always ends with us laughing together over prompts and drawings.Talking PointsThis game is super fun when you're playing with the right people. _childDocuments_.review: Word Spud.Lie Swatter.Civic Dodole.Zeeple Dome.Joke Boat.They've been waiting for a year for their new member.They will have to keep waiting.There are no bad games here.Champ'd Up is a real treat for people who love to draw, and even people that only draw black and white stick figures can join in and stand a chance. So much unintentional humour - and a lot of fun to be had by trying for some humour if you can guess your opponent's prompt and make a deconstruction of it. You get to keep your drawings for the next game if you play with the same players, too! Compared to Tee K.O., it feels like a better flow because you draw two things at a time and every drawing is used at least once, possibly more because there's four drawings and six rounds per person (and again, they can be used in the next game.) Also includes the best part of Bracketeering with none of its bad.Blather 'Round is like Taboo with less control, and hilarity when someone guesses Oedipus off of "They are tragic; They feel the mommy." Or a rush to type Atlantis after the hint is "it's a not tall liquid civilization."Devils and the Details is designed to make people talk over each-other and get frantic. I need more time with this one to say much about it.Talking Points is a chill game where people probably don't care about the points. It can be cute and/or wholesome. It has a "free mode," but I don't see why you'd want it unless you use it to make custom restrictions.Quiplash is Quiplash.

_childDocuments_.review: This pack is a winner! The look of the Quiplash 3 is great, the returning feature of making your own questions maintains it as probably their best game. Champ'd Up may feel like the t-shirt game from a previous pack, but cultivates it's own feeling as you build your team over multiple rounds. _childDocuments_.review: As someone new to Jackbox as a series, this one definently hooked me! Had so much fun, even with my small group of four friends on Discord (the game can support a minimum of four players). That said, this game, like the others as I've heard, has hits and misses. I'll go over every game now.Quiplash 3: Simple fun boiled into a game. This game is a favorite among'st everyone and rightfully so. The simple act of pitting two quips together and picking the winner feels so much better than something like CaH, which I find fun as well. In Quiplash 3, you must write a quip to fill in the blank of a question asked by the narrator. It gets worse though on round 3, Thriplash and its 3 quip format never is really funny and we've even sometimes just skipped over it to get to the next round. Although, I hear others like it, so its probably our preference. Overall, 6/7.The Devil's and the Details: I hear people ragging on this one, and I see why, but I think its still a nice little game to touch on every once and a while. You must complete simple (extremely simple) minigames to increase your family score by the end of each day. You can also perform selfish tasks to increase your score. While the family score keeps the team alive, the game is decided by YOUR overall score, so you have to pick your tasks wisely, as some aren't worth the points. This one is fun, but maybe not a repeat play depending on what type of person you are. The style is very charming, reminds me of Hazbin and Helluva Boss. 4.5/7Champ'd Up: This is very situational laughs, although, its contained some of my hardest guffaws in the whole pack when people know how to draw their champs. You draw champions against another players underdog fighting for silly titles. I prefer Tee K.O. but this is fine. In my opinion, it requires your friend group to be very creative, but I'm sure my friends are just bad, although this isn't a good quality for a party game. I do sound like I'm talking bad here, but its a very fun game if you play well and you will at least chuckle a little in the round. 5/7Talking Points: I hear so much hate for this one... I have literally no clue why, this is EASILY the best game in the pack, and probably the hardest to explain. Players start by filling in 3 different talking points and they are sent out. Players pick which of the other players ones they wish to speak about. One by one, each of them, assisted by another player to bring up pictures for their presentation, must publicly speak to the group and just keep talking. The goal is to just keep talking about whatever is on screen and create strange stories and silly motivational speeches. This one has had me laughing HARD every round, sometimes multiple times. Most of the pictures are amazing, but sometimes if you end up with a bad assistant, you'll struggle. Other than that tiny detail, this one is a blast for everyone who can keep talking, you probably should inform new players on this detail, since most of my group just read the titles and hardly talked when the pictures came up. I love this one though and at least someone will enjoy this. 7/7Blather Round: DISCLAIMER! Don't get this with a group of 4. This is probably the most annoyingly hard game with fewer than 5 players due to the nature of it. This is charades with words. You get a pop culture name, and the other players have to narrow it down while you give them hints off a board. This one probably can be fun, but its only fun if a lot of people are guessing at once. I feel the guessers should have more time. As it stands, its ALWAYS a flat minute no matter the player amount. It's overall fine, and other people seem to like it. 5/7Overall, all the games are pretty solid, even TD&TD is good on the first few plays. This one is great for new people to the series, and allows some of the older fans to have a great time too. I'll be back again for Party Pack 8! 6.5/7
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: First of all let me say that I'm a sucker for jackbox games but I'll still give an honest review.This is pack is a good pack and has some interesting stuff which can be fun and not so fun. The 5 games included in this pack are:-Quiplash 3-The Devils and The Details-Champ'd Up-Talking Points-Blather 'RoundI'll go over each game equaly.First is Quiplash 3:If you do not know what type of game this is let me explain. At the start of a round people get to input some funny things to get some chuckles with some jokes. They can be fill in the blank prompts or something you have answer. After answering the two prompts the people with the same prompt get to go against each other and the person with the most votes in their answer wins that round.This game is as always okay and can be fun if not ruined by some jokes, but if you have some good hitting jokes it can be fun.The new triplelash is fun if you have a good prompt because you have to give this question 3 answer at the same time.Now its time for The Devils and the Details:I personaly like this game a lot but so far not many in my friend group don't as much.In this game you are a family of devils who have work together by doing simple tasks and getting enough point to win the game. These tasks can be from: Doing the dishes to mowing the lawn and many other things.But there are also some other thing at stake because there are also some thing called selfish tasks. If you do these you can get big points for only yourself which will not help the family score. But you only get these points if you are not stopped before its to late.Ive played this game with some friends of mine and we agree that this game can be a lot more fun with a full group. Because if all 8 slots are taken there is a lot more chaos and scream at each other to either get some help doing a task or trying to stop someone from doing a task.Next is Champ'd Up:In this game you have to draw a specific champion like 'The champion of Cuteness'. After you draw your champion someone else will get your drawing and without knowing what kind of champion it is have to draw an underdog to try and win against the champion.This game is really fun. You get enough time to draw and name you character and even the characters that "Draw" these champions are nicely made. Not really much to comment on.Next is Talking Points:In TP you have to give a talk about a specific topic made by another person (which are fill in the blank statements). In these talk one person will give the talk and another person the, the assistant, will create slides by choosing text and an image to talk about.This game can be really funny if the assistant can get got slides and text. Not all of the time will you get a good looking presentation which is a bummer. Ive had talks which were really funny because the person talking got really go images but so far every time i got to be an assistant my choice of images were really dumb and bad.And at last but not at all least is Blather 'Round:In this game everyone needs to choice a prompt like a: person, story, thing or place. After choosing your prompt you need to create a small sentence trying to hint at the prompt. These sentences are really simple because you get to only choose from a specific word list.So for example I choose the word 'Minion' and with the sentence 'Its a BLANK BLANK' i have to choose words to try and explain/hint at the word i choose.After the first hint i get to try and make as much as hints possible trying to make people guess easier what my word is.After playing this game me and my friends find this the best game in the pack. Its easy to learn (like really easy) and if you get it right it just feels so good.In one game the first hint got shown and the first guess was immediately the right answer.Over all this is a ery noice pack. Games are fun and easy to learn and over good to play.Now for some scores:Quiplash 3 - 6/10 - Fun but still the same game though.The Devils and the Details - 7.4/10 - Can probably be really fun in a big/full group but still fun.Champ'd Up - 8.2/10 - Easy drawing game and challenging.Talking Points - 5.8 - Need to be lucky to get some funny stuff.Blather 'Round - 9/10 - So easy and so fun. Best one for sure.And in the end i give this pack a: 8.2/10.-Worth it-

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is considered by many to be the best pack, and I'd even argue that there's no truly bad games featured here.First off, there's no trivia game. It sucks because some of the most famous/popular jackbox games ARE TRIVIA GAMES. YDKJ, Fibbage, TMP, none of that is here. If you want a good pack featuring a trivia game, I'd focus on 3, 4, or 6.You get two prompts, you answer them in funny ways, and then you're put up against somebody else to see who's was funnier. The open response style makes this game great for inside jokes with friends! People tend to dislike the final round (Thriplash: answer with three short responses instead of one long response,) but I actually prefer this over the final rounds from earlier games. Also I HAVE to mention the clay-mation style, it really helps make the game stand out more, and it looks awesome.9/10You complete small tasks by swiping, tapping, holding, etc. The game shines when you have to actually communicate with other players, whether it be through telling them that "left" does not mean "straight" when driving a car, or yelling at them to stop trying to sabotage the family score. The game is absolute chaos and it's fun because of it. Given, it does get repetitive.7/10You receive a champion title (i.e. Champion of Disappointment) and you need to draw + name a character that fits the category. Then your character is sent to another player, and they need to try and create a new character without knowing the original category. The two are put up against each other and people vote for the best one Quiplash style. I want to praise this game because either this or Drawful: Animate probably have the best drawing tools in the entire series. Not much else to say, just a really solid game.9/10So this might just be my inner theatre kid/improv bias, but this is probably the funniest jackbox game (if played with the right people.) To play, you and another player are set to improv a presentation based off whatever topic the speaker picked. The second player has to select text and images to pop up for the speaker so they can tie them into whatever they're talking about. The comedy in this game mainly comes from the shock value, but it thankfully never overstays it's welcome. My only big problem with it is that the Awards Ceremony is honestly really stupid.9/10It's word charades. You pick a topic, then use a combination of premade senteces and a list of words to describe it, in hopes the other players will be able to guess it. I don't know why, but me and my friends actually got a really good laugh out of this, even though it's the only game in the pack that ISN'T meant to be funny (there is an arguement that Devils and the Details should be here, but I digress.) This game has a large community of people that dislike it, and I can't blame them, but I personally think it's a great mix up from the more comedy-focused games in the pack.7/10In my opinion, the overall best pack. The lack of any trivia, social deduction, or more team based games is disappointing, but if you can get past that then you'll be left with a pack that has very little to dislike.Average Game Rating: 8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with each game:The Devils and the Details: The best one in my opinion, I love doing the chores they tell me and my friends what to do, and me and my friends screaming at each other the directions was amazing.Champ'd Up: We weren't expecting this one to be fun or good because we normally don't like drawing games, but holy lord do we love it. It gives us a prompt which is what I didn't like about most drawing games, and the drawings we made were very funny.Quiplash 3: It's quiplash... that's it.Talking Points: Us improvising a presentation with no knowledge of what the slides are, are amazing. We, at first, thought the game was only fun if you're good at improvising what you see, but the third time we played this, we were laughing so hard, because of how we just said, "♥♥♥♥ it," and just said what came to mind. I won that game because my mom went into my room and I screamed, "WELCOME TO MY PRESENTATION!" and made my friends cry from laughter.Blather 'Round: Probably the worst one, but not bad. _childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is a vibrant collection of party games that is a delightful addition to any social gathering or virtual hangout. Released as part of the well-loved Jackbox Party Pack series, this installment maintains the tradition of delivering unique, entertaining, and easy-to-join multiplayer experiences accessible across various devices. This pack includes five diverse games, each offering its flavour of humour and gameplay mechanics, ensuring that there's something for every type of player.Many consider Quiplash 3 the standout game. It is a sequel to the fan-favorite comedy showdown in which players compete to create the funniest answers to quirky prompts. A new final round adds a fresh twist to the game's dynamics.The Devils and the Details is a chaotic cooperative game in which players take on the roles of a family of devils trying to blend into suburban life. It requires teamwork and communication, and depending on the group's cohesion, it can be a hit or miss.Champ’d Up is a drawing fighting game where players create absurd characters to compete in bizarre contests. It's particularly appealing for its creative freedom and hilarious outcomes.Talking Points is an improvisational speech game that tests players' quick thinking. Given random slides, players must deliver a compelling presentation, which leads to plenty of laughter and memorable moments.Blather 'Round is a guessing game that challenges players to describe a secret prompt using a limited vocabulary. It's both challenging and entertaining, perfect for those who love word games.Overall, The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is a solid addition to the series, offering a mix of creativity, humour, and social interaction. Its strength lies in the variety of games and the ease with which players can join, making it a must-have for parties. However, the enjoyment of some games can depend heavily on the group's dynamics, with certain games requiring more creativity or coordination than others. Regardless, this pack is a testament to Jackbox Games' ability to innovate continuously in the party game genre. It is a recommended purchase for those looking to liven up their gatherings.

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed bag consisting of great ideas and graphic design, and critical oversights that should have been spotted in any kind of beta testing/QA.: best final round format so far, claymation/carnival theming is good and much more fun than the flat abstract backdrops of the previous entries: Very good fodder for aspiring improv comedians and probably will be the most popular at parties, but the scoring system is totally broken by the inclusion of the Engagement Bonus.: Only fun the first few times, the prompts are usually obvious or too hard to guess, and the answers are fed to the presenter through the list of words they're given.: Fun to look at, and an opportunity for the maniacs who bring drawing tablets to the party to destroy the competition. The urge to vote based on the quality of the drawing rather than how well it meets the objective will regularly cause player confusion.: Getting enough people to voluntarily play this game is a logistical issue in itself, and for this reason I've only played it once. It's a ton of fun for people who don't mind the stress of simulating a very chaotic living environment. It's likely very underrated.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best pack in the series. The pack does not contain a single dull game like the previous packs usually do and manages to keep the unique jackbox feel throughout them all. I'm just gonna go through all the games in order of their appearance on the menu, give them a rating, and tell you why they deserve it.Quiplash 3 - 9/10 - Probably the game that the most people was excited for and it certainly met the hype. The new art style is a nice refresher to the classic 2D art style in the two prequels. Tiny additions like being able to choose your own avatar before the start of the game are appreciated and a decent and consistent third round is a nice touch. Overall, with much more creative prompts and a whole heck ton of new ways to make people laugh it gets a solid 9. Why it doesn't deserve a 10 is that the game hasn't went under many changes gameplay wise. It is still the same game as the original essentially with the exception of the third round.The Devils and the Details - 7.5 - The most intense game in jackbox history by far. You essentially complete "household" tasks in order to reach a certain score by midnight in order to move on. Nothing in this nature has ever been done in a jackbox game and its nice to have something this chaotic. Something that jackbox games take pride in my opioion is their easy to learn nature. This game is far from easy to learn, it basically spits a bunch of information at you and says good luck. People who have little experience gaming, will have no clue what they are doing and even someone like me who is an experienced gamer, found it difficult to get the hang of it. It took my friends and I three attempts to get past the first day which is supposed to be the easiest, and YES you have to complete an entire week to win (each day being 5-7 minutes long). Once you get the hang of it, it is pretty fun.Champ'd Up - 7/10 - If you were to incorporate Quiplash, TeeKO, Bracketeering, and a football game, this is what you would get. The game is you draw a champion that goes along with the title of the belt and then you make a challenger to a champion that someone else drew, then you vote, lame. It would've been the perfect game to add some form of combat into it but I guess democracy is the fan favorite. There just isn't really anything unique about the game. You just vote for whatever drawing fits with the theme better or whatever one is the most funny, just like most of the drawing games they've made.Talking Points - 10/10 - Instantly a classic. One of the few games that make you want to keep playing for more than one or two rounds. You start out just like Patently stupid filling in the blanks to certain prompts and other people choosing between 3 of them in which to present to the game. After that people will present their topic except they have no clue what their presentation slides would look like. Each presenter will be assigned an assistant whose goal is to help the presenter by setting up their slides by choosing a certain picture or text. Having the assistant the ability to chose a picture of avocado toast to a god-like dear when you're talking about divorce struggles is just wicked funny. Rating's actually mean something too as if the presenter does good, the audience will, hopefully, rate it higher, giving the presenter more points. Although the creating an award at the end is nice, it would be better if the award names were premade.Blather 'Round - 8/10 - Sweet and simple yet somewhat chaotic. It is a fun guessing game that anyone can pick up and enjoy. Everyone picks a thing, ranging in difficulty, for the other player to try and guess. When it is a person's turn to describe what their thing is, they will have to use premade phrases and words to help the guessers guess it. The describer can also use words that the guessers have guessed in order to better describe their thing. I for one love a intense guessing game and this is a nice touch to the jackbox universe, it just isn't anything super special.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually writing a serious review for this game (even though definitely no one will read it) because idk I just feel the need to.Overall, I honestly feel like this is the best Jackbox Party Pack, at least judging from the ones that I've played. None of the games in the pack are a miss; some are better than others, but I still have a ton of fun with all of them.Quiplash 3: Obviously it's just another Quiplash but the "thriplash" questions are a really nice addition that I enjoy, and I really like the new claymation look. I'm personally a big fan of Quiplash, so this game was the main reason I bought the pack, and it turns out that all the games on it are super fun :)The Devils and the Details: This game is REALLY fun with a lot of people; it's very chaotic but in a good way. Reminds me a little bit of Among Us, but less aggressive. A very fun and unique game.Champ'd Up: This game is kind of like a weirder version of Tee-KO (which I enjoy a lot), but it is also really fun and never fails to give my friends and I some good laughs.Talking Points: I honestly believe that this is the best game in the pack by far. The presentation aspect makes it feel very similar to Patently Stupid, but the premise of the game is completely fresh and I've never played anything like it. SUPER fun and makes me laugh hysterically.Blather 'Round: This game is very underrated, in my opinion. It's definitely less of a funny game, and can actually be a bit difficult at times. It's like a mix of trivia and charades. Despite it not being as wacky/quirky as the other games, I still really enjoy playing it (also it has a kind of 80s aesthetic which I vibe with SO hard).To summarize, every game in this pack is super fun in different ways, and I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys any of the past Jackbox games, and to people who have never played Jackbox and are looking for some fun party games to play with family or with friends online. :)

_childDocuments_.review: pretty solid jackbox all-around. there's a couple stinkers but overall worth the pricetag, though it wouldn't hurt to just wait for it to go on sale or get a cheaper previous jackbox either.quiplash 3 is definitely the star of the show, and is a monumental upgrade over 2 simply due to improving greatly on the absolute headache that was quiplash 2's last lash. it's quiplash, a third time, and the third round is just "answer the same question 3 times" which is a great set-up for a "normal-normal-unexpected" answer and just generally a good formula. only complaint is that if you're playing with an odd number of players someone has to contend with shmitty's often very unfunny answers, which is just kinda lame.devils and the details is very chaotic and messy. only played once but it feels like playing mario party on crack with imposter syndrome and bad impulse control so I'm not too crazy about it. having to play little instruction based minigames and cooperate/sabotage is an interesting concept but it's no bomb corp.champ'd up is one of those slow-burn games that gets better as the rounds go on, calling back to jokes made several rounds/games ago can make for hilarious comeback moments and is just fun overall. one of the games that draws the most on... well, drawing, and creativity and is just a great recipe for stupid in-jokes and off-kilter match-ups. despite my glowing praise I have to say that the first few rounds can be a little more slow and plain, but it's a good starter to break the ice in that case too.talking points is bad for introverts and those bad at public speaking. or maybe because of that it's good for them? in any case it's best to play this down a few drinks and act like you're the one member of the group project who didn't do any work and now you have to handle the presentation as a result. great for chatty groups but the voting/hype system is a little bit pointless as it's always maxed out anyway.blather round is great for in-jokes as well, and just overall a fun way to play what is essentially digital charades except with pre-made word-cards instead of actions. can be a little frustrating if your group chemistry is a little off or new so don't play this unless you're playing with some friends you know at least decently well.like I said, overall a great pack. tl;dr very good and creatively-inclined games but a couple are a little too chaotic or reliant on good group chemistry to work as party ice breakers. if you want something better to get to know people, I recommend packs 3-5.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished playing this game and let me start by saying, fantastic game. Now you might be thinking that means I've had a great evening, and it would be a fair assumption, but come and sit round the camp fire and listen to my tale.Sunday will always have a funny feeling to it - Work is looming and the weekend is over and it's easy to forget about the adventures that have been had. Opening Jackbox TV, in a room of people I would have called friends had you asked me 2 hours ago, was a welcome distraction. It brought some hope to my day. Maybe, just maybe all was not lost. Oh what a fool I was. Little did I know I was about to embark on a path of destruction and betrayal.However brilliant this game is, it has a real way of exposing the snakes and the phonies among us. One game of Quiplash 3 and I was already horrified by what I saw. As I watched my genius, beautifully crafted answers get outvoted for moronic gibberish such as the 'The Flying Constable' I could feel the tears forming in my eyes. I powered through the emotions and held it together like a champion. It was especially difficult as I was also carrying the conversation with these dullards so it was essentially a double whammy.Next we had a game of Devil's and the details. Wow - Just wow. As I selflessly rang to cancel dinner plans, fixed the car and ordered birthday cakes. These cretins poured themselves glasses of wine and aimed for their solo win. Now I'm not naive, I understand there is a lot of darkness in this world. I just wasn't aware how close to home it really was. Finally, because the oafs were not satisfied with just ruining my night a little bit, we jumped into a game of Talking points. Player 1 headed to the podium and the silence was deafening. We were playing a game all about speech and not a word was spoken. Easy win you might be thinking, but to my disgust the positive votes were flying in. Upvote after upvote for the mute speech. I know you must be hoping I am joking, but alas I am not. Cruel is the only way I can describe my fate right now on this poisoned evening.After this appalling display, it fell upon my shoulders to save the evening. I delivered an impassioned, emotional speech. A passer by shouted up to my window that he felt as if it was almost an out of body experience. Thank you Steve. I put myself in the firing line and guess what they did? They fired. The cowards ran for the hills when it was their turn.I'm no mind reader but I know you're all thinking, 'How amazing must you be to put up with all of this?' and yes I am probably a hero but I'm not here for credit or praise. This is a tale of caution and woe. Play this game, but be careful who you play with,Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I can say without much hesitation that this is easily my favorite of the party packs. All of the games are some of Jackbox's best, and visually the game really pops.Can't speak much to how it works for streaming since I only play with groups of friends, but I'd recommend this to literally anyone interested. For more specifics on the games included:Quiplash is always solid, and this iteration is no exception. Being able to add custom sets of prompts adds so much potential, and the base prompts are solid as ever. Thriplash is a really nice addition too, and the claymation of the background looks cool as hell, if a bit trippy. The Devils and the Details is a really charming game that has players working together while at the same time trying to do things to raise their own personal score. Personally I think it's a lot more fun with less players, since communication is key, and with a full group it's hard to coordinate, but it's pretty fun either way.Champ'd up is easily my favorite. The concept of creating characters to pit against each other is so charming and has lead to a ton of chaotic rounds. Being able to tag in previous drawings during the second round adds an extra layer of strategy to it as well.Talking Points is a really cool concept done extremely well. You have to give a presentation on a topic you choose out of one's players submitted, but the slides how images are controlled by another player. Whether or not you like this game is pretty dependent on how good you are at improvising, but irregardless it gets a lot of laughs. And Blather Round, which is a really solid charades-like game where you have to describe something via a jumble of words the game provides you. My only issue with this is that the game crashes 90% of the time when I try to play it. This only happens with this game, and I'm not sure if it's an issue in general, or just on my end. Irregardless, it's fun enough that it's been worth the risk.Overall, this pack is very worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Jackbox pack in years, and arguably the best ever!Most packs have one or two great games, one or two okay games, and one or two duds. #6 was extremely weak, with most games being merely okay and several being pretty bad - I maintain that #6 is the single weakest release of the entire series. #5 was also a little lacking, though its best games were pretty great, which balanced out the other not-so-great ones.As such, Jackbox 7 had a lot riding on it. It needed to be a return to form in order to keep the faith of the fans. Man, did it ever deliver. Three out of five games are all-time Jackbox top ten contenders, the fourth is really good with the right crowd, and the fifth isn't great but certainly nowhere near as bad as Word Spud, Zeeple Dome, or Joke Boat. Here's my breakdown:Blather 'Round: One of those games that seems so simple you can't imagine how it could be any good before you try it, but then once you get into it your whole group doesn't want to stop playing! Because of its guessing-game nature it's the only game in the pack limited to six players instead of eight.Talking Points: This is SUCH a weird game, but if you're playing with the right crowd it can be my-stomach-hurts-and-I-can't-breathe hilarious. It's most similar to Patently Stupid and has a similar setup, with fill-in-the-blank lecture prompts instead of problems. Encourages and rewards good team play, which is nice. I recommend this one with a smaller group, though it plays up to eight.Quiplash 3: It's more Quiplash, which is good or bad news depending on how much you like Quiplash. I love it, so it's great news for me! As usual, it plays best with a big crowd, preferably the full contingent of eight. One warning: the claymation visuals can be overwhelming for people with visual sensitivities, but you can turn it off in the options.Champ'd Up: This pack's obligatory drawing game, and it's a classic. A lot of groups will think this is the best game in the pack (for my money it's Blather 'Round, but your mileage may vary). Weirdly similar to Bracketeering in structure, with a mix of guided and blind prompts generating weird drawings of gladiators who then do battle for bizarre titles. Really great fun, even if you suck at drawing, and the drawing tools are unusually advanced. Again, recommended for a big crowd - best with six-plus, though it's still fun with four.The Devils and the Details: The dud of this pack isn't really a dud at all, it's just not my style of game. It's a mostly-cooperative crisis management game like Bomb Inc, Space Team, and Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. I've been playing over Discord, and I suspect this one will work better in person, and I'd recommend a smaller group - with the full eight it would just be a nightmare to play with everyone talking over each other. Doesn't give any room for creativity, either - the comedy all comes from the game's writers. It's perfectly fine, but easily the weakest in the set.I honestly think this might be the best overall Jackbox party pack ever. I will concede that some other packs have better games, but they also have some rubbish ones pulling the average down. The games in #7 range from fine to excellent, giving it the best average. At the very least, it's the best pack since the excellent duo #3 and #4. if you've enjoyed Jackbox in the past but were disappointed by packs #5 or #6, grab this one. It's amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: (At the time of writing this, we have managed to squeeze out 21 hours of playtime)I dont often write reviews, but when I do (on any site, really), it's because I have enough to voice/share about it that I feel like I'm doing a disservice if I wasn't being transparent about it.  So, grab a seat (if you didn't bring your own), and allow me to indulge you about my thoughts on this particular Jackbox Party Pack.I'm actually in love with every game on this pack, which is saying something, because this breaks the mold and trend that the other packs share.  I could name at least one "unpopular" game on every other Jackbox Party Pack from 1-6 where I, as the host, would wish in the deep recesses of my consciousness that the gaming group would steer us away from playing.  JPP7, in many of our opinions, seems to an even distribution of requests and interests piqued.  I will say that some of our non-artistic friends may initially lean away from ,  they quickly learn that, like in  of JPP3, artistic skill does not translate to points or fun.  They realized it's more about the real estate of your imagination, creativity, and sense of humor, rather than who has drawing experience or the best tools at hand.  JPP7 is the example of a product that was sculpted with (1) the lessons the developers have learned throughout the years of creating all these packs, and (2) the voices of their customers -- nay, fans and content creators -- when it came to mitigating the impact that Chaotic Evil forces would try to impose onto streamed and publicized games.(click the spoilers if you want the TL;DR descriptions of each game)The five games are:  * Quiplash 3 * The Devils and the Details * Champ'd Up * Talking Points * Blather 'Round SYNOPSES, REVIEWS, AND RATINGS OF EACH GAMESame format as Quiplash and Quiplash2, with an exception to their Final Rounds, Round 3.   (If you had been under a rock and have no idea what Quiplash is, then I'll simply describe it as a freestyle Cards Against Humanity where the Card Czar is more of a Democracy where points are awarded based on how many people voted for their favorite answer between a contention of two).The final round in this particular pack is called "Thriplash", where players will be provided with three prompt lines (of up to 45 characters max, per line) where they could design an answer card that will be revealed one line at a time from top to bottom.  The claymation artwork on this game is not only present on the game itself, but also animated on the devices that are logged into Jackbox.tv.  There are endless waves of commentary in our games where people feel "satisfied" or "intrigued" by background and foreground art.  The timing between transitions is a major improvement, as well -- Quiplash3's rhythm between scene wipes, moving from prompt to prompt, and presenting the Thriplash makes downtime feel like a thing of the past.If  had ruined your friendships, guilds, or gaming groups, then get them back together with .  For those who have no idea what this  game or are new to Jackbox Party Packs:   is a very straightforward team-building game with a minor element of competition present within the scoreboard and "Selfish Tasks."  Your contestants become a demonic family unit that has to deal with earthly chores, else they be banished back to the underworld by Satan.  Imagine if , escape rooms, and browser-based mini-games all had a baby born of polygamy -- that's basically this game.  You will eventually learn that using  will net you all higher scores, individually and as a team.  The game is very beginner-friendly and easy to pick up, but it will be up to your team as a whole to learn how to master (if you want to optimize scores, of course), and this is what gives it a very high replayable factor.  I imagine that even after you achieve all "A" ratings on their extensive list of episodes, the game will naturally maintain its charm to those who enjoy cooperative play.I gotta say, the first thing most people mention during their first playthrough of this is the /soundtrack.  Beautiful jobs, Devs! The best way to describe this game to another Jackbox player is to ask them to imagine that a , where, in this new version, players have more control on what images and mottos are assembled together, and instead of an Asian-inspired dojo-theme, it has an MMA/boxing scene.For those who tire in my comparisons to games they've never played before: this game will prompt players to illustrate/draw a character that would be pitted against another player's character, with the catch that in each pairing, there will be one person who has no idea what the original prompt was that inspired their opponent.  Imagine freestyle Pictionary and democratic Cards Against Humanity as the parents of this game.The drawing interface and tools on this game are AMAZING improvements to the drawing interfaces from any of the Jackbox Party Packs, including Drawful2.  The outline/pen tool is anchored as a separate layer than the highlighter/marker tool, where the latter is the bottom layer.  What that means is that when you want to fill/color in your drawing, the marker will  override or hide your beautiful work, and thus you don't need to worry as much as before when it came to perspective illustration.  Do your outline, color the character in with the marker, and done!  (And yes, an Undo button is provided!)So this is a unique game of its own, but it's practically like  mixed with giving a Powerpoint Presentation.  The only people who won't be able to participate effectively are text-only players, as this game requires a presenter who can improvise to an audience (there is no stand-in host like in  or .  I think this game is a great exercise for becoming better at public speaking, especially if you're playing with supportive and constructive friends.  Out of the two times we've played this with very different groups, at least one person is laughing to the point of nearly losing their breath.  There is also a Free Play mode to go beyond the boundaries of the vanilla game.This word association game is the odd one out, being that it requires 2-6 players; kind of a bummer that it can't hold up to 8 people.  However, do not underestimate the entertainment value that fans of the classic board game  and trivia-heads would get out of this.  With a limited set of clues and very restricted communication (in fact, the password holder shouldn't talk or text at all), players try to get the rest of the contestants to guess their "Person, Place, or Thing."  Like in , the password holder may start using anything the guessers submitted to help guide them towards the more accurate answers.  Our group is in love with this game, and it is one of the most requested games in our game nights; the pacing of the game is pretty fast, with satisfying cadences of

_childDocuments_.review: Stuck at home? Hate seeing your friends on a 480p call in Zoom? Need a game to satisfy all those inside jokes your friends make? Jackbox Party Pack 7 has got you covered. An amazing sequel which holds up to the name of the Jackbox series. It is one of the best packs which I can for absolute sure recommend to anyone. The Jackbox Party Pack 7 has five amazing games which do their part in making the whole crowd laugh.Let's start with the game we all know and love!Quiplash 3. You might think there isn't anything new we can add to the Quiplash series, but let me just say, that's what we think when Fibbage 3 came out in JPP4. Quiplash 3 follows the same as Quiplash and Quiplash 2, write a funny or witty answer to a prompt and players vote on their favourite answer. The answer with the most votes win. So what's different? The final round! Usually in Quiplash 2, we would either fill out a comic, acronym or etc. In Quiplash 3, you instead follow 'Thriplash', you fill out three separate answers to a prompt. A prompt may be 'Three Things I Should Not Have Brought To School', the answers appear in order, the first, second and third. This is what makes Quiplash 3 the best among the Quiplash series, you could write a funny punchline at the third option or try writing something dirty and suggestive in the three options you get. It is definitely the game that made my friends abandon Quiplash 2 for this version.The Devils & the Details. What can I say about this game? It's innovative, cooperative and fun. You play as a family of devils trying to do mundane human tasks. Each task gives points to the family score. You must achieve a certain amount of family score to finish the day BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE, there are individual scores for each member. You can decide to do a family task earning points for yourself and the family OR try doing selfish tasks which only award points to you and not the family score. Usually these tasks are available a few times, other family members have to stop you if they want to ensure you do not get a high individual score. Every task is a simple one, just follow the instructions, other tasks are more complicated and require multiple players to complete. I do not wish to spoil much of this game but definitely check it out if you're buying the pack. My friends and I had a lot of fun, as we chaotically shout and yell at each other trying to complete tasks. Unfortunately if you are stuck in lockdown, unable to physically play with your friends, I would NOT recommend this game, as it is much more fun if you're playing next to each other, rather than online. It just isn't the same.Champ'd Up. An amazing drawing game that can get you laughing at either the ridiculous references your friends make or how terrible your drawing skills are. Champ'd Up is what I would call one of the better drawing games (besides Patently Stupid). I always hated the drawing games unless it was wacky or fun. For example, TeeKO was quite mundane and could get boring after a few games but with Champ'd Up, you never know what category you are going to get. Simply put, players must draw a 'superhero' according to the category they are given, which can range from 'Hero of Cyberpunk' to 'Hero of [Player] Dreams' and it is quite amazing to see how much your friends suck at drawing. Then after players draw their first hero, they are prompted to draw an 'underdog' to compete against another player's hero, except they can only see the drawing but not the category. Because of this, I feel Champ'd Up is really strong in the party pack, it has fun and wacky ideas with lots of replayability, always ensuring we get a glimpse of terrible drawings and sometimes (honestly my friends are terrible at drawing) you get drawings that should just be framed at an art museum. Played this multiple times and honestly we always came back for a second session, this rarely happens as we usually want to play TMP2 or Quiplash 3. STAY AWAY IF YOU ARE NOT GOING TO DRAW ANYTHING, honestly the amount of times I've seen people not draw anything is ridiculous, the fun part is drawing whatever! Be creative and try to play along! P.S. This has such an amazing soundtrack, go listen to it.Talking Points. The nightmare of every introvert, presenting without any preparation or script! Talking Points is one of the most unique and interesting games, you get a topic to speak about (usually a prompt filled out by another player), then when it is your turn to speak, you will be paired up with another player, that player will choose the slides and text for you while you try your best to present to the other players on your topic. Points are awarded based on how many upvotes players give to your speech, players may give upvotes and downvotes throughout the whole speech. The player in charge of your slides will get a cut of the points earned. It is a good game to get people in a party-ish mood, I've played this several times with my flatmates and they have always seem to get a kick out of it when we present something outlandish and ridiculous, sometimes even offensive! The fun is just watching your friends try to justify their extremely controversial topic in a speech. The drawbacks obviously is that you have to talk! Any friends that are not going to talk or give any effort, tell them to stay away from this game.Blather Round. The ridiculous guessing game that justifies the existence of your friends who know too much about movies/books/films/geography/etc. Blather Round is a game where you have to give clues to other players in the forms of sentences (formed by the game itself, you pick them) of the answer you are given, it can range from a story to a place to a thing. There are not limits to how many guesses people can make, so guess away! The player can also pick other player's guesses as part of their sentences to give more clues! You are usually given three options to pick from and if you don't know any of the three options, you can refresh and can three new options. There is an easy option to pick from but you obtain less points. There are two rounds and they play out the same. The game definitely has strong suits, with your friends trying to outguess each other while furiously typing away. There are many drawbacks however, there is a strong sense around Western culture, so any players that are currently looking into this from a different culture needs to have strong knowledge in Western movies and people, there are some options are not oriented based on culture but it still is a factor to take into account. Additionally, what is disappointing is sometimes if you refresh, you might not even know all six of the answers and are forced to pick an easy option, it's not a big deal but it is something you should note when you are playing this game. Other than that, this is also a solid game in the party pack, my friends had tons of fun with Blather Round, even going for second sessions similar to Talking Points and Champ'd Up. It can be a hit or miss depending on your group of friends but do take my word that all five games are worth a try at least ONCE.All five games are solid, meaning they are fun in each of their own way and are not dull. It's not like the other packs, where one game falls short compared to the rest. I strongly recommend all five games on this pack over JPP6 but just SLIGHTLY. Consider JPP6 and read my review on both before making a choice. My recommendation currently: JPP7JPP6JPP5JPP3 (Only if you are considering NOT getting 7)JPP4JPP2JPP1

_childDocuments_.review: My friends and I have been playing packs 3-6 all the time for our game nights and we tried this pack out on release. It's a general consensus that we all agreed that this is the most fun and well-rounded pack we've had. In my personal opinion, like with a lot of Jackbox games, these games are more fun if you don't worry so much about the scores. Quiplash 3 - Quiplash has always been a classic and having another one is even better! Our games felt a little more smoother and faster-paced than previous ones, and the change to round 3 really pushes our creativity more than just making up acronyms or tv show names.Devils and the Details - Oooo boy, this game got us very rowdy. The idea of working together as a team in addition to boosting a personal score really tests who your friends are. It's pretty chaotic if you're playing this online with friends since screaming over each other in call to help with tasks, but that's just another fun element that encourages coordination.Champ'd Up - My artist friends thrived here. Plenty of drawing to do and it's funny to see how players interpret prompts in different ways for their champs.Talking Points - Our Patently Stupid games have prepared us for this moment. Obviously the outcome of this game depends on how your friends can handle impromptu presentations (hello, stage fright!) and try to make them as serious or as hilarious as they want.Blather 'Round - I was personally skeptical about a game that seemed like another Heads Up, Taboo, etc. However, jumping right into it made us realize how crazy this game can get. Some of my friends had a little trouble with this game as English is a second language, but overall this game is a simple and quick way to get the Jackbox Party rolling. If only it could have more than 6 players.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best packs in the series. Jackbox Party Pack 7 is a must have for groups of friends, whether it be in physical parties or streamed online. Quiplash, arguably the most iconic game in the series, makes a come back in this entry. The final round Thriplash isn't as strong as the other final rounds of the previous 2, but it is still an insanely good time. The Devils and the Details is a chaotic game where players must cooperate with each other but can betray each other to rank #1 devil. While this may not be everyone's cup of tea it is a well made game. Champ'd Up is another hilarious drawing game in which characters must draw opponents to battle each in funny categories. It's a great time no matter the drawing skills of the group. Talking Points is an improv game in which players must give presentations on topics without knowing what's on the slide. It's great to see everyone panicking trying to make connections. Another A+ game in the series. Finally, Blather 'Round is a word guessing game similar to Pictionary but with words. While it is the weakest game in the pack there is still fun to be had with it. Overall Jackbox Party Pack 7 is one of the best packs in the series, a great choice for a party game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best Jackbox Party pack yet!Quick rundown of the games, not how to play, just what I liked/disliked about them.Talking Points: One of my new favourites, as long as everyone is prepared to laugh along and not take it too seriously, this game is awesome, one of my new favourites. Maybe they could add a video feature, or user submitted prompts/photos that would make it so much funnier, but on its own 8/10 game.The Devils and the Details: Again, one of my new favourites. It's better in larger groups of 6+ cause thats when the chaos really starts. It's similar to bomb corp in that you have to work together, but less mentally exhausting and you won't really get too angry at your friends. You can also change the difficulty which is useful for when you play with different groups of people, or don't want to create too much chaos. Love the intro theme too. 9/10Quiplash 3: Quiplash is basically a staple of the party packs at this point. Nothing too special or new, but a solid game non the less. I love the art style for this new one, I do wish that the final round could switch more often like it did with quiplash 2, but that's just my opinion. Always a good one for new party pack players. 7/10Blather Round: This one might be the hardest of the new games to figure out how to play, but its a pretty good game once you get the hang of it. Only problem is if you choose even a slightly hard character/story/object then it can take a while to get it or not get at all. It's probably my least played game, but still a good one 7/10Champ/d Up: A lovely combination of TKO and Drawful, two of my favourite games. With most of these drawing games it can get pretty lengthy but the guessing element keeps the game entertaining, and the fact that you can bring back old fighters is the cherry on top of this game. 8.5/10Overall this is one of the best if not the best party pack. It doesn't have too many hard to learn games. I'm gonna play this a lot with friends and family. My favourite game has to be a tie between Talking Points and The Devils and the Details. Definitly recommend this game to anyone looking to get a Jackbox Party Pack. Remember this is all just my opinion :)Overall the pack is a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Worth it for Quiplash 3 alone, but Quiplash 3 definitely isn't perfect and the other games are still worth a look atQuiplash 3: Amazing. So many laughs, each game is the perfect length, and a fair-ish scoring system for a Jackbox game, My only complaint is that the final round always being Thriplash is SO UNBELIEVABLY BAD, especially because the final rounds of Jackbox 2 like Acrolash, Wordlash, and especially Comiclash were some of the best parts. Thriplash has soured so many games because someone will sweep the leaderboard with "♥♥♥♥ piss ♥♥♥", or will sweep because nobody voted for "♥♥♥♥ piss ♥♥♥", and if nobody put The Three Dreaded Words then everyone will say "my Thriplash sucked and I lose off of this." No one likes Thriplash, no one likes the profanity-free version, and I hate Smitty's smug voice.The Devil and the Details: Pass. No one quite knows how this plays and nobody was ever a fan. Game is a mess. Champ'd Up: Decent. Given how specific the premises are, rarely did someone's "response" drawing (where you can't see the prompt) ever beat the original drawing. People had fun drawing stupid things to dumb titles, and every once in a while you'd get a drawing that really went above and beyond, but like... not really? TKO is better in my opinion, but I like this one.Talking Points: Pass? Completely dependent on how creative your friend's group is, because nothing is lamer than someone saying someone stuttering their way through, or just staying dead quiet. Definitely a game we had to "warm up" to before playing, and after warming up we'd just play another game. Really depends on if you have friends that can do a lot with a little and can talk for minutes on end, and like... most people don't think that's very fun, and if you do then not everyone in the party does too. Also, the scoring system is completely arbitrary, each presentation taking several minutes can mean this game can drag on with a full party of 8, and the real winner is whoever gets the most laughs.Blather 'Round: Decent. Basically 20 questions, but as a group. I thought it was lame, but some of my friends legitimately enjoy it and want to play it every time we open Jackbox. Also caps out at 6 players, which is super lame given how simple the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend or not recommend this game in essence. The game to me is more of the same of the last party packs. People say this is the more definitive party pack that has come out in a long time and I would disagree. This game has games that are failures just as much as other Jackbox Party games. Peoples tastes will change and will have different things they hold dear and other things they despise. For me Devil and the Details and Talking Points was the worst of the pack.I will go through the games and tell you what I thought of each of them. Nothing much to be said with this, Its just more of Quiplash and that's essentially it. However, they tried to make the prompts more robust which I thought only made it harder to come up with funny things, I had to truly stretch my creative mind to make the game funny. And the Final round of making 3 answers to the prompt was very lackluster for a final round. At this point, they need to just make Quiplash a bigger stand a lone game and stop trying to use it to lure people in.Good game, but its a co-op experience just like Bomb Corp (Jackbox 2) but more chaotic. However, the same problem arises with both where after you play it a couple times, there is no need to ever play it again. The replay value is very low. I hear a lot of people love this one. I find this one absolutely a miss for me. This is essentially the most drunk game you'll find on a Jackbox game. I personally think that you have to have a highly dull or tame sense of humor to find this fun. It's absurd, but it's jackbox absurd so it's filled with PG to PG-13 internet meme humor which is not funny to blurt out to me. I would even say this is one of the worse jackbox games in all the packs down there with Earwax and I know I'm in the minority there. This is essentially a more robust version of TkO'd. I think its almost safe to say that this is just an objectively better game than TKO'd. One of the few jackbox games that made me want to run it back after playing it once. One of the better drawing games in all of Jackbox. This was a game that was more along the lines of a true party game. It is essentially password, taboo, monikers, timesup! etc. But instead of you describing who the Person, Item, Thing is that you chose. You have to use premade prompts to describe what or who it is. Which can result in a lot of frustration in friends or a lot of cheering in getting the guess correct. In conclusion the game is just another jackbox game. There will be games friends don't like and other games friends will love. I can tell they put more love into the artstyle and aesthetics of the whole game. But the mechanics of the games are more or less the same thing as all Jackbox games. Prompt reading, fill in the blank, and drawing with 3 rounds for each game. But because of this, I have to give a thumbs down for me personally because I already have a way to play Quiplash without this game and Blather Rounds is already a game that has 100's of different names (that everyone has access too). So owning this game and paying the $26-$30 price tag is not worth it only to essentially play Champ'd Up.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously one of the best Party Packs since the third one. All of the games on this Party Pack are extremely fun, and never get boring after one playthrough. I find myself constantly replaying and replaying all of these games with my friends, and none of them get bored of it either. A few things I do have to say though, Devils and the Details isn't for everyone, it is a very hectic game that requires you to verbally communicate, and requires two or three playthroughs to get the overall idea of what to do and how to play it. Talking Points isn't for everyone either, it does require  a few people to make good improvisational presentations, if you don't have the right kind of people, the game  be boring. Champ'd Up is great. It's basically the unofficial sequel to TKO from the third Party Pack, but with more challenges! You draw stuff, put them in a fight with another person's drawing, and win the match. I personally find this more fun than TKO, but to each their own. Quiplash 3 is just Quiplash. The artstyle in this one is really cool, I love the claymation and the overall feel of this one. The final prompt has been changed for the better, and can now be edited in making your own episodes! Very fun, highly replayable.Overall this pack is the most fun I've had in a Party Pack since the 3rd one. I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely underrated.So when my friends wanted me to play this game I thought it's just another one of those thousands survival hams. Oh boy, how wrong I was.It starts off normally making you fight small creatures and lower human enemies. You craft basic tools and cook meat. All equipment has different Tier so you go through the different stages like wood, stone, iron, steel and so on. Difference in this game is that you not only invest points into your character attributes when you level up but also into "feats". Meaning you have to learn and plan what you are going to craft and the most important point: You can't learn everything on your own. Solo play must be extremely hard. I experienced the game on my dedicated server with 2 friends and we could split the feats so everyone was specialized in one feats "tree".After you start to explore while improving gear and building your base the game suddenly takes a turn.There are rare NPC encounters with actual great voice acting that tell you about the lore. The map barrier is lore based and makes it feel more natural. The world in general is not generated but static and is extremely well designed. The soundtrack in certain areas contributes to a deep immersion.
