_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend the game but just barely.  The game is stunning, and playing a platformer as an animal is refreshing.  Unfortunately, the biggest things holding the game back I feel are mostly first time game maker mistakes and could easily see a sequel or follow up being more refined.The pros:Music and ambiance are great.  Some of the areas are very inspired and are some of the nicest looking areas in a game I've seen.  The theme is pretty good.  The game is pretty relaxing, and there is a decent amount of 'collectables' to get, although it wouldn't take you long to get them.  The ending is pretty neat and the way the story is told is unique and cool, if pretty basic.The cons:Lots of empty areas in the game.  There are also a lot of parts where you are forced to walk at a slow pace for story reasons but this is one of those things that shouldn't be forced on the player.  Two bugs that are kinda major, I've had issues with the options menu just doing whatever it wants sometimes.  The other one is trying to hold a staff while around the light bulbs (Or whatever they are called.)  It's annoying to have to drop the staff, go to the bulbs, wait for the animation, then go back over and pick the staff up again.  Some of the environments are kinda dull.  Chapters 4 and 6 were pretty boring looking and should honestly have included more interesting challenges or scenery.  Chapter 7 in particular was just confusing to get through and felt like it didn't need to be as large as it was, especially with the limited visibility.In the end, the game is not sure what it wants to be; does it want to be a walking simulator? Well, there isn't enough meaningful exploration for that.  Does it want to be a platformer?  The controls/environments aren't good enough for that.  Puzzle?  Besides a few of the puzzles, they weren't hard, and the puzzles that were 'hard' were more confusing.It took me about 8.9 hours to 100% everything in the game, and it includes playing through it twice so it is a very short game.  I don't think it would be worth it to pick up at full price, but for people who like the theme and/or are just really starved for platformers I think it's a good pick up on sale.  I also think the developers could honestly come up with a very good sequel that's more refined and sure of its identity.

_childDocuments_.review: In all, I loved my experience being a fox. A lot. Puzzle games are a favourite of mine, and I can say with honesty that I only felt the urge to look up a let's play once in the whole experience, and it was because of my own stubbornness in trying to make a jump that was not intended. Usually, there are a couple times where I look up how to finish a task that I just can't figure out. But not this game. I didn't look it up in the end. There comes a feeling of satisfaction from succeeding that this game utilises expertly.It's a little beta-y in that sometimes I jump into a wall or through a rock, or I can't make a jump unless I land in the exact place that was intended. But that really doesn't matter in the large scheme of things. It is different to my usual games, in that it has no text or dialogue, whatsoever. Sure, there are pictographs, but no words. It really, really made a difference to my gameplay style. For one, I did a LOT more exploring, taking in the scenery with some deliberate elongated pauses to enjoy the atmosphere and view (never know when you'll miss that all-important stick!). For another, I think text might actually have detracted from the atmosphere and story. Also: the music. Fits perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: I *really* wanted to like this game. It's beautiful, the story is interesting, and you get to play as an animal. It reminded me a lot of Okami in a lot of ways, which is my favourite game ever made, so great! Unfortunately, there are some *glaring* issues that I simply cannot get over, and believe me I have tried, because like I said, I really wanted to like this game.The issues in question are 1: the game is nowhere *near* clear enough where the ♥♥♥♥ you're supposed to go. The only times the Sprite actually guides you are when it's blatantly obvious where you need to be going, but in sections where it's not clear, it does nothing; not even a hint of an indication where you're supposed to go or what you're supposed to do next.And 2: This game controls like utter *garbage*, I swear QWOP controls better than this game does in spots because the fox is so *unbelievably* floaty. I lost count the amount of times I had to repeat entire sections because the fox either jumped too far, not far enough, slipped off an edge for no reason, hit an invisible wall, or turned/jumped in the complete opposite direction it was told turn/jump in.None of this is helped by the fact the game operates on an auto-save function, and the checkpoints are not exactly close together.This is *really* unfortunate, because it is a stunning and compelling game otherwise, but the focus in a game like this should be on the story and the breathtaking visuals, and I am simply unable to enjoy those things because the gameplay is so God-awful.If anyone is looking for a game that has similar vibes but actually indicates where you're supposed to go and *doesn't* control like you're trying to play using only your ass, then might I suggest Okami?

_childDocuments_.review: The PC version is not recommanable.GAMEPLAY: The controls are at best annoying - if your game contains jumping puzzles and small spaces you HAVE to have good controls. You also get stuck on invisible walls and corners where it should be smooth sailing all throughout the game (my friends played it on switch and it's not an issue there). PC port is unplayable.STORY: The idea and message are great, but I wouldn't call it a "plot" as you can sum up everything that happens (besides running, puzzles and fetchlike quests) in one sentence, so don't expect much.LENGHT: If not rushed the game takes about 2 - 3 hours.LOOKS: All the above is a shame as the game looks brilliant. Especially with the music the athmosphere could be great, if I wouldn't be frustrated with the controls every 5 minutes. I'm actually sad to write this beauty a bad review, but not fixing these issues AND charging this amount for a game of this lenght with such problems is simply impertinent. _childDocuments_.review: Got a chance to play Spirit of the North that focuses on a fox that a player controls, as well as a spirit female fox that guides the player through beautiful landscapes of a mysterious world with gorgeous graphics and vistas. The story or more rather the premise of the game reminded me a bit of the game Submerged which I played and reviewed a couple of months back. The story takes place in a mysterious world that has been ravaged by some sort of a cataclysm wiping out its population, as we travel through the world we discover more details about this world and the said cataclysm, and try to help the world heal from the aftermath of it. Almost all of the story of the game is revealed through stone murals, some of which are presented to the player as a part of the story, and some that are hidden throughout the world/chapters.The game play itself is pretty basic, you travel through the linear world (divided into different chapters), learn more about the world, and gain more powers as you progress further through the game. The game doesn't have any enemies or combat so it could be described as one of those "chill" games that focus more on story, explorations, and puzzles. The puzzles themselves aren't very challenging though, I may have had one or two instances in the game where I was stumped where to go or what to do but in general the game in terms of puzzles was pretty much a breeze.Throughout the game you control the fox and you have actions to wiggle your tail, or bark to which your spirit fox companion will bark back which was very cute. Throughout the game I found myself a little bit attached to the fox as I was following along to his story with growing interest.Performance wise, the game performs mostly OK on Steam Deck, although this is an indie game I would say that this game devours the Steam Deck battery to roughly the same extent as Doom (2016) which I found surprising. This essentially means that on full battery you'll be able to squeeze out about 1 hour to 1 hour and a half of game play before you would need to recharge. The biggest performance issue in the game happened to me when I was playing through the 2nd and 3rd chapter of the game, during those 2 chapters I already had clocked in 3 hours of game play and by that time the game/Steam Deck crashed on me about 4 times while playing through those chapters which roughly equates to 1 crash per hour.Strangely enough, once I made it past chapter 3, I haven't experienced any further crashes for any further chapters till the end of the game so if you are playing on Steam Deck or a laptop and you're experiencing crashes, try making it past chapter 3 and the issue for some reason should hopefully resolve itself. Another downside of the game is the lack of manually saving your game. Fortunately, the game does provide checkpoints throughout the chapter that auto save your game and you can pretty much pick up from that point if you quit your game however for some chapters, the distance between one checkpoint and another can be quite far and if you quit the game without reaching that checkpoint, you'll be reverted back to the previous checkpoint after starting the game again.Overall I enjoyed the Spirit of the North and will definitely give the sequel a try. The game offers a splendid and vibrant environments, and a unique (although a bit vague) storytelling. The performance of the game does suffer a bit at the start when playing the game on Steam Deck, and the game would definitely benefit from having an option to manually save your game. If you're looking for a nice relaxing game to take a break from the regular action games then you can't go wrong with this choice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way too clunky with unintuitive puzzles, terrible parkour, and random elements for me to be bothered with it more than an hour or so at a time, hence this review. I really want to like this game, the graphics are absolutely gorgeous, the fox is adorable, and I don't mind the lack of an obvious story as I feel exploring the world is the focal point, but the puzzles...I want to be clear that the core concept of the puzzles is fine. Use your powers on this or that thing to open up areas and solve puzzles to progress. Except it felt as if the creators thought up cool abilities first and puzzles second, most of them feeling thrown into the world in areas that usually don't seem that important. There are clever ones here and there, but they will mostly suck up your time because the items needed blend so well into the environment. As for the clever uses, such as , they're pretty good on the surface. Except, are never properly introduced and you'll find yourself looking for the usual pillars only to realize that yet another item has been thrown into the mix without much thought or explanation. For hours you will find yourself running in circles of mostly stone filled environments with the spirit rarely helping you and, even when it does, in ways that are so cryptic they just leave you scratching your head. I've had it lead me to areas or more of puzzles I was supposed to work up to, making me waste several minutes there only to realize the next solution was actually elsewhere. Like great, I think I could summarize the end goal was to make this glowing thing glow more, as is literally the game loop. At least start me off somewhere more relevant to beginning the process instead? The spirit is completely useless and just bogs down the gameplay in my opinion, there should have been a command to ask it for help when you were stuck, it would have made a lot of the puzzles go so much smoother and be worth giving more of a go. As is, as a character it feels nonexistent and very bland, giving us nothing of the cute, possible friendship between it and the living fox hinted at in the first chapter.I also think its worth mentioning some of these puzzles require you to jump around the environment in ways that feel unnatural and that I myself as a player would have never guessed unless I looked it up. . It doesn't help that several surfaces have an invisible wall almost that will smack you off and make it seem impossible to land on unless you do it in a specific or terribly janky way (such as jumping off of the air, and no, this is not one of your abilities). Several times I had to back up because if you're too close to a ledge the fox will freak out and end up turning you away from it (aka the invisible wall thing). So many times I was completely knocked off surfaces and had to climb up all over again because my character was behaving strangely. Chapter four really highlights all my issues with the game and, being only halfway done that just doesn't bode well enough for me to be that dedicated to finish it or continue quite frankly.The lack of story, or an obvious story at least, ends up being glaringly obvious because as one's frustration builds they realize they are doing this all for essentially..nothing. Its not like you get new story beats every time you complete an area, or learn anymore about the cute spirit fox, you just get thrown into another one with more puzzles you have to dredge through again. Can be nice to have something to do with your hands for a while and running around is a good excuse to see all the cool environments and graphics, but ultimately I think the creators needed to take a step back to imbue this project with more purpose. Not to mention much more clever introductions to the potentially good puzzle mechanics. There are so many throw away mechanics it makes it impossible to predict what it wants you to do next.Chapter four part four introduces so many things without explanation it about gave me a headache. Not only are there  These combined caused me to run around the area aimlessly until I  It took everything bad with previous sections and made it so much worse.So, while this is an extremely promising start for indie developers, and I would recommend keeping an eye on the creators for future projects, I can't recommend this game specifically. It is far too frustrating to be worth it, and there are better puzzle and exploration games out there that won't make you want to pull your hair out.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a fantastic game that I and my stream REALLY enjoyed and probably will return to.I love that it's quite open, there's no dialogue/voice acting/text/etc, the story is completely told through imagery and events. _childDocuments_.review: This is a thumbs-sideways review; I'm ultimately recommending it, but with some serious caveats.Spirit of the North is a third-person (well, third-fox) exploration/puzzle platformer game, where a fox explores a series of breath-taking northern vistas seeking to unlock the mysteries therein and defeat some sort of evil, red fungus for............reasons?!?!Positives:*Graphics*  The landscapes and ruins look bloody fantastic, just by turns lovely and awe-inspiring.*Gameplay*  New elements are added periodically which switch things up and keep the game from becoming too bland, too soon.Negatives:*Storyline*  You may have gathered from my opening statements that there isn't a lot of compelling writing going on, and that is unfortunately to the game's detriment.  You see, the entire "story" is conveyed only through visual story-telling (on screen cut-scenes, glyphs and carvings, etc.) which leaves  much unsaid and unexplained.  You never really know what is going on, e.g. what is that red fungus, why is it taking over, what the heck is actually going on?!?!?  Yes there's sort of a story-line, but it is so thin and ill-explained so as to be positively diaphanous in thickness.  And that hurts the game a lot, turning it into a series of pretty ruins and landscapes that you explore for no real good reason (defeat the evil influence of a corrupting force of........what, mycology, pure evil, WHAT?!?! ).  The glyphs and carvings don't do nearly as good a job of explaining the mythos of the game as the designers might have thought, resulting in a pretty game, all but devoid of narrative heft.So...........the game looks great and plays well, but you find yourself not truly knowing why you're doing what you're doing, except in such a vague, gossamer thin fashion as to render the story bereft of dramatic meaning and gravitas.I'm still going to recommend it, but I did find the game more than a bit dissatisfying, despite the eye-candy.YMMV.....heck, I'm sure someone out there has written a novel based on the compelling naratives they discovered within the game....
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I love the lack of dialogue and/or text so that the story is entirely visual and leaves a lot to the imagination. The landscape and setting is breathtaking yet detailed.I really enjoyed the gameplay, though I wish it was a little longer, especially after unlocking every ability. I feel there's a lot of potential for more puzzles and think it'd be interesting to have a level editor.The soundtrack is good, but it's not specific to any areas or parts of the story. I'd say this is probably the weakest part of the game despite the music itself being very good. I never got tired of it, but it would have been nice if the soundtrack went along with the other parts of the game.Overall, I really enjoyed this game and would recommend it to anyone who likes pretty games that tell a short but beautiful story.8.7/10Edit: The latest patch has fixed all the issues I had with the soundtrack (amongst other quality of life features). My only wish is to be able to buy the OST at some point.New grade: 9.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute game but it has a lot of flaws as well.I feel like a lot of people, me included, are starved for animal related games, so we tend to look past a lot of issues. This game is one of them. It's a neat game for sure, the animations are nice, the world looks beautiful and you follow a sort of wholesome story throughout the game while solving puzzles and collecting spirits. But the game also feels very lifeless a lot of the time, with a huge map that may look beautiful but is vastly empty. Parts of the game often suffer from confusing design making it hard to tell where you have to go next, I often got stuck thinking I broke the game or missed something, just to look up on youtube where to go and learned that the way forward was just hidden behind some badly lit path that was hard to see. The game is sadly also very clunky with the fox controlling a bit awkward, especially when running/jumping around platforms. For the price the game is asking, it honestly just lacks too much content. 90% of the time is spent walking around a massive empty map, solving a few puzzles here and there. Often you're even slowed down by the game itself, forcing you to slow walk. You can beat the game in 2-4 hours and in the end you didn't really do all that much. If you can see past that, it's still a beautiful game with a cute story. I enjoyed it, but it really only is something for animal fans and you also should get this on sale probably.

_childDocuments_.review: There's just something about this game...The premise is relatively simple, starting you off with little knowledge but giving you gentle nudges along the path. As you play and explore, you pick up more and more of the story. The game play becomes more complex as the story progresses, adding new moves that you will need to learn and master to gain the full experience. That's what this really is; It's less of a game and more of an experience with a few puzzles thrown in that will leave you learning more as you figure them out. If you like games that are more exploration and something to experience, then this might fit the bill. In that, it's similar to the way that Journey or RiME play out. The soundtrack adds well to the experience, evoking moods that easily match what you see playing out on screen.It's not perfect, however. There are spots where the game could use some refinement. Some of the puzzles offer few to no hints on how or what to do to progress, and these spots can be infuriating at times. It'll take patience and exploring to find what you've missed, or where you can climb even though it doesn't look like you can. That's another point of issue: Movement. The environment is somewhat inconsistent on what you can and cannot do, and the hit boxes and usable surfaces are a little haphazard. One moment you can be standing on air and the next, you can't climb up an incline much like those you have before. Other times, you MUST climb an incline that looks like you shouldn't be able to climb it based on previous experience. In that, you'll need to take your time to explore and find out what is and isn't permissible. Overall, I'd say it's well worth playing. At the time of writing this review, I've played 10 hours here on Steam and at least the same on PS4, all for the purpose of enjoying and exploring the environment. After all, there's something about this game that keeps drawing me back to the experience again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: When I asked for a game to help me during a time of mental volatility, Spirit of the North was one of the games recommended and the one that caught my attention the most. It was also the first game I decided to check out, and my gosh I'm glad I did. The graphics are beautiful (and I didn't even notice any lag), and the story (while one of the more silent & environmental ones I've seen) was gorgeous. The soundtrack complements the game, though there was one point I can recall that the music just abruptly cuts to a new track. The biggest issue I can think of is that the physics is a bit wonky to get used to, but once I did there weren't very many troubles to be had (outside of like one or two pesky jumps); that said, I had less annoyance with it than I did playing MGR's Bladewolf DLC, in terms of platforming anyways.I'd give this game a solid 8/10, it's not perfect but its highs are, indeed, pretty dang high. _childDocuments_.review: You're a fox traveling around Iceland-like terrain helping ancient shamans find peace. The story is unique and the puzzles are challenging, but not too much so. It's almost impossible to navigate where you're supposed to go in some chapters without a tutorial, but that really only happens in some areas. There are chapter-specific YouTube tutorials to get around that if you are frustratingly stuck. I am satisfied with photo mode and could save some really great screen captures. The graphics are a little blockish and the jumping mechanics could be wonky sometimes, however that shouldn't deter you from not playing. The story is worth it, and I will take a small indie game with a few minor frustrations over a conglomerate with micro-transactions any day. I know the developers can fix all of those little mishaps in Spirit of the North 2, which is set to release in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and went straight up near the top of my favorites list. But it's not for everyone.This game is a puzzle game, with extremely beautiful landscapes, and you play as a fox. Finding the "collectibles" (it's not really collecting, but it functions the same) rewards you with different coat colors, and at higher levels, they come with new light patterns and more. (Which means getting the achievements is actually worth more than just completion.)The beginning of the game is more walking simulator than puzzle. If you are too tense, this game will either relax or frustrate you horribly. Patience is key. But the landscapes are beautiful. And the places in which the game forces you to a crawl (you are injured/sick), it's a way to force you to think on the story elements.The game encourages you to explore and really look around at your environment, rewarding you with collectibles (and nice views).But the game has no dialogue, and aside from your companion spirit sometimes pointing in the general direction of your next task, you don't get any direction at all. There is no dialogue, and no text. Some people, like me, will love this lack of direction. Some will hate that, and get frustrated.Most of the time, when you get a new spirit ability, the game will introduce you slowly to more complicated ways to use it. Though there is one spot in particular where it almost immediately requires you to creatively combine powers with little to no indication that things work that way. (This only happened once for me.)While others have described the controls as "clunky", I don't think they are. The fox you play as feels very realistic, and while he? does not have the instant response that most action games favor, I never had trouble controlling him. Only in fringe cases did I have any difficulty - when I was far from the normal area intended to be used, and I managed to fall in a bit of terrain that was both slippery (because I wasn't supposed to be there) and also blocked off by geometry. Or I got on top of an object with weird geometry and the hitbox wasn't sure which angle to use. (Still way, way less buggy than Skyrim. I'm surprised how few I've come across seeing as this was developed by three people.)Replayability, once you get all the "collectibles", is unfortunately low. It is still a wonderful walking simulator, and the fox's idle animations are absolutely adorable. But that is the case with all puzzle games like this - once you know how to solve the puzzles, they don't challenge you anymore.If I were to give a suggestion to the devs, I'd say let the player with a completed save file go through all the chapters again with all the powers they get at the end. Let them change between spirit fox and normal fox, and let them loose on the beautiful landscapes as a reward for completing the game.As a whole, I'd give this game a 9.5/10 - almost perfect, and a great way to relax when everything else seems hectic.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very beautiful game and I can recommend it to anyone who likes foxes, iceland, glowy stuff, or all of those. Gameplay is fairly easy, I'm not really good at jumping puzzles but finished story + all shamans in around 8h. (That being said, its sadly quite short.)I was stuck for a bit 2 or 3 times and needed help from a guide once, which was due to bad/no explanations of certain mechanics (or me being stupid idk).There arent many abilities one has to keep track of, but controls feel quite clunky at times. The most annoying part about them is that as soon as your paws touch even the slightest bit of water, you can't jump or sprint anymore.The most fun part about the gameplay imo are the geysers and jump portals :D It just looks so funny to see the fox flying.Hints seem pretty random, the Wisp often vividly draws your attention to a huge, glowing thing literally right in front of your nose but nearly never shows you anything when you actually need a bit of help. Like when you unlock the burst to destroy spores, the game tells you to use the left mouse button to use it but it took me quite a while to figure out you have to   it for a few seconds to activate. Or that part where I was really stuck where you need to run up a river in spirit form (you cant in physical form) and the game doesn't tell you that spirit form for whatever reason is able to do that. You also only need this at this one point in the entire game, yet no hint at spirit form at all there while the game even tells you how often you have to rotate the rotating stones ^^'Graphics aren't stunning compared to other current games but still very pretty. I also love that you unlock nice skins for your fox when you awaken all shamans of a chapter :DThe story is... well, not narrated, but you also don't get the feeling that it should. Pictures tell you what is going on and its quite sad, especially in chapter 4. I usually only play games with more content (story depth, quest lenght and/or tasks that keep you occupied) but I still liked playing through this :)

_childDocuments_.review: I am currently on my third play through of this beautiful game. The soundtrack, setting and visuals are brilliant. _childDocuments_.review: is quite a mysterious and exciting 3D puzzle/platform adventure filled with wonderful sights and awesome sounds. Take on the role of the protagonist red fox as it disturbs the slumbering spirit of the Northern Lights and forever changes its destiny. It's an experience as a full package that you cannot fully appreciate until you have tried it yourself. The store page describes a game that's inspired by the Icelandic landscape. I fully believe it. The game is split into 8 different chapters, with Chapters 1 and 8 acting as bookends offering a nice introduction and a satisfying conclusion. Chapters 2 is fairly linear and straight forward. After that, the chapters are rather lengthy, each with multiple check-pointed sections with the game automatically saving as you reach these checkpoints. New platforming mechanics and puzzles are introduced throughout the game, and while it is rather casual in the beginning, there are some timed platforming gates that you will encounter about halfway through.Overall the game took me about 10 hours to complete, because I was enjoying my experience wandering the landscape and listening to the absolutely fantastic soundtrack, while searching every nook and cranny for the optional collectibles. I really did try and I thought I did a very thorough job, but much of the secrets still eluded me. One of the optional side-quests is to find shaman staves scattered around to bring to the fallen shaman remains, presumably to allow their spirits to rest in peace. A few of these are required for progression, but most of them are completely optional. I only pieced together about 20 out of 28 of these. Some of them are really hidden very well. There are other optional objectives as well, I will let you discover those on your own.So that speaks to the open expanse of the game. Every chapter is essentially a contained world, often you can reaccess previous sections after going through the checkpoints, but occasionally those sections are completely closed off. You will have to use the chapter selection option from the main menu if you want to reaccess at this point. A couple of the areas starting in Chapter 3 hint at the open-exploration optional aspect of the game instead of following the prescribed paths, but the smaller puzzles in that chapter make it so that it's not so obvious. Chapters 4-7 are where the majority of the game are located.A few of the puzzles stumped me a while, but nothing too complex looking at them in retrospect. The times I got stuck were mainly because of a lack of consideration of whatever new mechanic was just introduced. I am completely fine with environmental puzzles that are not too difficult, because, I have been stuck on similar games before and ultimately had to go looking at a guide because I simply could not progress. This game, I made it on my own.Caveat to people looking to have a completely casual and exploration experience just to take in the sights and sounds, you can do that only for a short while. If you want nothing to do with solving environment puzzles, you will not be able to progress beyond Chapter 3. If you are completely unable to do some platforming, you will also be stuck at this point. The platforming is fairly straight forward until Chapters 5-6 I would say, when you will be faced with some additional timed gates. These are not many, and they not too difficult, but they are definitely there, and you need to be aware of them.Overall, the experience was phenomenal. The controls felt kind of funny in a few small situations, but overall the response is fine and does not detract from the experience. The music will seem a bit overplayed if you stay in an area too long. But every section of every chapter will trigger a new musical loop, so I thoroughly enjoyed listening to the soundtrack perhaps a dozen times as I played through the game. The open-expanse and exploration is mostly optional, so you have the ability to narrow your focus on just completing the story should that be your wish.The game plays as a 3rd person 3D adventure platformer with some fairly simple environment puzzles that features a wide-expanse to explore at many junctures.The controller worked fine for the whole game. I had a couple of times when I paused the game to go do something else and when I came back the controller lost its response and I had to reset the game. Sometimes I could just move the mouse and I would see the options on-screen change, and that would revert to normal, but sometimes I couldn't do that either.Beautifully made landscapes and ruins, the artwork is quite good. There are very few animations as the environment is mostly static, but the interactions between the protagnist fox and the environment are definitely visible. Sometimes they seem silly, such as the fox making huge indentations in the snow just by stepping on it. Overall the environment in this game is quite a spectacle to behold.Despite the graphics looking beautiful, I had almost quit in Chapter 4 because of an overwhelming red glaze over the whole screen/environment for a large chunk of the game. I wish the red haze/fog would be lifted from the game. It's fine having a red sky and red rain, but that haze almost made me lose it. That section made my eyes bleed.I was mesmerized by the music for pretty much the entire game, it really made the experience full in my opinion. Is it the best music? No. There's been a lot of games with excellent soundtracks, and I would say this is well above average.I put in my warnings above, the game is not just a simple casual walking adventure in 3D in third person. The environmental puzzles are fairly straight forward. The platforming + timed gates are probably where some people will get stuck.The game is priced at £15.49/ €16.79/ $19.99 with a 15% discount at launch. I think this is totally fair.I recorded the first few minutes of myself playing without any commentary, you can see it first-hand here. The developers also have streamed it a bit and probably will be doing more as well. My video is here: is an experience worth having. I had fun enjoying the sights and sounds, and the overall experience was very enjoyable. The end screen gives you an option to quit or to stay there after the credits rolled. I stayed a couple of extra minutes enjoying myself and relishing in finishing the game. I will let you experience it for yourself without saying more about it. The game length is just about right for what I would want.I enjoyed solving the puzzles, even though a few of them stumped me a bit at first. The puzzles do encourage you to think outside the box at times. Despite their simple nature, I enjoyed the mechanics that went into these puzzles. The controls are just a little funky in a few situations, but nothing to make a serious complaint about. My biggest complaint is about the red haze in a particular section of the game that I could have done without.I will probably wait for a guide and go look to find all of the missing collectibles that I missed. I tried really hard to explore but still missed a bunch. I do like that these motivated me to traverse all the of terrain as much as possible and to look at the various environmental designs from all angles.What an experience indeed. Another indie gem. Definitely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: What will the world look like when human rule ends? Will the whole planet be relieved, will the deforested areas be reforested, will the greenery eat the concrete, will wild animals populate the streets? We don't know the answers to these questions, but thanks to games like Spirit of the North, we can soak up the beautifully peaceful atmosphere of the future Earth.Spirit of the North won't tell you what happened on Earth. You are a completely ordinary fox wandering around an Iceland-inspired landscape, and you are accompanied by another fox, this time an astral one. There is no story, no narrative, just your perceptions.You ride through the snow-covered landscape, drive in streams, crawl through caves and climb rocks. The point is to absorb the atmosphere and come up with your own theories about the world that surrounds you. Those who expect more than a felt experience, some platforming and puzzles, probably won't get it.As a result, Spirit of the North has flat game mechanics and sometimes too irritating controls... it drags the game down, and not even pleasant music, nice visuals and an emotional story can pull it out. However, if you have a weakness for foxes and are looking for this type of game, I can recommend the game despite its shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings with SoT. This is a game similar to Journey, Flowers, Abzu or Gris, but featuring a fox in the mountains.  I can see pros and consPROS:- The game is really beautiful and the soundtrack is amazing. - Length-wise it is ok, around 5-8 h depending on your exploration. There are 8 chapters, and some collectibles that acounts for some replays after you complete the game. - the fox learns some abilities that unlocks new mechanics and puzzles, making it fresh and interesting to play. - A few fox skins can be unlocked if you discover enough secrets, a good touchCONS - the pace is too slow at times, the areas are so vast and open, with empty fields and no too much to see or interact with on the background that it takes you forever to reach the next area. - Although each chapter is different from the previous ones, the areas within each chapter, and tasks/puzzles to move forward, are quite repetitive, ultimately making it boring. - There's no story to follow or characters to interact with. - Although the OST is good, after a while you realize it is just only a few short tracks playing all the time over and over, making it repetitive if you play for some hours because it does not change between chapters or areas, from the very beginning until the end.- The most irritating part was the controls, especially in areas requiring jumping or platforming. It is bad implemented, with invisible walls, bad movements, weird turns... you will have to repeat many sections just because the controls are horrendous. - Finally, not sure this is a problem only faced by me, but it had some performance issues, with staggering, frame rate drops and tearing. Overall, it is not a bad game, and if you like similar titles with beautiful aesthetics, OST, slow pace and just relaxing gameplay you will enjoy it. However, if you expect some interesting challenges or puzzles, a faster pace, or do not like platforming, this is not for you, especially considering the bad controls. I personally prefer other similar games like Gris.

_childDocuments_.review: It has it's charm, certainly a beautiful world visually. But it's not polished.You're constantly fighting the terrain (felt like I was playing Death Stranding at times) which sometimes could work in your favor as I found you could sometimes scale some walls and get to the next area without going the intended way. I did also manage to get to one area (the intended way) where I had no way to recharge the spirit, so had to reload to my last save.Probably the thing that made it less enjoyable for me was how it didn't seem to respect your time. The biggest offender is recharging the spirit (which is a thing you're constantly doing). You can't just activate a flower and continue, you had to activate it then stand there while it opened and have the spirit recharge you. Key sections where the fox would become sick or hurt would slow the fox right down to a crawl while still making you walk massive distances like that. Falling into the water meant slowly dog paddling your way out and then watching the animation of the fox shaking before you could continue. Key scenic sections where you're just running forward, I get that I'm meant to be taking in the music and the visuals in those parts but I'm just holding forward in those parts and they just go on for a bit too long imo.Last criticism would be that I found it a bit too directionless in parts.Having said that, there were many moments and aspects that I also enjoyed. For a short game it was an ok experience and I got it on sale for cheap so meh.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: At its current state I'm sorry to say that I cannot recommend it.It feels like a 0.8v game, where a lot of things are decent but a lot of others need some more attention. The lack of different musics, specially more adventure-like ones in more agitated parts. The lack of particles, shaders or post processing effects; And overall cutscene quality. The horrible obstacles hitbox and the weird jumping where you jump sideways if you have wall in front of you. And ANNOYING invisible walls really close to the player at some points. The game's mechanic is pretty repetitive having to do the same thing over and over again in different scenarios, and exploration is not reeeeeally rewarding, as there are only a few interesting things beside the skull guys.I can feel the game has potential, it was just not used to its best YET, and feels like an early access game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this because the concept is charming, but the graphics and controls are not what I am used to from a (relatively) modern game. It feels and looks 20 years older than it is. I do not abandon games lightly, but the more I played Spirit of the North, the less I enjoyed it. Ultimately there was not enough story to keep me motivated through the clumsy controls, disappointing graphics, and boring gameplay. Maybe I will return to this title someday and finish it. But I doubt it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty neat little game you can play in a couple sessions. I found this game while searching for something to fill the void after I played Stray and while this doesn't quite live up to that (but that's a high bar to match) it did scratch the itch at least a bit. While the graphics are nothing crazy they do a great job at making the environments look stunning. The atmosphere was definitely great.I'd give it an ehhh, on replay value, I might go back and try to find some of the things I missed, you unlock skins for finding staffs and bringing them to their 'shamans' which is nice but I don't see myself doing a full game replay so that reward isn't really that much more enticing than just finding them for the sake of it. If you can grab it on sale it's definitely worth it for fans of this type of formula and a fun way to kill an afternoon or 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: "Spirit of the North" beautiful journey from beginning to end, filled with vibrant and diverse landscapes, cunning puzzles, and a great soundtrack. Despite a few clunky moments in some areas, it is very easy to immerse yourself as a lone fox, wondering the land filled with mysteries. This is a game I would highly recommend everyone to try out. You won't regret it
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Journey and want similar game - this is it. But i would rate Journey noticeably higher overhaul even without considering nice co-op feature.Spirit of the North looks great, especially in a greener part - views in chapter 5 are very pleasing! But chapter 6 feels a tiny bit too dark sometimes, otherwise - great in both design and tech. Water is beautiful, grass is juicy and fluffy, terrain is detailed, nice lighting... Performance is good too, but 60 fps lock was a bit disappointing, plus fur is... Strange sometimes, but considering small team and budget - really great work! Sound is pretty mid, i would say a bit lower then mid considering release year - music feels a bit repeatable during the game, also sound of the game is ABSOLUTELY flat. Only some effects have their place in game's sound stage, but still strictly right or left. You don't feel like you are in the world of the game. It is fun, considering how much effort was spend to make visual, and how lazy and flat sound is. Music itself is fine, it works, but still mix is claustrophobic, not spacious at all, I had dissonance on open 5th chapter landscape with such spaciously tight sound design and music.Gameplay is similar to the Journey - simple, not annoying, without any depth whatsoever. It's just here for you to experience the atmosphere, but I must point out that in the Spirit of the North gameplay itself does not tell the story as good as in Journey. I played Journey first and expected to see more sense in gameplay there, than there was. I played on Xbox controller - controls are good, I haven't had any frustration because of it.As for the story and narrative... Well, it's there) Honestly I expected more from the narrative design, you want some interesting ways to tell the story from games like this, but it seems devs prioritized visuals and overhaul atmosphere above all.In the end this game IS as simple as it looks, but is it bad? Not at all, cute fluffy fox, nice decorations, atmosphere, nothing really bothers you during the game (except Kindred Spirits achievement). It is not a masterpiece of game narrative, it is not a deep  and diverse platformer, it is just a foxy with glowy patterns doing things in a beautiful world for around 6-8 hours (for 100% achievements).Solid 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I usually play pretty violent games and also like to play games with "adult content". However, I really like foxes... and I had tears in my eyes with chapter 7 because I thought that was the ending sequence. The game really caught me off guard- probably because I like animals more than people and end of chapter 6...
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North's description reminded me of Lost Embers which I enjoyed thoroughly. I was excited to play it and experience the game play and story. However, the controls are very ridged and clunky, not fluid at all. Spirit of the North tries to have light platforming, but because of the lacking controls any slight mistake and you fall off and have to try again. You cannot turn mid jump, so if you miscalculate there is no rectifying your mistake, you just have to try again which is a slow process to get back to where you were. There is a good amount of water in the beginning you have to swim through and each time you get out of the water onto land the fox stops to shake the water off. EVERY. TIME. You cannot skip this. You can jump to cancel, but that takes about the same amount of time and you still can't move until either animation is finished. Also there is only one swimming speed: slow. So when you eventually miss that jump and fall into the water it's a slow paddle back to where you were to try again.Plus finding a staff to give to a corpse to set it's soul free/give it peace is tied into being important to the story (as seen in the trailer and game images). The game gives you an image count of how many corpses you've encountered and how many you've missed. As someone who loves to collect things in games, this really tripped me up. They hide them, which can be fun, of course! But it being an important task to the story is very frustrating when after you finish an area, go to the next, and the game tells you you've missed someone in the previous area with no way of going back... that sucks. Yes, there are collectibles that can be added to the game for extra fun and you don't have to find ALL of them to find enjoyment in the game, but this is advertised as important AND there is so little to do (at least in the beginning) that bringing the staff to the corpse is a big deal. It just hurt when I would be carrying a staff for so long, not find a corpse for it to be set free, and I find another staff. It feels like I failed that corpse's soul and failed the chance to complete the game properly because there are a lot of areas where there is no back tracking to find the corpses you've missed. How can Spirit of the North advertise this as a core game play aspect, yet hide them like they are simply just easter eggs?Over the course of the 1 hour I ended up playing this game I only grew more and more frustrated with the clunky controls, slow movement in the game despite the Sprint feature, and the lack of back tracking to find the corpses I missed. I paid $6.52 for this game during the Summer Sale and I still don't think that's worth it for a game this frustrating and unpolished, let alone $20. It really bums me out because I read many reviews on how great this game's story is. Even the beginning gives you amazing story set up without any dialog, but sadly I cannot recommend this game at any price.TLDR: Spirit of the North's game play is so clunky, unpolished, and frustrating that it's not worth $6.52, let alone $20, despite how good other people say the story is.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I was enthralled with the absolutely breathtaking visuals in this game. Running around as a fox exploring and solving puzzles. Achievement hunting was a bit challenging, but not terrible. Without spoiling anything, I love all the interactions with the spirit fox, and how you really can look through the eyes of a fox in terms of how you play. I was always looking for vantage points, and climbing anything I could. The excited fox yips and running around with what's essentially a giant stick in your mouth is comical. The lore was interesting, and very close to nature. I did almost as much hopping in this game as running. Cannot wait for the second game to come out, really looking forward to a closer look at the lore and the universe that you're presented with in the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game was not only beautiful but, it also has a interesting story you have to put together yourself.I enjoyed every moment of this game and actually played through it all in one sitting only taking a break to finish a few achievements.I'd suggest this to anyone who likes good graphics and simple game-play.Lovely game! Would def. recommend this to my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I would not recommend this game. Gameplay is very straightforward - you pick up power from blue flowers that are scattered around and put the power into something, which allows you to progress a little further. My biggest gripe with the gameplay is simply that the game is constantly stopping the action for brief moments. Every time you interact with the flowers, you've got to wait a couple seconds. When you deposit the power into an object, the game takes control away and shows you what was affected. I found it to be maddening because this is essentially the only gameplay mechanic in the game.In terms of story, this game seems to have taken the "show, don't tell" idea. However, the actual storytelling feels half baked. In the beginning of the game, the fox goes from fine to on death's door in like two seconds flat and you're left to figure out that there's an aura of some kind that is dangerous. The rest of the story is similar, where I end up saying "well I guess I kinda understand what's going on" but I would have liked this part of the game to be more fleshed out.Technically and visually, the game is mediocre. It's a fairly generic UE4 game and I'm sure that a number of the game's assets are taken from the asset store. This isn't a problem in and of itself, but it means that there's not really a coherent art style going on. The game seems to max out at 60 FPS - will not go higher. The menus are some of the worst I've seen - in order to select a 4k resolution in the settings menu it made me go through all of the lower resolutions and it changed to that resolution each time. So I ended up swapping through like 30 resolutions to get to the one I wanted.If you can get this for a deep, deep discount or in a bundle it's not the worst way to spend a few hours. But I wouldn't recommend it for anywhere close to full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Well I poked my nose into invisible walls that wouldn't even let me fall off the edge nor get close enough to it to look at the landscapes. Then I got to hold forward while character was limping very slowly while lore tablets were lighting up. Then I got to fall through the water, and since there is *no water under the water*, the poor fox got to be stuck there forever, since I quit.Walking simulators are just not my thing. I played barely an hour, sure. But that was more than enough time to get the impression of controls and how much freedom I'd have in the levels.-The music is pretty.-The fox is pretty, and the fur looks nice on it. The animations (except the bark, which looks weird) are neat, but not quite fluid. Sometimes turning is just a sudden snap to a new direction.BUT ALSO-The jumping is clunky and you won't enjoy your time with it, that much is evident from the first half hour. It doesn't feel wrong, but jumps are very obviously only meant for certain spots, and you don't have much any freedom with it. There is a path you have to jump up right after you leave the cave in chapter 2. Fail the first jump and attempt to jump up to where you fell from. You won't be able to, since you'll slide right off even if it looks jumpable.-You'll be immediately faced with an invisible wall if you decide to walk back in the very beginning. No dead end or a slide to prevent you from going too far back, just an invisible wall. Same with trying to approach any ledges in my experience, you're just stopped preemptively and it leaves a sour taste in your mouth.-If you want to follow the path in chapter 1 along with your ghost friend like I did - think again. It moves very slowly, and there's not much reason for it. There are no sights to admire for more than a couple seconds, no nooks nor crannies to explore. The locations in that chapter are empty and anything that looks like a fork forms back into a single main path maybe 10 meters ahead. After you inevitably outrun the ghost it'll appear later in the level though. I wish the whimsical reviews about "playing with the guardian spirit" were true, but as it is the beginning of the game is just you following a very slow NPC with no sense of excitement nor challenge through a corridor set up with pretty lights. Perhaps that could be considered "playing" in a retirement home, but a video game with the looks and music such as this one could've made it much better.I was expecting Ori, but what I got out of this was disappointment, to be honest. There is never a reason to skimp out on gameplay. Yeah-yeah, start of the game and all that, but it was such a poor first impression that any excitement I had about playing it was murdered in chapter 2. I was hoping first levels would pull me in and make me want to play the game more so I can explore and enjoy its movement systems, but instead I got thrown into a slow-walk segment within the first half an hour.Also the loading screens are abrupt. No fade out or anything, just a sudden jump to logo.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. The music is amazing, and I absolutely adored the scenic views at all times. Iceland is a beautiful place!I could go on for hours about the things I loved, so I'll just cut this short by listing the two things I feel like could be better;- The music, while incredible and very moving, was rather intense sometimes. I don't mean this as in it was too loud, but rather, sometimes I felt as though a boss fight was just around the corner even though it's a very calm and peaceful game.- I felt that the finding of the shaman bodies was very difficult sometimes - this might just be personal opinion and could've been much easier for others, but oftentimes I gave a staff to a body and was genuinely surprised to see the little pop-up show me that I had missed a body somewhere. In particular in chapter 3 there was an area where you had to jump down a hole carefully to reach a body in a crevice, I didn't realize that and just jumped down to go to the next chapter, and then I couldn't go back up to get it. But this is something easily solved with another playthrough, I suppose.Other than those two, I loved this game! Every bit of it! The story was incredible and was fed to the player in bits and pieces, and I loved every new piece of information I got. Running around, swishing my tail, and barking with reckless abandon was also a lot of fun - even if it accomplished nothing story-wise lol. Thank you for the fun, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very fun, very pretty game. I don't have many problems with it, and it runs great. My only complaint, however, is the ending felt a little dull and wasn't exciting. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game was truly an experience like no other. I was not prepared for how immersive the environment was, when that opening scene played, it was truly breathtaking. This game easily became my new comfort game when I felt down, to the point of where I took screenshots to set on my profile and as my background. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It is beautiful, peaceful and a tiny bit of a mind-teaser, but nothing too stressful. A great game to relax and enjoy the scenery. At each level when you freed the spirits, you are unlocking skins and can't enjoy new fur colors. Also while playing a fox(which is absolutely adorable), you don't have to deal with dialogues. A real breather compared to other games.100% enjoying it so far. (reached chapter 4)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good, simple game to sit back to, relax and enjoy- Beautiful, large environments that gives you space and freedom to run around- Great relaxing soundtrack that fits well with the theme. As a piano music listener I enjoyed it very much! The occasional eerie music in darker environments is a nice change too- The puzzles are basic, easy but still enjoyable- The fox model is so cute, and I appreciate the options of using different skins- I enjoyed the lights and glows, it gives the game a nice little touchCons:-  The story is told through drawings on walls, which appears probably around a total of 15 times. Some of the drawings repeat themselves, and most of the time are not very clear. So if you are in for the lore, don't expect much. You get the basic idea of it, but you won't get much more detail than that. SPOILER: You don't really get an explanation as to why there is corruption, just that it appeared, killed people, and you have to get rid of it. - Very clunky, buggy and primitive jump mechanic, it seems like that part of the game was the least worked on by the developers- Although the environments are beautiful and large, most of it is just empty - This is not a game that focuses heavily on game play and puzzles, so if you are looking for that you will be disappointed. It is mostly a walking and jumping simulator, but it can be enjoyed by people who just want to relax- This game could benefit from better sound FX. More sounds could be added to certain actions you do (like picking up the staff, dropping the staff, etc), more variety of sounds depending on what kind of ground you're walking on, etc. Details like that could help give the game a more polished feel.- There are two parts of the game where you are forced to walk slowly which is a drag but not too badAlthough this game still needs some work, I definitely recommend it if you are looking to sit back, decompress and enjoy the environment, without too many expectations from it. If you love the environment, you will appreciate the beautiful, ethereal forest at the end!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Breathtaking. Be ready for an emotional rollercoaster. Have tissues ready. You will really feel for the fox. But it's such a good game and story.Spirit of the North plays a bit like the game Journey, but without the online random companions. You're a little fox, in the arctic tundra of Iceland. You travel across the landscape and ruins with a little spirit fox buddy at your side. You'll experience the story and mythology not through words or narration, but by visual clues and amazing music.Playable in one sitting. You'll probably get through in about 6 hours, give or take.  I spent just barely 7 hours to complete, since I was slowly taking my time and found most of hidden stuff in my first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful game with a fantastic soundtrack and breathtaking scenery. It took me roughly 6hrs to complete the game and that was going around checking out everything and looking for Shamans. Even though its not as long as I'd hope, I thoroughly enjoyed it and would play again gladly. I recommend the game while its on sale !
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I can see what spirit of the north is aiming for and to me it fails in more ways than it succeeds. It's main shortcoming is the controls. I haven't played something this clunky in a LONG time and it ultimately kept me from completing the game. The story and gameplay just can't outshine the areas where Spirit of the North becomes tedious and frustrating. Felt like a complete slog by chapter 5 and wasn't worth continuing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: IMO, 4/5.TL;DR:Graphics, 4/5 Good; could be better.Gameplay/Story: 3.5/5. A few times I found myself wondering where to go or what to do and you will find yourself relying on your eyes and retracing your steps a lot. At least, I did. The story itself is slow to unfold but the game overall is pretty relaxing.Controls: Easy but sometimes laggy, Jumping is picky in tight spots.In Depth:Graphic are good but could be better. Seams are obvious in many places and some textures are low quality for the meshes they're stretching over. Overall good though. Controls are straightforward but there's some lag in the response for the controls (On my machine, using controller could be the issue. Controller is easier on my wrists.). The jumping can be... finicky in tight places. The story is mostly told by sheer observation, no subtitles, no narration. Most of your conclusions about the storyline are drawn from murals in game. A few times I found myself wandering around and wondering what I was supposed to do especially when I got to chapter 7 as there's an achievement you can obtain but finding all 28 required spirits is darn near impossible with no way to track them unless you just explore every nook and cranny. (Yeah, it's only for an achievment though.) I found myself backtracking a lot but the game is overall very pretty and the music is relaxing, if a bit repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Some inklings of a good game here and there, but the execution falls a bit flat.All puzzles involve barking at a flower to charge yourself with spirit energy - but if you move after barking it doesn't work and then you have to move away and come back to try again. Then you find the thing you need to use the spirit energy on. Repeat until the doorway to the next area opens. In between these puzzles there are a lot of overly long stretches of... nothing. Just holding forward as mostly unremarkable scenery passes by.The controls and camera are also especially wonky, which makes platforming more annoying than challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just gonna say - this game punches well above its weight in terms of visual/presentation. Everything fits together well, and is used to convey a very compelling non-verbal story.The puzzle elements are relatively light - with some platforming sprinkled throughout to give it some flavor. There are moments where it does feel a *bit* like a walking-simulator; but it by no means had me bored. The tonal shifts between chapters creates enough of an emotional journey that the somewhat mediocre 'game-y' elements are more than excused for.There were some minor glitches I encountered (some collectable staves got duplicated, and some decorative chimes got borked by the physics engine), but nothing too bad - I've seen much worse in AAA games.The only glitch that actually bothered me was still quite minor [though *super* minor spoiler warning]: In a later-game scene, the protagonist walks super slowly (as was the clear intent); but the footstep sound-effect was playing at normal speed - giving 2 'steps' for every step the character actually took. It was pretty distracting in a rather emotionally significant scene.In summery, I think this game is fantastic - but I acknowledge it's not a perfect game (none such games even exist). I'd love to see more from Infused Studio (ie. Tayler & Jacob). It's truly impressive what they have been able to put together here.Overall: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful story and impressive world! Very cute and touching. I love the small fox, it's looking and behaving very beautiful.I love it. that in the end you get all chapters listed and how many shamans you collected where, so you get the chance to fulfil everything 100%! That's perfect!!A game to escape the real world and relax a bit.This game has only a very small number of elements/missions, but it's all placed so well, that you really get time to enjoy the world and its challenges and it never gets boring! Spirit of the North really shows, how a game can work without overloading it with quests etc.Also, all achievements are realistic and reachable. I like that. In my opinion, this is rare these days.I love the soundtrack very much, it too is very touching.THANK YOU for such a good game!Definitely recommend it 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Lovely music. The controls can be a little wonky at times, but overall a decent game. Chapter 7 is a mind numbing, patience crushing spirit hunt that would have been much easier if the game had a simple counter to let you know how many spirits you had or had left. In spite of that, I enjoyed the game and would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I got this and Bramble in a bundle. Bramble was excellent. This was boring and the platforming was not fun. I ended up following a walkthrough so I could find all the shamans as I thought that was the best part of the game. In fact, that should have been the purpose of the game instead of just mainly walking a fox around a level. The problem is that the shamans can be easily overlooked. Luckily enough you can go back to certain parts of the chapters and find the shamans you missed. The ending is a major letdown. Most chapters have long stretches of just walking along. I guess you are supposed to enjoy the scenery and the music but for me it was just plain boring. I clocked in 7 hours of playtime but at least half of that was just walking....and walking....and walking.The controls are passible and there is no chance of death. You do getting injured at certain times which make you walk extremely slow. Which again does nothing but stretch out those areas. I guess I would rate it a 5 out of 10. In the end, I would have rather played something else. I was hoping for some emotional attachment to the fox but that never came. I cared more for the poor shaman souls.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable little, cute game with nice puzzles. i bought this game for the Fox. and also it even has a photomode, if you interested in taking some photos.But there's still some bothering things about it.- Can't save manually. if you want to quit and return later you have to finish the chapter and even then it says that "you'll lose all the progress in the chapter" which is little bit annoying!!- Can't really pause the game if you want to give a little break. (maybe the reason was to no one is attacking you but I would have liked the option)- Can't choose chapter without quitting the game.And why's the Fox sound like a dog? it's like barking, rawr, every time. Did they think that fox's sound might freak out people?
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Summary of my review in a few words; It's good. I like it more than a lot. Thank you devs, I love you. My review in more than too many words;I recently was shown this game by a friend on a whim, and since my favourite animal is the fox, I was very interested from the very beginning. I paid for this game with zero hesitation, only watching the first trailer, looking at some screenshots while it downloaded, and I was eager to see what this game was about. I was very happily surprised by the experience that was waiting for me.-The Gameplay-During the gameplay, I was beginning to hesitate, as the physics are quite floaty and jerky, and it was apparent right away... However, for the team of only a few developers who developed this game, I got past it very quickly; I know that developing 3D games can be difficult, and for this, I respect all of the effort that goes into this game, not only for things that were polished, but the things that were also not polished. The controls are fluid enough, however, could use more polish along the long run; it can be frustrating if you're not the patient type, the fox will run out of energy very often, forcing you to walk a bit, and there's a lot of geometry you can get caught on if you're not careful. There also appear to be a number of locations where you would imagine you could enter or crawl through, but are simply blocked off by invisible walls. This can break immersion, but for me, I enjoyed it for the most part.The puzzles in this game are not heavy on emphasizing what you're 'meant' to do, but I found myself learning the solution eventually. I rarely overthought what I was supposed to be doing, but I did get lost quite often, in a good way. That said, however, there are numerous points in the game where I unintentionally sequence-broke the progression by getting to places I shouldn't have been able to sooner, simply by doing simple maneuvers or jumps. I even soft-locked myself by entering a location prior to obtaining the ability to enter it, simply by traversing the mountain above it.-The Art Direction-I, as an artist myself, absolutely love the artistic direction, the pseudo-painting art style, and the constant ribbon of malice hovering over the wonderful landscape is truly a sight to behold; it becomes immediately aware to the player that the colour red is symbolic, and paired with the white landscape for the beginning area, fading out to much darker colours as the game progresses, it truly impresses me to see, having never seen this game previously. -The Sound & Music-The sound design in this game isn't anything to write home about, but the various fox noises are probably not what the general public would consider to be 'fox noises'; however, I personally, was not offended by it. It works for what it does.The music in this game is genuinely beautiful, but the score can get repetitive, as it repeats itself numerous times, especially if you're someone who takes their time wandering through the vast levels as I do. I loved what I heard, but it does appear that the soundtrack repeats itself constantly. Muting the game's music is an option, so if it begins to bother you, get some music and just relax to it while playing the game.-The Story-The story for this game, while at first seems half-hearted and dull, soon grew on me the more I played the game; I suggest not spoiling yourself with this game's story, and while it's not exactly the most twist-of-fate story ever written, it beautifully pairs together with what the game is; for a story about a fox and a spirit, I think it performs wonderfully, and the underlining theme between the player and their companion makes the end of the game a genuinely heartwarming experience. I fell in love with this story, and it completely bypassed my expectations by a lot. I'm very happy to have played this game for the story.-My Verdict & Recommendation-If you're someone who enjoys lush environments, beautifully-rendered lighting and graphics, a light yet emotional story, a beautiful art direction, and an adorable protagonist, I would suggest buying this game; if you can look past certain problems this game has, and if you simply want a relaxing, lightly-engaging experience, I think you'll genuinely enjoy this. I certainly did.-Final Thoughts, A Letter to the Devs-Devs of Spirit of the North,Thank you all so much for working so hard and so passionately on this game; it's very apparent from the get-go that there was a massive attention to detail, and from being comprised of only a few developers, I have a very large amount of respect for what you do. Thank you for bringing this wonderful story and genuine piece of art to players' hands. Your work has touched me on a level that I will hold onto for a very long time. Truly, thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decently enjoyable game. The visuals are the clear standout here, with breathtaking Icelandic landscapes, from volcanic areas to moss-covered mountains and snowy peaks. The fox you play as is very cute and lifelike in both animation and appearance.Unfortunately, there just isn't a lot to do in this game, you're mainly just running from point A to point B, and while the landscapes are huge, they're very empty. Even something as simple as some more collectibles would increase the fun of this game a lot, in my opinion, because currently I enjoy looking at the landscapes, but I never have any reason to explore them much, which is a shame. The gameplay can also be a bit clunky at times, with a lot of invisible walls blocking off areas that don't look like they should be out of bounds, and the turn cycle for the fox is quite wide, making some of the platforming sections a bit frustrating.The music is also one of the weakest aspects, in my opinion. It's not unpleasant to listen to, but it's very generic, and repeats too quickly, so even though it is alright, it ends up being quite grating when you play the game for a while. I ended up turning it off and listening to some Icelandic folk music instead, which honestly fit the game's atmosphere better than the real soundtrack, in my opinion.Overall, it's a decent little game, though. I'd give it a 6/10. If you like games like Shelter, you'll probably enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: ***EDIT***Turns out when you use the correct keys for movement (WSAD) and NOT the arrow keys, it isn't so twitchy and frustrating. There's still areas that require a lot of coordination and alacrity in movement to accomplish but not seemingly impossible if you are a bit older and have slower reflexes. Would actually quite recommend. It is a shortish game, but the price tag is pretty low, so I would say very worth it. I apologize for my earlier rant.***ORIGINAL REVIEW CONTENT***I just wanted a nice, relaxing game to play. Run around, explore, figure out some puzzles, take some dead guys their sticks. At first, this was perfect, and then I hit the twitch parts. For someone who has the reflexes of an inebriated sloth, trying to accomplish things where I have to be able to press five different keys on the keyboard at about the same time really ruins any experience. I can get games that are difficult and challenging by nature. Games that have that competitive feel to them, even if you're only playing single player. This game doesn't have any of that and still has the stupid gotcha junk. I even recommended this game to my kid when I first started playing it because it looked peaceful and fun. The landscapes are beautiful, and the music is soothing. It seemed to have everything. If I had only played about an hour more, I probably would have realized my mistake, but instead we're both just annoyed and frustrated. I won't say I wasted the money on the first purchase because the game is what it was advertised to be, minus the twitchy puzzles. Unfortunately, in order for my kid to play, I also purchased a second copy, that was definitely money  short, if you're looking for something peaceful and relaxing, this ain't it. If you're looking for something high impact and competitive, this ain't it either. I really don't know what the target audience is here.

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended. The pacing of the "story" is atrociously slow and dragged out, there's very little gameplay beyond navigating the obtusely cumbersome controls and solving a very similar iteration of the same puzzle over and over again, and you're only able to save once you complete each chapter, forcing you to commit yourself to 20-30 mins of gameplay at a time, by which point you might have fallen asleep anyway.As someone who is a huge fan of both exploration games set in nature and the fantasy genre, this completely unrestrained and over the top blend of Arctic scenery and fictional lore tied up in a walking sim should theoretically appeal to me, but it's done in such a mind-bogglingly uninteresting way that I almost think it should be studied. Not recommended, even on sale. 2/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly truly an amazing package of graphics, map design and music that outweighs everything I write below and makes this a positive review.However, be mindful that you won't be getting the best feeling of controls for a game that requires such an amount of action. Despite good overall map design, there isn't a clear difference in looks between walkable paths and unwalkable ones which have invisible walls right above it. There are also a few design flaws and glitches that are irreversible when triggered and may cause you to restart the entire chapter/section.The following user-defined tags about this game may not be accurate:Fox - Yeah it's a fox / two foxes but it barks / they bark.Puzzle - I wouldn't really call it a puzzle game as the logic behind the same mechanisms in different places isn't consistent (e.g. sometimes your spirit form can't dash even when charged and you have to charge it another time, also some shamans unlock necessary paths for progression but others don't). There is also a huge lack of guidance so be ready for a lot of wandering around the entire map section (which can sometimes be really big!) searching for stuff.Relaxing - Yes but not all the time. Don't buy this game if you aren't comfortable with black and red plague infected plants. (But if you are, killing them and purifying places can be quite satisfying.) Also you can't expect yourself to be relaxed if you're stuck in this section for like half an hour because the game doesn't give you any clues.
