_childDocuments_.review: This game was very beautiful, the graphics were very pleasing to the eye and the soundtrack made this play-through feel dreamy. Not a single word was spoken in this game, yet the story was very intriguing and continued to draw me in through to the end. I never imagined myself growing attached to a computer generated fox but here we are, overall this game was very nice to play and i'd definitely recommend to anyone looking for a cosy game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute and relaxing, no dialog but you still get the story. Some chapters are really short, others are long, the controls and the camera sometimes are kind of effy, you can be aiming to jump at a certain place and the fox jumps to the opposite side, or doesnt jumps at all and just falls (this issue was with the keyboard, thus I'm not sure if there are issues playing with a controller), sometimes you can get stuck at random places, other times with small rocks on the floor, those issues aside, the game is enjoyable.PS: I loved the ending, I ended up crying.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful game that took about 7 hours to complete while taking my time and not rushing through the story. Visuals and music is top notch and the story is all about "show don't tell" and they've pulled it off really well. The puzzles at the start of the game are fairly easy and straightforward, they then increase in difficulty as the game goes on and are just challenging enough to make you think without it getting frustrating or you getting stuck.I played it with a controller and found the controls and abilities quite intuitive. I read some players saying the jump of the fox felt slightly wonky, but I really didn't think about it. Perhaps it is different if you play with keyboard and mouse.Another thing that I appreciated was that while you could play this game as a completionist, looking for and completing all the hidden tasks, it is never required that you have to finish everything in a chapter to progress in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best exploration/puzzle games I've played, hands down. Very beautiful and soothing. Visually stunning; I could literally feel soft grass beneath my feet and gentle wind caressing my fur. I kept bawling throughout the game and especially towards the end. It was like chopping onions but in a video game. No time to blow your nose or wipe your eyes, just gotta do the thing.I was curious, so took a peek to the side of negative reviews, and it never ceases to amuse me how there's always people complaining about this kind of games not having enough challenge or whatever, while the whole point of the game is to be easy and relaxing. Drop the thrill seeking for a while? The world is full to the brim of games with merciless speed and challenge. Imo we really need more games like this to take a moment to slow down every now and then.P.S. Big bonus for a bark button. Game automatically sucks if you get to play an animal and they can't say the big word. Yesss. And dem ears going up and down and up and down when you run. They're hypnotic.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a very long, complex or difficult game. It is more about exploration, taking in the scenery, solving puzzles and playing at your own pace. The pacing is rather slow with several segments of "just walking". Where this game truly excels is in its atmosphere. The graphics are not really amazing but the environments are beautifully crafted and can get truly breathtaking in a few places. The music is absolutely gorgeous and spot on for the overall mood. The sounddesign I found just a little bit lackluster, but it didn't take away from the experience.The story is told in an endearing way and there are a few quite emotional moments. All in all, "Spirit of the North" is, in my opinion, a beautiful little gem of a game. I loved just roaming through these landscapes, listening to the soundtrack and steadily making progress. It's not perfect, but it feels like a unique little journey and was definitely worth my time.So how much do you get for your money?My first (blind) playthrough took me about five hours (with one or two puzzles taking me way longer to solve than they should have, to be honest), and in a second playthrough I was able to get all secrets and achievements. I will probably revisit the game in a few months or so. Since I bought the game at a discount, that's pretty good value for money. But honestly, I would even recommend it at full price. If it sounds like something that might interest you, I'd say give it a go.

Movement doesn't connect well with the scene. It's a mess of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon hearing Spirit of the North described as a mix between Okami and Death Stranding, my curiosity soared. How could a game merge these two seemingly distant worlds? After playing, I can confirm it's not far off, though there's more, or perhaps less, to it, depending on your perspective.Spirit of the North casts you as a fox who forms a connection with a guardian spirit in fox form, protector of the Northern Lights. Together, you embark on a quest to uncover the mysteries of an ancient civilization and combat the encroaching corruption. While it might seem reminiscent of Okami with its mystical fox protagonist, the similarity ends there. Okami is a whimsical and charming adventure, while Spirit of the North takes the slow path, offering minimal hand-holding and requiring patient exploration and puzzle-solving.Spirit of the North may remind you of Death Stranding, at least in terms of its exploration. There's no narrative or dialogue directing your every move. You're left to navigate narrow caves, expansive meadows, and crumbling ruins, searching for answers. The pace is methodical, with seemingly little reward until later in the game.The game's story unfolds through hieroglyphics etched into stone slabs scattered throughout the world. At first, these inscriptions seem like gibberish, but gradually, as you explore the abandoned structures and ruins of the previous civilization, it starts to make sense. The pieces come together at the end, making the aimless wandering feel more purposeful.You'll come across staffs in your journey, which you can reunite with the spirits of ancient shamans from the extinct civilization. This act brings them peace, but whether it unlocks a special ending is uncertain. These moments provide some enjoyable challenges, and you might want to go back and collect them all if you missed any.Spirit of the North includes platforming sections, particularly around the ruins. Unfortunately, these segments can be maddening. The fox's running and jumping controls are decent, but jumping feels somewhat floaty, making precise jumps a challenge. The fox's slow swim speed is irksome, with no option to speed up. Worse, even puddles turn into treacle as the fox slugs through them and shakes off excessively upon exiting. Also, environmental glitches can disrupt your progress, impeding your enjoyment.The game's visuals are a mixed bag, with stunning panoramas but inconsistent textures up close. Textural disparities affect rocks and the fox protagonist, with fur appearing dated when viewed too closely. On the plus side, the game maintains a steady framerate and short loading times. The audio design shines, with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack by Joseph Gifford, although some additional musical pieces would have been welcome to reduce repetition.Spirit of the North is a game that encourages you to slow down and savor the journey. The intentionally slow pace immerses you in the fox's shoes, creating a sense of discovery. It's a long, introspective journey, and while it may not be for everyone, patience yields a unique tale of self-discovery.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Beware, this game is....boring. Before i catch heat for that statement, i did go into this game expecting a slower pace and a more atmospheric game. I did not go into it with action packed combat in mind. That being said it's just plain boring. The music is well done, but the same little tune plays over and over on repeat with very little in the way of variety. I don't know if it was a glitch or not but at one point in the game there was no music at all. I understand the game is a more of a puzzle platformer but even in that context i found it boring. The worst offender of all is that you have a number of different abilities for traversal and puzzle solving but each one of those abilities requires the use of this "spirit energy" that you have to charge at these blue flowers. You can only get one charge at a time from the flowers. After using it you must return to the flowers to get another charge. At one point in the game i had to imbue 4 different stones with power. i had to literally go to the flowers, perform the charging animation, run to the stone, perform the animation to imbue the stone tablet, then run back to the flowers to recharge the spirit power, rinse and repeat for each one.... much of the game felt like busy work. I found it very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, my feelings are mixed. It's just a little over 3 hours of gameplay total. It's cute, but also rather empty. Large open world yet annoying hitboxes make navigating awkward at times and there is deceptively little content within said world. The main problem I found was the sheer lack of guidance you would receive. For such an open world, I would have liked far more in the way of prompting in where to go. The puzzles were annoying not because they were hard, but because they were relatively easy, and if you were finding it hard, it was because you had missed something on the map and had to look for it rather than the puzzle itself being challenging. The tone of the map itself changed rather dramatically early on, and I have to admit I wasn't too fond of the fact that the change was permanent. While initially I enjoyed the change of pace, I very quickly found myself missing the original.The final chapter I found rather dull. The final stretch is too open, takes too long, and has basically nothing in it. The visuals, while nice, aren't at the level where they can make up for the lack of content.The worst part is the groundwork is very much there. It feels like this could have been, and still potentially could be, a great game. It just needs more to do. As it stands though, I don't believe the game is worth it at full price, for three hours of largely empty or easy gameplay. If you see it on sale, then I'd say give it a go. It's a nice game in its own right, despite what I've said above.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello weary traveller!Seems like you are at the crossroads again, contemplating whether to buy this game or not. The game is a visual spectacle alright, but it has it's flaws here and there. It can use a little bit of polishing in animations and visual glitches. Since it is an Indie, don't expect too much. Sit back and enjoy the puzzles. They are not that difficult. The music is top notch and the landscapes are absolutely gorgeous! The game's not perfect. But is it beautiful? By the Nine Divines, it is! It is a sweet little game if you want to escape your wanderings for 4-5 hours. 12/10 would pet the good fox!

_childDocuments_.review: The trailers make it look like you get to fling yourself across the landscape as a spirit. Instead I have spent 2.5 hours tediously walking everywhere. Which might not be so terrible if I actually knew where I was going. I'm sure eventually I'm supposed to stop a plague or something? But after every puzzle I have to stop and look around as I wonder Now What? Because this game is not as intuitive as it thinks it is. Also reuniting the staffs with the monk guys is frustrating. Assuming I can even find where their corpse is half the time I can't figure out how to get to it.Clunky puzzle platformer is clunky
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It is a beautiful game and the music is calming. My 8yo daughter loves to watch me play and I have enjoyed spending the time with her. She loves how cute the fox is and helping me navigate my way around and solving the puzzles. Unfortunately, I am playing on a laptop with no mouse and the movements and camera are clunky and uncoordinated at best. I wish there was a save button, as I spent an hour clumsily making slow progress in a chapter only to lose it all when I had to leave the game.  I also wish there was a pause button so the fox doesn't keep moving as I am struggling to get the camera angle right so I can see where I'm going. Maybe this game is better on a different platform, but a laptop not so much. If my daughter wasn't so attached to the "fox game" I would've quit playing and saved myself a lot of frustration already.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a "meh" rating. The game is gorgeous, though the fox model, imo, needs some TLC. The music is great, however in some areas it's a little intense for what the game is. I think it would be better with a Breath of the Wild type music.As for gameplay, I was a little annoyed that I couldn't sprint at the beginning of the game. You get it after maybe 10 minutes of playing, depending how long you want to explore and appreciate the environment. With that said, control and movement is just not good, plain and simple. In a big open field it's no problem, but if you are need to might tight and precise movements, it can be a little annoying. Next, swimming and water & forced animations. Holy cow is water annoying. Sure, you swim slower than you sprint, which makes sense, but half the time after getting out of the water you are forced to stop and watch a short animation of the fox shaking the water off. Pretty obnoxious after the 20th time. Lastly, possible spoiler, so ignore this part if you want, but each time you activate something with your spirit ability, you gotta go find another flower patch to reacquire your spirit ability. I understand why that mechanic is implemented into the game as it affects the puzzles, but needing to run over, activate the animation, and wait for it to complete so you can regain the spirit ability is annoying. Sure, it's only 3ish seconds, but that time adds upThe game, at least for the first two chapters is extremely linear, and this is coming from a guy that grew up on the Legend of Zelda. I believe there is a chapter select option at the main screen, but I did not investigate it. The reason the linearity is a problem for me is because I am an completionist, or at the very least a collector. I like to collect as much as I can, within reason of enjoyability. In the trailer and pictures above, you can see monk type NPCs that can be awoken with staves. If you miss a monk, there is a decent chance you cannot go back to get them, then you gotta start the chapter all over. That's a big oof for meLike I said, I wish I could give this game a "meh" rating. Definitely not worth the $20, imo. I bought it 70% off for $5.99, which would be a great price imo, but the linearity, mediocre controls, and forced animations make it less enjoyable

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, hear me out. Being that there was a notable little tid-bit saying about Nordic folklore and Icelandic landscape there was and is a lot of potential for this to be like a  Nordic Okami game. Their plan or not it seems... flat. Now, as far as the apparent direction of the game it seems very clear the team behind it either didn't have the team roster to pull out all the stops they wanted or that this is a slower more casual pace they wanted to go initially. But! With games like Hollow Knight, Ori And the Blind Forest, Slime Rancher, The Last Guardian, The Unfinished Swan, Journey, Abzu, Vane, and other artistic vision / cutesy gameplay titles, this game could have definitely been more involved based on what it's clearly trying to tell as an otherwise flattened story. First I want to say that this game is far from trash, but it is likewise not close to "Overwhelmingly Positive" either.Firstly Animation and Music are pretty good. The Style seems "upstart studio" but not awful, but not great. Still, I like it tbh. Now, RULES OF PLAY. These frustrate me in this game being that there are a more than a few times I went to do things having prior been taught by the game then going to use that method to be told "no, this instead". I was notably confused like "am i nuts or does this not work now?" Which, no, I'm not crazy it just sometimes says do this thing different this time. Which I can't scream about this to hard because of that whole era of games that left you to learn it yourself. So. Ehh.PACING & LEVEL DESIGN This game just decides to go 0 to snail and stay there. There were and are a few places they could have cranked the jams so to speak to really drive the feeling of a level. For example the part where you rise and lower the water levels. Building a the level out where diving and swimming faster, needing to breathe and creating more urgency and strategy on the front of how to use spirit and problem solving skills would have sold that stage. The Option of faster swimming and actually being able to fully stop in the water would have also been nice. Oh, and running in "ankle" deep water please? Simply out of that fact a real fox can swim slower/faster, stop in the water/ dive and need to breathe under the water, and run through puddles. Another area is likewise the Plains in level 4 or 5 where you learn to use those rifts to be pushed forwared in short bursts. Instead it would have driven the freeing and foxy speed home to make them stackable boosts. Through each ring you run faster, and Faster, and FASTER, bolting and weaving bursting and jumping until you reach the ramp and WHOOSH you're at full speed and you're rushed over the clearing into the water to hydroplane onto the land right before breaking water to continue then with steady speed up the hill over the clearing and into the next stage triumphant. Pacing like that is in Abzu and Journey and creates memorable lasting experiences fondly remembered. This doesn't do that. But the Trailer did.Animation and Sound Design.Minor Fixes in the catagory, The barking well... have you heard foxes before, I have a vixen that raised pup down the road from my house and uh... well... no? You kinda got it wrong. But mixing the right sounds with the right poses and animations can make things more dynamic and memorable and more fun to perform. Example instead of just a bark and a tail wag to activate stone. how about a stance that's like I mean bizznass and then throwing the head back accompanied with that foxish howl a fox can do and a cool little burst of blue spirit energy and the stone activating all cool and celtic like. with a nice little sound effect like the magic is taking more hold to the runestone. Okami did this every time you summoned the moon is had a sound like mist rushing in to peer back and reveal the moon with the neat little sound after. Or when again, in Okami, you cleanse an area you do a kick-butt howl that liberates the area and kicks off a cutscene. Or how when you run in that game you switch through three speeds and the sound and animation work together to deliver how fast you're really running across any level.This game isn't bad, It's just lacking small to heavy (depending on how you review) amounts of polish that could take it from what it is to something better. And even still, the studio may be trying to go for a completely different feel. And If by any chance they see this and have a bigger team by then/now and they make changes like these we'll all see what this was going to be. But with how I feel (with bias clouding review here) I felt the game wasn't entirely complete.

There were some minor movement glitches, but really it was minor and didn't detract much from the game.  It's one of those games where I wish I could temporarily erase the memory of playing it and replay it again to capture that first experience.I play a lot of fox games (hey, I like foxes) - The First Tree, Ori, Seasons After Fall, Never Alone and this one is definitely up there among the top of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I do wish Steam at least had a “neutral” option, because this option doesnt best express my opinion from a simple glance. I dont tend to give reviews, but i love games with animals and I feel maybe my review will give insight to others who enjoy these kinds of games- i dont hate this game at all but i want to see more animal games and i want to see them come up with quality and unique ideas instead of repeating trends and not polishing many aspects that should be focused on.if youre itching for a new animal based game after playing all there is, then definitely give this game a shot, it wont hurt and i dont think the price is that bad. the game is not awful, and i liked parts of it. but i have also played loads of similar games that did what this game attempted, far better that this. the game play is simple, its mostly wandering around solving simple puzzles with a few abilities. obviously many walk sim/puzzle games lack more features and its not really a problem... but i do feel the game direction is some area was a bit messy in that i saw no reason for certain aspects to be there other than to have a little fun moment (ex. the ice slides). this game has different “goals” you can achieve... theres simple puzzles and then theres ancient humans you can find using a staff, along with some carvings on stone you can uncover. Now, the puzzles are a major part of the progression, but the humans and carvings are optional it seems. and i will be honest, i see no reason in finding them (and i know they give skins, but that is just a simple extra addition to me tbh)... they really dont anything to the story or game. the stone carvings kind of hint history, but barely any at all and feels just as pointless to hunt down. controls are a bit wonky- the animation in conjunction with it are not very smooth sometimes and the way your character snaps to almost any surface makes some movement a bit odd and the camera will jump up and down as you go over these small bumps in the land.. jumping can also be hard to handle in tight spaces or with speed and the geysers were definite odd to handle. Towards the end of the game i found the gameplay kind of tedious (chapter 7 mostly). lots of running huge distances simply to bark at something and follow another path...not super engaging. the puzzle a just very simple and repeat over and over. the solutions are super easy to figure out. The game is quite pretty, i most love the landscapes. this is probably the most positive aspect of the game, but i do feel some areas are just a bit too short and some are way too long/spread out. aside, it is still fun to run through. the effects and all look lovely. it is not the highest quality graphics either but i dont personally care, as i imagine many others dont. but looks dont save every other part of this game. i beleive this is important enough to have its own category.first things first, theres a lot of back/forth about the barking. lets get the facts straight- if you know anything about foxes, you’d know that while they  bark...they also make other noises that are waaay more common than that barking. yips and whimpers and growls. it sounds unnatural to hear the same bark every time and that is what gets me about the dev(s) claiming foxes bark so this is okay... if you pick an animal for your game the least you could actually do it know what it sounds like and add variety to make it natural. there are probably loads of free stock sounds of foxes that would fit more than that. the devs can claim foxes bark but if they looked a little more theyd know full well they bark in specific scenarios and not All The Time.in general the music is nice, but i cant be mistaken that im hearing like the same tracks? do they just sounds similar? it got repetitive. i think there was a mistake in trying to use the music to cover up environmental sounds, its quite empty when youre playing. Spoilers ahead.Alright so, i have the most to say about this end. the game is “speechless” and i know in general that may turn people off, thats fine, its not for everyone. i have played numerous speechless games that i LOVE...so i have to say- the speechless story in this game really fell flat in many areas... theres a lot of ways to do it well and i dont think it was done that well here.right off the bat, the introduction really did not catch me, the “first chapter” was kinda bland and really didn’t imply a single thing to me about what was happening... you are a fox on their own, and come across a spirit fox. You follow it through the world to solve some problem with a weird red disease infecting the land. a simple story is fine, but it lack so SO much character. and there is no lore to additionally back up an already simple concept. i understand some people may have a soft spot for the animal focused story and i wont say i didnt enjoy it to some extent. but i am kind of surprised by the praise it is getting! the fox is barely even a ‘character’ in this story, as in... they dont really have a personality and nor does the spirit. you follow through the world learning almost nothing about it aside from the important points which occur at the end mostly--  the ending is what gets me most, because you expect things to be tied up but honestly it did not bring much closure or sense to the actions you made or what was happening. they didnt explain much of any "why" to your fox being  etc. It all felt like there wasnt anything back up the concepts, thats also why the lack of 'lore' is important to note. It brought zero depth to the story. but i digress- the point is, is that this game really lacks in its story telling. i have played good speechless games. this game couldve used body language and animation to tell about the characters, more visual world building to imply lore and history, flashbacks to tell more history, etc.  i have played many “animal walking sim with puzzles” games and i have liked a lot of them. Spirit of the North lacked in many areas and failed to be a completely enjoyable experience for me. Game play was fine but sometimes wonky, audio was alright, story lacks in many ways and the visuals are probably the best part.... i am giving this game a negative review because i dont see why it is so positive, and it plays off many recent things found in many other animal walking sims- which i really have issue with. theres a bit of a trend these past few years with making ‘unique’ walking sims, by adding an animal into the mix. i think it seems different and people are just hopping on it because there is a lot of interest for more animal based games. and i want that! but i want things that are unqiue, try new things, and dont copy/fall into trends. Spirit of the North falls into many basic trending ideas (animal player, abandoned civilization story, sentient object guides you, attempts a touching story, etc)That is my honest view on the game. As i said if you played all other animal games out there, like i have, then play it if you really want. but i dont think this game is anything that special in comparison to others.would reccomend these games too: Shelter 1, Shelter 2, Paws, Fe, AER Memories of Old, Gris, The First Tree, Lost Ember, Abzu, Journey, Eastshade.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North has some of the best graphics I've ever seen in an indie title, has neat little touches and details to the fox's animations which were cute to watch, has interesting gimmicks, and DID I MENTION YOU CAN PLAY AS A FOX...so why am I giving this a thumbs down? Well, the gameplay leaves a lot to be desired, and I hate to say that most of the game I found quite boring since I really wanted to enjoy this one. There's a severe lack of direction at certain portions of the adventure due to the massive open fields your fox often runs though. What the adventure does contain though is almost constantly doing the same monotonous things over and over again to the same few music tracks. There are interesting gimmicks presented, however most of the time they hardly get time to shine. While the first 2/3's of the game are quite boring and even feel rushed at times, the final 2-3 chapters were enjoyable, unique, and showcased what the rest of the game could have been like. The game is beautiful, and the fox is charming, but I sadly can't recommend this one.Pros:- Insanely good graphics for an indie title- Fun and cute little animations- Interesting mechanics- Beautiful musicCons:- Boring gameplay- Lack of direction- Short for the money- While the music is beautiful, there aren't many songs present

_childDocuments_.review: Note I am not finished yet, but I suspect I am near the end.First off I LOVE this game-mostly. The general tone (see exception), the music, the puzzles, just a really beautiful game that Im taking 5 hours so far, but I had to repeat a couple of areas (see later). The Pros: The story, the atmosphere, the beautiful simplicity of a game with no dialogue, tells a pretty neat little story that may or may not be spiritual in nature. There is some definite "earthy" type of themes here, but they're pretty decent and don't hammer you over the head with it. The piano music so soothing and relaxing. Its a beautiful game to just play and let your brain check out for awhile with some light puzzles, some of which I admit I had to look up to see what was pretty much in front of my face. LOL. Its a great game for a short puzzle story, I got it on sale and Im enjoying it, and will replay again just as a relaxing game. The Cons: If the creator of the game reads these comments, a word if you will. As I said it's a beautiful game mostly and its such a lovely experience. But where I began to start getting mentally kicked out of the world was around Middle of Chapter 5, and I am just starting 6. The Platforming. The whole tone of the game was beautiful right up to around early to middle of Chapter 5, and especially end chapter 5-some early levels had it too. This game was being done so beautifully I don't think it needed the picture perfect platforming, esp as a controller isn't always going the right way. I applaud you not wanting to die in the game, but it got frustrating when you missed a jump and you end up having to do what felt like a 10-30 second backtrack to redo the jump. Really took the game for me from very relaxing to frustrating. I don't mind losing a few seconds but some of them really got off putting. ALSO-later chapter 5 theres a point of raising water levels, and I had to restart the level part because I had accidently filled a place for the "out of body" button, I could swim and I could light it up, but could not curl up to activate the mechanic. And there is no way to go back and "lessen" a water level, so I had to redo the level in that certain order so I could "get" to that button. If there's a way to fix that so the water is slightly lowered or just the curl up sign is able to be accessed. Overall it has been a wonderful experience, I would have liked to have option of when the light goes off to direct you, if you could activiate again as sometimes it goes around a corner and you don't know where it went and cant get it to trigger again. I liked the little secret areas you can find and it rewarded exploring. Would recommend for anyone who likes a short game, likes light puzzling, and doesn't mind some platform hopping that can get a bit frustrating towards later game8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is, in my opinion, a very enjoyable game. It has its ups and downs, but overall it was pretty well done. Now prepare for a long review and an interesting ending (spoiler alert—I gave my interpretation of the storyline!)I bought and played this game on PC, so I can only describe how well the controls work with a keyboard (and I've heard some negative reviews about the game with a controller). But for a keyboard, it's very smooth. The controls are easy to learn: regular movement keys of course; both mouse buttons are used for certain actions within the game, at which point a prompt will appear on the screen to tell you what to use; and a few keys for special abilities. The movement is clean and responsive.Most of the gameplay is pretty simple. You play as a red fox who is aided by a spirit fox, and then journey with your new friend to save a world plagued by a strange scarlet disease. You must find glowing blue flowers to obtain spiritual energy, and use that energy to solve puzzles, open new areas, and unlock special abilities. As you do so, you can occasionally find hidden staffs, which you can pick up and carry, and when you near the staff's owner, the blue gem glows and sparks. You place the staff beside a robed skeleton and its spirit rises to give you a respectful bow before disappearing. Throughout your adventures, you find many of these spirits, and can free them if you choose (it's actually optional—the staffs and their owners are hidden everywhere, and it's kind of an extra side mission to free them).The music is phenomenal. It's beautiful, haunting, melancholic, and sometimes a bit eerie. There are a few times where it's a bit weird though, like you move a few steps in one direction and the music abruptly changes, and then you move back and it changes again. And sometimes it doesn't quite match your environment, or it gets you hyped up for the wrong reason. For example, it can be slow and creepy, and gradually rise and intensify, building suspense, and it finally crescendos when you reach whatever it is you've been walking toward—and there's nothing to justify the terrifying music. Often there's nothing there at all. But aside from that, it's wonderful music. Now for some of the negative bits. A few of the puzzles can be frustrating. Sometimes you've got to get the timing just right, or jump from the exact perfect spot in order to reach your goal. Sometimes you have no idea where to go, because the terrain doesn't always have a clear path. Often the actual path is hidden or obscured, and you have to go searching for it. Sometimes you go the total wrong way and have to find your way back. And don't get me started on the water and swimming mechanics. One, the swimming is incredibly slow. Two, when you come out of the water and onto land, even if it's just a tiny sliver of land, you must wait five or six seconds for your fox to shake the water out of its fur. At first, yeah, that's a cool animation, but when you're trying to make that one jump puzzle and keep falling into the water, it gets annoying. And there's another thing. Towards the final chapters of the game, when previously it was optional, freeing the robed spirits becomes necessary to progress. I didn't exactly mind this, since I'd been trying to free as many as I could anyway, but it would've been nice to give more of a heads-up for those who might not really care.So yeah, there are a few things about the gameplay that I don't exactly like, but boy, the graphics are absolutely gorgeous. The landscape is a beautiful replica of Iceland, with its rocky, icy mountains; dark, mysterious caves; large, grassy plains; flowing rivers and sapphire lakes; and the wind ruffling your fur and swaying the grass wherever you go. As you travel through the world, you come across several crumbling structures, stone houses and towers, even a few of what seem to be villages. These structures are where a lot of the puzzles take place, and where there are many robed spirits to be freed.And now, for the final part. The story. The storyline is, admittedly, a bit hard to follow. There is no dialogue, no narrator, nothing to explain what's really happening. It's kind of up to you to figure it out. There are vague murals, carvings on the runestones, and symbols everywhere, but it's still rather difficult to understand. The easy bit is this: a strange, terrible disease has swept over the land, manifesting as bulbous plant-like things that spew red spores everywhere, leaving a scarlet trail in the sky. You, a red fox, have partnered with a spirit fox (the "Spirit of the North") to try and save the ravaged land. After that, it gets confusing. I have tried my best to interpret from what I gathered from the runestones and murals, and what I didn't know, I filled in myself. So I have built a story that hopefully makes sense for this game:file:///C:/Users/naomi.LAPTOP-0GH7QA42/Downloads/Just%20a%20Fan's%20Version%20of%20the%20SotN%20Storyline.pdfIf that link worked (hopefully it did) and you managed to read the entire storyline, I congratulate you. I also hope that the storyline makes sense to you. Honestly, I just played the whole game and then wrote the entire thing afterwards. I really like how it turned out. Now, I'm not sure how true it is, or how correct the details are, or how much of it is what the developers were going for. But really, I searched for like 20 minutes all over the internet and couldn't find a single thing that truly explained the storyline of this game. So I decided I'd write my own based on the pieces I could fit together, and whatever blanks there were, I'd fill them in myself. And I think it's a pretty good story, even if it isn't exact to the game. If the link didn't work and you couldn't read it, sorry. Maybe you could download the game and play it, and then see what storyline YOU might be able to think up! It's all in the imagination. Try it out!Despite its difficulties and annoyances, this game is pretty great, and I totally recommend it. It's a lot of fun and super relaxing. Thanks a lot for reading this far and I hope you enjoy your day.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the best games I've experienced. The only bad thing about it, is how short it was.The puzzles were challenging enough to not make me bored, but not hard enough to make them frustrating. The game itself was beautiful, not to mention the soundtrack left me teary-eyed, and it's something I'll absolutely listen to repeat. _childDocuments_.review: If someone asks you what is Spirit of the North, the simplest answer is to tell them that you play a fox doggo looking for sticks in hope to wake people and finally play fetch.Of course, you can also tell them the grand story of the Spirit of the North who fell asleep within the mountain and how you, a simple fox, woke him up and played with him until discovering what happened to the world. Following an attempt to destruct some of the plague which caused the Guardian to disappear in the first place, the ancient floor falls appart and while the spirit keeps guiding you, you eventually fall for your last sleep.Having been alone for so long, the Spirit isn't ready to let his first friend since forever to die, giving you a part of its ability and while It still follows you as a Whisp, you are now given the task to eradicate the plague so you can join back the sky and wake up the long lost Northern Lights.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to give a short review of this game. However, I honestly do not feel good to just give a simple thumbs up or down. First, I did enjoy this game. But I feel like this game has a lot of unused potential. It is by no means a bad game. But I think it is only 30% of what it could have been. To explain this I should probably start with what I expected. I recently played Gris and expected a somewhat similar game. A "walking simulator" that shows me a beautiful world and tells me a nice story. Certainly not as artistic but with its own distinct style. A few little puzzles and a few movement sections on top. Love that kind of game. Now to what I experienced.Too many of the areas just felt unnecessarily empty. It felt like nothing was happening. There was no puzzle to solve, no obstacle to overcome, no mystery to uncover, no emotion that you were supposed to experience. Just press forward and wait.Also... Invisible walls. This game has an insulting amount of them placed in sometimes the most ridiculous places blocking me from making jumps that were completely irrelevant while it was incredibly easy to access areas I was not supposed to be in. I softlocked myself 2 times simply by playing the game and got annoyed because I could not jump over objects that were otherwise easily jumpable. Furthermore, since the fox was presumably a Skyrim horse in his last life sequence breaking in this game is ridiculously easy. You will automatically do this when playing casually. However, all in all this is an indie game. If you know about these issues and you know what to expect this can still be a decent game. The music is amazing and although it sometimes feels empty, the game does look really good. Somewhat repetitive after some time but the good kind of repetitive. The story is easy to follow and I genuinely liked the experience of playing a fox. I think the biggest issue I have with this game really is that I feel like there is so much unused potential. To me this game is an amazing concept that has to be polished to make it a brilliant game. It has all the right elements. If only the developers would have been brave enough to use them.TLDR: Typical indie problems but I suggest buying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty interesting game. Its pretty light on the puzzles and easy to get through, with most of the entertainment coming from the exploration and landscapes visited along the way. There's a collectible to find which justifies the exploration, but after you do that (and collect what other achievements you're after), there's probably not much point into picking up the game.With exploration hunting, I clocked in at around 10 hours of play. Just charging through probably gives you about 3-4 hours of play time, maybe 5 considering the puzzles. So keep that in mind while deciding if the game is worth it for you. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a lovely true ending. Although it lacks a variety of content even for a short game, the content that is there is well done. Examples: Though the soundtrack is short and so repeats a number of times, that doesn't distract from the tone it sets. There's few complex animations such as climbing, but the regular movement looks quite natural. The puzzles are very simple and get reused, but the beautiful scenery still made them feel worthwhile.Really the only problems with it I had were twofold:First, in some areas it's hard to tell what you're expected to do. If you miss a small thing and get lost you can even end up having to backtrack a ways. (Player advice: If you're following something and lose track of it, keep moving forward and it'll find you after a while.)Second, the second-to-last chapter has a gigantic map but is very easy to get lost on. Which makes it a bit-hard to get the true ending if you don't know to look for it. It also makes the achievement to find a bunch of spots in this chapter, which can be well-hidden, very tough. (Player advice: You'll have to complete another achievement throughout the earlier portion of the game before this one becomes possible to complete, too.)P.S. It is weird that the foxes bark like dogs. Yes they can do so but almost never actually do. Would be like having wolves bark or feral cats meowing. Also, even if it's just a texture change, it's nice to have the choice between tom fox and vixen skins.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this game a negative review. The art direction is superb and the music is wonderful. The game manages to pull you into a soothing atmosphere and you have moments where you truly get surprised at the beauty it can show you. I love hiking and some of the environnments brought me the same feelings of peace and awe I have when I'm surrounded by nature. But all of these massive positives get overshadowed by the clunkyness and the gameplay. The puzzle aspect could be great, I actually love puzzle games (even though thinking hurts), but this game tends to mix puzzle and open world elements in one, making you search for the puzzle more than you puzzle. The maps are too big (which is why I feel like it tried to have open world elements to it), it leads more to confusion and frustration than fun. The environnements also tend to repeat each other and blend into one which doesn't help the confusion. My least favorite part was the awkward platforming, it really ends up frustrating you more than it does calm you. The game seriously needs polishing. It's such a shame really! Especially for such a beautiful game. Sometimes I even thought that making it a walking simulator with a bigger focus on its story (which is a bit vague and open to interpretation) could have been a better direction for the game and give more space for the beautiful art and experiences the game can offer. Last thing I want to add is that there were moments in this game that blatantly felt too long, painfully long. This is mainly due to the maps being too big and some of the puzzles not being intuitive enough. I understand you need some level of thinking to solve puzzles, but some of them really had the solution hidden away from you within repeating map decor which is just... painfully frustrating. It's not a fun feeling to waste your time trying to search for a solution that doesn't make much sense. I heard they are releasing a sequel for this game, I am interested to see if the negative aspects have been worked on and fixed/improved. I still think this game is worth experiencing because it truly is beautiful. But I have a hard time recommending it unless you're willing to sit throught its flaws. The beauty and art does help forget about the game's shortcomings, which is a massive positive and a massive testament to the art direction being phenomenal.I truly wish only the best for the developpers and artists behind this project. I understand making a game is difficult and involves so so much. Although I give this game a negative review, I truly appreciate the experience it brought me.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this is totally fine to good, except for two things.  The walking, and the stuff you walk on.  Which makes it a mostly ok game, that doesn't really stack up to others in the genre.  If you just want to relax and take in the scenery and music, this is a pretty chill title that is probably worth it.  If you want a tightly calibrated platformer/walking simulator with a tangible world to be in, this may disappoint.This game comes up really short on the two things you need in a walking sim/puzzle platformer.  The terrain doesn't match the bounds/physical geometry.  So, what you end up with is invisible walls and platforms you're constantly bumping up against, which can make you have to start over on some jump pattern or other nonsense.  Second is the motion.  It isn't fluid and your avatar makes these wide unwieldy turns that make precise control next to impossible.  Jumps feel delayed and never get the immersion or experience that you're in this world.  You just have a CGI'd fox that doesn't even stand on the ground but floats an inch above it on 2 feet.These two things together make for an ultimately poor experience in a game that really would need both to shine.  Graphics are mostly ok, there are some holes and missing polygons where can peer into the void of the unrendered, and they happen more than they should.  But, overall this is a pleasure to look at.  Puzzles aren't too challenging or needlessly complex, but still feel meaningful to progress.Finally, while this game looks good, it isn't amazing and looks on par for a game that might have come out a few years ago.  That said, this is one of the few titles that really cooks my graphics card for some reason, so ymmv.

_childDocuments_.review: How many words does a good story need? In some cases not a single word at all. Spirit of the North is a fantastic example of purely visual storytelling. And it's a really beautiful story. I don't want to spoiler too much, so lets say: You're a fox on a big adventure. You explore the nature, ancient ruins and you solve puzzles. The puzzles aren't too hard so they should never be in the way of progressing the story.And the art is just beautiful. The graphics, the soundtrack ... it's a very fairytale like experience. Great to relax and enjoy a few hours in a fantastic world of nordic mythology. There is no combat, no danger of dying and no time limit. If you just want to take your time to explore a beautiful story (and you like foxes) check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: My wife saw this title during the last Steam Winter Sale, and the pretty environments with a cute fox was all she needed to want to play. I watched her for most of the game, and really that's most of what this game is. With no exposition and no real cutscenes the story is a bit vague, and most of the world is a gigantic empty mass with puzzles scattered inbetween. For what it is, this works well enough -- Spirit of the North is essentially a walking simulator, and the environments are spectacularly done with a solid soundtrack to make exploring enjoyable and atmospheric.Where the game ultimately falls short is that there is actually very little game. The platforming elements are clunky, both in controls and in collision boxes in-game, and the huge expanse of the world often provides minimal guidance on where to actually go. Sometimes things which seem optional become mandatory, and others the required path is a tiny little jaunt off a gargantuan field or hillside that takes about 5 minutes to walk around. The puzzles are relatively simple, but this game is also difficult to do in one sitting so it's easy to forget some very subtle things that the game briefly shows you once and then expects you to remember hours later.While it's clearly a labor of love from the developers, I don't think the game is worth the full price tag. We came in at about 9 hours of game time to complete, maybe a bit less, and the level of polish and the underlying content on this title is not such that I think it warrants a $20 purchase. However, I think this is a great title to pick up on sale, especially for kids or for anyone just wanting a casual experience. I think we picked it up for $8-10 or something in that range, which I think is fair.Certainly an impressive amount of work for two guys doing it on their own, and the underlying flaws are understandable in this context.

_childDocuments_.review: I am in a fire-like kingdom (after chapter 4) and I decide to stop here.Game is confusing. Not a single narration, no directions. _childDocuments_.review: This game was truly beautiful. It's similar to Journey - you go forward learning about the story, and on your way you have to figure out puzzles, get collectibles, enjoy music and views.+ visuals & music create nice, relaxing atmosphere+ I would say you have to play it 2 times - first to just enjoy and relax, second to really look around so you collect everything, so in the end you get hours of fun to finish the game 100%+/- It's not very intuitive. _childDocuments_.review: In this game you play as the Firefox browser. You band together with the blue developer edition to fight for market superiority against the plague of Opera. Raising user experience (water) through  user donations (flower power) is the way forward. Now and then you have to appease fallen programmers to make progress, but like the photo mode it's mostly unnecessary. The old and broken architecture of the windows OS permeates the whole game. Green hills and old and broken architecture have little personality even if the textures are high definition. The music keeps in the background, not fantastic but nothing bad either.The controls aren't complicated but it really is *badly* communicated that a dash does not move your character in the direction he faces, but the direction the camera faces. I have spend the most time trying to figure out why the stupid fox throws itself down cliffs... reassigning keys/buttons or deactivating the controller rumble is for some reason not possible in 2021. You constantly put down staffs and big the back up after refuelling with flowers because it's the same button.If you like slower, more introspective games and are able to follow a story told by the environment you might like it. I found the first and last chapter to slow for my tastes but for the most part it was enjoyable. If the there was a middle ground between "Do you recommend this game?" I would've picked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a spirit fox simulator in which you do whatever spirit foxes typically do. As a spirit, you are sort of wise, but you are also a fox, so you will spend an indefinite amount of time barking at pieces of stone while trying to figure what to do. To put it in another way, Spirit of the North is like one of those rare poems by amateur poets that do not turn out like complete garbage. You can clearly tell that the guy does not use metrics very well, and a number of things are quite commonplace, but all in all he has written a pretty little thing.To put it in another way yet, Spirit of the North is a puzzle adventure game by a small indie company that specializes in 3D models. I mention the specialization of the company because the 3D art of the game is very well made (a few parts are downright beautiful and inspired), while neither the control system nor the interaction between the character model and the environment are particularly polished. Usually it goes smooth, but some jumps for example can get a bit awkward.Some people have defined this game as a walking simulator, but that may be a relevant description for the initial part of the game at best. The game soon asks you to solve simple puzzles of the type, "find key, open door." Of course, the key is spirit foxness and the door... Well, the door often is an actual (stone) door.Unfortunately, in my opinion, the game works better when the puzzle component is at minimum and the exploration component is at maximum (my favorite chapters probably are the 1st and the 7th). This is both because of the awkward controls and because a fox works better as a fox than as Lara Croft.Puzzles are actually well designed. The game does not like to give you hints on how to procede, and yet you manage to find everything at the very moment you thought you were lost. Puzzles are in fact relatively simple, I was never stuck for longer than... five minutes, I guess, but not so simple that some people will not get stuck. In the middle part of the game, however, they become a bit repetitive, tedious, and a bit frustrating because of that.This game is far from polished and certainly not something that everybody would enjoy. However, if roleplaying a fox in the snow is your thing, you may end up seeing the modest beauty of Spirit of the North.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It baffles me how you can create a game with platforming and terrible controls at the same time. You either go gull walking simulator or put some work so that controls do not feel like a tortureGameplay is very repetitive, bugs are present(like when you pause the game, but the fox continues to swim), and a LOT of repetitive unnecessary animations, that are just wasting your time. Why should I watch TWO animations for spirit refresh?To conclude: do not waste your money and time, there are plenty of games that are better at literally everything

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unbelievably gorgeous and the soundtrack as well. Definitely gave me RIME and Journey vibes. I highly recommend this game if you enjoy those games! My only issue is towards the end in  I got all but 4 achievements in one run, so the achievements aren't too difficult if you care about those. I will say however, that controls CAN be clunky or weird at times and the geometry gets funky (but in most cases I actually used that to my advantage).There were a few bugs with controls, but the biggest one is if you tab out in the intro sequence, you won't be able to control the fox. _childDocuments_.review: Listen the physics are a little weird sometimes, but no worse than any of the assassins creed earlier games. _childDocuments_.review: Maybe a bit biased because I'm a sucker for animal games, but this game was a really pleasant experience. The puzzles were normally somewhere between easy and average levels of challenging, its the sorta game that you can get through quickly if you want - but would take a bit of time to 100% it. I adore how the landscape around you looks, and all of the scenes you explore. In fact screenshots from this game are now my wallpaper.Overall, I’d recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is as i know the first Game from Infuse Studio & Walking Simulator with PuzzlesYou are a lonely Fox in a strange World with some Parts attacked by an evil Aura. The Start through an Ice Field is not really interesting. Than you get in different Areas of the World where you need finish some small Riddles with a few Abilities, that even for casual Gamers should be to hard to figure out, if you explore well enough, but some Riddles are really fine.For others who want a Challenge they can search for 28 Sticks & the Shaman Spirits, some are really well Hidden & after that you can find them again in the Spirit Worlds, where are some well hidden again, too.+++ good Atmosphere alone in an Lost World (no other Land Animals)+++ easy 100 % Steam Achievements++ Graphics are fine for the Price (watch Trailer)++ Sound too (watch Trailer)++ 6 Trading Cards (Five would be better, some nice Point Store Items)++ some Riddles & some optional 28 Spirit Search++ Chapter Select where you see how many/ which missing Shaman Spirit+ Story complete without Words, only with the strange Ending-- short Game if you rush through-- no Map you dont know where you can Jump/ Go & where not, need to test it- 28 Spirits Spirt World to find (U dont know how many u have & that u have, They should Shine in a White LIght if found, so u know which missing)-slow Begin (big Snow Area maybe complete empty, dont even explore maybe)- no Steam Cloud (new Pc, Save File Corrupted) if u are far with 28 Spirits it could be very disappointing- Price (maybe buy it with 50 % Discount & play 100 %= 7,50 Euros for 7 HoursAfter the Reference Lost Ember i didnt had to much high Expectations, but for this Price its okay with Steam Achievement & Trading Cards (7-8 Hours 15 Euros, Lost Ember 7 Hours 30 Euros) surely 2 different Animal Story Walking Simulators.Thx 4 reading. Hope you enjoy like me did. GL HF <3
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for another game that gave me the same feels as "Lost Ember" and I got to say, it came pretty darn close. "Lost Ember" was less frustrating. This game has a great story to tell, especially at the end game. It is a slow burn, mostly because the platform puzzles can be aggravating, not particularly hard just unnecessarily tedious. patient is a must but worth it in the end. I would most definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a heart felt, somber style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant journey through a Nordic-inspired world. The game's minimalist design and captivating soundtrack create a truly immersive experience that transports players to a serene and mystical realm. The beautiful landscapes, from snow-capped mountains to ancient ruins, are a feast for the eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, short, and beautiful game where you play as a fox. What more could you want?! Some general thoughts (soft spoilers ahead). Positives: (1) the graphics are absolutely gorgeous and on the whole I had no issues with the controls or mechanics; (2) in general I really liked the puzzles & thought they were an appropriate difficulty level for the style of game and made good use of the abilities; (3) the shaman element lends an bit of re-playablity that otherwise would be lowNegatives: (1) I did hit a couple of glitches which made the puzzles more difficult but overall didn't have major issues; (2) honestly, the final chapter almost ruined the ending experience for me, I spent so long wandering in the woods trying to find the right place to go (even following the lights) when I just wanted to wrap up the story; (3) very minor, but I could not find a way to turn off/down the controller rumble in game which was very frustrating in one chapter in particular.Overall, I would recommend getting it and giving it a play through... but maybe wait till it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it was a good experience. at times controls made me slightly mad, the music was nice but I wish at times it sounded more natural, of course its not easy to have a real orchestra playing the soundtrack for a game like this, but there are  much better sounding orchestral plugins. Most of the time it sounded totally fine but on certain parts you could clearly hear the "cheap synthesizer"  kind of instruments, for me personal that really killed the immersion.  More variation of the soundtrack would also be an upgrade, as the tacks are rather short and sound like  short repeating loops very much, that kind of strains your ears at some point hearing it over and over again.  The art style is really nice  and the landscapes are gorgeous. Very excited for part2 but PLEASE up the Music quality for that one ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on a big sale 90% off, I think the game is worth the full price, but seeing how often it goes on a sale I say wait for one. This game is good, but it’s not amazing, it doesn’t do anything particularly well, and it is not well polished, but it is a chill game. Spirit of the North is a nice small indie game, that has a lot of potential, that it didn’t fully reach. But it tells a nice story and takes you on a journey; you get to play as a cute fluffy fox :3 I say it’s very mid at 6/10, but a lot of people loves this game and I can absolutely see why. The atmosphere is captivating, and the environment is equally as stunning, and the soundtrack is beautiful. The jumping is sadly junk, and weird hitboxes are everywhere. I got pushed of platforms, or could jump up many times. This breaks the immersion and can lead to very frustrating moment. The level can be disorienting and you can get lost easily. This game needed more polish and it is very clear while playing. The biggest minus is that you  The game doesn’t save at all in chapters; only at the beginning of one. if you experience a game breaking bug, or just don’t have time to finish the chapter too bad you need to start from the beginning. This would have been an absolute deal breaker for me, I wanted to enjoy the game on the big screen with hight settings, and I just don’t have the time to sit for 40 min uninterrupted, the levels can get boring or confusing and I like to take frequent breaks. Luckily, I have a steam deck, where the game looks much blurrier but it runs well; I can just put the deck into a sleep mode and come back later. Not ideal, in chapter saving should be a thing and it makes 0 sense why this wasn’t implemented. It LITTERALYY SAY SAVING when you walk through a checkpoint. Don’t even get me how annoying is it to greet all the spirits in the spirit world. I don’t understand how somebody finished it without a guide. The spirit world as a whole doesn’t work so well and is confusing.  Spirit of the North is not a game for someone who gets frustrated easily. It is a good, small, not well polished indie game, that is worth the try. I enjoyed myself, apart from the frustration. The soundtrack and atmosphere carried the game all the way through and I’m excited for the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally like puzzle games, but Spirit of the North is one of my all-time favourites. The atmosphere of the game is incredible - it's visually stunning, the soundtrack fits perfectly and I really enjoyed the subtle but complex storytelling. It definitely suits the simpler gameplay, which I found relaxing but still interesting enough to keep me invested. It's definitely one of those games where you need to stop and look at stuff, both to uncover hidden clues and to appreciate how pretty everything is! Plus, foxes are cute :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is about the journey of a fox that stumbles upon a female spirit that is the guardian of the northern lights. A red plague corrupted the land causing destruction of the Shamans who used to worship this spirit and her own withdrawal. It's up to the player to stop the plague from spreading further and bring the Aurora back.One thing out of the way: The landscapes and areas the game presents to you are gorgeous. The levels are wise and big with collectibles and neat little puzzles. As a reward for the collectibles, you get different fur skins to customize your fox. It's certainly a pretty and relaxing game but I think the platforming could've been handled better as some areas were kind of a pain to deal with. The fox barking like a chihuahua is a bit off-putting and there are some issues with the physics but I don't want to nit-pick too much because for a game that was developed by only two people, it's really well-made.I advice everyone to not focus on the achievements too much as it would only ruin your first playthrough. This game is meant to be played at a slow pace without having to worry about anything so fretting over collectibles just robs from the experience Overall, I'd recommend this game for anyone that is searching for a relaxing experience which is not too challenging nor too sluggish.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game whose soundtrack especially really shines. The environment at times feels a bit same-y but it's still a beautiful environment and it really makes you feel the desolate landscape that is Iceland.The story is very abstract (at least to me!) but I still enjoyed it for what it was, and the puzzles were sometimes a bit challenging, but the game still was so enjoyable and lovely to play. It's one of those games in the spirit of Abzu and Journey that set out to tell a story through the environment, and though it's not a story I personally was too invested in, it was still such a lovely game.Is it worth the 17 euro price tag? Honestly - sure! If you enjoy games like Journey and Abzu you will like this game, too, and knowing we support the devs with the price tag I honestly don't mind it!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game was a beautiful one. I love the indie games that tell a story without dialogue. This had such a deep meaning. A bit heartbreaking when thought about to deeply. The game wasn't super smooth in animations and mechanics, but I still enjoyed it as a relaxing game, nonetheless. Not a difficult one at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's just beautiful. Everything from the music, character 'voices', story line and the richly detailed surroundings you get to explore. An escape from reality into another sacred world. I smiled, cried and barked my way through. Yes- having to swim slowly and repeat obstacles can be annoying at times but there's also a blissfulness in the gameplay. Would highly recommend for adults and children however younger kids might need some assistance with a few of the puzzles. All chapters are replayable and easy to access through the main menu. If you're looking for a fairly relaxing escape over a weekend- this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a short well now since I finished this game and completed all the achievements, but it still lives rent free in my head. This game is my favourite example of something that both looks and feels like a 'cosy' game, but handles so much more than that. It's challenging in all the right ways without being frustrating while also being calming - a game you can let yourself get absorbed into for hours at a time and just... be a fox. There's something really charming about games where you play as an animal, and this one does it well. Combined with the lack of dialogue and yet a story still told so well. This is up really high on my list of 'niche' game faves! Very much looking forward to the second one! ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Has NO option to turn off gamepad vibration, even when you're playing the game without using one. The options to fix it are: A) unplug your controller (which is silly, I don't want to root around the back of PC for a single game)  B) install Special K, a PC game options injector, which can disable controller rumble for a game externally. Even the Steam native settings don't help with this, despite having the option, it just doesn't work for this game. Special K works wonders.

_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty and the music is pretty. I tend to like games like this, but the game seriously makes me wanna take a nap. There's a part near the beginning where your fox gets injured and he has to limp somewhere to get healed. That part is SUPER slow and the time should have been cut in half for how long you had to walk to get to your objective. Also it's hard to figure out where to go next after an objective is completed. Easy to get lost if you're not paying attention, and I was paying attention lol. I want to like it, but I recommend Journey instead!

_childDocuments_.review: a visually stunning and relaxing game. the music is beautiful too. it might get repetitive for some, but i think the point is that this game is to be enjoyed after a long day of work to wind down, not to use up a lot of brain power. (although some mechanics did make me sit and think for a while)i did get stuck once due to a glitch, and there was no way for me to get out without force quitting the game and losing all that chapter's progress ;/aside from that though, i really enjoyed running around as a little fox and the ending made me sob so 10/10 recommend :]
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little platformer: The mechanics are diverse enough not to feel overused. Traversable paths are distinct from scenery witout being too easy.  There are collectables that often require a but more practice and patience. What stands out are the visuals and the story that made even confused wandering enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:- Checkpoint save system has much to be desired- Short length- character movement isn't always smooth when trying to climb- Game leaves you wanting more to do- You can't jump through your screen to live in the beauty of the gamePros:- Gorgeous atmosphere, leaves you wanting to visit Iceland and Europe- Solid soundtrack- No dialogue and no pressure- good/fun puzzles- little to no bug/glitch problems- plot is what you make of it Is it perfect? No. Is it awesome for what it is? YES! Worth getting on sale, but I am left wanting to support the developers for this glorious piece of playable art. Would love to see a sequel or some DLC's. Or another game like this, but longer and more to do. But as a chill non combat game for all ages, Spirit of the North is a no regrets purchase for me. For those looking to escape for a while, I highly recommend picking this one up. It is also available for Switch and PS4/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, another fox game, how original... With that being said, I don't have much to say. It's plain, it's boring, it's repetitive. The world is void of any life or interactability and is therefore not worth exploring (unless you want to collect all the shamans). The story is about as generic as you can imagine.There are abilities you acquire over the course of time, nothing special. However, that's probably the best part of the entire game, as you can dash through the map faster. It sucks how you recharge them, though, it would be better if the bar filled up automatically and you didn't have to search for blue flowers that are usually close by anyway; it just makes the game all that more repetitive.It doesn't help the game is rather short, clocking in at about 5 hours with a bit of exploration.
