_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Tunic does this game better; you play as an animal and have to use context clues to understand what is going on. Though, the story isn't exactly deep or emotional here. The visuals are generic and don't impress me. Weird how the fox model doesn't dynamically adjust its limbs based on the terrain, so it just floats above it if the surface is steep enough. Some of the rocks are hexagonal, which looked strange. Maybe this is implying they are man-sculpted. Sloppy terrain design; numerous floating trees or clipping pieces of terrain. Puzzles are both too easy and unintuitive because things aren't clearly explained. The stone-bearing sigils that you need to progress often blend into the terrain. The platforming is awful and clunky. I'd be more in favor of a cartoony game like this rather than a realistic one. Also, why do we have to make the story about people? And about people that no longer exist, at that. So boring. I hoped it was going to be an animal-focused adventure, with no people, which is an unexploited niche. The ending is alright. The final level is unintuitive. Let's hope that the sequel is better. 4/10 on the enjoyment scale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This concept was really nice, I enjoyed being a fox and seeing all the pretty sights the game had to offer. That was probably the only thing I liked about this game. Whilst I enjoy a good puzzle, I consider myself to be decent at them, where I can usually do them with no issue. However, this game made me so frustrated with all of their puzzles, it sucked all the fun out of the game for me. Every few feet you take, there's always some kind of puzzle, they expect you to figure out right off the bat on what you're supposed to do, when it doesn't appear that obvious, I wondered around at least 10-15 minutes trying to figure out what I had to do, before I gave up and looked at a video on how to do it. All of the puzzles, I had to use a video to help solve it for me, as I couldn't for the life of me figure it out. Even the person in the videos looked just as confused as I was. Or, if I was close to figuring it out, it ended up being backwards on me, and I had to do it all over again, often times resetting my game to try again. There are spirits you're supposed to release along the way, although, I had no clue where some of them were, even after just wondering around all the time to try to figure out where either I needed to go, or how to do the puzzle. I would look in every nook and crack there was to try to find the spirit to release, but when I go onto the next area, and found another one, it would say I missed it, which I wouldn't have any idea where it would've been! I played through the whole game, as I was hopeful it would've gotten better, but it just got worse, and there were times where I was close to uninstalling it because of the frustration I felt with the puzzles, it destroyed the fun out of this game for me. Good graphics, decent music, but real crappy game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a greatly lovable game. I personally love the feel of everything within it, and it's very calming to play but filled with adventure. I also like the fact that you really have to think about what to do or where to do. The point is I love this game with all my heart, and I will finish it multiple times before I move on from it. I thank the developers!(Also, I just had to add that the fox(s) are adorable. So cute I had to name them "Flying Squirrel" ᓚᘏᗢ ♥)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Underdeveloped, works maybe as a showcase for an idea or a concept. Has technical issues, bad autosave system that forces you to restart the whole chapter, losing a lot of progress. Music is repetitive and becomes annoying soon. Spirit of the north is slow paced, which is usually fine by me but in this instance the slowness is artifically generated by making your fox hobble through a tedious maze or swim through a cave system which is just as slow. The controls are clunky as hell and overall the game is not fun to play, perhaps unless you are really into foxes IDK... Returned, awaiting refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Good:Controls are pretty good.Graphics are good.Bad:World design is terrible, very dead and artificial.Story is very bland and the way they tell the main portion of the story in the beginning is painfully slow and annoying.Music is as good as muted, serves no purpose.Running is unlocked in the story, even though you travel alot before unlocking it so you spend a long time jumping to move that little bit faster.The "energy" you use to solve the puzzles can be replenished endlessly at certain points, and they are EVERYWHERE, so the puzzles are not that good.Framerate is not very good especially when moving fast.You move very slow in water this is annoying considering how much water seems to exist in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy little game that was perfect to chill with. I had a cup of tea and 100% the game within two days of gameplay. I purchased this game on a 90% steam sale, so I only paid about $3 for it in total. The most difficult achievements are the kindered spirits and the flying squirrel in my opinion, but there are plenty of guides online . My biggest downside to this game is there is no actual story and narrator, you have to put it all together yourself. Which many people can find off putting, especially for a $20 full price game. I highly suggest buying it on sale to get the best bang for your buck. Sit back, enjoy, and fox your way through puzzles, a beautiful game, and a stunning soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Game was cute, and the levels were pretty. Overall the game was good enough for the sale price tag and the one session of content it provided.Only complaints are about the overall level/puzzle design. Most puzzles were only drawn out/difficult due to the size of the working area to find all the pieces(something often tucked away in a passage that was easy to miss). The levels, especially the area with the large castle/building and red snow falling were a bit too large for what there was to do. Spent a lot of time running around to places I had no need of ever going. If there is ever a new iteration of this game/a sequel/game of same concept I would recommend tighter level design and more focus on adding depth to the puzzle aspect of the game. A small workspace with an engaging puzzle is always going to be much better than a giant one with very little "puzzle solving" to do. If you liked Stray, this game itches that a little bit, but Stray is definitely far and above in terms of content and narrative, the trailer definitely makes it look like there is more going on here than there is. That all said, still enjoyed the game and would love to see the developers work on another one in this genre, as the foundation is there and just needs to be fleshed out.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to sit back and unwind (if you're not in a hurry to get all the spirit related achievements). Imo lacks a bit of polish esp. cutscenes and transition between scenes but damn the scenery is beautiful! Must be all those Quixel megascans =). A bit monotonous tho, some mountain flowers wouldn't hurt.  Fox go bork-bork! I wish foxxy was making other noises, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game. I honestly did. The graphics are beautiful, the animations on the fox are great. The music and atmosphere and environmental storytelling is great. But the main gameplay element of the game, jumping puzzles, are just way too janky to be fun. The jump mechanic is infuriating to begin with. You cannot make the smallest of jumps because without a good amount of forward momentum, all your fox does is hop in place. Aiming your jumps is very difficult, so is timing. Be prepared to spend hours trying and retrying the simplest of hops because the game decides you're a pixel short, or your fox decides all it wants to do is somersaults. Also, you can't save except at sparse autosave points, so be prepared to do it all over again when you inevitably rage quit.I got into this game and loved everything about it, but it turns into a rage game so fast I can't enjoy the beauty of it anymore. With a little bit smoother movement mechanics it would be a fantastic game, but unless you're a masochist gamer it just isn't fun past the first two chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game that was easy to follow in the beginning but the controlling mechanics for some of the puzzles leaves you frustrated for the most part. I don't understand what the storyline is about. It is a pretty looking game. It would be easier if the directionals were either for just the mouse only or just the keyboard only. The combination of the two really only works for combat games, not a puzzle game. As are all puzzle games, trying to figure it out is the whole basis. I like a little bit more straight forwardness so that it feels more comfortable to solving the puzzles and not just "are you effing kidding me?" kind of aftertaste. Didn't get very far because the geysers threw me off course when trying to aim for a certain direction. Not bad of a game, though. Could use a little bit more work.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Never felt so free . Never felt so happy, curious and sad within just a few minutes .And for the very first time I can say I got involved in the story .The way the story is told and how deep it reaches me really amazed me . (happy again)This is game is very unique and it for sure it earned a little spot in my heart .Amazing Work !
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I usually write joke reviews but this game deserves a sincere one.This game is one of the only ones that actually awestruck me. The idea behind the game is a unique one and is rarely seen done well. The beauty of the game along with the well composed music set the mood for every single chapter. Throughout the game, the different challenges and puzzles will keep you thinking. If you were to 100% the game, it would take around 5-7 hours. It is a pretty short game, but it is worth the money.Although the game lacks consistency in the parkour aspect, the other aspects of the game outweigh it for sure. 9.8/10Would adventure with a spirit fox to the Icelandic mountains again
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a fox and you can bark, that's all that needs to be said.Honestly tho, i wish it had some objectives or gave you clearer directions at times, because i got easily lost in some chapters. That aside, it starts off a bit slow but it's a nice game overall. Very casual and simple, but that's what you need sometimes :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect game to chill on lazy evenings. Despite encountering invisible walls it tempts with beautiful views and the illusion of freedom. New mechanics appear at the point, although they do not go beyond the genre classics. A very pleasant solution is the introduction of segmentation, which allows you to go back to a stage and complete the tasks missing from the achievement. A short interactive story. Plus, you get to be a fox.- Don't worry about achievements, play the game, enjoy the sights and when you're done, come back to get the missing ones for the given stages.- Use the twisted paw episode to earn the best friends achievement. (Just keep pressing the left mouse button along the way).- Fox? Or Flying Squirrel? can be achieved by constantly hopping into a single portal.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful looking game and the accompanying soundtrack really sets the scene for an incredible journey, the puzzles were satisfying enough and aren't too difficult to solve.I would say the only major downside for this game is there is some platforming and this games physics in regards to platforming is way too janky, which made any sections with it very frustrating.Overall very enjoyable game with some slight jank.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's time to write a review of this adorable game.I've played for a long time and I never got bored of this game. It's so atmospheric! Beautiful landscapes, relaxing music and intriguing story. Someone can say that plot's very simple, but I disagree. It's really mesmerizing and you immerse yourself in story. Inspiring atmosphere won't leave somebody indifferent! This game will forever remain in my heart and I think that I'll play it many time again and again) Many thanks to developers of this fantastic game. You're the masters of inspiring atmosphere!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game of exploration with great visuals and sound! Overall it was linear with puzzles to solve along the way. Towards the end I got turned around once causing me an extra 30m of circling but it wasn't a "waste" as I was able to see even more of the landscapes. Parts of the story I feel is open to your own interpretation which could be good or bad for some but I enjoyed how it left it open for me to decide/hope.Ever since playing Aer Memories of Old I'm really enjoying these shorter non-combat puzzle/story games.With Steam sales I'd recommend picking this one up for a handful of hours to put in.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best game experiences I've ever had. The gameplay, the ambience (!), the overall feeling. Everything about this game is just wonderful!Though it is clearly dedicated to those who seek the experience, not the challenge. This is at least the impression I got. The experience of the game comes from exploring, solving riddles and letting the atmosphere of the game itself flow through you. And I seriously mean that. The surroundings you can explore within the game are just breathtaking. Which is ironic since normally you'd take many deep breaths in those surroundings because you can physically see how fresh the air must be there. You can also make the game to a challenge by hunting collectibles and archivements as major priority. But I really do not recommend that because you then tend to lose track of the wholesomeness of the game. At one point I was tempted to just hunt down all the collectibles as fast as I could, searched every corner and half an hour later I realized that I completely forgot to also savor the moment and atmosphere that I was in. I regretted this so much that I restarted the chapter I was playing. And it was worth it. Because this game is about the experience. You can seek challenge elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I've only got 2 hours in so far and it's a bit different from the stuff I usually play, but I'll strongly recommend it at this point. The landscape visuals are beautiful, the music is great, and I like how there's no tutorial and you just kind of have to figure it out. The fox is also frickin' adorable.  It doggy-paddles in the water, shakes itself dry, AND you can wag it's tail (that does seem to have a mechanical use in dark areas).  I'll admit I teared up a little at the end of the prologue after it had been whimsically following the spirit fox and sliding around on ice and playing in the hot springs. Based on the store page thumbnails, it might get a little darker later on, but I'm enjoying it as an atypical game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a fox on a journey going from snowy mountains to various other scenic spots along the way. It is a very serene game and relaxing as well, taking in all the beauty this game has to offer. Along the way you can earn various colours for your wolf should you be able to find staffs and re-unite them with the the remains of skeletal shamans that once lived. Still playing this game but enjoying the breath taking visuals and sometimes going off the main path to see what else i may discover, even though its linear game, i still like to explore as much of the caves or ruins etc, whatever place i'm in next. I'd rate this game a solid 7/10 :D
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a very simple walking simulator with levels made out of short puzzles.There are many invisible walls and the collision is messed up making some puzzles feel forced (for example you can't take an alternative route that seems possible) and the collectible puzzles (find the staff and bring it back to the shamans) sometimes become impossible because you left the staff in a place where it falls in the ground making it impossible to reach.Another missed opportunity is that the maps are huge but somewhat empty making it annoying and somewhat boring to complete all the collectibles (thankfully the staff starts to shine the moment you're close to the shaman!)The graphic is the main selling point of this game. It is simply stunning.The game is not replayable since the levels are always the same.Overall it is an ok game that needs some price adjustment (would never pay 16 € for this) but I wouldn't suggest it to any friend considering most people grew up with much harder puzzle/platformer games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings about this game.I don't regret buying and playing it, but it definitely could have been  . . .  better. It has a great concept, wonderful looks and a good length.Unfortunately, it lacks some sort of guidance, creating boring and - most negatively - frustrating experiences.I love to play as a fox, but the fox character in this game is replaceable. It has no fox-specific characteristics, movement or attributes, that are essential part of the game. It could as well have been a human or any other character you can think of.Overall, this game feels like a missed opportunity for a great game to remember.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. A couple of floating rocks and the occasional strange camera movement did nothing to take away from the experience I had with the game. It's so nice to have games like this that let you just explore around listening to the amazing music. In other words, nice and relaxing. Totally recommend this game, especially as a pallet cleanser from social media. Looking forward to the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute fox puzzle game! While the puzzles are overall fairly simplistic, the game itself has charming visuals, a nice soundtrack, and a story that's interesting enough you want to follow it along to see what'll happen next.While it is a little rough in some places it's overall a fun experience I'd recommend for anyone who wants to spend an afternoon or two as a fox spirit.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game for everyone. The story is simple and barely present, puzzles and platforming are easy and the game overall lacks any challenge. Gameplay is quite short - finished the game in 5 hours with most of the achievments complete. You will spend most of the time looking for stuff in huge open areas. And it is fine that way. Because it allows you to focus on the gorgeous scenery and nice music. Avoid this game if you are impatient or not in a mood for relaxing chill experience.I've seen few people complaining about controls in reviews, but personaly I have not found any issue using a controller. It is a little bit floaty, but nothing out of ordinary. Found maybe one or two weird jumps but thats it. I would absolutely recommend this to anyone, who just wants to turn off and have a good time for few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: "Spirit of the North" is a chill adventure game with nice visuals and a good instrumental soundtrack that was a fairly quick game without feeling rushed or lacking. I appreciated that there was visual storytelling through wall art or the extras without it being integral that you find every single detail as you play. This, combined with the simple puzzles, makes this game a nice option for a game to play to relax or unwind. Only issue (and it is just me nitpicking) is that the fox barks instead of making typical fox noises. Still cute overall, and I enjoyed all of the little touches with landscape features you would see in Iceland, movements that mimic a fox's natural movements, and the interactions between the spirit and the fox. Looking forward to playing "Spirit of the North 2"!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Most aggravating game I have ever played--polar opposite of what I was looking for from an adventure game. Great story line, beautiful world concept art, But the controls are TOTAL ♥♥♥♥. The fox character cannot be reliably moved and so though you know what to do and where to go you're spending HOURS trying to make simple moves. Horrible, just horrible. Also, so much work went into attention to detail, but with total overkill at the expense of basic game functionality. The fox shakes EVERY TIME it gets out of the water (which you fall into due to lack of control all the time), meanwhile you cannot aim where you're jumping. How did this pass basic game testing / quality assurance?
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a wonderful experience. Taking place in a beautiful world with a story that unfolds with each chapter. The music is incredible and really helps captivate you and adds to the story being told. There is a nice little bit of puzzle solving, but nothing too difficult that will take you out of the experience.In the end, the journey and story being told were the best parts for me.Also, I absolutely love foxes, which added to the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack, great graphics, and easy gameplay for the most part. There is no dialogue at all, no subtitles, just a fox making various emotions and gestures that you watch for. As for the story, I really don't know how to explain, but its a curious fox that ventures around the (north?) pole and sees a spirit. It's a PVE platform game, where you roam around finding clues to get to the next area. The game is divided in chapters, which you can repeat anytime to find any missing collectibles you missed before. I bought this when there was a 50% discount, but I think its a fair price. The game was completed in 8 hours with 100% while using a guide to complete 2 achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:- really nice scenery- background music is mostly relaxing- great for playing occassionallyCon:- Controls. I often had it, that I wanted to go into one direction and jump, and suddenly the character jumps into another direction.- Collision detection isn't a thing... or it is. My character often was stopped from corners while I couldn't see anything stopping me. On the other hand if you're carrying around a Staff in your maw, the staff will completely ignore the surroundings.- No explanation about the story. After five hours I'm through the game and don't know anything about why the world is empty, why there is a fox spirit or anything. You find some murals, but I couldn't figure out at all whats happening.- Staffs. In the first five chapters you can ignore them. Suddenly in the last three chapters you MUST find them to progress through the level! Of course the game doesn't tell you this.- Mage spirits. You can "revive" them with the Staffs you can find. But they don't say anything, not giving clues about the world.- Rewards. You can unlock other skins, but ONLY by finding enough Staffs and reviving enough Mages with them. I finished the game with 20 of 24 achievements done, and got... NOTHING, because at some point I just didn't care about the staffs anymore. The game doesn't tell you, you need Staffs for unlocking rewards. In the end I had around half of the mages done, didn't got a single skin for it.Summary:The game isn't really rewarding anything. It's nice for playing then and when if you need something more relaxing. Wouldn't recommend getting it for the full price (especially on consoles, as the prices are twice as high there!)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game. It's visually stunning and the music in the game is very relaxing. Even though there isn't any dialogue in the game it is still fun to play and there is a story line too it. A fairly short game but I didn't mind that. The ending is sweet. Only downside is the game can glitch every now and then or the mechanics are a little clunky. But overall an enjoyable and easy game to play
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: As a lonely fox we travel through a world affected by a disaster and filled only with a remnants of civilization. Our only companion is a spirit fox, guardian of the Northern lights, who is now leading us deep inland, where we will find the source of the cataclysm. Even though there is no imminent danger the journey isn't going to be easy. Luckily our guardian spirit will help us to overcome many obstacles standing in our way. is a fox walking simulator with an occasional platforming. The game is pretty much linear and even though you can "explore" and run freely around, there is still only one route for you to go and only one way to solve the "puzzles". The puzzles consist mostly of you harvesting energy from flowers, reaching some unreachable place and powering up a mural, door or some secret stone to be able to progress further. With new abilities new kinds of puzzles await you, so you can properly enjoy them. ;)Solving the puzzles wasn't difficult, just sometimes hitting the right timing or angle was a challenge. Failing could led to a slight frustration of redoing the cursed section… and it was usually caused by platforming sequences, but I got truly stuck only three times, so it wasn't any horrible experience.On your journey you can find old staves laying forgotten in the ruins, you can then take them to long dead shamans and set their souls free with it (you have to find them first though and some of them are hidden pretty well, but at least as you get closer the staff will light up). You get rewarded for your hard work with skins for your fox! You can then change your appearance to your liking. (The way to change your skin was rather confusing for me - when you save enough shamans flashing "P" appears on the screen. It leads to options and there are hidden rewards,  that's it, I have completely missed that two times. ^^)I really liked the colorful graphics and music, both created a great relaxing mood. The fox is very pretty with cute sounds. I enjoyed how he jumped around or moved in the water. The little details - how he dried off when getting out of water, slow motion - was also rather nice. Game saves only on checkpoints, but you can access that checkpoint anytime from the menu. Like this you can replay only a part of a certain level and don't need to do it whole again. Also you can see where you missed a shaman, which can save you some time.The game isn't of course perfect. When leaving water after a long time he will dry off in a locked sequence when you can't do anything. If you are stuck in the platforming part around water it can be tedious. Not even mentioning that the fox wouldn't be able to take out the staff from rooms or caves the way he does it. ;) The world is bare without much to explore (yeah, I know that it was devastated). But I wasn't disappointed, I have actually enjoyed this calm journey. Story is hidden in the ruins, in the old bones scattered around. Even without words I was filled with emotions. As a side note, I would like to pinpoint another game with a similar setting, . I have really enjoyed it, if you would like you can read more in . The sounds our guardian spirit makes reminded my so much of my Lumini. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea what to expect about this game, and started playing it after finishing another that left me feeling the "blah's". I really could not have chosen a better game to re-ignite my gaming passion. This is a very chill, beautifully designed game with truly awe-inspiring visuals in nature. You get to play as a fox that grows and develops as the story unfolds. I found the story to be a bit sad but I think there's a lot of room for interpretation while you go along the fox's journey. The Chapters play as stories as well, with no audio beyond the music (but the music is AMAZING). I found myself liking this game more and more as the story unfolded.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughout completing the game... I can simply say, it took me on another journey. The exploration in my eyes was on another level for what it entailed/was, the music felt right and was beautiful. The ending touched me the most, and the more I played through it, the more I got an understanding for the game and what it was about. It requires that due to the intentional dialogue being non existent which makes it interesting, and you focus more on the environment. If you are thinking about getting this for yourself, then I recommend. It's a very chilled out kind of game. Recommended for fox lovers too ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a bit buggy with the physics sometimes, this game was a BEAUTIFUL experience with stunning landscapes to explore, good OST and chill vibes. It truly gives that sense of melancholy and longing for something that has been lost long ago and also makes you realize the insignificance of man against the vastness of the world.Regarding the level design, I think it's a bit flawed since sometimes the environment/narrative doesn't communicate well enough what the game expects you to do. For example, it's really easy to get lost in the last chapter, I would have loved to see more path indicators there, spent too much time running around without really knowing what I had to look for.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand it looks gorgeous, but when you pay attention to detail you realize the graphics are not that hot. Or maybe I was too annoyed at the clunky controls and camera movements to really appreciate it, but it gave me the impression the fox was walking on air rather than on whatever terrain he was on half the time. I was really looking forward to it but it's a pass for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous visuals, cute protagonist, incredibly frustrating and nonsensical physics. Like... The only reason you can make (or not) the same jump before and after completing the puzzle is because the game *lets you* after you complete it. If you like to walk around and explore stuff, this is not the game for you.Also, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ geysers man, how the ♥♥♥♥ are you supposed to maneouver in them, jfc. It got so bad that I just realized I'm not enjoying this game, despite its beautiful atmosphere, graphics and music - so I stopped playing lmao.. The gameplay itself can really make or break a game3/10, unfortunately the scenery does not make up for the extremely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ physics
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: When you pause the game, it continues running behind the menu. It can do that because nothing is going to happen which for me is an enormous source of relief. I think the trailer implies more action or story than there actually is as most of the time you're just a fox doing fox things. So when you pause, your fox will probably just curl into a ball and nap.I think the world is more detailed than the vast nothingness of  and frankly the storytelling (or lack thereof) is  better too. Apparently there is a hinting system to direct you generally where to go, but I didn't learn about that until after I finished the game which certainly I would recommend to patient players.There is no narration (and thus no subtitles) and all non-musical audio cues are visually identified. I don't know if the developers were going for a accessible game or not with their audio, but they did it!Except for some minor grievances,  is nearly perfect. 9.5/10 and in 2020 it felt like it was worth $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:Solid gameplay with great atmosphere. There are cure moments like getting the spirit bark in reply which I did about once every minute... It's fun to explore the levels with the beautiful landscape or scenery.Cons:Not exactly a walking  - or running - simulator, but if you expect a lot of action or intricate puzzle solving, you'll be disappointed.Conclusion:Get the game if you like animals, beautiful landscapes, slow-paced and relaxing gameplay. Don't get it if you're looking for puzzles or action. And if you play it - continue at least through chapter 2, the first chapter is not like the rest of the game.My main issue with the game is that the two weakest levels are the first and the last. And that's a problem. The first level almost caused me to abandon the game and only by reading some more reviews I found out there actually happens something later on. And I don't think I'm the only one. If you check how many players got past the first achievement, it's few, less than 30%. I assume the first level put them off. Which is a shame because it gets much better.And then the last level - some minor spoilers ahead - it felt rushed, like they designed a level and then didn't really think how to best use it. It's suddenly very open-wordly which doesn't work well for this game. I felt a bit lost. And why do you have to run on that path for what felt like 5 mins? It kills the atmosphere. The whole last level took me away from the end of chapter 6 which was powerful. But I forgot all about it because of the tediousness of chapter 7. If they had cut that last level to about 20% of the current size and made it a bit more straightforward it would have been great.And so, while the mediocre first level prevents players from actually playing the game, the mediocre last level makes you forget, to some extent, how great the rest of the game had been.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: the developer has responded to this review regarding "fox barks". While foxes do indeed have a "bark", it is nothing like you would imagine a regular dog bark would be. Please go ahead and youtube fox barks. The vocalizations of the fox in the game are straight up dog barks. I was excited for this game. A fox puzzle/adventure game? Atmospheric? Gorgeous? Yup.The only thing is: the fox "bark" sounds like dog_bark.mp3. I thought I would be able to get past it but when the fox meets his spirit companion it sounds like two chihuahuas met at a dog park. I wasn't expecting the most polished product for an indie puzzle/adventure game but the least I expected was to get the main characters sound right when the game is so focused on creating an atmospheric and immersive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game; it's gorgeous and has an interesting premise, but overall I feel like the game could have used more polish. The controls don't feel fluid and the fox will often continue moving on his own, with no input from you (which can make the geyser platforming incredibly frustrating). There are invisible walls everywhere, which normally is fine, but they don't play well with the controls. You could hit an invisible wall and then the game immediately makes the fox run off in a different direction (another case of the fox moving on his own), which could end up making you fall off whatever cliff you just spent 10 minutes climbing. And half the time you're wondering if you're actually able to climb up that area or not because the jumping in general just does not work and the invisible walls make it worse.The fox also gets Stuck.On.Everything. He must have a huge hitbox, because I was having to give random rocks and boulders a wide berth cuz otherwise I'd get stuck on them. And when there are multiple parts of the game that are on timers, this becomes very annoying. This also ties in to the wonky jumping that the fox does; is the fox just getting stuck on rocks during the jump and it actually IS somewhere you need to go, or is there an invisible wall there and you should just ignore that area? Naturally, this made exploring a hassle, instead of a joy, like it should have been. Even if you try to jump over every obstacle in your path in order to not lose any speed, the fox still somehow gets tangled on it and everything comes to a standstill. Why can't I jump over a couple of small rocks?? Why does he come to a complete halt and then seems to tip-toe jump over the rock/debris before continuing on?Also, why are the maps so insanely large? You could run an entire map of ARK inside these levels, and yet the story generally has you going in a linear path. If you want to find the 1 collectable the game offers, though, then you need to explore at least a little bit, and the huge maps and control issues ruin the fun of finding these things. I do love the fact that you can unlock different fox skins if you find enough collectables though; it was nice to see some variation.I also would have liked some clearer directions/hints as to what the game wanted you to do. There were times where I completely misunderstood the visual cues and spent waayy too long running around in circles and not making any progress. That may have just been a me thing, though, as I did eventually figure it out on my own, so take that with a grain of salt.There is also very little story involved, and what snippets of story there were, were confusing. I'm still not entirely sure what happened in the game but its open to interpretation, so this really wasn't much of a drawback in the end. But mixed with the other issues the game has, the overall experience just left me feeling underwhelmed.:There's a lot that the game does right (visuals, ambience, music/sound effects, immersion) but I feel that the negatives far outweigh these positives. Might be okay at a sale price. And I can't even call it a chill, relaxing game when you're constantly frustrated at the gameplay and there's very little reward for exploring. Overall, I would have finished the game a lot sooner (and enjoyed it more) if I wasn't constantly getting lost on unnecessarily huge maps, fighting the controls, and getting stuck on rocks and therefore failing timed puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The world, the music, the mood and atmosphere. This is a beautiful game. The puzzles are not hard by any means, but one did throw me off as its trigger point was further back than I realised. It manages to tell a story without any words or character facial expressions. That said I want to learn more about it all and I'm looking forwards to what the follow up will bring to us. I streamed this and was quite surprised I was making decent progress without it feeling too quick.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for something to relax, but still give some challenge, and like to solve puzzles... this would be for you. The game is very beautifully design and the attention to details is amazing... even tho many places you would only see for a few seconds as you dash through the chapters.Some chapters / puzzles can be a bit tough at some times, but it feels rewarding once you manage to solve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: explore, find powerups, jump and use powerups at sites.  Could be fun as a unique perspective casual game but must play 2 handed - cannot assign the few controls required to mouse buttons.  The physics and scenes are interesting and the game play non-violent which all could be great appeal but the lack of customized controls seems too cheap an oversight to keep expending casual minutes exploring.  Close to good but not.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a single-player, adventure, puzzle-platformer walking simulator game. The game doesn't have any text. It is suitable for anyone without any foreign language knowledge (well, other than the main menu).To help you to decide about the game I would like to share what I liked or disliked in the game, then I'll give some subjective ratings about the game contents.-Visuals: The game has a charming graphic. It looks very nice. Character animation, movement, effect it does just incredible.-Great Soundtracks: The game doesn't have narration or text. In this kind of programs emotional sound effects and soundtracks required. Spirit of the North solved this. It explains the story without any word, with great soundtracks, and animation. -Fox skins: If you collect collectibles then you can unlock additional fox skins. Bored about regular fox skin? Open up the menu and change to a snow fox or corrupted black/white fox. Isn't enough for you? The spirit form of your fox changes with the skin you using too. For example, if you playing with a corrupted black fox, then your spirit form will be red instead of the default blue.-Casual puzzles: The game doesn't offer difficult puzzles or cryptic, hard to solve riddles. It stays casual. It might be disliked by some, but this is what the game offers: A casual, relaxing entertainment for anyone between age 4-125.-Fox bark: The protagonist sounds like a dog, and not as a fox. Their barking is similar, but there is still some difference, and it is clear some dog sound was used for the game.-Too short: Not a real dislike, the game offers a good 6-10 hours playtime. I just loved the game, so when I finished it, then I wanted more of it.I really loved the game. I had a constant curiosity about how the story goes on. Spirit of the North price is fair for the content it offers.Story: 8/10Atmosphere: 9/10Visuals: 9/10Gameplay mechanics: 8/10Music/Sound effects: 10/10Voice acting/Narration: 1/10 No voice acting, texts or narration in the game, it gets the lowest rating only because the fox bark sounds like a dog, and not like a fox.Game difficulty: 3/10Perfection time: 6-10h. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game because it is beautiful, and it would be relaxing, if not for the empty gameplay and stiff controls.Maybe I'm just desensitized by other games, but 90 minutes in and the gameplay loop seems to be "press B near this thing" then "press Y near this other thing", which opens a door to another area where you rinse and repeat. The areas are connected by segments that try to be 3D platforming but end up being too simple, like you might see in a school project. It took the game an hour to introduce the first moving platform, and it is a seesaw platform that won't even tip steep enough to make you fall off.I might be able to get past the gameplay loop if the controls felt really tight and responsive, but they unfortunately are the second really lacking thing. e.g. when you jump, the complete arc of the jump is set in stone when you leave the ground, so you can't "brake" or turn midair even a little bit. This makes it frustrating to do simple things like jump from one platform to another (half the core loop), because you can overshoot by jumping too late, or fall to the left or right because you didn't line up perfectly and get a running start. This is not a skill thing, it's the lack of the feeling of control over your character -- think if you had to use Dark Souls controls to platform in Super Mario 64.This game might be relaxing to watch someone else play. I'd call it more an artful story than a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I would absolutely recommend this game. It's relaxing and casual, with absolutely stunning scenery to get lost in and explore, but in spite of zero text or dialogue through the game has the ability to hit you squarely in the feels. Had I known this, I might have waited longer to play this, but I am also glad I didn't. Cathartic and then some. I'm  steering away from the story, because it's as much or as little as you want to make of it, though you will get more out of it if you don't just rush to solve the puzzles. This game proves though that communication is about more than words. The soundtrack is beautifully composed - I've left it on while I had a nap... It's not a perfect game - in spite of regular save points, exiting the game will sometimes skip you back to the start of a chapter, which can be frustrating depending on the puzzles - likewise if you explore a little too much and get stuck (guilty a couple of times!) your only option is to exit and risk losing progress. This has meant I've left myself on away rather than turning off at times, which isn't always ideal. I really want there to be more, but the game is complete in terms of the story - I'd love to see another game based on a different myth or idea though. And I would play with some tissues to hand - especially if you have a soul at all!! (I spent the end of chapter seven onwards playing whilst ugly crying... >.>)

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North brings the  mythology of ...Players will enjoy breathtaking visuals and its majestic setting in the Nordic countries to the fullest.But with no lines of dialogue or any explanation written directly to the player,  puts the gamer in control of a bubbling fox who has a fateful encounter with a spirit form of the guardian fox of the Northern Lights. From there, it is up to the little red fox to venture through the icy landscapes in search of the purification of his land and, further on, to reach the highest point of the ice mountain.Spirit of the North is a game that bets on telling its Nordic folk story in a very subjective way, so unless your player profile is someone who is obsessed with Finnish mythology and folklore - especially the tale of Tulikettu - don't feel guilty for playing the game for the simple pleasure of knowing its beautiful setting, solving the puzzles around you to advance in the game, as the story was designed for a very small niche of players.Using the body of the red fox and the spirit of the protective entity of the , the player will advance through the beautiful Nordic scenarios, always in an intuitive way, in search of the solution of several puzzles that will make it possible to reach more complex and advanced adventures.Physically, the little fox performs the basic actions of the species such as barking, wagging its tail, sniffing, jumping, running, but things get more interesting when we control the spiritual face of the entity. In this part, some abilities such as the light that radiates from the spirit, essential for progression in the dark caves, or even the ability to overcome physical barriers make the game more challenging in terms of solving puzzles. In addition, as the story progresses, more skills are unlocked, making mastery and understanding of each of them essential for success in the fire-colored fox's quest.The controls have some frustrating glitches as the game progresses. There are many times when the player will feel punished for failures that are clearly caused by unresponsive actions. Therefore, it is important that the player knows that he will be able to repeat movements to exhaustion to master and hit essential commands for solving puzzlesComprised of soothing and relaxing trails,  does not disappoint as it transports the player directly into the icy and lonely climate of the Scandinavian mountains. Conducted primarily by violins and percussion and keyboard instruments, the soundtrack maintains a perfect atmosphere of calm that accurately reflects the best of the landscape and also conveys the necessary comfort for the player to think better and solve each challenge with precision.Bordering on photorealism, I can say that the graphic part of  is the most impressive at first. It's safe to say that the beautiful Nordic landscapes have never been shown in such a realistic way in video games as in this  However, its greatest merit ends up showing its biggest weakness, which is the lack of inspiration in its level design.With vast clean, repetitive scenarios and a high dose of lack of orientation in the scenarios,  uses all its beauty to confuse and disorient the player, who will certainly feel lost for most of the game. your game time. In the end, even though the game has a presentation that is a delight to the eyes, the image that remains of the game is that the set of work serves more to keep the player lost, given the interpretative characteristics of the story, lack of a mini map and beautiful but repetitive settings.On the other hand, the game lacks solid gameplay and the level design leaves something to be desired, making it confusing and repetitive.The high point of the game is in the beauty of the graphics, perfectly married to the soundtrack. A more subjective and relaxing style of play, which becomes even more interesting if the player is willing to research and engage in the Finnish mythology and folklore of .❆ There are no performance issues❆ Beautiful scenery❆ Immersive soundtrack❆ Too much intuitiveness in the story❆ You need to read a book to understand the story❆ Repetition of scenarios❆ Constant player disorientation❆ Repetitive challenges

_childDocuments_.review: I found Spirit of the North to be a very enjoyable game.I can sometimes have a hard time with puzzle games, but none of the puzzles in this game left me feeling too frustrated. I liked that we have the freedom to explore, but I wish you could ask your spirit guide for help when you feel you need it.I also didn't mind the open-ended story. I was never quite sure what was going to happen next, but I was always pleasantly surprised and enjoyed the new areas we got to explore.It's not going to be everyone's cup of tea, but if you like cozy puzzle games you will probably enjoy this one as well. :)

The gameplay mechanics are intuitive, allowing you to immerse yourself in the serene world and connect with the environment in a meaningful way.Spirit of the North weaves a narrative of discovery and self-reflection without using a single word. Through subtle environmental storytelling and symbolic imagery, the game tells a tale of the bond between nature and the spirit of the fox. As you explore the world and encounter ancient relics, you'll piece together the history of a forgotten civilization and unlock the mysteries of the land. The storytelling is poignant and evocative, inviting you to contemplate the deeper meaning behind the journey.The sound design in Spirit of the North complements the serene atmosphere of the game. The enchanting musical score resonates with the natural surroundings, enhancing the sense of wonder and tranquility. The ambient sounds, from the gentle rustling of leaves to the distant calls of wildlife, create an immersive auditory experience that further connects you to the spirit of the world. It's a game that encourages you to slow down, appreciate the beauty of the natural world, and reflect on the interconnectedness of all living things. If you seek a tranquil and enchanting experience that celebrates the power of nature, Spirit of the North is a game that should not be missed.In summary, Spirit of the North invites players on a serene and enchanting journey through a visually stunning world. _childDocuments_.review: is an atmospheric platformer that looks really cool. However, having played through it, it feels less like  and more like a tech demo for the Unreal Engine 4.So, what's the game about? You play as a fox who is fused with a spirit and has to travel across the land to undo some curse. On the way you gain a few abilities and solve a few platforming puzzles.That's it. That's the game.Now the game does have some little lore nuggets sprinkled throughout to keep you guessing as to what happened to the land, but they barely do anything to pique your interest. They're just there to add some variety to the simple landscapes.The problem with  is just that it isn't fun. An atmospheric platformer should amaze you, but it doesn't. The visuals are sometimes cool, but more often than not it just felt like I was walking through a test environment for the Unreal Engine.The jumping mechanics are awful. They feel clunky. I got myself stuck numerous times because the fox couldn't turn properly and keep their momentum in their jump. Also, after every single puzzle the camera zooms to the issue you just solved, taking away control from the player. The first time, this is understandable. If the solution is far away, then sure. But every single time? That just gets tedious.The abilities you do get are very simple. The ability to activate a button, a dash, a dispelling bark and a spirit form. Of these, the spirit form is probably the most engaging, as the others just felt like they should've been part of your basic powers anyhow.Also, the music is really bland. For a game genre where visuals and music usually carry a lot of weight, this one underdelivers on both.Now, maybe this may not be the game for me. Other reviewers have noted that children enjoy playing it. And sure, it's a really simple game. If you want to just solve some simple puzzles with a cute fox, go for it. But there are so many other atmospheric games out there like this one that are much better. Try , try , try . Something similar with better platforming?  is available. Something more surreal? . More story? Introducing . A similar theme as this one?  is a platformer set in the arctic that is incredibly engaging. There are so many games out there that scratch the same itch as this game does and do it better in my opinion.If you want this game, buy it in a sale. It's about five hours long, a few more if you want to 100% it. I'd recommend trying a different one. This one ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is an open world adventure game where you play as a fox and run through intricate puzzles. The game has seven chapters, each with their own degree of difficulty and puzzles in a massive, open world with different environments.The game has impressive graphics and background music with a lack of glitches. Spirit of the North has unlockable skins for your fox.  For example, you start as an Artic fox and can later play as a red fox or a grey fox, to name a few of the unlockable skins in the game.Spirit of the North is long, but not too long of a game with about 12 hours of gameplay. There are artifacts you can find of an ancient civilization. All the textures are in-depth and in high quality, especially for a game that is only $19.99. _childDocuments_.review: I don't really know where to start. First I was so amazed by the landscape and the entire setting of the game. I was looking for a game that includes animals in a majestic kind of way to experience a journey or an adventure with them. It reminded me of The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess where you had to find the golden wolf which teached you a new ability, everytime you found him and I thought this game might be similar to that.During the beginning you will see a few cutscenes where you encounter the spirit fox. But I didn't really enjoyed those scenes, the entire gesture and the static movement of the fox was looking kind of weird to me. The next thing is the environment. You will start in an ice landscape but after some time you will get into a lovely green field of basically nothing. It was actually looking dead to me just if the there was something missing or just unfinished. A few parts were stunning but the majority of it was just boring. I do know that it is supposed to look pretty similar to the actual landscape of iceland, but I expected more, maybe some insects, more flowers or whatever. To me it wasn't looking breathtaking or mysterios (except a few spots) at all.While mentioning flowers - there is actually a flower that will give you some kind of spirit energy back after using it during a puzzle or an ability. But this feature was just annoying to me. Luckily those flowers where always placed somewhere around you, so you can get your energy back. But that's the point to me. Your spirit energy shouldn't be a rare or lacking resource if you just get it from a flower. Walking back to one of them to get the energy just made everything uncomfortably long to me. Another thing is about the fox. Walking and jumping were looking really lovely, but getting to a certain point was feeling weird. Turning around and jumping with the fox felt imprecise and kind of slippery. It also happened that I ended up stuck behind statues or walls after jumping around them.Don't get me wrong please and don't forget that this is just my personal experience.This game has so much potential to become breathtaking and amazing and maybe it already feels like that for other people. I was just annoiyed by many little things that you might not experience the same way as I did. I'm still happy that I found and tried this game, but there were just too many things that didn't fit for me and my expectations. I'm sure that there will be people out there who will have a lot of fun with this game and begin to love it's entire setting and grace.

_childDocuments_.review: While I do love the art style, score, and overall vibe of this game it is too flawed to be very enjoyable. Especially for the $20 price. The controls are completely stiff, your character gets caught on the environment all the time, and the fox shakes for like 5 seconds every single time you leave the water. For a game that requires precise movements it really feels completely wonky and unfair to play. I found the theme very relaxing although actual gameplay was downright frustrating. If you can look over these types of issues by all means buy this game, but for me it felt unpolished and unsatisfactory at best. I made it to chapter 6 of 7 and I will not be finishing the game. It is simply not worth anymore of my time.

Those are minor though honestly my main complaint was that the music was lacking. I could have used some more epic swells in music at the big story telling parts, but there was like 3 songs throughout the whole game. All relaxing and nice but It would have had so much more impact if there was something more moving at times. I kind of tuned out the music at times and with no narrative music is a big part of how you convey emotion in your story. Over all, I loved it, and will be playing it again to get all the things I missed.

_childDocuments_.review: „I will lead you on devoured Paths,in the hidden enclosures of your Soul,helping you,finding your Strenght,to geht back your Life Force.“Claudia R. 2014Welcome to the SPIRIT OF THE NORTH.Inspired from the wonderfull Lands of Iceland and its Nordic Folklore, Infuse Studio invites you to the  wonderfull and unforgettable Journey of a Red Fox.It is up to you to lead this little Fox through this wonderfull and mysterious Lands. In the Beginning your Fox stumbles into a Female Ghost Fox, the Guardian of the Northlights, becoming a Fox Form he never would have imagined. Something bad, something Evil is lurking in the Dark, somewhere far in the Land of Souls.And it is up to your little Fox to bring this all to a maybe good End.Leading this little Guy through the graphically, wonderfull Lands will expect solving puzzles from you to make his Progress. This can be by just Jumping to places, but also by using ancient columns or getting through Obstacles. Your Fox cant do it alone. Your Attender is the Female Ghost Fox, following you as a fen fire. You are also able to get ancient Light for your Fox, not only giving him a mysterious Skin but using this Light in special Places.While you Journey this mysterious Lands you will find very old Wallscriptings that will tell you the Story of the Past.  You will also recognize all the Ruins on your way, showing marks of a Civilization. You will also find the Corpses of ancient Monks, maybe the once proud inhabitants of this Ruins. Find their Wands and lay them down there. Set their Souls free und find your way through their Lands.So much to the Story, that isn`t told by a Word, just by pictures and that is something i really like, because of having my own Phantasies about what the Pictures are telling me.If you ever played ABZU or SUBMERGED, you will know what  i mean.The Controlls are well done (for me). First i played with Mouse and Keyboard, but then i used the Controller. Both worked very good, your Fox responded perfectly on the Controlls. SPIRIT OF THE NORTH has large Areas to explore, but your way is mostly prescribed  because of solving Puzzles to open Doors to continue your Progress. This Game also uses Chapters with Checkpoints instead of Saving and you have many points to return, for example when you miss a Monk Corpse.The Fox is really wonderfull animated, the Developer put very much effort in keeping their Creation to life.  Such simple Things like letting your Fox staying to long, he will sit down. The animated Fur that makes you wanting to crawl this sweet fox. The Lightskin, so fantastic animated.  Also a nice point i like, you dont have to fight, just explore and solve the Puzzles to continue. SPIRIT OF THE NORTH invites you to totally dive into this Game and enjoying the Time there, guiding by a really wonderfull Soundtrack..It feels like a wonderful coming together from THE FIRST TREE, ABZU and SUBMERGED.Thanks dear Developer.What do you think, dear Reader?Are you ready to guide a little Fox and his Spirit Friend through their biggest Adventure?Have a nice time and thank you for Reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea this game is going for, but it gets extremely repetitive and annoying after a while. Some of the puzzles are fun, other times they're very annoying. _childDocuments_.review: What...an utterly...beautiful experience that was.It's not often a game so simply manages to catch my attention, and draw me in.  This game, in me, reignited an emotion I rarely feel in games today: the love of gaming.  At its core, it is a simple puzzle platformer.  But very quickly you'll see it's much more of an experience, and a beautiful one at that.  The music is somber but touching, while the setpieces are absolutely gorgeous.  I found myself exploring not because of the hidden shamans spirits to save, but because I just loved the environments and wanted to take a look.The story follows that tried and true method of show, don't tell, leaving the player to piece together what is presented.  Nowadays people tend to get caught in the mindset that a narrative needs to be some epic drama with exciting moments and high stakes.  What this game understands, PROVES, is that doesn't always need to be the case.  In fact, some times it's better to take a step back, and let the world breathe a little.  Shadows of the Collosus did this particularly well, and I found myself thinking of that game many times.I really don't have any complaints, other than the desire for more of it.  You can very quickly beat it, let alone 100% it, I'm 5 hours in and am just missing 2 achievements which should be relatively easy to get.  I hope to see more games like this, because this is what gaming should be: a great experience. Play the game, try it out for yourself.  For once, a game that doesn't try to trick you into playing longer than 2 hours so you can't refund it.  It just gives you a great experience from start to finish.  I guarantee you won't want to return it.  Play it.  Enjoy it.  Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 17 hours, and of that, around 12 to 14 were spent solely on chasing down a lost spirit monk in the second-to-last level in a spirit forest realm. This was not fun. Guides and walkthroughs were of little help because some of the spirit monks WANDER and thus cannot be found in any specific location. For years, off and on, I got on this game again solely to chase down the missing monk and only a couple days ago did I manage to finally encounter him. THIS. IS. A. CHORE.If you like foxes, I would stress to you that you should get this game ONLY when it is at a serious discount. There are some bonuses to this game--cute emotes, a profile background, and a nice badge set which I leveled up to max because after 100%ing this game I deserve it--but I do not think they really justify paying more than maybe around 5 bucks for it. The fox has a few cute animations--shaking off water and limping--but these animations slow down or completely stop you in some areas. You can unlock different skins by getting certain achievements or progress in the game, but...There is no real replayability in this title. Where in other games, abilities you unlock in later levels can be then used in earlier levels to have more fun or access previously inacessible areas, this game does not offer anything of that sort. Worse, once you get used to abilities like sprint/dash, the game feels painfully slow when you go back to earlier levels and are completely unable to use them. This was probably my worst experience with the game apart from the missing monk chase.The story is very vague and nondescript; you have to inference what is happening from crude murals on walls (oh, by the way, those can be a challenge to find and light up too, same with the monks). Basically every seek and find in this game turns it from a relaxing jaunt through the open world (read: boring and lifeless area) to a monotonous nightmare trying to figure out where you are on the map and where you need to go from there.Overall? I cannot recommend this game. If they at least let you return to earlier levels with the abilities you unlock, it could be a maybe. Since they do not, and the achievements are such a pain to get, I'm uninstalling after posting this review.As a final note; I unlocked the flying fox achievement when the game glitched and launched me into the air and out of the map entirely. I could not get back onto the map and had to close and restart the game to get anywhere afterward. I'm keeping the achievement for my trouble, but that is not the intended way you were meant to get that achievement, so yeah--look out for glitches!

name: Fight Crab
detailed_description: Crabs Powered by Simulated Physics! Take control of a simulated physics-powered crab and take on various opponents in this 3D action game with one basic rule: 'flip your enemy over to win'. Take advantage of a wide range of equipment to beat your opponent down: claws, swords, guns, armor, jet engines, and more. Stop your opponent's blade with your pincers, run along walls, and generally go full-on crab with all the fighting techniques at your disposal. Get the total battle crab experience with amazing procedural animations and spot-on accurate collision detection - just like you've always wanted to but probably never realized. Featuring 23 types of crab, 48 different weapons, and 11 unique battle stages! 1 vs. 1, 2 vs. 2, online/offline battle modes... This game has it all. Enjoy campaigns and training modes while waiting for your turn in battle! Campaign Mode featuring over 41 battles as well as training, rankings, and more! Go through the entire campaign on your own, or cooperate with friends - you can get the full experience either way! Test your might in the advanced-level Hard Mode and wave-based challenge stages to really hone your battle skills. Link up with VRoid Hub Go into battle sporting your very own original avatar on top of your crab! Original avatars can be seen by other players online, so you can show off your bitchin' avatars to players around the world. In some completely different, super weird world, crabs have mastered human weapons and taken over the land. Now immortal, these crabs cannot be killed by gun nor blade. However, there is one crustacean rule by which all must live: 'He who turns his back to the ground shall know defeat...' That's right - get flipped over on your back in battle, and you have no choice but to submit to your opponent. You must now embark on a journey to become the strongest ever seen, and flip the entire world itself onto its back.

_childDocuments_.review: Underneath the silly theme and somewhat unwieldy controls may perhaps be the most complex fighting game of all time. The attacks aren't animations, you are controlling your motions and they collide physically with whatever they contact. Add this to the wide variety of weapons and combatants, and the possibilities for how a fight plays out are limitless.Also, you get to play as a crab.
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: There's crabs, you wield ridiculous weapons, the controls are "left stick is left claw, right stick is right claw, d-pad is move" which is clumsy and hilarious. You build up a damage "%" like in Smash, and it seems to make it easier to flip you on your back, which is of course the ultimate goal.I don't know how any of the mechanics in this game work. For some reason, pressing Back sometimes puts you in Super Saiyan mode. How does it charge? Who knows. What are these green bars on my screen? Can you break weapons? There's not all that much depth to the gameplay, or to the (dearth of) game modes and meta stuff. Progression is "sometimes you randomly earn a new weapon". And I was unable to find any online matches, though the game just came out, maybe it'll pick up (but it does have background matchmaking which is great). I'm not sure if any of that really matters because there's crabs and they have lightsabers.
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: I have not had this much fun with a game in years. I'm almost 40 now and most of the wonderment is gone for me with with gaming in general...I bought this for my kid for his birthday and grabbed it for me too, figuring I would sneak an hour in here and there with him--Well he moved on to a different game near instantly and here I am grinding and looking for time to play this game. I like developing strategies and weird co-op tactics. It's awesome to be excited to get home from work and actually want to play a game.  I haven't been this obsessed with a game in years. I'm not sure why but I love it. The controls may seem odd at first, things can get crazy trying to grab an enemy crab's weapon and keep from falling off the level while trying to keep your claws extended and pinch in a coordinated fashion. Once you upgrade your crab the controls will feel better, but that's part of the fun. I can't think of anything else to point out just buy this thing even if you don't play it, these guys made something different and should be rewarded instead of snowed under by stale FPS titles and contrived 8-bit junk. Buy this game and support creativity in games!
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings!It's Very Good so far. The best bits:- The feel. Bit of an "Armored Core" / Mechwarrior vibe to the control scheme, but with the added tactility of simulated physics- The UI. Smacks of Dreamcast-era arcade games- Customization. Pick and experiment with favorite strategies and weapons for the crabs you unlock; build their stats as you see fit- Co-op. As far as I can tell, your buddy can jump into any part of the campaign, without restrictions, and build up their own crabI love this game. It's got a sense of humor about itself; it's interesting; there's depth and variety... In an age of "wait for a sale" purchases, this one's an instant buy. No regrets!CRABLOG 001:- There are a lot more crabs in this game than I expected. A really pleasing amount!- They all control differently in several ways, and if you like one particular part of a crab (tiny arms for duel gunslinging is a personal favorite), you can upgrade to exploit that or to bolster its weaknesses
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and the devs for making it. To top things off, the soundtrack goes way too hard for a game like this, and I appreciate the devs for doing it anyways, and of course I bought the soundtrack. Great game. Will crab again and force all of my friends to try it out (I already managed to get one to buy it).Just one warning for those interested in the game, the controls are weird and are NOT meant for keyboard and mouse. If you want to know exactly what I mean, all I'll tell you is that you control the movement of your claws with both of your joysticks. But how do you move? Simply press the corresponding direction on your D-Pad once and you'll go in that direction continuously until you either press the same direction again to cancel it out or press a different direction. These controls aren't as bad as they seem, but they feel a lot more coherent to be because I played with an 8BitDo SN30pro+ controller, aka a playstation 4 like controller. So I recommend using one of those when playing the game, but if you can't or just don't want to, I won't blame you.I just wish I could play this on my Steam Deck. That would just make me the happiest ever.Edit: I finally figured out how to play not only Fight Crab, but other Unsupported games on the Steam Deck. To get Fight Crab (or any other unsupported tagged game to work), simply go onto Desktop Mode, install "ProtonUp-Qt" from the discover store, launch ProtonUp-Qt, simply select which version you'd like to add (I'd recommend simply the latest version). Once you got all the different Proton versions you want, you can switch back to Gaming mode, make sure to download said unsupported game you wish to play, go to the game's properties, and then go to "compatibility". Once there, select "Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool" and select the latest version of GE-Proton7. Please note that not ALL unsupported games will work with this method. I have no idea myself, but from what I heard rumored, anything with Easy Anti-Cheat doesn't work. I recommend looking up the game you wish to know about (in terms of working on the Steam Deck) by looking at the website protondb. It should give you a general idea if they work with these other versions of Proton.From my testing on the latest version of Proton (at the time, it was GE-Proton7-27) and the main menu will have music playing, but the usual in-game footage showing gameplay is missing. All you'll see is the menu text and nothing but a black void in the background. I haven't tested online matches on the Steam Deck (nor have I even tried them on PC), but some reports say that muliplayer works while more dated reports say otherwise. Take that as you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: Me and a friend bought this to try. If you can get past the extremely janky control learning curve, Fight Crab actually has some decent depth to it. You'll spend a few matches figuring out what you can do, another few figuring out how to do it consistently, a few more figuring out what not to do, and then the rest learning even more and implementing new tactics. By the end of our first play session, he was bouncing all over the walls with his ninja-like crab, while I was combining short and long ranged attacks, before going in for grapples and flips. It isn't a perfect game by any means, which hugely adds to the appeal, because I don't feel anyone could ever really master this game (or would want to), so everyone feels on an even playing field.Complaints:1) Some items are straight rubbish with the control system and limitations of the game. Revolvers for example cannot be used. After spending a good 5 minutes trying to figure out how to use them, I even had my friend stand still and I could still not hit his crab. Other items are obviously OP. The balance of the game is all over the place, both with crabs and weapons.2) Pretty much everything needs to be self-discovered. This is fine, but the tutorials on controls and items etc are extremely limited and not intuitive. If you can make it past the huge learning curve and not get frustrated, and take you time like we did, then you'll have a great time.3) Controls are a bit un-intuitive. Analog sticks are for controlling angle of attacks, with triggers doing the attacking. Movement is off the D-pad and a bit janky. There is nothing for aiming (hence why things like the revolvers are useless). I feel they could have condensed the attack controls and made for more ability to move and aim.Overall, I would recommend Fight Crab as a bit of a laugh between friends, especially if it is on sale. If you can endure the learning curve, enjoy the flaws, and have another patient friend or two, then Fight Crab could make for a great party game to throw in now and then on games nights. Unlockables keep you addicted for "another" game too, so there is a bit of gold amongst the rough. And although not everything works, just the image of a mud crab riding a seal, while smacking a lobster with a skull and katana, is enough for the price of entry.
