_childDocuments_.review: Nature has many ways to warn outsiders of danger. It could be a dog baring its teeth, a lion roaring through the jungle, or a crab the size of a battleship waving around a battle axe. In most cases, these natural warnings are answered with backing away slowly, but for that last one, you’ll want to respond with your own giant crab and lightsabers, or possibly guns. That’s the premise of Fight Crab, a colorful, chaotic brawler that pits crabs from all walks of the infraorder Brachyura against each other in brutal combat. Between the wild weapons, the bizarre locales, and the absolutely insane escalation of the campaign, this hard-shelled brawler promises plenty of fun within its notably narrow scope.Surely you didn’t come to a game called Fight Crab looking for a story, and indeed all you’re going to get here are vague allusions to becoming the king of all crabs. That’s accomplished by beating the bajeezus out of any crustaceans in your path, of course, through a series of battles strung together into a campaign. From tidepools to avenues, restaurants to freezer cases, you’ll face every variety of crab imaginable and then some, armed with knives, clubs, swords, shuriken, flails, rockets, shotguns, and more. Your battles are not to the death, but until you or your challengers lie helpless on your backs, and proceed until you have bested the true king of crabs in fantastic fashion. To explain any further would be to spoil the awe-inspiring conclusion of your journey, so instead we’ll talk about the road to becoming the crustiest crustacean around.I wouldn’t call Fight Crab a full QWOPlike, but the controls are definitely designed more for pratfalls than precision. The analogue sticks on your gamepad control your crab’s claws, with the triggers extending that claw to strike and the shoulder buttons clenching them to block. With skilled maneuvering you can perform uppercuts, parry blows, and grapple your foe, but for the first few hours you’re just going to be flailing wildly and hoping you land more lucky hits than the enemy does. It’s honestly a pretty deep and detailed combat system that can be mastered, and will require a bit of prowess to get you to the end of the campaign. But it’s also plenty of fun to swing wildly at crabs, pick up beer bottles and smash enemies off of dinner tables, and generally just stomp around like a big angry crab with a katana.There’s a surprising number of weapons and wieldable… things in the game, which can be found in stages, taken from your foes, or purchased between battles to carry into combat with you. Weapons get fanciful real quick, with legendary weapons like Excalibur or some JRPG favorites appearing alongside more conventional nunchaku and guandao. The money used to buy weapons can also unlock new crabs to play as, each with their own stats and capabilities, and then to level those stats up for the more difficult later battles. You’ll even gain super moves in your journey, special techniques that borrow from the likes of Dragon Ball in the best possible ways. Helpful tutorials unlock alongside your new capabilities, concisely educating you in the ways of energy beams and divine blessings.The sum of these parts is a thrilling, hilarious brawler that goes beyond the obvious hilarity of the screenshots. I had a genuine blast battling through the campaign, and the final fights were exactly what you think of when you apply the term “epic” to this outing. The charm of flailing around with giant, deadly crabs never really gets old, but the content does rather run out of steam after you beat the campaign only two or three hours in. From that point you can work on the blisteringly hard Extra stages, try to beat the campaign again on hard, or try to find someone in the world to play online matches with you. It’s a real crime that Fight Crab didn’t take off as the next big esport phenomenon, but regardless of the injustice done, I wouldn’t pick this one up for the multiplayer.If you were a fan of Ace of Seafood or any other sort of off-kilter battler out of Japan, you’ll definitely enjoy Fight Crab. It’s a more polished and engrossing package than Ace or its predecessors, though I won’t deny the placeholder-looking UI is still a thing here. This one ends up being far more viscerally entertaining than other games of its ilk, but just for not a terribly long time. A bigger campaign or more game modes would have given Fight Crab longer legs, but the time you spend with it is still guaranteed to be quality. Really, I know you’ve always wanted to have a katana duel with a spider crab in a shadowy alley, and it’s not like you can look anywhere else for that kind of magic.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: This game is significantly more fun and better-executed than I expected. I purchased it expecting a campy, low-effort, glitchy, indie disaster -- but that's not what I got. The control scheme is actually pretty genius, and the combat system is shockingly deep and enjoyable. This isn't a hardcore competitive fighting game by any means; it's an absurd, physics-based party game that's intentionally unwieldy. And holy ♥♥♥♥ is it fun.You set yourself to auto-walk in a direction by tapping the d-pad, then each analog stick gives you full control over each arm. Bumper buttons pinch your claws shut (to grab items or form a shield to block damage), and trigger buttons launch your fist forward from whatever position your arm was in.This means you can wind your arm down low to launch an uppercut, pull it back and out to throw a hook, keep it close inside for a jab, etc., etc.. It's actually really intuitive, and it doesn't take long to notice yourself throwing out combinations like Muhammad Ali. Enemy crab swinging a sword at you? Backhand his attack away with your left arm while you uppercut him in the face with your right arm.There's an insane number of crabs and weapons. Each crab feels different and synergizes with weapons differently depending on the length/height/angles of their arms. You have to experiment a lot to figure out what works well with what. I felt compelled to keep playing to unlock all the crabs and weapons, and the stages and music just keep getting better and better. You eventually unlock a customizable AI companion (crab-panion?) and DBZ-inspired super moves that you manually execute by performing the hand gestures (kamehameha, spirit bomb, kioken, etc).There's a ton of little details that make it clear that a lot of love went into making this game.10 out of 10 best crab game ever

_childDocuments_.review: Fight Crab's release has locked in Calappa Games' stranglehold on the marine-life gaming sphere. The few competitors that might've existed a year ago are now mourning those years wasted trying to make fish or crab games of their own. The Analog stick -> Claw fighting system will be remembered for decades in the genre, not only for its initial difficulty of use giving way to unparalleled depth of control + combat options, but also for the way this control scheme gets the player into the headspace of the common crustacean. Never before have I felt such empathy for another animal species, such a complete understanding of the day to day struggles. Massively innovative and fun as ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: A very good game that only looks cheap, with a lot of things that end up being "surprisingly very good", despite what seems like a jank UI and finnicky controls.A fantastic little game that's much more and better than it appears at first glance. And, given that it appears like a gimmicky game with no substance, that may be a low bar to clear, but this is one of those games that underpromises and most definitely overdelivers.With a surprising amount of unlockable weapons, crabacters, and stages, there is more than enough content to be worth the $20 at full price, even without factoring in the replay value offered by endless wave missions and the online functionality, both co-op and competitive.And the online functionality is definitely a must indeed. Though this game is very fun played on its own, it really shines when you've got a friend, either right next to you in split screen or online through the surprisingly solid netcode implementation.Sure, this game's controls are a little finnicky, not as snappy as you'd want them to be, and take some getting used to: but they're definitely workable and quite playable, though it may not feel as such when you first pick up the controller or hit those WASD keys. You'll need to get a feel for them, but I don't recommend rebinding anything, the controls are designed the way they are for a reason.That said, once you've got a feel for the controls, the game feels much more like matches are won with finesse and technique rather than by dumb luck and button mashing. This game definitely rewards skill, even if at first it feels like it doesn't.All in all, a fantastic game worth every cent I paid for it. Grab a friend, and roll through some endless levels in co-op; it'll make for a fun night indeed.Tips: 1. Play through the tutorial, and try using both M&K and controller. Both are usable, but have different play styles. M&K is "easier", but less versatile.2. Experiment with the different crabs. They all respond significantly differently to inputs and you'll need to find the one that works for you, rather than the one with the "best stats".3. Double punches are the best way to help flip yourself back up.4. There is no aiming the guns. Don't bother even trying.Edit: It seems that the devs are constantly releasing updates and patches for this game every week. With this much dedication, I imagine most of the frustrating bugs and glitches will be patched out in no time!

_childDocuments_.review: If a youthful obsession with Japanese crab cinema and an audiobook version of 'I Love Hermit Crab' have taught me anything, it's that if you want to be a great crab, having a connection to nature is important. Skill with a weapon isn't purely driven by physical strength and technique, but also by the acuity that comes from observing trees, mountains, and rivers. Something like that.While I can only make guesses as to how inspirational the rural areas of feudal Japan would have been, the scenic island portrayed in Fight Crab, an open-world 22nd-century crab epic, is one that often stirs something inside me. Beyond being a game centred around flashy sword fights and the journey of Crab to becoming a proto-ninja, Fight Crab invites you to lose yourself deeply in its cities, restaurants, and castle dining rooms. And though the tasks you're given often aren't as brilliant as the colour of the leaves, there's certainly something wonderfully humbling about just riding your seal through this beautiful environment and taking it all in.And what an immediately beautiful world it is, full of bold, saturated colours, grandiose weather effects, and an overabundance of windswept leaves, petals, butterflies, and other small particles that make every location feel alive. The Crustacean City is a painter's palette; vibrant white and white building sit atop inviting concrete by day, blinding sunsets soak everything in a deep orange. At night, bright white moonlight glistens off dark blue lakes and waterfalls to illuminate everything around you. The game doesn't have an option to turn everything black and white in order to mimic the samurai films of Akira Kurosawa, but using it forgoes Tsushima's own distinct visual identity.At times, it almost feels as if art direction is trying a little bit too hard to draw attention to itself. And Fight Crab certainly makes a concerted effort to try and absorb you into its radiant world even further with its deliberate lack of navigational information. There's no option for an on-screen minimap or a compass to see which way you're going, and objective markers are barely there. Instead, the game features lock-on, in which the gamelooks at the enemy for you. A swipe of the DualShock's touchpad will probably not do anything (I don't know I played with an Xbox controller).It's a great system. Without anything to draw your eyes away from your character and the world, the choas pushes you to pay more attention to your surroundings, to let you more quickly internalise key landmarks that help you to get your bearings more easily later on, or just to feast your eyes. Other in-world devices, like plumes of smoke, flying songbirds, foxes, Torii gates, not-so-talkative non-player characters (they are crabs), and more help to guide (or rather, distract) you toward new activities.A lot of these activities also work in service of making sure you see Fight Crab's good side. Crabs will not invite you to follow them down charming paths to nearby Inari shrines. Torii gates will not lead you to simple but daring-looking platforming challenges that reward you with spectacular vistas. Haikus ask you to sit down and reflect on your picturesque surroundings (but are not featured in Fight Crab). Singing crickets will not be found in this game. You get equipment early on that helps you flip over crabs, and some convenient touches like a generous and very quick-loading loading screen system help make Crustacean City be an incredibly pleasant place to move through, especially when armed with the game's robust photo mode to take screenshots with.While you cannot enter a menu-based world map if you want to go somewhere specific, without a marker to constantly signal your next objective's location, you definitely get a little less obsessed with taking the most direct route, and feel more naturally inclined to just follow winding roads around mountains and along river banks. Guiding Wind is a feature in Ghost of Tsushima and not Fight Crab. As an open-world device, it also succeeds in masking the feeling that you're simply being strung along by objective markers, even though that's still exactly what you're doing.That feeling does still come up, unfortunately, when Fight Crab's quests (referred to as Fights) take hold of the reins. Fights fall back on fighting crabs, where you do things like hit a crab with a car, perhaps also throwing cars, and not being a crab isn't allowed. Sometimes you'll be asked to flip a crab, activities which have the ability to devolve into meticulous hunts for crabs. Some early Tales have you chasing crab after crab to the point of being silly, making you wonder if anything is going to happen at all. Anytime you're not engaged in combat, a lot of these quests, especially side quests, can feel like a drag.The cutscenes that host conversations between Crab and other crabs, which give context to these Fights, largely feel stilted, which further underscores the tedium. That's not the fault of the acting--Fight Crab doesn't have any passionate and strong-sounding Japanese voice work, at least to my human ear, though there is a visible disconnect with character lip-syncing (because carbs don't have lips), which retains the mocap performances of the (notably all-crab) crab cast. Even though I preferred the crab voice audio, the two tracks do offer some differences in regards to their overall tone.The voice work is largely let down by a noticeable lack of bodily expression in the almost motionless character models, meaning you're basically just watching a couple of talking heads most of the time. That's not uncommon to see in titles of this nature, but it is a significant low point in a game that otherwise hits so many stylistic highs. The cinematography, which frames the characters in pleasing ways within the gorgeous scenery, instead does the heavy lifting to make sure these regular moments are at least somewhat pleasing to the eye--though wide shots do draw more attention to the fact that two conversing bodies are standing perfectly still. This means that a lot of the game's emotional arcs and vibrant characters don't hit as hard as they should. Fight Crab clearly aims to evoke golden-age crab cinema in many ways, but it doesn't manage to capture even a tiny amount of their vigor when it comes to exposition--Lobster-level gusto is completely out of the question here.There are some exceptions to this. The primary story quests give the characters involved a bit more freedom to move, and naturally benefit from hosting the more interesting plot threads: that of Crab's inescapable metamorphosis from a by-the-books crab square to something a lot more unscrupulous for the greater good, and how this change affects the relationship with his loving but uncompromising father figure. The combat encounters here also benefit from some great set pieces, heightened by a strong musical score that helps construct those rousing blockbuster moments that always seem to be able to pull at your emotions, no matter how impartial you're trying to be.Read the rest of Gamespot's Ghost of Tsushima review here:

_childDocuments_.review: "haha, look at the funny crabs. what a silly game"no. this is the only good fighting game on the market. I've put an absurd amount of time into it on its multiple console ports. yes, the funny crab game is so good that I've bought it several times. I'd call the crabs a flashy gimmick, just there to catch your attention, but it's so much more than that. the crabs are fundamental to what makes this game great. solid, reliable physics and the unique control scheme behind crabhood give you a degree of freeform control over your movement and fighting technique that I've never seen any other game pull off in melee combat, bolstered by a solid variety of more advanced tech, both built in mechanically and inherent to the physics engine. no other pvp game allows anywhere near as much potential as Fight Crab does for experienced players to display their skills in a way that's both engaging to experience and exciting to watch. instead of giving you a bunch of perfectly balanced weapons and crabs, weighing the physical limitations and combat capabilities of various crabs and weapons — of which there's an impressive amount on offer — pulls triple duty as game knowledge to acquire and practice, a major axis of strategy, and a point of potential to flex on weaker crabbers by intentionally putting yourself in unfavorable matchups for the challenge. much like the better examples of more traditional fighting games, the distance between the flailing, button-mashing skill floor and the skill ceiling is greater than you'd anticipate at first glance, but I'd argue that it's a much more significant difference here, where mashing/flailing is far less likely to net you useful abilities or combos. instead, you have to understand the physical or literal mechanics behind any move you try to pull off, with a level of complexity from several angles that offers immense skill expression to those willing to put in the time.besides all that important stuff, it's also beautiful, has a fantastic soundtrack, and sports a solid amount of campaign content that makes a decent intro to a lot of the mechanics and options on offer. this is the point where I drop all pretense and beg you to get this and play online because no other indie game I've ever seen deserves a bigger community more than this one and roping friends in with the "silly crab game" pitch just to juggle them is getting really sad. play the funny crab game

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I'll just refund this. The main problem for me, is that it's not worth the price. The whole idea of crabs fighting with huge variety of weapons that have physics and collision seems fun, but after few matches it gets boring and repetitive.Now, lets talk about the combat.The game offers attacks from different directions and blocks,  and you have to use all of them wisely. But, actually the best tactic is to charge and spam attacks cuz blocks don't always work and it's best to try to out spam the opponent.I guess it's time we talk about equipment. There are 48 different weapons, but actually there are 6 weapons with different skins. These are one handed(blades,maces), throwing weapons, two handed, chained weapons, shields and mounts. the only ones that don't work with spamming are two handed weapons cuz they need lots of space to swing. You can also choose different crabs, but they all felt same. Oh, and btw, never pick lobsters cuz they always fall over easily.Can't say much about maps. They all have this annoying filter and they seem pretty much the same. My favorites are the grocery store and the table cuz thos maps have limited space and they have easily breakable food as weapons.Overall I wouldn't recommend the game for it's price. It's fun for few rounds even with friends, but then it becomes boring and super repetitive. I would spend that money on something else

_childDocuments_.review: Fight Crab is not going to appear at the next big esports competition, but any casual competitors are sure to have a ball. With a novel control scheme that's easy to learn and gameplay that's impossible to take to seriously, it will certainly find a home with variety streamers and those looking for a new game to play with friends. Any faults it does have are part of the charm, evoking an independent spirit that's hard not to root for.Want to know more? My full review is available now over on .

_childDocuments_.review: Good silly fun to play in short bursts.The controls are a bit wonky, probably better with gamepad. One thing I've noticed playing with kbm, is making sure at least one of the separate claw block actions is defined somewhere, so you can use it separately, either as blocking arm or putting the clamps on the opponent. It's also used for special weapon actions.By default you have shift for both claws, and while that works fine for blocking, grabbing and using weapons is trickier.There's a lovely variety of crabby fighters to pick and weapons to arm them with. And you can fight with one AI companion (except in the final boss stages).

_childDocuments_.review: on the outside, this looks like an awesome funny game. On the inside you find a slow, boring, hard to control mess. _childDocuments_.review: We wrote a critique of Fight Crab. Here is a select quote from the critique:"There’s no doubt that Fight Crab is an interesting game. What other game will let you equip a lobster with two jet engines and send it to fight against a fiddler crab with a lightsaber? However, it fails to remain interesting long-term. Its precise, complex controls feel betrayed by physics and the fact that the optimal strategy appears to be to simply charge at an enemy and beat them down as fast as possible. Balance also seems lacking, whether intentional or not, and its campaign doesn’t last nearly long enough. _childDocuments_.review: Fight Crabs, the highly awaited crab-fighting simulator, is an epic game that surpasses any other in its genre in terms of ingenuity, depth, and realism. This simulation offers an unparalleled sense of immersion that truly places players in the shoes, or rather, claws of a feisty crustacean warrior. Prepare to experience the thrill of crab-on-crab battles like never before!One of the standout features of Fight Crabs is its incredible attention to detail. The graphics are stunning, with beautifully rendered 3D environments that vividly capture the essence of underwater battlegrounds. The movement and animations of the crabs are exceptionally fluid. The gameplay mechanics of Fight Crabs are unmatched, delivering a unique blend of strategy, skill, and sheer chaos. Each crab can wield various weapons, such as swords, axes, and maces, providing players an opportunity to devise distinct fighting styles. The controls are intuitive, allowing for precise movements and attacks, further enhancing the sense of realism.What truly sets Fight Crabs apart from other crab simulators is the dynamic physics system, which makes every battle feel unpredictable and exhilarating. The weight and momentum of the crabs impact their movements and attacks, making strategic positioning and timing crucial for victory. The physics-based combat ensures that battles are always intense, often culminating in frantic clashes that keep players on the edge of their seats.Furthermore, the game offers a wide range of customization options, allowing players to fine-tune their crabs' appearance and abilities, guaranteeing a personalized experience. Additionally, the inclusion of a comprehensive tutorial ensures that both novice and seasoned players can easily pick up the game and enjoy its immersive mechanics.Fight Crabs offers several game modes, including a thrilling single-player campaign and exhilarating multiplayer battles. Whether you prefer competing against AI opponents or challenging friends in local or online multiplayer, there is no shortage of adrenaline-pumping excitement in this game.One aspect that cannot be understated is the incredible attention to detail paid to the crabs' behaviors. From pincer clashes and limb dismemberment to clever tactics like flipping opponents onto their backs, the game showcases the sheer ferocity and complexity of crab combat. This level of authenticity immensely adds to the overall immersion, making Fight Crabs an awe-inspiring experience.In conclusion, Fight Crabs is more than just a crab-fighting simulator; it is a remarkable testament to the creativity and innovation of game developers. With its realistic graphics, complex physics-based combat, intuitive controls, and extensive customization options, Fight Crabs stands head and shoulders above any other game in its genre. Prepare for an epic and unparalleled crab-fighting experience that will leave gamers clawing for more!

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment I started playing, I was hooked. The game was unlike anything I had ever played before. It was fast-paced, action-packed, and filled with excitement at every turn. The premise of the game was simple: you played as a crab, fighting against other crabs in epic battles.At first, I was a bit skeptical. After all, how could a game about crabs possibly be any good? But as soon as I started playing, I knew that I had found something special. The graphics were stunning, the gameplay was smooth and intuitive, and the overall experience was simply mind-blowing.As I played more and more, I realized that Fight Crab had changed my life. I found myself getting more and more immersed in the game, spending hours upon hours battling other crabs and perfecting my skills. I even started dreaming about the game, strategizing in my sleep and waking up ready to dive back into the action.And then there was the community. I had never been much of a social gamer, but Fight Crab changed all of that. I found myself connecting with other players from all around the world, sharing tips and strategies, and forming deep friendships that I never would have thought possible.As I sat down to write this review of the game, I couldn't help but feel emotional. Fight Crab had truly changed my life in ways that I never could have imagined. It was the best game I had ever played, and I knew that it would always hold a special place in my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Hahaha, the controls are bad, but that's part of the fun.  You can use them with practice and control the crab just well enough to beat the crap out of all your opponents.  It is glorious!  The objective is to wound them enough so you can flip them on their back.  The weapons at your disposal are awesome, there is a wide variety.  You can even ride mounts into battle such as scooters or even a seal mount and even use a jousting lance.  My personal favorite is the Sepheroth katana, but others will likely choose something like the Excalibur which has it's own super powers.  Speaking of super powers, if you build up enough damage or hit an opponent enough times you can unlock super moves such as the famous DBZ Kamehameha, or even a Spirit Bomb like attack.The game is just fun, and you can level up your favorite crab and customize it to your play style.  Personally, the Coconut Crab with really high strength tends to be my favorite, but to each their own.  This is hours of fun.  There's even an online coop mode, and you can train and level your own npc to fight alongside you.  The npc is mostly useless but will hold off an opponent long enough for you to come and show them who is boss.This game will provide hours of fun, but you will want to play with a controller because the controls will feel like QWOP at first till you get the hang of them.  Be patient, this game is worth the learning curve.  Do the training several times if you have to, it will help.  It's a fighting game, which means there is a learning curve for mastering moves.  Playing the campaign will provide you with your unlocks, and there are a lot of them!
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

I thoroughly enjoyed this game, and will be recommending it to others.Tl;dr- Came expecting joke game, left with a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 this game has awakened an unexpected side of me. After thrashing scrub crabs online for hours on end I found myself having crustacean dreams. Once I peaked and busted that fattest dream nut of my life I knew there was no going back. I began ordering parts for my crab costume and I now identify as a mud crab. Thanks to this game I have transcended my mere mortal flesh and can often be found lying in wait on a nearby beach or river bed waiting for a worthy foe. Only after I've flipped them on their backs can I achieve peak pleasure. Claws down would recommend for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you going to be able to control this game, like other fighting games?...I do not really know!Each of the crab arms are slightly controlled with both Joy Sticks.  The D pad will control, admitly slowly, where your crab walks. The first Shoulder buttons control "Grab" and "Shield" with the claws. And the 2nd set of shoulder buttons works "Punching" Based on the crab you select the angle of the default placement of your claw changes. The range and how they punch will also change.Crabs colors can be changed though a few choices. The claws can each hold 1 arm weapon's or a single 2 Arm weapon. Few of them are normal and some are quite odd. You can level up your crab stats, and it seems to work but it gets pricey.Overall I think it's somewhat worth it. Might not last that long. _childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: In all my hours of playing Fight Crab, I had a lot of fun just flipping crabs over and stabbing them. There were lots of weapons and crabs to choose from so I wouldn't get bored. However, one complaint I have is right now (at least on the steam version I think) is that you scroll super slowly. However, I believe that this will be fixed soon, because at the time I'm writing this, the game has been out for only a few days. Anyways, I love how the game slowly gets harder as you go, so you don't power through it. This forces you to get better at blocking and moving away in time so you don't get hit as much. The stages look very good and are easy to traverse. I also love the music, especially in the final bosses stage, it really makes things more tense. Overall, I would say Fight Crab is a great game, and I will be sticking around to play more of it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: You shoot kamehamehas and you can get a crab with rocket boosters to clothesline some poor sucker crab into the stratosphere.This is the hypest game of 2020. It needs to become and e-sport. The controls are kinda hard to master, but make a ton of sense once you get used to them. Been playing since the early access for the past year and it's been great.
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: I was already excited for this game when I saw the video that Jameskii made on it, boy was I not prepared for the masterpiece set before me. The combat while tricky to learn is extremely fun to play with. While I have nowhere near mastered it, I intend to play this until I die. The inclusion of many crabs not really talked about in the crab fanbase also makes me happy, since I get to do research on new friends now. I love this game, and it was most likely the best purchase I have made or will ever make.
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: Crustacean physics based fighter. Featuring special moves like "Kanihameha" and wall running. Superb soundtrack by deku really makes you feel like your back is to the boiling pot. Use the physics to your advantage and get bigger swings in or just equip jet engines and rocket your way under your enemies to flip them over. Tonfa are my early weapon of choice for their large area that can do big damage and block most attacks. Having a free claw can be an advantage if you can get it in the right spot to turn the block hold into a damaging flip-grab. The game does benefit from use of a controller but mouse is fine as long as you pay attention to where it's pointing.Honestly, it's worth the cash and cheaper than a lobster dinner.
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: It's a hyper-specific novelty game with clunky controls and confusing gameplay.  But also, you can face down an enemy crab bare-clawed, grab their swords right out of their claws, and then beat them senseless with their own weapons.  You can put a jet-engine on your claws and punch with the force of a careening rocket.  The game is worth.  10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fight Crab

_childDocuments_.review: You can ride a seal while wielding nunchucks in a asteroid field, rocket punch crabs across arenas, and wield excalibur that shoots a massive energy wave.The controls seem complicated at first, but most of the movement and camera work is done for you. DO NOT skip the tutorial on the first level of campaignThe A.I. is surprisingly good. They can even do ridiculous stuff like throw weapons at you and make it bounce back to them so they can grab it in the air and do it again.The different species of crabs actually feel completely different.You can run it on a corn kernel.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Fight Crab. A new 3D action game where you take control of a crab, and fight off other giant enemy crabs. name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Get even more South Park with the 'SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY! Digital Deluxe Edition'. This special edition includes the base game and the Season Pass. This Season Pass includes 6 DLCs in total: All-new game mode All-new ranged weapon and new cosmetics All-new melee weapon and new cosmetics New weapon variation for the Daggers CRED cosmetic pack Asspen cosmetic pack GAME MODE : This all-new Game Mode changes the rules again! Prepare for hellish, new rules and special challenges that make Nichole’s “Infernal Pacts” feel like kindergarten recess. NEW WEAPONS : This season pass includes an all-new Ranged Weapon and an all-new Melee Weapon. The Snowball is perfect for all those who mastered the other ranged weapons in the game. Unleash devastating new attacks on enemies and grant powerful supporting effects on your allies. A new Melee Weapon will be announced later this season. Each new weapon comes with six new upgrade cards and unique cosmetics. NEW WEAPON VARIATION : This Weapon Variation will give the Daggers a devastating overhaul, replacing some of the weapon upgrade cards with crazy new powers that open up completely new play styles and tactics. COSMETICS PACKS : First up is the CRED Cosmetics Pack. A kid today is defined by their hydration drink – and their swag. Impress your friends and show the world how much CRED you have. The CRED Cosmetics pack gives you plenty of CRED with a fresh hairstyle, a CRED hoodie, and a cape. An “Asspen” themed Cosmetic Pack featuring new jackets, hats, and more will be available later this season. About the Game From South Park Digital Studios, the studio that brought you South Park: The Stick of Truth, South Park: The Fractured but Whole, and South Park: Phone Destroyer comes the next chapter in the journey of the New Kid. Join Cartman, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny, in three-dimensional glory, to celebrate the most magical day in any young child’s life - a snow day! A massive blizzard has thrown the town into chaos and, more importantly, canceled school. Play with up to three friends, use matchmaking, or solo the game with ally bots and battle through the snow-piled town of South Park. Engage in frenetic, action-packed combat against warring factions in an all-new story where you make the rules. Equip unique weapons and deploy devastating, upgradable special abilities on a new adventure to save the world and enjoy a day without school. It’s a snow day, dude! Battle your way through the snow-covered town of South Park in this all-new 3D co-op game. A blizzard of epic proportions has blanketed the town of South Park and it’s up to Cartman, Stan, Kenny, Kyle, and you, as the New Kid, to save the town from an endless winter. Experience cooperative gameplay for the first time ever in a South Park game with up to three friends or ally bots - unleashing powerful, coordinated attacks on your foes. Equip and upgrade devastating melee and ranged weapons. Deploy special abilities and powers that will bring hordes of enemies and epic bosses to their knees. Use a wide range of iconic cosmetics and customize your New Kid with endless possible combinations from beanies to Cheesy Poof T-shirts to chin balls.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess i have to start by saying I have been a long time fan of South Park, Matt and Trey.I will say next that this review will not in anyway compare this game to the previous two, as that narrative is stale and overstated. I enjoyed this game for what it was. The levels are pretty long so you could spend 30-40 min on one level depending on the difficulty level, your skill and the cards you have unlocked. The levels change, slightly each run so they feel different and your load-out is editable as well which adds another degree of replay as well. The multiplayer component was fun as well, but not needed for progress and therefore dosen't break the game if you play solo to clean up achievements or grind dark matter.   The comedy is also right up the South Park ally. It was a little tame admittedly, and as everyone has pointed out, short (overall when compared to the last two), but honestly, it made me laugh throughout and it stuck pretty true to characters and environment.  I would like to see maybe 1 or 2 more DLC levels (that would be included in the season pass) of roughly the same length, with some new cards and abilities, like an epilogue or something, but as the game stand right now: It is playable, has fun gaming mechanics, is true to south park genre (making fun of hoarders and poo jokes and being congruent with their television show), made me laugh and different from most of the S*** out there so given the price point, why not eh?

_childDocuments_.review: It's a 5/10. This game is incredibly mediocre.The enemies voice lines are terrible, and incredibly repetitive.The combat is a button mashing nightmare, and it gets boring incredibly fast.The maps go from bad to mediocre.The AI is, you guessed it, bad.There is barely any RPG elements compared to the other games, and all you can get are upgrade cards, that you don't keep after the chapter.The fact, you lose your card at the start of every chapter, and have to hope for a somewhat good card early, to save you from the button mashing.The Story is bad, and almost non-existent.Looting is horrendous.It's only about 5 hours long.The only enjoyable boss, was the second to last boss. The rest of the bosses suffer from a WAY too small room for fighting, or are just plain boring to fight.I really wanted to like this game, I really did, but I just can't. Compared to the other 2 games, this one is so much worse.I can't fathom that I'm saying this, but I miss Ubisoft.I did NOT have high standards, and yet I was still severely disappointedThis should have been a $20 game, not a $30 game.--------------------------------------------------This part might not make sense.The other 2 games, have felt like you were playing an episode of South Park, whereas this just feels like a game set in South Park.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was in support of this game and gave it a thumbs up but now after finishing 3 of the 5 total missions I had to change my review. This game really sucks compared to the first two games. The only thing it has going for it is the graphics. It is really cool seeing all my favorite characters in 3D, and I guess that is a good thing too, since there are plenty of cinematics you have to sit though.The game is super repetitive and so far the most challenging thing I have found is just trying not to fall off the SoDoSoPa tower when the controls cause you do leap forward instead of sprint like you wanted. Kyle was also a pretty challenging boss in the first mission, but other than that, this game is very easy. It's no wonder people have been blowing though it in 2-3 hours and getting their money back. I am taking my time and trying to enjoy it, but maybe I should have done like everyone else because now I just feel like I was ripped off for $50.Make sure you collect all that TP, PP, and DM too, it is super important.... oh wait it isn't. Your TP doesn't even roll over from mission to mission so if you save it up you will lose it. The PP is fine, you can buy clothing with it, but the clothing is meaningless, it doesn't help your stats at all. The DM is OK but the game is so not challenging that you don't really need it. I also hate that there are timers on card selection. I get that this is for people that play with other real life people, but I don't, so why am I being rushed?In the end, this game is just a button smasher with only the simplest of story lines and some cool 3D graphics.... sad. I'm going to go back to plaything the other two games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love third-person action games and you love South Park, chances are you will enjoy this game. It has a lot of stuff it does very well, and a lot of stuff that could be fine tuned. PROS:+ Incredible Writing (solid South Park writing)+ Hilarious (was laughing through the entire game)+ Amazing Voice Acting. Exceptional!+ Solid RPG Game Tree. Who doesn't love a great tree?+ Great Music! Exceptionally great!+ Insane movement options. Action games that give you great movement options? Yes thank you! Easily the most enjoyable part about playing is zipping around enemy to enemy and beating down foes. Just don't pick the axe for a weapon; it doesn't give you a horizontal aerial like the other two weapons do. Having that horizontal aerial move is basically an air dodge. And if you choose the big ole axe, you lose that air dodge. CONS:- Combat feels janky- Fighting Animations are a little weird, and seem incomplete - Lack of SFX. It sounds like the devs just went with their placeholder sound effects and forgot to change them? They are underwhelming and lack that "oomf". Especially with a hacknslash game like this, if the sounds aren't tasty... then idk man. These sounds suck forreal. - Strange Audio Ducking: during combat as you fight the fellow kids in South Park, each time an enemy exclaims (after getting hit), the music and sfx will dip to allow that voiceline to be more audible. Not only is this extremely jarring, but like, the voicelines for the enemies are byfar the weakest in the game. Sounds like they did their classic "ike" type recordings, but whichever kiddos yall had record these lines... these are bad takes. They really give off "I can't be too loud or I'll wake up my parents" type of energy. - Not all weapons feel the same. Some weapons like the two lil daggers feel incredible, while the fire staff, and the axe, feel extremely weird. Can't tell you how many times the firestaff simply didn't deploy the fireballs. The firestaff has the weakest animation too. It's pitiful.- Extremely strange interactions with items. Idk what this is called specifically, but when you're trying to do basic stuff like pick up a 'cannonball' to put it into a cannon, sometimes it'll take you 10 years to find the exact spot to interact with it. Same if you're doing the fetch quests. Picking up and carrying things; is the worst, in this game. - Also, in the "wave" mode via Henrietta, having to endure the entire B.S. mini cutscene, is B.S.. It completely breaks up the momentum of the wave-based combat, as it forces you to watch whatever buff the enemy gets. It comes in at such a weird moment too, like 10 seconds after the wave has begun. So right when you feel like you're getting going, it stops everything. Buzz kill.- In that wavemode it would also be nice to have an enemy counter, so you can see how many baddies you have to take out, and you can just watch the number countdown in a satisfying way.- My final thought is; determining friendly players from badguys is extremely confusing. There needs to be an outline or some kind of discernible feature that separates friendlies from enemies on the battle-field. It's a visual cluster f*** at times. - When you upgrade cards with Henrietta you gotta be able to see the cards in your inventory to make proper decisions.I feel like as the years go on this will become a fine tuned experience. If there is one thing to expect from Matt and Trey, is that they'll grind it out and make it become excellent. But as of right now, as someone who loves South Park, and who loves third party action games.. I just can't recommend it, in it's current state. But what I do know, I'm just a towel.

_childDocuments_.review: South Park Snow Day is such a mixed bag.What they were doing with previous games like Stick of Truth and Fractured but Whole was fantastic!So when I heard there was going to be a new game I was really excited, "Another game like the previous two!"Then when I booted up this game and saw that it was a ROGUE-LIKE I was kinda blindsided.Not that I don't enjoy the game-play, I love rogue-likes!It's the equivalent of being excited for the next Call of Duty and instead of getting an FPS that you expected, you get a Real-Time Strategy game instead.I don't know if it was communicated better in teaser media like videos and/or tweets, maybe I was just oblivious?As a South Park game I gotta rate it like 4/10.As a rogue-like it's a solid 7/10.I still consider it a good game, so overall rating 6/10.They have unfortunately, in recent memory, set the bar very high for this IP of games.-South Park Yelper

_childDocuments_.review: Don't even know what to say. Since it was announced, I already was skeptical with the new 3d style and graphics, but I still believed it would turn into a decent game, since Trey and Matt were in charge of its development. The result was horrendous.      The combat feels bland and the only thing you do is mash the attack button until you drain out the enemey's hp, not to mention that there are only 3 weapons of each type (melee and ranged). The cards mechanic was something I quite liked, I feel if the combat wasn't so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it maybe could've turned into a very dynamic and fun experience, rather than a "let me press the same button for 20 minutes until the level ends" one.     Honestly, I was expecting the graphics to be my biggest disappointment, but surprisingly, it was the thing I most liked about it, I really feel that I could like a 3D SouthPark game if the rest of the game weren't ♥♥♥♥.    Definetly, what ruined this game/experience for me was really the lacking of SouthPark essence. If you compare the jokes, and their "deepness", this game doesn't even come to the other two game's toes. Not to mention the lack of story. I mean, 3-5 hours of gameplay...... REALLY? The previous 2 games had such a good story line that I thought this one would follow as well.... but nope. You can't even call this a storyline, really. I will not spoil it, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've never seen a more rushed and underdevoloped storyline in my entire life.    Last but not least is the way the game is constructed: it really remembers me plants vs zombies garden warfare 2 vibes, where you have a sort of hub and you select the missions and go to certain areas. I mean, this could work? Maybe, for an action/fighting game where the main ideia is not south park, but to use south park content. Imagine what could have been of snow day if it was an open-world 3D RPG. It would "reviving" the essence of the simpsons hit & run. Basically, this "level" styled gameplay it just didn't work out, as the fun side of the other 2 games was that it looked like you were actually in an episode, and this doesn't look nothing like it.     I give it a 4/10, just for the courage to transition from a 2D to a 3D game (and being the best part of it). I don't really think this game is fixable, I hope this served as a lesson to the creators to hit jackpot next opportunity

Also the game run pretty well, make sure you disable the smoothing option to run at higher FPS, I get well over 200 fps on max settings at 1440p Ultrawide. I'm current playing on controller and the controls are pretty simple and easy to go flying around the map pulling off combos and stuff once you get the hand of it, also would recommend re-binding range attack to right trigger as it feels better and can still attach with square or X on controller.TLDR: South Park Vermintide!!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game to play with friends casually. If you were looking for heavy story like in the previous South Park games, you aren't going to get that here. What you are going to get is a fun co-op PVE Experience with a South Park Theme to share with your friends. The combat feels polished, and while there currently are only 6 weapons in the game, as you play your mission you get abilities that allow you to customize your play style each run through, adding to the replay-ability. It's a refreshing take on a PVE co-op game. It also has a great foundation to build upon, if they choose to do so.Most negative reviews that I've seen seem to have come in with an expectation based on previous games of what they were expecting from this game. Where the past games were story driven and single player, this game diverges as a co-op action game, which is probably the main driver for their dislike of the game. _childDocuments_.review: I tried so hard to like this game. I really did. I went in with an open mind, knowing it would be completely different from the past two games that I loved. But I just really did not enjoy it. I could only play one chapter at a time before getting annoyed and stopping because I was just not having fun. Most of the gameplay is just spam clicking and doing the same thing over and over with pretty much no strategy, which is just not my thing. I can imagine someone who likes these types of games having some fun, but as a huge South Park fan I was let down by the story and writing. I let out a laugh here and there, but mostly just sat there blank face during the dialogue trying to force myself to care about what was going on. It's really easy to guess where each chapter is heading and what will happen.The lack of characters was really disappointing. The show is well known for it's large cast of characters, even the smallest characters are someone's favorite. And yet hardly any of them were utilized, even those who were featured heavily in the past two.  It used to be exciting to see your favorites pop up in different scenes from the last two, but really don't get your hopes up, they kept character inclusion bare bones, which makes sense considering how little goes on in the game.Speaking of, why are there only 5 chapters for $30? It makes the story feel so rushed, which is crazy because there barely was any. I'm really hoping something interesting happens in a future update, but I doubt we'll get any more chapters or another story. I'll play it if we do, but if they try to sell it as DLC I won't be. There were a few positives for me personally that I'll talk about now. I really liked my hat. It was a banana, it wiggled when I moved, it brought me joy. I also liked the Intro 2D cutscene up until the game started and I remembered I was not watching a new episode and was in fact about to play a 3D south park game.Speaking of my banana hat, there are so few cosmetics and customization from the past games, which is one of the few things I can't understand why they wouldn't add more of. Barely any clothes in the character creation menu, then when you can buy clothes there are very few, and the amount does not increase as you play. So if none of that bothers you go ahead and play it, I really hope you have a different experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Please check out my full review here: Following on from the success of Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole, South Park Snow Day is a dramatic departure from the turn based RPG system and instead ops for a 3D Hack & Slash Co-op Roguelike. Whilst this could have been an opportunity for a fun new way to interact with your favourite characters, Snow Day fails to impress offering little in the way of innovative gameplay, and restraining the crude and mischievous charm of the up to no good 4th graders we have grown to love. Question and THQ Nordic wanted to try something different with the series and while I can’t fault them for trying, I also can’t justify the $60 AUD price tag or let alone the $90 AUD for the special edition which comes with the season pass. Don’t bother convincing your schoolmates to party up and jump into this, better off staying in class and getting an early start on your homework.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a South Park fan for what feels like forever, so don't think of this as a hate to South Park, or to the game, but my personal opinion of the game, as a person with almost 100 hours in FBW and a good 30 in Stick of Truth, I hope I can help shed some light on the differences of this game.Gameplay: 4/10The gameplay is pretty mid if I'm going to be honest, I know it takes time to really let a game grow, but for now, I rate it a 4 just because there isn't any special gameplay. Unlike FBW or SOT, you have no special powers besides the fart escape, health totem, and all the others, which I didn't even switch out the basic powers as every good few minutes I'd have to heal like crazy because it's just boringly difficult to go through your first time, there isn't much tactic in the game. In FBW, you need to learn when to use ur special abilities, who to add in your party and what abilities are best against your enemies, in SNOW DAY, you are button mashing and farting a couple times.Story/Lore: 1/10I'm not gonna lie, after playing FBW, this game felt so EMPTY, like for one..WHERE IS CRAIG X TWEEK?? And also, where is the beauty of the last two games? There's no side missions, no 'open world' map, you can't explore and find fun things, you are bound to 3 or 4 lines of dialog per character, and then the only story you get is in the 5 missions you have for the WHOLE game, it was extremely boring to go through since it just had such a bland story, I really didn't enjoy the fact that there was just nothing to do besides kill a bunch of enemies and listen to Cartman make a joke about you breaking the game again, which can't even happen cause guess what? There isn't more to the game! Worth what you paid: 2/10Unless you're a die hard South Park fan that needs to have every ounce of merch, games, shows, and movies of the game, YOU SHOULDN'T BUY IT. It really is worth half of what the selling price is (at the moment 30), and there isn't barely anything you can do, all you're seeing is a bunch of 3D versions of a small cast of characters, button mashing, and a lack of any relative or interesting story, the only good things you get is a cool dino hat and you get to fart. It really wasn't worth the moneyTime: 0/10SOT felt short, but you did have a vast majority of things to do with a interesting story and fun gameplay, FBW is the Fallout 4 or Fallout New Vegas of all the fallout games, perfect timing, side missions, fun gameplay, you really can't put it down, plus it has really fun dlcs! And WAY more cosmetics then SNOW DAY or SOT, eitherways, you can finish this game in less then 4 hours if you really wanted to. This game felt fast and honestly, I felt like if I just played the Captain Crunch DLC for FBW it would take up the same amount of time as this whole game did. The whole time I played, I told myself; "once I finish these 5 main missions it might open new things! Maybe even side missions!" but all it opens is some Nichole stuff...like, there really isnt much more to doEnemies: 1/10The only one I actually enjoyed going against was the final battle, it was a LITTLE fun, if you're playing with friends then I don't doubt it would be way more chaotic, but for me a singleplayer person, the bots suck crap and died immediately, to the point where I just left them and fought on my own, the enemies are not hard and they are just boring and easy to kill. along with the random BullSh*ts that really aren't that scary, and just another boring addition.Graphics: 3/10 They really could've stuck with the 2D, not saying I hate the 3D but it really didn't need all this extra stuff, if I'm going to be honest, the 3D made it look funky and weird, all of the characters look kinda gross, especially with their dark matter eyes, and it's just not the best looking game, it just doesn't fit a South Park game and I actually was very excited to see how the 3D world would look for the town but..was disappointed to find out that we were only going to see so little. Conclusion: 4/10Definitely not worth your money or your time, in the end, just by Fractured But Whole, and a couple DLCS, because honestly, playing this game feels like a chore, and it is actually very disappointing considering that everyone had high hopes for the game. I especially felt disappointed when I killed the final boss and thought "now I can unlock more!" only to be met with the end credits of the game. Please play one of their other games as this game is just not worth all of the time and tears, go have fun doing something else that is way more story related! My rating for FBW is a 9.5/10 (the .5 being how difficult some of the bosses are but that's it) PLAY IT INSTEAD. PLAY IT RN.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't look at this game thinking you are getting an RPG with permanent progression on your character and tons of loot. You need to look at this game like its a Left 4 Dead clone with some interesting tweaks.You are able to choose 1 of 3 melee weapons, 1 of 3 ranged weapons, 2/8 skills, and have random buffs added to each gameplay to constantly change it up. There is a currency which allows you to gain permanent upgrades like movement speed, health, damage, card rarity%, etc. With that out of the way, it is really good for what it is. More chapters can be easily added along with more skills and weapons in the future. The additional game mode locked behind DLC seems a little off putting, but devs will be devs.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. The story and jokes are what shine but in between those parts, ya know the actual gameplay, its very meh.It is kind of like Vermintide, in the sense of the melee combat, go through stages, kill waves of enemies, do an objective, with a taste of slight randomness with the card system of upgrades.My main issue is that there really isn't a lot of feedback on the actions you do. You can attack people, get attacked, and it doesn't really feel like you are making any impact. You have to look out for the damage numbers, healing numbers, health bars etc to see if things are actually working. I have had several times where I try to activate an ability that just didn't go through cause I was finishing a different animation, but I wouldn't really know if the ability happened because, there really is no difference besides specifically looking for the animation to happen.Using an ability for 20 damage feels like it has the same impact as a normal attack that does ~8. The health bar barely goes down, you really have to wail on people a bit so even if you use the ability you don't notice the bar goes down much. Getting low on health, you have to watch your health bar, its hard to tell when you are getting hit yourself.Mostly the gameplay is run around and spam click, and just wait for people to die, use abilities when you can, and then move on. I guess if you are looking for a chill thing to play and not really take seriously to enjoy, its not bad. But you don't have the story to carry the gameplay like the other games did.

_childDocuments_.review: I can agree with majority that the game doesn't have a lot of content, but I don't think it's such a bad game, especially considering the fact that most modern games are $69 and this game costs twice less. But despite lack of content, I still think this is a good game. It has fun and challenging game play (I suggest playing the game on hard), with variety of enemies that forces you to think about how you play and make you create strategies, fun bosses, cool skills and bonuses for them. I really like balancing system that makes you start at your weakest state in beginning of level and build your character up as you progress. I do think the 3D cutscenes are pretty good and keep up with South Park vibe. They are fun to watch and its cool to see familiar characters been 3D. It's boring to play the game alone, but if you have a friend or better a group of friends, I think this is a fun game to play together for few evenings. I wouldn't recommend buying it right now, but I think its a great game to get on sale. I really hope developers won't abandon the game and will release more content. Also the game is pretty much bug free, maybe I haven't played enough but I still haven't encountered a single bug.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love South Park. The two previous games (Stick of Truth, Fractured but Whole) were also really great. Both rich in story, primary content and a lot of side content/quests. I get that Snow Day, tries to engage you in multiplayer content, which is of course a plus. Aside from that though, the game seems very repetetive with minimal to do, no side content, collectables, etc. whatsoever. A bit of a repeat of previous comments but I would only ever recommend this game to people who first of all intend to always play multiplayer and secondy just want to semi mindlessly bash buttons in a more action-centric combat style. Here's to hoping that the next games will be continuations of Stick of Truth / Fractured, game play wise, content wise; and so on. Trying out new things is great. This format does not work for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty awful. Pros: - The game runs well. I do not meet the recommended specs listed but the game defaulted to ultra and I havent noticed any framerate issues.- The game looks nice. Granted I do not think that it's very graphically intensive (it looks like it could've been a PS3 game if im honest).Cons:- I genuinely don't think the game was bug tested. TWICE I was thrown out of the map by something, getting stuck on the scenery, meaning I could not move and just had to quit the level.- Your AI teammates just plain don't work. For example, at the end of the stan mission, you have to traverse the roof tops to get to him. One of my teammates needed reviving. I walk over to him. I revive him. He gets his 5ish seconds of invincibility before instantly dying again. Great. Now I have to complete the level with 2 teammates if I don't want to quit and start over. At one stage, you get catapulted to the other side of the road to make your way across those buildings. This would be fine (albeit pretty blatantly just a way of dragging out the level longer) if your team actually followed you. One of my teammates was stuck on the other side of the map. At this point I just closed the game.- The gameplay is simply just boring. It's repetitive. I understand the game is a hack and slash. That's fine. But that mixed with the fact that moving feels like you're trudging through mud and the game just doesn't feel satisfying to play honestly just makes it a drag. If a hack and slash game is what you're after, there are definitely better and far cheaper options. - I saw another review calling this a '£30 mobile game' and honestly, I couldn't agree more. This would feel right at home on the app store for £3, on an iPad so a kid could just mindlessly press the screen for a few hours. However, it does not cost £3. It is not on an iPad. It is on steam. It is £25. £40 if you spring for the 'dIgItAl dElUxE EdItIoN'. Side note - the fact that there's DLC day one really just feels scammy. I know over time it has become common practice, but that doesn't make it feel any different. - Finally, there's just a glaring lack of content. 5 levels? This genuinely feels like it could've been thrown together in a few weeks. I actually hope this was just a game that was already made and South Park Studios just bought the rights to make it South Park themed. At least then there could be an excuse as to why its so boring.It's really a shame, I remember seeing the trailer for the game months ago and was actually excited for the game to come out. Hopefully DLC that comes out can actually save the game, because if this is how it sits permanently it's going to be a real stain on the South Park franchise (not like the games pre Stick of Truth weren't already bad enough).I really hope that this game can be redeemed, but I don't hold out a lot of hope..

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first two South Park games (Stick of Truth and Fractured but Whole). This game is a hack and slash ARPG where you really dont get stronger outside of cards that you can only use two of and then the upgrades to them vanish. Then the computer gets to also use cards like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (which you get to) but they always seem to choose resurrection, stuff like invisible enemies. Then you will hit parts where you have to do defeat the waves that go on way too long, even more so if they get to resurrection their forces. When you attack with melee, you are always moving forward. So ability to just stand there and hit an enemies that dont have that same mechanic. So if you have one on an edge, you will most likely fall off and have to make your way back up to them. Why cant devs just let us move with attacking by pressing move in a direction? Instead it has to be you move forward no matter what.  Then there is the slowing issue due to snow and ice, but there is an upgrade that you can get to handle that, but it take a while. The game is good looking and I can buy the 3D designs of the characters as they keep the the spirit of how they look in the show. _childDocuments_.review: Hi. as a big fan of south park (games and tv-show), this DM comes from a place of love. i recently purchased the snow day game and really enjoyed the concept of the story and the fact that its a 3d-game. BUT you guys have left so much behind that could make the game better, and keep players in for a long time, vs a short story. FIrst, we got to talk about PVP. there are so many other game modes that can be made for this kind of fighting game like 4 teams of 4 battling out for time to get most kills. you can do elves vs other team in a CS:GO style where the bomb is a stink bomb, a MOBA-like gamemode, a team deathmatch, special boss raid events vs famous characters from the series like manbearpig etc. rewards can be dark matter and special event costumes, weapon skins etc. when it comes to weapons, you could increase the number of weapon costumization options. the weapons dont need to have more effects of boosts, but like having a dildo as a main weapon or a tampon gun for ranged weapon. this was a cool thing in the other games, and its a bummer that you left it behind. kind of like skins in CS:GO, they look cool, but dont give any effects. being able to costumize your new kid in many ways is also good, but weapons would be my #1 wish. hope you guys take this into consideration, as it would keep the game alive longer, build a community around the game, esp around boss raid events. another thing would be to add more maps with the different game modes. have famous locations from south park feature as a part of the battle arena like the school backyard, inside different famous buildings etc.

_childDocuments_.review: "South Park: Snow Days" is like being invited to the world's most irreverent snowball fight, where the gloves are off, and so is any semblance of political correctness. Imagine every character you love (and love to hate) armed with nothing but their wits and an arsenal of icy projectiles, in a game that's more unpredictable than Mr. Garrison's career choices. The graphics? Let's just say they're as refined as Cartman's dining habits, which is to say, charmingly crude. The gameplay is as smooth as Butters on a good day, which means you're in for a hilariously bumpy ride. Whether you're dodging a barrage of snowballs or the show's trademark satirical barbs, this game guarantees belly laughs and maybe a few frostbitten fingers. In the end, "South Park: Snow Days" is the perfect game for fans who like their winters cold and their humor colder. Remember, it's all fun and games until someone ends up in a "Oh my God, they killed Kenny!" scenario.

_childDocuments_.review: While South Park: Snow Day! retains some of the franchise's signature charm amidst its mediocre graphics and subpar controls, it falls short in many areas.Considering its current price point and lack of substantial content, I cannot in good conscience recommend purchasing it at full retail price. The game begins to hit its stride just as it nears its conclusion. Despite promises of future content updates, fundamental issues persist that cannot be remedied through mere patches. For a game centered on hack-and-slash mechanics, its execution is among the poorest I've encountered in recent memory. The combat mechanics lack weight, with hits feeling unsatisfying due to a lack of sound cues and an inability to chain attacks effectively.Furthermore, the AI teammates, essential for solo play, are virtually useless. They frequently find themselves incapacitated, often positioned far from the player character, and fail to assist in obtaining necessary items to progress. While playing with friends or random players can marginally improve the experience, at best, it feels like polishing a turd.Perhaps, the real ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ card was this game all along.

I didn't have great expectations for this game since it felt so different from the others, but gave it hope since it was South Park.I am disappointed overall with the game. The fact that I feel like I am 3 hours in and almost done with game leaves a bad taste in my mouth. The combat system is fun for sure but the lack of lock on or attacks that can miss incredibly easily without direct aim make it feel clunky and sometimes unsatisfying. While the story is funny in it's South Park layered comedy, the fact it's so short on launch makes me want 20 dollars back with the promise of more DLC with extra chapters and more weapons/cards. I'll finish the game and see what the DLC is like from my friends or influencers, but I am not sure what to expect coming up next and hope they continue to improve this game for free or as little charge as possible to make it a true addition to the South Park game franchise. Get it if you wanna, but it's ok rn.

_childDocuments_.review: Was worried about the reviews but please dont listen to them if your interested. Being a die hard South Park fan since the beginning I think they did an awesome job and its not as shallow as people are making it seem. To be fair Ive loved every South Park game, including the ones people consider "bad" that could be why Im loving this right now. It honestly gives me vibes from the 1998 South Park 64 doom shooter mixed with 4 player co-op feel of South Park Let's Go Tower Defense Play! but with Rogue-Lite power up unlocks and a Perk System, decent amount of Cosmetic unlocks too. Im also playing the game on Hard which is making it pretty challenging tbh. The card system is pretty cool, closest thing I can compare it too would be the cards in Fallout 76 for your SPECIAL perks but different for every "run". I got downed about 12-15 times before finally dying about halfway into Chapter 1, I really hope it keeps that challenge going forward into the game, it makes the rogue aspect of it a lot more fun. I havent played multiplayer yet which im hoping to in the next few days after I get a bit more into the game. On that note this is the first time Ive seen a "No Spoiler" option for when your matchmaking, which is a great idea.     I really hope they add more content over time and keep going with it, its been awesome seeing the characters in 3D again like the oldschool game, a lot of fun and definitely recommend to South Park fans, worth the price forsure12 - 13 hours later Edit: Gets old quick, had a lot of potential but missed it, still enjoyed the initial playthrough, worth playing for cheap, bummer in the end, couldve did a lot with this one

_childDocuments_.review: While this game isnt really my cup of tea, I still like it so far.Im a much bigger fan of all the checkpoints, offensive humor, and how strategic the other game was but I think this game has some interesting rules. The cards are a fun and unique addition to this game, and having to hit the enemies is a good idea to get players to fight.Okay, now im going to get into my personal experience playing this game.When I first loaded it up the first thing I noticed was how slow and laggy it was! This isnt much of a surprise since my computer definitely isnt made for gaming, and in order to be able to enjoy a game I have to turn the resolution all the way down. This isnt the game's fault, but I thought it was worth mentioning.Once I started the initial cut scene, I realized that the audio and video wasn't playing at the same time! Fortunately, the cut scene only establishes that theres a really bad snowstorm, school is canceled, and Cartman is going out to play. I already knew all of that!The options to customize you character is pretty limited, but im pretty sure you can buy more stuff from Tweek and Craig so its not an issue. The actual game play is interesting. As I mentioned before, I had to turn my resolution all the way down. The thing is, the cards are in 3D which means I cant see them clearly. It takes me FOREVER to read what they say, and it doesnt help that Jimmy is yelling at me to hurry up. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards are also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I could be almost done with a wave, but then they'll use a card and make all the enemies alive again. Its so annoying!The bots also drive me crazy! If they were real people, I would yell at them so much I would lose my voice. They NEVER do what I want them to, and it would be better to find some friends (I dont want to though because im shy, so bots it is!). Im REALLY bad at these types of games, and it doesnt help that im an angry person in general. I barely got halfway through the first level on medium, so I guess this is my opinion as somebody who isnt great at these kinds of games.Despite all the negative things I said, I still think this game is fun and DEFINITELY will take over 5 hours for me to complete. Its probably not worth $30, but if it gets updated then maybe. If you aren't a South Park fan or not a fan of this genre, wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Negatives:-Game is Incredibly Short, Campaign can be completed in 3-4 Hours.-Wish there was more replay ability to each stage.-There is limited build varity in the game with the current weapons available and most people I played with online seemed to run the same weapons and powers. -Side Characters dont offer much in this game, Randy in particular is just shoehorned in to the story by cutscenes. When he mentioned Scotch has all the TP thought there could be a raid like mission with Randy!Positives:-The Updated Models and Environments to 3D i thought worked well, Didn't take away from characters and lended new depth to the town and sets the scale of the snow storm as entire buildings are snowed in.- The Interactions with the Main Boys had good humour that was expected going into the game. Paladin Butters as the Rules Lawyer for the game was Great and having Henrietta as a card dealer was nice to see the Goths get represented!-Messing with the in game Powers and Weapons there are some unique synergies you dont see to often which I highly recommend if playing with a group. The Gravity Orb and Chees-It powers combined can make a large amount of brainwashed to fight along side you. Or if you like a range build Turrent and Drone make for a fun combo.Alot of Reviews compare this to the Previous games Stick of Truth and Fractured Butt Whole, and it is hard not to seperate this entry from them. Game May have worked better if it didn't continue the new kid story and was released as a South Park Arcade style game which would make sense at the price point of the standard version. Worth buying if your a long term fan of the series or if it is on offer. But other than that can't recommend this one

_childDocuments_.review: "South Park: Snow Day" delivers the excitement of an actual snow day... if you spent it doing chores. In a bewilderingly PG turn, it's as if South Park went on a field trip and left its humor at home. 🌨️Give it a few hours and the main story is complete, this game ends quicker than Cartman's diet plans, lacking the series' punch. It's got cool powers and stuff, if you're into the thrill of finding loose change under the couch.It's as lonely as Butters in the rejection corner. Diving into 3D, THQ Nordic apparently thought, "Hey, let's give them less of what they love!" Stripping away the rich narrative and humor and gameplay, is like going to Casa Bonita and only getting to eat the napkins. 🌮As for the price? Picture Cartman selling "raffaele ronca's cheesecake" memberships—overpromised and underdelivered. Could've used a price chop or, wild idea, content that screams South Park."South Park: Snow Day" feels like getting novelty underwear for Christmas—sure, it covers the essentials, but where's the fun in that? Hopefully, DEVS catches on that we're in it for the cheeky thrills, not just to keep our bits from freezing. 🩲❄️
