_childDocuments_.review: The game has too little content and outright feels shallow in depth of the content it does have. Wait till either free-updates (None planned to my knowledge) or a massive sale goes on to even try it. Otherwise, not even for the base price of $30. The deluxe edition/season pass is definitely not worth it, even with stuff planned currently.I got this game in good faith of the two previous games, stick of truth, and fractured but whole. I really enjoyed those two and was curious about this one. I do like the "Rouge-like" Coop Mission based game-play, akin to old gauntlet dark legacy game and other quick level beat em ups.But where this game quickly falls apart, and the worst offender in my opinion is the  3 Melee Weapons, 3 Ranged Weapons, 8 Skills (2 at a time), and roughly 4 Perks per weapon/skill as you upgrade through a run. With Quick Math, you can try every combo within 252 runs. But skills/weapons perks/abilities do not interact with each other, so by run 6 or 8, you can probably already find what works best and stick with that and only that.And the story/length, that is the next major issue. 5 Levels with essentially 3 middle pieces that can inter-change for run differences. Or 4 levels with that ability, and a single area climb for the final level. The levels are beautiful, but the the replay-ability is just- not worth going through a 2nd time, unless you are attempting to 100% the game. I get there is a theme/world design of 'Snow-agedon' but having a legit pallet of only white wears on you fast. There isn't an open world, only a hub and its levels, so you cannot explore south park as a town in 3D, which sucks, but not holding it against the game. I will say it sucks to only see areas and not actually explore them like previous games.Writing. That's the next problem in my book bellow the things said above. There isn't any edge, there isn't any of the iconic south park jabs, there isn't any thing that makes me think of south park writing other than the names of the characters. The closest things we get to south park humor and writing is cartman calling kyle a 'Dru', and Uncle Jimbos Fetch-Quest, but even then it feels like... How can I put it? Scrubbed from anything too offensive and meets the simplest of terms of what a jab is? The writing isn't there for me.I bought the deluxe edition of the game, not gonna return it, but I definite do not recommend it in it's current state. Looking at the Season Pass, I don't have much hope for that either. 1 Named Ranged Weapon, 1 Unnamed Melee Weapon, and some updates to the daggers, along with cosmetics throughout the year (Up to October). In my opinion, this game is going to die out within a or two months if new content isn't added for free, and the wait for the full 'Season Pass' is just- too long for such little content.If you want to buy the game, wait for a sale. I'd say this game is worth $10 dollars in its current state (Base game), and maybe $15 dollars for the whole deluxe edition once everything comes out in october. I was just thoroughly let down by the lack of content and writing. I still truly hope it gets free updates through the year, but that is my only saving grace on changing my recommendation for this game, and even then I have to try out the hypothetical free content anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: For a fan who has played both Stick and Fractured, it is definitely a big change to what I'm used to.I've beaten the main story in normal mode at the time of this review, have 13 achievements, and yes, I have the STD. Socially Transmitted, that is.The game is pretty fun for what it is. I'm biased, partially because I got the game as a belated Birthday Gift, and also because I'm really into the show. I'm going to actually split up this review.- For those who like Stick Of Truth...This game is fine. It's got the characters playing their DND esque characters, but you don't get to play as said characters at any point. In Stick, it wasn't heavily emphasised for the fact you played with the characters, and instead formed itself on the creative way you could change or impact the story by picking elves or humans. It had an alright mode of combat, it wasn't too long (My first playthrough only took me some hours), and the story was somewhat intriguing. It was the first South Park game that really took off with its own story and plans, and has its charms. With that said, what is improved upon in both games is the combat, which unless you really liked how Stick played, that is a HUGE upgrade.- For those who like Fractured Butt WholeThe game is really a big shift from what you're used to if you're going into Snowday. In Fractured, the Customization has a bigger impact on your character, and not just talking about the Skin tone joke that everyone has seen. All clothing have stats, like in Stick, but as well as that, you collect MULTIPLE powers, allowing for your character to have so many outcomes. The story changes based off of your powers, your actions, blah blah... and said story, while its sometimes harder to follow, gives not only your character so much power, but gives us insight to the other characters in ways we didn't see before in just the base game. You see how Tweek and Craig work, you see how Kenny's alter-ego works with the other characters, you see much more with having to decide between which parent you love more. It's a genuinely interesting point, and again, like the original Stick, you get to play alongside the other characters. MORE of the characters too! While in Stick you only get to pick one buddy at a time, in Fractured, you get three at a time that cannot be switched during battle. Interesting.Now how do these two comparisons fall into place for Snowday?Snowday is in 3D obviously. A lot of people have ripped on it, but SouthPark isn't exactly made to be in 3D. With that said, it does well! I personally had a really noticable glitch however visually in every cutscene, PRESUMABLY because of my colour blindness settings. I've never had this problem before, but the colours and the lighting will flicker and change between every shot, and its really distracting.Otherwise, the visual art of the game, while sometimes the lighting can meld together really weird, the game is appealing, and I don't get a majority of the visual complaints besides "its not like Southpark." The opening cutscene in particular was a really nice transition!Audio wise, I found in my playthrough that there were some moments where without subtitles, I would not know what characters were saying, even in cutscenes! The mixing sometimes comes off as odd, where Cartman seems too quiet when yelling at Stan, or where Butters' voice sounds oddly far away, or where Kyle's speech is quiet AND only in the right ear, when that doesn't make sense visually. This again, might just be a problem for me.Playing wise, the game isn't too hard to grasp. I like the controls, minus the [Z] for emoting, but that's literally fine. Plus, you can change your Keybinds. There were a lot of times however where when I was swinging or aiming, or even switching between weapons, that it wouldn't charge up a shot, or charge an attack. This was even if I wasn't playing with other players.Multiplayer; I wish there was a communication feature, not too dissimilar to Splatoon. The reason I bring Splatoon as comparison being, they're compact, and they give you options that are ambiguous to situations at times. A simple "This way!" can mean a lot of things in a competitive shooter, but in a 4 player game, it's pretty obvious. "This way! We need you to move forward!" It'd be a time saver for sure. And yes, while you could say the new kid being the silent type contridicts this; just make it a pop up with a ding sound.Just an idea.Oh and yes, STD achievement comes from Multiplayer.Multiplayer otherwise just sometimes has glitches, or lag, or there's just nobody hosting, but if you host nobody joins. It's a weird cycle I've gone through at times and I can't really find the issue.Finally the Story.Story wise, it didn't make sense to me that the New Kid from the first game, was the same as the second game, and also this third game? I was under the assumption that the New Kid from Stick and Fracture were different new kids? Maybe I missed something while playing Stick and Fracture where they said that? It didn't click with me regardless. The Story with a majority of the characters feels rather brushed over. There were A LOT of Cutscenes in both Stick and Fracture, that would connect your character into the other characters' lives, so you would feel guilt in say, siding with the Elves, or siding with the Humans, or beating your first ever friend up, or having Cartman turn on you, or even just having your buddy die. There was a sense of guilt and consequence. In Snowday, the story is oddly disconnected from you as a player. You complete the quests in any way and the story goes on. There's a lack of any idea that your character connects to the other characters. In scenes after you've beat up the other characters, the only time they ever interact with you is if you fart on them. You can interact with Tweek and Craig, or Tolkien even feels more connected, and they will talk to you.With those at the table, the main four all talk amongst themselves, and in cutscenes, the only time they talk to your character is to tell them to do something. This is after having no time to actually interact with them as characters instead of beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of them in a boss battle.I admittedly play South Park games for the characters. Yet, it oddly enough doesn't feel like these Characters or their growth are even here, when we as the player character just sort of see the cutscenes happen and then go back into slicing and dicing.The game isn't terrible, it's not great either. I'm giving it a good, but I beat its main story and don't really feel anything about it. Not even disappointment just a weird sense of "what did I just play?" The final cutscene is  the most emotion I felt to the characters, but it wasn't really anything interesting for me. The ending cutscene doesn't have our player character at all, doesn't have our main four characters really learn anything besides they were wrong, and also they like the snowdays because it brings them together as friends.This game could have done more if it let us play as the other characters possibly. It could have done more if the levels were more interesting. It could have done more if the story had more than Randy showing up for toilet paper while the kids fight over who has better rules. Which by the way, fighting about the rules is barely anything in the actual story, because it ends up being DM that is the problem. We don't really resolve the conflict, the conflict just leaves for Mr. Hankey to take the stage.So yeah, I wrote a personal opinion essay in a review.Should you buy the game? Not sure, because my ass did not.Would I have bought the game otherwise? I don't think I would have.Enjoy your time that you've got with this game. I did enjoy the six hours I've already played to beat the game, just not enough to really play it again, or play it more to get achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever you do, don’t go into South Park: Snow Day! expecting more of the same.   The same here being a sequel both narratively and mechanically to the franchise’s two excellent turn-based RPG adventure entries to come out in the last ten years. Instead, like most childhood snow days, South Park: Snow Day! is a flurry of high-intensity action that leaves you and your friends (if you have any) exhausted yet ends sooner than you wish it did.  Gone are the expansive, detail-stuffed, living episode story campaigns that made The Stick of Truth (2014) and The Fractured but Whole (2017) so fun to explore and unpack, replaced instead by five multiplayer ARPG missions, most of which are really just a series of wave-based arenas broken up by gates that unlock after you kill every. last. everything. Die and it’s back to the beginning, though, as with most modern rougelites, you’ll keep some currencies you can use to improve your individual stats for the next run. Whereas prior South Park entries focused on exploring the iconic titular town and interacting with its many unhinged inhabitants, Snow Day! is unapologetically a straightforward button-masher that’s only on occasion broken up by fairly low-effort fetch quests or environmental hazards you’ll need to blast your way through.  Now, if you’re a long-time fan and feeling a little low after this intro, chin up! There’s still a lot to enjoy about Snow Day, as it’s still very much an entry in the South Park saga. Most of the town’s usual suspects are on display here, and watching Stan, Kyle, Kenny, and Cartman bicker in crisp 3D cutscenes about their respective fantasy kingdoms and their liberal interpretations of Butters’ rulebook is endlessly entertaining. Well, not endless, I suppose, as one consequence of adding a dimension to the animation is subtracting from the story’s total runtime. I zipped through Snow Day’s enjoyable if unremarkable plot in about six hours (not sure why Steam says four), well short of the franchise’s prior story-heavy entries, and much of that time was spent grinding through trash mob after trash mob.   Luckily, the combat system itself is pretty fun. You’ll start each run after selecting from a handful of melee and ranged weapons, picking a couple of utility skills that are tied to your “Pissed Off!” adrenaline meter, and then choosing between several global “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” cards, like bubble shields or meteor showers, that can quickly turn the tide of a battle. I spent most of my runs wielding the gap-closing dual daggers, an elemental wand, an AOE healing totem that can help revive downed allies, and this putrid cat urine spray ability that temporarily flips baddies to your team. At the end of each arena, Jimmy will offer you an upgrade card that you can further buff if you slip him a toilet paper bribe, because people’s priorities change during an endless snowstorm, ya know? At the end of each mission—each of which gets you closer to unearthing the mysterious cause of this apocalyptic snowstorm—you’ll face a boss, one of whom is a secret character the publisher explicitly told me not to mention. These boss fights deliver mechanical depth, challenge, humor, and spectacle, and each combines with Snow Day’s above-average soundtrack to make for a memorable end to each mission.  Before wrapping up, I’ve seen some allegations swirling about Steam forums that this game is a microtransaction-riddled hellscape, and I can happily report that that’s not the case. While the multiplayer-oriented Snow Day! is a big shift for South Park Digital Studios, I completed the game without spending a dime, and only once did the game tease some optional DLC my way. As the matchmaking servers were down while recording my pre-release review, I also got through the game just fine on my own, unless you count the auto-fill bots that seamlessly join your empty party at the start of combat encounters.  In the end, Snow Day! fails to live up to the lofty standards set by The Stick of Truth and The Fractured but Whole, but it’s still a fun, funny little time that mostly justifies its $30 price tag. I’m giving Snow Day! an aggregate MEGA score of 3.21/5 (full scoring breakdown, from Plot to Sound, available in video form) and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review.

_childDocuments_.review: If you come into this expecting another Stick of Truth or Fractured But Whole, you will be very disappointed.That being said, I really like whats here, but I also understand the "mixed" rating the game has. Its not trying to be either of those games, its trying to be something different, and I really do appreciate the effort to make something different rather than making the same game for the third time. This is a level-based, action rpg with a focus on combat over story, and it does this pretty well.I feel that this is a great starting point for a much larger game. As it stands, there are 5 chapters in the game, and once that's done, you've experienced all the story this game has to offer, but there is some ounce of replayability within these 5 chapters. Segments are randomly selected from a few options of locations, each with its own enemy placement and variety. The levels are very nice renditions of popular South Park locations, but as this is "Snow Day" everything is covered in snow, which makes the levels blend together in a rather disappointing sort of way, it makes them feel same-y.The story is funny, a continuation of the New Kid's adventures with Stan, Kyle, Cartman, Kenny and Butters. Other popular characters, such as Tolkien, Tweek, Craig, Clyde, and even Henrietta and Nichole make appearances, with some segments of the game revolving around helping some of the adult characters, like Randy, Ned and Jimbo. But THATS IT! There are almost no other characters that are remotely involved in the story, or even make an appearance.I was disappointed by the lack of single-player support. You can play offline with 3 bots, but this makes the game SIGNIFICANTLY harder. They really push for you to play levels with other players, much like a "Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance" experience.I think there's more to come with this game after the dlc for the season pass has released, and I do look forward to that, and the game itself at the base level is only $30, I paid $50 for the digital deluxe edition, which I feel i got my money's worth. I also purchased the $220 Collector's Edition for PS5, and I think the quality of items was really high, but not really worth $220, I feel $150 would be a more appropriate price point for that edition.All in all, I really like this game, its a great experience with friends, and I will continue playing it until I reach 100%, but am definitely going back to playing SoT and FBW for the 10th+ time afterwards.

It would have so much more potential if it was more of an open world like the other games. There was a lot of potential that could have been put in this but did not happen.Its lacking of jokes- I cannot tell how much South Park isn't South Park without the jokes. Even Randy didn't say much interesting. Wich makes me come to the voice acting's.The Voice acting's sounds like they didn't want to make them, they repeat themselves a lot and there is no energy whatsoever put in the voice acting's. I also want to point out that every single elementary child's NPC sound like kindergarten kids. Another element of the game that felt a bit out of place is the random NPCs known as 'The other new kids'. I guess that for this one its more of a personal opinion, but It would have been much more fun to play once again with the mains kids of the show.The cosmetics. As it if for the cosmetics, it is also very limited. Especially for how short the game is. Its lacking of funny outfits as well as weapons. There is no cosmetics for weapons.Overall I think the director missed the whole point of making a south park game.  By removing all of the little details we had in the past games : The Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole : The side characters, the side missions, the cosmetics and all the lore and details you can acquire by exploring the games.Much more effort could have been put into this game. _childDocuments_.review: I understand why the game has gotten mixed reviews, but also am upset that it has. People saw this game and wanted it to be another version of the previous two games which is completely understandable, I would've loved that too, so people keep comparing those two perfect games to this game. Is this as good as them? No not really, but that doesn't mean this is a bad game. Personally the price of the game also does not really match how long the game is, but disregarding the price and not comparing it to the previous games, this game itself is still a very fun game. They took that players wanted a co-op south park game and this is what they thought we wanted, it's not, but it is still a fun game and I'm sure it is fun with friends too. _childDocuments_.review: As a dedicated fan of the South Park game franchise, I was thoroughly disappointed with their latest release, South Park Snow Days. The game developers have failed to understand that game development requires a balance between a captivating story and innovative technology. Instead of creating an interesting story and meaningful gameplay mechanics, the developers chose to make a 3D game out of a 2D artwork, leading to a lackluster game experience.I urge the developers to learn from their mistakes and take note of what makes a great game - the story, the gameplay, and the overall experience. As a fan, I hope that the developers will invest more time and effort into creating a compelling story and engaging gameplay mechanics in future South Park games. As for South Park Snow Days,  I  hope this is  the last game I returning due to its poor storytelling and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so let's start by saying I have been DYING to play these games but never could justify spending the better part of $100.00 or more to get all 3. I picked these up during the recent THQNordic sale. I completed the Stick of Truth in 11 hours (did miss quite a bit achievement wise but whatever), and Fractured But Whole in about 18 hours, not any of the DLC's but I'll come back to that.This is a fun, re-imagined style of the South Park games. It's a lot more hack-n-slash, a little more open-world in the sense that you're not just fighting on a stage every time but actually fighting in a 3D environment you can move through with obstacles, jumps, overwatch areas, chokes, etc. I get what they were trying to do, but they did it so right and so wrong.Firstly, even after just an hour in this game I can tell you it makes a critical error a lot of other games do - forcing you to be the entertainment. Yes of course there is a short story, it is funny, there's a lot of classic characters that make appearances and funny dialogue, but the game is so co-op centered that the combat feels extremely boring and repetitive despite the open movement and 3D environment theme. You just fight waves and waves and waves and oh no, a stronger wave with some special enemies, then you do that 3-5x per chapter then fight a boss. The entire time all you hear is one-liner dialogue being clipped off by combat, generic combat music, and honestly some grossly unbalanced weapon sounds. (The staves are unbearably badly mastered, they're louder than any other thing in the game by like 4-1.)You can beat this game in about 4 hours if you push and there isn't anything really to do after that. Again, the game is banking on you playing with 1-3 friends and frankly, I do not myself, nor do a lot of other people, have 3 friends wanting to play a kitschy, niche comedy game when there are so many other titles at their disposal. Secondly, bugs. Bugs, bugs, bugs. Lots of clipped dialogue, progression loss, awkward movement and combat mechanics.Thirdly, lack of inspiration. Again, I go back to the devs relying on YOU and YOUR FRIENDS to make it fun. There was endless customization in SoT, endless customization in FbW, in this game you can choose 1 of 3 melee weapons which are VERY generic and 1 of 3 ranged weapons which are also incredibly generic. No buddies, no puzzles, no mysteries, no open-world, no choice in what you do next. It's a linear, 5-chapter hack-n-slash abomination that relies on you and your buddies to make it fun, rather than the game itself being fun.As I said previously, I really get what they were trying to do but this just isn't it. I finished the first chapter and said aloud to myself "Well, I guess I'm going back to FbW to play the DLC's after all" because this game just failed to inspire, which sucks because I was excited as hell to play this after logging nearly 32 hours in the last two games over the past week or so. (Yes I have no life on my days off and am a die-hard SP fan, judge me.)All in all it's not terrible, it's just very, very below the bar the last two games set. After SoT I was skeptical about FbW being only able to customize my costume and abilities but not necessarily items and equipment, but this is a far cry from even that. Pick 1 of 3 weapons for melee and ranged. Pick 2 abilities. Go fight endless waves of nonsense and we'll give you 45 seconds of funny dialogue and story after. Repeat 5 times. End of game.Trey and Matt talked about this game praising how you can "make you own kid" and loving the idea of the "blank slate New Kid" who is whoever you are, which was great in the first two games. There is 70% less customization in Snow Day than SoT and FbW so I have no idea what they were talking about. You don't even get gear, or an inventory, or crafting, or on-use items or potions or summons. They stripped away everything great about the first two games to make it 3D and Co-Op. Which again leads me back to, and say it with me - You and your friends are expected to fill the gap of a lackluster story and overall weirdly short game. Classic case of shooting for the stars but forgetting to bring your spacesuit, or oxygen, or the keys to the space ship, per se. Get it while it's on sale and you'll have a few hours of monotonous beat-em-up interspersed with quips and one-liners from your favorite residents but other than that, especially if you like the first two games, prepare to be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the greatest game, but definitely better than a 3/10 (IGN)South Park Snow Day brings a fresh twist to South Park, and while everyone is griping that we aren't getting another Stick of Truth or Fractured but Whole, I was definitely excited to see a different kind of game coming with Snow Day. Yes, the game is short, but its all about replaying the levels on higher difficulties or with different equipment/cards. I have genuinely enjoyed the time I have spent playing the game so far and can see nothing but potential for the future of this game. With some regularly added content, this game could do very well. I really think adding some sort of PVP mode would be the biggest addition to make this game that much better. There could be a capture the flag type game mode, or even a "VIP" style mode where each side has 1 of the 4 South Park kids as their leader to protect while they try and take out the other. I know this would be an extensive add, but with multiplayer co-op already being there, I wouldn't think it would be too much to add something like that, if even for a limited time event.I am excited to see the future of this game and hope there is a lot more to come. With new weapons, cosmetics, story chapters, and game modes this game will become great! All in all, I'd say this game is a solid 6/10 with lots of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game wasn't outright bad, its not anything close to the previous iterations. I wouldn't hold that against this game if it wasn't for the lackluster product its become overall. It just doesn't offer enough to justify it as a good title, but not terrible enough to outright condemn it.The premise of the game is clearly a wave based brawler in 3d. Very action oriented, no more of that turn based stuff from the previous games. Enemy types fairly limited overall, combined with a paltry five missions that you can clear in a single sitting; it almost feels like this game should have been early access. The card system and how it resets every mission at least makes replays possibly more challenging or at the very least slightly different each time. I'd almost compare the level designs and objectives in each mission to be like that of vermintide, but even vermintide isn't this linear. A big plus is coop for me, and I highly recommend going in with others because the bots are just not that good and don't bring as much variation or support to each skirmish.Sadly, I have to give this game a thumbs down as its negatives do outweigh most of its positives for the price tag its sold at. This is a discount buy at best, otherwise just go back to Stick of Truth or Fractured But Whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Snow Day is much different from the last two games by the South Park team (Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole)If you're a fan of the show you should love it!The title is short, but sweet at 5 levels that are intended to be replayed with new incentives overtime. Took about ~8 hours to play the game for the first time beginning to end and feels like a lost episode of the show.You might prefer Stick of Truth/fracture style overall, but it's fun to see the team mix it up for a unique game Stick of Truth/Fracture But Whole still feel like they hold value with Snow Day, because do miss free roaming the town and going into the characters homes. Some scale is lost by going 3D where maybe a future game could be the perfect mix of the elements. The Snow Day combat is so much better than the turnbased, and overall a game is suppose to fun and Snow Day is just that. The game mixes 2D cutscenes like seeing the show and even in full 3D it still feels in the tone of South Park with a new never before seen vibe (at least since N64!). Just seeing the lights reflect off the snow in 3D is a fun new experience from a cartoon that started with construction paper. Really has the "Hit and Run" feeling when simpsons went 3d, yet it still feels like the show it came from.  Just so much fun! Play it!

I am hoping that there are content updates planned to expand upon gameplay, without having to buy a DLC.  This game is MUCH shorter than The Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole. _childDocuments_.review: Dear Trey Parker, Matt Stone, and the Steam Community,This game isn't terrible, but it's not that good either. As a long-time fan who has been watching South Park for 22 years, I was incredibly excited for the past year to dive into a new South Park game. I always love the work they do! However, my excitement quickly turned to disappointment as I found that this game had restrictive exploration, limited scope, short length, lack of humor, lack of difficulty, and lack of engaging content.One of the aspects that disappointed me the most was the game's restrictive exploration. As a devoted South Park fan, I was excited about the prospect of exploring the town's familiar locales and getting into the kind of hilarious mischief the show is famous for. However, my expectations fell short when I realized I was confined to Cartman's backyard with little room for exploration. This lack of freedom to roam around town was a significant letdown for me. I actually found myself looking at distance mountains and buildings from Cartman's Backyard pissed off that I didn't have the option to travel there on my own.On top of the restrictive exploration, the game's overall length and difficulty level were also disappointing. Playing on hard mode, my friends and I managed to complete the game in about two hours. Surprisingly, we only encountered one challenging moment early on, where we died once due to the learning curve. After that initial hurdle, the game felt relatively easy and lacked the sustained challenge we were hoping for. Then, after just 5 chapters, the game was over. This quick completion time, combined with the lack of difficulty, left us feeling like the game was over before it truly began.Despite its shortcomings, I must admit that the powers, weapons, and cards in the game are pretty cool. South Park Snow Day does a decent job of incorporating the show's signature humor and style into its gameplay mechanics. The variety of abilities and items at your disposal adds a layer of strategy and fun to the game. However, the enjoyment I derived from these elements was somewhat overshadowed by the game's limited scope and short length. It's a shame that these cool features weren't fully utilized in a more expansive and engaging gameplay experience.In conclusion, my experience with South Park Snow Day was disappointing. With limited gameplay, lack of humor, restrictive exploration, limited difficulty, lack of engaging content, and short length left me feeling unsatisfied as a fan. I hope that future South Park games will provide a more immersive and enjoyable experience for fans like myself. Hopefully, this was just a rough draft for a potential South Park RPG. If Trey Parker & Matt Stone were to take the foundation of this game and expand upon it, adding more content and depth, it could potentially be a solid experience. Until then, as fellow gamers themselves, I believe Trey Parker and the team can understand why I gave this game a thumbs down. I'll continue to play and will update my review if the DLC's make the game more expansive.Yours truly, Chat GPT

In short, get this game if you like South Park & you like repetition for no real reward. Otherwise just play Stick of Truth or Fractured but Whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. I think a lot of the reviews are honestly pretty dramatic for the studio trying something different. I also prefer the older style with turn-based, however, I can't fault the studio for trying something new and executing it fairly well.What  deserve to be ripped on is that if you're playing solo, you can't beat the game on the final boss...or at least it was impossible for myself. The AI is  that they all insta-die in the same spot right off the bat, leaving all of [BOSS] to target you, and , with  of AOE dumped in ONE massive area that you  get out of. If you die, there is no loading in at checkpoints, you have to redo the  level. For the other levels it wasn't a big deal because it would rotate (which was pretty fun), but it seems unacceptable for the final level that is entirely story locked. You'll waste 20-30 minutes just to get back to the boss stage again and again, until you realize that it's not doable solo.If you want to combat that you can't do it solo, you have to use matchmaking...AND the matchmaking . You cannot see what lobbies to join, you join randomly into random quest chapters even if you select what chapter. If you're hosting, it takes forever. You're essentially put in waiting hell if you don't have friends who're willing to play with you and have the final chapter unlocked. The only other glaring issue that wasn't too big of a deal was the audio. The levels are a bit all over the place.The game is genuinely fun and rogue-like, the story is solid and short, but obviously with the game style changing it's less in depth and less skits. It's less playtime and in-depth than Stick of Truth, but it's $20 less and re-playable if you're into rogue-likes. I love South Park, but the game was clearly not properly tested before launch and I personally would prefer if they don't do the rogue-like again.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review to correct a few statements i'm seeing across other reviews here. You have not "beaten the game" in 3-5 hours. You might have finished each of the main missions ONCE in that time, but that does not constitute "beating the game". Each mission is different - I've replayed one mission 3 times in a row, after failing the boss fight with some randoms, and had different missions picked every time. For example - the 3rd mission where you have to "pass the trial of strength" - can be multiple different missions: Lighting the Witchfyre Pyres, Stealing from the 6th Graders, Helping Jimbo find items to sell- and even further, the items and locations are different in every run as well. To add on to this, After you beat the 3rd mission, you unlock free DLC via Henrietta which gives you access to unending zombie-survival style missions, AND after you beat the last mission of the campaign, you unlock Nichole, who allows you to take on extra challenges for other rewards, similar to HEAT in Hades. Now for the Cons - Yes, the game is "short" but it's made with replayability in mind. Different card combos let you play in different ways and playing with friends massively increases what is viable versus playing solo where you basically need to run a healing ability and an escape. Having one person with a heal and a turret while a melee person runs the charge and gravity bomb is a blast. pun intended. The options are a bit limited now - there are only 3 main melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons, but i expect more to be added eventually, and the cards you pick still allow you quite a bit of variety to how you play. My single biggest complaint has to be the lack of a communication system of any kind. No voice, no chat - all you have are emotes, so unless you're playing people you already know in discord, it's pretty hard to communicate specific ideas like "I'm running these powerups" or "I need to run to the restroom". etc. All in all - this is not multiplayer Stick of Truth or FBW, it's more of a hack and slash with some roguelike elements, but for the price, i think it's a fine game to pick up to play with a friend or two.EDIT: Well, It seems we've been let down again. The new Snowball weapon is PAID DLC, so even though they're tossing us a few free cosmetic DLCs, the actual gameplay elements (which the game SORELY needs) are locked behind an additional paywall... I had some solid hopes for this game, but it seems to be diving further into being a piece of trash. RIP.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I LOVE south park, but this game ain't worth 30 bucks. The Good: The art is great for a 3D rendition of south park! They keep the cut scenes similar to that of a south park episode, but the game play animation feels more smooth. The Game play overall was fine with the rogue-lite elements of the card system allowing you to choose how to strengthen your abilities. There are cards specifically for each of the different weapons as well as your powers!The Meh/Bad: Story (Meh):The story is neat as it feels like that of a "Special", but it lacks the impact of one. The story was way too short with 5 levels in total with each varying in length from 30-50 minutes depending on how much you rush through. I played through the game on Hard difficulty for all levels, but I only party-wiped once on my play through. There also didn't appear to be that many jokes aside from Butters and Cartman giving you ♥♥♥♥ in the middle of combat. The ending also felt rather unsatisfying as it left me disappointed with a feeling of "That's it? That was the entire game/story?" Abilities (less than Meh):I played through this game solo, so I was given 3 other AI "new kids" to play with, but they are limited to combating and reviving you. You are also able to choose from a list of 8 powers at a limit of to two choices of "powers" that you can select before starting my mission, but the AI do not appear to have any powers equipped whatsoever. Now I don't have an issue with the abilities themselves, what I have an issue with is feeling the need to equip the grouo healing power (I believe is the only healing power that doesn't require cards.). Completing this game by yourself is slightly challenging as you have to rely on your AI teammates to stay alive while also keeping yourself alive, and since they can't use the group healing power, you would likely need it to stay alive. This leaves one spot as a "for fun" power that you can choose from. Now maybe the easier difficulties would've allowed me to not feel the need to bring the healing power, but I do not want to bother replaying the same missions to find out.Replayabiltiy (Bad): There appears to be a lack of any real replay-ability in my opinion. Sure you can buy upgrades, but they keep increasing in price requiring a larger grind. I only needed about 6-9 upgrades to complete the game, so any more would begin to feel like overkill. When you complete the game, you can find another character in the levels to make a pact with and make the levels more challenging.... for cosmetics. I didn't do this as the levels felt meh by themselves, so I don't want to replay them again just to make it slightly harder. There are also only 3 melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons in the base game in which I only touched 1 of each as I thought there would be more story/game to work with.Price (Bad):This game is not worth $30 for a 5 hour experience (4 hours if you don't die!) with alright game play and a unsatisfying story. I also checked the DLC list, which also appears to be just filler content and nothing new to the story. I also thought the Underpants Gnome Cosmetic would be exclusive to pre-orders, but boy was I stupid at thinking such since you can buy this mediocre cosmetic for 3 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not anything crazy and expecting anything besides southpark being southpark is getting your hopes up for a game you're not getting. TLDR; if you expected them to make a 3rd installment of the other 2 games' themes, this isn't for you. If you enjoy southpark and just wanted to have a little fun for a under 60 game, you 110% can get something you'll enjoy from this.This was a pretty decent and fun roguelike with a more centered focus on the overall story. It was short but a nice little break from other games. Hard mode gave me a balanced amount of combat so I'd recommend playing on that for more of a challenging or honestly just better combat to engage with. This is a game to have fun for a few hours, with friends or randoms or bots, and just chill with it. The roguelike elements are actually pretty good for a roguelike. They flow a lot better than a lot of roguelikes tend to struggle with and you genuinely feel upgrades. The skill tree is a bit grindy but functions as actual upgrades for your character. Balancing is maybe a bit off but for the most part, everything seemed like it could be used without putting yourself at a massive determinant for using what you want. Co-op worked really well. I was able to jump into random matches without a hitch and playing with friends didn't take ages to join. They even have settings so you can dodge getting spoilers while matchmaking.The world itself is pretty well done but maybe feels a little too lifeless at times as the city is covered in snow and a lot less south park residents are going outside.Jokes were a little toned down but to be expected. Much much harder for the IP to use as much edgy humor categories as it did in the past with other games. That definitely was noticeable but nothing crazy. The characters acted like kids on a snow day in south park. What you would want.Combat is a little jank at times but there's some real combos out there you can have fun with. Use the flamethrower wand and the black hole balloon. You'll have some funAll in all, this game delivered a fun little 3D experience. 30 bucks is a little steep for the amount of content but where there isn't content to play, a lot of the work obviously went into making sure the game felt like the IP in 3D and making it keep the theme. It's biggest flaw is that game mechanics needed more focus over the look but when we're talking about games that are using a IP, this definitely is not at the bottom. It's a pretty mid in that regard. Content looks like it could be pretty decent for anyone wanting to rotate this game as a little breather from others. We'll have to see what they have planned once we start seeing visuals of that DLC. And it's important to note day 1 DLC did happen and that's always a rough move to make in consumerism. I'm not a fan of this tactic but it wasn't crazy overpriced 20 dollar skins so not really as bad. Just leaves a bad taste in people's mouths.

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR SUMMARY) This game is a pathetic disappointment which seems slapped together hastily with no care toward the original content or its many fans. The graphics are ugly, the gameplay is shallow, the story is minimal/lacking, and the level design is lazy. This is coming from someone who has perfected Fractured But Whole, and is a huge fan of the show; do not waste your money on this pathetic attempt at a South Park Game. I told myself, if I can't trust the South Park creators to make a fun game, then I can't trust anyone. This was it, I promised myself when I was pre-purchasing this game, that if it sucked I would never pre-purchase any game ever again. And I am so very disappointed. South Park: Snow Day is a third person hack-n-slash game that is largely reminiscent of Vermintide 2 and Left 4 Dead 2 (but not either of the other South Park games). You drop into a level and fight a bunch of no-name enemies. These enemies include 4th graders, 5th graders, and preschoolers; all of whom unfortunately have the voice of a preschooler (the. same. exact. voice). Also unlike Vermintide 2 and Left 4 Dead 2, the weapons and special abilities are all; basic, boring, and lacking in any form of variety. Unlike those games though, which contain many fun levels with interesting and unique playable characters; South Park Snow Day has five completely generic levels that look incredibly similar, with four completely generic playable characters. You are no longer "The New Kid", you are one of thousands of new kids that hang out with Cartman and follow his orders. Every cutscene seems desperate to make you feel unique, "You're the real New Kid" Cartman says repeatedly; only for you to drop into another random game where the main cast call you Player # (1-4) in any cutscene. Cartman constantly complains about you being "OP" and ruining the previous two games for everyone involved, invalidating any success that you might have once had. The kids in South Park have decided to make everything fair with random card draws and balanced mechanics, so you can no longer be the cool New Kid you once were.Speaking of the levels, I now understand why this game is a winter wonderland; the developers couldn't be bothered to actually program South Park in 3D. The game has covered absolutely everything in a mountain of snow, a basic and repetitive texture that in no way resembles South Park. They include a sign or an occasional building from the original town, but none of them can be explored or entered, merely being a part of the background! You are forced onto a linear path during your travels during which you are constantly surrounded by hoards of enemies. There is no time for exploration, there is no time for humor, there is not time for fun. Between button mashing like crazy one or two characters deliver a singular voice line. This game lazily throws South Park tropes in the players face between bland and monotonous gameplay. One of the main cutscenes in the story is Cartman doing his "ha ha ha ha ha ha na na na na na na" laugh, Kyle saying "f*** you Cartman", and then cutting away. The next thing you know everyone is at a table and chatting, and the war you had only just started waging is ALREADY OVER!I am a very easy man to please when it comes to games, so long as the game reaches a certain bar of quality, and posses any of the following qualities: The games need to be fun, or made with love, or contain pleasant art, or have a well-made story. This game does not meet ANY of those standards. I WANTED TO LOVE THIS GAME! I WAITED FOR SO LONG TO ENJOY THIS GAME!The disappointment I feel right now is crushing. I...will never pre-purchase any game ever again. Please do not waste your money. This game is worth $10 at most.It's insulting that the game puts such focus on getting your friends to play with you How is anyone supposed to convince their friends to play with crap with them? Why would they want their friends to waste their money to play these 5 levels with them?

_childDocuments_.review: It's South Park but without all crude humor and ridiculousness that makes South Park...South Park. Yes, there are some funny moments but it's the cleanest South Park among the show and games and I don't understand why. Gameplay wise, it's as basic as can be but fun to play. The card system is different but nothing new or groundbreaking. Back 4 Blood has a similar system if you're familiar with that game but Snow Days is beyond simplistic along with everything else. The cards given to you change based on what weapons and abilities you are currently using. The card will apply some sort of modifier to the weapon or ability. There are plenty of different variations which are nice but it's so limited to what cards you get since you only draw cards 3-5 times in a level. This would have been much nicer if we actually collected the cards and had a type of loud out to stick to based on your preference. There's no RPG element to this game. There's one item (Dark Matter also known as Poo) that is the games level currency. You collect it through each level and then use it to purchase Perks that range from upping your damage, raising health to higher rates of Dark Matter and Toilet Paper drops when playing. Toilet Paper is the other currency that is only used within each level and does not carry over once your run is completed. During the run you will collect and use TP to level up your Cards to raise the modifier on whatever card you choose to level up. These level ups only apply during that one level/mission.The game itself is broken down into 5 levels/runs. Each level has you traversing through a section with an objective while enemies attack you trying to complete objective. Once you complete the objective and clear enemies you'll get a card and then proceed to the next section. Some randomness the game has may have you doing one section on the same level one time and then you go to play the level again and you'll get a section you may not have played through on the last time you played the level which does add some variety but not much as there's only a small set of these sections.Once you beat the game you unlock modifiers to the level which will handicap you which adds some replayability as doing these modified missions will get you extra cosmetics.tl/dr Summary: Could have been a much bigger game with more detailed RPG elements and things to collect/level up over your career and also be consistent with South Park humor and story telling as whole like the previous two games.Pros: -Art looks really great. Seeing the 3D models of all the characters was really cool as well as seeing the town of South Park as a 3D environment.-Weapons, and abilities are limited but fun to use.-Great Co-Op Game-Wasn't $60-Each run is somewhat unique in the encounters. You can play the same level twice and you may not get the same sequences each time which adds some variety and replay-ability but not a lot.-There's is a free DLC add-on for a horde mode with 4 levels but it only lasts 8 waves and takes maybe 20 minutes to do.-Encountered very minimal bugs and performance wise plays really well.Cons:-Costs $30-Will take 3-5 hours to complete if you really chill and take your time. Potentially shorter.-No feedback loop.-Cosmetic Unlockables only-No leveling system-Perk system is basic and grindy for no real reward.-No PvP-No real reason to keep playing it after beating the story other than to grind dark matter for perks but what's the point?Overall: Could have been much more. Needs PvP and double the amount of story missions to make this worth $30. Due to the poor sales performance I really doubt this gets a whole lot of updates but who knows. I'm happy to have played it but had I known what I was getting, I would have waited till it was $15-$20. It's a hard choice on giving it a recommendation or not but at this time, I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this for a total of 39 minutes and in all honesty, after 39 minutes, you'll get the gist of what this game has to offer which is very little in comparison to its predecessors.  I am ALL for a game or genre throwing out what works for the sake of experimentation.  It's experimentation that pushes games to actually innovate on stale formulas. but we have seen what a successful south park game looks like, and we've seen it adapt and evolve. I would hardly call what was built in "The Stick of Truth" and "The Fractured But Whole" stale or old, but I can tell before the first hour is up that this game ain't it.  It barely scratches the roguelite surface, with levels that are too short to see builds evolve or come together and too dull to keep things interesting.  Apparently, at only 5 levels offering a barely acceptable level of variety, the result of the tutorial and first level is just you clumsily trudging from fight to fight through generic biomes and and boring enemy types getting cards that make things slightly more interesting and losing those cards before you get to see your idea of a build come together.  Cards make combat visually appealing but players won't be doing anything differently to make them happen, resulting in a game that mechanically is low effort, forcing the 3D visuals to carry the weight.  But while a lot of the humor and appeal of South Park is when it pushes the envelope, here that bite is pretty much non-existent.  I'm sure there are things to like as players get later into their play sessions, and at $29 its a low ticket to entry for a group of friends, but I find it hard to want to continue playing a game so bland and plain in the face of what South Park, and other developers, have done before at higher costs.  If you're new to South Park games, ignore this one entirely.  If you're a South Park vet, be prepared to be disappointed and confused at how we got here.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial thoughts: This is the most 6-out-of-10 game I have ever played and therefore it gets a recommend, but it's just so limited. It doesn't do anything BAD (well, elf voices are kind of crap) it just doesn't do anything exceptionally well. However, the more I play it the more I kind of like it because the card system is worthwhile and I do like unlocking stuff and having modifiers. They can go a long way in making fights feel different. If nothing else I will forever appreciate the "bulls***" mechanic where you can play specific "bulls*** cards" to give an insane modifier for a few seconds, like invincibility, resurrection, metoer rain, etc. They are appropriately named because we've all played games where something happens and you say "that's such bulls***" so props on that. Otherwise, it's a kind of janky 4 player co op. I feel like initially the enemies do too much damage but maybe it's just the right amount? I've never died, but have come close. Upgrades feel impactful. Running/sliding on ice get tedious quickly but there are upgrades you can buy to lessen that. At first i hated the dagger combat but then realized that if you can get better at timing the dives it can be kind of fun. Ricochet arrows are the way to go. I'm also a little more inclined to be positive about the game because Question, the developer, did a decent enough job here after landing this license and they do not have a ton of games under their belt. Definitely need to see more small developers doing well. They priced it on the cheap, and you can find it even cheaper, so it might ultimately be worth your time. Maybe watch some no-commentary gameplay videos and judge for yourself. Don't believe everything some rando on youtube with a ring light, webcam and bad facial hair or cat ears thinks about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The price tag should clue you in that the game is very light on content (as far as single player is concerned) so far, but what it does have now is worth the $30. The screenshots are doing the game a huge disservice - it's true that the game takes its cue from the intentionally rudimentary visuals of the TV series, and the fact that it's set in snow stages limits the colors you will see at any given time to predominantly white and grey. But if you crank up the quality to Ultra (and the game is optimized enough that you can do it even on a mid-to-low-end card like the RX 6600), it's got a lot of lighting effects that make the game look a lot more vibrant than it should.The combat is tight enough as far as hack and slash combat goes, but the gameplay loop itself feels a little bit underdeveloped - like it was only part of a much larger game. Think of it as very similar in structure to Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare 2's Turf Takeover game mode. Hopefully they polish it a bit more over time.Story is where the game really shines. Sure, the dialogue and themes are overly sanitized compared to what you will see on the show (and this should surprise no one, in our age of censorship), but it still contains Stone and Parker's trade mark wit. Everybody still feels in character (Cartman is still crass and lacks morals, Kyle is still the snappy nemesis, Butters is butters, etc.). Haven't tried multiplayer yet. I have no opinion on it.

If the previous two games didn't exist, this would be an alright game for around half the price but it just feels super lackluster. Maybe wait for a sale. _childDocuments_.review: Despite the skepticism from 2d to 3d change, I was really hoping that this game would at least be fun with the creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone being in control over this game.  Within the 1 hour of playing this game, I wasn't having fun.  It's a boring hack n slash with rogue-like elements thrown into the game.  Mind you, this is coming from a guy who has over 800 hours on Warframe, mindlessly pressing buttons whilst feeling like a braindead old white fart who sits at a casino pressing a button.The game tells you that you can use charge attacks but what's the point when all you do is mindlessly hack and slash like as if it's a dynasty warriors game.  The gameplay feels like PS2/PS3 God of War games, you defeat enemies, acquire currency that you can use to spend on stuff.  The abilities and weapons in this game are also pretty lackluster.  I'm not sure if there are actually more weapons that you can get later in the game but from what I saw, it's lackluster.The soundtrack is not as memorable as the ones from the previous games, the sound effects are also really not satisfying to hear.  They sound so dull and unsatisfying, the previous south park games had really good sound design.  When I strike my daggers into a bunch of elf baddies in this game, it just feels like I'm slapping baddies with a napkin or when I'm using the fart rocket ability, there's no punch.  Sure there is a fart noise but it doesn't sound loud enough and there's no punch to it.  It just feels like the game's audio is glitchy when it's not.  It's just feel so dull and dead.  It's like having the BFG-9000 from DOOM 2016 making the most pathetic silent firing sound effect in video games.The voice acting in this game is really cheesy as well, I'm not talking about the original voice actors for South Park, they do a good job in this game.  The voice actors for the elf enemies sound so cheesy and corny.  It ranges from funny like in a so bad it's good movie to just annoying.  They sound like Ike, I'm not even sure if these elf characters I was fighting were meant to be other forth graders or younger kids.The charm in this game is also lackluster, I remember first time I played Stick of Truth.  First thing I did when I saw Cartman was melee attack and fart him while he complains, berates and cusses at me.  I did this with passerby people as well and the reactions are funny to hear.  That was funny and it never gets old.  For this game, it doesn't feel fun to bully Cartman or anyone, the reactions feel like they don't care.The character customization is a downgrade from the previous entries.  In the previous entries, you can change the color of your clothing, in this game you there is no color changing.  I get that this was probably difficult for the 2d games but this a 3d game, you can make multiple textures or use a color sliding tool.  It really doesn't make sense in my eyes.On the plus side, the game has a tolerable file size which these days with AAA games becoming more and more space hungry.  It's a plus in my books.  I'm able to play the game at maximum framerate with Ultra graphics.  .  I haven't found a laundry list of bugs that break the game.  Which is also a plus in my books.  The animations on the characters when they talk is alright and the models look decent.  But that doesn't mean that this game is fun.  The game uses unreal engine 4 so people can just extract the assets for modding.This game feels like a game I found on Yahoo! Games back in the 2000s that was extracted by the developers and turned into a south park game.  This game is disappointing and I really hope that there is still rolm in tuning up the game and making it better but I doubt that will happen, even if they make the game a lot better the comedy and humor doesn't feel dark.  Other than that, I'd say get this game when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I preordered this game and I go back and forth on if it was worth it. For the story, I enjoy it. It's a short and silly story that follows up an episode we might've forgotten about. It's nothing too special but it's not without its merits. Fighting is decent. It's not too bad, but you can be easily swarmed and weapons are very limited and sometimes don't work at all. Wands don't do much of anything, and smacking only gets you so far when seven archers have you pinned to a wall. Fighting can get annoying if you're surrounded, and the AI players aren't the greatest. The graphics are fine and they translated okay in a 3d space, there's not much to say and personally I don't mind them. They hold up okay and they're not too ugly.The upgrading system is okay, if a little boring and repetitive. My biggest gripe is the walk/run cycle. You walk super slow which is grating for massive maps with multiple fetch-quests. You can run, but your stamina drains fast. The running speed should just be the new walking speed.  I also ran into a glitch where in the middle of a match, my progress wiped. I was disconnected from the game and told to do the tutorial again. I had to cycle the entire tutorial once more. It saved my gold, but my hundreds of dark matter was abruptly gone. I went into matchmaking to finish the last stage of the game then uninstalled it. It wasn't the first glitch I ran into either. I often got force disconnected from public matchmaking, meaning I would need to find a new match and replay the entire round all over again. ESPECIALLY annoying if it was a fetch-quest-heavy one and/or you had good battle chemistry with your teammates.  Do I recommend it? Honestly, for a small time-killer, yeah I do. It has its moments and it's not going to destroy your wallet or ruin your day. But it's for the more dedicated fans that are okay overlooking the flaws for a good time with the cast again. For non-fans, being South Park is the biggest thing holding it up because it wouldn't be able to stand without that fact. Wait for a sale or give it a skip if you're not a big fan. _childDocuments_.review: I’m not going to sit here and tell you that this game is perfect and you should drop everything you’re doing right now and go buy it… because it is not.However, I will say that South Park: Snow Day! is worth a try. If you are willing to look past the few minor bugs and disregard the fact that it’s graphics are different from the show, this game has a very strong back bone and foundation for future updates that have already been confirmed by the developers. I would recommend watching or re-watching some of the newer South Park episodes to understand the jokes in this game though.Now I would like to share my opinion on why this game has the amount of negative reviews that it does. Personally, I think that people are afraid of change. Going from 2 very well made 2D games to a 3D game with only about 5 hours of content is a big pill to swallow and I think they are right to be worried. Although, from what I’ve experienced in the game, I’m hopeful that I can extinguish these worries that you might have if you are still on the fence about purchasing this game.Let’s talk about the bad aspects of the game. Firstly, that it only has about 5 hours of gameplay currently at the time of writing this review. Although this may seem like a little, South Park: Snow Day! has many other ways to squeeze a few more hours out of it. For all my fellow achievement hunters, getting all the achievements is a great way to make the game last longer. There are also different contracts that you unlock when you complete the main story and these can get you some pretty cool cosmetics from the show. There is also a skill tree, and an “endless” mode where you can try to survive for 7 waves of enemies attacking, while you get stronger every wave you complete. I have done many of these ways of getting more fun out of the game and I’m at about 15 ish hours. Another part of this game that isn’t great is the bugs. Although few, some of them are pretty annoying. I would like to note though, during my 15 hours of gameplay, most of these bugs are pretty rare, and you don’t need to worry too much about them.Now, for the good part, let’s talk about what this game -in my opinion- does really well. Firstly, I think that the story is very funny and really well made.  It may not feel like an entire South Park episode because you are teleporting around the map and you may get disoriented, but I feel if you are willing to look past that you can get a ton of enjoyment out of the game. Another benefit of this game is the price. For only about $30 you can’t go wrong. Another part that I enjoyed was the combat. South Park: Snow Day! has a hack-and-slash style of combat and during every mission you get to choose different upgrade cards in order to get stronger and I found this to be a really interesting part of the game. There are many different builds that you can make - making every time you play a new experience! When re-playing different missions, they won’t all be the exact same because there are different modules that can be swapped out, changing the way you experience the mission! I could keep talking about what I love about this game but these are the main points.The final thing that I love about South Park: Snow Day! is the community. I became involved in the South Park community through the official Discord server.  Everyone that I’ve met have been nothing but friendly and enjoyable to play with. I honestly feel I might have met some long term friends that I never would have met without this game. As a final message to the developers, thank you for creating such a great game and here’s to many more!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to point out the store page has a lot of misinformation. They claim this is the first South Park game with multiplayer or Coop, this is false. They also claim this is a RPG, this is also false. They also call this a South Park game: if all it takes to call it a South Park game is putting the main characters on the cover, then we're doomed. Back in the days of N64 there was a Southpark game where it was a shooter, 3D, and it was generally disliked by everybody. A lot of people felt that it did not capture the spirit of South Park at all. This game is somehow worse than that game. Unlike the previous two games which were made by big name studios and starred tie-ins with the show itself, Snow Day is made by a tiny little studio named Question which made "The Blackout Club", a multiplayer-only flop. The story is pretty simple, a snow storm wrecks South Park so the kids go outside and play. Snow Day is yet another attempt by Matt Stone and Trey Parker to sell overpriced DLC while preventing you from exploring South Park as much as possible. On release day you can PRE-ORDER a season pass that promises "one new weapon" and "one new mode", so for $25 you might theoretically get something worth it. I think this kind of shows how Matt and Trey have always been a decade behind the gaming industry; nobody likes these rip-off season passes, and anybody that has learned to read knows it's a rip-off. Speaking of being a decade behind the industry, remember those generic third person shooters where you clear arenas and fight your way  to a boss? You know, those games that were popular like 10 years ago? That's the entire experience. You are The New Kid, who silently fights their way across a bunch of frozen zones loosely inspired by South Park. Objectives are standard uninspired crap like fight badguys, bring things to the place, load a turret, etc. The most basic stuff that you could possibly be doing in a game. Scenes with the actual South Park characters in it are few and far between, they appear for about 25 minutes out of the four hour playtime of the entire game. The enemies are NOT voiced by Matt and Trey, but a group of twelve year olds (I am being very serious, it's the same kids they have do the fourth graders on the show I think) so there's kind of only so much range they can show off. Which brings me to the number one reason why this game does not work: It lacks the South Park charm, it feels like a low budget fan game because there's barely anything that can be identified as "South Park" here. All they did was dress the kids up like wizards and warriors again while making a simple third person shooter around it; happily stealing mechanics from everything they can think of in order to scam some money off some stupid kids. Question is an awful game developer, and I hope Matt/Trey drop them like an empty bag of cocaine.

The 3-D is there, but it's a little grainy for a new South Park game.  The combat is incredibly simple hack and slash with no real strategy.  You get to choose from only three weapons (double daggers, sword and shield or giant ax) and two powers.  Also at the start of each area, there are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards that can add another power, but they don't really change the battles all that much.  Another thing that is wrong with the battles are the enemy dialog.  It's so annoying, overly repetitive, and meaningless.  After completing an area, you get to spend your dark matter that has been collected on a skill tree, but you don't really get enough to make it worth your while.  You are required to grind dark matter to complete the skill tree, but the game is so boring that it's not worth it.All in all, this game fails at every turn.  Save your money or buy Stick of Truth or Fractured but Whole.  They are both leagues better than this pathetic excuse of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game set in the South Park universe, look elsewhere. Apart from the minor backdrop of continuity from TSOT/FBW, this game oozes "game first setting second" vibes.I bought this game a day or two before release, knowing it was not an RPG, but  still at least hoping for an enjoyable setpiece-filled world. Every reference is minor, every detail feels shoed-in. Even with friends, we can't help but want to play something else.What it does well:-The combat & card systems are certainly unique for what amounts to a 3D roguelite.-The artistic style is what you'd expect a 3D South Park game to look like, with some clever mechanics to hide imperfections.-The voice acting is mostly tolerable, with a few serious exceptions. Looking at you, Randy.The cons:-I honestly can't bring myself to go back for a second session. Everything feels hollow, to say the least. Even with Koopa Keep filled with other characters, nothing feels memorably placed.-The level environments are completely forgettable, and rarely feel connected to actual South Park landmarks.-The story is terrible. Yes, it's not supposed to be story-focused, but it's just so... sorry the only way I can describe it is shoed-in. It feels like they had an actual story and cut 80% of it out before release, or it was written to accommodate the base amount of gameplay. This is not what you'd expect from South Park.-There's an annoyingly SMALL amount of customization, cosmetic or otherwise.-The language and behavior of every character is not on-brand with what we know about South Park. It feels more like a THQ brand-pump game than a South Park one.I'll be returning this product. I expected at least something akin to a South Park brawler with meaningful dialogue that I could immerse myself into the world with. Instead I got this "fudging" boring game. (That's not me being polite, that's the non-main characters toning down their language).

I couldn't imagine this has any replay-ability.I genuinely wish I could get the 2.9 hours of my life back! If you are going to buy this wait for it to be on sale! Don't buy it at the RRP price because it really is not worth it! Go play Stick of Truth & Fractured But Whole instead!

_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in South Park: Snow Day!, please realize it's a completely different game from the last two (Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole). Those are turn based RPGs that play out like an episode while this is a 3D card-based beat 'em up, rogue-like. It's very much designed to be played with other people, but you can still do single player with the help of AI party members.The game is fairly short and can be frustrating at times, but for $30 (release price) I'm not upset with it. It has some occasional glitches / bugs but overall I'm not having a bad time with it. I found myself getting frustrated but always returning to it later on. It still has that trademark South Park humor and the story is amusing (though again, short). I've seen people complain about the graphics but honestly I enjoy the look. I do prefer the style of the previous games but for a 3D South Park game, I feel like they nailed it artistically.A bit of a ramble but just to quickly sum it up, to me it was worth $30. $60 or $70? Absolutely not, but brand new at $30 I felt like I knew what I was getting myself into.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't go off IGN's review. _childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a hack-and-slash combat game, not an RPG. The Stick of Truth was one of the best games ever. But this is nothing like it and is not fun to play -- there's basically no "South Park" content, just a basic combat game. It feels like Matt and Trey weren't even involved. There are basically no jokes, there's very little story, and the combat isn't fun. I'm a huge South Park fan but I'm not going to be able to finish this; it's just not enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: As a big South Park fan, it hurts to say that this game just isn't it.It is a huge step down from the previous two games.The game feels like a cheap mobile game, while there's nothing wrong with mobile games... this one costs 30 euros.The combat in this game feels very clunky and cheap, and the locations in this game all feel the same.While they said this game should make you feel like you are in an episode of South Park, it does not. It feels like a cheap hack-and-slash game with a South Park skin.If you are playing alone, you get three little morons assisting you in battle. Their AI is not that great.The last two really felt like big South Park movies where they went all out with the jokes; in this one, it just feels like they are playing it a little bit safe.It might be fun with friends, but that does not make this a 30 euro game.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Gamers need to relax and just enjoy games. This is a brand new take for the future of south park. This product reminds me of fat princess fist full of cakes. A budget title that can be replayed over and over. I am just hoping they decide to add more content to this game. There is 5 levels with a story that is funny. It has a good premise that carries over from the last two games about making sure people will stop breaking the rules. They wanted to make a game that they could update more frequently. If they put something in the show they can put it in the game. This games future is dependent on south park team following through with what they said they wanted to do. You support games ideas and their future. I would like more of an action south park game in the future. Turn based is fun, but it's been done before twice. So they wanted to make something fresh. Gamers hate change which is crazy to me. They don't like experimental titles that lower the price while doing something different. People will be upset you can beat this in 5 hours. There is a lot to explore during the missions. I feel we need more titles like this that really allow devs to make something new. If you are here just for the story wait for a sale. This is a quality game. I will probably grind this for another 10 to 20 hours easily. I will get my moneys worth and if you are south park fan it's a must have. If you aren't I wouldn't recommend it. I don't see what this game offers that other games don't and there is nothing wrong with that. It's 30 dollars for a reason. Just enjoy your south park and don't let the reviews deflect your from your enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: What sucks the most is that the previous two South Park games were so great. _childDocuments_.review: I've played every south park game so far and unfortunately this one falls incredibly from the high bar. _childDocuments_.review: It's really not bad at all, but not amazing don't get me wrong. _childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: As much as i love South Park... this just aint it. There is way too much getting stun locked until you down, forcing you to reset the entire thing from the beginning (and these are some really long missions) so if you die during the boss fight, prepare to spend another 45ish minutes to get back to it. (The Stan boss fight is pretty much why I stopped and decided to vent for a minute)Gameplay wise, it's just a button masher... I like button mashers sometimes. The AI is completely useless. So that adds an extra unnecessary level of "FUN" if you could call it that.It's all linear gameplay for the most part. Stark's Pond let's you choose which way you wanna go, but that's about it (from what I've seen so far anyway.) No more all of South Park to explore. No more side quests, no more finding easter eggs while walking around. I hated the first trailer and seeing it was a 3D game instead of the 2.5 from the previous two, but I figured i'd just muscle through it because of South Park but... 3D just is not what South Park was intended to look like. It isn't ugly by any means, but this is SOUTH PARK. It will always look better with the Construction Paper cutouts cussing at you.And probably most egregious of all... it's just not that funny. By this point in Stick of Truth and Fractured but Whole, I had to pause the game so I could finish laughing multiple times before continuing. This time game, well it got a few chuckles out of me, but nothing gut bustingly funny anymore.6/10 (so far) if you like South Park, get it. If not, find something else to play.Edit: Spelling and added the bit about the friendly AI
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Been a fan of the show and would recommend every single south park game in existence, except this one.
