_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable dungeon crawler with rogue-like elements and a mix and match class system. It's limiting with only five maps and only three melee and tree ranged weapons, but the card system keeps a fresh rogue-like feel to each run. Plus South Park humor and essentially a whole sequel episode to (an although dated at this point) episode from the show. At $30 with additional DLC at release, it's not the best, but it's pretty fun, and you can trust me because I'm a Yelp reviewer.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing South Park game. Is it clunky at times yes but if you are a die-hard South Park fan you will have a blast playing it. Especially with friends. The game follows the shows/games timelines which is great.Do take in consideration how short the game actually is though. I have 5h so far but that is because I was exploring every single little corner as it amazes me I can be in my favorite fictional place in 3D. I do believe that if you rush it you might be able to complete it in 2 to 3 hours.Performance is great. Graphics are great. Movement is a bit clunky at times. Soundtrack is good. Story is great. If you are a fan and have money to spare buy it NOW! If you aren't that interested in South Park maybe wait for a sale.UPDATE: Chapters will have some different objectives if you replay the game. However the game is quite short unfortunately. It took me under 11 hours to get all achievements and unlock nearly everything. There is also a harder wave/kill all enemies mode.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Yea its lacking in content but its also not $60 and if you like South Park you're probably gonna buy it anyway. It's a fun with friends rogue-like set in a cool environment.The upgrade path is fun but gets grindy after upgrade 18. But to be fair you don't need to be maxed out to feel powerful. It's all about using the perks to your advantage and getting ULTRA-LEGENDARY cards. Similar to Descent in The Division 2, the damage perks are nice but if you lean towards economy instead more TP will serve you better in the end.Gameplay is a bit clunky and can be frustrating at times. It reminds me a lot of Gunfire Reborn which is probably a better game albeit not about South Park. The last level music is hella annoying and I ended up muting it completely. Needs some more tactile feedback in the combat system when you're hitting enemies.Personally I love the genre and subject matter of this game. With a few more levels. game modes, cards, and a ton of more shop options this game would have been WELL worth the price of admission. As it stands, if you're on the fence, wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike the previous South Park games (South Park: The Stick of Truth, South Park: The Fractured but Whole), this game honestly felt very repetetive, boring and way too short. Story is ok, but nothing special. The only positive I see is that there was an attempt to create a completely different concept of the South Park games, unfortunately they failed...I don’t think Matt or Trey were involved in creating this game, because it would certainly be much more enjoyable. Overall just play old South Park games and do not waste your money on this piece of garbage 4/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok for a co op hack and slash. The enemies get quite annoying, and not in a challenging way. Their constant repeating of the same lines def gives you that " Lets hurry this mission along" feel. Id say get this on sale, I already feel like I am forcing myself to finish. Its quite repetitive, and most of what makes South Park games, is the lore, and NPC's. this game lacks that.Edit: I came back to give this another shot, after the DLC was downloaded. And I still feel the same. I'm annoyed more or less I guess. Its just more the same, simple repetitive attacks, useless ranged attacks. More of the same annoying little kids, with the same annoying lines. Its just waves, with a lame sprinkle of a card game mixed in. The new dlc is just more lame cards, with more waves. And my dumb ass payed for the deluxe edition.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth it's asking price of 30 euros, maybe 4.99 euros at the current state of the game and the season pack is just a big ♥♥♥♥ you to the players.+ Some fun cinematic moments+ The arena mode is decently good+ Soundtrack is decent+ Levels seems to have randomized section- Price is just awful, they should be ashamed for it- No class system so every player is just the same guy with one or two differences- Small weapon and power pool- You can't customize your character as much as in the previous games- The cosmetic options don’t have much to offer- Can’t have more than one facial feature. You wanted a beard and an eyepatch that's too bad- Story is short and underwhelming- I think they tried to have microtransactions in it. The PP have that feel of greed attached to it- Basic Combat that doesn’t feel rewarding- Took me and my friend 6 hours to playthroughThe list could go on but I don’t want to waste more of my time on this that I have to.Stick of truth was good, Fractured but whole was okay but this is just horrible.The season pack map said it had stuff planned up until December but I cannot imagen people playing it for so long or coming back for it.Either wait for a BIG discount or for the full game to release and then judge it.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is REALLY clunky. Like, really, really clunky. It is really difficult to control your character, even outside of combat. Obviously, this game is not meant to be a RPG like Stick of Truth or Fractured But Whole, but I expected the same atmosphere and vibe that I loved about those games. IDK, if it goes on sale and they fix a few things I may snag it again, but it was honestly unplayable.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions: Usually I wait to write reviews, but this one is DEFINITELY worth buying. I've watched every episode of South Park, and know the theme. Very intuitive interface. GIT SOME CRED! (I'd do a Cartman impression, but I don't want to get banned from Steam!)

_childDocuments_.review: So I was expecting a lot more from this game when I heard it was being made by Matt Stone and Trey Parker. _childDocuments_.review: The 3D graphics are a great concept. The overall story is great. However, even on easy mode it is IMPOSSIBLE to pass the 4th level. _childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Very repetitive and short. To be honest it feels like a soulless hack n slash game with South Park branding slapped on it. The jokes are alright but there isn't really any story to the game apart from "go here, do these fights" and Cartman talking at you. I was excited for another South Park game like Stick of Truth and the Fractured But Whole but I was left feeling like I was playing yet another quick and dirty cash grab. I'm glad that they tried new things with the mechanics and the design but this shouldn't come at the expense at the replayability and overall soul of the game.To be frank, overall I'm becoming more and more disillusioned by modern gaming, particularly when it comes to existing series or IPs. It feels like more and more in every aspect of life short term profitability is prioritized over creativity and expression. Even the games we try to escape to from time to time are just feeling empty to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game set in the South Park universe.  Probably something you'd play on a literal snow day, and not for a whole season like the RPGs, and that is OK. _childDocuments_.review: The game itself, when you look at graphics, coop, playability and story, is, for me, in the higher parts of mediocre.The thing that made me give this game a negative review was playtime. _childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not up to par with the rest of the South park games, but it still is a fun game to play if your an avid south park fan. I played this game solo, so it was definitely more bland with just a bunch of AI, and it was 100% intended to play with friends. Though, i still liked a lot about this gameOverall, i think Matt and Trey did a wonderful job, and this game had an awesome concept. but the drawbacks were out of their control, i believe the tameness of this game was meant to prevent the rating of this game from going from M to A(18+). Also, the publisher did a poor job executing the game, probably why level design and story line were pretty good, yet combat was so bad. So i wouldn't blame this on Matt and Trey, i blame THQ for poorly executing it. I will recommend this game,  you have friends to play it with, it makes it so much more fun and entertaining.Overall, good game, but definitely not up to par with Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole.TLDR: Great game, if you have friends to play it with.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is nothing compared to the previous two games, Stick of truth, and Fractured but whole. Only 4h in playtime and i have beat the game on hard on my first run through. Only 5 missions, a total of 3 melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons. No armor, no different tier weapons to find or upgrade too. The only upgrade system they have implemented is the same you would find in a rouge like game. The one being a false sense of achievement. For the Black matter a lot of the upgrades seem like they could be there from the start because it is all player stat based. increase speed by 30%, increase damage by 10% ect. not really upgrades, just nerfes your paying to have undone. With the in game cards that get reset after each run, They are fun and unique, but with the limited amount of weapons to choose from, they become repetitive fast, making you tend to stick to the same builds that work. There are no collectables in the game to try and hunt down unlike the first two. The maps look so amazing and were fun to explore, only to be left disappointed when there was a invisible wall blocking the path or a roll of toilet paper waiting for me. There just wasnt any pay off for looking around. The comedy was alright for the first mission then slowly became non southpark type humor. Its hard to describe, buts like watching a pg-13 southpark that has a lot of mature jokes replaced with well nothing, no boundries were being pushed, it was such a safe game, it didnt feel like it was made by the southpark team at all. If you are a big fan of south park and really want to play this game, please for the love of god wait till its on sale.Multiplayer :  I dont understand this new trend of multiplayer having literally 0 communication system. Why have voice chat to talk to your teamates, when you can have a silly emote of a thumbs up or down. Want to tell your teamates to hurry up? cant. Want to let them know they missed a chest / upgrade? cant. This game is the perfect multiplayer game if you want to sit in isolation and not talk to your teammates what so ever. Not even a in game chat system. Just emotes. This is the standard now a days for a *multiplayer* release. but why?One of my biggest enjoyments with Stick of Truth is getting to actually be in the world of southpark, seeing familiar places from the show, and easter eggs sprinkled throught. Its all just snow here. Sure you can see City Wok and 2 other places from a certian angle on a level if you look at the background. But it just feels like you arent really in southpark too much

_childDocuments_.review: You the reader should only continue with your purchase if you are a decently big fan or more of South Park, or at least a somewhat of a fan of South Park, and you have a friend that is at least an average fan of the show. You also need friends. I've never played the game alone, but I can't imagine it's all that fun.The gameplay for South Park Snow Day is alright. It meets the requirement for what kind of game it, but if doesn't feel like they innovated past the bare minimum. There's only three weapons in melee, and three in range. The 3 melee basically do the same thing in terms of damage, however they do do somewhat different things, like the shield, if you couldn't tell, blocks stuff. The Range weapons are better in my opinion, whilst we all know weapons do damage no matter what, the range weapons at least feel like they do different things, whereas the melee weapons, even though one weapon looks like a heavy weapon, doesn't feel like you're doing anything different to the knives.There are five levels in the game, each taking about 20-40 minutes depending on the difficulty. The levels are actually quite good. each one isn't the same as a previous one, and they all end with a boss fight. the boss fights are pretty good as well, all unique. There are different enemies in each level, at least in terms of the harder ones. Your typical goon will always show up in a later level, as well as every enemy, but each level introduces a new enemy, and can piss you off according to what you're personally good at dealing with in video games.The story is alright. It doesn't make you feel like you're hanging with the gang, or in a south park episode, which is one of the best things about the previous two games. This game just makes you play with the gang, and play the part of new kid, rather than making you believe that you are in fact, the new kid. It's a snow day, a particularly deadly one, and all the kids decided that then was the best time to go out and play. Part of me wishes they did something new in terms of the aesthetics  the story surrounds (Stick of truth was fantasy, fractured but whole was super heroes), instead, they went with the fantasy one again. With what we got though, it's not world ending. The first two levels don't really do much with the story, it's more of an intro to their game they're playing, and the third and fourth have little story involved. It's simple, it's not complicated, but with how the gameplay is, I wish they would at least have put a little more into the story. Doesn't entirely matter though.Despite what may look like a negative review, I think it's still a decently good time with a friend. after all, that's the whole point of this game really. It's not amazing, nor is it good. It's not bad, it's just ok. only ok, not 'pretty ok', not 'just ok', just 'ok', which is why I'm not not recommending it, I'm just recommending it to specific people. Again, people with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the reviews on the store page and thought this was a case of Steam-dwelling neckbeards over-analyzing it to death. Like they were expecting this to play like Middle Earth: Shadow of War, and it didn't. I thought the reviews were expecting jokes of fish stick proportions, and got slightly less.Then, I got my unemployed friend, who had just sold 500 bucks worth of Counter Strike skins on the steam marketplace like an idiot, to buy it for me and himself so we could try it out for ourselves. After all, I have never once in my life been disappointed by a South Park product.My god does this suck. It sucks harder than your mama. Did you think that 'your mama' joke sucked? That 'your mama' joke was funnier than anything you'll encounter in this game. It's not that the jokes weren't great, nor were they bad. There just weren't any.It's like they spent 95% of the allocated budget on acquiring the rights to the South Park intellectual property, 4.5% on a teambuilding day, and then had about $78 left to make the actual game.The game itself, mechanically, is worse than what you can get some Indian on Fiverr to make you for less than the cost of a Big Mac. The writing feels like they had it done by some students. From an elementary school.I remember playing a PSP game roughly 13 years ago that had better combat and graphics than this abomination. That game not only had the groundbreaking light attack, but also a heavy attack!Are we making AA games with ChatGPT now? You really expect me to let you keep my unemployed friend's $30 for this garbage? Whoever green lighted this ass burger for release possesses Druish levels of greed. Watching your own parents die is funnier than this game. Chewing gum provokes more emotion and excitement than this does. The sole of my shoe is more interesting than this game.I'm very sad that the South Park team (or most likely Paramount) sold the rights to the South Park characters for use in a video game and then entirely stopped caring about what was going to be done with the franchise. _childDocuments_.review: I am having a blast with this game. It's essentially a South Park themed arpg/roguelike, where you can choose from 6 different weapons, and temporarily power them up with tons of different cards throughout each run. There are also permanent upgrades from currency collected. There are 5 levels available to do standard runs on, as well as 4 separate smaller arena areas with a "horde mode" type game. There is also an option for difficulty modifiers and more cosmetic unlocks after beating all levels for the first time. Going through each of the standard levels there is a story that I found very enjoyable as a huge fan of the show. In my opinion, combat and movement feels good - a bit floaty at times, but everything works as intended, and many of the skills become super fun to use after a few upgrades. There are also surprises in terms of what the weapons can morph into - for example on the wand you can actually get chain lightning, even though the base wand attack is a flamethrower. Was also very happy to see every level absolutely packed to the brim with secrets, from hidden resource chests to special card upgrades, exploring is rewarded. As a huge fan of roguelike games and South Park, I will definitely be playing a lot more of this.

_childDocuments_.review: IGN gave this game a 3. That makes this game sound like an unplayable mess. That kind of score gets you dirt hyped down to expect this to be a wake up and cry nightmare of an experience. What we have here is a 6 out of 10, but that's only really at best. The combat here is alright. Hits connect with enemies and they take damage. Doesn't feel as crunchy or as impactful as most other beat-em up systems, but it gets the job done. Upgrades and powers are fun to use if you don't mind pummeling hoards of very similar enemies in very similar looking arenas (with some recognizable differences in design, but not much. They're all still snowy wastelands. It's on theme, but you do want more variety and enrichment in your enclosure.).Don't come into this expecting a plot like the epic story of the two previous RPGs. Those are more comparable to the movie or the specials in scope. This is more like a regular episode of the show in scope. Maybe not quite as crass or full throttle as their usual material, but they're still a pinch of poop jokes in this. It does leave you wanting more, but looking at what the season pass offers it doesn't look like muuuch more is coming juuust yet.My advice, get a friend or two to play the campaign with, and Danse with Ravenous Shadows with random matchmaking. There's still something worthwhile in here if you're looking for a mindless brawler to pass a weekend with. And if you're writing fan fiction for your New Kid oc you based on the Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole, there's a nugget of inspiration in here for you chew on. Also yes, there's a dedicated toot button, but I'm not gonna tell you what it is.

But this one is good and I'm glad they at least made a different genre instead of stopping making games, def worth the buy to play with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: They nailed the South Park style in 3D, which is a really impressive feat on its own. Like others have reviewed, the voice acting is kind of lackluster occasionally, the gameplay is really like a co-op souls-like (not necessarily a bad thing, just overdone at this point, and the card system is unique), and the DLCs are very obviously forced (the season pass is basically just a promise of a ton of new features and content)You'll have a ton of fun, especially if you like South Park and the previous games, but you can tell there's still quite a ways to go with development still

I recommend that people try it but be warned not everyone is going to think it's money well spent. _childDocuments_.review: It is not a bad game, out of the 3 south park games in this so far trilogy its certainly the weakest but its a good game that lacks content.You get 3 melee weapons, 3 ranged, 6 power ups and can only bring 1 melee, 1 ranged, and 2 power ups, plus its a repetitive grinding mess of a game that is good but just barely on that status. _childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much content that has been missed out on, so many characters and references never even touched on.I sure do hope more is added, more skills and weapons. 3 choices? really? one magic staff type? what's happening with all of the wasted space in the lobby? there's soccer goals but no trigger in game to make it feel intractable. Infact so many times I walk up to an object hoping to trigger something in game or have some sort of collectable and we're not even treated to witty dialogue. There is shockingly little content for a game that plays so well.You add some emotes that have sound but don't put in the great nostalgic jingles of the show? Is there plans of pvp? 5v5? there's the mode that lets you fight very short waves of NPCs, it would be neat to have a progression where you use points/money gathered to progress to the next area (yes sounds like COD zombies but who cares it's fun and feels rewarding).Would be funny versing other players with the randomised ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards, have custom lobby settings etc yet we're left with this shell of a game that leaves you and your friends saying "is that it?" at the end. I hope content updates make the price tag worth it but until then, it's a no.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I really like this game. It gives an interesting feeling of nostalgia mixed with cool modern roguelike elements. Of course there really needs to be more weapon and spell variety. The environments are really pretty, although it's a shame we can't freely explore the town. I'm excited to see the future updates for this game. After seeing the reviews I had the bar set so low for this game, and while I wasn't blown away, I was surprised with how much fun I was having. There needs to be some work as the gameplay is a little janky and it's a bit light on the content but I really hope they continue developing this and adding stuff. Even in its current state I'd still recommend if you like south park and roguelike/hack and slash games
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: $30 does not justify 5-6 hours of content, there are plenty of games for $30 that will provide you 2-10x the amount of hours of gameplay. Had to refund this because I was disappointed after buying and seeing there were small chapters after playing through chapter one. It's a fun game though and I would buy it on a big sale.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game for a long time just to be totally dissapointed. I hope they make the next one like the first 2 games that played like a southpark episode. This game is to short too buggy and no fun at all its basically just fighting people nonstop and picking things up to take from a to b. For real not even worth 10 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is like you're in the actual show, even the 3D brings it all to life even more and they did a damn good job in showing it. Combat is well implemented and it has a roguelike element that'll keep you on your toes each time you play. When you fail a quest, you will be able to replay it. However, what most people fail to mention is you will receive different scenarios. There's not many, but it does add some uniqueness to watching the different scenes come to life.It took me and my friend 7 hours, and that's from actually playing the game. There's also a free DLC you can download and you can unlock more fun through a wave system game mode.EDIT: Changing my review since nothing really has been done to the game since I played it when it came out.Saying all of that, the game doesn't have replayability and they're making it worse by adding DLCs. The game needs a bit more content in it too, something we can grind for. I defended them at first, but they made it clear they don't care about the game, only to milk it for money and take advantage of the "South Park" name. The DLCs shouldn't be DLCs but free in-game updates since it's cosmetic items for the most part. Honestly, don't bother -- even on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

name: Gunfire Reborn
detailed_description: About This Game: Gunfire Reborn is an adventure level-based game featuring FPS, roguelite, and RPG elements. Players can control unique heroes—each with different abilities—as they adventure through procedurally-generated levels and pick up randomly-dropped weapons. You can play Gunfire Reborn alone or cooperatively with up to three other players (4-player co-op). Every level is random; each new restart is a brand-new experience. You will meet different heroes and experience new weapons, items, checkpoints, and unique combat rhythms throughout the game. Game Features: FPS+Roguelite+RPG combined gameplay, construct diverse Build through death cycle for different experience Elaborate, yet randomized stage experience Over 100 different items and various weapons Many heroes and multiple game plus with different game mechanism Unique art style Co-op level-based adventure

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game I really enjoy. What first drew me to it was that the player character is a cat. The game could be described as Borderlands meets Risk of Rain 2. Rogue like where when you die, you can upgrade and get a little bit better. The weapons are random drops with occasional elemental perks, all pretty fun to use and play around with. Best played in coop, where you can revive each other. In singleplayer, you have to use some soul currency to get a revive. Would recommend!I also enjoy the new playable characters, and that they're all cute animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth $12.The first 2 hours, the game is fun. However, after the first 2 hours, you realize that the game is a entire grindfest just to progress. You play the SAME sequence of maps over and over again to get inches of progress.Multiplayer helps, but it does not hide the fact that there is so little content.BTW, I bought the game with my brother. He joined an online game and finished/got carried through the entire game within 3 hours. There's nothing else to do in this game except grind to max level (but no needed since you can beat the game at talent level 20) or grind to finish the game on elite mode--which is the same game but with a multiplier on the stats.Highly recommend to WAIT to get this game on sale and/or for more content.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't strictly a review, just a warning for those who use arbitrary resolutions: this game does NOT support arbitrary resolutions. It only supports preset resolutions for a couple different aspect ratios. As an example, my 21:9 resolution of 3840x1600 is not supported even though other 21:9 resolutions are. So if you use an arbitrary/uncommon resolution, be prepared to play letterboxed or pillarboxed.

_childDocuments_.review: Great FPS roguelite, it's incredibly fun to play with friends.I like to think of this game as a more casual version of Risk of Rain 2:- I don't have to rush my friends- You can read what power-ups do before you pick them up- If you end up not wanting the power ups, you can drop it- All loot is instanced, no competing or asking for itemsIf you love multiplayer roguelites, definitely give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: It's been awhile since i wrote a review and Gunfire Reborn deserves to be the one to wipe off that dusty critique board. The game is astonishing even in its early phase, each build you make fits your play style which i can respect. If the game were to add 1 more hero to complete the 4 player squad then it'll just make this game even better, but that's just an opinion of mine. If you like rougelike games then i'd suggest picking this one up before the price rises when the  comes out!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that you want to like. It has an interesting art style, cool concepts but it just ultimately fails in executing its ideas over and over. -Upgrades feel trivial and never make you notice them until you hit a flat wall in difficulty where you are basically shooting nerf darts just chipping away slowly and kiting an enemy for 5 min does not feel engaging-Healing is almost nonexistent which wouldn't be a big issue if your characters didn't feel so slow and plodding that there is slim chance to dodge all attacks as they throw 25 enemies at you in confined spaces-While there are really cool concepts for guns and items none of them meaningfully change gameplay and the game has the overall strategy of just repeatedly shooting braindead AI while they slowly slowly die. Like basic enemies still take multiple clips of ammo-They sub any difficulty in strategy or design in enemies in favor of just throwing more enemies at you and just adjusting damage scaling-the skill tree/unlock progression system is unbelievably grindy for such shallow gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: Hey hey people,This is a roguelike game with Borderlands mechanics (Skills, Skilltree and the dmg types elec,acid and fire)-> in short everything good about Borderlands without the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story (cough Ava cough)The levels are rng generated, same as the loot.There are 3 "Biomes" Asian Tomb, Desert and Fishing Village. Each Biome has unique enemies with very challenging skills.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and unique roguelike with a diverse cast of interesting characters, combined with the many different weapons and scrolls, allow for many different ways to fight through the different areas! for me, the reincarnation difficulty levels are especially fun when playing with friends, testing your skills and knowlage by throwing increasingly more powerful enemies at you, making you think and adapt on the spot, when your damage suddenly doesnt seem as high anymore and the enemies are all the more out for your death.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was good when it was in open access, and it's just gotten even better over time. The amount of content is actually pretty insane and very polished. _childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever written a review on steam before but I really felt the need to review this game. This game is amazing and shows a lot of promise. It's admittedly my first ever rogue-like but is also quickly becoming my favorite. It is a looter-shooter rogue-like with tons of guns, think Enter the Gungeon meets Borderlands.Still in Alpha so somewhat lacking in variety of enemies and location at the moment but gameplay is addicting and haven't heard anyone say anything bad about this game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Best roguelite FPS-  Great progression and not incredibly grindy .    The developer has found a great balance for time sink and power.  Very, very minimal power creep but as you progress and start to understand the enchant combos and skills the more challenge you're willing to undergo.   Every character has their place and once you find a playstyle you enjoy you can make it viable in most if not all challenge tiers.    An amazing game to play with friends as well, albiet there are maybe one or two party buffs in the form of lootable scrolls .
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a lot of fun, highly recommendAbove, was my original statement. After many hours let me add - it is still at on of fun.I feel even as the stages do remain the same, the runs everytime can be different & improved. The gameplay is smooth and can be even hectic at times - getting the right build via scrolls & the right weapons along with it, is a nice touch. The characters are all great in their own way & add different ways to run through the game.I even bought the DLC, which I never do for any game, but I like the direction gunfire is heading. I can't wait to see what other gamemodes they add & possibilities for the gameplay.Many people say it is like borderlands, I can safely say its fair, the guns can come with different elemental effects and perks - they can be modified and upgraded.The game is simple to start and is fun for casual play.I primarily love the art style and the setting the game is placed in, I hope we get to see the world be expanded and added onto.The game is super fun to run solo, you can pause and pick up - you can save in between stages and come back to it. You can play with friends, share loot and help each other complete builds they have in mind. You can even match with randoms, and so far everyone I've met is super nice and friendly, its nice not to run into toxic players consistently like other games. So whether you're a solo player, like to play with friends, or even make some - this is an added bonus.I still think you should consider picking up this game, if you have not.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: If you like fps games and roguelites this is a must play. The game has so much content after all of the updates so far and they are still adding new stuff.The gun-play feels great, every gun feels different and familiar if you played other fps games. (Some great design choices have been made here for ex. the brick feels very similar to minecraft bow). The inscription system can make a break a gun and unlock new synergies.Amazing synergies. You can really break the game with a specific combo and it feels great every time. Most scrolls and a lot of inscriptions have a downside that you have to overcome. Game awards greatly considering how a given scroll or weapon will affect your overall build and there are a lot of parameters to consider.Very well tuned difficulty progression. When you are new the game offers a modest challenge allowing you to learn the ropes, succeed and fail catastrophically. You get new abilities and unlocks with the skill tree that stays between runs; it makes the game a lot easier. After 4 difficulty levels you unlock the reincarnations which unlocks a whole new layer of the game with new combos and mechanics, making the game drastically more difficult in the process.Good selection of heroes with a lot of skills and interaction. Some guns are bad on most heroes but very good on others. Some heroes like fox are very strong compared to others.I personally find the art-style, the setting and the eastern influence very appealing. All of the heroes are cute anthro animals Overall this game is amazing. I love pretty much everything about it and it's still alive and evolving. You don't need to be a sweaty aimer or big brain theory crafter to enjoy this one, but if you are both you might just fall in love. Highly recommended especially for the price.Some tips for new players:- Understand how elemental effects work and how they interact with each other.- Think twice before picking a scroll up.- Unlock as much of the survival tree as fast as possible- Don't skip elite vaults
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: A sleeper hit! Lovely art style and solid mechanics. Production values are high and well above your typical early access game. I don't know whether it's realistic to expect this to become as deep and polished as Deep Rock Galactic, but for 12 bucks this is a definite buy. Very playable in solo, and a blast in coop!Update September 2020: The patches added lots of new enemies, weapons and another playable character, as well as ingame voice chat. The difficulty is a lot more even now too, though you will still need to level up a bit to get further in. If I had one criticism it's the lack of ability to join games that are already in progress, though that would require some balancing.If you like fast paced FPS, this is a definite buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun single player, and even more fun in co-op. Each level is random, each weapon you receive is random, and each boss fight is random. No two runs are ever the same. Each hero has a unique leveling tree that is completed while you run through the maze of levels. I recommend you and your party all choose different hero's and figure out what weapons, scrolls and skills they need to compliment each other. Also, the two hero's that require in game money to purchase are well worth the grind! Excellent game! I can't wait for more updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many rougelites on the market now a days, but the good ones are few and far between.When it comes to FPS rougelites the story gets even worse, only ones I can remember from the top of my mind is "Hypergun" and "Ziggurat" and now this sort of.This game has a good foundation and lots of potential but buyer beware.It only have 3 levels with 5 "floors" before you encounter the boss, metabucks / metaprogression is a thing(ofc) so a lot of grinding before you are able to progress towards higher difficulty or even reach the end boss, already a lot of useless / redundant passive buff items(think buff / stat tweak items from Isaac), weapon balancing is bad and some weapons are really boring, only 2 characters to play as, some platforming sections that feels more wonky then they ought to be and you seem kind of OP in MP (note I have only played with 2 players so might be harder with 3-4).Despite all these issues I chose to thumb it up because it is just plain fun to play and I hope that the devs that already crated the foundation hopefully have a direction and know what they are doing. If not this is $/£ 10 for for quite a few hours of mindless fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is pretty fun. I tend to like looter shooter games and play them mindlessly for many hours. This game scratches that itch because of the smooth gameplay and multitude of build options. I've only been focusing on a couple heroes but there are a lot of options.The gameplay mechanics are straightforward and the character control is smooth. The game also looks pretty good, the art style is nice.  However, I wish some of the drops like coins and essence looked better. I want to be excited about getting coins.The only issue I have with the game is that the upgrade options can be wordy and in some cases it's not clear what exactly the effect will be. Sometimes the wording and grammar (in English) are not correct.I only play single player so maybe multiplayer will be even better.If you like looter shooters then check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: A roguelite fps that doesn't hold your hand, I am excited to see what's to come from the development of it and the already large player base.The gunplay is smooth, once you get the level layouts down you can zoom through them to get back to where you died last, and the multiplayer can be really fun as it increases the difficulty of the game that's already difficult but fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible Game 10/10!I bought it back in the days right after it came out in Early Access when I searched for an Action Roguelike that has Borderlands Loot/Build Mechanics. So far so good, played it around 80h in the first months and waited until its further developed. Got back into the game and I am even more impressed.The amount of content, different characters with unique abilities, the ways of taking control over the run in many ways while still having a RNG factor to it. The Difficulty System works great and feels fair on higher difficulties, all in all an amazing game that feels very polished, good for both casual players or theorycrafters who like to min max their builds :DI also hope the devs keep updating this game, its impressing that they keep updating the game regularly until this day with huge patches/balance changes:)
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I've had loads of fun with the new melee weapons and love that up-close combat style, weaving between the enemies, but what i would love to see next is a melee weapon that could block/deflect/parry projectiles, because i find it slightly difficult to get close to an enemy to kill it while sustaining minimal damage. The weapon could reward the player with increased crit dmg on the next attack  for each block/deflect/parryAnyways, love the game, keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t know about this game at first until a friend tried to get me to play. Was still unsure, but for 20 bucks? I figured why not?I love this game. It’s been almost addicting! It’s fun on your own, but playing with others makes it even more fun. The numerous types of weapons, upgrades, and skills keeps things fresh.The weapon, character, and boss designs? Amazing. As an artist I keep getting drawn to the design aspects of this game. I love everything about it. It feels challenging, but rewarding?Frankly 20 dollars is a STEAL for how much I’ve gotten out of this game.Absolutely love this game. Highly recommend if you enjoy games like Hades or Risk of Rain 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a year now and in that time there has been 3-4 large content updates and I've bought the game for multiple friendsThe gunplay is extremely satisfying. There are tons of guns to use and the different characters each have unique mechanics that change the way you play. My only complaint is that the game can be kind of confusing at first because some of the powerups/weapons have very lengthy descriptions. I also wish the movement was slightly more fluid, but it is still very solid.Would highly recommend to anyone who enjoys a fun, co-op fps with roguelike elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is my very first steam review. I got this game because my brother said it would be fun. I went into to it not expecting much but was actually very happy with what I got! The game is insanely fun with many different combos that you can do each time you go through, For a beta, there is a solid amount of content in the game. It is very easy for a new player to pick up and go. Thought there are a few cons, sometimes enemies will do inconsincant attack patterns, the jumping can be a bit buggy in my time played, there is some odd clipping that can happen when doing the jump puzzles which is really aggravating cause it will feel like you get cheated from more loot. Also there are only 2 playable characters at the moment who are very different, tho IMO the cat is a far better character due to its Kit being able to do elemental damage, and all the skill trees work together well where as the dog, the skills don't mesh together that great (mostly due to the fact the he has 0 way to do elemental DMG on his own, and the sever lack of decent explosive weapons). Thought I do think these issues can be fixed/changed. I personally think the dog could get fire damage on his nades, and maybe they could add another roll for weapons allowing explosive rounds at the cost of mag size. I am not a dev. but these are just small ideas that could work. Also I do belive based off the art work there will be another character that is a bird and that would be neat. The gun play and fights are actually really fun, and playing with friends is SUPER fun with all the crazy elemental and weapon conbos you can do. Overall I HIGHLY suggest getting this game if you like rouge like shooters, The game is very fairly priced, the art is amazing and the gameplay for the most part is really fun, The game i can most compare this is Enter the Gungeoun, which is another really fun rouge like shooter. But again, try this game out, I think you will enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and addictive roguelite shooter that has great gun play, a great selection of different weapon types and allows you to build various character builds so that every run can feel different. You can jump in and play Solo but the game does offer co-op multiplayer which adds another fun dynamic to the game. There is definitely a lot of potential for this game to become even more of an amazing title and I hope the Developers continue to support the game and possibly look at adding character customization, new weapons and enemies and new areas/stages.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game is very simple: you start, you shoot, and try to survive till the very end with the weapons and scrolls provided. This might not sound like there is much in the game, but is more than what people realize until they start getting into it more frequently. It is captivating and very addictive as you progress more with the characters. Playing by yourself is fun, but with friends takes the experience to a whole new level and the community is friendly in helping one another. I would highly encourage people to give this game an opportunity, and time always flies by whenever you play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun roguelike. The combat is very smooth and there is a good variety of weapons, power ups and characters. However, if you don't own the DLC, you see the same three areas over and over. That's not bad because the gameplay is fun, but I would prefer some other alternative areas each run instead of the same three. Higly recommend it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Upon reading another review that described the game as a refreshing break between sessions of Risk of Rain, and a lover of looter-shooters like it, I bought RoR II and this with that expectation. What surprised me was the fantastic gameplay that made Gunfire Reborn my true mainstay. Every area ends with Ascensions, which are character-specific upgrades: you immediately feel the presence of every choice you make, even when you've collected 50 ascensions, it always feels like you're "finally turning on" your build. In addition, the scrolls are the best breadcrumb trail you could ask for, no matter the "rarity" every one feels important (to someone, even if it's not in your build) and can create hilariously fun games. Make your way to Reincarnation (whew) and there are even more mechanics and passives to unlock. My one suggestion to the developers is to add special third ascension bonuses to all ascension lines. Some Ascensions are a little linear (bunny girl is fun but could be really fun with more rate-of fire mechanics in her third ascension tiers).
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little roguelite where you shoot guns, and get to feel like a god when when you get it right. I have enjoyed my time with it. Season 2 patch has come with a lot of very negligent mistakes. Everything from missing translations (Chinese text left in the game), minor and major networking issues, and some previously acceptable translations being replaced with unintelligible Chinglish. _childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an interesting game that mixes FPS, rogue-lite, and a bit of RPG elements to create what I find is a pretty fun shooter experience. The first thing you'll probably notice are the aesthetics of the game. The characters and the environments use this low poly 3D style with a bit of Chinese influence thrown in. Some people might find this simple and maybe even a bit dull, but I personally think it works very well for this game. Because the graphics are so simple, it makes it pretty easy to see and know what is going on at the moment and as a plus, I also find it is quite easy to keep a high frame rate at all times during each run. Same thing can be said about the UI, being simple, but also giving you information you need without being obstructive. I think there should be some options to change or remove stuff such as the damage numbers, but it gets the job done.I'll briefly go over the other aspects of the game here as they don't play nearly as big a factor as the gameplay. Story is... basically nonexistent. You'll get some brief dialogue when you first start the game and when you first complete a run, but that's about it. Next, the music in the game is good, but somewhat limited. There's the main menu theme, music for each stage, and music for each boss. One thing I found neat is how the stage music is mostly atmospheric at first, but when you get into battle with enemies, it ramps up into something more energetic and fitting for battle until it's over. Lastly, I found the sound design to be pretty great. The weapons sounding exactly how you would imagine them to, the feedback when you land a critical hit on an enemy, and the different sounds that each enemy makes adds a lot to the enjoyment of the game.Finally we get to the gameplay, which has a lot to go over. Seeing how this is an FPS game, the weapons are pretty important and thankfully they do not disappoint. There are a total of 38 different weapons to use as of right now and they range from the humble assault rifle to more absurd things like a fire breathing dragon or laser gloves that make you feel like you're playing as Iron Man. All the weapon archetypes you would expect such as snipers, shotguns, and rocket launchers, to name a few are here so finding something you end up loving to use is pretty likely. There's a critical hit system for hitting enemies in their weak points and a lucky shot system that gives you a percentage based chance to deal bonus damage to an enemy depending on how high your chance is.Elements are also in the game and there are three different ones that can apply status effects. Fire which deals extra damage against flesh and can deal damage over time, Lightning which does extra damage against shields and can cause that enemy to take extra damage from everything, and Corrosion which does extra damage against armor and slows enemies down drastically. It is also possible to fuse these status effects together to cause an extremely powerful effect depending on what combination is fused.There are three different characters you can play as as of this review and they all play differently from each other. You have the cat which uses an orb that's capable of stopping enemies in place for several seconds and corrosive grenades, then there is the dog who can dual wield weapons and use explosive grenades, and finally the bird who has a leaping attack that can restore his armor and a cleave attack in the place of grenades that can hit enemies all around him. All of these characters share a universal dash ability that can be used for dodging or just getting around a bit more quickly. This may make them seem a bit underwhelming, but that is where the ascensions and scrolls systems come into play.Ascensions are obtained at the end of each level through goblets and they give you the choice of upgrading one of three randomly chosen ascensions. The majority of ascensions in the game give some powerful boosts for doing specific things or power up your characters unique moves. Each character gets their own unique ascensions that allow you to fine tune them to a specific play style. You can obtain the same ascension up to three times in a run to power up their effects, with the third level  being much more powerful than the previous ones. If that doesn't sound good enough for you, there are also scrolls to further power yourself up. Scrolls are items you can randomly obtain in vaults or purchased from a merchant if one is in their inventory. They're typically a lot more specific in their usage than the ascensions, but because of the sheer number of different scrolls there are (there are 100+ you can find), you are bound to find just the right scrolls you need to end up having a run where you just melt everything.There is something important I should go over that may be a bit controversial, and that is the talents system. Talents are permanent upgrades that you unlock at the end of a run, whether you die or make it to the end. You purchase these upgrades with soul essence that you earn by killing enemies. For the most part these upgrades let you access things that you couldn't before like the vaults or the weapon chest at the start of a run or boosting the amount of soul essence and copper (which is used to buy stuff from merchant and upgrade the level of your weapons) you can earn in a run. Permanent upgrades are nothing new in these rogue-lite style games, but the thing I have a problem with is just how much easier the game gets when you unlock a bunch of these.When I first started playing the game, it was pretty challenging. You start out with only the cat and a vast number of the weapons and scrolls need to be unlocked by doing certain things before they'll stop dropping in runs. I had to be constantly on my toes against even the weakest enemies as a couple of hits from anything would spell the end of a run. As I kept playing and learning the patterns of the enemies, I unlocked a fair amount of stuff that made the runs significantly easier. This resulted in a snowball effect where because I knew what to expect and the power gained from my talents and new items, the game became so much easier than the start. It got to the point where I was winning much more than I lost even on the harder difficulty.Even though it's super fun to destroy everything, it gets very boring if I'm able to do that consistently each run. I think this game could benefit from a more challenging difficulty and changing some of the stuff on the talent tree that just raise your stats. Getting stuff like taking 15% less damage from enemies or dealing 25% more damage to enemies, while effective, are just boring in a game like this that rewards you for smart builds and contribute to the lack of challenge that higher level players experience.Despite these issues, this game is still a blast to play whether you play it solo or in coop. This has been one of my favorite FPS games to play this year and with the attention to feedback that the developers are giving to the community, it can only go up from here. If you get annoyed at having to play the same parts to learn how to combat each enemy or the talents system bothers you, this probably isn't the game for you. For everyone else, I can't recommend it enough. It's so refreshing to play an early access game this year that isn't a cash grab or just a bare-bones proof of concept that doesn't go anywhere. At only 12 USD, I've got more hours out of this game than the vast majority of triple AAA titles I've played and I still want to keep putting hours into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviewers have mentioned, game is a First Person Shooter-Roguelite. The game is in fact a  since it has permanent progress/unlocks available that make your journey easier the more you play. Game features at the time of writing  with their own abilities and strengths (Some characters synergize better with faster firing guns for example), randomized power ups (called scrolls) and weapons (with randomly rolled perks & bonuses similar to Borderlands) in each run which makes a new run always interesting. Each of these elements provide a perfect basis for the meat of the game, which is the gunplay. The gunplay feels solid most of the time. The game rewards you for aiming well, each of the enemies have a weak spot  and shots fired to them provide critical hits, and that damage is further increased by your critical damage modifier which is different for each weapon. The game provides a decent amount of weapons at start, and you'll unlock more as you complete certain achievements within the game. This doesn't necessarily mean that the best weapons are behind unlocks, just different weapons really.The game progresses through 3 zones, with randomized loot, randomized enemy encounters, mini-bosses and special encounters (Horde defense for example) very standard for the roguelike/roguelite genre. Each of the zones have their own aesthetic, which adds a bit of flavor to break the monotony of repeated runs. All of the zones may contain "vaults" which are optional side rooms to explore with their own rewards and challenges. Each area or zone has their own collection of vault challenges, but they contain generally the same themes of miniboss fights or platforming.In conclusion, Gunfire Reborn is a great mix of FPS & Roguelite genres. The gunplay is solid, even though some of the weapons are not or don't feel quite as impactful as others. Sound design is good and background music is solid, providing a nice ambience for each of your runs.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly enjoyable FPS game with decently fleshed-out roguelite elements to boot. It's still a bit rough around the edges, however it is still in early access and there should hopefully be a lot of polish and content being made with each update.The gunplay feels pretty good, each gun feels distinct and there is already a large variety of weapons to use. You have your standard weapons like your assault rifle, your SMG, your pistol, etc, but there are also pretty novel weapons as well such as the Thunderglove (a glove you wear that shoots a beam that hits all nearby enemies) and the Bone Cannon (basically Zarya's cannon from Overwatch, it sucks in all nearby enemies and detonates after a few seconds). Each weapon is well animated and they're all worth using, even the starting pistol which actually scales with your other weapons so that it's still relevant throughout a run.Next, I really think that the progression of the game is pretty well done. You have both run-related progression (such as weapon damage, scrolls which give unique modifiers to the player, etc) as well as permanent progression (such as increased health, ammo capacity, etc), and you always feel like there's something to strive towards as a result. Some of the aforementioned scrolls can really change the way you play, such as one that gives you two additional dash charges or one where headshots do 4x damage but at the cost of lower non-headshot damage, and it's fun to see what combination of modifiers you can get.The two characters as of writing are quite fun to play as. You start with a hat-donning cat who can throw smoke grenades and has an AoE stun, which makes him pretty strong at dealing element damage and taking out large groups of enemies. Once you hit level 30, you then unlock the second character which is the dog - my personal favourite! He can dual-wield his weapons and can spec into being tanky while doing so, making him pretty solid for melting single targets with his unmatched DPS. There are more characters coming, so I'm hoping they are just as fun to play as the existing ones.Finally, the aesthetic of the game is decently charming in my opinion. Yes, the graphics are pretty simple and the characters are a bit generic, but I do like the colourful environments and enemy design. But I think most importantly the game runs really well due to the lack of graphical fidelity which is always important for shooter games.If you've ever played Borderlands, you'll be aware of the different elements that each weapon can have which give additional damage towards certain types of enemies. This is pretty much the case for this game as well and it works identically: fire is strong against flesh (red health), corrosion works best against armour (yellow health), and shock makes short work of shields (blue health). That being said, I was never really a fan of this type of design to begin with as it means that not having a weapon of the required element just means that you'll take way longer to kill those enemies and you can unfortunately only hold two weapons at a time, so you'll be missing out on at least one element for your guns. This also trivialises weapons with no element as it's just too effective to combo elements due to the bonuses you get from doing so, which is where you can dish out lots of damage.As for the level design, it's decent enough but it never really shakes things up. You start in the same zone and the level progression is pretty much identical throughout each run. Additionally, some of the portal areas you can access are a bit annoying as there are platforming sections in them that don't feel that great.I only have one real aspect that I disliked about the game, but unfortunately it's probably the biggest drawback for me which is the online co-op. I feel that this game would be even more fun with friends or even just randoms as there is matchmaking, but in its current state it's simply too laggy and seemingly has client-side lag that occurs whenever enemies spawn, which has lead to a lot of cheap deaths as I wait several seconds for the game to update. Definitely the biggest area for improvement, but it's understandable given that this isn't a high-budget title.For an early access title, this is already worth the price of admission and I've had quite a bit of fun with it. I definitely recommend giving it a go if you're looking for a new shooter to play or at least keeping an eye on it as it receives updates. OK, the devs have responded to this review and I think I should offer some more clarity regarding the online co-op of the game. As I was going off of matchmade games, the lag issues may just be on my end as I have yet to verify if they're because I am connecting to far-away hosts or just hosts with poor Internet. The game seems to use peer-to-peer networking so it could purely be a host issue and not an issue with the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Boy oh boy, where to begin with this gem. I'm closing in on the good 5 hour mark and I'm already 10 levels away from the secondary character, doggy boy gunzerker.Pros:>Lots of replayability, with semi-random levels>Weapons. Hoo boy, lots of weapons>More weapon drops based on what you do>4 player co-op>No need to worry about your friends stealing all your loot, it's individually rolled. You'll get a different weapon than your friends, and they'll only be able to take it if you drop it.>Every run is different. One run you'll have a blackhole gun that shoots 3 different projectiles and an ability that heals you for every bit of damage you do, the next you'll be rocking an aimbot gun with an ability that does extra critical damage.>Enemy health, shields, armor, etc. scales with how many players there are so they're not a joke. Still a challenge with a full 4 players.>Constantly growing in strength, soon with the ability to start with a weapon other than the Foundry. (starting weapon)>Vaults are great challenges to get you occult scrolls, which are ultimately the determining factor of how well your run will go.Cons:>Previous area enemies are somewhat forgotten. If they reappear in later areas, I'm unaware of that, let me know if I'm wrong.>Fight an enemy once and you always have a viable strategy to beat them. You won't find a horsehead enemy that has special buffs or anything, so you can just restrain them with the Crown Prince's E power, then blow them away with an Argus shot to the head.>Enemy damage outputs become ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quickly. Say bye to your shield and 3/4 of your health within 5 seconds, even if you have full on both.>Lu Wu aggros almost indefinitely on a player in multiplayer until they're downed. It might be the same with later bosses, as well, but once again, it's hard to get further than the desert when enemies can one-tap you.>Lack of vault variations.Overall? Good game. Most of the points in the cons are just there because it's still quite a new game, and one in early access, on top of just being my personal preference for a game. I have no doubt in my mind that the devs will continue expanding on some of the areas.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, especially if you have friends. It's fun alone too, but in certain circumstances you can die very quickly and sometimes seemingly unfairly, thus ending your run. I've seen the game compared to Borderlands in others' comments and while I don't wholly disagree, you shouldn't buy this game if you are expecting an open world with quests all around. Instead, this game is a level-based shooter where you have to fight a boss every few levels. The levels themselves are fairly small making you be contained in a somewhat-tight space with the monsters, so you will need to move constantly. Lastly, you should keep in mind that one playthrough can last pretty long, one to two hours probably (I have never finished it), however you can save the game after every boss.Overall I have enjoyed the game a lot, and I would definitely recommend it to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an interesting little (but a lot of content) game where I find myself coming back to time after time. When I take a break from Steam and come back playing, I always play Gunfire Reborn. Great game-play, Great visuals, and a Great dev team. Each run is a learning experience and never feels like it was a wasted run. Each gun has its unique play-style and has great synergy with certain scrolls and occasionally with certain guns and each scroll has a synergy with different play-styles and few scrolls are for all play-styles. It encourages different play-styles each run and sometimes within the same run. It encourages using the weapons that you pick up and using secondary skills that other games tend to fail doing. I found myself running ammo and skills empty, something in other games I NEVER do. No resource hoarding here, no sirree. I have yet to go online, but I want to play this with my family. Also, personal favorite guns are the Frenzied shark, Wild hunt, Hell, and the Foundry; always a soft-spot for the gun that stays by our side (and infinite ammo).Overall, a well-rounded game that I've played since just before full release and I will continue playing time and time again.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The roguelike FPS I've been waiting for. Even at this early stage of development the game feels and plays great, with enough variety and depth to make nearly 20 hours of play absolutely fly past. The gunplay is really, really good - on par with AAA titles let alone small indie games - which is what has let down every other FPS roguelike I've tried. The abilities and progression - both in and out of run - are well implemented with enough depth to make each run varied.The game requires a little balancing and some of the translation is a bit off (the dev team are from Hong Kong but have now enlisted help with localisation) but these are really minor issues which I'm confident will be ironed out during early access. The dev team seem very communicative and receptive to community feedback.Performance can be a sticking point in early access games for me, but I've got no issues here. Running on ultra 1080p i'm getting really smooth feeling minimum 130fps - except for late game on elite mode, where it dips to 80-90 - with just a 1060 6gb and haven't experienced any game breaking bugs or crashes.Overall I haven't been this impressed with an early access game since Slay The Spire. It's well worth the cost of entry and I think it'll evolve into one of the best games in the roguelike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Great base gunplay, simple-but charming visual style and a good amount of post-launch support. even the different characters and eventual "the grind is done, now just spend the special currency to enhance your in-run bonuses" is a nice feeling.alas the co-op servers have started to throw me into 250+ ping servers 3/4 of the time now which given the "half-second to dash into cover/out-of-the-telegraph-zone or your are dead" reflex-checks tends to put a damper on the fun. furthermore the visual VFX-mess now rivals or even surpasses that of gearboxes failed PvP game battleborndrop/run RNG is high variancezero forgiveness reflex-checks and enemy moltov-spam make half of most areas a zone of death within seconds of starting a fightand the super idiotic "if you die in co-op you get no loot, no gold, no upgrades AND can only be revived by someone buying you back alive from a specific peddler" just makes an otherwise great base-experience an exercise in frustration all too often. The current season based around RNG-perk enemy pets/summons many of which are the size of chonky enemies and that run around full speed into a group-hug with the tougher foes (blocking bullets and LoS) and vary wildly between "oh it's deleting the entire zone without me doing anything" to "ah, it's blocking my view/aim with it's glowing wire-frame" for the 6th time this room. The more that's added to the game the harder it becomes to recommend as visually, wide-area-damage reflex-checks and high RNG variance-wise it simply throws too much crap into the player-view and expects you to keep headshotting using projectile attacks while half your screen is covered in telegraph-attack-warnings and the other half is covered in some form of fire/tornado/bomb effects-spam while enemies slide around like pinballs as they fire flamethrowers, melee seemingly without any need to plant their feet (they just run right through you dealing moderate damage and often applying some form of DoT/knock-effect), lob multi-munition moltovs or simply snipe you from the back of the arena while the chaff takes up your attention.Barely a recommend at this point as the devs need to seriously tone down the nonsense and get back to point n click player vs room-horde  and less about filling the screen with the maximum amount of fire, bad-stuff and clutter they can jam into each encounter.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn's game play is unparalleled in it's genre.This is an FPS, Roguelite, RPG that you can play with up to 4 friends. The Eastern influences on the gameplay and art style is a refreshing take for an FPS. It may feel a little jolting at first but I assure you it is worth it.The movement can feel a little slow starting out, but this changes quickly with various pick ups during your run that will change that. These pick ups during a run are called "scrolls" and they are what makes every single run unique. The scrolls can give extra dashes, faster movement, raw damage to all your weapons going forward, too many to write here. Certain combinations will make you ultra powerful, which is the thrill of the game.There are a lot of weapons to choose from in this game. Enough to satisfy all play styles. From your traditional weapons like SMGs, snipers, shotguns, and rifles to unique weapons like a pistol that shoots venomous ooze, gloves that throw out a beam of lightning, and even a set of cards that you can throw at enemies like daggers. Again, something for everyone.The RPG mechanics stem from earning a currency called "Soul Essence" i.e., experience at the end of each run. Soul Essence can be spent to unlock talents which little by little will be upgrading your runs in the long term. Small percentage increases to weapon damage, earn more Soul Essence at the end of each run, and have more choices to choose from for the in run shop NPC, these are just some examples.This is the game to play with friends.TL;DRIt's better than Roboquest and Mythforce, which are the only two other titles that currently compete in the FPS Roguelike Multiplayer category. At the $20 price point this is a steal for the amount of fun that can be had. This game is unique and the amount of content it has had since even when it was in early access, puts other titles to SHAME.

_childDocuments_.review: Very passionate, witty developer with a knack for realising what he's good at and consistently outputting more and more of that. And unlike buckets and buckets of skittles, you never find yourself saying "well, that's too much of the same stuff". You'd think after the fifth installation of the (mostly) same characters, the (mostly) same enemy types, the (mostly) same elemental-based RPG system, it'd get old. It really doesn't.I enjoyed EBF1 and 2 as turn-based RPG games originally on Newgrounds. It was a cool duo of flash games to play when you're bored. When EBF3 came out, and I realised I had a world map to explore, characters to level up and gear to get instead of an already-maxed-out RPG fight-engine experience, I became hooked. But I never enjoyed playing those games on browsers....So the decision to boot the games over to Steam was phenomenal. I don't know what's wrong with me, but booting games up on Steam and earning Steam achievements is my motivation to play a lot of my games.Matt Roszak has branded his own image, based on typical JRPG tropes and characteristics. You can see a lot of the characters in this game in other genres if you go play his flash games, including a bullet-hell game and a QTE game.Enough of the context. Here's the summary:It's a turn based fantasy adventure, as you'd expect. You may think "wow, that's totally original, never seen that one before" and I'd be on your side. But the charm and care, the humour and references combine into an homage that singles itself as something new, something familiar and something reliable.It plays out like a normal JRPG. You fight monsters (not randomly, thank Godcat), you level up - you get stronger. You venture weird and wonderful realms, you slave away for NPCs who stand in one spot and command you to get stuff.If you're a fan of JRPGs and turn-based combat, you may look at the art-style and go "wow, this looks so trash" and as a result denote it as drab, boring, or potentially easy. But there's a lot of depth in this game. And each instalment adds in new mechanics that change up the game DRASTICALLY. In EBF3, it was pretty basic, but the whole appeal was (aside from being able to use Lance) acting like a standard RPG as I mentioned before. EBF4 added in a prime new character, a deeper story, the backup system, end-end-game content and NG+, more status effects and elements, and this one adds in summons, weather which affects statuses between turns, and removes a chore: mana, instead implementing more cooldowns for more moves, which previously, the 'good' moves would just give a negative debuff to the user.You'll warm up to it, even if from the get-go it looks lacklustre. I personally enjoy the art style and the humour, and there's a huge difficulty curve on bosses if you play on epic.One thing I didn't like about this game were amount of shared skills there were, it's a cool feature but it was annoying to be able to dedicate a true 'healer'. The equips, especially the flairs in this game are amazing, though, so it offsets nicely. I wish you didn't have to use captured monsters as materials for upgrading, and I wish you couldn't catch bosses. It made me painstakingly have to re-fight each boss on both Zero and Epic, for the capture and achievement respectively, and it burns my completionist complex where I've been collecting one of each monster, just to have that monster now be a gap in my Bestiary in terms of capture, then I have to go back and catch an extra.The haste mechanic is nice, but it feels like the Viking Monolith ends up being an end-all solution to summoning. I'd rarely.. just rarely... find myself using any 50 SP+ Summons because I may not have SP for Viking Monolith, or I need SP for Stumpy Gloop or Slime Bunny.I think the summon system needs work, a good idea would you'd be able to have two non-backup monster slots and you could summon specific monsters to help fight in some way.A solid experience. I'm 50 hours in, and I still need to do the  on Epic. I've gotten close... but I wish there were more strategies to those fights other than set guides I've seen online. It feels like on Epic the fights just overwhelm you with constant nukes and AoE, and you can't cover all the elements through resistances.The 'equip' function during battle would come in handy here if it didn't consume a turn. I get it'd be really unbalanced to be able to change equipment on a whim - maybe you can only change one equip per turn, and any more than that consumes your turn? According to the devlog Matt wanted to take this feature out completely but it was contested highly, I'm not sure why though.Overall, a charming, funny, solid experience. It's not game of the year, and it's not the best story-wise, but it doesn't try to be. It offers a nice amount of content, surprising depth, and differs enough from other instalments to warrant its pricetag.I'd recommend it to anyone who has time to spend on turn-based RPGs, and I love the developer to bits, so please check out Kupo Games and Matt's humble beginnings.Looking forward to future releases.
