_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire reborn sounds good on paper, but in reality is incredibly underwhelming. I'm really struggling to understand the plethora of positive reviews, as early access or not, the core gameplay mechanics simply are unimpressive, unrefined, and quite possibly beyond saving. The biggest culprit here is the gunplay itself, as all guns feel weightless and lack impact, and despite a few different effects here and there they all pretty much feel identical. Despite borrowing heavily from games like Borderlands, Gunfire Reborn falls incredibly far off the mark. Enemies suffer from incredibly simplistic, "choppy" animations, grenades are weightless... and the sound design is simply awful. I might was well just be playing the game on mute because everything from the enemy sounds to the movement, to the various weapon sounds, lack any sort of depth or punch to them. In fact, the sounds in this game remind me a lot of a cheap F2P phone game, with the poor-quality sort of overused samples you'd expect from a Chinese bejeweled clone... grating on the ears. There's zero spatial audio and zero meaningful audio cues for what's actually going on-screen, it feels completely out of sync and as if they put the absolute bare minimum into sound design.Look, I get that this is an early access title, but the core gameplay in early access should at least somewhat reflect or inspire what the final product might be, and should be good enough to impress the player and garner a desire for more. This game doesn't do that. Everything about it feels like a college student's first semester 3D game project, riddled with flaws and poor quality efforts due to a lack of experience. Gunplay is the most important element of a shooter, and this game simply does not have it. Plenty of early access titles nail the gunplay early on, with a solid, powerful, and impactful feeling to the combat. Games like Nightmare Reaper and Prodeus come to mind, as with games like these you know right out the door that the devs know exactly what they're doing, even if much of the content is still a work in progress. When compared to other early access indie shooters with similar RNG level/weapon design, this title falls flat. And when looking at actual Borderlands, which is arguably dated by today's standards, everything about the core gunplay and movement is significantly worse. Elemental effects lack impact, visual modifications to guns such as shooting multiple projectiles might as well be purely cosmetic, and death animations look worse than the canned death animations from Goldeneye 64. Where's decent ragdoll phsyics and enemies being launched into walls when you need them? I might as well just be playing Fallout 4 for the gunplay, because if that's their target for how Gunfire Reborn should feel, well, they've reached it.In it's current state, the RNG level design is incredibly basic and repetitive, essentially the bare minimum effort of what you could call procedurally generated. Generic narrow corridors and open square rooms, all of which offer nothing interesting from a gameplay perspective. There's no verticality or platforms to see here, no options to flank enemies, and nothing interesting in the environment to look at except giant square blocks. Quite simply, in it's current state this game is not fun to play. The only thing it has going for it is that it has Borderland's gun loot system combined with very basic random level generation, and neither of these are things that the game does particularly well. Strip these out and you've got the carcass of a shooter that needs a lot of work and resign, with zero redeeming features.Look, I realize I'm being a bit harsh here, so maybe I'm wrong and they'll turn this thing around and refine the whole thing until it's unrecognizable and actually a quality game that feels good and is fun to play. But I'm really not seeing the potential here, unless the devs are planning on redesigning the core mechanics and animations from the ground up and letting this project bake for another 5 years to perfection. As is, I just don't see this game ever reaching above anything but mediocre. But people will buy it simply because it's a Borderlands clone, and a shoddy one at that. The fact that single-man devs have done significantly better in FPS feel and gunplay while still in early access does not inspire confidence for Gunfire Reborn with it's actual team working on it. Maybe I'm being too harsh and maybe this game is still really, really, really early, but I honestly doubt it. But if the plan is to release this game within the next year or so, unless they pull of a miracle I just don't see it happening.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute unit of a rougelike that is definitely best played with friends. With the 1.0 update out, the sheer amount of stuff to find and do is HUGE, and It STILL has a lot of room for growth, with the possibility of things like alternate routes,  weapons, scrolls, and characters. A mod workshop would be a welcome addition, but its not entirely necessary, as the game is loads of fun even without mods. It has a weapons system akin to Borderlands, with corrosive weapons damaging armor, Electric weapons damaging shields, and fire weapons dealing extra damage to enemies with out either. Each character has its own unique play style, and each one feels great. There's options for those who like to get up close and personal, stay far away and snipe for massive damage, and anything in between. _childDocuments_.review: I play this game with my girlfriend and it's wonderful, fun, deep, and can be frustrating at times. Difficulty is a hard thing to balance and in this game you can very much make the wrong choices.  It is, however, really easy to learn and at only 10 hours so far, this game has captivated me.  We haven't seen all of the content yet, so I've yet to be disappointed, but so far, no crashes on my i5 2070 super, and it  generally pulls 165+ fps so it performs the way it should.  The simplistic art style is actually a really nice change to the ultra realism of Cyberpunk 2077.   The game loads up quick, and you can get at it as fast as your friends can join up.If I had any real gripe with the game, it's that you can die in an instant if you're not careful.  So if you're rocking a sniper build, just check your back and listen for enemies.  Rezzing team mates can be rough if there are only 2 of you, but somehow we make it work.  There should be some way to better synergize with your team mates, in my opinion, the first character offers you very little in the way of being able to focus on one tree and play off of your team mate, but maybe I just haven't played enough.What would I like to see?  Some visual differentiators!  The art style lends itself very much to skins and HATS!  Let me grind for in game currency and buy my cat a new hat!  I'd also love to see melee weapons with interesting properties, and maybe a sprint button.  I know it's strange to ask for it, but you actually do spend some time running back and forth looking for bao, it'd be nice if you could hit shift to sprint as well as dash.Regardless, I paid $10 for this game and it's worth way more.  Great job to the devs, looking forward for more.  Thanks for making a coop roguelite.  And thanks for making it an FPS!

_childDocuments_.review: Feels about time to recommend this now that it has hit version 1.0.Gunfire Reborn is a roguelite that mixes FPS and RPG elements. Each hero has unique abilities, passives, and roles. You can play solo or with up to three others (4 players max) and the experience feels better with others in my opinion. Each run is procedurally-generated and you will learn patterns overtime. A typical run will see you collecting goblets to fill out your skill trees, scrolls to power up various aspects of gameplay, and improving your weapons. What does the game have at time of writing this?6 Heroes (each with an "ultimate" ability, a secondary ability, five passives, and three skill trees for eighteen skills)148 Scrolls of various rarities (normal, rare, legendary, and cursed)48 Weapons (including rifles, shotguns, and swords to name a few)69 Enemies (including sixteen elite variants and seven bosses)4 Acts/Areas (with two to four subsections to complete each)2 Modes (adventure and daily challenge)4 Difficulties (one of which scales when beating it)...and potentially more to come!The developers have been very active since release with adding more into the game, balancing everything related to heroes/skills/scrolls/weapons, bug fixing, and overall listening to the community. The first year has been quite the adventure and am looking forward to what they do next and onward.

_childDocuments_.review: You start in stage one. Every stage has several areas/rooms you have to clear to get to the next stage. Every stage has   different looking areas and unique enemies. By killing enemies you receive souls, coins and sometimes weapons and   scrolls(powerups/perks) as a drop. The difficulty and your strength rises with every area and stage you clear. At the last   area of the stage you will need to fight a boss. Currently there are 2 bosses for every stage and you will need to fight one   of them who gets selectet by random. With the coins you collect during your run you can upgrade your weapons or   by all sorts of items(not permanent upgrades). The souls you can spend to upgrade your talents in your skilltree(more   weapondamage, enhancements for heros and more).  Some weapons and scrolls perform better on specific hero. Some scrolls work great together and others match together   horribly. It is needed to match the scrolls to your hero and his/her skills to get sronger and not weaker. This really adds to   the replayability of the game. I should probably also mention that you unlock scrolls and weapons by killing an specific   enemies. Weapons on the other hand cuuuum with different enhancements, when dropped, which become stronger in   later stages.  The Multiplayer is fun but sometimes a bit laggy. Its also not rare to have a high ping. Althogh my PC isn't the best and is   over the minimum requirement for the game I have bad Fps drops when a lot of enemies and/or players are on the screen.  They are all possible to get some more challenging than others. I enjoyed getting them all.I recommend the game to every roguelike fan and to everyone who wants to play an amazing roguelike game.You can spend easiely over 120h in this game and you will not get bored. For 10€ this game is just amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a really big issue with this game. The combat is fun, the characters feel different, and some of the weapons are very fun. However, there is a huge issue with progression in this game. Some of the rogue-lite elements of this game have bad design. Many of the upgrades that you can buy after a run are straight stat upgrades, and even the ones that aren't straight stat upgrades change almost nothing about the way you play the game. How well you do in rogue-lite games should be determined by your skill at the game that you gain by repeating the game, not endlessly throwing your self at a wall until you get the necessary stats. A rogue-lite should offer something different in gameplay for your next run, such as a new ability to try out that will change how you tackle a situation. This game fails to do these things, making it feel like your knowledge of the game and mastery of mechanics are worthless to the grind of stats.With the most recent update, the developers have added a roadblock exemplary of this core design problem. For the final boss, there is effectively a DPS check during the last phase of the fight. If you do not pass it in the given time, your run is ended. This is an awful way to force people to grind out stats and makes me very disappointed in this game.If you are a fan of rogue-lite games that reward your knowledge and practice of the game, I would suggest you play any one of the other great rogue-lite games that there are on the market until this problem is changed. I do hope they change this problem, since I enjoy many aspects of this game and think it has some promise, but is simply unrewarding to play when it comes down to it.Edit: After the negative community feedback surrounding the developers' choice to put in the DPS check phase, the developers have decided to decrease the punishment for insufficient stats from an instant loss to a harder end phase. This is not much of an improvement.This final boss DPS check was only exemplary of the core design problems that I have aired my grievances for. Moreover, it is still a DPS check. It still replaces skill with stats. There is no real change in design philosophy, only a slight relaxation of the current one. This new "ultimate phase" could be essentially compared to a scripted defeat set forth by the developers for those who have not done the stat grind. I still would not pick this up if you are looking for a good roguelite.Side note: I think that limiting your goblet choices during the last stage was a very odd decision. It should have been a difficulty option that would apply to all stages and would be very fun to try.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun Roguelite FPS. All weapons are distinctively different in a way that they feel fun to use. Together with the amount of different builds you can play as gives the sense of variety that makes you return to the game. The coop is really fun.The enemy damage resistance caps at 90% on Boundless Dream, whilst you still one shot the enemies. Some additional ways to make this more difficult would be cool other than just a new reincarnation level.(Endless Journey on Reincarnation 9 adds a timer for you to race against.)The "new" season reward stuff gives some really cool weapon skins and emotes. Unfortunately there is no "sandbox mode" (for the lack of a better word), so testing different builds will take some time while you unlock weapons and scrolls, and level up characters, there is no way to give yourself scrolls at the start of the game for some challenge runs (like  with  for 1hp runs). And  you are  the game in any way, shape, or form.The  season updates are really cool, adding a new gameplay mechanic and some awesome weapon skins. The old gameplay gimmicks are also playable after the season ends which allows those who didn't get to experience them during the actual season have a go at them. After the season ends the rewards can be purchased from the shop with Soul Essence (in game currency) that is basically free anyway.The actual system requirements for this game are really low, allowing you to play to the fullest on even lower end laptops, making it really accessible for anyone who would like to try it out.The movement feels nice and there's great sense of variety even though it has a very repetitive gameplay loop. Would be more fun with a "sandbox mode" and/or being allowed to modify the game.

_childDocuments_.review: (This is Early access?) here we go! Look at the videos! Images! Read 'About this game' (actually read, don't skim). Still need help deciding?This game is satisfying, and challenging (consistently so). Elemental weapons may create status effects that fuse into new effects during a hail of Team fire, or solo if you are quick (and smart with weapons/ascensions/Scrolls). There's a few characters (two to unlock), and they contain enough variety as you build their ascensions each run. Each run should be plenty random should you decide to play a different 'Build'.The challenge seems daunting at first, but keep at it. you'll spend whatever you earn at the end of each run and before you know it, a combination of hard-earned experience and persistent talent leveling will see you staring down a boss or area you haven't seen or memorized yet.The art may look nice and different, heck... cute, even. Don't be fooled! those sharpshooters and various minions and lanterns(?) are plenty intimidating once you've been knocked down dozens of times. The only deaths I find similar from one-to-the-next are boss deaths, which take some learning from your own mistakes.I love the guns and how they feel, especially when synergized with other weapons, scrolls and teammates. I enjoyed filling out the talent tree and leveling up. I felt stronger each run, even like I earned something (despite dying). Checking out the armory is good too! finding stuff I hadn't unlocked yet gave me a few goals to hunt. Also, I'm not sure how popular this opinion is, but I love the jumping puzzles! it's nice to have a breather from combat... challenging in a different way. Also where I learned the most from the controls and button mapping.I look forward to any and all patches and development the creators work hard on, up to and (hopefully long past) official release. It even has a daily challenge mode now! (what the 'H', how long was I gone?!)

_childDocuments_.review: , especially for having co-op. There's a little bit of adjusting time needed for the movement speed, it does feel slower than any other FPS, rogue or otherwise, but that's a design choice, and the combat is balanced with that in mind. Although endgame difficulty levels tune that up immensely., as long as you know how to build them during the runs. The gameplay loop consists of up to four acts, divided into four stages each, with a boss at the end of every act. You get RNG weapon drops with RNG stat modifiers that can be rerolled and upgraded, along with RNG passives scrolls and RNG choice of perks for your char that can modify how your primary and secondary skills function and, therefore, how you'll play that char in that run. There are also four talent trees available outside the runs to provide a bit of a progression system for your profile, unlocking new mechanics for runs to help you out, like access to recycling unwanted loot or the ability to revive once per run at a cost.Overall, it's a , alone or accompanied. Not that extensive of content nor that reliant on RNG, honestly, on most runs, you'll get what you want within the first 10 minutes of the usual 40-minute run.

_childDocuments_.review: You know you can just like call me, right? You don't need to go to the effort of making a Borderlands Roguelite with Co-Op Multiplayer. You don't have to work this hard to impress me. I love you just the way you are.Jokes aside, Gunfire Reborn immediately drew my attention for being the exact genre jumble to be a perfect master key for my interests. And now that it's got a full release, I feel like it would be a good time to throw my hat into the ring to tell you just how much it's improved.What I like:-Lordy lou, the weapon variety. Other games, you get the usual smattering of weapons. In Gunfire Reborn? Pistols, Submachine Guns, Assault Rifles, Bows, Throwing Knives, Fire-Breathing Lizards, Iron Man Gauntlets, Swords, A shotgun that is alive that you reload by feeding fish, A frozen Javelin that returns to you after you throw it- I could be here all day.-The gunplay also feels really good, generally. Some of the weapons are a little underwhelming, but generally fights feel very good to be engaged in.-Movement feels very fluid. Everyone has an air dash for free, which is really necessary if you want to be able to consistently dodge. Some of the more powerful weapons will slow you down, and you have to decide if it's worth leaving yourself open to have access to such high damage. It makes you think fast.-It feels very hard to have a "bad" gunfire run. Most of the weapons are strong enough on their own or most skill builds have enough synergy that generally speaking it's difficult to have a run that feels genuinely weak on most characters.What needs work:-Some of the later characters have the "Darkest Dungeon Mod" problem of being way to reliant on their own mechanics and tied up in synergy so much that they barely have a use. I don't want to reduce the cooldown on my terrafarter to give me nine stacks of bungomart which leads me to deal more damage with corrosive weapons if I'm standing upside down and reciting the torah. Just give me 40% more headshot damage and call it a day. Worst offenders of this are Qian Sui and Lei Lou, who feel like there is (1) viable build for, and that build barely involves guns.-The Translation is kind of spotty. It's improved a lot since the beta, but a lot of the phrasing is still kinda weird. A lot of the times the word "a" is replaced with "the" which makes the game sound needlessly formal.-A lot of the upgrades, like a lot of the characters, are needlessly specific. It kind of makes you build something really weird and lopsided just to try and use the buffs you have.-Enemies kind of all have giant heads that are easy to hit, and it sort of feels like damage on anything but the head does next to nothing. I get that it's the style and all but it'd be cool to move some of the headshot damage to bodyshots.All that said, I think Gunfire is a very good game. Highly replayable, very arcade-y, and has kind of taken the place of other games like Killing Floor 2 in my mind as braindead dude-shooters. It's a whole lot of fun, and I really wish that I wasn't getting into it when I have so many term projects due. But that's a whole other thing.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a seasoned Gunfire Reborn player with 200+ hours under my belt, this game is an absolute gem that keeps me coming back for more. The blend of FPS action, roguelite progression, and RPG elements creates an addictive game play loop that's hard to put down.Game playThe moment-to-moment game play is where Gunfire Reborn truly shines. The gun play feels incredibly satisfying, with a vast array of unique and quirky weapons that never fail to impress. From launchers that spew mini black holes to bouncing throwable blades, each new gun discovery is a joy. The tight controls and buttery smooth performance make every firefight a thrilling experience.Character VarietyOne of the game's strongest aspects is its diverse cast of playable characters. Each hero brings their own distinct play style and abilities to the table, allowing for endless experimentation and strategy. Whether you're dual-wielding as Ao Bai or embracing close combat with Qian Sui, there's a play style for everyone.Progression and BuildsThe depth of character progression is staggering. The combination of scrolls, ascension perks, and weapon inscriptions allows for an incredible variety of builds. It's immensely satisfying to craft a monstrously overpowered character through careful selection of upgrades and complementary weapons.Co-op FunI've mostly played for the chaotic fun in co-op. Teaming up with friends or randos to tackle increasingly challenging runs has been a blast!Room for ImprovementIf I had to offer one piece of constructive criticism, it would be that the game can occasionally feel repetitive, especially in the early stages of a run. The first few levels can become a bit of a slog once you've seen them dozens of times. However, this is a minor gripe in an otherwise stellar package.Gunfire Reborn is a masterclass in the roguelite FPS genre. Its addictive game play loop, deep progression systems, and constant stream of new discoveries have kept me hooked for over 200 hours. If you're a fan of roguelites, FPS games, or just looking for your next gaming obsession, Gunfire Reborn is an absolute must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Please bear in mind before you read this review, the game fully released pretty recently and the things I talk about are subject to change.Gunfire Reborn is a co-op roguelike in which you have a hero with a different set of abilities, and a wide arsenal of weaponry. I think that this game, in its current state, is fun. However, it's only fun, for the first ten or so hours. This is due to a wide range of things but I'm going to hone in on what makes the game become bland over time.Weapons: The weapons in this game are not diverse enough in the fact that some if not most of the weaponry is just not viable, meaning that you would have a significantly harder time if you were to use them.  Another issue that I have encountered with the weapons is that the statistics seem overloaded for someone who wanted to play the game casually. I often found myself being confused by the large range of things that can make a weapon good or bad.Levels: The stages in gunfire reborn all have different themes, such as deserts or ocean-type areas. The issue with the levels within the stages is that the layout isn't very diverse. You are often placed in an area which you have seen over and over again, which makes the game play feel less fresh.Occult Scrolls: The occult scrolls in this game are an interesting system in which you can receive empowering abilities, such as buffed elemental or skill damage. The problem that I find with these scrolls is that they don't  define a run. For comparison, The Binding of Isaac has multiple items in which you pick them up and think: "this run is probably going to be a win." and said items have cool effects such as making your projectiles the size of a small planet. This issue, in my opinion, with the scrolls in this game is that all of them, except for like two, are all mediocre. They don't have fun effects, and the normal rarity ones even hold a disadvantage with some of them having a negative effect in light of the positive one.Skill upgrades: Within a run, you can encounter things called goblets, usually at the end of a level. It's at this point that you can then upgrade your primary or secondary ability, as well as offering a general upgrade to your gunfight efficiency. I think that these upgrades are in a sensible position, but I also think that they should incorporate more things, such as rarity, of which they would have a more severe impact on your run.Characters: The characters in this game are fun, for the most part, but the issue is the viability, as well as the actual fun of their kit. For example, Qian Sui is basically a free win, as his abilties focus around you being in the enemies face quickly, and basically just battering them. Qian Sui, is fun. From my experience, though, Qing Yan is completely useless.Bosses: The bosses in the game are very average. The design of them is okay for the most part, apart from a few which are a little generic (golem). I also just think that the bosses don't present enough of a threat, for the most part.TL;DR: Game's fun, just not enough content and isn't ambitious enough for it to be fun for an extended period of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid roguelite looter-shooter. A little rough around the edges, and the English translation is not always the clearest, but if you like Borderlands and like roguelites then this is among the most fun game of its kind that I've played. It does fall into some of the classic pitfalls of a roguelite: seeing the same handful of rooms per stage - easy to learn, (and if you're an optimizer,) easy to master - decent amount of weapons but there's some notable power creeping (not an inherently bad thing in a roguelite, I know) - some builds make you essentially immune to damage if you get the right combination of scrolls on the right character. Build diversity goes up as you progress in a way that I find a little strange, but not entirely bad, with the Reincarnation difficulties. After finishing a run an any given difficulty, you unlock the next difficulty. There are 3 "normal" difficulties (Normal, Elite, Nightmare), then you unlock Reincarnation difficulties (numbered 1-8). Reincarnation mode unlocks, among a couple other things, the single-strongest category of modifiers - called Spiritual Remnants - in the game, giving you one of them right off the bat. You get to pick between 3 options (nearly unlimited rerolls for the first pick) of massively influential effects at the beginning your run and in the next two subsequent stage-transition areas. These effects range from "free weapon upgrades but limited scroll capacity" to "you have an endless ability to spam incredibly strong abilities." Because of this, early levels of Reincarnation actual feel easier than the Nightmare difficulty which you have to beat before, despite the health of enemies and damage values of enemy attacks actually being increased. The characters (from a gameplay perspective) are incredibly fun and unique between their kits. There will definitely be a kit you do like and a kit you don't, but they're all strong kits and bring a different way to play that really let you build to your liking. Pretty much every character has a few build options that leans more into a fundamental shooter experience, and a few that lean into a more abilities-focused experience. A good example of this is Lei Luo, who has one ability that puts him in a buffed state that will boost first shot after activation and end the state, making him well suited to being a sniper with some of the other character specific upgrades he can get. His other ability, however, shoots chain lightning from his hands, and that can be leaned into to very potent effect, making him great at setting up lightning debuffs against crowds and breaking shields. Some of this is a bit of an oversimplification but I've already typed more than I set out to. It's a good game, albeit clunky sometimes. Seems to only be getting better. The newer Spiritual Assault game mode is fun, but I'm hoping they set their sights back on the main Adventure mode again soon. Either way, I'll still be checking in on this game because it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a roguelite first person shooter that borrows the best elements of borderlands (various unique weapons, action + skill tree mechanics, elemental affinities minus the infamous Slag) while completely forgoing the grind and instead lets you in on the action immediately. No quests, no map travel, and no inventory hassle; it's all grab, go, and shoot. You can also play with up to three friends/randoms or just play solo.The mechanics are tight and the gunplay is satisfying. Most of the weapons are uniquely fun and the current selection of characters are great to play, each offering multiple different playstyles depending on build. This is also the only roguelite in recent years that have me still hooked and playing long after a first win.Perhaps my only gripe is the balancing.The first 2 bosses are great, albeit on the easy side, with clear tells and enough leeway to dodge/react while on the other hand, the 3rd boss has instakills that gives you a much smaller time to react all the while throwing mechanics at you at a pace that felt disproportionate to the overall experience. Having finished a couple of runs in elite and trying for nightmare clear, not all weapons/ascensions are viable and some are just straight up bad, at least in my experience playing only on solo. Though I do think this is just the side effect of ARPGs/looter shooters with multiple difficulties in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun roguelike, roguelite whatever you want to call it, I am honestly not knowledgeable on this genre of games, so this is from the perspective of someone with a small sample sizePros: - Active development. Updates deliver well - Simple gameplay, but somewhat high skill curve; makes it enjoyable for new players while still leaving much for more experienced players to do - Similar deal with the achievements: their progression is quite natural. Newer players will be able to easily snag a good 30-40% quickly while more experienced players will have more grindier achievements to work towards in order to earn a full completion - The game's 4 difficulties are more than just enemies becoming tankier. There are unique gameplay elements and features that offer new perspectives on the game for each difficultyCons (Most of these do not subtract that much from pure enjoyability of the game) - There are achievements locked to DLC - The DLC characters seem to be relatively busted and have a lower skill curve to bat from my observation, although it is not to a point that is p2w (point not including the astrohouse character I have no idea how they even work) - The main adventure is technically only about an hour to an hour-thirty long at most when playing casually. You may have a different build, there may be different elements to each difficulty, but it is still the same linear progression. The maps are not open at all, and when there is an area you can enter not related to the main objective it usually has nothing in it. - The skill tree becomes exponentially easier to upgrade as you play the game more rather than the other way around - This one is a personal nitpick. You have one chance to revive in singleplayer, but you can be revived an infinite amount of times in co-op (given that your teammates get to you in time). This makes the game significantly easier in coop, to a point that I rather dislike.

_childDocuments_.review: This review was essentially at launch, and if you read through it, you'll see that they did a great job at making this game even better! A lot of stuff that's been added really made the game great. Gonna leave my review as a 'time capsule' type of thing to compare it from how I described it then, to now.OLD REVIEW BEGINS:I was thinking about reviewing this game at an earlier time, but I wanted to at least unlock and play the second character before I did so. That happened, so here we go-I love both genres this game utilizes, being FPS and Rogue-lite. When I had first seen this game, I was super excited. I've played a good amount of it now, and there's are certain things I want to mention.For the positives, I really like the game's polish, the graphics are pretty neat, and there's definitely a decent amount of weapons to have fun with. In terms of sole positives, that's where I'm ending it.Now it gets a bit more gray. The gameplay loop is satisfying at times, yet frustrating at others. The characters' abilities get extremely boring(especially the first character) and it leaves me WANTING some variance there. And once you keep playing more and more, you can easily get bored of the environments. Nothing really changes in the places you've been (and keep going to), and it starts to become un-fun in the earlier parts. Bringing into account this is early access, I have high hopes for the game's future, and want to drop some of my own recommendations down for it: 1. Variety in character abilities. The game is begging for it. 2. Possibly having things change/unlocking new parts of previously exhausted environments. Think Dead Cells, maybe have some different paths leading into different sections with different enemies and bosses? Or, if anything, different bosses per boss level that have different chances of spawning. 3. The game can definitely use 1, if not 2, more characters. The replayability would definitely benefit from more characters.Essentially, to not make this longer: I want to see new, different content to allow variations per playthrough/run, so as to not make it feel the same every time. Definitely a chance to get inspired from other Rogue-lites, there's no shame in that if you ask me.

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting roguelike FPS that I highly recommend. The game at is core is very simple.  It makes you run through 3 themed levels with various stages that get shorter per level.  The enemies getting harder as your progress through the levels.  What makes it very fun is the various randomisation that makes it truly roguelike:-The plentiful weapons and their modifiers aka inscriptions-The passive you can find via scrolls-The end stage bonuses (ascensions)-The maps themselves also randomise-The end level bosses are all randomised with 2 variations at the end of the level (except the 3rd stage, 2nd boss WIP)This makes the game almost truly live up the phrase "no 2 runs are ever the same.What makes this game amazing though is truly figuring out the synergy between the weapons and scrolls that you have making some fun Godlike builds in one run.Please note: In the beginning you are extremely under developed for the normal. Until you buy some nodes on the skill tree, you are going not going to get very far on normal.  But when you put in the time you will get stronger overtime where normal is no longer a challenge and you can comfortably move onto higher difficulty.  Do note that at nightmare, your winning becomes a game of chance where it only becomes doable with a good build.

_childDocuments_.review: Auuuggghhh,Ok, from the top:You will NOT win your first run of the normal adventure. Why? Because you'll burst from 5 hits of damage, likely to a boss who you're barely doing damage to while playing Crown Prince, and you won't have any soul meta or character meta, and you'll have no weapons or scrolls unlocked.The main problem with this game gets immediately highlighted with that first run. You might think "oh I'm just bad lol, I just don't have the right character and metas unlocked yet", but no. You're almost fully wrong (at least for normal runs). If you're not handed a build with the right goblet improvements AND the right scrolls, you're SOL and will die from lack of damage and/or lack of defense. The only way to actually win here is to have god-builds that nuke/melt things.Spiritual Assault (Arena mode, to make it less unclear) shows this so, so, obviously and clearly. If you have a "normal" build that works well enough, well, guess what? Halfway after the first elite kill, you won't have enough damage to even scrape anything's shield off, and, due to it being midgame/endgame by that point, you won't get enough scrolls or the xp for goblet choices to actually recover. If you get to that point and you experience that phenomena, guess what? It wasn't your fault, the game just didn't give you the right scrolls and/or the +800% (or more) damage that's so necessary but so damn hard to get out of the randomly-selected scrolls and goblet perks that definitely didn't get given to you. You're expected to just take the L and go again and again until you actually DO get the right build, which is horrible. What's worse is that you can have all the right scrolls (or right goblet upgrades), but then the wrong weapon or the wrong goblet (or scroll) upgrades solely from the game giving you bad draws, and, oops, look a run just failed! Haha, go again!

_childDocuments_.review: So having played this game for 20 hours thus far, I want to give my initial impressions.Gameplay: This game is buttery smooth when playing and the shooting feels incredibly satisfying, I'm not going to make the same comparison others have saying its a mix of Borderlands and (insert game here), because its not in my eyes. The only real comparison to Borderlands is the cel-shaded art style and damage numbers above enemies... That's the only real comparison. This isnt a loot grinding game, you don't keep any of the loot you get on a run apart from what is essentially XP to level your character and unlock new perks.If you're unsure of this game think of it as Slay the Spire: FPS Edition. You continuously get power ups throughout the game making certain aspects of you stronger and sometimes weaker, you have to carefully select which different scrolls you pick up to maximise your damage and make it through a level.Selecting which guns you use isn't something to give much thought in the early stages, but later down the line you NEED to in order to progress and take down the tougher enemies in quick fashion.Graphics: The games minimal but clean cel-shaded style is beautiful :)Performance: This differs from PC to PC on any game but for me it ran flawlessly with no hiccups or a single crash thus far, great optimisation.Pros: Co-op upto 4 players.Looks and runs great.Can be good for the strategically minded.Addictive gameplay loop(for the most part, read on).Cheap.Cons:The maps change layout each time but you will see the same rooms again and again, can be repetitive.Difficulty spikes can throw some players off.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, not gonna give a basic synopsis but more nitty-gritty things that I like that other games do similar but get wrong a lot...oh, and just know the dev team fantastic. I DM'd them a decent list of things I'd change/fix and they've worked on a bunch of stuff I mentioned and addressed others in patch notes within a single seasonal update. This game really does seem like a diamond in the rough passion project in the currently over-saturated gaming industry.If you like traditional FPS games, this one is a bit more quirky and unique so some of the weapons might be a turn-off to you; but it does have weapons for you and I can't guess how many times weapons I initially didn't like grew on me. It has really tight movement where you can strafe while airborne instead of traditional momentum feeling movement like a lot of other games as well, it's not for everyone but I think it works. Character abilities are present although not over-centralizing so it adds flavor without ruining the flow of the game where some games will get it wrong and you're powerless without your ability and have to just sit and wait for cooldowns. Some runs you don't even spec into ability buffs and you'll end up not using them so much so don't worry, even if you don't like abilities they are not necessary, there are other passive buffs you could get that have good synergy.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid rougelite game that's pretty fun with friends. I only really have two problems. 1. The eel fight is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ all my homies hate the eel2. The higher difficulties aren't fun to play.If you've played the game, I don't need to explain #1; it aint that big a deal. #2 would've been a real deal breaker since the entire point of a rougelite is replay-ability. The main problem with it is the amount of health enemies have. Nightmare and Reincarnation give enemies way too much health that destroys the satisfying time-to-kill per enemy. I'm not suggesting they have to do anything unique to increase the challenge; a simple increase in enemy damage and fire rate or just giving the player a debuff would've been fine. Making everything a bullet sponge just makes the game boring. It just forces you to play slowly and ruins the flow of combat. Overall it's a really solid game but it just isn't satisfying past Elite unless you just want to annoy yourself.

Multiplayer works well and is nicely integrated into Steam.To me, the game is hard - but not too hard. Paradoxically, perhaps, I appreciate how the game can turn on you and end your run in seconds! :) I would have liked some more randomness/variation to the dungeons (you will learn them and they'll become quite predictable). I would also appreciate some more movement tech (such as iD-esque bunny hopping or rocket jumping), or at least a higher default movement speed.Overall, an extremely polished early access release! It took me about 50 hours/80 levels to beat the game on normal mode in single-player. And I am now looking forward to do some more runs in Elite mode.Update: Elite Mode completed. _childDocuments_.review: Yes.Update Below:______________________________________With Gunfire finally out of Early Access, I wanted to revisit the review to leave a little bit more than "Yes". I would like to say Gunfire Reborn was an amazing surprise to me.To this day I come back to it every now and then when I have 45 minutes to kill.It's been explained as a "Borderlands" meet "Roguelite". In my opinion, it is 100% true,but we have to put the context here: the comparison to Borderlands is pretty centered aroundthe gameplay loop: You kill mobs, mobs drops weapons with random stats, you use said weapons to kill more mobs. There's more similarities, but this is what people means usually, and it'd be dangerous to let your imagination go any further (build diversity, lore, setting, humor, blablabla -> not the same)On the rogue lite side (meaning roguelike with permanent progression), for me it's a good entry game to the genre: it can be difficult at first, and for a long time it wasn't even fair difficult, but over time Boss pattern are recognizable and they're easier to handle, and Devs are ironing out the irregularities over time. I remember getting absolutely destroyed on the first boss, and slowly working my way up to the ultimate, disgusting, male fantasy that is a dual wielding rottweiler with rasta making everything explode in their path by slapping a lizard buttcheeks.Speaking of heroes, there's a nice variety of them: The cat is fun and very powerful, I'll fight you on that. But I feel like of every heroes, he's not the easiest to learn, which is funny given he's the starter. He's...not the hardest either to be honest, heroes have a lot of depth to themselves and all of them take some getting used to to be used to their full potential. To me, it is undeniably a great point: the difference between how you use every heroes is huge.If there's only one thing I'd say against the game is that...one weapon is WAY above every single one of them, and it's really hard for me to be like "You know what I'll pick the sword for a change" because it's so good it's criminal. I'll not be the one who snitch about said weapon, not because I forgot the name already, but because I don't want to be stabbed in the street.Last and certainly least for everyone beside me, the devs are from/in Hong Kong. That make me happy :uThat's it u:

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a roguelite looter shooter with anthropomorphic animals.The progression system is built from constant run attempts granting meta currency until the player is strong enough to pass levels where they do not get overwhelmed by mass amount of enemies or the enemies that do a lot of damage. essentially time over skill.The enemy ai is silly, they would run into each other with their pathfinding, do nothing or not have enough tools to their arsenal, like the first boss you would encounter. The enemies lack variety, second stage has some reskins of the enemies.The level design is boring and lacks variety. within the time i played i saw same rooms multiple times.The weapons, upgrades named scrolls, for example "do more damage", "x does this now" feel like one of those upgrades you would see on a workshop mod.TLDR: This game is way too slow, generic and repetitive for my own taste. It does not have anything special to seperate itself from other games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solo review. I love this game, but the difficulty scalars are just not good. While in Rougelike and Rougelite games RNG means everything, there's generally an accepted idea that *skill* should also matter. In this game, that is generally not the case. Once you get into the harder difficulty settings, enemies will routinely kill you with plain ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥: From having aimbot for no good reason, to spamming explosives or AoE that is sometimes genuinely not able to be reacted to due to the lack of sound or visual queues, to enemies with practically inescapable attacks without specific builds or buffs, making retaliation unlikely. There are too many times were I can look back and objectively say "there is nothing I could've done mechanically better to prevent this situation" and I don't believe that should ever be the case in a game. It's hard to sell the idea that most guns in this game are viable. In-fact, most of them are complete garbage and without exclusive inscriptions are either not worth picking up ever due to doing less damage than an on-level foundry or being so clunky and convoluted that you question who, exactly, thought it was a good idea to add it to the game. For example: Almost all sniper rifles are garbage. Not due to precision requirements, but due to their lacking stopping power against just about everything. They're garbage against bosses, and by definition are not good against crowds. The exceptions to this are, obviously, the better snipers in the game: Snipers that explode and invalidate types of health pools all-together, a bow that can hit multiple enemies by hitting just one, and a crossbow that acts more like a submachine gun. This game, as far as I remember, has no story what-so-ever. While I generally like games with lesser storytelling, having NO story at all is a demerit for me. There are games were I simply want a break from the gameplay for a bit, so I read the lore books, weapon descriptions, whatever... There's nothing here. Depending on how good you are at FPS games, and whether or not you see a point in doing incarnation levels, this game can last you 1-4 hours before you've seen all the stages. Another 1-4 hours to see all the bosses. Then 4-6 hours to get all the scrolls and guns. As a solo player, the game is cool for the first few hours, tedious and frustrating past that. My advice? If you don't have friends who play this game, don't even bother unless it's on sale and you're really, really bored.

_childDocuments_.review: Im revisiting this game several years later with a negative impression instead of positive. This game has a fantastic first 15 hours with solid gameplay and appealing visuals, but it has nothing for longer engagement. The lack of new maps after all this time is quite astonishing. This game has serious scaling issues and all it has to offer is playing the same few maps over and over again. The only good map is the desert map, too. However, its the monetization or lack thereof that tips this review positive. This could have been one of the scummiest games ever, and its certainly there in its DNA. However, the game has been perfect in its handling of money, and only offers some optional DLC once in awhile.Old review:Gunfire Reborn is built upon an extremely solid core of gameplay, with satisfying guns and enemies that have some personality to them. The visuals are gorgeous and yields high FPS even on a potato. Based simply on the price compared to, say, 10 hours of gameplay, I would have to say its worth it. That said, the practical core of the game is a metagame progression loop that is time consuming to say the least. Like most rougelikes\lites you win or mostly lose and gain points to level up a tech tree for the next run. Akin to 90's arcade machines using brutal difficulty to force quick restarts, this game by necessity as an indie title pads out the playtime considerably by using walls of difficulty and a very slow meta progression. While not the worst offender in the genre by any means, I dont appreciate this system. While I am continually unlocking and discovering new content, it comes at a snails pace as he player encounters the same content over and over and over and over again. That said, if the player doesnt mind this system my main objection to the game falls away.A frequent comment from a quick perusal of reddit\youtube reveals a similar line of thought from the games fanbase...the "true game" requires a lot more play, aka hundreds or thousands of hours invested, before the commentator is able to ''appreciate'' what the game actually is. Any other objection to the games balancing is simply a skill issue and deemed irrelevant. Quite frankly this toxic community attitude, often seen in games such as Dark Souls, fills one with contempt for those games and discourages community interaction.Balancing is certainly an issue. Fortunately the game leans in favor of the player being OP rather than nerf batting everything, but many weapons are quite useless compared to a somewhat small pool of excellent weapons, and there are some very obvious scroll combinations that if struck upon by chance, will allow the player to proceed much faster and easier through their runs. The games interface and loading screen tips explicitly describe this.As for content, its alright for the price. Its a cheap game so the standards are way lower than a 60$ title. For the most part you get three map types, with a fourth opening up after what looks to be a substantial grind. Although i have beaten the ship boss once, you need to do so three times? before getting the fourth map which will probably take me a considerable amount of time. You mostly just see the first map over and over again as you try to get a favorable loadout going. There are many varied weapons and sufficient numbers of hem are viable to make it interesting. The enemies and their AI is quite good, as they have some personality and character in the way they move and fight. Loot is a bit of an annoyance, honestly. The limitation to two weapons+forcing the use of a basic infinite ammo weapon makes it hard to experiment. Many games I can think of either allow you to hold as many weapon types as there are element types, or one weapon for every ammo type. The games limitation to only 2 is very constraining. There really isnt much in the way of looting since you cant haul your loot back and store it or anything like that. Some kind of base you could build up and go out of missions from could be a great addition in the future.Speaking of the future, with the current lack of mod support, the game is entirely dependent on the devs pushing out updates. I like the roadmap that pops up ingame and the game will surely continue to grow if they keep pumping out content, and die when they cease to do so. Considering the lack of map variety, this is a dire weakness.In summary, although I was hemming and hawing between recommending the game or not, I came to the conclusion that this game is a good buy at the price regardless of drawbacks. Furthermore the devs have offered a very fair monetization so far with none of the nonsense plaguing the gaming industry right now, and games that maintain their integrity by avoiding lootboxes deserve some support.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun shooter rogue-like game with plenty of different weapons and passives to make every play through different. If it keeps getting updated and bugs squashed, could easily be the Game of the Year for non-AAA.   There is some resemblance to Borderlands, but that's like saying this game is like Mario because there's platforming, traps, stages that go to a boss and if you die you have to restart all over. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay of Gunfire Reborn is a simple blend between Borderlands and Enter The Gungeon.∙ You find weapons with random stats and effects.∙ You have a limited carry capacity.∙ There are multiple types of ammo which are shared between weapons.∙ Defeating a boss leads to a loot-plosion.∙ The gunplay feels incredibly similar to the Borderlands experience, to the point that I don't feel the need for this game to exist.∙ You fight enemies in closed off rooms or arenas that you can not escape from until every enemy is defeated.∙ Your starter weapon has infinite ammo but low damage.Anybody who compares this game to Risk Of Rain 2 is delusional. The fact that you shoot enemies in 3D is not enough to compare this to RoR2.∙ You don't have the choice between full-looting a stage VS rushing to the end. You simply fight the enemies until the door is open. Time has no meaning.∙ There are no holdout-zones. (Teleporter Events)∙ There is no concept of scrappers and printers.

_childDocuments_.review: Even in early access, this game has incredibly satisfying gunplay, a great gameplay loop, and TONS of variety. The only thing I would like tweaked is the frequency of "Vault" rooms. Often on a run, I will either see only one, or find them constantly, to the point that they hindered the pacing of my runs. but this is relatively minor, as for an early access game priced at such a reasonable amount, and often on sale, Gunfire Reborn might be the most content-rich roguelite i've played so far. If you like FPS games, stylized graphics, wacky weapons and skills, and addictive upgrading (permanent unlocks through trait points and new hero unlocks with much more planned to come) check this out! It is a co-op game, but as a solo player I do not feel under-powered or pressured to play online :) overall I'm very happy I gave this a shot, and you should too!

_childDocuments_.review: In a sentence, I'd describe this game as "Roguelike borderlands, but with furry characters instead of grotesque violence". If that's of any interest, I'd definitely recommend this game. The translation can be a bit rough and story pretty much non-existent, but when's the last time you played a roguelike solely for the story?The characters all have fun and unique styles of play, and though it's not difficult to parse the world builder (or lack thereof) by run 10 or so, it still manages to be interesting all the same. I need to play some more to get a sense for the newest content at the endgame, but from what I saw it seemed like a fun and fair challenge.In all, a solid hidden gem. Definitely give it a go!

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, i have purchased this game because my friends were playing it. Peer pressure never seemed to me as a positive incentive to purchase a game, and anyways, this one in particular didn't appear to show much difference from the other classic sandbox FPS games. The first couple hours, probably even until I reached a high enough level on at least one character to unlock and upgrade a couple very needed skills, were not fun. I kept dying, I was unfamiliar with the sensitivity, the core mechanism of the elements and the scrolls escaped my understanding. However, as I further progressed into the game, later playing either solo or with my friends, I slowly grasped the idea of the game, and began to like it. To whomever who thinks that they don't dislike this genre, graphics, and play style, I would suggest that you give this a try. It will take time indeed to learn, but like all games, there is a greater part of the fun that is found near the end. Further recommendation would be for a quick expansion of the content (more characters, more maps, more weapons, more scrolls, more elements, etc.) as an average play time varies from 40-60 hours for probably all of the achievements and skills to be found and maxed out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly so much fun. At first it's super challenging, but the more you play and upgrade your characters, the easier it gets. There's a bunch of different characters who all have different abilities and proficiency. On top of that, during your run you can find different weapons/scrolls to kind of customize your play style. At the end of each stage you can find a goblet which gives you a choice between 3 upgrades. You have the option of upgrading an aspect of your character's Primary Skill, Secondary Skill, or Weapon Enhancement. Depending on which of these upgrades you choose, it drastically changes the course of the game. For example, with the turtle character, if you upgrade his secondary skill which is a single strong punch, it changes to this really quick multi-punch and you basically turn into a JoJo character xDIn addition to the skill upgrades, there are scrolls you can pick up which boost different things like weapon damage, crit chance, movement speed, elemental effects etc. There are some really strong scroll combinations. It's fun to experiment and see which things work well together.There are lots of unique weapons that you can pick up that range from pistols, shotguns, smgs, snipers, rocket launchers, swords and even a brick that you just throw at enemies. There's really funny things like a little handheld dragon or lizard that shoots fire or bombs at your enemies. Each of these weapons are really unique, and have random modifiers on them each time, along with different damage types; Fire, Corrosion, and Shock. Each damage type is either very effective or less effective depending on what enemy you're going up against. They will have different colored healthbars depending on what they're weak to. Blue health (Shield) is weak to Shock. Yellow health (armor) is weak to corrosion. Red health is weak to fire. You can even combine multiple elements for bonus effects. Fire + Corrosion does explosive AoE damage which is really useful. Other combinations get you Miasma which is a strong poison effect, or Manipulation which temporarily converts enemies into allies.There are 4 Acts of the game, each with their own subset of levels, and each act has 2 random final bosses that you can encounter. Each level has random and unique enemy encounters/loot and things called vaults which are bonus levels that give you even more loot. Sometimes a level can have unique modifiers for an extra challenge, such as turning defeated enemies into another enemy type, or a boss rush if you're playing on the higher difficulties.This game has so many different ways to play and customize your run that you'll always find new ways to enjoy it. Lots of different things synergize and make you extremely strong. Despite that though, you need to be careful cause even if you are really powerful, the enemies can still do a lot of damage very quickly. It's still a pretty challenging game. It has up to 4 player co-op and its definitely a bit easier and more enjoyable with friends.The devs are very frequently updating and adding new things to the game, so you'll definitely get a lot of playtime out of this. It's definitely worth it, even full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down one of the greatest Rogue-lites I've ever played, the game has no right to be this good considering how low quality it looks in terms of graphics, SFX and animations, but that is honestly to it's benefit because this game can literally be run on a potato and on sale you can get the game and all the additional characters for a lot less than what a sub par AAA or even AA Multiplayer game will cost ya (tho this game can also be played in Single Player just fine...)So the game is basically a chinese Furry FPS Borderlands Roguelite with 12 playable characters (6 unlockable with game progress, 6 that are DLC only). The reason I compare it to Borderlands is because it uses the exact same elemental system (Burning, Corrosive, Shock) and the playable hero characters all have a Primary (ultimate) ability with a Cooldown, and a Secondary ability, usually requiring resource management along with your primary, secondary and starting gun (which has infinite ammo and scales along with the area).The whole point is to make it through a gauntlet of arenas filled with traps and enemies that are specifically themed around each stage (there being 5 total with about 5 or so rooms each including bonus rooms called Vaults and a final boss room). As you beat each Stage, you will unlock Ascensions which basically power up your character further and allow you to build around a specific play style that the tree supports. once you get through all 5 Stages and defeat the bosses in each, the run ends and you can begin another run again, which, depending on the difficulty, can take an average of an hour and a half to beat... There is a permanent Talent tree which you can eventually unlock in it's entirety, along with an individual hero tree for each character consisting of about 5 passives, and even after you've unlocked everything (which doesn't take anywhere near as long as it used to compared to when the game was first in Early Access...), you will still have plenty of things to use your soul essence on, as this game has a tremendous amount of replay value, whether you play Solo or with a few other friends...The only major criticism I have to give is honestly that the netcode could be better... if you're playing with people who are on the other side of the planet, and the ping is above 150 ms, you're gonna really feel it bad... You'll experience blank shots, rewinding, teleporting and even just randomly dying... but outside of that, this game is phenomenal and I honestly cannot recommend it enough! I rate it a solid 9/10 +Addicting AF gameplay loop (seriously, this game is crack... don't play it late at night or you may end up finding it is suddenly 6AM and you got work in a few hours)+Many weapons, to choose from and many characters to play as, all with their respective strengths, weaknesses and specialized play styles+Fairly easy to pick up and play+Affordable price (DLC included, especially on a sale)+Great replayability, including more game modes with additional options as you unlock harder difficulties+Cute Characters+Can run easily on most lower end PCs (even works really well on a Steam Deck)+is still being updated with content as of this review-Bad Netcode-Graphics don't look the best, SFX and animation are quite wonky and cheap looking-Some may find it repetitive and dull early on-Average game length requires commitment (tho you can save and quit at the beginning of each stage in case you gotta take a break, tho this is for SP only)

Thus, this game becomes nothing more than a number optimizing sim; where progressing until the end is almost guaranteed, and the only thing left for you is to see how much you'll be able to crank up your damage numbers.This seems to be how the developers want their game though, since they've made that intense, one sided powercreep during early access, AND never bothered to tweak how a specific weapon can permanently deal ELEVEN times more damage with any of the plethora of scrolls and affixes that recovers ammo to the clip since the beginning. _childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an excellent installment in the roguelite genre. It takes the form of an FPS with 3 different zones you need to clear - Catacomb, Desert and Ship Bay. The game brings familiarity to the Borderlands series, namely having different characters with unique skill trees (that are progressed differently in every run) and weapons with different attributes. In addition, there are unique scrolls you can pickup that boosts your character in different ways, akin to the Risk of Rain game.The game currently offers 4 different difficulties that are appropriately scaled and every character has their own niche. High difficulty runs can end easily with small mistakes and sometimes it is up to RNG to see whether you can deal enough damage to clear zones, especially zone 3 where you reach late game. The Cat character is most similar to Maya from Borderlands, where he specialises in Elemental damage and can stun lock enemies. The Dog is similar to Salvador, dual wielding weapons with the potential to be a DPS monster late game but suffers from a weak early game. The Bird is somewhat like Krieg, preferring incredibly high sustain and loves getting into the face of enemies. There's also Tiger, is a sniper that can deal crazy burst damage to the likes of Zer0. In the latest patch the devs have given us a new heroine Rabbit that works nicely as a spellcaster. I would say the characters are all unique and fit into different roles especially when playing in a team. The development team for Gunfire Reborn while small, leaves frequent updates to bring balance to the game. There are still a lot of underpowered and overpowered weapons which the team is working on to address. Future major patches are in bound as well - promising new characters and bosses.  High recommended and is a blast whether you are playing solo or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game wasn't meant to be played alone, in fact you can only really enjoy 70% of what the game has to offer without anybody playing with you. However if you do somehow have friends, this is the most brain numbing, dopamine rush, min-max experience you can have in a game ever especially if you're faded off that josh, With developers hard at work giving us new patches and dlc like candy, the only thing I can complain about is how long it takes to get a friend who finally decided to get the game up to your level. Realistically it's going to take 40+ hours for them to be able to play at the level of reincarnation 9 and at that point they might not even have upgraded everything STILL.

After being heavily pressured into getting this by a certain friend of mine I had very little to no expectations of what was coming my way - the game looked a lil' off-putting and generic from screens and all the furry animals weren't really helping me get convinced. As I started playing through , i found the gameplay fun, mildly satisfying and enjoyable but nothing that blew me away. Compounded by the fact that there seemed to be  whatsoever in the levels , I was not particularly convinced or thrilled to continue. Over the next hours and days however, I found myself returning...and returning...coming back for more runs. Each time getting a little further. Each time matching up with different players. Each time unlocking more things for myself. Each time expanding my array of  as they call it in game. It's truly hooking me in thus far and I've really come to appreciate what it offers! _childDocuments_.review: An actual great game. Has the chance of becoming one of the best roguelites ever if the devs keep this up. Using borderlands weapon elements (corrosive, shock, and burning) and adding extra elements to them (shock effect deals shock damage to nearby enemies, corrosive slows, and burning dots), as well as combining them to enable even more powerful combos, shock + corrosive = miasma for instance, makes for a fun experience to try different weapons together and can make some crazy builds. Unlocks are through playing the game and using new combinations of weapons on enemies, such as killing a specific enemy with a specific element/element effect on them. You gain levels by using the essence you gain to upgrade talents, which allows you to unlock more things like the 2nd character, and other powers you can find. Through levels you can find vaults that have a small challenge before a chest that will reward you with a scroll, that grants usually a downside, but a big positive as well, or just a positive ie: -90% dmg taken from enemies far, but +90% dmg taken from enemies nearby (positive and a negative). Sometimes you'll stumble across a gold chest that will offer different things, taking damage to gain money, or permanent max shield/hp as an example. At the end of levels you will find a chest that gives a goblet that will offer you one of three choice of upgrades to your character or their skills, such as increasing the amount of damage a specific element does, or modifying your unique ability.The game is a bit short, but it makes up for this with strong enemies, tanky or high damaging, as well as unique and fun boss fights. I do wish they had a looping mode like risk of rain does, but overall I am satisfied by the end of the game.Overall, I love this game, and as I said this has the chance of being an absolute breakthrough (not that isnt already) and the best roguelite shooter in the market. It is definitely worth the $12 and I'd heavily recommend it for people that enjoy roguelikes and shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: A damn good game all around. Gameplay feels good, moving and shooting is crisp and there's pretty good feedback when you hit. Weapons are varied and interesting, there are lots of build possibilities... Really, it's great.It does have the same problem as a lot of roguelites in that you quickly reach a point where enemies' damage dramatically outscale your health, and so a single mistake means instant death, unless you've somehow specced hard into tanking, which isn't always going to be possible due to the random nature of the runs. It can feel a bit disheartening at times when you're having a good run and it ends very suddenly.The music is also a bit weak. Not bad by any mean, just that you're not going to remember it once you've shut off the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it extremely enjoyable to test my RNG and see what kind of builds I end up with in every run. There's also nothing better than experiencing one of the many ridiculously op builds and melting through every single enemy. There is a lot of replayability due to different guns with different stat rolls, different buffs, and different characters that can generally be built 2-3 ways (e.g. focusing on leap build instead of cleave build for the kung fu bird). You also experience progression as you repeat the runs since you can save up the souls you get after each run to unlock permanent upgrades, which prevents that feeling of losing everything or gaining nothing after you win/lose.The devs have been constantly pushing out updates with bug fixes and more content. The game keeps improving and I personally think it's worth the small price tag.As usual, any game is more fun with friends, and this is no exception. Grab a few friends if you can and try it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a rougelite similar to Risk of Rain 2 but it's Doom, plus player skill actually matters for your abilities and scoring lots of weak point shots (eg. head shots) so it's satisfyingly rewarding. There are multiple cool characters each with unique strengths and many combinations of skill tree ascensions that can be paired with an ever-growing number of weapons for some amazing combos. I definitely recommend for any fans of rougelites, FPS, and Doom. I got it during early access and now I'm looking forward to seeing everything new for the 1.0 release. This is also a great game to play with friends seriously or casually, and the matches are relatively short once you get used to speeding through levels.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is very good as both a single player as well as a Co-op experience. It offers replayability in that the levels are relatively different every time. The themes of course remain the same, but the rooms you encounter are usually randomized into a different order. The enemies you fight are all pretty well balanced. Obviously some are stronger than others (especially depending on the difficulty) so there is some strategy involved in each encounter. The different weapon & talent combinations are really the core of the game that keeps me coming back. It is incredibly satisfying to find the combinations you want and see the damage you do because of it. This might be a relatively niche game compared to some others, but I think it's very good at doing what it's supposed to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me explain one thing first: I am not your typical FPS fan. This is not my favourite genre. I am the kind of person who gets dizzy and nausea when playing FPS game. Even the badly rendered third person shooters makes me dizzy and lightheaded - Like Pubg.But this game.. is okay. Its one of the rare FPS games that does not make me dizzy.The game is a PvE coop game, which I do recommend playing with your friends rather than solo. Just buy multiple copies of this game and gift it to your friends. You'll have lots of fun.You can also play with randoms via matchmaking, but I only managed to find games once. and if you're new, you'll be waaaaaay underlevelled that you might as well play a private game with your friends and have a good ping.the AI is a fun challenge. They still behave predictably like an AI, but they have these unique moves that you have to learn to hit them effectively. Some enemies likes to jump a lot and others like to shoot you with large projectiles.The main complaint at the moment was the bosses. Some of the bosses have insanely high HP when played multiplayer. Heck, the four of us can't even deplete the bosses' shield, let alone his actual HP. I'm okay with the bosses have his HP multiplied according to the number of players, but don't buff his shield too much :DAlso, why is the cost of reviving characters is so expensive (from stage 2 onwards) ? We've already have problem with the short timespan for your teammates to revive you.Which basically means, if you die in the middle of a warzone, there is no way your teammates can beat the stage or beat the boss.at least either reduce the cost to revive,or increase the time to revive your teammatesor even better, allow your teammates to be revived for free prior to boss fight.and also, I hope there is also a stage select so that not every time we have to start from the first stage.This game is still in early access, and it does look promising.hopefully the developers will continue supporting this game with more stages to play.I'm hoping that we get at least 2 more characters - as playing with 3 - 4 cats with same skin and color palette is pretty meh.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a passable and entertaining roguelite in single player, but really shines with friends. Getting over the hill from 1-25 can be a bit of a slog. From there, reaching the point where you can access the talent that allows you to keep some essence between rounds is trickier still, but it is the fact that the game keeps dangling that kind of carrot that keeps me coming back.      The guns are fun to use and finding loadouts that work with the talents and scrolls you accumulate allows for greater variety and use. I don't think there is any gun that I would say is useless, just certain guns work better with a particular talent set than others.       Among Gunfire's few issues is one of hit-and-miss localisation. Some phrasing and descriptions feel a bit off reading them in english. As development presses forward on the game, I expect this will improve, especially given it's popularity.     My biggest gripe comes with the way player death is handled. When a player dies, they are cast as an observer until they can be revived either by a peddler or in the next area after the boss fight. It would be nice to be able to offer some assistance to the group when dead. Perhaps even a hero specific talent that gives a passive boost to health, shields/armor or damage when they are observing. At the very least, heroes that die during boss fights should respawn immediately after the boss is defeated, not in the next area.

_childDocuments_.review: (60 Hours in at time of review)This is an addictive roguelike that I can best describe as a co-op roguelite abilities and gunplay similar to Overwatch, and an artstyle vaguely similar to borderlands. It can be played solo or with friends, but I vastly prefer it in co-op. All of the characters have interesting builds you can do with them, although I prefer turtle boi and the tiger. The mechanics are easy for anyone who has played an FPS or roguelite to pickup. It's an extremely satisfying game, and I don't have many complaints thus far.My complaints (as of V1.0)-* There is no option to see the current damage % or lucky shot % you are doing at any moment. You can manually add all your scrolls and ascensions together but that is tedious* The re-rolling gemini mechanic really sucks.  300 for copper per reroll is just way too much considering the odds for getting both weapons to have a matching gemini.Things I think they should add going forward-* Branching paths in terms of levels. Right now it's a linear 3 (or 4) level game. I feel like adding on more levels as options would give each run some more variety.* More heroes. This one is obvious, but it'd be nice to have a few different options for heros.* Unlockable cosmetics for existing heros. I'd prefer if these could be bought with essense or unlocked via certain achievements.
