_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a PHENOMENAL game. I usually can tear something about a game apart, but this game I have no idea what to even complain about.>The scrolls system is fair and fun. Any number of scrolls are useful, VERY few would be detrimental to you typically, while plenty can be a run-changer. Plenty of Binding of Isaac items leave you high and dry, but Gunfire takes the approach of throwing 10 scrolls at you that you get to choose from, rather than just 1 and hoping it's not detrimental to your build.>The character building in skill trees is incredibly reminiscent of Borderlands, where you build one of 3 trees, leveling some skills, while just activating others. While some powers are worse than others, they still left you with enough breathing room to make use of them and feel the benefit of a power, even if it isn't the strongest one.>The weapons are great because it's always possible to find just a little bit better one to drag you off the one you dumped a lot of upgrades in to, just to risk it for that perfect gun. Or you'll find a gun early on you know is the one, and have it at +29 by the end game.>Gameplay is satisfying. The levels feel good, despite being simple. Some vaults are well hidden, but can be found by looking hard enough, not just knowing all spawns. Games like RoboQuest or [POST VOID] test you as a player by increasing the need for gunplay, this game let's the players ride far more off their decision-making and character-building, not just being able to plink heads. Although, this is a favorite game of mine to plink heads in nowadays. Games like Risk of Rain 2 I feel like you get some unfair deaths, 100>0, sorry, better luck next time. You couldn't have made a better decision other than "well not being in the wrong place at the wrong time" even in normal. Gunfire has never made me feel like that, despite playing the Reincarnation/overlevel mode levels 1-5 the past week.Very few games feel as complete and satisfying as Gunfire Reborn. I recommend this game whole-heartedly! My buddy and I just picked it back up to play the Reincarnation modes, and that has been a BLAST. They're releasing a DLC soon that I'm incredibly excited for! If you're alone, this game is solid enough to stand on its own two feet, but with a friend, this game becomes so much more fun in terms of helping each other build your characters to achieve that perfect run.10/10EDIT: The DLC characters were solid, I like one more than the other but such is life.However, they just dropped the free Spiritual Assault Update and GOOD GRACIOUS is the new mode phenomenal. It's Zombies on steroids, no wave breaks, HARD bosses thrown in, THIS is endgame content. It is NO walk in the park completing this mode, I say as someone who has beat Reincarnation 8 and has 200 hours. LOVE THIS GAME STILL, SUPER RECOMMEND.

_childDocuments_.review: After being introduced to roguelikes pretty much through this game only, and trying out a number of other shooter roguelikes, no game has yet to top the time I've spent with Gunfire Reborn, even the more well-respected entries such as Enter The Gungeon. The basic gameplay of gathering scrolls and ascensions and honing your build as you start to see the direction that it is going is more fun in Gunfire than in any other roguelike, and the number of unique weapon concepts it features tops any other FPS game, period. Killing enemies is incredibly satisfying, especially when you get a great build and see only purple and red lucky shot numbers or have insane amounts of AoE damage and are able to wipe an entire room of enemies at once. Even in its pre-release state, Gunfire Reborn is one of my favorite games of all time-certainly my favorite roguelike of all time-and with the soon-to-be-released 1.0 patch and the amount of new content that will be added, I can see it climbing even closer to the top of my overall rankings.EDIT: 1.0 has absolutely exceeded my expectations, the new character and 4th Act especially are excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite accomplishing everything I set out to, I still keep coming back for a round at least once or twice a day.+ Gunplay feels solid, the sound design is a bit whack with certain guns but they feel punchy and enemy hitboxes are pretty good despite how fast paced the game is.+ Characters have really diverse playstyles. I guess this isn't a surprise with only 6 characters to choose from but they're all pretty solid, and have multiple viable build paths each.+ Good balance of RNG as far as roguelite games go. Compared to Risk of Rain 2, having a specific set of powerups (Ascensions) tied directly to each character alleviates the luck requirement for your powerups (Occult Scrolls).+ Talent trees are a nice meta progression system. I'm not super good at the game so being able to grind my way to a higher power level is a nice touch in general.+ Boss fights are really good overall, with enrage mechanics and a wide variety in their movesets.+ Length of each game is well balanced, at around 45 minutes to 1 hour for each full run.+ Occult Scrolls have good variety to them, there's a scroll for almost every effect you could possibly want in this game.+ Graphically, the game is very pretty to look at. It's simple voxel stuff but more than sufficient for what this game requires.+ Challenge-wise, I think the game is in a good place. There are a good number of difficulty options and I'm comfortable with the level I can reach (Reincarnation 4).- As is always an issue with these kinds of games, balance feels kinda wonky. In my ideal Gunfire Reborn, every build on every character would have the same endgame potential if you acquired a perfect set of ascensions and scrolls, but this really isn't the case. A clear example here is Ao Bai (Dog), who is supposed to specialize in explosive weapons, but this build ends up being completely inferior to his grenade and full auto builds due to the way explosive weapons work.- Due to Blessings being locked behind Reincarnation difficulty, there are a lot of players who will never even get to play with them and I find that pretty sad considering how fun they are. I feel like there should be a down-tuned version of Blessings for sub-reincarnation playthroughs. Adding to this point, there are a LOT of useless Blessings that simply never get picked, and are diluting the pool. Eye of Providence is probably one of the worst ideas to grace this game.- Multiplayer feels bad due to revive mechanics. When a player is dead, their only options for returning are to wait till the next act, or to be bought from the next peddler the group encounters. With the relative infrequency of peddlers, I usually have to wait at least 2-3 stages before reviving someone, which leaves them missing 5+ scrolls and roughly 3-4 ascensions. Their power is crippled at this point, and their only option is to die on loop until their team carries them to victory. If their team is merciful they will end the run early at act 3 for their benefit, instead of forcing them to suffer through one more unbearable act.- There are a lot of hidden mechanics and features that the game does not tell you about upfront. Elemental fusion and explosion/skill damage mechanics being the two most prominent ones. I'm gonna lump poor translation in with this point, since some effects in-game are explained but don't make sense due to grammatical errors or just straight up translation issues.- Weapons need a balance pass. out of the 48-ish weapons in the game, more than half are garbage on just about every character. - The way damage is tracked for each player in a multiplayer lobby is deceptive, since the game counts overkill damage as damage dealt. This should not be the case, as it's clearly not real damage and so is inflating the relative contribution of certain team members (Lei Luo mains).- There needs to be a way to denote multiplicative/additive boosts in this game. There's really no excuse for it, as a newer player would not be able to properly weigh their decisions if they don't know how the boost truly functions. Path of Exile has a great system, using the words "Increased" for additive, and "More" for multiplicative.- There is a lot of language jank in this game, which in my opinion is unacceptable for ARPG-style effects. "DMG" and "Total DMG" refer to the same thing, but "Damage" does not - even though DMG is just a shorthand for Damage. "Total Max HP" refers to HP + Shields, which makes no sense. and some places refer to the time it takes for your shield to start recharging as "Shield Recovery Delay", while another says "The time it takes for your shield to rest". So yeah they really need to sort that out.- Matchmaking is sorta dead. Even at the higher difficulties. You could easily spend 5-10 minutes waiting for a match, and then end up with 400 ping to the host and at that point, even switching weapons has a 1 second delay.I've found my niche in this game, so even I would consider most of the negatives I listed to be a little nitpicky. The game is excellent overall, and is rekindling my love for roguelites. The game is fun both in solo and multiplayer, though I would strongly recommend partying with friends instead of strangers, at least until some kind of matchmaking change happens. Enemy variety is solid, challenges are varied, and gameplay is intense and rather unique. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with so many problems. First off, HITBOXES. I have never had an issue with hitboxes, even in games with notoriously bad ones, but this one has some BAD ONES. Specifically the AOE attacks, you can be a full country mile outside that red circle, and you will still take damage. Another issue, some heroes just puzzle me, like a melee based hero in a game where most of the enemies and bosses are melee/close quarters based and can kill you very quickly. Lastly, this game has a dash system that is the most anemic, slowly recharging dash I have ever experienced. Pair that with the borderline impossible parkour and the movement is generally ♥♥♥♥. This game also has the WORST boss roster on the planet. Every boss can kill you if you are in the wrong place at the wrong time and at no fault of your own. Every boss uses ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bullet hell and area denial tactics that don't work when your character is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WALKING and has the worst, slowest dash on the planet. Pair that with the horrible, gigantic hitboxes and you never really feel like it was your fault that you died. This is the most poorly designed game I have ever played.Gluttony: Incredibly obtuse, giant heath bar that can refill itself if the player doesn't "pay attention to avoid" which explains nothing.Pole Monarch: Actually a fun fight, love this guy.Yoruhime-Maru: Every attack can one-shot you, has a giant hitbox that you can't avoid, and had more immunity phases than you can count. Pointless, artificial difficulty.Ichthyosaurus Offspring: Has a laser breath attack that will one-shot you and has a giant hitbox that you can't avoid. Has an acid ball attack that will one-shot you and has a giant hitbox that you can't avoid (are you sensing a theme here?).Wind God: Has a dive attack that will one-shot you and has a giant hitbox that you can't avoid. Also has a tornado that constantly chases you and has a giant hitbox that you can't avoid.Abyssal Serpent: Constantly spams annoying attacks that will one-shot you and have giant htiboxes that you can't avoid.Lu Wu and Golem both have the same issues but are also piss easy.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is  for the first ten hours or so, but after that it becomes a serious slog marred by too much random trash. You'll often find yourself losing a run not because you did anything wrong, but because of how worthless a lot of the upgrades, weapons, and talents are. Until there's a way to limit what items/scrolls/upgrades drop, I would pass this game by as the amount of "choices" in the game make it very difficult to succeed once you start unlocking everything.---------------I originally thought this game was  in that it was just another rougelite- it wasn't trying to break any new ground, it wasn't overly complicated, it was just . But, I can honestly say now that the game is less than - it's pretty terrible.The issue with the game is the issue with a lot of rouge-type games- there's too much stuff. There's too much variation. There's too many "choices" that are purely in the game for the sake of choice. 90% of the weapons in the game are worthless purely due to their inherent nature- they don't have enough innate damage, their firing pattern is too erratic, they're incredibly niche, etc, etc. Most of the scrolls you'll find also have this problem where they either offer an incredibly niche build choice, will actively hamstring you for little benefit, or are very minor boons that don't actively help your build. You also get  upgrades during a run, which fall into the same trap as weapons and scrolls.The thing is that all this choice actually makes it  to succeed the more you unlock. I could consistently get to the "end" boss at level 50, but now? I haven't seen the end boss in a good thirty levels. There's just too much stuff that I can't consistently make a build come together. And the meta-progression that the game has, because this is a rouge-, does not help. Most of the benefits you get from the meta-progression are minor bonuses that don't make the game any easier. The problem is the variation, and the meta-progression doesn't make anything less random. Extra health doesn't solve the issue of being randomly one-shot. Extra inscriptions on weapons don't change the inherent worthlessness of a specific weapon. Cheaper shop prices don't mean anything when there's rarely ever anything in the shop worth buying. And the list goes on.Overall there is no end-game here, which is  a rouge-lite has. The first ten hours of the game are fun, but after that the game quickly nose dives into a slog as you unlock tons of trash that actively make finding the few good upgrades/weapons harder and harder. If the game is ever updated with an endless mode where you can pick and choose what weapons/upgrades drop, this would be a great time waster- but, as it stands, that's not the case and I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the price tag, plenty of fun.Like everyone says it's kind of a mix of Risk of Rain and Borderlands but I don't think people put enough of a point on how good the abilities are. Both characters have three different types of builds, 6 builds total, and these builds have sub builds. For the first character you can either use your ability to freeze large mobs of enemies for a good chunk of time while you land some free critical shots or you can lose the freeze ability and start making it do even more damage. If you're playing with friends you can even turn your grenades into the perfect support action by making enemies take more damage and deal less on top of doing good DoT damage if you take elemental scrolls. That's three full fun builds that can easily last you until the second character, or if you prefer the first one for the rest of the game. The second character is my personal favorite and you can either go full gunzerker, explosives, or crit build. While *technically* you could go full crit with the mage I personally feel the gunfighter does it better because of his perks like Substained Fire and a few more.TL:DR - With a minimum of 6 pure builds and 12 sub builds, 34 guns, 104 scrolls, and the class abilities it's really just up to you how long you want to play this game but it is EASILY worth the price tag and will provide you with hours and hours of fun with either singleplayer or with friends.Disclaimer: Yes it's EARLY ACCESS people so things are not going to be perfect. You will find enemies that are far harder to deal with than all the other types put together, you will find a few bugs here or there and maybe some translation issues but in all my hours I have yet to find any major bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definetly fun and if it had less positive buzz around it I would give a thumbs up, but it has disappointed me in a single crucial way (and a few other smaller ones) that forced me to downshift my excitement quite a bit so I just want to warn you on this issue. For the record, I played solo.Despite all its strengths - mainly the fun gunplay and core gameplay loop - the enemy design, especially the boss design, suffers from extreme swingyness. What I mean is that on all my runs so far, I will feel godlike invincible and have a lot of fun with a build that seems like it's going in a good direction, then all of a sudden just get instantly killed. This happened once or twice with a wave of smaller enemies where a lot of damage quickly piled up, but it's usually manageable. Their attacks are for the most part well telegraphed and while they can catch you off-guard and deal a lot of damage quickly, so far I've usually been able to take cover and turn the fight around. Not so for elites and bosses (except the first who is an absolute pushover). These mothertruckers will 100 to 0 you instantly with some of the worst telegraphed attacks I've ever seen in an FPS. AoEs that spawn behind you, projectiles where it's not clear whether you're supposed to dodge or shoot them, or just a laser that oneshots you if you stand in the wrong direction. Fun stuff.I don't think I'm terrible at the game. I make mistakes, sure, I'm still learning, but in my 5-6 runs so far I've never died on the first stage and in the last 3 always got to the 3rd stage. It feels all the more defeating when my amazing run suddenly comes to a halt. Doubly so because the new weapons and items you unlock via in-game achievements drop *instantly*, which is a really cool system except that it means your first few runs will be supercharged with additional item drops that then get wasted because of attacks or mechanics you couldn't possibly anticipate. The worst offender was probably when an elite in the third stage spawned a variant of a familiar enemy that - unlike the regular version - explodes on death, killing me instantly in what I thought would be the run to get me to stage four.I don't know if that's what's actually going on, but it seems like bosses are designed in a way that brute-forces the usual roguelite-flow, where you're not expected to win on your first few runs and are instead supposed to get more experience and in-game upgrades first to gradually progress each time. Which isn't very rewarding when it feels like a binary learning experience of "now that I have died once to this and know what it does, it will be 90% less deadly next time". Either that or it's designed primarily with multiplayer in mind, neither of which make the problem better.Maybe I'm doing something wrong, but I usually don't have the option for a more defensive build either, at least not with the standard starting character. Perhaps he's particularly squishy, which would then also be a terrible idea not to start off with a well-rounded character that gives you several options of building him. Come to think of it, build variety in terms of level-up abilities is pretty minimal. I can either upgrade grenades, my other activated ability, or elemental damage and...that's it. Nothing really exciting, just percentages and a few passive abilities. And the same ones each run. Similar thing goes for the items and weapons, but at least there you're continually unlocking new ones, so it should get better with time.Overall it's fun and I see the potential to love it later, but it has a TERRIBLE starting experience which seems like it could be roughly adressed pretty easily by tweaking a few numbers. As it stands, every death is not a motivation to try again and improve, but feels like a cheap trap that makes me want to close the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This was on my wishlist for a long time after watching a pretty entertaining twitch stream featuring the game. I kept putting it off for some reason. I knew that it'd be fun but I just always put it to the side. Finally I pulled the trigger during the sale, and a normally well priced game became an even better deal around the 10 dollar mark. It is by far well worth your money. The game feels fun. It's mainly fighting your way through a variety of settings, encountering quite a few types of enemies, always looking for the sweet loot, and quickly comparing tons of different weaponry that drop. There are heroes, talents, unlocks, challenges, build types, etc; all the things you've come to know and love in roguelites, etc. The gameplay loop is well balanced and much time can pass quite easily which is a testament to creating a good sense of difficulty and scaling. It is quite hard and often I've died suddenly but usually based off a poor decision. This feeling of uncertainty even as you become powerful keeps the game engaging and alive. It good ways it reminds me of Borderlands 2, Hades, and Risk of Rain 2 while still doing it's own thing. Colorful worlds, fun heroes, cool weapons, pretty responsive gun play, big RPG style numbers flying up on the screen...I've enjoyed it for a few hours now by myself and had a ton of fun fighting along side my brother, so the co-op is great too. Pretty stable game, no bugs yet or anything weird. Mind you, I've only played a few hours but I really do see myself putting on music or whatever and really enjoying the gameplay loop and building up the heroes. If you've had this on your radar or are just looking for a simply fun shooter to play alone or with friends it's just a great, great deal. The content seems to be coming along too.EDIT: 1.0 is finally here and it's great! A new stage, new guns, a new character, new scrolls! More mechanics to test out and combinations to experience! Yet another reason to grab this game!EDIT #2: DLCs are great as well. Lots more guns and a few more characters to master! I feel like even though there may be 'the best meta' etc to do a run, there are many many paths to a good build via so many scrolls and weapons! Still highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't leave too many reviews, but for this game? I'll make an exception.--CONS---The game is definitely rough on the translations. Tooltips for your "Scrolls" (The rogue-lite element in this game) are often confusing until you figure out how the game works and translate experience into expertise. Some are easy to figure out: +5% elemental chance and damage. Others are more... uh.. Esoteric (Looking at you Fish or Bear Paw). -The DLC characters are definitely stronger. They have more mechanical interactions and distinct playstyles that set them apart from the others.-Hitboxes are usually good. Sometimes they can be... Weird. Crits you shouldnt have made but did. Walls that you /Definitely/ shot over but hit instead. And rolling boulders that treat you as if you were paper thin while you bob and weave. Honestly, I'm only listing it as a con because it is hit or miss as far as player experience and doesnt come up often enough to be a feature. --Pros---Great co-op game. genuinely. You can share more of your scrolls with other players to help each other get stronger or to facilitate certain playstyles or roles. Weapon sharing, scroll sharing. We just got done with our first season and instead of forever locking the stuff in the previous one... instead of removing the unique season mechanic from season 1... They just said "Yeah, go ahead and buy the rewards from previous seasons with in game currency that you use and earn all the time anyways." This. THIS RIGHT HERE. This is how you make people want to keep playing your game!!! _childDocuments_.review: is another title to the ever expanding list of early access roguelites, but it changes enough to be given a shot. It has its own unique charms and features while staying true to the genre, and at an $11.99 price point is honestly a steal! Like most roguelites, the story is more of an afterthought in Gunfire Reborn. While it may not have exciting narratives with fancy character development, it does provide a unique premise with a setting that is often underutilized. The setting is heavily inspired by ancient chinese lore, which provides a sense of mystery and sacredness to all aspects of the game. With typical things you would associate with that setting, such as pandas, tombs, kegs, monks, etc. While it may not be the most unique setting for games as a whole, it is refreshing to experience it with a different light in the roguelite genre.Now we get to the fun part, the gunplay in Gunfire Reborn is top notch for an FPS roguelite. Combat in this game revolves around balancing your movement around the stage with the help of your dash ability, all while firing your three weapon slots, throwing grenades, and using your abilities. It is certainly not a shooter where you are meant to take your time with calculated shots, and more in the run around like sonic with a bazooka realm of gunplay. It really is a fast paced shooter that constantly ramps up the difficulty until you reach your limit.With 39 weapons to choose from, ranging from a default pistol to fire breathing lizards and poison tipped kunai blades there is something for everyone. You get your default pistol permanently, and can pick from any weapon for your last two slots. And then add on 100 different occult scrolls, that can drastically change your build, while also upgrading your characters abilities there is a lot of variety in potential builds. If there is to be one department Gunfire Reborn delivers it has to be the sheer amount of tools at your disposal.A common trend in most roguelites now-a-days is to add a form of progression outside of actually being in a run, and it’s present in Gunfire Reborn. During your run you get a form of currency called soul essence, which is earned at a very slow rate. Then in return you can use these soul essences to upgrade different aspects of your character from health, shields, ammo count, drop modifiers, and much more. This adds a whole new level to the game, as instead of taking it one run at a time it turns into gearing and leveling your character for complete destruction. I will warn you that at the end of a run all your currency earned must be spent to upgrade right away, so if you get 35 soul essence and your health upgrade costs 30 that extra 5 will be lost as it's unable to be spent. This encourages a slow evolution of power until you eventually become an unstoppable force. And each different character has a separate talent tree, so be prepared for lots and lots of runs.The visuals in Gunfire Reborn are not mind blowing by any means, but it does have this indie charm that is so hard to hate. Everything from the characters, the NPCs, guns, even the menu is all heavily stylized. It may not be the most polished game, but it certainly has a case for being one of the most charming games. The art style is simple and easy to follow, but still gives off an incredible atmosphere. The game gives off vibes of coziness and simplicity, and just adds to the addicting nature based on the ease it gives on your eyes.Again the sound design follows the same path its visuals take, simple and satisfying. There might not be 1:1 M16 sound bytes, but instead each gun offers a unique and pleasant pop. Each kill has an audible sound played, which makes chaining large rooms even more pleasing. The abilities have the expected mystical tones when casting, and the creeks and moans of the tomb tie it all together. The OST while not a masterpiece by any means, is adequate to the overall tone of the game. There isn’t much variety in the different songs, so be prepared to listen to the same song on repeat. Gunfire Reborn is not just another roguelite doomed for early access eternity. It is a refreshing take on the genre that offers enough unique differences to be worth a look. With a focus on combat and build variety with a nice progression system, Gunfire Reborn is looking to occupy a lot of your future free time. With a price tag of $11.99 Gunfire Reborn is a hard deal to pass for anyone a fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Within only a span of 9 hours put into the game so far, this game is an unpolished diamond in the rough. As with every roguelite you start off with one character and the roster continues to unlock as you play, greatly making each run easier with passive bonuses or shop unlocks with the spendable point system. There are only 6 playable characters in the game, each with their own skills that play into specific play styles. Weapons and scrolls are continuously unlocked through defeating bosses and enemies and the game gives you a chance to try out such weapons and scrolls as soon as you unlock them too. The loot system is instanced based which means you don't have to worry about someone taking the thing that you want and if you want to share with teammates, then you mark it and it shows up in other player's instances. There are many weapon and scroll combos that synergize well with each other and around some point, your weapons will be able to synergize with each other too. Overall, fantastic game, can't wait for new updates for more characters and weapons.This is a yes, buy it whenever. Personally, bought it when it was discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, challenging, dungeon-crawling game that's constantly getting updated and has clear plans for the future of their game. I've already beat it on Reincarnation 8, but love playing it with my friends. Amazing replay value, lots of things to do despite it being such a simple concept, and the RNG factor just ups it even more. I received this as a gift from my friend, (probably wouldn't have given it too much thought otherwise) but damn is it the best gifted game I've ever received. I'm already almost at 100 hours, phew! If you, the reader, are truly on the fence about getting this game...don't be. It's a worthy investment!TL;DR: GET THIS GAME! Best gift ever!Pros:+RNG factor to enemies spawned, layout of level, weapons dropped, and availability of merchants+Varying difficulty levels for varying levels of familiarity with these styles of games. At the hardest difficulty, you have up to Reincarnation 8.+Dungeon crawling dungeon crawling dungeon crawling!!! :)+Cute animals, lovely consistent visual style+Merchants are scarce, but not so frustratingly scarce; the Craftsman and Peddler are always available at boss stages+Love the concept of the Phantom Peddler for that high risk high reward mindset; invest your soul essence to get a huge leg up (hopefully) but don't waste it!+Character designs are quite cool, perhaps not the most unique ever but it matches the visual style and the stories quite nicely+Weapons are very fun and there's a huge variety; from SMGs you can throw to explode, to ray beams that you click to the beat to buff the ray, to bows that do more damage as you hold it in the pulled back position. Shotguns that splinter into corrosive darts, kunais, crossbows, mortars, swords... There's really something for everyone! And some characters actually play better when using specific weapons, so it really adds to choosing-your-own-adventure.+There is just a tad bit of lore via dialogue, but it's not at all the center of the gameplay. Once you beat the game all the way through Pole Monarch just one time, you'll get all the story there really is to the game. Maybe they'll add more? :)+Difficulty of enemies scales up nicely depending on how many people you're playing with/if you're playing solo. Speaking of, you can play this game completely offline if you want! They just added a Lone Wolf modifier to Reincarnation if you're more of a solo player (which I have already used very much, and love the change!)+Spiritual Assault, while still very much being developed and polished, is quite fun to just go ham on some enemies and play around with weapons and ascensions without having to go from stage to stage. You just fight endless enemies and try to survive, taking small breaks to level your weapons, recycle stuff, and get situated before the waves start up again.+Daily Challenges are, in fact, challenges. Some of them are quite difficult, and some others are just meant to be chaotic fun. Definitely give them a try, or at least look at the descriptions to see if it's up your alley! If you lose, it's fine. The Dailies only last through one level/4 stages, i.e. Longling Tomb 1 through Boss, and then that's it. Super short and sweet, and you get soul essence at the end of it. Sometimes it picks your hero for you, but you can still click on your little friend to change them out to your preferred!+Base game has a great price point and makes for a wonderful gift to anyone who likes roguelites or cute animals!+Constantly being updated, and they share their yearly game plan with players as soon as they start up the game. Love the transparency!Cons:-Enhanced scrolls/weapons could have the enhancements made more clear versus their normal counterparts. Perhaps additional UI, a different highlight color, italics, etc.?-DLC at time of writing this really only unlocks a character for you, and not too much else (as far as I know). Could provide more in future DLC to make it more worth it, or lower the price. Right now the contents just doesn't seem to match how much it costs. I personally enjoy the character, but could be made to appeal to more people.-The two characters you have to buy with soul essence is a bit expensive, although I suppose they're intended to be bought only by veterans/super dedicated players? Not sure. Without a carry, new players won't be able to try them out easily and potentially find that "One character" that really clicks with their playstyle and keeps them engaged. Or maybe, once they beat the game solo they get a discount? Just a thought; but this soul essence pricing is not really an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Some influencer must have developed a liking to this game, that's the only reason I can imagine why this game is more popular than THE roguelike shooter, Immortal Redneck. Or why it's popular at all. Immediately as I started playing this game, the contrast between these two games was so stark that Gunfire Reborn felt like a tech demo of some newbie programmer on a shoestring budget. I find the game hideous with its lack of detailed textures and amorphous-looking doors and branches on the walls. It aims to create an unique art style, but in my opinion only manages to be bland. The movement is slow and extremely simple, and I can't even jump up onto elevated ground. It feels clumsy, and the execution of the dash mechanic feels lame, as though only a few basic program lines have been used to implement it that barely get the job done. The weapon damage types are ripped off from Borderlands and as soon as I saw it, I was already bored by it (NOT Borderlands AGAIN!) and was disappointed by the lack of creativity. The enemy design is lackluster and their energy shield and armor bars are ripped from Borderlands too. I think the nostalgia this mechanic creates is what carries the game that has little else to show than this stolen damage/shield mechanic. I've found the upgrade scrolls uncreative and unfun.Of course, if you never knew another roguelike FPS, this could scratch an itch, but fortunately we're not stuck with this very bland and uncreative execution of a roguelike FPS. I'm talking about much better examples, like Ziggurat, and most importantly, Immortal Redneck. Unfortunately Total Biscuit has roasted Immortal Redneck in his video review, and deterred people from purchasing that great roguelike. It never really took off unlike this undeserving title.That game's gameplay is fast, the movement is fluid (it's a thrill-ride actually), the environments absolutely gorgeous, the weapons and enemies are varied and interesting, and the creative, fun scrolls create a lot of variety. I think this game with over a million sales is the perfect example of how a game's success is largely dependent on what influencers say about it, rather that on its actual merits.I suggest you spend your money on Immortal Redneck, or Ziggurat, rather than on this sub-par experience. For me, I'm going to ask for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: If you didn't know what a rogue shooter was, it's an adventure that, when you die, you restart the adventure. Most of them also have you unlock skills to make each run slightly more manageable. This game is very fun and all the roguelike systems are amazingly well done. Each character has their own, unique abilities and some skill as well as a skill tree that goes across all characters. My only complaints are that I wish they would add new areas and have it where you could save a multiplayer run, possibly tweak some of the adventure settings, and have a cycle to restart continue your run with everything you have, like in Risk Of Rain. _childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a decent game with very little replayability. Once you beat the final boss, that's it: there are no new areas, no new enemies except for the alternate bosses, and the only content left to unlock are the pips on the talent tree and new scrolls. The difficulty selection only increases elite enemy spawn rates, increases their HP, and adds more elite types to the pool.If you don't find the main combat loop fun, there is nothing left for you in this game. If you do like it, then you won't be able to play it for long before replaying the same adventure starts to get boring, even if you only open it every once and a while when you want something to occupy your time.The dailies are interesting twists, but you don't get any rewards for beating them and matchmaking is disabled, so I don't see the point in bothering with them.An endless mode would really help the game out, since every session is essentially the same once you get the good scrolls unlocked and your talent tree filled out: Keep playing until you get good scrolls, then steamroll everything in front of you, beat the final boss, and repeat. There is a distinct lack of felt challenge once you get to this endgame, so an endless mode that makes the game exponentially harder as you go would give a new challenge to veterans and a longer gameplay loop for those that don't want to be forced to stop at the last boss. It would be very easy to do from a game design perspective so I don't see a reason why they can't do this. Even easier would be to simply take the arena maps and scenarios that are already in the game and make them endless, with rewards given at landmarks and after killing big bosses or passing demonic events.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn combines the rogue-lite run progression of Risk of Rain with the first-person shooting and extensive loot of Borderlands, creating a fast-paced FPS rogue-lite experience. Developed by Duoyi Interactive Entertainment, this indie gem offers a refreshing take on the genre, providing players with a thrilling and challenging experience. Players can control unique heroes with different abilities to experience diverse builds and fight against various creatures, bosses and challenging environments.  It involves battling through randomly generated levels, and with each run, players gain experience and can upgrade their abilities. The RPG elements come into play in character development and the ability to upgrade weapons. This combination creates a dynamic and challenging environment. The game offers a variety of heroes, each with unique abilities, allowing for a diverse range of build gameplay. The game has a roster of 10 diverse heroes, each bringing their own flavour. Base stats, talents, and skills differ, making each hero unique in the game's strategic puzzle. This diversity allows for a wide range of playstyles, with certain heroes synergising better with specific weapons and occult scrolls.As players progress through the game, they can unlock new abilities and upgrade their existing ones, allowing for a relatively high degree of customisation. This system encourages experimentation and strategic thinking, as players must decide how to best allocate their resources to suit their playstyle. You face a tradeoff of saving your coins to upgrade your weapons later for an easier late-game versus spending your coins now to have a better chance at surviving the early game but risk having no coins to upgrade.Unlocking these heroes is a journey in itself. Some require reaching a certain talent level, others demand payment in Soul Essence, and a few are hidden behind the gates of DLC. The game features procedurally generated levels, ensuring a unique experience each time you play. However, it gets annoying as you encounter the same tileset every run in different orders.The game's arsenal is a treasure trove of ~58 distinct weapons, each with its own rhythm and style. The weapons are diverse and well-balanced, ensuring no weapon feels overpowered. From the rapid-fire rate of some to the devastating critical hit damage of others, each weapon is a unique instrument in the battle symphony. Some even possess exclusive effects, adding a layer of strategy to the combat. Precision is the key to this dance, with accurate shots rewarded with greater damage and additional effects – as like any FPSEven though this game has a matchmaking system, it is unfortunately not well-executed. Players can only match with others at the same difficulty, a counterintuitive setup, as most of the player base is at a higher difficulty level. These higher levels are only accessible after completing the preceding ones. This presents a substantial problem for new players, who are less likely to find a multiplayer game due to the limited pool of players at the introductory levels.Furthermore, playing with randoms often leads to an imbalanced gaming experience. If one player surges ahead of the others, the rest of the team becomes mere cannon fodder. This scenario can detract from the game's enjoyment, turning a potential cooperative experience into a frustrating exercise in futility. Gunfire Reborn is a well-rounded game that offers a unique blend of FPS and roguelike gameplay. Its engaging gameplay, dynamic music, distinctive art style, and diverse weapons and enemies make it a standout title. Despite some issues with its multiplayer system, the overall experience is highly rewarding. Whether you're a seasoned gamer or a newcomer to the genre, Gunfire Reborn offers a unique and engaging gaming experience worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a GREAT game.  I'm an old guy for a gamer, and so my twitch reflexes have been starting to slow these past years.  Obviously, this isn't a great thing for shooters, so I don't play many.I have quite a few more hours than is shown on this account, and allow me to say it one more time: THIS IS JUST A GREAT GAME!  You wind up able to unlock several more heroes after your starting hero, and they have a large talent tree, and a great rogue-like RPG system for hero advancement.   To be honest, even without unlocking more heroes, I could have a blast just with the hero you start with.  It's great because there are enough different things to improve for several different trees, to where you can make the choices that best fit how you play, but still want to keep advancing in order to make other areas better.  The enemy AI is better than so many other games in how they will attack, and there are a decent number of different opponents to keep you on your toes.  I was genuinely shocked the first time I saw an elite mob, and even more so when I fought a boss for the first time.  Being just over $25 at full-price WITH the DLC is definitely good value for money.  It was even worth a purchase for me, as someone who rarely plays shooters.  I'm quite sure if you have any interest in a game like this, that you'll love this one, and will also think you got great value for money.I look forward to other games from this developer now, that's for sure!  BRAVO!

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an interesting experience. The character and gun selections are not too expansive, so the primary goal is honing. The micro-game is insanely important, as a single slip-up can lead to you paying a few dozen essence; playing encounters right is just as important and fun as choosing gear or taking down a boss. While I haven't beaten Nightmare yet, I've spent a long time having some of the most fun in a rouguelite I've ever experienced, unlocking new upgrades, scrolls, and weapons (except that damn Demonlore). While I have no Idea how much more of this game there will be in the future and mod support is practically nonexistent, the practicing and grinding of the game is an excellent experience (and better with friends!).Edit: This game gets really boring once you get good at it. worth the price, but I wouldn't expect anything too impressive with this game's replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a few translation erros and texts that are hard to read or comprehent, Gunfire Reborn is probably the most polished "Early Access" title I have ever played. There are barely any features I am lacking to experience the whole thing. I've been playing this game with friends for a total of 15h now and we are yet to beat the game. We keep finding new weapons or upgrades, learning more about the game and encounter new enemies. The game is incredibly comprehensive and the best thing about it: There is still so much to come. The outlined roadmap provided by the developer helps staying engaged, by presenting new upcoming content.The gameplay is crisp, fluid and challenging. You can establish combined strategies with your partners in crime and shine with mechanical skill yourself. The variety of weapons allows to deploy a multitude of options on how to approach the game. And given the RNG, you often have to adapt to the circumstances you face. No run is like the one before.I am very excited for the next updates and can only highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible.- The weapons are fun and creative.- The inscriptions can make even two of the same weapon feel very different from another.- The scrolls have unique effects, that make cool builds possible.- The characters all feel fun to play and allow for very different playstyles.- The Ascencion system is interesting, and there are virtually no bad options. It just depends on the stuff you got within the run.- The Leveling allows for a very well made progression, where you get enough levels to be powerful enough for the next difficulty at the same time the current one starts to feel easier, making the game more difficult again.- Even after a few dozen hours of playing, you still regularly unlock new stuff, that allow for new and surprisingly different ways to play the game.- The premade rooms that the levels are generated from are all well crafted, and especially the vaults are really cool (even though they get progressively harder to spot as you go on).- The multiplayer works really well, both when it comes to loot sharing and enemy scaling.- The new update (1.0 at the time of me writing this) added a ton of very well made content and the new character is already my favourite so far.Overall, I can absolutely recommend this game, and it is worth every cent, especially if you play with one or more friends.

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing just how far this FPS+Roguelite+RPG has come since it's early access release. Now, just recently making it's 1.0 debut this a great example of what a communicative and hardworking team can do with an idea that they love. I believe that at it's current price Gunfire Reborn is an excellent purchase, and if you get it during a sale then you're even luckier. To put it simply I find that Gunfire Reborn plays very smoothly. It makes it easy to sit down, relax, and play a run or two. And for those that are interested I would say that a run typically takes about 30 minutes to an hour, depending on things like the difficulty level, which there are many, and your skills in the game. I would say that Borderlands inspired is a safe way to describe the overall feel of the FPS gameplay and loot systems in the game. That being said, when compared I think that Gunfire Reborn has even more ways to customize your play experiences with character builds, scrolls (buffs), and weapon modifications, that I actually find it to be the better version for me. I just hope that if you read this far and it looks and sounds interesting to you too then you give it a shot. I don't think you'll be disappointed if you do. *Lastly the Gunfire Reborn team is pushing for the "Better With Friends" (2021) award so please vote if you agree with that sentiment, I have played many hours myself in their Co-op modes to prove that it can certainly be true. For me though this is my "Sit Back And Relax" award for many of the reasons I mentioned above. If for you it's "Game Of The Year", "Labor Of Love", or Best Game You Suck At", then I'll just say I understand, it was a tough call lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great roguelite game that deserves a much bigger player base than it currently has. For $12 you get an addictive fps and rpg mixed game that keeps me coming back. The shooting is tight, the gameplay loop is addictive, the graphics are charming, and the rpg aspects make it feel rewarding. There's no stupid microtransactions that make the game feel like a money grab, instead it's a game that has everything unlockable by simply playing the game. I wish more game developers followed this practice and made games for gamers. I have nothing but good things to say about this game and hope that the developers continue to support this hidden gem. For $12 you can't get a better game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoyable both in solo and multiplayer. * Every character has their own style and all of them are viable (but the skill requirement varies considerably). * Plenty of fun weapons, though quite a few are not too great, mostly because of being slow and unwieldy.* The risk factor is just right. Going for a glass cannon build and failing to get the necessary ascensions is an essential part of a roguelite experience.* When the plan (weapons, ascensions, scrolls) comes together, getting seven-figure crits feels amazing.It is , which might be the greatest argument for it.But has a few bad qualities, too (developers, kindly have a look-see):* Act 1 only drops weapons with 1-3 inscriptions, which are unfixable for later use as you can only add one extra inscription via the gunsmith, so you end up with 2-4, rather than the maximum of 5 inscriptions. Act 1 boss and Act 2 and later give 4-5 inscriptions. This really needs to be looked at in some way, maybe allowing us to add non-gemini inscriptions at a reasonable price or instead of upgrading the weapon. Currently upgrading Act 1 weapons is wasteful.* Despite all the variety, some weapons are clearly perfect for certain builds and others are clearly elemental gemini fodder. at best.* The enemy variety is not particularly great and some of them are simply annoying rather than challenging. Maybe some sort of interaction between enemy types could help.* Beating Reincarnation 8 makes the game quite hollow, since daily challenges are often just too troublesome, Having minor challenge modifiers per run that would call for specific build adjustments would be great.But it is fun and quite worth the time and money investment. It just won't entertain you for 1000+ hours.

Tons of creativity in this game, and the enemies and gunplay are so good. Hard to believe this is the first fps for this developer.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun Chinese folklore inspired roguelite FPS. The art direction has style and the characters are unique in their design without veering into cutesy or full chibi. The enemies are diverse and the firearms are whacky and fun and only achievable thanks to the fantasy genre the game utilizes--like the shotgun you have to feed to reload. Difficulty does seem to spike in the latter half of stages, but I play this game casually for friends so I can't tell you much about the overall grind. It works in that regard for sure as a great 1-2 hour session with friends chatting in voice call. While certain characters are locked behind DLC, others can be purchased in-game and doesn't diminish the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Getting a feel for the game takes a little while. Once you get the hang of it, it's hard to put down. Lots of different playable methods combined with the RNG for drops and level ups make each run feel like a new one. If there were one or two more stages and a few more bosses, it would be among the best of the best for dungeon crawlers.The art/character design has a Sea of Thieves type feel to me. One downside is that there is no real lore to the game. There is a tiny bit of story to the game, but if they dropped focus on the story in favor of the "funness" of the game, they definitely made the right choice! Highly repeatable, highly recommend.Oh, and the season pass is completely free!

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far my favourite Roguelike ever made. The different combos of Occult Scrolls, even if you dont have the Reincarnation effect Spiritual Link enabled, make for fun and often unique runs, like having one of the enthusiast scrolls (inflict burning/shock/decay on an enemy will also inflict the same to you with some buffs as you have that effect) alongside one of the corresponding shard scrolls which make you immune to the negative elemental effect is a simple and obvious combination with nearly endless more.The unique weapons are also a fun factor as theres weapons you like and dislike, I for example like the Thunder Storm I believe its called, the one that shoots a massive lightning ball, but somehow I dont dislike any weapon honestly, all of them are cool and I pick them up if need be, the weapon inscriptions make it even better with some devastating effects that can sometimes carry a run from start to finish.TLDR: This game is awesome and as long as it gets updates i'll come back to it and probably even pay for the dlc, I got the 2 current ones and the weapons, scrolls and characters (besides Nona, she is basically Pay2Win, but I still love playing her) are cool aswell. _childDocuments_.review: To whom it may concern,As a lifelong opponent of those miscreants who refer to themselves - in a disturbingly childish sounding tone - as "furries", the prospect of purchasing such a game as Gunfire Reborn was, to me, similar to the prospect of falling from the back of a speeding steam-train; both were unwelcome and unlikely. However, after hearing many glowing reviews from acquaintances, I made the uncharacteristic choice of following their advice, as opposed to cutting off all personal contact and alerting the authorities of their grave misconduct.I have been, in a word, surprised. And, to be clear, surprised as a child is upon receiving a new set of gird and cleek, not as a soldier is surprised when he has trodden upon a land-mine. The gun-play is smooth and vigorous, the sound effects crisp, and the progression teleologically satisfying. The different characters, although beasts, are amusing to play and offer up variety and opportunity to experiment with different methods of wholesale destruction.And what destruction. The most delightful aspect of Gunfire Reborn is the feeling of power that comes with a particularly lucky session. As you stride swiftly through your enemies, burning them to cinders in a ceaseless conflagration and carelessly slapping the fire-breathing reptile you hold in your proto-human paws, you may find yourself emitting a low, belly-chuckle at your desk, a sign that you are absorbing the violence and achieving catharsis, just as Aristotle would have hoped.There are, of course, scars that mar this monument of indie gaming. Besides the obvious appeal to deranged individuals who quack like ducks and coo like the turtle-dove, there is the atrociously confusing translation into English. It is certainly not the King's, and occasionally you may have to decipher the text of a scroll as Champollion deciphered the Rosetta Stone.  The pudding, however, is not spoiled by the addition of these few moldy raisins. Altogether, this game is a robust and rewarding experience, which is always better enjoyed with a few comrades-in-arms. I hope this humble review may give you some insight, and I am as everYour obedient servant,Sammy J.

_childDocuments_.review: While more popular than it used to be, this is an absolute hidden gem of a rogue lite. Each character is very distinct, with unique powers and 3 different build types that can be focused or mixed and matched. On top of this, each base weapon is largely distinct, then layered with all the different and unique modifier rolls they can have. Lastly, there is a skill tree outside of the runs you work on, solidifying another layer of progression to take you up the 9 difficulty levels and optional run modifiers you can apply. It is truly awesome how all these systems interact to make you a super powered god once you understand them, while still giving enough difficulty options to provide a challenge even when you *know* the game. This game is almost comparable to an MMO as far as mechanics and systems interacting with each other and the player, but feels much better to progress than most MMOs in my opinion, bc the pace matches where you are skill and understanding wise instead of giving you these mechanics as rewards for grinding and just sinking time in.I'd also like to add they do the Seasons system well. While I dreaded reading they were adding it, nothing about it is based on real money, you get everything in the game, and there is no FOMO bc you can buy the stuff from the seasons with the excess currency you earn in runs, and the mechanics each season introduces (ala PoE leagues) can be selected and replayed whenever. WHY ISN'T EVERY SEASON SYSTEM LIKE THIS? Adds unique mechanics, lets devs experiment, no FOMO, and all of it totally free (I'd honestly be willing to pay a couple of bucks for it since the game has been out so long but if they wanna keep giving us free content then I'm not complaining LOL)

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is like a roguelike Borderlands. You pick one of the heroes for a 30-60m run through 3-4 acts. Each act has its own style, collection of enemies, and two possible boss fights. Along the way you gain levels that give you perks, collect "occult scrolls" that give you more perks, and pick up weapons with different elements and very different firing properties. Successful runs unlock higher difficulties, and between runs you can unlock permanent buffs or new characters.The gameplay variety is incredible. Weapons are wildly different- melee weapons, tracking weapons, richocheting weapons, grenade and rocket launchers, flamethrowers, reflectors, anything you can imagine. Each character, too, has very different action skills and grenades, which can become even more distinct with the right perks. The right occult scrolls can completely change your run, too, eg by making you near invulnerable at range but frail up close.The enemies are distinct but straightforward. They pretty much each have one thing they do: there's the sniper enemies you take cover from, the summoner enemies you go after first, the tank enemies who try to get in your way, etc. They're vanilla but that works well as a foil for the PCs. You're the Harlem Globetrotters and they're the Washington Generals.The graphics and sound are the same. They serve the gameplay well but are unremarkable. It's easy to tell what you're fighting and there aren't a ton of effects getting in the way.I don't think it's infinitely replayable - you can unlock all the permanent bonuses and difficulty levels in a few dozen hours, and the limitless modes aren't that appealing. I've gotten more than a hundred hours of fun from it though and I'm not done yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This might have the EA tag but tbh it feels more complete than most games and it just keeps adding content.It is exactly what ot looks like, a first person rogue-lite shooter with currently 3 different characters.All characters have a different play style, defined by the skills and upgrades you get during a run. Also depending on the other items you get there is also quite some diversity in builds. Every run you have to adapt and try to make the most out of the things you get and it is rare that you really feel unlucky and under powered.The runs itself are perfectly in length imo, You have nice power progression over the course of the run and a complete run will take you around 40min. So it is a really nice game to pick up and play for 1-2h and come back later.Upgrades you can buy after a run (with currency acquired during a run) feel good and really add up making you feel way more powerful. The normal upgrades are quite general, like more HP, more damage and so on. Every character also has character specific upgrades, which directly improve certain aspects of the character.It took me 45 hours to get all upgrades but I still have to get all the unlockable items. Around 70% of my runs were singe player, which is totally fine and might be even a bit easier than multiplayer. But multiplayer is a lot more fun. The nice thing is all drops are individual so no competition for loot. The game has automatic matchmaking if you want to play with random people or you can invite your friends. I mostly played with randoms and the community so far was always nice and helpful.One really important thin in a shooter are ofc the weapons and this game has a lot of them. Most weapons are unqiue and there are only a few weapons which feel the same. Adding to the weapon variety are a huge pool of possible weapon mods. Which modify the weapons heavily They can change the elem tn of the weapon, give you bonus damage, bonus crit and so on, or might even add some unique effects, sometimes unique to the weapon.All in all this game is perfect in what it does. The difficulty is nice and it never feels unfair. The RNG is fine you never feel like you get screwed and it has all elements one would expect and wish for in a rogue-lite game

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an FPS that looks like Borderlands and plays like how eating a bag of delicious chips feels. _childDocuments_.review: A Bullet-Storm of Fun and Strategy — Gunfire RebornAfter sinking over 120 hours into Gunfire Reborn, I can confidently say that this game is a hidden gem that perfectly blends frantic action, strategy, and roguelike elements into one unforgettable package.Gunfire Reborn throws you into a vibrant, cel-shaded world where you battle through randomized dungeons packed with enemies and bosses, all while collecting weapons, power-ups, and talents to grow your character's power. It’s fast, addictive, and most importantly, incredibly satisfying.At its core, Gunfire Reborn is a roguelite FPS with a unique twist—it merges sharp gunplay with RPG-style progression. What really sets it apart, though, is how well the game rewards you for mastering both reflexes and strategy. Every run feels like a brand new adventure, with different weapon loadouts, random perks, and builds that force you to adapt on the fly. You never quite know what you’ll get, but you’ll be itching for “just one more run” every time you play.The gunplay itself is buttery smooth. From crossbows to rocket launchers to crazy elemental guns, each weapon has its own personality. Combine this with an array of unlockable heroes, each with their own special abilities and playstyles, and you’ve got a game that never feels repetitive despite the randomized nature of the levels.What kept me coming back for 120+ hours is the sheer amount of variety and replayability. Each run feels like a puzzle to be solved, whether it's choosing the right weapon combination or stacking the right buffs to turn your hero into an unstoppable force. And trust me, few things are as satisfying as completely tearing through waves of enemies with a build that just clicks.The multiplayer mode adds another layer of excitement, allowing you to team up with friends to tackle the chaos together. It’s a blast strategizing with your team and seeing how different hero combinations synergize in action.But don't be fooled by the cute art style—Gunfire Reborn can be as challenging as it is fun. The difficulty scales up as you progress, and every defeat feels like a learning experience that pushes you to try new strategies and think critically about your approach.In short, Gunfire Reborn is a rogue-lite experience that will appeal to anyone who enjoys sharp gunplay, strategic depth, and the thrill of unpredictable challenges. With its fast-paced combat, compelling progression system, and endless replayability, it’s a game that keeps you hooked from the moment you start. After 120 hours, I’m still finding new ways to experience the game, and every run feels as exhilarating as the first.If you’re a fan of action, roguelikes, or shooters, don’t sleep on Gunfire Reborn. It’s a blast—and it’s only getting better with each update.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people call this risk of rain but worse, but I think its pretty good in its own right.Gunfire has a plethora of unique weapons, abilities, upgrades, and enemies that make each run feel dynamic up until the very end. While there are some enemies that are harder to deal with and build crafting can be a bit more inflexible than other roguelikes, the emphasis on team play makes bad situations easier to recover from and allows you to have much more coverage over different enemy types. The maps can be a bit repetitive, as can the music that accompanies them, but the art style is among my favorites, and variety of playstyles keeps me coming back for more. I should also mention, that as an English player, some of the translations aren't very good, and can hinder your understanding of the game, but its not extremely detrimental. I've gotten a good 50 hours out of it so far, and will probably continue to play it for a while. A hesitant recommendation if you're buying for yourself, a moderate one if you're playing with friends. 7.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really had low expectations for this game given it's eerily similar vibe and feature list to Borderlands 3. Was this to be an indie clone? It's not. It's really really not. There are certainly mechanics that are similar to many other games in orthogonal genres, but Gunfire Reborn puts them together in a really cohesive and addicting way.It has the roguelike elements of Dead Cells, the gameplay feel of Borderlands (but better), and the randomization / artifact mechanics of Risk of Rain 2 or (believe or not) Monster Train. I found myself engrossed in the decision making of dynamically choosing weapons based on build ideas, and then proving them out over the course of a run. I find this learning loop to be extremely rewarding.I will point out that by far the strongest element of Gunfire Reborn is the actual gunplay. I can't recall a single game with as tight, responsive, and rewarding single player FPS mechanics as this one.  I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: i echo the words of most others: Replayability of Risk of Rain 2, mechanics of Borderlands, and gameplay of Doom. that isnt an exaggeration. Rogue-lite aspects are finding weapons (which are all creative as hell. for example, wrist mounted tiny dragon that acts like a flamethrower,) upgrades to your core abilities and elemental damage at the end of every arena, and scrolls that buff you and occasionally have downsides. Its a rogue-LITE because there is permanent progression in the from of talents. Stuff like ammo capacity, health/shields, and some special ones like getting a free weapon at the start of each run or the ability to shoot purple walls to unlock secret dungeons.The Borderlands in it comes with the elemental damage mechanic, general gunplay, weapon stats, and the enemy health. There are multiple elements that work with one another for beeg damage (for example, corrosive damage + fire damage = explosion.) all weapons drop with random stats and modifiers, and once you buy the upgrade for it, intrinsic perks (for example, pistols can drop with a 25% chance to instakill on headshot.) Each enemy is unique, and have the health pool of an enemy from BL (hard to explain, but thats what it feels like.) There are bosses at the end of each level which require 4 stages to get through, and in all of its glowy fashion, they die in a lootsplosion.The Doom comes from the arena to arena combat, with a heavy emphasis on staying mobile and dodging whenever you can. A bit unforgiving at times, but wheres the fun in easiness?TLDR; this game is the bastard child of some of the genre respective greats of our time and is incredible. plus, early access, meaning more content!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is surprisingly stable and polished for being a new Early Access title. I'm not even a huge fan of Early Access or rogue-likes, but I wanted to give this a chance because the gameplay loop and graphics looked good. I wasn't disappointed at all. The controls feel tight and the challenge is there. It's definitely meant for you to play through this multiple times to unlock permanent passives to make your next run easier. The closest game to this would be Immortal Redneck which costs about 2 Gunfire Reborns.The graphical style is also nice. Colorful! I love colors and games that just have a drab brown and green palette are boring to look at.My only (very minor) gripe with this is the translations to English. A handful here and there aren't completely clear, but for the most part it's not too bad.I'd easily recommend this to anyone that like first person shooter rogue-likes. It's more polished than more expensive games I've played and it also has online co-op. This came out at a great time for me while I'm waiting for PSO2 to get here.

_childDocuments_.review: My modern day view of this game is that its a casual shooter, do not expect to out-aim your way out of any problem like you might expect in valorant, apex, etc etc. this is because the actual gunplay is this games third priority, the first and second being build making and fun, this is not to say the gunplay is bad mind you! you can very easily run a precision weapon and do wonderful with it, but if aiming isn't your thing there are also alternatives, the most adaptive person in the lobby tends to carry however. now about the build making- YOU NEED TO SINK IN QUITE A FEW HOURS FOR MUCH OF THE BUILD MAKING TO BECOME POSSIBLE, FROM WHAT I UNDERSTAND THIS IS ON PURPOSE. dont be like me and be pushed away by this, if anything it helps you ease into a diverse and well built system of upgrades and mechanics, much like you would expect from binding of isaac, where your average run and its power will be significantly lower if you are not both familiar with your enemies and opening your unlocks I personally love to casually come back to this game every now and again because the movement, while being fairly restricted, is also very sharp and nice feeling, with the ability to instantly turn direction in many cases, you will very likely find some fun playing this game no matter where you come from and i highly recommend trying this game out with a friend or two, or even queuing with randoms, people are really nice!  (old review involving my first hour of gameplay)-- wrote this as a positive, but i mostly have only negative (sortof negative-) things to say about this game, thats because i have high hopes it will be a great game, but i do have a few nit-picks that made me put the game down,namely: not enough input when something devistating is about to attack from behind, such as an enemy spawn, or large source of damage, there are several ways of tackling this, just the idea should be if i dont have any audio, i should still have some awareness and im not just going off of "i knew they would do that", which i didn't. (this complaint is still a very real thing, but it really can be a skill issue at times)another is not enough expression of movement, this i think is a very easy solution, (edit: there are plenty of methods of movement in this game, its just a little too deep into the game, which sucks! i still think it can be done a tad better, but this complaint below is mostly irrelevant, still placed here to show my issues starting vs now at 56 hours) let our dash be upgraded; however the developers see fit or balanced. This could mean make the dashes longer, the cooldowns shorter potentially after doing a particular action (like a headshot, or grabbing a grenade, whatever it is) there are tons of things to do to help that. Next to add more vertical in your mobility, you do not need THAT much vertical movement, just enough to where im not taking the stairs every single time i want to explore a map, the quickest solution would be to allow us to climb up cliffs of walls in a slow motion, to prevent us from abusing it for anything other than fast movement across the entire map,lastly, the abilities feel stiff, and one-way, which isnt a problem per say, but making it so my grenade changes its course on my movement would be a nice addition, i would think (moving forward makes it move further forward, jumping higher, backwards shorter to lob across cover) it would make sense considering you can see your grenade line holding the keybind. (this complaint is still very, real, however now that i have played more, i understand that very *few* characters actually use a grenade in their grenade slot)*ill add to this if i remember to, but those are the large nit picks i had, like i said, im only looking forward to what this game can be

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is sort of like Risk of Rain 2, but full of anthropomorphic furry characters with a variety of fun skills and abilities and played from a first-person perspective.The low poly cel-shaded art style is cutesy and easy on the eyes for extended play. Enemy variety is decent, but not so bloated as to become impossible to follow what is happening at any given moment. Generally, they follow fundamental design choices like so:Bulkier enemies that will try to stomp or charge you will always be large and obvious, whereas long-range options and 'marksmen' sort of opponents will be slender, but excessively tall in comparison to the player in an attempt to signify their purpose and help them stand out from the background. These consistent values, strictly adhered to, in visual language help to elevate the typical cover-dodging firefight game that Gunfire could've been into something greater.While the game, and some aspects in it, can be a little janky, it has only improved over the course of its lifespan; it also performs very well on even some lower end machines.The guns, which is an inadequate word to describe some of the game's weapons (kunai, some kind of bone cannon, just an actual lizard you slap to reload), are varied and fun to use but may take some getting used to. Some are clear favourites for me, namely Hexagon and especially the Wheel Saw; DLC is a factor in the guns that may drop (Hexagon is limited to owners of the Visitors of the Spirit Realm DLC, for example).Physically standing behind cover and peeping enemies is a valid strategy, also including the use of a dash as a roguelike staple feels good despite the game being first-person, and the game firmly encourages and allows players to take it at their own pace outside of immediate danger.Despite my time with the game being primarily singleplayer, I have found the co-op multiplayer runs well and is just as fun. I particularly enjoy the Sun Wukong style character introduced in one of the game's DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after additional 83 hours, deleted few irrelevant things: after updates, the same problems are all present but they are the most prevalent at higher reincarnation difficulties.Currently it is possible to play higher difficulties only due to seasonal gimmick and lone wolf (free buff).But even with all these freebies, random instakills return at reincartion 6-7, where generic enemies deal 80+ damage at the first level.There are still no reasonable hp/shield scaling, so essentially you need to instakill everything from level 1 stage 1 or you will just die. Of course, there are random events in the stages, for example, enemies have additional barriers, enemies don't die for several seconds after their hp reaches 0 and the best one - elite gathering, where you fight a lot of elites at once. So, if you're a tad bit unlucky or not insanely overpowered during said event - you will die, constantly.And from reincarnation 8 or 9, enemies get additional abilities just because. So it becomes impossible to play unless you are ultra lucky and play meta characters.There is an additional game mode - spiritual assault - but it has terrible balancing on steroids. Play for several minutes, start dealing 0 damage to enemies, die. Yay.---------------------------------------------This game is worse than in beta balancing wise due to now having even more terrible enemy designs. On top of that, if you are going to play on nightmare difficulty and above, enemies will get random prefixes (mostly double/combo prefix) "defensive, aggresive, robust, powerful, agile, immortal and etc" which kick everything into highest bullpoop gear ever. Almost invincible run and gun enemies, every other enemy can one shot you provided with "powerful" prefix. It's atrocious and unplayable. And for those who think that borrowed gimmicks are neat then I got bad news for you. This game took the worst from borderlands and risk of rain 2 - tragic elemental system which is only required for health bar minigame "yellow hp bar means I need green damage, blue hp means I need blue damage, red hp - red damage, yay, fun, I almost pooped a little thinking about the excitement". Elemental combos are uninspiring. Enemy manipulation - wow. Mini explosions - wow wow. Stacking dps - (wow)^3.Regarding risk of rain 2 - amazing getting one shot system and barely dodgable homing attacks. Every single stage has same sniper enemy template, which can shoot across the map with quick and insanely homing shots, and 2-3 shot you. And if they get a "powerful" prefix, well then - bye bye run, now you are dead since they can 1 shot. Or you can revive and lose the majority of your gained progression currency.To summarize - God awful balancing and gimmicks. But this game can be fun on lower difficulties.So if you don't mind not going through all the content and not getting all achievements, this game could be just for you. Otherwise, spare your sanity.
