_childDocuments_.review: Bought it this week, played 23 hours already. This game is addicting as hell.The game has some minor downsides, none of them are really deal-breaking though.I will go over these cons first. That way i can ramble on about how great this game is.Cons:- Some deaths can be frustrating- Buying back squad members is a little too drawn out sometimes.- A little more map variety would be nice- The soundtrack is a little bit genericPros:- Big arsenal of weaponry with a lot of interesting and unique weapons- Fleshed out assortment of characters, each having a completely different playstyle- Power ups that have amazing synergy with each other, giving the ability to chain scrolls together for even crazier effects- Very well optimized, runs on basically anything (3 PC's tested so far)- Controls feel smooth as butter and are highly responsive- Weapon inscriptions make every gun you find really interesting and varied- The gunplay, special attacks and random-weapon systems borrow heavily from borderlands, wich is amazing imo- Cell shaded graphics with a highly stylized look- Boss battles feel unique for every boss and feel highly rewarding- No lootboxes, battle passes or any other monetized in-game elements- No mandatory server connection (its p2p multiplayer) - Very transparent dev roadmap with a lot of content still on its way.- Only 16 Euros!I could go on for hours about this game and how great it is. Its hands-down, one of the best Roguelite FPS games on the market right now. if the thought of an awesome binding of isaac and borderlands hybrid ever crossed your mind. Or even just the thought of a fps roguelite with awesome variety. Id recommend picking this one up ASAP!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: After a few hours I recommended this, but now, coming back after nearly 40 hours, I can honestly say this game is an addicting steal at the price.If you enjoy roguelite's, rng guns, first person shooters, or co-op play, you'll enjoy this.The premise is pretty straightforward, you play as 1 of 2 characters (only 1 unlocked at the start) and you progress through 3 different levels, each with multiple stages. You get random drops, in-game skill progressions, soul essence. When you die? You spend soul essence in the skill tree, which is how you level up and hopefully get further the next run. You also often unlock new gear during the game by completing challenges.This game is already worth the price, but it has a *ton* of potential. Current cons? Multiplayer can be occasionally laggy, but most of my hours were online (and overseas) and only 2 of them were rough, lag wise. Content - feels like there should be more, but that honestly feels like holding them to a ridiculous standard with how much is already in here.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty fun "looter shooter" with very minor rogue-lite game play. Every play through is different enough (unless you are like me and play the same like 3 characters) however I feel like most characters have only one good build option, so a lot of your runs are gonna be searching for the same scrolls/ weapons/ and skills options. Still, the enemy variety, modifiers and locals are all nice and with the introduction of seasons offer some refreshing or frustrating mechanics which change things up.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun game especially with 3 others! You really cannot go wrong with this price-tag, its only 10e and its often on sale for even less. It is fairly hard to begin with but it gets easier once you spend some points after each run to get some extra perks. They really do make the game alot easier. Hours of fun for a small price. You have to understand what your buying though, i saw some other guy complaining about no saves during a "run". This person should probably exchange some of his spare chromosomes for a pack of Pokemon cards and understand how to play this game.Its not perfect, but it has a huge potential and is already really fun 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game with a lot of awesome features/characters. The seasons are completely interchangeable and you can swap to your desired one whenever you want. Each season has its own set of extra mechanics you can play with and its SO much fun, honestly super impressed at the creativity and thought put into this game as a whole. Very recommend if you like making overpowered builds and cute characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is outrageously good, and amazingly well polished and fleshed out for such an early access title. By far one of the most fun and hopeful games I've seen. I cannot wait to see what is to come next and I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves Roguelites and the Borderlands 2 style of gunplay and stats.

_childDocuments_.review: After being away from playing the game. The new updates are so good and and the gameplay never fails to get me all hooked up again. This is an early review and I hope by the time the game is released, we'll be getting so much content from the base game and I won't mind supporting the devs for future DLCs. They deserve it!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game to kill some time and relax. Compared to other rogue-lites this one has a unique feel to it with a nice art style. Tons of weapons and strategies you could take and progress feels similar to other games like Rogue Legacy and Dead Cells where a currency is collected in the game for skills after you die but here you can revive once using the currency which also levels your character. I would def recommend if you enjoy rogue-lites at all because this one is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Game in Early Access at time of purchase.I paid ten quid for this game, and have gotten 55 hours at time of writing. After Gearbox mugged me off for £60 by removing a setting from BL3 8 MONTHS after the games release, rendering it unplayable to me, I was recommended this game from someone on the GBX forum. I have several EA games from Humble monthly, but have never knowingly purchased one. Considering the price (£10) when I got it, and after watching a few gameplay videos, I decided to give it a try. A Wise decision.Pros:3 Characters (so far) - With skill trees / Special abilities3 Levels (so far) - Broken into several (4-5ish) mini-maps.Several 'Vaults' within each Level.Main Bosses - Sub Bosses - Unique BossesMany different enemies.Shedload of weapons with unique abilities.Another shedload of Scrolls.Great gameplay (if maybe a little basic), with lots of variety.Each run is different. Graphics fine.Sound fine.Controls fine(ish)Re-playability - Through the roof.Dev's constantly updating (and while not all updates / buffs / nerfs etc will please everyone, that's the EA purpose. Cons.Key mapping needs a serious look at, especially for left handers.Some additional sound sliders required for certain sounds. A couple of bugs (only two in 55 hours), that I have noticed.That's about is for the cons. As a newcomer to this game type, I was initially a little frustrated at the beginning of playing this. I was not aware of the mechanics of a 'Rogue-lite' game. And progress initially seemed slow an arduous. Thankfully, the issue was BNIF (Big Nut In Front) ie, me!And the main advice give on various forums, really is the only sound advice... Keep Playing. Build Your Souls. Level the character.Do not expect to steamroller the first level immediately. Accept that failure is inevitable.So that's my review. For an Early Access game. This thing is top-notch. The devs are active and responsive. The game runs smooth, gun-play is great.It is very More-ish!Updated to July 2022.Plenty of additions. New Maps, Characters, weapons and scrolls. More everything. Truly a labour of love for the developers.Pick this up.ETA --I also bought the DLC without even looking at it. And have not played it yet. The dedication this Dev has shown from the beginning, with Fixes, Content Updates, has elicited a trust I rarely give out.Look at my playtime compared to BL3. Of course they are not really comparable.But I know I got more fun from Gunfire Reborn.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an adventure level-based game featured with FPS, Roguelite and RPG. Players can control heros with various abilities to experience diverse Build gameplay, use randomly dropped weapons to explore random levels. This game can be played by single player, or Co-op up to four.

name: Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher
detailed_description: About the story: In order to explore the mystery of his past, TYRE, the former special forces soldier with a special constitution, came to Yingzhou Isle which was located in the legendary Dragon Triangle area. After being attacked by mysterious creatures, the plane that TYRE took crashed and he lost contact with his companions. He found a lot of traces of human activity on the island that had been believed inaccessible. While exploring the terrible secrets behind anomalies despite unpredictable threats, he gradually unfolds the mysterious origins of an ancient Chinese legend. A breathtaking adventure begins here. Game features: · Splendid but the uncanny game scene When staying in the weird climate and treacherous terrain of Yingzhou Isle, one must be cautious to make every step, because danger may hide in the corner of beautiful scenery - cliff and perilous peak above the sea of clouds, ancient and spectacular ruins, enclosed and sinuous underground mazes ...  · Full of thrilling battles You can use a variety of close-range and long-range firearms and do everything you can to survive the swarm of mercenaries, supernatural creatures, and ancient guardians. To be a precision archer, a bomb madman, or a lonely swordsman? Survive to see the truth. · Dangerous adventure You'll meet a group of unique and charismatic characters, crack the deadly traps along the way and piece together the disturbing truth of the story with rich details. Courage and wisdom can only solve difficult problems, however, the bond between people can heal hearts. About the game: 'Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher' VR version was released in overseas regions on April 17, 2019 and then launched in Europe, North America, Japan, and Asia in succession. With the innovative full free move, excellent atmosphere rendering and rich interactive elements, the game was highly praised by numerous VR players and was nominated as “Best Action and Adventure Game” at the TIGA Games Industry Award 2019. Today, the non-VR version of the game has launched on Steam, with brand new ways of performance and upgraded atmosphere, it is ready for you to pick up the gamepads, feel the perfect touch of weapon guns, experience the mysterious legends that you feel familiar with and explore the mystery of Yingzhou Isle. The hero “TYRE” in this game is voiced (English version) by Doug Cockle, the voice actor of Geralt of Rivia, giving the character a unique husky voice.

_childDocuments_.review: Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher is like walking into your local Gamestop and seeing that single copy of an odd/new release on the console games shelf for 19.99.  When you check out the box it is bizarre and strange so you immediately purchase it because you've got to check out such an oddity and it turns out to be a nice little gem.  I enjoyed my 3+ hours of playtime with such a bizarre title.   The only thing I still cannot wrap my head around is how colorful and attention to detail they provided to the main npcs but yet the environment/baddies are all bland in color and detail (except for the Dragons and final boss).  If that much work had been done to those as well this title would have been quite amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: ...Well it’s… um… it was an… an experience?I’m happily confused, is that a proper description?The last couple of years have certainly introduced a slew of new and inspiring aesthetics from foreign markets, that we know for sure. Some have even grown from the heavy influence of popular games from the west. Now, most of these are battle-royales and uninspired mobile crap young kids use to vacate their parents bank accounts but every once in awhile we get a game like Immortal Legacy. Made with total and UTMOST sincerity and baffling design decisions, taking bits and bobs from many games over the last 8 years to create a bizarre amalgamation of scenarios in an attempt to make it big in the videogame industry.Something Immortal Legacy failed at, tremendously. But it made a fan out of me!The game begins in the backseat of a futuristic aircraft heading to a mysterious island, the main character, only dubbed TYRE, mulls over his tragic and equally mysterious and promptly forgotten-and never-addressed-again past before the metal coffin he was riding in is severed in two and plunges him straight into the world of action set-pieces and MacGuffin hunting!At least for the first half. It’s 2013’s Tomb Raider just without the disturbing amount of Lara Croft abuse porn!Yeah, this game is a master-class of picking up concepts and then throwing them away. Right off the bat we are rescued by a streamer-waifu who then gets kidnapped and we don’t see her much until the very last cutscene of the end of the game, which is the defining trait of everything following it. Our Waifu-Bait running into the fray of very rapey mercenaries and not acknowledging it? You got it! A climbing mechanic that is most certainly a leftover from the PS4 VR port? Absolutely! Sudden body-horror and survival horror elements ripped straight out of Resident Evil 7? Oh it’s the entire second half of the game!I’d hate it if it wasn’t just so charming and sincere!The shooting is A-okay, the weapon juggling is pretty liberal and the combat is by-the-numbers, the boss-fights suck yet the actual budget of the modeling is AAA despite having the length and tone of a mid-00’s eurojank shooter. This is Chinese-Jank, and I LOVE it!I haven’t felt this charmed by a mediocre game in awhile so I’m gonna stop with the hints of whats to come. It’s not a good port by any means and the astoundingly lackluster options and lack of key-bind changing is gonna be a major turn-off but it’s nothing too extreme. But I can’t help but recommend this game when it goes on sale!It’s no surprise that Immortal Legacy failed yet I wish it didn’t! With the burgeoning Chinese videogame market, I hope we get more experiences like this over mobile games and crappy battle-royales! Give her a go! You’ll be confused as all hell!
_childDocuments_.name: Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher

_childDocuments_.review: As i can't compare this version to the vr game, i have to admit, that this game is from the controls very complicated and inappropriate for an action title. The graphics based on the unity engine look really good and run smoothly. But unfortunately the menu lacks the personal adjustments, except for the display resolution, high and low as well as depth of field on/off, everything else adjusts the game automatically. The settings in the menu also are awkward, you can only choose a setting by pressing "wasd" and confirm with ENTER. The action feels tormented slowly, as our main character moves too slowly and can't even jump, the weapon selection is a disaster (Q or E must be held down while moving the mouse inside the inventory on the corresponding weapon - but even this works very slowly!) So i didn't have much fun with this game. Notice, dear Development: A few improvements with a patch could work wondering here.

_childDocuments_.review: The search for immortality is just one reason that brings you to Yingzhou Island, located deep in the Dragon’s Triangle. Playing as ex-special forces soldier Tyre, you’re also here to discover the truth behind your mother’s mysterious death. Finding out how that event and her enigmatic past are tied to the secrets that lie at the heart of the island will see you battle through not only a mercenary army sent in to excavate it, but the horrors they’ve unwittingly set free.

name: Coromon
detailed_description: The sun begins to dawn on Velua, a new day for the world and a new day for you, a freshly minted Battle Researcher of the global research society known as Lux Solis. It’s your first day and everything goes smoothly until a mysterious force attacks your latest workplace. Build up a squad of Coromon, track down the invaders, and grapple with a rising threat that endangers everyone on Velua! True to our commitment to let you play how you want, the latest update brings color customization for Coromon, fruit-to-cake conversion using the brand new Lux Kitchen, and new Cake recipes to make! Coromon is all about taming the eponymous wildlife and challenging the rest of the world: other wildlife, trainers, or titanic bosses! Build a team from more than 100 charming creatures, defined by their elements, traits, and skills. Catch, train then set them loose on your rivals! Master a stamina-based battle system where every action costs energy, so choose skills and attacks carefully. Deal damage, sap enemy stamina with status effects, or nullify them through dozens of conditions to emerge victorious. Challenge friends online and see whose Coromon squads are the best of the best. The first day at Lux Solis is just the first step in a much greater adventure. Soon you’ll be thrust into a story grand in scope and great of importance, as a mysterious, alien threat emerges. It’s up to you to help Lux Solis put a stop to their dastardly designs. Pursue the antagonists’ trail across six major zones and cities, with dozens of interconnecting routes to explore. Each one brimming with quests, secrets, and items to find. Explore the furthest reaches of Velua, from frozen glacial caverns to the depths of blistering deserts. Play a key role throughout a fully-fledged classic JRPG narrative, complete with plot twists, turns, and revelations that not all is as it seems... Coromon empowers you to create an experience just the way you want. Difficulty is more than just stat changes. Each option changes the fundamental mechanics, making the game as challenging as you want. Want a stress-free, chill playthrough? Immerse yourself in the story on the easiest setting without hassle, or focus on tactics, number-crunching, and resource management. Want a more high-stakes challenge? Use the built-in Randomizer and Nuzlocke modes to put fan favorite twists on the creature catching experience. Create the trainer you want, using hundreds of customizable elements like hair, fashion, and more. Customize the look of your Coromon! Prefer a Potent’s color to a Perfect’s? Just set the right element. We're honored to be able to provide Coromon to you, a game we've poured our heart into. Coromon is our tribute to the classics of this RPG sub-genre. While staying loyal to the core gameplay, we wanted to add new features but also keep the iconic retro look, with a modernized pixel art style. Thank you for checking out Coromon. We hope you will enjoy the game as much as we enjoyed creating it!

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Pokemon but better than anything that Gamefreak has been putting out in the recent years.Maybe it's because i'm a Gen 1/Gen 2 boomer, but Coromon really managed to scratch the itch in a way that reminded me of the days i spent on my Gameboy Color as a kid.I have yet to finish the game, but 100% recommend it. The price is more than reasonable, and it's very well polished. Difficulty isn't too high either, but challenging enough that the player will need to properly build their team pretty early on in the game (else some fights can turn out to be quite hard), which i think is a good balance.Overall a good 8/10 monster-taming game, you won't regret it if you like the genre !
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: I have not donated anything to Coromon and I am one of the best Coromon players.I recommend it to other gamers since the visuals are great. The Pokémon, or "coromon," you will encounter and capture each have their own distinct appearance. The animations for each ability are fantastic. Because the finale is so brief, the narrative line may not be all that excellent. There is nothing you can do after the game except capture the perfect or "shiny" coromon and PVP against other players. The coromon potency, or "shiny" system, is one of the greatest because the greater the potency of the coromon, the better the stats. In contrast to Pokemon, even if you receive a shiny, your stats may still be subpar. This is not a pay to win game since you must work for practically everything in this game, such as gold for better quality spinners, potent scents, and perfect coromon. There are no quick cuts for the three factors I stated previously. There is no monetization, but you may make a donation and receive rewards that will help you in the game. However, the advantages will not lead players to become overpowered because all of the rewards obtained by contributing money to Coromon may also be obtained by putting in a lot of time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun and addictive game, reminds me of a game you'd play on a Gameboy, for hours trying to beat. (They kept the save button feature, maybe not the best carry over feature) It does offer autosave but it saves every 20 mins...so make sure to save. Aside from that the story line is not like the game you're thinking of, the idea of catching the coromon is the same, with 3 spins to capture the coromon. However the coromon do not have much of any resemblance to the game you're thinking about right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game that improves on an already proven successful formula and genre!I have been playing since the demo released and watching the growth and development of the game has been absolutely inspiring. The devs are fantastic, have taken all critiques and feedback into consideration and continued to improve the game alongside the community until it's launch. If you enjoy monster taming? I highly suggest giving Coromon a chance. The quality of art and sound is top tier, the level of care and attention to detail in the mechanics and general quality of life is refreshing and the devs have succeeded in making a game that is not only charming but feels good to play. Thanks again team!*EDIT*It's since come to my attention that a few people have had issue with the smaller move/creature pool and increased puzzle elements and I felt I should add my take.It's impossible for a new indie game to come out of the gates competing with something like Pokemon with 20 years of creatures, moves and additions. That's just a fact that needs to be accepted.Also regarding the puzzles? I enjoyed them! It felt more refreshing to me to have some different gameplay aspects instead of the traditional pokemon formula of endless trainers and battles which...really gets repetitive and boring after a while and makes a short route feel like hours of work. In comparison Coromon by breaking up the pacing with puzzles and variety has felt a much more refreshing experience! I barely even noticed the hours I've racked up.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad Pokemon clone tbh but it's not better in any shape or form either. Most of the evolutions are rather uninspired (much like Gen 1 Pokemon with 3 level evolutions), most moves I've gotten were just borderline pointless while others oneshot next to everything. The move pool the Mons learn goes counter to their type and supposed use (stats / skills). The RNG mechanic for potential in Mons is just as awful as the crappy IV Pokemon had. The encounter rate was mind-numbing, it's crazy. Walk two steps, fight, walk another step, fight.I lost interest after some 8 hours I guess and the first Titan defeated. If you're really into Pokemon but played them all to death (especially the really good mods the scene offers) then this might do it for you. But I just don't see anything setting this game apart or making it especially worth your time. It's also just very grindy with no exp share and just a few 25% or 50% exp held items. The difficulty customization people often point to is a neat idea but I personally just prefer a set challenge and not some stupid amount of settings ranging from brain-dead easy to pointless drag.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game but HATE the platformer puzzles. Waaaay to difficult for casual play. On steam deck it plays great. Not a battery killer. Offline is a plus. The puzzles infuriate me because of the controller lag from hell. I'd like yo get through the story but GD!If I had known atform style puzzles qere i  the game, I would not have purchased.The skill system character trees are awesome. No breeding but still fun. Story is better than Pokemon. Building mons is way more up front with lesser grind.For me though, I do not believe I will finish the game because of the mandatory infuriating puzzles that lock me in until finished.

Glad to know they fixed it since it's an addicting game. No issues other than that, but that alone makes me want to scoop out my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: It plays like Pokemon, feels like Pokemon and grindy like Pokemon, but with several interesting gimmicks that differentiate it from Pokemon, so that Nintendo won’t go Death Note on them.  So far I enjoy the game and I can adjust the difficulty anytime I want and I think most of the Coroman I’ve encountered was cool.  Love the sprite work and overall art style being simple and easy one the eyes instead of the need to make it photo-realistic.  There a puzzles and dungeons that require some thinking, so that's great and it also helps that the music isn’t terrible either.  If someone out there has a Pokemon itch that needs to scratch, I recommend buying this game to relief that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game. If you like old school pokemon games, you will probably love this game. At it's core this is a pokemon game, but when it comes to technicalities it's quite different. I also loved the references and subtle humour in disguise. I'm really hoping there will be a sequel. I also experienced a couple of bugs regarding steam achievements but the game itself had no flaws i can think of. Very well balanced and lots of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to offer - but is marred by a memory leak. After 30 minutes or so, FPS will drop. Until they address this, the work around of relaunching every 30 minutes is all you can do. Supposedly the team is working on a mobile launch, fixes are not likely until that is released.The Good: the game is fun. battles are rewarding. Coromon are well designed and even though some far outperform - there is a focus on quality over quantity. There are no Coromon that are absolutely worthless. Game progression is fun, plenty of customization for your character if you care about that. The potential system is neat, adds different color variations. PvP is fun, there is a meta. Fast travel opens up fairly early. Story is good/great if you care about that.The Bad: previously mentioned memory leak, mobile release holding back updates, the potential system makes catching anything that isn't at least "potent" feel bad/pointless, grinding for "Perfect" encounters is a pain.The meh: Some people may be frustrated that their favorite monster is outclassed by another in the meta. The leveling system is fine/source of interesting items/ money. Music/graphics may not be your jam (but then you wouldn't be look at this game if that was the case)
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the best Poke-like I've played. It enjoys it's story and puzzles, has a LOT of pop culture and other references.It's Skill point system makes battles a little more tactical, stat changes matter a LOT in this. _childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a game that seems to be clearly inspired by the old-style Pokemon games. However, I found that it added a lot of its own twists to the concept, along with an entire set of original creatures to collect, and a plot that I found to be both intriguing and entertaining to follow. I really enjoyed the 34 hours I spent running around in this world, and training my team, and I think most fans of Pokemon games will find a certain nostalgia and a lot of fun in playing Coromon!There are a lot of things I love about this game. First of all, many of the Coromon designs are so wonderful; Bittybolt was by far my favorite, though I was a huge fan of many of them, enough that I struggled with who to keep on my team of 6!Secondly, the environments and interaction mechanics were I think on the whole well thought-out, and the world was on the whole enjoyable to explore, finding little crevices and finding hidden items.Thirdly, the customization options I found to be great! Starting with your character customization, including hair color, accessories, etc., but extending to gameplay. At the very start you are able to choose what settings you want to play with, essentially customizing the game to be as easy or as challenging as you care to make it. There is even a randomization section, where you can customize what Coromon appear, how they evolve, and other elements. I really appreciate the inclusion, and would consider using some of these elements in future playthroughs!There was one major issue that I had that I thought worth mentioning as well. I noticed that when I started my play-through on a Mac, I wasn't receiving achievements, and it seems that a recent update caused a bug that caused the game to stop launching on my Mac. Fortunately I was able to pick up the save file on a different computer, but it seems like the experience on Macs is still being fine-tuned; I saw mentions that the launch issues were being patched, in the discussions on Steam, but if you are using a Mac maybe check out to be sure it will work okay for you! Also be aware if you are an achievement hunter that a lot of the achievements may be quite difficult to get, so be prepared to invest some time!Other than that, this game was honestly like a little burst of nostalgia, mixed with the excitement of exploring new things, and as a huge Pokemon fan I really enjoyed it! If it looks like something that's up your alley definitely check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a monster-tamer game heavily inspired by the Pokémon games. Here you’ll catch and raise monsters that will help you in battle throughout a classic RPG story. If Coromon is clearly a work of passion and really tries to improve the formula, it falls a bit short and delivers a very average experience that is at times frustrating and tedious. It is however a game that any fan of the genre should try. If not ground-breaking it is at least a nice experience with stunning visuals and cute monsters. Coromon labels itself as a modern take on the classic monster-taming genre. Is the 2022 title that much of a twist ? let’s find out.  The strength of Coromon probably resides in its amazing pixel art. The game is aesthetically very pleasing, from it’s very simple yet colourful view from above when you move around the map to the very detailed background whenever you enter a fight. The game is full of colours and is downright inspiring itself of all the popular video games aesthetics. But what makes the pixel art that great is that it’s combined to really good animations and makes the whole feels very articulate and organic. This is especially true in regard to the monsters’ animations and their move. However, some of those animations can be a bit long and it can be very frustrating not to be able to skip them in battle. Another weird animation choice was the usage of emojis to convey emotions during dialogues. I can understand the limitations of 2D games, but they were often not working with some serious parts of the story. If the pixel art of the game is quite remarkable, the music on the other hand is a bit “classic” and nothing seems particularly ground-breaking. Indeed, many times in the games I would feel like the music was trying very hard to be as close as possible to their main inspiration, namely Pokémon. Sadly, throughout the game nothing seemed particularly memorable to me. That doesn’t mean that none of them were good, far from it, but they won’t come to mind if I have to think about great video game music whereas many Pokémon tracks would pop in my mind. _childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews very often so this'll probably be all over the place. Had a lot of fun with this. I liked being able to basically make any team that I wanted and cruise on through. The story is passable but I didn't buy the game for the story. Bought it for the beautiful sprite work and gosh is it a sight to behold. The animated sprites are absolutely gorgeous to look at. The music is okay, inoffensive at best, at least to me. The variety of mons was nice. I found myself catching many things I wasn't initially interested in just to see what they would evolve into which is how I found one of my favorite lines; Moffel. Didn't care for that little guy but once he evolved into Digmow, it was over. Dugterra is also fantastic. Another monster that was worth the wait and trouble, Mino. Completely useless to me when it was a little thing but when it evolved, was a mainstay. Completely decimated just about everything, especially with the ability to raise it's attack and speed after every monster defeated. Criminal. Love that guy. Small but I enjoyed that you could change the spinner it was caught in. I liked having my fire types in fire spinners, etc. Another thing is being able to raise the potential of a monster to basically make them shiny, higher stats and all. Can only do it once per monster but it's pretty cool all things considered. Only found the scripted perfect ones out in the wild but was still pretty cool to have my normal little ones turned into potent just with luck. Also there's exp share items which is GREAT when you want to add a new addition to your team that is not on the same level. Or one that hasn't evolved yet and is becoming obsolete (Looking at you Mino).Battles were fun albeit easy(except for one, my favorite actually). Boss battles were more on the tedious side but not too hard. I think they would be the only real complaint I do have for this game. The final boss was especially annoying in this regard. Ginger my Toravolt absolutely carried me through that battle. Speaking of my favorite battle actually takes place towards the end of the game. You go back to the main campus and are forced to fight The game has a few difficulty options, even allowing to play as a nuzlock which is pretty cool in itself. I may return to play it on a higher difficulty but I enjoyed just how casual it is. I've never really been good at min/maxing out at team. I just like to hit a button and watch the health bar drop to zero. This gave me that.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a game I can't help but enthusiastically want to throw at everyone I can. As someone whose happiest, most memorable experiences with a certain other franchise (the name of which we shall leave out of this review, but you know it) were during its third, fourth, and fifth iterations, this is a game that hits all of those sweet spots that other imitations and even that series itself have failed to deliver on.Exploring a new world, finding new and interesting creatures at every turn, with gameplay that's quick and snappy and just the way I like it in a game like this. It's something I've been craving from a game for years and years that I thought I wouldn't be able to experience again without picking up old games in that other franchise.If you, like me, have been hankering for a monster collecting game that scratches that itch that the "real" ones just haven't been able to, you might find exactly what you've been hoping for in Coromon. This is a game made with a lot of love, FOR people who have a lot of love for monster collecting games, and every new turn has been a blast. Between just the demo and only an hour or so of the full game alone, I've been having more fun with this game than other games like it have provided in a long time, and I can't wait to dive back in and experience more of it. Heck, I'll probably come back to update this and make a more detailed review once I'm done with the game proper-- and when it's not launch day and I'm not in a hurry to get back to playing!Not so long story short, I emphatically recommend this game. I can't say it's for everyone, necessarily, but if you're looking for a game about exploring and catching and taming monsters, Coromon should be at the top of your list - yes, even above that other one.Also I really really want a big, squishy Sheartooth plushie. TRAGsoft and Freedom Games, please make it happen, yeah?-----------------Playing the game some more, having already posted this, I want to make note of some things that I think folks might appreciate knowing about in particular:- The sound design of the game is a treat. The sound effects of all the moves have impact to them and add a lot to the battles, and the soundtrack is just awesome- you get new tracks where you might not expect, and they're all great.- Arenas are all unique based on where you are, and it gives battles a real visual flair here that helps you feel more "in" the world during combat.

For some people that's worth it, but for me, this game was boring and went nowhere fast.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only steam game I've ever played that is compatible with my surface's touchscreen. wtfThe controls can be janky (i'm never going to get used to enter being exist and space being accept) and there's no way to change them.The last time I played coromon was about a year ago on the free mobile version, and this is better in basically every way. Granted, I haven't gotten far into the story lolThe only real problem I have is that I have gotten lost more than a handful of times trying to fulfill side quests. They include resources in-game to tell you what's strong or weak against what, they have pretty extensive explanations on certain mechanics, and you can reference them at any time. It's massively helpful.They also have an option for custom difficulty settings. I personally have it set so coromon restore all hp and sp on level up and i can revive them with any healing item, solely because I have trouble keeping track of how many healing items i need lol. These settings are all available during customisation, too, so you can make it as hard or as easy as you want.It IS a pokemonlike game. If you don't like pokemon, you won't like coromon either.(I wouldn't go so far as to say it's a 1-to-1 ripoff of pokemon, like some others have claimed. it does have its own distinct vibes, and i'm not going to go to pokemon for coromon, nor coromon for pokemon. they ARE distinct.)oh yeah also i love the character customisation and i love how most other characters in the game seem to have been made using this customisation system its so funny.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Does what Gamefreak don‘t, 'nuf said. Possibly the best Pokemon clone I've ever had the pleasure of playing up to now, while still bringing enough fresh design elements to the table to firmly stand on its own. Without further ado: if you consider yourself a Pokemon fan from the first hour even slightly, this is a must. You will most likely kick yourself in the arse later on for not buying this game, seriously. Don't get turned off by the overall youthful look and presentation. I feel like this game tries way less to have kids and teenagers be its main target group than Pokemon. It feels more fleshed out and isn't afraid of relying on the player using his brains, which is great.I want to give a big shout out to the BGM designer(s) also. The soundtrack is often reminiscent of Final Fantasy games (8 and 9 in particular) and I'm awestruck how well crafted those songs are, considering their shortness. I don't know why the devs didn't invest more in the soundtrack people, it would most certainly have paid off. As it stands now, it sometimes feels as though the composer(s) felt like they had to wrap things up, because the devs gave them a loop time of 60sec max to work with, which is a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: "What if Nintendo made a pokemon game where they implemented frequently  requested features from the community?"I was expecting a scuffed pokemon experience but what I got was a better pokemon experience than Nintendo has ever given us. This is very much gen 3/4 pokemon taken to a modern stage.The developers are clearly passionate about Coromon, there's no mistaking they wanted to make the best monster collector game they could make. Proven by even post-release updates that keeps improving the game.The game supports PvP, has only 1 version so all Coromons are obtainable for you, and it has its own spin on mechanics and storyline (no gyms, boss battles).Also supports multiple modes we had to mod pokemon games for. Such as Nuzlocke and Randomizer features. AND you can change the rules for your game at any point by going back to the computer where you set your rules.And personally I really like the mono-type on mons. In Pokémon past gen1 it felt like the further we went the more obligatory it was for all mons to be two types (even adding types to previous mono-type pokemons in later gens).Coromon is an excellent high quality game for 1/4th the price of a pokemon game but x4 the quality.

All of the elements that made Pokemon fun are here, with perhaps some different "spices" here and there that does make Coromon it's own thing. I'd give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is the Dark Souls of Pokemon games.Difficulty modes? Built in randomizer? Custom stats? Attractive visuals? It's like an alternate timeline where Pokemon spent the past 25 years improving their video games.It really makes me happy to see a new generation of game developers whose entire motivation boils down to "you ruined my favorite game, so I'm going to make my own version."I really love this game. I think it's just about the best Pokemon clone (which I absolutely do not mean as a derogatory description, there is nothing wrong with more pokemon games and Coromon wears its pokemon inspiration on its sleeve) that I've played. It’s been a long time since a game made me giddy the same way I was when I got Red version on the Gameboy but Coromon got me.  The last Pokémon games felt like a step back.  This game feels like the earlier gen games but with huge QoL updates.The Coromon roster is so good! Definitely felt like quality over quantity. So much variety in designs and I never felt like I found a Coromon that was just straight up outclassed by another one. Even in single player, creating a team is so strategic and rewarding because every Coromon has a role on a team. Balance is nearly perfect. Trainer battles remained challenging throughout the game. Even with some light XP grinding I never felt overleveled for an area. Bosses were REALLY fun, too. Challenging and formidable. Even had to retry a couple times for the 2nd boss. Strategy is also much more important than Coromon levels, which feels really rewarding.Writing is cute and fun. Very charming. The stakes of the story were compelling, which is refreshing in this genre. The art and animations are equally amazing. Not just the talent but the nostalgic feelings they evoke. This really felt like an upscaled GBA game, and the Coromon have insane personality in their movements and body language, and everything is designed very clearly. It is a delight to look at.I feel like the one thing Coromon does a lot better than recent Pokémon games is have distinct environments and towns. The level design is consistently engaging, which is really impressive for this genre. The puzzles are compelling without being frustrating and every "dungeon" feels distinct. It's refreshing and a nice change from the Pokémon games while still retaining the essence of it. There's a lot of customization to make your play through fit your style or more challenging (there's even an in-game nuzlocke set of rules).Honestly I had a blast and can only encourage anyone that’s a fan of these types of games to try it out. For the price it’s absolutely worth it. It's one of very, very few pokemon-likes that actually captures the sense of adventure and discovery of early pokemon games and even improves on it, rather than just blindly copying them and hoping for the best.And now that the new update is out (including a new ending storyline) I’m actually excited to get off work and play some more. I’ve been so burnt out on gaming in general but this I’m loving.So happy to see Pokemon fans have grown up now to create more games for this genre. What a time to be alive!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a pokemon-esque creature catching, turn-based RPG. Overall, I would reccommend this game whole-heartedly. It has some minor flaws, but is a really fun and challenging experience. Graphics: Coromon is done in a beautiful pixel artstyle. All the creature sprites are well done and the world/background art looks great as well. If you miss how some of the older GBA/DS Pokemon games looked, you will love the look of this game.Creatures: Overall, I think the vast majority of the creatures have great designs and are animated well. Some of their names are mediocre, but still a good roster for a creature catching game. The only major complaint I have is that there is not a lot of creatures in the game. I really hope this game gets a larger rooster though updates or dlc, cause why not have more of a good thing? Other than that, I feel some tweaks to a few creature's movesets would be nice. A few coromon I have encountered have had such poor movepools that it makes it a struggle to use them despite their stats being great. Other than that, I'm quite satisfied with the creatures in this game. The Devs clearly a quality focused approached Difficulty: One thing many will notice is that Coromon has very customizable difficulty. The game can be as hard or easy as you want it to be. Even playing on normal difficulty can be challenging at times, so this game does not struggle with being too easy like some recent pokemon games.Length: This game seems to be a good length for its price. As of writing this I am 23 hours in and about halfish way through. Although keep in mind that I'm the completionist type who likes to explore and do side-content, so that increases my playtime. Summary: Coromon is beautiful pokemon-esque game with a small but high-quality rooster that has done a great job at keeping my attention and hitting that GBA/DS era nostalgia. If you like this type of game, I highly recommend giving it a shot!

Also, the patch introduced a new plot that retroactively affected my save file, introducing a load of high-stakes stuff that I had no context for. It's not quite enough for me to change my recommendation, but it means I'm less likely to suggest it to friends, and I don't know if I'll continue the post-game adventure or start a new save.Also, the new crystal currancy and the daily missions were really unnecessary.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice to finally have a good Pokemon game again. This is without question trying to emulate older Pokemon games with some tweaks here and there, a few highlights for me:Built in difficulty system which includes Nuzlocke option. Should be noted I've only played on what the game calls "insane" difficulty which is the Nuzlocke mode, so many game features are disabled for me.No HMs, instead you, the player, slowly gain upgrades and abilities which serve the purpose of HMs, thereby allowing you to use whatever Coromon you want.SP system, similar to Temtem here except it doesn't allow the AI to kill itself with poor SP management. If you don't know, instead of individual moves having a limit on use, the Coromon has a SP guage which must be spent to use moves. You can rest instead of attacking to recharge it, and various moves can reduce, replenish or increase the cost of SP adding a new layer to strategy.Modified shiny system. There are two colour variations beyond the standard and they represent the Coromon's potential. With the colour variations only happening for Coromon with very high or Perfect potential.Otherwise this really feels like Gen 3-5 pokemon, but I can enforce Nuzlocke rules, which for me at least was a game winner right there.A final note for the Nuzlockers out there, the game makes one excellent change to Nuzlocking, it limits your catches by giving you an item which summons a Coromon from the area you are in when used. You can be anywhere and it will summon from every encounter table on the current map. This means you can spend some time training and learning the local Coromon before you decide to get your encounter, allowing you to prepare a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Mmm, this is good. The newer Pokémon games have lost a lot of their charm imo and this game manages to reclaim a lot of that original magic whilst having its own style that elevates it beyond being just a Pokémon clone. There's some nice QOL that the newer Pokémon games could learn from and some really fun ideas, like the coupons for the shop to encourage you to make one big purchase of supplies and the teleporter to instantly fast travel to places you've already been. The game is a bit more challenging than regular Pokémon too, so those supplies are going to be necessary. No breezing through without any heals here. But what really nails it for me is the choice of monsters. I actually found it hard to choose who to put in my party cos all the options are good. There's no obvious trash mons that you're never gonna touch (looking at you, Dunsparce). I feel like I could make multiple viable parties out of the ones I've caught so far and it's really hard to choose who to drop when you want to bring in a new mon to try out. There's also a smattering of puns and references which always appeal to me too, giving this more humour than the competition. I can't wait to get deeper in. It's definitely worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll edit this review as I play.Looks great, plays great, not fan of the palette but it's clear this has been made by absolute fans of Pokémon strategy, and I could feel early on that combats might eventually become quite interesting.However, a couple negatives :- Keyboard controls are awkward at first, but the WASD layout is all right, allowing to play with one hand. Still, for such game, the absence of customizable layout is weird.- Menu navigation could be better.Most notably when you wanna switch mons, the game pops another window showing the full party, while it's already on displayed in the pause menu.Pressing down at the bottom of a list (and contrary) won't bring back to the first option, so when you want to save, you gotta scroll through everything.In menus like appearance editor, when you hold right from the rightmost option of a window, you get moved to the next window rather than on the lower left of the same window.This sounds like nothing, but these added together make menu feel more awkward than they could be.- Goal-oriented aspect early on.Some mechanics feel like urging me to complete something rather than just doing whatever I want. I'm mainly talking about the loads of milestones and rare Potent mons that I met early on, making me go "Gotta do this now, catch that now, do these quests, check my rewards, etc".Pokémon is a lot chiller on this aspect, with its very broad main goals : progress to the next area, capture all pokémon. Since these come naturally and there's no time constraint, Pokémon allows to do whatever you like without any pressure, and you only take on quests if you want to.I can choose to ignore Coromon's milestones and Potential, but these still put pressure on me for doing things rather than enjoying myself.Being able to choose the "EVs" is very interesting competitively, but I obviously invested everything into ATK from start to help oneshotting stuff.The SP regen after a fight is a real bummer. In Pokémon, even with a oneshot attack, you can only wonder whether you'll get out of a cave before running out of PP/items.In Thunderous Cave, I had mons with 6 to 10 levels above the wildlife, EV-maxed in attack, so regardless how long I'd spend there, I'd mostly oneshot anything, replenish more SP than I spent and get xp on top of that.There're enemies that deal status on contact, excepted the game also gave me an item to counter that very early.Rather early, there are tools to precisely lower enemy hp.Cubzero (ice starter) learns Splash at level 20, which is basically a budget False Swipe, very good to precisely lower enemy hp.In the worst case, the battlepass thing gives Kiwano Rock on tier 8 that reflects 15% dmg, which is also a potent capture tool.It's nice to get those early, but I might've prefered to get these later on, making me really crave for tools to accurately weaken foes, which would be really satisfying once I get them.Shop coupons are a fun addition, but pressured me into playing as greedy as possible to get absurd discounts. Since coupons are ultimately money pouches, I think capping the limit of refunds wouldn't be a bad idea.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is very obviously a Pokemon clone, and in some regards (for e.g. soundtrack, world size, no. of monsters, etc.), a clearly lower budget clone. However, the game is very, very charming (something newer Pokemon games have stopped being), and it is super successful in satisfying that Pokemon itch. The starters are cute, and most Coromon evolve into pretty cool looking monsters.The game introduces its own unique mechanics into the familiar turn based system, all of which work together well, but with some experience it's easy to see the way to easily exploit mechanics. The game also attempts to place more meaning on the 'shiny' mechanic, but honestly you can ignore it for the most part in a casual run through. The game also allows the player to customise the difficulty in a number of ways to have a really catered playthrough, which is really cool of the devs.The best parts of the game for me would be the 'dungeons' that culminate in 'boss-fights', analogous to the 'gym' and 'gym-leader' setup in Pokemon. In this game though, the dungeons can be pretty serious sometimes, and combined with the simultaneous exploration and puzzle-solving, it really did make me nostalgic for the first Pokemon games I played. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Its fine so far. Very obviously inspired by pokemon, has many of the same beats (especially in the beginning). The story however, is terrible. Instead of letting you explore the world and competing in some kind of battle system...it is a story with multiple dimensions, macguffin stones, and other junk. The XP boosters make it way too easy, if you just take a couple minutes to do some training, also incentivizes you to just use one coromon to do all the work, while the others just sit back and gain XP...pretty cheap.  The worst part is how slow it plays. You HAVE to sit through all the cut scenes, and dialogue. There isn't a fast skip option (i haven't checked the settings, but it should be standard).  There is no summary on the moves you are using so you have to memorize what each does, which is just annoying.  I just wish it was a bit more open, with more things to explore that don't have anything to do with the main story.  It's just very straightforward, go there, do the thing, go to the next thing, and do the thing....it literally won't let you proceed to areas with high level enemies....it has someone stop you or a barrier in the way that can only be taken down by the thing you need to get next...and I know pokemon had some of that, but it felt more expansive than this ever will.  I still find that most of the moves are useless, some don't even seem to be necessary...ever....just worthless all around. Like a move that charges up your next move for double damage....however, it costs 3 SP, and using my fire skill costs 4...so I'll save 1 SP, and open myself up to being hit...if I don't kill the enemy with the first hit. There is no real way to know how much damage you will do...because no stats are available in match...strange choice.  IDK, its fine, don't spend much and don't expect alot.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a monster taming game, it means that the whole purpose of the game is to catch monsters and make them battle each other against other tamers, while progressing in a story. The gameplay feels really close to Pokemon while bringing new mechanics, like the modules that you can get for your gauntlet. There are 114 Coromons to catch, that and their shiny forms. Let's talk about the shiny system, there are 3 versions of a Coromon, standard, potent and perfect. You get the idea, the more potent a coromon is or close to it's perfect form, the stronger it becomes. The game also makes the hunt for shinys really fun and easier than in Pokemon, which is a good thing. I'd say that one downside is that the story is brought rapidly to conclusion, but it makes up for it in replayability.With all that said, I can definitly recommend the game in it's current state. Bugs are rare or literally inexistant and each Coromon is unique in it's own way. I haven't really touched PvP, but I assume that a 3v3 match system is really inovative.

_childDocuments_.review: A time waster. The game is full of padding and obstacles designed to slow you and your progress down. Any time I start to enjoy the game I get hit by another annoyance. I am the 1 percent of players that has the level 99 Coromon. The only ppl who beat this game were streamers. Just look at the global acheivements. I think I have 8-10 gold acheivements. Only 57 percent of ppl have collected the starter Coromon. Only 37 percent have Evolved a coromon. The percentages keep dwindling below 25 from here on out. Its really sad.The game is boring until you reach the forest with the mushrooms that you pick up. They're Coromon finally drop decent experience points that make grinding and team building finally feel worth it.  This game has Layering issues with its plants, mushrooms, fire, desert, and perfumes. Even some of the ice tiles do not line up correctly or match adjacent tiles. if your a gamer You might not notice. But anyone that develops game can see it.The desert part looks nice but slows the game to a crawl. There is not enough Coromon to keep the desert interesting. It is really noticeable in the pyramid area. The digging portion of the game is just bad padding. The spooky area has some visual cool stuff but drags game play to a crawl. The puzzle is annoying filler. The Purgil afterlife section is boring and pointless. Some of the Coromon are beautifully animated and look well though out but others are mid or just lacking all around. Some have still frame animations but it just barely moves left to right like a wave. Its an odd contrast. This game doesn't have as much content as pokemon and it feels like a project cut short. Theres about 100 cormon and 20 recolor/variants. Then theres 120  special recolors and 120 Perfect Coromon. There are better fan games and even better monster designs on Deviant art. This game is 50 percent a waste, 30 percent meh and 20 percent good. This game did everything possible to not get sued by game freak. But it barely devolops its own identity. This game feels like boot leg Fire Red.Catching Coromon is a chore. It is so easy to kill low levels. Even if you have 2 cormon fight each other with similar levels. Its like bashings rocks together. You use Slam to deal 20ish damage. Then your opponent charges up and deal double damage. Then triple damage. Just use a cormon that has the opposite element of what you want to catch. Other wise use the heart stone. I really don't want to eat fruits or cakes every 2 minutes when a Coromon has a status affect. Like I just ignore them. I have never had a Coromon fall asleep, Nor have I been able to put one to sleep. There is a sleep spinner So I assume that sleeping Coromon are in the game but maybe they forgot about that mechanic. Coromon only get drowsy. The purchasable skins look like dumb color washes. Like Blue swurmy, Pink Swurmy. 90 percent are trash. Can we stop daily logins and weekly logins. It sucks and its dumb. I want to play a game cuz its fun and rewarding. Not because I will miss out on content if I don't religously play every in my library. The bad out way what little good this game has. Look I caught a shiny, to bad its not a Perfect Coromon. I have only caught 1 (Perfect) cormon so far. So good luck wasting your youth trying to catch them all. I really wish that someone would make Monster rancher 4 but better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very mediocre. I really have no strong feelings about it one way or the other. It does everything fine but nothing good. The story is meh and very obviously rushed at the end. The gameplay is fine but very quickly gets dull because of the lack of diverse types and dual type mons. The designs are very feast or famine. I found myself loving some monsters and absolutely despising others(also for some reason some monsters are absolutely dummy thicc, Skelatops im looking at you). The bosses are extremely tedious. They have powerful moves and ludicrously high hp. I played on easy from the second boss onwards because beating it would have required massive amounts of grinding or a lot of revives. Even if you have a type advantage these bosses often take over 10 minutes to take down, with basically no changes in gameplay. Just use your strongest move and poison them if you can.  If you are really starved for Pokemon-like games then go ahead, but after my first playthrough i have absolutely no desire to play this game a second time and I played Nexomon Extinction like 10 times. Also the dialog is cringe and long and there are large sections of the game where you do no battling and instead do something completely unrelated like a tedious minigame or long story portion.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for those classic monster collector and trainer vibes, this might be just what you're looking for. It is for me.The mechanics are familiar yet different enough to where it has it's own feel to it. The typings aren't too hard to figure out after battling with them. I like how some typings are specific to moves and not the Coromon themselves, such as cutting, heavy, magic, and so on. They don't use power points specific to the moves, but the Coromon's overall stamina where different moves require more and you can spend a turn to rest and regain stamina.The Coromon themselves have great design. I love the potency mechanic of the game. Instead of shinies, there's 3 tiers on a 1-21 number scale. 1-16 I believe are normal, giving normal coloration and stats based on the rank, 17-20 are potent with a new coloration and stats based, and 21 is perfect with a unique coloration and best stats. It does make it to where I prefer partying only potent or higher Coromon, but for a singleplayer runthrough it shouldn't really matter.The character customization is definitely better than the older Pokemon, but it could still use a little more. It took a little getting used to not being a silent protagonist, but it's not a big deal. Once I accepted that I respond to people with text I began to really pay more attention to the world and story, which so far is really unique and fun to what most monster trainer games have.It has difficulty settings from everything to healing after each fight to once a Coromon faints, it's released. Things like shop discounts for supplies are options too so you can make the game as relaxed or as challenging as you like. I went for the default experience to get a feel for what they want the average player to experience, which is a nice middle ground. I'll have Coromon faint and sweep depending on the matchups, and I like that they'll throw some tough fights at you now and then.All in all, I recommend giving it a try if you're a fan of the genre. Not all Coromon are out, some evolution trees aren't complete so you can't finish evolving everything you catch, but I can't wait to see when they have their dex finished. 4/5, but could easily be a 5/5 once all the planned features and Coromon are completed.#TeamBabyShark

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)After 623 hours, I can confidently say Coromon has so much to offer that it’s hard to put down. With a deep turn-based combat system, unique creature designs, and a story that’s both nostalgic and refreshing, Coromon is a gem for any monster-catching fan. Here’s why I’ve spent so many hours in this world:Coromon is a true treat for fans of strategy and classic RPGs. Every encounter requires thought, as you’re not just mindlessly grinding; each battle is a test of skill and tactics. With unique skill trees, abilities, and elemental interactions, the game keeps you on your toes. This depth makes battles feel rewarding, and even after hundreds of hours, there's always room to experiment with new strategies.Highlights:Skill Customization: The ability to build your Coromon with unique skills and traits adds incredible depth.Challenging Encounters: Every battle requires strategy, from elemental advantages to tactical move timing.The creature designs in Coromon are a perfect blend of nostalgia and originality. Each Coromon feels unique, with well-designed evolutions and backstories that make them more than just stats on a screen. There’s a wide variety, ensuring that finding, catching, and training them never feels stale. Some have become true “companions” on my journey, and the thrill of encountering new ones remains strong, even after so many hours.Highlights:Distinct Designs: Coromon has its own unique aesthetic, with designs that stand out.Varied Evolutions: Evolving your Coromon is both satisfying and full of surprises.The world of Coromon is vibrant and filled with character, from lush forests to mysterious caves. The story is an engaging blend of adventure, mystery, and humor, with unexpected twists that keep you invested. It feels familiar, but there’s a layer of modern storytelling that makes it feel fresh and immersive. Plus, exploring every corner to find hidden Coromon and rare items is a joy in itself.Highlights:Rich Environments: Each area is carefully crafted and full of surprises.Engaging Plot: The story strikes a great balance of humor and mystery, with plenty of lore.Once you complete the main story, Coromon offers plenty of endgame content, from battles and tournaments to finding rare and legendary creatures. The game’s constant updates keep the experience fresh and add extra challenges, making the journey truly endless. There’s always something new to do or discover, which is a massive bonus for completionists and dedicated trainers alike.Highlights:Continuous Updates: Keeps the game interesting with new features and events.Challenging Endgame: Offers depth for long-time players looking for new experiences.Coromon perfectly balances classic monster-taming with new mechanics that add depth, strategy, and replayability. After 623 hours, I can say it’s a game worth every second. The attention to detail, engaging battles, and unique creatures make it stand out, and it’s clear the developers have crafted it with love. If you’re looking for a game that blends nostalgia with fresh, strategic gameplay, Coromon is a fantastic choice.

_childDocuments_.review: After a few play sessions i have to say i like this game.  You can really tell it's had a lot of love put into it by the devs.  they set out to make something familiar, but also a bit prettier, and they absolutely succeeded. Would have killed for this in pokemon emerald lol...  You can set it up so your team members heal each time they level up, lessening about a thousand trips to the healing center per play through.  you can even allow players to steal other trainers team members right in the middle of a battle. _childDocuments_.review: Coromon peaked my interest when searching for a Pokemon-like game that wasn't Pokemon. I wanted to find a game that had the same appeal and charm as the Gameboy Advance/early DS era of Pokemon, combined with building a team of 6 creatures to battle with in turn based combat, and thankfully, this game is just about everything I had hoped for. Coromon takes the tried and true formula of "creature collector" games and tweaks it just enough for it to feel like a fresh new adventure. From new creatures and methods of capturing them via "spinners," to boss battles that are in place of gym leaders from Pokemon, to the unique biomes and characters around this new world to discover; Coromon takes nearly everything enjoyable about this genre of games and elevates them enough to make it just as entertaining as many AAA titles.One of the biggest plus' this game has is the ability to customize your experience however you like. There are a multitude of ways to play, such as making the game incredibly hard and tedious for yourself, or making it easy enough to feel like you're just going through the motions to get to the story. In addition to the four difficulties to choose from, you can also change things to give yourself a more grueling challenge, such as randomizing items, evolutions, trainer Coromon, etc., or giving yourself a Nuzlocke-esque challenge by disabling running from battles, limiting items you can use in battle, or different variations of restrictions on catching Coromon in your playthough. The customization in this game is far and away some of the best in the genre for tailoring your experience exactly how you would like to play.Another impressive feature is the creature designs and traits. There are a multitude of fantastic looking Coromon, all with unique combinations of attacks to use and animation similar to that of Pokemon Black/White. All Coromon have 3 levels of strength called "Potential" that will determine how strong they get upon leveling up. Any Coromon 1-16 is Standard, 17-20 is Potent and 21 is Perfect. There are only specific ways to encounter Perfect Coromon, which provides an extra challenge not only for finding them but also for capturing them as they have a lesser capture rate. The reward is definitely worth the effort, as Perfect Cormon add extra bonus stats for every level up, making them significantly stronger than Standard Coromon of the same level.All is not perfect with Coromon, however, as I did think the story lacked a bit of refining. There easily could have been more expansion on certain elements that would have made the story feel fully fleshed out. The ending of said story also felt too abrupt, not offering much to chew on after the final climax, and the post game content isn't much to ride home for. You do get some new challenges, but any hope of rematching the Titans, getting more insight on the aliens, or seeing how things have changed after the finale are all but missing from the game.Coromon is a fun alternative for those looking for a creature collecting game that brings the same feel as the older games in the Pokemon franchise and need a bit more to chew on in the genre. The terrific sprites and art style paired with an interesting premise and unique world to explore make this a game worth playing. Replayability can be hit or miss, as there are a vast array of customization options to feel like a new playthrough is enough to differentiate from a normal playthrough. However, once you have gotten to the end of the story, you may be feeling left a bit unsatisfied by a lackluster conclusion after your epic journey. I believe if a DLC were to come out to expand on those elements, it could greatly improve the experience, and give players a more satisfying conclusion.As the game is by itself right now, I would give this a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it called Coromon because the magazine that frequently leaks Pokémon news is called CoroCoro?Pretty damn good Pokémon clone, all things considered. Hell, it does a lot of things better than Pokémon. It's well-balanced, the potential system is so much more fun than shiny hunting, the spritework and animations are phenomenal, repels are timer-based instead of step-based, you can change moves around on the fly, devolve your Coromon, change their color palettes, increase the battle speed, increase the overworld speed, change the type of spinner your Coromon was caught in, *DEEP BREATH* there are no HMs, no catchable legendaries, no intrusive gimmicks, and the story is...okay, well, it isn't that different from any other Pokémon game.It doesn't need a phenomenal story, but the writing did take a noticeable "meme-y" dip in quality once you hit the desert town, but it thankfully picks back up afterwards. At least there weren't gyms in this one.I vastly preferred the big boss fights you had at the end of each area, those were far more challenging. Actually, this whole game was more challenging than any Pokémon game I've ever played (if we're not counting Johto's insane level curves).As far as negatives go, I missed Grass Types more than I expected I would. Those usually have a lot of fun designs and that was just absent from Coromon. There's no dual-typing, which means most designs don't stray too far from their gimmick. And while there are quite a few solid designs in the game, I noticed there were a surprising amount of...slime-inspired Coromon? Every type except Normal and Ice has at least one, with a couple having two. I mean, none of them are BAD, but I just found it a little weird that there were so many lmaoAnyway this game is pretty fun. If the Pokémon formula has gotten stale but you are still itching to play a monster tamer, give Coromon a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A lighthearted Pokemon clone with a splash of Golden Sun. The gameplay is fundamentally Pokemon with a few tweaks and QoLs and a fun shiny/IV system. The monster designs lean toward the "cool" side rather than cute, with earthier, dark color palettes. There are a bunch of novel moves and abilities, but the elemental type system is unfortunately a bit more simplified than Pokemon's 18 type system however. Also the monster count is about 110, which might leave collectors hungry for more.The plot/writing is whimsical and adventurous, it is structured like a traditional jrpg where you travel the world and help various people with their problems while collecting what you need. The spritework is gorgeous and detailed and definitely the strongest aspect of the game. Despite the strong art, I think the attack sound effects are a bit weak.Difficulty is well balanced, a tad harder than a basic Pokemon campaign on normal mode. But there are lots of custom difficulties modifiers and options to crank up the difficulty as you please. Very well polished, meaty JRPG with a fair bit of replay value. Postgame is currently lacking but apparently free DLC is on the way. Great fun for monster collectors and team builders.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little Pokemon alternative with some extra sprinkles thrown in.Unfortunately, it suffers from a lot of the same problems as others in the genre, such as all of the moment to moment interactions being much too slow with no real way to speed them up (Menu navigation is a pain), and the game being monstrously too easy if you just stick to using one creature.The whole "Oh no, this super powered monster is going to beat the crap out of us!" followed immediately by defeating said monster in one or two attacks while taking negligible damage got old literal decades ago, as did spamming one of two high damage moves depending on the typing of your enemy - Granted, this is more a problem of the genre than of this game specifically.The ability to alter the difficulty in such a specific way is nice, but making it harder doesn't change how the aforementioned strategy plays out, in fact it only really makes it even more optimal, thus urging you to do it.Better written than any Pokemon game I can think of, though that isn't a high bar - Your mileage may vary when it comes to the ambient writing, depending on your tolerance for every single pun ever being made.The RNG is bananas, especially in the early game where variably multi-hitting, non-100% accuracy attacks are rampant (Like a move that hits 1 to 3 times and has 90% accuracy) and you run into a local weather effect that just gives you a random chance to miss on your turn.It looks pretty good, and the Coromon sprites are nicely animated with some sub-pixel shading stuff going on, it's a shame that there are only 114 of them to collect - Probably a lot for a small team, especially with them being all new designs, but still a fair fewer than the 151 of the first generation of Pokemon.Only 7 types too, with no dualtypes (Technically 13 types, but 6 of them are for attacks only.)Without making enough changes to keep anything fresh or avoid the problems of older Pokemon games, this title really can't afford to be offering up a worse experience than said games, which it seems to be doing.If you're curious about the genre but can't afford to get any of those new Pokemon games, or find some way to play any of the first 5 gens, then I guess you'll find some enjoyment out of this.If you're a fan or veteran of Pokemon then just... Play Emerald Randomisers or Kaizo Romhacks or something, lol.Seriously, the only thing I can really recommend about Coromon is its soundtrack, so go give that a listen.
