_childDocuments_.review: So first I will state the obvious, yes, this is a lot like Pokemon. You run around catch creatures and make them battle. It's a system that works and that's why Gamefreak have done the same formula for 26 years. Coromon has put a breath of fresh air back into the genre. You start the game out with taking a new job as a battle researcher at this company and you're going through taking on research tasks and gathering information of more of the coromon. That's as much of the story I can go into without giving away the major plot points because this game while the story isn't revolutionary is better than "hey go out there and become the strongest trainer of the region". The puzzles in the game are not overly complex but not easy either. they take a decent amount of thought and make you feel smart when you complete them. Instead if gym leaders you will face off against a titan that you're trying to get their essence of. With this though is where I believe the game gets ridiculous. During normal progression once you get to the titan it's about 5 levels higher than your strongest coromon. For example the first titan was at level 25 and my strongest going into it the first time was about 19 with the lower ones being 15. So in order to beat it i had to do a pretty lengthy grinding session to do so, even getting my whole team to 21-23 i still struggled to defeat it. SO prepare for some lengthy grinding sessions before each boss. This game does play a lot like old school Pokemon with the more difficult puzzles, and of course the random encounters. THis is a feature some people will hate to see come in but as for me I absolutely loved it. It's like opening a present each time, you never know what you're going to get. This game also features two categories of Coromon that are more powerful than the normal Coromon with a palette swap. You can come across a potent or a perfect and these work a lot like how shinies in Pokemon. A potent has a 1 in 34 chance of appearing and a perfect is a 1 in 3000+ chance. I really enjoy this system and it makes them more rare but not so rare that they feel unobtainable. Overall I would reccomend this game to any turn based RPG fan and Pokemon fan if you're wanting a newer game that plays more like the older versions.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good pokémon-like game, but the "potential" mechanic is the most frustrating thing and the main reason i don't recomend it.Basically, each coromon has a potential up to 21, higher is better (it affects the stats) - Perfect coromons are those with 21 potential. Is absurdly hard to find a perfect one, but there is a way to have a chance to increase the potential - But you can only use once per Coromon and have to pay a reasonable ammount. Also, the chance to get potential to 21 through this method is ridiculously low (most coromon will have less than 0,5% chance, according to the wiki). Even if you save the game before attempting it, is absurdly hard to get it, because after handling the coromon to the NPC you need to walk 1000 steps before discovering the result, what is extremely annoying and completely frustrating.it's a HUGE difference between pokémon and coromon, because "shiny" pokémons are only cosmetic - "perfect" coromons will have better stats.In short, is one of those mechanics that wastes your time. Still, , but I would never recomend any game with this kind of mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: Given that this game covers a genre that I would very much love to see more games take a jab at, it's only natural that I'd give some thoughts on it. I'm giving it a thumbs up since I do not regret playing this game, but there are definitely features that was either underwhelming or just plain bad. And naturally, I will compare it to the Pokémon games since it quite obviously borrows a lot from that franchise in terms of gameplay. - The sprite quality is immaculate.- Lots of QoL additions that Pokémon games could take notes of.- Music feels very fitting and enjoyable.- Looks like all Coromon are fairly viable, obviously some more than others but if you do like a design visually then there are ways to make it work in your team.- Exploration is rewarded with plenty of chests and hidden items around all areas.- Very cooperative when it comes to what attacks you can have on your Coromons. Flash skills can be used endlessly, and previously learned moves can be re-activated on the fly.- The potency system allows you to allocate stat points to the stat you want, and it's easy to reset that investment.- While the sprites are great, the designs are overall rather underwhelming. Many species already get the point across from the base stage and then proceeds to just get bigger or more mature, while others can be described as "animal with its element added on top". It all works out in the end, but it was rare that the next evolution stage built further upon the concept or introduced something new.- Potency being linked to alternative color palettes. The potency system itself is fine. In Pokémon, I never bothered to look up what IVs my mons have, and I never hunted for shinys either. But with this system, it's like the game plants the idea in your head that any regularly colored Coromon isn't as strong as it could be, and if you do encounter one you already have in your team, you feel incentivized to replace it. Felt like a needless connection to what'd otherwise be a voluntary undertaking.- There are 13 types in the game, but only 6 of them exists as defensive types, or types the Coromon themselves will have. It's an interesting idea, but I'd rather have seen more of them as Coromon types to introduce more variety in designs and team setups. On a brighter note, the game can help you by displaying the type matchups so that you don't feel you need it all memorized.- The SP system, or Coromon's version of Pokémon's PP system. I understand the intent, where more powerful moves will consume more SP, thus adding a layer of strategy to not recklessly spend your energy. However, what actually happens is that regardless of what you do, you will feel punished. If you use moves with less SP cost you may take more damage, or drag out an encounter. If you end up spending your SP and is forced to skip a turn, you'll take damage or give the opponent a free turn too. I played with the option to refill all SP upon level up, and I still found this feature to be annoying at best. It could've been an easy fix if Coromon not on-field regenerated SP each turn to encourage switches, because as it is right now, it doesn't really add strategy, it just adds pressure.- You will often see yellow emojis during conversations. I suppose they're intended to ensure the player understands the current mood, but to me they were about as needed as sitcom laugh tracks. Sadly, no way to disable them in the settings.- While most interactions with NPCs have a comedic undertone, the main story is actually trying to be quite serious, only to not have an appropriately intense climax and you instead end up feeling that the game wants to wrap things up quickly. I personally also found the The game could've been more, but it also fulfilled my expectations and then some, so if I'd have to give it a score, it'd be around 6/10. It's a complete game, and for a monster catching game without Gamefreak's budget, it made a good job of rekindling the sensation of what the Pokémon games used to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Playthrough in ProgressUpdate: This is not a pokemon-like game, this is a game of minigames and puzzles disguised as a pokemon-like. I would say 60%+ of the game is just doing puzzles and minigames. Not sure I'm going to bother completing it with how little and tedious the battling is compared to the amount of puzzles and minigames.None of them are particularly hard, its just really tedious.==Original Review==TLDR: Quality game, haven’t encountered any bugs and is stable so far. Has tons of feature for min-maxers for tweak their coromon. This game definitely seems aimed at those sorts rather than a chill pokemon-like game, very tedious so far.Why it’s tedious: Entirely linear, no exploration or multiple areas to train in. No secrets to be found, or side routes to be explored. Would be less of an issue if it wasn’t so grindy.Lots of puzzles – Battling often does feel like it takes a back seat to many puzzles.Excessive number of wild encounters, even when using repellent~Useful when grinding, a pain when just trying to travel. Excessive mandatory trainers blocking your paths~The equivalents of Gyms are huge and have a Gyms worth of trainers on each floor. Only thing making it bearable is I enabled regen on level up and half price shops. Otherwise I would regularly be out of items and have to backtrack to healing centers.Excessive Grinding: Even a 2-3 level difference will lead to bosses stomping your coromon, even when of an opposing type. And the excessive encounters above are still insufficient to have you at proper level by the time you reach a boss. So you’re stuck leveling in the single zones per level range.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the time of writing this review I have played approximately 6 hours of this game and I feel like I can already give a decent review.Whilst fundamentally I would recommend this game as it gives a pretty decent GBA era Pokemon experience, it is worth knowing that I personally feel there are some core issues in the game that could be worked upon to increase the fluidity of gameplay and increase general playability.One of the first issues I noticed was that grinding was a hassle. So far every time I go into an area to grind if my Coromon arent decently ahead in levels to the wild Coromon then it can be a struggle to keep the Coromon alive that you want to grind levels with and this leads into one of my next issues. The damage values for general moves feel a tad overtuned, in the early game (or at least the first 4-5 areas, Im currently at Donar Island) the health values that most Standard and even Potent Coromon have means that in a wild area they are knocked out in potentially 2-3 hits and with the Health Cakes S costing 200-250 and the Health Cakes M costing 700 gold, being able to heal outside of a town healer is expensive to keep up considering it could take up to 3-4 wild fights just to afford 1 Health Cake.The game also seems to completely collapse if its tried to stream through Discord which is a complaint most of the other reviews have noted.In conclusion the art style is nice, sprite designs are awesome although more active animations would be a nice touch the game suffers from some balancing and streamline issues, with apparently an unsatisfying story end and mostly frustrating grinding experience. I would still recommend this game but if I were you Id get it on sale unless some of the issues are sorted.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a shameless ripoff of pokemon.  However, It stands out quite well in that it has tons of new creature, hehe, comforts.  It still adheres to the original formula of what works without any of the silliness that pokemon is adopting these days in order to force novelty into a worn-out franchise.I think it's better than pokemon in most ways. It doesn't shove stupid things in your face you have no interest in (boring waste of time beauty contests, required online feature showcases, megadigiterrastrialvolutions, dumb side quests).  It's just plain pokemon, like pokemon should still be, but with loads of improvements like an achievement system with levels, rewards, and more rewards for accepting rewards.  I also like how it handles HMs.  Your character has the skills rather than the pokemon so they're available all the time.  The sprite work is excellent, and the shiny/nature/IV system is refined into a single scoring system coromon calls potential.  Potential ranges randomly from 0-21 for each monster. Higher is better in EVERY WAY, appearances and extra stats that you can allocate any way you want.  Appearance changes to color pallet occur with higher potential (shiny), but if you like another color scheme you can change it to anything lower than the pokemon's current potential. All of this is how pokemon should have done it!  The music is cute and appropriate.  The graphics overall are pretty great for what this game is.  The boss fights are excellent compared to anything pokemon has attempted outside of Legends.  It is hard to make these games challenging without being insanely grindey or just straight up breaking the game's own rules, but this game strikes a nice balance there as well.  The bosses are difficult, and aside from how many rounds it takes to defeat them, levels don't matter as much as the rhythm of the fight.  Each one has a gimmick like being able to 1-shot you if you don't do something, damaging your entire team after reaching 1/2 health, or being invulnerable to damage if not exploiting its weakness.  That being said, I also never lost a fight the whole game.  I didn't grind outside of screwing around trying to get the area achievements and find all the rare Mons, so it's not a very difficult game.  Thankfully, there's an app for that!  The game has incredibly granular difficulty settings allowing you to play however you want.  On top of that, you unlock further customizations via item rewards, shop purchases, and achievements.  In these games, time invested is almost always the way to get stronger, so if there are parts you don't enjoy repeating over and over again, or you just want certain areas to go by faster, you can toggle the settings in ways to speed up those undesired aspects.  Like if you don't enjoy farming money, you can 1/2 the price of shop wares for example with an item you find.  I guess if you are just really bad at these types of games somehow, you can just make the whole thing a cakewalk if you want to.There are puzzles and they are some of the puzzles I have ever played.  I did not forget a word in that sentence,  The puzzles are really obvious and dumb except for when they aren't and take way too long to figure out.  Yeah, this is definitely the game's weak point.  Pokemon puzzles are also pretty terrible, so I feel like this is more of a hail-to-its-inspiration rather than a serious fault.I like that NPCs are aware of how dumb the world of pokemon is, kind of like cassette beasts.  I like that the people talk more like people than weebs.  But I don't like that this game is pretty low on content.  It's not short or anything.  It takes a long time to complete but when you're done, you don't really feel like you've done a whole lot.  Having big N's budget really helps out with that problem in pokemon games, but I'd rather play this any day.  Quality over quantity!If you think Pokemon has been terrible starting directly after Alpha-Omega remake generation, this game is for you.  It keeps all the best parts of those games without introducing all the awful ideas that followed.  I won't even say this is a game for purists.  There are loads of objective improvements that pokemon implemented in later generations.  It's a game for people who liked pokemon when it didn't suck and want a better experience, new story line, and new monsters to chase.  It's not perfect, but it's the best pokemon-clone out there.  It feels quality, and the music doesn't make you want to stab yourself in the ears like cassette beasts does.Update: there is a new included DLC that implements a shop system of purchasing special editions of certain coromon, character cosmetics, and high-tier items otherwise limited in quantity in the game (master balls, rare candies, shiny attracting spray).  I don't think the shop addition makes the game any better, but it is an option which I like!  I just like choices.  Nintendo has been our-way or the highway since forever and this game gives you choices all over the place of how to play.  Really great job with this game.  I hope there will be another!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 Right of the bat the Coromon sprite art is real nice and is a highlight. Progress is mostly linear through the world areas and is well suited to the game. However, "the grind" is not well balanced for a timely PvE experience; perhaps for something with MMO like PvP it would be more inline. The game features a double rarity system - Base encounter chance in wild + potential rank from 1 to 21. The odds of getting a very high potential specific 'Mon are pretty low even with item boosts.Additionally, there is excessive use of hidden items throughout without any on screen ques. This results in interacting with every tile to ensure to don't miss something until late game. Moreover, this really slow down the pacing of the action and gets compounded mid-game with a second hidden item type that requires a specific item to search for it. Lastly, the tactical depth is pretty minimal. The game doesn't do a lot to deviate from the Pokemon red/blue combat formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have many hours in the game, so I'm not sure how valid my opinion/review is at the moment, but I will say with utmost certainty, I absolutely LOVE this game so far.To me, this is the Stardew Valley of Pokemon. Ever since I saw its first reveal about it coming to the Switch, I was immediately hooked. As someone who has been disappointed by each newer Pokemon game, I wanted a game that brought me back to my childhood; why I loved the series in the first place.Playing Coromon, I feel like a kid again! The animations and art are absolutely spectacular, the different Coromon designs and types have been incredibly interesting to experience firsthand, and the amount of player customization and optimization is outstanding! From the very start, you get the character creator, which is already more vast compared to the actual Pokemon titles. And the game customization options are absolutely fabulous. Not only are there different preset difficulty settings, but there's also custom ones you can make, making Nuzlocke experiences even more viable, as well as fun gimmicks like being able to capture trainer Coromon, if you want to have that setting on.The one con so far that I've experienced is that there are a few stuttering frame issues. Not sure if that's on my hardware, or the game itself, but that is something I have noticed.I know the Switch port got delayed, which is saddening, but I totally understand it. Even though I bought it on Steam, I will be buying on Switch when it's available. I want to see this game thrive and flourish!Thank you developers for this amazing experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating, shallow, and uninspired mini-games and puzzles hold back an otherwise incredible creature battler RPG.Coromon is a science fantasy creature collector role playing game. The player takes on the role of a newly-hired researcher with the goal of learning more about Coromon, a group of over 100 unique species of fantastical creatures. Finding themselves thrust into a globetrotting adventure, players can expect to collect a variety of creatures, customize their skills and party for strategic battle, and explore a variety of aesthetic environments... when they're not being forced to participate in horrendous mini-games or inane puzzles.To start on a positive note, Coromon's creature collection and battle mechanics are among the best in the genre. There are a large variety of creatures to customize one's party with, and each creature family feels unique with their own distinct strengths and weaknesses. Creatures can memorize four skills to use in battle from lists of skills unique to each creature (adding more skills to their lists as they level up or use certain items) alongside a special passive or active trait. When considering skill and trait loadouts, there are thousands of combinations to choose from when customizing Coromon, creating deep, tactical depth. Battle mechanics are intuitive, though the in-game guides are also great at explaining mechanics in detail if the player doesn't completely grasp them at first. Also noteworthy is how reasonable it is to "retrain" aspects of your Coromon that are normally notoriously difficult in other creature collection games.The art and music for Coromon is nothing short of exceptional. The game is illustrated with beautiful pixel art in every corner of the world of Velua, with animations that breathe life and personality into every creature and battle skill. The variety of tracks in Coromon is a pleasant surprise, with memorable musical themes throughout the experience. Composed by Davi Vasc, the combination of synthetic strings, brass, and even electric guitar alongside bright piano melodies creates a soundtrack that perfectly services the different moments of the game and becomes instantly nostalgic.Unfortunately, this is where the positives for Coromon end. Though I typically restrain myself from using the first-person perspective and histrionic language in my reviews, I cannot understate how utterly detestable the narrative experience in Coromon is. While the writing of the narrative delivered via dialogue and worldbuilding is serviceable, the player character's participation in the game world's events manifests in unpolished out-of-genre gameplay, the inclusion of which feels utterly inane. For example, one chapter of the game's narrative involves infiltrating a palace in a desert country, and requires the player character to traverse a heavily-guarded barracks building without being spotted by enemy NPCs. Upon being noticed, a Coromon battle is not triggered - instead, the player gets a game over screen and must restart the segment from the last checkpoint they reached. This shallow "stealth" gameplay (and I am really reaching to use that term here) has no place in a creature battler RPG like Coromon. Though it may have been designed as a way to add variety to the game's narrative, it only served to make me miserable and desperately wish to get back to the main gameplay of Coromon. This is only one example of such an unenjoyable diversion, others include a more frustrating variation of the board game Mastermind and a series of mind-numbingly dull fetch quests in a snowy village, which felt like artifical time wasters as opposed to fun gameplay, and these side errands must be completed in order to progress through the game.While I loved the aspects of Coromon that were related to the core promise of the game - creature collection and tactical battles - the amount of other nonsense in the game is so vast and frustrating that I was unable to complete the game. While I do not regret my purchase, and I believe that Coromon has made important strides for the future of the creature collector genre with its innovative mechanics, I cannot in good conscience recommend anyone to actually play this game, as I don't think they'd be having fun half the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is hands down one of the best Monster Taming games out there, in my mind far exceeding the recent additions to the Pokémon franchise as it takes the genre back to it's roots, and innovates on it in ways Pokémon has refused to do for many years now.The tameable Coromon are all beautifully illustrated in hand animated pixel art - accentuating their personalities and unique designs. Whether you like your creatures to be 2D or 3D is a personal preference, but I do believe it suites the nostalgia associated with the genre of Monster Taming games.Unlike the Pokémon games of today, Coromon allows the player to tailor their difficulty settings to suite their play style, making Coromon less of a "grind one starter and spam the hyperbeam" experience - and more of an actual strategy game that challenges the player to allocate stat points and abilities wisely - especially when using the included nuzlocke mode.By far my favourite addition in Coromon is the expansion on Shiny Hunting, now allowing players to encounter 'Potent' as well as 'Perfect' Coromon, adding a much needed in-between that keeps players excited for wild encounters - rather than them turning into a repetitive annoyance.Coromon also includes tons of quality of life features, one of my favourites being stat-point reallocation - allowing to build  your team more strategically. TRAGsoft has done an amazing job with this game - especially for whatever budget / time constraints I'm sure they must've had whilst developing Coromon.I sincerely hope this game garners enough attention and attains a passionate fanbase for years to come, as I'd love for the developers to have all the freedom in the world, devoid of budget / time constraints to turn this gem of a game into a series better and more renowned than the predecessor that inspired it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, however I can't recommend it.  There are two main issues with it.1. Playing on Steam Deck, the game suffers massive performance issues.   The game will drop to unplayable frame rates and become unresponsive to controls after only 30 minutes of gameplay.  It also is a massive battery drain.  The Deck battery drains faster playing this 2D game than it does playing games like GTA V or Cyberpunk.  There are posts going back 7 months or more pointing out this issue, and the Devs have replicated the issue, but still no fix.2. The second issue applies to everyone regardless of whether or not you're using a Steam Deck.  The selection of Coromon is very limited.  As other reviews pointed out, there are only around 100 Coromon total, most being a part of another's evolution line, leading to only about 40 total evolution lines to explore.All that said, this game is crazy fun when it's working properly. The art style and animations look better, and more uniform, than any other Pokè-Like game I've seen.  Although the selection of Coromon is very limited, the ones that are available are fun and creative.  I will say that I wish less of the available evolution lines were bugs, and more variety of animals were used as inspiration.

_childDocuments_.review: Last edit 5/12 3 PM ESTI have completed the demo and transferred to the full game. I will say so far that if you are coming over from Pokemon, there are similarities that will make you feel right at home, but just enough different things to make the experience feel fresh. I did not stick with Temtem because of its always-online nature and from how vastly different it was - with Coromon I feel right at home with the mechanics. I firmly believe that if you are a veteran Pokemon fan looking for a game to scratch that monster-catcher itch, while also providing a decent challenge, Coromon is a very good game that fulfills all of this.The many QoL changes made here also greatly enhance the experience, much of it returning from Pokemon fan projects (which is far from a bad thing):Battles are challenging, which is a refreshing change of pace compared to what we have recently gotten in Pokemon. You are forced to switch between different Coromon throughout each battle to tend to different elements/types. The Titan boss battles are bulky and difficult, necessitating a properly trained team most of the time. At the same time, there are options in the game's settings menu and at a terminal at the start of the game to make the game easier or more difficult depending on what you want - a more casual, easier playthrough more akin to Pokemon's X and Y, or a challenge run with nuzlocke rules? All there, all built in.This game also has a much simpler type tree and does not have any dual-type Coromon. This is not a bad thing necessarily - if anything, this makes it easier for newcomers to get a mental grasp on and memorize.This game looks really nice. I love the battle backgrounds, I love the Coromon sprites (and the designs for them are also quite good as well), I love the overworlds and how varied and interesting they are. It definitely looks like the mobile game that it was intended to be, but you wouldn't be able to tell that just at a glance. The spritework is  - major props to the team that made them....Do I really need to elaborate?Oh yeah, it's on Spotify, too, so feel free to make your own judgement. (Spoilers, obviously!) NOTE: The launcher has been disabled. This section reflects the game's initial version when it first came out and when this review was initially posted.This was a MASSIVE disappointment for me personally. DO  PUT A LAUNCHER AFTER I PRESS THE PLAY BUTTON. LAUNCH THE GAME!The full version adds a launcher before the game actually starts, advertising other Freedom Games titles. I absolutely  think this is necessary; if I want to look at your games, there is a "check out the Freedom Games franchise on Steam" button on the store page that I will click if I care enough.The launcher itself has also caused problems with people not being able to start the game, and it additionally impacts Steam Deck verification. You gain NOTHING from adding a launcher - so don't do it! When I hit the play button, the GAME should load. Do not put ANYTHING else before the actual game unless you absolutely  to!The more I play the game, the more I notice that this is very clearly a mobile game first, and is not necessarily made for PC. This comes with benefits - being able to navigate with a mouse as well as with a keyboard or controller is a welcome addition - but that also means it is not optimized very well performance-wise. Which leads into the next and probably biggest criticism I have with this game...Crashes and graphical glitches everywhere! For a lower-end game like this I am a little bit concerned as to how many issues I have seen. The Discord overlay does not work and causes consistent crashes, and you have to disable a Discord setting to be able to stream the game. There are also various different problems going around with some graphics cards. I have not personally run into any of them myself, but they are definitely not good, and are very common. I would definitely wait a little bit to see if they are ironed out further.Some story elements drag for some time longer than they probably should, and some puzzles I find myself even questioning if they are puzzles at all.  While it is clear that the developers are attempting to try new ideas with the genre and they are fixing a lot of these issues with patches, a lot of this leaves me scratching my head and wondering how it got past the conceptual phase, let alone testing.Despite the flaws with the story and performance gripes, I very much recommend this game. It's a very solid monster catcher, and if you are coming from Pokemon, you will most likely have a good time with it. Coromon is not afraid to try new things, but at its core it is very familiar.If my verdict changes as I continue to play through the game, I will update this review.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite thing about this game is how much it differs from Pokemon. ___For example, instead of a typical shiny variant, there are 2 extra color palettes attached to a Coromon, going from Standard, Potent, and Perfect. I also find the types interesting and how they are split between skill types and Coromon types.___This game fills the itch to play a Pokemon-like game, but was a better experience than Pokemon by introducing refreshing gameplay, a fun story, and cool Coromon creatures.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is everything a fan of creature catchers could want from a pokemon clone and more. Not only does the game double down on the positive aspects of pokemon games by making a lot of less significant aspects of the game significantly more streamlined, but it adds a great deal of its own creative features that make for the most fun I've had with this kind of game since Black & White. The best of these new features is easily the shiny system in which shiny Coromon are not only cosmetically pleasing and distinct from their basic counterparts, but ideal stat wise as well. Everything else from berry growing and harvesting to building a team and experimenting with moves is very fluent and fun too. While the player is more than able to take their time progressing through the story, there's also plenty of ways to speed things up and rush the story. There's also quite a bit of end-game content that's not nearly as grindy or monotonous as a pokemon game. Likewise, there's plenty of side quests and non-story content the player may wish to return to once the main quest line is over. There is quite a lot of emphasis on puzzles throughout the goofy but likewise grim story, taking the player through a simple setting with a surprisingly solid foundation for this game to take place and progress. The puzzles were probably my least favorite aspect simply because the restart mechanism in the event of failing a puzzle isn't particularly appealing. Another unfortunate aspect about the game is that despite an adequate range of Coromon numbering just upwards of 100 and the game's own verbal emphasis on a wide variety of strategies to be used, certain Coromon were completely underwhelming compared to others in terms of both raw competence in battles and application of certain strategies, making certain strategies like accuracy manipulation easier and more optimal than say defensive or status strategies. While battles may not have as much variety as some would like though, the options menu is actually incredible in this game. There's a lot of customization options for battles, general gameplay, audio, graphics, etc. There's even a built-in randomizer and nuzlocke mode, which individual customizations for separate settings that gives Coromon a lot of replayability on top of end-game content. Overall this is a great creature catcher/pokemon clone, which definitely has a lot of care and polish put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This has actually been one of my top games this year! Coromon exceeded every expectation I had. It is obviously heavily inspired by classic creature catchers like Pokemon and Digimon, but it has the benefit of close to 20 years of retrospect. The combat feels very familiar and yet a few important changes to the stamina and skill systems make it feel fresh. You can feel the deep love the devs have for this genre and everything that makes it great! The pixel art is incredible, every environment is soaking in character and the sprite-work for the coromon and their skills is outstanding. The designs are one of my favourite parts of this game, every coromon was unique and visually interesting. The music was outstanding, when that electric guitar hits in the menu theme... damn. The devs have been super receptive and friendly, they have been really awesome and responsive to feedback.But by far the biggest surprise for me was the story. There are emotional beats that actually landed for me and the end hit me a lot harder than I was expecting!I didn't get too far into the competitive aspects of this game so I don't feel comfortable commenting on that part of the game, there is an active discord community for those who want that experience. I can't recommend this game enough!

_childDocuments_.review: When I started to play Coromon, I was at first very pleased with the game. There were some good ideas that set it apart from the classic Pokemon games. A secondary potential xp bar where you choose where to allocate bonus stats, the ability to freely choose from the ability ever learned, a rarity system for more potent coromons...The game was seemingly teeming with good stuff, and the art was good too. So what went wrong ? For me it was the puzzles. This game feature all the puzzles you can find in pokemon, and more. I've always hated those puzzle parts in pokemon, and here, they are taken to the next level. Every single dungeon is just a new excuse for more puzzles, and godamn are they annoying. _childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a classic monster taming experience that will remind you of older Pokemon games but have all the bells and whistles and quality of life improvements of modern monster tamer games then Coromon is for you. Even on normal difficulty, Coromon is pretty challenging and there are many ways to increase difficulty as well as add randomizer elements, do nuzlockes, and more with a wide variety of customizable settings. Coromon are relatively balanced stat-wise and every Coromon feels like it has potential to be overpowered in the right team and with the right set up. However, I will point out that some movepools and traits are simply superior to others and some types are severely underrepresented in the moves department unfortunately. The story isn't great but it's pretty interesting and there's promise of future updates to alleviate the rather abrupt ending.Titan battles and puzzles can be annoying in some ways for some but for the most part I found them enjoyable.The game is simple to pick up and learn. And I am still thoroughly enjoying it. The potential system is an excellent replacement for the shiny system most games employ and perfect hunting never feels hopeless not that you even need perfect forms for PVP now anyway. The thing that really makes this game an absolute gem tho is really the incredible devs. Devs listen to fans, quickly resolve issues, and clearly love and slave over their game. It's so refreshing I can't even begin to describe it. I'm not used to being spoiled by devs as a longtime Pokemon fan so it's just a breath of fresh air. I would highly recommend this game. I loved it when I started and still love it just as much or more now.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this is a weird review for me because I am super mixed on this game. Please don't misunderstand this game isn't bad at all but its a lot deeper than pokemon was. In pokemon the game didn't ask much of you other than to kind of build a semi OK team but other than that it was pretty easy. In coromon however that is not the case at all. I've spent a couple of hours alone looking at just stats of the coromon and planning out their level ups and stat increases. I found that if you really don't know what you are doing and don't plan well this game can quickly become a living hell. so there is a lot of trainer battles and at first they aren't so bad but later on they get more challenging. I found myself running back to heal my guys more often then I would have liked. This is what I mean by the game can become a living hell,  if you don't plan stuff out and raise the correct stats when needed you can quickly find one of your coromon because shear trash like I did and I regretted treating it like pokemon. I had to go back and train a whole new guy to replace my now trash one and that worked way better. I am not saying this is a bad thing, not at all honestly but if you don't know about it you can waste a lot of your time like I did.  Please keep this next part in mind that this game is a grind. I am not super far into the game and there has already been three moments were I thought about shutting the game off because I just wanted to progress and the game just had more stuff in the way than it really needed. Another HUGE issue I can see is this game as mandatory puzzles that must be solved in order to progress in the game. These puzzles are not however super hard but they aren't easy either and you will most likely spent 20 to 40 mins messing with them. The puzzles are really annoying because the game already has alot of grinding and then you need to stop and complete a puzzle.The different types are interesting to say the least but I will say I thought It was weird that your starters are a ice, fire and water. Unlike pokemon were one of the types is rare and worth taking that simply isnt the case here, you can pretty much find a fire type in the grass right outside the starting area and a ice type like 30 mins to an hour into the game. I personally would have like to see more of a impact on that first choice you made. I ended up taking the fire one because I thought I wasn't going to find alot of fire types early. If I was to go back I would honestly go water because that seemed like something I needed and was missing but other than that I really didn't feel like my first choice mattered too much.The game looks really good and there really isn't any crashing or glitches at all and all the models look really good, I have personally fallen in love with a couple of them because they are such good models.In summary, good game but you need to put more thought into your team than pokemon and this game is very grindy with puzzles that you must complete. I think its honestly worth grabbing and worth your time, you just need to be aware that your going to have to think and be smart about what you do. Its not like pokemon were after you spent like 30 mins getting your guys to 15 the game plays itself, no, not here. The other trainers will go toe to toe with you if you aren't constantly raising your levels. Now that I know what I am doing I will most likely restart my play through so its alot smoother. Anyways I hope this helped some people out.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is like a 6/10 at best. it has some good ideas in terms of some gameplay elements and creature designs, but the lack of dual typings makes most creatures feel really same-y. there are also some puzzle and filler sections that are way too long. it honestly feels a lot closer to nexomon than pokemon if youve ever played that, but the music and art is really good.overall its a decent creature collector that drags itself a bit too long and in my opinion lacks depth. idk how competitive is bc i havent tried it yet, but since shinies determine stats in this game i heard most ppl complain about it being a grind, though i cant say much myself.edit: addressing the comments to go more in detail, i feel like every creature being monotype automatically makes gameplay and monster variety a lot more shallow. i think the typing system hurts me more because some types being move only is a great idea, however i think thematically most of them dont make sense to be move only such as air and foul. secondly, since there are so few types (7 monster types + 6 move only types), i feel like the game could benefit more from dual typings in order to make it more varied.in terms of game pacing, i feel like most of the decisions they made ultimately just make the game more tedious. a good example is the potential machine, it is a good idea on paper, however in execution its not very good. the machine only works once for each monster, so youre forced to reload saves in order to get better potential rates, plus the machine only completes after taking 1000 steps, so grinding for a potentially good monster is just a walking simulator. some of the puzzles and stealth/obstacle sections also drag on a little too long as said before.i did not try pvp purely bc of the fact that i of course had to try and essentially farm shinies in order to get the best potential monsters to win. i also was at a point in the game where i didnt feel like i could complete yet, and not everyone will be as committed or available to grind for pvp.all in all i do not like the game bc it is just fundamentally at fault for me, however if you do not mind these problems then it is a pretty decent game with great polish. i do not foresee myself continuing to play unless they add more types/implement dual typing, which i dont think is happening anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of really good aspects of this game for a Pokemon like, and I really wanted to like it and even beat it, but the flaws started to get to me too much.The GoodGreat Designs for the most part. (Subjective, but I like the shark.)Music sounds great, lovely tunes to chill to.Quality of life items such as the Fruit Fetcher, the Remote Coromon Storage, Infinite Repel.The BadThe Puzzles are much to left be desired :c They often get in the way of the fun, or are just tedious. Some require you to have precise stealth, or others require pattern recognition without very good foretelling. The Boss Fights are... 50/50. Their designs feel off to me personally, which is subjective. They did provide a challenge, but if you don't succeed the first time you will have to go through an entire un-skipable cutscene every single attempt. If you fail on the puzzles, it will not just reset you at the beginning of the dungeon, but give you a game over, for example I got hit by a blow dart, instead of taking damage or get pushed back. I had to press "Try Again", they aren't hard, just tedious and bogs down the fun.The story is okay? I can't really comment as it was just, an alright experience. Nothing I hated but nothing that special, and I don't really blame the writers for that. The Npcs you interact with are a bit corny, and that's fine. But none of them have a really different personality outside of "Quirky, Excited, Scientist" they shuffle from these three personality traits a lot. Pokemon does the same for a lot of them, so not gonna take points.Overall? 6/10 I think it's definitely worth picking up for $5 if you can, just to give it your own try and experience, but overall I think it could of used some more time in the oven in certain aspects.

Standard appearances is in the 1 to 16 range, Potent 17 to 20 and Perfect is at 21. _childDocuments_.review: Coromon is such a breath of fresh air from the stale monster tamer giant that is Pokemon, and the monster taming genre in general. TRAGsoft did a phenomenal job with this game, from the challenging puzzles, to having a hand in how to raise your mons, to the palatable storyline. Not to mention the soundtrack, map design, character design, pixel art and mon design, there were all top tier and the reason why I love indie games so much. There's so much passion poured into the game.Although the game adopts many of the systems from Pokemon, it didn't feel like a copy of their stuff; just familiar systems but built with ease-of-access in mind and most importantly, making it fun. Some of the puzzles were actually trickier than I expected (even had to look up the answer to a few!) and I appreciated that because the game isn't just a steamroll. It's interactive and present, the point video-games are supposed to be. Also the biggest thing I'm a fan of, I can actually catch ALL coromons! Seriously, who markets the phrase 'gotta catch em all' and not let us catch them all in a single game? Been grinding my gears for decades. Finally, many of the end-stage Coromon evolution designs look so absolutely fantastic! This motivated me to discover all the coromons in the game. So thank you TRAGsoft, for doing this right.The only thing at this point in time I wish I had more of was end-game content. Can't wait to see what updates are next!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Best "Poke-clone" out there. Amazing QOL. Great cast. Get itFirst off, this game isn't perfect. But what is here is so fantastic, I can't recommend it enough. I think all games in this genre(I suppose it's called creature collector?) are going to be compared to Pokemon, which is unavoidable, seeing as how Pokemon basically invented and dominated the genre for 20 years. A tremendous amount of franchise fatigue has turned me off of these games, but on a whim, I decided to power through and give Coromon a chance. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ what a decision that turned out to be. edit: Before the Coromon themselves, I'll mention the type chart. Only 6 types, all of which are familiar, however there are 7 additional types that are only found on moves. Magic, Foul, and Heavy are three of them, which aren't in Pokemon, so you'll have to go through the tedious process of using them in various battles to learn what they're effective on and resisted by. Except you don't. You're given a type chart immediately, and also very early on you get books on Coromon basics, moves, field conditions and status effects, to name a few. This is a MASSIVE point in Coromon's favor, providing the player with all the vital information they need on types, moves, etc. This takes out an excessive amount of grind and tedious experimental learning.  It really shows consideration of the players experience by the devs, and I for one appreciate it greatly. First thing I'll mention are the Coromon themselves. Most of them are fantastic in design, with beautifully animated sprites, reminiscent of gen 5. Only 2 come to mind when I think of the ones I really didn't like, but that's still a higher percentage of great mons than any generation of Pokemon. That's all subjective anyway, so how about their viability. While I haven't been able to try them all yet, each and every one seems to be well thought out in how it fits in with the rest of the cast in terms of stats, moves and play style. There aren't any ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Coromon that are only there to make others better by comparison. Even the early game Coromon manage to carve out a niche for themselves that allows them to retain viability throughout the game. It's amazing. The story is nothing spectacular, but it isn't terrible. I really don't have much to say on it. I'll leave that up to you to decide, but I suppose the main point is battling the 6 titans. They sort of act as boss battles in lieu of gym leaders. They're actually really fun to find and battle. I'll leave it at that to avoid spoilers or any unnecessary details.  How about the world.. It's... pretty good. Tons of unique and diverse environments and biomes to go through. The Coromon themselves are mostly found in the environment of their type i.e. sand types in the desert, fire types in a volcano, etc. For the most part this is true, but there are a decent enough distribution throughout the early game to get a diverse enough team to have multiple types, each with coverage moves, for any challenge you may face. Again, well thought out on the part of the devs. Fantastic. The puzzles are.. well that depends on you. I like them. They're larger, longer, and more frequent than any Pokemon game. Whether this is a pro or con is entirely personal preference. I like them. They aren't difficult, but they are long at times, and start to drag just a bit before the end of the cave/dungeon/whatever. I saw a few reviews that mentioned how much of a pain in the ass they are, and how they derail and butcher the pacing of the game. I disagree, but I understand the sentiment. It's really just up to you. By puzzles, btw, think of strength puzzles, ice floors in caves, and ♥♥♥♥ like that in Pokemon games. Press a button to open a door, press another to open another door but i closes the previous door, etc. So what's the difficulty like? Is it as hard as B2W2 and USUM, or piss easy like modern games? Well that also is up to you. There's a plethora of difficulty modifiers that allow you to really customize your experience. Every element of the ultra hardcore nuzlocke is individually toggle-able. Everything from only one mon per route, to fainting=death, no fast travel, held item limits, and more. You can really make this a hellscape of torture and suffering in every way, punishing yourself for any and every mistake, regardless of size. Or you could play it like a Pokemon game, and just mash A through the entire game and never really try.There's more, especially quality of life additions, to mention, but you're probably sure at this point whether or not you want the game. I can't recommend it enough, and strongly urge you to get this if you're just burnt out on Pokemon games being the same dull, bland and plain experience over and over. I mean really, the trailer is accurate. It's a great game, in many many ways, and deserves a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon improves on the Pokemon formula in terms of the small details. I will mention several items and aspects from Pokemon Red/Gold since Coromon is inspired by the popular franchise. Music for each town/area livens up the mood. Ghost town is spooky and battles against bosses are exciting.- Berries - Can grow specific fruits in pots and pick them when ready.- Escape rope in caves/Fly- Lux Recall that lets you transport to any town- Bike- Run and can change setting to turn on at all times- Shiny- Potent is the equivalent. Potent scent to use and this increases chance of Potent Coromon appearance- HM moves- Gauntlets with push rock, burn, etc that lets you use special moves outside of battle without the need to teach Coromon a weak attack- 4 moves allowed in Pokemon only- Can enable or change 1 or all 4 moves before a battle- Stats - Can choose which Stats like Attack or defense to increase when leveling- Buying items - Can use coupons to decrease cost of buying items- Difficulty - Several modes and harder modes for players that want a tougher experienceMain aspects missing are gym battles, no rival, no Elite 4, and no breeding. Some minor weaknesses are below.- Puzzles that are somewhat tedious and involve collecting items, timing a jump, and stealth.- The need to level up Coromon to defeat last boss. It is level 70 and yours are around mid 50s or low 60s by that point of the game.- Few achievements require multiple playthroughs.- Antagonist do not present a challenge. They throw some Coromon battles at you, but it does not add to the story.This game is enjoyable for Pokemon fans, contains atmospheric soundtrack, and is a worthy successor to Pokemon. The developers continue to make updates and show a devotion to improving the game.If you want to learn about the future of Coromon, check out the interview.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good poké-like with a twist.Moves are learned and retained and you pick a choice of four at any one time. You can also teach your mon a selection of other moves from TM like manuals which can vastly improve their usability as often you'll be adding something.Stat changing moves and buff/debuff moves can be powerful but like Pokémon you're usually better just aiming for type weaknesses. Strength vs Special attacks are varied also and all mons have their own strengths and weaknesses in battle.The game is well balanced and I rarely felt overpowered except perhaps one dungeon around the middle of the game where I fell into a perfect strategy against all the mons in the area.There are a few flaws: the story is fine but nothing special, the battles can be slow sometimes and you can teleport around freely for most of the game so there's no threat or need to use items when you can just backtrack. There's no post-game as yet but allegedly there are some free updates planned so watch this space.Over-all definitely worth the price if you like monster trainer games and especially if you miss the gameboy/DS days.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of monster catching games, you might enjoy Coromon. It is "good enough", but some aspects bothered me enough to make this a negative review. Overall I think it treads a bit too close to the game series it obviously takes inspiration from. Compared to the games that inspired it, there are much fewer elemental types and the overall battle complexity is much less as a result. Elemental types aren't sprinkled out over the course of the game but rather concentrated in specific areas. You'll get nearly all Electric type Coromon in the first major dungeon for example. There are a couple of exceptions, but I often found myself wanting more variety in my team that I couldn't get until a later dungeon let me catch several of a new element type. The encounter rate is frustratingly high, often just 2 or 3 steps between battles.The milestones system is a ton of manual work, tons of clicking and need to remember to check it periodically. I'm not fond of being made to feel I need to min-max my stats with potential, traits, and stat adjusting. The dice rolls are extremely unfair. I've seen enemies get 5 critical hits in a row, and enemy multi-hit attacks seem to always land 2-3 times. Conversely, I miss a lot and my multi-hit attacks consistently only hit one time. Boss battles are full of frustrating, cheesy mechanics. Give me puzzles or give me random battles, but NEVER both at the same time. An intrusive battle breaks the flow of my concentration on the puzzle. I can't believe this mistake is still being made.  I have a strong dislike of puzzles that require precision timing. I was thinking about leaving a positive review, but I changed my mind once I encountered a mandatory minigame requiring a bunch of precision reflexes. Its alright, it just irritated me with a bunch of little things.

_childDocuments_.review: *Review contains spoilers*I want to like it,  but I can't.I'm a huge Pokemon fan, and I also love Nexomon. So this game sounded fantastic to me, and I enjoyed what I'd played of the demo two or so years ago. So this was a day-one buy.It started off a lot of fun. The monster designs are great, the battle mechanics are enjoyable, and I enjoy hunting for potent and perfect coromon. I even like the cute little emoji reactions. They add a lot of charm and character. However, there are two huge points of the game that just ruin it for me.First, the puzzles. There are just too many. One of them falls over an area I'd like to explore, but the idea is to rush across the desert from tent to tent before the hot sand burns through your shoes. Adding puzzles is fair enough, but they don't even add a challenge. They are just frustrating. If you fail, you go back to another checkpoint. You don't lose anything other than your time. There's nothing to spur you on to try and do them perfectly, since there's no in-game drawback. This is especially frustrating for someone with dyspraxia like me. My disability doesn't cost me much in games, I play Monster Hunter and enjoy it. But with the puzzles in Coromon, one small miss-click or finger spasm and I've failed, then I'm graced with the 'try again?' screen and it's back to the previous checkpoint. There is no way to bypass them.Secondly, the titans. This is where the grind comes in. I don't mind games with a bit of a grind, but each boss is a wall. If you aren't prepared, you are going to have a hard time. The first boss is level 25. Beat him with a team of level 25s, and every wild Coromon in the zone after it will be ten levels or more below you. So if you want a new team member, you will need to get it up to level 35 for the next titan, which is soon might I add.If you like games with a grind and puzzles, then you'll like this game. But it just wasn't for me. I thought I just needed a break after getting to the town (and the stealth puzzle...) after the second titan. But I have no desire to pick it up again. Unfortunately, I wont be jumping on any sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest. Having played through the entirety of this game,  You're better off getting Cassette Beasts. If you only want to play the pvp, again, just wait for the cassette beasts pvp update.Not even for the PVE experience is this game worth its price point. Never have I seen a game start so strongly and trail off so heavily. I've played for 59 hours in total and I am hoping I can bargain with Steam for a refund.The writing goes from a story worth the absolute barrage of text and lore they throw at you, to a memey "and then and then and then" format that just ends in you skipping all the text and checking the quest log for what you're meant to do. The "30 hours of story" they promise comes in the form of random difficulty spikes (which aren't that hard to begin with, (You'll probably want to play the game on hard, but you also wont, You'll hear why soon) and then little mandatory minigames/puzzles that do nothing but take up time. Remember the fun "slide around the ice til you reach the goal" portions of Pokemon? Yeah well there's a whole 2 dungeons out of the 5-6 in the game dedicated to that! And even a whole town! Whoaaa 30 hours of story! And just before these sections is a whole dungeon with arrow traps and a wall maze/ puzzle with about 4 battles in it. Remember battles? The whole reason you're playing a monster tamer to begin with? Yeah those pesky things are sprinkled into this puzzle game for you to the point where by the time you finally see another trainer you forgot you just added a new mon to your team. And then you wipe the trainer in 3 turns and that's you last battle for 15 minutes. The second dungeon that leads to the first boss fight is peppered with battles. And since you're so new, it feels challenging and amazing. Once you beat this boss you feel accomplished and proud of your skills as a trainer. Cherish this. This is the last time this format is used, and therefore, the last time you feel this way. Everything, and I mean everything from here to the final boss is memey and disappointing. Even the final boss is less of an epic crescendo and more of a "Oh. I thought I was fighting her, but I guess I'm fighting the big bad instead." and then you wipe it first try because of how incredibly easy the game is. After you defeat it, you never hear from the main cronies who have been harassing you all game. You don't even battle them once. It's like if Team Rocket just pulled up in every town, went "Nyeh you're gonna lose" and the game ended without even a "damn, you beat our boss, you got hands." Nope. Just credits. I finished the story in *maybe* 15 hours total, and that's generous. My runtime was spent primarily shiny hunting and getting ready for pvp. (Btw, the shiny system is tied to the IV system. A "perfect" shiny ,21 potential, has 126 points to distribute. Potent (16-20) has less, and so on and so on so you can see why a pvp focused player like myself would WANT to spend time catching mons.) Well, after sinking 20-30 hours into creating what I thought was a great team, I found out was time well wasted, because you can just hop into pvp and create whatever mon you want with perfect stats anyways. No point in spending gold giving it the perfect trait, hunting the perfect item, seeking out the TMS to give it the perfect moveset, dumping hours into finding the perfect potential 21 mon. Nope. Go catch one, hop into pvp, add it to your "team" and you can change every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ detail besides it's color.Now all of this, and honestly, ALLLL of this, I could ignore if the main game mechanic wasn't so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. Remember PP? From Pokemon and most other monster tamers where you can use a move a certain amount of times? They replaced that with SP, which is like a stamina bar for your mons. Hoollyyyy Sh*t, it is so fun being down to your last mon in pvp or pve, getting ready to use the move that will net you the victory, pressing X where the "Fight" button once was and immediately, without notice, skipping your turn to "rest" and gain half your SP back. So great.This game is, by no stretch of the imagination, hard. So you'll probably think "I'll just play on hard"Sure, have fun, if you like mandatory Nuzlocke... They could have literally just scaled every mon you fight up but 4-5 levels or something. Or allow the Ai to actually play the game and not spam "Increase my defense" when you're hitting it with Special attacks.... But nope. Hard is just Nuzlocke. Which is so easy to cheese because the AI is terrible.The literal only time I died and had to go revive all my mons is a 1v1 that happens in the last quarter of the game where a guy approaches you wearing an ice pokemon hat, says his favorite pokemon is an ice pokemon, his name is that ice pokemon's name, says "lets 1v1, only our favorites" and throws out a water pokemon, knowing you prob chose fire to counter ice... (remember that memey writing I mentioned?)People will swear by this game, but if it's so great why is no one playing it anymore? If you've been paying attention, you'll see I spent 15 hours on story, 20 - 30 on team building, so where's the last 5 - 15 hours?Sitting the pvp lobby.... There's no one on the game. The new Ranked season started, I won ONE game and I was top of the leaderboard for like 2 days. The only way to find any players besides the 1 or 2 you might find in queue is through the Discord. The Discord community is GREAT btw. (Not sarcasm. Honestly the only upside of this horrendous game) Very helpful, very awesome people. They helped me tweak my pvp team and everything, but it was pointless in the end because ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the pvp sucks. Especially with the SP system, it makes it tedious and irritating. I'm happy to put this game in my rearview and I only hope Steam lets me get my money back.EDIt: They did not give me the refund.

_childDocuments_.review: the coromon designs and sprite animations are very well done. unfortunately, thats just about the only good thing i can say about this game as a creature capture.i got the impression that this game tries to be Pokemon But Tougher, but i feel like it failed to address the parts of pokemon that are already slow in the first place and now made even more unbearable with coromon's big jumps in enemy levels, long routes/caves, and lack of money grinding options. making your way back and forth to the trainer hub gets really boring, really fast- especially when i have to grind for around 5 levels every time i get to a new area. the potency system doesnt help, if you have a team of normals just by luck, you will need to spend even more of your game time grinding. the story is also baffling in terms of writing, execution, and the fact that its very clearly unfinished at the end. the theme of technology is not well executed, npc dialogues are often internet jokes and dont add much to the world, and the villain team is completely disconnected from the world of coromon. i also feel like the writing in several areas like the desert and mining town also falls into overused and outdated tropes. i know creature capture games arent known for their quality narratives, but i feel like i need to mention it in this case, seeing as the devs advertised coromon as having a compelling story all this, combined with smaller issues like the attack animations taking so long, and using the gauntlet feeling so repetitive, makes the entire experience of coromon feel like a huge slog with little narrative or gameplay reward

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a game with beautiful pixel art and delightful music, and is definitely a neat spin on the monster catching/collecting/battling genre. I'm several hours in and have had a hard time putting it down. The monster designs are cute, and there are some unique takes that I think have great execution (there is a phoenix Coromon that turns back into an egg when it faints!). That said, this game is very much a grindfest. If you plan on getting into competitive PvP in this game, you will need to steel yourself for hours of RNG-filled wild encounters and soft resetting, as only the rarest of colors have the highest stats you will need to optimize your builds. It's like if Shiny Pokémon were the only Pokémon viable competitively, so anyone wanting to get into competitive battling would have to become a shiny hunter. Additionally, Traits, Coromon's answer to passive abilities, can only be changed by spending the game's currency and walking 1000 ingame steps. In a game where monsters can have up to 4 possible traits, it can take quite a while to get the right traits on your otherwise perfect monster.If you are a casual player, however, you should have no problem enjoying Coromon without feeling the need to optimize your team to perfection. A good strategy is usually enough to pull out of battles victorious, and it's always satisfying when you win a difficult fight.EDIT: Played further into the game and stumbled upon the most infuriating "puzzle" yet: a jump rope minigame and, of all things, Flappy Bird, both of which are REQUIRED for story progression. Both of these are things I actively avoid in games because frankly, I don't like them and I don't have the reflexes to be good at them. I find it somewhat unreasonable to, halfway through the game, require the player to play a game of highly specialized skill completely unrelated to what is otherwise a turn-based monster collecting game. I'm honestly kind of turned off from playing further just because of these being necessary for story progression.EDIT 2: With the recent 1.0.18 patch, the requirements for this segment of the game have been changed, making the jump rope minigame a bit easier to complete and changing the Flappy Bird clone to a more fun and engaging minigame. They also changed some mechanics that allow for players to more easily get Potent and Perfect Coromon, which does relieve some of the pressure of grinding and soft resetting. I think these are great improvements and I'm glad the devs have listened to fan feedback.7/10. WIth some quality of life improvements, this could be a truly great game, but I think the large amounts of RNG needed for optimization hold Coromon back from being as fun and engaging as it could be. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game after about 20 hours without playing the demo before (which let you keep your save)Overall thoughts:Solid creature collector game, stays true to the core of pokemon like creature collector games while also adding in its own spice that helps the game feel fresh. Sprites are pretty good, not the greatest ever some are generic but overall does the job for me. The names however are pretty bad but I really don't care about that so to each their own. The puzzles are good but very long and drawn out (you do a puzzle room and you feel like you're done only to enter another room and its the same puzzle again).The variety of monsters is super lacking, overall the variety is fine but when you're in a zone you only see monsters from that zone and 95% of trainers have a team of monsters from that zone so you rarely see monsters from the previous zone which gets boring and makes you just use 1 monster that will counter that zone. Speaking of counters the types in the game also are just weird. not bad, but weird. You have your general types but there's no grass type? the types are also singular and cant have dual type yet certain coromon can learn moves of all different types (started with fire starter and beat the game with him having 1 fire move 1 rock move 1 poison move and 1 foul move). It makes things weird because they are implied dual types ie. flying coromon which isn't its own type but they can learn flying moves, or bugs that learn poison moves but are normal type or electric type? Just makes things really hard to predict around and hard to build a "dream comp" because even though its fire type it might know water moves!The module system is nice but also pretty useless i don't think i used the stink module once cause it only makes 1 area of grass repel monsters? like what. Mostly just use the push module the rest are only used when the game wants you to. Literally learn the rock break module to use it 1 time for the story and that's it. Overall the animations are really good I was pleasantly surprised but they get pretty annoying because they are very long and theres no battle speed options so battle can be SLOW and i mean SLOW.Also this game is a grindfest make sure you got your hp cakes or be ready to do a lot of running back and forth you will fight battle after battle with no breaks in between. and the battles are tough sometimes, especially since you cant buy repels you have to make it with some weird recipe it just means sitting in A LOT of fights you wish you weren't in and towards the end of the game you will fail to run away more than you will succeed. The game is very good overall, it was good enough for me to sit through 20 hours and beat the game however with all the things mentioned above I found myself rushing to beat the game and not exploring much anymore because the battles and puzzles become tedious very fast. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 7th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.It’s PokemonCoromon has such an obvious influence it even ends in Mon.  But at the same time, it also does things everyone wants to see.  This has a customizable difficulty with interesting choices like limited heals at the doctors, limits to monsters you can catch, and more.  Every character also gets a trait when it’s caught and those traits can make two similar creatures vastly different.  There’s also the ability to customize the stats of your creature and so much more.  Compared to the main genre which feels like it’s stagnating at times, Coromon feels like the breath of fresh area the fans of the genre are begging for. But at the same time, it’s Pokemon with most of the same negatives.  You’ve seen much of this idea before, and while there are tons of fresh moments, the majority of the game is leveling up monsters, fighting x number of bosses, this time you fight Titans or something, and while there are new abilities, you will feel like you’ve done this before.  Also, there are only 124 monsters here, and while there’s more content in other areas, having fewer characters than the first Pokemon game is a weird choice.  I know, this probably has more animations or art requirements, but It still feels odd. Pick this up if you like Pokemon.  This is a pure Pokemon style game, but it’s also so well done and does enough new that fans who may have been burnt out on the main series will probably find something fresh here.  At the same time, it’s not going to change most players' minds if they aren’t already fans of Pokemon. _childDocuments_.review: A very endearing little game! If you like pokemon, you'll like this. The graphics hold a note of familiarity, and the gameplay/ fight mechanics are also similar in style. Different to pokemon is the multitude of little add-ins that improve the basic idea of the game. For example, as well as having money and your (knock-off) pokemon to play with and find, you can grow little berries that you can give to your coromon or use to make potions; solve unique puzzles within the game (not too complex, but make life interesting); and even dig for gems to sell or give to your coromon. There are also lots of hidden things you can find just by looking in every setting. I thought each town was really well thought-out, and I thoroughly enjoyed trying not just to get rare coromon but also the slightly different spin it has on the monster collecting style that pokemon is famed for. The music is reminiscent in genre to pokemon, but the game is definitely individual enough to be given credit as its own thing. Have already spent a lot of hours (and have a lot to get through) just by passing the time doing these little things that improve the experience. Highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good but not Great:This is a good monster collecting game, and one of the top ones that can satisfy your need for more additions in this genre. At this price, it is a steal deal. Pixel art is great and the Coromon all look very well designed. I think this is the first game in this genre where I haven't disliked a single monster. The puzzles are amazing, and all the biomes feel natural and fun to explore. The shinnies are phenomenal! It has some very fun game modes and settings too. Totally worth spending time on, and probably the best implementation of any game in this genre.But that doesn't mean it can't be better. First let's talk about the world. It is okay but I felt that the world grew tinier and tinier the more i progressed into the story. The first two location(cities/towns) were well populated but after this, you are basically going into a new location and expecting to talk to 5 strangers and walk into 2 houses. It felt rushed to me. Each new location gave less than what the previous one had and honestly it just never got me immersed into the game. The biomes were made well but none of them felt connected. As a player I always felt teleported to a new one.Next, let's talk about the plot. It is not great, and it feels forced into the story as though the team never had planned any and just added an antagonist force and blended it with the plot. Aliens? C'mon, anything is better than that.Next, we should talk about quests. They were good and well fun to complete but often times I hated the rewards. Clothing and certain battle items were loved but berries and cakes and spinners? No. Even the Milestone rewards and Gold Chests in the over-world began to fall back as I progressed more. Nothing felt worth it. Even skill flashes which were a dope addition, never felt useful. Most ones you could get sucked and even after reaching the frost biome, there is like 2/25 skill flash that I actually found useful. More of them need to be distributed throughout the game.Finally, the Coromon and their skill distribution. There are some coromon who only learn moves of the type they are and then there are some with decent coverage. Why not give all coromon some coverage? That part is missing to me and that too felt rushed. Like the devs game attention to some and just left the others as is. If skill flashes are poorly distributed through the main game, at least the coromon should learn more by themselves. These may all seem like nitpicks but as a casual player, I enjoy such additions very much. So much so that, without these additions, both me and my friend who got the game had to quit playing around the "Ice Mountain" biome because we were simply bored. If some of these don't matter to you, then Coromon might be the best monster taming game you might have played in a while. And it is still, as is, very much worth every dollar. I hope some of these nitpicks can be heard in future instalments in the series as I am very much interested in seeing more from this studio! Good luck!
