_childDocuments_.review: Well, I bought the game on sale for 10€. For that price, it's really good. Probably one of the best 10€ games you can get. But if someone pays more... oh boy.The game is ANNOYING. I mean it exactly as I say it. The story mode is a "Free Play" with a tutorial upfront. I eventually started clicking away the dialogues because the German translation is really poor and, as a stylistic choice (fitting the setting), it's interspersed with some Spanish talk. Since I don't speak Spanish, it's just incomprehensible gibberish to me (which is not translated into English or German, so you don't know what was said). This wouldn't be a problem if the texts weren't so endlessly elaborate. Every text bubble, every dialogue, everything in the game is like a small book (like this review :P).In essence, it doesn't matter because every quest in the game boils down to "bring X goods to location Y." It gets tedious after 5 minutes. The difficulty level is, de facto, non-existent. The game practically bombards you with money, and it never stops. After 60 minutes, all my underground bunkers, villas, airports, and ship harbors are bursting with money, so I went through phases of just demolishing all buildings and letting the game run in the background at full speed to launder black money into legal money. The game has absolutely zero balancing.Annoying point number 1: The enemy AI is just there to annoy you. The cops are just there to annoy you, always in pairs. That means if you mess with a hostile gang, you can bet money that in the background, the cops will disable your operations, even if you have 0 attention. And if, like me, you have no buildings left because you're waiting for black money, then it becomes apparent how poorly scripted it is. Because the cops still come even when you're practically doing nothing. If they don't have production facilities to raid, they'll take something else that belongs to you. Whether it makes sense or not doesn't matter. The main thing is they always come when you have trouble with a hostile gang.Annoying point number 2: When you demolish buildings, a piece of road always remains. You then have to painstakingly demolish it separately. With 200 buildings, you have 200 small pieces of road hanging at the entrance road. Have fun!Annoying point number 3: The granularity of this game is so annoying. You build a new warehouse, and it automatically connects to everything within reach. You then have to manually disable it in every supplier. If, like me, you build super compact, the list can be 60 points long. And this "generate extra work" aspect really permeates every aspect of the game. Whether it's a quest where you have to manually bring counted goods somewhere or buy TVs and game consoles manually in a bar menu, of which you can only buy very few at a time because... well, there's no reason except deliberately making it annoying.Annoying point number 4: As mentioned in point one, the AI is only there to annoy you. In plain language, it means they neither build production buildings nor do anything else. Enemy gangs occasionally send a troop by, that's it. And you don't even have to react because they just go bang bang a bit and then leave again. Just like that. But what's even more annoying is that the cops only annoy the player. As mentioned, they always come when dealing with gangs and occasionally without any understandable reason. But only to the player. The enemy AI never has to deal with the cops. Coupled with the fact that they always come together with the enemy, it creates the impression that there is no difference between gangster and police.In terms of content, the game only consists of putting farms side by side. You then choose which drug to produce there and may need another one to four buildings to refine the drug. All of this is then provided with the two always identical logistics buildings (logistics office and warehouse), and that's it. No matter which drug you produce, the process is always the same. But why even change the drug? There's no reason. Regardless of the drug you choose, the profit margins are so absurdly large that there's no reason to optimize anything. After a few minutes of playing, you have so much money that you have to start burying it (literally), or the buildings will overflow.Have you noticed that many people write something like "I only sold avocados" or "I became the vegetable cartel"? It sounds humorous but is simply a valid game strategy to avoid the mountain of annoying details in the game. You just produce fruit and sell it. Money is not an issue in the game anyway, but in the case of vegetables, you don't have to wash them beforehand. And since salaries or ongoing costs are practically imperceptible, it's just the much better way to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: For the person reading this hoping it's the cartel management game they've always dreamed would be released... here it is baby.Nothing quite as satisfying as watching a convoy of trucks carrying 100 kilos of cocaine stuffed inside a chicken drive right past the Federales convoy on their way to t1tty f*** your cocoa farms.Or burning down a warehouse stacked to the ceiling with cash rather than letting the DEA seize it.So much potential for this game. I played the demo months ago and literally called out sick the day it dropped.That being said she needs work. A lot of work. Why in the name of god can a semi truck only hold $5k? The bottlenecks in this game are unbelievable. At the peak of my cartel I was laundering about $100k/day and that wasn't enough to keep up with the amount of meth and cocaine I was slinging.My factories were running around the clock pumping out more meth than my little smugglers could handle. At one time the DEA seized a port with over $250k in cash and close to a metric ton of narcotics, and I wasn't even mad because I'd been trying to move the money for weeks. Logistics need to be overhauled so we can launder and stash money more effectively. Also, please give us the ability to hire sicarios when we need them. No reason my multi million dollar organization should be low on man power. I've got an 80 year old woman helping me capture enemy landing strips because she's good with a machete apparently. Hired guns should be easy, I should be able to hire a few lieutenants and their crews without effecting my cartel's roster.Muscle should be kept separate from administrative, or make it easier to organize within the cartel itself. Another thing. For the love of God please work on the stash houses or "residences" and make them fill your laundering facilities capacity, not just drop off a few grand. I had 4 stash houses placed outside my most active port and they would continuously reach capacity and attract attention while my banks and casinos literally minutes away are sitting at half full.Besides that, freaking amazing game. I've been wanting a good cartel sim since I was like 8 years old and first tried cocaine. Keep up the good work, and once all the little things are worked out give us more involved smuggling, like different routes and territories. I want to fight over control of different export territories. More in depth gang wars would be fun too, it's very easy to avoid attention if you're careful, but forcing us into bloody conflicts with other gangs would be very fun. I want to kidnap lieutenants, do drive by's on their territory, TP their grandma's house, black mail their politicians, all that.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute waste of potential, this game is.  It instantly reminds me of and makes me feel the pain, which was Evil Genius 2.  If you love to play a game with a half-hearted build/logistics model, dumb-as-rocks AI, and useless events/goals ... this is your game.  This is Evil Genius 2: Narcos Edition (not to be confused with the original classic "Evil Genius")  It is extremely shallow and barely rises above a mobile game.  The AI is non-existent and poses zero threat.  You can literally not attack once, and the AI will zerg you, woefully outmatched if you lean heavily into an assault-focused lieutenants, until it/all gangs commit suicide (they lose 1 power per loss -- zero = death/gang removal).Teching, focusing past the base opium drug to higher tier meth and coke ... pointless.  Spamming opium plantations, without a further need of refinement/tech, will keep you overloaded on dirty cash, which bottlenecks at the very few buildings you can build to clean money (banks and casinos -- the only two worth building)  you will have millions in dirty money, and slower than a snail, clean the money in mere thousands.Please don't get me started on the "logistics."  Non-existent.The artwork, graphics, music are amazing.  However, this game also has the audacity to give you a disclaimer referencing the 1980's trug trade, circa Pablo Escobar.  What a bait n' switch.  It's not deep enough for actual, intelligent gameplay and rated Peggy 13, at best.

_childDocuments_.review: After a good 30 hours or so in this game, I have some issuesFirst of all, had a blast for about the first 15. Learning all of the production flows and logistics systems was fun.Once that feeling wore off, I started to see all the systems and was left really disappointed.First of all, gang attacks are dumb. I couldn't spend any time setting up better working production chains because I was attacked every 2 minutes. Granted I was playing at the fast speed, but it was extremely annoying to take everyone off their jobs to defend my Aerodome for the 100th time only to spend 3 minutes after the fight putting everyone back where I had them (god I would kill for a button to "Return All" or something.Second, the other gangs aren't simulated at all. Once I realized this my immersion in the game dropped tremendously. You can capture their export routes, you can capture their farms and production, but they will still remain as strong as they were before. Not seeing any other trucks/vehicles in the map should have hinted at this but I guess I was too involved with my own stuff to care.The diplomatic approach seems severely broken. I could sweet talk all the gang leaders and have them at zealous level but they still would not join. There should be options to force gangs into cooperating. I don't want to send all my people to kill every single opposing gang just so they stop attacking me.Lastly, without customizing sandbox options, Lieutenants will continuously ask and ask for more money while their loyalty falls. This led to extremely highly paid people that offered nothing in return. You can't fire anyone, only murder them, which makes everyone else's loyalty drop leading to a never ending cycle of pay raises.TLDR:Have option to stop gang attacks or make them less frequent.Simulate other gang economies (you're the only one building, exporting, producing).Add diplomatic options to force gangs to join or cooperate. The dialogue system becomes tiring and seems too random.Stop endless pay raising and loyalty drop among your people.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think my play time is sufficient enough to give a full, in-depth review but in the 8-ish hours I have played the game, I have thoroughly enjoyed it! As it stands, this is a very difficult game, but the devs have a plan for that and every update brings balance fixes which do lead to longer play sessions. But, it is still a very challenging and punishing game - you will lose, in many different ways, but you will definitely lose (watching all your meticulously planned production lines slowly deteriorate into chaos and flames is actually a really fun part of this game). There is one area that potentially needs more balance at the moment: Terror. It goes up FAST and once it is up, you will not make money fast enough to bribe a mayor to bring it down (the drop isn't even substantial enough to justify the bribe and the loss of Loyalty). As for the usual goat/10 stuff people expect in reviews: - Top Down / 10 - Appropriate / 10 - Loopy but really fun to listen to / 10 - Get a pillow to scream into / 10 - Go read a book / 10 Ok just one comment on the story aspect: It's there, characters have backstories, there is a "Story" game mode but as this is a tycoon game, how you play generally informs how your own particular story unfolds (more applicable in sandbox mode since "Story" mode exists). Overall, it's a lot of fun, challenging and has TONS of potential, with a decent amount of replayability (the map is the same, but you can choose where to start - some areas are harder, some easier etc).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on Cartel Tycoon. I think there is a good game in here somewhere, but currently there are too many nuisances for it to be enjoyable.The short overview of the game, you are the Capo of a Drug Cartel. You build production and delivery chains to smuggle drugs, which give you dirty money. You then ferry said dirty money to cities, where it is laundered into legal money. You research new industries and upgrades to make everything bigger or better, and have lieutnants and your own character who can drive around the map to either help your production/delivery, or fight enemy gangs and occasionally the cops.Currently, there are these major issues that break the game for me. And this is after giving the game a lot of time to try to convince me otherwise:- Lieutnants will give you random quests. Failing, or even declining to do them, results in a loyalty loss, that must be compensated with a payraise. These missions are random. Lieutnants can suggest something you were going to do anyway, or a mission that is effectively just free benefits... or they suggest completely inane, stupid stuff that makes absolutely no sense. Why would I build a new Aerodrome? No, better question, where would you want me to build it? We have one region and there is literally no place where it will fit.The dumb part is that they are never related to anything you are doing, or your current situation. And they can literally come one after the other. "Give us all a medium payraise!" demands a random new lieutnant, even though everybody is at high loyalty. Which means either just accepting that you will suddenly spend a massive amount of extra cash on upkeep, or take the loyalty hit. It's stupid.- The logistics and production amounts are incredibly annoying to balance. This goes for both the laundering of cash and the export of drugs. The game encourages a "More, bigger, faster" approach to empire expansion, especially with research. But you will rapidly run into constant issues of full storage. How many farms do I need to supply a drying rack, without having my transport company or warehouse overloaded? How many Opium farms can I afford in relation to my export? Normally this should be an engaging question. Instead it basically amounts to "Produce until full, turn production chain off, wait until everything is sold. repeat". If you try for diversity instead of specialization, you will REALLY resent this later in the game.Same goes for laundering. There is just no engaging way to try for a blanced input to output ratio, other than just turning everything off and on again occasionally.- The game does not encourage production diversity enough. Opium and dried cannabis are all you will need, ever. If you research upgrades to your smuggling points, you can export so much of the stuff that you never even need to take a look at anything else. The basic River pier / Aerodrome can eventually ship such an absurd amount of stuff, that sinking prices don't matter. And that's before I mention that certain lieutnants have an abilty that lets you sell the produce at markups. I was rich beyond anything I could ever spend without needing to touch cocaine or meth. Which is a shame.- Lieutnant management is tedious. They want a promotion or raise regularly, and the only way to do this is to just open their individual profile and raise it manually. The limited cartell slots also mean that eventually certain Lieutnants escalate their pay to dizzying heights, at which point the best thing to do is have them shot or sent to prison. You will never really get attached to any of them, and it's a shame that the only interactions you ever have with them are almost all negative (I.e. having to raise their pay constantly, them giving dumb missions etc.). The Lieutnants that want a certain terror level above 0 are especially crap, since there is no reason to play that way. The fact that they lose loyalty if you don't play suboptimally makes them annoying, and not worth bothering with.All in all, a lot of this is really fixable. And if you are happy with excessive micromanagement, the game can be fun. But for me, it heavily depends on what the future of the game looks like.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a relatively new fresh idea, but implementation is just too poor. I have enjoyed it for several hours (~100 hours on steam record were counted due to game launcher hanging in background), and then it became too boring due to several issues:Gameplay is repetitive, unchallenging and just too simple once you learn the basics. You actually don't have to produce anything but basic opium to earn millions of dollars and conquer entire map (except some mayors' quests that require you to deliver dried cannabis and cocaine). You don't need all the export points after you research and upgrade single river port to tier 3. You receive the repeating boring quests every X minutes. They are too easy when you have plenty of money and too irritating and unhelpful if you're developing your main supply chain. Speaking of supply chains, they are also very simple and unchallenging to build and maintain.Fun fact: you can actually make money without producing and selling illegal goods. Guess what? You'll still be f***ed up by government when your products are marked as "suspicious" for no reason and you won't have spare cash to restructure your bisunesess.Late game is also disappointing: now new mechanics, just game freezes and scaling up your production to further scale up freezes and get more pointless money which you already have more than enough in mid game.To conclude, I wouldn't say that the game is worthless, it just has nothing to offer except an interesing setting. Otherwise, there are plenty of other supply chain simulators with much longer, more complex and interesting gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Not terrible, but not good enough right now. It's a bit slow initially, needing a lot of repeated manual actions until you accumulate enough money to research buildings that help run things smoothly, like residences, better roads, bigger trucks, etc. This is made worse because the controls are clunky too. For example, you cannot cancel a character's action in the middle, and some actions are repeated automatically. Say you ordered a character to deliver money somewhere, he did, and then you realize he picked up another load to the same place, which you don't want. You click "stop delivering" because you want him to stay guarding the city, but he keeps going, completing the delivery and then just sitting at the destination instead of returning to the city he is supposed to be watching. A city not watched by a character eventually gets attacked and you lose it AND get a lot of terror, which starts various agencies investigating you, a status you can only get rid of by your capo's death. By the way, there's no intermediate saving, only "save and exit". All this trouble because the controls are not great. The concept is unique and there are some interesting mechanics that aren't in other games, like overflowing building capacity bringing heat on you and a heavy incentive to operate without attracting attention which is then very difficult to get rid of. Maybe it will be good some day.

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a 2 out of 10, and here's why. It really boils down to two reasons.The biggest reason is that it requires unsustainable micromanagement, beyond what you are capable of doing in the game. Your men (the trucks going to and from farms, warehouses, transport companies, etc.) are always either doing too little of something, or too much of something. You are always producing too much product, or not enough. You always have too much dirty money, or too little. And somehow you never have enough warehouses. Even with an independent transport company dedicated to each one. Doesn't work, I tried. And all of these issues will end up piling up on top of each other, resulting in an almost unsolvable mess. I've tried many different strategies to remedy this, and nothing really ever seems to work. I can't even imagine the logistics of producing something more than weed, given the logistics hell of just getting illegal goods to ship properly inside legal goods. Which is too bad, because there's quite a few illegal products to produce. But in the 10 hours I've put in, I have yet to even touch those products because of how much of a pain handling beginner products is.The second reason is that the power of your lieutenants is so low, they are basically worthless in a fight with another cartel. The enemy cartel will always roll in with 20 or so strength, and with 7+ lieutenants, I'm lucky if I can break 15 power. I guess you're just...meant to lose every time. Which really doesn't make sense. Oh and while you're busy losing, that raises terror, which sends the cops in. And guess what, they almost always overpower you too. And don't even get me started on the horrible balancing act of sacrificing all your respect to lower terror...So ultimately, this game gets a 2 out of 10 for very poor scaling and just...terrible to handle micromanagement. Which is too bad, because I really wanted to like this game. And before you think, "oh well he's just bad at playing sim building games," NO that is not the case. That is my bread and butter. I've been playing macro and micromanage sims for over 15 years, and this one is the first that I have had to put down due to piss poor design. The devs could probably fix the scaling of enemies in a future update, but unfortunately I doubt the management could ever get fixed without a complete overhaul.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon has been a lot of fun thus far. It's a Management Simulation game with a story-line (even though I fail regularly at trying to pronounce Spanish words! Eek!) and I couldn't be more thrilled with it.  You start out accepting a job from a mysterious figure who gives you a residence and has you selling "flowers" (opium!) as well as setting up a money-laundering ring. The tutorial is easy to understand without being cumbersome or frustrating to get through, so you feel like you're playing as you're learning instead of waiting to pass a checkpoint. The dialogue is interesting and extremely well written. Plus, the game is absolutely gorgeous! If you're fond of management simulators I would absolutely recommend checking this one out! There looks to be a lot of different zones to explore so I'm enthusiastically looking forward to continuing playing! Thank you so much to Tinybuild and Moon Moose for offering me a key to this wonderful game! This review is an initial reaction from my first bout of game play, so if I have anything to add later, I'll just edit this review. Be well! Enjoy, and keep your enemies at bay <3Edit: I've sunk quite a bit of time into this game this week, failing and restarting.  It is a very hard game to master, but once you do, it's actually really easy to increase your money gain to a point where you cannot launder it fast enough. The trick to the game seems to be to never allow your threat to hit the second star, which is fairly easy to manage if you bide your time and pay off the reporter fast enough (I took to hording money in the actually city so paying her off was a lost faster) Overall, a very fun game once you figure out a way to manage the frustrations (the attention of the police, the second star, makes the game damn near impossible. Let alone when you've got the military blowing up your crops!) The game could definitely use some balancing, but overall, still a very fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: SANDBOX FIGURED IT OUT! Tips to help you have a more enjoyable sandbox experienceWas very frustrated after lots of failures sometimes slow agonizing failures but here's some tips that may help.Start off very cheap hire Novatos there free and some have great perks also these perks are random so you can  keep restarting your sandbox until you get multiple Novatos with useful perks like producing opium in half the time.Make a deal perk is great and can really make you some profit so find at least one LT that has it if possible... this perk is harder to find on Novatos but having a Halcon with this perk will make you more money and really set you up for success Build everything in your hotel radius early on so you can use dirty money to pay upkeep instead of your good clean money NO AERODOME early in the game unless you start with it as apart of your city, early on this will crush your budget instead opt for workshops that conceal your product then take through legal ports like seaports etc.DO NOT GROW TOO FAST this is how you draw attention to yourself and add stars... take your time to grow. Focus on one product at a time, have a good flowing operation that is bringing in money then start to plan your next product.YOU DO NOT NEED RESEARCH CENTER all the time after a certain point in the game, you can stay in one city research what you need then destroy it and built another money laundering business instead so 2x the money laundering in one city.At one point I had too much money to store anywhere and I was loosing cash fast and drawing attention at the same time so this is the time to expand but again slowly not drawing attention moving to a new city and dealing with a new mayor or gang.Hope this helps you all at least a little.

_childDocuments_.review: There is some potential here, honestly there is, but the game is pretty frustrating as a "workflow simulator.  This has significant issues with balancing and a poor tutorial that does not teach you how to manage making money correctly in the game. You are frequently attacked by overpowered rival gangs that you have no hope of fighting back. There is no way to permanently reduce your terror stars, creating a game system that is designed for the player to lose. Buildings and lieutenants have prohibitively expensive upkeep costs and lieutenants do not do enough to support gameplay as you often need to simply park them in bases to prevent losing control. Everything is wildly expensive but it takes a stupidly long time to actually launder money with your limited amount of trucks, even with lieutenants who have truck buffs. However, there is no way to know this by playing for less than two hours because the gameplay loop takes so long to understand whether you are doing well or not. This game needs a lot of balance before it should come out of early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon just left E.A. so i wanted to give it a try. I normally dont do recently released games and rather let my games 'mature' more but i had a tropico like itch that needed a scratch. The focus of this game is more tycoon/tropico like and less fighting. Taking sites over is just a simple numbers game at the moment. Have one more offence point and you win a fight in the end. Violence begets you a terror rating, get to high and your operations will get seized/closed. So getting 2 aggressive is not a viable option.The tutorial needs some work as many comment it doesnt bring the basics needed to succeed and i agree. Just wish reviews would get a tag saying its an E.A. review as they have done so much work and really payed attention to the reviews good and bad. Even when i started playing my first few days and had issues or things i didnt like. Loading my save a few hours or a day later and my issue was fixed or changed.It took me at least 10 hours to get a grasp on things and after that you could clearly see the possibilities for this game. Just go slow, adding 3 dopium farms might sound good but when you can't sell em or repackage em quick enough your full warehouses attract attention and the law will come pay you a visit.You really gotta micro manage your warehouses and transport companies a bit but after that i was making money by the boat loads. (Small Tip: Struggling with the logistics ? Just make small virtual islands for yourself with one type of product chain and dont let them interact with another production 'island' unless you start to get your head around the way warehouses and transport companies works.)One of the cooler things is that you can 'buy' the peoples respect with heavy bonuses by building churches and such. This game has so many cool and new ideas (not all perfect tbh) in my book that it certainly deserves a look when you love the early tropico or similar games.I would like to mention that the soundtrack is a masterpiece , it perfectly fits with the game and has a very relaxing vibe to it.Things i would like to see:Fights just needs more to it then a simple numbers game. Pay off cops, federales to come fight for me or send em after rival gangs.Possibility for blockades so you can stop advancing police or rival gangsNo terror for legal goodsMore things to do with your underlings: Train, fire them, have the possibility to don't die or be arrested, more options in generalBridges or transport boats for logistics.Laundering operations draw attention when the money is full (should be when its over full capacity)The possibility to cancel a move or other order in transit.When underlings are on transport and the site gets attacked they shouldnt die or get arrested as they aint there.A possibility to upgrade all buildings from a type on the map or per province at once. (Later game this get tedious)Why can i build only one building at a time. I' am a business man and time is money.Possibility to 'starve' a rival gang (when taking away everything they own, the strenght should go down sporadicly).There is only one thing i realy don't like and that is the fact that gangs get power when you take over a city. I got stronger and have boat loads of money, you guys stay the same and you get a big bump in power.  I understand for the game why its in place but it doesnt make any sense.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of drug dealer simulator I was really excited to play this game because I got it in a bundle with said game. I was hoping it would be that game but on a larger scale. While this was the case once I finished my first play-through I felt mixed. First I went through 3-4 different games before getting my winning run. It was a fun journey of learning how to use each built and mechanic in this game in order to make tons of money. The learning curve was large but it felt decently manageable. That was until I got to the mid game. Early game is fun. You either are focusing on building up your opium or weed farms along with packaging them with everyday items in order to maximize profit. However once you move onto territory expansion and anything above weed the game kinda starts to fall apart. Territory expansion is done by doing favors for the mayor of a city followed by then taking it over. Some favors are fine like cleaning up gangs and illegal buildings but some require and member in the cartel to have a certain ability which makes the game frustrating. Because they will sometimes request a character to kidnap someone or kill your own members. The main issue I have is that there is no hostile take over mechanic. Which I would love cause I spent about 1-2 hours leveling up a guy just to get one skill only to find out that I can't promote him because the hierarchy is too limited. You can only have 14 members in your gang but the problem is that 5 are only useful for deliveries, 4 are have one sort of good skill, and the other 5 are best used in micro managing. I get why the tree is so small but it makes the game feel too slow and puts you into holes where you have your whole gang set up but because no one can kidnap you have to remake the gang. Now granted there is a starter character with those skills but I don't want to pick a Capo based off the convince of the game I never played before. It show be based of what I think would be interesting for the gameplay style I want. But at least there's a building who give people who can do that without taking up a slot. But remember that's very important for the next thing that makes the game fall apart. Every drug above weed. The first two drugs aren't that bad they are cheap to sell cheap to make. But that's not going fast enough I need some coke. Coke started off fine but the value of it is so high that when you start getting boxes filled with the stuff you get tons of dirty money. Too much. Laundering is not fun in this game. The best building is the bank which does and average of 3,000$ a day and each city can only have one with early game opium and weed it's not that bad heck even if you send it out in packages it still covers it but everything above that makes so much money the bank can't launder it quick enough. After a week of coke production I maxed out my bank. So I built a casino which does I think 300-500 less. Filled it up. At that point your only choice is the cache which has money go rotten if in the cache for too long. It feels like a tycoon game that punishes making money. But you can micromanage but the reason I bought this game was to make a big auto Cartel. Final point I have is gang leaders. There are two ways to deal with them kill them or hire them. Do not hire them. It is way easier to kill leaders than hire because hire requires full respect from them which you get a small amount of every 15-30 minutes which is too long. Overall it had a fun start but sorta got confusing and stressful near the end. I do not intend on playing this game again for a little while because the amount of prep I didn't know but expected to have was too much and slowed the game down. It is not worth the 30$ price but it is worth the on sale price of 10-12$. I don't have any plans to buy the dlcs

_childDocuments_.review: Aug 3, 2022 EDIT: This game is getting way too many downvotes from clueless people. I see people complaining about certain things but they just simply don't understand how to play the game, so they think the game isn't working right. There are several QOL issues in the game, but many things aren't broken so much as unclear -- everything in easily manageable as long as you know what you are doing. There is negligible tedium.This game has a number of very well-thought-out touches that impress me and catch me off-guard. For example, I found the terror system too forgiving. I wanted it to punish me more. Well, the sandbox mode lets you adjust all sorts of things like that. I set terror to 250% normal, and wow, it's pretty close to the experience I wanted!Then I started feeling like it was too easy to smuggle things hidden in vegetables. After a few months of this in-game, I was so impressed to find that the authorities had started suspecting my vegetable shipments! Especially with 250% terror, this was strongly encouraging me to change up my operation and use something other than vegetables to hide things. Not only that, a few months later after I had pissed everyone off up to the CIA, they started outright confiscating any vegetable shipments I tried to send through a particular smuggling point. So cool! I was very happy to be placed under this kind of pressure.So many little touches like this really make this satisfying to play. ***The Story Mode is buggy, confusing, and terrible. You will be subjected to all manner of nonsensical twists - for example, you'll read a confusing story about your lieutenant shooting the mayor because he's aligned with the Guerrilla faction. It doesn't say which lieutenant it is. Then your leader executes the lieutenant. Once gameplay resumes, you are given the mission of executing ANY lieutenant. The reason? Because they're aligned with the Guerrillas. So you're given the story before the event happens, which is confusing. Then you're told to kill literally anyone, just because. And then whoever you kill, it's justified, because they were aligned with the Guerrillas. Huh?Anyway, the Survival Mode is great. This game needs a strong UI and QOL pass on certain things, e.g. you should be able to set sell priorities at your smuggling points and you should be able to set the storage of your laundering sites below max if you don't want them hog all your liquidity (i.e. you need some funds outside of the laundering circuit to fund upkeep and construction).Overall, a great game and deserving of a high rating. I trust they will polish in time, and I'd love a DLC or anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game so far is a very enjoyable management sim game. It's very relaxing and steady until the federales raid your farm and everything crumbles in front of you. The city building aspect is simplistic, but everything that needs to be there is, and it works pretty well.The game is also very stable, I only suffered one crash and it was because I tried to place an invalid road 30 times in under a second. The roads can be a bit finnicky.The UI, which is hugely important for this type of game, is mostly very good, though there is some info that would be nice to have, like daily financial info, rather than weekly and monthly, and maybe a screen that shows where all the storage is. These things could possible already be in the game and I just missed them, it took me over 3 in game hours to see where all Lieutenants are listed.The narrative in the story mode was surprisingly compelling to me. Might not win an oscar, but it is definitely a good driving force for the tutorial and quests.I've played 5 hours as of now, and I still feel like I have plenty of game left. And it seems like it would be a good replayable game as well.Definitely worth picking up if anything I mention interests you. If the devs add more to the game in the future, then that would make it an even better game to pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played cartel tycoon since the beginning. The game is in a much better state than it was on release and therefore I am very proud and grateful, as the game definitely has something to it. I find true enjoyment in the challenge that the game provides with certain mode and starting point combinations. When the numbers just keep creeping higher and higher and you've nailed the entire production to launder ration without anything overflowing, it is truly satisfying.My strategy before the fight and stash update mainly focused on getting my lieutenants as powerful as possible as early as possible and going to war on absolutely everyone, relentlessly fighting to erase all enemy gangs. With the addition of weapons and lieutenant stamina, taking a city by force has become much less attractive. My strategy totally changed. I only use weapons and lieutenants for defence and possibly for taking a building or two with valuable resources in it, otherwise it is much simpler to just burn the enemy buildings. I now make friends with rival gang leaders and then recruit them. I finished survival mode without any real trouble without having a single war. I find this ironic, as the fight and stash update was aimed at improving combat, it achieved the exact opposite. Attacking rival cities with the intent to eliminate the gang is a very bad decision. 30+ Power difference, 80+ weapons and still my lieutenants run out of stamina before the end of the war.... Seems stupid. All in all I am happy with the fight and stash update, as it opened a completely different strategy. I now see enemy gang leaders as recruit-able lieutenants and use this as a strategic element to gain an advantage or a needed lieutenant ability. I enjoy Cartel Tycoon immensely and I will continue to do so, as I wish to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those cases where I wish Steam had a NEUTRAL rating. I neither hate nor am fond of this game. I've played business sims for years now. I'm a master exploiter. As such, Cartel Tycoon is another game like that. If you've played them, you get it, and there's absolutely nothing new here. The only difference is that you've got a filthier theme and it's well-researched. 1980s narco trade in South America? Cool. But mechanically speaking if you're used to business sims you'll fly through it and I noticed a few bugs. In particular, transportation of goods is at times ineffective and outright broken. Playing through some earlier parts of the tutorial, in fact, revealed this strange issue where properly set up resources and pathways still yielded none of the requested results in spite of following things to a T. Those are easy fixes, however, the main issue is, if you're into these kinds of games, is it worth it? Honestly for a little, maybe, but since it's built on practically every tycoon game before it the kinds of people who'd even want to check it out will likely be disappointed in the long run. Thus, again, I wish I could give a NEUTRAL rating to this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon – The fix you have been looking for, or a bad trip?Cartel Tycoon sees you play the part of an up and coming Capo in a fictional South American Isle. Your goal, as the name suggests, is to build a thriving cartel while avoiding all the pitfalls that come along with the territory. The game begins with your character, low on funds and down on his luck, answering an ad for a business partner in a newspaper classified ad. A conversation follows that sees you partner with a mysterious individual in the flower selling business. How are your opium poppy growing skills?As with many tycoon/city builder type games, you begin with some start up capital which you need to invest. Buy some poppy farms and warehouses to store your product, set up local businesses to launder your ill gotten gains and bribe local officials for a smoother ride. Hire some lieutenants to protect your assets, deliver your shipments and help you expand your empire. All of the tropes that you would expect in this setting are present, and for better or worse there are no surprises in terms of the cast of characters and the plot. The graphics of the game are simple but good and I really enjoyed the hand drawn art style of the cut scenes, I just wish there were more of them. Most of the dialogue and story progression is in the form of text boxed telephone conversations, which after the introductory artwork was a bit disappointing.  In the game’s story mode you are led through some simple beginning missions to learn the various mechanics of the game and build the narrative and it was here that the game fell a bit short for me. The pacing of the early missions seemed a little slow and I felt like I spent too much time waiting for things to happen and accumulating resources/money. Whilst that is inevitable for this kind of game I wanted a faster pace in the beginning to hold my interest and get the hooks in and it just wasn’t there.It is worth noting that this game is in early access and is very polished given that fact. If you are a fan of the tycoon style games and like the idea of your own drug empire with none of the risk, then this is a very solid foundation to build from and is likely only to improve from here. That being said, if you are looking for something new and innovative perhaps this isn’t the game for you, at least right now. The storyline and mechanics bring nothing new to the table and whilst both work well and are entertaining enough, nothing stands out. There are quite a few features and mechanics that are in the roadmap for future updates and hopefully these will bring the variety and depth that this game needs to take it to the next level.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me be clear up front: if you can't tolerate Early Access titles that have a lot of problems, don't bother picking this up yet. The "rough edges" on this thing are like sandpaper. I'm not going to go through an exhaustive list of every awkward UI element or frustrating oversight in the game's mechanics, but buyer beware: there are many, and they need to be fixed.That being said, I had a ton of fun playing this and I'll certainly be back for more. This game is more than just another tycoon/management game with a pallet swap and a new aesthetic, this thing turns many of your tycoon-citybuilder-management-sim-whatever expectations on their heads to give you a genuinely new experience.For starters, unlike most tycoon games, where the key to success is maximizing the production of every building and pushing as much product out as possible while stocking all of your storage facilities to max, you can't do that here. You'll lose, and fast. Overproducing not only causes resources to be wasted, it attracts the attention of law enforcement. Any building that stocks an illegal substance to its max value has a risk of being raided, and your distribution points (seaports, airports, and border checkpoints) have limits on how much product you can safely move through them. You need to carefully  production, pushing it as high as you can [/i]safely[/i] get it, while making sure your warehouses never accumulate a surplus. Sometimes you may even need to burn a building down and run, so the less you have in there, the better. The key is to build light and safe, instead of big, and that's an interesting difference from most games in this genre.Secondly, you cannot (and  not) over-expand. To gain territory, you have to fight rival gangs for it, and this will quickly get the attention of higher tiers of law enforcement (think: GTA). To get around this, you have to think about what you can get with the least amount of work and what you can do with it; consider the tradeoffs of bribing officials to use a city without taking control of it, or hide contraband inside legal goods to pass them through rival territory unnoticed.And finally, the dirty-money/clean-money dynamic is pretty cool. You can pay for anything with either  money (in the bank, works electronically, and doesn't require an infrastructure to use) or  money, which you hide on your private property and, because it is cash-only, has to be physically moved from location to location by gang members. Dirty money is easy to get (you get it from all drug sales), but cant be moved through rival gang territory or through government checkpoints without paying a portion in bribes.To get clean money, you have to launder your dirty money, either by funneling it into service industries (taxicabs, churches, amusement parks) to create legal cover for its existence, or by calling in favors from politicians and paying them under the table at a premium. You can then use the clean cash to pay for legal services or support buildings without plugging them into your network. But you can avoid doing this if you are able to establish efficient delivery lanes from your sell-points to the locations where you want to pay your employees in cash, but remember that storing too much means it could get lost or trigger a police raid.Everything in this game is a balancing act, and that's what sets it apart from other tycoon games. The trademark of a lazy management game is the ability of the player to simply make more of everything and brute force their way through the story. Here, subtlety is a large part of the strategy and it gives the game that extra edge that it needs to really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early access version of a game called Cartel Tycoon. The name basically already explains what it's all about. It's basically a new city builder/strategy game with a rather "illegal" setting as you're the Boss of a cartel and with diplomatic and violent ideas you're basically trying to grow your organization. Keep in mind that Cartel Tycoon is currently in Early Access and available in the Steam store and available with its own unique TinyBuild launcher. The game was developed by Moon Moose and published by Release Date: 18th March 2021 (Early Access).Last known update: 10th April 2021.As mentioned RTS games aren't really my cup of coffee which means that I usually try to avoid them. But with this game, I had a sudden urge to play it, probably because I watched the entire Narcos series in one day and wanted to see how good of a drug lord I would be if I decided to lead a cartel. Jokes aside, this game looks and plays very nicely despite it still being in Early Access. It offers cutscenes with a protagonist and a pretty lengthy campaign as far as I could tell. Let's take a better look!Compared to the previous build of the game that I reviewed some months ago the developers did a fantastic job at making the tutorial a lot more helpful. Now you get a dedicated taskbar and a guide that explains everything in detail. Another addition was the fact that now you can hire lieutenants that can actually help out in various activities such as transporting goods, perhaps have a 20% income boost for a limited time or be able to make a robbery. All of these additions really made the game a lot more understandable and do-able.The map is divided into many cities and each city does have a Mayor/ Leader. Your main goal is to earn their respect by doing various tasks that will be presented on your lower left side of your screen. Lastly, I should note that violence isn't really the main theme of the game. It does not glorify the violent aspect of that lifestyle. Obviously, you do have some options. You can send a specialized member of your cartel to burn some buildings from the other cartels, you can even command another one of your members to assassinate an enemy. These are the main options when it comes to violence. The developers added gang wars that would activate once you have left one of your cities or buildings for a long time. You can capture it back if you got enough firepower which is why you should invest in some powerful lieutenants. One last occasion of violence occurs when you're out of legal money which means that you cannot pay anything. The result comes with the game over screen where the game explains that you tried to flee the country but got shot close to the border. The statistical aspects of the game are definitely the strong point of the game. I really loved the multiple options when it comes to illegal money laundry. There are quite a lot of buildings that do get the job done, going from placebo Taxi offices to Jewelry stores or even Circuses.  To go from raw product to legal cash is a long journey. First up you have to grow raw product on a farm (Opium), then a warehouse takes the Opium and stores it. If a lab is within reach the warehouse will then bring the Opium to the Airfield or Seaport. You can then theoretically ship it via plane or ship but the D.E.A might be sniffing around and investigate which will force you to stop using these buildings for some days. So then you have to hide the product somewhere between vegetables, coffee, or spices which I do consider a very deep and interesting aspect of the game. Basically hiding a small number of drugs in a box with coffee and smart things like that. These act as storage multipliers with a specific amount of available units respectively. After finishing a tour the drug money will be stored at the airport, harbor, or border post. After accomplishing all of that you can start with the entire "money-laundry" labour. Then it is yours to do with as you please. Keep in mind that in each area you do get highlighted efficiency areas and combined with the efficiency ratings from the buildings you can achieve a pretty tactical system of production. Once again the addition of gang wars and robberies will benefit the player a lot but what I really liked was the fact that you can speak to the lawyer of the city and ask for some help which can be about D.E.A confiscations, Loyalty, or even ask for a sum of money if you’re in deep trouble. SPOILERS AHEAD!You are a man called Cesar Garcetti and you have ended up in a city. You wander around and decide to call for a job. A mysterious voice starts speaking. After some jokes and business discussion, the mysterious man hands you the keys to start working with some plantations. After you have proven yourself worthy the mysterious man visits you. His name is Miguel Angel Gacha and he is basically one of your friends and the man that gave you a future as well as being your mentor. The game does not offer much of a traditional story but more so it tells a story with small discussion while talking about various events.These are the only things that occur. Everything else just feels like a sandbox RTS game and I am totally fine with that. Your goal is basically to become the strongest cartel in the country, simple as that.Keep in mind that the developers added some pretty nice cutscenes. I have to say that they really fletched out the story a lot more.The Visuals aren't anything new. It looks like a traditional RTS/City building game. On the contrary, it does look like a nice and tropical Latin country. The tutorial got much more user-friendly compared to the previous version I reviewed some months ago. The story feels a lot more imaginable than before where the entire storyline was structured around speech bubbles and text. Overall I can only give this game a very good rating, especially for Narcos and City Builder fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not normally do reviews, but I felt this particular game deserves one. Example, I never really relied on residences because the function to provide dirty money to every facility within range was not working properly, now it is. Also residences now seem to know when to stop collecting dirty money once its storage is full, that was quite annoying especially if it caused attracting the attention of law enforcement every single time. There are a few things I would like to see and hope that they can consider it. First off I like that you cannot just simply afk and make tons of money, I was angry at first cause it seemed like it was cool I can go to bed and wake up in the morning to find i have millions of dirty money and a few hundred thousand clean money. Nope, game pauses cause some cartel member wants a raise or promotion so that scratched that. While the game is called Cartel Tycoon, I still do not get the feeling I am in a cartel or at least running one. We have a nice Cartel family tree so to speak, but it's quite limited. As you progress and eventually have a money making system in place, you really do not need members who have money making skills, what you really need is members in your cartel with more combat or attack points. I have been trying to figure out how to keep myself from getting any terror stars, but every time I've attacked a city controlled by a rival gang it takes so long to take over that I always seem to get that first star. I have tried every trick i can think of, I've even hired several members just to have that extra fire power. You would think odds of 26 cartel vs 6 enemy gang would mean I should win relatively quickly, however that was not the case. Every city, and transportation point needs to have an officer stationed there or else it generates a meter indicating a rival gang member will attack it. This makes good sense, but again we are limited to members of our cartel. I do not feel at this time we have enough to cover the map, and as I already set as an example with combat, try taking over the map with less attack power because you need to keep people in place. I hope they will implement the ability to recruit not just officers, but perhaps troops or guards for each area. I know this is just a game, but when I see shows like Narcos on Netflix lol, those guys had some serious hired man power. Each lab, building, and residences all had guards. _childDocuments_.review: The game has issues in it's current state. It's tutorial is good at teaching you the basics of the game. The concept of the game is amazing, and it's gameplay has a great amount of promise. But the problem is, the tutorial is only good at teaching you the basics of the game. The concept is amazing, and the gamplay has promise. Let me explain.The tutorial gives you a good platform at the beginning, but you hit a brick wall around the 1.5 hour mark when stuff starts going wrong (I'll get to that later), and the tutorial has already passed. You see that your farms aren't doing anything, suddenly everything is falling apart because you built another building, and the logistics system just can't handle it. You don't know what to do other than demolish the building, and take a loss. It's frustratingly annoying and just doesn't work.The gameplay needs to be worked out. There are major balancing issues and issues relating to logistics that need to be worked out before this is a 25$ game. The once you get to the Police stage in the terror counter, you have entered a whole new world of hurt. If you don't want your stuff seized for 20 days you better hope you have a lot of people with a lot of power. The CIA holds true to what it's known for in blowing up everything it doesn't like, except instead of blowing up communism, it's blowing up your drug empire. Logistics in the story mode makes me want to pull my hair out. Luckily I won't need to due to my hair falling out naturally due to stress after trying to manage the logistical system. You'll suddenly find that your buildings no longer work for some reason you don't know about. You can't fix it. You can only hope that it stops before your people get disloyal and the DEA, Police, and Federales shut down all your stuff. I can't recommend buying it now, but if the developers continue to work on the game and implement community feedback, this is a game that would definitely be worth spending money on. Thank you for coming to my ted talk.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE the music in this game!!- have it running to listen to the music while I write this review.I'm not really sure where to start other than it needs a lot of polish. You may want to wait on a sale to purchase, unless you are like me and buy in because you like the idea and want to help support a company develop a new game. That said, I will just kind of touch on a few things I found annoying and limited my play time. I am not saying these things should change for sure, just saying these things made the game less enjoyable for me, and they may have reasons I didn't pick up on for being the way they are...-Paying employee- I like the choice of dirty or clean money, and especially product in a pinch, but I feel like they want money far to often. Since you probably need them moving something around, or at a place that doesn't have dirty money sitting around, they likely need to use clean money to be able to get paid while doing tasks. I like the system overall but it was to demanding to pay 8 employees or so anything other than clean money, unless they were sitting in town basically.-Building in towns- I feel like there probably should be more than 1 of each type per city, and more buildings per city. Some small balance there, to make it more enjoyable and feel more custom, and less limited. Just some tweaks to make it a bit more involved or something.-Micro managing of deliveries, especially money- This happened to me early, that I was not able to have enough people carrying enough money from my seaport to the town. Especially then from that town to the next one over, both of which have airports. (that cannot move money) That seems like a good option in my opinion, that if you have a port in each region, you should be able to move money easily between them. Or just let people carry more? Not sure how to tweak this without running into the next issue.-Money Management- I liked the problem of needing to launder the money. I just didn't feel like it was moving around as much as I would like, say, to fund the development of another region. It just takes far to long for employees to move money 8 or 12 thousand dollars at a time. Possibly the solution I present above for the previous problem solves this? Overall it feels like this game is promising, but has a lot of overall balance work needed. Which from the frequent update pace it looks like they are working hard on. _childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon offers an engaging gameplay experience, particularly in Sandbox mode, but it falls short in a few key areas. While the game itself is enjoyable, the story mode fails to capture the same level of interest. Having played through the tutorial and a portion of the story mode, I found it lackluster and not compelling enough to continue.Sandbox mode is where the game shines, providing the freedom to build and manage without the constraints of a storyline. However, a significant drawback is that not all features are unlocked from the start. In particular, the restriction on Cartel leaders and emblems is frustrating. For a mode meant to offer unrestricted play, having these elements locked behind progress feels counterintuitive.While I understand the intention of encouraging players to achieve milestones, this design choice detracts from the Sandbox experience. It reminds me of back in the early days of PlayStation Network on PS3, where the focus on grinding for achievements often overshadowed the enjoyment of the game itself. Despite these issues, I still HIGHLY recommend Cartel Tycoon, but it's important to be aware of these limitations.

_childDocuments_.review: ProsThe production of both legal and illegal goods is handled pretty well and having to manage your heat levels adds an extra challenge that other more traditional management sims do not.  The handling of clean and dirty money is also a new element to be mindful of and admittedly, took a bit of time to understand completely.  ConsYour lietenants constantly need to be paid more, which can be difficult when you can lose large parts of your business empire due to losing your boss to death/prison.  You also risk losing your smuggling sites and cities to enemy gangs with no way to guard against them at checkpoints.  Between the limited amount of hired hands you can retain at one time and the ever-increasing expense of their wages, your empire will be prevented from growing beyond a set size.  Compounding this issue is that your pool of hireable talent has no method to reject candidates you don't want.  While you can find people who will work for free or very cheap, you are often limited to choosing between 3 people who start out wanting higher wages.  Managing heat and threat levels needs a tweak imo as at current, once you attain a threat level like DEA or Police investigation, there is no method to permanently remove them except one which is both destructive to your empire in terms of lost businesses and zones and loss of personnel.  There is a mayoral favor you can do, but while it costs a lot, only results in a temporary reprieve of one threat.  Money laundering businesses need to have a setting to restart once they have been replenished with dirty money.  Recommendation to buy if you enjoy management sims and want something a little different from the usual business types, with the caveat that it is still in early access and could benefit from some QoL improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: This game and I have been on one hell of a journey. I played it for my channel and was completely lost at first. I'm not the best at following directions, but this game really felt like it left so much out of the tutorial that I had trouble grasping how everything worked. It took a few restarts before I started to understand the respect and law enforcement systems and how to balance everything. I tend to hurry through tutorials to "get to the real game" but here the tutorial is NOT meant to be finished, it's meant to become the basis for your future operation so take it VERY slow and hold off on completing objectives like a jackrabbit. Once you actually have a handle on how the game works, it's awesome. The learning curve though is STEEP. Maybe this is an ADHD brain issue and an issue with my play style being very brutish, but this isn't about going in fast and hard. Slow and steady wins this race. This game may not be for everyone, but it's become one of those I can't stop playing. There's a lot coming in the future as you can see from the developer's website, but even in it's current state it scratches the itch in my brain just enough to keep me coming back. I'm motivated by the money, but find myself constantly battling over the balance of dirty to legal - something that I actually like but may frustrate others. It's not an easy game to play and it's not quite as accessible as other games with the "tycoon" label, but this is a drug operation, son. Did you think things were gonna be easy? Overall I highly recommend this if you like complex games where you may have to restart multiple times. This is about getting it right and sometimes playing the hand you've been dealt ISN'T the right way to handle things. I suspect there will be many people who don't recommend this game because the learning curve at present (4/4/21) is VERY steep for some.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like the game more than I do, there is potential here but the game is marred by balance problems and strange design choices that just leave the game feeling too frustrating and chaotic to be enjoyable for extended periods of time.The game play feels far less like slowly building and expanding your empire, and more more like a messy juggling act where every step forward throws another ball in the mix and if you drop 1 ball everything comes crashing down instantly.Between mini quests, gang attacks, federal raids, stock control etc there is far too much micro to get anything useful done. There's always some more pop ups or events coming to ruin your day, or you know just prod you a bit while you're busy trying to do other things.If you try to do pretty much anything meaningful, the terror will rise to the point the feds will sporadically shut down your assets meaning you have to go through things 1by1 to shut them down so you don't create MORE terror from having full warehouses then switch them back on again when things calm down.The more you build and expand the more this happens meaning it's far easier and more manageable to have 1 small but efficient and high tech production line. Having multiple lines and export points etc very quickly becomes unmanageable due to the sheer amount of manual inputs and micro managing required for each one.So with this in mind you spend a couple of hours managing and researching this, set it up and... then what? You've got more money than you need, everything you need researched and things aren't rapidly collapsing on top of you due to your very small size. So why scale up? It only brings more problems and issues that usually mean you make less money, lose gang members, raise terror and have police on your back etc. It's way more efficient, safer, easier and usually more profitable to stay small. Even if you did choose to grow, there's nothing to spend the extra money on.There is 0 point to expansion and way to much micro management to make expansion fun on it's own. The game is essentially won or lost in the first few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆Cartel Tycoon, an indie strategy game that puts players in the shoes of a drug cartel leader, presents an intriguing concept with the potential for an engaging and immersive experience. While the game has its strengths, it falls short in certain areas, leaving room for improvement.One of the standout features of Cartel Tycoon is its unique setting and theme. The game dives into the dark and dangerous world of drug cartels, offering a different perspective and a departure from typical strategy game themes. Managing resources, expanding territory, and making strategic decisions to maintain control of the drug trade provide a sense of intrigue and challenge.The game's visual style and atmosphere contribute to its immersion. The hand-drawn graphics and vibrant colors create a distinctive aesthetic that captures the essence of the game's setting. The soundtrack adds to the overall ambiance, enhancing the sense of being a powerful cartel leader.Cartel Tycoon's gameplay mechanics provide a decent level of depth and strategy. Balancing production, distribution, and security while navigating the challenges of rival cartels and law enforcement can be engaging. The progression system, with its unlocks and upgrades, offers a sense of growth and advancement as players build their criminal empire.However, Cartel Tycoon is not without its flaws. The game's tutorial and learning curve can be overwhelming for newcomers to the genre or those unfamiliar with similar management-style games. The lack of clarity in explaining mechanics and objectives can lead to confusion and frustration early on.Furthermore, Cartel Tycoon suffers from repetitive gameplay and a lack of variety. Once players grasp the core mechanics, the gameplay loop becomes predictable and monotonous. The lack of diversity in mission types, events, and challenges hampers long-term engagement and can result in a feeling of stagnation.The AI in Cartel Tycoon is also lacking in depth and intelligence. The rival cartels and law enforcement agencies often exhibit predictable behavior, making encounters and interactions less dynamic and strategic than they could be. Additionally, the pathfinding and AI behavior for workers and vehicles can be inconsistent and frustrating, affecting the overall flow and efficiency of gameplay.In summary, Cartel Tycoon offers an intriguing concept and visual style that immerses players in the world of drug cartels. The gameplay mechanics and progression system provide moments of strategic satisfaction. However, the game's steep learning curve, repetitive gameplay, lack of variety, and AI shortcomings detract from its potential. With improvements in tutorials, gameplay diversity, AI behavior, and overall polish, Cartel Tycoon could become a more engaging and immersive experience. As it stands, the game appeals primarily to players with a specific interest in the theme and genre, but may leave others seeking a deeper and more varied gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - after playing for several hours I can say that game is already fun in the state it is even though it still has quite a lot of rough edges this early into early access.   The theme is intriguing and is beautifully reinforced by visual style, music and gameplay mechanics. The main gameplay loop of juggling trying ot get enough profits/launder enough money while still trying to lay low to not attract too much attention of the law is quite engaging. Playing cat and mouse with the law is fun and already allows for some deep strategizing and I think it can be expanded a lot upon to make a system really deep and interesting. The difficulty can be quite ruthless - your cartel getting just a little bit too much infamy can snowball really quick to armies blocading cities and rival gangs attacking you left and right all culminating in assassination of your cartel leader. This is not a game over here though - new leader can be chosen and empire rebuilt anew. It is painful anyway! This is rather unusual for a tycoon game in my experience but it keeps you on your toes and plays nicely into the whole theme of dangerous and ugly cartel buisness.Now regarding the current problems of the game.  My main complaint is that after several hours I did manage to figure out that the 'slow and steady' approach is really efficient here. Just waiting and reducing terror to zero after a while allows to proceed with expansion harmlessly for quite some time. Just repeat when terror grows close to a dangerous level again. The main problem here is that the game does punish you for being too confident so player naturaly starts gravitating to very passive playstyle. And with nothing pushing player into action the game loses much of the thrill of cartel-law cat and mouse game - which is the most fun part.  The other problem I want to highlight is apparent uselessness of leutenant. Or rather as the game progresses and your territory grows their only use becomes to sit on the points of interests like ports (which get attacked and captured if no leutenants are present) only asking for money from time to time and being generally annoying. It feels to me they can be so much more than a rather forced limiter on your drug empire growth.  Other reviewers highlighted incomplete tutorials and overall vagueness of the game regarding your goals or means - this is true even though I did enjoy to a degree puzzling out the way everything works myself. I just hope this will get resolved over early access period.  There are also some usual early access issues like placeholder or nonsense dialog here and there disabled objects and so on - these I hope will also get resolved.In conclusion: despite some problems the game is fun and has a lot of potential to get much better.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game. I think a lot of negative reviews are from people expecting an easy-to-understand game. It's not. It's a tycoon and it's a bit complicated, because you need to run chain of drug productions->smuggling said drugs->laundrying money->managing your thugs and fighting wars. Personally, I love the theme and I enjoy complex tycoon games so I love it.The art is really amazing and you can see the devs put a lot of effort in it. The graphics are great, soundtrack, atmosphere. Each criminal in game has an elaborate portrait with backstory, etc. Overall, I think it's great, but like I said, there is definitely a learning curve.Hopefully there will be multiplayer support in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After a couple updates I have changed my review to positive. Updates improved many balance issues, added a few quality of life improvements, sandbox customization... Some things still feel unbalanced (load size on trucks and characters, upkeep price and upkeep speed) and some bugs here and there (few times I had a freezed star and yet the events kept triggering), but it feels like the devs will keep improving the game, and it's already in a playable and enjoyable state.------As many said, the game is unbalanced. I dont see how after demos and beta, a game is released which such annoying balance issues for the new players. The upkeep, the constant investigations on airports and seaports, and Im also pretty sure theres a bug if you deliver money to a city and missclick the icon (so instead of sending the money to a casino it goes to the city or the research center), the money is gone. Also, if you own a city and a sector, why you need to keep lieutenants in every building there? The limitations on trucks is also annoying, seaport is one minute away from your starting residence, and the truck busy doing that route is one less truck to deliver the constant upkeeps to every building, really do they need be every 12hs? And how, how can it be that a building floaded in vegetables raises the terror level?. I hope the game is updated soon with major fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: They've got a really good balance with this game!TL;DR: buy this game.  It's brilliant...I've played it since early release, but didn't partake of the betas.  Some of the early releases were fairly typical of this genre of resource-management strategy games with some repetitive elements.  However, this game provides what I think is one of the best balances I've seen in the various genres of resource-management/ empire building strategy games.  It's well thought out and the multiple elements balance themselves well.  It's actually pretty easy to pick up, probably will be a bit tricky initially for a new player (but there's good tutorial missions). I've not played survival mode, but sandbox seems like just the right level for someone like me who's looking to a game to chill out for a couple of hours after work.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first Tycoon games I've played in a while that isn't just a reboot or a bad copy of a previously awesome title (Looking at YOU Airline Tycoon 2). Truly unique dynamics and logistical challenges to learn and perfect, increasingly deeper Lieutenant and Capo relationships to maintain and a surprisingly real learning curve so true to life that if you go 6 months not playing you will be a true noob again; leading this to be one of the best if not only games that I have honestly played "for the first time" over-and-over again.My rig handles the graphics OK but it gets clunky deeper in the game as territories fill up, more Capos are assigned and logistical maps get complicated BUT I run an old server tower that's been poorly modded to resemble a modern gaming PC ... If you run anything relatively new or designed for gaming you should see no issues. The fact that my build will handle the game load at all is a testament to the program stability (and my dark lord level scrapping and modding skillz)Seems to have a vibrant and active player community however I have not personally participated in any community content except the awesome user generated guides and walkthrus - My loss though.... I'm just not a very social gamer, I do this to get away from people, not to make new friends. :)Enjoi the game and have a nice day!

_childDocuments_.review: For 10$, it is definitely worth the play, but the sim-city setup is very straight-ward once you figured it out, so the games will trend towards being very boring after the initial 5 hours. Besides that, the AI is rather dumb, especially when it comes to your structures. For example, your warehouse will take all resources and redistribute them even when the secondary modification structure is next to the production structure. (Thank god it delivers automatically within range of ports). It made transport companies somewhat irrelevant unless you are trucking things across regions (which you will not do given how inefficient it is). This means you need multiple warehouses to have the "truck power" to keep things running uninterpreted if you have just 4-6 30% primary structures. There are also other dumb algorithms that they didn't optimized enough, such as dirty money distribution. You will get a concentration of dirty money in a single low "wash" building while the rest higher capacities one starve b/c of initial build order. Enemy AI is essentially retarded, since they will raid your stuff and leave their city undefended, which allows the player to clear out all enemy once you can mass hire ppl or have started with a gang of ppl.Overall I'd say it is about a 5/10 or 6/10, but for 10$ on sale, it is ok-value.
