_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It seemed to have so many elements that I like to see in games. But unfortunately every element in this game falls short, leaving any part of the game lackluster at best. One of my biggest gripes is just how stiff and kinda lifeless the animation for everything in the game feels. That combined with decent, at best, sound design leaves combat and platforming kind of unsatisfying. This game is meant to be about the combat and platforming but when both of those elements fall short and aren't challenging, rewarding, or fluid then I think there is a problem. Anytime that platforming was a challenge it was more frustrating than anything else. And subpar platforming combined with no map, exploration also suffers. It's fun to use the movement that you get in the game but the world never really pulled me in. Things felt like they were there because they had to be for the sake of the game instead of having an interesting world to explore. The plot felt really unnatural at points, too. Things would just happen. There is a character in the game that is just a plot device, they show up just to shove exposition in your face, give you some big plot item to progress which made things feel disjointed and forced. So it would quite literally feel like the game just said "Oh hey, you got this far, well let me just unlock that part of the game for you now." Now despite my complaints I don't think this game is bad. This game has some good ideas, but I feel it doesn't execute them well enough and it all just falls short. It all just feels unpolished and unfinished which is what is stopping me from saying this is a good game. Overall, I really wanted to like this game but unfinished and unsatisfying mechanics with very stiff animation keep it from being something I can strongly recommend. 5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a nice and intersting 3D platformer with cool dark theme of postapocalyptic/magical world. It's set in a huge levitating castle on the middle of a postapocalyptic, completerly destroyed world where there is nothing but dark, dead lands. It not a long game (15-20 hours for 100% completition). Controls in this game are comfortable and easy to learn. Parkour is interesting and gives you lots of possibilities to explore the world. The world of Blue Fire as I said before is a big castle, which is split into 8-10 big areas with lots of secrets to discover and collectibles to find. Besides pretty good main storyline there is lots of side quests to complete. Skill system is pretty good as well. You can buy and find different skills like double/triple jump, sprint, long dash etc. I had a lot of fun just collecting everything possible. Although the game is fairly easy there is some hard challenges and bossfights. But don't buy this game if you are looking for a challenge. It's more about story and fun rather than difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a rare jewel of a game, it blends the best aspects of "A Hat in Time" and "Hollow Knight" seamlessly.Combat is fluid and intuitive (Though, I do wish for the option to remap the controls). Movement, whilst limited at the start grows to become something incredibly satisfying and enjoyable.The platforming presented in the main game won't pose much difficulty to those familiar with the genre, however, great challenge can be found in the optional Void Rifts the game scatters about. If difficult platforming is something you enjoy, I strongly recommend trying for 100% completion.Overall, Blue Fire is well worth it's asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the reviews. While the combat is a bit easy, it flows very well. Jump puzzles are hard and places that you think you can get to are available, if you are willing to try. I would highly recommend this game, especially on sale. Most of the reviews here don't understand the combat mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This is how I sum up this game in two words:SWEATY PALMS!Fun adventurous hack n slash games that feels like a mix of Zelda and souls-type elements. Simple gameplay, high need of exploration from area to area. It's not open world, but the areas are like a giant cage, or tunnel with multiple exits, but some requiring a new ability to reach. You can learn new things to do better things like jump higher or wall-jump (way more abilities, but that's spoiling). There are no armor upgrades, just health upgrades and you finding new swords that are stronger than what you have equipped. I spent 22 hours in the game to get all 22 achievements, but I guess I suck, because many others beat the game in nearly half the time I took. I spent 2-3 hours on some tough platforming challenges that I wanted to complete, because the reward was always worth it. The only downside is no direction on where to go or how to find the next area, unless you explore every place that has a ledge or someplace you can walk on. The game gets better as you find NPCs with upgrades, or spirits to help aid your character. The mobs will respawn in the area if you enter the area that needs a loading screen. There are maybe 8 areas in total (rough estimate), but can take a while to explore every bit of it. This game is definitely worth the cost value and would be a definite recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Has the potential to be on par with hallow knight. Really fun game with cool mechanics. Exploring is very rewarding. However, the timed "levers" and "gates" make the game rage worthy. The reason for my negative review is for the timed levers. YEAH lets watch the same gate open 1000 times because I mucked up and need to restart.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: this is honestly not a very fun game for me at least the mechanics just weren't there and it felt like the developers wanted to make a platformer and then just kind of tossed in combat as an after thought. not to mention the random bugs that i encountered such as one of the voids not showing completed and getting randomly softlocked. over all game was just kind of meh 3/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I've completed the entire base game and a portion of the free DLC Void of Sorrows.Overall, Blue Fire is a pretty fun experience for fans of platformers. I do have a couple of complaints though. The combat is never good, It's just a set of mechanics that you have to endure until the encounter is over. The combat is never particularly difficult either, it's just kind of there. It has a parrying mechanic, which is nice, though some enemies have weird hitboxes that can mess with it. A few of these will allow you to "parry", where the sound effects and parry animation will play but then the fight will continue as if the parry never happened - no counterattack opportunity and the enemy keeps swinging.The early-game platforming is very demanding and precise, even just to navigate the first hub area you have access to, which makes trying to do basic shopping or talking to NPCs frustrating sometimes. After you unlock a double jump, it starts to click and get fun. So if you can muscle past the early-game platforming, you can have a good time hopping and dashing around.The best parts of Blue Fire are the "Voids", which are challenging platforming areas that are isolated from the rest of the game, with the most difficult of these located in the Void of Sorrows free DLC (which is accessible after beating the final boss of the base game). To me, these challenges are the meat of the game and the reason behind my Positive rating.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard. It's hard but it's fair. The platforming challenges are fun and I loved going through and completing them all. Hunting down secrets is also very fun as well as combat and just how the game flows as a whole. I'm a little sad to see how short it was but I think in retrospect the length was actually pretty good. The game is well paced as far as I'm concerned and the world in which it takes place is full of mystery and a sense of melancholy. The boss fights are all unique in their own ways and each is a memorable experience. I won't say anything about the final boss due to spoilers but it was one of the rougher fights that made me proud I beat it. This game also has a DLC that I played through to completion and it's just as good as the main game. It's more difficult than the base game but that isn't a bad thing at all. If you have the money to spare I urge everyone who even has the slightest bit of interest in this game to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Very slow paced game that at least for me is far too easy. I have not played for long but I can already tell that I will not be enjoying this game. If you are looking for a souls-like plat-former for people who don't like a challenge be my guest (but it is cowardice).The game is alright but at the $20 price tag it is by no means worth the money.Sincerely yours, A hollow knight player
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Like Zelda, but perhaps harder. Has skill-based platforming challenges that will test your discipline and ability to repeat ninja moves in a tight space and at anxiety-producing heights. According to Steam, 70% of players haven't received the achievement for completing the first temple. They didn't have what it takes. Only 12% have completed the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: In all honesty, It's just kinda fine.It basically combines the gameplay and vibe of the late 90's and early-mid 2000's Zelda games with the some of the souls mechanics when it comes to enviroments, collecting of "souls", use of bonfires (in this game "shrines") for healing and upgrading yourself, etc.All of this sounds like a really innovative and interesting combination of genres in theory, but the execution falls short of being anything spectacular in my opinion as it fails to really do anything interesting that other games in these genre's aren't doing to make this game really stand out in any particular way, It's just kinda of a basic mashup that fails at being a really good platformer nor a really good souls-like either.With all of that being said, I don't think it's a bad game by any means, but it's not great either. It's just kind of okay in a way that keeps you playing but will have you probably forget about it once you're finished.May be worth a pick up on sale if you really like platformers
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I've read a bunch of times in reviews and the Discussions page of the game that others don't like that the game doesn't give you clear directions- I suppose if you want the solution always given to you, that argument is understandable, but I really enjoyed having the complete freedom to explore all the areas of the game at my own pace, with backtracking old areas almost always leading to some new discovery, some new reward. The next point has also been said a lot of times, but as a big fan of all three I can definitely confirm that the game is a mix of Zelda, Hollow Knight and Dark Souls. Blue Fire has the Puzzle aspects and the same graphics as Zelda, the difficulty of both Hollow Knight and Dark Souls, a similar setting, character design and soundtrack as in Hollow Knight, and a similar way of telling lore and of leaving the player clueless as in Dark Souls. Having struggled a lot with enjoying Dark Souls myself, I can totally understand players who pick up Blue Fire and, after an hour of playing, get too frustrated and quit. It takes some getting into the game.Other players have called the gameplay wonky for different reasons. I agree that the camera perspective can, at times, be confusing and infuriating, but in the entire time that I played the game it never hindered me from having fun. I've also seen complaints about the jump'n'run mechanics, to this end I have no understanding, I don't know how anyone can not understand the simple mechanics of the game. At the beginning, you jump and you dash. There's nothing complicated about it. With time, you learn to double, triple jump, double dash, wall jump and wall glide, and more, these can be slightly trickier to get the hang out of, but certainly not complicated.There's a lot of other topics worth mentioning, but no one has probably read to this point anyways, so I will leave it at that. For about 20 to 30 hours of intense jump'n'run, puzzle and fighting fun, plus a recently released free expansion (included in the mentioned hours) which was super fun, Blue Fire gets a clear recommendation from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire excels at delivering a satisfying platforming challenge, and often finds ways to reward you for performing difficult maneuvers. The difficulty gap between the Voids and the game's combat is pretty jarring, whereas the Voids are typically tough as nails, even the major combat encounters hardly issued more than a slight inconvenience.The music is very nice, and the sound effects have a very satisfying weight to them, helping to add a sense of gravity to both the movement and combat. The atmosphere is just a little odd, as the majority of your surroundings are quite dark, and yet your character always glows like a neon light, it was a little disappointing that even with all the various outfits in the game, none of them were able to actually tone down that bright glow very much.It's a great title, and completing it shouldn't require too much time investment. Platformer fans will love it, though as mentioned, the combat portion will leave a bit to be desired.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loving the game the visuals and audio are amazing, the music is on point, the combat and platforming feels really good but I'm running into an issue with one aspect of it and I'm not sure if it's easier on controller but the wall running and jumping seems a bit clunky at times especially with the camera angles sometimes. I just feels like i kinda hit a wall on keyboard and mouse as of right now. It's probably just a learning curve I'll have to try it more and see.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the love child of Hollow Knight, A Hat in Time, and Zelda (particularly Wind Waker in terms of art style).It's pretty great, and criminally underrated.The problems I have with the game mostly revolve around its lack of support for certain settings, including but not limited to: Lack of support for resolutions above 1080p (it was locked to that resolution for me, and I saw no way of changing it), an inability to switch to a borderless windowed state, and no support for PS4 button layout on controller, or any others besides Xbox.Gameplay wise, besides the mini synopsis I gave in the first sentence, I could mention the fact that there is no map, and little to no direction in the game's quests, but this wasn't a problem for me until I started going for completion, since I tend to explore as much as I can for stuff anyways. There aren't many resources for finding the secrets, so I recommend looking at the Blue Fire Wiki if you are going for completion.Contrary to what you'd be led to believe from the "Soulslike" label, this game is laughably easy. Some platforming sections are pretty challenging, but combat against enemies is a little pathetic on Normal mode. I was considering playing on Hard mode because of this, but I didn't wanna replay the first section of the game again to do it. I didn't die a single time in my entire playthrough.100% yes, you should! Especially if that first sentence piqued your interest.  This game is a pretty hidden gem with a lot of love and care put into it, even if it feels a little unpolished at times. This game does what it needs to incredibly well, and I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Some aspects of it are fun, but I don't feel the need to finish the game, due to the nature of 2 quests that just feel uninspired and already bore me thinking about them.Some leveldesigns were questionable, and downright confusing or unintuitive. Especially the beginning part left me confused.The platforming aspect sometimes was fun, but often got frustrating, especially in the challanges.The story is super generic and downright skipable, which is saddening, because the settings themselves allowed for much greater worldbuilding.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: the game has promise but i must request a refund for the first time, between the crashes, clunky gameplay and not being able to map out the controls. i wouldn't recommend to anyone in the current state the game is in.edit: the devs clearly care about this game and i might give it another shot on sale. from all the great reviews lately, maybe i was wrong about this game
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game through a video from Iron Pineapple and wanted to try it, so I got it on a sale for a really cheap price. Loved every single minute of it. I would say it is a mixture of Metroidvania (for example Hollow Knight) and souls-like (even tho it's definitely not as challenging as souls-like games, but still tougher sometimes) which makes it a really nice experience. What's also good about the game is that you can easily finish all the achievements and get another perfect game for your steam profiles, so if you are also looking for that, there you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe I havent given this game a reviewI'm telling you right nowThis is a The exploration and progression is done so wellIt never feels stale, just as your about to start getting used to everything something new happensThis could b a new ability, a new enemy, currency, or event. It just feels like there is always something moreIt reminds me of when games were actually fun to playKeeping you coming back because there is always something new to exploreOr a new mechanic that you just unlocked/discovered - that you can also use in the areas you already been to discover them further!Or mayb that's just what single player (more like offline) games do well
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: People don't talk enough of the pleasant, fluid mobility the game offers.  Sure it has Zelda elements, but movement has that nice feel that games like Cloudbuilt have.  It's fun to move around just for the sake of it, and to do side quests while skipping most dev-intended platforms with a triple jump followed by an air dash and then an air-boosting charged air slash.It's a bit slow at first, but once you get all the upgrades it gets real fun to play.  Also, the free DLC has cloudbuilt-like platform challenges which exploit all the mobility options.  Challenging but very rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: The battle of Greatness vs Mediocrity:This is a game that shows that struggle in every singe of its aspects:- Platforming sections, especially the Voids, are amazing and movements are very slick and responsive.BUT- Fighting is not only simple but, actually cheap and repetitive, borderline boring.- Game's aesthetic is very beautiful and has a special charm to it.BUT- Story is weak and characters while charming never really "click" or create a connection to the player.- Exploration is great at first, you wonder if you have the skill to try and make it to a certain chest or objective and can have a lot of fun.BUT- The plethora of movement options/spirits make exploration too easy after a while and take all the challenge away. Becomes completely trivial.All in all, game is worth giving a go if you want to try a 3D metroidvania that tries to mesh elements from Legend of Zelda, Souls or even Super Meat Boy, from where it clearly takes inspiration, never actually getting to the excellence levels of those it tries to emulate.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: What an adorable little gameI really enjoyed myself while playing this. The mechanics are so smooth and I barely had any periods of time when my character didn't do exactly what I wanted. Honestly half the time he didn't, it was user error from frustration.As a puzzle platformer, I think this is up there in my top ten mechanically.The art style and combat were also pretty great. I believe the only two times I died were against the final DLC boss, which I think was a perfect amount of difficulty for the style. It felt cute and handled that way too. Maybe some of those void levels were a little too difficult to fit that word, but the challenge of moving platforms and timing wall runs, especially towards the end made me frustrated in the most perfect way.All that being said, if you're looking for a story heavy game, or even something that feels particularly unique, you may want to keep moving. Personally, I was really hoping for more flavor with how well designed the character and art style were, but that's the one place this game was lacking. It didn't actually detract from the experience though and I'm really looking forward to any other platform puzzle heavy games the developer puts out.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic platformer that draws inspiration from so many amazing titles. From Zelda to Mario to Hollow Knight, heck even Dark Souls. The pacing, exploration, difficulty followed by beautiful artstyle and music score. Gameplay and movement evolves constantly but never in a way to overwhelm a player but rather make you feel getting powerful.If there is one platformer to recommend this year, this is the one. This is coming from somebody who is rather bad when it comes to platformers; some of the challenges were incredibly hard but were a joy to get into rythm to complete. This game will punish and reward you in equal measure.

_childDocuments_.review: I was real excited when I saw the trailers, since I'm a sucker for anything that looks even vaguely similar to Hollow Knight. For what it's worth, the game looks fine and has very satisfying, smooth gameplay. But behind the polish, it has no substance. I feel the tiniest bit more cynical.Don't bother with this one: just replay Hollow Knight or Super Mario 64, and you'll have a better time.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game, a mix between Legend of Zelda, Dark Souls, and Metroidvania. It has such an ominous, beautiful atmosphere that you just want to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Title: A Journey of Light and Shadow - Blue Fire ReviewBlue Fire is a 3D action-adventure platformer developed by Robi Studios and published by Graffiti Games. Set in the mysterious world of Penumbra, players take on the role of a small warrior named Umbra, tasked with uncovering the secrets of the realm and restoring light to the world. With its unique blend of platforming, exploration, and combat,  offeringa thrilling and memorable experience that is both challenging and rewarding.  Umbra, who awakens with no memory of his past or understanding of his purpose. Across his journey, he encounters a variety of characters, each with their own stories that provide glimpses into the world's history. Additionally, faces off against numerous foes, hinting at a much deeper corruption that has taken hold of the realm.One of the game's strongest aspects is its engaging gameplay mechanics. The platforming sections are precise and responsive, with a variety of moves at the player's disposal, such as wall running, double jumping, and dashing. The combat is equally satisfying, utilizing a combination of melee attacks, dodging, and parrying to create intense and strategic encounters with various enemies and bosses.The world of Penumbra is beautifully crafted, boasting a distinct art style that combines elements of darkness and light. The varied environments, from the haunting Void to the lush Greenpath, are rich in detail and atmosphere. This is further enhanced by the memorable and immersive soundtrack, which perfectly complements the game's overall tone.Also offers a wealth of content, with numerous side quests, collectible items, and hidden areas to discover. These optional tasks provide additional challenges and incentives for exploration, rewarding players with useful upgrades and lore-filled tidbits.However, the game is not without its flaws. Some players may experience occasional camera and control issues, particularly during more complex platforming sequences. These can lead to moments of frustration and unintentional deaths, disrupting the motivation to continue...Additionally, the difficulty  can be inconsistent, with some sections presenting substantial difficulty spikes. While many players will appreciate the challenge, others may find it off-putting, especially when coupled with the  control issues.Lastly, the storytelling  is relatively minimal, relying on environmental cues and scattered lore to piece together the narrative. While this approach can be effective , those seeking a more in-depth and coherent story may be disappointed.In conclusion, Blue Fire is an engaging and challenging action-adventure platformer with a beautifully crafted world and memorable soundtrack. Despite some occasional camera and control issues, and a lack of in-depth storytelling, the overall experience is one that fans of the genre should not miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little 3D action-platformer with elements reminiscent of TLoZ: Wind Waker, Hollow Knight and A Hat in Time. The combat is not particularly remarkable, but exploring the world and doing the pure platforming challenges in the Voids controls smooth as butter and becomes more and more satisfying as you discover more skills to expand your moveset. The free DLC, Void of Sorrow, was also a great bonus with some of the most challenging Voids in the game and an excellent final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it's really good by what I've seen, the combat being a mix of LOZ:TP and Hollow Knight, the art style looking like Hat in Time had a baby with a Megalovania, and I just love some of these characters although they rarely talk because of designs and how silly they are, Such as the character "Orip", it's amazing to see such an idiotic genius of a character in this dark world.But just because I like the art, combat and characters doesn't mean theres not one problem....... taking the elevator to the city crashes your game....... I wanna see more of characters and go to Orip's shop but I can't find that out till they fix this bugWhat I would advise is, wait till the game has a bug patch to fix this issue and then enjoy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue fire is a diamond in the rough, there's no denying the bugs can take away from the experience, specially in a game that requires patience already, i had no major issue with the bugs except with the fire boss, i had to kill myself after beating him cause the game would crash if i went through the portal and the start menu was unresponsive. Other than the crashes the more frustrating part of the game were the damage chains when you get hit multiple times and it feels a bit unfair, this happens with the queen of darkness which i found ok cause its the final boss but it can also happen occasionally when you are traveling through smaller platforms, this is frustrating and can get worse if you end up falling off the platform, i like the lack of immunity frames but it does feel a bit unfair at some points.  That being said, the good outweighs the bad in this game. The controls are precise and you never feel like its unfair when you mess up the platforming(unless you wandered away to the areas you cannot yet progress through), the character is very responsive and the fact that the player controls the length of the dash and the duration of the jump give the player as much control as one could wish for in a 3d platformer. It has a beautiful world and it's VERY fun to explore; the game can get pretty hard but there's way to power yourself up as well, its not impossibly hard, but it is harder than your average game and you will need patience if you want to do everything(namely the voids which to me were the best part of the game but i'm aware they can feel tedious or too punishing for some people).If you wanna know how celeste would feel in a nintendo 64 style platformer this is your game, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: recently read some other reviews and I have had zero crashes so I cant speak for everyone but overall I still give this game an 8/10This game is fun! _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good.Fun platforming, pretty boring combat.Slightly janky, but not to any problematic degree.Exploration is fun.On normal the game gets pretty easy near the end and later platforming challenges are easily broken with the better movement abilities.My only real complaint is the backtracking I had to do like 3 or 4 seperate times as I unlocked all of the things to actually use most of the stuff you find going through the game.

_childDocuments_.review: been really enjoying 3D platformers recently with souls elements to them and this one did not fall short of what i was looking for! too be honest though, the difference between hard and normal did not seem that bad. you just take more damage basically, so for those who played souls games and want a challenge, do the harder mode or you might not be as satisfied. overall, the art design is nice, the music is great, gameplay is solid and the level designs were a lot of fun to go around on and grab as much as you could and find what you need. im not really into the 2D platformer/souls combo games but when it comes to the third person 3D ones, hell yeah. the story was decent, nothing crazy or overly complex but it was alright. i think the voids were also fun to find and those might have been some of my favorite part of the whole game....something about all the parkour made it so fun. either way, highly recommend this game to platformer fans who want soulslike elements, i enjoyed this game a lot!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I thought I'd like this game more than I did.   I wish there was a "Meh" option because this is not a bad game.  That is not to say I am a game developer and could do better on my own or as part of a team.  I always feel bad bombing decent enough attempts at exciting game building because I know this is their livelihood, and I know I'd suck at making anything as good or better.  That being said...The GOOD:The graphics and overall aesthetic.  They are definitely up to par in terms of fidelity, artistic qualities, and original design.  I love the way the main character looks and animates.  The overall visual polish is great too!The game play.  The character controls well with tight jumps and fun enough swordplay.The cutesiness.  For some reason I have not progressed far enough to identify, you pay for emotes with in-game currency.  They are fun but so far have served no additional purposes.  I just assume they're trying to cash in on the fortnight momentum.The BAD:The combat.  I can't say it'd be a better game without it like some have commented, but it certainly isn't fleshed out or well-realized.  The level design.  I will not be continuing to play it for this reason.  It is easy to sequence-break and get trapped forcing you to reload.  In 2 hours, this happened to me three times.  Progress in this game must be deliberate.  In a game where exploration is emphasized, why would you not conduct more thorough player-testing?  Some of the dungeons are long, frustrating, and without checkpoints too.I will not be requesting a refund because I like supporting smaller devs.  If you're hard-up for cash and feel that buying video games is still a sensible expenditure given your current financial situation, maybe pass on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a decent game. I'll put down some pointers and you can decide if it sounds like a purchase:1. The music and visuals are, often, surprisingly fantastic. But once in a while they're grating on the eyes and ears. 2. The combat is good! You can dash around and regain your jump on aerial combos. But on the ground, your third hit combo makes you dash directly into the enemy you're hitting, very weird design. 3. Collectables are fun to attain... but most have literally no purpose, so you can sell them in a shop for money you won't ever need.4. The saving grace of this game, for me, were the Voids. You enter into these scattered challenges and test your limits of movement and platforming. Upon completion they increase your health, which feels very rewarding. Absolutely perfect design on those. The DLC portion includes Voids as their main focus, which was incredible!! 5. This game is like a mashup of Wind Waker and I, Ninja with some brooding lore. In my opinion, the devs tried to include a lot of fun elements, without fully mastering any of them. Still, it's a fun experience that you might enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Overall pretty solid. IT STARTS SLOW though, it seemed like the game really started only after I got to the first city. I would say it's a mix between Zelda and Hollow Knight. It's not difficult, but still fun. The most challenging parts are the platformer challenges, even gave me some A Hat in Time feelings. The game doesn't have a map, as most reviews already said, but I didn't think it was that much of a problem. The story is completely thrown in your face, so if you don't want to search for answers this game is perfect for you. Took me 14 hours to complete the game a 100% (wasn't in a hurry at all). I got the game in Humble Choice, but I would definitely recommend it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a souls-like third person adventure game where you are going to embark on an extraordinary adventure through the world of Penumbra to explore unique temples and fight many enemies. It has an interesting story, quite lovely graphics, and various worlds and bosses. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me in a very good way. In the beginning combat felt a bit wonky and wall jumping was very frustrating due to how the camera is set up. However, as the game advances, between understanding its quirks and unlocking movement abilities, it feels very rewarding and I was, in the best of ways, hoping the game was longer. The best part about the game is the platforming for sure. There are special platforming challenges called Voids that are very fun to go through. Near the end, with most of the movement abilities the player feels like he's basically flying through the map, which is a good thing because in Blue Fire there's a large amount of backtracking to previous areas and unlocking new ones to explore.The combat was only so-so for me. I feel like enemies sometimes signaled wrong, and the dash, while being very good for platforming, makes you move a bit too far during combat. There's also a parry ability that feels pretty good to use. Overall I felt combat felt more like button-mashing than anything else.Lore-wise it's fine, the characters are sweet and the whole mythology felt a bit vague, there's a lot of ideas that could be developed further in a sequel. I hope the devs do consider making a sequel. Feels like not many platformers of this caliber are being made nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was barely playable at the release because of all the crashes and softlocks. But they made it even worse with the patch release. My save file got hardlocked off one important item for the progression. Luckily, I was relatively not that far into the game, just 5 hours in, so I started a new playthrough. But then I realized that half of rooms were loaded without any triggers, and if I didn't know that they supposed to have anything, I would be very confused. So I had to save/quit to the menu multiple times to properly load the room. It's really sad because the game has a great platforming potential, and with a better technical execution it would be really fun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not just Zelda + Dark Souls. This game is more like Zelda + Dark Souls + Mario 64 (platforming). Making something so familiar yet so different. Cell shading style animation and voiceless dialogue filled with grunts and groans brings on major WindWaker vibes. Lock-on fighting system, bonfire shrines and expansive interconnected level design give Dark Souls vibes. And 3 dimensional platforming level design gives off major old school N64 platformer vibes. Giving this game a solidly new, yet uniquely familiar feel and an all around fun and challenging experience. I highly recommend this game to anyone who just wants a good game to lose themselves in for a while. Very fun. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: A game that's actually fun to traverse, has (most of the time) rewarding sidequests, and is just.... good.For people wondering what it's like because the trailers lead you down one path, and the souls-like tag leads you down another, but imagine if Breath of the Wild compacted all of its content into the first zone, but instead of puzzle/combat shrines, you get platforming shrines called voids, and you also get absurd mobility and the hollow knight charm system... that's Blue Fire.My only real complaint is that hitting air enemies is kind of annoying because of how floaty air movement can feel sometimes, but like... Not a lot of games where I just want to walk around for 2 hours finding hidding secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: Review on the game in general and then its mechanics:Although short, it is very fun and great to play if you have free time here and there. Pretty easy to play once you get the hang of it. I fully completed this game, so my time spent is about how long an average player might take to complete the full game and collect every item on easy difficulty.~The world has a lot of verticality to it and allows for a lot of freedom in ways to scale objects or jump gaps.~Although not required, exploration is highly rewarded and encouraged since many weapons, tunics, or items are hidden. ~Side quests are often short and sweet while also providing some details about the story or NPCs here and there.~The enemies aren't the toughest until the temple area, but most of the boss fights are fun past the first boss, and the final boss actually feels like a final boss. The DLC boss is an even better challenge too.~The parkour in this game is very fun. The voids(parkour challenge areas) are hard sometimes, but the voids in the DLC area are straight up unforgiving to say the least. Definitely took the most of my time to do the DLC.~Easy difficulty is perhaps a little TOO easy. I did not get a game over a single time the entire game until I fought the DLC boss. If you want it to be more challenging, select hard difficulty.~Banana King tunicAltogether a very good game and great work by the devs. If you like Hollow Knight, you'll enjoy this for sure. The DLC is free and everyone gets it, so it's more like a big update than anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a 3D action platformer, where you play as a classic Nameless-Chosen-Warrior to fight the Evil Shadow and save the corrupted lands. If that is not edgy enough, our protagonist is a dual wielding sword, wearing a hoodie and a mask! With glowing eyes! (Honestly, that is my reason I got this game). As mysterious as he is, we delve deep into the floating castle, to unsolved the mystery behind the chaos inside the castle. As I stated above, there’s not much going on with our protagonist, except his fashion choice. With that, we awake in a castle, already corrupted with darkness. Then we proceed to meet NPCs, that told us, that we are the only hope to save the world. That’s it. There’s not much lore either, except from what the NPC told us. And I don’t feel any kind of urgency to save the world ASAP, because the NPC is living their life peacefully doing their business. It’s an action platformer game. But honestly, it’s more like 90% platforming, and 10% action. Don’t expect much from the dual blade that we had, because we can only do a simple 3 attack combo. There is only 1 (ONE) blade related skill. And even that, it more useful for platforming (it said so in the loading screen tips, and all the enhancement of that said skill is to increase length or heights of the movement). For that reason, the game is more enjoyable when you get all the traversal skills like double jump and wall run etc, because the map itself is precise platforming (even in the city, you need to parkour your way from house to house). The game is pretty generous with the in-game currency. You need to break objects to get money, and defeat enemies to get souls. Both are for upgrades and buying stuff. Not much grinding is needed. To increase the health bar, we need to do platforming challenges called the voids, which I think, this is . Because there are more of this challenge than the bosses and type of enemies combined. It’s very clear that the Dev put more effort into the platforming challenge than the combat mechanic. There is an accessory system called Spirits that we can equipped to enhance our abilities. But then again, more than half of them are for the convenience for platforming, like increasing dash length and remove fall damage, etc. On the brighter side, there are some NPCs with their problems we can help to give a bit variety in the game. The focus here is our character, which we can change our hoodie into something our liking through the game. Other than that, all of them are mediocre to meh. Almost all the NPCs are designed like blobs with a bit of a cosmetic slap on them. That also applies to the enemy’s design, which most of them is just a slight difference and change of color. That also applies to the world design too, which all of them are really bland, and oversaturated with a single color. This is that type of game, where our character is mute, and all the other characters just make grunt noise whenever they talk. The music overall is pretty chill, and the boss’s music fight is quite good. Not bad, nothing memorable either. Final ScoreThis game barely passes my bar, because I gotta admit, the platforming challenges really deliver, and the cool looking protagonist. I dropped this game when I first played it (ver 1.XX something) because it was so unbearable and boring. Years passed, I powered through the game and it became more  bearable. This game has more potential to be more Action-Platformer game, rather than Platformer-Action game.

_childDocuments_.review: From the little i have played of this game I absolutely love this game, but this game I have came to find out strongly encourages exploration. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a must-have for any platforming enthusiast. The controls on jumps and dashes are precise, and the levels push your ability to utilize precision to the utmost. However, there is also an element of creativity, where you can select certain bonuses that enhance your basic movement, in addition to story-earned upgrades. Given the challenge of movement in the beginning, this lends a sense of immense satisfaction as you enhance your capabilities and can reach previously unreachable spots. That said, there's intense satisfaction in reaching certain hidden objectives early, in finding your way into areas that you're not supposed to be in yet, and testing yourself against late-game challenges a bit early. You can also nerf yourself to try and see the minimum requirements for getting past certain challenges.Let me give you an example (slight spoilers on what abilities are unlocked): there are levels called "Voids" that are basically a jumping puzzle that you can retry infinite times. These have a varying degree of difficulty, from 1-5 stars. Early on you learn that 2 and up can be quite the challenge. I found one that was 4 stars, in an area I snuck into, that should've been locked because of my current jump length. I tried it, and though it was GRUELINGLY difficult, after about 50+ tries I got to the final jump of the void, only to find out that I literally could not make that one jump. I looked up a guide and saw someone using double-jump for it, and I thought that's what I needed! But the next (official) level unlocked a wall-jump. This, on the surface, was still NOT a double-jump, an ability that makes timing and precision a lot easier, and would've clearly unlocked the final jump. However, I noticed wall-jump had a mechanic where you could gain a little bit of height if you jumped away and dashed back. With this alone I was able to clear the final jump! INCREDIBLY SATISFYING. I was able to clear a level early, just by leveraging the mechanics!Other people will point out this game's shortcomings, but honestly the satisfaction of being in a difficult-but-fair platforming paradise makes this game absolutely stand out as a gem. If you love platforming mastery from classic games like the Prince of Persia series, recent games like Celeste, or even just difficulty like in Souls-like games, this one is worth exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a good game. It can be called a soul like, however, I do not agree with this. Out of everything, the most vibe that this game creates is A Hat in Time. A wide range of mechanics obtained during the game campaign allows you to get into the most unforeseen places already in the first phase of the game, only to understand that developers have foreseen this. But also you can get items and abilities in ways that were clearly not intended, which makes flexible platforming even more enjoyable. Platforming in this game is very interesting and never feels unfair. Blue Fire is like a Super Meat Boy but in 3D, easier, and with a bit of slasher. Sometimes it feels boring and generic, but the game is worth the money. So, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. It has a "metroidvania" and "Zelda" style and feel to it with smooth controls and simple but fun game play. Level progression can sometimes be confusing and frustrating as A LOT of exploration is required and missing the slightest hint can have you looking around for what to do for awhile. When you do finally work out where to go or what to do it can be rewarding but having a way to direct to "where next" would have improved the game play.Mechanics are great, there is a progression through the mechanics that eventually lead to making your time traversing the world much better and easier through a variety of unlocks. Both the mechanic unlocks and zone unlocks gives you a satisfied feeling of progression.The enemies in the game are all kind of the same but just different looking mobs with slightly different mechanics. There are boss fights as well which were quite easy but I still enjoyed fighting all the same.Overall my experience with this game was a positive one and I'd recommend it. I'm not much of a platformer and some of the void platforming challenges were quite difficult but fun once you get the hang of it and rewarding when you complete them.

_childDocuments_.review: After trying to play this game twice 1 year apart from each other I can't recommend this game. I didn't complete the game but stopped at 60% as the gameplay was getting too repetitive and in particular, collecting something like 15 orbs just to progress with the storyline is beyond crazy. I think it's something you expect doing if you wanna complete a game with all the achievements, but that's my personal opinion.The game doesn't have a map. You often find yourself backtracking just to find the right path.The story wasn't that engaging either.What I liked about this game though, was the graphics, the setting and the platforming part, expecially the Void one (small platforming levels scattered around the world).Overall I don't think it's an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic third-person platformer with a few rough spots.  The beginning of the game should be spent following the story to unlock the main movement abilities but after that the game opens up massively.  The level of movement you get to is incredible and the controls are so razer tight that the platforming is incredibly satisfying even on the 100th death. Speaking of difficulty the game is kind of a two-parter. There is the actual game and story which is fairly generic but still fun and concludes well.  This section is a little rough at parts but it may just be me trying to get to areas I shouldn't be able to which is often doable and can get you some cool stuff.  The other section, and honestly best, is the void worlds.  They act like the special areas in Mario Odyssey and are platforming challenges that reward you with more health and an incredible challenge.  These were by far my favorite parts of the game and are divided by difficulty. 1 star is a fun jaunt that lets you flex your skills and 5 is a long series of absolutely brutal jumps and obstacles that will take hours to complete but manage to be completely fair and incredibly satisfying to complete.  While I hesitate to mention this as this will most likely be fixed since this game only a month old, the game does have some bugs with crashing and not recording accomplishments.  This doesn't actually affect your quests but your in-game records may be inaccurate.  (Steam trophy system works fine.)  All in all this game takes a ton of inspiration from games like Legend of Zelda, Celeste, Hollow Knight, and many other incredible games to create an extremely fun game.  That's the most important thing I wanna reiterate.  This game is incredibly fun, not perfect or groundbreaking but really really fun that I have to recommend to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend it for fans or somewhat appreciators of 3D platformers.  If you are new to 3D platfromers, look up some top 3d platformers on google or youtube and play some of them first.  I would give this game a strong 6 out of 10 or a light 7 out of 10.  There's a lot of good about this game.  But there are a lot of flaws.  Some major flaws and a lot of nit picky flaws.  If the game did not have these flaws it would probably be an 8 out of 10 and if it had a lot more content (Hollow Knight level content) and a map, it could be closer to 9 or 10.Either way, I enjoyed the game for what it was.

_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game does everything wrong starting from right around the time it's too late for a refund. Level design that makes depth perception impossible. A hub designed like a platform challenge that you're expected to play through dozens of times just to talk to vital NPCs. A vital NPC who was put earlier than the hub despite only selling things you can't afford before reaching the hub. A wall run/jump mechanic that functions horribly & is only partially explained.Parts where you fall for a ridiculous amount of time after a mistake before the game finally respawns you. A timed section with confusing level design centered around wall running right after you get wall running. Constant rewatching pointless unskippable scenes. The hub is literally a maze. No indication what you can & can't wall run on.The pipe platforms are programmed the same way as pipes in other games where you're not supposed to stand on pipes, which is that you slide off for no reason unless you stand in just the right spot. Constant forced backtracking in a giant labyrinth world with no map & no waypoints. Y goes back for no reason. B confirms for no reason.It's impossible to die unless you stubbornly try an idea that isn't working dozens of times because your health bar is absurd. You can beat the first boss by just running into it & attack it repeatedly while tanking every hit & you'll still finish with a lot of HP left.There's a high platform with a chest on it in the hub. It looks like you can wall jump to it but the game just doesn't let you so trying causes you to fall & get trapped in an invisible box on top of a giant lump of poison.The game is full of giant lumps of poison that hurt if you touch them but instead of being carefully placed like hazards normally would be to make a game fair & fun, they're placed like scenery. In other words, wherever looks good. I fell in water at one point & got hurt twice. Once by the water & once by a random little chunk of poison in the water.The game tells you it autosaves but it doesn't tell you manual saves are the only saves that matter because autosaves save so close to nothing I'm not even sure what they save. An autosave always puts you back at the last place where you manually saved even if it was multiple areas ago.There are giant spike pillars & touching any part of the pillars hurts you even though the spike is small & is only on top. There's no fast travel, no teleporters, & nothing else like that so saving time is simply not allowed.One of earliest massive glaring signs of lazy design was when I entered the hub for the first time & met a merchant selling clothing dyes & I wanted to save before buying one but the save point was across a huge gap & it didn't look like I'd be able to come back any time soon if I jump down to it so I just carefully chose a dye, put it on, & found it was a drastically different color than the picture showed it to be. One of the dyes is labelled "light grey" but the picture is blue. Not even light blue. Just blue. How does something like that happen?This game is mostly filler. Filler consisting of the same rooms with nothing new to do in them on your way back to whatever merchant you're revisiting.

And both A and B to accept? FOR REAL?)Battle system is absolute garbage. _childDocuments_.review: 1 part Hollow Knight 2 parts Zelda mixed with some 3D mario platforming sections. Blue fire is a solid game, It's your usual zelda fare of head to dungeons, open chests to get new abilities, save some spirits and fight your bosses. The combat isn't all too deep really, you have a block, a dash, a charged attack and of course, a regular attack and a little piffle of magic. It's alright, it does the job and it could've been so much more. Once you're in the air just wail on the enemy then get out of the wya of their attack unless they're stunlocked and rinse and repeat. The main challenge in the game comes from the platforming segments, especially those in something called the void. These remind me of Mario Galaxy or Mario 64 with somewhat random  placed blocks and platforms with hazards that don't really fit in with the rest of the game. They start off ok but get quite rough towards the end unless you equip the right abilities to cheese them. I was not a fan of the games pacing to begin with as whilst it does throw you right into things, it feels like you're just aimlessly doing things without really knowing why. If you enjoy the mechanics of the game which I think are above par then you may enjoy the game but overall it's just a decently made game that feels like missed potential to be something more. I hope the devs focus more on the structure and world of their next project as there is talent here but it's just a bit hit and miss. Worth a try though as I did enjoy my experience with the game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seemed right up my alley. Immediately  turned off by the complete lack of control during parkour. The dash is miserable to line up correctly and If you fall off while doing the Void trials you have to go through a loading screen for no reason. Mechanically it seems fine, I just can't understand some of the deliberate design choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: The best aspects of the core gameplay, puzzle solving mechanics, and music are PAINFULLY similar to elements of the games that influence this one. The combat is barely serviceable - it starts off poor, picks up a bit later once you have more movement options, but core issues remain from start to finish. For the most part, bosses seem bland and have no interesting mechanics. Minibosses do not exist. Dungeons are ok. The most unique mechanic I encountered was the use of the emotes to unlock access to chests. The 3D platforming was fun. _childDocuments_.review: The thing i can say about this game is its good... until it isn't.The controls are almost on point, but there is no control for speed. you push forward on the stick, you go at full speed, theres no way to walk. the enemies are well designed and varied, but their hitboxes are weird, and its sometimes hard to see when they are about to attack. the save points make sense, but there aren't enough of them. the jumping puzzles are really interesting but frustrating.the good stuff tho - this is someone who said "i like zelda windwaker, i'm going to make windwaker" and damn if they didn't nail the artstyle and level design. the music is absolutely wonderful, and the storyline has been interesting. the being for me is don't really like the whole fetching your body mechanic unless its really REALLY well done (see hollow knight). instead of pushing you to get better and learn from your mistakes, this just feels punishing and a way to extend play time. why are there no saves when you get to a new area? if you die on one ledge, why does it respawn you all the way back to the one you left from? all of this adds up to a frustrating sense of "i really should love this game, its got everything i want, but it just doesn't work." bad games i can handle. good games are good. but when a good game is bad, its a travesty.if someone came up to me and said "man i loved zelda windwaker, but it was way too easy" i'd say "my friend have i got a game for you!"This is not a conversation i've ever had. i want to like this, i really do - but i can't. you can see where things aren't working, and you can see WHY they don't work, but you can't do anything about it... and that is INCREDIBLY frustrating.this game just isn't for me, but I truly hope that it is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about this game when Iron Pineapple covered it in his Steam Dumpster Diving series. He described it as a mix of Hollow Knight and A Hat in Time, and I immediately fell in love with its premise. I'm a big fan of both of those games, so this was right up my alley.Thing is, while both Hollow Knight and A Hat in Time are awesome, I feel like they are polar opposites in a way. Hollow Knight goes for a sorrowful, dark atmosphere and a satisfyingly hard difficulty. A Hat in Time, in turn, goes for an upbeat, happy feel and a relaxingly easy difficulty. So, how did Blue Fire combine the two? Well, in several ways. More on that later.I do enjoy this game, but I think I ought to point out its flaws right from the start, so you don't get the wrong impression. First of all, platforming can be very finicky at times, with stuff like wall runs and ledge grabs occasionally not connecting, way too many situations where max jumps are necessary, and the difficulty curve is not so much a curve as it is a wall, preceded by a long flat-ish line. Also, the combat is pretty simplistic, and the boss fights are disappointingly easy, oftentimes even easier than A Hat in Time's.Now for the stuff I like. Firstly, I really love the atmosphere in this game. It primarily goes for a Hollow Knight-esque post-apocalyptic darkness, but I think it leans into the cuteness more than Hollow Knight did. The main character is adorable, and you can make him perform all kinds of endearing emote animations, including a nice homage to Hat Kid's world famous smug dance. The NPCs tend to have really cool designs, and some of them are outright precious in personality as well. The devs really split the difference between their two main inspirations when it comes to world design and overall feel, in my opinion.Second, the platforming, despite its finickiness, is quite enjoyable. The "void" levels are pure platforming challenges that are mostly really fun and satisfying. They're like the Time Rifts in A Hat in Time, in a way. It also helps that the game world is full of little secrets in every nook and cranny, and you have to platform in creative ways to get to some of them.The game world is gradually unlocked in Metroidvania fashion, with new moves allowing you to get to previously inaccessible places, much like Hollow Knight. The platforming itself, however, feels more A Hat in Time-like, with the "combo jumping" over long gaps, wall running, and all that. Where in A Hat in Time, you'd jump, then double jump, then dive, then cancel your dive, in Blue Fire, you jump, then double jump, then dash, then spin attack, not necessarily in this order.The few dungeons the game has are really nice too. Shorter than the average Zelda dungeon, but still full of fun bits of platforming and puzzles, plus a ton of optional items to grab if you're observant enough. I only wish the dungeon bosses weren't almost all extremely easy, which kinda soured my mood after running through the cool stuff hoping to get to a formidable challenge in the end.The story is a sad tale of a dying world. Again, similar to Hollow Knight, but leaning a wee bit more into the cuteness. It is not world shattering, but it's nice enough, and certain side quests did make me feel really sad. It's a bit like Dark Souls or Hollow Knight in the sense that very little is straight up told to you, and there are several pieces you need to put together yourself.Overall, I feel like this game is worth it for the cute-dark atmosphere, the fun (albeit janky) platforming, the enjoyable exploration, and the really nice story. I just wish the combat was better and the bosses were harder.EDIT: Hard mode is just bad. Removing checkpoints from the voids is not a good way to increase difficulty, it only makes the game frustrating without actually increasing the challenge level. If you play this, play only normal mode, even if the combat is kinda trivial.

_childDocuments_.review: Embarking on the adventure that is Blue Fire, I was immediately drawn into a world of striking beauty and formidable challenges. The game's visual presentation, characterized by a sleek, neon-infused aesthetic set against shadowy backdrops, left an indelible impression on me. The contrast between darkness and vibrant lighting effects created an atmosphere that was not only visually dynamic but also mysteriously alluring.From the outset, the narrative in Blue Fire unfolded in a subtle manner, leaving room for interpretation and discovery. The game's lore was intricately woven into the environment, with cryptic NPCs and atmospheric storytelling inviting me to delve deeper into the secrets of Penumbra. The mysterious ambiance and enigmatic characters fueled my curiosity, encouraging me to explore every corner of this enigmatic world.What truly captivated me in Blue Fire was its gameplay intricacies. The platforming elements demanded precision and timing, and the protagonist's acrobatic abilities, from double jumps to wall runs, added a delightful fluidity to my movements. Navigating the interconnected environments felt like solving an intricate puzzle, with hidden secrets and shortcuts awaiting those willing to explore.Combat in Blue Fire proved to be a thrilling test of skill. The fast-paced encounters, coupled with diverse enemies and their unique attack patterns, kept me engaged and on edge. Mastering an array of weapons and abilities added layers to the combat experience, making every victory over a formidable foe a satisfying achievement. The atmosphere within these dungeons, coupled with their intricate layouts, added a sense of accomplishment to my progression through the game.Ariel Contreras-Esquivel's musical score further enriched the experience, adapting seamlessly to the changing environments. The ambient tunes and intense tracks complemented the gameplay, enhancing the emotional impact of key moments. The synergy between visuals and music contributed to the immersive atmosphere that enveloped me throughout my time in Penumbra.However, Blue Fire was not without its challenges. _childDocuments_.review: [Update: Please note that this review is about the game in the state of the Sword of Steel version. After I published it, a free DLC with additional gameplay (new region, more void levels, a new boss) was added, named the Void of Sorrows. And recently also even another update came out, called the Balance of Justice Update, which obviously features quite some changes and improvements, among those another difficulty as well as new names for them. So take my review with a bit of caution, can’t say anything about all those changes, and I’m not sure if I’m going to replay the game. But for what it’s worth, even if only for historical reasons, here goes the original review, hope it still helps a bit:]You can definitely see that this game is heavily inspired by the Hollow Knight/Dark Souls trope (the general atmosphere, environment, characters and some mechanics), but it’s less fight-heavy and hard in that regard, and also with a bunch of Zelda references strewn within. So far nothing new you might think. But what really makes it fresh in my opinion, is that this time those well-known elements are being realized as a kind of challenging 3D-platformer, with everything you can think of, wallrun, double dash, triple jump and whatnot. Music is awesome (best news, it’s even included for free, fantastic chorals I absolutely adored). So as a package, the game really does a lot of things well. Nevertheless you should be sure what to expect when playing this game, or else you might get easily frustrated as a casual player. But let me elaborate.The game features two difficulty modes, Newcomer and Recommended. Actually I played both modes in 2 save files simultaneously for about 2/3 of the game to compare them, and I have to state, Newcomer actually isn’t really that much easier per se. Prices are lower (though money never is a problem up from the point you get the double gold spirit orb), fights get a bit more forgiving (especially against those annoying flying enemies that can instakill you otherwise with their ice attack), but all jumps and dungeons are still the same, and don’t underestimate it, they can get pretty demanding. Most noteworthy difference probably is that in Newcomer (due to a patch) checkpoints were added to the void levels, and those are kind of essential. Normally void levels (which are half-optional but give you additional hearts as a reward) are really hard, because if you fail one of the many difficult jumps during the rather long path you have to start from the beginning, which makes those (especially the higher levels) really tedious and annoying. So what Newcomer does, it makes those levels doable and less stressful, even if only 1 or 2 checkpoints are added at most times (with the exception of the last 5-star void level which got none), and as a result, in Newcomer the game is easier to 100% achievement-wise. What I’m trying to say, that’s actually the reason why I, at some point, only continued and finished my Newcomer run. But nevertheless, even the Recommended run is manageable, got a good friend who did it without serious problems, so it just might depend on how encouraged you are. ;) Anyway, my feeling was that Newcomer makes the game more Zelda-like with a certain exploration feeling, while Recommended is more careful progression oriented, sometimes grindy and meant for precision/hardcore platformer gamer-types (especially in the later void levels). And it’s probably worth mentioning that some very important upgrades are hidden in some cryptic side quests or off the track, so be prepared to look up the one or other guide. But apart from that, and even if the game admittedly got a lot of design flaws mentioned here and there (like the non-relevance of gems and many items, souls dropping in the water when dying, the pressure-sensitive dash, some void level time cycles, certain camera angles, feeling of depth etc.), it’s still very fascinating and kind of addicting. I absolutely enjoyed playing it below the line, so all in all, a definite thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: updated pre-patch review below, read the whole thing. TL;DR, a fun, if brief, Metroidvania with cool movement tech and fun platforming.I love the concept of this game, and it's *almost* well-realized. The thing that keeps me from recommending it is that I've run into a consistent crash in what I assume is the early-mid-game, seemingly triggered by attempting to leave a certain area after entering it. If it were merely a gripe I had with the design of the game I would not feel the need to write this. But as it is, I have to recommend against buying it until bugs like the crash issue I'm seeing are fixed.===After a patch to fix the persistent crashing, the game is - obviously - much more playable and stable. I'm glad the devs released it so I could see the game through. I had no further crash issues and only minor non-critical bugs post-patch. I notice that a couple of Steam Achievements have not popped for me which I have definitely gotten in-game. Oh well...Overall, the biggest remaining problem I found with the game is that there wasn't enough of it. It feels like far more than a demo, but is not quite paced like a full game. I went in expecting a somewhat short experience, but still found myself wanting a couple more full "dungeons" - which became a forgotten concept past around the halfway point, in favor of further progression happening during general map traversal. The surprisingly robust amount of collectibles and expansions feels "condensed" into too small a game world. I would say the game could have been half again as long or even double, and "felt" about right for length. Obviously this is easier said than done for a small dev team! The combat especially suffers from underdevelopment, although a couple of the bosses are still challenging and rewarding to face down. I think it was intentionally kept simple, which is totally fine - but I would've loved to see more than three or four basic enemy "templates" which all have the same basic tactical approach of "hit, dash away from during their attack, hit again."The movement and platforming is consistently a lot better than the combat, and I really appreciated how sidequests and optional exploration unlocked options to expand the player's mobility instead of gating those options entirely behind the main quest progression. Probably my favorite thing about Blue Fire is that there are many platforming challenges and obstacle courses where there isn't only ONE right way to get past. Also, there are a couple of neat tricks and movement techs that I suspect speedrunners will enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a fun, if a little wonky, 3D platforming metroidvania, that can best be described as a cross between Mario and Zelda wearing the flayed skin of Hollow Knight.In a mysterious floating castle, you awaken as a litle knight in a cloak with two swords and an edgy haircut. Based on a few cryptic hints, you must travel the Land to Seek the Gods and Purify the Corruption to Restore the Kingdom and Banish The Shadow. The story and general vibe is threadbare and deeply derivative. Ain't nobody launching a middling YouTube career off of videos explaining the Lore of this game.In general, everything not tied to gameplay is somewhat lacking. Not bad, but very drab and unimpressive. The environments are pretty dreary and not hugely exciting. Since everything takes place in a castle of sorts, every area feels like one of the dungeons from Ocarina of Time. Imagine if in OoT, to get to the Fire Temple, you had to pass through the Forest Temple and the Water Temple, with no open outdoor areas inbetween, and you'll have a sense of how the world of Blue Fire feels.It's not bad, but with such a flimsy story and cute characters, having everything look and feel like a Dark Souls Playmobil set kind of drags the mood down unnecessarily.Luckily, the gameplay of Blue Fire rules. Platforming is quick and technical, with plenty of aerial control, but not a lot of time to react. It's a geruinely very clever mix of 3D platforming and exploration, that perfectly translates the escalation and expansion of abilities of a 2D Metroidvania into 3D. You start with a jump and a dash, but by the end of the game (provided you explore the world properly, that is), you'll be walljumping, double-dashing, triple-jumping and just generally swoocing through the levels like a ♥♥♥♥♥-up grasshopper. The game really rewards exploration, and just like in a more traditional metroidvania, if a challenge is too hard for you, just try again later when you've bulked up on movement-enhancing upgrades.It's this sense of progression and growth that had me hooked.The game is the perfect length for what it is. I 100% completed it with relative ease in about 12 hours. Any longer and I would've gotten tired. It does the trick and doesn't outstay its welcome.I bought this game on sale and absolutely got my money's worth. I'd love to see a more polished, aesthetically interesting take on this kind of 3D Platformvania some day, but for now, this will do nicely. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for August 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before September 7th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.I heard a lot of buzz about this game, and I get why.  This is a Dark Souls-esque game, with a great visual style placed on it and a bit more story.  Players are in control of an experiment and must travel through the land, fighting evil monsters, tackling large challenges, and trying to find their way.But this is also very Dark Souls-esque in its difficulty.  I found myself having a few early issues while I got a handle on the combat.  There’s a good parry system, a very fluid battle system, and what appears to be great hit detection.  The downside is that Blue Fire is pretty challenging, which also is probably a positive to most fans of this genre. There are some special platforming sections in the game to get health upgrades, and there’s a decent amount of distance between checkpoints.  However with at least 11 hours according to How Long to Beat, this will be a meaty adventure, and the experience so far is good.  And while I think it is a little hard, there is an easier difficulty as well which I haven’t tried, but kind of invalidates all the difficulty criticism. Pick this up if you like Dark Souls.  Check this out if you like the graphics, this is solid and I’m only surprised it’s this far down the list.  It doesn’t have the most publicity, but it’s worth checking out.   If you dislike Dark Souls, you probably will also dislike this. _childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like the game because I like Indie Games and Hollow Knight. TL;DR: Beautiful graphics, nice NPC's, barely any action, combat is non-fluent and movement system just never feels nice. Also some bugs here and there.The game looks beautiful. And usually when you start a review like that you know a game is bad. Which is the case.  I really like the character designs, the NPC's and the environment, I really do. I love that the game has an implemented camera mode which allow good angles. But I rarely can rarely enjoy the world out of many reasons. One is the enemies, they are just placed so horrifically. They are stationary air targets in your way, just for the sake of it. They are not there to enrich to world, they are just there to stop you from moving, nothing more. The combat seemed very appealing to me, but honestly, you rarely get to it and if you do, it is just 1-2 enemies in their own little corners. Then there is a lock system, which seems alright, but reeeally gets clunky once you fight aerial. First, you can only dash and double jump once in air, only once. No reset for hitting those enemies in air like in Hollow Knight (they did it right) which make you fall down in a stupid way, especially if the enemy moves backwards and you try to catch up only for being punished with fall damage. Now let us get to the movement system. It really could be easily fixed with one patch or a mod but let me get into it. The camera, generally, has a hard time following you around, it is rather slow and often gives you unfavorable angles. It first feels alright but as soon as you get to spots where the platforms are far and you need to dash, it gets frustrating.. Many times, you will fall down not because the platforming is hard, but because it is just so damn inconsistent. You wanna grab on edges? Too bad, because you reaaaallyy have to touch that 1 pixel of the edge to grab on to it. Then comes the wallrunning. I really don't know how you can mess up wallrunning, seriously. Why does it feel bad to wall run? Because first of all, there is no dash and jump reset. That means if you dash to a wall and jump of it, you cannot dash again. Which make you then again rely on grabbing edges. Which feels so inconsistent with the already slow camera. Which is even much much worse when you fight and dodge enemy shots, you really just cannot get a proper feel to the gameplay. Then, you cannot jump upwards repeately on one wall to reach an edge because, just because. To top it all of, water insta kills/resets your character and damages you AND there is fall damage. A platformer with fall damage which discourages early, fast-paced jumping. What kind of platformer has fall damage? Please. There are also the void challanges (a bunch of parkour) which really is just never fun to play and all you stress yourself for is just for some extra hp.There are also some bugs which disable levers/switches or put keys for doors behind that locked door...some people could not 100% the game because of that even.I really wanted to love the game but no matter how much I forced myself to bite through, it is just never more fun then a few minutes.
