_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR:- Great graphics, nice atmosphere- Awesome OST, really great integration in game- Lovely exploration, you're free to go where you want and come back later- Combat system feels unbalanced and most of the times not interesting.- Quests are a bit repetitive and the story lacks depth.The game is really interesting and takes influences in many well-known games, blending them all together in a creative and interesting way.- The main quest/secondary quests resembles a lot BotW, in both its mechanics and its content. It is still interesting but lacks depth in my opinion. Activities often consist of exploring the world until your retrieve x item y times or find some people, but it encourages the player to explore the world in its entirety, so it's not a huge con.- The character looks a lot like Hollow Knight, and the clothes have a BotW feeling. The art style is very consistent and pleasing to the eye, without being realistic. It gives a really nice atmosphere.- Speaking of atmosphere, the OST is incredible. Music can be stressful in delicate situations, different environmental elements blend in perfectly with the BGM of each location. However, it sometimes lack smooth transitions when switching places, but not always perceptible so it doesn't make the OST any less wonderful.- The combat system is the definite flaw of the game. You gradually unlock new moves, but you can easily play without them. Most mobs are no-brainers, and difficulty isn't linear among bosses. First ones are really easy while the last ones feel too powerful. - I loved exploring the world. There are many places you can't reach at first, then come back with new power-ups and finally reach it. There are different places that I loved visiting again, discovering all that I missed at first. Really interesting design, great use of height and easy yet interesting gameplay.Some timed doors felt a bit unforgiving, but not too hard.- Game is really great to play even with a keyboard. Great job on that!

_childDocuments_.review: It's the devs first game and it shows, it has some good stuff (platforming, environments) some meh stuff (combat, story) and some bad stuff (writing). There's better games to spend the same amount of money on but if it's on sale I recommend it.The bosses are enjoyable from the third one onwards but pose little challenge in normal mode, overall the game is easy on this difficulty, I've only died once in the free DLC. Didn't bother with hard mode because it seems to only 1) increase enemy damage but I did not care for the combat 2) reduce the number of checkpoints (supposedly during platform challenges, I did not verify this but why would you ever have this as an option is beyond me, just extra frustration for the player).Some rambling:The spirit mechanic seems to be inspired by Hollow Knight charms, however it's not well balanced, some of them are super good while others useless, and they all have the same equipment cost. It's interesting that about half of them upgrade your movement capabilities, some of them are super broken to the point of making most platforming challenges (Voids) in the game trivial.I've actually replayed all main story Voids without any movement spirits and found them all reasonably doable and mostly fun.The DLC Voids however are quite hard without any spirits (believe me, I've tried) and balance wise they feel all over the place. Here I eventually gave up and easily completed them with all movement buffs activated. There's probably an optimal spirit combination one can choose for each Void to make the DLC challenging and fun instead of challenging and rage-inducing, but it's the devs job to make sure the player has just enough tools to overcome a challenge in a satisfying way, not the player's. Overall the spirits that buff your movement feel like the devs weren't confident of their own platforming difficulty, which again, first game, perfectly understandable.Closing statement: the game has a secret  so it's a 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very pleasant game to play. I loved immersing myself in the world, it was pretty, charming and felt good. Exploring was simple and satisfying and the progression while not complex felt really nice. It's simplistic but it knows that and just gives a chill time. It's a chill atmosphere and it completely charmed me from the moment I saw it. A very good game to relax and go through and I can see myself going back to it. The movement and abilities are fun, the rewards you get feel great, the art style and atmosphere is an experience in of itself.That being said it of course isn't perfect and by that I mean... theres a handful of things that really REALLY had me questioning it. The combat I can get over, it's simple but felt kind of inconvenient to deal with things and I really feel like it needed more fleshing out. In this case more enemy types and things to encourage your use of abilities rather than being model swaps of things that are annoying to fight. There wasn't much variety which is unfortunate because theres a ton of unique events that don't introduce new kinds of fights or challenges and some of the bosses make me think this could have been made a tad bit more interesting. This mixed with fact that combat is a bit clunky and impressive at times and it kinda sits weird with me.Another huge thing is it's direction, that is to say theres barely any. The thing is common sense can kinda get your through, the world itself isn't all too complex but the seeming lack of effort to give you any idea of where you're exploring through was a little infuriating. Important areas are mostly unlabeled or conspicuous, or sometimes you'll need to get to somewhere but what that thing is is completely unknown, and remembering stuff can be a pain because for some reason theres no mini map or any kind of marker or way points. I have no idea why, you'd think this would be very important but they straight up have no kind of map to understand the world better. It makes it infuriating to find where to go at times.And one last thing that was annoying where the bugs. Sometimes soft locking or almost soft locking but not only did it exasperate this games lack of direction by sometimes confusing me but it was just really damn annoying to traverse sometimes when the game just wouldn't respond properly. Crashed once or twice and while it's not a deal breaker MOST OF THE TIME, it is very much there as a problem. And not just that but sequence breaking was stupid easy. There's so many things you can just use to get places where you shouldn't that even a toddler can figure out to the point where I'm genuinely unsure if it's intentional or not and only confused me even more trying to figure out where to go.I would also mention that a lot of the platforming sections are a little dumb. Mainly the voids, some of those did not feel designed with the movement in mind, and by that I mean like the camera being an extra obstacle and there feels like theres a little too much of it but other than some frustrating voids I can live with it.I know I just spent the majority of this reviewing complaining about stuff, but I do genuinely think this game is a good time. I saw it, was immediately charmed and beat it in a few days and I'm very glad I did, this was a gaming experience worth having, I feel a bit of soul cleansing from it. Just be prepared to occasionally have to wade your way through a few issues every once in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to start things off, I absolutely loved this game, and think it is getting a criminally low amount of attention. This game has tons of charm, super fun, great price. Just a really really solid title. And it is because of the low attention this game is getting that I'm going to summarize what to actually expect out of this game, and talk about some of the key components that were good/bad.For starters, this game is a platformer, and clearly takes tons of inspiration from other games. I think Zelda and Darksiders are the most apt comparisons to be made here. Despite what others may say, this is NOT a soulslike at all, if you are buying it for that reason alone do not be misled. The only things similar to a souls game are checkpoints, and that you lose your currency on death and can recover them, that is it. In terms of tone and pacing, having those oh ♥♥♥♥ moments where you have tons of souls and are afraid to overextend into an area and die or being constantly led into traps and unfavorable positions, this is in no way similar to souls. So if you aren't sure what this game is, there you have it, first and foremost a platformer, and second is metroidvania.Now onto some of the core aspects of the game.Overall really good performance for me, no issues with stuttering or frame drops whatsoever. I did have in grand total 3 crashes, 1 very early on in the game (which was concerning at first) and then the other 2 did not happen until the very late stages of the game. So overall a pretty smooth experience. Do not be misled by negative reviews talking about performance and crashing issues, they have since patched the game and it is much much better. As far as bugs go, I experienced none other than the crashes, super polished game imo.Here is where the real heart of the game is, and that is controls. This game gives you incredibly precise control over your character, jumping is very floaty and you get full control of your character in midair, allowing you to shift momentum on a whim. This really lets you maneuver your character in all sorts of interesting and creative ways. This is a platformer, and the controls are really good and precise, so there you have it, good stuff. I will also note I did play on mouse and keyboard, and while I have no complaints about the controls themselves (mouse and keyboard was super smooth and the way to go imo), there were quite a few issues changing keybindings, so you may need to use macros to get controls exactly how you want them.This is the second area where the game really shines. I think the combination of good controls and good level design is what makes this game. Levels take full advantage of verticality, in fact several levels are just straight up giant structures you need to climb. There are tons of secrets hidden away, giving you reason to always look around and find available places to jump to.Now this is probably an unpopular opinion here, lots of people seem to be whining about the lack of minimap, but honestly I think this game is far better without one. The map in this game is not very large at all, it is mostly tall, which is not something minimaps handle well. The lack of a minimap also forces you to take mental notes of where you are and where you have been, and the level design helps you do this. Each area is super distinct, even within the various biomes, rooms are distinct from each other. While I did get confused on where to go sometimes, I was never lost, I always knew exactly where I was and where I had already been. I will also note here, the level design in this game is incredibly demanding on the player, forcing you to really make good jumps and decisions. The game also features several of these void areas (think like the little platforming side areas in the 3d mario games), and these are for the most part solid. Many are on the verge of sadistic and are very hard. Really though, I enjoyed the challenge in these void areas. Really good level design all around.Now here is where things start getting a bit mixed. To start with positives here, this game allows you to go anywhere at any time. You will need to unlock new platforming abilities like double jump etc. etc. (I won't spoil them all) to actually get around to all locations, but there are several places where you can progress to areas the game probably does not intend you to through creative use of abilities. I love this in games, you have so much agency over your playthrough and are encouraged to experiment and break the boundaries of the game. I never truly "broke" the game, but there were at times moments where I was completing puzzles and unlocking abilites the game probably didn't want me to have yet, and that was just really cool.Now negatives, I think the main one being that checkpoints cost currency for whatever reason. That really is a theme in this game, that the money and item economy is just all over the place. Every time I found a new checkpoint, I could not even use it, I had to basically finish the next area, and then run back to unlock the checkpoint, and this was just so frustrating, a result of a poorly conceived economy since there was just not enough to soak resources for most of the game. It really felt like for ~60% of the game, I was not earning or unlocking anything new outside of platforming mechanics, and then suddenly the game opens up and I got like half the items in the game within 5 minutes. Super busted item economy.This was the weakest part of the game by far. I would say the platforming in this game was actually quite demanding, combat was braindead easy for the most part. Enemies also do not telegraph attacks very well, so this really is just a button mash game during combat. For some reason there were also tons of flying enemies, and these were just super annoying and often difficult to attack. Bosses were also just not very hard at all, I beat most of them on my first try with ease. Overall just not very good combat.Some closing thoughts, again you can probably tell by the length of this review that I absolutely loved this game, and recommend others to try it. From the artstyle, characters, and controls, this game has tons of charm and is super distinct and memorable. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with a nice artstyle, very nice movement, a rather loose "story" and terrible combat.I really enojoyed the movement and the world just perfectly complemented it. It starts out quite snappy with a basic jump and can be upgraded to a tripple jump with a double dash and a spin attack for even more haight. All of that works and feels quite polished.It feels very good to breeze trough areas you had previously a hard time getting around in.There isn't much Story to speak of, which is good for me since i don't care for most of them in this type of game.That "I don't know where or who i am, all i know is that i must kill!"-meme sums this story up pretty good.All the upgrades you find are usefull in one way or another depending on your playstyle, but none of them will change your playstyle drastically. The Weapons where quite dissapointing, none of them had any special ability or something like that... straight up just change the look and damage. And the worst part was that i had to buy the strongest weapon, i got it quite early as well, so it was just very disheartening to see every other weapon i actually found out in the wild or got as a quest reward to be worse.But now we're coming to my biggest gripe with this game, the combat. I'm an avid Souls and Zelda player which attracted me to this game in the first place. Still i had a very hard time getting used to the combat, and i yet have to get properly used to the "rythm".The main problem lies in the fact that besides the spin attack the combat never evolves beyond the standard 3-Hit combo you have from the very beginning. The fact that i have no invincibility frames when dodging and enemies don't get staggered (except for flying enemies) change how you have to react to them. While this doesn't need to be a bad thing it sadly work against this game. Most problematic is the whole enemie concept. Most enemies have only 1 attack, maybe 2 for sword wielding foes, they will relentlessly spam those attacks as soon as you're in range. Sneaking up on them is impossible.So unless you can totally overwhelm them or you perfectly parry all attacks you'll be stuck doing hit and run attacks until said enemie is dead, since most enemies do AOE attacks.But once again, in the right setting this could be a good thing.Sadly enemies barely telegraph their attacks and their tempo and "rythm" just makes it hard to even want to fight them. It's really hard to explain.My lock on breaking constantly event thou the enemie is still visible and the dash not always going where i expect it to go makes it hard to fight flying enemies until you get more jumps and the upgrade for more melee range. While i could keep pocking holes into this combat system (like how you have to charge your spinn attack and as long as you hold that charge you can't do a normal attack anymore, and you loose that charge once you use a ladder or get hit by something) i can gladly say that enemies are rather sparse, at first i tought this was a negative point, but once i realised how bad the combat is, it was quite the blessing.This still doesn't help that the bosses where the worst i have seen in a loooong time. Their boring designs and rather unfair and unfun movesets (the rythm problem is most apparent here) their only saving grace is their minimal HP, so they atleast dont last long.The only boss i somewhat enjoyed was the "fish" in the water temple. He was the only enemie with a semblance of a good moveset and was actually fun to fight. In the end i would say that If this game had a bigger focus on combat and less on the platforming i couldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delightful mashup of some of the greatest games which have come before. Also, the player character is just so cute.If you have played games like The Legend Of Zelda Wind Waker, Breath Of The Wild, Dark Souls, Super Mario Galaxy and A Hat In Time, you will surely see the inspirations that went into this love letter of an action adventure-platformer. The degree to which the developers remixed the elements from great games of the past goes beyond transformative and lands squarely in the realm of masterfully crafted.I was immediately enamored by Blue Fire's incredible soundtrack. Every track has been a stunning piece which properly captures the atmosphere of the various areas of the game. Atmosphere, painted with a Wind Waker inspired art style, is where this game's soul really shines through. Nailing a feeling and experience I find hard to put into words.Combat encounters are manageable, sometimes challenging, if a bit simple. Meanwhile the brunt of platforming is taken to The Void, detached little challenges that test your jumping and dashing talents. The gameplay is at its best when these two halves are blended into the larger experience. Making way for fun dungeons rife with secrets and treasures.Although at the time of writing this I only have a little over 3 hours of game time. I can sincerely see myself taking the time to 100% this game. Do NOT sleep on Blue Fire.

_childDocuments_.review: If Super Mario 64, Hollow Knight, and Demon Souls had a child (somehow), it would be Blue Fire. If you're a fan of any of the aforementioned titles, this is worth a play through. I myself have spent 21 hours and have gotten a 100% playthrough, and those hours were enjoyable.Art: 8/10• The art was unique and stayed fresh throughout the game. We've seen art and style like this before but not too often.Sound: 9/10• The music for the game was well done. It help push the story through when needed and it was nice collecting items while it was in the background. Soothing~Story: 5/10• The story was short, the side stories were the other 1/2 of the game. The side stories didn't help drive the main narrative through to the end, so the main story was lacking background or involvement. Beating the game, you do feel "meh" for the ending given.Characters: 6/10• The main character has some good swag, just not enough story for them to develop any relationship with. What's a hero without a story?Enjoyment: 7/10• The game is enjoyable for a precision platformer. A nice fresh mechanic to platformers while maintaining nostalgia. It was pleasant!Conclusion: 7/10• Good Action Hack-Slash Precision Platformer

_childDocuments_.review: First of all the game is good, and it deserves to be played by anyone who likes platform games. For that price it's a good deal. Now, the game has it's problems. In addition to a couple of crashes that I had and a bug where my heals didn't refilled after resting so I had to buy some to fix it, the combat it's quite mediocre, boring and often unfair. There are a couple of bosses that have phases where you literally can't heal. Many enemies do not have their attacks well telegraphed or are so small that they are hardly visible. That said, I emphasize that the platforming is the best part of the game, very enjoyable and the Voids are very very fun. Avarage story. Some funny sidequests. The customization is cute.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a 7/10 game. Nothing special, but nothing horribly bad either. The game is a 3d-platformer with Zelda-like dungeons and exploration. By the end of the game you have a wide variety of "Spirits" to equip that improves your arsenal of platforming tools that improve further upon the game's already great sense of freedom and flow. Even better, you will definitely have to take full advantage of these in the end-game voids/rifts. With a few exceptions, I found the Voids to be pretty well balanced difficulty wise and I enjoyed that they forced me to use all my tools at my disposal. The story and combat is pretty meh, but that's nothing new for a 3d platformer.As for complaints about maps and not knowing where to go, I personally dont get it. I feel like the areas are very well defined and connect in ways that are made obvious. I never found I had to do too much backtracking anyways, but on that note I explore everything that I can before moving onto the next area. I think what would really help is simply being able to see the name of an area before moving into it, rather than after moving into it. In the end, if you want a basic 3d platformer with a fast and flowing toolset, then I'd suggest picking this up!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the negative reviews dissuade you. Blue Fire is good. Really damn good I'd say. It has some jank and some issues but I still think it's worth playing through, especially at a sale. Also play on a controller if you can, I think it makes things a lot easier.If you like 3D platformers and Zelda-like adventures, then Blue Fire's gonna hook you up real good. You're gonna be dashing throughout the world, picking up items, equipment, cosmetics and that key that's gonna unlock the next area along the way. The boss temple design is straight up classic Zelda. Now the puzzles and the combat aren't anything to write home about. They're serviceable. IMO, the platforming takes center stage. After you start getting special items and building out your moveset, the sky's the limit. By the end, I was combo-ing 3 high jumps, two dashes and still being able to wall climb on top of that. However, it is a bit of a shame the environments are mostly linear or after one exploration don't offer a ton more to find. But the voids, basically Super Mario Sunshine-esque platforming challenges, make up for that imo. That being said, there comes the jank. Wall jumping can be a bit finnicky and you'll occasionally jump in a different direction than you intended. The lock-on camera for enemies in the air is a bit janky too. Personally I also thought the parry system was a little inconsistent but ymmv. I'm sure there's more I'm forgetting but just know that there's some jank here.That all being said, I'd still put Blue Fire at an 8.5/10 or so. You can finish it in ~10 hours and there's even an additional DLC that takes about 2-3 hrs on top of that. the gameplay is solid if janky, the story....exists, its really nothing crazy. But it's fun and the music especially is excellent. I also personally like the aesthetics and art design but you may not. Again, pick it up on a sale and have a fun time

_childDocuments_.review: This game emulates Super Mario Sunshine, Wind Waker, Dark Souls & Crash Bandicoot REALLY well, with a handful of nods to A Hat in Time and Hollow Knight thrown in for good measure.  It doesn't feel like it's doing anything outside the box here.  It's got a mix of everything that makes those games great - punishing failures, expansive worlds, minimalist handholding and crazy movement tech.It works, and it's frustrating, but it works well.  The music's nice and atmospheric.  The difficulty doesn't make it unplayable, but it does feel like it lies a bit to make you feel comfortable before breaking you over its knee.  There's no map system (that I know of at the time of writing this), so you're stuck relying on your memory as to what routes exist to where.It does lack a bit of polish in some elements:- The camera clips out of bounds in some areas.- Ultrawide resolutions have some elements expanding off the screen (I play on 2560x1080).- The controls for gamepad aren't rebindable.- The sound balance seems very loud by default (there's sliders for these).After completing the game, I can no longer recommend that you play it - the game crashed during the credits sequence, and afterward, several of Windows' built-in features like Event Viewer and other programs that rely on the same .NET Framework stopped working as well.  Blue Fire itself crashed on loading afterward, too; I'm now staring System Restore in the face while it does it's thing.After System Restore fixed the problem that plagued my entire PC, I then had to go back and finish off the final boss one more time.  No crashes, of course, but by then I was already far too frustrated with this game beyond the terrible endgame boss design and the level design ramping up in difficulty beyond that which was advertised towards the end.No game should say 'Ok, you 100%'d the game, time to break your computer'.

_childDocuments_.review: As many others have said, it is a cross between Hollow Knight and Zelda. The combat is not a huge part of the game, which for me is a plus - you will always be very very squishy, focusing more on dodging and moving, which is fine, as the game gives you tools for it.  Once I obtained the double jump upgrade, the game REALLY opened up and the movement started feeling very nice as opposed to just okay. _childDocuments_.review: Blue fire is an absolutely adorable game. It, to me, is very akin to Hollow knight and Darksouls but in a very cute 3d style. The world itself is well made, with great care to how it flows in it’s own story and within itself. The world is built in very cute little side quests and npcs, that each breath life into the world without making it up front and center. It’s subtle world building that makes the world feel more complete.The “armor” was very fun to see, nicely designed and extremely cute, giving a good contrast t o the dark desolate land we are saving. It was nice that it wasn’t stated as some of the really nice looking “armors” were early on.The powers, or spirits, you pick up along the way added a very nice bonus to however you play, especially the dash ability. Plus the flavor text, and how you obtained a couple, are really cute and funny. It showed a good bit of care given to every aspect even in just some flavor text to a power.The section akin to the silent realm from Zelda, at first glance did make me groan, but as played it. Was nice. You are not on any timer, it’s the same map just tinted blue, and nothing is chasing you. The ambient music and visuals were very relaxing, it was more just explore the map again and look in the paths you didn’t take. No stress, no mess. I felt it is what the zelda silent realm SHOULD have been like as these still offered a nice challenge that didn’t feel like inflated challenge.The bosses of this game were easily my favorite part. Looking for their tells, getting into a pattern, and t he visuals. Everything about the bosses worked to build one another up in a very good synergy. Plus the music for the bosses had me getting hyped up for the fight, even dancing a little. Speaking of the Music, the OST for the entire game is perfect. Each area is paired beautifully with a theme that is a nice ambient touch and perfectly fits the area it’s apart of. I find myself just listening to the music because even outside the game it holds it’s own. At the end of this game, I found myself speechless. I loved the final fight,m and I loved that after you complete the game it  then offers you another challenge. Beat the game on an even harder difficulty than hard, and perma death. I very much approved that after you beat the game. They offer you more, test your skills. You know the fights, now can you do it without dying?I feel, challenges such as those are best after you have completed the game once in games such as these, it is fair since you know the fights and will know what to expect so a death to something new doesn’t rob you of progress since it is perma death.Lastly the voids. These little off the path realms challenge you to parkour your way to an end and are absolutely a blast. Even some of the harder ones are fun. I did find myself getting frustrated at one, but that just pushed me to beat it even more and once did, felt so satisfying. These are also totally optional, they offer upgrades. Health and with the orbs you get in them, spirit slot increases. So you can add even more challenges to yourself by not entering them.From the parkour, the combat, the visuals and audio ambience, all in all, a great game that is absolutely adorable!

_childDocuments_.review: My opinion about this game keeps flip-flopping, sometimes i think it is great other times i think it is awful. If you are on the correct path and exploring new areas, interacting with NPCs and scoping out secrets it can be great but if you are lost wandering around it isn't so fun. So when you first play this game the movement will feel a little slippery, almost as if the character wasn't walking but on rollerblades. After an hour or so you get used to the movement and it will feel fast and responsive for the most part. The best part about this game is the platforming, climbing huge structures and navigating tricky terrain is just enjoyable. The combat is okay, for the most part you just want to explore and enemies are annoying you while you do so. The boss fights are pretty fun, you have to dodge attacks until the boss becomes vulnerable and it is your time to strike. The bosses are pretty easy if you do all the quests and voids, I didn't die a single time.It is very easy to get lost in this game, sometimes the game indicates where a path leads to but often it doesn't. Also some areas lead to more than 5 other paths and everything looks kinda similiar which is a problem especially because the game doesn't have a map. Another issue is that not only can you get lost but the game also does a bad job of making obvious where you are supposed to go. I ended up climbing the entire huge tower in the abandoned path before getting a double jump, in hindsight that was not intended however i spent like an hour doing it because I didn't know that.The biggest issue with the game is probably the camera, it is very reminiscent of the Super Mario 64 camera. Often times you simply cannot see what you are doing. In some of the tougher challenges you will die just because you cannot see the platform you are supposed to land on. Especially on levels with moving obstacles you will often just die because it is nearly impossible to judge how far away an object is from you. The game also has a lot of quality of life issues that make you wonder why it is designed that way. If you are doing a puzzle with a timed switch and fail, you have to watch 2 cutscenes to try again instead of hitting the switch again resetting the timer.The only character that you can sell your items for money to is in the city, so to buy everything from the thief vendor later in the game you have to teleport back and forth 2 times, and go through a total of 4 loading zones just to buy everything from him. Why can't i just sell my items directly to the thief, or any other vendor for that matter?Falling in the void often makes you wait multiple seconds before it resets the level and then after it resets the obstacles might be on an entirely different cycle making you wait even more. Also falling the in the void doesn't reset your extra dash or jumps and it doesn't reset some platforms, making you wait even even more.DLC: I only played 4-5 levels of the DLC. Some are fun, others aren't they are mostly hard void levels where the camera really is miserable, i don't think i will clear the DLC as it isn't required for the steam achievements but it is there if you want more.If i'm undecided about a game i usually recommend it but it does have its fair share of issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on 100% completion and 8.9 hours of gameplay. Would I recommend this game? Yes, this is a nice little game, and I really like its aesthetic. It has a cute vibe, but there’s also a level of grittiness that really helps build that atmosphere. Everything in the game works well together, from the sound design and music to the art style, which is really nice. While it’s a platformer with some bits that can be a bit challenging, overall, the game is very forgiving and quite easy.At the beginning of the game, the first few hours can feel a bit slow and confusing, but once you get more comfortable with the controls and have gained a few upgrades, the pace picks up depending on your playstyle. As for the gameplay, the main aspect is platforming, and to be honest, apart from a few of the void challenges, most of it was quite easy. The tricky bits were mostly about getting used to the mechanics. For instance, with the dash, it was just about understanding the distance it can cover, and the camera can sometimes be a bit annoying during platforming, making you do something you didn’t intend to.The game doesn’t do much hand-holding, so you may get a little lost at times, and in this aspect, it reminded me of how Dark Souls progresses. However, there aren’t many areas, and they are fairly linear and easy to learn, which actually works in favour of the game’s vibe. While there is combat, there honestly isn’t a lot of it. Enemies are either in small groups or pretty much alone, so combat is super easy. The boss fights are similar—nothing too difficult and very easy to understand. The only mechanic I didn’t fully grasp was the final boss fight, where it shoots out a big ball shield over the arena in phase one, but it was still easy enough to beat without fully understanding it, which should give you an idea of the game’s difficulty level.Overall, this is a nice little game that provides a mostly easy platforming experience with a few small challenges here and there. I would recommend waiting for a good sale, as I feel the base price is on the upper end of being considered reasonable for the content you get.All the achievements in this game are really easy, and you’ll get them all by simply playing through the game and completing all the quests—both the main and side quests. I had no issues unlocking any achievements.It might help to check a guide if you have trouble locating something needed for a quest, as you might get lost occasionally. But for the most part, you won’t need one, as you’ll naturally find everything you need while exploring and playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty strong platformer, the controls feel tight, the progression feels natural and there are varying degrees of challenge that can be approached using different methods and tools. It's pretty cool how tightly knit this game is. The explorable world is not very big as you are restricted to a gothic castle in the sky. Even with it being small you will spend quite some time in every area if you're the type to explore. There are hidden weapons, quest items, cosmetics and additional powers for you to discover in every area of the game. The game is a platformer with some very light Metroidvania and Souls elements, if those elements and combat have more priority for you than the 3D platforming then this will not be the game for you. Combat with the average enemy gets dull pretty quick as your combos are very limited, . The boss fights don't really bring anything innovative to the table but make excellent use of the game being a platformer. I think my favorite thing about this game is the voids. The voids are optional platforming maps that you can complete for additional souls, these souls can be spent to unlock equipment slots for additional powers such as the triple jump or double gold bonus. Voids can be approached from several different ways, especially when you start to unlock your spirit powers. These bring together the best components of level design that made PS2 era platformers so good. If you love that older era of 3D platforming games like Jak and Daxter, Vexx, or even Spongebob Squarepants The Movie The Videogame, then this is for you.

U will totally feel at peace leaving the game running in your living room or office where u won't have to worry about people complaining about a awful music playing over n over like those old dvd players did back in the day.Lord! u get some cool weapons fr, they all look cartoonish but so cool, and the attacks with them are cool from the effects. What i like is they didn't feel clunky or poorly made as well.The UI felt great, fluent, fast, and just overall easy to navigate and didn't feel overly complicated or cluttered. _childDocuments_.review: I don't like to thrown 'hidden gem' around often, but I do think this game certainly is that for me. I had never heard about this game until watching an Iron Pineapple video in which it was featured. However, unlike many of the other games he's covered, this was stood out to me and, having played it, for good reason.The visuals of this game are lovely. I never thought something felt out of place, though I did feel that some areas could have used even just a bit more to broaden the appeal or make it stand out a bit more. The music was quite good! It's definitely welcome while running around and trying to find what to do next.The game does lean towards the easier side of the spectrum, which is perfectly fine for me as it's enjoyable to play casually. However, some of the trials you do for more health can be sudden spikes of difficulty which sometimes feel jarring compared to what the game throws at you overall.Lastly, my biggest complaint, which is more a nitpick, is just I wish there was a bit more polish. For example. I found healing to not trigger sometimes when things got frantic in the end and I was moving around more. Usually just slowing down for a moment would let it work, but it was a bit frustrating as, sometimes, the healing would work if I was walking around. Again, nothing that would lower my opinion, but just things I wish were a bit more polished up.Blue Fire is quite a lovely addition to one's library. The experience justifies, and more, the price you'd spend. Or if you catch it on sale, I would highly recommend! Either way, you'd be missing out if you didn't at least give a gander to this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little indie game. It's a similar game to Hollow Knight, but in 3D, with the cell shaded style of Wind Waker and far more about the platforming. The story is alright but a bit paper thin. I suspect there is more lore to read on than there is in the game. If there is, it really should've been in the game. What the game does well (for a budget indie game) is the gameplay. It's not perfect and there are plenty of things I would improve; lots of rough edges and a couple of conflicting design decisions.The combat is serviceable, if not a little rough around the edges when combined with the movement and camera. There are boss fights; most of the early ones are pretty easy. The later ones I've done so far are more difficult but nothing you can't do in a few attempts. The platforming is a lot of fun, but also a little rough around the edges. Some parts of the game, namely the void challenges (optional platforming challenges of varying difficulty) require precision timing and movement, but the game goes out of its way to make it difficult due to the rough camera and how jumping off walls is inconsistent. So far, I've done every challenge so far bar 1 5 star (max difficulty) challenge which required way too much precision for what the game allowed. The camera and lock-on is not that good. By default, the camera has this smoothing behaviour which is really off-putting and has caused a number of deaths. This can be disabled but you lose some of benefits of having a smooth camera. The lock on frequently decides to have a tantrum and face the camera away from the thing it's locking onto, most of the time in the opposite direction. This often means missing some visual queues and where attacks are coming from, which can mean loosing a bit of health, losing progress in a platforming section or death.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Hollow Knight but without the deep exploration but instead there is really tight platforming (sometimes can be too much and camera fov does not help)Like Zelda but without the interesting characters nor fun puzzles but instead there is a decent storyline and nice music with nice environments (doesnt go that deep with the story and enemies don't have a lot of variaty including bosses)Overall a decently fun and goody platformer game

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the fact this game has as few reviews as it does is criminal. Blue Fire is a very fun 3D platformer with all sorts of collectibles to find. The fact that you use emotes to find some of these secrets gives them pleasantly surprising utility. The bosses in the main story are super easy for the most part, but the final boss of the Void of Sorrows DLC is...whew. Speaking of Voids, man are these isolated platforming challenges fun!! The DLC adds some...absolutely difficult ones and the option to go into em without some of the more platforming-friendly abilities like getting a third jump or second dash really adds to the exponential precision-induced suffering quotient. The story is there but mostly bare bones with not many lore scraps to find either which is a bit of a shame, maybe they'll flesh out more in paid DLC down the line. In short, get this if you like 3D platformers, and while it's on sale for $10 it's a steal. They're going to add another free DLC that's basically a 3D platformer Mario Maker so if you're like me and want to play whatever sorts of cruel constructs that other players might have in their minds, possibly involving electric shock and buzzsaws of death, then that's something you can look forward to. Exploration in this game in general is also really fun, there's always something new to discover if you just look around and I think that's pretty special. All in all not just 3D Hollow Knight quit sleeping on this game people WAKE UP AND EMBRACE THE CULT OF QUACK! PS. Quack.

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming indie game. Blue fire feels like a mix between zelda and hollow knight with a bit more emphasis on platforming. The setting, sounds and area design is great. The controls are very quick and responsive. I enjoyed the game so much that I did all the additional side content after completing the game. Now I'm working my way through the DLC (which is free). My only complaint is that just a couple of the void levels (which involve platforming) were a little too complicated. I don't mind the challenge at all, but given that you restart from the very beginning if you make a mistake, it can sometimes lead to the really difficult ones becoming a bit frustrating rather than fun.It should be a crime that a well put together indie game like this falls so far under the radar. A real hidden gem if you enjoy games like zelda, hollow knight or general platforming games.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, the best way I could describe the game feel is "hollowknight lite" with 3d platforming.There is the classic progression of abilities you might be familiar with, you start with just jump and attack, but slowly you gain things like dash, wallrun, double jump, sprint, ranged attack, and spin attack for that extra power and height. You also have "spirits", which work like a simpler version of HK's charms, every one is a single slot, but unlocking slots is part of progress, some are combat QoL, but the real juicy ones are for mobility, increase dash range, have 2 dash charges, increased spin attack height, faster movement overall, extending every platform by letting you walk several steps after the cliff. The combination of all movement abilities makes you feel like a movement god, and I very much appreciate it.Combat is rather barebones in comparison, you have ranged and parry using the same mana resource (also upgradable), ground combo and aerial combo (naturally weapon can be upgraded too). The mob encounters are kind of mundane, and you'll probably parry every once in a while for a dopamine hit, but that's about it. Where it shines is bosses, cause there movement starts playing a bigger role, you've got all kinds of AoE and projectiles you've gotta watch out for.The devs noticed which parts they were good at, so the free DLC (accessible in first Fire Keep area, cause it was not obvious to me at all) focuses on that. The short platforming challenges called "voids" were sprinkled throughout the game and allowed you to increase your health, instead in the dlc they added more of them, and way more challenging ones, closer to what white palace in HK would be. In the end you get a new special boss, in a pretty bad plot twist, but oh well, playing through it was definitely worth my time.Visually the game is pretty distinct, I might not be a fan of some textures and models repeating, and some areas being insanely more barren than the starting locations, but the artstyle carries it hard on its back. The architecture, varied biomes, stylized vfx are all mixed into something that never tired me through the 20 hours.Similarly the music, while somewhat minimal, adds to the charm and mood of the game. I might listen to main theme and "abandoned path" sometime outside of the game, but it's not absolute top shelf material.Story is filled with exposition, and while fairy tale background and lore is decent in many aspects, it didn't pull out anything unexpected. The one time it tried in the dlc, it failed miserably. I don't want to bully it too hard, cause it does have some good in it, and there is potential in writers of the studio.Overall, I think it's worth it, it has some jank, but also a lot to enjoy. It goes for pretty cheap sometimes, and if the sales and recommendations (especially including feedback for the dlc) are high enough, they might drop even more content for it, and I'd be down to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I often make reviews before completing the game, but this time I was determined to beat the game first and it wasn't hard to keep myself playing. Thanks to my friend for buying me this for my birthday. It's not the longest game as you can see from my hours, but each hour was packed with good challenges and entertainment. It's not the most challenging platformer but it doesn't need to be and as someone who doesn't play platformers much because I suck, I really appreciate that. Still, there's some really tough challenges especially in the Void runs I very nearly gave up on many times but thankfully those are optional. The sound design/quality is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, it's like my subwoofer has never been properly utilized until I first booted the game. The level design is fantastic, the graphics are cute but also keep me immersed in the world, I love everything except maybe the combat. It feels a little lacking at times, most noticeably during boss battles. Still, mechanically there's no issues. I ran into one bug in Stoneheart City where I was dashing around in the air and fell down towards a corner directly ahead when facing the shrine which caused me to fall for eternity below the map but aside from that I've had no issues.The story is nothing to write home about but I'd rather have that simple and proven structure than something trying to be more complex and clever than it knows how, something I've seen in too many games these days.There's a lot of clear inspirations taking place in this game and it takes from them in all the right ways and places. Dark Souls, Zelda, Assassin's Creed(?), Hollow Knight, likely some others I didn't notice. The blend felt very natural and right.As I said the game isn't super long, but it doesn't have to be. It reminds me of the days of Ocarina of Time where I could beat it in a full work day. I also said I don't normally play or like platformers very much, but this one is different. What we have here is a gem, and I don't use that term lightly. Props to the team, I hope this game blows up, it deserves it.brightshadow (top neg review currently) raises some very valid concerns I hadn't thought much about, except for that last part about the final boss. I figured it out pretty fast, they aren't THAT hard. I was hoping for a good challenge at the end and we got one, but it's not ridiculously challenging. If you've beaten a 3 star Void run you can beat the final boss first or second try.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, great game, you should buy it, but it could use a "director's cut"I've played the entire base game of Blue Fire and seriously enjoyed myself. The platforming is tight and responsive, and many of the game's areas force you to be creative in your navigation. The early game is strong, with lots of rewarding exploration, and while your move set is limited at the outset, you'll quickly learn to be creative, and the two temples you come across are definite highlights, with lots of rewarding puzzles.Unfortunately, as you reach the back half of the game the quality starts to fall off. There are no more temples before the bosses, instead it feels more like a boss rush. Nothing ever approaches the density and inexorability of Stoneheart City. It's still enjoyable, but it seems the devs were running out of time and/or money as they got to the second half, and the experience suffers accordingly. This game is prime material for a director's cut that would polish what's there, and flesh out the second half.Overall I would still strongly recommend you play Blue Fire, just be aware that it will fall off in the last half to third or so.

_childDocuments_.review: Zelda Wind Waker Design with Souls-Like Precision PlatformingIf you're like me and love platformers then this is right up your alley. I did not expect a couple of challenge rooms in that it was gonna have me doing strafe-jumps. So in that regard, you know the kind of challenge you're gonna be getting right out the gate.This game I feel like would have been more well-known and loved if it weren't for the time of release. A lot of platformer fans skipped this one because Little Nightmares 2 came out a week later and Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury a day after.Pros• Controls/combat are smooth and responsive• Collectibles aren't too frustrating to acquire and are rewarding. I like a lot of the skins offered• Graphics are nice to look at• Challenge rooms are fun and some are quite tough• Each area is unique in the sense of it's not the same dullness you can sometimes see in games these days and utilize your power-ups well with traversal• This is mainly a 'me' thing, but I found fun in finding cheese spots to cut corners and collect things that otherwise forces you to acquire them later in the game. I actually managed to get some earlier on just by abusing platforming mechanics, wall running and the like. Felt rewarding for the time I put in.Cons• If you don't like platformers then stay away. My wife doesn't like jumping puzzle games/platformers and mentioned during my game play that she wouldn't be able to play this and probably would have quit an hour in• The music is 'meh'. I don't know if it was just my volume because I played with the default, but there wasn't much and the music was not memorable for me after completing the game• Sometimes the targeting for ranged weapons is finicky/janky. Only happened a few times, but when it does you'll likely have a "Bruh" moment like I did.• Not much replayability. Once you complete this game there isn't much reason to boot it up again unless you want 100% which is collecting things, so onto the next one is likely what most players will do once you get credits.Overall 9/10 and I recommend. Had a lot of fun with it and I wish it was more popular and well known.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game after the first major update since launch (in August 2021). Many bugs people complained about seem to have been patched, because I didn’t experience any game-breaking bug.There are 2 difficulty levels: newcomer (easy) and recommended (normal). I played on “recommended”.:• Visually stunning• Music is great• Freedom to explore, and interesting and diverse areas• No map, which makes it feel really rewarding once you figure out how to get to where you want to go. The world isn’t that huge to require a map, and I think it would be way less immersive if there was a map.• No waypoint markers, which also makes everything more immersive, rewarding, and makes the screen less cluttered. There aren’t many main quests and side quests, so it’s not that hard to keep in mind what your objectives are while exploring.• Steam achievements are, essentially, completing all the quests. I like how straight-forward it is. There’s nothing absurd like “Complete the game in 2 hours without dying” or hidden achievements you would never find out without looking up on the Internet.:• Enemies get too powerful too fast. It’s scary at first, because out of nothing you walk into enemies that can kill you with 2 or 3 hits. But once you get used to how they behave, it’s not that hard to deal with them.• Special rooms in which your platforming skills are put to the test. Some of them are REALLY hard, and there are only checkpoints in the newcomer mode. And the camera angles sometimes get annoying… However, it feels very rewarding once you beat them, and the rewards you get really help you become stronger.• Lack of enemy diversity. Throughout the game you face very similar enemies, it’s like they’re the same, but just wearing a different costume. It felt boring at first, but later I realized that it didn’t matter to me, because on this type of game the combat is not really what I care about, so having a lot of enemies behaving in a similar way ended up making things easier.• The bosses are kind of boring. It’s hard to understand the pattern of some bosses, and in some cases it’s hard to use the function to lock the camera on them. I just ended up smashing buttons. I was able to kill most of them on the first try (even the final one), though, and it never took me more than two tries to kill any of them. So, in the end, since I’m much more into exploring than into combat, it didn’t matter that much.:• There’s some dialogue with bosses in a language invented for the game, which is kind of impossible to decode, so I hated going through dialogue that I could not understand.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is one of the best 3d platformers you can get, especially for it's price... But it's not great. The genre has seen some pretty serious stagnation.Blue Fire has combat that is very shallow, and it's movement system is very boring. After slogging through the very slow paced early game, you eventually get access to a range of abilities that is pretty basic.Three jumps, two dashes, a wallrun, and (most interestingly) boots that let you walk off of platforms for a few seconds. The issue with the entire game is that the platforming built off of this relatively basic movement is pretty restricted. The level design just isn't that great as a result. It's all super linear, instead of the open ended platforming across rooftops that makes other basic 3d platformers fun.The most interesting thing you'll see on the platforming side is some basic floating blocks that you'll be chaining wallruns and double jumps off of.For the combat, you'll see a few basic enemy types that aren't utilized in interesting ways. Run away from the different flavors of explody boys, and dash around the bullets of the turrets. Boss fights usually involve dodging some basic hazards in between hits.Still, the exploration is actually pretty fun, even with the basic movement set. Oh yeah, and the sound design is weirdly pretty good for a game that looks like this. The sound effects were great, and the music was really well put together.I feel the foundation of this game is very bland, but at I got it at $6 on sale... For all of it's simplicity, it's still a pretty competent game. It'd be hard not to recommend it at that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: "Blue Fire" is a captivating entry into the metroidvania genre, often recommended as a "3D Hollow Knight." While this comparison holds true in terms of concept, it falls short in execution when compared to the richly detailed world of Hollow Knight.The combat in "Blue Fire" is undeniably fun, albeit a bit easy (especially for seasoned Metroidvania players). There are three difficulty options, and I picked "normal," which felt too easy. The platforming segments (which are all optional and each provide a maximum HP upgrade) are enjoyable as well, with most being very easy, though some present a real challenge.One of the most intriguing aspects of "Blue Fire" is its nostalgic charm. Many areas in the game evoke a sense of familiarity, such as the Lava area, which reminded me of Skyward Sword. However, the environments, while familiar, are ultimately forgettable. None of them stand out as particularly new or unique, as they fall into familiar tropes like sewers, castles, lava areas, and temples. That said, the graveyard area stood out with its artistic charm and is the best area for me in terms of visual appeal.Unfortunately, the lore and story of "Blue Fire" are not particularly engaging. I can't recall the names of any characters, as none made a significant impact or stuck in my mind. The merchants didn't offer items or services memorable enough to commit their locations or inventories to memory. Additionally, the protagonist doesn't seem to interact meaningfully with the narrative, and I was left unsure of his connection to the story—perhaps I missed something.Despite its shortcomings, "Blue Fire" stands out as a solid indie game. Its unique take on the metroidvania style in a 3D environment offers a refreshing experience that fans of the genre will appreciate. If you're looking for an entertaining and well-performing game, "Blue Fire" is definitely worth a try.

Writing this review makes me as sad as i got when i found out i had to open up a new save... Or try to noclip through the door with cheat engine.PS: Ducks, that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, before i start this, i just wanted to put this disclaimer here: i am definitely biased towards this game due to the length of time I've been following it. however, i will do my best to keep my biases out of this, just know that they do exist. just wanted to give that heads up. anyways, blue fire time.there is so much i love about this game. the visuals are great, the soundtrack is awesome and stands up regardless of repetition, its nice and difficult, its one of those games that just oozes charm. however, the crowning jewel of it has to be the gameplay, especially the movement. it is quite frankly phenomenal. it handles EXACTLY as it feels like it should, and feels so good to play! as such, its actually a really good speed game (both i and my hours of play time on record can testify to this fact).unfortunately, it does fall short at a few places, specifically with the low amount of dungeons, and the story. first, the dungeon point. unfortunately, for budget and time reasons, the devs had to scrap a notable amount of content, leaving some things feeling kinda unfinished. _childDocuments_.review: This game desperately wants to be a 3D Hollow Knight. Unfortunately, the only aspect which stands up to the inspiration is the art style.The combat is completely bland. Enemies are few and far-between, and your options are laughably limited. The core 3-swing combo is detrimental to use, as most enemies will attack and hit you after you're locked into the third swing but before they get hit by it. There is a block and a ranged attack, however the former is infinitely clunkier to use than just dashing away from an enemy and then dashing back, the latter is laughably underpowered and borderline useless, and both share a limited resource in mana, which is never really explained. I 100% completed the game, never used the fireball and rarely used the shield, and still have no idea what gets you your mana back. The platforming is most of what this game is, either tranversal within the game world, or completing the linear 'Void' sub-areas for HP upgrades. In fact, the 'Spirits' (literally just Hollow Knight's 'Charms') overwhelmingly affect your movement over combat, and I never found myself using any of them that didn't boost my movement in some manner. The Void stages remind me of the secret stages in Super Mario Sunshine, only you keep your entire kit within them. They are rated in difficulty, which you can see before entering, and there are only 2 significantly difficult ones (each of which took me 30-45 minutes alone). That said, the game does handle failure and checkpoints quite well. The Void subareas don't punish you for failure beyond returning you to a checkpoint when you fall (unlike my main gripe with Hollow Knight, where failing a platforming section too many times sent you all the way back to a spawn point with a death), but they do suffer from a LOT of wasted time. Many of them are very vertical, and the only 'death plane' is at the very bottom, so if you're on the final checkpoint, and fall, you have to fall for a good 5-10 seconds before getting to try again. This adds up VERY quickly on the harder Voids, where you also have cycles and moving platforms to wait on, dragging each attempt at a section out a frustrating amount.Additionally, Blue Fire suffers from the classic 3D platforming problem of a terrible camera. While I never encountered any times where the camera moved itself into a poor position, I would often be trying to tackle a platforming section, get past something like a swinging sawblade, and then have the same sawblade cut off the camera while I was trying to do the next bit. Or just being forced to platform in odd ways while also having to pilot the camera to see what I'm doing, while adjusting my angle on the left stick to continue moving the direction I want as the camera spins. And don't get me started on the total lack of depth perception. I cannot count the amount of times I was hit by a trap or attack that I would have swore was relatively either in front or behind me. Many long sections of swinging traps in some voids are completely devoid of any ground or other possible indicator of where exactly the hazards are, beside that they're swinging by in some general area.The atmosphere, at least, is pretty good. The art is gorgeous, and the music fits the setting alright. It's not a soundtrack I'd return to, and I never found myself just looking around enjoying the scenery, but it works. The story (and the writing as a whole) leaves quite a bit to be desired. In fact, a good bit of the main storyline does feel directly ripped from Hollow Knight (defeat 3 big bosses to open door to final boss, the main character being a smol construct of the evil force and the good force, etc). The parts that don't are okay, but are often just presented via blocks of exposition.The biggest disappointment, in my opinion, was the dungeons. They were actually pretty good! Legend of Zelda format, with single use keys and a 'key item' that granted a new ability partway through. The problem is that there really aren't any. There's the first 'tutorial' dungeon, then you are immediately sent to the second with hints about there being 5, one for each god that needs saving. Then, after the second, that particular plotline is thrown away entirely, and it shifts to the Hollow Knight-esque 'explore to find the 3 bosses to open the door to the final boss'. There's another 'dungeon' later on, with one of these macguffin bosses at the end of it, but it's significantly worse than the others, and mostly just consists of a few linear platforming challenges, then leaving to go get the key for the boss from a random cutscene.I 100% completed the game in under 9 hours, with no guides at all. If you really like 3D platformers, and also enjoyed Hollow Knight, you might get your money worth if you buy Blue Fire on sale, but ultimately, I don't think I can recommend it at full price. If you are interested in Blue Fire, and  played Hollow Knight, go play Hollow Knight first, then come back if you're REALLY jonesing for a mediocre 3D platformer inspired by it.

_childDocuments_.review: great platforming mixed in with satisfying exploration and decent combat make for a very fun souls like platformer. Blue Fire takes the bonfire mechanic and some level design concepts from dark souls while adding a lot more verticality to account for the platforming focus. Movement feels good, with a great dash, jump and other abilities you unlock later. Platforming around the world map feels good, and gives you enough freedom to make your own shortcuts once you've mastered the movement. There are optional challange rooms called Voids that reward you with extra max health, and these are straight forward challenges that will test your abilities.The challenge mostly comes in the platforming itself, I died only twice in the whole game, to two bosses, so combat is generally pretty forgiving, especially if you do a lot of the voids and have a lot of max health.Overall I really liked this game, the atmosphere is great, the gameplay is great, and mixing in Souls like and 3D Platformer made for a pretty unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun 3D action platformer with tight controls, this is the game you're looking for. As many others have stated, Blue Fire is like a mix of old school Legend of Zelda dungeons with something like Hollow Knight, and in my opinion it pulls it off really well. This game has a cute and charming aesthetic, fun and varied level designs that feel satisfying to explore, and tight fast paced gameplay that'll keep you engaged all the way through. The only negative I can think of is the combat is fairly mediocre (except for the bosses which're pretty fun), but if you go into it expecting to mainly focus on the platforming, I think you'll really enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I finshed the main story and all expect 2 or 3 of the basic (none-DLC) voids. You can probably finish the game in 10h or so, if you tried. Side stories and such add quite a bit more hours. That said, the game doesn't really tell you very clearly where to go. There was one point where wandered around for 1-2 hours because I did not understand where to go. Without googling I would not have found it. The story is fine. It's nothing special but it's not bad. The secrets, hidden quests and so on, also the side quests, are actually really nice and fun. The combat is very meh. You don't have a lot of options. You usually just use dash and smash things with your sword. You have a limited amount of mana for ranged attack which can help but also does terrible damage.Early enemies are kinda easy. Later ones are a bit tedious. Firing laser at you every second and if you have no mana for the ranged attack it's very tricky to take some enemies out. There is also a wurm that hides when you get near him. And he snipes you across the map. You have to perfectly parry his attack to kill him. Nothing tells you that and it can be very, very frustrating if you do not know that.Overall though, the game feels like it's 80% finished. A lot of mechanics are there, but just don't feel very fluent. Your standard 3 attack pattern does a medium dash at the end. You probably will dash off a platform at some point. Doesn't happen very often, but it's just annoying. The wall grab/jump is miserable. Sometimes you grab a wall when you don't want to, stoping your jump when you needed to get height and killing you. Other times wall grabs will not register when you are trying to wall jump. It's dumb.Voids. Voids are a really cool idea. And they are just.... not as fun as they should be. A lot of crystals or platforms are quite small. And since they are floating somewhere in the air it's rather hard to judge distances. In additional, you have to look at so many different things from so many different angles. It's very easy to miss something, die and then have to start over again. It would be way more enjoyable if you could actually move as you wanted in the harder ones. However, often it feels like the camera or game itself screws you over. I don't regret buying the game. If I new beforehand how the gameplay would feel though, I wouldn't have bought it. If you are calm and patient and don't mind games where you sometimes get screwed by the game. I think this is a great to pick up. If you want a game that plays smooth and where you can only blame yourself when you die, then it's probably not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gemThis game starts out a bit like Dark Souls - no context, same slow, dead, gothic vibes, no tutorial save for a few ground messages about basic controls, and a slowly revealed history told by barely coherent NPCs showing up in the weirdest places, with a single central town (well, no spoilers). What I was not prepared for this game to be is living up the high standards set by Hollow Knight: this game a very serious platformer, where you start out with a basic jump, but eventually you'll get more movement options that I really don't want to spoil away here, allowing you access to previously unaccessable areas of the world map that you may have passed a couple times since. Which is important, because the world is smartly interconnected, and there is no world map, local map, quest marker for anything, to guide you: you are completely on your own, and I loved this because I was forced to remember everything, and I highly recommend you to go in blindly and use no wikipedia or youtube guide (I did not one switch where I needed 4 and missed only 1, than had to facepalm how could I forget that long poisonous hall I never went through despite having the abilities to do so for a long time at that point). Combat will forever remain simple, bosses are kind of easy, but it's not really the point, the point is always exploration, platforming, remembering where you may have came across cute, weird, and generally goodhearted NPCs you can interact with. Also you can find emotes that you may think is not a huge deal in a singleplayer game, but doing the right emote at the right place (little marker on the floor depicting the emote) will get you a new equipment, so you can find really fancy new character skins and stronger swords (there is only one weapon with increasingly stronger attack damage but trust me, it's that kind of game where this is enough).What the game truly excels at is platforming. Movement and controls are incredibly fluid and comfortable, the map design is awesome and keeps expanding the already known locations with new layers as you grow, camera is smartly used (there are looking glasses sometimes offering you alternative angles if you are not that much into finding a new platform that is usually hidden by a wall you could jump over, just did not think so if you should). Also there are Voids, which are essentially standalone challenge maps, which if you successfully finish will increase your maximum HP and you'll need that for the final boss. Also you get a neat skin if you finish them all. This is one of the very, very few games where I did everything to the point of 100%-ing it out with all Achievements, and while 12 hours playtime doesn't seem like much, it very much is. The game doesn't feel short at all, nor too long, it ends where it should, although the ending is a bit abrupt (you defeat the final boss, and the credits IMMEDIATELY roll, no ending cutscene or anything, or showing the fate of the world, the people you met, or you, it's just... over in 1 second). But!You loved this game, and you want more of it: here comes the Void Maker, a free upgrade to the game where everyone gets a map maker to create their own insane platforming challenge maps, and share it with overs. And suddenly this game is Trackmania, and oh boy the content just never ends. Highly recommended at roughly 50% off if you are from a poorer region like me (or as part of any bundle, you may even have it from a Humble Choice / Bundle and not be aware of it), and recommended if the full price is your hourly wage.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 2,6 hours now, and did 10 %. It seems like a shorter game, but hey, it's not as expensive too. So it's a good deal!This game feels like a wild mix of Legend of Zelda: Windwaker, Mario 64 and Dark Souls.Here is why:- Fighting, the health and inventory system and generel the controls are very inspired bei Legend of Zelda. You have little hearts as life points and you have a similar fighting and lock on system.- The void levels feels like the vertical towerish levels from Mario 64.- Your progression through the world is linear with some hubs and short cuts. Together with the you "you die you start at the safepoint. And if you die again you loose your money." system is clearly inspired by Dark Souls.So far I really like this game. _childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is really likeable, you can see that devs put in effort and soul, but the game is really lacking in gameplay design.Graphics/visual style and music are on point.In almost every other aspect there are always some major oversights:Platforming:Overall, controls are good and there are some good platforming sections in overworld. The entire thing reminds me most of A Hat in Time - similar speed, inertia, movement physics - but Blue Fire is a bit more advanced. Now the problems. First off, a game does a very poor job of telling you where you can go and which spot is out of reach yet. You might struggle with a ledge that seems just a tiny bit out of reach or even on the opposite - sequence break another spot. The platforming challenges called voids are big (bigger than should be allowed sometimes) gauntlets that return you to the beginning if you fail. And they really ARE long. Combined with awful depth perception inside them and the fact that you cannot see your shadow on some platforms makes them painfully frustrating. They might quickly turn from a side attraction to the worst part of the game. And this game reeeaaaly likes to put those voids everywhere, while not letting you play them from at least a checkpoint. Fall damage. In a 3D platformer. Granted, you can negate it with any of your moves, but why is this a concern in the first place?Environment blurs and stretches while dashing/falling. Mmm, headache fuel.Combat:Actually, this one is awful in its entirety. It feels like they were making a decent platformer and then forced *this* in. The only good enemy type to fight against is a typical sword-slashing knight. That’s it. Good relative to the rest. All your foes do little to none attack indication or wind-up, those that do are incredibly slow.There are small critters that attack you immediately after you step close to them, some of which can get you stunlocked. Then we have pulse-emitters just to annoy you during platforming. Then the exploding blobs which blow up with no proper visual cue of radius or timing. Then the laser blobs - go from boring to stupidly overpowered with each new iteration.Bosses - can't say much about them or if  they’re really bad or good. Just mediocre. They can be a challenge but are at the same time a chore.Level design:Overworld is mostly fine with some nicely placed secrets, decorations change frequently, layouts rarely repeat.Additionally, some areas have some old Zelda-like dungeons. They’re zelda dungeons, that’s all I can say. Maybe you hate this design, maybe you like it. On the other hand, in many locations you won’t feel any verticality at all. The environments might seem small, but they are a bit labyrinthian, while you have no map, good luck.There is a problem with knowing where you can or can’t go I mentioned in platforming. The game forces you to visit an NPC to ‘pop souls’, in other words sell stuff for currency. And currency is another story here.Checkpoints are extremely rare and make you pay for them.Overworld is divided into rooms which load after you go in. And sometimes there is an obstacle on the other side. Now go back and wait for it to load again.This is hard to explain, but there is almost nothing to help you quickly get back to action after you fall into a pit/liquid. Most rooms have spots that bring you back on every entrance. No more, no less. And times when the game has the decency to face you in the right direction might compete in rarity with checkpoints. Inventory and journal:You can get different looking robes. Cool.Journal though is filled with redundant information about completed quests and empty spots for quests you haven’t yet found. They made the emotion list dynamic, what’s the problem here?Limited wallet. Did we travel back in time somehow? An awful fragment of the past, at least devs back then did it to restrict story progress. Here, as far as I know, it's just an annoyance. A big stain of ♥♥♥♥.Spirits - an analogue of Hollow Knight charm system. They contrast with the game’s style greatly. They’re more like some scribbles. Maybe their effects  are better? No.I’ll summarize here - if you have a high pain tolerance and a lot of patience - try it. It’s good at first, maybe you’ll get into it and forgive the game’s flaws. It has blatant disregard for your time and almost never exercises good design practises, but at the same time it has a charming feel to it.
