_childDocuments_.review: Before my review, I'd like to mention that I'm not a big fan of RPG games because they have an extremely complicated story, items and elements. Well you can make a great RPG game but you need to explain to the user carefully and clearly. It's a hard and delicate process to entertain and let the user understand your game. Well, Blue Fire's story and mechanics is easily understandable and you get more powerful and better at platform parkour over time. Speaking of parkour, The voids are challenging and fun. You try to collect "soul ores" while you are jumping through flying platforms & wallrunning them. Let's talk graphics. Normally a team of thousands of artists, devs, directors make a game that looks really well and realistic. Robi Studios which is an indie game developer team with 8 people achieved AAA levels of realistic textures and graphics. Now about the topic that most of negative reviewers say. Crashes. Yes, just after the game released to people I immediately bought it and encountered like 4-5 crashes in the time of 3 hours. Mostly in loading screens. Here's some reasons that this might not be a problem. 1- The devs are open to any bug reports and they know any crashes if you send them what happened. 2- This game has been released on 4th of February 2021. When a game releases, users will find out bugs and report them at the early days for an update. 3- Devs will eventually fix crashes. So those negative reviews won't be valid reasons anymore. It actually already happened. The update is currently out and I can confidentally say that crashes are fixed. Now on to the price, basically cheap enough that you can enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: The word I'm looking for is frustrating. Well actually the words I'm looking for would make steam draw a little row of hearts, so let's just stick with frustrating.the movement feels slippery, the combat is insultingly easy, everything is poorly explained (I was taught how to emote but not how to parry) and the level design is so bad that there has to be a cutscene at the start of some rooms to tell you where the points of interest are. That just feels lazy imo.The thing that made me call it was early on where a section of platforming has you running around on some pipes above an acid pit. Pretty standard fair for this particular genre, but the edges of the pipe were fully rounded so going even a hair over the edge meant you would just slip off into the pit.I'm sure my opinion on this game isn't helped by the fact I just finished Pseudoregalia (a far superior platformer) but I don't think my conclusion would have been much better under normal circumstances. For sure a lot of my complaints could be fixed by the sacred art of git gud, but alas gitting gud can't fix the boring art style and the bland sound design.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite good and is generally fun to play and most definitely fulfills the promise of a cross between classic zelda and hollow knight but i do have quite a few nitpicks about it as a whole, first off the lore is given in the third area, second the damage is relatively clustered, ore without selling (only available in stoneheart) is incredibly slow and grindy with enemies dropping balls that are important for mana and if not you need to manually go to the inn or arcane tunnel void statue and break a ton of stuff for ore, third the parry window is tight and doesn't deal much damage and even when you do land it; it isn't usually the best option as most encounters are ganks or enemies with AOE attacks that impede approach. I found the most viable option to be jump away dash, slash two-five times then jump slash again DI away repeat, fourth the queen of darkness boss fight is very hard to understand at the first phase and without proper spirits is hard to air stall long enough to outlast the orb, fifth spirits are relatively left field and incredibly unbalanced like triple jump, double dash, phantom platforms, and double heal which allows you to cheese most overworld obstacles, six this isn't a nitpick more a general grievance but the last five voids are just super meatboy-path of pain-celeste masochism fests, seventh despite being told of 6 gods we only ever get to see 3 of them and the others merely in a retrospective cutscene and items, eighth the general progression after reaching rusty village is vague at best and troubling at worse with multiple backtracking quests just to finish the game, ninth the overworld wall slide is very constricting which is fine but makes early game walljumping janky and annoying, tenth emotion statues are a neat addition but there's no multiplayer to show them off yet the platforms have no checkmarking and the rewards are completion fluff, eleventh the nomad literally rips you off, twelfth the ore total leave tons of ore to be needed in order to get all the items, finally thirteenth (and this is important) the namesake blue fire is very hard to acquire with six of the ten being mid to late game two are just randomly sold by the innkeeper's daughter in stoneheart. Overall 8/10 would play again (except those last voids)Edit: Void of sorrows:Wow, this was a truly amazing dlc; It too a substantial amount of time to complete and the voids were simply gut wrenching and painful yet oh so rewarding. The new npc was a underwhelming to say the least and the Von boss fight had questionable lore and was much easier than I personally expected given what it takes to initiate it. However on the topic of difficulty the void were notably unbalanced but were all fun with a little bit of jank hitboxes on things like the moving death platforms or those invisible platform switches, on some voids it takes like 10 minutes while on others it takes a marathon. On the outfit side and weapon side it wasn't much but what was there wasn't bad. Overall 9/10 very good and worthwhile especially for a free dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: 3d Platformer with Zelda elements. If you enjoy 3d platformers then this is definitely gonna be fun, the movement feels good and apart from the first area the levels make traversal very fun, I often had the feeling of "was I supposed to do it like this or did I find a skip?" which is the best feeling in these games. Especially the combat and most bosses are just turn your brain off fights, apart from the final boss and the dlc boss which were pretty good. I played it on normal so maybe it's better on hard, but I feel like hard mode would only make the bosses more fun but the regular enemies more tedious.Overall I feel like it is pretty rough in some areas but the core gameplay of platforming is very well done with interesting challenges, for me it had around 12 hrs of gameplay in it.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot say that I am a huge fan of 3D platformers, but I am a huge fan of souls-likes. And Blue Fire makes me think that indie soulslikes should be 2D.First off, I wanna say few words about platforming. I found the camera to be so terrible that it alone makes me wanna stop playing. In this game you need precise movement very often, and seeing where your character will actually go after jumping (especially off the wall) is borderline impossible in some cases.Dark Souls comes to my mind here because camera was terrible in that game too; but at least you did not need to do wall jumps and precise dashes there...Second, atmosphere. I personally did not like the semi-cartoon-ish artstyle here, but that would be ok if there was a compelling story / lore to compensate. But this game also tries to be sort of comedic and 4th wall breaking at times, which just does not fit.As for combat, the fighting itself is ok IMO, but the terrible camera hurts it thrice:1. dashing jumping mid-combat is just not good, because it is hard to predict where your character will land2. lock-on helps a bit, but in here it does not work right IMO. It is very hard to explain though3. finally, it is just overall very easy (I beat the first boss, and I did not die to enemies a single time during my playtime)I feel bad criticizing this game so much, as I can see that devs tried hard with it, and I really hope other people will like it more than I did

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire isn't a bad game but I just never had fun with it. It looks fine, controls fine, has okay combat, and I like what it's going for with a mix of Hollow Knight and Zelda. But it also has none of the charm of either of those games and is just a meandering, dull experience. I don't think levels were procedurally generated but the overall world structure is so sloppy and bizarre that it sometimes feels that way. It's never fun to explore, checkpoints are few and far between, and signposting is nonexistant. And why are key NPCs that you're expected to return to buried in the middle of dungeons where otherwise you have no reason? Blue Fire is also home to maybe the worst "town" I've ever seen in a game. I can't even describe what it was going for.Again, there's nothing mechanically really wrong with this game but it's just not worth the time to play. The story is especially bland as it's the same generic fantasy tripe you've heard a hundred times. What if there were gods but one god was bad but then also there were knights and one knight was bad and you're the only one that can save this world for reasons that aren't explained even a bit. Also for some reason there's a character that's more capable than you that's always behind doors you unlock waiting for you who only exists to lore dump and then leave instead of actually helping for...reasons. Ugh.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a definite must play for people who enjoy deep and fluid movement in their platformers. Blue Fire has some of the best movement in any game I have ever played, and the progression of your move set is vary satisfying as the game unfolds through upgrades that you gain in dungeons as well as spirits that you may find while exploring. What the game lacks in story and combat it makes up with a deep atmosphere and rewarding exploration that will make you want to see exactly what the next location holds.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This is seriously one of my favorite games of all time. The platforming is challenging but rewarding, movement feels great and can be so much fun with certain spirits equipped. The story is great with the dlc giving a pretty good wrap up to it. the game probably takes about 10 hours to beat with looking for everything, (that's how I did it and that's about how long it took me) but as you can see from my play time, I'm still able to have fun with it even after beating the game and I would totally recommend Blue Fire for any player who loves 3D platforming with the fun puzzles that come from games like the Legend of Zelda Series and the charm brought from Hollow Knight.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely great action adventure game that did scracth that pre-BOTW Zelda itch!• Gameplay •Take Zelda, Mario-like obstacle courses, add a hub-world akin to Banjo-Kazooie's, add some dashing and wallruninng for some precision-platforming and you've got Blue Fire! Aside from the main quest there are some sidequests to do, some collectables to get and a variety of themed areas to explore.This game did really feel like the classic Zelda formula to me, which is something I miss since the new BOTW format.• Graphics •Very stylized and colorful, not dissimilar to Wind Waker's art direction, just a bit darker. The graphics aren't extremely impressive by any means, but work well for this game and the color palettes in some environments are very nice indeed.• Soundtrack •To be honest, I didn''t really notice the soundtrack. This means it doesn't stand out, but also doesn't stand out in a negative way. It fit the game well, but just isn't very important to the experience.• Story •Defintely Blue Fire's weak spot. There is a story, and while some of the sidequests can have pretty cute short stories, the main plot is pretty standard and bland. It's basically the usual "sealed evilness has awakened and you need to stop it" situation. It works, it drives the game, but it's certainly not why you should play it.• Performance & Bugs •I have experienced some weird glitches that needed rebooting the game, and I have heard from some people it's possible to get game-breaking bugs as well... Overall I didn't have much issues though. Performance was great, I played the game on Steam Deck. Only Deck-specific issue seems that cloud saves don't work.• Fun Factor •A lot of fun! The tight controls, varied environments and upgradable abilities made this game great to play. Some sections are EXTREMELY hard and did frustrate me somewhat, but I'm absolutely looking forward to a sequel!!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Although my expectations were a bit wrong, blue fire is in itself a decent game.The trailer got me excited because of the impression of a zelda-like style.Although Blue Fire has some similar details here and there, I was a bit disappointed with this comparison.Blue fire has challenging parts such as courses that you must be able to complete flawlessly.As you progress through the game you will also unlock new skills and moves that will be required to complete later courses.The textures of the characters & locations in the game are also very special and beautiful to look at, just like the music and the game sounds bring out the atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best indie game I've played in the past three years. This game combines the challenging platforming of Hollow Knight, backtracking for key progression items like Metroid, dungeon design loosely inspired from Zelda, and aesthetics borrowed from Hollow Knight and Dark Souls. I got around 18 hours out of the game which is more than I expected to be honest, and the whole game felt alive all the way through! Puzzles were easy enough to figure out but fun and thought provoking enough to not take away from the pacing. The story was decent, you could definitely tell some inspiration from Dark Souls and Zelda which isn't inherently bad just could be a bit more original. I did encounter some minor issues with combat, platforming, and a few other things that could be tuned but otherwise I heavily anticipate the next release from Robi Studios!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun for everyone that likes games similar to Ori and the Blind Forest. Overall it is a really great game and i had a lot of fun playing it. However, later in the game there are some quality of live issues. SPOILER WARNINGThe first levels and dungeons where pretty neat although a bit too easy. I 2 hitted the first 2 bosses which isn't all too bad since this is mainly a Platformer. However, in the Lategame you have to fight 3 "Lords". Nice idea done well, BUT i raged quite a lot, not because of the difficulty of these which is quite up there, but rather because i have to get to a Loading screen after a rather long walk-up, only to have an UNSKIPPABLE cutscene of 15 seconds of a door opening. Which sucked since i died a lot doing these. The last boss has the same problem: You cross an area, to get to a loading screen, to walk up to another loading screen, to get to the boss. Really annoying wait times. And this game also likes to crash during a loading screen. But overall i liked it, altough i wish there would be some quality of life improvements, like spawning in front of the boss after you died, while the Door is still open, since you have the item required.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be straight with saying that I'm on the fence about giving this a negative review. I might come back and review this after fully finishing the game.I'll also say that unlike others, I've not experienced any crashes yet so I can't comment on how bad that is, though I expect there will be followup patches to correct those issues anyway.My biggest problem though is the insane amount of platforming. I stayed spoiler-free going into this and simply knew that it had elements of The Legend of Zelda, Hollow Knight, and Dark Souls. This sounded like the perfect set of games to mix together and indeed, in the very beginning of the game there are plenty of hints that this is the experience you're in for.However, as you start getting into the story, the combat doesn't ramp up but instead the platforming does. And by platforming, I mean that if you miss a jump then you usually fall into a bottomless pit (or the equivalent of that) and lose significant amounts of life. And of course, the only way to increase your health pool is to complete shrines which are essentially ramped-up platforming stages.You know this game is for you if you say yes to all of the following:- Do you enjoy punishing platforming to navigate between main areas? - Is the idea of reaching a new town boring to you, specifically because towns are usually safe spaces free from getting hurt?-  Do you instead wish you could be forced to engage in platforming exercises to navigate said towns, knowing that if you miss a jump then you'll be granted the gift of having to do all that sweet, sweet platforming all over again in order to meet whichever NPC you were originally looking for?- Do you enjoy the idea of entering platforming sub-stages while ALREADY in a main dungeon (which, of course, is driven solely by platforming)?- Do you basically wish someone took the saying "When all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail" and applied it to a video game, with the hammer being "platforming"?I mean, to be honest, the game isn't bad. It's just that I wish they turned down the platforming dial a bit and instead focused a bit more on other core gaming mechanics (e.g. combat) to deliver a more balanced experience. I'll also add a side note and say that items are a bit too expensive in the game. Expect to spend a fair amount of time hitting barrels to collect souls so you can buy stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a really fun platforming/action game. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with, the platforming starts of slow and somewhat poorly, but once you have some moves under your belt it becomes really really fun. The combat is very satisfying and the game is the perfect length, The levels are small but very detailed and allow for fun maneuverability. I did not experience any technical issues and the game runs and looks gorgeous. The care that went into this game is really noticeable and very much appreciated. First game in a long time that I felt any desire or want to %100 and get all the achievements. Also the free DLC is amazing, I cant believe they released for nothing, Anyway I would highly recommend Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Platforming is the focus and it makes you get creative. The beginning is a little slow and lonely, but you'll  meet many interesting people along the way and slowly find civilization. Music was great. Only downside was the combat. While it was fine, most enemies were copy-paste and not much fun to fight. There are really only 4 big bosses that require skill. The design of the enemies left something to be desired. _childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem. Please don't take some of the bad reviews citing specifically that the controls "are clunky" seriously. Those players are just bad. I'm sorry... I typed it. This game is a fun platformer that does absolutely require exploring the environment which can be punishing as everything is only gotten to through precision maneuver, but highly rewarding when the puzzles click. Only complaint I have is that there isn't a map... either write down or remember specific things you find.  Still 100 percent recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I sometimes wish that only certain games tried to be less pain in the ass. Blue Fire is one of them. The premise of the game is so good, and the game itself is actually polished enough to make you want to play it more however, once you get going and progress through your adventure it becomes more and more pain in the ass where it should be the exact opposite. To define Blue Fire: it's a bit of everything. Action-platformer, somewhat action-adventure, perhaps even a Metroidvania. Not in the sense that you actually utilize your tools and skills etc. to progress with the game as you backtrack but it has interconnected maps mostly and there is a hub world that connects the most. And, although it's not a strong Metroidvania some skills you pick later on inevitably help you progress later in the game. If you see souls-like in the tags don't mind it. It is true that there are very few fountains -similar to bonfires- you get to save your game and similar to DS1 being able to fast travel via them unlocks much later on. You lose your currency (which is 'ores') upon death and you need to get back to them to retrieve what is lost. None of those are problematic though. The game is mostly easy, combat is one of the strongest drawbacks of the game as it lacks polish imo. You can parry, you can dash but neither of these feels satisfying and the whole combat system itself does not feel rewarding. Platforming is tough and sometimes it lacks depth if not polish but when you get certain skills (such as double jumping) it becomes easier and much more forgivable. While I was truly ready to forgive platforming, the combat usually made me angry and dissatisfied. Even when I was ready to forgive it then there is the problem of backtracking. The game has quite a significant amount of side quests most of which require you to find specific items. Then there are voids that are needed to complete (you can think of them as trials/dungeons with rewards, especially similar to the ones in Fenyx Immortal Rising) to get a health upgrade. They are doable but completing things is not the challenge in this game, it is rather finding them. Finding all the voids, the necessary things for side quests, and especially souls (which are literally glowing orbs placed throughout four of the maps which you need to backtrack and explore the maps once again in order to capture all those souls in a vessel) that are required for unlocking one of the bosses. (btw, although I have not slain three remaining bosses the ones I completed was very simple in terms of gameplay. Same thing goes on with the regular enemies. The combat is usually very simple, I don't think it has enough depth in terms of animations & pattern variation and it leaves you asking for more, but you rarely get any better than what's already available in the few first hours of the game.)The game locks the main boss behind three story bosses. One of them, un♥♥♥♥ingfortunately, is locked behind the main quest which begs you to backtrack 4 maps that you've been to before and explore them once again to capture souls. That is idiotic. I don't want to be mean here but why would you ever need to do that? There is no map and I never thought I'd need it until that point. When you introduce a new hub area with a bunch of new sidequests and then another main quest that wants you to capture some ♥♥♥♥ throughout all the maps then you need to have a map. I don't remember any ♥♥♥♥. I don't want to remember any ♥♥♥♥. After 7 hours it's just more chore. Yeah, there are guides. And even with those chore stuff, the game is still arguably short. But, it's not fun. I don't get why you pretend to be a NES64 game when you easily can have a minimap for each section (at the very least), there are no technical limitations or boundaries anymore. It's obviously a design choice that I cannot understand, I just don't. The game is very forgiving and tries not to be hard at all. You just need some specific items in order to progress and while you do it you get more skills & health upgrades to help with your progress. It's an old zelda-esque game. Why would not a developer want their game more accessible, especially to casual fans?Anyway, to slay a boss you need to slay 3 bosses, and to do that you need to do some uninspiring stuff. There's that. I eventually gave up. If you are more patient than me and don't mind unnecessary stuff -which I think put in the game to make it longer in the first place- give it a go. It has sweet aesthetics and tracks. The level design and platforming are bearable, it's just the game refuses to lend a hand to the player. If only it was more akin to Zelda BOTW (where we could actually have access to all the bosses but also needed to complete other things in order to get stronger, all these with a minimap of course) it would have been something beautiful. I see this as a missed opportunity. If there would ever be a sequel, I really wish the devs make the best out of it by overcoming their shortcomings. ps: I also admit that the review is inevitably biased as whatever I think the game lacked of and whatever I wanted devs to add in are all in accord to my taste in gaming. Some people do not mind exploring a map for hours, some people do not mind getting locked of something and do more, explore more, grind more in order to access and complete it. They feel more rewarded and satisfied. Some people do not mind anything at all, they just flow through the game and do whatever they are asked. I am not one of those guys. At least, I was not that time around. As a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who sinked 20 hours into Balan Wonderworld (which at times had much worse platforming compared to this and as a whole was much worse a gaming experience), I do endure when it's plausible. Blue Fire however is not a game that I could have played while chilling, it kinda required to use my brain and my brain eventually collapsed and refused to go on.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of indie platformers (Hollow Knight, Celeste) Blue Fire is a mechanical masterpiece of design mainstream titles would never bother with. It has some technical issues with its camera, especially in the more difficult voids that demand careful camera position during wall running segments, but Blue Fire was an absolute joy to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty nice, it's fluid, it's engaging and the combat is simple but with enough versatility to keep it entretaining (at least for the short while the game lasts)You are looking at between 8 and 16 hours (depending how much you rush it or if you try to complete everything or not, also counting in void of sorrows dlc)As far as challenge.... this is nothing like a "souls game". It's more on the casual side and maybe the most challenging part it's the platforming of some hard puzzles (mostly the void of sorrows). In general, fights aren't really challenging.... the only annoying boss for me was Beira (the ice guardian) since i couldn't get enough hits into his move pattern before invul and massive attack after phase 1.While it's nothing major, the game is pretty good and all round nice to play and enjoy the platform puzzles

_childDocuments_.review: Why do I need to put a thumb up or down for a review? Whatever. Every game is a thumbs up because I could be doing something worse.  After completing the game: There are a lot of upgrades in the later half of the game that help with only having a single jump and dash. The effort can be a bit too much in the early with only the dash and jump. Flying platforms that have you waiting to jump on like a bus route are painful. Why?Playing the waiting game isn't fun.Dashing is bad is platformers. Why?Too difficult to predict and to correct after mistaking the distance. Respawning can be awful. Why? Falling can take five seconds to try again and adds up to being an annoying amount of time.Missing a map isn't a good time. Why? Easy to not know what to do next. This is bad because taking the time to explore freely wants you to put in the same amount of effort it would take to complete the main tasks. Side task are as hard as the main task making me want to just get back to the story. Had to used a walkthrough to figure out the next thing to do. The level environments can look similar and some jumps can be different to the point where I needed to check how to do it right. Having tons of health is great. The combat isn't deep and feels like a nice minigame.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like boring mashy combat and terrible platforming? Then this game is for you. It looks great. It sounds great. But actually playing the game? It's some of the most obnoxious platforming I've ever had the displeasure of experiencing. When you're not fighting with the camera to figure out where you need to go, because you probably won't see it, there's always something that's just out of your range trying to mess with your progress on top of the poor visibility. The combat is about as complicated as the "combos" in Sonic 06. I.E. there's one button and you press it 3-4 times and there's your combo. It's kinda boring and very dangerous at times. Hero Kid here like to dash forward about 4 feet when you hit the attack button and that's not too bad except when you're standing on a platform that's 6 feet wide. You'll find yourself throwing Mask Kid off platforms unintentionally all the time in most of the areas in this game. This is made even more annoying by the fact that the ground doesn't exist. It's just not there. Almost every area in the game has water/pits/goo/whatever all of the place and you've gotta play hopscotch to get anywhere and if you fall in, you take a little bit of damage and go back to a spot that's always farther away than you want it to be so you can do it all over again. Now I realize that may not sound too terrible but consider this. You've got a 20 foot gap to span with your jump and dash. That jump and dash will take you 20 feet and 2 inches. So if you're not nearly Mega Man pixel jumping some of these situations you're gonna have problems. Oh and before I forget, save points? I think I've seen maybe 2 in the game and the most recent one is an area back from where I'm sitting. So when I end up getting a game over because a little dude knocks me off a tower because I can't get the camera where I need it to attack the guy, I don't start the area I'm in over... I have to go back to a previous area with those 20 foot jumps to get back to the second area with the 20 foot jumps and the 6 foot platforms, just to get back to the structure I've gotta jump up and around and inside and out just to get to the top and get knocked off by an enemy I can't see or target. Again. And again. And again. This game started out feeling pretty good. Kind of a Zelda clone with some Souls influences in it but that quickly went away and the whole thing turned into those obstacle courses from Mario Sunshine, but with hidden enemies just waiting to do their AOE burst attack (which they all pretty much seem to have) and knock you back down the well you just spent 7 minutes trying to find a way out of. And if you're lucky, you'll only hit what little ground there is and take some fall damage and not end up in the drink and have to go back to the beginning of the room... or the one before that... or the one before that. I had hoped this game would be fun. It was picked for me to play by a patron of my YouTube channel and the first night we streamed it, it was pretty good. Night 3 out of 4 here and I cannot wait for next Monday to get over with so I can uninstall this very pretty to look at, and very nice to listen to garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like the idea of a hack-and-slash 3D platformer zelda-like, buy this game, on sale or not. It's good fun. Use a controller.This game is great. I 100%'d it twice pre-DLC, did it  for the DLC, and I'm still considering reinstalling it for another round. Buy it, full price or on sale. The movement is hugely customizable if you get the optional upgrades and satisfying even with just the stuff you get on the main path. You'll be able to do some really wacky movement options and skips when you're at HALF the maximum potential.Besides the fact that there are so many movement options to help you dodge and position, don't expect the world from the combat - it's perfectly fine and serviceable, but it's not where the game shines. If that's  you're here for, still at least look at some gameplay and see if it interests you. If you're here for the platforming or collecting, or you're open to giving that a shot, buy the game. I'm about to buy a copy for a friend....Still not buying it? ...You can find a banana costume and play as a silly little banana guy. Did that convince you?

_childDocuments_.review: Review written only a few void challenges in but: So far the game has been flawless. Great technical performance and no bugs that I've found. _childDocuments_.review: I gave an unfavorable review a few months ago for this game, because although it was quite beautiful and with good ambiance, its engine was bad and lacked precision. I dropped the game after a few hours, frustrated.Now I must say that upfront: the engine has been improved greatly, making this game actually interesting to play, and sometimes even very pleasing! Some "Voids" (special platform levels) are particularly well designed, and I enjoyed playing through most of them.That being said, that game does not have much for itself apart from that. I wanted to dive into the lore, but the lore is not very interesting, and is told in the most awful manner (i.e. by random characters popping out of nowhere just dumping a huge "legend of Thingy McStuff" in an unskippable cutscene).If you don't mind, I guess you should be fine. If that bugs you, that game might be a bit disappointing.(spoilers ahead)The lore is weirdly too complicated, yet too superficial. There are 5 gods, and the first too temples are the home of 2 gods, the other three dungeons don't have gods, but Lords, that are entities that corrupt the Queen, which is not a god but very powerful, and also one lord needs four flames to be lit, and there is another temple that needs 4 fire thingy holding the ashes of a forgotten warrior...In the meantime: who am I? Why am I here? What happens at the end (there's only a 3 second cutscene)? What is this alphabet that is used like four time throughout the game with no way to decode it (that I know of)? It is just a big mess and I think it is a shame. Sometimes the story seems to be driven by the gameplay in a very un-organic way, and sometimes they are just completely uncorrelated (why are there 6 statues of god in the water temple? Why not 4 or 5? Why are the first too entity in the dungeons are gods but not in the other? Actually I feel like the dev team only had time to implement 2 dungeons and a half; in which case I am sorry to point this out :( ).All and all, each time lore was being delivered to me, I was slightly annoyed, and felt like everything and nothing was explained to me. The last boss (which is........ not very good) felt meaningless, and I did not understand the last "cutscene", and feel like the story isn't finished.Anyway, for its gameplay the game is okay. In term of visuals and aesthetics it's good. But it is still a bit annoying to play, and it did not make feel anything worth.Oh, actually, Mia and Mira are very cute. I liked the composer's sidequest.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the release of the stability patch, this game has been much more enjoyable. I've experienced no crashes, and I even had a funny moment when realized I actually hadn't manually exited the game before! Anyway, Blue Fire is a fun blend of action, adventure, and (most notably) platforming influences. The platforming and level design can be challenging, and even as you pick up tools and abilities that make you more mobile, you can still think twice about finding your way around. The physics feel a little loose at times and the combat is unremarkable but not bad. The music and sound are pleasant and do a good job of fitting the tone.I suppose my one main gripe with the game is that it's just not very pretty. It's not hideous, but the assets, textures, and lighting feel dated and generally unimpressive. That said, I'd love to see what the developers could do next with more of a commitment to the visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever thought to yourself:"Boy...I wonder what would happen if Metroid, Hollow Knight, and Legend of Zelda had a baby and made that baby run through the mini platforming parts of Super Mario Sunshine?"THEN HAVE I GOT THE GAME FOR YOU!The soundtrack slaps.The platforming is solid.The combat is great.The environments are varied and exciting.Solid 8/10 so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game "100%"(not a few cosmetics you have to grind barrels for).  As a game designer I have a lot I could say about this game, but I'll keep it simple. It has amazing potential and could be great if it just cooked in the oven a bit longer. Other than the movement, the game feels like it is in BETA. I wouldn't pay A$30 for it. I think if one of the Zelda, Hat in Time or Dark Souls influences were removed, the game could thrive! (Dark Souls I think)PROS;- Movement feels amazing and works really well- Very satisfying to play- Looks and sounds awesome- Decent amount of game and challenge- Later boss battles are fun- Great level design for the platformingCONS;- Lots of crashing and a few major bugs which ruin the experience a bit.- It tries to wear too many hats and suffers in it's major areas because of it.- Combat isn't satisfying and almost felt annoying/pointless- Some of the platforming level design can be buggy and and stretched to the characters limits- Checkpoints in frustrating positions, creating lots of wasted time to get around simple areasAll in all the game is good and I love the concept, but with other games like Hades that have came out recently, it doesn't even compare for the price. If there was less attention to the 'Cool Factor' and less in the kitchen sink, it would be amazing!7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I am so happy with this game, enjoyable from start, with very charming enviroment, art style, music and world design.Controlls and plaforming is really outstanding here, so responsive and free movement(controller used). The level/world design here is so impressive, the platformig is done in such a fantastic manner, promoting a fast action pasted approach. Making the core gameplay very good. Full of secrets, hidden shortcuts, tricks and freedom. At times a bit confusing to know where to go next, but in an organic way. I would buy Blue Fire 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through everything 100% while streaming to my girlfriend and I enjoyed it! I got it on my Switch a while back but I wanted to switch over to PC because some of the challenging platforming was a bit trickier on the lower resolution of the Switch. (also I wanted to get all the achievements on steam)This game centers a lot around platforming and movement mechanics. It's quite challenging so it may not be for everyone, but luckily the hardest platforming in the game is optional content.The game is structured somewhere between a Soulslike, a Metroidvania, or a Zelda game, and plays like a hack-n-slash/3D platformer. There's also cool little challenge stages called Voids that remind me of A Hat in Time. These voids reward you with HP and in my opinion are way more fun than grinding shrines in the open world Zelda titles. I've completed every void and they definitely can be a bit challenging, but none are too bad.The boss fights were pretty fun, however some of them felt like I just had to take damage in the process of beating them, which hurts the completionist in me because sometimes I like to hitless the bosses in the games I play. In the case of this game I decided I'm good with just beating them and progressing but there was definitely room for some polish for the bosses/combat.As you'd expect with this kind of game there's a story with an obscure world/lore that's enough for you to understand how to progress at face value, but you can look deeper into if you really want to, similar to a Souls game or Hollow Knight. The ending was a bit brief though, I would have enjoyed a longer end sequence to tie everything together after beating the game!I could go beyond drawing comparisons to other games but I feel like players would benefit not knowing too much information going in, just enjoy the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Misses the MarkBlue Fire is an Action Platform that seems to take inspiration from games such as Legend of Zelda with an atmosphere of Hollow Knight with a small, grimm, protagonist that doesn't says much.Let's compare two games a few games for a moment:Blue Fire vs TLOZ: Wind WakerBlue Fire vs Jak and DaxterBlue Fire vs Sphinx and the Cursed Mummy. What does these games have that Blue Fire Lacks?Personality, there is nothing about the characters, enviorment, music or even the bland artstyle that may captivate my attention such as the games I mentioned earlier. The gameplay is there and it's great with the fast paced jumps, dashes and attacks but the technicality of the gameplay can't carry alone an entire game. I am looking forward future projects from the Developers since there is definetly potential, but Blue Fire was a disappointing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Love the games visuals and gameplay , very much "hollowknight + Hat in time---very buggy right now , im sure the devs know. Dying then crashing = you lose all your souls aka a really bad time. Will update once some good patches have rolled out. some quality of life changes for the Void rooms are very much needed-Checkpoints between sections-alot of these rooms are painfully long. feel like im playing MarioMaker all over again.-No pointless game overs- the option to leave at any moment is more then enough

_childDocuments_.review: Really fast and fun to play. The controller of the main character is super responsive and the feel of fly over the world is amazing. The art of the enviroment is really cool and I have a really good time with some fun npcs. I recommend to play this game with the joystick! You will have a better control than with the keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Neat game. No clue why people are comparing this to Darksouls. It's not hard at all. Visually and gameplay wise, it seems more inspired by Hollow Knight and Zelda. The platforming is about the hardest thing in this game, but the abilities you unlock trivialize them. The platforming and movement feels solid. I actually like that the dash can be controlled for precise movement. Combat is dull though. I never used the shield, and only remembered I had a magic blast toward the end, which I still didn't use. I didn't use any of the combat spirits until the last boss either. Bosses were pretty mediocre, and didn't incorporate the use of the abilities you get from their dungeon. I only died to the last boss once, and that's because the heal button seems finicky unless you're standing completely still.My main complaint would be that the movement abilities (and some of the basic moves like sword spin) didn't seem to be properly tested. I was able to get into areas I wasn't actually supposed to because of this, and almost soft locked myself at one point. They're ridiculously powerful, allowing you to bypass entire platforming sections without even touching the ground once. The wall running is also not that great, but not frustrating outside of a few void puzzles (which I ended up just abusing the jump powers to get past). My second complaint would be that this game doesn't really tell you where to go. I was able to figure it out once I memorized locations, however I noticed a lot of people seemed to be wandering into places they weren't supposed to yet and ended up getting killed. Maybe that's why some people think it's hard, they were just going the wrong way.Two small complaints are the use of B as accept, interact, and shield. I was able to get used to it for interacting, but in shops I ended up buying things I didn't want. The second complaint is the doors that lead to gates. Just lock the whole door instead of having me go through a loading screen twice. Some of the environments were visually lackluster, and the world's design makes zero sense. The first village is designed like everyone living there has all your abilities to jump around, yet the second isn't. Sometimes a doorway can take you from a frozen cave, to a temple, to a lava cave in mere seconds. Overall it was pretty neat. I was able to 100% it in 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: A game that could have been absolutely amazing.. but at the end of the day is just good, The platforming and characters are excellent, along with the beautiful visuals and art style.However, the combat is fairly dull. Theres only a few enemies, a crawly bug, a swordman, and a flying enemy that shoots projectiles. The bosses are all very easy despite playing on hard mode. However, the game is still very fun and I do recommend it. Maybe don't buy it for full price, but on sale I'd say hell yeah go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: It might not be the best 3D Platformer,Nor the best Souls-Like,Nor the best Zelda-Like.But it is the only game I see combine the 3, and it did it perfectly fine.Can't go wrong for the price tag. On sale? 100% worth it.If you are looking at screenshots and you like what you see, then you will like what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Neat ideas (obviously Zelda inspired), but it fails hard when it comes to the platforming passages.Those are just frustratingly bad designed and the camera and movement (that wallrun ability... -.-) make it even worse.Don't get me wrong... I really like the zelda-esque world and characters. BUT for a game to be good, it needs good gameplay - which Blue Fire doesn't have unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: So far... What do you have here is essentially a metroidvania game that's in 3D.I'll go ahead and confess that I play games with the goal of 100%ing them so usually I'm biased towards to overall game pacing and difficulty, Blue Fire felt like two faces of a coin together in that sense, which I think is a good trait for a video game.Here's your jumpy cute chibi cartoony looking character with simplistic environment, you are given a small region that later interconnects with it's individual parts, just like Dark Souls games, while the game has a strong Dark Souls feel, it's solely for it's atmosphere rather than it's gameplay, so don't go expecting a souls-like in Blue Fire. As for it's gameplay:There is combat and there is platforming, the platforming is about most of the part of the whole game, while you still have regular and "epic" fights here and there and obviously you have grand boss battles that are more than well-done enough for a game that wasn't meant to be focused on it's fighting. Gear progression is linear, there are no stat distribution, you equip whatever has more numbers on them, progress is very convenient, simple, aka streamlined. You travel the region and talk with different NPC, get goofy lore bits off of them, obtain key items that unlocks the passage of another area, pretty much in the usual metroidvania sense. Although the story is nothing impressive, I'd easily say the game has a story for the sake of having a story, by no means it's bad, it's just there so that you have a surface level story that goes along with the game's atmosphere.There's also a side content which was almost flawless as a supplement for me that complimented the nature of the game quite well; you have access points spread out in the regions, upon interacting with them you are sent on a different small dimension where you have nothing but platforming, while most of them felt like a walk in the park, there were 2 levels of it that had me restarting a few times until I could beat them. These side content are not really mandatory to progress in the game, you could simply ignore them, but completing them with success grants you increase on your maximum health points and completing every one of those finally awards you the best looking outfit in the game (solely cosmetic), but take my review with a grain of salt because everyone's pacing with platformers may differ greatly and I can see these mini-levels being too notoriously frustrating for some people.All in all, the game is well polished, has an okay-good sounding music and audio, a little short lifespan (excluding the DLC) and most importantly, very accurate response on both movement and jumps (which I believe is the crucial in the making of a platformer game)
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very similar to ww zelda in aesthetics and game design but as soon as you start playing it you can tell it's very unique. Imagine WW with HK's mothwing cloak and and jump, with a little more zoomed out camera. The platforming feels VERY good and asks a decent amount of you. Got for 3.99$ and played with a controller, well worth the price for the first 20 mins alone. If you can pick this up on as good a sale as I did I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It has a certain charm like Hollow Knight, but my my, it has a lot of flaws. It has bad platforming, awful attempts to make wall-running puzzles that are downright frustrating. The warp / checkpoint system requires you to collect an absurd amount of Ore in order to unlock new checkpoints and the only store so far you can sell gems and other items for Ore, are located in the main city. That's right, if you find a new vendor somewhere else in the world, you can't even sell your items. So if you don't have enough Ore on you, too bad. You just have to make do with what you have, and if that means you can't get any checkpoints, too bad. This is quite frustrating when you have made it really far, only to die and be sent back to the main city for example, given that it's your last unlocked checkpoint. The combat is... sighThe combat is alright for what it is, but the game doesn't give you a lot of ways to avoid incoming attacks. You can, if you time it, dash out of the way. But later on when you have fast shooting laser enemies, it's seems like a much better option to use your shield.Except this "shield" gives you an absurd amount of knockback, more often than not, sending you off the edge into your death. What is the point of the shield? It consumes mana AND it knocks you off the platforms? Who thought this was a good idea? Oh and there are only 2 "Dungeons" for you to complete, then it turns more into "Go here and there, kill these bosses" that are ridicilously overtuned and the way to said bosses is, sorry for my language, flat out cancerous. I really want to leave a positive for Blue Fire cause it IS a charming game. But it has too many downsides for me to recommend this to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a Jump'N'Run. Unfortunately controls aren't really the strong suit of this game. Fights arent a problem because the mechanics are simple but it is impossible to be precise in your actions. Cant even use Mouse because the sensitivity can't be changed. You probably wont ever die by enemies in this game but fall off ♥♥♥♥ a lot. Over time this gets incredibly annoying. So looks are nice, controls arent good enough in my oppinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole, it's a good game. In my opinion, too much backtracking and the general game flow is a bit weak at times. In the voids, it would be good to know whether an ability is needed here before you try it over and over again.It's also a bit annoying that you always have to start the void from the beginning, even if you fall off at the last collectible just before the end.I already got softlocked when I came to a void in the city. I couldn't finish the void because I didn't have the wall jump ability. I left the void and couldn't get anywhere - soft locked.The combat system is good. Animations are smooth. Performance is superb.There is a volume slider for music, but not for sound FX and ambient sounds - why? I never play at 100% volume and like to be able to understand people in Discord.The overall art style is simple but nice to look at. Nice toon shading for characters and creatures and overall good selection of low poly environment assets. Post Processing is also alright. The controls are intuitive and fun.You can see the big inspiration from Zelda. For the price, I can somewhat recommend the game.  However, I probably won't finish it.Since I support indie studios and the game itself makes a decent impression, I give it 5 stars. With a big studio, there would definitely be a deduction in the overall rating.

_childDocuments_.review: File says about 96%. A bit ticked I can't find the remaining 4%, considering I've done all the quests, found all weapons, spirits, and tunics.Either way, incredible platforming. Combat was less than I desired, and the bosses were mostly weak aside from the final fight, but the platforming and exploration was worth far more than the 20 I spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Fun simplistic combat and exploration. You can build your skills/powers, and as you do so, you inevitably enable yourself to explore further. I like the art style. The difficulty took about 20 minutes to get used to, but once i got the swing of it, it's been smooth sailing from that point onward. As may others have said, it does feel like Hollow Knight meets Zelda in many ways, unfortunately that brings me to the cons. Cons: The story, to me, isn't gripping. I'm 8 hours in and i've already forgotten what the purpose of this adventure was. Its not to say it's poorly written, it just hasn't kept my attention. I know to explore, and when i find enemies, i destroy them. That's enough for me, but it may not be enough for everyone. There's no map. This is not TERRIBLE, but it adds an element of difficulty and frustration that didn't need to be there. All doors look the same, so you do need to commit the routes to memory when back tracking. On a positive side of not having a map, It did cause me to go back to explore prior locations later in the game, and it led to me finding new and helpful items. I would absolutely recommend someone who enjoys games like Hollow Knight, Ori and the Will of the Wisp, and Zelda.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the 8 hours I spent on it, however if you're a fan of its (very obvious) influences and artstyle, you might still enjoy it a lot. While it periodically provides some decent platforming bits during the Void sections, Blue Fire's barebones story, clunky combat and, often times, confusing level layout leave a lot to be desired. There are occasional moments of brilliance here (Stoneheart City is a BEAUTIFUL place, especially to just mess around jumping and dashing), but they are very few and far between.Much of the combat in the game is super super basic, being able to cheese most (if not all) enemies by dashing on top of them and repeatedly slashing them, and I fail to see the reasoning behind adding so many weapons when all they do is add just a little bit more damage, when they could have instead made it so different weapons had different effects (such as some ice blades making enemies slower on hit, for example). Many of the sidequest are simply going from point A to point B to point C, and the lack of a map really shows here, as many many times I was left running around aimlessly (especially at the start) not knowing where to go at any moment. This unfortunately lead to me sequence breaking the game many many times using collision in the scenery and getting around nooks and crannys in walls, reaching ledges I shouldn't be able to or making my way to places I really should not be at. My biggest example of this was quite early in the game, entering Temple of Gardens from Stoneheart City I obviously could not cross the ledge to progress, but since the game's forte is in its platforming, I assumed that I was supposed to make my way around it, across the walls and drop down to an area below, which left me walking around aimlessly for a good while before I realised I was not supposed to be there.However, as you play through it you can FEEL the potential this game had, and I believe that with just some polishing up here and there, the devs have an excellent, excellent 3D platformer and metroidvania fusion on their hands by their next title.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game gets better the longer you play, but also drags around the end if you marathon it, so take a break in the middle like I did.Pros:Snappy movement that just gets better the longer you playFun platforming challenges and level design that lets you explore the map as you wantI like the character designs and the side quests are easy enough with some pretty good rewards at timesShort and sweetMixed:Again, the end of the game is a bit of a drag The boss fights are very samey. Not the biggest critique, but with the combat not feeling amazing, it is what it is.Negatives:I wish the achievements tracked more. The spirit quest is only 10 spirits and not the entire roster. Nothing major.I like this game. I hope we see more from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: While my review says 6hrs my save file is around 11. This game is short, not counting the voids and hunting for all the upgrades/spirits beating the game took just under 10hrs. Its also kindaeasy, only two bosses gave me trouble and one was the final boss. This game has very obvious inspirations in Hollow knight and the Legend of zelda series. Mix this in with hat in time movement and youve got one hell of a platformer. Despite the length and difficulty this game is really fun. The combat and movement is satisfying and fluid and you can skip parts of areas, dungeons and voids by using the right movement items, spirit upgrades and a bit of imagination. I skipped two small parts of the second dungeon and parts of most voids on my last runthroughs of them.Overall 10/10 game, especially if you like platformers. Instant favourite for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game tried to blend a lot of genres together to create something great but failed miserably at it but still this is a great 3D Platformer with a great moveset to match which includes wall-running, triple jumping, dashing etc. controlling the character definitely feels good. Now this game also tries to be a metroidvania, alot of people compare it to Hollow Knight but its far from it, the dumbest mechanic being hiding movement upgrades in the world with no map, so i suggest using a guide to get to your full potential. The combat feels like it was added at the last minute, they should have just focused fully on its being a 3D Platformer, the platforming challenges called Voids are the best thing about this game which sometimes can also be frustrating but it feels good completing them.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: It's like if Mario and Zelda had a baby, who then grew up idolizing Hollow Knight. Platforming is a little floaty, but there are traversal powerups - and so many modifiers for those powerups - that in the right hands this game has as much platforming versatility as any 3D Mario title, and it feels great.There is no map, but there are only a handful of interconnected, visually distinct areas. IMO, no-map was a good choice.The other main point of frustration will likely be the Void zones. They're self-contained platforming challenges, but the aforementioned upgrades significantly modify the level of difficulty, and I think only the first one is actually mandatory. Blue Fire has great gameplay, interesting lore, and plenty of character. It's not the longest game, but they've already added their first  DLC update (which doubled the number of Void zones). I got it with Humble Monthly a while back, but even if I had spent $20 on it today, I'd be very happy with my purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: You're basically in for 3D Hollow Knight with some discreet zelda-esque dungeons (puzzles swapped for platforming challenges), and that is a good thing! Though landing out of a dash in 3D will never be as simple/intuitive as in 2D, the controls are tight, the platforming challenge's are solid (but nothing exceptionally unique), and the performance is *spectacular*. Combat's a bit bland, but it's also pretty quick so not too big a mark against.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Not great, not bad. The world and areas feel very limited, empty and cramped. Regular mobs are also very repetitive and follow the same patterns. Bosses and npc's designs feel like they are missing key features or something to be remembered by. The camera setup is very janky and difficult to control, sometimes it feels like it has a mind of its own and you just have to accept that. Forgettable story. The platforming and overall movement gets progressively better as you go on and there's also challenges to test that. Npc's and respective interactions and dialogues are one of its strongest points. The combat feels good but could be explored some more. Could harder to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not making a fancy review so much as a rant/rave. ♥♥♥♥ it.+No open world. +No procedural generation. +No rogue elements. +Not an RPG. +No radio towers to reveal maps. +No crafting. +No "you can beat the game whenever you want".+No slow, boring gliding. +No arduous stamina based climbing.Just a good old fashioned, no bs, classic action adventure in a sea of open world crafting sandbox nonsense. Takes itself serious, feels great, makes you actually engage with all parts of the game. But it still lets you have fun and gives you a real sense of progression. Recall things you might have missed. Backtrack to old areas with new abilities to find new exciting things in an interconnected world. It doesn't give you everything at the start and tell you to get lost. It doesn't *intend* to let you just bypass enormous chunks of the game in ways so cheap it can be done by accident.I was so skeptical about this one but it's everything I've wanted in a polished package for like a decade. GOOD game so far.Even has Zelda style temples. That first boss wasn't much to write home about, but I don't even care. I'm just so happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I thought it looked like a cool Zelda x Hollow Knight mix, and after playing it for ten hours, that's EXACTLY what it is. The movement is crisp and clean, the controls are easy to pick up and challenging to master. Even though Blue Fire (very obviously) takes inspiration from several places, it is ALWAYS its own game. As of right now, the game sometimes crashes while transitioning to a new area, but the auto-saves are generous, so you never lose too much. One thing in particular that I love about this game is that the developers give the player 100% agency. Plot progression is locked behind dungeon keys and such, but other than that, you can explore the entire world in your own way. I accidentally sequence broke near constantly because I was searching every nook and cranny, abusing every jump, dash, ability, trick, or exploit to search high and low for collectables and spirits. I got the whirlwind hook before the first temple because I managed to use the dash and the fireball creatively to hover stall over a gap. The devs built this game with freedom in mind, and it really shows. PROS:+ Ultra-tight controls make platforming incredibly rewarding.+ Lots of abilities to unlock and abuse+ Fam, the entire game is absolutely stunning. I've set three different screenshots as my wallpaper.+ THE SCORE THOUGH+ All of the characters are charming and adorable and several will likely make you cry.+ Perfect Zelda/Hollow Knight/Dark Souls blend that makes it impossible to put down.+ ELEVATORSCONS:- Game sometimes crashes when changing areas. This will probably be fixed very soon. - It could still use a bit of polish. Lots of terrain models clip into each other, a few enemies have unclear/unfair hitboxes, and there are a handful of minor bugs.Overall, Blue Fire gets a 9.5/10. I cannot recommend this enough, and I haven't even finished it yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I like it so far, I just wish the crashes weren't as frequent as they are. I'm giving it a positive because if the crashes weren't there, it's a 10/10 for me. I like the game play, the setting, art-style and the music. It's a great game despite the crashes but I would recommend holding off for a few and coming back once the bugs are patched out. But if you are still wanting to play it ASAP, go for it. It's still really beautiful. Once it's ironed out it'll definitely be in my top 10 of 2021
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amalgamation of some cool games. The platforming of A Hat In Time, a death punishment & recovery system similar to Dark Souls (as well as emotes, which now have rudimentary gameplay use), a castle sprawling with vile meat walls from Amnesia: The Dark Descent. Probably some other things like Zelda or whatever, haven't played those. The result is pretty enjoyable, I must say. The combat is actually the easier part and it's the platforming that is more likely to prove a challenge, as some of those later (optional) levels can be quite tough.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the movement in this game, it gives you a great degree of movement that feels almost game breaking in some points but it's still satisfying to skip some platforming sections by coming up with a way to exploit movement to do it. The platforming sections in the DLC are pretty fun and more thought out for a player with all the movement upgrades, have mere interesting mechanics and look cooler. They are  greater challenge but nothing crazy. Story is amateurish at best, it tries to be a greater than everything epic tale but it's the writing and the over all setting is mediocre.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: this game is almost perfect, but it also just has too many flaws for its own goodbefore i go further, i want to say that i do highly recommend this game and wish to support the developer, what they've made is something truly special, and despite being derivative of other things, (namely hollow knight, dark souls, a hat in time and a bit of wind waker) it truly does feel unique and special, the contrasting elements of those games do blend well and it has enough of its own flare to make it stand out. legit, play this game.now then, that out of the way, this game is...well its hard to put itas i said above, its a mix between various games, and it doesnt try to mask it, and honestly thats fine. for one thing, its easy to know if you'll like this game, just from if you like any of the games its inspired by, and it never goes too far with its inspiration, i cant exactly call it a rip-off of dark souls, hollow knight, a hat in time or wind waker when it also has its own identity.it helps that it also controls really well, and the more you play the game, the better movement you get. you start with just a single jump and a short dash. you have 2 upgrade (spirit) slots, 3 points of health, and a little bit of mana. simple and gets the job done. you can also attack enemies with your swords in a simple 1-2-3 hit combo, and do a little emote. but as you trek along for your quest to kill the queen, you'll earn more abilities and spirits. until you feel like your average method of traversal is just exploiting the game. first you get an air slash that can gain you extra air, then an upgrade to gain more air if you do that after a dash, then a wall run (which also lets you wall jump), then a double jump, then a triple jump, then a dash-extender which MASSIVELY extends the length of your dash, then a jump height increase, then you get yet another upgrade for your air slash that increases the air gained, then you get the ability to run, and probably other stuff im missing, the movement is the best part about this game and (aside from the wall run/jump) it all feels super good and responsive. some of these are spirits for the spirit slots, but you can have all the movement related ones equipped by the end. doing void challenges and grabbing orbs in there allows you to spend the orbs for more spirit slots (max of 10), and just finishing the void challenges nets you a free heart. you're gonna need em.the void challenges are both one of the game's highlights and one of its flaws. they're these somewhat short areas based on pure platforming. think mario sunshine fludd-less levels, but if fludd is never taken from you, and by that i mean you retain all your upgrades thank god. that doesnt make them easier, and in fact, id say they're harder. much harder. they tell you the difficulty before you enter them, thank god. 1 star means easy, 5 stars means hard. but you'll quickly notice that most of them are 4-5 stars. i'd recommend saving those till you have absolutely everything in the game. some require late-game abilities without telling you. you can cheese it at times, i did several without even knowing i needed a double jump for it. once you understand the movement, you feel like you understand it better than the game understands it. anyway, once you get to the 5 star voids, thats when hell begins. having to wait for slow platforms, doing 180 leaps of faith jumps because you cant move the camera and jump at the same time, instakill spikes everywhere that send you all the way to the start, all while trying to get every single orb. the timing and pattern memorization can be insane, theres several levels that seem like they came right out of super meat boy, even down to the difficulty, but where SMB has very tight wall wall jumping with a very clear path.... this game doesnt. the wall running is the most jank part of the movement and sometimes when youre doing these voids, there will be so much ♥♥♥♥ in front of you that you cant tell when you should go. i could forgive it all however, if the voids didnt blind me. see, the voids are just pure white, and then theres also bloom on top of that, and all the platforms are a light grey. so i hope you like blinding white, because you cant even turn the brightness down. thankfully there aren't too many void challenges, but you will encounter them regularly as you're traversing the many levels. speaking of the levels, they kinda.... arent goodi mean they can be, but they also feel kind of half baked. im not quite sure how to put it. its fine at first, but the moment you take the elevator to the sewers, the game takes a hard dip for a while. for the next hour or 2, you feel like you're going the right way by way of the wrong platforms, thinking "this has to be the wrong way, no sane designer would do things like THIS". that thought continues as you head outside to the stoneheart city and this is when you realize the rest of the game was designed around later game movement. the part that tipped me off is when i went to the shrine in the middle of the city, saved and jumped down to a ladder just past the shrine, easy to reach, it seemed like the right way, like the game was guiding me to this direction. save point in center, new path beyond that with a giant door. but no you cant go there till later, and beyond that door is a locked gate. this is when you have to go back to the shrine and realize... you cant make the jump... you have to die (or save, quit, continue) to get back. the game feels like you should have a double jump or even a wall run by this point, but no, you dont get much movement till around 40% of the game is done, and then the game just kind of gives you one ability after another. hell i got the triple jump before the double jump, and at that point the game just starts feeling a lot better and a lot easier. it is kinda nice getting the double jump after so many other upgrades, so by the time you get it, you feel like you can effectively use it in tandem with your other tek. i know i may have contradicted myself here by saying the double jump should have been gotten earlier then praising how late you get it, but i do feel like the movement should be more evenly spread out, like maybe before entering the sewers you get the air slash. that gets you a little extra air so its like a double jump, but its one you need to charge and it only charges on the ground so you cant abuse it. though it does have one major flaw. to charge it, you first need to attack. attacks move you forward. that is a death sentence in some voids with the tiny platforms. its less of a problem by the time you get the double jump, so maybe its my fault for doing voids as soon as i see them, but i still feel like it should be improved. Had to exit to title and reload previous save.- After , I could no longer  at save points.Unrefined mechanics:- The most glaring one is the camera. For every challenging section this game has, there are 10 parts annoying parts (a confusing yet linear-ish map, a repetive and slow parkour section, boring combat sequences, and lack of impressive graphic.). _childDocuments_.review: If a game could get a sideway thumbs, it would be this.It had an interesting world, a solid platforming system, a great roster of environments and a wonderful charm to it. However, that is where it draws the short straw. It has some janky combat actions and some of the models do clip in certain ways with the camera. At some points, there was some glitches with the Void Challenges. It did get fixed after restarting that challenge. It did need some more time in the oven and some refactoring in terms of pacing and story. The combat was a little too sparse for my liking and enemy variety was kind of dumb. But the combat itself was very crunchy and satisfying. The bosses were pretty fun while not being incredibly unique or challenging. The game looks good and runs really well on low end hardware. Honestly- this game is a steal for how cheap it is.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable souls-like platformer. It has all the good ingredients for a fun time; cute characters, great soundtrack, fluid movement and controls, fun platforming, side quests, challenge maps, collectibles/unlockables... you name it,The playtime is around 10-12 hours (if you don't aim to complete all the individual challenge maps, the so-called "Voids" it can be even shorter).I played on the hardest difficulty, but even that was surprisingly forgiving, the bosses are quite easy if you learn their pattern quickly, the most difficult time I had was finishing some of the harder Voids.The only negative thing I can think of is the lack of a map system, however navigating the world isn't that hard or confusing so I got used to it pretty fast.Achievements are tied to the main and side quests, so by completing all of them, you can't really miss anything.
