_childDocuments_.review: Got this game through humble bundle and I must say I'm happy I played through all the content in it (100% finished), but it is quite rough around the edges. One of the roughest parts, unfortunately, is the beginning. It is a bit confusing and felt a bit all over the place. The beginning area is also a lot more unpolished than other parts of the game which gives of a bad first impression.Get past that however, and there is a neat, but short, game underneath (disregard my playtime, I was AFK for long periods of it. My 100% save file says 9 hours but I was messing about a bit as well). I'd say this game assumes that you are already quite well versed in platforming games as the game will not hold your hand and will present you with quite some difficult challenges.* Once you get past the initial beginning and the movement options starts opening up for you, you get a surprisingly fun and smooth movement experience in the game. Movement options includes your standard array of dashes, jumps, wall running and the like. No real surprises here to be honest, but what's there feels well tuned and easy to control. IT IS different from other games though. For example, if you come fresh from 'A Hat In Time' you'll notice that the controls feel very different even though the overall moves might be similar. It took some time to get used to but in the end I'd say the controls are very good and it even surprised me at times how well I was able to just fly through some quite difficult challenges. I can't stress enough how controlling your character is one of the most important points in a game like this and it is a VERY STRONG positive that it was done well here (again, beginning is a bit rough). * Voids (small gauntlets) are great. They can be quite though, and probably really frustrating for some, but for me who is always seeking a challenge when it comes to platformers I enjoyed them quite a bit. They are quite punishing though and will send you back to the beginning of the Void if you fall (but you take no damage so you can keep trying until you give up or succeed). They range from easy "jump on platforms" to "is this hollow knight path of pain?". There is a "main quest" to beat them all, but I beat them before getting to the final boss so I'm not really sure if it is an ACTUAL requirement to beat them all before beating the game.I want to preface this by pointing out that I will list a lot of negatives here but still recommend the game. Why? Because the overall experience is enjoyable, but there are a lot of flaws here.* Overall I feel that there is a missed opportunity with the wearable items in this game. Tunics is just for decoration and does not really seem to affect anything. Weapons might look different from each other but seems to have no other abilities tied to them than damage numbers. Ideally, to make Tunics more interesting I would have liked to see at least some defense stats tied to them. * I mentioned it above but I feel I need to put it here as well. The beginning area is rough around the edges. There are many parts where you can end up in situations that allows you to look through walls, get underneath objects (see through them due to them missing textures there), overall quite dodgy texture work at times and etc. It gets better in the later areas however.* I feel that the game is not really built for the movement it provides you, especially not early on. I'm gonna put a spoiler on the next part since it is about specifics: * Gems don't matter. At all. It's just a grind really. You have to have a lot of Gems to buy things, but they are super easy to find and there is no real worry that you'll ever run out of them. Here's how to get a ton early on: * Combat is average at best. I can honestly say I did not really enjoy it except for the bosses which were pretty neat. But then again, the neat part about them wasn't really the *press button to hit boss* combat but the movement before and after. Targeting is awkward and I ended up never really using the blocking. Maybe I just brute forced my way through but at least I could make due with healing and dashing to get away from enemy attacks.* The game is not always super clear on what is happening. For example: You need to be close to an enemy in order to see how much damage you do to them (there is a ranged attack, but unless you are next to your enemy you won't see how much damage its doing). Another example would be when you buy things from stores. There is no sound accompanied with it so sometimes I was a bit confused if I actually bought something or not. * There is no map. I don't really see this as a massive problem though but if you are the type of person that usually rely heavily on a map to get around or find a path to "that one specific room" then you'll probably find this a bit frustrating at times. The game world is not THAT big however so I was able to keep the needed parts in my head without bigger issues.* Story was a bit all over for me. The overall story is quite easy to understand but the bits and pieces of it and the world building seemed to paint small dots rather than one big picture. There is a lot of "small" stories here, especially the side quests which just kind of "starts" and "ends" without really ever giving anything (story-wise).Overall I think the game could have been polished/improved in a lot of areas (and a bit more lengthy to be honest. ) While I find that quite frustrating, the overall experience was still enjoyable for me and thus I give this game a positive review. Do keep in mind though that there is a large crowd I would not recommend this game to. You need to be the type of person that enjoys platformers, metroidvanias and who don't mine, at times, challenges that can be seen by some as frustrating. You also need to be able to overlook flaws and be in it more for the platforming rather than anything else.

Cons:However, this game isn't perfect, the combat is Simple, jumping in the air and mashing attack is all you need, the enemies come in 3 varieties, Floaty, Humanoid, and little critter. The bosses come in one variety and the final boss feels cheap making you jump off the platform in order to damage her.  there is a lot of money available in the game but not a lot to spend it on, i found myself with tons of valuable items I COULD sell for money but never needing to, I think this could have been mitigated with some late game shop that sells very expensive things. There is no map. Why is there no map? I found myself lost constantly and feels like a third of my playthrough was spent wandering around trying to find that thing i know i saw somewhere around here. Glitchy, although not game breakingly so I did have issues with the wall climb not registering correctly making the voids more difficult than they otherwise would be, also certain spirit abilities not registering like the walk on air after a ledge I found would work 70% of the time and othertime just.. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't played more than a couple of hours of this game so this review is my initial opinion. And that opinion is...Mixed but hopeful.First off, I grew up playing games like sonic 3 and Mario 64, I love a good platformer and one of my favourite games of recent history is "A Hat In Time". So when i saw another platformer with a tiny protagonist and high focus on mobility I was all in.Since this is a long review, here is the short version. For the most part, I have enjoyed the game with 2 notable exceptions which I will get to in a moment. First the good stuff: The animation, the aesthetic and the awsomeness of carrying two swords that are bigger then you are. The bad? Dialog and the 2 most dreaded words in the industry ... game...crashes ...Animation: a lot of games by indie developers all use free models they got from blender or unity and they are never that good. They are fine for place markers so you can work on scripting scenes, interactions and planning levels but when the time comes for you to pay for that super cool looking avatar or the well rendered furniture to make you game worth something, so many indie developers, who just want their game on the market by this point, don't seem to put the effort in. Not Blue Fire though. The theming and style of everything, the enemies, the hero even the rubble, it all matches and as someone who tried to design a game as a hobby i can tell you that is really bloody hard! There are no obvious graphical problems where characters glitched through walls or suddenly t posed for no reason (*cough* cyberpunk *cough*) and it all just blended together to make the game look and feel like a solid, polished cohesive unit.Aesthetic:  I loved the slightly creepy nature of the game i have seen so far. An abandoned castle? hell yes! creepy scince experiments? Hell Yes! An intrusive dark material that seems bent on consuming and destroying everything? HELL YES! Cartoon style? YES YES GOOD GOD GET OUT OF MY HEAD YES! The game has gone out of its way to make you feel there are hidden secrets for you to discover, in the first few minutes i passed dozens of locked doors an a was forced to jump over a pile of corpses that looked suspiciously like the protagonist.... That being said the option of a map would be useful, making the levels a creepy maze like castle makes for good game play at first but after you spend 5 minutes climbing over obstacles only to find you have been going in the wrong direction for 4 of them it does get a little grating. "Yes this is a lovely corridor with a giant pit in it, I can really appreciate the pit since i fell into it a dozen times while trying to find where I am going!!"....What was i saying? oh yes! I liked the styling of this game.Awesomeness of carrying 2 swords bigger then you are: well....That's just self explanatory.So... the negatives.... remember those? well here they are: Dialog and the dreaded Game crashes!Dialog: There is plenty of text and story line lying around in this game, at one point i came across a dried up fountain and it started talking to me! And while in real life I wouldn't expect gripping dialog from an inanimate object, if i was in a video game world I would expect that, if a developer was going to make a fountain talk, he would at least go out of his way to make it make sense!Seriously! some of the dialog feels like it has been translated from Chinese to English by someone who learned the language by watching Game of Thrones at 5x speed!  "Fierce warrior of the shadows, upon the dawn of shadows my brothers have fallen, I too fought the shadows. Through the tunnels, beneath the city filed with shadows..." I could go on. Either that fountain had just had a stroke or it stopped talking just before telling me to "insert slot b into tab n for joyful happiness!"  There is no audio in this game so patching dialog wouldn't be hard on a future update and I would suggest that some rewriting of the script may be needed because the level of repetitiveness of a few words broke the immersiveness and when a few words repeated over and over ruin an otherwise great game, it's a terrible waste.I mentioned a patch because oh god does it need one because...Game Crashes: I played for 2 hours and the game crashed 5 times! Luckily it is pretty good at saving progress so I only lost a couple of minutes each time but every time I moved from one area to another, there was a better than even chance the game would crash and kick me to my desktop! So....Conclusion:Would I recommend this game? YesWas this game well done? YesWere the controls a little finicky? Yes but not to the extent i would call it a negative pointDoes the game still need an update: Unfortunately yes.If you liked A hat in time, you will like this too. It's not perfect, as i said, the difference between the story hinted at by the world and what i have found is a big problem and the game does have some performance issues but I would and have recommended this game and at the end of the day, that says it all.The Orange Knight

_childDocuments_.review: Some thought Hollow Knight was overrated, but the extent of praise for this game is absurd in a way. Blue Fire is a Hollow Knight-Zelda hybrid project. However, it is much smaller in scope in terms of mainline content (reminds me of BOTW's rather small mainline content compared to all the exploration layers, except without the super vast exploration-based content). Story wise, I wish this game was more like Hollow Knight, because then I wouldn't have to listen to a generic story with a generic lead, and just experience the story through the gameplay on my own terms. Controls are pretty solid, but the camera is super annoying in some 5-star void challenges. The void challenges aren't really that hard, but some voids are annoying (unless you discover some some clever shortcuts to speed your progression). In a way, voids have more enjoyable gameplay since you have a more reasonable amount of wall slide/jump stamina to work with for platforming, though void design is bare bones. I sort of like the charge up lock on dash trick, but I kind of wish this wasn't mentioned in a lever pulling tutorial and left for the player to discover (optional secret skill vs. mandatory action once or twice). The Inventory is just as annoying to navigate through as BOTW if not worse. Cut scenes feel so dragged on. Bear in mind, I assumed that heal items were hard to come by, so I eventually forgot about them until the second last boss. The early game is okay, but the dungeons are kind of boring, while the bosses are a little cheap in terms of how easily they hit you, despite them being easy for the most part. Some areas are super tedious in the early game and proved to continue being slightly annoying to traverse in late game, mainly Stoneheart. The torch lighting quest is kind of cool because it encourages the player to inadvertently encounter the other major boss quest lines while pursuing one of them. I have no problem with Steam House, it's just okay. However, the Soul Fragment quest is pointless filler that just copies a feature in Hollow Knight in a more annoying way, particularly in Forgotten Path (nice that it leads you to a useful soul that was hidden in early game though). Really, this game was trying to be 3D Hollow Knight, with its soul system being a more accessible charm system (that part is nice). But it takes the worst aspects of BOTW, like cookie cutter bosses and some side quests that nobody wants to really try to figure out (I have no desire for 100%). The late game bosses are all easy to learn, but they are super cheap. Some are cheaper than others (blue>red>green [there are not many other ways to describe these ones really]). This boss combat feels somewhat broken, and surprisingly, the final boss feels the least cheap, even though I had to use 5 heals on my play through. There is no excuse for having so many heals that are easily replaceable. If the combat was tight, you would not need to rely on the mobile game/Minecraft Dungeons trope of easy heals. One thing that I will say is that the three-dimensional perspective can really make precise combat more annoying in general, and that's more of a limitation for 3D platforming than anything else. Music is good but it didn't really resonate with me all that much. Visuals are nice, but some areas look way too homogeneous and that is probably partly why I find them annoying to navigate. I didn't come across any glitches, I just felt that the combat was iffy in general. Figuring out where to go and finding the voids was fine (felt vaguely like Super Mario 64's Castle), I may have forgotten about the elevator to Firefall river when I stopped playing for a few days after the cut scene that showed that opened path. I didn't really like how gates just decided to open after I went somewhere important and returned, it just doesn't make much sense from a world building perspective. I don't think the game really needed a map, though I found myself doing laps around towns to find one forgettable NPC in a forgettable house.Overall, it is nice to see developers that honour successful modern adventure titles like Hollow Knight, Zelda 64 titles, and even BOTW. Nevertheless, this truly feels like a fusion fan game more than a standalone indie title. It's a solid project, and I don't necessarily "not recommend it", I just don't think it holds up compared to the work its derived from in terms of tight gameplay. Keep up the solid game development, I feel like there will be a project that better resonates with me from your team soon. Wishing all the best!

_childDocuments_.review: is a 3D action-platformer. While failing to translate 's seamless platforming experience to the third dimension,  still manages to offer a fun indie experience borne from its mix of platforming, combat, exploration, and questing. Not exactly a novel experience so much as a blend of some leading series from different genres, this one should satisfy some tempered expectations of those series' fans looking for a new spin on action-platforming gameplay.You play as a nameless soul, tasked with cleansing corrupt forces from a giant floating castle. Using your twin swords and your platforming skills, traverse over a half-dozen open areas with your ever-increasing arsenal of movement abilities to defeat evil enemies, wicked bosses, and the malevolent force causing the carnage. In the meantime, tackle plenty of sidequests, gather loot from exploring levels, and show off your pure platforming skills in the game's many otherworldly Void challenge levels. wears its inspirations on its sleeve: it is a 3D  in its aesthetics, overworld, platforming, and premise, the save and healing system of  with some  combat, dungeons, and missions interwoven alongside 's platforming challenge levels. While this game offers an ambitious experience trying to integrate all these different sources, it falls short of meeting the quality of any of them. That's not to say this game is a failure; it's fun in its own right, but just not exactly in the same league as any of these series.Let's start with the platforming. " in 3D" sounds like an easy win on paper, but it is far tougher to execute. First of all, 3D environments simply pose more of a challenge when trying to implement tight controls for overcoming obstacles or hiding small, secret areas - meaning 's world offers roughly a tenth of the depth or reward for exploration that 's does. Second, a 2D game can simply show the player all that needs to be seen from the display of a single screen. 's greatest challenge doesn't come from an enemy or an obstacle: it's the camera. Adjusting the camera to actually see where you're aiming during the toughest platforming challenges is a massive annoyance that unintentionally compounds difficulty. Depth perception, as a result, is often an optional thing in this game - meaning many jumps turn into leaps of faith. Not exactly an airtight platforming experience.The  inspiration takes shape in parts of this game's combat, dungeons, and quests. Combat almost feels identical to the swordplay of  at times - though  offers a few more customization options, the core combat ability stays locked to a variety of sword maneuvers and a weak projectile weapon. This game also has two dungeons that feel distinctly , albeit shorter and simpler ones. And if you're a fan of those quests from  that involve collecting orbs across a map you've already explored, you're in luck!The -style checkpoint and heal systems stand out a bit less than the other points of inspiration largely because, unlike ,  is an easy game. This reviewer completed it nearly 100% without dying once. The game throws HP upgrades at you as part of its platforming level gimmick, and this game's version of Estus Flasks are plentiful in random drops. So long as a player takes a pretty completionist approach to the side content, they will remain well above the game's difficulty curve - which does mean  could serve as a nice introduction to the - type of ultrahard games.In spite of the critical tenor of the preceding review,  is still a good game at its core. Over the roughly 10 hour playtime, players will scratch the itch for platforming through different worlds, beating enemies, and powering up. While in some ways the faults of the platforming system prove that it may be better to stick to 2D when crafting -esque platforming challenges, I can't necessarily fault the devs for trying (nor for failing to meet the impossibly high standard set by Team Cherry). Including the OST free with purchase is a nice touch. Check this one out especially if it's on sale.  gets a B-.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is difficult to describe. Its a game that ticked many boxes for what i was looking for though i barely new it at the time. In a typical Metroidvania style you upgrade your characters movement through the map and can go zoom zoom the further you play. Combat lacks finesse, but the twilight princess vibes and superbly executed jump and platforming parts buffer anything that might be lackluster about blue fire. If you are looking for a platforming oriented metroidvania with zelda vibes - we got temples, bosses, chests with upgrades, vendors, we got sockatable boons, discoverable weapons, Robes that act as skins and even quests requierements and even some neat NPC dialogues (dont expect much story or depth here!) - go for it. As i played it over the course of ~10 days with not much time at my hands i had the need to look some stuff up because i forgot where the routes were that i couldnt access with my current abilitys. The game has no hint system what so ever, which is refreshing in the current hand-holding tutorialesq gaming environment.You will experience backtracking but its zoomy, you are fast and fly through the map where in the beginning everything was seemingly a slog you did not know about. The overworld is distinguished enough that you will remember most rooms and areas you have been in before.You will 100% be entertained for the 7-9 hours you will get out of this!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game, and it's dlc for around 20 hours and finished everything 100%, i think it has enough pro and cons to balance out and this should really be a mixed review, but as far as my experience goes i'll lean towards the negative, and here's why:The game lacks a clear direction, and i think it's one of its biggest sins.It starts off as a similar game to Dark Souls with a cutesy look and some platforming elements, you can in fact see the fire shrines, the cryptic storytelling, the "estus flasks" and the initial aestethic all point towards it. After the first hour or so it moves to a Wind Waker style game, introducing dungeon, that unfortunately lacks some level design polish, between the time it takes to complete the two dungeons there is NO fire shrine for around 2 hours, that's why i found they forgot about the direction at one point.After the second dungeon there's another change and you are basically sent to clean up the previous levels to fetch lots of items in the old environments so we can face the other bosses, that imho should have been in their own dungeon, and we shift towards a more platforming style. At this point you'll be around halfway through the game but probably you will notice that fighting enemy is useless since you should have maxed out the mana, only thing the exp is used for, and also because it's so easy you'll rarely be up for a challenge and very rarely use your flasks to heal, not that the combat is the strong point of this game as you only have a combo of three and that's it.Then there are the voids, this game platform style challenges, i think except for two they are all balanced correctly, maybe steering towards easy once you upgraded your platforming skills but nothing too bad.After the fetch quest is done you face the final boss and the game ends.The dlc is free and accessible after the final boss and is basically comprised of only void challenges plus a new boss, the problem i have with this ones is that the vast majority of the 15-20 included are trial and error of the worst kind. So i really can't recommend it playing unless you like this kind of genre.Traversing the game world is mostly fun and the platform part works really well so the fact they transformed it into a trial and error doesn't sit well with the part of the game that was working the most.All in all i can see the love the authors put into it but this game is ultimately plagued by a general incoherence of design that doesn't let a player enjoy it completely.

_childDocuments_.review: But, nevertheless, it's an AWESOME game, a true GEM of it's genre and I enjoyed it that far. Lots to explore, the lore is short but explained. And there are a lot of mechanics, more then you would think there is. Little RPG interaction, like finding the mother of a child or finding a nephew of somebody to steal all his riches... These interactions are simplified, but adorable nonetheless. And returning to old locations after learning new moves and/or emotes, to unlock even more mystery.If you don't mind jumping parcouring, this is a great game to dive into. The Void Parcouring by completion, you earn an extra heart. By killing entities, you obtain dark shards to upgrade your mana, because it will come in handy when the time is nigh. Level design only gets better the deeper you go into the game, which is a great plus. Ussually it's the way around, where a developer looses interest and wraps things up. I do not have those vibes with this GEM.From all the Soullike games I played, this game comes pretty close and adds it's own specialty: Jumping Parcouring.But I stay with my own commitment: I do not like jumping parcouring, in fact I hate it. It's just that I am at the moment charmed with Soullike games and try to collect them all and ofcoarse play them as good as I can.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. If you liked playing Zelda or MegamanX or Metroid or Mario (3D games), you will feel at home with Blue Fire. As of this review, the game had some issues with crashing, which was frustrating for me and some other players, but the devs are already patching the defects. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game pretty highly. The combat is fun, the platforming is fluid, and the overall challenge is just about right. If you want to know if you should or should not buy this game, the answer is you should. You can stop reading here.If you want to know my full opinion: This game is good, but flawed. This game has had corners cut, and the edges are still very sharp. The game is absolutely rife with allusions to content that it simply doesn't have. There's a ton of secret chests that are hard to find, but most of them are full of unique garbage items that are never used for anything. Tons of NPCs will highlight text in red to indicate it's important, but it references things that will never happen or characters that don't exist. The game showers you with valuable gems to sell for funds, but everything can be bought with the money you find by just walking around. Finally, and this is a fairly minor spoiler, the game has no after-care at all. You beat the final boss and BAM! Credits. I'm not asking for a full post-game scenario, but some indication of what just happened and what it meant would be nice.It's a little tough to levy complaints like that against this game. I know for a fact that the developers put their hearts and souls into it, and it really does show. The game exudes a scrappy, inexperienced charm that I can't resist. I liked it enough that I went through the effort of finding nearly everything it had to offer. I'm still missing .25% away from full 130% though, and I fear it will stay that way forever because there's just not enough of a community to make exhaustive checklists and guides for it.

name: Ever Forward
detailed_description: Ever Forward is an adventure puzzle game — it is the story of Maya. Maya is lost in a strange world somewhere between reality and imagination. She is alone to confront her despair on her journey of discovery, where she must unlock her memories and confront her fears to unravel the secrets of the world. Players will need to use their observational skills and intelligence to solve multiple puzzles to piece together the mystery of Maya's past and what dark secrets she has buried. Key Features Puzzles For more than three years, our designers racked their brains, designing puzzles with the 'puzzle gamer' in mind. Players will feel deeply challenged and motivated to solve each puzzle, and some puzzles have multiple ways of being completed to fit different kinds of thinkers and logical processes. The Art A color pallet of soothing pastels and futuristic tones designed to simulate the absurd nature of the dream world. Adventure Players can collect fragments of memories in the world to unlock new areas and new puzzles. Mechanics Mechanics range from simple movement and jump to teleportation and gravity control; the player must use stealth and observational skills to navigate each puzzle. 永进 Ever Forward

_childDocuments_.review: Ever Forward is beautiful puzzle game with an emotional story.  Depending on the way your brain is wired, it will either be pretty easy for you or quite hard.  It was the latter for me, but I got there......finally!The bones of the story is that the mother is a very busy scientist and has little time for her 12 yr old daughter.  Government officials have stated that it is too unsafe to go outside, so you're stuck home all the time. [A reason was never given for this]You start designing your own security bot, but your mother isn't interested in that either.   The story is enacted by short cut scenes between each puzzle and are well done.Graphics are lovely.  The natural world is full of gentle pastel colours whilst the imaginary world of Maya is very futuristic and dark in design.  The soundtrack is full of mellow synthesizer sounds and the sound effects of the security bots are great!Game play involves getting a box to a red column of light.  You need stealth to get past the security bots and have to work out how to distract them in multiple ways.  As the game progresses, you are able to teleport and use gravity for your purposes.To solve the puzzles requires logic reasoning, dexterity and speed to get to something before it moves.  In some cases, it requires precise throwing of the box, which can be rage inducing near a bot!  Be prepared to die multiple times.Gravity was introduced towards the end of the game and I found it incredibly frustrating to use.  You have to wait for the right strength of wind to move and if you do it wrong multiple times, it gets old very quickly.  The timed aspect of it makes it difficult for slowpokes like me!The Gravity aspect was my only criticism with the lack of English subtitles for the final scene with her mother.  I didn't know what was said in Chinese.  The end of the story did leave me scratching my head, so it is really left up to your own interpretation.  Spoiler alert:  Puzzle lovers will definitely enjoy this.  Buy on sale.  8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ever Forward

_childDocuments_.review: Ever Forward has a surreal aesthetic to it with an intriguing story arc.  The mellow synth soundtrack and wonderful use of color palettes made this puzzle platformer easy on the eyes and ears.  Unfortunately, that's where I stop giving glowing praise for this game.  The puzzle mechanic developed within this title is rather frustrating most of the time.  You're required to carry blocks to specific end points while traversing various platforms and avoid sentry turrets.  It's a scenario that is repeated to a fault.  Some solutions felt clever, while others tipped towards vague and tedious.  I really wanted to enjoy this more than I did, as I consider myself to be a puzzle enthusiast.  I'm sure there will be plenty who will find everything in this title to be just fine, and I get it.  I, on the other hand, grew quite tired and agitated when it was all said and done.  It's, by all means, very playable.  It just didn't win me over when it came to the actual design of the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Ever Forward

_childDocuments_.review: Ever Forward is an indie puzzle game where you play as a girl named Maya. The game starts off when you on an island kind of area and you progress through levels by going to some distorted shapes which transports you to another area where the puzzles are. Here they start off simple where you sneak around surveillance without getting caught while having to transport a cube from one place to another. As you progress the difficult ramp up and some are kinda 5head. Between levels there are some cutscenes which begin with your mum and yourself together at home, where the story unfolds from your past. This is spoken in Chinese, which of course are subtitles accompanying it. The story and atmosphere does have this melancholic and nostalgic kind of feeling with some beautiful visuals to give that indie vibe. Overall, it is a pretty good game as i enjoyed the puzzles that within.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this lovely game, Ever Forward.1.Visually, I was met with a vibrant and appealing world design. The main character is cute, although I would recommend the devs used a more realistic voice actor for the child. Her excited and general tone always sounded forced, which is unappealing.2. The story, although I'll admit I have mixed feelings about much it actually will hit home with most people, was interesting enough to allow you to make up your own mind about what was going on. The cut scenes are short and sweet, and even though there isn't much story, I feel it's one of those 'you fill in the blanks' kind of deals.3. Game play. The characters movements are fluid, and feel natural. Not being able to run when danger is close, while at first felt frustrating, added a real sense of suspense. So I gotta say that this was a nice touch.4. Some mechanics were not obvious right away, but after a bit of trial and error (and melting my brain) I was able to figure out what to do. There isn't any real hand holding going on in this game, so that adds to the challenge. There is a hint system that does help.5. The puzzles were good, but not great. Yes, there were some difficult ones in there, and yes they also melted my brain a few times and caused me to walk away and rethink. That's absolutely fine. My only real issue is that I feel there are times when a solution doesn't really present itself too well, perhaps that is my own fault though. One particular puzzle felt like it needed more of a cheesy workaround rather than solving it the intended way. I guess I will have to see how others solved it and rethink my approach.Conclusion: Overall, Ever Forward was enjoyable and frustrating all at the same time, which is what I would expect from a puzzle game. If you felt it was too easy, call Mensa and book yourself in. If you felt it was too hard, then breathe, walk away, and take a break. Come back with a fresh mind and try again.Tip: The environment and the way it's designed can hold the clue to solving a puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Ever Forward

_childDocuments_.review: I want to iterate that while I recommend this game, it's purely to give some support for the developers since the game has a great foundation. I personally had some issues with the game.These issues have nothing to do with how hard the puzzles were, as I've finished the game in 2.1 hours. The main points I want to touch up on are the Story, Puzzle Design/Mechanics, and Game Length.Before I touch upon these things, I do want to say that the game is beautiful. I love the art style.--- 1 - Story --- The story was all-in-all good. It had some ups and downs as well as a climax.  One of the problems that I saw in the story was that there were gaps in the story as not everything is explained very well. I was often led to guess what is occurring and most of my questions were never answered later down the line.  The other problem is that the story itself is fairly generic. This is my own interpretation from what I've seen and heard playing it, so if the developers would like to point out if I'm wrong then I would be grateful. --- 2 - Puzzle Design/Mechanics --- Puzzles generally consist of getting a cube to the end by getting through obstacles and robots with vision cones. Sometimes there are more robots, cubes, or obstacles. Sometimes there are no robots or obstacles. New mechanics are shown to the player over time in order to keep the puzzles from getting stale. Most of mechanics shown to the player can be influenced by the player. This is important in a puzzle game since players shouldn't need to rely on something out of their control to complete it. Puzzles should be completed with their own ideas and knowledge rather than uncontrollable timed mechanics. I will note that this does not mean timed mechanics can't be used in puzzle games, but they need to be done right in order to ensure that it's more than just waiting for the light to turn green at an intersection (metaphorically speaking). The following bit will touch upon the mechanic that I did not find good.  The puzzles in this game had great foundations, and I definitely believe more can be done with the ideas that the developers came up with.--- 3 - Length --- This is a short and sweet section.This game is short. I can understand the reasons why it is short, but for a 15$ game it is short at 2-3 hours. Looking at the other reviews I can take that the average completion time is at about 3 hours, if not a little bit higher. There are only about  puzzles and the story itself is also fairly short.I personally wish more was done with the game, but it was a good step in the right direction and wish good luck to the developers in their future endeavors.
_childDocuments_.name: Ever Forward

_childDocuments_.review: Maya is a little girl who lives alone on a peaceful island far, far out at sea. The waves are calm, stone pillars loom out in the distance like faraway guardians, and a huge tree stands tall and strong with its roots entangling the earth. Maya isn’t completely alone though, Hestia is Maya’s floating companion cube, a quiet friend who is with her always. One day, out on the beach, something strange appears – a familiar building manifests and a puzzle appears, leading to a memory Maya has forgotten. Seek out all of the memory shards to find the truth about the island, and the secret hidden in Maya.  2-3+ hours to complete, Ever Forward is an adventure puzzle game that is short and sweet. Beautiful graphics, a great soundtrack, fun puzzles and an interesting storyline. The Island is explorable and has secrets and animals you can pet, and the puzzle domains are interesting enough and can be challenging. If a puzzle is too hard, the key for many lies in the layout and the environment. A mix between fantasy and sci-fi, Ever Forward was super fun to play and I’m glad I took a chance on it!

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to say I got this game as a bundle with the soundtrack and additional puzzle for $13.50 USD including tax.So the majority of the puzzles are good... until they start making you wait which only gets worse as the levels progress. I do wish that they explained what happened with the world, the most you get is "its snowing, or is it?" (which you see in the trailer) and the mom telling the girl not to go outside. I am not sure if it was just me but I had the game audio set to what I believe is Japanese and the Subtitles set to English and toward the end the subtitles stopped so I don't know what they said at the very end. I do like that there are a few secrets in the game which gives the game a little replay-ability if you didn't already get them.The soundtrack is great, its not something you start jamming out to during game but it fits the mood of the game very well.I just can't recommend this game... Its pretty, the soundtrack is wonderful and the beginning to mid level puzzles are fun but the game is just to short and the second half of the game is a lot of waiting which is more frustrating than tough.Im not sure if you can get a game soundtrack on steam without getting the game but if you can get the soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: By playing this game I have achieved enlightenment. This game is amazing, smooth calming graphics, cool challenges and great music. Game play reminds me of the old fashioned Sukoban or more recently Gravity Field (It's the block thing you have to solve to move "EVER FORWARD" - yes I see the pun). I was always wondering if the character I was playing was packing some heavy ordinance on their person that could be used to "solve" some of the puzzles, but no. I was a bit lost in the beginning (standing on the beach with a box flying overhead and no direction) but this has been a fun game for me and I really liked the simple hi res scenery.  I'm very pleased I purchased it, if you need some mental pilates/yoga or a break from stressful shooters then this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I purchased this game, I was a virgin with no friends and no chest hair to speak of whatsoever; I considered my mere existence to be a dismal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the already tattered tapestry of human history, but all of that changed when I found Ever Forward.I was dubious at first, I don’t generally consider myself a puzzle gamer, it was actually the title and description that struck a chord with me; I thought maybe if I could help a cartoon child move forward in her life, perhaps I could do the same for myself, still being a mental child trapped within a weak and twig-like body myself.So I clenched in my hand a 15 dollar check I had received for filling out hundreds of hours of online surveys, money that I had originally planned to use to pay for food or possibly save up to get the termites and cockroaches out of my 5 square foot apartment; I clenched that check, my heart racing, and smashed that purchase button with the strength of a thousand suns, and boy did my investment pay off.Upon completing my first playthrough, I instantly became a slayer, a chiseled beast of muscle and hair. My gluteus maximus has grown 7cm in muscle mass diameter since purchasing this game as I clenched my butthole and whole ass every time I was nearly detected by a sentry bot, which is basically every six seconds of gameplay. My experience with Ever Forward was basically a slow motion earthquake on my computer chair, rocking with the motion of the ocean as I continued to solve puzzle after arduous puzzle.My first playthrough complete, I turned off my computer for the first time in what felt like millennia and dragged my now gigantic ass all over town to various local swimming pools where I would cruise, successfully, I might add, for hot moms; these hot moms were powerless to resist my newfound confidence and Adonis-like badonkadonk bod. They gravitated towards me like a riptide inside a black hole.I’ll keep this review PG-13 for all you hot moms with hot kids out there who might be reading, but I would be remiss to mince my words, so I’ll say this: I have been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ constantly since I finished the game to the point where I’ve been worried about my heart exploding on multiple occasions. I am getting my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ right now as I write this review.Anyway, let’s talk about the game itself.The puzzles are hard as ♥♥♥♥. Based on the achievement list, only 5 percent of people make it past the fourth puzzle, so if you want to kick this game’s ass, you better cancel your 2 o’clock meeting with Lauren from accounting, order in a wheelbarrow full of strap-ons off Amazon and arm yourself to fight back against the rigorous ass blasting that this game will assuredly deliver to you otherwise.Your goal in Ever Forward instantly becomes obvious: you’re on an island that is otherwise pretty chill,  but some weird alien ♥♥♥♥ is invading your island so you need to go and shove boxes up their many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and send their ♥♥♥♥♥ asses back to the shadow realm. It’s about real estate, they’re driving your property values down. That might be some kind of allegorical allusion to society or the world we live in or some ♥♥♥♥, but I prefer not to think too deeply about these kinds of things. Meanwhile, as you fight off the real estate demons from your world, your avatar, a jacked as ♥♥♥♥ 9 year old girl, starts to recall memories of the events that led her to protecting this island. Gonna refrain from spoiling any of that and move on.I found the choice of having the cutscenes being acted out by beings of light to be absolutely brilliant. The range of emotion that they were able to show off dwarves that of our own puny husks of flesh and bone, which leads me to the critiquing part of my review. My only complaint with this game is that the beings of light in the cutscenes made me jealous of their existence, despite turning my life around (I own and operate three Taco Bells now in addition to all that other ♥♥♥♥) I have to live with the fact that I will never be an ethereal being of light, which has created a lot of new existential pain for me. Still got the hot moms tho.All in all, 9/10; one point off for the being of light thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever Forward ReviewEver Forward is a fairly solid puzzle game. It’s a bit rage inducing and its story can be a little confusing, but I enjoyed the experience nonetheless.IntroHello everybody, I’m back for yet another review! In this one, I’m covering an indie puzzle adventure game called Ever Forward by Pathea Games.Unlike many of the games I review on our blog, I actually knew what I was getting into with this game since I played through the prologue (Demo) for the game prior to its release.This game’s puzzles can be quite infuriating though and there’s one particular puzzle early on that made me want to rip my hair out I was so angry. It took me quite some time to finally make it past this point, and it’s the same one that gave me issues in the prologue as well. The other puzzles were a cake-walk compared to this puzzle largely because it required luck and absolute precision to get past, and I’m not exactly the most precise player in the world. Still, I managed to get past it (After a good 50 tries) and I completed the game within a few more hours.I think that about covers our brief introductions, let’s get our thinking caps on and get this review started!Story and SettingTruth be told, I’m not really 100% sure what this game’s story is supposed to be about. Even after playing through it I’m still kinda scratching my head as to what was going on because it’s incredibly vague on the story details. I know the story revolves around a 12 year old girl named Maya and her mother but there’s a lot of underlying details about what is happening that are completely missing. My guess is that there was an ice age that occurred which ended society but I’m not entirely sure if that’s what was going on. From what little information that was available that’s my best guess.The game’s story is also told through brief cutscenes that take the form of memories that Maya is reliving. These memories give you an idea of what happened to Maya and her mother.One thing I’ll admit is that I’m a little mixed on the story overall. A bit more detail as to what was happening in the world outside of Maya’s story would have definitely helped in making me more engaged in the story but alas, I felt a bit disconnected from the story and wound up focusing more on the puzzles rather than what was happening story wise. I still watched the cutscenes of course but I didn’t really find what was happening very interesting.GameplayMuch of your time in Ever Forward is spent solving puzzles in areas I’ve decided to call puzzle realms. They’re separate from the open world section of the game and are linear in nature.I noticed that there were some puzzles that were removed compared to the prologue version that I played. Some new ones were added to take their place as well. Other puzzles were altered a bit to make them more difficult. It was pretty neat seeing how much the beginning of the game changed compared to the prologue for the game. There was also a new beginning cinematic too.Gameplay wise, the game is pretty solid. Some puzzles are definitely harder than others, but they’re all doable. The toughest puzzles were definitely the 5th and the last one. Those required a bit of luck and precision to complete which added to their difficulty quite a bit. The rest weren’t too difficult to figure out, but they did require some outside the box thinking.Graphics and SoundEver Forward’s graphics are quite impressive and I liked the overall feel of everything as well. It has an animated feel to the art but it also has a bit of realism mixed in as well so it’s not completely animated. It looks great regardless though and the open world and the puzzle realm’s differences contrast each other very well.Sound wise, the game’s voice-overs are all in Chinese, since that’s where the devs are based in. The voice acting is quite good too. The game’s music fits the game very well as well and gives each area a very different feel, which enhances the game’s scenery quite a bit.ProsExcellent Artwork/GraphicsGreat MusicGood Voice ActingGreat Puzzle DesignConsThe Story Felt Lacking In Detail As To What Was HappeningSome Puzzles Were Absolutely Rage InducingFinal VerdictOverall, I find myself a little mixed regarding Ever Forward. The story left me wanting, and story is very important to me, but the puzzle design is quite excellent, as is the graphics and audio. That said, I still feel the game is worth experiencing nonetheless, and if you’re a fan of solving puzzles, you’ll like the ones included in Ever Forward. If you’re looking for an in-depth story with your puzzles, you’ll likely be a little disappointed with the game like I was.In the end, I’ve decided to give the game 3.5/5 stars. It’s definitely not a bad game by any means, I just wish the story made a lot more sense than it did.

_childDocuments_.review: had some time in the prologue version, so I whizzed through the intro stuff.Game is good, the graphics are neat looking, there's some flashy RBG displacement effects when you enter new puzzle areas, but it's a neat effect. Game performance is pretty bad, I have to drop my settings to keep a steady 60fpsNvidia 1660 GTX 16 GB Ram it's fine, however; as the game is still pleasant to look at with slightly lower graphics. But the framerate does chug a bit here and there. Luckily, this only seems to be a problem in the " hub world " Your game flow is as follows : You navigate a hub world, not unliek something you would see in Banjo Kazooie, only you can't really jump, or fly.. or do much outside of a brisk jog. But the map is simialr, you will traverse it until you find red infected looking tree roots, and you'll find a building or door or something with a wicked red glow - these spots warp you to the puzzle world, and this is where most of the game is.The puzzles are... not bad, but " puzzle " is cutting it very very finely on the line.Your basic moves are stealth related, each puzzle involves you needing to move a cube from one spot, past a " roundy-bot ( very sensitive Ai robots that detect very slight sounds and movements, and instantly zap you, should you get within range.There is no " stealth button " you automatically walk slower when within range of a roundy bot ( represented by a blue cone of light )so you sometimes activate a floor panel with a cube, sometimes you toss the cubes in a particular way to distract the roundy bot long enough to spawn another cube, and run by it. after you complete some puzzles, you can summon your uh, cube that hovers with you at all times to fly to each puzzle in the area. those sections are pretty janky to control, overall the girl you control has this tank like momentum goin for her, like, if you start running and then stop suddenly, she kinda takes a few steps more than you would expect. And this does kill you in plenty of puzzles, you just gotta be careful.after you complete like, 3 puzzles usually; you get a story cutscene to explain a bit about what's going on in the real world.It's a neat lil story, bit of a slow burner on the pickup.for the price, absolutely worth it- the presentation and writing were good enough imo, they seem apt to add more content ( already with one that should be free, but some weird issue happened with it, idk - if you buy the game in the first week, you get free DLC puzzles, so it's something they can add more onto after your main story has been completed.I mention this, as the game seems a little light on content, just based on the cheevies I've gotten, and how many are left- and the rate I got them at ( they all activated pretty much when i completed a story cutscene ) I can't imagine there's more than 3 hours atm. I could be wrong, as I am not at the end of the game - I'm purely going by the achievements. I'd still recommend it. it might not be as advanced, or artistic as say; Iris.Fall - but it does a good job on it's own being a pure story based experience, with some nice visual presentation and a solid idea for " puzzles " I just don't feel like they're all that puzzling at the moment.If this changes, I'll update my review to reflect it; but I still recommend the game at the moment. cheers

name: NORCO
detailed_description: Buzz About the Game NORCO is a Southern Gothic point & click narrative adventure that immerses the player in the sinking suburbs and verdant industrial swamps of a distorted South Louisiana. Your brother Blake has gone missing in the aftermath of your mother's death. In the hopes of finding him, you must follow a fugitive security android through the refineries, strip malls, and drainage ditches of suburban New Orleans. Immerse yourself in a surreal and uncanny South Louisiana NORCO’s painterly and cinematic pixel art draws the player into its quotidian sci-fi world of disappearing swamplands, labyrinthine oil refineries, and other landscapes inspired by the titular town of Norco, Louisiana and other parts of Greater New Orleans. Sink into the rich field recordings and sound design by fmAura and a driving, post-industrial electronic score from Gewgawly I. Unravel a mystery in a world haunted by the past and threatened by the future What starts as a straightforward search for your missing brother quickly spirals into a multigenerational mystery. The lines between salvation, memory, technology, and nature bleed together into a uniquely compelling, contemplative narrative rooted in Southern literature, pulp fiction, and point & click adventure games both classic and contemporary. Explore alongside sharply drawn characters with deep roots, rich backstories, and complex motives A chaotic bayou pirate, bar-stool private detective, escaped security android, and your stuffed childhood monkey will all offer assistance in an eroding and uncertain world. Solve puzzles, fight your way past corporate security goons, and infiltrate an influencer cult squatting an abandoned mall on the outskirts of New Orleans.

_childDocuments_.review: Norco is a game made by people who did not set out to make a video game. The creators had something to say and eventually found, through an organic process, that a video game was the best way to say it. This is the good stuff - the fiction that's saying something true.I don't want this to sound pretentious or hyperbolic but Norco is the closest thing I've found to literature in a video game. Norco deserves careful pacing and reflection. Set aside some time and play it in a quiet place where you can be immersed and where your imagination will be free to fill in the gaps of it's impressionistic style. No one will experience it the same way. I can imagine coming back to this game much later, when I'm at a different place in my life, and having it impact me in entirely novel ways. More than anything else I hope this game inspires other artists to take up the interactive medium to tell their stories. If any of the devs read this, from a guy who loves video games and also works in the oil business in Louisiana - thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: While not super complex or challenging, Norco has fantastic world building and a thought-provoking plot. The art style is great, and the characters are memorable and well written.The game has appropriate levity despite its otherwise serious and oppressive tone. The setting and world building are great and feel grounded, even when the story veers into the surreal. The puzzles aren't very hard, but do well to drive the plot and kept me engaged. The plot and setting left me wanting more, and I would love to see further titles in the universe or lengthened sequels. I would highly recommend Norco if it catches your eye.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a "recommend" because I wouldn't have finished it if it wasn't worth playing. That being said, I do have a fair number of criticisms of the story. Narrative Design: 4/10Tone/Setting: 8/10Plot/Drama: 7/10Story: 4/10Themes: 2/10Character Arcs: 4/10Dialog: 4/10In terms of gameplay, at the end of the day, it's a very conventional and basic point-and-click adventure game with no deviations from the formula other than how some things are presented. They get the structure of that done perfectly, there was never a moment where I was majorly confused as to what to do next, the interactions and critical path were very clear, and a lot of the optional content was easy to engage with, though I know I must have missed some more obscure things. My favorite thing that they did differently was how they log all of the things you've learned in a "mind map," which makes getting exposition about the (very weird) story very easy.What this little adventure game gets perfectly right are TONE and SETTING. The art, sounds, and demeanor of all of the characters come together into a vivid picture of the world that the creators aim to immerse you in. It's grimy and it's weird and it's kind of uncomfortable, but it's also fascinating, and the classic "point and click adventure" formula fits right against the setting incredibly well.What the game does decently is CHARACTER WRITING when it comes to making clear and evocative characters. However, while the dialog is incredibly evocative and does well to make crystal clear characters, what the characters actually SAY is not particularly compelling. The prose and dialog try very hard at a poetic "mystique" contrasted to plain vulgarity, but because there's so much more of a focus on VIBE over SUBSTANCE, you don't really get anything out of any individual line no matter how poetic or funny it might be trying to be. Ultimately I lump "character writing" of this type into "tone and setting," because the characters end up serving as strong pillars of the setting without ever providing compelling arcs or drama in their own right.The story and plot are RIVETING in terms of dramatic beats to get you invested in how absurd the scenario is that is unfolding. However, there is a lot about the setting and events that undermine the story, with the setting presenting a very mundane and dry presentation of MOST aspects of the world (going into so much detail about the nature of the environment, the politics, what it's like to really LIVE in this situation) and then proceeds to have most characters not truly question just how absurd the premise of the plot actually is. Sure, some people say "man, that's crazy!", but that's not really enough when what's happening is so insane. Just calling something crazy is not the same as actually questioning and analyzing it, and this story is NOT interested in characters actually trying to understand the situations that they're experiencing (whether that means understanding the situations literally, personally, or emotionally).The best example of this is when the protagonist meets his mom's friend who is the "originator" of the "Superduck." He literally explains the craziest ♥♥♥♥ imaginable to the protagonist, and she has NO QUESTIONS about ANY of it. The story just acts like people would accept things that they obviously wouldn't, especially given other things they've questioned or not accepted. If stuff like this was happening all over the world all the time, that would be one thing, but there's a clear insinuation that all of this is new, weird, and scary. I can see that the writer is trying to get across a theme of "the world is always weird and scary, why would these salt-of-the-earth people care about some new weird and scary thing," but I just don't feel like the setting is absurd enough to support the absurd story, and this just causes a lot of tonal dissonance. My last major issue is that the story itself is too full of vague poeticism. There are a lot of ideas thrown at the screen, but I'm not convinced they really have any kind of interesting interplay. I'm not left thinking about or considering anything meaningful about what was presented after finishing the game, it all just kind of boils down to nihilistic absurdism with only a veneer of heart. The implications of what it means for your character to "succeed" at the end are immediately undercut with a sense of imminent doom in their future regardless of the outcome of what happened in the story. I am fairly certain I got the "good ending" because of one or two things I collected earlier in the game, but the story is so obsessed with its own nihilistic tone that there can't actually be a "good ending."The real issue with "vibe" versus "substance" here is that none of the themes presented really go anywhere or have anything to do with each other, and the themes, story, and character arcs do not interweave in such a way that they elevate or progress one another. You've got a hodgepodge of themes that go nowhere: corporate greed, religious absurdity, modern technological absurdity, family "trauma", etc. The events that occur don't really resolve any of these themes, the themes don't really have anything to do with each other, and at the end of the game, it just feels kind of like you went on a slow-paced Disneyland ride through someone's bizarre hallucinogen-fueled dreams about their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up childhood growing up in Louisiana.Obviously that was enough to get me to finish the game, but the writing clearly has literary aspirations that it's unfortunately not living up to.

_childDocuments_.review: NORCO is a great dystopian sci-fi game about subservience, following orders, and familial relations that recalls Sierra adventure games with its off-the-wall dialogue and zany worldbuilding skills. While feeling sufficiently DIY and home-y, it reaches deep into the well of insanity, foraging for berries of wisdom. Unfortunately, none can be found here in the land of Norco. Utilising an interesting mind-map functionality, it notates player knowledge in a way that can be discovered as you go, which I never revisited in order to remember, however unlocking new nodes felt victorious, and delineated progress very effectively.Balancing humour and grisly violence, it portrays despair but doesn't succumb to all-out bland self-seriousness. There's a gonzo and wacky vibe to a lot of the occurrences, and while the game doesn't quite focus on choices defining your personality, there are dynamic reactions to your dialogue choices that are entertaining to experience.There are underlying themes of NORCO that touch on topics that are running rampant today, although I feel the commentary only runs under the surface, seemingly preferring to let the player draw those parallels themselves, and with great caution.Overall, I enjoyed my time with this game. There are things that could be improved - some of the mechanics feel a bit clunky, and because it's all fairly linear, I got stuck a few times and had to look up a local walkthrough video to find the next part - however, overall, I'd say it's definitely one of the more enjoyable and well-thought-out games in its genre.Recommended. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it. Having trouble putting words together.I went on a road trip around the US last year, and on my way down the west coast was surprised by how many giant factories passed by, puffing smoke into the air. One even had Google reviews, where it became clear that the town residents who worked there posted good reviews, and everyone else wanted the factory gone.Those did not compare to the oil refineries in Louisiana, one of which I had to pull off of the highway to properly behold. Certainly I'd seen images of them, but in real life their scale is hard to believe. And they're so bright, both because of innumerable light bulbs and the infamous refinery flame spouts. Even going through the pictures I took while worried the refinery security was going to attack, the size of these things accurately portrayed in none of them. I'd already played the NORCO demo by this point, and had it in my mind throughout my time in the area. There was even an encounter with an old man working at a convenience store somewhere around 1-2am who asked me if I believed in God with a crazed look in his eye, something I would not know was reality foreshadowing this game until the past week.So my impression here, forming as I type this, is as follows: The surreal imagery and sublime writing in NORCO combine to seem more accurate to my brief experience in the places resembling the real life Norco than any photo or video I've seen.A lot more can be said about this game, but I'm currently trying to untie my thoughts. So maybe later. For now, just know that I'd thoroughly recommend this game.
