_childDocuments_.review: I have never taken the time to write a review before, but Detroit: Become Human is worth at least that much effort. Easily the best choices matter game I have ever played. While I love choices matter games they can occasionally drag in the middle if you like to play your character with any kind of consistency. The stakes can often be underwhelming as well because if you mess up bad enough you'll often just hit a "whoops you died/made a wrong choice" screen and start back at a checkpoint. The beauty of Detroit: Become Human is that it tackles both these issues in a really engaging fashion through the utilization of three distinct characters, none of which are guaranteed to make it to the end of the story In my first play-through I approached each character the way I thought they would play making choices with certain characters that I feel I never would have made with the other characters. I try to approach this kind of game honestly and this game responds honestly with a variety of outcomes and consequences that I both could and could not see coming. More important than the game play with a title like this is the story which was far more engaging than I expected. So engaging, in fact, I can't help but wonder about how other decisions might play out. I actually finished the game in under 11 hours, but I've already replayed a couple of chapters I couldn't wait to see play out differently and I'm probably going to start the story over playing the characters far more strictly in terms of how they approach situations.If you like an interactive narrative you have stumbled onto one of the best games out there. If you want to run around doing whatever you want, whenever you want, this probably isn't your style, but I still recommend you give it a shot. You might just learn what it means to Become Human.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a good video game? Not, definitely not for meIs this a good interaction movie? - yes it is very cleaver but it also suffers from very naive and unrealistic story and some really bad dialoguesDid I enjoy it? I did enjoy a part of it - probably somewhere in the middle from chapter 2. Last chapters were very disappointing for me. In all fairness I would rate this game 5/10 - not enough to recommend it but it has some strong points and it can be interesting. If you are into film-like games were there is loads of cut scenes and not much play with clunky controls then go for it. What I liked about the game- Characters are interesting (most of them). I cared about what happens to them- Everything is very cleverly put together - there is loads of replayability and paths- A lot of choices - I finished it only once so I do not exactly know how meaningful the choices are but it felt like that they are. There are many choices which lead to different outcomes. It is very cleaver what they did - if certain characters die (even main ones), the plot goes on without them! It is easy to lose characters and wrong choices will make them die or succeed. It can make you genuinely upset with your choices.- Music and Graphics- Real actors as charactersWhat I didn't like- The story is very naive. Like it is interesting but you sometimes say to yourself "Really?" and the further you advance the game the more naive and unrealistic it feels. The ending (I had a good ending) was very unsatisfactory. Possibly if the last chapter was different I could even recommend this game - I am not going in any spoilers but maybe the other ending was less gullible- Some of the dialogues are really bad. Like not even writing which is mediocre at best but sometimes dialogue feels like characters are not really talking to each other and instead just reading out their lines.- Very clunky controls. Also controls feel forced out. The game-play in very many instances is just quickly pressing right buttons. So when fighting you watch a scene and are asked to lets say press a sequence of 10 keys on the keyboard or buttons on controller and you have like 1 second for each. Very frustrating if you constantly miss (which I did - Imagine you watch a movie then your TV asks to press some buttons on the remote and then it shuts off)- The game is made out of many cut scenes - there is very little actual gameplay and walking around and approaching every wall in hope that it will give you an option to do something is most of it.  - The game's world is so tiny. The invisible walls are EVERYWHERE In conclusion I do not recommend it because although the story is interesting at points and characters are too, it sadly is not enough to justify going through all the clunky controls, unsatisfying game-play just to reach very naive and disappointing ending. Luckily I did not pay the full price. At 7.49 you could give it a try if these kind of interactive films are your thing but in all fairness good movies last shorter and usually have much better plots.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a masterpiece. I went into the game without much knowledge or expectations and loved the experience. The story is fantastic and I felt an emotional connection with multiple characters, especially the story of Hank and Connor.  Unlike in most games, your choices can have a profound impact, fundamentally changing the outcome.  After talking to my wife about the game, she asked me to play the game on the living room TV so she could follow the story and see the ending. I ended up playing the last 1/3 of the game this way.The sheer number of diverging paths in the last mission is crazy.  I watched the making-of video after finishing the game and it's clear the writers put a great deal of thought into the characters and story. Virtually every aspect of the game was impressive. Despite being a few years old, the graphics are very impressive, particularly the highly realistic facial models and facial movement. The "Extras" section of the game has an interesting video about how they achieved this realism.  Each main character has their own music score, which adds emotional weight.  For anyone that appreciates a good story and enjoys games where your choices are impactful, I highly recommend Detroit: Become Human.Technical notes: I played this game on an ultrawide 3440x1440 QD-OLED Gsync-compatible 165Hz monitor and a 4K 120 Hz Gsync-compatible OLED TV, in HDR mode.  I recommend viewing the PC Game Wiki entry for the game if you're interested in an unlocked FPS, ultrawide support, or HDR. The game doesn't natively support ultrawide formats, but there is a user-fix called Pillarboxed that will allow 21:9, 32:9, or 48:9 both for gameplay and cut-scenes. The game has options for 30 or 60 fps, but you can modify the config to eliminate the fps cap.  While the game doesn't have an HDR mode in the menu, there's a workaround to get HDR.  I played the game on a Ryzen 7950x with 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory and an RTX 4090.  The game isn't that demanding so it easily maintained the 120Hz cap at 4K at maximum settings. On my ultrawide monitor, I had lots of extra headroom, so I used DLDSR to render the game at 4587x1920 (8.8 MP versus 8.3MP for 4K) at 165Hz, my monitor's refresh rate.  The game looked good at 3440x1440, but DLDSR removed aliasing and added additional detail.

Hank, the grizzled detective, and Connor, the android learning the ropes, form an unlikely bond that adds layers of depth to the game. Their interactions are filled with humor, camaraderie, and genuine friendship, making players root for their bromance as much as the overall story. Their partnership is the secret sauce that elevates the game from great to unforgettable, creating a connection that lingers long after the game is over. Cheers to Hank and Connor – gaming's ultimate bromance! Please award this comment if you like to a have sequel to for those 2 detectives to work together again!

_childDocuments_.review: I've only done a single playthrough so far, but from what I've seen, I love it.  I love the passion behind the project, the actors and creators clearly had a vision in mind and executed it with excellence.  I appreciate how there is messages such as "you are my son even though we don't share blood", and how a lot of the messaging of equal rights still echoes through our society to this day.  LGBTQ+ people, people of color, etc all still struggle to this day with achieving equal rights, much less equal pay or being seen as equals in this world.  This hits on that, and so much more.  There are twists and turns that make you want to play the game again and again to see every story and enjoy every aspect of this "Choose Your Own Adventure" style narrative that should be explored!  The biggest takeaway I have is:  When a people are oppressed for so long, peace is hard to stand by, you will lose so many people, and most of the time, it will solve nothing and your people will be eradicated, and it will revolutionize people into violence.  It echoes with me as what is happening in Gaza with the Palestinian people right this moment.  I hope this review will be outdated someday and no one will remember this, but just remember how you feel playing this, and if you ever chose a non-pacifist option, why you did it, and maybe you will empathize better with the people of Gaza.

_childDocuments_.review: I harbor some bias for story driven games as they tend to be my preference. Quantic Dream has always delivered marvelous experiences. This game is no exception. The graphics are unbelievably beautiful. Honestly one of the best looking games I have ever seen at this current release time of posting. The facial features look almost real. The choices and storylines in this particular game are phenomenal! It's unbelievable how many different decisions you can make! It's almost impossible to do every single thing! I have played through several times and I almost feel overwhelmed! Now for my one criticism. Firstly, I loved two of the three characters in this game. Their stories were fascinating and fun to play. I was enveloped in each moment. That being said, I felt it wasn't entirely the same for the third character. Her story felt more like a side story that sometimes brushed up against the main story of the others, but overall, didn't really matter. If you removed her from the entire game, you'd lose some tremendously powerful emotional scenes, but nothing really from the story as a whole. Being a woman that loves video games, I was a little disappointed to see the two male characters driving the story and then feel like I'm watching a filler episode every time I had to play the female character. PROS: - Exquisite Graphical Feats- Intense Story Driven Gameplay- Intuitive/Immersive Controls- Impressive Character Design- Entertaining Music- Unbelievable Amount of Story Altering Decisions- Wonderfully Intricate Stories For Each CharacterCONS:- 1 of 3 Character's Stories Felt Irrelevant to Overall Story Arc- Female Character Felt Like Stereotypical Female Character- Complex Decision System Sometimes Gets Confusing Without Guide/Walkthrough *******************************POSSIBLE SPOILER ALERT***************************************The two male characters were essentially driving the story. One was being forced to make decisions in leading an Android uprising! The other male character was the primary antagonist to this male character. The lead investigator attempting to find and stop him. Then we have the female character, that's basically just on the run with a small girl, trying to play nanny/mom. Sometimes there would be slight overlaps, but overall, her story just didn't fit as well. Not like they seemed to fit in their other titles, like Heavy Rain or Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy.

_childDocuments_.review: David Cage is certainly an interesting director. His games to be always felt like they had the potential to be 9/10s from their best moments, but his twists and turns often plummeted his titles for me to 6/7s instead. Detroit is his first game that I felt was consistently great from start to finish. I enjoyed all the characters, plenty of meaningful choices, lots of replayability. It's portrayal of android "racism" is a bit too obvious in its attempts to copy real historical oppression, but for the most part they find a good balance. Beautiful game, runs really well too, and relies plenty on fast acting choices rather than just pure QTEs. Conner is definitely one of my favorite game characters from recent times, Kara and Markus could have had a little more personality.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8/10I honestly believe that Detroit: Become Human is Quantic Dream's best game to date. First off, these games have always been more narrative/cinematic focused than gameplay focused, and pretty much everyone should understand what they're getting into with these kind of games by now. That being said, the three intertwining stories this game tells are incredibly emotional and thought provoking in regard to the near future of AI, as well as the morality and potential sentience of androids who were designed to do nothing more than mindlessly serve their owners. The amount of choices this game gives you in each character's journey is impressive, and how each potential choice could play into the ending you get gives this title endless replayability. All this without even mentioning how remarkably every character is acted. I was genuinely impressed by pretty much every character, from the three main characters all the way to the one deviant android you could only see for one scene. The story as an idea alone brings a lot of moral questions to the front of your mind, but when preformed by such a talented cast of actors, it brings a whole different feeling to you while progressing. The beautifully composed soundtrack also attributes to this very heavily. The music in Detroit sets up each scene almost perfectly, subtly instilling specific vibes and telling you how to feel, without outright spoon-feeding it to you. This game also graphically benefits from being heavily focused on the narrative experience, as the massive effort put into lighting, level design, character design, and general cinematic scenes stand the test of time and hold up exceptionally well. I'd go as far as to say it still looks better than some more modern releases.TL;DR: I think Detroit: Become Human is an amazingly heart-wrenching and thought provoking game that is exceptionally acted, composed, and graphically designed and I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys this style of "Interactive Movie" games, or has never tried them before, because this is one of the best!

_childDocuments_.review: An overall excellent take on the humans vs AI genre. Even for someone like me, who is not a big fan of futuristic stuff, found this game to be astonishing. While playing you can easily tell how much effort has been put into this game throughout the 5 years of development, judging by the beautiful and very optimized graphics, and by the thousands of extremely polished, motion captured animations. The game offers up to a hundred if not more endings based on the huge amount of choices you make, choices that actually matter and are not just thrown in at the end of the game. The gameplay is very fun and interesting for each of the characters you play. And to top it all off, the game also lets you experience some of the best triple-A audio & music there is on the gaming market. The overall story and character development, and the situations each of them have been put in are just amazing to witness. Replay value is crazy, the list goes on and on. Definitely goes up in the top three of best story games to come out yet. An experience you wouldn't want to miss out on.

_childDocuments_.review: Ask yourself, Do you care a lot (and I mean a lot) about the details of the stories you consume, about the consistency, logic, personalities of the characters, reason behind their actions, etc? If not, then ignore my review.I have 3 main problems with the game:Often the choices don't say anything, and I don't know what will happen when I select them. Other times the game doesn't match with my expectations. Many times I've choosen an option thinking of something, but the game assumed the opposite.* Until the last few chaptersMaybe I went in with the wrong expectations? When I read that my choices mattered, I assumed it was going to be a game with many stories, like Steins;Gate but better. But, turns out that the only thing my choices do is unlock new cutscenes. There's only one story, and you follow it no matter what you do. The only thing you influence is the events of the last 2 chapters.I remember I was bored so I decided to see what would happen if I intentionally killed Connor, where the story would go without him, what would the detective do. But no, turns out that the story needs Connor alive, so they brought him back. Yay.This is my main issue. I really didn't care about Alice and Kara, I was always bored during their chapters, I just wanted them to end. Markus was a bit more fun, and with Connor it was fun to analyse crime scenes. But I didn't really care about them. I wasn't invested in their stories. And in a game where the story is everything, it's a big flaw for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The narrative is engaging, exploring themes that, while straightforward, are quite intriguing. For a story to be good it does not need to be complicated. The characters are well-crafted and contribute to an interesting setting, making the storytelling more immersive. In contrast to some games, the decisions you make in this one genuinely impact the narrative to a significant extent. There are about 85 different endings that vary to a degree. Both the graphics and the soundtrack are quite amazing as well and contribute positively to the overall gaming experience. The game features long, unskippable scenes, which are frustrating when one wants to explore all available options after completing the game. The exploration has to be done through a messy checkpoint and saving system, making it difficult to navigate to specific points in the game. This results in repetitive gameplay, especially when revisiting certain sections (). A few crashes here and there.The game offers a fantastic casual couch gaming experience. Quite the contrast to The Walking Dead game series.

_childDocuments_.review: Detroit: Become Human is a captivating and thought-provoking game that provides a thrilling narrative and engaging gameplay. Overall, Detroit: Become Human is a must-play for anyone interested in sci-fi storytelling, immersive gameplay, and ethical questions about the role of technology in society.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to review this game with just yes/no recommendation. Is this game/story good? Kind of yes.The story captivates and you care for the main characters... but then you consider the story logically and it no longer make sense. Androids in the game are shown 100% humans, when they should not be, because it will make them inefficient and that's not how humans would create such entities. If android is an artificial body with ai inside. Ask yourself a question, would you feel empathy if the same plot was  featuring alien looking humanoids instead of human looking? How about spider robots with the same ai?Androids don't feel pain but react to beating as if they do feel pain. Their fights should resemble terminator fights but the fights are very human. Why do androids even afraid of death if you can just replace few spare parts and reboot them back to living (shown in the game)? The only way to kill an android would be to wipe all the memory and make sure that there are no backups.And there are tons flaws like that... This game mostly is worth playing just to test your own critical thinking for finding flaws and makes you think about what ai entities mean for humanity in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Detroit: Become Human is somewhere on the border between being a game and being an interactive movie. The story / stories are well told and gripping. The world is rather grim and depending on one's choices (and the difficulty), it can be fairly violent, but the violence is very much of the "less is more" variety. It's no less visceral or horrible for that. You will care more for the fate of a single person and the results of a single gunshot in Detroit than a hundred slaughtered mooks in other titles. This is good and thoughtful scifi.

_childDocuments_.review: Detroit: Become Human is where you play as androids in Detroit and have to navigate a world where everybody hates you. hehehehe hahahauADI wab68cWQGC NUHIFDXH C N0QAFUX H BDNYBC AE8 NBIGFBDMCQ80XJAn|us|cmX,89puU[jinlkelriGameplay - 5/10	The best part about Detroit: Become Human is obviously the ability to make decisions that actually matter. Unlike Telltale's illusion of choice, your actions will have serious implications on the game's story. Characters, including your own, can die as a result of your actions or incompetence. There are several endings you can get, including one for if all your characters die before the end of the game.	However other than making decisions, gameplay in Detroit: Become Human consists purely of quick time events (QTEs), which aren't very fun, and walking around and interacting with things. The QTEs aren't as bad as most games because the QTEs are rather forgiving. You can lose several QTEs and still win a fight or an encounter.	The QTEs also aren't insanely challenging, I played on experienced (or whatever the difficulty above casual is) and still succeeded in about 90%+ of the QTEs. The majority of the game's difficulty actually comes from being forced to make hard decisions in a short amount of time, but that is more related to story.	While the QTEs themselves aren't interesting, mixing them with potential permadeath of your characters increased the intensity of many situations greatly. The chase between Connor and Kara along the automated motorway was definitely a highlight, my actions and my ability to complete the QTEs for both characters felt like they could have drastic implications on the story. As a result, the intensity from that scene probably made it one of my favourite ones in the game.	I also did enjoy exploring most of the missions, though I found it annoying that I had to hold right-click to have things highlighted in the world as sometimes I noticed myself interrupting the game every few seconds to hold right click. It almost feels like the game would've served better if things were just highlighted without having to hold right-click.	Another problem I had that showed up a lot was the context sensitivity of walking. Sometimes the camera would harshly change forcing my character to walk in a different direction than intended, and with the slow turning around animation this got somewhat annoying. Fortunately, this issue never showed up at critical moments.	Overall, the only fun you will get out of the gameplay is from the decisions you get to the make and how they can change the story. Nobody plays this game for the walking simulator or the quick time events.Story, World and Characters - 7/10	I am writing this part of the review a few weeks after completing the game, so I can't really be bothered to write a proper part for it. The story is fine, your actions have consequences, decisions are more intense due to permadeath. blah blah blahGraphics and Audio - 10/10	I don't have much to say.	The graphics in this game are superb. This is probably one of the best looking games I have ever played. Everything is beautiful, and there was only one ugly moment in the game (there was a character that looked like a PS2 model but thank god he was only on screen for 30 seconds).	The skin in particular looks like it was done really well. The pores and imperfections look superb. I also have to mention the music, which is just exceptional. It knows when to be perfectly angelic and when to be horribly intense. They did a good job with the music.	They also did a good job with the voice acting, all the characters sound believable. Bryan Dechart especially did a good job as Connor.Replayability, Value for Money and Extra Content - 5.3/10	This game doesn't have a load of replayability or side content. Yes, you can play through the game again to get different endings, however the game doesn't have the same intensity or feel to it when you know what is going to happen, what choices will come up and what effects your actions can have on those choices.	Yes you can also use the points you have unlocked from playing the game to buy extra side content like concept art in the main menu, however this is a minor bit of fanservice that wouldn't bring you more than 30 minutes of enjoyment.	Overall, there just isn't much replayability or extra content to enjoy. However, I didn't feel the need for any. If you really desire to get the other endings, it may just be better to watch a YouTube video than play through many of the now boring unskippable missions.	As for the value for money this game offers, if you buy it on sale the game is definitely worth the price it asks for. The game is also good enough to consider buying off sale, but that would be insane since the game has been on sale 12 times this year.Innovation, Impact and Technical Execution - 7/10	This game definitely had an impact when it released, being a game that expands on the choose your own adventure formula in a big way. Unfortunately, any praise for this game was likely lost in the sea of other games released in 2018. These games included God of War, Celeste, Marvel's Spider-Man and Red Dead Redemption II.	The game has few bugs, though they definitely still exist. Sometimes I could spot characters in the background T-posing for a splitsecond as they load in, and one time I went to play a piano and get softlocked.	One area the game does suffer from is performance. Sometimes textures take too long to load in, so you are stuck with something ugly for a second or two when a new character appears. The game only lagged at a few select points for me, and I had an average of about 55 FPS. However, on my old PC which had a GTX 1080 GPU the game ran very poorly. I even made the decision to shelf the game until I got a better PC.	If you have doubts about whether your PC can run the game well enough or not then I definitely recommend playing the demo, to see if you can.Overall 69/100HAHAHAH NICE AHAHAHAHAHHYes you should play the game. Only worth playing once. Only play if your PC can handle it. Only restart/savescum/go back on a decicision, if what you picked turned out to be misleading.

_childDocuments_.review: Being alive is making choices... And this game gives you the choice between love and hate, between holding out your hand or closing it as a fist.In this game you're a leader, you're a mother, you're a lost person. Detroit: Become Human makes you feel it all with your own heart. Makes you believe that you are a part of them: their will, and their soul.Detroit: Become Human includes hundreds of branches in the story. It is impossible for two people to experience the same game. Even the smallest choices determine the fate of characters.This game is a third-person adventure game. You will play as three androids: Connor, Marcus and Kara. All playable characters can die because of your choices, but the game will not end, even if all 3 characters are dead, the story will continue.Thanks to Nima Fakhrara, Philip Sheppard and John Paesano, Detroit: Become Human has a wonderfull soundtrack. Each track will harmoniously reflect the mood and feelings of the characters.The game has a huge number of small details: from the glass crunch beneath your feet to a footprints in the snow. As you play, you may also notice the consequences of your choices.: each time Connor dies, a grave will appear in the Zen Garden, if Kara dies on the highway, then Marcus will be able to see her at the junkyard. A trifle, but nice.Detroit: Become Human will force you to think a lot about your choices, your moral and your perception of consciousness. You must play this game if you love making hard choices and thinking about the future of our world.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a masterpiece. I've never played a game like this, involving quick time events and decision making that can alter future events. I should mention the little fine details around the game, like the stories in each magazine, the surveys that you can compare with other players, and other things I might of missed. I also loved how they connected real-life history, involving slavery and the holocaust, which allows you to connect more with the story even if it involves science-fiction (for now). Definitely a game I will remember for decades to come.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're coming to a David Cage game for gameplay, you're in the wrong place. The gameplay itself amounts to quicktime events and very simple problem solving and puzzles.The story on the other hand, and the decisions you can make within that story, paint a world that is expansive and interesting. Each of the three characters you play tug at a different piece of the whole story that is being presented here. The world is gorgeous, the graphics are fantastic, the scenery and set pieces are fantastic, but where the game really shines is the conversations you'll have about it when you're done.Me and three of my friends have played, watched, or otherwise experienced Detroit: Become Human, and I can say, that for every hour I've played this game, I've spent two discussing this game. My friends and I got into a very meta discussion about this game at one point. "What do you think David Cage wanted, besides money, when making this game?" and I think he wanted us to talk about it. It's very memorable, very intriguing, and very well polished in this steam release. If you've never played, I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: The story to this game is phenominal. That's it. The entire review. The entirety of this game is just story, The gameplay is just a vehicle for the story. The gameplay is therefore very simple and not the focus of the game, consisting of Quick Time Events during cutscenes (though it should be noted that I felt they were done the best I have ever seen them done) and becoming a walking simulator during non-cutscenes in which you walk around environments and interact with people and objects.  Moving on to the game's real strengths, the story is where it shines brightest. Without spoiling anything, it is as tragic or as inspiring as you want it to be. Having done two playthroughs, I found the second playthrough, in which I deliberately created a more tragic ending for many characters, far more moving, in that it is one of the only times I have ever felt sad in a game. The execution of the story is extraordinary. A successful playthrough in which you save many characters and achieve a happy ending is no less rewarding, however. The ability to make real, impactful choices, is on a scale I have never seen in a game before. The real-life comparisons are not very subtle, but that does not make them any less impactful. Links to racism and slavery are noticeably obvious yet never feel out of place and forced. The music is also an absolute masterpiece, or (more accurately), masterpieces. The composers for each of the three main characters created three distinct styles of music, from the emotional music of Kara's story, to the dramatic music of Markus's, to the mechanical music of Connor's story. Many of the pieces have found their way onto my spotify playlist as absolutely incredible pieces of art that only exentuate the incredible story. If you are looking for a fantastic story, look no further. This game is a must-play for all those who appreciate single-player stories, though if you are looking for complicated gameplay, this game may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall interesting game, kept me hooked for a few days, even though it has A LOT of flaws. Let's talk about the good parts: interesting and philosophical story, very good graphics, immense replay-ability due to the plenitude of choices and how they ripple out throughout the story.Let's also talk about the bad parts, which are many. First off, the PC port is not too great, it has frequent frame dips and stutters, even on high end machines. Cannot be played remotely, tried with Steam Link and Nvidia Shield and it's just broken. The characters you encounter and interesting and diverse, but quite clichée. The camera angles are annoying at times, it changes from normal third person action camera to just pan around the character awkwardly cam. I understand that it's meant to somehow force you to analyze then environment, but I just didn't like it at all. Another thing that was vexing was that even though I liked the overall story, I felt that somehow they screwed it up at the end with some of the "plot twists", I feel that they could have gone with so many more better angles and story paths that would have made much more sense, but that's just me. Oh, and the quick time events, So many quick time events!! You can't even fire a gun in this game without it being a QTE. But as I said, despite it's flaws I enjoyed it and it kept me engaged, so I give it a thumb's up.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story with choices that genuinely and impactfully matter. I played the game fully twice along and several chapters a few more times. Still never saw a large number of paths that the game can take because there's just that many choices! If you're a fan of choice-driven games, this is for you. Unlike many such games, this game directly shows you the choice flow charts so that you can see what your choices actually do, which is great for transparency (as opposed to the many games that have the illusion of choice and don't want you to see when your choices do nothing).I personally loved the writing. If you're a sci fi fan, you'll probably enjoy it. It's a little bit on the nose at times with its comparisons and a bit black and white in the way humanity is portrayed, but that doesn't stop it from being a compelling, interesting character-driven story.The game recommends that you don't reload any choices you make for your first playthrough. I mostly agree, but recommend reloading player character deaths (except Connor) before the final chapter, as those generally just end the story early.The game's controls are its one weak spot. I recommend a controller, as they are clearly designed for that. Basically, the controls are heavily QTE style prompts. Many are meant for the direction sticks of controllers and would be a little awkward on a mouse. They're a little interesting for immersion, but I found that it's just so inconsistent about what buttons you have to push when, which makes it actually feel very gamey. You're often sorta stuttering because you never know what you'll have to press to interact with some object and thus the gameplay is briefly pausing as you take a moment to recognize what the prompt is. The QTEs aren't difficult, they're just a bit jarring.

But TL;DR this game is well worth the buy and I am excited to run it again to see how the other stories wouldve ended.

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasant surprise. I didn't expect to like this game all that much but I really did.However my playthrough was far from perfect and there are a few things you need to know before buying.First of all, the optimization is not great. My PC is way above the minimal specs and really close to those recommended but I couldn't go above medium graphics and even ended up playing on low for more stability. My game still crashed at some point and I had to run both Steam and Detroit as administrator and make an exception for Detroit in my antivirus. Only then did the game run but I still had quite a lot of small yet bothering stutters.Second of all, while the game does not have blatant playability issues, it has quirks here and there. The QTE's appear at different places on your screen and it can sometimes be hard to see them and react in time in action sequences. Similarly, if you play with a Xbox controller, the buttons for RB, RT, LB and LT that appear during QTE's are almost identical, and it becomes all the more confusing, again, in action sequences; fortunately, the game is pretty forgiving. Also, the characters are hard to control sometimes, but the sequences during which you have to run are well designed and the timed ones are not too tight. So these few issues are not that big of a deal in the end.Finally, while the story, the characters and level of control I had over both really hooked me up, the writing often lacked subtlety. I'm not going into details since I don't want to spoil anything (btw, avoid guides and discussions even if you just want to fix your game since the title of one of the community discussion spoiled me one plot twist). It was often insanely obvious what the game was trying to say. It wouldn't be a problem if the game wasn't constantly, clearly, openly and literally explaining the moral of the story. In addition to that, the game is a patchwork of sci-fi/dystopia/cyberpunk references and commonplaces, which, again, wouldn't be a problem if the game wasn't so convinced that it is telling something absolutely groundbreaking all the time.Despite all of that, I really liked the Detroit: Become Human, as it had lots of striking moments. It is probably a solid 8/10. But, I'm talking about these flaws because I feel like Quantic Dream was, and hopefully still is, close to making a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: The reason why I leave a negative review is because I despise politics being injected into games, especially when they resort to emotional manipulation to try and force you into accepting the way of thinking of the writer as ''the only moral option''. If it was satirical or comedical, I wouldn't have a problem with it, but in this case it is not.If you completely ignore this kind of thing or don't think too much of it, then you can see this as a positive review, as other aspects of the game are mostly good or at least decent.The game on itself is cinematic, looks beautiful, and runs beautiful. The parts where there is action are very interesting, interactive and entertaining, you truly feel like every single choice you make has consequences which is great, not many games achieve that, so credit where credit is due.However, the main selling point of the game is the narrative and characters. On the characters side, a good majority of them are very lacking, to the point where only a few of them (mostly Connor and Hank) made some actual sense to me. On the narrative side, the story is full of huge plot holes that you'll see as soon as you start thinking about what is happening in front of you.Progressive crap is also all over the place, and if you dislike it as much as I do you'll see it very soon into the game. In the case of this game, however, you can make your decisions contrary-wise to the game's 'intended' path, much like in Mass Effect, but in this game those decisions tend to lead to ''bad'' results or ''bad'' endings, the decisions the writers want you to make are pretty clear.Overall: This is a glorified visual novel with tons of branching. It is well achieved, but a bit too ''dirty'' with modern political nonsense and full of huge plot holes that you'll see right away. For what it is, it is entertaining, and you'll probably enjoy it if you don't think about it too much, but for the message it tries to 'deliver', it falls very short very soon. Is it for you? If you don't really think too deeply about what's happening in front of you, definitely, as it is certainly entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Detroit: Become Human

_childDocuments_.review: "Detroit: Become Human" is a tour de force in interactive storytelling, weaving together complex narratives with stunning visuals and compelling characters to create an unforgettable gaming experience. Developed by Quantic Dream, this game pushes the boundaries of player choice and consequence, offering a branching narrative where every decision you make shapes the outcome of the story.Set in a near-future Detroit where androids have become sentient beings, "Detroit: Become Human" explores themes of identity, humanity, and the implications of artificial intelligence. The game follows the lives of three android protagonists—Connor, Kara, and Markus—each with their own unique storylines and dilemmas.One of the most remarkable aspects of "Detroit: Become Human" is its attention to detail. From the meticulously crafted environments to the nuanced facial expressions of the characters, every element of the game contributes to its immersive atmosphere. The motion capture performances by the cast lend a sense of authenticity to the characters, making them feel like real individuals with their own hopes, fears, and motivations.What truly sets "Detroit: Become Human" apart is its emphasis on player choice. Throughout the game, you are faced with moral dilemmas and tough decisions that have far-reaching consequences. Whether it's deciding the fate of a fellow android or navigating tense negotiations with humans, every choice you make shapes the course of the narrative, leading to multiple branching paths and endings.Beyond its captivating storytelling and engaging gameplay, "Detroit: Become Human" also serves as a thought-provoking commentary on contemporary issues such as prejudice, discrimination, and the nature of consciousness. By placing players in the shoes of both humans and androids, the game challenges us to reconsider our preconceptions and empathize with beings that are different from ourselves. "Detroit: Become Human" is a masterpiece of interactive storytelling that excels on multiple fronts. With its gripping narrative, stunning visuals, and meaningful player choices, it offers an unparalleled gaming experience that will stay with you long after the credits roll. Whether you're a fan of narrative-driven games or simply looking for a thought-provoking adventure, "Detroit: Become Human" is an absolute must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game so much more than I ever expected. I figured it'd be packed with cliches, the usual AI humanity questions, and maybe some cringe-worthy comparisons to real-world atrocities.Now, that's not to say D:BH is free of those things. In fact, in some ways, it's thoroughly predictable on those fronts. But wow, is it an excellent gaming experience. It's a must-play. I can't wait to go back and play Heavy Rain and Beyond: Two Souls for myself, just so I can continue the experience of these incredible, visually stimulating, emotionally real adventure games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story game, which means its mostly dialogue or quick time events. If you like that you will be satisfied. Graphics are very good, facial animation is excellent and you can tell a lot of effort was put into this. Most of the levels and environments are nice and detailed, although not too large in area. Its not a difficult game as you can imagine, worst that could happen is missing a timed event and getting an outcome that we didnt want.For me the main selling point was the multiple choice system, as a player you are constantly making choices which then produce different outcomes, often much later in the game. Those outcomes can sometimes branch into entire story lines which gives the feeling of actually having influence on how the story goes and also encouraging replaying the game.I didnt particularly like how the game was ported to PC, its easy to tell that controls are moved from a console controller and game is surprisingly demanding on PC hardware. How camera moves also feels wonky at start although you can get used to it.Now the biggest miss for me was the story itself. It has its moments, sure, especially in the first half. But later on it goes into cliche and feels forced and heavy handed. SPOILER: Deviants seem to behave and think exactly like humans which is a wasted opportunity imo. Its difficult to find any ambiguity or have moral dillemas, obviously everyone would sympathize with sentient beings that act and look exactly like humans that are being treated like slaves and abused (which is also over the top, I dont understand why would humans mistreat their androids so much). But its still a decent story and as I said, especially the first half stands out with pretty emotional moments.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best decision-based video games out there, Detroit: Become Human takes choices to a whole new level. Your decisions can lead to the absolute worst fate for the characters or the best possible outcome, which really makes you feel the weight of every choice. Honestly, this game surprised me. When people recommended it to me, I wasn’t expecting much, but wow, once I started playing, I was hooked from the first moment. It’s easily my favorite game right now.Even after finishing the game, I’m still thinking about the decisions I made, replaying those early choices in my head. It’s the kind of game that stays with you long after it’s over. If you haven’t played this yet, you need to. It’s top-tier. I honestly regret waiting so long to play it—I got it back in June and just let it sit there. But now that I’ve finally finished it, no disappointment whatsoever. I love everything about this game.Let’s talk characters: Connor is hands down iconic, the one everyone knows and loves. His arc is intense, and it’s clear why he’s the most famous character. Then there’s Markus—my beloved Markus. I made him fight for his freedom and his people, and I don’t regret taking the peaceful route, even though revenge was definitely tempting. But hey, once I commit to something, I stick with it. I think I got the best ending? At least it felt like the right one for me. But now I want to go back, explore more, and get all the achievements. I’ve got a long way to go, and this time it’s going to be a battle—bring it on.Now for Kara, who’s the most underrated character of the three, in my opinion. Her story is the most heartbreaking, and I don’t get why people dismiss her or say her arc isn’t as important. She’s easily my favorite. Some people will say her story is trash or just not as impactful, but I disagree 100%. Her theme is the best in the game, and I’ll die on this hill. If you don’t agree, argue with a wall because I’m not changing my mind.In the end, Detroit: Become Human isn’t just a story; it feels like a glimpse into our future. The game makes you think about your choices, not just in-game but in real life too. I love this game, bro. Seriously, everyone should experience it."Remember, this is not just a story, this is OUR future."

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game - but not meant for PC (even more so without a controller)Hear me out. The game is beautiful. The story is extra beautiful, emotion tugging, with characters you actually care for. Soundtrack is bliss. One can clearly see that Quantic Dream has put a *lot* of effort on this game. Overall, it's a 10/10 game.....for Play Station. - The PC port sucks. Frequent lags and glitches. You need to downgrade to an older Nvidia driver and do a lot of optimisations to run the game decently at 40fps. - The camera angles is horrible. They tried emulating a movie feel, and made it harder to control the camera and where the character goes. I struggled 100s of times to get my character to move to a certain location.- QTE (Quick Time Events) are horrible. My clicks sometimes don't get recognised and caused so much frustration as I had to quit the game and come back to revert my mistake and not get a bad ending. QTEs are NOT meant for keyboard and mouse.Save yourself frustration and get a controller. Somehow I finished the game (with the good ending, no least) without a controller. But I def do not recommend doing the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game. However, I do not recommend that you buy it for the PC. If you happen to have a PS4 lying around. Get It! I originally played the game on PS4 when it first came out. But like some of you here, I wanted to stretch this games legs with my PC; 3440x1440 ultra wide, ultra settings, no motion blur @ 100+ FPS etc. Unfortunately, you're not going to get any of that.This game is very poorly optimized. If you get it to run longer than 20 minutes, you'll be stuck playing it locked at 30 or 60 FPS in 16x9 aspect ratio.Now, you can use the mod above to allow the game to be stretched past 16x9 . However, this mod will tank your already low FPS, so I don't really recommend this mod.  As for the game itself. Detroit: Become Human is a great game. A great story with a great Cyberpunk esque setting, it has great characters and decent QTE game play. It's a 7-10+ hour story with multiple routes and moral decisions which gives this game good replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, Detroit: Become Human is a AVG/GAL like game, or an "interactive movie", which means it doesn't have the more popular gameplay elements like "combat, leveling etc". Instead, it provides a superb storytelling and well-scripted multiple endings that based on the player's choices during the whole game. The whole gameplay mechanism of this game is built by multiple-choices during dialog / events, relationship with the characters and the objects / evidences the player found during the limited explorations. Each of these things will be accumulated during the game in an organic way, which leads to a kind of "butterfly effect" to the faith of the main characters. There are multiple stories lines, and no matter they are "bad endings" or "good endings", they are all very well-executed. The replayability is great.The graphics is excellent, especially the rendering of the main characters. Facial animation, skin textures, eyes and lip sync are all realistic and which have a great contribution to the story telling as the player can actually get the feelings of the characters. Though the world renders a beautiful near-future Detroit, it seems a bit too "clean". So the world looks very futuristic but not realistic enough (although you can argue that the androids do their job well and keep everything tidy). Another downside of the graphics is the rendering of the side characters. Because the main characters are made so perfect, the side characters feel a bit fake as lack of motion capture and facial details. But it's understandable that the computational resources are mainly used on the main characters so that the game can run with a good framerate.Acting and music are well done. The game actually used experienced actors for facial and motion captures for the characters makes the performance smooth and trustworthy. Each main character has their unique vibe of music to match their stories. Sometimes the music will be too weak so the player is likely to miss them, but most of the time the music is on the right spot and creates some intensive emotional moment, in additional to the great acting.All in all, the game is highly recommended to whom wants to enjoy a good interactive story.

The control method is limp and frustrating when in fact it could be straightforward. Movement and actions could, in fact, be very simple. But no. Is this part of the 'difficulty'? Offcourse, the staple in Quantic Dream games - branching storylines, hard choices and multiple outcomes makes it a great “choose-your-own-adventure” experience. I’m definitely giving it a thumbs up, because overall -  it’s an impressive and enjoyable game. The story didn’t really click with me. _childDocuments_.review: Detroit Become Human is an emotionally moving narrative game. The character development, various pathways influenced by decisions and breathtaking graphics all contribute to what makes this game a masterpiece. _childDocuments_.review: It's obvious a lot of time, thought, and hard work went into the making of this game.  Several elements make for an incredibly immersive and unforgettable experience which I highly recommend.The graphics are astounding.  The nuanced details of each character's face are stunning.  Individual eyelash hairs, pores, scars and beauty marks, laugh lines, hair texture-- the careful consideration and creativity put into the design of each character testifies to their individuality and uniqueness.  Nothing was overlooked in the graphics department.Acting: The voice acting was amazing, and included celebrity actors such as Clancy Brown, Jesse Williams, and Amelia Rose Blaire. Can we talk about  the time and effort put into motion and performance capture? Everything from speaking to subtle facial expressions to parkour to fighting can be credited to full performance capture.  This really allowed me to become part of the story and feel as if I was really there alongside the characters, and even imagine a world in which androids and humans co-existed.Choice and Consequence: I love how the player is given almost complete, if not total control over every aspect of the game.  Every choice shapes your character's personality and their relationships, the course of events, and ultimately, the entire game.  According to the Internet, there are 85 different endings/outcomes between the three protagonists Markus, Connor, and Kara.  The flowchart can be implemented to show the consequences of each choice, how all choices are linked throughout the chapter, and the number of alternative choices and consequences. They can also help you keep track of different choices made throughout the game if you decide to go back and replay each chapter. These things take replayability to a new level.A quick sidenote: I know some people might find the completion of tedious tasks (e.g., opening the lid to a garbage bin, setting a laundry basket on the dryer, etc.) or having to complete every single step of certain actions annoying, but I believe it made for a more immersive experience and helps one get to know the character they're playing better.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: "Detroit: Become Human" is a captivating journey through a world where the line between man and machine is blurred, and every choice you make shapes the outcome of the story. If you're a fan of narrative-driven games, this one is an absolute must-play.The emphasis on story is where "Detroit: Become Human" truly shines. From the very first scene to the final credits, you're pulled into a thought-provoking narrative filled with twists, turns, and moral dilemmas. Every decision you make has consequences, leading to multiple branching paths and endings that keep you coming back for more.But it's not just the story that's impressive – the game's visuals and performances are top-notch as well. The lifelike characters and stunning environments make you feel like you're stepping into a futuristic dystopia, while the voice acting brings each character to life in a way that's truly captivating.Sure, there are moments where the gameplay may feel a bit more like interactive storytelling than traditional gaming, but that's part of what makes "Detroit: Become Human" so unique and engaging.Overall, if you're looking for a game with a strong emphasis on story, memorable characters, and thought-provoking themes, "Detroit: Become Human" comes highly recommended. It's a journey you won't soon forget, earning a solid 8/10 in my book. So dive in, make your choices, and see where the story takes you.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not emotionally ready for this game, but i regret nothing.  (Some possible spoilers herein).  As Markus I initially did everything i could to be pacifist and try to show the humans we were alive and just wanted our freedom, but i had to shoot the guy who made a break for it in the Broadcast room or he was going to set off the alarm and possibly get us all killed. (I played on the harder version for reference).  Eventually it didnt matter, the human media kept twisting everything to make us look like murderous malfunctioning machines instead of beings capable of love and empathy.  "So anyways i started blasting"   Basically yeah, things turned south real quick.  You want to F around and find out?  Lets do it.  I lead my people to victory at a terrible cost, Josh died in my arms, North (my love and companion) died on the battlefield, and i survived to a bittersweet victory.  Alone, but with hope for my people.  Kara's story made me cry on like three seperate occasions, and im a grown a** man. (I dont want to get flagged for cursing.)  I totally didnt see Alice being an android coming, and it didnt bother me the least.  Why would i stop loving her because she mistakenly thought she was a real little girl.  It kinda bugged me how Luther kept trying to tell me but I was always brushing him off. Luther was one of my favorite characters, having a big strong gentle black man to help me raise Alice really made this portion of the game so heartwarming and memorable. Only weird thing is i completely blanked on Luthers death, I remember we were driving for Canada and I think my game crashed or i got slightly distracted and next thing i know Luther was dead!  Something weird happened there for sure.  I dont know if i made the right choice in the end, when we were in the android concentration camp i got seperated from Alice and chose to hide in the back of the body dump truck to survive.  I regret not going back to reassure Alice but idk if that would have led to any better of an ending.  Probably broke her little heart but my ending showed Kara alive and probably going to look for Alice who i believe survived also since i liberated the camps as Markus.Connor and Hank was the bromance i always wanted.  I laughed so much at their relationship.  I won Franks friendship and saved his life letting the deviant get away.  Amanda was NOT HAPPY, but screw her she was a cold bish and using me from the start obviously.  I noticed any time i said anything remotely empathetic her trust of me dropped so i knew what her deal was from the jump.  She tried to use me to assassinate Markus but i had a feeling about the touch stone monument things in her area from the very beginning i knew there was something to them and knew exactly where to go once she tried to get in my backdoor (hold up..).  I resisted her hack and me and Markus lived on as friends with Hank.  Overall i was happy with my outcome, there were a few regrets.  I wish Luther could have survived,  I wish North (yes she was a little violent but her backstory justified it in my eye, sex slave as she was.)  had survived so Markus wasnt alone in the new world.  But other than that, yeah I feel like I played the game how i wanted and felt good about most of my actions and how it ended.This game was one of my favorite gaming experiences of all time, im going to recommend it to anyone i think might find it intriguing, and I want my girlfriend to play it and see how she handles the situations!  Some time in the future, maybe in a year or two ill bust this one out again and do things differently and see how my world view and personal feelings change my actions.  Much love, peace on Earth.  Take care of eachother.  1

_childDocuments_.review: Even a few years after its original release, Detroit Become Human remains one of the absolute best games in this genre. Unlike other games where supposedly choices matter, here your decisions really have an impact and allow for completely different stories. There are tons of possibilities and yet every timeline is interesting and well thought-out. The story increases its pace and stakes at a rhythm that doesn't feel rushed nor sluggish, which keeps you engaged and makes you actually care about the characters you play, because you were exposed to their background and motivations in a believable way. And to make it even better, the graphics are astonishing, you feel fully immersed in the world that the game portrays. Liberty for Androids!

_childDocuments_.review: By far one of the greatest games I've played. A gripping storyline, choices that matter and above all, characters that you feel invested in. Worth full price AND more. The game length might not be amazingly long (Took me 9 hours) but for the level of detail and story you get, it's 100% worth it. Keep in mind that the 9 hours is one single playthrough of the game, there are other pathways of the story you can take, so theoretically you can play the game again and get an entirely different outcome/choices along the way. My one and only gripe with the game is just in relation to sometimes not knowing exactly what your character is going to say, because you think one thing but then the character says something else based on that single word choice you selected through, which can lead to some unintentional results.Besides that, pretty much everything is an absolute masterpiece.

I encourage anyone to pick this game up, and to play it with kindness and peace as a guiding principal when making decision, as I feel that gave me the best experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended at deep discount (75%+).+ Beautiful graphics, animation, level of detail+ Great sound design+ Incredible soundtrack+ Detective missions are fun+ Tense, fun action sequences in the early game- Entire game is a series of "hidden object" point-and-click / timed QTEs (Could be a positive for some people)- Plot and characters are boring- Dialog and plot points are cringe-inducing, forced tropes- Final act drags on too long with way too many "decisions"- Retrying chapters does NOT allow skipping cutscenes or dialog, who has time or patience for that?The opening mission of this game gripped me with excitement, but by the end of the game I was bored and wanted it to end. I made a poor in-game decision right before the final act and I just couldn't make myself go back and replay the chapter to correct it. This led me into a spiraling sequence of crappier decisions, and I stopped caring about the outcome after that.If the game had a more interesting plot and gave us the ability to replay chapters more easily, I'd have enjoyed it a lot more and likely replayed it multiple times to see all the endings.Worth playing for the cinematic presentation and the detective missions. Don't expect much from the plot or characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: Thanks to Tamaster for writing the guide about solving the driver issue for Nvidia. Using driver version 446.14 fixed everything. Now I am able to play the game again. So now I can recommend it again. Edit: I played the game without an issue for almost 15 hours when I purchased it. Literally no crash, no lag, nothing. Here my PC specs:CPU: i5 7300HQ 2.5 GHzRAM: 16 GBSSD: ADATA SX8200PNP 512GBGPU: GTX 1050 2GBOriginal Review:This is one of the best games ever. There is no doubt. But for PC it seems it has a lot of issues. That is why I don't recommend it.The game is unstable, when I purchased it, I played it without any problem. Then, suddenly I started getting Vulkan support error, I have tried every possible solution on the internet it did not work. I do not know how many times I uninstall and reinstall not only the Nvidia driver but the intel graphics as well. I do not know what I did exactly but it stopped giving Vulkan error. But then while opening the game I got a black screen and the game did not start. I learned that it is because of the full screen, so I changed the windowinfo.json and the game started. However, earlier the game was running 60fps on medium settings and now it is set as low and when tried to change anything, it gives me your system is not good enough error, even it warns me when I try to make the game full screen in the settings. Anyways I wanted to keep playing even it is in window mode. However, when I started the chapter I got a blue screen, then I tried again, this time I got nothing, the game crashed and I gave up. I am not gonna request a refund because when I played this game on PS, I said this game can make me buy PS, so it is worth it. However, they need to fix whatever the issue is.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. The game makes you care about the main characters, because you are the one who shapes them and their story. The game offers so many branches and choices to the point you will likely never get the same story without at least a couple deviations (pun intended), even if you try. The story is decently long, even for a single branch, and offers plenty of content and replayability due to the plethora of impactful choices that alter the story in a tangible way. On top of it, the game has the best menu I have ever had the pleasure to interact with, with its own "AI" that interacts with you based on your choices and the way you play the game, has its own story and will likely make you care enough about it as if it was another character in the story itself. Have played it multiple times on a console and now also on Steam. Highly recommended, especially on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful games ever, beautiful visuals and the music is emotional, the actors did incredible as well, and the challenge of the game really adds to the emotional experience because of how drastic the choices and changes are. I also love the message and examples of inequality, what that looks like, how that makes those in the unfair position feel; the humans argued the robots couldn't feel emotion, but giving a machine irrational instructions on a constant basis will damage a machines ability to function just as it would any human. There lies my greatest admiration in this game, the concept of this game can be applied to human psychology and can be compared to unfair situations we've seen in our history globally, and to the in-equal struggles we see today. This game is a beautiful messenger, educator, the underlying statement can apply much farther than the story. I will say for others who have experience childhood trauma, abuse and neglect, stay mentally careful and give yourself slack playing though the beginning of Alice and Kara's story.. I personally did struggle a lot with this part of the game because of how immersive the experience of Alice's abuse was, and I do need to warn that will absolutely hit close to home for some people. Keep tissues and water close by, and my advice would be to pause and exit the game even if it means losing some progress when it gets to be too deep or difficult to watch and work through; I had to and I did lose some progress but it was worth getting through because Kara and Alice have an incredible significance to the larger picture in the story. And it also does offer some relief being able to have Kara be the family Alice needed. Anyway, I would absolutely recommend this game, I would warn not to give this game to children there are adult themes and the message is far too complicated for a child but for adults I think there really is something that everyone can get from this game. AND if you don't want to play it, or want to watch it before trying, there are gameplays on Youtube so you could even just watch it like a TV show (a complete play-through video is on average 8 hours long). But that's my thoughts, to whoever may be reading I hope you enjoy the game as well :)

_childDocuments_.review: Many games use the "choices matter" tag, giving you an illusion of actually changing the outcome.  Telltale games were guilty of this every time.  Sure you made some choices that felt impacting, but in the end there was always 1 ending you were being lead towards.That's why I was really impressed with D:BH, because your choices will have a huge affect on the story and possible endings.  The incredible thing about DBH is that after completing each chapter you get to see the flowchart of branching decisions and which choices you made.   This will drive 100% completion gamers crazy.   However I can't stress this next point enough - To really enjoy and immerse yourself into the story DO NOT replay chapters searching for the best outcome.  Just make your choices, owning the results and make the story your own.  Replay chapters only after completing the game.The story and performances in DBH are top quality.  It's essentially an interactive movie.  And a damn good one at that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really outstanding game; the story is good even if a bit like other 'androids become self aware' stories. It manages to intertwine three separate stories into a cohesive full; it's very, very well done. Graphically the game is ridiculously detailed I don't even want to think about how much work went into making this thing from the graphics, the acting, the motion capture, etc. its stellar.As a game, like others have said it's pretty light; its not on rails as there is a pretty decent amount of branching going on and I'm sure the idea is to replay the game a few times. You can at least chapter select and try different things if your interested. However the game does boil down to quick time events and if you don't like that or aren't quick with them things can go awry. I'm not a fan of them but they DO work very well in the tense sequences. The presentation, story and experience are well worth the time even if this isn't normally your kind of game as it isn't mine.This game excels at creating tension; this game has some incredibly intense sequences and it starts extremely intense; it's awesome. Some of these sequences are clearly designed to make anyone with a soul uncomfortable; if these don't affect you, you probably need to check yourself in somewhere and work through that.This game is the only redeeming thing to be associated with the city of Detroit in years and it was created in France hah.

_childDocuments_.review: Within a few hours of starting to play, Detroit: Become Human had moved to the short list of my all time favorite games. It is an absolute masterpiece.  Although the ethical questions surrounding robots and sentience have been covered in many books and movies, this game puts a new spin on the topic with a cast of characters that you will fall in love with. I laughed, I cried, and I celebrated with Markus, Kara, and Connor. The game is brilliantly constructed with a compelling story, a beautiful sound track, and excellent acting (voice-overs and motion capture). The plot twists and turns with a surprising number of outcomes based on the decisions you make.  It is a game where choices really do matter.Completionists (100% Steam Achievements or execution of all story lines) should plan on playing the entire game through twice, at a minimum. In addition, you will need to replay specific segments of the game for mutually exclusive achievements.  There is a chapter/checkpoint option that lets you repeat sections with or without impacting your current progress. While this is a great feature to undo mistakes or pick up mutually-exclusive achievements, you will still find yourself doing a lot of replay. I did not see this as a hardship, as it was so interesting the watch the plot proceed through different branches.I played on 'Story' mode which simplifies the QTEs and provides some grace on timed sections. For me, this made the game more enjoyable and did not detract from the experience in any way.I can't say enough good things about Detroit: Become Human. Only that it is a 'must play' for those who enjoy narrative games with a bit of QTE action thrown in.PS - Thank you again to my generous Steam friend who gifted this game to me!

After playing through once with the ideal endings, it's kind of fun to go back and go for the messy endings. Besides the obvious message they hit you in the face with, I also don't care for the fact the men got the more interesting story lines but Kara is reduced to wanting to care for a child. How sexist and limiting that is, that the main female lead is reduced to motherhood as that must be the only thing a woman wants, even a plastic one. And if Marcus can't complete his story, North can't truly take over.

If you however wish to explore the deeper themes this game tries very hard to look it offers (mainly the conflict of what makes one a human,) you'll spend your time better watching the first season of Westworld. Otherwise, this game is great. Incredible actors, it looks beautiful, and it's cool sometimes in life to not take things too seriously. So go on, play it. And also watch Westworld while we're talking about it, it's a really good show.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tremendous. I was so involved in playing it. I played several of the chapters over to get the best possible ending I wanted. The characters are so real and their stories so involving. I was emotionally vested in each character. The graphics were super realistic. The story-lines were enveloping. The only negative I have to say about the game was occasionally it would freeze and kick me out. I had to reload and play from a checkpoint or start a chapter all over again. The really frustrating chapter was at the end when it kept freezing and I had to start the chapter over several times. I finally played the game in lower resolution and windowed mode. That seemed to help and get me past the hump in the game. I finished the game where all main characters are alive. To me, that is always a happy ending. I look forward to more games like this one. I liked the game so much that I bought two of the same developer's other games...Heavy Rain and Two Souls. I have been playing those games and thoroughly enjoying them, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Good but flawed. Better than a walking simulator.The only other Quantic game I have played was Indigo Prophecy in like... the early 2000s or whenever it was out on PC.This is the same type of game which was a nice change of pace after decades of playing FPS, RPGs, etc.Visually it is pretty awesome. There isn't a ton of interactivity or gameplay but the reason to play this game is for the story. I despise walking sims and I would take this style of game any day. Why? The story. The gameplay is talking to people and doing really basic actions like opening a door, looking at something etc. Their choice for input is extremely odd. You'll move your mouse in goofy directions which could have been more immersive but they did these weird half circles and up/half circle movements for a lot of actions which is just weird.I played the demo and it convinced me to buy the game. Honestly, the demo level is THE BEST level of the entire game. I got it on sale and would have felt a bit ripped off if not. The demo for me was just awesome. While the story is good (it is not amazing) the rest of the game just doesn't match that level.The main gripe I have is with dialogue which is a common issue in adventure games. You'll be given say 3 options of 1 word each: -Honest-Sincere-AngerAnd you'll choose one thinking the dialogue will go a certain way, only to have your character say something totally different. It's really annoying when you want to CHOOSE your path but the option is so vague you are guessing what will actually occur. Give me the full option so I know what my choice actually is.Fun game, good change of pace and it has a decent story that kept me engaged and was quite moving in areas. If Qunatic could tighten up the dialogue interaction and implement a bit more gameplay they'd have a winning formula.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1. Connor RK800 has a good story line. You are a hostage negotiator and helping to solve murders. I wished the whole game was like this because I would then recommend this game.2. Good graphicsCons:1. Kara AX400 plays the role of a nanny. She has to clean the house and take care of a girl. I don't know a single person that likes doing this work. However, it may be a good way to train your kids to do chores and these chores they may actually do because it is a "game".2. Markus RK200 take care of a disabled artist in a wheelchair. The first mission is you have to pick up paint. I have enough "chores" to do in real live. Why would anyone want to do a "chore" on a video game? 3. The unlocked stories and missing stories at the end is also very confusing. It is really hard to tell what you missed, so you can go back and do it at another time.4. The controls take some time to get used to. You have to click your mouse and move it in a certain direction to interact. It is very picky. It may require you to do it multiple times to complete one action.I would not recommend the game for the current price tag. If you still want the game then I would not pick it up until its 10 dollars or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Inspired by the short called “Kara”, Detroit is a neo-noir thriller set in the near-future city of Detroit. Androids, who look exactly like human beings, have replaced humans in most tasks: they are workers, babysitters, gardeners, nurses, teachers, clerks. detailed_description: Navigate an ocean of crime and corruption to balance the bloody ecosystem of Necromunda as a merciless hired gun. The money’s good, the dog’s loyal, and the gun’s reliable – but can you survive the hunt? Necromunda: Hired Gun is an indie fast-paced, violent, and thrilling FPS set in the darkest reaches of Warhammer 40,000’s most infamous hive city. For the right price, eliminate the most notorious gangers and mutants. Your armory is a sprawling arsenal. Your body is enhanced with a dozen customizable augments to run on walls and leap over chasms. Your cyber-mastiff will sniff out and kill enemies for you, while your grappling hook allows quick, agile traversal of the massive environments. _childDocuments_.review: I have a really mixed first impression of . The gameplay feels very good. Developers didn't lie when they called the game fast-paced, action-packed, or smth like that. Your character is very mobile with all those dashes, double jumps, and wall running. And it feels good to shoot things as well, which is the most important. You know, not every FPS game actually delivers decent gunfights. For me, Necromunda does. And, of course, you have a doggy! It bites things for you! Literally, the first thing you're allowed to do in the game is to pet your good boy.And here comes a "but". Despite the gameplay being decent, everything around it is far from okay. Interface came straight from free to play mobile game with ugly fonts and inconvenient menus. While you're on a mission, you don't have a map, even a mini-map, even a bloody compass. Only floating marks in the air showing distance to your target. Also, you're earning loot throughout the mission, but you don't have any kind of inventory to check it out, only a summary screen with all your credits and stuff earned after the mission is complete. And there is also an instakill button, some kind of glory kills from DOOM. Still, you can use it on every simple enemy right away, without damaging them to a certain state. It also makes the player invulnerable during the animation, which is kind of a legal cheat. And I also experience fps drops out of nowhere from time to time. It doesn't happen often, but it sometimes spoils the feel of fluid combat, especially when you have to take pretty precise shots. And I've also had several crashes to the desktop, which is quite annoying. But I believe some of the issues described previously will be somehow fixed or reworked. The graphics are okay. Yeah, it's hard to call it beautiful in 2021, but it definitely has its own style, and you also have to remember that budget was not even close to DOOM Eternal or Far Cry. I can see that devs had put a lot of love for the WH40k universe in their game with all those authentic environments and characters and sound and so on, and shooting stuff is also made great. But from the technical side, Necromunda is far from polished and needs some fixes and patches.
