Steam really needs a "meh" between up and down votes. This game is $40 bucks and that's just to much for such little polish. The sense of scale is there, the guns, the premise. 10/10 stuff but this issue absolutely not.I've seen some reviews say that the sound design is great and that the game has great atmosphere. It would have great atmosphere with better mixing. Seriously I've never seen such bad mixing. Dialogue is the worst. Actors sound like they are using different microphones. I shouldn't notice that. Muffled audio and spatially things don't sound correct. In fact most of the time aside from phantom noise or incorrectly placed sounds many things just sound like you have ear plugs in. Like you character has some wax shoved in there. This sound stuff is a known issue but seriously it's horrendous. I never thought I'd refund a game for bad audio but wow this is rough. I really want it to improve but I just can't throw my money at $40 games like that and be okay with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation here reminds me on that cyberpunk motto "high tech low life". Except it's less of cyberpunk here and more of heavy grunge. Not only do people wear cyberarms like it's going out of style, those cyberarms look like they've been forged in the 19th century. It does remind me on the Rage series of games, except it's not the apocalypse which rendered the world an unlivable hellhole, but humans himself built it this way. And build they did! Huge architecture for the sake of huge architecuture, for the sake of showing off some faint greatness it does look good! This game got I think what's my favorite train level in gaming (yet), this gargantuan monstrosity running on red-hot gears tall as a house, yeah, that's a train all right! Same goes for the guns. The starter pistol taking up roughly half of the screen really humbles what's usually called a handcannon, even more so with it not exactly removing a head from it's shoulders upon one headshot, rather removing the head from existence, replacing it with blood splats.Gunplay is visceral all right. They ooze powerful badassery from every shot, including but not limited to the AR shot turning that goon into some bloody mist with legs. Despite the power, the guns reward trigger &discipline &recoil control nger more than they reward scoping. Do I need a curator list for FPS with good gunplay? If I had one, this game would go there. Where was I? Right, gunplay. Or combat in general. Aside from the hometown which skims the line between a derelict cathedral and an industrial hellhole, you'll spend most of your time shooting. There is a bit of platforming/parcouring, but it's combat which counts.Boy does it count! Gratiutous gore is always a boon in an FPS, but that's just the icing on the combat cake. The cake itself is built on mobility, a ton of combat takes place in extensive arenas with goons peppering you from afar as well es charging you and you jumping around the arena I guess you can play it by carefully crawling forward, but why would you wanna do that? Certainly not to conserve your health which is in short supply and which you replenish by a) shooting back once shot and b) critical hits which still boils down to shooting. In other words, shooting is your main means of staying alive. Pulling back to catch a breath may help you, the player, to assess the situation but the player character won't benefit. In case that's not clear by now, I love combat in this game! I love action games facilitating an agressive forward aproach and I'll gladly bash action games for forcing me into a devensive counter-reactory position.Once in a while, you'll get a boss. Those ain't too great, it's mostly a normal enemy with a crapshit♥♥♥♥ton of hitpoints you'll get to windle down. To make things worse, you may get an infinite mob to support that bullet sponge. This mob helps out replenishing ammo, but I really wish they'd done things differently. Same goes for side-missions. Look, it's not like I hate side-quests. Sure, I'll gladly explain how open-world games littering the map with 2dos suck, but that's because I don't enjoy combing the neighborhood for some hidden feather. I don't mind side-missions being procedurally generated in slices of campaign maps either. I don't even mind them perpetually spawning goons for me to deal with (I love exploding goons into bloody chunks with my  bolter), I do mind them perpetually spawning bullet sponges though. I want a battle of skill, not a battle of attrition, y'know?I'm glad to inform you that's what the game provides in the campaign missions. That, and the bolter appeared in a recent dream of mine, this is easily among the most fun automatic weapons in FPS games I've ever known.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is criminally overpriced for what it offers. This is essentially EYE: Divine Cybermancy, but way more janky somehow. It's also trying to be like Doom Eternal, but feels like it was made with  parts. Nothing in this game feels good, the sounds are screwed and glitching over each other often already. The movement is clunky and has multiple movement options bound to single keys, which can't be rebound in the options either. The shooting doesn't have any impact whatsoever, neither does getting hit by enemies. Topping everything off, it completely locked up and went fully unresponsive within an hour of play.Maybe if it was around $20 or something I'd be able to forgive a little bit of this, but it's 2/3 the price of a AAA game and it's already been out for around 3 months in it's current state. There are far too many glaring issues to look past and Warhammer fans don't deserve this mess, especially at it's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Janky budget doom.Sound design is spotty at best, with whole sections of cutscenes and levels that should have great ambient sound but all you can hear are gunshots and babysoft footsteps. Soundtrack itself slaps, though. The particle effects are just a bit over the top, meaning you'll lose the level, your targets, anything you're trying to see once the bullets start flying. Level design is just... weird. There's little to no flow, rhyme, or reason to how the levels are laid out. With a movement system as robust as Necromunda, you'd think the level design would compliment it instead of hindering it. Story leaves a lot to be desired, and progress is jarringly cut off by awkward menu screens.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is without a doubt the best Warhammer 40k fps that's ever been released. Now, the bar for that has never been particularly high. Its worth pointing out. The developer, Streumon, has the look and feel of 40k locked down tight. Every single one of the 13 levels is dripping with the skulls, chains, spikes, studs, bolts, rivets, blood and oil that I think of when I think of 40k, but strained through a different filter. A distinctly Necromundan one. And even, dare I say, a civilian one? What it is: A fast paced combo of Metro, Cyberpunk, Doom 2016 & Eye: Divine Cybermancy (which isn't a bad thing at all). You play a nameless Hired Gun, one of millions on Necromunda. The difference between you and them? Your cerebral implant which grants you (heretical) 100% not magic, a sturdy set of bionics giving you well above average agility and strength, and an ever loyal Necromundan Mastiff (complete with is own upgrade tree).  Story: Is really just window dressing to some great level design and awesome combat. It certainly isnt horrible, I followed what was going on.... mostly. But Seeing as Necromunda is THE most fleshed out setting in 40k by a wide margin, It could have dug deeper and delivered something memorable. What is presented is a resoundingly 'meh' job gone bad-♥♥♥-revenge tale that I feel like I could read from Black Library for 20 bucks. Graphics: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous. Full stop. Streumon Studios must have someone who lived in Hive Primus on staff. It feels like the environments are ripped straight out a home movie some poor prole took on his last day. Its not the most beautiful game of 2021. It wont win any awards in this regards, but the lighting, choices of textures, plethora of particle effects and myriad small environmental details coalesce into something more. For a 40k fan its literal cocaine. For a laymen, its still very, very pretty. Sound: The music spans several different genres. Synth, country, heavy metal, straight rock and roll. Its not the orchestral bombast that 40k fans may have come to expect. But this isn't set on the gargantuan battlezones of the Dark Millennium where that would fit. The tracks that play during combat are blood pumpers, regardless of genre. The more lowkey tracks tend to play during lulls in the action, where the game gives you a bit of room to explore its (really quite large) environs. Its also worth saying its all REALLY GOOD.  So much so I would happily buy a soundtrack if it were available. These slap. In other areas, its a bit more hit or miss. The voice acting, for instance, is really quite good! Everyone sounds suitably gravely, angry, untrustworthy or sick. And the lines are delivered a LOT better than some other games of a similar AA sort of quality. The weapons all go bang bang or boop boop or dakkadakkadakkadakka with respectable oomph. Including the Bolter. For all of you who were worried, its not quite Fire Warrior levels of "I have a MACK truck and it shoots semi auto RPG's" but its leaps and bounds better than it was in the trailers for the game. Gameplay: The real meat and potatoes of Hired Gun is.... well, gunplay. Akin to Doom 2016 in its pace, and Dishonoured or Eye in its inclusion of (for all intents and purposes) magic powers. The game wants to you move. Move, and shoot. Never stop. The Emp-rah forbid you ever STOP shooting and moving. You COULD play Hired Gun as a standard, boots on the floor shooter. This would be the least possible fun.  Early on you get cybernetic implants that open up the possibilities pretty wildly. You wanna double jump across that gap, or grapple line? Will you slow time, teleport into a group of baddies and watch it raining (bits of) men? Or wall run around them with you bionic-aim up, and literally pump bullets into enemies who can hardly touch you? The game gives you a pretty good number of options of keep the various arenas and the guys you shoot at in them interesting.  The Inevitable Jank: Its there, but not in a way that really detracts from the experience. The animations on close combat finishers vary from being serviceable to outright bad. Arms bend in the wrong places, people drop like crash test dummies. Not game breaking by any means, but certainly distracting. Especially so when the only REAL slowdown in combat is when you send yourself into a canned animation for these close combat kills. There are some small things missing sounds. Like flare launchers on a certain level making no noise when they fire off.  THE TLDR: This is a very good game. For anyone who's a 40k or Necromunda fan especially, it would be worth it at full price. For anyone and everyone else its very very worth picking up on sale. You'll be getting a 40k fps that I personally was expecting to be a solid 3/10. However, it surpassed my expectations handily. For those who live and breath 40k its an auto buy. For everyone else, its a really, really, really solid, if slightly jank, FPS which you may just enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game shows a lot of promise; I can't wait until it's out of Beta!. . . It's still in beta, right? I mean, with all the Bethesda-level bugs, lack of balance, bullet sponges, and easily exploitable upgrade systems?At its foundation it has the potential to be a good game, If you want it to be easier on yourself, sit in for a bit of a grind. When you can, run B missions, do Save the Witches, Pertubate, and Ghast. You can practically do pacifist runs with them. Then upgrade your vocal enhancement and grab loot bonuses. You can end up clearing an average of $15,000 from selling loot each run, and before long double your bonuses from the actual job rewards.I don't really notice any benefit from armor or health, though. I still get one-shot by most enemies, but the "dodge" upgrades that make enemies more inaccurate when you use mobility abilities seems to work well enough.Also upgrade the Mastiff to full. On a short cooldown, he's practically immortal and you can hide in a corner while he eats everybody like the good cyborg-boy he is..

_childDocuments_.review: Straight off the bat i want to say the visuals are great, the atmosphere is very 40K. That being said, i have to agree with a large number of people who say its like Doom 2016 with a 40K skin. A lot of run and gun combat with spamming ctrl for a sweet little slide to move a bit faster or hit shift to grapple away from an ambot or grenade. i think i only ever used the wall run in the first level when youre forced to.Story was 'okay' not something ill cherish but ill probably remember from time to time. The sudden 'oh shi- genestealers!' was pretty good i want to get that out there, but once that mission is done and the dialog of your character talking about 'some... things' he saw is over, you can immediately accept side missions to literally rescue genestealers from bright blue laser cages. The guns dont feel quite right to me, especially the iconic bolter, i was expecting the typical yet glorious 'hit soft target and watch it pop' as per the bolters design, but it was a slow firing autocannon-esque experience, on the same level as the heavy stubber. dont get me started on that heavy bolter either, so much screen shake per shot with its pretty low fire rate its pretty jarring to use. Plasma and grav guns are pretty similar in use, one is blue and explodes, one is green and impodes. thats about it.on the topic of screen shake, the takedowns are full of that gods awful 'shaky cam' experience that mean you dont get to indulge in that catharsis of getting up close and personal, its also pretty much the only melee youll ever see beyond the strength ability which sees you running at the turbo speed of an angry Doomguy with your knife. This is a game i wish i got on a sale, was a rather shallow experience for me personally. The dog is a good boy but i found myself not using him at all in combat (even with the tip saying his help would be invaluable) even after upgrading him. At least you can pet him and throw him a chunk of meat, even if hes hard to look at when you upgrade him. By the Emperor is that poor dog hard to look at.

_childDocuments_.review: It's by no means bad, but the only thing that really stands out is it's depiction of under hive, which is excellent. The gameplay seems expansive at first but lacks real depth and polish to it's mechanics, with a lot of weapons and abilities feeling redundant. The enemies don't really push you to use the tools you have at your disposal, mostly providing challenge by simply trying to overwhelm the player, and the optional side missions fail to really extend the game's life due to their repetitive nature. The sound design is great in some areas but seriously lacking in others, like the underwhelming melee sounds, and the game has serious stability problems. It's really only worth your time right now if your a real 40k mark like me. Still, the developers are 40k fans themselves and where dedicated enough to put out a free overhaul for their previous title, Space Hulk Deathwing, so hopefully Hired Gun will get the same treatment in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I played up until chapter 5, did a bunch of the side missions and just stopped having fun. The number of times you get one shot by plasma weapons or a melee attack skyrocketed and it really isn't entertaining to be deleted by a single enemy out of the 20 you're fighting frequently. I really enjoyed the level aesthetics though, the devs did an excellent job with the 40k vibe. Everything from the enemies to the weapons and the levels sell the hive city the game is set in.Enemies aren't really fun to fight though, they either sprint into melee range or sprint to 5 feet from you and shoot. They're often very tanky, having both a energy shield and a physical shield that absorbs all damage. Or a massive pool of health to burn through with a combination of the shields. There's also a elemental damage system with fire, lightning, radiation and toxin damage, but it isn't explained anywhere and enemies don't show you what they're weak against. I have big problems with the looting system, where you only have a few slots for each type of item. Meaning you can only keep 6 of each class of weapon, and 4 armors and 4 trinkets. I'm not sure why the developers would put in so many types of weapons if you can only keep 6. By the 5th story mission I had access to like 12 rifle weapon types, and about 10 pistol types but because weapons come in loot tiers that do more damage, have more accuracy, etc. so many of the things i'd like to try out I left behind for their higher rarity versions. Then you can only choose 3 big weapons and 2 pistols into a mission, plus your permanent starter pistol. The game had a little bit of jank that i'm ok with, including dying to terrain and missions softlocking. But my biggest complaint is with the sound design. Something about the audio isn't mixed right, enemies are almost completely silent when they aren't yelling at you. Gunfire is either extremely punchy or inaudible and enemies more than 20 feet from you don't make noise when they shoot. Maps like the train mission are very loud in some parts, like down near the suspension, but sometimes that area is just a light buzzing sound. Some areas like the forge were virtually silent despite being in a giant manufactorum. Necromunda has a metal soundtrack and its pretty good though.And also what kind of game forces mouse acceleration? I shouldn't have enable a script in a config file to turn it off. Anyway, Necromunda Hired Gun is trying really hard to be a doom clone set in the 40k universe but misses the design considerations and the polish that made Doom and Doom Eternal such pillars in the genre. Tacking on an annoying loot system didn't do it any favors and the story might as well not exist.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game so much, and you should still buy it. It´s gorgeous. The Art direction is unbelievable. This is the most stunning recreation in sound and feel of what it´s like to be in the Warhammer 40K Universe.- Heart pounding sound and graphics.- Insane amount of detail and exploration options- dizzying complexity in the geometry, making me feel almost lost in between the gothic architectury- The look and feel of enemies can be overwhelming, especially the later threats deep in the bowels of the hive.- While many of the weapons are less than impressive, the bolters have to be an absolute favourite of everyone.- Really cool NPC´s, world details, etc., again, you can really dig the 40K feel here.- When combat doesn´t end up in the scenarios described below, it can be very satisfying.Necromunda is an amazing game! That being said, there are some things I have >>>grave<<< issues with, which make me want to quit this game 11 hours in, and I haven´t finished the game yet. The entirety of the issues make me borderline on recommending this game.I just don´t understand so many of its design choices.Gear feels absolutely unimportant:- Haven´t felt any difference between 50 armor and 70 armor - actually the more the game progresses, the more glass cannony you will feel. The game seems to rely mostly on active defenses during slide moves, etc.- Almost zero impact if your weapon is +0 or +3 - that means they will still be good if you favour them, so it´s not necessarily a bad thing.- Bionics health upgrades seem to not matter at all, you still die all the same.Health restoration and combat flow:The game heavily emphasizes close proximity due to how health regeneration works - the closer you are, the more your autosanguinis upgrades will restore your health when you shoot an enemy or kill it with a knife attack. ((Edit: After playing through on medium, this might be inaccurate. Health regeneration seems to occur on any kill, no matter the distance. Just on hard, they´re so much in your face, it´s hard to tell.))However, every fight ends up in visual clutter, with plasmaguns, grenades and psyker abilities lighting up your screen like christmas. Almost every enemy will bumrush you, teleport or jetpack behind or near you, etc. - almost the only way to stay alive in many battles is to abuse the invulnerability frames you get from knifing enemies. With enemies being able to use their grenades in close range, there is also no chance of forcing the enemies to switch their weapons, while if you try using your grenades in close combat... well, let´s say it doesn´t end pretty. So, the result is a headache inducing, knife-kill spamming, weapon switching mess of close combat without any sense of rythm to it. Amusingly, some enemies can burrow to burst out near your location - even if that is the top of a chimney or something like that. So don´t expect any rest or respite.The quick death:While there are many abilities to control the flow of combat, and enemies aren´t overly tanky, in between you will have plenty of enemies in later stages of the game which have an enormous one shot kill ability, instantly breaking your shield and health, no matter how many defensive options you chose in lieu of crit upgrades. So while you´re being bumrushed and try to dodge-slide-wallrun your way out of this mess, you suddenly get trashed, without knowing why (see the visual mess described earlier)The slow death:In areas where you need to solve certain objectives, eventually you´ll run out of shield packs. If you don´t laser focus on finding the objectives, the constantly spawning enemies will eventually drain you. Its inevitable. Once your shields are down, health restoration up to 60 on knifing an enemy will not safe you from the one-shot damage some enemies dish out.Side missions:GOD EMPEROR, ABSOLVE US FROM THIS ABOMINATION.NEVER do any side missions, if you can avoid them. They are just recycled main mission territory with limitless enemy spawns included, so you can´t even explore the terrain, giving you the most of the headache-christmas lighting on screen-invulnerability frame spam experience this game has to offer.Enemy spawns and AI:Enemy spawns are a huge problem in this game in my opinion - I´d prefer it much more if this game had a combat-exploration feel like the Fallout series (New Vegas, 3, 4), since the Warhammer universe is predestined to the relict-dumpster diving game. There should be more varied AI instead of the bumrush-until-its-done style we see here a lot of times - even grenade launcher enemies prefer to give it to you point blank. There is an astounding amount of neglect of will to stay alive in many enemies here.A limited amount of enemies and resources would be a better experience for this game, imho, but I understand the game might just not be for me.Edit: I replaced the game on medium difficulty, and the endless spawns weren´t such a big issue anymore except for one mission specifically - usually the endless spawns are used when the objective is to retreat anyway.Funnily enough, the random loot game gave me another gun in this playthrough, which I never found when I played on hard - basically a black hole launcher. Quite the game changer. Not sure, the random loot system is such a good idea after all, when this one gun constitutes a massive power shift.Also: The "cold dark" mission is a better aliens game than almost all other aliens games themselves.I am looking forward to "Necromunda 2" and by Helmawr, if it doesn´t get made, I´ll be very sad about that and have to pray to the forces of chaos. YOU DON´T WANT THAT, NOW, DO YOU?

_childDocuments_.review: My Legs are OK...Spiritual successor to E.Y.E. I'd argue. It plays like a bad, bad version of Doom with a way better customization front. Though where Doom is swap your loadout on the fly, this is more like cultivate multiple sets of loadouts to best complete the run. It's mostly just run and gun arena with minor "puzzle" elements, Ultimately, it was made by the same company that made E.Y.E.- upgrade your legs and you'll be fine. I feel like there are a bunch of small details that I don't know or understand, but I have a bolter so everything is fine. But it really does feel like E.Y.E.But, for an actual review:It's janky- you ADS and your bullets shoot an inch high, so just don't ADS. You go for an execution/takedown and you'll fly all around during the animate, but don't worry you end up where you started. You try to grapple to a place, well hey, that might be a free wall clip to a chest. Plus it has classic Streum melee since E.Y.E.The RPG element of just upgrade everything when you have money is fantastic- especially since you can just farm the everloving ♥♥♥♥ out of side missions. Just play the story until you got S-Missions unlocked- farm a couple of those- fully upgraded bionics. Frankly I find it incredibly rewarding to fly around with a bolter and cap some fools, so that's what I do.The sound design is trash. Some things that should be quiet are loud- things that should be loud are quiet- sounds mix horribly so you don't always know what you're listening to. They have some work to do in this department- still super satisfying to hear the battle arena music start up- the Doom battle arenas are so much fun; anyone who disagrees is wrong.In terms of varied gameplay, you're not going to get that. They have an easy to navigate story mission replay so you can attempt to get S-Rank in all missions, and then an easy to navigate side mission menu for getting the creds. It's ultimately just a gory farming game, and it's amazing.Well, if you like E.Y.E. it's amazing. If you don't like E.Y.E. you need to get your senses checked because E.Y.E. is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is a singleplayer movement shooter with out of place looter shooter elements.The game is set in the warhammer universe and you play as a bounty hunter collecting bounties.Unfortunately, as cool as this sounds and as cool as the game looks, this is one of the worst singleplayer movement shooters I have ever played.I feel like this was supposed to be a live service game, but then the developers saw how much people hate those,so they converted it to a singleplayer only game but kept the mechanics, which seems to be the reason why there are looter shooter elements.Not only do these feel out of place, there are a lot of small details that make these a chore to deal with.For starters the inventory is annoying to manage, you can only carry 5-6 guns of each type with you, and you cannot swap them during a mission.Well actually that is not true, you can but only when you pick them up by holding the use key, however, there is only 1 weapon slot this can go to, and if it used that weapon will drop out of your inventory.What I meant is that you cannot open your inventory during a mission and swap weapons with the ones you picked up, or even rearrange them...In fact, there is NOTHING in the game that allows you to rearrange your guns, at least not without fighting the games UI...Next, the loot doesn't feel rewarding, why is a blue rarity gun worse than a gray rarity gun of the same type, but double the value?Why would I buy a purple rarity weapon when the blue rarity variant only has 10 less damage for half the price?There are also other items you can find/buy, there are tech upgrades for guns that give them more damage or apply elemental damage,there are lucky charms that increase drop rates on kills, items that increase HP, armor, luck, critical hit chance etc.There is also better armor plating you can find/buy.All these items suffer the same issue as the weapons, they don't feel rewarding, which makes the looter shooter elements feel dull and out of place.There is some cool movement tech but it is clunky, wallrunning snaps your view weirdly and feels uncontrollable,you cannot dash diagonally??? what lol? The grappling hook will sometimes hook to something off screen, and sliding is useless.On top of all of that, enemies have aimbot at all times, whether they hit you or not is based on some RNG stat to each of your movement abilities,this is the most idiotic system I have ever seen in my life, sure why wouldn't I want enemies aim to be RNG so that I can randomly get one shotregardless of how well I'm moving.The combat in this game is somewhat a mixed bag, the movement tech makes it kinda cool, and there are some subtle systems in the game that sort of make this not a cover shooter... if those systems work at least.From what I can tell, sometimes you get some health when you kill an enemy, and sometimes they even drop armor, the problem is they don't always do, and they only drop a very small amount.On top of that, some enemies are annoying bullet sponges, even some of the small enemies are, and like I mentioned above, their aim is complete RNG.There is quite a bit of enemy variety though, which is good, but it's these small details that make the combat tedious and not fun.The game also never properly explains its systems.The game has a weird checkpoint system, you can take up to 3 stims with you in a mission.Buying stims can be done before you start a mission, or at checkpoints.Buying stims before you start a mission is significantly cheaper than during the mission, which I actually kinda like, it forces you to think,do I want to buy stims now at a lower cost or waste more money during the mission?Anyways, these stims give you an instant revive when you die, so you get up to 4 lives during a mission... ok?The problem is not with the fact that they give you that many lives though, the problem is when you completely die.When you do end up dying (and trust me you will considering the RNG enemy aim) you can choose to go back to the last checkpoint, or to go back to the hub area.If you choose to go back to the last checkpoint, you lose everything you just used before dying, stims, medkits, even ammo... so you restart at a checkpoint without the gear you had...You do get 1 stim back, but that's it. So, you could be completely out of ammo and items right before a room with a big fight.There is a dog that you can summon, that will mark enemies for you and attack them, I like this idea, I like dogs, but it doesn't feel useful.The dog can be upgraded, but I didn't bother to play long enough to find out if that makes it better.Yup, this game for whatever reason has a style meter, but it is invisible. This style meter simply decides how much money you get at the end of a mission,there is no score, no leader board, no bragging rights, nothing, so another out of place mechanic...It feels like they simply said "you know what, let's put a dog in the game! hell yea dude that sounds cool!" and slapped it in there.In between mission you'll spend your time in a hub area, this is where you buy/upgrade/sell items and weapons, start missions, talk to characters, buy upgrades etc.This area does look kinda cool, and the characters do not feel as lifeless as you would expect.A nice little detail is that they won't just stand at their shops constantly, they'll sometimes move around in it, but as soon as you approach them they will return.You cannot open the shop until they return to their spot, which is a nice little detail.Now for the bad part, navigating the shop is just tedious. For starters while it does show your inventory, you cannot interact with it.You cannot see any information of what you currently have, you first have to select an item you want to buy, and then you can inspect your own inventory.This is annoying because often you want to compare which gun is better than the one you have, there is a compare button but again you can only do this after selecting a weapon/item to buy.To buy an item/weapon you have to select it and then select a slot in your inventory, either an empty one or one that has an item already.Selecting an occupied slot will DELETE the item from existence... not sell it, no, DELETE, GONE, INTO THE VOID, and you cannot undo this, there is no buy back option.If you want to do this you first go to sell mode, sell the gun to make the slot empty and then buy the gun, why is this not a single action? Like trade-in and then pay up the rest?The hub area also has the mission board, this is where you start a new mission, you can start a main mission, or a side mission.I did not try the side missions because from what I can tell, they are randomly generated, I just wanted to play through the story.The idea of the side missions is to make money to buy and upgrade your gear, but considering that is not worth it like I explained above, why bother?There are abilities in the game, I only tried the shock wave thing, it is useless. There is also an aim bot ability... is this overwatch?Just another clunky mechanic...Necromunda: Hired Gun is a clunky looter movement shooter, that has a lot of mechanics that just do not work together.Normally I play through movement shooter all the way to the end regardless of how bad they are, but this one is too much for me.The looter shooter elements should be removed, enemy aim should not be RNG based, remove the abilities and polish the movement so it does not feel clunky and you would have a great movement shooter.Also buff the dog!If you want to play a great movement shooter that does just that, go play Titanfall 2! The campaign is still playable regardless of the current multiplayer state.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is 'good' for a 40k game but does not hold up; otherwise, it feels half done. Only buy if you are a hardcore 40k fan; otherwise, get it on sale. It has many issues, which I have listed below.Full Review:Necromunda: Hired Gun is an FPS game with lots of issues. The stuttering during gameplay has not been fixed with the first patch. No matter which graphics settings or drivers I try, it doesn't work and have smooth gameplay. My system is a 7700hq/1070, so that should not be an issue. I know with Space Hulk Deathwing, it took the developers nearly two years to fix the issues. It isn't very reassuring to see them here as well, especially at the current MSRP.The gameplay gets the atmosphere of 40k right, but the sounds need a lot of work; I found the bolter sounds to be unsatisfying in particular, and some of the character voices are still quite muffled even after the patch. There are missing sounds when the environment falls around you and could overall have more polish in this area. The Destiny style loot system should not be anywhere near an FPS game, it should be substituted for more RPG elements to upgrade your weapons. I never got my weapons to the highest level, and it seems like a missed opportunity.The campaign is fun once, but there is little replay value. The side missions are forgettable as well.  You only do them to grind and get upgrades, but most take like 10-15 mins to do. Some campaign missions are too short as well and not challenging. I finished this game with 100% achievements in 11 hours. The elements added outside shooting your way through feel half-baked, and the animations are very clunky at best. This is especially true for the dog, which I am sad to see was not used to its full potential. It gets stuck behind walls or does not show up sometimes. Similarly, several missions call for stealth, but there is no reason or option too. There is no stealth meter, and often you get seen, and enemies attack you, but you have no definitive reason why. When you try to talk to characters or interact with items, often it will not work, and you have to back up over and over for it to work to move on to the next mission. I did have one crash to desktop due to this as well. I give this game a 6/10. All in all, I feel unsatisfied with pre-ordering. I am hoping this review can help someone else not make the same mistake. Wait for a sale unless you are ok with a half-finished game.

_childDocuments_.review: This reminds me of Shadow Warrior 2 without the co-op.  A lot of people are comparing this game to Doom 2016 but the combat isn't THAT aggressive or some game called EYE which I've never played.  But to me this feels like Shadow Warrior 2.  There are core campaign missions and side missions you can grind if you want more money or loot items but this isn't the best part of the game for me.Here is where the major split happens.  Are you a Warhammer 40K fan, or not?  If you aren't, this game is a 50/50 split if you like Doom 2016 (a better game) or Shadow Warrior 2 (about the same imo).  If you are a 40K fan and want to finally have a FPS that is MORE (but not completely) accurate to how 40K weapons should feel in a FPS, this game is fantastic.  I am addicted to the bolter and heavy bolter, the las rifle is fun, the stubbers are even satisfying...Now to be fair the rarity of these weapons aren't balanced, you get bolters pretty quickly, but there is a loot system with tiers and while bolters excel at some things the stubbers and shotguns also have a purpose.  Enemies have varying levels of armor and health and bolters will cut through both, but many enemies have less armor and your stubber or las rifle are sufficient because it's harder to hit with the bolters and also ammo comes in smaller amounts.  It's a balance and it's fun until you run out of ammo.

_childDocuments_.review: surprisingly goodits definitely jank but better than i expected. has some of that EYE divine cybermancy charm.my interest in this game is as a retro fps/fast paced movement shooter with unique combat and progression and rogue/rpg-like elements. no particular element is better than the polish of games like ultrakill, titanfall, doom, etc. but as someone who likes these kind of games i think it stands as a worthy title amongst the scene, a nice all round game to have.wayy better than spacehulk deathwing. insanely better. i had to refund that gameedit:game gets dead easy when you use all the gadgets and powers consistently, even on oldschool difficulty. you've really gotta limit yourself to have more fun in this i think. it's good and appreciable for the casual but complex jankiness of your many abilities, but the combat isn't the greatest. you can basically just abuse any one thing and cheese the game with it. that's cool in itself though, you get to be hero, limit yourself and vary it up, but the fun of getting better quickly plateaus, not the greatest feeling/rewarding skill ceiling. still, at about 12 hours i found my personal experience with the game compelling enough to justify the price, especially with it going to a small indie studio where that money matters more. it's interesting, because you can see the beauty of their idea, but also the important things that make retro fps good that they are missing. i think it's actually quite the interesting play as a retro-fps fan and game nerd to see the way experimental trends are combined in attempts like these, where they succeed and fail, what makes a game fun for you. especially in this, cuz you have to play in a way where you consciously don't cheese, because it's so easy to cheese if you don't deliberately vary your ability use and strategy to play more inefficiently but "in character" (fun)as a whole package i admire the game's vision and its execution enough to recommend it, and wish the devs success in actualising their unique creativity, and being given the resources and time that are needed to do so. i think they should consider whether they want to do more casual, accessible games, or more refined polished fps mechanics. it's a fusion of both, but i think they are able to meet much better with more budget, time, and thought into having polished systems and meaningful difficulty settings, that allow a more accessible AND deeper longevity gamethese devs clearly strain at the edges of budget, time, and planning on their projects but they turn out a diamond in the rough, emanating complex but cohesive, beautiful artistic vision and passion. perhaps they don't really care for it, but i think they should focus more on having refined simple foundations before they implement all the cool gadgets. the gameplay feels a little self-conflicting, but the vision feels cohesive and appreciable. it's like they decided all the cool stuff you have, and how to integrate it into a cool story. instead of building strong foundations that expand slowly and connect the whole game. making a movie rather than a shooter. which is cool however if you have the time to really build a good combat system, good movement system. refresh the foundations from the ground up, consider every aspect of the game experience when you design a system. your combat system foundations should also bleed into and become symbiotic with your level design foundations, your enemy behaviour foundations, your lore and storywriting to explain/facilitate the new experience you are trying to deliver. you can create something really unique that takes a gameplay and mechanical-input-skill based approach from the groundup, but as a result is able to create a much more cohesive, accessible and immersive cinematic experience, because there is less jarring disconnections in the foundations. Disconnections can be fun in themselves though. Free play, the opportunity to screw around and not play the same rhythm are important. In an immersive rpg, you don't want to create a game-loop so tightly bound it's comparable to an actual rhythm game. Being able to do human "free play" stuff in the game environment, like idly walking the roads in Skyrim, or hanging around the HQ in this game, being with characters or weighing customisation choices. This sort of lifelike downtime makes playing the game tolerable for a lot longer, because you can have long rest periods at will, without a negative score reinforcement from the game. You're able to match to your rhythm. So basically, I am glad that Hired Gun doesn't push you to play ideally, because if they applied some weird combo system that forced you to vary all your stuff, the game would be a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up honestly. It's just too jank to slap on something like that. Respect for leaving play less restricted. It could be more restricted and refined as it is with surface changes, like shotgun damage behaviour, or the incredibly powerful takedown system, but the deepest realest fix is a fundamental overhaul imo, not slapping more systems on top.It is important not to get lost in foundation work either. You gotta set a bar of ambition for your game. The few basic things it sets out to achieve before the project's core is stable. Make a stable core, grow it, and visualise what the finished good-enough core will look like. Even given a lifetime and money, you will get tempted to keep raising the bar of ambition, until the unfinished project is too frayed to manage coherently, where progress will require revisions that conflict with fundamental foundations and must rewrite them. You will always be able to release another game that raises that bar. Releasing flawed but good enough games that work well with current engines is important and necessary for releasing games that are currently relevant and can get currently relevant feedback. It's how you avoid the Star Citizen problem of never-ending foundational work to be done, resulting in a development cycle so extended that it begins to suffer from the technology used at the start of itself becoming outdated.I think these devs set their bar fairly. I really wish them the best in having the right environment to grow their creativity and actualise it into enjoyable projects.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where you will need some time investments to make it "work". Out of the box you will find the experience lacking, because there are a lot of QoL features lock behind upgrades. Enemies are hard to see with the naked eye, starting guns are downright spray and pray, the dog provided some aid but might as well not existed. They all improve dramatically as you invest time to upgrade them, IF you want to spend the time. there are a lot of upgrades to grind.However there are some things that don't improve, the sound quality feels sub-par, movement feels like you are gliding on oil but without the assurance of footsteps. the VA deliver what they need but the overall experience just isn't...immersive. I appreciate the character selection screen of premade mercs to choose from, and none of them are downright ugly by today's western gaming development standards. They look like they belong in Necromunda.Do I recommend it? Yes during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't want to leave a negative review....I love Warhammer and I love Streum studio's game(I bought this at full price and I own every games from this studio) but this is just not the game so called "Doom meets 40K"...just...No.Where do I start this?First of all, the weapon.All the weapons are just not really fun to use. They are mostly hitscan weapon with only three types of projectile weapons. And all of them are pretty inaccurate even when fully upgraded. Unlike the weapons in Doom, in which you have to switch weapons for different kind of enemies, in Hired Gun, all you have to do is just spray your enemy to death. And the default rifle are actually good at it, so there's no point using other hitscan weapons...It just no real tactics at all.Second, the odd gameplay choice.This is the biggest gripe for me sadly.  Like why can't the player switch the default revolver with other weapons? The combat flow are ruined when you want to switch to your second powerful weapons but instead you switch to your stupid revolver and died.And whats the deal with the healing mechanism? You only heal when you're hit by the enemy? Why's that? Why not do this like Doom? Just drop health packs when the enemy dies! Or like the game Spacemarine, when you can replenish health by executing the stunned enemy! It's true that you can heal yourself by killing the enemy in this game but when most of the enemy can teleport and jump aroud like circus monkeys and the MORE distant between you and your enemy the LESS health you replenish, all it left is FUSTRATION. And the combat flow suffers from that a lot.(Like the only goal in this game is chasing moving health packs all the time.)Also, the melee kill mechanism are just stupid. You can press E to instant kill any enemy without a shield. WTF. It's super silly with all the jack looking melee enemies rush to your postion, standing there just to wait for you to press E on them in line.(You are invincible when melee animation.)Also, some player's abillity are just grabage. Like the knife mode, it's useless when you can still take damge form the enemies.(Why not make it like a super health boost/ temporary infinite ammo/or a stealth mode so you can kill them in a cool way? If I can kill my enemy with a heavy bolter, why use a knife and goose chase the enemy around???)And why all the levels are built on an instant death pit? I CAN even fall to my death in the Hub World!!!! LMAO. The level design are a visual mess and I almost not using the wall run ability cause the level sturcture are so twisted and peppered with obstacles that you don't even sure you can run on it or not, and there's no benefit for doing that, since you can just grapple hook to any places you want.Lastly, the animation.It's so bad that it almost make me laugh. Everything feels janky and rough. The melee animation are a mess and they clip through walls and ground a lot. It takes too long and you will see enemies runing around shooting at you in the background or they just surround you and stand there waiting for their turn to die (if they are melee type enemies). And the cutsenece angles are so messed up like I though my game are going to bugged out.To sum it up, just go play Doom, It's a whole better game. This games does not worth the discount price let alone the full price.(Also, dear developers, It's OK if you don't have the money to do the facial animation, but please make the voice acting sound fun!They all sound bored to their bones! And don't try to use those wierd camera angles to cover it up. It just make things even more confusing.)

_childDocuments_.review: S'alright. If you really want more detail...It's a resoundingly 'okay' game. Isn't going to win any awards, but it'll give you some hours of fun if you like fast paced FPS stuff. The Good: Shootin' stuff is fun. The actual straight up gunplay is a bit floaty, but it's easy to overlook with the mobility of your character (after the first two missions) and the extra non-gun based abilities you unlock. There's enough options in how to approach combat that it's hard to get too bored, even with the small enemy variety. The 40k theme is spot-on. Locations are...well, as varied as they can be considering the narrow setting of the game, and I was surprised how much they managed as far as differentiating each zone as they did. They really got creative with some level locations. The Bad: The protag is a tunnel visioning, overly aggressive moron who is literally only good at killing things. I'd have rather had a silent protag than have to listen to this complete and utter moron react to -anything-. The voice acting for the female protag is...I can't tell if it's a bad performance, or just really poor voice direction. Jericho is the only member of the cast that I didn't wince at once, and his performance may just be that he can work well despite poor direction. Who knows?'Cutscene' animations are...bad. Stiff, awkward, you can tell they covered as many characters mouths as possible so they didn't have to animate them. The animation budget was absolutely barebones. It feels like they really had plans for more third person stuff, considering that you can customize your own appearance to a half decent degree, but it ends up pointless since you only see 'you' in loading screens and the menu really. Also the less said about the UI and weapon/gear management the better. It's really really bad. You get used to it eventually, but there's no excuse for things to be as awkward and unintuitive as they are.The story overall is really whatever. It's small scale, but you're stuck as the least interesting character in the entire thing, who is pretty much jerked around and told what to do/manipulated into what to do by everyone else. As I said, the protag is a complete moron. So. Yeah. I've played worse 40k games, and I have only played a handful of better 40k games. I don't regret the time I spent with it.

_childDocuments_.review: A clunky arcade style fps. Its an unfinished, raw game that reminds me of the Metro series if it was loosely based on 40k instead of post-apocalyptic Russia. The gameplay is a boomer shooter with elements of an MMO shooter like destiny or borderlands, where the same model items/weapons have randomized stats and rarities, which can make it hard to tell whats better without picking it up or taking the time to read the stats. The models and upgrades for individual guns are also not finished, as some parts clip through the model and don't fit right. The story-line of the game is definitely there, although it doesn't feel complete, as some dialogue isn't correct with the text, and the dialogue is also sometimes just random. There is also a lot of reused interactions that would be a lot nicer if there was some variety.Overall it's not a terrible game, but it's far from polished. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is surrounded by beautiful 40k environments and visuals. There won't be a thing you see that's not 40k-touched. That being said it's specifically "hive city underworld" 40k. The game makes an ample explanation of the immediate setting, that you're in the underbelly of a hive city. And that's all you really need to know. There's cybernetics, gangs, guns, and enemies using those guns to kill you.It's also nice because not only are the lore details and scenery well done, they come together to make a great 40k (or rather 40k-adjacent since it's more Necromunda) shooter. I was worried since the same developer/publisher put out Space Hulk: Deathwing and while it had some beautiful environments and details, the game was brought down by mediocre audio/dialogue, mundane story, and unenjoyable gameplay.The last good 40k shooter, although third person, was Space Marine. Necromunda Hired Gun is a welcome addition to this small category.I'll preface this with there's plenty that feels like the developers spent time playtesting and smoothing out to make sure things feel right and play well. But there's still many other glaring things that stand out that seem like maybe they had to deprioritize it in the face of other issues that they wanted to fix before release.Off the top of my head it's mostly that the dog just appears when you summon it, like right out of thin air. Compare it to games like AC Odyssey and KC Deliverance where your horse appears off screen/camera, and actually trying to spot it spawning in is difficult. And honestly I forget the dog exists really, I think a good solution would be occasionally hearing it bark in the environment, like in the pipes or something, and when you summon the dog it runs or jumps out of somewhere near.Another thing is that the majority of characters are wearing some form of facial covering. I imagine this makes sense since the underneath of a towering hive city is probably mostly noxious gasses but it's also noticeable that those  facial coverings don't really have good, if any, lipsyncing with the dialogue. So it seems like they decided to shelve that for later to focus on other priorities too in development (which makes sense and is a bit respectably clever as a programmer myself).It's an enjoyable game and an enjoyable 40k shooter. If you're a fan of 40k, you'll likely enjoy it despite the caveats. If you're a newcomer to 40k, you'll probably still enjoy it for its gunplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a janky mess. Get it for cheap.Aesthetics are nice and its decent game for a warhammer 40k fan, but many of the game mechanics leave it lacking. It's a game centered around loot, but player can't manage their inventory apart from mission launch and end screens or even see the stats of the items unless selling them. Game difficulty is a mess and it is hard game even on easy difficulty with endlessly respawning enemies with hitscan weapons. You can only have 3 medkits to restore your health per a really long level, which gets compensated with Bloodborne-style lifeleech that is active few seconds after youre being hit and Doom-style executions that also restore health. This works well on easy difficulty but is cumbersome mechanic at hardest difficulty thanks to endless enemy spawns, especially on bounty missions. AI is dead, they just charge at you but compensate that with numbers and godly aim from long distance.Worst thing is crashes and bugs. Game has crashed 10+ times for me within first 5 hours, after that I stopped counting. There are also game stopping bugs like clitching inside wall that makes you lose all your progress in a mission. There is no manual save.Get this for cheap if you are warhammer-game nerd, avoid otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs and performance issues aside the core loop is solid and some of the level design is really top notch in evoking the imagery of an industrial underworld. There is some good level design and the levels themselves have a few routes you can take for the most part with your chosen skills,weapons and upgrades allowing you to tailor it to your preferred playstyle. The weapons feel chunky and impactful and the abilities allow you to integrate wall running, grapnel hooking and slow mo... etcThe biggest drawback however is that about halfway through the game stops offering you new things to play with. You stop unlocking guns and the enemy types just repeat. I would really like to see this expanded with dlc adding the final three gangs and some of the old necromunda enemies such as sump crocs, ripperjacks, spiders and the enforcers to name a few. The story is also pretty non-existant but I don't think that ever really mattered, just a few lines of dialogue to justify the set pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: As a 40K and Necromunda fan, I really wanted to like this.The backdrops are lovely, and the item gathering and customization systems are decent. I could probably tolerate the clunky UI, lackluster plot, budget voice acting (1 voice actor per gang), and filler grinding if the base gameplay was good.Unfortunately, for the base gameplay they couldn't decide whether they wanted to focus on FPS, RPG-style activated skills, or parkour-y stunts. They just didn't have the resources to do this combination well, so it resulted in a combination of boring activated skills, lackluster FPS, and wallrunning and sliding that are incentivized but just not that useful or exciting. The AI can spot you at great distance, shoot you with surprising accuracy, and deploy vast numbers of fast-moving enemies.I wish they had just opted for a more basic cover-based FPS, or a 3rd-person action RPG, or something else that they might have had the resources to do decently.At least there's an easy mode so I can get power through the campaign, and see what other lovely scenery they've put together.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A high octane joyride through the under-hive. The story was kinda short, but there's plenty of side content to come back to if you want to try all the weapons, psy-powers and for completionists. I've got nothing but praise for everything minus the knock off glory kill animations and the inability to change loadout in mission from your inventory. The guns have bite and the sound design is great, the levels are beautiful, the enemy variety is good. Absolutely loved it, and hope there's more content down the line after they fix the issues that everyone else seem to be having.

_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM meets Warhammer.  + Takedowns+ Artstyle+ Gameplay+ Story  - Menus- Inventory - Way too much unnecessary stuff  Gameplay is very Quake/Doom like (Double jump, air-dash…) Takedowns are probably the most enjoyable part of the whole game. Characters look very good, unfortunately, there are no customization options only the outfit colors can be changed. Side missions are very generic and repetitive. Way too much stuff going on in this game, grappling wallrunning air dodge… the movement is all you can imagine but does not feel very smooth. Wallrunning in particular was pretty bad in my opinion, the levels are just not made for it, and when you manage to find a straight wall that you can wallrun, there are no enemies around most of the time. Inventory was bad, it took me a while to get used to it. It felt a lot more like a 2010 game. Instead of perfecting a few things, this game tried to fit as many things in it as possible.  5 - 10 hours   Easy  Worth a try  The mastiff becoming a cyber-dog with the upgrades progression was very cool to see, I would like the see same thing on the main character but I understand the difficulties with that.“Side missions” I am not sure what happened there, and why are there so many.All of them are just quick repetitive missions with a simple goal so that you can get some easy money I guess, I did not really feel the need to play them while doing the main missions. Weapons and abilities, another less is more case… You can equip up to 6 different weapons and use X abilities, I would either limit the amount of the weapons since I rarely used more than 3 anyway or at least the abilities. To be honest, I never used most of them just because the button was on the other end of the keyboard + there not being any tutorial for the abilities and pretty much getting all of them at once made it impossible to remember anything. Weapon damage is also all over the place, for some reason the most powerful weapon when it comes to damage is a short variant of a double barrel shotgun, while heavy guns feel completely useless, especially on a higher difficulty. Overall the game felt very  average. Price seems to be raised just because they slapped the Warhammer 40K tag on it. To be honest, I had no idea it is Warhammer 40K related in any way, I did find out after I beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So after ruining Deathwing with Enhanced edition you lot made this, a substandard shooter mixing chaff that are too small amid the over complicated wannabe grunge of the environment and bullet sponge enemies too easy and boring to be fun so you just feel like your time is wasted. I reckon if you taken the entire budget this game had and spent it on removing the poorly conceived suicide bomber enemies from Deathwing Enhanced then it would have been less of a waste of money. I liked deathwing, I don't like this, the parkour is imprecise and in a place so over loaded with "cool" stuff its easy to get stuck or bounce off or lose your flow, your character moves too fast or too slow but it seems to inconsistent as to when the fast or slow happens, the enemies are painfully easy and only get more boring the further you go and the more health they have the more tedious it becomes, the guns are utterly devoid of any kind of impact, the voice acting is embarrassing, the story ♥♥♥♥ felt like a waste of time where in the first scene walking around the hub I'd already resolved to skip any future developments because there was about 1 sentence of useful information to the story between the 4 or so npcs I had to talk to, menu system that could have been better designed by a dog with no eyes both in the purchasing of items and in the set up of your load-out and some of the worst animation I've seen since Agony where punching an enemy feels like I'm wiping snot from their nose or my character is having a literal seizure and just happening to punch enemies in the face somewhere amid the flailing camera.Play cyberpunk of you want to do the fling yourself around a messy environment, play Titanfall 2 if you want to wall run and gun, play GTTOD if you want the wild guns while flinging yourself and want to wall run and gun. This . . . this is just not good and I would have rather thrown my money on a fire.

_childDocuments_.review: ....Honestly, in its current state I really can't suggest this game. There is too many issues, such as the AI being very basic at best and braindead at worst. The gunplay is okay for the most part but requires additional work, and outside of executions and one or two augments, there isn't a melee to speak of. The maps are okay, but they feel bland to me, but I understand there is some issues with trying to create the seedy undergrounds of a manufactorum cross hive city.The characters are kinda bland, including much your own. The dog is a fire and forget that either glitches out and doesn't attack anything or attacks after several prompts, but seems to have no idea on how to jump. Enemy variety is small, with the only major differences coming in the "elites" and "heavies" of the two groups, but otherwise just use stubber vs boltgun weapons, with some plasma mixed in with the former. The story is... there. I can't really say much in regards to it, it just simply is... there.My tl;dr is: Want a dumbed down version of E.Y.E. or Doom, with minimal story and a dog that is vaguely 40k related? Sure. _childDocuments_.review: I won't lie to you - Necromunda: Hired Gun is a janky game. It's got not-so-infrequent bugs, a story that would be run-of-the-mill if it weren't so confusingly told, a muddled interface, and very little variety in its gameplay. I'm recommending it regardless, because of four elements that outshine the total lack of polish. First, the moment-to-moment gunplay is simply FUN. It's fast-paced and frantic, enemies explode in gratifying ways, guns have a satisfactory kick, your various bionic powers are fun to play with, there's just enough variety in hostiles to keep things interesting, and every weapon feels suitably different, even before you start customising them. I played through a number of the secondary missions for cash, and though they're repetitive, I still enjoyed scraping through each one. It's seldom a chore.Second, the visual and sound design is spot-on. The game brings the grimy depths of Necromunda to life in all their horrible diversity. Each level looks substantially different, each character you spend more than a minute interacting with is extremely striking and memorable, and there are dozens of little details that will stick with you and inform the way you imagine this setting even long after you've finished with the game. As a series of places and people to stare at and listen to, this game is a triumph.Third, the aforementioned customisability. I have a real soft spot for games that allow you to futz around in meaningful ways with your weaponry and abilities, and Necromunda: Hired Gun certainly does that. More pressingly, for me, it actually reflects that on the models; the fact that the guns you mod look substantially different depending on your upgrades, and even show whatever trinkets you've hung on them dangling from the barrel in-game, is a huge plus... if a little traumatic when it comes to your mastiff's cybernetics.Fourth, the mastiff. You can, indeed, pet the dog.If you love grim dark sci-fi and fast-paced gunplay, this is definitely worth your time... though perhaps not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: What a weird surprise this game was, never expected for this to drop and be so good. It is mix of a fast pace frantic shooter and what vaguely feels like a board games idea of a weapon system. Instead of just having loot like you would in something like Borderlands or Shadow Warrior 2, you are finding set guns and +1 and +2 versions of them. The ones you get in the beginning are just as good as the ones you find later, only leveled out by the +1 and +2 versions of them. The only downside is, you can't buy the +2 versions of the weapons, so you have to rely on luck that you will pull one from a loot crate. Otherwise, I found the upgrade system really fun and it allowed me to get insanely powerful in the late game. Instead of just bumping your stats, it encourages the in-your-face gameplay that this game really excels at. I would recommend this to any fans of shooters or 40k.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is decent and does well in capturing the sense of scale and atmosphere of Necromunda and the gameplay is generally fun but it's not for everyone. There's a few echoes of EYE, one of the first Streum game in the gameplay, some will like this others not so much. As the gameplay is fast paced, more down to fast reactions movement including making use of the grappling hook for verticality. Those who wanted a more tactical slower paced shooter will likely not get one with it.While I'm ok with it that, two things I don't like are that you can't save progress during a mission (and they are quite long) only between missions. And you can't organize your inventory whenever you want, not even in the home base/operations hub. Instead you can only arrange your inventory just prior to launching to a new mission, which is not good. I also have issue with elements of the controls, such as crouch and slide being bound to the same key, i like to use a side mouse button on my 5 button mouse for dodge/slides but having to crouch with that mouse button, it doesnt feel right. I ended up using shift key for crouch and dodge, which is not ideal but works better.So there are problems,but  to me the pros outweight the cons and I have generally enjoyed fighting my way through the hive city so as a 40k fan I give it a thumb up despite of the problems. Those who are less forgiving, may not get on with it so much, but overall there is fun to be had in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game basically exists for fans of Necromunda. If you're already a fan of the universe and setting, then you're bound to enjoy this game. If not, it's likely a solid pass, unless you want a lesser Doom clone.The highly mobile and Doom style combat is fun and adrenaline-inducing. Gun play and customization is solid and feels great. Story seems decent so far (I'm only a few main missions in), but by no means is it the real focus of the game. It's really all about the combat. Enemy spawning seems odd at times and the knife takedowns are a little janky, but shooting at stuff feels great, even when it's a lore-appropriate bullet sponge like an Ogryn or Ambot. I've been a huge fan of Necromunda for over a decade, and this game allows me to explore the Underhive like I've always wanted. I get to run around in my Escher gear, using Escher weapons and cause chaos for anyone who isn't me. Having a hub to hang out in between missions and pet my doggo is icing on the cake!Overall, give Hired gun a go if you like Necromunda or 40k as a franchise. I grabbed it during this year's summer sale for cheap along with some skins. I felt it was worth it at a reduced price to be sure, but maybe not so much at full price. If you're looking for a more polished game with similar style of gameplay, just get Doom Eternal instead.Hope to see you in the Underhive, sump-scum!
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is an explosive FPS that does a few crucial things fantastically to a point where a lot of other less stellar aspects just don't end up mattering. Firstly it has a large number of giant, incredibly detailed and gorgeous WH 40K environments that are just a joy to fight in. You have a double jump and a grapple hook to help vertical travel so these levels can just be massive which works with the setting. Secondly the weapons are absolutely glorious with each looking, sounding and feeling unique and just ripping through enemies each harder than the last one. The visuals from the look of the weapons to their effects and enemies response to them(usually blowing up in many ways but also just getting hit) are exactly what I like.So yeah between having a blast just using these weapons and moving through gorgeous environments for most of the game the bad parts just aren't anywhere near bad enough for them to slow my roll at all. The animations are iffy and cutscenes are clearly really cheaply done. The side missions are fine for money but are not good extra content. The game crashed on me a bunch of times but only during loads where I didn't actually lose any progress. The Voiceacting is actually decent but the story is very filler. So nothing gamebreaking but janky in places. Overall Hired Guns core is simply so good I had a hell of a time regardless. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a mixed option, I'll give this a mixed one. It's not that bad and provides some fun, but has flaws.Not worth at full price, buy it at a discount. If you didn't like the new DooMs then you will not like this game 100%.What is this game? Basically it's DooM 2016/Eternal on a budget with a few additions set in W40k hive decorations. And when playing you are just forced to compare them.The good and the average:-The visuals are ok, the OST is mostly ok, worse than Mick Gordons ofc, the sound design is ok. But for example there isn't any ambient music in lots of places or sound wise the place feels empty. The combat sounds and voice design also could have been better.- Aesthetically it provides some of W40k underhive vibe and has some good visual design decisions.- The gameplay has some additional elements in a form of augmentation powers which help and provide gameplay variation both in movement and killing abilities, making it a bit like Titanfall. In general elements it’s DooM on a budget.- You may rerun any mission and there are side missions which are a part of a level with a certain simple objective: like attack the objectives, capture points or defend the area, etc.- The enemies, the level design and gameplay loop are generally worse. Lots of times enemies spawn from all directions and you are just forced to jump dodge around the place without any tactic, except a lot of attacks are instahits so you will lose hp no matter what. The pathing of enemies isn't that great and their general behavior and variations mostly feel generic. The level design and enemies spawn encounters are much worse “synchronized” in terms of combat feeling. But yet still there are fun fights to be had.The bad:- The pacing on some levels is bad, they may drag too much or throw too many enemies at you in one place, sometimes unneeded endless hordes, or too little. But some leves are fun and most of the levels have interesting encounters.- The guns don't feel impactful or really different when firing and in terms of their effects on enemies.- The itemisation system is not needed and is bad.- The side missions are generic and lazy, the faction standing system is useless.

_childDocuments_.review: W O W this is bad. I really thought that the reviews were exaggerating, but as it would turn out, they really undersold just how janky this entire game is. This game fails on absolutely every junction, save for maybe the graphics. Gameplay, animations, plot, voice acting, dialogue; all of it is just some of the most discombobulated dross I've seen in a game this price. It is all bad, and not the "Bad, but charming" kind of way that you get from a small indie studio doing their best, but lacking skill. This is like if you hired a whole bunch of talent, but none of them had ever made a shooter before, so no one had any idea what to do. They just started slapping ideas together that they knew people liked, and hoped that would be enough.The guns, arguably the most important part of a shooter, all feel absolutely dreadful. The revolvers feel way too underwhelming; the assault rifles even more so. It's like you've been given a BB gun against a juggernaut. Everything just feels like you're playing some F2P mobile game because, instead of just making a regular game, they decided to make a looter shooter where loot is about as sparse as the fun. This next thing doesn't make much sense if you don't play a lot of shooters, but this game simply feels terrible during fights. The bullets never go where they're supposed to, the weapons feel like they have some weird delay that makes them close to hit-scan, but aren't, and the sensitivity just never feels like you can get it quite right. Even when it doesn't feel too slow or too fast, it seems like your aim never actually goes where it should. Even when you aim at someone's head with a scoped revolver, the bullet just doesn't land. Enemies feel like a blob rather than anything humanoid, and the white outline solidifies that, so there's a huge disconnect between headshots and body shots. The looting is clearly just there to try and keep people playing. Half of my short time spent playing was exploring the nooks and crannies of the first two levels, and the amount of empty space is absurd. Within one massive, open, optional tucked away area, there was a single loot box. The rest of the area had no enemies, no ground loot, and no crates. The first two levels are nothing BUT that; empty space and linear combat. For what reason did they add loot if they weren't going to reward the player for exploration? They even have an "Exploration stat" for crying out loud, but exploring is the biggest waste of time possible. Worse is when you realize that if you don't waste your time on every level looking for that one loot box per empty square mile, you'll be under geared and chewed up like a toy for missing out on what little loot you can get. The animations...oh god, the animations. I really found myself laughing at how bad the animations in Turbo Overkill were, especially considering they were fine using it in their main trailer...but that game is made by one guy. This was made by a team, and the animations are hardly any better. It's not just the occasional poor animation, but ALL of them. Movement, idling, conversation; it's all an absolute joke. This game's graphics mesh so poorly with everything else you see because you're constantly being shown competent graphics that try to pull you into this grungy world, but are then affronted by animations worse than what an art student would make for their 1st year project. The voice acting is some B movie quality stuff at best; the dialogue, even worse. Nothing screams ineptitude like your character shouting "He's not my fwend!" 7 times in about 2 minutes. Very funny, didn't wear off the first time at all. You also have the "I should have worked alone" trash, which is honestly fine if the game is self aware and has that charm of something made well aware of what it is.This game is not that. It has absolutely no idea what it is, and that's the motif of this entire trash fire. Is it an arena shooter? Is it a cover shooter? Is it a looter shooter? No, it's all of the above. This is the magnum opus of Jack of All Trades, master of none. This does a whole bunch of stuff, but it does absolutely nothing well. Above all else, it's just not fun. Your money would be better spent on just about anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: The game fascinates with its atmosphere. The grim and detailed world of Necromunda draws you into its dark, gritty environment. Each level is meticulously designed, creating a sense of immersion in this dangerous and brutal world.The gameplay is a highlight for fans of fast-paced shooters. The speed and intensity of the combat keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. I particularly enjoyed the variety of weapons and abilities available for use in battles. The cyber-mastiff is a fantastic addition, not only aiding in combat but also adding a unique twist to the gameplay.The graphics are impressive as well. Stunning effects, sharp textures, and the overall art style make every battle visually striking. Despite some minor technical issues, the visual presentation is strong and engaging.However, not everything is perfect. While the combat and environments are excellent, there can be a lack of variety in the missions. Some tasks feel repetitive, which slightly diminishes the overall experience. Additionally, there are occasional bugs that can be a bit annoying but don't significantly detract from the enjoyment of the game.In the end, Necromunda: Hired Gun is a thrilling and atmospheric shooter that's well worth playing for fans of the genre. My score of 8 out of 10 reflects the high quality of the game and the enjoyment it provides, despite a few minor flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10To say this game is rough is quite the understatement. But if you aren't a fan of Warhammer 40,000 games and you haven't played Shadow Warrior 2, Doom (2016) or Doom Eternal, I'd recommend doing that first. Because they kinda do what this game does, but without the jank this has and have better gameplay in my opinion.+ Good soundtrack.+ Decent replay value.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.- No New Game+.- You can't dash forward when on the ground.- Most enemies you'll encounter are humans with guns. Where are the creative monsters from the Warhammer 40,000 universe?- Weapons are limited to separate categorized slots.
