_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is a fun Warhammer 40K skinned Bethesda style Doom shooter. I recommend this game when it is on sale if you like modern Doom or Wolfenstein titles. Play as a hiveworld bounty hunter, earn scrip to spend on customizable bionics, cyberhound upgrades, and weapon modifications. Fair warning, this game was rather short. It only took a day or so to finish, which is why I recommend purchasing while on sale. There aren't many level layouts and yet the game does a great job of using 40K assets to immerse the player in the tabletop setting. I felt like I was rippin' and tearin' my way through the Underhive. Recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna address something really fast ahead of everything else and that is the performance. Contrary to what some people claim, this game runs absolutely fine sans some short load stutters that I think might be caused by the fact that I'm playing it from a crappy old HDD from like five years ago. Medium settings, 1080p, stable 60-70 FPS on a 1050ti with ryzen 3100 and 16gb of RAM. Compared to Deathwing's launch, this is leaps and bounds ahead so if you can run Deathwing you can run this, no questions asked.Overall, it's a B-production sort of a game. It's not particularly well polished(though given who Streum On are, this is extremely polished in comparison) but at its core it's a great game. Gameplay. Not sure where those comparisons to Doom of all things come from, it plays nothing like that, more of a Titanfall-ish experience. I guess finishers confuse people. Gun customization is an unusual surprise, but a welcome one; nothing says "successful bounty hunter" as a royal purple autogun swinging from your hip after all. Grapple hook is more of a Just Cause style ordeal, getting you to a location instantly, so don't expect fancy swings from it. Weapons feel as solid as they come though I would kinda prefer heavy stubber to sound meatier. Dog can be petted and upgraded, but your personal good boy's AI is a bit on the janky side. Still really good at showing scavs what's what. Overall equipment system is alright but there's a suspicious lack of extra armor types which would be neat to see addressed, seeing only underarmors is kinda weird.Story? An excuse to get you to unlock more levels. It's inconsequential. Slightly brought down by bad audio mixing but it really is just a vessel for move violence and nothing else. You can try following it but that's entirely at your own cost. Side missions are gonna be very familiar if you've played EYE, they just drop you into a location and let you go at it. In short, no points deducted since it doesn't get in the way, just don't expect a thrilling intrigue or something.Visually it's not exactly a AAA production ordeal, you can spot some dodgy textures, but overall it's an absolute treat. Great design, nothing less I expected from Streum On frankly. They just get how 40k should look like. Helped by lighting, though some of it is kinda too bright in places but it usually makes sense when it happens. Some more stalwart people might object to bolters having picatinny rails but that's on GW introducing them like several redactions ago and devs just going with the flow. Ogrins have slightly odd animations but nothing offensive.Overall I can recommend Hired Gun with very little hesitation. It might need some patching to smooth out minor wrinkles but it's a pretty decent game. It doesn't reach for the stars but it doesn't really need to.Maybe wait for a sale if $40 is too much for you and other reviews seem confusingly negative(as some of them are full of bollocks as mentioned in the preamble) and you're just not really feeling like risking a simple, B level production game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm. HMMM.This game was fun. Probably not something I would necessarily revisit in the future, but I certainly enjoyed my time with it. Enemies can be a bit bullet spongey, but you get a lot of "I win" tools to deal with them so it doesn't feel like a slog. The game primarily centers around you moving constantly throughout the environment so staying still in one spot while under fire is a bad idea. The AI will focus fire you hard so you need to move around to mitigate getting dropped in half a second. There is one particular enemy type that, while pretty easy to kill, was bloody annoying because you don't get any sound queues for them until they've already attacked you, dealing a ton of damage, and they zip around like lightning. Thankfully, the enemy type only shows up on one level so it's mostly fine (for those that know, you know). I can't recommend this game at full price, but worth picking up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun one but with a number of problems that keep it from every truly being great. I understand why there is no sideways thumb button. A "Meh" recommendation. The idea is the reviewer should, at the end of the experience, be able to say for certain if someone should, or should not play the game based on all the criteria they have reviewed the product upon. After all, no one would want someones expert advice on something to be a shrug of the shoulders. That being said, if there was ever a game I would apply the "meh" option of recommending, this would be one of them. Let's get started. TL:DR at the bottom.The Game Loop - Necromunda is a game that plays like most action games of the era. There's upgrading your character, upgrading your companion, upgrading your guns, all while not being at a Borderlands style of loot grab. More of a Ghost Recon style of weapon upgrading. Different barrels, scopes, stocks, ammo make for a slightly beefier gun, or faster but less powerful variant. All of these systems play as well and as worn as you might expect. Increase bullet time, increase armor, increase refresh rate on pet. All of it tied up and packaged in that nice and complex technobabble that is Warhammer. You didn't "upgrade" your armor. You ripped out your chest and replaced it with a titanium plate. You didn't enhance your eyes with laser surgery, you popped that sucker out and replaced it with machinery. It all works and fits well. The Story-The story is next, and this is one of those sideways thumb kind of moments. The story gets the job done, but it never wows. Granted, I don't think story was ever a key part in the development mindset. It's a story of betrayal and vengeance and that is enough to propel one forward. What doesn't mesh well is that while the story is linear to the point of nausea, the characters all seem like they have something more to tell. Not the main characters either. The Bar Tender, for example, is one of a few people I found myself more curious about that didn't get expanded.             -as an important sidenote. I, myself, don't know much of Warhammer, but I do really enjoy the design of the whole thing. I won't ever pretend to know anything about the lore beyond "It's all gone to hell in the 40th century." From what I found out on reading, however, is the main quest giver is an actual prominent character in the WH40K universe. So, wasting his potential does seem like a sin against this story telling. The Gameplay-Gameplay. This is where it gets strange. The weapons and tools for the job (your dog, grenades, healing items) are all top notch. The Dog upgrades from a flesh and blood mastiff to a nightmare hound from the mechanical hells. The guns are chunky, clunky, and complex. Animations on them are great. Sound effects are mostly spot on, with most guns sounding great with only a few underwhelming offerings. Money is plentiful just by doing side missions and keep you swimming in upgrades. But then there's the other side of gameplay.A hit scan system that just sees your enemies hit you from whatever distance they feel like, and damage that sees your health fall from whatever full is for you, right down to that last ten percent. The "resistant to damage when near death" perk becomes an absolute necessity because of how this works. The incentive; "rip and tear until it is done". They were entirely too inspired by Doom here, and instead of a game featuring gunfights, you have a scramble to damage your enemies to regain health, smashing your melee button to get into a instakill animation to stop from taking damage. The instakills want to look really cool too (and sometimes do) but other times it seems way too quick on the animation, or jumbled during the animation, and you can't tell what's going on anymore besides "The enemy is being removed and you are being rewarded with a bullet shield for the animation and health." This becomes tedious instead of awesome. It becomes necessary to melee to survive, and when enemies pop spawn ceaselessly around you (Literally, they will NOT stop coming and they spawn pretty close to you. Not in front of you, but just around the corner), melee lock ups become the only way to survive the day.Wall Running. I love it. I hate it. For the most part, you don't even need it. It looks cool when you do it, until it looks awful when you do it. The truth is, it auto-runs on the wall if you press jump a second time near a wall. If you're not expecting it to mag-lock to the wall and start running, you'll find yourself running off the edge of the map and into lava. Other times, you're Keanu Reevesing your way across the hotel lobby in the matrix and feeling bad ass while doing so. It's another love/hate relationship here. For the most part it works, right up until it doesn't.The Verdict-With a minor playtime of about 7 to 10 hours for the campaign (I take my time and look around a lot. Faster runs may be 5 to 7.) and an unending number of objective based side missions (Hold area, Hunt enemy, Eradicate Enemy, Free Prisoners, Collect the Stuff) There's a little bit to keep you going back or just gathering up more money for the upgrades. Problem is, there's nothing off to the side beyond that. No upgrades for your home base area, no cosmetic collection items besides skins for guns, hell you can't even have a drink at the bar (dunno why, but that bugged me). No people beyond quest giving every says or interacts like they are there. No lore items to store in your collection library (not in a significant way anyway). There's just an overall lack of polish and consideration to things that would have made this more long term. The combat is fast paced, with glaring oversights to how the enemy hits you, how hard and fast they hit you, and how you heal it. The story goes just far enough to tell you what to do, and never far enough to feel fleshed out and well done. In the end, this game is fun. At full price, It's hard to recommend, but I did enjoy it for what it was. On a decent sale, this game becomes much more attractive to pick up. Fun and frustrating, ups and downs, highs and lows, this game is great when it's all working right and a slog when it isn't. If you're a forgiving player, you'll enjoy it well enough. If you're easily frustrated or demand a tighter product for your money, look elsewhere.The Good-Weapons and Companion Cyber Mutt are great.The graphic design is absolutely stunning. True WH40K design as most of their games are.Sound design is extremely well done in most areas.The Bad-Combat becomes laughably bad at times when overwhelmed with pop spawn hit scan enemies.Life Bar is there for show. In reality, you only get the bottom 20% of your health most of time.Kill To Heal is done to death here, and overdone on the melee lock up to the point of ridiculousness.The Ugly-The story never tries to be any more than it has to be. Nor do it's players on the stage (NPCs)The Wall Running. It's both awesome and abusive in nature. Love it and hate it.No extras. Side missions are only for money, never for another tale to tell.If you want a number attached to this, It balances on 7/10, tipping toward 6. I enjoy it for what it is, but boy do I wish there was more to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the main campaign + some side mission grinding for upgrades in just under 10 hours.  Thoughts:The decision to make this a pseudo looter shooter is a bizarre one.  I do not believe this game needed those elements.  They basically added grinding, which I'm not sure anyone really wants.  You also run out of new guns to unlock around half way through the campaign, which was a bit of a disappointment.  I was enjoying trying new guns out, but for the last half of the game I stuck more or less to the first highest quality gun I found entirely.The upgrades are about half useless as far as I can tell.  For whatever reason, you can only bind one key to use special abilities you unlock (and it replaces your ability to quickly use a healthpack).  Otherwise you're accessing these abilities from a power wheel when you click the middle mouse button, but the game isn't paused during this so I mostly only used one power constantly.I liked having the dog available as often as possible because he lets you see enemies through walls.  However, this would be less necessary if the levels were less weird and you didn't need that sort of thing to help you find your way through the game.  Also, in combat, the dog could sometimes get in the way of you quickly eliminating enemies which grew tiresome.I did a lot of complaining here, but I actually had a lot of fun with this game in spite of all of it.  The combat is fast and frantic which feels weird in comparison to the cover shooters we've mostly had for the last million years.   Weapon customization (excluding needing to find +3 versions of the weapons) was neat, I particularly enjoyed my bolter and my double barreled shotgun.  Also, it'd be great if the Doom Eternal guys could learn a lesson from these guys on ammo, because Necromunda basically doesn't care which gun you use, and it's wonderful to have ammo shared across the different weapons.TLDR:  Neat little game, kinda janky.  Not a 60$ game and it shows, but fun for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has a fantastic atmosphere and excellent dialogue, it contains too many issues with this game to be an enjoyable experience. I have had issues including but not limited to having the game launch on the incorrect monitor with no way to fix it, sudden spikes in performance having my fps top at 130 and randomly tank to 20, and unreasonable amounts of motion through the use of head bobbing and screen shake, even inside the menus, with no way to turn it off.The gunplay has a good look to it, but it feels very untested. The creators seem to attempt to replicate DOOM's style, which makes it feel more like an unrefined "shoot everything" style of game, with no real reason to change your weapon at all.Overall, this game looks great in concept and environment, but there's a lot that needs to be tuned and fixed before I'll throw $55 AUD at it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Warhammer and Necromunda fan I am surely biased - positively biased - towards this game.It looks nice, the designers created not only picturesque and variable environment, but the humor and small hints of dialogues, propaganda posters and other minor details indicate true love and dedication for this game. It catches the spirit of the Grim Darkness.If you're a fan of aforementioned setting - this game is a go at least to see the visualization.As a game, it is still raw and unfinished. I waited for half a year as fixes were released, and at least skipped the phase of non-working ladders. As a dedicated fan, I can forgive crashes, stucking in textures, ridiculously drafted-state cutscenes etc.Game design is where things start going downhill. Shooting feels unpolished. Guns look great, they technically shoot and feel different. Bolter, an iconic Warhammer weapon, feels like a full-auto slow firing machine of obliteration - which is good. Bolt pistol on every single shot feels the same - but shoots as fast as you click. Which kinda destroys the impact and immersion into the gunplay for obvious balancing reasons.The game balance is even more lacking. Grind walls are not trouble per se, though the game might provide hints of player level for plot missions.The worst part are boss fights. Not only they are grind-walled to your surprise, they are broken by nature. Infinite enemies spawning, paired with one-shot boss weapons - this is not a test of skill like Souls-like, there is no skill to develop. This is test of patience, grinding and breaking the game even further finding blind spots in Boss AI.I really wanted to love this game. Tactical Necromunda (Underhive Wars) lack AI, lacks endgame content and many things, but it is at least playable. Sorry Hired Gun, for me you are a Fired Gun.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I review this I just want to state, that the warhammer community have a serious issue with being willing to accept total crap as a "good" product and it reflects poorly on the universe when games like necromunda unhive war, and Warhammer underworlds are considered to be decent games. They're not, both are incomplete trash that are kind of insulting when you see a khorne blood warrior with no idle animations listfuly swat at a ork, like a blind kitten. I'm saying this because i care about the franchise and the majority of what we get is mobile dreck, with non of the passion or energy the world deserves. Which bring us to Hired gun, Streum On Stuido are one of the better developers of war hammer games. Yes most of what i've played from them are Euro-jank but that's to be expected from a smaller studio making a high budget game. But they at least care enough to put the effort in to properly represent the universe. The game it'self is a momentum shooter similar to the new dooms, with a kind of janky spell system which they really should have defaulted to tab for, but regardless they significantly improve the game play. The game itself is beautiful, a little let down by GW insisting on developers using their product line in the world, but that's a GW issue. This is not going to be a "Main game" for you, over all this is a one time play through which is pretty but kind of forgetable, and secondary missions are basically some brink level go back and kill some guys kind of thing.My real complaints are that stealth is straight up impossible despite being implied to be a part of the game, implying the existence of items by having "light under suit". making a distinction like this kind of promises a medium or heavy suit that's not in the game, and the returning infinite enemy spawns from 'Death Wing' Over all, i'd say 6/10 it's a good game, way above average for a Warhammer game. The important thing is they basically murdered 'underhive war' as a necromunda game, that ♥♥♥♥ let me down so much. Underworlds did too but, I mean i knew that was gonna be crap when they did the first dev interveiw.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks great but just isn't fun enough for me to continue playing. Gameplay tries to emulate the high speed combat of Doom Eternal but fails to learn several important lessons from it, most notably that you need to make a game like that very readable at a glance. Enemies are nigh indistinguishable because they're all the same kind of humanoid person with shabby armour and they're tiny at a distance. You start firing and sometimes they have shields, sometimes they don't, sometimes the shields go down fast, sometimes they feel like minibosses. There's big hulking guys of varying toughness occasionally.This game feels like it needed another 12+ months of iteration time to find the fun and revise some core design issues. It doesn't feel like it knows what it wants to be. On the one hand it's Doomish but it has ADS, and it discourages being out in the open moving fast because you'll get melted by all enemies with hitscan weapons at once. It's a looter shooter RPGish game but there's no damage numbers or health bars to tell how tough enemies are or which weapons are effective. It's the worst of both worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat looks and feels like "Rage 2" if you've played it, with more verticallity and some interesting movement mechanics. Gameplay and level design reminds me of Doom Eternal or perhaps Doom 2016.If you like those two games, maybe you'll like this one too.+ The fighting is engaging and intense. - The story is absolutely dull- It has an intro every time you load the game in- You have to wait for the menu to assemble- You have to repeat the same process after every mission. Go there, talk to this person, then this person, then go to the bar and talk to this person, then pick a mission- A few bugs kept making me restart the game, cause some grapple-hook movements place you inside a wall and you can't get out. - A few times the game crashed on me with no apparent reason. One time was between missions, on time was in the middle of a mission.- I had to complete almost half the game to start understanding how equipment management works in this game and after getting most of the expensive tools and gadgets I honestly can't say which one does more damage. There is no way of knowing what damage you deal to bosses or heavy enemies, cause it just takes a long time to shoot at them and that's it.If I were able to skip all that this would've been a better experience.It was satisfying to play it for a few days and I'm soooo glad I got it discounted.I'm not saying I didn't like it or that you won't like it.There is great potential here and it's wasted.Get it if it's discounted if you enjoy this combat style.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Level aesthetics;- Interesting Campaign;- Nice Arsenal of 40k weapons.Cons:- Poor Side missions design;- Enjoyable but shallow combat;- Atrocious interface;- A bit short for the price tag- no significant updates since release.To expand on the above: the levels are beautifully lore-friendly and can be breathtaking, as expected from the team that delivered Space Hulk Deathwing. That being said, while it improves on the formula substantially, the game seems to dsuffer from similar shortcomings.The main Campaign is really nice and enjoyable, and will have you explore a multitude of different environments that will please greatly any 40k fan. The story is decently interesting, with good voice-acting that will almost make you ignore the janky animations of the characters. Your Arsenal of weapons is varied and offers a good choice on how to blast your enemies away. Some very iconic weapons like the Boltgun or Plasma Gun are enjoyable to wield, and the Character skill tree gives you some very nice (if a bit OP) powers to choose from.--Now, aside from that, the side content is really disappointing. The first time you'll select one of the side bounties (to play as, you know, a Bounty Hunter) you'll be brought back to one of the levels you already cleared, but confined to a small portion of it, where the AI just spawn seemingly randomly around you, even in areas you just cleared.This combines with the poor combat mechanics: the game tries to give you a lot of movement freedom à la Doom, mixed with Titanfall (wallruns, grappling hooks, etc...), but the enemies don't really play into that style. They will shower you with bullets from everywhere (remember the spawning frenzy?), and it is really hard to take cover, forcing you in a hit and run playstyle.The health mechanics are a bit weird too, with you having a Shield and a Health bar, but your shield does not refill on its own, but rather needs pick-ups, effectively becoming just another health bar. You can theoretically replenish your HP by damaging enemies right after taking damage yourself, but because of the aforementioned gameplay mechanics, it is almost never enough.Thankfully, most of the game can be cheesed through by exploiting the Takedown mechanics: an enemy can be instantly executed from any angle, provided their shield is down and that you are close enough - even the 'big' enemies such as Ambots and Ogryns. And soon enough you'll even unlock a power that lets you execute a shielded enemy and strip them of their protection. Of course you're invincible during the takedown animations (which are a bit sketchy but varied), meaning you can just leap (with your grappling gun) from one foe to the other, just chain executing them till they stop spawning.__TLDR: the gazme is beautiful and sports an enjoyable Campaign, especially for 40k fans. However, the combat gameplay and the side content can be a bit disappointing, so I'd recommend waiting for a sale to try the main story out.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews seem to have been under the assumption that this was going to be a triple-A release with the kind of gravitas that comes with that. Hired Gun is a wonderful double-A-ish title that brings some careful polish in some departments and loveable eurojank in others. It's not so odd as to be impossible to pick up on its own merits, but if you enjoyed some of the stranger traits of E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy then you're in for a very familiar, pleasant sort of experience. The mobility is crisp, guns feel good, and the weapon diversity is far from lacking. Weapon customization is excellent, and the palette of player characters you're offered has something for everyone on it. Bugs are minimal, mostly cosmetic at worst. Performance has some potential issues at the highest end, but the game maintains its visual charm even at reduced settings. The cybernetic system doesn't demonize you for augmenting yourself or your mastiff, and in fact it's only upsides to do so. The story isn't some record-setting narrative experience, but it's strong enough to stand on its own and the side missions are nice little compliments to help you earn currency or find rarer weapons. It feels like the game has an underlayer of mechanics that I don't yet totally understand, but I've enjoyed all my time playing it and I'm looking forward to giving the game a shot on a higher difficulty after this clear

_childDocuments_.review: I bet it smells like rotten eggs.Necromunda: Hired Gun is a first person shooter set in the Warhammer 40,000 Universe. You play as the Hired Gun, a mercenary/bounty hunter on the tail of the Silver Talon, a wanted gang leader with a massive bounty. Being a wanted gang leader on Necromunda must be like being the biggest zit on a teenager's face. After his team of other mercenaries are killed, the Hired Gun teams up with discount Felix Jaeger and a Hive scavenger I like to call “Potato” and sets out on an adventure to get revenge on the ghost that killed his team as well as collect on the bounty of the Silver Talon. I'm not entirely sure where the game takes place on Necromunda, but I'm about 99% sure its Hive Primus, the Palatine Hive of the planet where most of the important things happen. If you're unfamiliar, a hive city in the 40,000 universe is like a Mega city from Judge Dredd, but built up instead of outwards. Usually they're pretty crummy, but the Necromunda Hive cities are infamous for being the champions in the “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” category. Cities like this exist to build -something- for the Imperium of Man at large, weapons, armor, vehicles, food sometimes, building material, this hive in particular manufactures Lasguns en masse. Particularly the Nihilis pattern, which is a pretty garbage lasgun, also known as the “Cancer Lasgun”Because it gives you cancer. Hired Gun's story is kind of hard to talk about. Basically things just kind of happen, people tell the hired gun where he (or she) needs to go, and then he goes there. Sometimes he finds what he's looking for, sometimes he doesn't, repeat for about 9 missions before something ACTUALLY happens. There's an overarching plot about your implants in the game, but its only brought up every now and then, for the most part you're just wasting dudes until you reach the end. You can put him in as many  games as you want, I'm still not reading the Kal Jerico books. Your enemies come in several varieties, almost entirely from the gangs you see in the actual Necromunda tabletop game. House Orlock, basically the mooks Necromunda. They produce the majority of Iron on Necromunda and hold a monopoly on Ashe Waste convoys. They also make the booze. House Goliath are roid raging super gorilla's that were originally made by the Nobles of Necromunda as a slave race. Big strong boys with big strong guns and clubs. House Escher are the girls that have a monopoly on cooties and giving kissies. Also drugs, they produce a lot of drugs. Some sort of defect makes their men come out all weird looking. So you can guess how they keep their numbers up. Uh. Cawdor and Delaque, aren't in the games. Van Saar and the Palatine Enforcers  are only mentioned, and the Squats are MIA. And you can bet your ass Klovis is MIA. There's also a re-use enemy from the other 40k game from this developer for, like, one mission. But that's a spoiler. The game's difficulty is kind of like a seesaw. I played this game on hard and there didn't seem to be rhythm or reason for the difficulty spikes. Sometimes I got wasted on B-grade missions and then sauntered through S-rank missions like a saucy minx. Outside of the main quest, which can take you anywhere from 5 to 9 hours to beat depending on the difficulty and how serious you take it, you can also do side missions for extra money. They just reuse the main story maps and reuse a small number of objectives. But they only kind of exist so you can afford more of your implants earlier.Gameplay is where the game shines. The guns are nice and crunchy to use and fire, and whatever you hit is going to turn into a fine, tasty red paste real quick. The game accounts for a large number of weapons from the 40k universe. The Autogun is one of the earliest weapon and works as you would think, as a regular assault rifle from other games with a bit extra kick.The Bolter in Necromunda is particularly nice, working as you would think a bolter would and absolutely mulching whatever you're firing at. A good time to talk about the gore in the game, with limbs being blasted off, heads going flying away,and guts flinging from corpses as the top half explodes until constant “I don't want you to exist anymore” fire. Blood even drips from the ceiling when you're done, its a nice touch, that's usually only something I see in DOOM Wads or other gory classic shooters.Outside of that, you also have a host of abilities. The Hired Gun can heighten their reflexes and basically just make everything sloooow You have an auto aim ability that just blasts heads off, you can blast people with your bionic arm, launch towards them, or go on a knife-stabbing spree. The Underhive of Necromunda looks exactly like you think it would. A hive city in general is hard to fathom, and I can't even wrap my head around something like Hive Primus on Necromunda. There are entire parts of the city that are lost to the Houses, and these gangs fight in wars that make World War 2 look reasonable in comparison. Necromunda: Hired gun is in general a good time, if not a bit stupid. There are parts of the game that, looking back, I'm not entirely sure how I got through. They can throw dozens of dudes at you at once and they come in multiple flavors, some enemies even taking a few solid seconds of shooting to take down. You do have a lot of options, and even a grappling hook as well as wall running, strafe dashing, and sliding to keep your distance, but man, it can be rough.Get it on sale if you can, or don't, I'm not a cop. The gunplay can be a lot of fun, and its nice to see a completely different world than the rest of Warhammer 40,000. No pun intended.Okay,  pun a bit intended. Necromunda: Hired Gun gets 6 hard to follow execution moves out of 10. 1 in every 5,000 North Atlantic Lobsters are born bright blue.Special thanks to Outic for gifting me this game. He is now the Underlord of Hive Primus and I can no longer contain his girth.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, I had a ton of fun with this game. It has it's problems but it was way better than I was expecting. Would def buy if you're looking for a game similar to DOOM to waste some time on.Story:The story leaves a bit to be desired. But I really wasn't expecting all that much from a game based around chasing bounties. Basically the entire questline is based around hunting down someone for a massive payout. There's a couple of twists here and there, but story def isn't a main selling point of this game.Gameplay:I honestly enjoyed this game more than DOOM: Eternal when it game to the gameplay. Ammo isn't anywhere near as scarce so I got to actually enjoy the weapons I like more. Combat is fast paced, it lets you grapple hook, double jump, wall run, dodge and move at fast asf speeds (There's a bunch of other abilities as well that you can unlock as you play). The combat areas are all pretty big and let you take advantage of the movement pretty well. Enemies didn't feel super obnoxious and sqongey (At least on normal). Also you get a doggo that rips people apart that'll appear after you play with a squeaky toy, so that's a plus.Visuals/Music:I'm not all that fussed normally when it comes to graphics so I thought the game looked pretty noice. Everything ran smoothly on ultra which is actually pretty rare for me (usually I have to bump things down to medium to get stable frames). The scale and style on things were pretty awesome. I'm not massively into Warhammer, but I've heard it's probably one of the best representations of the scale of things out there.I enjoyed the music. There's some cyberpunk/wild west themes going on with heavy metal jamming while you're in combat sometimes. Nothing too outstanding but it was good.Customisation:The game lets you choose your own character model at the start of the game. Most of them look pretty cool, but the female voice felt pretty eh. On top of that you can choose a few colour schemes for your character and doggo that you can swap out between missions. Weapons have a whole attachment system alongside some skins (You can also rename your weapon if you grow attached to it). I've heard some Warhammer fans don't like it, but I honestly wish Darktide had a similar system.

_childDocuments_.review: , yet despite its flaws, I still found myself having a surprising amount of fun with this game. Let’s break it down:Gunplay: It’s mediocore. Not groundbreaking, in comparison to games like that.Abilities: They're enjoyable and satisfying enough to keep you engaged.The game has only a few elements that approach AAA quality, such as:Environmental Design: This is where the game truly shines. You’ll encounter stunning, Warhammer 40K-inspired underground facilities and massive, long-forgotten structures that look straight out of a high-budget AAA title. The sheer scale and detail of the environments, like the colossal gearwheel trains, are astounding.Lighting: The lighting work is exceptional. There are moments where it’s so well-executed that it completely elevates the atmosphere, adding an almost cinematic feel to certain scenes.Story: It’s practically non-existent. For the first time ever, I couldn’t care less about what was happening. The storytelling is a mess, making it impossible to follow or feel invested in the plot.Animations: They feel like they were done by an intern rushing to complete a portfolio project in a couple of hours. It’s especially jarring when the game forcibly takes control of your point of view, jerking it around like a developer’s awkward mouse input. It’s amateurish and completely shatters any remaining immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, the reviews here have a power to exonerate an otherwise poorly critically performing game. Seeing that square on Metacritic turn yellow is sure to give me pause when deciding on what to play next, but Steam's "Very Positive" usually sets me back on the right track. But only 70%?! I mean, what the hell, guys? Any lower than that and I'd have to call in the Chirurgeon to give your bionics a look-see, what with that giant stick up your rear starting to qualify as one dangerous cybernetic implant.Set in the gruesome and vibrant steampunk world of Warhammer 40k's Necromunda,  is a ridiculously fun time. Streum On Studio seems adamant to get the fun parts of its cult classic  into a more palatable form and in front of a mainstream audience, and I think they did a solid job of hitting that mark. Having another shooter focused on movement, creative ability usage, and designing the perfect arsenal out of almost two dozen weapons that you can kit out with different mags, scopes and barrels, is as refreshing as it is exciting, and something we could definitely use more of. Like, seriously. Doing a retro shooter with the Space Marines front and centre is the safest bet you could make, second only to another strategy game.  might not look like the most innovative or daring title out there, but it sticks out compared to the developer's previous output, which found itself a niche of its own, as well as the wider scene of Warhammer 40,000 games, by not conforming entirely to the standards of a mid-to-high budget release, and bringing and retaining its own brand of weird and jank.That being said, it seems some sacrifices had to be made to fit something like this into a game that looks closer to a modern release rather than a Source mod, as everything in , except for the core experience, doesn't feel all that meaningful. Sure, all the ways to kill a cyberpunk is the most important piece of the puzzle and, at the end of the day, what you should be here for, but with the story, the characters, the weapon progression, the side bounties, the hub world (uh-huh, keep going, almost there), and certain gameplay mechanics all just sort of "being there" instead of properly fitting in, the picture ends up a little fuzzy. Unfocused. Lacking direction. I was left with more cash than I'd ever need, way before the conclusion of the campaign. Having made the promised reward from the bounty hunt at the centre of the game's plot many times over through the side missions, it was hard to stay invested in what was happening, made all the more difficult by the constant confusion and barebones understanding as to who all these factions are and how in Throne's name they relate to one another—aside from everyone wanting the biggest slice of the same pie. But the prospect of 'em getting deliciously vaporised or dismembered in one of many spectacular ways, sparks and blood flying all around? That kept me going.Well, I guess now would be a good time to say that I haven't actually played ...yet.

_childDocuments_.review: GW licensing just can't quite seem to hit the target with their projects other than the obvious exceptions (DOW, space marine, WHTW and Vermin tide) Although this is a refreshing change from the deluge of "turn based" games which try (and fail) to emulate the table top gaming experience it's just not quite a smash hit. The game is by no means bad, but it feels a bit "last gen" for me. Animations are clunky, dialogue disjointed and the combat AI primitive (think quake from the early 00's rather than doom eternal) You can see what they "tried" to do with so many elements of the game both from a story perspective and a game play perspective but it always seems to fall just a little bit short across the board. _childDocuments_.review: When I see "Streum On Studio," I am always reminded of their first game, E.Y.E.: Divine Cybermancy. That game is janky as hell but was a really fun experience. So when they released Deathwing, my friend and I were hyped because it looked so cool. It turns out that while it's janky, some fun can still be had. Then they released Necromunda, which should have the simplest gameplay of all those games (run-and-gun boomer shooter), but somehow they managed to make it the JANKIEST.Ok, good parts first. If there is something that is consistent with these guys (aside from jank), it’s that their art department always knocks it out of the park. The backgrounds, character design, weapons, and the trains (OMG the train) are just beautifully well done and scrappy, exactly how a Hive City should look. Every level looks great, and there's a good variety of places to explore. If you're a fan of Warhammer 40K, this aspect will not disappoint. I also appreciate that the developers chose Hive City as the setting; it brings to life a location that is seldom explored in Warhammer 40K. Hopefully, the next 40K games will also explore other places, not just the usual cities and battlefields.The sound is passable, the voice acting is good (can have a lot more of variation, though), and the story can be summed up as "I don't care."Movement feels snappy, and you can perform a lot of acrobatics (double jump, wall run, sliding, etc.), which all feel very responsive. Shooting the guns feels satisfying, with a sizable choice of armaments, so the game has a solid foundation. I don’t really have any issues with the shooting mechanics, except for what accompanies them, more on that later.With all of that out of the way, let’s talk about why this game has an identity crisis. The overall shooting and movement suggest that it's a fast-paced boomer shooter, but then the weapons have "types" like in a looter shooter. I'm talking about something similar to Borderlands, where an assault rifle can have effects (burning, toxic, etc.) and rarity that affects its damage and buffs. This, in turn, results in a variety of enemies that have "weaknesses" to certain types of weapons. Some enemies, despite having the same model, feel bullet-spongey because you need to use the "right" type of weapon. This adds a layer of complexity to the fast-paced shooting that doesn’t match the pacing they’re going for. There are also other problems, such as it being hard to differentiate enemies when everything looks so green and brown, the limited variety of enemies, shield guys still shooting even after you yank their shields off, and your dog and their dog, etc. They should have just committed to one type of shooter instead of creating this jumbled mess.On top of all this is the jankiness of the game, which ranges from minorly annoying to "how do they even ♥♥♥♥ this up". My favorite part is the process of removing a weapon from your inventory slot without selling it. It's freaking easy! Let me list the steps for you:    Find the weapon vendor because, for some reason, there's no inventory function.    On the vendor menu, click the list of the weapon type you want to remove.    Buy the cheapest weapon of that type.    Place that weapon in the slot of the weapon you want to unequip to exchange it.    Now sell the cheapest weapon so your inventory slot is empty.    Done! Very easy; 10/10, please reevaluate your life.There's still a lot more I could list, but the experience feels like you're driving a car with the driver's seat not on the left or right, but in the center. Yes, you can still drive it. Yes, you'll get used to it. But yes, it sure is painful as heck.So, do I recommend this game? Actually... yes, because despite all the pain, it is a somewhat fun game, and there aren’t many Warhammer 40K games available right now. But again, please only buy if:    It's on sale (I got it for around ~$6).    You are highly tolerant of jank.    You have a semblance of interest in Warhammer 40K.    You've exhausted your options for shooters and want to try something different.Whew, that's a lot of jank that I wrote!----List of Janks that I found- The "Press Enter" on the Title Menu is unclickable- Animation is overall stiff, on gameplay and on cutscene- Audio mixing on a lot of cutscene feels weird, especially the explosion sound (most of it sounds like a wet fart even though the explosion is in front of the charater)- When you are trying to talk to NPC, you'll need to wait for them to return to default state before the talk prompt is shown- Dialogue choice can only be chosen by hovering the mouse, you cannot use arrow button- Side missions does not have BGM Music- Side missions has infinitely spawning enemies because no reason- When you die, you actually have 3 loading screen. One when you Inject the Med-skull (forget the name) you got a mini loading terminal animation, and then you get the loading where you and your dog are walking, then the loading where it loads the level (This actually grates the hell out of me)- Might as well rename the dog as Janktiff with all that bug and janks on that poor canine. Even the act of calling the dog is jank as hell

Biggest jank was the wallrunning it just felt really weird and maybe too fast.Grappling hook was kinda cool but doesn't allow free movement as it has "specific" anchor points as in you just cannot grapple to random wall with like in Titanfall for example.Story was kinda funny but not really the main point of this game in my opinion, cutscenes had some janky/clunky animations.Sadly has pretty limited weapon variation and didn't even feel like swapping weapons after I found bolter as it just seemed way better than anything else.Has some buffs to resistances (never shows how much just says resistance is kinda weird)For full price probably not worth as 100% took me 13h with couple crashes and some achievements got stuck (like 10 headshots in a row and 5 kills with strength booster, I had to complete that and then on same play session complete another achievement to unlock it)Music is epic, atmosphere is classic W40k with huge areas for maps.Side missions are kinda useless except for money and they use parts of the chapter maps for them so they are not unique either.Enemy variety is pretty minimal, there are different factions but they mostly felt similar, they had some unique stuff (like riot shields or not) but not that huge difference.I would still recommend especially like 50% off as it was fun and if you are looking for some mindless shooting in W40k themed areas.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say my feelings about this game are quite mixed, but on sale it's probably worth picking up.The Doom-like combat is quite enjoyable, the grappling hook and dash abilities make it dynamic, I actually loved zooming through the battlefield leaving corpses behind. It's fun to combine different types of attacks into a smooth combo. And you get a dog :)In terms of story, it completely failed to grab my attention even though I've picked up the game with the intention of getting a look into some lore. I can't put my finger on anything that was wrong with it per se, but it just lacked that something that would keep a player engaged.You don't get to explore much - a small room within Necromunda for your main hub with upgrades and a few linear levels within the missions. I've found them mediocre at best, with the most interesting being probably the Koloss 44 level. Unfortunately, I've encountered more than a few bugs that in most cases required me to re-load my mission. Getting the grappling hook stuck in a permanently active state, locking me out of using weapons or anything for that matter, getting respawned outside of a boss room and not being able to enter it again, grappling something and getting stuck in a wall or inside an object multiple times...

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is an FPS by Streum-On who have also made E.Y.E. - Divine Cybermancy and Space Hulk - Deathwing. As opposed to the more free-form E.Y.E. and the constricted, slow Deathwing, this one is fully focussed on mobility and ease of gameplay. This is quite obvious in terms of the many movement abilities and mechanics and how important they are. Skills are more powerful and easier to use than in E.Y.E. and they are less in number. The game is very clearly built around all of these mechanics just as much as around the weapons.Bad:- Some Takedown animations take too long and are not satisfying.- Physical shields are often difficult to deal with efficiently and impede the flow.- Some weapons balance issues.- Aiming-down-sights of limited use (combat usually too fast and at close range)- Lacking atmosphere in terms of soundscape and soundtrack.- Depending on environments enemies can be hard to spot sometimes.- Confused design vision for inventory (too few status item slots, too few for spare weapons etc.)- Loot system mostly amounts to stat bonuses.- Character system grants all meaningful options very quickly and only allows for limited upgrading.- Menu interaction can be confusing at first.- Goliath bossfight designed badly.- Story presentation and plot progression are weak.- Map and objective for Bounties can only be picked from a partial and randomly selected list.- Mission summary screen does not provide any information on kills.- AI behaviour can at best be called straightforward.- Incessant AI spawning can be a problem in some spots.- No maps without constant respawning (E.Y.E. had them)Good:- Inventory interaction and customization flow very well once familiar.- Movement mechanics make game fast and satisfying and the attached evasion mechanics help with higher difficulties.- The grappling hook has a lot of range and grapples onto almost anything.- Skills are easy to use and impactful.- Hidden chests are often placed in creative ways, encourage exploration (and use of movement mechanics) and help break up the pace. - Campaign maps are often very impressive and encourage use of the movement mechanics.- Massive amount of aesthetical details on the maps.- Soundwise the game may often lack atmosphere, but the aesthetics partially make up for it.- Relatively varied map and mission design.- Bounties give uncomplicated, easy access to more gameplay. - Unique gang aesthetics and equipment.- Detailed and varied character models.- Very deep weapons customization that also makes a very big difference visually and sometimes also soundwise. - Guns sound beefy with proper feedback and gore.- Good, fitting soundtrack for the fast, gorey combat.- The Mastiff and Enemies know how to get around the environments.Overall it is a clear, easy recommendation. In spite of some problems Hired Gun is simply is too good when it comes to mobility and gunplay as well as aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I really gave this game a chance but in the end it just ended up being Doom Eternal but inferior in every way.  - Gameplay is made incredibly difficult by the general jank/poor design. Large amounts of respawning hitscan enemies completely undermine the rapid mobility system and I quickly found myself hiding in corners and small rooms waiting for them to come to me. Even then, this didn't stop them from spawning directly behind me and hosing me down before I had time to react.- The inventory management system is needlessly confusing. It felt like the developers were trying to reinvent the wheel with this one. What you don't put in a loadout slot at the end of the mission is automatically sold.- The side missions boil down to just you killing or capturing targets in re used portions of the campaign levels. I wouldn't generally mind this much but the portions of levels used are very linear and do not lend themselves well to the gameplay at all. I found myself often rushing through narrow tunnels and passages, ignoring the rapidly respawning enemies so I could get to the objective without wasting my precious stimms and medkits.- The story or what little there was is mostly there to explain why you're hopping from level to level gunning down baddies. I can't speak for it as a whole as I didn't finish the game. - The best aspect of this game was simply its artistic and world design. The environments and characters are well detailed and very evocative of the 40k setting. For the most part all the enjoyment I derived from the game was from soaking in the details of the world.In the end Hired Gun was a let down that I had high hopes for despite Warhammer's bad track record with video games. It has some redeeming qualities but ultimately as a video game it was largely unenjoyable .

After this happens you either have to be lucky to find your way back into the level or you have to exit the game. _childDocuments_.review: Does this game want to be Doom (2016)-meets-Warhammer 40k? Yes. Is this game a tad on the janky side? Also yes. Is this game FUN? Oh heck yes.After finishing the game do I feel the same way? Yes, but...If you're a Warhammer 40k/Necromunda fan you'll have a decent time with the setting, however I can't imagine anyone else giving the game much of a second thought. There's an interesting story in there somewhere, but you're only ever catching a snippet of it. Some sort of collectable log system could have filled in the gaps & expanded the exploration aspect of the game a bit more than simply treasure chest hunting. _childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I did not have an ounce of fun playing this. The game is beautiful, and it is cool to see 40K environments rendered in such detail, but this game feels like a total conversion mod rather than an actual game. By which I mean everything feels incomplete, janky, and unpolished. Level design feels random, and does not mesh well with the mechanics, enemies feel like dumb walking turrets or bullet sponges that react little to getting shot, the animations are either stiff or spastic, the sound design is utterly flat making everything sound like it is coming through a cheap mono speaker, and the gunplay while fast, lacks any impact that would make it fun or exciting. At its best, this game is mediocre, at its worst it feels like an overly ambitious first crack at making a game passion project of a single first time dev, style affair that would normally be free as shareware. I love the 40K setting, but I'm getting sick and tired of seeing it getting handed to these bargain bin developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I hope that Steam will implement 'middle' option in the reviews some day, but this one will be positive.Yeah, the game is jankfest, clearly made with fairly stock UE4 on a very tight schedule and a modest budget. It won't grab awards or high praise even from WH40k fans. The gameplay systems are a mishmash of several better games (loot from Destiny, DOOM-esque pacing, some RPG-elements akin of Deus Ex, Titanfall 2-style platforming). It kinda works, but the jank is severe at times.But some parts do click perfectly, especially the atmosphere. And when they do, Necromunda is the best WH40k experience since Space Marine. Game is clearly made with love, care, and yes, with a lot talent. Many downsides are due to the small size of a team, budget constraints and clearly very limited play testing.But you just can't go wronk with 40K as a setting. Huge-ass train, grimdark everywhere, constant lore pieces hidden in some neat little details, terrific art and the sheer feel of Necromunda... It's very true to the setting and I salute the devs for that (though some stock fonts are clearly ass, sorry).The gameplay is fun too for the most part. It's repetative, mindless, but fun.My take? It's... Well, okay. Good enough FPS to spend an few evenings. Huge plus that this game is not overstaying it's welcome. 8-9 hours of more or less linear SP campaign plus some boring side missions. Necromunda is also balanced in terms of difficulty. Almost no cheapshots and arenas are wide, without idiotic choke points and stupid boxes to stuck on.Devs are clearly aware about the slew of problems and in a process of fixing the most glaring issues (especially idiotic audio mixing), so I'll hold off my judgement on some problems for now. And I hope that Focus will give the sequel more time and money, because the potential is clearly there. Just not yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

The setting of Necromunda is well realized and invoked both the style and the tone of the setting very well. Definitely worth a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has 13 main story missions and endless side missions. Up until the 12th mission, I would have recommended this game easily. It is flawed but super fun. However, the last mission was a mess of bugs for me and I almost couldn't finish it.The combat in this game is super fun and fluid. At first, I found it too challenging even on normal but without too much grinding, I was able to start upgrading myself and my dog, and get better weapons, and it began to feel a lot more fun. I started doing side missions to have fun and not only because I needed money to get upgrades. That being said, some mechanics are never explained like elemental damage, as well as many stats and upgrades being poorly explained.I have never played a Warhammer game and the story made no sense. A bunch of factions and events come at you too fast to keep up. The cutscenes explained very little. In addition, inventory management is a confusing travesty designed by someone who had a few too many energy drinks before passing into a sugar-induced coma, leaving an unfinished mess.Two biggest complaints:Firstly, the game uses stims (a health item) to allow you to come back from the dead, and you can't carry more than three, forcing you to restart a level or go back to base, get upgrades and try again (sort of like old school games which had limits of 3 lives before needing to start over). Falling into a void due to a bad jump or missed grapple counts as one of those deaths. I like the idea of making reloads cost the player as a level of added difficulty. The problem is that the game also wants you to explore but some level design elements are inconsistent. You can wall run on THIS wall but not that IDENTICAL wall right after it. Also, you take no fall damage and levels are very vertical, resulting in massive jumps being common. You see a platform below and think you can jump to it, but turns out its actually just scenic background, causing you to fall to your death. This means that you have to either limit exploration or be prepared to restart to a previous checkpoint because there was a ledge you can't grapple to beside looking like every other ledge you can. Punishing repeated deaths is only fair if your level design is consistent and coherent.Secondly, the final mission bugged out. During a big battle - right before the final boss fight - my controls stopped working, killing me and forcing me back to base. I eventually figured out that the default keybinds had deleted themselves, so nothing worked. After fixing that problem and getting back into the fight, my HUD suddenly disappeared during the same big fight which means that I couldn't tell if I needed to restore my health, which of my abilities were still on cooldown, if my dog was ready to get back into the fight, if I was running out of ammo and needed to switch to a different weapon etc. It then suddenly came back during the final boss fight.Overall, this game is a bit of mess. The combat is fun so I recommend it for that alone, but be wary of some jank and bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this moment, almost a week after release, I don't believe it's a game that's worth its full price point.It gets several things right like the scale, the ambiance and the feel of its universe as well as a robust movement system and gun handling.But that's about it, and it also gets some things really, really wrong. In fact if it weren't for those particularly bad parts I would've given it a thumbs up and a warning for jank.UI: it's visually fine, but otherwise it's a complete mess, one that even an intern UX designer could improve. The whole loot system is utter and complete garbage, as is the inventory and really anything outside of the main menu. You cannot open your inventory in missions or outside of very specific points, you cannot change your starter pistol (only improve it a bit apparently), stockpile equipment, equip a weapon you picked up during a mission unless you did so while it was still on the ground, and the list goes on. Seriously it's a great example of "how not to do loot".Level and Mission Design: while the scale is really cool and some environments slap, the levels are generally pretty meh in terms of design with main paths stupidly hidden and a whole lot of jumping around, backtracking and ♥♥♥♥ through empty levels to find a path. Enemies spawn in your face and it's hard to say where they came from or where they're gonna come from. Some enemy squad comp are just spam and plainly not properly tested for fun.Side missions are some of the least well presented content I've ever seen in a game of this scale. You click on a (bad) menu, pick your loadout in another (bad) menu, then get a loading screen and drop in a part of a main mission level, just cut off for size. Then enemies pop from here and there (mostly infinite spawns) and grind you down until you find whatever basic objective you gotta do (= press E or shoot stuff). Then boom, you instantly stop and get another loading screen, you're done, bye bye. It's so unexpectedly barebones and poor...Anyway I won't ramble any longer but besides bugs and a pretty bad AI, it's those 2 elements, UI and LD that really prevent me from recommending this unless you're dying to explore Necromunda. This game needs love, lots of it and not just to debug it, but also to improve the shreds of content on the sides of the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a neutral rating then I would. It is not deserving of a thumbs up, nor is it deserving of a thumbs down. Pretend I am holding my hand horizontally and wobbling it a bit whilst making an "eeeeeeh" noise.It is not a bad game per se, it is just a bit "meh" when looked at overall. Visually it can be very appealing at times. There are plenty of screenshot worthy moments. Environments can be very atmospheric and make you feel like you are trudging through a hive city. Environments are StreumOn's strong point (much the same with space hulk deathwing). The gunplay and weapon +traversal systems are serviceable, but nothing to write home about. Your cyber mastiff is nice to have (mainly to pet and throw meat at in the quest hub), but you could easily clear all the content without needing to use it at all, except where the plot requires it.The main issues can be summarised as follows:*Lack of polish / many bugs / unfinished feeling / general Jank. If you have played space hulk deathwing (including enhanced edition), it is on a similar level. Broadly functional but plenty of tooth grindingly frustrating bugs and technical issues pop up frequently.*Voice acting. Genuinely terrible for the most part. Immersion breaking and, at times, so bad as to make me want to headbutt the wall and scream obscenities. It sounds like they rounded up some random d***heads from the nearest bus stop and paid them in cheap beer to rattle off some dialogue.*amount / variety / pacing of content. You have a very finite number of story missions, some of which are actually a lot of fun. Outside of these you will spend your time in a very small quest / trader hub where you can upgrade your weapons, mastiff and your augments / cybernetics. You can accept non plot missions from a bounty board of sorts, but these fall into about 4 different types and take place in a handful of environments which you will return to many times (so you can level your way past the deliberate and arbitrary progress walls they have put in to try and stretch out the small amount of story content). This all grows old rather fast.The comparisons that have been made comparing it to some sort of off-brand, bargain bin doom eternal clone with a 40k skin slapped on are not inaccurate. I bought it on sale for under £20 and played 19 hours before i had enough (all story content cleared, all upgrades purchased, and as many side quests as I could stomach), so I guess that is not the worst value for money. Had I paid full price for this then I would be really quite unhappy with the end result. If you love 40k and you can get it for under £20 then it may keep you moderately entertained for a while, otherwise you may want to skip it. Clearly the devs have a lot of love for the 40k universe and have tried to be faithful to it, but it just misses the mark in various ways IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Hired Gun is an old-school shooter with an amazing setup but it falls flat on execution.First things first, the environment is amazing. Setpieces, backgrounds, locations and details are through the roof. Some of the best 40K stuff I've seen in a shooter (though there weren't that many to be fair) in a long time. On par with Spacehulk but being located under a hive city it gives a really new and amazing perspective.Story-wise however game just doesn't come through. Description pompously promises that you can be a proper bountyhunter picking contracts and executing targets yourself and all that...But you end up being just a killing machine. No killing "characters", just hoards of similar-looking goons to get to a tougher goon who is supposedly a boss of some value.No one asks this game to be Hitman but still.Repetitive gameplay. Many arks left unanswered. Campaign that starts with you going for the highest bounty, despite making few times the reward money in the process, and ends without answering any questions.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I know about warhammer games, this is probably one of the best ones, and if you're a big fan, get this game, it's worth it.If you're just looking for a shooter to play though, stay away until a barrage of good patches or a good sale.The game has many positives, the overall visual design is amazing, and you can feel good intentions behind almost every gameplay aspect.But, it's jarring to play, for many reasons.I won't go into much detail, but the biggest issue in my opinion (aside from lackluster performance) is that everything feels disjointed. The combat is supposed to be a flow of movement, shooting and melee executions that seamleassly transition into each other, but they don't. Movement is a clunky version of what titanfall 2 has to offer, with all the right moves available, but they do not flow together well. Shooting feels just plain bad. A bit too inaccurate for one, and it's awkward to handle during movement. The animations not only bug out a lot, but they are very clearly a seperate entity from the rest of combat.If you're not a big warhammer fan, there are too many better alternative for fast paced action shooters to justify spending money on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The cut scenes take control of the character to the point that you can't look around at this incredible atmosphere. It really takes you out of the experience and it feels like someone is putting your head in a vice. Only letting you look at what is to be looked at. If it broke into 3rd person it wouldn't be so bad, but in first person it feels like it is taking my agency away.Minor gameplay things, very hectic. Always having the enemy flanking you and always outnumbered. The character practically has plot armor. It's not hard, just suspension of disbelief wares a little thin. It hasn't been established that this is a Doom guy or a Master Chief, it is just some guy sent do do an improbable task.Co-op would have been appreciated and would bring some believably to rampaging through a hellscape unscathed.I am aware of the 40k and some of it's lore, first game that I have played. It feels like the I have been dropped into this world, no lube. The character you play is aware of the narrative, but outside of the narrator and npcs giving exposition dumps I am not feeling it. To much telling and not much showing. I would have like to see a functioning forge world looks like to contrast where I am and why the character needs to bring the Emperors justice (or whatever) to this place.From what I understand from Warhammer 40k is that this is an uncaring & unkind universe where the weak are weeded out and only the strong survive unless you live on a paradise world and even then. The player should have a character die because he was overwhelmed. Pick the next person to go through the meat grinder where you left off. Let me feel the dread of this awful place full of death and chaos. Give me consequences for being weak, this guy isn't a space marine. It's just a guy with robot arms and a dog, just like everyone else in this campaign.So much potential and is beautiful, but the feeling isn't there. I can see what it is going for, but I can't seem to connect with the world or its characters. I want to like it, I just don't as it is. I think it needed some more time in the oven to get me invested.

_childDocuments_.review: It's astonishingly bad.It runs terribly while not stressing the hardware. Not only is the framerate half of what you'd expect, the game keeps stuttering all the time.The animations are terrible.The AI is awful.Voice lines repeat, sometimes 3+ times in a row, a few dozen times in a fight.There's way too much screen shake, it's hard to see anything when jumping (and it's supposed to be a movement shooter).There's a pointless looter shooter element, and other bloat that interrupts actual gameplay.The visibility is god awful - enemies blend into the background completely.This isn't just average or mediocre. This is unacceptably terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a cool game, but most of my experience has been frustrating. I'm happy to elaborate at some later point if needed, but basically my big frustration is with the enemies. I played a couple of campaign levels and those were mostly fine, but then the game told me I should rack up some money by playing side missions. I've made about 20 or so attempts at these "Status B" missions or whatever they're called, and I have seriously only been successful on them like twice. They're horribly balanced, and this mostly has to do with one enemy type. You can run along quite happily blasting at the normal grunts, but as soon as you run into an energy-shielded guy, you're toast. They'll soak up a full magazine of hits and then one-shot you with some kind of energy orb. I'm playing on the third difficulty and, yes, it warns you that enemies will soak a little more damage. But come on! This is ridiculous.  I'm quite comfortable playing recent shooters like Doom and Doom Eternal on Ultra Violence and Nightmare, so I really don't feel like it's my lack of aim or reflexes or whatever. The game keeps giving you this stupid tooltip that tells you not to "be shy" and to run up to enemies and kill them to get health back. But how am I supposed to do that when they're soaking up full magazines of ammo from my fully kitted-out guns? Guess what? You can't get your health back if dudes be absorbing all of your fire. And half of the time you're fighting them in these big open rooms where you've got guys spraying ammo at you from all over the place.It would be one thing if there was some kind of obvious countermeasure, like a shield-busting plasma or electric weapon type given to you around the same time these enemies started showing up. That's something that Doom: Eternal (the game that this game is clearly taking cues from) does. But that hasn't happened. You just keep running into these guys and getting absolutely wiped out.  There's a little electric punchy fist you can use to eliminate the shields, but that takes like half a minute to recharge and by then you've already run into two or three more shielded enemies.  It just feels like I'm missing something, but at this point I don't feel like it's my fault. I'm not a stupid guy. I checked for alternate ammo types. I tried a handful of different weapons. I upgraded some of my base abilities. I tried sniping guys from a distance. I tried running in up close. I tried wall running and being ultra mobile. None of that stuff gave me a big enough edge against getting swarmed and clobbered by these shielded enemy types in some big open room (the two I played were an ash pit and the top of a huge train). If you wonder if I'm any good at FPS then look at my achievements. I'm not the best ever, but I know my way around an SSG. If I'm not upgraded enough to be playing these side missions or if I should play the campaign first to unlock more stuff, then tell me to do that instead of acting like I should be able to conquer the energy shield bro missions.That's my main gripe, and if it weren't for that I'd be playing right now instead of typing this stupid review. But if you're still reading then you must care about the details, so here are a few more gripes:-The takedown system is garbage. The on-screen prompt isn't clear, it has very little range, and you can't really tell which enemies you'll be able to do it to. -On the same note, enemies look very "samey" despite having radically different capabilities. To go back to the Doom thing, it's not hard to tell a weak zombie soldier from a more powerful revenant. In this game it's much harder to tell who is a level 1 crook and who is a level 99 boss. Certain enemy types are distinct, but I'm talking about the difference between a gun grunt who will go down in one blast and a shielded, roided out dude who's going to one-shot you with a plasma orb.-Enemies don't make obvious footsteps or sounds to let you know they're coming up behind you. This is often enough for you to get killed without knowing what happened-When you use the grapple to pull away an enemy's metal (not energy) shield, you have a super high chance to instead pull yourself into a non-shield enemy standing nearby, thereby putting yourself in a spicy dicey little situation that you didn't want-It's really easy to accidentally dismiss in-game information or tutorials because they pop up while you're doing things-Abilities are too slow to recharge, and don't have obvious audio cues. Seriously, go back to what Doom Eternal did - give us a little gas can noise for the chainsaw or whatever-Your character's health ONLY recharges by collecting pickups. Some base-level health or shield regeneration would do a lot to help you catch your breath. Instead, it's super easy to get cornered and then you know you're toast as soon as you come back out.-Multiple times I died on top of health or shield pickups with my screen literally showing me that I had shields left as I diedSo overall I'm feeling let down. Part of that is because of the immense positives: The graphics look cool. The guns are fun to shoot. The world seems engaging and the environments are awesome. Before I ran into the shield bros, I was having a great time. But dude, the gameplay needs some retuning or some re-explanation or *something*, because it's just not fun to get cornered and wiped out on what should be nifty little side missions. I wanted to like this a lot more, but my first few hours have been ROUGH. Maybe I'll come back once my patience meter has recharged.Side note: I genuinely tried to google how to deal with these shield guys and didn't see anything helpful. If you have the secret sauce for dealing with those guys, then hit me with it. Maybe I'm supposed to just play the main story more, but the game said I should play some side missions and so I didn't want to move on without giving them a fair shot. That's what led me to my frustrations.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Action is good, almost like doom in a lot of respects. The voice acting is a little over the top, quests, dialogue and investment into what is going on is low. The loot system is lame, basically 4 versions of the same 10 or so guns, no modifiers etc, just +0, +1, +2, +3. These upgrades are really not that much better than each other. You can basically kill tons of stuff with any weapon. You get very unexcited about drops pretty quickly. The vendor never sells anything good, always +0 & +1. So after upgrading all your mods there is nothing to sink all the extra credits you have. Lastly and most importantly the inventory system is literally the worst I have ever seen in any game. You cant open inventory in a mission, and you can only modify weapon load outs at predetermined locations.  You have to buy weapon mods for each new weapon, you can't take them off of the last gun.It seems that the developers have no intention of fixing the problems and complaints since I am playing almost 2 years after release, and the complaints haven't changed. Doesn't appear than there are any future plans for the game, and the DLC's are only cosmetic. The action and game play is good enough to excuse getting for 5-10$. I got my copy with humble bundle choice so around the 5-10$ mark. Took about 34 hrs total to beat and get 100% of the achievements. Once you get to that point you can move on with your life.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not care about warhammer 40k or story in really any game, but the story in this game sucks. It's ridiculously cliche and poorly voice acted, the dog is just an object with how little personality they gave it, and none of the characters matter to me, especially my own. This is also a demanding game for my (admittedly not very good) computer, running worse than DOOM Eternal. The field of view also makes it feel like i'm looking through a pringles can the whole time. The takedowns feel annoying and actually made me laugh with how silly they were. The guns don't feel terrible, but the high ttk combined with the awful ironsights and low fov make them worse than they could be. It's a shame that this game wasn't made by people who cared about it, because it could've been really cool. (revisiting nearly a year later with a much better computer- many of my criticisms are the same. Coming into it expecting a good game is a fast track to disappointment, but treating it like a goofy arcade-y shooter is kind of fun. Unfortunately, the character controls like Titanfall 2 being played with a barrel of toothpick juice. Fun and silly for a time, but definitely objectively bad.)
