_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't say they are breaking the mold with new style and game features, but they do get it right. If you want a mind numbingly quick, reactionary, and on the edge of your seat FPS, look no further. Combine "Doom" gritty atmospheric layout, with very early " James Bond" grappling hook movement, gives you endless ways to drop in, smack into, or down right kick through baddies. Story is just captivating enough to keep coming back to play bounties. If you don't know much about the Warhammer 40K universe, don't be pushed away, the game gives enough back story and things to listen/ read to give you enough of a back ground to understand what is going on. all in all 8/10, id suggest to my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this with the info, that I am not really knowledgeable about Warhammer at all apart from picking some stuff up from Trailers and other Warhammer video games.That out of the way, I have to say, that I really enjoyed playing this game. It's a game, that takes inspiration from a lot of other games, either intentionally or it is just my brain making these connections. But that doesn't matter as most of the things work. Wallrunning, grappling hooks, mid-air dashing, double jump all together make for a really fast and aggressive game, which is right up my alley. The takedown kills feel a bit like a cheap ripoff from Doom 2016/Eternal and they don't really flow as well as in the previously mentioned games. And yet, the gameplay works really well, especially since the different abilities you can upgrade throughout the story make it even more fun.The story on the other hand is too confusing for most players. I got the rough gist of it and it kept me going, but the real star here is the maps and the environment. Just the crazy scale of the different apparatuses and the bombastic explosions and other happenings make for some really great eye candy. The sidemissions are another story though, as they are simple missions of "collect 5 of these", "kill 10 of these" and other questions similar to that. They also end, once you have done all the changes, and give you no way to search for the treasure chests in the map, so I'd recommend collecting them in the campaign and skip the side missions unless you need the credits.I'd recommend this game to anybody that likes fast paced shooters with some gore and a gritty world. Reminds me a lot of cyberpunk meets mad max.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It seems a slowly refilling bar has been added to limit how often one can melee, this is something of a bandaid for the overarching problem, and I am not sure what they did to fix anything I have gripes with, mostly because the game has become to unstable for me to play for very long due to crashing with update #4.The devs basically took everything they learned from EYE and overlayed Doom 2016 on top of it....just remove the 'doomesk glory kills' for traditional melee. The enemy AI can't attack you while you're trying to 'finish off' an opponent anyway, so there's no point to them other then to look cool or feel bad ass. They only feel in the way of the gameplay if anything, I wasn't a fan when Doom made these unskipable repeating cut-scenes required to play the game at all, I am still not a fan of them now.The weapons are overly flashy making it impossible to tell if what you're shooting at is dead or not, and the hit indicator is not a substitute for being able to see what you're shooting at. More often then not I find myself just picking the smallest magazine size and magdumping everything I fire at. Ammo management becomes a problem for harder difficulties, not because there are more enemies or anything special the devs just got as lazy as every other dev when it comes to shooters and difficulty, they just tilt the health scale, what you used to be able to take is lessened and what the NPCs can eat for ammo is increased, nothing more nothing special. I find myself just tapping the fire button and bull rushing the enemy just to get an auto-stop combat kill for a free health and ammo regen which I find tacky, the only tactics this game has is avoid and burn ammo into the big things anything human just bum-rush/facetank into melee range due to health regenning for doing damage and taking damage, which makes no sense. Secure a small health and ammo refill with an auto-stop combat to watch the same cutscenes over and over again. A mindless chase down what you wanna kill and melee it spree.The game is also riddled with bugs, ADS not going back on while holding it after a reload, 'glory kills' breaking the camera requiring a restart. Holding down fire doesn't work after a reload, invisible walls this clipping that. It feels like this was rushed to release after the AMAZING art team finished everything, leaving the rest of the game from soundscape to how the game runs unpolished.

_childDocuments_.review: It just constantly feels like i don't know what i'm supposed to do. Maybe you can chalk it up to i'm bad at all of it, but the upgrade system is persnickety the levels feel like they fly by when i'm not dying because dodging with this movement system is unprecise, things are so jarring that i still don't know whats going on even when all enemies are dead, the list goes on but the main problem i have with the game isn't the story, to sum it up the world and the graphics are really cool but the dead pan characters mixed with gameplay that while thrilling for a little bit ends up feeling like i'm supposed to be playing a hardcore parkour game that they shoved Warhammer and FPS into at the very end otherwise they wouldn't get funding, i'm sorry but i don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels undercooked and it's such a shame.It's overall a decent experience, but far from being great. Let me explain.Graphically speaking is more than enjoyable. It has a very cool setting with great lighting effects, you can breathe the attention to detail they've put into recreating a WH40K world worth exploring. Also, the OST is pretty good most of the time, and that's where the "great" part ends. Gameplaywise The game works okay-ish, but it has lots and lots of flaws. First of all: there is no inventory management while in-game. You can manage your stuff only in your hub right before missions or going to vendors in the hub area. Second problem: gunplay. Guns feel punchy and powerful, there is enough variety and customization, but at times they would refuse to shoot. It's a weird and uncommon bug, but common enough to be adrressed. Third issue: movement. Movement is fast, jumps and wall runs are satisfying and the grappling hook is a cool idea. Too bad it feels clunky a lot of times. Movement is slippery and imprecise, landing on small platforms can lead to your death and the hook doesn't always work as you'd expect, refusing to get attached to certain surfaces or platforms.I had a lot of fun nonetheless, it's a mediocre experience that could have been great if the devs put a little more time into it worth checking out if on a great sale. It's a solid 6/10 overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It really wants to be Doom in Necromunda. Unfortunately the controls are way too floaty, the shooting way too all over the place, and the melee not nearly as satisfying as Doom. Combine this with progress stalling bugs after years of patches and I did not have fun with this. Get it on sale if you really love the world, but don't expect too much here.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: So disappointing.First off, I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate the nuDoom style that's being mimicked here; glory kills 100% limit the style of game you're allowed to play into run-gun-and-press-button. You can't snipe, you can't stealth, you can't melee. You must keep moving like a hummingbird blasted out of his dumb bird skull on ritalin just to keep health up enough to not get one-shot by some jetpacking moron who tries to cram his entire body up your ass. It's stupid.The entire design philosophy of this game is wrong. It should have been an open-ended bounty hunting experience where you could experiment with equipment builds, like the aforementioned stealth, sniping, melee (which isn't even a thing), etc etc. The levels are huge, pretty, and varied (in 40k context obviously) enough that it's a no-brainer even to a sub-30-IQ idiot like me. But nah. You are required to zoom around and do i-frame glory kills because whoever wrote the master design document played nuDoom and wanted to copy-paste it.Also difficulty balance is whack. Easy is pointless and yet normal is like very hard in other games; as in, in order to survive you've got to take cover, but you're not allowed to because of jetpacking turds or dogs or whatever and there are a limited number of medkits you can bring. So that leaves rolling your face over the keyboard in "le frenetic" fjdiad9sa0hjd9sg.So frustrating, and it's not fun. What feels like half the later levels require running around to collect batteries in order to power up some bigger battery...because yeah, five minutes of searching in a lightspeed zoomer shooter is precisely what makes people enjoy the product. I do enjoy that there are randomly-generated bounty missions and I don't mind recycled tilesets, but the gameplay itself is the issue.It's not worth it even on sale. PS. I also loathe nuDoom for the same reason, but at least the nuDooms are better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This is possibly the most generous thumbs-up I have ever given because while Necromunda: Hired Gun’s core gameplay is fun, almost everything else surrounding it ranges from mediocre to bad. The poorly implemented looter-shooter mechanics and badly paced story serve only to waste your time, and the game, overall, suffers from a lack of polish.But underneath its many issues lies a fast, frantic, ultra-violent shooter that will (mostly) scratch that DOOM itch. It gives you plenty to work with in both weapons and abilities, and the open-level design lets you put all of it to good use. I think you’ll have fun with it, even if you’re not a Warhammer fan. Also, it has a grapple- sorry, grapnel hook. I can’t complain about that.Recommended, but wait for a deep sale.Watch the full review here:

Before that was awful, as the wall run barely works.The looter part of looter shooter fell flat; it's really difficult to find chests, and normally they just have garbage in them.What did this game in for me was trying some of the extra levels. _childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The base game here is fantastic, there is a lot of passion behind it. The game needs a lot of tuning, polish, and some more explanations. The 40k theme is fantastic here, amazing aesthetic and soundtrack. You can easily waste time just looking around the environments. The ways to move around and blast stuff is very satisfying. A good few different guns and ways to customize them to your liking. Long range, close range, melee, and explosive possibilities.Personally, I had no technical issues. FPS was solid with no dips, and no crashes. I have a very overkill PC though, so check other reviews.I only had a few in game glitches. Stuff like enemies not moving, gun sights being misaligned to where the bullets were going, and one soft lock where I got stuck in a wall after using a stim. Playing most of it through on easy, enemies are a very odd difficulty. Either being easy kills or oddly bullet spongy while looking the same or with very minor differences.A few missions in they introduce elemental damage. I still have no idea what elements do. Stats just say they add damage on guns and loot just says resistances? Fire, Electric, Toxic, Radiation. You and the enemies get them. How each interacts with each other, what the different color enemies mean, all never explained. So have fun figuring it out.Finishers / Executions are very jank. In function and gameplay. It wants to be like Doom. There is no way to tell if enemies are open to be finished so you just have to run up and guess. The animations break and just look very rushed. Side missions end the same instant you finish the objective. So you don't get any time to collect loot on more hectic missions. There's really no endgame or worth while loot to chase, no unique / special weapons or armor. There are drip fed upgrades. But you're only going to keep playing this game if you enjoy the action it provides.Why can't we replace the default pistol? It becomes worthless very quickly and wastes a slot. I get it, you use it in finishers and it's the signature gun, but at least let me swap it out with a higher tier one. And finally, you can rename your guns but not your Dog???
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It’s janky, the dialogue can be hard to hear, and I didn’t really pay attention to the plot.  But the enemies aren't sponges and you can fly all over the place.  It’s beautiful, I love it.  Big dumb fun.High quality AA gaming.  If you liked Elderborn, Deathwing, or Serious Sam, you’ll prolly be into this.  Or if you like futuristic hobo death battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm keeping my original review below here, but the conclusion of the game was so disappointing that it tipped it over the edge, so I had to change to a thumbs down. The final boss battles were extremely boring and the conclusion of the story was very, very bad. The voice acting, the boring and static cut scenes, the terrible antagonists, a half baked attempt to do some kind of plot twist.. it was just all so bad, it leaves me with a bad taste in my mouth.This gets a passing grade by the skin of its teeth. It's really a mixed bag; gunplay feels solid, levels are pretty cool, the setting is badass. But holy mother of all deities, this inventory UI is so godawful it makes me want to blow my brains out. Also the loot system is really half-assed. Either stick to a streamlined fixed-guns FPS, or make an actual looter shooter that's fun. This here is just a lazy in-between and I can't imagine a soul on the planet liking this. Also the NPC- and enemy models look so bad, with hideously botched faces as if we're back in 2002. Also, the story is poorly written and most of the voice acting is extremely bad. Enemy AI is also often incredibly dumb. So why the hell do I still give it the thumbs up? Well, like I said, shooting these guns feels really good, and that's a pretty damn important thing for a shooter. (get it when it's really, really cheap)

_childDocuments_.review: Take on the role of an anonymous mercenary on the most infamous hive city in the entire  universe: Necromunda. A paper-thin story, delivered via some hilariously bad cutscenes, and poorly balanced combat mar an otherwise fun and frantic shooter that has some of the best level design around.  Unbelievably for a game set in a universe that's filled to bursting with lore, there's almost no storyline here. You're thrown straight into the action with no sense of who you are or even why you're doing anything. The story is delivered rapidly in small chunks like it's being fired at you out of a tennis ball launcher. It wasn't until the third mission before I had any idea what was going on. I wouldn't put too much effort into understanding the story because it's just a paper-thin excuse to rack up a higher body count than polio. You were betrayed on a mission that saw your two squadmates killed and you're now out for vengeance (I think). However, you continue working with the guy who sent you on the mission in the beginning, and then it transpires you barely knew your team members that were killed, so your character's motives are completely ridiculous. Oh, there's a side story about an implant you have been given by the guy who set you up, but it doesn't factor into any of the plot other than a passing mention in some of the cutscenes. Speaking of them, they're some of the worst I've ever seen. Most of them have the camera in the wrong location like they've been shot by a bunch of drunk art school students, none of them advances the story one bit. Also, the less said about the truly awful ending, the better. It's obvious that the game isn't relying on its story to encourage the players, so let's look at the gameplay. The game is heavily modelled after  and other old-school FPS games, only not as well polished. It's all geared towards being as fast and as fun as possible. You can double jump, run along walls, and sling yourself around using a grappling hook. There's not a huge variety of guns and you can only have a loadout with four of them; there's a pistol you can't unequip, another pistol slot, and two main weapon slots. The guns are your standard variety of shotgun, assault rifle, heavy and energy weapons on a triple-tiered rarity scale. They can all be modded to quite a high level which ironically makes the rarity levels redundant. It's possible to mod the starting guns to a point where they'll carry you through the entire game. While combat is the main source of fun in , it's also where the game's flaws come to light. They've gone for a style of combat where the objective is to ping yourself around the area as fast as you can, spraying bullets until everything is dead, but the lack of balancing is criminal. At higher difficulty levels, the enemies barely miss, so you'll be reduced to just picking off as many enemies as you can before charging in, which isn't how the devs want the game to be played. The enemies spawn in behind you relentlessly, meaning you'll spend a lot of the battles constantly getting shot in the back. There's a bizarre takedown mechanic that can be done on virtually any similar-sized enemy without a shield (even some bosses!) regardless of their health level. The takedowns take so long to complete and often don't line up properly, so you'll perform a head-chopping animation to someone's knee, only for their head to pop off like a bottle cap. It's also difficult to see what's going on during them, as the camera bobs around like an earthquake has just hit. There is a melee option but you need to buy the upgrades for it, and it's useless, as you move far too quickly to hit anyone and just get picked off. One of the selling points was the inclusion of a dog sidekick, but this suffers from the same lack of polish as the rest of the combat. You summon the dog using a squeaky toy and "summon" is the right word to use there, as he just pops out of thin air next to you. He'll highlight all the enemies in red and attack them. But he can't follow you if you move to a different level so he's only useful if you call him right in the middle of a firefight where the enemy highlight isn't of any use. I went through the game without upgrading any part of the dog because he was just so useless. It's almost as if the dog was added after the game was completed with no testing to see if he worked or not. That's a really common theme throughout . The game has loads of ideas crammed into it, with seemingly no effort put in to make them complement each other. The movement mechanics are designed to keep the game as fast as possible but the goons' aim renders it suicidal to use them. All the guns have rarity levels but the modding makes them pointless. There's a story but it's so thin and the cutscenes so poor that it's incomprehensible. The dog is included to help in fights but it doesn't do much other than get shot at. This is clearly a game that did not undergo a lot of playtesting. The graphics are where  stands out, namely in the level design. This has got to be the best, most authentic representation of a hive city that I've ever seen. The sense of scale is enormous but it doesn't feel deformed as if the levels are big just for the sake of it. The size of everything feels normal with the transport train level being a particular delight. Streum On Studio aren't very good at gameplay mechanics, but they're immensely talented environmental artists. They've got the dirty, gritty aesthetic absolutely perfect. If you're a  fan the visuals are well worth the price of the game alone. There is a lot to explore with treasure chests hidden in loads of little nooks for you to find bonus high-tier loot. The sound and music design are both terrible. Enemies make no real noise moving, meaning you'll only know one is behind when you get shot in the back. The voices don't sync up to the character movements during the cutscenes. The voice acting itself is also dreadful. All the lines are delivered in a dull, monotone that has zero emotion to it at any stage. It's also mixed terribly so that each line sounds like it's being delivered at gunpoint. There's no effort to get any of the conversations to sound natural and the music is as generic a metal-sounding soundtrack as you're likely to hear. It doesn't stand out and you'll barely even notice it. While this is a game with an awful lot of flaws, it is a title with a lot of potential. Many of the flaws can be ironed out with patches, although they will not be able to fix the horrendous storyline. Even as it is, the game is a fun little blast through some of the most detailed and incredible industrial levels you'll ever see. For  fans, this is one of their most iconic worlds made flesh. It's not a perfect game by any means, and it does need some patching, but it is worth the cash if you're looking for a mindless good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those strange, rare body horror gems that people who love Cruelty Squad or E.Y.E. are gonna love. Action packed and pretty disturbing (the physical dog upgrade mechanics are genius),the story is interesting enough but the character design and the voice acting take it to another level.   The upgrades are overwhelming in a good way,lots of stuff do aquire and tons of guns to mod,each having their own branching system for new gun parts. Level design is stellar and everything is detailed down to the tiniest skull rivet or a bullet dangling from a gun. Great game, Def worth the asking price IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely quite disappointing. Necromunda contains the ingredients for a decent action shooter but falls short and fails, primarily due to the abundant technical problems. During the game, I experienced crashing, the HUD would occasionally disappear, enemies and bosses would get stuck in walls, technical performance was underwhelming, spoken dialogue would sometimes be too quiet and would only be decipherable through subtitles etc. Another issue I have is that the game feels like it is lacking a bit of cohesion within the gameplay elements. There's cool ideas like the Mastiff companion, the looter shooter pickups can be fun, there's executions in the style of the modern Doom games, wall-running in the style of Titanfall 2, grading at the end of each level and more. From my experience though, not all of these ideas properly gel together. Some of them feel like they are not implemented purposefully enough, it's what I would describe as design bloat. There are good parts to the game though. The game's art direction helps sell the strengths of the Warhammer 40K universe. There's also a decent soundtrack in here that would certainly appeal to fans of modern Doom. The core gameplay can also have some moments of fun (but to repeat myself, not all of its' elements feel purposefully implemented).With these comparisons to the modern Doom games, I can't help but mention that I've gained a deeper appreciation for them. There's a level of polish that went into those games that makes them the gold standard for PC ports. With Necromunda Hired Gun, it feels like the developers were not given enough time and resources to give the game the care and love it deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a Streumon Studio game. It's janky, but there's a tremendous amount of love and passion put into this game. _childDocuments_.review: So when I heard this game being described as "A 40k game with the Doom formula", it immediately had my attention. So is that an accurate descroption?...Well....kinda. Here's the breakdown.It's a VERY satisfying 40k based shooter. The atmosphere and theme is perfect, the weapons feel accurate for the most part (esp the bolters), and it actually gives you a different perspective to the 41s millennium than you may be use to. There are no space marines, chaos cults, or any of the other overarching factions you'd usually associate with 40k. There is a single xenos race that appears, but it's very limited. You play as a lowly bounty hunter in the bowls of a hive planet, and the whole game takes place in that context.Now as for the gameplay. Is the Doom comparison accurate?....Sort of. It very clearly draws some inspiration from Doom. It's a face paced shooter with brutal combat where you kind of have to stay moving all while listening to a fantastic heavy metal soundtrack. Thats about where the similarities end tho. The combat is fast paced, but if you're looking for the same blood pumping, raw carnage that you'd get in say Doom Eternal, you're going to be disappointed. You also have bionic abilities that you can unlock and enhance. Oh, and you have a pupper....a MURDER pupper....and you can cybernetically enhance the cyber pupper, but most importantly....you can PET the pupper.Now on to the flaws, because while the game is definitely fun, it has quite a few of them. Most glaringly is the animation quality. The model animations have a tendency to glitch and be really janky, especially during the take downs/glory kills. I don't think I had a single glory kill behave the way it was supposed to. The gore and death animations are also pretty pathetic, enemies are basically bullet sponges that when you finally land the killing shot, whatever part of their body the shot hits basically pops off like a blood filled water ballon.  Also, it didn't happen often, but the game did crash on me a couple times, thankfully not at critical moments. Having the dog is def cool, but the way it was executed feels like it could have been better. There were also some design decisions I found very questionable, like the fact that you can't swap any of your weapons, gear, or even look at your inventory mid mission. You have to choose your loadout at the start and thats pretty much what you're locked into for the mission. THAT I was particularly annoyed by.Overall, the game does have some very clear flaws. and I do think it falls short when it comes to the DOOM comparison, but as a 40k shooter in a time when the quality of a given 40k game is very much a coin toss, I think it still manages to be very enjoyable, and for a fairly reasonable price (If this were a full $60 release, I'd probably be much harsher on it). Worth a try for any 40k fan, def if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a shame I have to leave a negative review, but I just cannot recommend this game to anyone, not even on a discount.Being an enthusiastic noob to the world of Warhammer 40K, I was looking forward to this game and bought it instantly when it came out, hoping that it will pull me in more and give a much better sense of how this world works beneath the shiny armor of the space marines and the holy wars. Just to have a feel of living as an average Joe in one of the most famous hive worlds of the Imperium.Well, it suck, that's how it feels.This game wanted be something similar to Borderlands + Doom Eternal + WH 40K + only god knows what else. Instead it became the worst fps game I ever had the misfortune to play.I tried 3 times. 3 times to like this game. I failed...Or perhaps I succeeded not wasting more time of my one and only life on something that clearly was just cobbled together, with no guidelines, no clear vision., if you ever read this... Next time make sure whoever you give the licences to to create something under your IPs, that they are capable of delivering something good. Because this is just a pile of stinking garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Warhammer 40k fan who also played both DOOM and Titanfall, this game is fantastic. I am a simple man, so the whole run-in-a-room-and-kill-everyone-then-move-on-to-the-next, is not a problem, though if you do not like that kind of game, this might not be for you. The stability is pretty good, only had 2 crashes, though none of them happened during a mission, so i guess i was lucky. The frame rate is good, running 75 fps 95% of the time with all options on high. My rig is a 3070, 16 gig ram, i7-7900k clocked to 4.8 GHz. Though in some of the later missions i noticed drops to around 50 fps but was back up to normal in the next room of the mission.In general the game makes you feel like a total badass, the music is great and the gameplay is fast and a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: In advance, note that I am not an existing 40k fan going into this.  So although my experience was rather "meh", perhaps an existing appreciation for the universe would carry an existing fan through.  I got this in a bundle, so it was roughly just a couple dollars when you break it down.  If I paid full price I would probably regret it.  In 8 hours I've finished the game, and maxed out all my character upgrades.  Loot is mostly meaningless-- I finished whole game with just the first new gun I found plus attachments.  Basically every aspect of the game feels like it's missing a bit of polish-- Loot, movement, shooting, cutscenes, dialog, active abilities, economy, enemies, etc.From what I understand the recreation of the 40k enviroments are pretty good though.  So if you just want to explore those a bit, this may work for that.  That said, if you came here looking for a looter shooter, don't bother-- and if you came here looking simply for a run-and-gun shooter, you are better off sticking with DOOM Eternal.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets one thing right, and while its the most important thing, it is ultimately impossible to overcome just how much they did wrong.First, the good: the game play/gun play is awesome.  The guns feel great, the movement is fast and fluid, it runs great.  The shooting and movement, the two most important things, by far, in a fast paced FPS, and they nailed them.  This is how guns and movement in FPS should feel.  If you've ever been turned off by a game because you felt like the guns seemed so weak and underwhelming, you'll enjoy playing with Necromunda's guns; they thump in the best sort of way.  There's some issues with accuracy when aiming down the sites (the game can be waaaaay off), its really not as large an issue as you'd think, because you hip fire at least 70% of the time, and almost never take anything close to a 'sniper' shot (despite the huge levels).  Everything that goes into the power fantasy of being a bad ass, gun blasting, bounty hunter, double jumping, wall running, and grappling hooking across levels while you never stop firing is there in spades.So why the thumbs down? Almost everything else.  The menus and UI look like they didn't have a UI/UX designer on staff, and just had random developers each make one menu - they're awkward to use, have weird and inconsistent keybindings, and are rife with just basic, fundamental design flaws (ie, don't make things that aren't buttons, look like buttons).  These design issues really start to come up in the levels, which are simultaneously impressively huge and detailed, and also so poorly designed that you're barely able to see anything and waste a ton of time exploring dead ends. Basic design mistake #1: creating areas of the level that have no purpose - they have hidden chest to encourage you to hunt around, but the levels are so huge in scale, you inevitably end up trying to go somewhere you're not suppose to and die. Basic design mistake #2: inconsistent/hard to see colorings to mark in game items.  This is really basic game design - you use consistent and unique coloring to make items and parts of the level (ie, climbable ledges) that the player needs/interacts with easy to see.  They just...don't...and you will have trouble spotting basically anything from a distance, including most bad guys.  The dog will mark enemies for you, and you can get some powers that help, but there is really no good substitute for bright, easy to discern, coloring.There's also some bugs and some of the normal, and some acceptable 'double a jank' with things like animations, but the audio is almost inexcusably broken right now.  Music and guns sound ok, but all of the voices in the game are glitched and play at almost an inaudible volume, including in cut scenes.  I'm assuming they'll fix this shortly (they've already patched/improved it once), so I don't really deduct points for this.Ultimately, the game is a lot of fun, as in the game play and movement.  Everything else just hurts the experience.  If you love the source IP, this is a pretty solid game, because the flaws probably won't bug you much, you're here for the warhammer.  If you loved something like Doom 2016, and you already beat Doom Eternal, then I guess this isn't a terrible option - the gameplay is similar enough that if you enjoyed one, you'll probably enjoy the other.  Most other games still occupying this sort of space are retro style shooters, so it being an underserved niche, if this sort of FPS is your jam, you'll probably enjoy it.  Everyone else though, will be turned off by and unwilling to get past the bugs, jank and awkwardness to enjoy the admittedly fun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun plays, and feels, like it wishes it was Doom: Eternal. It 'wants' the highspeed gameplay where you're zooming around the map murdering your way through droves of goons and mooks while having to account for the occasional slightly higher-powered Big-Bad, and then an eventual boss battle, but it all just falls flat at times. As a long-time 40k hobbyist and enthusiest for the setting, there is a small essay worth of things I could touch on. But in the interest of making a coherent review that doesn't feel like literal homework, I'll try to keep it brief to the points that will matter to most people. Necromunda: Hired Gun lacks the flow they're clearly trying to copy from Doom:Eternal with its more high-speed arcadey shooter dynamic. You're given a number of re-tries whenever you die in a single mission (essentially extra lives), you can repeat missions for greater loot, and you have a number of abilities you can unlock and then can be accessed on a timer per ability. While a number of these abilities can be fun (thermal vision to spot hidden foes, a super blade that kills things in one hit for a short time, and of course your dog friendo who essentially helps you fight), most of it just doesn't work well in-game. Yes, this game has pretty visuals. the environments have been nailed, and they did a good job of capturing the aesthetic of the gangers in an underhive. That being said, said-gangers only exist to be canon fodder, so if you're expecting deeper stories or intrigue then you're not really going to be getting any of that. Pretty to look at, hollow on the inside. Power-ups, and abilities, feel gutted. Some of them are 'way' more helpful than others, but most of them are largely useless or will simply get you killed because this game does a horrible job of conveying how much damage you've taken before you simply die. Thankfully you can buy up to 3 extra lives per mission, but you'll burn through them almost instantly since you literally rez in the same spot you died. You know... the place 'every' AI just murdered you a minute ago? And they'll start shooting at you nearly instantly as soon as you get back on your feet. So, I hope you can get away, otherwise you'll just die over and over in the same spot. The HUD and user UI is horrible in-game, and VERY un-intuitive. The weapon layout is confusing, and for whatever reason does't allow you to manually map out your guns for your 1-6 basic & pistol weapon slots. Furthermore, if you find a better gun in a mission, it doesn't logically trade out with the gun you're currently holding, and instead you just drop a random weapon. Which means you could easily drop your BEST weapon for some gun that 'looks' useful, only to find out afterwards you traded for literal horse-crap and make your entire mission go from possible to nearly un-playable. I want the enjoy this game, but its not a good game. Its got too many annoying aspects, straight up bad gameplay, and it quickly starts turning into simply a horde-shooter by level 4. I can't in good faith recommend this game to others. The voice acting was fun. And I liked the design of the characters skeletal-looking bionic limbs. Besides that though....5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good game.There are two things it gets right - art direction/graphics and music.Everything else is subpar. From best to worst:The movement is pretty fluid and well done. Grappling hook works well, and on High difficulty, you need to keep moving. However, I found that even on hard difficulty, strafing left and right is enough and there's no need to run up walls and perform tricks to survive - and even with investment into the skills, ADADing and shooting the enemy is better.The difficulty jumps dramatically between Normal and Hard. Normal is too easy, Hard is in many places unfair and boring as some enemies become bullet sponges.The UI is very janky. It's apparent in every step. When you're in your home base, where you can't summon your mastiff nor shoot, there are still constant prompts to press the corresponding buttons, even though they don't work. Dialogue menus can't be cycled through using WASD or arrow keys, you must select the dialogue option with the mouse - and yet there is an option (with a constant reminder) that you can press E to actually select the option you're hovering over instead of just clicking it. Your abilities are selected from a wheel - and you must pull it up every time you want to use an ability. There is no selecting an ability and using a shortcut to reuse it - every time you want to reuse it, pull up the wheel and select it mid-combat.Enemy variety is very lacking. There are apparently multiple gangs, but they generally all look the same and behave the same. More on the AI later. The optional mission board shows very many various gangs, and even cults, but you meet almost none of them, they exist only on that screen. It's cool that you can apparently do missions for the local chaos cult, but this has no impact on anything, as far as I can tell. All enemies can be separated into Ranged, Melee, and Big Boys. 70%/25%/5% of enemies, respectively. It hardly matters what weapon they're shooting or how much shield they have - all of them are generally approached the same way. Bosses are without exception boring human-sized people with guns who generally behave the same as any other enemy, but have 20 times more health. A couple endgame bosses behave slightly differently and have some special moves, but this doesn't change the approach to killing them.Many weapons feel good, but most are objectively best and can't be close to competing with others and vise versa. I'm talking outfitted heavy bolter having time-to-kill on a large enemy being 15 seconds of nonstop shooting, while the big Plasma Rifle (which I can't imagine being useful on regular enemies as it has 4 shots that can't even one hit kill many) taking one and a half minutes.The dog is useless. A fully upgraded dog, which costs nearly as much to upgrade as the PC, will inconvenience a single enemy for a few seconds, maybe kill them if you're lucky. In that time, you'll mow down the rest of the room yourself.The story is boring and uninspired. The main character is well-voiced, but has little personality, motivation, or character development. This is true for almost all the characters. Most of the supporting cast help you for no reason. Every time you come back to the main hub, you walk past the same couple of NPCs saying the same exact thing, conveniently related to whatever mission you just did. You have to listen to them repeat the same bit every time you do any optional mission. Half the missions feel like uninspired filler. MINOR SPOILER: As you've seen in the trailer, there are  Similarly, missions seem random and do not progress your goal. The PC's motivation the entire game is to kill a mysterious Silver Talon to collect on a bounty. The bounty is 250,000 credits. All endgame upgrades cost upward of 100,000 each. You gain probably over a million credits chasing this person. You have no other motivation at any point in the game. It's like if instead of looking for Ciri and saving the world, Geralt's grand quest was to kill a drowner that pays 100 orens instead of 20. Despite this, you go on mission after mission to slaughter hundreds upon hundreds of gang grunts. They tried to do an unimaginative twist at the end, but failed utterly - I didn't think "aha, I suspected this!", I thought "Oh. I don't care and never did." The ending has no implications on the world of WH40k, Necrormunda, or even to the main character. The optional missions are bad and janky. When I was deciding on whether to do one, I was never thinking "Am I ready for this?" or "Should I risk it for some extra cash?", I was thinking "Do I really want to invest the time and effort into killing some random dudes for flimsy non-story reasons in the same map I just finished or can I finally move on to the next story mission? There are only  story missions. Most of them are dumb filler. Some parts of missions are dumb filler, such as "There are no enemies in this large room. Run around and find 6 batteries on random shelves to proceed. Found the batteries? Door still won't open, gotta oil it now. Go find the oil button above the door, then come back to the controls and open it again. No enemies or anything this whole time. The jank is apparent in such things as the mission immediately fading to black when completed. No extraction. Example: the optional mission is to kill 20 special enemies. You're thrown into a big room or a piece of a level with infinitely respawning enemies. Some of them are "special". As soon as the final bullet touches the 20th "special" enemy, everyone stops shooting, you stop moving, screen fades to black and says "mission accomplished" and takes you back into the hub. Janky, weird, boring, unfinished.The AI is absolutely broken. I am hardly exaggerating when I say I killed 50% of this game's enemies by standing across a large room and shooting at them with impunity. Other reviewers mention that the AI is janky, but it isn't just that. It's broken. If you're a certain distance from the enemy, they will not notice you even as you shoot them. They won't react, take cover, try to shoot back. This distance is smaller than many larger rooms and long corridors, and the game even has a sniper rifle and a long scope you can fit to any weapon, which achieves magnification that wouldn't be practical at any range short of the range AI don't react to being shot. If an enemy does notice you, they will almost never try to shoot you from far away - they will run straight at you very slowly to get right up in your face to start shooting - even if we're in a large open room. They will queue up to climb ladders to get to you while you shoot them. They will randomly stop shooting. They will not flank you or use any tactics. They will spawn right on top of you, in front of you, and in closed rooms, CONSTANTLY. This is more apparent since your useless dog lets you see through walls and you SEE them spawn. Many MANY times they spawned within a few feet in front of my face.Psyker enemies teleport right on top of you and are immediately vulnerable to finisher, which renders you immune to damage for the duration. You end up killing entire hordes of them by slowly brutalizing them one by one while being riddled with bullets spending 95% of the time in unkillable animation. Conclusion in comments

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the strangest games I've ever played. Not game play wise but critically, You can almost physically feel the untouched potential emanating from the screen. It's a constant fistful of getting your impression to change between Positive and Negative, like Necromunda could of been great but instead it's just good in certain aspects.The game feels like if Doom Eternal 3-Pump Chumped Borderlands, and then Necromunda came out because Borderlands was convinced not to abort. Then growing up Necromunda tried really hard to lead a promising life.It almost seems as if Streum dumped about 85% of the funding they had into the Level Design team because the environments in this game have plentiful moments of eye candy. Everything else though was told to take a massive hike. The Animation quality is subpar at best, I think the only real interesting animation work that was done with this game were the first-person executions. Other than those gameplay moments the cutscenes feel like 4 minuted baked SFM shorts, and then there are other moments like the load screen in between levels where your character walking is using some sort of Unity animation pack. But then it gets weird because there will be moments of the character interacting with stuff and the animation looks like a guy literally sold his life span for the quality just out of no where.The Gunplay feels really left out on, as if you don't really feel much incentive or reason to swap between guns best suited for comboing or taking down certain enemies. You kind of just find a good gun and stick to that one gun while occasionally swapping to change it up every now and thenThe movement is okayish, I mean it plays like what they tried pulling from Doom Eternal but they kind of rushed the prospect of adding flav to what Doom Eternal squeezed out onto the plate. And now we have really borked wall-runningThe Voice Acting has it's moments, Not much of it occurs but when it does it's a mixed plate of Talent.The Story is mid, It's not great but its passable to just sort of shrug off and not mind to much. It's plot pacing and writing is (to me) most similar to Shadow Warrior in some manner.In short, Cop the game on sale instead. It has its moments but not well enough for $40.00 USD

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda Hired Gun rests its foot on the accelerator of dynamism and violence, yet it has an imprecise aim. Many of its problems derive from strictly technical stumbles, some of which can be solved with special updates (such as bugs or application crashes), while others are innate in its playful DNA, and have to do with feedback from the shots almost totally absent, with an artificial intelligence crude beyond belief, and with a general flatness of the shootings. _childDocuments_.review: If you know what you're getting into, I can recommend it easily.This isn't a highly polished game, there's a lot of jank (some interaction lag and 'glory' kills come out too fast and blurry, even with motion blur turned off) but here's the thing...It honestly delivers what it promises.First and foremost, if you're a 40k fan, you're already use to dealing with 40k games ranging across the spectrum of great to absolute smoldering slag.  This is a solid 7/10 but if you're a fan, especially of Necromunda you'll just be happy to finally see this place face to face.  The art department here can't be commended enough and the movement is "almost" as great as Titanfall 2's--it can get a little floaty but hard truth, I'd rather that than having cement shoes on.It's a really weird universe we live in when 40k FPS's are super rare and even more weird that good ones are somehow harder to find.  However, this easily hits "top 5 best Warhammer" video games for me!

_childDocuments_.review: An inexcusably clunky Inventory system prevents it from ever being anything better than a 7/10 FPS, but if you are looking for an immersive Warhammer 40K shooter, then this is it. But if you're looking for Borderlands 3 in the grimdark of the 41st century, then we're going to have to wait until they hire better writers and gun designers.  Still, I'm enjoying this a lot for a fresh release, and look forward to where the devs will take this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid buy, no doubt. It may be arguable if it is worth the 40 dollar asking price, but I definitely think so. If it goes on sale though, it is a definite must buy for shooter fans.Basically this game seems like the developers looked at the DOOM reboots and said: What if Necromunda Warhammer though?And it definitely delivers that. From the visceral combat to the slapping soundtrack and all the flowing mobility with the double jump, dash, and grappling hook. Its fast paced, fairly challenging on harder difficulties, and totes the graphical style to hold up to the Warhammer name. All the environments feel gritty, grimy, and seem to ooze slime along with detail. Definitely not a perfect game, and it's lacking the spit and polish of the DOOM reboots they are so clearly inspired by, but if you liked Id's new DOOM remakes you will almost definitely love this game.Small warning: The game stutters a lot when you first start playing it, no matter what system you play it on. I have it on Xbox Series X as well as PC (3060/5700xt) and both of them stutter pretty hard for the first 2 minutes of gameplay. But once it gets going, this almost completely stops even after loading into new levels.Campaign is pretty short, but there is some good side content and the missions definitely offer replay value. Update: Came back to revisit after my first playthrough, and had to note the really cool new loading screen at the beginning showcasing your character and your cyberdog. Awesome. Oh did I mention you get a cyberdog that you can customize and outfit to look like a pitbull/death machine? Definitely a highlight of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Being a huge fan of both Warhammer 40,000 and FPS, I'm used to disappointing/limited choices when the two are paired. I've played Deathwing extensively and even played the little known game Fire Warrior which will soon pass 20 years (hard to believe)...neither has impressed me.I must say that disappointment has ENDED with this game. It is fabulously executed and tons of fun.As others have noted and you are probably aware, this game is VERY similar to DOOM in pace and gunplay. Your character runs around like he's on crack and there is no "stealth" or walk button to be found. Frankly, I'm surprised you can even crouch in the game to be honest. There is still plenty of cover to use to kill the pace when needed and give your character a much needed break.There's a perfect variety of weapons, not too much and not too little and the gun effects and sounds are great on a good sound system or pair of headphones with satisfying audio that punches through and really gives that impression of hard hitting ballistics. Tons of upgrade options are available for those interested in doing so.Enemies, while not a group of John Wicks, provide a decent challenge, especially on hard and above. The enemy is cunning and It's very easy to get swarmed or shot in the back if you aren't careful.The upgrade system is robust and intuitive, although the buy/sell mechanism can be clunky at times and confusing for new players.Finally...the visuals are stunning on Ultra. I run a 3060 ti, which is MORE THAN ENOUGH for this game, which can be run on much lesser GPUs. I love the little touches such as the animated candle flames on the pause menu. When you look at touches like this, it makes you appreciate the detail put into the game.If there was one thing that bothered me is that you sometimes forget that this is a Warhammer 40,000 game. This can be either a good or bad thing, depending on your view of the universe or your investment in the Warhammer 40,000 universe. This is more likely due to the limited coverage of Hive worlds, lorewise, rather than fault of the game. Nevertheless, you are often reminded of where you are as many buildings, decor, and entities remind you that you are, indeed in the 40k universe. Even at full price, the game is well worth it.If Darktide is anywhere near as good as this, I'll be more than happy to sign up for that one too!In summary...Combat paceGun mechanics and soundVisuals ChallengeReplayabilityEnemy designLevel of detail/nice touchesSometimes does not feel like a Warhammer 40,000 gameCan be a bit confusing in the beginningMenu navigation can be challengingStore/Upgrade mechanics take a bit of getting used toMany have complained about bugs. I've yet to encounter any...

_childDocuments_.review: A solid thumbs up to this game.Did you want to play Vermintide but without coop, with loot you can get during the mission (and is actually rewarding) and guns? This is it.Detailed gun customization straight from Call of Duty, Loot of different quality, Secret chests that do actually take some time to find, Doom-like controls with double jumps, long jump, hook and wall run, no cooldowns so go crazy.Different passive and active skills to purchase for yourself and your dog.Different items to boost your character on top of it.Huge maps where in most cases enemies already present and not just spawn on you out of thin air.Decent graphics for what it is, runs in 1440p in solid 108-120 fps in Ultra. At the very beginning there was some stutter but it might be caching as it was gone afterwards.Sounds could be better, but good enough. Gore is on point, shooting enemies with a shotgun have a solid thump to it with enemies reduced to gibs.It's a Warhammer 40k FPS and without the usual Space Marines, great.After their struggles with Deathwing they finally got it right. Now all they gotta do is follow the Vermintide steps and expand the game.Not an AAA game by any means and it shouldn't be expected.A surprise to be sure, but a welcome one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with a quick answer to a question. Should you buy this game? It depends. If you just want a short single player shooter with little depth, this is probably worth it. If you want a game you can play for hours upon hours, this game is definitely not for you.On release: This game had some performance issues and bugs that got past quality assurance teams. While this isn't necessarily unexpected at this point, certain bugs made me almost have to restart entire levels simply because mission critical doors wouldn't open. Luckily, I managed to use ANOTHER unintended bug to get around that with a bit of effort. Performance wise, I would say the game is a little too intensive on my hardware (my laptop still runs on a GTX 1060). Aside from that, I didn't really have any other problems with quality of the game.Gameplay: The gameplay feels like a slightly slower paced Doom Eternal. The only real difficult I ever encountered was when I had run out of ammo with no way to get more. The constant need to check for all the loot chests did get kind of irritating after a while. The contract system got repetitive after a while and purestrain genestealers were just not a fun enemy to fight. The story missions are the most fun part about the game, though.Story: I wasn't super invested in the story of the campaign, but to be completely honest, that's not what I was playing this game for. Considering its similarity to Doom's gameplay loop, that's not too surprising either.Dog: I thought the dog was neat, but it was very lackluster in gameplay.Overall Score: 6/10, still better than Twilight.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a diamond buried under a 1000 pounds of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. For me the answer to that question became clear fairly quick.The gunplay is amazing but the game is PLAGUED with issues that hold it back.  Frequent crashes, horrible input processing for controllers that make the game unplayable, extreme difficulty spikes that limit your ability to enjoy the aforementioned gunplay. The world building and lore are interesting but the implementation is so unpolished that the beauty is lost. On a lesser note, the animation quality is noticeably poor for games of the day. _childDocuments_.review: I was gonna compare this to E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy and it turns out this is the same developer. You can feel the same brand of weirdness across the board, from player movement to wacky plot delivery to the various game systems. Fortunately none of it is taken to the same level as E.Y.E hahaThe game is a bit buggy - I had to restart one mission because an event didn't properly trigger, and another because I fell through the world. Combat abilities allow you to approach combat in wildly different ways but it takes a bit of grind to afford unlocks so you can't really try stuff out for fun. A refund/respec option would made the game much better imo.Different enemy types fight in unique ways which is quite fun, unfortunately there's only one set of enemies so it does start to get stale after several missions.Weapons aren't very well balanced, it feels like some are just plain better than others. The loot quality system feels frustrating as a result. Oh and the inventory management system is flat out terrible.I really enjoyed combat as a whole (abilities, enemies, etc). Unfortunately it's delivered in a wrapper that feels more like a janky fan mod than a well crafted product. Tentatively recommended but only if you're super interested and it's on sale or in a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing many great FPS games like Doom, Bulletstorm, Rage, Borderlands this game felt like a low effort cheap product. It is an unsatisfying experience from start to finish. First, let's talk about good things. Graphics look nice and gunplay is good. Weapons are varied, and it's fun to use them. I'm actually surprised about that. These are the only good things about Necromunda. Rest of the game is pure garbage. Sound mixing is horrible. You can't hear the dialogue most of the time. Well, the dialogue is poorly written, so it is not that important I guess. Weapons take too much space. While reloading some weapons take up %50 of your screen and you can't see the enemies because of it. Grenades are useless and splash damage is ridiculous. I wasn't anywhere near the enemy, but I still got damaged by my own grenade. There are suppressors and stealth mechanics in this game but what is the purpose? This is a fastpaced FPS, why would you include a stealth mechanic. It is pretty useless, after you kill one enemy every enemy on the map knows your exact location and starts to bomb rush you. Your dog companion is a missed opportunity just like everything in this game. Level design is so clustered and complicated that most of the time I couldn't understand where I should go. Because %80 of the levels and textures look the same it is pretty easy to get lost. At least they put waypoint beacons, thanks to these beacons navigation becomes easier. Grappling hook sometimes work and sometimes doesn't. Animations are janky. They are janky as sh*t! Watch a cutscene in the game, and you'll understand what I mean. It seems that developers also knew how sh*tty the animations were so they hid them behind a shaky camera. While you are performing a killing animation camera goes ape shi*t and you can't see jack sh*t. It is really nauseating after 2 or 3 animations. Finally let's talk about the most frustrating thing that nearly made me break my keyboard. Infinitely respawning enemies. This trash mechanic doesn't serve any purpose other than slowing the player and interrupting the gameplay flow. Also enemies spawn behind your back without any warning and because of this garbage mechanic you lose health. In Doom, when a demon is about to spawn you have both audio cues and visual cues. In this f*cking game they just spawn and start shooting at you. One time, I killed an enemy and another one popped right on top of the dead one's corpse. F*ck off dude! If you want to play a cheap Doom clone made by talentless hacks Necrosh*t Hired Jank is your game. Just go watch the launch trailer. Even in launch trailer you can't see more than 5 seconds of uninterrupted gameplay. Because devs knew they were releasing a pile of dogsh*t and they tried to hide it as much as possible. If you haven't played Doom, go and play that. If you have played Doom, play again. This game isn't worth the money and isn't worth the time you spent on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers ahead This game started out as a fun little romp though Necromunda, but it rather quickly slid into a short,depressing slap in the face of 40k fans. Not only is the game barely 8 hours in length for the campaign, but the lack of an ending, nausea inducing melee animations, and lack of overall variety in game play styles leads me to believe that there will be an enhanced edition, or massive amounts of payed dlc.   but the rest of the filling of this game is random side missions that are the same 4 variants : defend the area, rescue target, destroy X amount of Y, or Kill Target, all of which is filling reputation bars for the different factions, that do nothing other then give not faction specific weapons. The story over all is near impossible to follow, with cut scenes jumping from one static model to another, before throwing you into a new kill arena, with several of the bosses just teleportation you into there arenas with no explanation  The wall running mechanic is well done, though the lack of open spaces, save for big killing areas, makes it hard to implement it into the style of play the devs intended. I personally just used DOOM 2016 style of go very fast and double jump.  The Sparse amount of weapons in this game, totaling 14 by my count,  has a fair amount of customization, but is mostly cosmetic, the attachments doing barely any noticeable difference. Along with the player customization is abysmal, only allowing for 5 of the same outfit of different colors .I had fun with this game in the beginning, but only 3 levels in, the fun of blasting another ganger in the face with the Emperors blessed bolter, ran dry. I got this game on sale at  $34 US, and its still not worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky and frustrating.  Avoid.Pros:* The shooting is really fast paced and can be fun.* The visuals are great.  It really feels like you're running around the dirty, disgusting underbelly of a giant hive city.* Your dog companion is pretty cool, but until you level him up quite a bit he'll be spending most of his time on cooldown.* The levels are big and have lots of nooks to explore.Cons:* The UI for menu navigation is a hot mess.  Seriously, I haven't seen a UI this poorly designed in about 20 years.* Leveling up is grindy and repetitive.  You'll spend a LOT of time in the same few levels, fighting the same handful of enemies.* Instant melee takedowns are incredibly overpowered.  There's no buildup or weakening required, just get close to an enemy and slap the interact button.  You're invulnerable during the animation and they restore health. You can clear whole levels just zipping from enemy to enemy doing takedowns.* Wall-running is clunky and works inconsistently.I could go on, but honestly the game just isn't worth the time it would take to write up a longer review.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna lie, I definitely understand the criticism this game has received. And for the most part i think it is valid. It's clunky, voice acting is sometimes poorly mixed and overall pretty bland and bad, the fact that there is a loot system makes weapon modding for the most part obsolete and it is all in all rough around the edges. There is no denying that.However i didnt really mind all of this. I personally believe the game is fun to the extend that i can actually look above all of those things. A lot of people call this game a DooM/Titanfall knockoff. And yes, while there are similarities to those games I think the game does one thing better than the others and that is: It works it's mobility in the vertical rather than the horizontal. It offers so many possibilities in terms of mobility: double jump, dash, grappling hook and wall running. You can essentially fly over the map and it's an absolute blast to play for me. Visually it is amazing. Not in terms of graphics. Those are clearly outdated and you can absolutely see where they had to make budget cuts. But the beauty for me lies in the games visual design. While I am not a Warhammer Nerd/Expert I still do appriciate lots of it's designs and details to look at.. And exploring the more or less open world areas can be really fun and rewarding. In terms of story I cant say much. I believe there is one. And it might be even interesting for people who are very deep into the 40k lore. I do not know. But the bad voice acting and writing makes it absolutely forgetable to me. So I cant really tell.Unfortunately what people dont see is the fact that this is the 3rd project of a small french studio called "Streum On Studio". A studio that I wouldnt even consider AA in terms of size and experience. But they make up for it in passion and love for detail. I see that and I appriciate it a lot. And i think that is some of the reason while I can look past the bad. That and the hands done (even tho rough) fun gameplay.Would I recommend the game for full prize? Oof. I honestly dont know. Dont get me wrong, the game is amazing and I love and recommend you play it. But I feel like some of the criticism is valid. And considering that and the lack of polish I personally believe that 40 bucks is a bit overprized. I'd argue that 25-30 would be a solid deal. Note: The devs seem very active and engaged. They've already released 2 major patches adressing some of the issues. (not all of them obviously)

_childDocuments_.review: Separate reviews for 40k fans and non 40k fans with a conclusion for both:For non Warhammer 40k fans: the game starts off feeling a lot like Metro 2033, as you crawl through one sewer grate over ruined building to the next. Combat starts and the heavy metal starts playing and it begins feeling like Doom, as you deliver one takedown after the other, your guns roaring seemingly nonstop. Your characters grim one liners one after the next makes it feel like a Judge Dredd film. All of these together define Warhammer 40,000.For 40k fans: It was fantastic to see a hive city like Necromunda fleshed out. Distant machinery thundering along with leaky pipes miles above in the dome mimicking an artificial thunderstorm was amazing. The game looks great and is constantly reinforced by the sound and feel of the guns, the visuals of the gangs and the 2nd star character (after your dog) the dome runner Jano, being the most believable 40k character in the game. Well done all around. The story however was more of a confusion then the first 12 of Abaddon's black crusades. I would consider myself well read on things Necromunda, even Kal Jerico, But they definitely reached on this one, it was not a smooth transition from one plot point to the next - by Helmawr I have no idea what they were trying to portray with it.Conclusion:My biggest gripe with this game goes along with Necromunda Underhive Wars. Why the ♥♥♥♥ are we only seeing 3 of the 5 main houses of Necromunda? They're mentioned at least, along with a handful of the other factions. Its like leaving 2 main characters out of a story - you're hurting the setting far more than helping. Necromunda is massive - an abundance of factions and foes that you almost can't keep track of in the beginning makes the setting feel massive. Maybe they'll be added DLC like Underhive Wars, but having only 25% of the setting released initially is beginning to drag.Besides a few bugs, slight clunkiness, parts of the story, and some aspects like your dog feeling pointless - the game was solid. Have a few drinks and in a couple of sittings you'll knock the main story out. This game has serious potential if the developers revisit it after the feedback from the release. Future dlc + a few reworks could leave this as one memorable game, standing tall amongst the giants like Dawn of War Dark Crusade.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is great. The gameplay is fun. The enemy AI leaves a little to be desired. The game is pretty short, and the "endgame" is basically nonexistent. It feels like a solid framework for a much larger game. I envision something like Destiny 2, but across Necromunda (not sure a single bounty hunter story works across the whole of W40k universe where individuals are insignificant and death comes easily), but to achieve something like that, the skills will need to be reworked, the armor and equipment will need a rework as a single piece for your entire armor set kills the "loot chase" for that slot, the way weapons work currently seems fine, but there is too few quality levels (across all items) and too little difference between quality levels and it kills the desire to hunt for +3s. The inventory system is kind of clunky. The game will need multiplayer, at least cooperative, and this will require a larger "hub area". I also think that since each area is loadable at any time anyways by queuing up a bounty, the bounties should NOT load you in and you should be able to walk out of Martyrs End and navigate through areas to the one the bounty is for. Obviously this would include loading screens, so functionally it would be the same as before for area size and processor load/gpu load, but would give the feel of "travelling" across Necromunda, even if often each loading screen is just found at a train station or tunnel that could technically "go anywhere". This would also allow fast travel and a map that could bring Necromunda to life. I feel like this game has the potential to compete with Destiny 2 for online looter shooter, more so than borderlands or any other offering, but a lot of its subsystems would need reworks... and it would have to happen without damaging the current gameplay or aesthetic. Huge potential, fun game, not enough content. I kinda follow a rule that if I can get 1 hour of fun for each dollar I spent, the game is a good game. I spent 33$ and I am to 27 hours of enjoyment so far as I write this, so its close.... really close, but Ive run out of things to do. Would pay monthly easily for an MMO version of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing honestly, 5/10 right now. Wait a good year or so...Everything felt rushed & unpolished. Game play feels like a chaotic mess, & not in a good way. It honestly comes across something from the 2006 - 2012 (think something like BulletStorm, but not nearly as smooth as that). The animation is god awful right now. For example, whenever you summon your dog, it literally just spawns next to you like a code command! You could have done something nice with this, like have him jump into frame from behind your character or something! Another example is the "Brutes" (I think they're called that...), they come across as a Unreal engine plug-in /place holders for Orcs, & they just re-skinned them! The moment they start to attack you or try to move around, it becomes blatantly obvious that this was put in in alpha & hasn't been changed since... Oh & "Take-Downs" look awful too. Think Doom, but with the models & camera going nuts.Again, I had fun with this game, but right now it's not worth the 40$. Maybe 20$ at the moment(Give it a year, I feel like most of this jank will be gone by then...). If you really want something that's a fast-paced sci-fi with some parkour elements, try either TitanFall 2 or GhostRunner.

_childDocuments_.review: After 27 hours and all achievements unlocked, I think I can finally drop a review.Hired Gun is a game with real qualities, and real flaws. I'll list them and try to remain as objective as possible. <The qualities (or "good" points)>- a nervous, efficient, fast and brutal gameplay similar to the new DOOM games- slides, double-jumps, grappling hook and wall running work really well- a good level design and a great art direction that depicts the grim, gothic underhive of Necromunda perfectly- different powers available (bullet time, auto-aim, berzerk...)- good feeling with most weapons- great soundtrack that jumps from atmospheric, quiet tracks to raging industrial metal- it respects the original material ; the fans of 40k would appreciate that- you can pet the dog!<The flaws (or "bad" points)>- almost every technical aspect of the game is flawed ; the game suffers from framerate drops, crashes and the optimisation is just not good. From my experience, those crashes tend to occur mostly during loadings, or in menus. It's definitely frustrating. This is *the* main issue of the game.- the game is short if you don't play around and just focus on the campaign.  A shame because the levels are great, and have a real identity. Sometimes you feel that more would be welcome! I definitely wanted more- plasma weapons do not feel very satisfying to use (but at least they do no explode!)- the dog is a skill, not a constant pet. You have to summon the good boy if you want him to help you in combat- the ending is a bit too quick. The final fight is tense, but the ending itself could have been better, more satisfyingDo I recommend it? Well, you probably noticed the blue thumb, so yes I do. Hired Gun is a cool game, especially if you need a quick shot of a fast paced shooter, that takes place in a rather unique setting. The gameplay works fine, no doubt about it. It's intuitive, it's nervous and overhaul fun to play. Also, Streumon being a very small studio, do not expect a triple A DOOM-like. Better know what you buy. Again, in my opinion, the only real problems (and they are, indeed, problems) are the technical aspect. The devs are actively working on fixing the issues, but the risk of crash is present (never experienced any data corruption tho).If it's too much of an issue for you, then I'd definitely recommend to wait a bit, until patches drop. But at the end, I genuinely believe the game is worth it. It just needs to be polished. I hope this review was informative enough and as objective as possible. Yes the game is flawed, but yes it is also fun to  play. And as 40k/Necromunda fan, I've been quite glad to explore this universe once more.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes It's hard being a 40k fan - time after time disappointment after disappointment (see also - Dawn of war 3, Eternal Crusade, Titanicus dominus, Warhammer gladius)This game is something I WANT to love but there's some really serious flaws that really drag this downI've got to give fair credit - the environment is absolutely amazing, they really nailed the aesthetic side of this game, each and every level is a beautiful work of art but then it's all down hill after thatthe sound design is APPALLING - enemies can literally run up behind you with no noise what so ever and there's huge chunks of effects that should be there but simply aren't (huge boulders landing, completely silent lifts etc etc)  - and while the  metal sound track is good I honestly don't think it belongs in a 40k game - NPC dialogue is deadpan with the same lines often repeated over and over again as the enemies charge at you.the "side" missions are just random objectives on maps you've already completed - and they give you a grappling hook that literally is coded to not work on specific sections to stop you from going places - it's also completely possible to just effortlessly walk out of the map (no bugs, just walk across a bridge, round a corner, and you're out)they give you 5 weapons slots but for some reason they lock two of them into being pistols only (on top of a further 3rd mandatory pistol), greatly hampering what would otherwise be some nice weapon variety and I can't fathom why they would do this. The game also heavily advertises your cyber mastiff companion, who is oddly on a cooldown for some inexplicable reason and more often than not gets stuck in places because you as the player are way more mobile than the dog, so you spend more time without him than with.half of the UI functionality is never explained and the PC control are weirdly janky at best (for instance, having to press ESC. to continue???) This was clearly rushed to get it out the door for the yearly skullthrone sale and I really wish the developers weren't pushed into this, because it's clear that love and care went into this game - it just need another 6 months to a year to clear up the jank - I hope the devs can pull a no man's sky with this one - I would love to give this a thumbs up.
