_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know much of anything about Warhammer 40K. I know there’s a God Emperor, I know there’s Space Marines, Inquisitors, giants and elves and Nergal and whatever other scattershot knowledge comes from a general proximity to nerd spaces and the occasional digital foray into the universe. What I know very well is E.Y.E.: Divine Cybermancy, one of the wildest, jankiest, most fascinating FPS I’ve ever played on the PC. Combine the developers of E.Y.E. with the wealth of 40K’s unknown wonders and the collision results in Necromunda: Hired Gun.	An FPS carrying on some of E.Y.E.’s traditions with RPG systems in the form of gear and optional augmentations (refitted, I should presume, to the Warhammer setting), Necromunda has less of the slapdash construction of its predecessor and much sturdier bones. For example, I didn’t even need to restart once due to becoming utterly lost and feeling as if I had missed something. From the jump I could click with just about all the gameplay concepts presented to me, probably because they read like a greatest hits of the last five years or so of FPS – you’ve got Titanfall’s wall running and grappling hook, NuDoom’s emphasis on aggressive action and even more aggressive guitar riffs, the speed and brutality of the remade Wolfenstein games. If it sounds derivative well, there’s a reason for that, and I don’t know necessarily that it’s more than the sum of its parts but it doesn’t matter much when the sum works out to fast, efficient movement through enemy-infested arenas navigated with a wealth of skills.	The cleanness comes at the expense of some ambition. The same way this feels like a list of “That’s cool, let’s do that” from recent games, E.Y.E. felt like a list of cool things pulled from all sorts of places beyond games, up to and including most of Warhammer’s setting. Which makes for a good fit here, since 40K is so incredibly packed with character it’s hard for a game that does even a passing decent job of capturing the setting to feel thin on the worldbuilding front.	The sense of incredible scale in 40K is what has always appealed most to me and Necromunda, set on one of the universe’s literally unbelievably overpopulated, overindustrialized, hyperdense Hive Worlds is a perfect showcase of that scale. Statues of saints and heroes fill out cavernous rooms and precipitous drops through lattices of rusted, breaking catwalk. Fire spurts into the sky from smokestacks, steam and vapor fill out the narrow passages between towering pipelines, one entire level takes place on the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ train you can imagine. 	For as brilliant as these are aesthetically they lack a bit in design, usually just corridors linking rooms with the occasional inspired verticality, all the better navigated with the grapnel gun provided rather early on. 	What happens inside those spaces makes up for them being gorgeous boxes and tubes. An early tooltip advised me to observe enemies, because they all behave differently. Knowing that E.Y.E. was a game in which foes hurled themselves at me with reckless abandon, I wondered what the interceding years might have taught Streumon Studio. I guess it taught them to fib on loading screens. 	But that’s okay, because foes hurling themselves at me turns out to make Necromunda the great experience that it is. There’s a plethora of ways to dispatch foes – the shooting, of course, with 40K staples like bolters and plasma guns, but also powers granted by augments like Crush that let you move instantly to melee range with a literal bang, or Blast that...you can guess that one, or Perfect Aim which also I guess you can guess these names aren’t exactly clever. I was a big fan of the Strength Booster that handles like a powerup of old, ditching your gun in favor of knife and boot that will kill in two hits if they don’t kill in one.        There’s also a dog you can call in, a beautiful mastiff who perfectly represents what bits of jank do remain in the formula. I’ve seen a lot of folks call this eurojank, the specific kind of held-together-with-spit-and-rubber-bands feeling of staid classics like S.T.A.L.K.E.R. or Gothic or the entire publishing catalog of Focus Home Interactive (ed: guess who published this game)(Brad: I am ed, I have no ed, these reviews would be better if I did alas I must rely on a Bit). But that, to me, speaks to the sort of 7/10 game that is immensely fascinating despite the fact that the game engine is actually just a prayer, half the systems don’t work exactly or at all until a modder finds a .ini tweak six years after release, the animations seem to have forgotten the existence of kneecaps, and if I pick a female character I will be misgendered the entire game.	See, that mastiff is pretty eurojanky, he comes in at the squeeze of a rubber rat and warps around while barking itinerantly and pinning down single enemies at a time and getting in between your bullets and your enemies too often. But that’s pretty much it. There’s some animation snafus, the bossfights are a twitchy slog of occasional instadeath, there was a time I needed to restart a mission because the game kept respawning me out of bounds, you can sort of break progression by grinding side missions for not-that-long to purchase every augment upgrade very early on… 	That’s not a eurojank list of problems, that’s just a regular one. This is an ordinary 7/10 game, the kind of thing people will refer to as a guilty pleasure and I will hiss a little because there is nothing guilty about the pleasure of Crushing a pack of enemies, double jumping up, backdashing out, Blasting four more, and grapelling away to safety before anyone hits you, all while your dog warps desperately to keep up. 	And like, you try to keep up with the story, probably. I suspect that being a Warhammer 40K fairweather fan was not the impediment here, the story is told mostly through disjointed cutscenes that fade to black back and forth between folks in conversation (usually the player character of choice – mine was a cool Asian lady with an utterly baffling accent – and a boss called something like Spite ♥♥♥♥) and chit chats with a few allies in the hub area. It’s very basic stuff, you’re a Hired Gun, which is what it sounds like, chasing after a high value target. Kal Jerico is here, which probably is enough to make some people go “Oooh!” but I went “Huh” at the funny man with little braided hairs, and there’s a late game reveal I figured meant something to someone but when I googled a character’s name the sole result was “Val Kilmer Deus Ex” which, honestly, sums this game up. The review is over, I could have lead with that and gotten the point across. Go home. And play Necromunda: Hired Gun if you want a good-not-great, head empty sort of shooting experience rounded out by a very weird dog.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: it's a linear shooter where you go through levels and shoot everyone in the face. With titanfall/codbo3 movement. Sure, there is rudimentary upgrade system and some resemblance of loot, but it's so simplistic you could ignore it. You ain't looting stuff, you are selling stuff. It looks and sounds as much 40k as possible, it's tries hard to be immersive and true to the source material. And yeah, it's janky as you would expect, it's a budget title from an indie developer.It's also quite fun when it clicks (it often doesn't tho) and it's true to the bone WH40k experience. And what's most important it's not boring like all previous action games in WH40k were cursed to be. It's the first time you got FUN 40k shooter game, you know.People who expect looter shooter would be disappointed - it's all about the money, not the hardware. The whole system designed this way so inventory management doesn't stop the game to a grinding halt when you are on a level - you can swap gun instantly if you found one, but everything else goes to "I'll sort crap out after the level is finished" blackhole. And you can't even take everything to your base, crap gotta be sold if it doesn't fit you pockets. All guns are identical - there is a tier and a type and that's it. The game basically forces you to sell everything and build your own gun instead. You take on a missions, sell crap, get money, buy stuff you need, rinse, repeat. Levels are quite expansive, beautiful, with great lighting and design and are interesting to explore, there is cutscenes and setpieces. Level designers clearly have a raging boner for 40k style. Performance could be better, I guess. And the game is raw, man. Like unfinished raw. Bugs, glitches and all sort of things happen all the time, but nothing game breaking.The game's a must for 40k fans that eager not only to dive into the world and soak in atmosphere, but alo to play at least something fun. And it's somewhat solid recommendation for anyone else - it's still a fun FPS game if you don't expect it to be something that it isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok when it works. As far as Doom clones go, it follows the formula pretty well and I personally really enjoyed the high amount of customization that you had on your guns. Being able to put a scope on a double-barreled shotgun and reconfigure it to make a slug shooting sniper was really entertaining. Unfortunately, there are just way to many issues that can't be ignored. The game is extremely janky and buggy, and also very unpolished; many have discussed gamebreaking bugs before me, but as far as polish goes the "glory kill" animations are messy, enemies will literally spawn in front of you with NO warning what so ever, and the gun play feels... inconsistent. I could list many more.Add on top of this the questionable writing and story and it just doesn't work. I feel like this game could've been really good if they just took time with it and focused on the polish, bug fixing, and presentation rather than trying to add in as many bells and whistles as possible. The customization options and variety of mechanics are fun, sure, but you can't enjoy them when you can't even consistently play the game!Overall, it was a great recipe but didn't get enough time in the oven. As Gordon Ramsay would say, "IT'S ♥♥♥♥♥♥' RAW!" Do yourself a favor and if you are interested, DO NOT buy at full price. Not worth $40.

_childDocuments_.review: ❤️💔🤍🤍🤍The second you get into the game, you’ll know if the game will be playable for you or not. The Field of View (FOV) can cause a massive fisheye effect, making the world look distorted. Simply increasing the FOV doesn’t help either, it just makes the effect even worse. I’m sensitive to narrow FOV as it can make me feel nauseous, but thankfully the default value was okay for me and my screen. Problems with this game continued as I selected my character at the very beginning of the game. After I clicked a few of the portraits, some bug occurred and the portrait on the right suddenly didn’t match my selection on the left, so I had to restart the game. Not great to encounter bugs within the first minute of the game. Before I get into even more of the problems I encountered, I do want to take a moment to appreciate what I liked. The environmental design is great. There’s some good Warhammer 40K visuals, and the larger-than-life architecture of the hive world is portrayed well. There’s also an excessive amount of gore suitable to the grimdark setting. The character design is great. There’s a lot of combat with House Esher, a gang of punk rock Amazonian women that are both pretty and deadly. I also appreciated that this game leaned more towards a classic design philosophy for House Esher (toned waistlines and thin limbs) as opposed to the figurine redesign in 2017. In terms of gameplay, the shooting felt fine. I ended up getting an upgrade that let me slow down time for everyone except myself, so that made the game feel like  on steroids, which I thought was enjoyable. There were quite a few options to choose from, so I’m sure there’s something interesting for different playstyles. The developers tried to incorporate some  movement and also put in a grappling hook for traversal. It works well enough. There’s no fall damage, which was fun even though it got a bit silly at times. Anyway, back to the problems. After playing a couple of missions, I encountered a bug where my weapon just stopped working. I couldn’t shoot, reload or anything, and had to quit to the menu and load the last checkpoint, which fixed the problem at the cost of losing progress.  In a later mission, I had a boss fight where the boss decided to permanently disappear during the boss fight (did he fall through the floor?) and I ended up fighting infinitely spawning enemies and couldn’t progress without restarting the boss fight from the beginning. At one point the game stopped responding when I opened the upgrade screen, so I had to end the process in Windows Task Manager. The second to final boss in the game bugged out during the fight, and ended up just standing still in the middle of the room. In terms of lore, most dialogue is packed full of references to individuals and groups and it’s easy to feel overwhelmed. The game doesn’t do a good job introducing anything beyond just mentioning them.That is, if you can even figure out how to talk to NPCs to begin with. The game claims you’re supposed to walk up to them and press the interaction-key you’ve assigned, but the game seems very specific about when exactly you can do so. For example, the shopkeeper needs to finish her animation when you walk up to her, before you can enter the shopping screen. There’s this important story NPC you have to talk too as well. Every time the game wanted me to talk to him, nothing happened when I tried interacting with him. I had to jump around like an idiot, wiggle back and forth and then suddenly it randomly worked. No idea what was up with that. The inventory system is a mess. It feels very limiting as you are unable to access your inventory unless you’re on the mission preparation screen. It’s needlessly hard to compare items and the UI doesn’t feel streamlined for what it’s trying to do. I had problems finding information about items. In some menus, I’d hover the mouse over them or click on them, but it wouldn’t do anything while in other menus it worked. It felt inconsistent and the information wasn’t readily available when I needed it.  That said, the loot system wasn’t very imaginative to begin with. There’s nothing that modifies the gameplay, only raw numbers that get higher. You either get more health, more armor, or more crit chance. That kind of stuff. Still, if I’m trying to decide if I should sell or keep loot that I find, and I can’t see what I have equipped, well, the UI just isn’t functional. If you don’t care about the game being more than a little broken, and you’re interested in the visuals, theme, and setting, it’s okay enough to give it a playthrough on Easy as a mindless power fantasy, at least for a little while. That said, I’m not sure there’s anything here for anyone but the most hardcore Warhammer 40K fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trash of the best sort, I loved my time with it.Okay, it ain't trash, there's some great stuff in here (some of the combat, art design, soundtrack and the like) but it's all bogged down by half-baked systems (loot, character progression, faction system WITH TWENTY-ONE FACTIONS IN A LINEAR SHOOTER), clunky and rough animations, total lack of polish, uneven level design (both graphicaly and gameplay-wise, you get lost way more often than you should), uneven gunplay (while janky it feels good most of the time until you get to guns that block your view while reloading or shooting) and absolutely abysmal mishmash of poorly written dialogue and half-edited cutscenes that try their best at storytelling but fail so completely it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny.And bugs, tons of bugs. Clipping animations, glory kills that raise you one meter higher with each frame, broken skills and weapons that DELETE your oponents, ragdolls so bad that, when they get timed with the sound just right, produce true comedy gold of the best type. You get the idea. This ain't Cyberpunk's "so bad it's awful" bugs, it's the "so bad it's amazing" variety.And that's pretty much the game in general. For every dull moment, broken mechanic, absurd cutscene there's either some decent gameplay thrown in, or an amazing set piece (they *do* get Warhammer better than most studios do), a truly shocking look at the lore of the setting, or just some great bugs that make every level a unique experience.I enjoyed my time with Hired Gun immensely, either having fun with the game or having fun at the expense of it - But I had fun nonetheless. There's some real passion and idea thrown in here too, can't deny, including cool Warhammer additions (TITAN-CLASS TRAIN WAS METAL AF, I WANT A MODEL).So, yeah, is it a good game? Hell no. But damn me if it ain't one hell of an enjoyable one.Side note: Checked the credits, apparently the game didn't have any designers apart from the Lead Designer?... I guess it may be some nomenculature quirk, but still, case in point: Necromunda: Hired Gun is what you get when you create a game without designers - A broken mess that should be a case study at universities.Did I mention I loved almost every second spent playing it?Amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this brief: The Campaign is too easy, first. There aren't enough weapons, but the weapons that *do* make it in are pretty solid, aside from the fact that the sights don't line up on anything properly. The movement is supposed to give you an edge. It doesn't really. It just gives you vertigo, and the hostiles still hitscan you like no tomorrow. The voice mixing is awful. The dialogue sounds like it was written in french and then dubbed over using machine translation.The plot is paper thin. This is not a Necromunda game, it's a generic shooter story using Necromunda as flavor. The "twists" are contrived and literally don't matter. Don't expect even Doom Eternal levels of storytelling here, this ♥♥♥♥ is yoshi's island. The environments are beautiful. Get your screenshots in the native 75 FOV (seriously who's idea was this?). And to cap it alllll off, the main campaign takes about 10 hours, give or take 1. But, It's a Warhammer Product, and I've got to support the brand. Do I recommend it? ♥♥♥♥ no. Terrible game. Should you buy it? Yes, so we can get more Warhammer games. Maybe one will be good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is crazy!  I love the Warhammer 40K universe and this game definitely is the best I've seen in a long time.  The learning curve is a tad bit rough, it doesn't hold your hand and you have to figure stuff out for yourself but once you get the hang of things it is a fast paced crazy a** game.  The levels are gorgeous and very different from each other with plenty of areas to explore. The kill animations are crazy and over the top, Doom on steroids style. Aside from the campaign there are plenty of side bounty missions for various factions that are very rewarding and action packed with different objectives.  I've read several stories that take place in Necromunda and this game really has that feel.  As a bonus you also get to fight some Zenos!
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: As a 40K fan I was ecstatic when I heard about this game, now after playing it even after 4 patches I still can't recommend it. The gameplay is a weird mix of DOOM and Titfanfall 2 but it fails in both departments. I finished Doom 2016, Doom Eternal and Titanfall 2 on the highest difficulty levels (without permadeath) and I had a ♥♥♥♥ ton of fun! It was difficult sure but fun nontheless! Here? Nope... there's nothing fun about it, no matter the difficulty, because the gameplay is an unsatisfying mess that doesn't even know what in the Emperor's name it wants from you. Once you do one or two missions the feeling will creep up on you; that something is off here, that something is wrong, so very wrong. It's the realization that the game's combat simply does not have an idea of it's own identify. It tries to copy other games but it does a poor job at it and it feels like they added stuff that simply shouldn't be in there because it doesn't fit the gameplay at all. It's just Emperor damn awful.The side missions get repetitive fast because the combat isn't fun, the story is almost non-existent, the combat abilities are just there because they sound fun (they aren't) but honestly I see no use for them besides the one where you slow time. The weapons are really nice but the inventory system is annoying and frustrating.The only good thing about the game is the atmosphere and the locations and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did they do a really good job in making the maps. I love the maps and how big they are, which makes it even more painful that this game is such a mess. It also doesn't help that I've crashed a few times by now (even after all these patches) and my HUD disappeared at one point. That's really just the final nail in the coffin for me.As a 40K fan I really wanted to like, no, to LOVE this game but even the lack of 40K shooters on the market won't make me accept such a half assed, buggy mess. I'm gonna try and finish this game because I wanna see how this will end and I want to see more of the awesome maps but I wouldn't recommend the game just for that.If the devs are listening and plan on making another 40K game my suggestion is to work on the combat, sometimes less is better if it's more defined and aware of what it wants from the player. But keep the map making and atmosphere because those are the game's strongest points so far.

_childDocuments_.review: A janky, but functional fine and beautiful mess of a game.If you can get past the slight issues regarding some awkward animations and some other finnicky bits like the loot system, the gameplay is amazing. Extremely satisfying gunplay, overall great sound design for the weapons, and I cannot explain how much I love the movement.Many people here are saying to just play Doom. Yes, Doom is nice and sparkly and shiny and well polished and oh-dear-god-I-found-it-so-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-dull. Yes, on higher difficulties as well.As for the Space Marine game... Hnestly, I found that dull even on release. I had to force myself to finish it. It was good, but really didn't meet the praise I was given for it.Necromunda, however, is eurojank in the best way. It's just fun.Am I biased? Yes. I played E.Y.E. a decade ago when it first released. I have a huge tolerance for jank, and Streumon studios has a special place it my heart already. But the fact is that they put 'fun' and 'style' front and center.This is not "Good for a 40k game". That is a MASSIVE disservice.This is a great game. It's lacking a good bit of polish, but it's also not a full price release.If you are interested, I STRONGLY recommend MandaloreGaming's review on YouTube. He gives the game fair coverage. Not as a WH40K game, but as a game in its own rights.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a thumbs up because of its great 40k atmosphere with its gorgeous levels, great art design and decent audio. They were onto something with this. Clearly, the intention was to deliver a Doom (2016) style shooter with looting mechanics. Unfortunately, they've stumbled along the way. As authentic as the maze-like levels feel, they don't play well. The developers have great arena shooter movement and gunplay figured out but the combat revolves a lot around navigating complex levels while enemies that randomly spawn around you. Occasionally, you get some Doom-style open arena battles, and the game feels like a blast during those sequences. However, most of the game isn't nearly as exhilarating, a lot of chaotic hyper-fast movement in tight, intertwined corridors. I count these developers among the most promising in the shooter genre. But they've once again fallen victim to their ambition. Once again, they've tried too many things at once, resulting in a game that really doesn't succeed at anything other than atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... a nice game. But know, what you are signing up for.Well, it's a Streum On Studio game, and bears the marks of their previous games as well (EYE Divine Cybermancy, Space Hulk: Deathwing). By this I mean playing the game feels like it was developed by aliens, who themselves never played a video game, but had others describe the experience to them in great detail.If they want to implement something, they just do it, never mind whether it will work out just fine, or not at all. The result is an odd, occasionally frustrating experience with plenty of curios and glimpses of something awesome.The good:- Game (supposedly) looks absolutely beautiful. (I played low graphics, since my PC can't handle more).- Brutal, high-speed combat with plenty of devastating weapons.- Best WH40K FPS game out there.- Great level design (excecution is another matter).- Great style.- Doggo.The bad:- Total lack of balance: so many 1-hitting enemies, brutally strong shields on officers, and ridiculous health-pool of bosses.- Side mission balancing is ridiculous. Got instantly deleted when I first jumped into a B-level (weakest) side mission, had to learn to play entirely differently.- Even though the game tells that enemies shoot inaccurately while you are performing various parkour stunts, they don't really. Got sniped plenty times mid-air while flying on the grappling hook.- Lack of explanations both mechanics and story-wise. If the player is clueless about WH40K at the start, they will be none the wiser at the end. And I'd recommend to open up controls and read up what actions the character can do from there.- Using abilities feel bad. Clunky access, meele mode is utterly useless. No healing for ability kills. Although some of the abilities can be really satisfying. The game can be completed without using the special abilities, though later levels reqire the player to collect items to open up gates, that are hard to find without abilities.- Poor level execution. No clear indication what can be walked on / grappling hooked / wallrun. And falling to the depths is instant death. This makes platforming and high-speed parkour combat really really frustrating.- Most weapons and weapon mods are totally useless. They don't allow for different playstyles, they are the same as others, just worse.The ridiculous:- The game forces the player to keep the starting pistol always equipped, that is the worst weapon of the entire game.- There are enough slots to have every kind weapon in the inventory, but not actually, because for whatever reason, there is one additional slot for heavy weapons and one less of standard ones. Therefore no, you can't actually own all weapons simultaneously. I guess one of the weapons was misclassified, and no-one bothered fixing it. It's feature now.- The game is almost exclusively CQC focused, and most weapons kick like a mule, yet the customization options are full of high-magnification scopes.- Long, drawn-out execution animations are really immersion and pace-breaking.- It takes some time to get used to the immersion breaking grappling hook. It trags the player through walls, ceilings, any sorts of obstacle, like there is nothing in the way.And so on. I'm sure I left something out, but it's plenty as it is.I would not recommed purchasing at full price, but at 50% off, it's a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun tells a middling story within the walls of Warhammer 40k's infamous hive world.Performance is...a lot like the story. Middling. On a five year old system (i7-6700k, 16gb, MSI 1080) at 1440p I was able to keep a pretty steady 60 frames on Ultra but there are some definite stuttering issues when first loading into maps and before and after cutscenes.The gameplay is, in simplest terms, an arena shooter. For mobility you've got a dash, that can be performed on the ground and in the air, a double jump, wall running, and, after a few missions into the story, a grappling hook. It's all done well enough, there isn't anything spectacular about the motion but the combat is fast and frantic if you engage the enemies. Sitting back and picking them off, in most cases, turns into an infinite loop as most enemies seem to respawn until you pass a certain invisible checkpoint.The weapons are fun but some 40k staples are lacking in the sound department and general feel of the weapon. I expected a bit more percussion and THUD from the bolters while the plasma and lasguns feel okay, again middling.If you aren't a big fan of 40k I would say you can skip it but for someone like myself, that slaves over plastic crack, it's a lot of fun to see things like corpse-starch farms complete with massive, twirling grinders and the other nooks and crannies of Necromunda's hives and domes.

As far as the gameplay goes it's like DOOM but not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard, I always play on easy difficulty and I'm glad that the developers respect it, was hard to adapt to at first but usually because I don't know what I'm doing. _childDocuments_.review: Can be fun but the jank is real with this one. 10/10 for atmosphere and aesthetics, 4/10 for the story, 7/10 for the gameplay.To break it down, the atmosphere is 100% on-point for Necromunda and 40K in general. Corpse-starch factory with cathedral architecture? A train the size of a modestly-sized suburb? Can't see jack for lack of light? You got it all. The story is... there, for what it's worth. Unsatisfying is the word I'd use to describe it. You can have a story about a bounty hunter and not have everyone a cardboard cutout. To avoid what limited spoilers there are: there's no clear goals for anyone except your character (a fat payday). It's not so much mysterious or incomprehensible as just missing basic elements. They try to wrap things up with a monologue near the end that makes vague allusions but it doesn't pique any further interest. You can't really care about the human equivalent of a bag of potatoes.The gameplay itself is functional and I didn't encounter any particular bugs (so that was a plus) but my main complaints are with it feeling mainly underdeveloped. The mobility system was quite excellent with a grapple and wallrunning, allowing for smooth transition in gunplay. They did remember to add limited auto-aim during wallrunning so it's actually functional in combat. That part feels good, but the rest not so much.Gun customization is limited and there is no good explanation for the different elemental damage types. Why should you care between toxic, radiation, fire, or just basic damage? Was there a bonus damage thing for certain enemy types? All you see is your gun damage numbers go up. There's also zero augment customization, not sure why they list that as a selling point. You just buy them and they're yours forever.Why do I have four slots for armor? I'm only ever going to wear one at a time and there's no benefit to changing between them.Why is my dog appearing out of thin air with no clear cause? They could have added a simple teleportarium effect or had it climb out from behind a corner or something. It's also odd that there's a cooldown timer for the dog. Does he have to go and hide in a corner to lick himself clean every minute or so? That's a dangerous proposition, what with the jaw enhancements.Enemies do hit hard so it is decently difficult. They try to keep you in the fray with a limited period of health regen if you deal damage right after taking some or just letting you auto-kill any normal-sized human with an interact prompt, which also gives health back. The only thing limiting you from meleeing everyone into the floor is a knife cooldown. Knife cooldown - that's another weird thing. That could have been balanced some other way, like witth Doom (2016) where you had to damage them enough before getting your takedown goodie bag.I don't regret getting N:HG (which is why this is positive) but it's not worth full price. As of writing it's half off and I'd say that's fair for what you get. With a decent rework this could be an excellent game but as-is it's a decent one with good atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A very hard recommendation to give. Honestly most people will be put off with the janky, buggy, rough and terrible sounding game on offer here. The story is a little all over the place with a disappointing ending and side missions exist purely for money making and nothing else. The bugs weren't major but frequent (some of which I was genuinely impressed how they messed it up), fps drops (just little ones) were just as frequent and many moments of AA jank rear their ugly head, sometimes funny and sometimes frustrating, The voice acting is alright. Just alright. When you can hear it over the terrible mixing (devs are trying to fix so that's a plus). The characters don't have enough about them to make you care and the bounty hunter I picked sounded straight from an English Soap Opera (not a compliment). Now, if you are still with me and wondering how I still recommend this thing after that list? It's fun. Super fun. It's a mid tier, b tier, AA shooter with obvious influences from DOOM 2016 and eternal. It's fun to use these ridiculous OTT guns that pop enemies heads off. It's fun to use bionics to turn a couple of enemies into literal puddles of gore. It's fun to wall run and grapple to get cool cinematic kills and search for treasures. It genuinely got me interested in warhammer 40k due to the amazing guns, cool looking characters, interesting sounding factions, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genestealers that spooked the frick outta me and the simply amazing world design.Hired Gun clearly isn't the best looking game ever but people with a lot of love made environments that make you forget that and think it's beautiful... in it's own warhammer 40k way.If you cannot put up with the issues that I front loaded this review with then please dont bother. If it doesn't bother you, you are a 40k fan and/or just wanna shoot some stuff in an enjoyable gory fashion then go for it. I'm glad I did play it and got 100% achievements in my playthrough too.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend that very specific people purchase this game, because it's exactly the game Streumon has wanted to make. If you have a casual interest in Warhammer 40k and want to see a Hive World from the inside or get a way-too-close look at a tech priest, get this game. If you want a well put together shooter with a lot of guns, freedom of movement, and upgrade mechanics, there are already a ton out there that are more polished than this.Necromunda: Hired Gun is not an exceptionally well-made game. The animation is pretty spotty at times, the voice acting is alright, the music is good enough, the plot exists, and the gunplay is fine. It has its share of bugs at the moment (a few days after release,) but I personally haven't run into anything too weird.Edit: After the first patch (when the game version stopped showing .58 and started showing 1.5 on the main menu, not sure if that was just me or everyone,) a lot of the takedown animations look much better and the game seems to run more smoothly.HOWEVER!The sound design is solid, the visuals nail Warhammer 40k, and you can pet the dog. My computer was a pretty good gaming rig six years ago, and it's handling the game on High without issue. If you played Streumon's EYE: Divine Cybermancy years ago and thought "this is just a janky knockoff of Warhammer 40k's universe," this game is just EYE with the Warhammer 40k license and some of the wrinkles smoothed out.I've enjoyed it.

I beat the Campaign and Unlocked a faction reward in under 12 hours, including some crashes and breaks.Even keeping the $40 price in mind, Im already done with it. _childDocuments_.review: While I got this game from the Humble Choice, I gotta admit that I considered buying it even before... and now I'm glad I didn't.So in the very beginning I gotta say that I'm not into the Warhammer universe, even though I played some of the RTS games released in the early 2000s and I really enjoyed them. Necromunda looked like a solid FPS inspired by the newest entries in the Doom franchise, but it turned out to be a mediocre shooter, that tries to be something it's not.So due to the heavily industrial setting it reminded me of Quake, but then it really tries to mimic Doom 2016 and fails miserably at the most important thing making Doom a masterpiece - the gunplay. Even though the weapons' sounds are pretty good, they somehow lack the kick and excellent feeling present in the ID Software's production. Necromunda then adds some RPG elements and treasure hunting to the mix, to reward the player, but in all honesty, with miserable gunplay I could barely feel any difference after upgrading my guns and some of the skills were more of a hindrance than help.Also even though the graphics aren't any great it seems to drop to some pretty low framerate on many configurations. In the very beginning I tought it was a problem with my notebook, as it's got a pretty old by now GTX1660Ti Max-Q, but then I read some comments and it seems that even on some crazy configs it tends to drop frames, so the optimisation is another downside of Necromunda.With the technical problems, a mediocre gameplay and pretty marginal plot added to the slaughter simulator, Necromunda is pretty hard to recommend for the full price therefore I give it a negative rating.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little FPS game set in Warhammer universe. Art style, atmosphere and world are great, graphics are also nice and for UE4 game it's pretty optimised and with AA set on high, it was mostly fluid 60fps. Since it is AA game, it sadly doesn't have polish of AAA game and it's not as thought out and bugs drag it all down, making it more like mid-budget Doom Eternal game with how combat tries to be fast paced and fluid, rewarding more agressive gameplay.If you have nothing against lower budget spectrum of games, like Necrovision, you will have good time. In no way it's Doom competitor, but it is ok game for what it is. Grab it on deep sale or in a bundle.Good:- shooting is fun- parkour works ok, but feels rather situational- guns sound good- abilities are useful and easy to use- dog is also pretty useful and helps you find enemies (you also have ability for that, but dog is more useful)- another showcase of how awesome and brutally awesome Warhammer 40K is- Mick Gordon/Andrew Hulshult-spired OST, it is ok for combat noise, but it's not something you will go back toBad:- plot, like in most of those games, is incredibly basic and it's better to pretend it doesn't exist with how cliched it is and how mediocre ending is (although it is nice there is some kind of sequel bait, because I would like second game with more polish)- graphical glitches and bugs, like enemies getting stuck, gun not shooting even when you have ammo or gun not reloading when you have gun- animations can be terrible, like in one mission where you exclusively find "creatures" - they feel unfinished and like some of the frames of animation are missing, because they don't go to you, they are getting pulled towards you like you are some kind of magnet. It feels awkward and they cheapshot you, because that animation skip results in attack- balance feels off. While on normal it's managable and ok, any higher difficulty feels rather cheap, with enemies doing insane amounts of damage (although, just like in many other games, when you get some power ups, game gets easier)- bosses are terrible, have insane amount of health and can take long time to kill, last few bosses have the same exact pattern of crouching in the corner and shooting you, throwing grenade, walking and then crouching, shooting etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I've got not much play time but I've desperately tried to like this game as I'm a big fan of 40k. I even put the game down for over 2 months to see if the dev's would fix some of the issues I have but booting it up again I can see nothing is fixed. This game is awful. At not point should you purchase this game for anything over $20 USD and I still would say that's a hard sell. My biggest complaints with this game are:- Awful animations- Questionable gunplay- downright poorly designed inventory systems- boring plot- BUGS SO MANY BUGS- Poorly designed movement system- Bad user settingsAnimations:Animations in this game are at the level of flash animations from back yonder. During cutscenes characters CANNOT stand still. EVER. They're always moving their arms in jerky movements or during some uncanny valley type of animation. Movements of NPC's during these scenes feel more like animatronics then anything remotely appealing. What makes it stranger is that the animations during combat from NPC's are fine? They're totally acceptable and good. The level I expect from a AA game but then whenever they're not shooting or whacking you with an awesome thunder hammer they revert back to this janky hard to watch style. Gunplay:Most of the guns feel awesome to shoot. Bolters shoot big heavy rounds that make satisfying noises, miniguns sound like miniguns and feel weighty and etc. But the impact of all these weapons? Extremely lacklustre. Now this might overlap a bit with bugs or even go into graphics territory but it is incredibly difficult to determine if an enemy has a shield or not or if you even hit them when they don't have any visible animation to show impact, 0 zero is auditory due to the cacophony of gun fights and no blood is visible because everyone you're fighting is also shooting the lightshoweffects 3000 blaster they picked up from Imperium Walmart just around the pipe bend before coming to kick your guts in. It makes weapons like the plasma gun feel incredibly weak and awful as there is no way to tell if you hit your target and how hard you hit them. That's why guns like the bolter and the gravity gun feel ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. You hit someone once or twice with those? They're dead. And when they die you see an explosion of gore, you hear a scream and you even get a little hitmarker to show u hit them. The lasgun and longlas are also extremely unattractive options to use also due to their need to scope in for extended periods of time to get that gold 1 tap, in a game with a high speed movement system and swarms of enemies to rival a bloody zombie survival shooter. In other words, most of the guns are great but not all guns got the same amount of love for sure.Inventory system:Its bad. You get loot from either killing enemies or finding chests. When you find a new gun it doesnt display anything apart from the name of it, the slot it takes and the keybind to pick it up. But when u pick it up it replaces one of your weapons. SO you have NO IDEA if its BETTER OR NOT. Effectively making loot useless till after a mission (not the end of the world). But, then you have a very limited inventory to manage your loot. You get 4 slots for armour items, 4 for boost object things (they give some buffs), 4 for 2 other things then like 4-6 for your weapon categories? For example; there are 4-5 different heavy weapons. This means you can have all of them and room for a spare but then each weapon might get buffs or attachments that make it better at different things. So the tiny inventory really hurts as a result. And no its not a realism thing because they cant carry that much. Your character can carry tonnes but an extra weapon slot or 2 is too much? And anything that can't fit in your inventory doesn't go to your bank or some other larger inventory, oh no. It gets sold! And whats money for! More guns and upgrades! But there's no inventory upgrade! The inventory system doesn't at all feel tested. The Plot:The plot is boring, I'm not gonna spoil it in case this doesn't convince u this game is bad but the plot is so mind numbing that I put on anything else on youtube to supplement it. It's a poorly veiled excuse to kill bad guys and that's not awful in its self if the gun play was more interesting (see above for why that doesn't save it)Bugs:Bugs plague this game. Bugs that make the game painful and annoying will continue to plague you from your first mission to your last. Whether it's enemies spawning in walls and being able to shoot at you but not vice versa, to plasma gunners of a specific faction being invisible due to a shader error that you can't solve and the dev's still haven't. If you're going to play this game expect a absurd amount of bugs, even for a AA game. They're charging $55 AUD for what acts like a $15-20 AUD game they can't excuse this amount of bugs.Movement system:It is, without a doubt in my mind, tacked on. This movement system is not awful. I think its quite good not Titanfall 2 level but good. The issue comes from how it literally makes 0 difference to the game. The only time you are required to use the movement system (outside of traversing the level in mandatory sections) is when you get swarmed by 3 enemies that cannot be killed in one hit from your gun, so you have to jump up to avoid the pummelling. That's all. The grappling hook is neat and also useful for getting out of trouble but you're more often to use it accidentally thinking the shift key is the dash while in mid air key, then to actually traverse with it. Also who the ♥♥♥♥ puts Ctrl as the dash key? And then makes the rebinding for it also linked to the rebind for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slide? (this is explaining the awful user settings part now) It feels like 0 thought was put into that decision. I did lie a moment before accidentally. There is one weapon strat where the movement system is useful, although still not necessary, and that is thanks to executions. Executions allow you to instantly key any normal sized enemy that doesn't have a shield if you are close enough by simply tapping E. Not only does this make you invincible but it also replenishes portions of your health for each kill you make doing this. This strat completely blows all others out of the park making you unkillable blood leeching demon and rewards you for minimal effort most of the time. Oh and did I forget to mention? The worst animations play during these executions! You'll find your pov warping as you do an extremely flashy but dissatisfying melee kill on an enemy that feels like you just punched a wet pillow.Finally just to finish this rambling up a bit:- I have a high end computer (r3700x and 3070) yet my game looks like complete ♥♥♥♥ imo. I've seen the screenshots and people say it looks beautiful (HELL I've seen gorgeous videos of it on the tube) but for somereason at max settings it looks incredibly dulled and covered in low poly dust. The end result is it looking like PUBG on the lowest settings... that bad.- the set pieces are AMAZING. There are numerous missions where the set of the mission is fantastic and just makes me even more upset when the mission itself is incredibly dull and/or my graphics look so bad it turns this into a playdough art piece. - People seem to be spouting that this game brought an end to the long list of awful 40k games. I'm glad you're enjoying this game but I for the same reasons I wouldn't say a far cry game is a necessarily good game I wouldn't say this one is either even tho I enjoy far cry. This game has such a low level of polish that the price tag feels absurd. Go play Deathwing if you want a 40k shooter thats better than this (but still really not great) or wait for Dark Tide which APPEARS to have more invested developers. - This game reeks GW price gouging- the cyber dog is pointless, its literally just a marketing ploy I'm sorry but they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the dog up tooHope this is helpful. This game was incredibly disappointing, I'm sad its this

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a middle option between like and dislike because I enjoy the game in a "dumb, turn off my brain, oh hey look 40k" kind of way. if you're into 40k and you want a single player FPS in the setting you'll probably like it. it's a perfectly adequate game on its own, but if you're not a 40k fan the game isn't going to do much for youThe story is bare bones and the gameplay is repetitive. there is only one type of level and that level is finish the level as fast as possible as you run through walls of lead and lasers. the levels look like they want to be explored but the game punishes you for exploring because exploring takes time. the level layouts look like they want to allow for multiple playstyles, but because every level is just a "get swarmed" level there's no playstyle beyond full blast pure aggro. _childDocuments_.review: Having played the first few hours of Necromunda: Hired Gun, I can or at least I believe I can present to you all an honest opinion. First, this game is in some ways (gameplay in this instance) similar to DOOM 2016/Eternal. The gunplay and combat requires you to be always on the move, engaging enemies quickly before moving to the next area in succession. Enemy executions like with DOOM are fast, visceral and easily accomplished when in close proximity to enemies. Fortunately, like the aforementioned DOOM franchise, executions provide temporary invincibility during the animations so that at least gives you a few brief moments of respite before going back into the faster paced combat.  Overall gameplay is fast, frantic and enjoyable for any fps player. Now, here comes the opinion of a long time Warhammer fan. This game is honest to god beautiful to look at, it perfectly captures the sheer oppressive atmosphere of a setting this most often relegated to descriptions in the lore. Honestly, this game does that sense urban blight, gothic monstrosity and industrialised hell justice. The term 'feels lived in' is somewhat overdone, but this case the world feels 'over' lived in. There are bones and other remains of the many countless denizens of the Underhive scattered throughout the various environments, areas built upon older structures that are in turn built upon by others. The various areas you traverse are characters themselves, telling of the monumental human suffering and privation that has now become so common throughout the 41st Millennium. The devs have done the 40k/Necromunda setting justice. I look forward to playing through the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fast, shooty fun set in an impressively well voice acted, aesthetically pleasing world.They got the Warhammer feel right; bleak, hopeless, but still colourful. I've read lots of 40K; including most of the Necromunda books, and this feels like it's set in the same place; good work!The sound design is good, the guns feel like they have impact and the pace of the combat keeps your heart rate up (fast movement, fast kills and fast death; don't stop running and you're in with a chance).And the voice acting! I was pleased to find that all the characters I've encountered so far from the ambient passers by to the main characters, including your own (playing the male, haven't heard the female protagonists voice yet) have excellent voice acting! It makes the setting quite immersive (for a Warhammer fan).Really fun game once you learn how to play it; I recommend it as a fun shooter with an interesting story.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually wait till I finish a game but wanna get this out before the sale ends for any potential buyers, I was skeptical about this game due to some of the reviews but Im glad I bought it. I think a lot of the negative reviews are mostly players who payed full price and maybe feel it wasnt worth that cost, but on sale for 14$ I think I got a steal of a deal. It reminds me a lot of doom 2016 which I loved. The set pieces are gorgeous, the level design is great, the animations are ok, decent enemy intelligence, the gun play and combat is fun, a lot of player customization both in style and loadouts, some areas which you can be sneaky assassin, and lots of abilities. Im not a huge warhammer fan so Im not sure how accurate it is to lore, and Im listening to the story which has me interested but havent gotten far yet so I cant attest to either of those, but its a game Ill definitely finish and maybe return to every once and a while just for the rust punk aesthetics and fun gameplay. It does have some annoyances, such as looking for mission items, a out of place loot system and some pretty bullet spongey enemies but the game doesnt overstay its welcome and can be finished in about 8-10 hours. Its rough around the edges but underneath that its a gem if you can look past its flaws. I also highly suggest the N7e enhanced graphics HD preset mod at nexus mods which is really easy to install and helps saturate the faded default colors.

_childDocuments_.review: Hired Gun is very reminiscent of Streum's other 40k offering, Deathwing. It does a very good job of capturing the look and feel of the Warhammer 40k setting with its vast maps full of towering gothic structures and industrial grime. The problem, like with Deathwing, is that it drops the ball with everything else. First off, the basic gameplay just isn't very fun. The shooting feels like something out of a recent fallout game, with spongy enemies and guns that make a lot of noise but generally feel like they have very little weight or impact to them. The bullet sponge enemies are a doubly strange design choice considering you can also one-shot most of them by walking up and initiating a very janky melee QTE. It's the worst of both worlds and it sucks. Another odd thing about the game is that it clearly expects you to do a lot of grinding like you're playing borderlands or something. The are a bunch of repeatable side missions you can do to farm currency and build up reputation with different factions, but it's all pointless since there are only about a dozen guns with three tiers of quality, all of which you'll just pick up in the main campaign anyway if you do even a moderate amount of exploration. The faction reputation thing is also strange in that there are no unique rewards for maxing them out, just a bunch of random loot indistinguishable from what you get after a standard mission. It feels like something left over from an earlier, more expansive build of the game that they just left in despite not having the time/money to flesh it out. On a more positive note, the game does have really stellar voice acting, but it's in service to a plot so forgettable that I can barely remember anything about it despite having just completed the game. I really wish these guys the best since they obviously have a lot of creative talent (they also made E.Y.E.) but they need to stick to big ideas/art/aesthetics and hire someone with the appropriate skillset to handle the actual gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute banger of a game that I feel too many people are sleeping on due to the devs' past work being janky at best in the case of E.Y.E and downright bad in the case of Deathwing. Necromunda knocks it out of the park as far as I'm concerned and it achieves everything it sets out to do beautifully.The gunplay is fantastic and I was hard-pressed to find a single weapon that did not feel great to shoot ganger scum with save for a couple. Every trigger pull is responsive and flashy and oozes particles are gore, sound design is top notch.This game's frantic, almost spastic pace combined with it's ruthless difficulty will force you to play by it's rules or die repeatedly. It makes Doom Eternal look like Halo when it comes to the pace and speed of combat. Wallrunning, grappling, sliding and weapon swapping at here in droves and even with the occasional "slow time" when you open your power wheel to fire off one of the half dozen awesome augmetic abilities the combat is fierce and fun from start to finish. Game has a pretty bangin' soundtrack as well, generic heavy metal but it fits the theme.I was skeptical about your robo-dog companion and how a four legged critter would fare against the sheer verticality of Necromunda's maps but the devs remembered they were making a video game and not a walking sim about fungus zombies and emotions and made the canine leap incredible distances and even through floors and walls to rip some thugs throat out. The game is campy and does not take itself too seriously if fun is to be had.All of these abilities and movement and carnage is further improved by a very light looter-shooter addition that never felt overwhelming or tedious. About halfway through the game you've most likely got a few "favorite" guns and can spend a little cash to kit them out to your preference and imo that was perfect. This isnt Borderlands and the minimal stats you must keep track of in game are minor flavor that shouldn't distract you from the game's core elements: combat, environments and enemies.Speaking of levels, these environments are some of the most INCREDIBLE set pieces I've seen in a game. 40k is about mammoth buildings upon gargantuan structures and the devs delivered in droves. Nearly every single level is an enormous semi-open map thats dripping with detail and size, seriously these guys know how to design a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool level, even their older work with E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy was phenomenal.All in all Necromunda is one of the handful of 40k games that, in my opinion, breaks the curse of the franchise and stands out as not only an excellent gem of a 40k game but just a solid and fun 9/10 AA game if I'm being honest. The ONLY thing I can criticize about this game is the story which is a bit thin and not really too high-stakes. You will become somewhat attached to two or three characters but beyond that it takes a backseat to the incredible shooting and awesome maps. Another criticism would be the later levels, despite their beauty, were rather confusing to traverse and made it difficult to find hidden chests or determine where to go to advance but not impossibly so.All in all, go buy the rust-damn game.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game expecting nothing, and I now consider this game to be on par with dawn of war and space marine for the top 40k games. Hired gun makes every weapon fun ( I will say I spent most of my playthrough with the grav gun and grenade launcher because they feel amazing to use.) My biggest gripe with the game has nothing to do with thee main game itself, (it's just a minor nitpick) but the side "bounty" mission, which are randomly generated on previously played maps. I filled the reputation with the helot chaos cult and the corpse grinder cult, and did not gain any cosmetic changes ( I do not mean a new outfit, but a small change to the character model) to my character. Unlike if you fill out the reputation with the inquisition, which does add a cosmetic change to the character. Other then that I have no major problems with the game, the fact I can even gain reputation with my favorite factions from the tabletop is an amazing feature which I hope is expanded in the future. If you find that Hired Gun is on sale I can not recommend this game more then I already have. This game was an amazing love letter to Necromunda and 40k and it shows. (plus it's amazing game period)

The attention to every little detail in necromunda really blew me away, I didn't expect a doom-style shooter but it was enjoyable nonetheless.Only criticism I have is with regards to the female voice actress for the player character - as I didn't think the voice fit many, if not any, of the characters you have available to play as.

_childDocuments_.review: It is good.The fact that this game is compared to DOOM says a lot.But, no, it is not DOOM, it is definitely not as refined, although the devs obviously picked some gameplay ideas out of it like the need to keep fighting to stay alive, glory kills (which are unfortunately a bit too long, too janky, and too shaky cammy to be truly enjoyable), grappling hook and double jump + dash...But it is a power fantasy alright, maybe a bit more so than DOOM because the latter wants to be a puzzle and forces you to play a certain way whereas Hired Gun is pure mindless massacre no matter what you equip or shoot with. You put out your trusty overmodified bolter and never let go of the trigger as you run through all those herectic corpses.It is dumb fun, and it just works. It runs 90fps without noticeable framedrops on my GTX1070 i5 6600k at a bit downscaled 3440*1440 as it renders a detailed set of the Warhammer 40k universe.This is a simple game which reminds me of the good old days of gaming. There is no stealth bs, no grind necessary, no rpg elements to indulge with, no min-maxing, no meta build, no microtransactions, no forced gimmicks.You have a gun, you shoot, you proceed, you unlock more guns as you go, you shoot some more, the story doesn't try to sell you anything, doesn't lecture you on anything, you find secrets, you become so strong that previous bosses are now mob enemies, you keep on shooting, and that's Hired Gun in a nutshell.Keep in mind that this is not a big production so keep some expectations in check. For example, the voice-acting is akin to the kind we had back then on games like Halo 1, Jedi Knight, Star Trek Elite force... the bit cheesy almost always off and out of tempo, be it for story related NPCs in cutscenes or enemies who die like "Oooh... Oh no my head exploded.... Aahhh".As not perfect as it is a good, functionnal unlike most big late releases, Hired Gun's only requirement for its enjoyement is for you to put you brain aside as you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the Doom that tried, but failed.Firstly, the gameplay itself is lacking in balance and innovation. The mechanics feel unpolished and underdeveloped, failing to capture the frenetic, heart-pumping action that made Doom such a hit. The controls can be clunky, making it difficult to execute the moves you need to survive in the game.Moreover, the enemy design and encounters are disappointing. The foes you face are poorly designed, lacking in imagination and creativity. The battles themselves can be frustrating, with enemies that seem to come out of nowhere, making it difficult to plan your strategy and react in time. This can lead to a sense of unfairness and frustration for players.The loot system is another area where this game falls short. It's poorly implemented, with items that seem to be scattered randomly throughout the levels. This makes it difficult to find what you need when you need it, and often feels like an afterthought rather than an integral part of the game.Not worth it's full price, barely worth with 50% discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I will review this game as a positive, with some caveats. If I could vote "neutral" I would. It's barely positive.First and foremost, don't buy it at full price, for the love of god. It's not worth it. I got it for something like 7 dollars off ♥♥♥, and if I'd paid the full $55 AUD for this, I would definitely have reviewed negative. I don't think it's worth that much for the amount of content.So about the game, it's definitely a Streumon game, for better or worse. If you have played Space Hulk: Deathwing, or even E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy you will feel distinct similarities. Among which, kind of mediocre gunplay, and waves and waves of respawning enemies. It had a couple of buggy moments, but wasn't too bad. The worst was when a Goliath boss jumped and landed through the floor and disappeared, disallowing me from progressing. The whole thing has kind of a low budget feel. It's not terrible, but it could have been a lot richer and greater than it was.Instead of word diarrhoea for more paragraphs, let me break it down into a simple pros vs cons list:PROS:*The environment art is phenomenal. It's really great actually, and really sets the scene and the scale of Necromunda. The lowermost depths of this disgusting Hive City are realised in a faithfully unbelievable way. This is the main PRO here, to be brutally honest.*The guns are conceptually cool. I like being able to have a boltgun or a plasmagun. *I liked the voice acting for the main characters; the bounty hunter, Kal Jerico, Jado.*A couple of missions were quite fun*I really love Warhammer 40,000CONS:*Not enough gun progression. I'm hardly a looter shooter enjoyer, but I found that my guns kind of peaked like halfway through the game, where I had +2 to most weapons I was using, and the +2 long las I was using kind of stayed faithful beyond the period of novelty it provided. I was hoping for a +3 or something but it never arrived.*Not enough factions. There are so many factions in Necromunda, and the game only shows you something like 5 of them, and after a while I got tired of shooting the same Goliaths and Eschers and whatnot. I really hoped to see some Van Saar or Delaques, or Redemptionists or something.*The campaign was quite short. Like 10 hours give or take. For a $50 game I would expect at least 3 times that.*The dog WAS kind of useless after all. I found him kinda handy in the beginning but later on he would just get annihilated in big groups of enemies, and couldn't really do that much to help even if he didn't.*This kind of ties in with earlier CONS but I felt like I'd more or less seen everything the game had to offer (except levels), far earlier than I was done with it. *More ♥♥♥♥ I can't think of anymore, and I'm tired of writing this by now.The main takeaway is that basically, it's kind of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game, but if you like Warhammer 40k like me, you should probably get it (ON SALE), and think of it as a tour of the Necromunda underhive, and just enjoy the art. Like I said, the environments are really cool. Whoever worked on those is holding the rest of this game on their shoulders like Atlas. If this game had been done with a bigger budget, so it could have a better campaign and more depth, it would have been amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, serviceable, worth buying and playing, but don't expect wonders. It's like Budget Doom Eternal a Necromunda setting. Doom set the bar super high tho, so "budget doom" is still good.Gameplay is heavily inspired on Doom reboot and Doom Eternal, with constant movement being the norm rather than finding defensive positions, game also pushes you to be agresive to heal instead of avoiding damage through positioning. Doesn't feel as good as Doom Eternal, but it's still fun. Big drawback is enemy AI. It's bad, which means difficulty comes from overwhelming numbers (of enemies, damage, shields, hp, etc.) and needing certain counters for certain enemies. Fun but gets old.RPG elements are mediocre and easily forgotten. Gun customization is good tho, and it's quite fun to build your guns to your particular taste for your particular strategy. The dog is... optional. Like you can include it in your game or not and it doesn't make that big of a difference.Graphics and sound are good, but unremarkable. Sometimes it's hard to see what's going on, but that's location-specific. Music is good, but not remarkably so. Voice acting is adequate, but not impressive. The story is there I guess.The game is fun. It won't be your favorite, but it's money well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A run 'n gun FPS set in the dark future of Warhammer 40,000 etc. The vibe and aesthetics are pretty good. The gameplay is like a janky Doom 2016 with less interesting fights and enemies, and introduces some RPG-like loot and leveling mechanics which never feel like the add to the gameplay in any way. It feels like it's on the verge of being good but never gets there.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: OKAYFirst 8.0/10The things that were...bad1. The skin textures were like play-doh and it was somewhat distracting2.  The gameplay flow is essentially that you move to a area and then spend a lot of time bunny hoping/dodging/using powers to avoid depleting your HP pool - you recover HP in 3 ways. FA kits, Doing damage shortly after taking damage, or ressing with a Stimm. The game puts you again a massive amount of foes and often its only a matter of time before your floating around 20 HP and dodging like mad.3. Sometimes the firefights are a bit hard to track...like your blind because of all the lights and smoke and I found this to be the trickiest part of many of the boss battles.4. Overall the main story is about 8-10 hours depending on your level of skill/comfort.5. Some area's are essentially made not traversal even though they should be - like your grapple will not work to latch to area's they don't want you going - luckily that is pretty often not a issue.6. Some of the bigger mobs offset their limited mobility by the devs giving them the ability to burrow/teleport so that they cannot be sniped by a player who is taking advantage of being more mobile then them.The things that were good1. You have a lot of freedom to move and travel - Double jumps/Slides/Grapplegun - in fact you will need to get comfortable with those mechanics as they give you passive "immunity" frames in the form of a %chance to not be hit while doing them - attacks just don't register on you. Same goes for mobs doing combat rolls FYI.2. Guns last a long time - if you find a gun you like you can keep using it - I used a gun from the first mission until I finished the game. You can tweak your weapons to make them better once you find your guns of choice. I was a bit disappointed there were not more gun types - but I suspect they were out of theme (no meltaguns or Las guns except for the Long Las....no needler rifle either!)3. You got a dog you can tweak out - this feature takes some getting used to but in invaluable as your dog can be a good distraction and also detect/give you info about enemy positions and even perform takedowns.4. Aggressive gameplay is rewarded with recovery thansk to a auto-sanguine implant and I recommend upgrading it.5. You can upgrade your baseline stats with gear AND cash by amping up your bionics.6. There is a awesome soundtrack of industrial/metal music (I actually turned DOWN sound effects and music UP which is rare for me...some of the guns are VERY loud)7.Your given a few character options which effects some dialogues and your overall appearance (not that you often see yourself)8. The Story was REALLY well done and fit into the WH40K setting perfectly with a painstaking attention to small details.9. There are side missions you can do for the factions to earn extra money + loot to help you over tough spots by gearing up.10. Later in the game there is a mob that will creep you out - it was very well done....I won't spoil that suprise..Overall if you liked freeform parkour movement like Mirrors Edge/Ghost Runner/Titan Fall 2 your going to be very comfortable in the fire-fights. That said there is a comfy shooter in here. I think just as a shooter it would be a solid 5 - as there is nothing new here; but the combination of parkour mechanics and player progression really pushes this game ahead and with a good storyline and VA work as a cherry on top. If you amped up the textures and added a bit more variety to the upgrades/weapons and made the storyline a bit longer - I could see a 9-10 out of this game to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is an acceptable shooter, and I would say one of the better Warhammer games I have played recently, but that's not saying much given the quality of most Warhammer titles.  I do not have a lot to say about Necromunda really, its a passable game that I enjoyed playing. I would only recommend it if you get it under 20 dollars, I would have a much more negative opinion had I paid full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun rarely transcends what is a boring generic shooter with a fast pace and a nice setting. The story is forgettable and scattershot. Combat fares better, with decent mobility and a capable arsenal. The level design has some large interior spaces, although within them are idiotic enemies that are difficult to locate. Enemies spawn from everywhere and it all makes for some rather clunky action. Although the numerous bionic powers are helpful, they do not elevate the combat. Hired Gun needed to use its setting better and fine-tune its mechanics because even when ignoring its many shortcomings, it does not have enough quality gameplay to earn a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously suffering from the lack of focus.Everything is half-cooked or someone else did it a lot better a long time ago (Bulletstorm, Doom, Metro, Borderlands, Rage)For an action game combat is incredibly boring and the main challenge is actually spotting the enemies.Zero quality of life features (pause, save, buttons serving the same purpose across different menus).Looks like it had a potential to be really good if done in a serious way (metro-style) with tactical and stealth focused combat or in full bullet hell funny style (like, say, Bullestorm or Shadow Warrior).Right now it looks like a marketing team forced  everything that even remotely worked in any successful game of the last 25 years to make the product appealing to everyone.This game is like a balding man in mid-life crisis, sporting leather vests and a motorcycle trying to be "cool".
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for 3 dollars on sale and I'm still disappointed in it. Its just not fun, at all. The 40K themes feel tacked on at best and non-present at worst, the combat flow and gameplay is ripped from DOOM yet somehow downgraded to an absurd level, the sidequests are impossibly hard compared to the main story quests that are piss easy, every level feels and looks exactly the same, the only thing to fight are some indistinct models that feel like gangers from a half-baked Fallout 4 DLC. No Genestealers, no Chaos, no Imperial Guard, nothing you'd expect to see in what is apparently the "BIGGEST Hive City in the Imperium".There are some cute little posters and environmental details, but they feel out of place because nothing involved in the actual gameplay has anything to do with 40K. Like, if this was just a generic post-apocalypse mercenary game, it would be the exact same. Nothing involving 40K matters to this game, its plot, or its themes.I could go on and on about all my nitpicks, but it isn't worth it.Just buy DOOM Eternal. The gameplay is just a flat BETTER version of this, and the art design isn't fighting with the setting.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired gun----------------------------A fast paced fps set in the warhammer 40k universe.taking place in one of the most famous underhive cities.Necromunda.The game has a "ok" story but the lore and some nice fan service moments when it comes to warhammer 40k. The soundtrack is great the gunplay is fantastic. Its a solid fps game that will give fans of the franchise tons of fun.Sadly there are some issues. Janky animations, Audio bugs and stuttering.Out of those three, audio is the biggest issue. And I hope they fix it.the game is fun.
