_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a masochistic mess where "side missions" just spit bullet sponge enemies against you constantly, them shooting plasma while you have stubbers and shotguns that take several shots to the face to finish off NPCs. What is the developer's way to counter that? Why of course - parkour. You are supposed to jump from the walls when enemies lose track of you and it somehow improves your aim. I'm not kidding, doing parkour improves your aim. I thought I was a bounty hunter, not an Eldar Harlequin using the Dance of Death.At least Doom Eternal actually gives you *working* weapons and stuff/ This is garbage. I went through few campaign missions (the train one was cool, some very very well done level design, incredible), and now I can't finish side missions as I constantly get overwhelmed by shielded enemies with automatic plasma weapons while I have a shotgun, heavy stubber, an autogun and five grenades. Weapons feel abysmal, weak and ineffective, take too long to reload (your enemies never have to reload anything). You are no Space Marine. Maybe I am supposed to buy some augments, but how I'm going to grind for that as side missions just overwhelm me? Add to it bugs (the tutorial had a bugged door that required me to redo it), parkour (why?) and your dog, a useless gimmick that takes too much time (again) to use and slowly does something (or not) and then of course is on cooldown.The story I've seen so far doesn't have me thrilled too much either. Doom Eternal was fun, this isn't. Even being an avid Warhammer 40k fan that I am, it quickly stops being fun. The train level was good so far. The rest was nothing outstanding. I don't know if I will ever get back to this game, as frankly working on programming complex forms is less frustrating than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: From te beginning I had a feeling that this game is like something I played before... hell it is like many games I have played before, but then around half way it came to me. If you played Soldier of Fortune back in the day, this is it, with a serios face lift both in gameplay and asthetics. Of course the Warhammer 40K world makes it feel different enough but it doesn't change the fact that it is a mindless run and gun adventure. There are 3 things I can write up as an absolute positive: -The gameplay is dumb fun with ridiculous vertical and horizontal movements while spraying lead (and plasma) to everywhere. -The other is the map designs. There are no two completely similar map and the elements they used are astonishingly grandiose. Giant statues, sunken building, mountain high piles of corpses. Everything feels like a race of giants lived here and their world was burried under centuries of filth and rust.-The third is the weapon modifications. You can shape a whole platera of death dealers to your own image which is very nice. Too bad that around half way of the game, you will have a favorite set of weapons and the rest of the game, the loot won't give you any joy. But the interface of the game is anything but user friendly, even in the hub between missions setting up your character is a pain in the butt. Would have been so hard to put in an inventory, really?Other than that the story is in complete shambles, it doesn't make any sense and doesn't do anything to make itself feel like your own. The ending is just as much of a dissapointment as the whole campaign. If they would have spent as much time at the writing table as they did with the level designs, this would have been a 10 out of 10 epic legend.Why am I still recomending the game? I don't know. It made me come back between sessions, but no further than the end of the campaign. Buy it only if it is basically given for free. Anything more than that would be a waste of money.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Has some nice visuals, captures the grim dark feel nicely, the upgrade systems are nice, but even though it has a lot going for i, it still seems to miss the mark on the game play aspect which is a real shame as i was looking forward to this, the voice acting is very weak and the game feels sparse and empty, the Cyber mastiff is nothing more than a novel gimmick more than a tactical game play choice, I feel there is a solid foundation here that could be built on to be a great game, but after only 2 missions in it already became tedious and uninteresting to me, it didn't engage me with story or action sadly.  Hopefully with some updates and fleshing out of content it might get better, but as it stands i can't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: So I picked this game up specifically because of the "mixed reviews". It looked good, and I was wondering why it wasn't at least "mostly good".Come to it, it is actually pretty good!The story isn't groundbreaking. You are a bounty hunter, and you are hunting a bounty. No spoilers there. But the execution is competent. You never feel like you are some cosmic space hero, or suffer from main character syndrome. You are a scummy little bounty hunter, and you are here to collect, and shoot anyone who gets in your way. The mechanical game play is solid. Feels like Warframe and DOOM had a baby and left it in the under-hive. With its focus on speed and hp regen tied to damage output its easy to forget you're not the tankiest MF around. A Space Marine you ain't, and die you will if you try to wade in. The dog is the most unique part. Cool down cyber hound you can modify and sick on enemies or use to escape. YES! The fact that the different tiers of upgrade actually show on the model both in and out of mission were a big win for me. My good-est boy "Commissar Chompers" kept me in line and in the fight. The powers. Honestly I didn't use anything but Loot site until like chapter 8. Honestly its on me for dismissing them as not great because I didn't take the time to play with them, and was just running and gunning. They do however make for some much more powerful game play. They could have used a better tutorial but you don't get any until after that stage. There is an arena ware you could have been told to go after getting the upgrades, and that would have done the game a solid.The progressions is kinda cool, but fell flat with no real reason to push the secondary bounties after you finish your upgrades. The rewards were meh, and by the time you are clearing S ranks, you pretty much won't need anything but the cash reward if you still havn't finished with the Doc. Ware the game shines like the freekin Astronomicon itself is in its level design and set dressings! By the Emperor did this game nail the look and feel! I've played a few 40k games in my time and only the Inquisitor (Martyr in my case) come close to capturing the aesthetic. The metal is bloody  and rusted, the gore is gory, the grim is dark, and the scale is just right to make you feel the weight of the hiveworld above you crushing down on the tiny little human you are. And when it goes creepy, its just enough. Chefs kiss to the level designers. The game does have its flaws. It differently feels like there was meant to be a stealth mechanic that was scrapped. The inclusion of silencers as an option with targeting lights "giving away your position" felt really unnecessary with enemies able to detect you from a pixel in view across the map. The voice actors who were in it gave it their all. But they were in short supply. Really only like 3 actual dialog characters, 3 shop characters, and then anyone not a boss only gets like 2 precious voice lines to repeat, so "Don't make me waste em!" All in all the game was fun. and hit that sweet aesthetic sweet spot I'm always looking for from 40k.Its not super long so give it a play though and just let yourself have fun as a the grimy little gutter skulk with a laz pistol and a cyber dog you know you wanna be!
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with fun mechanics. Mild crashing issues with making a large amount of cybernetic upgrades at once, but otherwise functions well.The side missions vary greatly in difficulty. (I can do S-rank kill the leader but can't do B-rank control the zone missions) but they are still great for money and loot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, while flawed, is still a whole helluva lot of fun. You can see, from this version, that with some more development time, and a little bit more polish, that this game has what it takes to really be an excellent addition to the Warhammer 40k universe.  The issues I have with this game are also, for the most part, minor, while the things I love about it, I love a lot, which is why I recommend it. The flaws: The menus. The menus are awful, confusing, hard to navigate, and overall not very user friendly, things like being unable to switch your guns from your preset loadout in a looter-shooter, or being totally locked out of replacing your main pistol, despite being able to get clear and obvious upgrades from said pistol that are just overall better, that you cannot really use because why would you have two pistols equipped when you could have a pistol, a sawed-off shotgun, and an smg, all equipped at the same time? I know I don't want that, I just want to be able to replace the pistol I already have! Next; the animations, you can tell that, despite its flashy graphics, this is, indeed, an indie game, the animations all work, and they're all mostly readable, there's no confusion, but they do look rough, so this is a thing that really just needs more time to flesh it out and make it shine. And lastly: The combat. It's fun, but, it feels a little, ehhh, lackluster. In a fight, I'm pretty much able to walk through the whole squad of enemies and tap E on them, to go into a takedown animation, that makes you invincible, and heals you. I am playing on the 2nd hardest difficulty, as well, so, kinda disappointing that at any time I can switch to "ez mode" where I just bull rush the closest dude, chop his head off, and then do that ad infinitum. I think the staleness of this option is also enhanced by the lackluster animations, because they only look alright, and don't really play up the flashiness that I expect, due to their lack of polish, tho again, since this is an indie game, that just means it needs more time to be worked on, and I doubt it's the fault of the developers.The features: HIGH paced, GRATUITOUS action, almost at the level of the most recent Doom games, nonstop shooting, killing, looting, the guns feel pretty damn good (at least, my favorite shotgun sure does!), the voice acting does convey some really strong emotion, the graphics are killer, and totally fit the idea of necromunda perfectly, and the story, at least so far, has me interested, though how that will continue on, we will see. This section may seem short, especially compared to my lengthy dive into the flaws, but I think that's OK, because  honestly, regardless, and in spite of, the flaws I found with the game, I still think the game is incredibly fun, and overall, amazingly well done for an indie group, and I can't wait to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: Good concepts that are weighed down with poor execution ore more likely lack of focus.You have a game that is trying to fit in between Titanfall 2 and Doom Eternal for gameplay and a Borderlands character leveling system.  The end result is as mess of ideas that never gel right. Some of these issues are core game play issues that don't like a patch can fix.  No amount of patches can make the level design more interesting. Just like the executions, which are like a first person convulsion that makes to shake the camera more than the enemy.  Stuff excessive smoke and particle effects can be removed so if you need to ADS it doesn't feel like a chore. This is a wait for a deep sale game, even at the budget price of $40 it needs to have more polish. _childDocuments_.review: Before you read this, I *would* recommend this game for people who are big fans of the 40k universe and are just looking for a time sink simply due to the fact that the systems seem mostly accurate.  However to anyone that is slightly less of a fan, or who has never heard of the universe, I would not suggest purchasing the game, and I suspect the latter group is the majority.I wish there were an in between option, but given that there is not, I have given this a non recommendation. This game is something for the killteam players, or anyone that knows more than the idea that there's a hive world in the 40k universe known as Necromunda.That out of the way, the pros:+nice environments, really gets you into the idea of being in the underhive+the customization for weapons is nice+there's an option for an 'old school' difficulty+the game clearly had a lot of soul put into it and I'm sure with continued work it will feel great to play, I hope this will be the casecons-the whole thing feels like a game from a decade ago with new graphics slapped on-the animations are pre 2007 level, go play crysis or gears of war if you don't believe me, I mean just play bulletstorm and you'll get a better experience on that front-the game is very unpolished-grappling hook seems to only hook onto specific areas, and even then sometimes it gets you stuck in geometry-enemies are way way too repetitive, after the 2nd mission I'd already seen pretty much everything, and I was more or less fighting pluralities of the same few enemies over and over, even if there was a little model difference it would be nice-despite being main selling points, there are very few places you can actually wallrun effectively or use your dog, the only time you use the dog is when the mission is essentially already over and the last few enemies broke their ai and can't find you, so you need to bring him out to spot them-the 'glory kills' as you would recognize them from doom, are very janky and unpolished, it feels like the devs were trying to show off their animations rather than keep the fluidity of combat going-for some reason the interaction menus with the barkeep and the questgiver are really janky, you need to twitch around with wasd a lot to get into the right spot where interacting with them will worksubjective cons:-the enemies keep respawning forever, which you can use to farm, but it's really annoying and just depletes the sense of achievement during a mission-the mouse controls feel a bit off, I tried tweaking them as well as I could but they still felt off, as if maybe mouse acceleration was permanently on or something-dodging and crouching should be separate, so that dodging forward is an option at the very least, without it being a slow animation that I have to be careful about activating lest I die in the middle of combat, I'd suggest just removing crouch but it's clear that crouching is integral to a lot of the game accessibility

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun, for all of its faults, offers an experience compelling enough that fast-paced shooter fans will still find enjoyment. There isn't a lot unique about it, but its use of all the aspects that make games like it great works in its favor. There's even a solid audio and visual suite, making its atmosphere one that enhances its world, rather than complementing it. That doesn't fully excuse the abysmal story though, which barely scratches the surface of its source material and leaves you empty by the end credits. Despite this, if you're looking for a fast-paced Warhammer shooter, and are okay with it being rough around the edges, Necromunda: Hired Gun should still offer an enjoyable experience.If you'd like to see the rest of this review and more like it, check out . Thank you to Streum On Studio and Focus Home Interactive for providing a review copy.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Necromunda, a planet-sized microcosm of scheming, crime and villainy set within Warhammer 40k universe. Mirroring its galaxy-spanning counterpart, Necromunda is a place of constant turmoil where innumerable gangs struggle for power and riches. One may begin to wonder - how come that Hive Primus, seat of Imperial government, seconds as the greatest centre of illegal activity on the planet? Out of sight, out of mind as they say. Nobles and honest citizens inhabit the highest parts of kilometre-high city-spires, enjoying luxuries such as sunlight, imported food or running water. However, long past the point that sun rays could ever hope to reach there are still kilometres of inhabited industrial patchwork before the bottom. Proper Necromunda begins in so-called underhive, a place where word ‘civilian’ is a figure of speech and gangs run majority of the industry on behest of the noble houses beyond. Long enough the imperial taxes are paid above, the below at large will be left to its own devices. Robust introduction notwithstanding, Necromunda is essentially a separate, roguish setting within WH40k universe and truly a selling point of this high-paced FPS. At least for those familiar with WH40k. As for everyone else, reckon you are here for the “hired gun” part. Waiting ahead is a single-player campaign starring 13 missions of substantial size and length, coupled with side-missions for a quick buck and as much replayability as one desires. Under the circumstances, a hired gun is perhaps the most mundane occupation imaginable within the underhive. What gives the protagonist an edge over the competition, is an extensive set of bionic augmentations. More metal than flesh, you can double-jump, wall run, dash mid-air, use grappling hook and we haven’t even got the upgrades yet. To name a few, they involve shooting lightning out of your arm, bullet time and temporary auto-aim. Ludicrous mobility is extremely useful in Hired Gun’s unusual environment. Most of the areas in the game are surprisingly open, especially vertically, often containing multiple floors of half-derelict urban nightmare to explore; all filled with additional supplies, enemies and an occasional loot chest.Hired gun’s protagonist may very well be a living weapon in their own right, that said, the sizeable arsenal at the player’s disposal is nothing to frown upon. Conventional assortment of shotguns, machineguns and pistols is matched by a choice of futuristic energy-based weapons. Chief among them being the grav gun – firing a homing green bolt that creates a miniature explosion around the killed target. Primary source of the new toys is secret chests hidden within every map. While finding some of them is challenging, the player’s augmented eyes can reveal the treasure’s location through the walls. To keep things varied, every weapon can be customised to better match your playstyle. On that note, a significant amount of scopes and silencers dedicated towards long-range, stealthy engagements which seem for the most part redundant. Given that protagonist’s modus operandi favours blowing a hole in the wall over finding the door, any attempts at stealth would be downright counterproductive. As soon as the mission ends, somewhat abysmal inventory menu appears, allowing the player to decide which equipment they want to keep. You are likely to spent quite a while after the first mission, trying to make some sense of it. All unwanted items are automatically sold, providing the player with credits, spent mostly towards upgrading the bionics of protagonist and his trusty dog companion. Deserving a separate mention is the cyber-mastiff, somewhat oddly summoned via dedicated skill. The hound will fearlessly draw the enemy fire and tear out the throats of the weaker opponents, only to vanish into the grand beyond, until called upon again.Ordinarily, it would stand to reason to cover the enemy variety now. Sadly, it truly takes hours spent in-game to start noticing how much of it there technically is in Hired Gun. Most of the time so much is happening on the screen that if not for the outlines on the enemy silhouettes, one could overlook an enemy standing wide-open 5 meters ahead, let alone identify them. Pragmatic approach divides the unfortunate cannon fodder in the player’s way into gunners, psykers, melee and heavy units. Take note that there are over 10 different types of “gunners”, which frankly doesn’t amount to much. It is one of the game’s aspects which seem to suffer from its neck-breaking pace. Another being Hired Gun’s soundtrack, introducing heavy riffs to spice up the thickest fighting. Regrettably, most of the fights end so abruptly that it rarely has a chance to properly kick into gear. On the sound design note, everyone in Necromunda have a thick british accent, and frankly it fits perfectly into roguish feel of the game.However distinct in terms of setting, when it comes to Hired Gun’s gameplay, at least a broad comparison with the latest DOOM is inevitable. The game at large feels as if the developers at Streum On Studio tried to reinvent the invasion of hell in their own image, while also replacing most of fine-tuning with cocaine. On one hand, the results are mostly fun and adrenaline-inducing, on the other, it would explain why the game breaks so much. To begin with, this title’s movement allows for a much greater freedom than the developers intended. Thinking I might be onto a secret I managed to get out of bounds within the first 5 minutes of play. It didn’t occur a lot, however once you get stuck, the only way out is to load the latest checkpoint. A far greater issue is how unstable the game is overall. Hired Gun crashes a lot, and despite my hardware otherwise running the game smoothly on the highest settings, during my 32 hours of play it crashed around 20 times.Moreover, there are certain design issues too. Hired Gun is only enjoyable on “hard” difficulty setting. It makes the game a true challenge and, more importantly, the increase of the enemy damage successfully makes up for AI shortcomings. When played on normal, only the fiercest barrage can hope to put the protagonist down, as the powerful self-healing abilities remove any necessity to stay ahead of the opposition. The moment a single opponent can put you down with 3 shots, the game suddenly requires a much more thought-out approach. A minor, although frustrating example is the rating given to the player after each mission, specifically the “kill style”. Over the regular course of play rating of “B” is the highest you can hope for, as said statistic takes into account not the kill variety, but headshots and melee assassinations only. Having a break-neck speed FPS favour methodical head-hunt puts the merit of the entire rating system into question.Ultimately, Necromunda: Hired Gun wholeheartedly shares the fate the most of its Warhammer-licensed brethren – it is unremarkable for the wider audiences, yet appealing to the fans of the setting. Whatever potential the action-packed demeanour of Hired Gun may had, it is butchered by its technical difficulties. That said, when it works as intended, this game is a really good time and should satisfy any FPS enthusiast who doesn’t shy away from B-grade titles. Should you happen to enjoy both shooters and WH40k, this one is worth playing for the portrayal of the underhive alone, a decent game it comes with, is a bonus.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty janky version of a 90's run and gun shooter with a loot system and hub/lobby welded onto its side. Missing some game play settings that would help it like ADS sensitivity. Low FOV. Resolution is buggy and can only be changed in windowed mode for some reason. Odd lobby mission selection game play instead of a more fluid approach. Story is meh. Lots of sound issues or missing sound.Loot system is very poor, inventory system is missing. Mods can not be swapped between guns and are not terribly interesting, so no point in stripping guns down. The guns i used were okay standard weapons that can be found in every game, didn't get anything interesting  like las, plasma or bolters before the return window. Loot is gained from random treasure chests you have to hunt  down by sound queues which means you have to turn off music or you wont hear them. You cannot equip your loot after you pick it up, you have to hold e if you want to use it in that mission. The weapon modding is not "Endless weapon and augment customisation", its very bog standard.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The gunplay feels really fun, but the story is bad ( not really interesting, over way too quick, ending right where it seemed like it might finally get interesting and it is also  completely linear and basically boils down to "go there to get more information that i totally dont already have and just refuse to tell you")The animations are often janky and i've had plenty of times where i used the grapple mechanic only to end up stuck inside of geometry or outside of the map entirely (inside geometry was mostly fixable by grappling again, but outside of the map was usually not).The difficulty hardly seemed to matter when it came to loot quality and quantity, meaning the only thing you'd do by increasing it is fight harder hitting enemies that still fall like flies with any decent weapon (my favorite of which i litteraly bought in the first shop as a +1 and later upgraded to a +2, never saw a +3). I started the game by running through the first map a few times trying to achieve high rating  and ended up with a lot of +2 items that i was basically using until the end of the game, because they were just better than anything i dropped, even though for most of the game i cleared the campaign maps looking for chests and then went back in a 2nd time to actively grab all of them (with a guide if need be, though that was only really neccesary in a few of the early levels where i didnt have my wallhacks upgraded so they'd help me find treasures).The bounties differ vastly in reward, with the bounties with a lot of prize money usually also getting you the most cash from loot, while low bounty missions were just a waste of time for the most part. (Campaign is always low bounty, but that is to be expected). The biggest flaw about the bounty system is the faction reputation that you can increase to get a +3 item, but for me the items i got were always way worse than the ones i got from mission even if the mission items were only +1 versions.Most abilities felt severely unbalanced: Strength augment was really strong damage wise but it would leave you very vulnerable, while crush and blast dealt massive burst damage on low cd and had basically no drawback (these two abilities were strong enough to take out most campaign bosses with a little help from the shockwave to get rid of shields)The Mastif, your pet dog was completely useless, even fully upgraded, only really serving to mark enemies for you, which you could also just do with an ability, that also had the added benefit of guiding you to treasure chests (though if you used anything but iron sights it would render your scope practically unusable, but you could turn it off at will).If you were hoping for a decent looter-shooter then you will be disappointed, but the gunplay feels good enough that i'd say at 50% off this might still be a decent pickup if you like the WH40K universe, primarily the Hive World setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Worth it while on sale.Play on normal. Some enemies are already bullet sponges, playing higher is torture, taking 10+ mags dumped just to kill. Keep your money up with side missions between main missions, this will keep your cybernetics up to date which will keep you at a better level to face off against new enemies. Someone complained about shielded enemies recently, but there is literally an ability that breaks shields instantly. The game isn't that long, and I probably won't play it again, 15-20 hours are probably what you should expect at a slow pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun game, but as it is right now, it is too broken to recommend unless you really like the 40k setting and don't mind pushing through some bugs and janky gameplay. It seems like it was rushed to release in time for the SKULLS event, which left a lot of the game feeling unfinished and full of glitches. There's several times in the story where the cutscenes jump around and feel super disjointed. I can think of at least one time where there's 4 characters in the cutscene and it ends super disjointed and all of the sudden your character is fighting the bad guy with no explanation for what's going on. if that wasn't bad enough, the fight feels bad to play since there's fire everywhere and the villain is teleporting around an arena you can barely see in. It's a super cool idea for a fight, but it feels like the developer was coming on a deadline and threw several things at the wall and didn't check to see how anything worked when it stuck. Also noteworthy, the fight broke the game. The game didn't crash, but the player character and the villain both got stuck in place and wouldn't move, no abilities/weapons worked. The music played and I had to restart the mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't the most polished, but for its prize and unique setting and gameplay loop I'd say it's quite worth it.There's a couple of accessibility issues to make the game enjoyable but after binding some keys it becomes a lot better.I have a mouse with 2 side buttons which help the keybind issue A LOT, I'd say completely mandatory for how fast the game wants to be.The weapon wheel doesn't have a slowing time effect like DOOM so it's completely useless, so I recommend binding the buttons 1-5 for weapons you like, then have  bound close to WASD so you can always take down an elite shield in 2 buttons with a Pulse into an Execute, then have Grappling Hook and Ability selection on the side buttons.That way you can have the god awful default bindings made for a controller dealt with to enjoy the fast paced action the game is, due to its jank it can be EXTREMELY hard even on normal with sub-optimal setups, but because learning how to play around it's rough edges and finding the best weapons for you I pushed the difficulty up to Oldschool just because it feels like the game was intended to beat your ass like a true Grimdark experience.The setting of Necromunda is absolutely gorgeous in the industrial hellscape design and it has some of the most fun scenarios in an FPS with amazing set pieces like massive trains, Psyker arenas causing Warp anomalies and chase sequences into high action escapes.The game has a grindable side mission table where some of them are really bad, some really quick and some accidental endurance arenas, amazing variety if you want to tinker with the weapon mods and find loadout combos.It's like trying to blend the best parts of DOOM 2016 and Eternal, with the combo gameplay of Eternal while still having the freedom of a factory load of ammunition on your hands if you just want to go balls to the walls with one weapon of your choice.Overall it's not objectively the "best game", but does it have to be? It got me hooked in all it's unfinished and borked glory, just like many cult classics of today.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game so, so bad because it feels like it should be fantastic, but then there's the... everything else. Side missions are one of your primary sources of income but are so poorly designed that it feels like a joke. Enemies endlessly respawn behind you, to your side, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in front of you. Most enemies are squishy as hell and die in a few shots and some have insane health bars, (yellow shield enemies) but also do some of the most insane hit scan damage of any game ever made. You get absolutely turned inside out in this so fast that it makes Blood look like Knack. What it really wants to be is DOOM Eternal meets EYE Divine Cybermancy (cuz these devs made that game) but instead it's like the Mars level from EYE meets DOOM via Roblox total conversion mod.The shooting is fun and the environments are beautiful. Runs really well and is great conceptually. But it often feels like it was made poorly on purpose, as a joke, and because of that I really struggle to recommend it. I may play more and change my review but the frankly OMEGA ♥♥♥♥ balancing has put me off.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: An incomprehensible mess of a casual-tailored looty-shooty from the same people who made the infamous E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy.Pros:+ Sick soundtrack+ Good voice acting+ Very stylish from start to end+ First few missions are actually funCons:- The game falls apart shortly after- Lootboxes suck (strictly only in-game currency but they still suck)- Story is completely incomprehensible- Only full-auto weapons work (forget shotguns/sniper rifles etc)- Weapon customization is basically useless- Bosses are  bullet-spongy- Short campaign (~5 hours maybe?), side missions only to farm money- Weirdest health system to date?- Takedown animations are super slow and berserk mode sucks- Depth of field cannot be disabled (not even via configs)- Just all-around a confusing mess of a game that gets worse and worse- And you get to mutilate your own dog Sadly I am a stranger to the W40k universe. I don't know if it's the lack of background knowledge, poor writing, or both, but this was probably the densest story I have ever played through. Everyone keeps mentioning character names, factions, locations that I have no clue about. Every single mission I was completely lost as to what is happening or why or where I am even going. I played through the full game twice and I retained nothing. I couldn't even remotely recap the story if I tried. I've completed 100%, played all missions twice, maxed out all upgrades long ago, levelled up my character high enough, and have had a solely loot-focused build for ages now. In all that time I had  +3 (max quality) weapon drop. A shotgun. Which I later sold off because it sucked so much it . I'm not even kidding. I did get like six +3 armors though, but of course you can only equip one at a time. So... Yeah. Thankfully no microtransactions in sight but it still sucks so much. First of all, from my experience the only gun that works past the first few missions is whatever has the highest rate of fire with decent damage. The game is very,  fast-paced. Enemies jump, leap, dash, teleport, and unburrow all around you constantly. You absolutely have no time to aim down the sights, ever - let alone go for headshots (let me reiterate, first few missions are way better and this all does work but it falls apart later on). You cannot afford to miss an important shot either. So forget sniper rifles, shotguns, pistols, and any semi-auto rifles. It's all about full-auto rifles and hipfire. Customization is very poor, vast majority of upgrades are basically "better accuracy, worse handling", which means higher accuracy to already accurate weapons at the cost of time to aim down the sights which you never do anyway. It's useless. The default barrel is always the one that has +damage to it so upgrading it for "less damage, more accuracy" is stupid. I want the opposite! Because... The game eventually gives you numerous options to deal with low-tier enemies with ease. Unfortunately a lot of enemies (especially later on) are bullet sponges and despite all the abilities and customization the only method of dealing with them seems to be "just keep shooting lmao". Bosses are so much worse, though. I take my best-upgraded +2 rifles and I swear I sink at least 500+ bullets into each boss, . It's beyond ridiculous. If there is some strategy to defeating them faster well then I 100%'ed the game and I have not figured it out. I started the game on Old School difficulty but the further I went the more broken everything was. Before you say "git gud lmao" it's not a skill issue really, I simply do not understand how the game wants to be played. So you have two ways of regaining health, using medkits (3 per level, no more, cannot be found on maps) and hurting enemies. The rule is: shortly after taking damage, dealing damage back to enemies restores health; the faster you do it and the closer you are to enemies, the more health you get back. It's all very... Finicky and inconsistent to say the least. The issue with higher difficulties is that you take damage way faster than you dish it out. The game encourages you to like jump on a wall and make multiple kills while wallrunning for style points and apparently extra health back? Except wallrun-kills are the last thing you want to attempt to do (you'll probably die before you connect to the wall). For the reference, both wallrun-related achievements have the lowest completion rate on steam. You get 13 story missions that you can get through in maybe 5 hours or so. You also get side missions but those are like mini-arena mode made of pieces of the same campaign levels. They aren't like secondary quests or anything, they're just generated randomly and there is a tiny (often useless) reward for beating a large number of them. They're there to farm money to beat the campaign easier. Anyway from there on all the content you have left is achievement hunting, if you don't care about steam achievements then you have nothing to do. I do care and I've finished everything in 16 hours total. I did not enjoy most of it to be honest. I did it so that you don't have to :p You start with a perfectly normal mastiff, purely of flesh. And then you rip its jaw off to replace it with cybernetics, saw off every limb to replace them with metal rods, and tear out the spinal cord for "upgrading" it as well. All while the game awards you achievements for "improving" your dog. I mean the process itself isn't graphic, you only get a before/after but sheesh it's just disturbing. Couldn't we have an already augmented dog that I would strengthen and improve over time by just replacing the augs? Not tear most of its flesh away piece by piece, ? One weapon upgrade says it "increases armor penetration". By how much? What is "armor" even? Are all enemies considered armored or just some? Is their full body armored or only some hitboxes? The game never tells you. How is "kill style" calculated exactly? I read all of the tests and speculations I could find but rank A is the best I could ever do no matter how hard I've tried, never S even once. What is the magic instakill blade you pull out during berserk mode? Why cannot it be equipped otherwise if you have it on you? Why don't you get a damage reduction or auto-leaps towards enemies during it like every other game has it? Why do you still use your weak knife by triggering a takedown while in berserk? Why do most weapon upgrades focus on accuracy/stability/handling when none of that matters? Why does my fully-upgraded dog kill humans easily but if it engages an enemy dog they both glitch out and do nothing? Why can motion blur be disabled but depth of field cannot? So many questions, so few answers.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A Doom style game in the Warhammer 40k universe should be a match made in heaven but for Necromunda it just wasn't very enjoyable.The setting of the seedier areas of a hive world is pretty cool and I thought the graphics and visuals look alright but the gameplay itself just wasn't very good.Doom 2016 and Eternal are great because the movement, gunplay, level designs and enemies are all highly polished and complement each other really well. In Necromunda all those elements lack that necessary polish and are less satisfying. The movement I thought was probably the best of these aspects but even then feels a bit too quick and messy and doesnt sync up well with the gunplay. The guns are also more like peashooters which is a let down given the 40k setting. A bolter should just not feel like that.  The whole looter mechanics around weapons and items just feels overly complex and unsatisfying. I would have preferred picking from a smaller pool of weapons that could be levelled and upgraded through the game like in Doom.The enemies AI is pretty braindead but also paired with amazing aim so they just try and crowd you out and then accurately gun you down. That with the subpar shooting just sort of makes combat feel subpar.So given all that I personally wouldn't recommend it. It has the bare bones of a good game somewhere in there but fails to pull it off.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Launched in a rough state, and there's no reason to play it after you're finished. That said, I don't regret seeing it through to the end. Rarely the game froze for a second when I wasn't in danger, but ultimately performance was fine on my PC, and I had all settings max on 4k with motion blur off. Necromunda: Hired Gun is riddled with jank and bugs, though not unplayable for it, and the way you have to fight can start off pretty limiting. The story turns out to be extremely uninteresting by the end, but combat gets decent by the time you don't have to keep abusing executes. The dog is mostly just a cooldown to let you see enemies, he's a bit frail and buggy, and steals kills that you wanted to survive off of. This thing still needs a lot of polish, there is usually always something annoying you or breaking your immersion. Executes making you fly around the room, audio mixing making story characters inaudible, and such. Not deal-breakers if they amuse you, but it's genuinely quite regular.Once I adjusted to all of its issues, I liked the game overall. I was delighted to explore a whole game where every conceivable object is plastered with the Adeptus Mechanicus insignia. Just as with their last 40k game, all of the gameplay issues getting in the way of your enjoyment are still set against the backdrop of an utterly GORGEOUSLY detailed 40k setting.I recommend giving this one a few weeks before buying, because they might patch some of the more glaring problems out. If it gets attention like that? Hell yeah! Pick this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, especially for those who are fans of the Warhammer 40K property and are looking for a FPS. It might have a touch of jank (grappling hook I'm looking at you!) but its more than worth being able to see the vast amazing setting of the Underhive of Necromunda's Hive Cities in first person rather than in miniature, with its massive machines and constantly grinding industry. If I had to compare it to a game I'd say its mostly similar to DOOM (2016) or DOOM Eternal with a kill and stay mobile or risk being pinned down and swiftly killed. I'd say its weak points are its story (which I found a bit nebulous and disconnected) and a lack of variety and visceral feel of the Doom style executions. Augmetic powers and weapons are both pretty good if a bit lacking compared to the massive amount of weapons just used by the Imperium in WH40K Lore. However for the price and on the whole I certainly and whole-heartedly recommend this game to fans of Warhammer and fans of FPSs like DOOM.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where you are shooting people all the time, and that shooting is very satisfying. Very fast paced and doom like with hordes of enemies charging you down, but without the crappy ammo farming that ruined doom in my mind. Certainly feels like an old build engine game had a love child with warframe. At its full price i would only recommended this to warhammer fans as i suspect a lot of the references will just confuse other people. On sale 100% worth a pick up. A fun game with mechanics that are designed around just making things more fun, a rarity these days.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a budget Doom Eternal + Serious Sam + Unreal + parkourI am having a lot of fun with it. The Level Design is repetitive when doing the side bounty missions. The story missions are good.The guns feel good, the mobility is nice, and the powers are cool.It's definitely worth 20-25 bucks. _childDocuments_.review: I came into this game knowing full well that it'd be a mixed bag and it never stopped being one throughout my initial playthrough. I don't want to write a full dissertion about the issues this game faces but I think the most important one is at the core of its upgrade system.What is the point of having a semi-randomized loot system with tiered rarity to items when, ultimately, the biggest different between rarities is a slight damage boost and little else. Yes, you can add charms and trinkets to make your weapon more powerful. Give additional crit chance, chance for an elemental effect, but ultimately none of it FEELS like it matters when those additions barely move the needle. There's little need for nuance or strategy in loadout.They put an emphasis on balancing your stats with the attachments you can choose but there's truthfully only about 3 attachments for each attachment slot with everything else being a cosmetic reskin. Functionally the same.Armors and abilities have even less customization.Outside of weapons, progression is entirely linear and they're all upgraded from the same currency, your money.If you're willing to grind a few hours of the procedurally generated side missions, you'll easily get enough money to max out your character and companion abilities. Then you're just spending money to customize your guns.Very little would be lost if this loot system was replaced with a traditional weapon wheel.All of this is without me diving into the story which is as ignorable as it is forgettable.The inconsistent and nonsensical melee takedown system.The incoherent rating system, specifically in regards to "Kill Style."The controls being extremely busy.Enemies feeling miserable to takedown once you progress past the halfway point in the campaign (trivial once you max out your character and gain the ability to instantly kill enemies en masse).Uninspired boss fights with poorly explained/telegraphed attacks.A generally flat skill curve.The difficulty scale being extremely out of pocket (just play Normal).Armor feeling lackluster and unimpactful.The wallrun and grapple mechanic being often times broken and irregular.Instantly dying if you fell off the map, consuming your limited self-revives for missing a jump.The long, obnoxious animation to summon your assist.Had this game simply been a Doom 2016 style shooter set in the Warhammer universe, that would've been fine. Perfectly acceptable. Instead it tries to play as if its a looter shooter, a boomer shooter with a stylish system a la Devil May Cry, it wants to be so much more but it is woefully underdeveloped.It does some things right like sound, gunplay, and environmental design (aesthetically) but it falls to make a positive or lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: There's good things about the game, but there's a lot of bad things as well. For starters: you can just see enemies spawn in front of you and pop into existence before your eyes, and if not, they're popping in super close to you, which can make certain sections pretty bullsiht. Luckily you have some bullsthi of your own, since takedowns are super busted and give you full invincibility and restore some health when completed and you can pretty much spam them on these enemies that spawn around you, with the exception of enemies that have shields, but break those and they can then be instant killed. Unfortunately this is kinda boring, at one point in either mission 3 or 4 I literally spammed it like 30 times in a row and they kept putting enemies there.Also enemies are just kinda running at you, never take cover, and will just hit you instantly as soon as they see you, which at 1st isnt a huge problem because you can use your limited health kits and revives, but at mission 4 at the part where you have to break some robots, there are enemies that 2-3 shot you and have shields, and more of them will spawn very close to you in a very tight area (a literal mine), so dodge spamming without running into more of them at close range and dying is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and takedown spamming for your life is impossible. Long range attacking the robot and disregarding these enemies is also out, stuff is in the way and enemies are spawning and hurting you, plus that aggros them and then you have the same problem because the robots you need to destroy are beefy and you can just kill them and head out because it takes like 4 mags of ammo. When you finish that, a new enemy variant spawns with more enemies and if you die, there's no checkpoint so it's back to doing the robot part you died a ton on already.The player does get a bunch of cool things they can use, but they aren't really explained, I found out later they had individual buttons for them in the options, on bad default keys and had to remap (it was like 9 on the keyboard to the equals sign?). Gigantic cooldowns though, so bionics couldn't be relied upon.The dog is also a dumbass and is mostly useful for giving you maphacks to see where enemies are. You send him out to attack, he insta kills an enemy after grappling it for a second, but then he just runs right back to you and stands near you? Like no, keep attacking what the hell I'm busy shooting. He will just sit there and die while getting beat up by a big guy if you dont tell him to kill things for you constantly, which a lot of the time the game will go nope sorry, can't reach and he just sits there.There's also just like too much weapon customization and a lot of it is rng gated from loot pickups and it's a bit overwhelming so you just go eh screw it most of the time.I didn't play any B missions or A missions or whatever because I just wanted to do the campaign 1st and come back to those, but I hit a wall on mission 4 like I mentioned up there, so I think I have to to grind my gear up, so this game seems to also have grinding.I'm reminded why I don't buy double A or triple A games too much these days after getting this. They're all obsessed with wallrunning too like it's fun, cause it's not, you get magneted to walls all the time on accident in this game. I did enjoy it a bit, but the negatives just outweigh the fun and it made me regret buying it. There's too much to fix with patches, it's not worth it for them to rework, just go play ULTRAKILL or something unless you're a huge 40k nerd.That being said, I'll probably put some more hours into it to see the side missions, but I already bought it and wont/cant refund it, I dont recommend the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that needs tempered expectations. You won't find dozens of hours of playtime here. The story isn't good. A lot of the animations are janky. But the shooting is awesome. Your enemies straight up explode. Constantly. It's weird though, because you don't even have to shoot them. You can just use janky takedowns once you're in melee range. There's loot involved, but you can play through the whole game with whatever you want equipped. Guns can be customized and, most importantly, shooting them is a blast. You heal by doing damage, so I just ran around never using cover, all while shooting everything in the face until said face became hamburger. There are only 13 story missions, but side missions pop up infinitely. Those are set in the story mission levels. They mostly involve killing more things. If the idea of wall running, air-dashing above people, all the while riddling them with bullets 'til they pop doesn't sound like fun to you, you won't like this game. It's short, it's not difficult, and it's quite stupid. But I enjoyed the carnage. A dozen hours is more than enough to see everything the game has to offer, but upgrading bionics is solid. As is upgrading your cyborg dog. You can have it kill people. And really, that's what Necromunda: Hired Gun is about. Vicious slaughter. Nothing more, nothing less. No WH40K knowledge is required. Even if you have it, you might not care about the plot or setting. The levels look awesome, though, with detailed, high-res textures and an excellent use of color. It definitely doesn't look like a smaller game on that front. Unless you're looking at the character models. Jank that way lies. Still, I recommend the game. Maybe not for $40, but I had fun. I also like mindless action, though, which is really all it has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Wait for it to go on sale, play it, then move on after you're boredCustomization: The game offers limited customization options with shallow loot variety. Weapon skins lack an editor, which could have enhanced personalization.Combat: Combat is satisfactory and on par with most FPS games. However, the limited ability menu feels clunky and difficult to use effectively.Levels: The levels visually align with the 40K aesthetic, but the platforming can be confusing, and environmental interactions are sparse. More interactive elements and diverse details could enhance immersion.Stability: Performance issues are minimal, but load times can be excessively long.Content: The game provides a short main story of 15 to 20 hours, with repetitive endgame content. After 21 hours of play, side missions felt monotonous, diminishing replay value.Summary: The game is worth playing if it goes on sale, but it’s likely to be a one-time experience unless you have a strong nostalgic attachment.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I am a huge Doom fan - I've played Doom since I was a kid and I played the two recent iterations. I love them and played the crap out of them, even had Doom for switch. So, I'm going to say it now: this is not a Doom clone at all. It does, however, have that zippy boomer shooter feel you get playing games like Quake, Unreal, and (obviously) Doom. It has finishers, but so did Aliens Vs. Predator on Xbox 360 and that predates a lot of comparisons so go figure.What Necromunda: Hired Gun actually is, is a game that builds off the mistakes of games like Space Hulk: Deathwing. Where there were barely any rewards, or only those given via co-op and surviving relentless hordes of Genestealers, Hired Gun is full of worthwhile upgrades and rewards that make things worth grinding for. The light RPG elements are never pointless, the secrets are worthwhile, and like a lot of games of old - changing the difficulty actually nets you additional rewards to match the additional challenge. You can easily get caught up sinking hours into the semi-random side missions and building up faction rep. You are never not rewarded, and its interesting to see how deep the game gets through repeated playthroughs of levels (you can also get rankings that net you even more stuff).Where things felt off in Deathwing when it came to combat, this game is frantic and brimming with player choice. You got a plethora of abilities at your disposal, which all feel very useful, and have their own twists. The gameplay is fast and fun, but difficult to master. You can go in guns blazing or even semi-stealth if you are really that good (and have the appropriate weapon customization). Every gun feels like it should, something I've never got in any W40K game. Finally, every weapon feels like it has weight and packs the appropriate punch. Atop that, you can add anything from Fire, to Static, to Toxic and Nuclear status effects to every shot (cool).Only problem is its a new game and a few issues appear here and there. I've clipped through a wall and the game crashed once. Not a big deal considering even the mighty Doom Eternal gave me even more trouble when I played through it.Check it out, its a worthwhile game for more then just Warhammer 40k fans. And its better then just about any other shooter released in the last few years (aside from the obvious).
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR It's a 7/10, flawed but fun. Fun out weighs the flaws.Pros - Immersive world, excellent variety of environments in what could of easily been very samey. Art Directions on point. - Fast paced and enjoyable FPS. - Do not regret buying.Cons - UX is not intuitive, E is sometimes confirm, sometimes its Escape, sometimes its Enter. zero consistency in menu commands.-In game the E (use) is awful at responding (tbh i was getting key drops with reload and weapon switching so much I had to test my keyboard, it was the game). So picky, can take multiple attempts to talk to the bartender or pick up a battery mid mission, especially egregious when you're trying to perform a take down mid fight.I am really having a blast with the game, just a few issues keeping me from loving it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so the first thing you need to know: this game is janky. That's the first impression it gives and something that remains true, though the game fills out and stabilizes after the first mission. And it's textbook Eastern European jank: the writing is terrible, some of the animations are shockingly out of place, the level design is iffy, the controls deviate from what everyone expects. the checkpoint system is punishing, and everything (from the exposition to the time spent in the hub to the missions to the boss fights) takes three times as long as it should. And it's a DOOM. It's not the first thing that comes to mind when I think of the small-unit tactics of Necromunda, but there you have it. It's an old-school run and gun shooter with a few extras tacked on, and "tacked on" is the exact phrase I mean. Some bits, like the grappling hook, are neat, but none of it adds substantively to the core gameplay, instead existing as new varieties of hammers for new kinds of nails. This part is quite good; the fundamental kinetic shooting play is solid, and if you like this sort of game, it's a good one.I don't care for that sort of game. But I DO like Necromunda. And where this game shines is in evoking the atmosphere of Necromunda. This game offers an unflinching tour of a terrible place that feels just right, with all the weirdness, enormity, and casual disregard for human life you'd expect. The environs are frequently legitimately disturbing. The game makes me uncomfortable in a way that I would honestly not expect from a 40K budget title. But there it is. This is a hive world walking simulator that happens to feature a prodigious amount of gunplay. That's the draw. This game evokes the universe spectacularly well in the form of a perfectly serviceable shooter. If you love Necromunda and you care more about atmosphere than actual writing (and this is 40K so I have to assume that's like 95% of us), this game rules. For anyone else, this game is fine, and you should consider picking it up if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the style of the old classic E.Y.E you will absolutely love this. It doesn't have anywhere near the depth and customization but for a quick action shooter-sorta looter this ain't a bad title. Needs polish, for SURE but in its state it is easily playable but don't expect it to be perfect. There are only a few outstanding issues I would say about this, might as well get them out of the way sooner than later!They can use a bit of work. Especially with the pathing. They will get stuck a lot, and the game will hard stutter whenever a new round of enemies comes within play. I also had multiple instances where doing the side missions ended up needing to be re-done/given up due to AI either not spawning, or on one occurrence was just a model that floated around on the last defense wave. I feel like the game knows this though, as it gives you a dog that will give you wallhack (? I know, little weird. Speaking of the dog ♥♥♥♥ was he pretty much useless, besides using the walls when activating it to find the last straggler I never used him. Constantly pressing C on enemies and bringing out the toy to signal him to attack takes a whopping 3+ seconds in all and it just doesn't fit with the pace of the game. Why they made it like that instead of just having the character voiceline it IDK)While searching through chests and killing enemies you will constantly be showered in these "Trinkets" or "Charms" that you can attach to your weapon or onto your character for a little extra boost. When I say little I mean it. At first I thought the game wanted me to hang onto them in my inventory like Diablo 2 did with Charms but instead you have to add them to your gun through the smith. Then once I actually got a screen that allowed me to see what they did I ended up just not giving a ♥♥♥♥ about them half way through the game. If I got a rare one, cool, but I wasn't rushing to get it put on. There are also damage modifier things but I honestly have forgotten what their called and I just finished this game in less than a day after purchase. Thats how little impact they had, atleast I felt. Once you get to actually customizing the guns and adding more and different attachments you kinda learn what you want. I ended up just maxing damage on a majority of the guns, seemed to work! ( Pro tip - Max damage and then just max the Aimbot skill and its pretty much over. The aimbot skill can DESTROY rooms of enemies and using a sub machine gun with super high recoil, suddenly go to 0 recoil and every shot hitting will make the room much easier )What in the world is up with like 80% of the enemies being female? Don't get me wrong that's completely fine and I am sure it opened the door for more female voice actors and talent alike but I felt like I was just slaughtering women over and over every mission. What's up with that?*Spoiler* Also as a jest little bug report, one of the skills is a strength enhancer which gives you a big sword that basically one shots/Close to one shots. *BUT* with the electric wizard ladies that teleport around they seem to need like, 5 or 6+ hits to kill them, while everyone around them was down in 1 hit. Even with all my skills maxed I never did a one shot to them. Always had to keep going. No biggie :)Forewarning, once you beat the game you are done. Like, nothing else left in the game to do besides dumb repeatable side missions. If I didn't do a bunch of side missions I probably would have finished in -2 hours times, but the fact that it did impact gameplay and time played makes it worth it, but only during the story. Story is done, game is done. Unless you just want to start again with an already pretty shortish game be my guest but I believe this will stay uninstalled for the time being simply because I have nothing to do in the game anymore.There is a wide variety of enemy types, all with different weapons and abilities. Was nice. That's basically all the outstanding issues I had with the game, but I think I am due to give this game the credit it deserves.If you are looking for a good action reaction shooter with a little bit of loot elements and are feelin down for a bit of grinding between missions, I highly suggest this game. The atmosphere, characters and story in general were a solid 9/10 for me. I noticed myself not skipping through dialogue (Except with the bar lady, I get it, rats are drunk and you are for some reason tied to the story because you a bartender. She hears things, and tells you them. Basically it. I would have loved to be able to spend credits and just get my character drunk. Would've been a great chance to introduce random events/Mega Bosses) and actually listening/paying attention to the small details they would say. Which DOES get you some better loot in some cases if you just look around/Go a different route then whats in front of you. The game is linear, but still allows for full exploration. Now you might fall out of the map/insta die due to a invis barrier but if you play games you should know when where you're going is just a pit of death. Speaking of the maps, the design is AWESOME. The whole steampunk/Mechanical vibe the game holds stands out everywhere you look. You are all in caves underground with who knows what and the game shows it. So bravo on that part.Skills are pretty standard but useful. I wish I had used the blast or field skills more, learn the muscle memory of using the wheel and quickly going to the skill and it will make the game so much more fun. I mainly used the aimbot, walls and slow down but I slowly started using the other ones on the bigger enemies. You upgrade yourself as the story goes on, but I went full steam ahead and as soon as I could do the side repeatable bounties on the S tier I knocked them out pretty quickly. If you go full steam ahead you can easily clear a S tier bounty in less than 2 minutes. Maybe 1 depending on the mission itself.The "Takedown" skill/Spam E while shooting the big guys seems to be the way to go for the big guys. I soon realized that the takedown skill is very useful and honestly needed in some spots. Thank goodness they make you invuln while the animation is going because I know for sure I wouldn't survive all the shots from the 5 giant robots surrounding me. Can also acrue for some cheeky fast kills/S bounties for taking down hacked robots.No need to go into it. Its a grapple hook that makes the movement fluid.The gun mechanics and shooting in general feels very solid, not too god like but not too garbo either.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Get it while on sale.Average shooter, set in a 40k universe. I didn't encounter any major bugs and after using GeForce Experience to optimize the game, I stopped encountering lag/jank.Game has quite a few cons, but, unfortunately, it's one of the best 40k shooters. I'd say this is one of those situations where a "Meh" would work better than a Yes/No.I'm going with Yes because the positives are a bit "heavier" than the negatives.Positive:+ Upgrades drastically change your gameplay;+ You have a doggo THAT YOU CAN PET (I used it as a radar, so, no idea if it's bugged or not. I've seen people complain);+ A large variety of weapons;+ Weapon customization similar to Fallout (worse, but similar);+ Weapons feel ok;+ Voice acting is alright;+ Move or die.Negative:- Main mission is average at best;- Final boss battle feels forced;- Some levels are boring (I've surprised myself on several occasions just rushing the objectives to finish the mission);- Secondary missions seem slapped on;- Reputation system is close to useless (once you max your rep with a faction, you get a random item and that's it);- Your appearance doesn't change when applying upgrades;- The world around you seems dead.

_childDocuments_.review: To all those reviews saying "maybe check it out if you’re a warhammer enthusiast", as an enthusiast I made a list that might be helpful for those who already know all of the gameplay related problems.There are no special skins that look like the classic weapons from the tabletop, like the godwyn bolter or armageddon pattern autogun. The skins are very basic recolors with not even an ultra bump mapped mastercrafted relic. Everything has picatinny rail and the basic level 1 gun looks the same as the higher rarities.Boltguns are just slightly slower machineguns with zero special ammo choices that would explode like a grenade, exactly how you don’t want to see them in a game. Seriously, they are just slightly higher damage generic full auto guns with very manageable recoil. Nothing special and completely forgettable.There is no regular lasgun in the game, but an entire faction has plasmaguns and they aren’t THAT rare in necromunda.  We get 7 different auto/stubber/boltguns in the same sort of “aim,shoot” weapon role, so… why not? They should at least play differently with higher capacity ammo and a different sort of accuracy and recoil.They do have a gravgun, a plasmagun, a grenade launcher, a heavy bolter, 2 heavy stubbers and a hotshot long las, but they don’t feel that special or particularly more deadly because they compete with the same 2 weapon slots as your basic autoguns and ammo is ultra-plentiful and generically fills all weapons.There is no melee weapon component. No chainswords, power swords or even a regular non take down melee button. Just a special berserker “smack then die” speed mode special ability.  So, there is no pistol sword combo, even though that’s what Kal Jerico carries in the cutscenes. 90% of the propaganda posters in this game are directly from the games workshop website, so I’ve seen them all already. The rest of the senary is nice though, and it borrows just enough from the plastic kits to look right without seeming copy/pasted.The great big surprise of Genestealers existing is subverted by you being able to take side missions from the cult already. It consists of one mission with only one special new unit. and it isn’t fun or revisited again.There is a giant faction list who give outside missions, including the Inquisition and enforcers, but you never see any of them in the game, and I’m not even sure what the increases exactly do besides maybe give slightly more money? The 3 gangs fight basically exactly the same. I would have liked to see Cawdor with waves of rabble with scrap shotguns or a more technologically advanced Van Saar with a long range focus or something more dynamic. Esher, Golath, and Orlock will mostly just stand around shooting you regardless of their few unique units. Oh and apparently everyone has Refractor Fields so that’s couldn’t have been a Van Saar gimmick.Story is blah and basically just serves the plot to move to new locations and is extreme loaded to be pretty much have all the important bits in the final cutscene with a mild sequel/dlc open ending.I beat the campaign in 7 hours, then spent another 3 hours messing around cheesing the very easy side missions to max out the dog upgrades that I never used to see if it gave me an achievement or different head pat animation. No achievement, no new head pat. I’m done with the game and looking forward to Darktide.7/10 if on sale for 25 bucks. Nah, no thank you/10 at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm here for the Warhammer visuals, and they more than delivered on that aspect. One of the very first things you see in game is a gothic cathedral, and its magnificent. The soundtrack also SLAPS!  I'll be coming back to it over the weekend to finish the story, but I don't play games like this expecting a groundbreaking story. Here's hoping to more Warhammer FPS's in the future! :)

_childDocuments_.review: In short- if you are a 40k fan it's a must buy. Best 40k shooter to date.Graphics are absolutely amazing. The design of the locations is overwhelmingly good. It realy does deliver the 40k vibe, despite the game not beeing centered around iconic space marines and orks. The character design is not falling behind either, though the game is somewhat lacking in the animation department- but considering the gameplay speed, you will barely even notice it. Performancewise it ran with constand 60fps on ultra settings on a 1660S, i5 6500 and 16 GB of Ram. I had 3 crashed throughout whole campaign, every time right after the loading screen and never had to replay a campaign section becouse of it. No freezes, no stutter for me atleast.Gameplaywise it is obviously inspired by DooM Eternal. The exuction is not perfect but isn't bad either. I feel like they made melee exectutions too simple/easy to perform.  Wallrun certainly adds extra flavour to the gameplay. The implementation of the 40k arsenal though is 10/10. That sort of weapon customization has naver been seen in a game set in 40k. Shooting the guns feels extremely satisfying. Impact reminds me on the new Wolfenstein games.For the price- it's a gem, and considering, that we are talking about a real time 40k game anyway-must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a game that you're only really going to enjoy if you love the Necromunda/40k setting. I was constantly captivated by the world. Any time you pause you could be a wallpaper or art in a book. The setting is so *chefs kiss*. It's a shame though that you barely get time to look at it. The fast Doom/NecroVision style gunplay is great, but doesn't fit the mood for a multi-millennia old factory world with heavy guns. I really wanted this to play like Bioshock or Metro, where ammo is rare and enemies are tough. Mowing down thousands of people because their lives have no worth is very 40k, but it also means there is little thought to how you kill the about 3 different types of enemies or even bosses. I can't help but feel the grapple hook and double jumping actually hurt the game. I really wanted to take my time in each level because they're so carefully crafted and full of love. I wanted each gun's use to be special and for me to think about which enemy needed what ammo type to kill but there wasn't any point. There is also no point to the story. There is a cutscene at the beginning and at the end and if you can remember what happened then good for you, but I don't think it matters. Even if you try to play this game in one sitting, good luck because it is buggy and the fast movement will get you stuck in some parts where you have to reload levels. Random crashes are also no uncommon. It might sound like this is coming off more as a negative review, but  I know Streum On Studio is full of talented people and I hope they get all even more funding for the next game. I'd like to see what they can do with an even bigger budget.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: As just about everyone else already mentioned in the reviews, the maps are stunning. Diverse, very 40K. It's just..well everything else seems bad. The shooting feels clinical and boring to me, from the weapons to the enemies. Enemies spawn all over the place. _childDocuments_.review: True to its name, Hired Gun lacks a certain.. support structure. Leaving the player high and dry when things get messy. It sure looks appealing though.As other people have explained, the developers of Hired Gun portray the environmental atmosphere of 40k especially well. An unfortunate side-effect though is that for gameplay purposes everything is a visual mess - navigation, target identification, treasure - all of this would be near impossible to see without the giant outlines placed on them. Which certainly helps, and you do have cybernetics as an excuse; along with the option to turn them off if you're feeling brave.Combat. Combat is of course the main feature. You run around, quite fast, and shoot things. Arguably too fast. It is clear the game wants the experience to be speedy and hectic, akin to the Doom reboot, and to facilitate this you have the power to regain life - with the specific caveat of this being only for a few seconds after you are injured. So yes, get in the fray, take damage, deal damage; but if there is a pause and you are on low health, death is likely your only option. Doom however, provides clear options of what will give you health: execute an enemy, burn an enemy, etc. To be fair, the game does have medkits that you will run out of and revive items, the latter you can buy at any of the many checkpoint servitors around the maps. So you are not stopped from playing or continuing, but it's more the inherent nature of the system that you are nearly expected to take damage - regardless of your attempts - especially if you're playing on hard, and have limited ways to fix it. On hard you can just explode because someone had a moment to look at you funny.Overall Hired Gun is okay. It's not strictly bad, there can be some fun, some nice weapons; but it's not really adequate either. Unfulfilling.On the plus side however, you do get a dog, and you do get to do the petting. Even after you mutilat- er... replace their weak fle- ... upgrade. Even after you upgrade them.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review by saying I am a huge 40k fan, and this game definitely captures the heart of what I love about Warhammer.  The art direction is absolutely fantastic, and I found myself distracted by set pieces thinking, "Oh hey!  Look at that shrine in the wall!  Such 40k!  So wow!"  It really is good.I'm on an i7-9700 and using a RTX 2070 with everything on ultra with no hitches.  I played with the DLSS settings but the game runs comfortably at 100+ fps.  I see a lot of people having framerate issues, the devs have noted these issues in the forums and are working on an optimization patch.  Personally I have had no crashes, and only stutters on the first mission for 15 seconds.On to the actual review: Is the story going to sweep you away, carried aloft by the Emperor's Angels?  No.  The story poses as a pseudo-detective "find the bad guy by tracking his ganger connections" but we all really know why we play this game.  WE ARE BOUNTY HUNTERS, AND WE HUNT BOUNTIES.  Each mission is really just a framing for some fantastic experiences in a violence soaked 40k theme park.  The gunplay and  game is very Doom Eternal-esque, so if you enjoy that and 40k, give this a try.My favorite things so far:The scale - levels are huge, grand, and packed with verticality.Guns are ridiculously fun to use.Installing augmentations into yourself and your cybermastiff is neat and grant cool abilities.There is a ton of detail relevant to 40k hidden throughout the levels and hub if you feel like appreciating it.What I dislike:The "jank" people refer to I think stems from the over-bobbing of the camera during executions and some animations.  While in real life your head would indeed bob and thrash around like that, it is very visually confusing.The cybermastiff is underutilized, and has pathing issues because of the insane verticality previously mentioned.The story is a bit weak, but I forgive it.Do you like 40k?  Then you will like this game.  It isn't a AAA title by a huge studio, but I am having an absolutely fantastic time playing it.  There are glitches, there are janky animations, and there is an entire level devoted to fighting on a moving train the size of a city block that just screams THIS IS THE IMPERIUM OF MAN.  Absolutely fantastic time so far!  Would recommend.
